headline: Bandh over NEET leak shuts schools, colleges in Telangana
full_text:
Bandh over NEET leak shuts schools, colleges in Telangana
Educational institutions across Telangana remained closed on Friday as a statewide bandh called by student organisations
Educational institutions across Telangana remained closed on Friday as a statewide bandh called by student organisations disrupted academic activities in protest against the alleged NEET-UG question paper leak, repeated irregularities in national-level entrance examinations and the Centre’s handling of the education system.
The protesters also condemned the alleged police lathi-charge on students demonstrating in New Delhi over the examination controversy.
The bandh, backed by a broad coalition of student and youth organisations, led to the closure of schools, junior colleges, degree colleges and universities across the state. Several universities also postponed examinations scheduled for the day.
The shutdown was called by the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI), Students’ Federation of India (SFI), All India Students’ Federation (AISF), Progressive Democratic Students Union (PDSU), All India Forum for Democratic Students (AIFDS), All India Students Bloc (AISB), All India Progressive Students Union (AIPSU), All India Students’ Association (AISA), Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI), All India Youth Federation (AIYF) and Students Islamic Organisation (SIO).
“We demand the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, as he is morally responsible for the NEET paper leak and successive failures in conducting public examinations,” AISF state secretary Putta Laxman said.
He also sought stringent punishment for those involved in the alleged paper leak, withdrawal of cases registered against protesting students, and measures to restore transparency and credibility in the country’s examination system.
NSUI state president Yadavalli Venkataswamy said the bandh was total and peaceful.
“We want exemplary punishment for those responsible for the alleged NEET paper leak, and ₹1 crore ex gratia for the families of students who allegedly died by suicide following the examination controversy,” he said.
The bandh had a widespread impact across Hyderabad and other districts. Several government and private schools declared a holiday in anticipation of the protests.
Telangana Recognised Private Schools Association president S N Reddy said a majority of the nearly 3,500 private schools within the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation limits remained closed. Private junior colleges and degree colleges also suspended classes.
Higher educational institutions were similarly affected. Osmania University, Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University (JNTU) and Kaloji Narayana Rao University of Health Sciences postponed all examinations scheduled for Friday, saying revised dates would be announced later.
The agitation also drew political support, with the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) and the Congress holding separate protests.
BRS working president K T Rama Rao participated in a demonstration organised by the party’s student wing at Dharna Chowk near Indira Park.
“Students across the country are frustrated not only over the alleged question paper leak but also over Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s unfulfilled promise of creating two crore jobs annually,” KTR said.
He accused security personnel of using excessive force against protesters, including women, during demonstrations in New Delhi on July 20.
“We demand the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and the withdrawal of cases filed against protesting youth,” he said.
The Congress also staged demonstrations in Hyderabad. State Congress working president M Anjan Kumar Yadav led a rally from the MLA Quarters at Adarsh Nagar towards the Indira Gandhi statue at Necklace Road.
He and hundreds of party workers later attempted to march towards Dharna Chowk, but police stopped and detained them before the rally could proceed.

headline: Abhijeet Dipke's mother breaks down as Pradhan resigns: ‘Couldn’t sleep, was worried about him'
full_text:
Abhijeet Dipke's mother breaks down as Pradhan resigns: ‘Couldn’t sleep, was worried about him'
Abhijeet Dipke's mother Anita had tears in her eyes as she recalled what her son witnessed over the past few days as he led the CJP protest in Delhi.
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke's parents broke down on camera as news of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan stepping down surfaced on Saturday. Interacting with the media, Dipke's mother hailed her son's “massive victory” and said she had sleepless nights because she worried about him.
“He had to sleep amidst mosquitos…he was diagnosed with typhoid,” an emotional Anita Dipke said, adding she couldn't sleep till 3 in the night worrying about her son. Dipke's father also turned emotional. Follow live updates here.
Earlier today, Dipke said he was diagnosed with typhoid but vowed that his illness would not slow the movement. The CJP has been spearheading a big student protest in Delhi since last month. A key demand of this agitation was the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.
However, with Pradhan's resignation and the government accepting all other demands of Dipke's outfit, the CJP has ended its protest.
‘Feel very happy today’
Anita Dipke, Abhijeet's mother, said she was “very happy” now the Pradhan has tendered his resignation. “I feel very happy today. It has been a wonderful day. I am extremely happy. He (Abhijeet) has finally received the reward for his sincere efforts...He was determined, and he kept saying that his demand had to be met...,” she told news agency ANI.
She also said that the family was worried at first because Abhijeet was alone, but got some relief after scores of students joined his cause at the protest site.
“Our son was alone there, even though many other students were with him. As parents, we were scared...When he was slapped in Jaipur, it hurt us deeply. We couldn't sleep that night...We plan to welcome him by distributing sweets and celebrating together…,” Anita said.
Abhijeet Dipke was manhandled during his Jaipur visit last month. While he was being carried on the shoulders of supporters, some miscreants in the crowd pulled at his scarf, slapped him multiple times, and attempted to pull him down.
Besides, ink was thrown on him during the Jantar Mantar protest last week.
What next for the CJP protest?
The CJP has called off its protest today, hours after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned. The announcement was made during a joint CJP-Centre presser that was held by union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, and CJP spokespersons Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.
The government has also agreed to withdraw all police cases against protesters. In the joint presser today, JP Nadda said that a copy of the FIRs filed so far will be provided to the CJP and no action will be taken. “We all have said that there will be compensation according to the rules and regulations, whatever maximum will be possible will be given to them,” Nadda said.
The CJP protest grew bigger after climate activist Sonam Wangchuk began an indefinite hunger strike that he ended after 26 days. Protesters had been demanding Pradhan's resignation over the NEET paper leak and other alleged exam irregularities.

headline: Faster trials, longer jail terms: What 2026 bill on paper leaks proposes amid CJP protest, how it differs from 2024 law
full_text:
Faster trials, longer jail terms: What 2026 bill on paper leaks proposes amid CJP protest, how it differs from 2024 law
CJP and Cong insist on nothing less than resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan; govt seeks to counter and assuage youth movement with law change.
Reacting to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests now on for about 50 days, the BJP-led NDA government proposed significantly tightening India's anti-paper leak law. The planned legislation seeks to double prison terms for several offences, raise fines up to ₹10 crore, and mandate timelines for investigations and trials.
While the CJP and the Congress-led Opposition succeeded in forcing the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG paper leaks and other issues, the Centre was already seeking to counter and assuage the youth movement with this legal framework plan. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in a video message earlier this week, had said those who “play with the future of the youth” would face stringent action.
Why amendment within two years?
There will also be Special Fast Track Courts and Special Task Forces to deal with organised examination fraud, according to a copy of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, to be introduced in the Lok Sabha on Monday.
If passed, the bill would mark the first major overhaul of the 2024 act. The amendment substantially enhances punishments for individuals, service providers and organised cheating syndicates.
This also means barely two years after Parliament enacted the first law specifically against leaks, the government has acknowledged that leaks continue to undermine confidence in the country's public examination system despite the enactment of that law.
While the 2024 act primarily created a dedicated legal framework to criminalise organised exam fraud, the amendment focuses on ensuring that investigations and trials are completed within fixed timelines while substantially increasing the penalties.
The Statement of Objects and Reasons accompanying the bill says the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, was enacted to prevent unfair means in public examinations and to “bring greater transparency, fairness and credibility and inspire confidence in the public examinations system”.
However, it adds, “In recent years, there have been some incidents of question paper leakages and malpractices in examinations conducted by public examination authorities, which tend to affect the transparency and fairness of the public examinations system.”
NEET leak link
The original anti-paper leak law itself was not enacted as such in response to the 2024 NEET-UG leak row. It became law in February 2024, months before the NEET-UG 2024 examination was held in May and allegations of paper leaks surfaced.
However, the law was technically brought into force only on June 21, 2024, as the government faced mounting criticism over alleged irregularities in NEET-UG and also the cancellation of UGC-NET.
The 2026 bill has a direct link with the NEET-UG leak of this year, as that leak is a major trigger for the ongoing protest at Jantar Mantar by the CJP, a satirical outfit which otherwise took its name from a comment made by the Chief Justice of India in another context.
What are the changes proposed?
The bill substantially enhances the penalties prescribed under the 2024 law, with different punishments for different categories of offenders.
- For individuals, the minimum prison term is proposed to increase from three years to five, while the maximum sentence would double to 10 years. The maximum fine would also increase five-fold, from ₹10 lakh to 50 lakh.
- For service providers involved in conducting public examinations, the maximum fine would increase from ₹1 crore to 5 crore in case of an offence. They would also face a longer period of blacklisting, with the maximum period proposed to double, to eight years.
- If the director, senior management or person in charge of a service provider is found guilty, the minimum jail term would now be five years, up from three, while the fine would rise from ₹1 crore to 5 crore. The maximum imprisonment would continue to be 10 years.
- For organised crime involving examination authorities, service providers or other institutions, the minimum prison term would increase from five years to seven, while the minimum fine would rise from ₹1 crore to ₹10 crore. The maximum sentence would remain 10 years.
Faster investigations and trials
Perhaps the most significant shift in the amendment lies in the introduction of strict timelines.
A newly inserted Section 12A would require investigations to be completed within two months, regardless of whether they are conducted by the police, a central investigating agency or a Special Task Force constituted by the Centre.
The bill also requires every state and Union Territory to designate a Special Fast Track Court to hear offences under the act. The proposed courts would conduct proceedings on a day-to-day basis and, except where adjournments are unavoidable and reasons are recorded in writing, complete trials within three months of the filing of the chargesheet.
Even pending cases would be transferred to these courts and completed within three months of transfer. The amendment further mandates the appointment of Special Public Prosecutors for every such court.
Another significant change is the proposed power for the central government to constitute a Special Task Force to investigate offences under the act. At present, the Centre may transfer investigations to a central investigating agency.
Appeals against judgments, sentences or orders of the Special Fast Track Court would lie before a Division Bench of the High Court and, “as far as possible”, be disposed of within three months of admission. Appeals against bail orders would also be permitted.

headline: NEW DELHI: The Centre has proposed expanding Ayush services across all military and field hospitals, with the Ayush ministry urging the defence ministry to set up dedicated outpatient departments (OPDs) and integrate traditional systems of medicine i...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: The Centre has proposed expanding Ayush services across all military and field hospitals, with the Ayush ministry urging the defence ministry to set up dedicated outpatient departments (OPDs) and integrate traditional systems of medicine into healthcare for armed forces personnel.
In a letter to defence minister Rajnath Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush Prataprao Jadhav said the move would complement the armed forces medical services by strengthening preventive, promotive and rehabilitative care for soldiers serving in diverse and often challenging operational environments.
Jadhav noted that while Ayush treatment facilities are already available in a limited number of institutions under the ministry of defence, a large number of military and field hospitals still do not have dedicated Ayush services. He said expanding these facilities would improve access to evidence-based traditional healthcare, particularly in preventive care, lifestyle management, rehabilitation and overall well-being.
The proposal seeks to integrate Ayush with the existing healthcare framework rather than replace conventional medical services. According to the ministry, the initiative is aimed at creating a more comprehensive and patient-centric model of care by combining modern medicine with traditional systems wherever appropriate.
Jadhav urged the defence ministry to establish Ayush OPDs and treatment facilities in all military and field hospitals, saying the Ayush Ministry was ready to provide technical support, professional guidance and institutional cooperation, including signing an MoU for implementation.
If approved, the proposal would significantly expand Ayush services within the armed forces, advancing the government's push to integrate traditional medicine with mainstream healthcare and improve access to holistic care for defence personnel.

headline: Ludhiana woman killed in Canada, man held for ‘intimate partner homicide’
full_text:
Ludhiana woman killed in Canada, man held for ‘intimate partner homicide’
Neighbours said Damanpreet Kaur and Ritish Kumar had been living together in a basement suite on Silverberry Road in Edmonton
Police in Canada have charged a 22-year-old Indian man with second-degree murder in the death of his 23-year-old partner, Damanpreet Kaur, a native of Samrala in Punjab's Ludhiana district, after she died of injuries days after being found unresponsive at a home in Edmonton, the capital city of the province of Alberta.
The Edmonton Police Service (EPS) said officers responded to a call around 6:44 pm on July 9 regarding “an unresponsive female with suspicious injuries” at a residence in the Silverberry neighbourhood in southeast Edmonton. “An adult male was taken into custody shortly thereafter,” the police said.
Arrested days after murder
Damanpreet Kaur was taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries, where she died on July 12, police said. The Edmonton Medical Examiner's Office conducted an autopsy on July 14 and determined that the manner of death was homicide (murder), according to the police. On July 23, investigators disclosed that the cause of death was strangulation, saying the information had earlier been withheld for investigative reasons.
“Ritish Kumar was arrested on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, and charged with second degree murder,” the EPS said in its release.
“This death is considered an intimate partner homicide. Police are not seeking any additional suspects at this time,” the department added. “Intimate partner homicide” is used in Canada to refer to murder involving a current or former romantic partner, regardless of marital status.
What led to murder
Police have not disclosed the circumstances leading to Kaur's death or any possible motive. They have also not said whether the man initially taken into custody on July 9 was Kumar, who was formally arrested nearly two weeks later. More details on Kumar were not shared.
Local broadcaster CityNews reported that neighbours said Kaur and Kumar had been living together in a basement suite on Silverberry Road. Members of Edmonton's Punjabi community described Kaur as friendly and said her death had shocked the local community. Gulzar Singh Nirman, a community member, told CityNews that he had spoken to Kaur's father in India, who was devastated by the loss.
Separately, a GoFundMe campaign has been launched to help repatriate Kaur's body to India and cover funeral-related expenses. “The costs of international transportation, documentation, and funeral arrangements are overwhelming for the family during this heartbreaking time,” the fundraiser states.
The campaign says the money will be used to transport Kaur's body to India so her family can perform her last rites. By Saturday, it had raised nearly its full target of $20,000.

headline: DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Saturday (July 25, 2026) urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to abandon his “misguided decision” to visit Karnataka for talks with its government on Tamil Nadu’s rights over the Cauve...
full_text:
DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Saturday (July 25, 2026) urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to abandon his “misguided decision” to visit Karnataka for talks with its government on Tamil Nadu’s rights over the Cauvery waters.
“If Karnataka refuses to release water to Tamil Nadu, it amounts to contempt of court. Its proposal to construct a dam at Mekedatu is in violation of the Supreme Court’s final verdict. Before taking any further steps on an issue as vital as the Cauvery dispute, the Chief Minister should consult all political parties and representatives of farmers’ associations,” Mr. Stalin said in a statement.
He said the struggle to secure Tamil Nadu’s rights over the Cauvery had a long history and that those rights had been firmly established through the legal process.
“The Chief Minister should understand the breadth and depth of the issue before proceeding further on such an initiative,” he said.
Mr. Stalin said there were doubts over whether the proposed talks were merely an eyewash, as the Congress was in power in Karnataka and was also a constituent of the ruling coalition in Tamil Nadu.
“The visit will serve no purpose other than enabling the government to claim that it made a direct effort by travelling to Karnataka for talks,” he said.
Mr. Stalin questioned why the Chief Minister had “fallen into Karnataka’s trap,” charging that its objective was to dilute Tamil Nadu’s rights over the Cauvery waters.
“Delta farmers are furious over the Chief Minister’s decision to hold talks,” he added.
Recalling the DMK government’s earlier stand, Mr. Stalin said it had rejected suggestions to hold direct talks with Karnataka because the neighbouring State had repeatedly failed to honour its commitments and would only prolong the dispute.
“The proposal to construct the Mekedatu dam itself amounts to rejecting Tamil Nadu’s rights over the Cauvery. It has always been our stand that there is no purpose in holding talks with Karnataka on this issue,” he said.
Pradhan’s resignation
In a social media post, Mr. Stalin said the resignation of Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan was not the final destination, reiterating that just as the farm laws had been repealed, NEET too should be abolished.
“The farmers of India did it first. The youth have done it today. Congratulations to the youth of India who protested across the country, both offline and online, and made this victory possible,” he said.
Mr. Stalin said those who believed they could mislead young people with “manufactured narratives and empty promises” had underestimated the clarity, courage, and conscience of a generation determined to shape its own future.
“May this awakening inspire a generation that questions, participates, and refuses to accept injustice. An informed and fearless youth is the strongest foundation of any democracy,” he said.

headline: 'Never asked for favor from government': Zoho's Sridhar Vembu defends X post backing Pradhan amid online backlash
full_text:
'Never asked for favor from government': Zoho's Sridhar Vembu defends X post backing Pradhan amid online backlash
Sridhar Vembu asserts that his advice is free from political bias and remains steadfast amid criticism.
Zoho co-founder and former CEO Sridhar Vembu on Saturday issued a fresh statement after facing criticism over his remarks expressing "sadness" at Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. Many social media users accused Vembu of defending the Narendra Modi government to protect Zoho's business interests in India.
Without naming any individual or group, Vembu asserted that his views were independent and said he would not be influenced by criticism or threats. In his latest post, he sought to reinforce that claim by highlighting Zoho's business model, its revenue sources and his interactions with governments.

Vembu says revenues comes from outside India
Addressing the criticism, Vembu said that around 90% of Zoho's revenue comes from outside India, earned by competing in the global market. He added that only about 2% of the company's revenue comes from government contracts, and whenever Zoho does business with the government, it ensures value for taxpayers' money.
“Some facts: about 90% of our revenue comes from outside India, won against tough global competition,” he wrote.
“About 2% of our revenue is from the government and when we do business with the government, we always save the taxpayer money, which we have the utmost respect for. We are also among the largest tax payers in our region,” he further added.
Post that drew criticism
Earlier, Vembu had expressed disappointment over Pradhan's resignation and praised his contribution to the education sector. In a post on X, he wrote, "Shri Dharmendra Pradhan is one of the finest public servants I know. He cares deeply about the youth of this nation, particularly rural students."

He also said that he had held several discussions with Pradhan on how to better equip rural youth with skills.
"I am sad to see him resign. He has put the nation above self, and my respect for him is even greater now. Thank you for your service, Pradhan-ji. Please keep fighting the good fight," he added.
Says he has never sought government favours
In the fresh X post, Vembu also said he had never asked any government for favours and maintained that his advice had always been offered without being guided by political ideology.

He wrote,"I have never asked for a favor from the government and I never will. When asked for advice, I provide it and I do it independent of political ideology - the Kerala Startup Mission, when the Left Front government was in power, wanted my advice. I told them Keralam has the potential to be a major R&D hub of India. Since then, we have invested in numerous R&D driven statups in Keralam."
Referring to Tamil Nadu, he added, "In Tamil Nadu, our Chief Minister has made a great new beginning and I am happy to support his effort. It is not because of political ideology but because I want good things to happen in Tamil Nadu."
'I love our nation, and I speak my mind'
Concluding his post, Vembu said the criticism would not change his approach.
"I love our nation, and I speak my mind. I will not bow down to attacks nor threats. The attacks make us stronger and help us achieve greater success."

headline: For millions of Indians, the workday begins with a laptop and ends with one. Eight to ten hours at a desk, endless video calls, back-to-back meetings and constant screen time have become the new normal. But while productivity has gone up, so has an i...
full_text:
For millions of Indians, the workday begins with a laptop and ends with one. Eight to ten hours at a desk, endless video calls, back-to-back meetings and constant screen time have become the new normal. But while productivity has gone up, so has an invisible workplace problem - cervical pain.
Doctors say they are seeing a sharp rise in young professionals in their 20s and 30s walking into clinics with neck pain, stiffness, headaches and posture-related disorders. What was once considered an age-related condition is now increasingly becoming an occupational hazard of desk jobs.
The growing dependence on laptops, smartphones and sedentary lifestyles has turned cervical pain into a modern workplace health challenge. Beyond physical discomfort, it is affecting productivity, mental well-being and healthcare costs, raising concerns about whether India's rapidly expanding desk workforce is paying too high a price for long hours behind a screen.
Understanding cervical pain Cervical pain refers to pain or discomfort in the neck (cervical spine) and surrounding areas, including the shoulders and upper back. It can range from mild stiffness to severe pain and, in some cases, may be accompanied by headaches, tingling or numbness in the arms if nerves are affected.
While cervical pain can occur at any age, it is becoming increasingly common among young adults due to prolonged screen time, poor posture and sedentary lifestyles.
According to a study published in 
The Lancet, nearly 200 million people worldwide were living with cervical pain in 2020. The study projects that this number could rise to 270 million by 2050, driven by ageing populations, sedentary lifestyles and changing work patterns.
The impact extends well beyond physical discomfort. The World Health Organization (WHO) says musculoskeletal disorders are among the leading causes of work-related disability and absenteeism worldwide, affecting productivity and quality of life across age groups.
A Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2019 analysis estimated that around 1.71 billion people globally live with disorders such as neck pain, low back pain, fractures, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and other musculoskeletal conditions.
Is cervical pain becoming a workplace epidemic?To understand how widespread the problem is, we spoke to 30 working professionals about their work habits, posture and neck health. Their responses point to a common pattern: long sitting hours, few breaks and recurring cervical pain.
Most of the respondents were young professionals. 26 of the 30 participants were between 24 and 35 years of age, underscoring that cervical pain is increasingly affecting younger employees rather than just older adults.
Ten respondents experienced cervical discomfort every month, nine reported symptoms every week, and seven said they dealt with neck pain almost every day, highlighting how common the condition has become among desk-based workers.
Shashank, 38 years old media professional, said that he suffers neck stiffness, shoulder pain and arm pain very frequently.
âI spend around 8 hours sitting every day on a chair which does not provide good support to my neck. I believe more frequent breaks and awareness about the right furniture in the offices can help employees work more efficiently. Bad furniture set up leads to poor posture which ultimately results in all kinds of problems,â he told TOI.
Dr Arun Bhanot, Director â Spine Surgery at CK Birla Hospital, Gurugram, said there has been a noticeable rise in younger patients with desk jobs seeking treatment for neck pain.
"The profile of patients has shifted dramatically. Earlier, it was mostly older people with degenerative changes. Now, we are seeing a steady stream of people in their late 20s and 30s," he said.
Long hours at the desk were the norm, with 21 respondents spending more than eight hours seated every day, while another seven reported sitting for seven to eight hours.
Despite prolonged screen time, regular movement was uncommon. Twelve respondents said they rarely took breaks during work, while 10 stepped away from their desks only once every two to three hoursâfar less frequently than doctors recommend.
Komal Gupta, 30-year-old journalist, while talking to TOI, said that she hardly gets enough time to exercise regularly, even though she knows it would help reduce her neck pain.
âMost workdays are packed with deadlines, so taking out time for stretching or a workout becomes difficult.â
Dr Surender Pal Singh, HOD â Physiotherapy Department at CK Birla Hospital in Delhi advises keeping the monitor at eye level, ensuring proper chair support and avoiding carrying heavy laptop bags on one shoulder, as uneven weight distribution can increase stress on the neck and upper back.
However, most of the respondents responded with no furniture or equipment support from the employer.
Gupta said, âMy office also doesn't provide an external monitor or laptop stand, so I end up working directly on my laptop for long hours, which puts additional strain on my neck and shoulders.â
Problem not confined to corporate offices Jyoti Jaiswal, a 29-year-old dentist, says healthcare professionals are equally vulnerable due to the nature of their work.
"Treating patients often requires us to remain seated or stand in the same position for long periods, which puts considerable strain on the neck," she said.
Jaiswal believes better workload management could help reduce the problem. "Proper patient scheduling is essential so that sufficient time can be given to each patient without rushing or compromising body posture. It would also give doctors brief breaks between consultations, reducing physical strain," she added.
Tushar Gaur, a 25-year-old accountant from Meerut, says his job requires him to spend long hours seated, entering financial data and working continuously on a computer.
"The prolonged sitting and constant screen time often cause severe pain on the left side of my neck. I've realised that taking regular breaks helps reduce the discomfort, but during busy workdays it's not always possible," he said.
Dr Bhanot said, "The head weighs around 4.5 to 5 kilograms in a neutral position. But tilt it forward by just 15 degrees to look at a screen and the effective load on the cervical spine rises sharply. Hold that posture for eight hours a day, five days a week, and the muscles and ligaments simply give in."
Recalling one of his cases of treating a 26-year-old software developer, he said, â he developed severe neck pain, numbness in her fingers and forward-head posture after working from bed for nearly a year with her laptop balanced on a pillow.
"There was no disc herniation, but significant muscle strain. With ergonomic correction, physiotherapy and scheduled movement breaks, she was largely symptom-free within six weeks," he said.
So what can be done?Respondents overwhelmingly felt that preventing cervical pain requires both individual lifestyle changes and employer support. Many said companies should invest in ergonomic workstations, including better chairs, adjustable desks, laptop stands and the option of standing desks to reduce strain caused by prolonged sitting.
Several respondents also called for more employee-friendly workplace policies, such as reduced working hours, flexible schedules and better workload management to allow employees enough time to rest, exercise and maintain proper posture.
Others suggested that employers should encourage frequent breaks, with some even recommending software-based reminders or applications that temporarily lock screens every 30 minutes to prompt employees to stand up, stretch and move around.
While the other things are not in our hands, taking some time to exercise is.
Dr Singh stresses that prevention is often simple but overlooked. "Standing up, stretching and walking for just one or two minutes every 30 minutes can significantly reduce pressure on the neck and back," he said, adding that even the best workstation cannot prevent neck strain if a person remains seated for long hours without regular movement.
Every notification, meeting and deadline keeps employees glued to their desks. Yet, taking just a couple of minutes to move every half hour could make the difference between a healthy spine and years of chronic pain. In a workplace increasingly driven by productivity, perhaps the next big investment isn't technologyâit's healthier employees.
Because the next deadline can wait, your health canât.

headline: NEW DELHI: The opposition on Saturday hailed the youth protesters after Union education minister
full_text:
NEW DELHI: The opposition on Saturday hailed the youth protesters after Union education minister 
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following massive student demonstrations demanding his resignation over the alleged NEET (UG) paper leak and other education-related issues.
The resignation came ahead of the third round of talks between the government and the Cockroach Janta Party (
CJP), an online satirical platform spearheading the protests at Jantar Mantar, Delhi's designated site for public demonstrations.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge credited both the students and the "united opposition."
"India's âStudents' Echoâ has finally reached the threshold of the arrogant power. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
This is the victory of our millions of youth who raised their voices on the streets across the country to fix the education system. This is the victory of truth and the defeat of Mr. Modi's stubbornness. This is the victory of all those families who lost their blood, their children, because this government is corrupt. This is the victory of the united opposition, who raised their voices from Parliament to the streets in the interest of the students.
 Now it is Mr. Modi's turn to apologize to our young generation and to take strict action against those who unleashed lathis, batons, and pellet guns on them," Kharge wrote on X.
"Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation; Modi-Shah are not invincible...They too will go!" Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut posted on X.
AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal described it as a "big win for democracy."
"Congratulations to the entire country on Dharmendra Pradhanâs resignation. Big win for democracy," Kejriwal said in a video message on X.
Here's who said what:
Manoj Jha (RJD MP): "First setback for Modi government, thanks to the resolve of our youths and students."
Kunal Ghosh (TMC MLA): "He (Pradhan) should have done it earlier... BJP was trying to protect him. This is the victory of the people and students who were protesting... This is the victory of the whole country."
Bhupender Singh Hooda (ex-Haryana CM): "Better late than never. This should have come earlier. There wouldn't have been so much damage. The young generation across the country has lost faith in exams, so the entire system should change. A new system should be introduced... The demand for Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as Education Minister wasn't just from Congress alone; it was from the youth of the entire country."
Shashi Tharoor (Congress MP): "The resignation of the Education Minister is an acknowledgment that accountability in a democracy cannot be indefinitely evaded. It comes after weeks of determined, peaceful voices raised by students, parents and citizens across the country who refused to be ignored."
Manish Sisodia (AAP leader): Dharmendra Pradhan did not voluntarily submit his resignation. The nation's children, the nation's students, secured Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. If this had been a voluntary resignation, it should have happened when the NEET paper leak occurred...The country needs a massive education revolution."
Sharad Pawar (NCP-SP chief): "In response to the insistent demand of the protesters, the Union education minister has finally resigned today. This fight, which stood firmly against oppression without fear and forced the government to accept moral responsibility against injustice, is a symbol of the power of democracy. This is a major victory for the unity of the youth power in the country."
Akhilesh Yadav (SP chief): "This is a big victory for the youth, but people from all political parties should learn from this that in the future, the examinations will have to be strengthened so that no papers are leaked and avenues for employment and jobs will have to be opened for the youth."

headline: Upon completion of 100 days in office, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Saturday (July 25, 2026) inaugurated and laid the foundation stone of 2,476 development projects worth ₹11,464 crore.

Upon completion of 100 days in office, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Saturday (July 25, 2026) inaugurated and laid the foundation stone of 2,476 development projects worth ₹11,464 crore.
Mr. Choudhary took the oath as the head of the government on April 15 and completed 100 days on July 23. He asserted that many historic decisions were taken within 100 days in all sectors, be it education, health, industry, agriculture, infrastructure, and good governance. He added that the Bihar’s overall development has gained new momentum.

People’s servant
In his address, the Chief Minister asserted that the government belongs to the people of Bihar and that he is the people’s servant. He pointed out that every decision taken during the first 100 days has been dedicated to the public interest, good governance, and the all-round development of Bihar.
He said that having the opportunity to serve as Chief Minister of Bihar is an emotional moment for him. Mr. Choudhary also said that continuous efforts are being made to ensure self-reliance for the 14 crore people of Bihar and to transform the State into a developed one.

Listing achievements

Additionally, 551 schools have been developed into model schools.
He urged the officials to work 15 to 18 hours a day to transform Bihar into a prosperous State. “We need to work towards establishing at least one industry in every district. Our goal is to attract investments worth ₹5 lakh crore to Bihar by November 20,” Mr. Choudhary added.
“The government is working to create extensive employment opportunities for the youth by encouraging major investments in sectors such as textiles, food processing, and electronics. Work is underway to construct the country’s largest airport at Sonepur, and a new airport is also being built at Sultanganj,” Mr. Choudhary said.
Stating that Bihar is the country’s youngest and most energetic State, he added that in the coming years, Bihar will emerge as a leading engine of national development, investment, employment, innovation, and industrial progress.
Mr. Choudhary also launched a magazine and a coffee-table book highlighting the achievements of his first 100 days in office.

headline: Karnataka Upalokayukta B. Veerappa on Saturday directed officials to initiate stringent action against unauthorised homestays operating in and around the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Hampi, observing that illegal commercial activities could not be p...
full_text:
Karnataka Upalokayukta B. Veerappa on Saturday directed officials to initiate stringent action against unauthorised homestays operating in and around the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Hampi, observing that illegal commercial activities could not be permitted in a protected heritage zone.
During a surprise inspection of Hampi, Mr. Veerappa took officials to task after learning that more than 200 homestays were allegedly functioning without required permissions or licences from the gram panchayat and other competent authorities.
Questioning how such a large number of unauthorised establishments had been allowed to operate, he sought explanations from the officials concerned and asked why they had failed to discharge their statutory responsibilities. Expressing serious concern over electricity connections having been provided to homestays allegedly operating illegally on agricultural or residential land for commercial purposes, Mr. Veerappa directed the Gescom officials to report to the spot immediately.
He instructed panchayat and taluk-level authorities to conduct a joint inspection and initiate legal action against all unauthorised homestays, including their removal wherever necessary. “Hampi is a world-renowned heritage site and no illegal or unauthorised activity should be allowed here. There is no objection to lawful business carried out after obtaining all statutory permissions, but violations of the law will be dealt with firmly,” he said.
The Upalokayukta also directed officials to initiate suo motu proceedings against the authorities responsible for permitting the unauthorised establishments to function. Later, Mr. Veerappa inspected Janata Street in Hampi, where he found commercial activities and habitation within the 100-metre prohibited zone around the protected monument. He instructed officials to identify an alternative site for traders and other commercial establishments so that all business activities could be shifted outside the prohibited area.
He further directed the authorities to ensure that only genuine traders currently operating in the Janata Street were accommodated at the new commercial location and suggested arranging a dedicated transport service to facilitate tourists’ access to the relocated market.
He visited the historic Virupaksha Temple and reviewed the facilities available to devotees. During the inspection,
Deputy Commissioner Kavitha S. Mannikeri informed him that permission had been obtained from the Archaeological Survey of India to install an air-conditioning system in the sanctum area to improve ventilation and that the work would be taken up shortly.
Lokayukta Deputy Registrar Aravind, Lokayukta Superintendent of Police Vasudevaram, Superintendent of Police S. Jahnavi, Additional Deputy Commissioner E. Balakrishna, Sub-Divisional Officer Vivekananda and other officials were present during the inspection.

headline: Rajasthan YouTuber kidnapped from studio rescued, two men arrested: Police

Rajasthan YouTuber kidnapped from studio rescued, two men arrested: Police
A YouTuber allegedly kidnapped from Rajasthan’s Tonk was rescued after a police blockade, with two accused arrested.
Two people were arrested after a YouTuber allegedly kidnapped from his studio in Rajasthan’s Tonk district was rescued following a high-alert police blockade in Kotputli-Behror on Friday, police said, adding that efforts are underway to trace the remaining three suspects.
According to police officers, Mahesh Gurjar was abducted from his studio in the Niwai area of Tonk district while he was sleeping with friends. The kidnappers allegedly bundled him into a Scorpio SUV and reportedly planned to demand a ransom of ₹20 lakh from his family, officers said.
Also read: 5 held for kidnapping couple for marrying against family’s wish
After receiving information about the kidnapping, the Niwai police alerted the Kotputli-Behror police. The Sarund police set up a blockade on the Neemkathana State Highway.
“The Sarund police acted immediately after receiving the alert from Tonk police, leading to the victim’s safe rescue,” Kotputli-Behror Superintendent of Police (SP) Satveer Singh said.
The SP added that during the operation, the suspect vehicle was spotted near the Sarund toll plaza. When police signalled the SUV to stop, the occupants allegedly sped away, driving over a road divider in an attempt to escape.
Police alerted nearby checkpoints and traffic units through the wireless network. The Scorpio was eventually stopped in a traffic snarl ahead. The accused abandoned the vehicle and fled. Gurjar was found inside with injuries, officers said.
Police scanned CCTV footage from the toll plaza and surrounding areas, used technical surveillance, and arrested Ashish Meena and Aditya, both residents of Sohela village. Three others are still on the run, officers said.
Police also recovered a country-made pistol and four live cartridges from their possession.
Also read: Faridbad: : 28-year-old held in Palla over kidnapping and rape of minor
The primary kidnapping case was registered at the Niwai police station. Joint teams from Kotputli-Behror and Tonk police are conducting raids to apprehend the remaining three accused.

headline: NEW DELHI: The government has debunked doctored videos circulating on social media that wrongly showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi making threatening remarks against those protesting at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar over perpetual NEET paper leak. The Press...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: The government has debunked doctored videos circulating on social media that wrongly showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi making threatening remarks against those protesting at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar over perpetual NEET paper leak. The Press Information Bureau (PIB) fact check unit said the clips were AI-generated deepfakes and did not reflect the Prime Ministerâs actual statements.
In related fact-checks, the government also flagged manipulated videos of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan and commerce minister Piyush Goyal that were circulating on social media, falsely portraying them as making similar remarks against protesting students.
In a post on X, the PIB fact check unit said, âPakistani propaganda accounts are circulating a video of Prime Minister @narendramodi featuring fabricated statements that he never made regarding the protest in Delhi.â
It added, â#PIBFactCheck: This is an '#AI-generated deepfake video' shared to mislead the public. Prime Minister Narendra Modi did NOT make any such statement.â
The fact-check unit said the original video shared by PM Modi had been digitally altered to create a misleading version. 
It further shared a link to the original, unedited video posted by the PM.
The fake video circulating online showed an altered audio track in which PM Modi was allegedly made to say, "We are warning people against participating in the Cockroach Janata Party protest. Those who defy this warning will face strict action from the Government of India to ensure that such behaviour is not repeated in the future. Students are advised to focus on their education, failing which they will be compelled to face serious consequences. We are issuing a clear warning to the students."
The original video, posted by PM on his official social media account on Thursday, has since garnered 334 million views on Instagram. In the video, PM Modi addressed viewers as âFriendsâ and spoke directly into what appeared to be a phoneâs front camera, held at armâs length, with no podium, studio setup or formal backdrop.
In the video, the PM said the paper leak issue had caused difficulties for lakhs of students and their parents. He said those responsible had been arrested and that steps were being taken to ensure students did not lose an academic year.
The Prime Minister also said provisions for fast-track courts had been prepared and would be taken up by the Union cabinet.
The fact check unit also debunked another AI-generated video that falsely showed the PM similar remarks about the cockroach janata party protests. In this manipulated clip, Modi appeared to say, âWhat is the problem with these cockroaches? Even if one paper gets leaked, what is the big deal? Students can simply appear for the examination again next year.â The PIB clarified that the remarks were fabricated and shared the original video, which showed the Prime Minister speaking about the monsoon and the ongoing Monsoon session of parliament.
Additionally, the PIB flagged another digitally altered video of Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan that falsely portrayed him threatening protesting students. The manipulated clip appeared to show Pradhan saying that âbig leaders do not resign because of these cockroaches; they crush them under their shoes and throw them into dirty drains where they belongâ and warning that protesters would âsoon face grave consequencesâ. Refuting the claims, the PIB said, âUnion Minister Dharmendra Pradhan did not make any such statement.â
The fact-check unit blamed Pakistani propaganda accounts for circulating the digitally altered video containing fabricated claims. The original video was posted on the occasion of Sital Sasthi and made no reference to the protests.
The manipulated clip surfaced amid continuing protests led by the CJP, which has consistently demanded that Pradhan be held accountable for the alleged NEET paper leaks and has called for the education minister's resignation as one of its principal demands.
In another fact check, the government flagged a separate manipulated video involving commerce minister Piyush Goyal, which falsely claimed that Goyal had made similar threatening remarks against Jantar Mantar protests.
The PIB said, âMr Goyal has made no such statement regarding the protests.â
The government urged people to verify the authenticity of videos and rely on official sources before sharing them.

headline: Peace in Manipur needs trust, IDP rehabilitation first: Conrad Sangma
full_text:
Peace in Manipur needs trust, IDP rehabilitation first: Conrad Sangma
He acknowledged that there was no immediate solution to the crisis but stressed that sustained engagement and confidence-building measures were essential
Stressing that peace in Manipur cannot be restored without rebuilding trust among its fractured communities, National People’s Party (NPP) president and Meghalaya chief minister Conrad K. Sangma on Saturday in Imphal called for sustained dialogue and reconciliation while asserting that the rehabilitation of internally displaced persons (IDPs) must remain a top priority in efforts to restore normalcy in the conflict-hit state.
Addressing reporters on the second day of his two-day visit to Manipur, Sangma described the situation as “very complicated” and said resolving the crisis would require patience, confidence-building measures and the collective participation of all stakeholders.
“The first and most important thing is that we need to move forward. Things have been very challenging and very difficult for the people of Manipur. If we continue to look only at what went wrong, we may never be able to move forward,” Sangma said.
Appealing to all communities to work together, he said peace could not be achieved overnight but had to begin with rebuilding trust through continuous engagement.
“We must give peace a chance. We must understand that we need to work together and live together. We have been living together for a reason. It is easier said than done, but we need to start somewhere,” he said.
Sangma said discussions with party legislators, state leaders, youth representatives and office-bearers during his visit were focused primarily on the prevailing situation in Manipur rather than organisational matters.
“The majority of the discussions were about how we can play our part in improving the situation, bringing stability and peace, and supporting internally displaced persons,” he said.
He acknowledged that there was no immediate solution to the crisis but stressed that sustained engagement and confidence-building measures were essential to restoring normalcy.
“The consistency with which we work and the trust we build must start now. As a political party, we must reach out to people as much as possible and engage with all sections of society,” he said.
Calling the rehabilitation of internally displaced persons one of the NPP’s foremost concerns, Sangma said the party had extended financial assistance to displaced families and would continue to advocate for their safe return.
“We have consistently raised the issue that every effort should be made to ensure that IDPs are able to return safely to their homes and villages. The government and the Centre are trying to achieve that, and we will continue to raise their concerns,” he said.
Asked whether displaced families could return before the 2027 Assembly elections, Sangma said every effort was being made to achieve that objective, although the process remained challenging because of the complexities involved.
On the issue of infiltration, Sangma said there could be no compromise on national security but stressed that decisions should be implemented in a manner that carried local communities along.
“There can be no compromise on national security or national interest. At the same time, decisions must be taken by carrying people along and ensuring that local communities understand why those decisions are necessary,” he said.
Sangma also underscored the need for economic revival, saying the prolonged conflict had severely affected livelihoods and stalled development in the state.
“We need a strong economic policy that creates industries and employment opportunities based on Manipur’s strengths. Livelihoods have suffered and the state’s development has been affected,” he said.
On the political front, Sangma ruled out a pre-poll alliance with the BJP for the 2027 Manipur Assembly elections, reiterating that the NPP would contest independently with its own manifesto and ideology.
“We have never had a pre-poll alliance in any state Assembly election. We will go before the people with our own manifesto and principles. Post-poll decisions will depend on the mandate given by the people,” he said.
He added that the party’s manifesto committee would deliberate on issues such as peace, rehabilitation, economic recovery and governance before finalising the party’s vision document for the 2027 Assembly elections.

headline: NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the response to his midnight post on Instagram Thursday, which got 305 million views, PM Modi Friday returned to the social media platform. "Thank you, friends. I had an opportunity to connect with you late last night. The way yo...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the response to his midnight post on Instagram Thursday, which got 305 million views, PM Modi Friday returned to the social media platform. "Thank you, friends. I had an opportunity to connect with you late last night. The way you responded to my video post and gave constructive suggestions, thanks to everybody. Your love will continue and our bond will strengthen," the PM said, reports Dipak Dash.
His remarks reflected satisfaction, with officials calling it a "successful connect" with Gen Z, who have been wooed by CJP and other opponents. Within minutes, Friday's video had garnered 9.3 million views.
This came barely hours after PM urged his Cabinet colleagues to use more of Instagram, saying it will help them stay connected with the youth. He was interacting with them after the Cabinet meeting on Friday. Official sources said PM's choice of Instagram to announce govt's decision to toughen the anti-paper leak law earned him around 1 million new followers.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked ministers how many of them were actively using social media platforms such as Instagram. 
He said the platform has been popular with large sections of youth and emphasised using the social networking site to connect with them.
PM Modi has been using Instagram since 2014.
His advice comes amid a growing sense that BJP, which successfully leveraged mass use of WhatsApp to steal a march over its rivals, runs the risk of ceding the advantage in reaching out to Gen Z, which is not as enamoured of the messaging platform and is more comfortable with the photo & short form video service.
PM Modi, a tech enthusiast, has repeatedly urged his ministers to hold interactive sessions with youth on this platform. He has said govt as well as BJP should more active on social media. Chairing the council of ministers meeting in Jan 2023, he had stressed that social media had emerged as the main source of information for large sections of the youth and its growing allure needed to be harnessed.

headline: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that 70 people have been identified for their involvement in the violence, out of which none of them are students or members of the Cockroach Janta Party; 11 persons have been arrested in connection wi...
full_text:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that 70 people have been identified for their involvement in the violence, out of which none of them are students or members of the Cockroach Janta Party; 11 persons have been arrested in connection with the violence
The Kolkata Police have registered seven first information reports (FIRs) in connection with the violence that erupted at the Esplanade area during a students’ protest rally led by the Cockroach Janta Party and several Left-affiliated students’ wings on Friday (July 24, 2026), demanding Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation. Six of the FIRs have been registered in connection with the attack on the media personnel and one is a suo motu case in connection with the violence. Eleven persons have been arrested so far, police said.
Also read: Jantar Mantar protest updates on July 25, 2026
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday (July 25, 2026) said in the State Assembly that 70 people have been identified who are not students or members of the Cockroach Janta Party. The Chief Minister said these cases will be investigated under the “Goonda Act”, a recent law passed by the State Assembly that allows preventive detention for a period of up to 12 months. Lauding the efforts of the police in dispersing the mob, the Chief Minister read out a few names of the people arrested in connection with the protest.
The march on Friday started from Sealdah station, where thousands of young students and people from various sections of society showed up. However, the peaceful protest turned violent when the police used force to disperse the crowd soon after they reached Esplanade. The protesters started a dharna at Dorina Crossing in Esplanade, following which the police baton-charged and also fired two rounds of tear gas.
In retaliation, the protesters also threw shoes and bottles at the police force. During the clash, several people from both sides and also a few journalists sustained injuries. The RAF and paramilitary forces have also been deployed in the area to maintain law and order.
After assessing the entire situation and damage, the Kolkata Police registered seven FIRs on Saturday morning. The first FIR was suo motu lodged by the Kolkata Police at Hare Street police station for allegedly delivering provocative speeches and slogans by the protesters, attacking the police personnel, and unlawfully gathering at Dorina Crossing.
No permission: police
Police said that the protesters gathered in the area without any formal permission from the police authority. “They had vehicles with them and were using microphones at high volume. They were giving provocative speeches instigating their followers to encroach on the entire Dorina Crossing. The continuous instigations of the leaders infuriated the crowd, resulting in the whole gathering becoming very aggressive and unruly,” said Additional Police Commissioner (Crime) Kunal Aggarwal.
The police repeatedly instructed them to leave the place and to maintain peace. But the crowd, under the instructions of the leaders, started hurling water bottles, shoes, sticks and stones targeting the police, reporters and passersby — creating insecurity for the commoners and others, the officer said.
Mr. Aggarwal said that some police personnel also sustained injuries due to the clash. “As they were good in number and they were trying to provoke the police, the latter showed very restrained behaviour and maintained an orderly situation, confining them within a certain ambit. Their act completely paralysed the regular vehicular movements and public activities,” he added.
The FIRs were lodged under Sections 189(2), 189(4), 189(3), 191(2), 190, 121(1), 132, 285, 352, 223, 3(5), and 3(6) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against multiple unidentified people.
The other FIRs were against the attack on journalists Rik Purakaystha and Krishnendu Majumder from R Plus News channel, Shiladitya Kar from the Ei Samay publishing house, Rahi Halder from Aaj Tak channel (India Today group), and Suman Mahapatra, Makhan Chandra Patra, and Dipankar Dasgupta from TV9 channel. All of them are currently undergoing treatment at SSKM Hospital.
The Chief Minister on Friday night visited SSKM Hospital and met the injured journalists. Mr. Adhikari promised necessary action against the attack on the media personnel. “Is this a protest against NEET? Those who have attacked journalists will be punished. Wait for a few days. We have identified them. They have no connection with NEET protests,” the Chief Minister said.
Earlier on Friday morning, he also called the protesters anti-national and said that no such activities will be spared in West Bengal. “We will drive these anti-nationals out of Bengal. If you want to stay here, such activities will not be accepted. I heard that the students from the hostel of Jadavpur University were forced to join this rally. We will not allow this,” he told the reporters reacting to the protest.
However, all the Left-affiliated students’ associations and the Cockroach Janta Party denied that the protesters harassed the journalists. In their official statements, they condemned the incident and said that some outsiders, probably plotted by the ruling party, entered the premises and launched the brutal attack on the journalists to damage a peaceful protest.
“Many of the students and protesters are also admitted to the hospital. We are condemning this attempt to mislead such a peaceful protest. It is shameful how the journalists were attacked,” they said in an official statement.

'Selfless service': BJP leaders hail Dharmendra Pradhan's tenure as education minister
Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday, after weeks of massive student protests in Delhi .
Senior BJP leaders on Saturday praised outgoing education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, highlighting his role in implementing the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and bringing structural changes to India's education system following his resignation.
This came after Pradhan resigned on Saturday, after weeks of massive student protests in Delhi seeking his resignation over exam irregularities, particularly the NEET-UG paper leak.
Himanta Biswa Sarma praises Pradhan’s role
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma expressed gratitude towards Pradhan, saying his efforts helped strengthen India’s education system and promote the country’s cultural identity.

“His unwavering commitment to implementing the National Education Policy, despite the political challenges it entailed, will be remembered as one of his finest contributions to nation-building,” Sarma said.
Nitin Nabin calls resignation a reflection of integrity
BJP leader Nitin Nabin said Pradhan’s decision to step down demonstrated the values of accountability and dedication in public life.

He added that the party continued to stand with Pradhan and extended his wishes for his future endeavours.
Amit Malviya highlights Pradhan’s education legacy

Malviya said Pradhan’s leadership focused on expanding institutions, improving inclusivity, embracing technology and strengthening India’s cultural roots in education.
“His stewardship was marked by structural reforms, institutional expansion, greater inclusivity, technological modernisation and a renewed emphasis on India’s civilisational ethos,” Malviya said.
He added that Pradhan’s approach was aimed at creating an education ecosystem capable of meeting the needs of the 21st century while remaining connected to India’s heritage.
Manoj Tiwari's response
On Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, BJP MP Manoj Tiwari told news agency PTI, "The Prime Minister himself has shown sensitivity, responsibility and accountability towards students. headline: FSSAI suspends nutraceutical maker’s licence
full_text:
FSSAI suspends nutraceutical maker’s licence
Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) suspended the manufacturing licence of Rehaan Healthcare after inspections found what the regulator
New Delhi: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) on Friday suspended the manufacturing licence of Rehaan Healthcare after inspections found what the regulator described as “critical non-compliance” and unhygienic conditions at the company’s health supplement and nutraceutical manufacturing unit.
Rehaan Healthcare, which manufactures digestive syrups, multivitamin syrups and other syrup-based food products, has been directed to stop production until all deficiencies are rectified and verified by the competent authority, FSSAI said in a statement.
Established in 2018 and based in Mohali, Rehaan Healthcare says on its website that it provides “scalable third-party manufacturing solutions”.
“Quality is not just a process at Rehaan Healthcare, it is our responsibility. Every batch is manufactured using carefully sourced raw materials, tested under defined quality parameters, and produced under strict hygiene and safety standards. We ensure that our products meet applicable AYUSH and food safety guidelines, helping our clients bring compliant and trustworthy products to market…,” the company has mentioned on its website.
However, FSSAI said its inspection found the manufacturing premises to be “extremely unhygienic and unorganised”.
According to the inspection report, food safety officers found spider webs, mould growth, flies, insects and exposed food waste inside the manufacturing area. “Sediments of filth and sludge accumulated under the manufacturing tank, disorganised storage of raw materials and poor housekeeping created a serious risk of cross-contamination,” FSSAI said.
The regulator also flagged major deficiencies in infrastructure and facilities, including inadequate storage arrangements, insufficient workspace, poor ventilation and lighting, damaged infrastructure, pest infestation and the absence of a valid drinking water test report.
“As the unit manufactures health supplements and nutraceuticals, a high-risk category of food consumed by children and other vulnerable groups, the unhygienic conditions and failure of food safety controls pose a serious and imminent threat to public health,” FSSAI said in its statement.
The regulator awarded the manufacturing unit an overall compliance score of just 12%.
The low score indicates a “very serious failure and non-compliance of existing provisions”, it said. In a social media post on Friday, the food safety regulator added: “The FSSAI License has been suspended with immediate effect.”
FSSAI has directed the company to immediately stop all food business activities until the deficiencies are corrected and compliance is verified by the competent authority.
The regulator also warned of legal action if the company violates the suspension order.
“The FBO (food business operator) has been directed to immediately cease all food business activities… any violation of this order shall invite appropriate legal action under the FSSA Act, 2006,” the statement said.
Rehaan Healthcare response???
In recent months, FSSAI has stepped up enforcement against food business operators over misleading claims and labelling violations. It has also issued notices to several e-commerce platforms. The regulator said these actions are based on consumer complaints, suo motu cognisance and routine enforcement activities carried out by food safety officers.

Amarnath Yatra resumed Saturday from Jammu after a six-day suspension forced by rain-caused disruptions, with a fresh batch of over 6,269 pilgrims leaving for the Kashmir cave shrine.

Meanwhile, Border Roads Organisation (BRO)has restored connectivity in Rajouri, Poonch and Reasi, the Jammu border districts where incessant rains triggered multiple landslides.
Working on a war footing under Project Sampark, BRO launched a swift and coordinated response to ensure uninterrupted movement of security forces and essential supplies in the three rain-affected districts.
âWorking tirelessly under hazardous conditions, BRO teams successfully removed debris, stabilised vulnerable stretches and restored traffic on the affected routes in the shortest possible time,â Jammu-based defence PRO Lt Col Suneel Bartwal said.

headline: Prashant Kishor’s gamble: Why Bankipur bypoll is key contest for political existence of Jan Suraaj? Explained
full_text:
Prashant Kishor’s gamble: Why Bankipur bypoll is key contest for political existence of Jan Suraaj? Explained
The Bankipur seat fell vacant after long-time MLA Nitin Nabin was elevated to the post of BJP National President and consequently resigned from the assembly.
Poll strategist-turned-politician Prashant Kishor will mark his electoral debut in the Bankipur bypoll, less than a year after his Jan Suraaj party failed to open its account in the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections. Thus, the upcoming by-election in Bihar has become a high-stakes battle for Jan Suraaj's political relevance.
While Kishor did not contest in the 2025 elections, he is now expecting to breach a BJP stronghold constituency.
Also Read | Prashant Kishor declares assets worth ₹105 crore ahead of key Bankipur contest
Bankipur bypoll 2026
The Bankipur seat fell vacant after long-time MLA Nitin Nabin was elevated to the post of BJP National President and consequently resigned from the assembly.
For this bypoll, the BJP has fielded Neeraj Kumar Sinha, who carries the weight of a party machinery that swept the 2025 assembly polls.
In the elections last year, BJP’s Nitin Nabin emerged victorious with a vote margin of over 51,000 votes, defeating RJD.
The Bankipur assembly bypoll will be held on July 30, while counting of votes is scheduled for August 3.
Also Read | BJP ramps up campaign for Bankipur assembly bypolls
What the future holds for Prashant Kishor?
D M Diwakar, former Director at the A N Sinha Institute of Social Studies, Patna, and presently associated with the Development Research Institute, Jalsain, Bihar, noted that the political landscape of Bankipur poses a big challenge for Kishor.
"Bankipur has been an unassailable BJP bastion since the 1990s," Diwakar said.
"Nitin Nabin previously built on his late father's legacy here, securing a massive victory with a margin of around 90,000 votes in the last election. In contrast, Jan Suraaj managed to pull only about 7,000 votes," he added.
However, Diwakar observed that the BJP introducing a new candidate creates a slight opening.
"When a party fields a new candidate with a strong local base, he/she can manage the constituency better. Prashant Kishor is banking on this transition to pull away dissatisfied voters," he explained.
"While a win for Kishor remains unlikely, Jan Suraaj can expand its vote share this time due to Kishor's personal credibility," Diwakar added.
"Because Bankipur is leaning toward the BJP, any votes Kishor cuts into will hurt the ruling party first," he continued.
According to him, this leaves two potential scenarios: either the BJP wins with a reduced margin, or if Kishor pulls off a massive vote split, the RJD candidate could unexpectedly benefit from it.
Diwakar concluded, "Establishing oneself as a steadfast politician takes time, but this bypoll marks his first serious test as a leader in the eyes of the public."
Also Read | Jolt to Tej Pratap's JJD as party candidate's nomination rejected in Bankipur over lack of signatures
What the voters want?
As the bypoll approaches, ground-zero sentiments reflect a mix of loyalty to past development and expectations for civic progress:
"It is clear what we expect. We want development, good roads, a drainage system, infrastructure, and continued development of educational institutes," said a local resident.
"This bypoll marks a fresh chapter for Bankipur. The BJP may have introduced a new candidate, but he is expected to carry forward Nitin Nabin’s long-standing vision, which makes it easy for voters to place their trust in him," noted the voter.

headline: Centre seeks SC nod to let retired judges on existing water tribunal hear fresh cases
full_text:
Centre seeks SC nod to let retired judges on existing water tribunal hear fresh cases
New Delhi: The Union government has moved the Supreme Court seeking a “purposive” interpretation of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, to allow retired Supreme Court and high court judges heading existing water tribunals to adjudicate fresh inter-state river disputes, arguing that such a reading would avoid the need to constitute new tribunals each time and ensure quicker resolution of disputes
New Delhi: The Union government has moved the Supreme Court seeking a “purposive” interpretation of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, to allow retired Supreme Court and high court judges heading existing water tribunals to adjudicate fresh inter-state river disputes, arguing that such a reading would avoid the need to constitute new tribunals each time and ensure quicker resolution of disputes.
In an application filed before a bench of justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta, the Centre urged the court to interpret Section 4(2) of the Act to hold that the statutory requirement that the chairman and members of a water disputes tribunal be nominated by the Chief Justice of India “from among persons who at the time of such nomination are Judges of the Supreme Court or of a High Court” is only a threshold qualification and not a continuing condition.
The plea, pressed by Attorney General R Venkataramani on Friday, seeks modification of the Supreme Court’s February 2 judgment directing the Centre to constitute a tribunal to adjudicate the long-pending Pennaiyar river water dispute between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. Instead of setting up a fresh tribunal, the Union wants permission to assign the dispute to the already constituted Mahadayi Water Disputes Tribunal, whose members have since retired from the constitutional courts but continue to hold office under the statute.
According to the Centre, such an interpretation would ensure the “optimal utilisation of the judicial and administrative resources of the Union” while providing an “expeditious and economical mode of compliance” with the Supreme Court’s directions.
Appearing for the Union, Venkataramani submitted that the government was “seeking a purposive interpretation of Section 4(2) of the Act so as to permit an existing Tribunal, whose members satisfied the qualification when nominated, to be entrusted with the adjudication of the Pennaiyar dispute.”
The bench, however, questioned why Parliament had not amended the statutory framework if such flexibility was intended. “You should have amended the provision...it would have been resolved by now,” observed the bench, referring to the mandatory requirement under Section 4 that the Centre constitute a tribunal once negotiations fail.
The Attorney General informed the court that the Mahadayi Water Disputes Tribunal had submitted its report and no proceedings had taken place before it since June 2020.
Senior advocate Shyam Divan, appearing for Karnataka along with advocate Nishanth Patil, opposed any immediate consideration of the plea, telling the apex court that the issue was “really serious” and required a detailed response. The counsel for Tamil Nadu also sought time to respond.
Accepting the request, the bench granted both states two weeks to file their replies and directed that the matter be listed thereafter.
According to the Union’s application, the tribunal submitted its report-cum-award in August 2018, which was published in February 2020. Proceedings on references were adjourned sine die in June 2020 on the request of the concerned states, although the tribunal continues to exist and its tenure presently stands extended until August 15, 2027.
The Centre contended that Section 4(2) expressly requires judges to possess the prescribed qualification only “at the time of such nomination”. “It is thus a qualification to be satisfied at the threshold and not a continuing condition,” stated the application, adding that members of an existing tribunal, having fulfilled the eligibility requirement when nominated, “do not cease to be competent to discharge the functions of the office upon demitting judicial office”, particularly since the statutory scheme itself contemplates tribunals functioning over several years.
The application further argued that the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act is a remedial legislation enacted to give effect to Article 262 of the Constitution and must therefore receive a purposive interpretation that advances, rather than defeats, the objective of speedy adjudication of inter-state river disputes. It also invoked the Supreme Court’s powers under Article 142 to mould relief in the interests of complete justice.
On February 2, the Supreme Court had held that there was “no impediment” to the Union government constituting a water disputes tribunal under the 1956 Act after negotiations between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka failed to resolve the Pennaiyar dispute. Disposing of Tamil Nadu’s original suit filed in 2018 under Article 131 of the Constitution, the court had directed that the state’s complaint be placed before the tribunal to be constituted by the Centre.
The Pennaiyar, also known as the South Pennar, originates in Karnataka and flows through Tamil Nadu before emptying into the Bay of Bengal. Tamil Nadu has for years alleged that Karnataka’s construction of check dams, reservoirs and diversion structures upstream has reduced downstream flows, adversely affecting irrigation and drinking water supply in several northern districts.
