headline: Nepal has formally requested India's approval to recognise its biometric National Identity (NID) card as an official travel document for cross-border journeys, alongside passports and citizenship certificates.
full_text:
Nepal has formally requested India's approval to recognise its biometric National Identity (NID) card as an official travel document for cross-border journeys, alongside passports and citizenship certificates.
At present, Nepali citizens travelling to India, particularly by air, must carry either a valid passport or an original citizenship certificate. Indian citizens entering Nepal are required to present either a passport or an original voter identity card with a photograph.
However, Nepal's National Identity card contains biometric information, including fingerprints, facial images and iris scans. The programme was launched as a pilot in Panchthar district and among government employees in 2009. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
So far, more than 4.5 million Nepali citizens have received the card, while nearly 20 million applications have been submitted.
Nepal plans to replace citizenship certificatesThe request comes as Nepal gradually makes the biometric National Identity card mandatory for banking, land registration, passport issuance and access to public services, with plans to eventually replace citizenship certificates.
"In the long run, we will have a single identity card replacing the citizenship certificate. 
It is verified, authentic and technology-friendly," Tiwari said.
"That is why we have requested India to allow the use of the National Identity Card while travelling by both air and land routes," he added.
India reviews the proposalAccording to senior immigration officials quoted by 
The Kathmandu Post, an Indian Embassy delegation met officials from Nepal's Department of Immigration earlier this week to discuss the proposal
The delegation was reportedly "positive" about the initiative and informed Nepalese officials that the request had been forwarded to authorities in New Delhi for consideration.
"We have already forwarded the proposal to the Indian side through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs," said Ram Chandra Tiwari, Director General of the Department of Immigration.
Officials from Nepal's Home Ministry also said that discussions have included creating formal mechanisms to record cross-border travel data and better manage movement between the two neighbouring countries.

headline: A sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) in Madhya Pradesh’s Panna district has sent a delivery executive to jail after he did not find the items he had ordered through an online platform. The district administration is considering issuing a show-cause noti...
full_text:
A sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) in Madhya Pradesh’s Panna district has sent a delivery executive to jail after he did not find the items he had ordered through an online platform. The district administration is considering issuing a show-cause notice to him.
A video of the purported incident that took place on July 21 and a conversation has surfaced on the internet where the executive, Vijay Kushwaha, can be heard telling Ramnivas Choudhary, SDM, Shahnagar, that he had delivered a sealed packet and that he could file for a refund under the platform’s the return policy.
The incident took place at Mr. Choudhary’s office. He had ordered two sets of two mobile covers but received only one in each box.
“You will go to jail within two seconds. You have taken the money for two [mobile covers], but there is only one inside the box. Are you returning the money or not? I am not filing for a return,” Mr. Choudhary tells the executive.
Mr. Kushwaha then says, “I have given a packed box and there is a return policy in this and you can return it. I cannot do anything about it.
“Why did you abuse me? You are using me in the wrong way,” Mr. Kushwaha says, after which the SDM’s staff tells him to get out of the room as Mr. Choudhary directs them to call the police.
After this, the delivery executive narrates the incident in the video.
Panna Collector Usha Parmar told The Hindu that while the delivery executive was released on bail on July 22, the district administration is going to issue a show-cause notice to the SDM.
When contacted, Mr. Choudhary alleged that Mr. Kushwaha was “talking rudely” and also “banged his hands on the table”.
“He gave the parcel to my staff and left. When we called him within minutes, he said he had travelled far and refused to come back initially. So, I scolded him. When he came back, he entered my chamber with mobile video recording on. I asked him for a refund but he refused and said we could call the police,” the SDM said.
“He is a resident of Pawai area in Panna district but lied that he is from Uttar Pradesh,” he said.
Panna Superintendent of Police (SP) Nivedita Naidu said that “prima facie the incident seemed to be a case of abuse of power”.
She said that while the police did not arrest the delivery executive, the local Tehsildar prepared a jail warrant against him under Section 170 of the BNSS, based on statements from the SDM and his staff, after which he was sent to jail.
“The SDM and his staff did not tell the police that the matter was related to online delivery. In their statements, they just alleged that the man was disturbing peace inside the SDM office. They did not tell us the whole matter,” Ms. Naidu said.

headline: NEW DELHI: CRPF director general Gyanendra Pratap Singh on Saturday said the force would conduct a professional post-analysis of the action taken by personnel of Rapid Action Force (RAF), a unit of CRPF, against anti-NEET paper leak protestors, inclu...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: CRPF director general Gyanendra Pratap Singh on Saturday said the force would conduct a professional post-analysis of the action taken by personnel of Rapid Action Force (RAF), a unit of CRPF, against anti-NEET paper leak protestors, including during the July 20 march to Parliament.
 âNow, since agitation has been called off, and once assembled people disperse, we would make a professional post-event assessment, like we do after every major assignment, and then let you know of the view of force headquarters,â Singh told TOI on Saturday. This is the first official statement from CRPF in the wake of allegations that pellet guns were used against protestors during the July 20 march to Parliament.
 Three people have claimed to have suffered pellet injuries in the police action. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
At least 47 RAF personnel too sustained injuries, allegedly from violent elements in the protests.
Sources said the post-event assessment by CRPF will go into all possible aspects of RAF deployment during the protests. This would include action taken by RAF personnel against the protestors, riot-control gear used by them and whether the ground situation justified it. It will examine if the RAF response was graded and in line with the standard operating procedures and riot control manual.
 An officer said the CRPF will also examine the provocation and aggression that the RAF personnel likely faced at the hands of external, motivated elements who may have infiltrated the protests.
CRPF sources said of the 47 RAF personnel injured during the course of their deployment for protests in the Capital, six have sustained head injuries and four, fractures. An officer claimed RAF personnel were hit by protesters with iron rods, likely retrieved from damaged railings. The accounts of the personnel regarding how the injuries were sustained, will be recorded as part of the post-event analysis. 
Delhi Police had clarified that they do have any pump action guns (PAG), but these are part of RAFâs standard anti-riot gear, along with shock batons. The CRPF review will probe allegations of firing of pellets by any personnel on duty, and if such action was authorised, justified and part of a graded response.
NEW DELHI
PAG, commonly known as pellet gun, is classified as a 'non-lethalâ anti-riot measure. As per the standard RAF drill, it is to be used only as a second last resort, with police firing being the last. Any RAF anti-riot action should start with engagement with the protestors or unruly mob, followed by warning on public address system to disperse. If all this fails, water cannon or tear gas may be used. Pellet gun is the next level of force applied, and may be fitted with a muzzle deflector so that the pellets hit only the lower body, leaving vital organs unharmed.

headline: As a spin-off of the ongoing war between Iran and the U.S., slain Iranian supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s jail diary is selling like hot cakes at the book festival in Srinagar.
full_text:
As a spin-off of the ongoing war between Iran and the U.S., slain Iranian supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s jail diary is selling like hot cakes at the book festival in Srinagar.
Buyers are jostling at the stall set up by the Mutahhari Fikri Wa Saqafati Markaz at the Sher-i-Kashmir International Convention Centre (SKICC) on the banks of the Dal Lake, with peak footfall of 20,000 visitors a day. Many local Shia clerics are recording videos on buying these books for social media platforms.
The front desk of the stall pavilion has stacks of books authored by Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, the architect of the 1979 Iranian revolution, and Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iran’s Supreme Leader, who was killed in a joint attack of the Israel and the U.S. on February 28 this year.
Read | Escalation trap: On the U.S. and the war with Iran
“Khamenei’s jail diary, ‘Cell No. 14’, has evoked a huge response. We are selling dozens of copies every day. We had a buyer who took 60 copies of it from the Chenab Valley of J&K,” said a salesman at the stall.
The ongoing war between Iran and the U.S. has generated a lot of interest among readers in Kashmir to know about the spiritual leadership of Iran, which has shaped the country in the past four decades.
“’Cell No. 14’ is the autobiography of Khamenei. It gives a peek into what revolutionaries in Iran suffered under the Shah regime. It provides a context to understand the Iranian government and its resolve,” said Rashid Ahmad, a student of Kashmir University (KU).
The appeal of Iranian literature is not limited to Shia readers of Kashmir, with Sunnis also turning up at the stall and showing interest in their writings. “Reading Iranian literature, especially the shapers of modern-day Iran, is essential to know how the country has married democracy and the clergy into one,” said Faiz Khan, a Political Science student.
Several local politicians and bureaucrats also purchased the autobiographies and books authored by the Iranian leaders from the stall, said another salesman.
It’s for the first time that Shia publishers have set up several stalls at the third edition of the Chinar Book Festival organised by the National Book Trust (NBT), which started on July 18 and will conclude on July 26.
“We had a very good response this year. Our peak footfall was more than 20,000 a day,” said Dr. Amit Wanchoo, chief convener of the Chinar Book Festival.
The nine-day festival, which J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha inaugurated, saw over 200 publishers and book exhibitors displaying a range of books in English, Urdu, Kashmiri, Hindi, and several other Indian languages.
However, the book fair was not out of the police scanner this year, in the wake of two pro-separatists making it to the school education department in J&K. Officials said all the publishers were asked to furnish the list of books and submit records on a daily basis so that no anti-India or pro-separatists were displayed in the stalls.
Last year, 25 books authored by renowned writers like Christopher Snedden, A.G. Noorani, Sumantra Bose, Ayesha Jalal, Sugata Bose, Arundhati Roy, Stephen P Cohen, Anuradha Bhasin, Seema Qazi etc, were banned in J&K for “exciting secession, endangering the integrity of India” and “propagating false narrative and secessionism in J&K”.

headline: NEW DELHI: If the students' protest held the Modi govt hostage for a week, its potency was amplified by the political class that blockaded the Parliament alongside.
full_text:
NEW DELHI: If the students' protest held the Modi govt hostage for a week, its potency was amplified by the political class that blockaded the Parliament alongside.
But the symphony was not perfect from the start as the anti-BJP bloc had two opposing streams. The one led by 
Congress viewed 
CJP with suspicion, haunted as it was by the spectre of the Anna Hazare agitation that became the nemesis of the Manmohan govt and was later found to have been orchestrated by RSS. But Left outfits and some regional parties backed CJP as the voice of the youth.
When the like-minded parties met an hour before the start of the monsoon session Monday, the NEET protest competed with "Ayodhya donation scam" row as the plank to be espoused.
Congress and SP argued that Ayodhya should be picked as the opening salvo against BJP. But a consensus emerged on taking up the "paper leak" protest first after a forceful push from other parties which argued that the opposition had to associate itself with the youth march to Parliament.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
For Congress, which had been protesting against "paper leaks" for two years, the issue of political credit was also a consideration. The AAP background of CJP founders Abhijeet Dipke and others made many sniff a conspiracy. But barely two hours later, the police crackdown on young marchers ended all equivocation.
All along, protesters were also actively courting political support. Activist 
Sonam Wangchuk, and later his wife Gitanjali Angmo, questioned Rahul's absence from Jantar Mantar, even as SP's Dimple and Akhilesh Yadav, Shiv Sena's Uddhav Thackeray and son Aditya, NCP-SP's Sharad Pawar, AAP's Arvind Kejriwal and scores of others visited the venue. 
CPI (ML)'s Dipankar Bhattacharya and CPM's M A Baby were among the first to lend support in early June.
Post-crackdown, the gap kept closing as the controversy intensified, crowds continued to swell and the story went global.
Amid scepticism about the newbie, Congress and opposition were assured by the fact that the Jantar Mantar stage of Dipke had been filled with student activists from the Left parties. It was evident in the way Rahul Saturday held a news conference with AISA activists to reiterate that protesters would not budge without the resignation of the education minister. It appeared to be a bid to queer the pitch for CJP, which was in talks with govt.
In the end, as Dharmendra Pradhan resigned, the political class and the Jantar Mantar platform were together in hailing it as a victory for the young seeking accountability from the govt.

headline: How global media covered CJP protests that led to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
full_text:
How global media covered CJP protests that led to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
As images of police action and thousands of young protesters flooded global headlines, the Cockroach Janta Party-led movement came to symbolise a wider debate on governance, youth aspirations and political accountability in India.
What began as a protest over irregularities in India’s education system, particularly the 2026 NEET-UG paper leak, quickly escalated into a major international story.
Images of baton charges, tear gas, candlelight marches and thousands of young protesters camping on Delhi’s streets travelled widely across global media. As the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) movement grew, international media increasingly covered it as a broader story about governance, youth aspirations and political accountability in India.
The resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan further intensified that framing, with coverage largely treating it as a significant political development for the BJP-led NDA government in its third term.
Here’s how some of the world’s biggest news organisations reported the protests.
REUTERS: MAJOR TEST FOR MODI GOVT
Reuters described the protests and Pradhan’s resignation as a major political challenge for Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term.
The global news agency described Pradhan's resignation as "a surprise", noting that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has a reputation for refusing to yield to public pressure.
Its reporting highlighted the political implications of the unrest, noting the importance of young voters for the BJP and the scale of mobilisation by students over alleged exam irregularities and wider concerns about unemployment and limited opportunities.
CNN: RARE CHALLENGE FOR MODI GOVT
CNN called Pradhan’s resignation a “rare and growing” challenge for Prime Minister Modi, noting that he is not typically seen as a leader who responds directly to street protests.
The network linked the demonstrations to broader concerns about governance and accountability, alongside India’s youth unemployment problem, arguing that the protests reflected deeper economic anxieties among young graduates beyond the immediate issue of exam leaks.
BBC: ONE OF LARGEST STUDENT-LED MOVEMENTS
The BBC described the CJP agitation as one of India’s largest student-led movements in recent years, placing it within the country’s broader history of mass protests.
It drew parallels with the Nav Nirman movement of the 1970s, noting that while some student uprisings have historically influenced political change, others have faded.
The BBC also said the CJP protests stood out for their scale and for the way they brought together students with broader concerns about governance and education policy.
"Whether that frustration can be sustained as a political movement, however, is another question," it noted.
THE GUARDIAN: FOCUS ON CELEBRITY SILENCE
The Guardian focused less on political implications and more on cultural reaction, highlighting frustration among protesters over the silence of India’s major celebrities.
It reported that many demonstrators questioned the silence of public figures over the violence against students and expressed anger at what they saw as “cowardice” among India’s biggest celebrities.
"Protesters were scathing about how celebrities had commented on global tragedies or injustices but turned a blind eye to the grievances of people at home, even when their most devoted fanbase were being baton-charged and teargassed by the police," it said.
The newspaper also noted that some prominent personalities only spoke publicly in the later stages of the movement.
AL JAZEERA: VISIBLE SENSE OF PUBLIC DISSENT
Al Jazeera described the protests as one of the most visible expressions of public dissent against the Modi government in recent years.
It reported that while the movement began with anger over alleged education irregularities, it soon expanded into broader concerns about unemployment, corruption and governance, reflecting wider public frustration.
It also quoted critics as saying that the growing disconnect between the government and India’s Generation Z "pushed the administration into a corner."
SCMP: MOVEMENT BEYOND CAMPUSES
The South China Morning Post (SCMP) said the protests were among India’s largest street demonstrations in recent years.
It noted that the movement quickly moved beyond university campuses, drawing support from opposition parties and civil society groups, and reflected growing concerns over job scarcity, corruption and governance failures.
“The BJP has lost some of the moral high ground it once used to criticise the Congress Party,” the publication quoted a political commentator as saying.
SHARED SENSE OF SCALE, DIFFERENT EMPHASIS
While each outlet approached the story differently, their coverage consistently reflected the scale and significance of the protests.
Reuters emphasised political impact, CNN focused on governance and youth unemployment, the BBC placed it in historical context, The Guardian questioned the silence of India's celebrities, while Al Jazeera and the SCMP underscored broader public discontent.
Taken together, the reporting suggested that the CJP protests had moved beyond their original trigger of alleged exam irregularities. By the time Pradhan resigned, the movement was widely seen as a larger expression of youth frustration over opportunity, governance and the future.

headline: Will live up to PM's expectations, says new Education Minister Pralhad Joshi
full_text:
Will live up to PM's expectations, says new Education Minister Pralhad Joshi
Union Minister and BJP MP Pralhad Joshi took additional charge of the Education Ministry after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned. He said he would work with humility amid NEET protest fallout.
Newly-appointed Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi on Saturday said he would discharge his responsibilities with “complete humility” and a strong sense of duty after being given additional charge of the ministry following Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation in the wake of students' protests over the NEET paper leak controversy.
President Droupadi Murmu accepted Pradhan’s resignation on Saturday, after which Prime Minister Narendra Modi assigned Joshi the additional portfolio.
Speaking after taking charge, Joshi said the Prime Minister had placed his trust in him by entrusting him with a “significant responsibility”. He thanked PM Narendra Modi for the opportunity and said he would work sincerely under his guidance to meet expectations in the Education Ministry.
“With full dedication, humility and honesty, I will work towards fulfilling this responsibility,” Joshi said.
The 63-year-old credited Pradhan with implementing the National Education Policy (NEP) and said several important initiatives had been undertaken in the education sector in recent years.
“In the last four to five years, Dharmendra Pradhan also implemented the National Education Policy, and several important initiatives were undertaken. The country has made significant progress in the new education system,” Joshi said.
He added that he would work to the best of his ability under the Prime Minister’s guidance and fulfil his responsibilities with dedication.
Joshi will retain his existing portfolios while also taking charge of the Education Ministry. The Lok Sabha MP from Karnataka’s Dharwad constituency currently serves as Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, as well as Minister for New and Renewable Energy.
Pradhan stepped down amid student protests over irregularities in the NEET examination. In a letter shared on X, he said he had submitted his resignation to PM Modi in the interest of students and to ensure that the protests were not exploited by “anti-national forces”.
“The situation that has emerged at Jantar Mantar and elsewhere in the country should not be exploited by anti-national forces. The unity of the country must remain intact. The future of every student in India should not get entangled in legal complications,” Pradhan said.
“Keeping these considerations in mind, I have sent my resignation to the Hon’ble Prime Minister,” he added.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) called off its 49-day agitation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar following the resignation of Pradhan and government assurances on the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters and organisers.
The decision was taken after three rounds of talks between a CJP delegation and government representatives, including Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh.
Announcing the withdrawal, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said the agitation was being called off in good faith, with the group expecting the government to implement the agreed terms within the promised timelines.

headline: India, US working to conclude trade agreement early: Govt
full_text:
India, US working to conclude trade agreement early: Govt
The additional tariff was imposed as part of the USTR’s final action following probes into the acts, policies and practices of 60 economies, including India.
India’s engagements with the US Trade Representative (USTR) helped secure a lower tariff for Indian goods, the commerce ministry said on Saturday, adding that both nations were seeking an “early conclusion” of the planned bilateral trade agreement.
The statement followed the imposition of 10% additional tariffs on goods from India on Friday, under Section 301 of the US Trade Act, 1974. “USTR has imposed an additional 10% ad valorem duty on imports from India. This is a reduction from the 12.5% duty initially proposed on 2nd June 2026,” said a statement from the ministry.
The ministry said the Centre engaged closely with the USTR’s office “through detailed written submissions and in-person consultations, including participation in public hearings.”
Also Read | NEET victims’ families seek reforms, say Pradhan’s resignation not enough
“As a result of these sustained efforts, India has been placed in the lower tier of additional tariffs under the final measures, providing a relative advantage to Indian exports in key sectors,” it added.
The additional tariff was imposed as part of the USTR’s final action following probes into the acts, policies and practices of 60 economies, including India, relating to imposition and enforcement of bans on the import of goods produced through forced labour.
A substantial share of India’s exports to the US, which currently attract no additional duties, such as generic pharmaceuticals, smartphones and other specified products, remain outside the scope of the additional 10% duty, it said. “Further, products already covered under Section 232 measures, including steel, aluminium and auto parts, are not subject to the additional 10% duty,” said the ministry.
Section 232 duties are applicable broadly to all countries with limited exceptions.
On account of these exemptions, an estimated 45% of India’s exports to the US remain outside the purview of the additional 10% duty.
For the remaining 55%, India’s tariff incidence is comparatively lower than that for most other economies covered, said the statement.
“The textile specific mechanism referenced in the final measures is yet to be established and operationalised. India continues to engage with the US on this matter as part of the ongoing negotiations for the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement,” the statement said, referring to the probable textile and apparel tariff-rate quota (TRQ) for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, and Malaysia, all of which use US-origin cotton and fiber.
The statement concluded by reiterating the government’s commitment towards the India-US Bilateral Trade Agreement,“as announced on 2nd February 2026 and in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026.”

headline: Will build Agra museum dedicated to Chhatrapati Shivaji by year-end: Yogi Adityanath
full_text:
Will build Agra museum dedicated to Chhatrapati Shivaji by year-end: Yogi Adityanath
UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said Agra's proposed museum will honour Chhatrapati Shivaji and not Aurangzeb. He made the announcement as he sharpened his attack on the Samajwadi Party, while tying heritage to development politics.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has criticised the previous Samajwadi Party government over its plan to build a museum dedicated to Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in Agra, and said his government will instead complete a grand museum in the name of Chhatrapati Shivaji by the end of this year. He said public money would not be used for a museum named after “an invader”.
Speaking at a function where he inaugurated and laid the foundation for 53 development projects worth more than Rs 342 crore, Adityanath also said the government had approved the acquisition of the ‘kothi’ (residence) in Agra where Shivaji had stayed. He also spoke about infrastructure, industry, tourism and farmer-related measures in Agra, while attacking the Samajwadi Party and Congress over governance and law and order.
Addressing the gathering, Adityanath said, “In Agra, the city where Chhatrapati Shivaji displayed his valour, the Samajwadi Party government was building a Mughal museum. Public funds would not be used for a museum named after an invader; instead, a museum would be constructed in the name of India’s national heroes.” He said construction of the Shivaji museum would be completed by the end of this year.
He added, “We have also approved the acquisition of the ‘kothi’ in Agra where Chhatrapati Shivaji had stayed.”
Targeting the Samajwadi Party, Adityanath said it had remained focused on its own development.
“Public funds became a medium for the ‘Saifai Syndicate’ to engage in loot. Whether it was stealing job opportunities meant for the youth, misappropriating welfare schemes intended for the poor, or the sinful act of snatching away the prosperity of our farmers, the Samajwadi Party and before them, the Congress, committed these sins,” he said.
He said the impact of this was that the state’s youth faced an identity crisis, farmers were driven to suicide, and daughters and traders lived in insecurity. In an apparent jibe at former Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav, he said, “Only God save a state where its chief minister would wake up at 12 noon, get ready by 2 pm, head to the gym at 5 pm, and enjoy spending the time after 7 pm with his circle of friends.”
Adityanath said this was why a mafia figure had emerged in every district and every police station and tehsil had effectively gone into the hands of goons. “Anarchy, curfews, and the rule of criminals and the mafia once plagued the state. The picture of Uttar Pradesh you see today represents a system free from all that. Today, there are no curfews or riots. Everything is truly well here,” he said.
On Agra’s development, he said, “We have already taken steps to establish an international airport in Agra. It is now developing into a new centre not only for industrial activity in the Braj region, but also for tourism. Connectivity has improved significantly.” He said the Supreme Court had approved work that had earlier been halted because of the Taj Trapezium Zone.
On Thursday, the Supreme Court allowed the Taj Trapezium Zone Authority to process around 400 pending applications for setting up non-polluting Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises in the ecologically sensitive area around the Taj Mahal.
The court, however, said experts from the Central Empowered Committee and the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute must scrutinise each proposal. It said that if any objection arose, the application concerned would not be accepted without the leave of the court.
Adityanath said Agra was becoming not only a smart city but also a new model of a safe city. He said Peru’s International Potato Centre had to open a branch somewhere in India, and land was offered in Agra. “This will benefit our farmers: their produce will receive value addition, and with much higher prices, their incomes will increase. This will bring prosperity to their lives,” he said.
He said work on multi-level parking, an Integrated Command and Control Centre, and the modernisation of the city’s traffic system would now move ahead quickly. He added that farmers’ concerns had been resolved after they were raised by public representatives. He also said the government was working to give Petha global recognition under the “One District, One Product” and “One District, One Cuisine” schemes.
Adityanath said development works were also being carried forward at Bateshwar Dham, Kailash Temple, Guru Ka Tal, Geet Govind Vatika, the birthplace of Atal Bihari Vajpayee at Bateshwar, Fatehpur Sikri and Sauripur Jain Teerth.
He also announced that a working women’s hostel with capacity for 500 residents would be built in Agra in memory of Lokmata Ahilyabai Holkar, and said the state government had approved the project and released the budget.
He ended with a warning on safety, saying, “There will be no compromise on the safety of our daughters and traders. Anyone who attempts to breach their security has only two destinations: jail or hell.”

full_text:
NEW DELHI: BJP has fended off numerous opposition campaigns built around allegations, contentious laws or policies, and suspected wrongdoings of a senior Union minister or a chief minister since PM Modi took office in 2014 without making any appearance of bowing to pressure. However, where the opposition could not succeed, street protests and the fear that they could have triggered violence have.
The resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, a key member of the Cabinet since Modi first took office in 2014, following unebbing protests is a significant political dent to the party, presenting the opposition a rare opening to build on youth anger after suffering electoral setbacks and desertions from ranks. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
Govt hoped to benefit from the optics of activist Sonam Wangchuk breaking his 26-day hunger strike by accepting soup from Union minister J P Nadda and agreeing to the gentle terms built on assurances.
With the protests, though, showing no signs of a let-up and Rahul Gandhi stepping up opposition's stir, BJP chose pragmatism over defiance, more so as it was confronted with Gen Z that did not deal in the old grammar of politics, making its irreverent slogans, memes and skits go viral.
Earlier, government had withdrawn farm laws in Nov 2021 following a year-long protest from farmers, while Modi had publicly announced in Dec 2019 that his govt had no plans for a National Register of Citizens to defuse the agitation against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act.
J Akbar, who quit in 2018 after his name surfaced in the #MeToo row, was a junior minister and carried little political heft. As BJP counts its losses, it will have to grapple with the challenge of winning over a generation which, many political observers say, had been showing signs of restiveness over a host of employment-related concerns even before these protests broke out, despite a section supporting the partyâs other planks. The view within BJP is that despite the immediate political price it has paid, it has shown its sincerity of purpose by engaging with protesters and conceding to them, belying the charge that it was âarrogant and insensitive

headline: Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation Saturday marks an unusual stumble in a political career that appeared to be headed towards more important destinations.
full_text:
NEW DELHI/BHUBANESWAR: 
Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation Saturday marks an unusual stumble in a political career that appeared to be headed towards more important destinations.
The architect of BJP's maiden victory in 
Odisha and facilitator of a series of wins elsewhere was first catapulted into the limelight while leading an ABVP-backed agitation in 1996 against an alleged Class XII question paper leak in Od-isha, during which he was injured in a police lathicharge.
Four years later, he won the Pallahara assembly seat on a BJP ticket. He became president of BJP's youth wing, BJYM, in Odisha in 2001 and was elevated as party national secretary in 2002. In 2004, he was appointed BJYM national president.
It was also the year he first entered Lok Sabha from Deogarh, when BJP and BJD were allies. Disappointment followed when he lost the assembly poll from Pallahara in 2009 after delimitation abolished the Deogarh LS seat and the alliance collapsed.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
Pradhan made a comeback when he was appointed co-in-charge of BJP's campaign for 2010 Bihar assembly polls, which BJP swept along with JDU. His nomination to Rajya Sabha from Bihar was seen as a just reward. As election in-charge of Bihar for the 2014 LS polls, he was crucial to NDA's sweep of 31 of its 40 LS seats.
Reforms in education under Pradhan
In 2014 he was inducted into Modi's first cabinet as MoS with independent charge of the petroleum ministry, despite resistance. 
Three years later, he was cabinet minister.
Amid the controversy over gas pricing, Pradhan launched a clean-up drive and put an end to the complete drip of corporate houses in the sector. His ministry's Ujjwala scheme helped expand LPG access. His work helped him get the education portfolio in 2021.
Pradhan's background as a grassroots worker also made him a crucial player in political battles. In 2022, he was made the party's election in-charge in UP, where BJP won 255 of 403 seats. In 2024, he successfully contested from Sambalpur. Though he retained the 
education ministry in Modi's third term, the reward was seen as less than what he deserved, considering he was the architect of BJP's organisational base in Odisha - a state where the party swept to office for the first time.
But things have been challenging for him since then, with paper leaks in 2024 and 2026, as well as the botched-up OMR rollout by CBSE.
In between, he delivered a success in Haryana in 2024, and Bihar, where he was BJP's election in-charge in 2025.

headline: Intent of infiltrators hasn’t changed since 1999 conflict, says Rajnath in Dras
full_text:
Intent of infiltrators hasn’t changed since 1999 conflict, says Rajnath in Dras
Intent of infiltrators hasn’t changed since 1999 conflict, says Rajnath in Dras
Dras, On the eve of the 27th anniversary of Kargil Vijay Diwas, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh here on Saturday said the "intent of infiltrators" hasn't changed since the 1999 conflict, as he asserted that the Indian Army is "fully prepared" for any such challenges.
In his address to Army personnel at a Shaurya Bhoj hosted in Dras, he also said the government has laid special emphasis on modernisation of the armed forces, and the endeavour is that the military gets the latest equipment and the best of the training.
Singh arrived in Dras on Saturday evening to attend Shaurya Sandhya - an event held at the Kargil War Memorial here as part of a two-day programme to mark the anniversary of Kargil Vijay Diwas.
Kargil Vijay Diwas commemorates the culmination of Operation Vijay on July 26, 1999. The operation was started by the Army to regain Indian territories in the Kargil district captured by Pakistani troops.
"We have to remember that even today challenges have not reduced; the intent of infiltrators hasn't changed, and even today it adopts tools like a proxy war or infiltration," he said in a veiled reference to Pakistan.
"I am fully assured that our Army is fully prepared for any such challenges," Singh said.
The defence minister said, this is "our century, the coming time is ours," and given the emphasis on Aatmanirbharta, "I am assured that Indian armed forces will become the best in the world."
In his address, he also saluted the armed forces and the valour of the soldiers.
"Today we are breathing free and living with our heads held high, as our soldiers in Kargil, despite plummeting mercury and dipping oxygen levels, have not lowered their guard," Singh said.
Singh said the pride he was feeling in Dras at this occasion cannot be expressed in words.
He said he was confident that till Indian soldiers possess the invisible inner strength, and a sense of nationalistic sentiment, "no force of the world will dare to cast an evil eye on India."
"In the last few years, I have had the opportunity to see closely many of the traditions of the Army, and one that touches the heart the most is Bada Khana," the minister said.
This is so because it is the only occasion when a jawan and an officer sit together and have the same meal, depicting an excellent sense of teamwork, he said.
"Your ability to rise above the limitations found in society is your true strength. And this strength alone enables us to win wars like the Kargil one," Singh said.

NEW DELHI: Acting on the Supreme Court's directions, the 
Uttar Pradesh government has constituted a new 
Special Investigation Team (SIT) led by senior IPS officers to investigate the alleged embezzlement of devotees' offerings at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya.
The reconstituted team is headed by Inspector General Kiran S, with Deputy Inspector General Somen Verma and Ayodhya Senior Superintendent of Police Dr Gaurav Grover as members. It replaces the earlier SIT, which was headed by Lucknow Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant and included Special Secretary (Finance) Neel Ratan Kumar among its members.
The apex court had, during a July 13 hearing, expressed the view that allegations involving theft and financial irregularities required investigation by experienced police officers. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohan directed the state to form a fresh SIT under a senior IPS officer and submit a status report by July 27.
The case centres on allegations that offerings made by devotees at the Ram temple were siphoned off instead of being deposited through the prescribed process.
Investigators probing the case earlier examined CCTV footage, donation registers, cash-handling records and financial documents, besides questioning temple staff. 
Their preliminary findings indicated suspected irregularities in the counting and deposit of donations.
The investigation led to the arrest of several accused, while police seized cash, vehicles, investment documents and other assets allegedly acquired using the misappropriated funds. Investigators also analysed bank transactions and other digital evidence to trace the alleged money trail.
With the new SIT now taking over the probe, the Uttar Pradesh government is expected to place its findings before the Supreme Court in a status report on July 27.

headline: 'Arbitration is starting to look like court process': CJI Surya Kant
full_text:
'Arbitration is starting to look like court process': CJI Surya Kant
CJI Surya Kant said arbitration is becoming like court litigation, urging faster proceedings, stronger case management and judicial restraint.
Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Saturday said that present-day arbitration is starting to look like the very court process it was meant to replace, flagging delays in awards and proceedings extending into multi-day hearings and heavy documentation.
“We now see multi-day hearings. We see heavy document production modelled on common law discovery. We see competing experts on every point. And we see awards that take years, not months…Arbitration is starting to look like the very court process it was meant to replace,” he said.
He produced the latest data by the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) to illustrate the long delays in arbitral disputes that take an average of 26 months to reach a final award. The London Court of International Arbitration’s (LCIA) figures show a median of 20 months. “By the standards of our conventional courts, these numbers are not shocking. But they are a long way from the speed arbitration once promised”.
Also read: ‘Judiciary always ready to address problems, suffering of people’: CJI
While admitting that the foundations of International Arbitration remain sound, he said that over time, layers of procedure have obscured the efficiency and flexibility for which he suggested tribunals manage proceedings with discipline, set realistic schedules at the outset, and ensure they are followed.
Speaking on the topic, “International Arbitration: Navigating New Realities and Stress-testing the Fundamentals at the Annual India Conference of the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) in Delhi, CJI Kant highlighted four areas of concern. These include, besides a strong case management, balanced transparency, sensible use of technology, and, restraint from the courts when asked to enforce arbitral awards.
He said courts must resist the urge to second-guess arbitrators as it poses a real risk of inconsistency, the very thing that undermines predictability between parties in arbitration proceedings. “As arbitration begins to confront disputes involving digital assets and other AI-driven technologies, that distinctly human role will become even more important”.

headline: Longer jail terms, faster trials: Proposed key changes in anti-cheating law
full_text:
Longer jail terms, faster trials: Proposed key changes in anti-cheating law
The Centre will introduce the Public Examinations Amendment Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha on Monday. The move follows the NEET-UG paper leak row and seeks faster trials with tougher penalties.
The Union government is set to table the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha on Monday, July 27, as it seeks to strengthen the legal framework against examination-related fraud. The amendments are aimed at strengthening the 2024 law by introducing harsher punishments, ensuring time-bound investigations and trials, and creating special fast-track courts to ensure speedy justice.
The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 seeks to significantly strengthen India's legal framework against examination malpractices by introducing tougher penalties, faster investigations, and time-bound trials. The proposed amendments aim to improve accountability, deter organised examination-related fraud, and restore confidence in the country's public examination system.
WHY THE GOVERNMENT IS BRINGING AMENDMENT BILL
The amendment bill is being brought against the backdrop of the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, which sparked widespread protests by students across the country and intensified demands for tougher anti-cheating laws, greater transparency, and stronger accountability in the conduct of public examinations. The move comes just hours after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) called off its protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Saturday, saying the government had agreed to its principal demands and assured action on the issue.
As per the Lok Sabha's list of business, Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh is scheduled to introduce the legislation. Following its introduction, he is also expected to seek the House's approval to take up the Bill for discussion and passage.
Amid escalating protests over the alleged NEET paper leak and mounting political pressure, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday unveiled a series of measures aimed at tackling examination fraud, including the creation of fast-track courts to expedite trials in paper leak cases.
The announcement came as students continued demonstrations in Delhi, demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, while the issue also dominated proceedings in Parliament. Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister on Saturday.
"We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks. Have directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps in this regard," the Prime Minister said.
PM Modi stressed that safeguarding students' interests remained a key priority for his government and warned that any attempt to compromise the future of young aspirants would be dealt with firmly. He added that the fast-track courts were part of a broader strategy to strengthen the integrity of the country's examination system.
The announcement followed criticism of the government's handling of protests, particularly after police action against demonstrators marching towards Parliament on July 20.
Meanwhile, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi intensified his attack on the government, alleging that there had been 152 examination paper leaks over the past decade without a single conviction. He argued that the recurring incidents had severely undermined India's education system and called for greater accountability.
WHAT CHANGES FROM THE 2024 LAW?
Against this backdrop, let us see how this amendment differs from the principal 2024 Act, which was enacted with the objective of bringing greater transparency, fairness, and credibility to the public examination system, inspiring confidence among candidates and effectively deterring persons, organised groups, and institutions from indulging in unfair means.
STRICTER PUNISHMENT FOR INDIVIDUALS AND ORGANISED CRIME FRAUD
One of the most significant changes proposed in the Bill is the enhancement of punishments for those found guilty of examination fraud. The proposed amendments significantly enhance penalties for both individual offenders and organised examination-related fraud.
For individuals found guilty of using unfair means in public examinations, the Bill proposes increasing the prison term to five to 10 years, up from the existing three to five years. It also seeks to raise the maximum fine from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 50 lakh, signalling a much tougher stance against examination malpractice.
The legislation also introduces stricter punishments for organised examination-related crimes. The minimum imprisonment for those involved in organised paper leak rackets or cheating networks has been increased from five years to seven years, while the minimum fine has been raised tenfold—from Rs 1 crore to Rs 10 crore. The enhanced penalties are aimed at deterring large-scale examination fraud and dismantling organised criminal networks involved in such offences.
TOUGHER ACTION AGAINST SERVICE PROVIDERS
The Bill also proposes stringent action against service providers—including agencies or organisations responsible for conducting examinations—if they are found complicit in examination malpractice. The maximum financial penalty for such entities has been increased from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore, while the period during which they can be barred from conducting examinations has been doubled from four years to eight years.
Corporate accountability has also been strengthened under the proposed legislation. Directors, senior management personnel, or any individual responsible for the affairs of a company found involved in examination fraud will face a minimum prison sentence of five years (the existing minimum is three years), along with fines of Rs 5 crore (the existing fine is Rs 1 crore). The provision aims to ensure that top executives cannot evade responsibility for organised malpractice carried out under their supervision.
SPECIAL TASK FORCE AND TIME-BOUND INVESTIGATIONS
To strengthen enforcement, the legislation empowers the Central Government to constitute a Special Task Force (STF) wherever necessary to investigate serious offences related to public examinations. The STF will be tasked with handling complex cases involving organised fraud, large-scale paper leaks, or other major examination-related crimes.
The amendment also introduces strict timelines for investigations. Police authorities, central investigating agencies, or the STF will be required to complete investigations into offences under the Act within two months, ensuring that cases are not delayed indefinitely.
SPECIAL FAST TRACK COURTS AND QUICKER TRIALS
To ensure speedy resolution of cases, the Bill empowers State governments and Union Territory administrations to designate any Court of Session as a Special Fast Track Court for the exclusive trial of offences under the Act. These dedicated courts will handle cases related to public examination fraud, enabling faster hearings and disposal of matters through a focused judicial process.
The Bill mandates day-to-day hearings in these Special Fast Track Courts, with trials expected to be completed within three months of the filing of the chargesheet. This provision is intended to deliver timely justice and strengthen public confidence in the examination system.
To support faster prosecution, States and Union Territories will appoint Special Public Prosecutors for these designated courts. These prosecutors will exclusively handle cases under the Act, enabling more focused and efficient legal proceedings.
FASTER DISPOSAL OF PENDING CASES
All pending cases under the Act will be transferred to the designated Special Fast Track Courts, which will be required to complete the trials within three months from the date of transfer. These courts will also be empowered to hear and decide connected offences arising from the same matter under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, or any other applicable laws.
The proposed amendments also streamline the appeals process. Appeals against judgments delivered by the Special Fast Track Courts will lie directly before a Division Bench of the High Court. The Bill provides that appeals should ordinarily be filed within 30 days, although courts may allow an extension of up to 90 days in exceptional circumstances. It also envisages that High Courts should endeavour to dispose of such appeals within three months, ensuring that legal proceedings are concluded without undue delay.
Individual Offences:
2024: 3–5 years jail | Rs 10 lakh fine
2026: 5–10 years jail | Rs 50 lakh fine
Organised Crime:
2024: Min 5 years jail | Rs 1 crore fine
2026: Min 7 years jail | Rs 10 crore fine
Service Providers:
2024: Rs 1 crore fine | 4-year ban
2026: Rs 5 crore fine | 8-year ban
Investigation Window:
2024: No deadline
2026: Mandatory 60 days
Trial Timeline:
2024: Regular court timelines
2026: Fast-track court (3-month trial limit)

headline: 10 defining images that captured India's watershed Gen Z protests
full_text:
10 defining images that captured India's watershed Gen Z protests
A sequence of photographs traced the CJP's agitation over alleged NEET irregularities from street clashes to talks with the government. The images showed the protest's spread across cities and its culmination in Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.
A tear gas canister thrown back at police. Water cannons turning protesters into silhouettes. A hunger strike ending with a hospital shift. A woman standing defiantly in front of a police van. And, finally, celebrations at Jantar Mantar after the Education Minister's resignation.
For almost 50 days, the Cockroach Janta Party's agitation over alleged NEET irregularities produced a series of images that captured a protest moving from confrontation on the streets to negotiations with the government - and eventually, a political victory for its principal demand.
Here is the CJP agitation in pictures, from the first clashes and hunger strikes to the moment its protesters celebrated after Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned.
THE PROTEST THAT REACHED PARLIAMENT
A protester throws back a tear gas canister towards police as supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party march towards Parliament on the opening day of the Monsoon Session, demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged examination paper leaks, in New Delhi on July 20. The image captured one of the most intense moments of the agitation as protesters confronted security personnel during the march.
THIS MOVEMENT IS NOT JUST IN DELHI
A 27-year-old model, Rhiya Ahir, stands with her arms outstretched in front of a police van during a demonstration in Mumbai in solidarity with the CJP's agitation over alleged NEET irregularities on July 22. The protest reflected how the movement found support beyond the national capital.

SHE STOOD BETWEEN THE BATON AND THE PROTESTERS
As a police officer moves through a tightly packed crowd during the protest, a young woman reaches out to protect fellow demonstrators caught in the confrontation. SOLIDARITY AT JANTAR MANTAR
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk and his wife Gitanjali J Angmo attend a protest organised by the CJP at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on July 17. Wangchuk, who was on an indefinite hunger strike, also reiterated his demand for constitutional safeguards and greater protection for Ladakh.
A MOMENT OF TENSION

'HAM AAPKE BACHCHE NAHI HAIN'
A moment from the CJP agitation captures the anger and defiance that became a recurring feature of the protest, as demonstrators challenged the government's handling of alleged examination irregularities and demanded accountability.
THE MOMENT THE PROTEST TURNED
Protesters clash with security personnel at barricades during a march towards Parliament demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination and expressing support for climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, near Parliament House in New Delhi on July 20.

CJP supporters celebrate at Jantar Mantar after Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned over the NEET paper leak controversy, bringing the protest's principal demand to an end. headline: Democracy, not rule by diktat: Anna Hazare after Dharmendra Pradhan quits
full_text:
Democracy, not rule by diktat: Anna Hazare after Dharmendra Pradhan quits
Anna Hazare urged peaceful agitation and dialogue as the Cockroach Janata Party ended its protest after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. He said public grievances should be resolved through democracy and not through violence.
Social activist Anna Hazare on Saturday said peaceful agitation, democracy and dialogue were the only ways to address public grievances, as the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) called off its agitation following the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
He stressed the importance of democracy and dialogue in resolving public grievances, saying, “It is democracy, not rule by diktat, and one should always follow the path of democracy.”
Speaking to reporters in Ahilyanagar, the 89-year-old activist recalled his own history of civil agitation and said lasting systemic change could be achieved through dialogue rather than confrontation.
“Any issue gets resolved through dialogue. Dialogue leads to solutions. Creating tension and going down the wrong path will not solve anything,” Hazare said.
Recalling his 22 hunger strikes, Hazare said he had never resorted to violence and credited peaceful agitation with helping bring about legislative changes.
“I did 22 fasts, never used violence, and because of that, 10 laws were enacted. Creating violence is not right. Whoever the person may be, one should never indulge in violence,” he said.
Hazare also stressed that governments must listen to citizens and prioritise public welfare. He said democratic avenues should always be used to resolve public grievances.
“One has to see what the public is saying. For the public's welfare, even if we have to step forward, there's no harm in it. But public interest must happen. Issues are never resolved by violence but by dialogue among people,” he said.
“Whatever happens through democracy happens. One should always follow the path of democracy,” Hazare added.
His remarks came amid political developments in the national capital following Pradhan's resignation. A CJP delegation held a third round of talks with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh at the Constitution Club of India.
Following the discussions, the CJP formally announced the withdrawal of its 37-day agitation at Jantar Mantar.
“Cockroach Janta Party declares that we withdraw the agitation in good faith, with the understanding that the agreed-upon terms will be executed within the agreed-upon timelines,” CJP Chief Spokesperson Saurav Das said.

Public transport is also set to resume normal operations after days of disruptions. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) said all stations across the network are now open for passenger services, with both entry and exit gates operational....Read More
The reopening of Metro stations comes after several stations in central Delhi remained shut and internet restrictions were imposed during the peak of the protests, which culminated in celebrations at Jantar Mantar on Saturday after news of Pradhan's resignation reached demonstrators.
Later in the evening, Rashtrapati Bhavan announced that Pralhad Joshi, who currently heads the consumer affairs, food and public distribution, and new and renewable energy ministries, had been given additional charge of the education ministry.
Celebrations erupt after resignation
With signal jammers deployed across parts of central Delhi, news of Pradhan's resignation filtered slowly into the protest site on Saturday afternoon. But once the announcement was confirmed, celebrations broke out almost immediately.
After a CJP delegation met Union ministers following the resignation, the movement's founder, 30-year-old Abhijeet Dipke, described the development as a landmark victory.
"This is a big win. It shows that the country is run as per the Constitution. This is just the beginning... I would like to thank Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. Thanks for calling us cockroaches. If he hadn’t said this, I wouldn’t have come to India and this movement wouldn’t have started," Dipke said.
Later, in a brief post on X, he wrote: "Going to take a nap. See you all in a little while."
Music, dancing and emotional scenes
Although the CJP officially announced the end of its protest and some demonstrators began leaving the venue, many others continued arriving to celebrate what they called a hard-earned victory.
Patriotic and popular Hindi songs, including Chak De! India and Rang De Basanti, echoed through loudspeakers as protesters danced, embraced one another and chanted slogans such as "Inquilab Zindabad" and "Bharat Mata ki Jai".
The celebrations spread beyond Jantar Mantar to Connaught Place, Sansad Marg and Tolstoy Marg, where groups of supporters gathered through the evening.
Protest that lasted 36 days
Saturday marked the 36th day of the agitation, which witnessed several dramatic developments over the past month.
The movement saw activist Sonam Wangchuk and at least three students undertake hunger strikes. Wangchuk was later forcibly removed by authorities, while protesters clashed with police during the July 20 march, when lathi-charge and tear gas were used.
More than 100 protesters and over 100 police personnel were injured during the violence. Authorities also suspended internet services in parts of central Delhi and closed several Metro stations amid heightened security.
Pradhan's resignation came after intense activity within the government and multiple rounds of engagement with protest leaders, bringing the month-long agitation to an end and paving the way for normalcy to gradually return across the city.

headline: CHANDIGARH: Twenty-seven years after leading the Army during the 1999
full_text:
CHANDIGARH: Twenty-seven years after leading the Army during the 1999 
Kargil War, former Army chief General VP Malik (retd) said the conflict's hard lessons - from equipment shortages and intelligence gaps to the need for self-reliance - transformed India's military capabilities, enabling the precision strikes on Pakistani airfields during last year's 
Operation Sindoor without crossing the border.
"The biggest operational lessons were the need to strengthen intelligence, surveillance and achieve 'atmanirbharta (self-reliance)' in military hardware," Gen Malik told TOI in an interview ahead of the 27th anniversary of 
Kargil Vijay Diwas. Those lessons, he said, shaped India's military preparedness over the next two decades.
Citing Operation Sindoor, he pointed to the armed forces' growing reliance on short- and long-range drones for surveillance and precision strikes, along with advanced rockets and missiles. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
"We did not have to enter Pakistani territory when we struck airfields and radar stations, causing major havoc," he said, contrasting it with Kargil.
He said indigenous and imported platforms, including BrahMos, Akash and the S-400, were now tested in real-world conditions. Combined with an integrated tri-services command under Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), they have significantly strengthened India's defence capability.
Yet, Gen Malik stressed that technology alone could not win wars. "The man behind the gun is always more important. We must look after them," he said.
Recalling his visits to the frontlines in Jammu & Kashmir, Gen Malik said the soldiers themselves became a source of strength. "...every six days, I would visit... While morale in Delhi was sometimes anxious or uncertain, not a single soldier ever told me the task was difficult. Every visit replenished my own morale."
Reflecting on the reforms that followed the war, Gen Malik said govt constituted Kargil Review Committee, whose key recommendations included creating the CDS position to improve tri-service integration and civil-military coordination. He added that commemorating Vijay Diwas was not only about paying homage to the martyrs but also ensuring the lessons of the conflict continued to guide armed forces.
Gen Malik said the valour displayed remained an inspiration for future generations. While the victory involved strategic planning at the highest level, he insisted the credit belonged to the young officers and soldiers who fought at unforgiving heights. "We must also remember the supporting arms and services. People often forget them but military functions like an orchestra during war. When every arm works in harmony, we achieve victory."
Invoking Bhagavad Gita, he said, "The true test of any plan lies in its execution. As written in the Gita: 'Action is superior to knowledge'."

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday directed officials to take a stern approach to the upkeep of civic amenities and warned that contractors could be blacklisted if work falls short. At a meeting with public representatives in Agra, he expressed displeasure over delays and poor-quality restoration of roads dug up for drinking water pipelines under the Jal Jeevan Mission.
He also reviewed development matters linked to Agra and the Mathura-Vrindavan region, asking officials to closely track court cases affecting the city, prepare plans to promote key industries, improve processes linked to Ayushman payments, and move proposals on transport and tourism infrastructure.
According to a government statement, Adityanath told Jal Nigam officials that merely making a dug-up road motorable was not enough. He said that if the work was found unsatisfactory, the contractors should be blacklisted and FIRs lodged against the officials concerned.
Referring to the recent Supreme Court permission to the Taj Trapezium Zone Authority to process about 400 pending applications for non-polluting MSMEs, he directed the divisional commissioner to monitor court rulings involving Agra so that the city’s development is not held up due to lack of legal advocacy.
Saying Agra has strong potential in leather products and defence manufacturing, the Chief Minister asked for a concrete plan to promote these sectors. He also said street vendors operating on footpaths should not be evicted and should instead be shifted to designated vending zones. He directed the Health Department to verify and speed up the settlement of payments related to Ayushman cards and empanelled hospitals.
Adityanath also chaired a meeting of the Uttar Pradesh Braj Tirth Vikas Parishad in Agra. He called for the early submission of a ropeway project proposal for Vrindavan and asked officials to send proposals for a combined road-rail project on the Mathura-Vrindavan rail route and for a land-pooling scheme to expand parking facilities.
Officials, in turn, presented a proposal for the construction of several key Master Plan roads in the Mathura-Vrindavan area. He also sought a government order on the Tirth-Mitra policy and asked for a proposal for 50 small electric buses.

headline: Assam flood toll rises to 62, PM Modi takes stock; over 7 lakh affected in state
full_text:
Assam flood toll rises to 62, PM Modi takes stock; over 7 lakh affected in state
Assam's flood toll rose to 62, with over 7 lakh people affected, as relief operations continued and waters receded in some areas.
The flood situation in Assam remained grim on Saturday, with the toll from rain-related incidents reaching 62 and the waters affecting 705,000 people across nine districts, according to officials familiar with the matter, even as water levels started to recede in some parts.
According to Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) bulletin on Friday night, 14 people died across nine districts in the last 24 hours.
Also read: Assam flood death toll climbs to 61; 14 more people lost their lives: ASDMA
PM Modi reviews relief efforts with Himanta Sarma
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday sought an update from chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on the relief and rescue operations that continues across the flood-hit districts. “He sought an update on the extent of the devastation, the ongoing relief operations and the challenges we are confronting on the ground. I briefed him on the measures being undertaken by the State Government and our efforts to reach out to every affected family,” Sarma wrote on X.
“Expressing his deep condolences over the loss of lives and property, the Hon’ble Prime Minister assured the people of Assam that this calamity is being accorded the highest priority and the Government of India will extend every possible support to aid our relief, rehabilitation and rebuilding efforts,” Sarma added.
Also read: Assam flood toll rises to 47 as six more die; over 6.53 lakh people affected across 11 districts
Army, IAF continue rescue operations
The Indian Army and the Indian Air Force (IAF) are also assisting the state government in its relief operations.
According to ASDMA, seven people died in Charaideo on Friday while six deaths were reported from Sivasagar and one in Jorhat. Till Thursday, 21 deaths had occurred in Sivasagar alone and with six more, the toll in the district reached 27. ASDMA said that one person is missing.
Also read: Why Assam floods: The obvious answer is Brahmaputra, but there's so much more to it
Rain havoc continues in other states
Meanwhile, two workers died, and four were injured after a landslide hit them while clearing debris from a stretch of road that was brought in by a previous landslip in Sikkim’s Namchi district on Saturday afternoon, police said. Six workers were engaged in clearing the debris that had blocked the road connecting Sada and Phamtam villages when a fresh landslide hit the worksite, burying the workers under debris.
In Gujarat, 35 rain-related deaths have been reported in the past two days, officials said on Saturday, even as the downpour in the state eased. Twenty-nine of these deaths have taken place in Valsad and Navsari, two of the worst affected districts, with over 7,000 people rescued in the last few days, they added.
“A total of 35 rain-related deaths have been reported so far in the state in the last two days as bodies washed away in flood waters were recovered and missing persons were accounted for after the rain stopped and rescue operations concluded,” Relief Commissioner Gaurang Makwana said.
Also read: Army deployed for rescue ops as Gujarat continues to receive heavy rain
Rain continued to lash several parts of Kashmir for the fifth consecutive day on Saturday. However, the officials said the flood threat has eased as the levels in most water bodies were decreasing.
In Maharashtra, the Palghar district administration has stepped up the distribution of financial assistance and relief packages to flood-affected families during the first week of this month, which left 20 people dead, officials said.
Also read: Thane civic body dispatches relief team to flood-hit Dahanu in Palghar
An ex gratia of ₹4 lakh per family was sanctioned for each eligible victim, and financial aid totalling ₹32 lakh has already been disbursed to eight families, it said. The process to release the money to the remaining families is underway, said officials.

headline: The Karnataka government’s proposal to include Kambala, the traditional slush-track buffalo race native to the coastal districts, for the first time in this year’s Mysuru Dasara has sparked a controversy.
full_text:
The Karnataka government’s proposal to include Kambala, the traditional slush-track buffalo race native to the coastal districts, for the first time in this year’s Mysuru Dasara has sparked a controversy.
Those opposed to it have pointed to what they call Kambala’s “incompatibility with the heritage and cultural identity” of Dasara and questioned the need to include a cost- and water-intensive sport when Karnataka is staring at a severe drought. The argument in favour of it has been that Dasara is celebrated as a State festival (Nada Habba) in Mysuru and that the buffalo race, being one of the oldest folk traditions in the State, should be showcased.
Preparations begin
Preparations for the Kambala have, in fact, begun, with the organising committee, headed by Ashok Kumar Rai, Puttur MLA, chalking out a plan to lay a slush track, gallery and other facilities. A plot, measuring around 17 acres, in Sathagalli in Mysuru, has been identified as the venue for the Kambala and is being readied.
Meanwhile, stakeholders — buffalo owners, jockeys, referees, helpers and organisers — at a meeting held in Moodbidri in Dakshina Kannada on July 19, agreed to participate in the Mysuru Kambala, likely to be held on October 18 and October 19, said Belapu Deviprasad Shetty, president of the Karnataka State Kambala Association.
“The Mysuru event will be an opportunity to showcase the culture of Kambala to others who are not familiar with it,” said N. Vijayakumar Kanginamane, general secretary of the association.
Two kinds of Kambala
Experts point out that while ‘Devara Kambalas’ are strictly ritualistic events bound to the land and tradition, other Kambala events held across coastal Karnataka have acquired the character of a competitive sport involving prizes. A majority of the race Kambalas organised in the coastal region are held on artificially built tracks and not on the traditional paddy fields. As many as 27 such race Kambalas are scheduled for the 2026-27 season (November-May) in the coastal region; about 20 Kambalas would be held on the artificial tracks, said Mr. Kanginamane.
Speaking to The Hindu, Muralidhara Rai, a member of the Kambala Organising Committee in Mysuru, said that around 100 buffaloes are expected to participate in the Kambala here, with around 15-20 support staff coming with each buffalo pair.
He argued that traditions like Kambala need to be encouraged on platforms like Dasara, which attracts lakhs of people. “Let Mysuru Dasara introduce Kambala to the global audience, as many foreign tourists come here to witness the celebrations,” he said.
Mr. Rai claimed that the footfall may go up due to the Kambala, thereby increasing tourism revenue. “The expenditure incurred in organising the Kambala would not be much when compared to the revenue the event generates,” he contended. Mr. Rai said the Kambala organised in Bengaluru ïn 2023 attracted nearly 10 lakh people.
Continued opposition
Meanwhile, Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP, several local organisations, green activists, and farmers’ groups have continued to urge the government to withdraw the event.
Organisations opposing the Kambala have formed a Joint Action Committee (JAC) to continue debating and protesting the government’s move. Besides questioning bringing a ‘’region-specific’’ cultural tradition to Mysuru, the JAC has also criticised the government’s priorities at a time when several districts are facing drought-like conditions due to monsoon failure and that it is wasting lakhs of litres of water for a sport amidst water scarcity.
During his recent visit to Mysuru, the Puttur MLA said that the Kambala event is expected to cost between ₹5 crore and ₹8 crore, and that the State government is likely to set aside a special budget for it.
Parashurame Gowda of Parisarakkagi Naavu, Mysuru, a member of the JAC, said that they continue to oppose the Kambala during Dasara celebrations. He also alleged that nearly 36 trees had been illegally felled and a few more have been marked for felling to establish a venue for hosting the Kambala.
“We don’t want an event at the expense of the environment. The Forest Department has already registered an FIR for illegally felling trees. We will continue to oppose the Kambala until it is dropped. A campaign on the lines of the Appiko movement will be held if more trees are chopped,” Mr. Gowda warned, while underlining that it is particularly ironic in a drought year.

headline: Communist Party of India State secretary M. Veerapandian made a strong case for abolishing the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), arguing that it was not only an assault on social justice, but had also created an atmosphere of fear and an...
full_text:
Communist Party of India State secretary M. Veerapandian made a strong case for abolishing the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), arguing that it was not only an assault on social justice, but had also created an atmosphere of fear and anxiety among students aspiring to pursue medical education.
He said education — both school and higher education — was the responsibility of a welfare state and should not be left in the hands of private institutions. “Education is not a privilege or a concession; it is a right. The government must take responsibility for providing education, just as China, a country with a population comparable to India’s, provides education to its citizens,” Mr. Veerapandian said.
As Balan Illam, the CPI headquarters, has emerged as a centre for protests against NEET, Mr. Veerapandian said the party had permitted students to stage demonstrations following requests from the All India Students’ Federation (AISF) and students affiliated with the Cockroach Janta Party. “We also took into account the convenience of our students staying at Balan Illam and neighbours on the road. We were convinced that peaceful demonstrations would not cause any disruption,” he said.
‘Complete exemption’
With reference to the celebration following the resignation of the Union Higher Education Minister, Mr. Veerapandian said that, as far as Tamil Nadu was concerned, the demand was for complete exemption from the examination.
“If other States wish to continue with NEET, we have no objection. The students’ demand for the Minister’s resignation over the alleged question paper leak is also justified. The government should hold talks with them. Suppressing peaceful protests through police action is an assault on democratic values and the Gandhian tradition of peaceful protest,” he said.
Reiterating that NEET was not an appropriate method for admitting students to medical colleges, Mr. Veerapandian recalled the views of the late neurologist B. Ramamurthi, who had argued that medical education did not depend solely on rote learning or examination scores.
Mr. Veerapandian said government-run institutions such as Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital and Stanley Medical College Hospital could match any world-class hospital. He pointed out that these institutions had treated and saved more than one lakh patients during the COVID-19 pandemic.
“We have doctors of exceptional talent and skill who may not have entered medical colleges through NEET. We need a serious debate on the examination. On the one hand, it is an assault on social justice; on the other, it creates an atmosphere of fear and anxiety among students aspiring to study medicine,” he said.
Referring to Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s opposition to NEET, Mr. Veerapandian said the Chief Minister should remain steadfast in his stand. “His recent statement suggests that he is firm in his opposition,” he added.
He also urged the government to earmark designated venues where public protests could be held in the State in future. “Peaceful protests strengthen democracy; they are not directed against governments, The government should facilitate such democratic expression rather than suppress it.” he said.
