Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen in Kolkata. (PTI Photo)
NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Saturday described her return to India after nearly two decades as proof that âinjustice can be long but cannot be permanent.âShe made the remarks at an event in Kolkata, nearly two decades after she was forced to leave the city in 2007. The 63-year-old writer had been living in Kolkata since leaving Bangladesh in 1994 amid alleged death threats from radical groups over her writings and views on religion.Nasreen, who has been living in Europe since leaving Kolkata, also clarified that her return to the city was not linked to any "political agenda.""Today, the opening of this door proves that injustice can be long, but it cannot be permanent. History remembers who closed the doors and who opened them...I am not here to speak for any political party, or against any party. I am here to speak in favour of women's rights," PTI quoted her as saying.She also expressed concern over what she described as a "rise" in religious extremism in Bangladesh."I am against all forms of fundamentalism, but I have spoken against Islamic fundamentalists because I have seen it from close quarters since childhood.
The rise of fundamentalism in Bangladesh is at an alarming stage. Freedom of speech is being curtailed," Nasreen said.Visibly emotional, Nasreen called her return a "fulfilment of a long-awaited moment.""It took me 19 years to say these words: 'I have returned to Kolkata.' I felt the pain of losing an address every single day. On August 8, 1994, the then government forced me to leave Bangladesh. The state may have removed me from my country, but it could never remove my country from within me," she added.Lamenting that she could not find a permanent home in either Bangladesh or West Bengal, Nasreen highlighted that Europe had provided her security but not a sense of belonging."Europe has given me citizenship and a place to live, but unfortunately, I couldn't get a small place to stay in the two Bengals. Europe gave me security, but it could not give me a sense of belonging. A home is not built by security alone; it is built by language, memory and culture," Nasreen remarked.Nasreen maintained that she had never been convicted by any court but had faced restrictions because of opposition from fundamentalist groups."I committed no crime. No court has ever punished me. It is a painful truth of our times that a writer needs police protection to visit the city of her own language."
Rejecting allegations that her writings were offensive, she emphasised that her advocacy had focused on equality and human rights."I only spoke about equal rights for women and men, and about human rights irrespective of religion or caste. I said that any rule or doctrine that takes away equality and human dignity must be changed."She also criticised what she described as the unequal treatment of women in the name of religion and backed a Uniform Civil Code across South Asia, arguing that religion-based personal laws discriminate against women."The real conflict is between secularism and fundamentalism, between the rational mind and irrationality, between innovation and tradition, and between people who value freedom and those who do not."

headline: Operation Sindoor planner Vice Admiral AN Pramod takes over as Navy deputy chief
full_text:
Operation Sindoor planner Vice Admiral AN Pramod takes over as Navy deputy chief
As DGNO, he was closely involved in the planning, preparedness, and operational readiness of the Indian Navy during Operation Sindoor
Vice Admiral AN Pramod, who played a key role in planning Operation Sindoor and led the Indian Navy’s response during the West Asia crisis, on Saturday assumed charge as the Deputy Chief of Naval Staff, the navy said.
He served as the Director General Naval Operations (DGNO) during December 2023-July 2026. “As DGNO, he was closely involved in the planning, preparedness, and operational readiness of the Indian Navy during Operation Sindoor and conduct of maritime security operations during the ongoing West Asia crisis,” the navy said on Saturday.
India launched Operation Sindoor in the early hours of May 7, 2025, striking terror and military installations in Pakistan and PoK following the Pahalgam terror strike that killed 26 people. Pramod was among the top officials who briefed the media after the four-day military clash.
Had the Indian Navy swung into action during Operation Sindoor, Pakistan would have been split into four parts, defence minister Rajnath Singh said after the operation, adding that the navy will draw first blood should Pakistan choose to repeat its misdeeds and direct terror against India.
An alumnus of the 38th Integrated Cadet Course, Naval Academy, Goa, Pramod was commissioned into the Indian Navy in July 1990. A Communication and Electronic Warfare Specialist, he is an alumnus of the Defence Services Staff College, Wellington, and the Naval Higher Command Course at the Naval War College, Goa.
In a distinguished career spanning over 36 years, he has held a wide range of command, operational, instructional, and staff appointments, both afloat and ashore, the navy said. His key afloat appointments include Executive Officer of INS Rajput, a Guided Missile Destroyer, and command of INS Abhay, an Anti-Submarine Warfare Patrol Vessel, INS Shardul, a Landing Ship Tank (Large) and INS Satpura, a Guided Missile Frigate. He also served as the Fleet Operations Officer of the Western Fleet during Operation Snow Leopard following the Galwan clash in eastern Ladakh. He participated in Operation Vijay in 1999 and Operation Parakram in 2001.
Pramod also helped plan Operation Urja Suraksha --- the navy escorted 18 merchant vessels carrying cargo worth over ₹9,000 crore during the West Asia conflict.
Meanwhile, IAF deputy chief Air Marshal AK Bharti, who was DG (Air Operations) last year and closely associated with planning Operation Sindoor, retired on Friday. The IAF struck two terror sites at Markaz Subhanallah in Bahawalpur and Markaz Taiba near Muridke, both in Pakistan’s Punjab province, while the army hit targets at seven places, including Mehmoona Joya in Sialkot, Sawai Nala and Syed Na Bilal in Muzaffarabad, Gulpur and Abbas in Kotli, Barnala in Bhimber, and Sarjal.
On May 9-10, the IAF struck military targets in Rafiqui, Murid, Chaklala, Rahim Yar Khan, Sukkur, Chunian, Pasrur, Sialkot, Skardu, Sargodha, Jacobabad, Bholari and Malir Cantt in Karachi. Pakistan lost as many as 12 to 13 aircraft, including fighter jets such as US-made F-16s and Chinese-origin JF-17s, to the air force’s precision strikes on ground and in the air during the military clash.
Air Marshal Tejpal Singh on Saturday assumed the appointment of Deputy Chief of the Air Staff, succeeding Bharti. Commissioned in June 1990 as a fighter pilot, the Air Marshal has over 3, 500 hours of flying experience. “He is a Cat A Qualified Flying Instructor and an Experimental Test Pilot. The Air Marshal has held key operational, command and staff appointments in the Indian Air Force,” the IAF said.

headline: NEET-PG 2026: Centre expands test city choices, introduces Aadhaar verification
full_text:
NEET-PG 2026: Centre expands test city choices, introduces Aadhaar verification
The Centre has announced changes to NEET-PG 2026, including wider test city options, earlier city allotment and more time per question. The measures add tighter security checks and a single-shift format to make the exam fairer and more convenient.
In a series of changes for the NEET-PG to be held later this year, the Centre will expand the choice of test locations, give candidates more time to plan travel to their examination cities, and give them more time per question in the test.
The reforms are aimed at making the process more convenient for National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for Postgraduate (NEET-PG) candidates, according to the Union health ministry.
"The end-to-end question paper preparation and delivery process has been further reinforced through multiple layers of encryption, secure offline preparation, time-bound finalisation of the question paper shortly before the examination, and controlled digital decryption only at the scheduled commencement of the test," the ministry said in a statement.
The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) has also operationalised a dedicated email address for reporting impersonation, touting and other unfair practices while issuing regular advisories to candidates to promote awareness and vigilance.
The ministry said that to strengthen the integrity of the examination process, Aadhaar-based authentication has been introduced during both the application process and on the examination day. Iris-based biometric verification will be used wherever fingerprint authentication is unsuccessful, it said.
Under the revised system, candidates will indicate three state preferences for their examination centre, with their correspondence state being the mandatory first preference, enabling allotment of centres closer to their place of residence, the ministry said.
Earlier, exam cities were allotted on a first come, first-served basis prompting candidates to rush to submit their applications as soon as the registration window opened, a source explained. Those who delayed often found all nearby centres filled, forcing them to travel to other states to appear for the exam.
In another key change, candidates will be informed of their allotted test city nearly three weeks before the August 30 examination, giving them more time to plan travel and accommodation, the ministry said.
The NBEMS has also rationalised the examination pattern to 180 questions to be answered in 210 minutes, allowing candidates more time per question while retaining the overall duration of the test, it said.
The exam previously had 200 multiple choice questions with a maximum score of 800 marks.
The source said that recently, the exam had been conducted in two shifts due to emergencies or postponements but the 2026 edition will be held in a single shift to ensure uniformity in the difficulty level and assessment of candidates.
Earlier, candidates often faced stress as the final venue and location details were released very close to the test date, leaving minimal time to book travel or accommodation, the official added.
Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda on Saturday reviewed the preparedness for NEET-PG 2026 and directed all agencies to ensure the examination is conducted in a smooth, secure, transparent and technology-enabled manner. He assessed the readiness of NBEMS, technology partners and other stakeholders and stressed that every effort must be made to ensure a fair and candidate-friendly examination.
A total of 2,73,183 candidates have registered for NEET-PG 2026, an increase of over 12.5 per cent compared to last year. The examination will be conducted in a single shift across around 340 cities and more than 1,300 examination centres.
Comprehensive security arrangements have been put in place for the examination, including advance sealing and verification of examination centres, CCTV surveillance, biometric authentication, candidate frisking, deployment of signal jammers, dynamic comput, live monitoring through central and regional command centres, and real-time supervision by independent observers and appraisers.
More than 60,000 examination functionaries will be deployed to ensure the smooth conduct of the examination, the ministry said.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: Average rainfall in India during the second half of monsoon season (Aug-Sept) is most likely to be âbelow normalâ, IMD said Friday, flagging the continuing risk of El NiÃ±o, which is associated with a weak monsoon.Last month, IMD had cited El NiÃ±oâs impact to forecast below normal rains in July. The monthâs rainfall turned out to be normal due to plentiful showers in central India. The met department attributed this to âintra-seasonal variabilityâ, saying a record 24 days were under the influence of âlow pressure systemsâ (LPS) in July against normal of about 13.5 days.
âFour LPS were formed over Bay of Bengal that led to good rainfall from Odisha to Gujarat. We need to further analyse the reason (for better-than-expected July rains). These LPS couldnât be captured by our long-range forecast model,â said Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, IMD chief.
July rain gives hope to farm sectorTwo long wet spells, one during the first week of July and the second from July 22 onwards, helped reduce the overall monsoon rainfall deficit in the country from 35% in June to nearly 13% at the end of July. Since the âmonsoon core zoneâ, where farming operations remain mainly rain-fed, largely coincides with central India, good rains in the region could aid recovery of acreage in the month.
Though overall acreage of the summer sown crops continues to be in deficit compared to the corresponding period last year, the deficit reduced from nearly 21% on July 3 to around 3% on July 31, giving hope to the farm sector in an El Nino year.During Aug-Sept, IMD said certain parts of peninsular India, central India, northern parts of northwest India, and east and northeast India may get ânormal to above-normalâ rains, but it may not change the forecast of overall âbelow normalâ quantitative rainfall in the country.

Uttarakhand CM approves ₹227 crore for Haridwar Kumbh works, road upgrade and police infrastructure
Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami has approved ₹227 crore for infrastructure projects, including Kumbh Mela preparations with ₹98.18 crore for ghats.
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has approved financial sanctions worth about ₹227 crore for infrastructure development projects, Kumbh Mela works, road widening, police facilities and welfare measures for ex-servicemen families in the state, according to an official government statement.
The largest component of the approval relates to preparations for Kumbh Mela 2027 in Haridwar. The government has sanctioned ₹98.18 crore for construction of ghats and an Astha Path on the left bank of the Ganga in the Gaurishankar area downstream of Chandi Ghat. Another ₹115.91 crore has been approved for similar works on the right bank in the Bairagi Camp area, the statement said.
Road and police infrastructure
The Chief Minister also approved a ₹11.95 crore project for utility shifting and relocation of water supply lines linked to the widening of the 1.65-km New Cantt Road stretch in Dehradun from two lanes to three lanes.
In Haridwar district, the government sanctioned the first instalment of ₹96.59 lakh against a total approved cost of ₹2.41 crore for construction of the administrative building of Sultanpur police outpost.
Scholarship and pension relief approvals
Dhami has approved ₹36.84 lakh from the Kargil Shaheed Parivar Chief Minister Assistance Fund for scholarships to dependent students of ex-servicemen pursuing engineering, medical and PhD courses.
The Chief Minister has also approved an increase in dearness relief for civil and family pensioners of public bodies and undertakings to 60% per month with effect from January 1, 2026, the official statement said.
The government said the sanctions are aimed at strengthening public infrastructure, improving connectivity, supporting Kumbh-related facilities and extending welfare support to ex-servicemen families and pensioners.

headline: UP man plots wife's murder, stages it as accident for Rs 44 lakh insurance
full_text:
UP man plots wife's murder, stages it as accident for Rs 44 lakh insurance
A woman found dead by a roadside in Uttar Pradesh's Hamirpur appeared to be the victim of a road accident. But within 48 hours, the case took a chilling turn. Police say a bank slip, technical surveillance and inconsistencies in the accident theory led them to an alleged murder plot involving her husband, an insurance policy worth Rs 44 lakh and three accomplices.
A woman found dead by a roadside in Uttar Pradesh's Hamirpur initially appeared to have been the victim of a road accident. Forty-eight hours later, police said they had uncovered an alleged murder-for-insurance plot orchestrated by her husband to claim Rs 44 lakh.
Police arrested Reeta's husband, Amar Singh, and three of his associates, alleging that they killed the 32-year-old and tried to pass off her death as an accident.
Hamirpur Additional SP Arvind Kumar said Amar and his associates allegedly killed Reeta to claim the insurance payout and use the money to settle their financial liabilities.
VICTIM'S BODY FOUND BY THE ROADSIDE
The case began on the night of July 29, when farmers returning after guarding their fields spotted a woman's body by the roadside in Hamirpur district.
Police reached the spot, collected evidence and sent the body for a post-mortem examination. At first, the circumstances suggested that she may have been killed in a road accident.
But police did not immediately know who she was.
A bank account slip recovered during the investigation provided the first major lead, helping police identify the woman as 32-year-old Reeta.
Following a complaint by her father, Sarvesh Kumar Gupta, police registered a murder case and began investigating how she had ended up dead by the roadside.
HUSBAND REPORTS HER MISSING, THEN IDENTIFIES BODY
Even as police were trying to establish what had happened to Reeta, her husband had approached Sumerpur police station to report her missing.
Later, when news emerged that an unidentified woman's body had been recovered, Amar also turned up to identify it.
Police now allege that both actions were part of an attempt to distance himself from his wife's death and create the impression that he knew nothing about what had happened to her.
That version, however, began to unravel as investigators examined evidence from the scene and turned to technical surveillance.
Within 48 hours, police said what initially appeared to be an accidental death had emerged as an alleged premeditated murder.
LOVE MARRIAGE AND INSURANCE POLICY
As investigators dug deeper, attention turned to Reeta's marriage and the couple's financial circumstances.
Reeta had married Amar around two-and-a-half years ago. According to her family, it was her second marriage, while Amar had reportedly been married twice earlier.
After her first husband died, Reeta began working in Kanpur, where she met Amar. The two fell in love and later married.
Investigators allege that financial troubles eventually became central to a conspiracy to kill her.
According to police, questioning of the accused revealed that they owed a substantial amount of money to Pushpendra Soni alias Sahil.
Police alleged that an insurance policy was then taken out on Reeta and a plan was drawn up to kill her, make her death appear accidental and claim Rs 44 lakh in insurance money.
Investigators claimed the accused had even decided how the payout would be divided. Amar was allegedly to receive Rs 15 lakh, while the remaining amount would be shared among the others.
HOW THE 'ACCIDENT' WAS ALLEGEDLY STAGED
Police said Amar took Reeta to an arterial road near Paudhiya as part of the alleged plan, where his associates were waiting in a car.
Investigators allege that the car was first used to hit Reeta, causing her to fall into a roadside ditch.
The accused then allegedly pulled her out, placed her on the road and drove the car over her again, killing her.
They then fled, leaving the body at the scene in an attempt to make the killing appear to be a road accident, police said.
Amar subsequently reported his wife missing and later identified her body, actions that investigators allege were intended to deflect suspicion.
48 HOURS LATER, PLOT UNRAVELS
The investigation eventually turned towards Amar and the other accused.
Police said evidence collected from the scene, technical analysis, surveillance data and questioning of the accused exposed inconsistencies in the accident theory and helped them reconstruct the alleged conspiracy.
Police arrested Amar and three others identified as Amit Gupta alias Ram, Pushpendra Soni alias Sahil and Abhay Singh alias Golu.
The car allegedly used in the killing and an Airtel SIM card were also recovered, police said. All four accused have been produced before a court, and further legal proceedings are underway.

headline: ‘Liberty not reliant on order’s brevity’: Supreme Court in Haldwani riots case
full_text:
‘Liberty not reliant on order’s brevity’: Supreme Court in Haldwani riots case
The Supreme Court refused to interfere with Uttarakhand high court’s decision to release Abdul Malik, the alleged mastermind of February 2024 Haldwani riots.
An individual’s liberty cannot hinge on the “inadequacy” or brevity of a court’s reasoning while granting bail, the Supreme Court underscored on Friday, as it refused to interfere with the Uttarakhand high court’s decision releasing Abdul Malik, the alleged mastermind of the February 2024 Haldwani riots.
A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana dismissed the Uttarakhand government’s special leave petition challenging the April 16 order of the Uttarakhand high court granting bail to Malik, observing that the top court would ordinarily be reluctant to interfere with a bail order unless it glaringly reflected non-application of mind.
Also read: Delhi riots: Tahir Hussain, 4 others get life terms in IB staffer's murder case
“Liberty does not depend on inadequacy of a court order. It depends on the prosecution’s case,” remarked the bench, adding that “not every bail order requires long and lengthy orders” so long as there is some application of mind and the order is not passed mechanically.
The state government had assailed the high court’s order primarily on the ground that it was a cryptic, non-speaking order granting bail to the principal accused in one of Uttarakhand’s most serious incidents of communal violence.
Senior additional advocate general Gaurav Bhatia, appearing for the state, argued that the law now required reasoned bail orders and that granting bail “in such a cursory manner without any justification” would have serious repercussions. He submitted that Malik’s house had been used to hatch the conspiracy behind the violence and that the accused could not be enlarged on bail merely because a co-accused had secured similar relief.
Also read: PM Modi forgives students amid abusive video row: 'Let's guide the misguided'
The Supreme Court, however, declined to accept the submission, observing that while a bail order must indicate application of mind, it need not contain elaborate reasoning in every case. “We are dealing with a matter where bail has been granted and not otherwise…Bail is bail, why should we ordinarily interfere?” the bench observed.
The bench also reminded the state that allegations regarding the conspiracy would have to be established during trial. “That you need to prove through evidence during the trial,” it told Bhatia, noting that Malik had already spent more than two years in custody.
When Bhatia argued that the grant of bail had demoralised the police because the accused was allegedly responsible for burning down a police station, the bench responded that the state ought to have expedited the trial instead.
Also read: 1 dead, another injured in terror attack in J&K's Kulgam
“If you think demoralisation of police is the reason you are here, you should have secured his conviction in the last two years,” retorted the bench. It noted that only one prosecution witness had been examined so far and questioned why the state expected the Supreme Court to curtail an individual’s liberty despite the slow pace of the trial.
“You have examined just one witness so far and you expect us to interfere with the liberty of a person?” asked the bench, adding that if the trial court was not proceeding expeditiously, the prosecution ought to have approached the apex court for appropriate directions.
The hearing also saw the bench question the invocation of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). “How is UAPA attracted? Someone throwing a bomb will attract UAPA? Why was it invoked?... If a mob goes and burns down a police station, can it invoke UAPA?” it asked.
When Bhatia contended that disturbance of public order attracted UAPA, the court drew a distinction between offences affecting public order and terrorist acts under the special law. “That would attract NSA and other laws, but how UAPA? Public order and UAPA are different,” said the court before dismissing the state’s petition.
The case originates from the large-scale violence that erupted in Banbhoolpura, Haldwani, on February 8, 2024, during an anti-encroachment drive to demolish an allegedly illegal madrasa and clear encroachments. According to the prosecution, a violent mob attacked officials carrying out the demolition, resorting to stone-pelting, arson, firing and petrol bombs, besides torching a police station and police vehicles. Five people were killed and nearly 100 others injured in the clashes, after which curfew was imposed in the area.
The police have alleged that Malik was the principal conspirator behind the violence, claiming he had constructed the disputed structure and incited resistance against the demolition drive. He was arrested in New Delhi on February 24, 2024, after a manhunt. Three FIRs were registered under provisions of the UAPA, the Indian Penal Code, the Arms Act and the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act.
The high court, in its April 16 order, had noted that Malik claimed he was not present in Uttarakhand on the day of the violence and was instead in Noida and Delhi. It also recorded the defence submission that there was no direct evidence of the alleged conspiracy, that the charge sheet had already been filed, and that the possibility of tampering with evidence was minimal.
Significantly, the state had fairly conceded before the high court that, according to the investigation, Malik was not present at the spot during the violence, although it maintained that he and his son Abdul Moied were the main conspirators. The high court also took note of the fact that Moied had already been granted bail by a coordinate bench before concluding that Malik too was entitled to be released on bail at that stage.

headline: Encroachments, mostly houses and petty shops, were demolished by civic officials on Anna Salai in Gudiyatham town on Saturday to provide easy access to Government Taluk Hospital located on the stretch.
full_text:
Encroachments, mostly houses and petty shops, were demolished by civic officials on Anna Salai in Gudiyatham town on Saturday to provide easy access to Government Taluk Hospital located on the stretch.
Officials of Gudiyatham municipality, which executed the work, said that most of the 120 encroachments on the stretch were built more than a decade ago. These structures are mostly extensions of existing shops and commercial establishments that resulted in reduced road space. “Such extension of buildings has affected traffic movement, especially ambulances, on the stretch. The drive was aimed at the safety of road users and to provide more road space for vehicles,” S. Dhanalakshmi, commissioner, Gudiyatham municipality, told The Hindu.
Municipal officials said that the drive was based on an order issued by the Madras High Court on a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) to restore the original width of the stretch by demolishing illegal structures on it.
Notices were served to those who occupied the stretch as per the court order. Affected families were also identified to provide them with alternate land of three cents. “Ambulances struggle to navigate the narrow space on the stretch due to encroachments. Pedestrians, including senior citizens and patients, have to risk themselves by using the stretch,” said T. Sudar, a resident.
Officials said that the demolition drive was also meant to restore the water channel on the route as most of the encroachments were built on it. The encroachments, mostly concrete structures, blocked free flow of excess rainwater during monsoon. It resulted in waterlogging in town.
The water channel helps discharge excess rainwater from storm water drains in town to Palar River. The stretch is two km, connecting key areas like Pernambut, Ambur, Pallikonda, and Katpadi with Chittoor in Andhra Pradesh. headline: Govt clears floating solar capacity boost, PM-Kisan extension
full_text:
Govt clears floating solar capacity boost, PM-Kisan extension
NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Friday approved a series of measures aimed at strengthening farmer welfare, expanding sports infrastructure and accelerating India’s clean energy transition
NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Friday approved a series of measures aimed at strengthening farmer welfare, expanding sports infrastructure and accelerating India’s clean energy transition.
The decisions include extending the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme until FY31 with an outlay of ₹3.15 lakh crore, clearing the ₹5,070-crore Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY) to develop 5,000 MW of floating solar capacity backed by battery storage, among others.
The government said the measures are expected to boost renewable energy generation, support domestic manufacturing, create jobs and ensure continued financial assistance to millions of farmer families.
Under PM-SSY, the government plans to install 5,000 MW of floating solar capacity between 2026-27 and 2030-31. Each project will be required to include a minimum energy storage capacity of two hours (10,000 MWh). Financial support under the scheme will continue until 2032-33, officials aware of the matter said.
They said the Centre will provide Central Financial Assistance (CFA) of ₹1 crore per MW for eligible solar photovoltaic projects after commissioning.
“In addition, a CFA of up to ₹50 lakh per project will also be available for undertaking feasibility studies, including bathymetry and hydrography assessments, environmental studies, and other preparatory activities required for de-risking the project development,” an official requesting anonymity said.
The approval follows an assessment by the National Institute of Solar Energy, which estimated a floating solar potential of around 102.18 GWp across reservoirs and other suitable inland water bodies in India. At present, the country has just over 700 MW of installed floating solar capacity.
“The CFA is primarily being provided as the installation process here involves the use of anchors, floaters and moorings. The subsidy covers that cost, so it makes it competitive and on par with ground-mounted solar projects,” said an official familiar with the scheme.
Officials said the programme is expected to reduce around 10 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually and generate about 16,000-17,000 full-time equivalent jobs.
In a separate decision, the Cabinet approved ₹3.15 lakh crore for the continuation of PM-KISAN from 2026-27 to 2030-31. Under the scheme, eligible landholding farmer families receive ₹6,000 annually in three equal instalments directly into their bank accounts.
According to the government, more than ₹4.47 lakh crore has been transferred to farmers through 23 instalments since the scheme’s launch in 2019. The latest instalment benefited more than 9.49 crore farmers, with over ₹18,984 crore released.
The Centre said an evaluation by NITI Aayog found that more than 92% of surveyed beneficiaries used the assistance for agricultural activities and farm investments, while around 85% reported higher farm income and reduced dependence on informal credit.

headline: The Union government has approved the advance release of its share of the State Disaster Response Fund of ₹2,117.85 crore to support seven flood-affected States during the ongoing monsoon season, an official statement said on Saturday (August 1, 2026...
full_text:
The Union government has approved the advance release of its share of the State Disaster Response Fund of ₹2,117.85 crore to support seven flood-affected States during the ongoing monsoon season, an official statement said on Saturday (August 1, 2026).
Of the affected States, Himachal Pradesh, Odisha, and Nagaland have already received the first instalment of the Central share for the financial year 2026-27.
“To ensure timely availability of funds for relief operations, Union Home Minister Amit Shah has approved the advance release of the second instalment of the Central share of SDRF to Himachal Pradesh and Odisha,” the statement said.
Himachal Pradesh has been sanctioned ₹193.95 crore and Odisha is to get ₹500 crore as their second instalments.
The advance release of first instalments has been approved for Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Gujarat, and Maharashtra by relaxing documentary requirements under applicable guidelines, considering the urgent need for resources for relief measures, the statement said.
The assistance approved for Arunachal Pradesh amounts to ₹44.55 crore, for Assam ₹379.35 crore, for Gujarat ₹500 crore, and for Maharashtra ₹500 crore.
“With this approval, a total of ₹2,117.85 crore has been made available to the flood-affected States to strengthen their ongoing relief and response measures,” the statement said.
Inter-Ministerial Central Teams (IMCT) have already been deputed to Arunachal Pradesh and Assam to assess damages. Two IMCT visits have been undertaken in Assam in view of the severity of the flood situation there, it said, adding, “On request of the Government of Nagaland, an IMCT is being constituted for the state.” The statement further said the Centre has been continuously monitoring the flood situation in close coordination with the State governments since the onset of the monsoon.
“Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the government remains committed to extending all necessary assistance to states for effective relief, rescue and rehabilitation measures and will continue to monitor the situation closely,” it added.

headline: ‘Congress betrayed us’: DMK says part of Opposition but not of INDIA bloc
full_text:
‘Congress betrayed us’: DMK says part of Opposition but not of INDIA bloc
DMK's Dayanidhi Maran has told HT that the party remains a part of the Opposition, but is not part of the INDIA bloc.
Dispelling speculation on the DMK ‘s strategy for the monsoon session of Parliament, party MP and former Union minister Dayanidhi Maran has told HT that the party remains a part of the Opposition and would join efforts to oppose the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) amendment bill expected to be taken up for debate next week.
The statement comes amid the Opposition’s efforts to form a joint strategy. A section of the Opposition is in touch with former Tamil Nadu chief minister and DMK leader MK Stalin. Opposition leaders told HT that next week, they will demand that Union home minister Amit Shah come to the House. It will also organise protests against the alleged theft of donations for the Ram Mandir outside Parliament.
DMK's big clarification on INDIA bloc membership
DMK leaders, however, have stopped attending the Opposition’s meeting held every morning at Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge’s office as the party snapped ties with the largest Opposition party.
“We are with the Opposition. But we are neither with the Congress nor a part of the INDIA bloc because the Congress betrayed us. But we have been opposing this government on various issues. We have always opposed the NEET and we want it to be abolished. We opposed the exam paper leak bill. Our role and objectives as the Opposition are solely guided by the interests of Tamil Nadu.”
Hitting out at the BJP, Maran said, “The BJP is trying to divert attention of the people from the real issues by bringing bills such as the one to protect Vande Mataram. Look at the situation in West Asia and India is facing a huge pressure on oil prices. The economic situation of the country remains volatile. But Congress is not trying to raise these real issues. They are helping the BJP.”
‘FCRA bill aims to browbeat minorities’
The DMK lawmaker said the party will oppose the FCRA amendment bill. “This FCRA bill is a classic attempt of the BJP to browbeat the minorities. DMK will oppose the bill.”
A section of the Opposition, led by the Trinamool Congress, has kept the communication channel open with the DMK. TMC’s Rajya Sabha floor leader Derek O’Brien said, “We are in regular contact with the DMK and AAP (the two parties outside the INDIA bloc). They are a key part of the Opposition. Our floor strategy is based on the coordination we have with all such parties.”
O’Brien said that the Opposition has decided that on Monday and Tuesday, they will demand Shah’s presence in the House. “All Opposition parties have decided that on Monday and Tuesday, we will demand that home minister Amit Shah’s comes to the House. He must face the Opposition. The protests over the Ram Mandir donation theft are equally important and we will raise it outside the House during those two days.
When asked about the FCRA bill, O’Brien said, there can’t be any debate on the FCRA amendment bill unless the home minister comes in Parliament. We know the BJP playbook: Introduce draconian bills like FCRA. Then bulldoze in Parliament with no debate. When Parliament doesn’t function, who benefits? The government. But the government is accountable to Parliament and Parliament is accountable to people. When Parliament doesn’t run, government is accountable to no one.”
The controversial amendments in the FCRA law include creation of a designated body to manage assets of an organization, if it ceases to have an FCRA certificate. The body can use the assets for public purposes or transfer such assets to ministries, departments, authorities or agencies of the central or state government. In other words, assets created by foreign funds cannot remain in the permanent custody of the organization.

headline: Bhiwani boxers Preeti Pawar, Jasmine Lamboria win CWG golds
full_text:
Bhiwani boxers Preeti Pawar, Jasmine Lamboria win CWG golds
Lamboria comes from a rich boxing legacy. Her great-grandfather, Captain Hawa Singh, was one of India’s most celebrated boxers
Haryana’s Bhiwani boxing legacy shone once again on the global stage on Saturday as Preeti Pawar clinched the gold medal in the women’s 54kg event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Moments later, fellow Bhiwani boxer Jasmine Lamboria added to India’s golden haul by winning the women’s 57kg title.
HT spoke to Somvir Singh, an assistant sub-inspector (ASI) with the Haryana Police and Pawar’s father, who said her victory is not just a victory for their family, but also a moment of pride for the entire nation.
“She developed an interest in boxing when she was in Class 8. Since then, she has never looked back,” he told HT.
“Her uncle, who is also her coach, trained and guided her throughout the journey. The family’s unwavering support also played a crucial role in helping her reach this stage. She has worked incredibly hard for this achievement, and I believe this is only the beginning. Many more victories lie ahead,” he said.
Singh said missing out on Olympics because of her illness remained one of her biggest regrets.
“It was a regret she carried with her for a long time after missing out on the Olympics due to illness. We always reassured her that her moment would come eventually, and all her hard work will pay off one day. That moment arrived at the Commonwealth Games. She has now achieved the first milestone by winning the gold medal, and I am confident she will add another gold at the Asian Games,” he said.
Meanwhile, Lamboria comes from a rich boxing legacy. Her great-grandfather, Captain Hawa Singh, was one of India’s most celebrated boxers, while her uncles, Sandeep Singh and Parvinder Singh, are former National Champions and international-level boxers who have played a key role in shaping her career.
HT also spoke to Sandeep Singh, one of Lamboria’s coaches, who recalled her early days in the sport. He said she began boxing in 2016 and, from the very first day, he recognised her natural talent and believed she had the potential to win major titles for the country.
Singh added that Lamboria had the advantage of growing up in a family deeply rooted in boxing, which ensured she received the right guidance from the very beginning.
“She has worked extremely hard. When you carry forward a family legacy, there is pressure, but there is also immense support and motivation. That support helped her keep improving and reach this level,” he said.

NEW DELHI: The Centre has announced a series of changes for the NEET-PG exam to be held later in the month, including expanding the choice of test locations, giving candidates more time to plan travel, and increasing the time available per question.The reforms are aimed at making the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test for Postgraduate (NEET-PG) process more convenient and secure, according to the Union health ministry.Under the revised system, candidates will have to provide preferences for three states for their examination centre. Their correspondence state will be the mandatory first preference, allowing allotment of centres closer to their place of residence.Earlier, examination centres were allotted on a first-come, first-served basis, prompting candidates to submit applications immediately after registrations opened. Those who delayed often found nearby centres unavailable and had to travel to other states.Candidates will now be informed of their allotted test city nearly three weeks before the August 30 examination, giving them more time to arrange travel and accommodation.
The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) has also revised the exam pattern, reducing the number of questions from 200 to 180 while keeping the total duration unchanged at 210 minutes. The move will provide candidates with more time per question.The exam was earlier conducted with 200 multiple-choice questions carrying a maximum of 800 marks.The ministry said the question paper preparation and delivery process has been strengthened through multiple layers of encryption, secure offline preparation, time-bound finalisation of papers shortly before the examination, and controlled digital decryption at the start of the test.To further strengthen security, Aadhaar-based authentication has been introduced during registration and on the examination day. Iris-based biometric verification will be used where fingerprint authentication fails.NBEMS has also introduced a dedicated email address for reporting impersonation, touting and other unfair practices, while issuing advisories to candidates to improve awareness and vigilance.NEET-PG 2026 will be conducted in a single shift to ensure uniformity in difficulty level and assessment. In recent years, the exam was conducted in multiple shifts due to emergencies or postponements.Union health minister JP Nadda on Saturday reviewed preparations for the examination and directed agencies to ensure a smooth, secure, transparent and technology-enabled process. He assessed the readiness of NBEMS, technology partners and other stakeholders, and stressed the need for a fair and candidate-friendly examination.
A total of 2,73,183 candidates have registered for the medical entrance test, an increase of over 12.5% from last year. The exam will be held in a single shift across around 340 cities and more than 1,300 centres.Security measures include advance sealing and verification of centres, CCTV surveillance, biometric authentication, candidate frisking, deployment of signal jammers, live monitoring through central and regional command centres, and supervision by independent observers and appraisers.More than 60,000 examination functionaries will be deployed for the smooth conduct of the examination, the ministry said.(With PTI inputs)

headline: I am back: Taslima Nasrin renews free speech call in first public appearance
full_text:
I am back: Taslima Nasrin renews free speech call in first public appearance
Taslima Nasrin returned to Kolkata for her first public address in the city since 2007. She used the occasion to defend free speech, secularism and equal rights while reflecting on exile.
Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasrin returned to Kolkata after a gap of 19 years on Friday, describing the moment as the recovery of "a chapter of my lost life" while delivering a forceful defence of free speech, secularism, women's rights and the right to criticise religious ideologies.
The event, attended by West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, marked Nasrin's first public address in Kolkata since leaving the city in 2007. During her speech, she thanked Adhikari and the West Bengal government for ensuring her security, while stressing that her gratitude should not be mistaken for political allegiance.
Speaking at a public event in Kolkata, Nasrin reflected on decades of exile from both Bangladesh and West Bengal, saying her return was more than a personal milestone. She called it a reminder that "closed doors do not remain closed forever" and said the day represented a victory of free thought over fear and censorship.
"I have not just returned to a city. I have returned to a chapter of my lost life," she said, adding that she was overwhelmed by the welcome she received after nearly two decades away from Kolkata.
Nasrin thanked Secular Mission chairman Osman Gani Mallick for inviting her to the city and expressed gratitude to Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari for facilitating her return and ensuring her security.
"I have not come here to speak for any political party. I have come to speak for equal rights of women, human rights, secularism, rationality, free thought and freedom of speech," she said.
RECALLING YEARS OF EXILE
The author recounted how she was forced to leave Bangladesh on August 8, 1994, after facing threats over her writings, and later had to leave Kolkata in 2007 despite not being convicted of any crime.
Describing exile as both a personal and political experience, she said the state had failed to protect writers from extremist threats.
"The state removed me from the country, but it could not remove the country from within me," she said, describing the Bengali language as her "portable homeland."
Nasrin recalled discovering Kolkata through literature, radio broadcasts and correspondence long before she first visited the city. She said poetry and literature had connected the two Bengals even when political borders divided them.
She also spoke about finding a home in Kolkata during her years in exile before being forced to leave in 2007 following threats from fundamentalist groups.
'FREEDOM OF SPEECH BELONGS TO EVERYONE'
A major part of Nasrin's address focused on freedom of expression and the dangers of governments yielding to threats from extremist groups.
She argued that exiling writers does not create lasting peace but instead strengthens those who seek to silence dissent.
"In a civilised society, the answer to one argument is another argument, the answer to a book is another book," she said, urging people to challenge ideas through debate rather than violence or censorship.
Nasrin said freedom of speech must extend even to unpopular opinions, arguing that the strength of a democracy is reflected in how safely dissenting voices can express themselves.
She also expressed hope that writers would one day no longer require police protection simply to attend events or publish their work.
CRITICISM OF RELIGIOUS FUNDAMENTALISM
Nasrin reiterated her long-held criticism of religious fundamentalism, saying she opposed all forms of extremism but had spoken most extensively about Islamic fundamentalism because it was the ideology she had experienced firsthand.
She rejected the suggestion that criticism of Islam amounted to hatred of Muslims, arguing that people deserve protection while ideologies should remain open to scrutiny.
According to Nasrin, reform within Muslim societies requires open discussion on issues including women's rights, freedom of belief and equal citizenship.
She also criticised governments that, in her view, prioritise religious pressure over constitutional rights and warned that compromising with threats only emboldens extremists.
CALLS FOR EQUALITY AND SECULARISM
The author devoted a significant portion of her speech to advocating equal rights for women and a secular state.
She argued that no religious law should deny women equality and called for legal systems to be guided by constitutional values rather than religious identity.
Nasrin also supported the idea of a common civil code based on human rights and gender equality rather than the principles of any particular religion.
She maintained that true secularism requires separating religion from state institutions, politics and education while ensuring equal rights for believers and non-believers alike.
HOPE DESPITE EXILE
Despite recalling decades of persecution, threats and displacement, Nasrin said she remained optimistic about the future.
She expressed hope that Bangladesh would one day separate religion from the state, guarantee equal rights for women and minorities, and allow writers and free thinkers to express themselves without fear.
Concluding her address, Nasrin became emotional as she reflected on returning to Kolkata after nearly two decades.
"No one can give me back those 19 years," she said. "But today's opening of the door proves that injustice can last a long time, but it is not eternal."
Calling her return a victory for freedom of speech, free thought and the affection of ordinary people, she ended with a message of gratitude to the city she once considered home.
"Today, you did not just bring me back to Kolkata," she said. "You brought me back to my lost life."

headline: Dehradun teacher dowry death: Husband, sister-in-law arrested amid outrage
full_text:
Dehradun teacher dowry death: Husband, sister-in-law arrested amid outrage
Police arrested government school teacher's husband and sister-in-law after a video allegedly detailing dowry harassment surfaced before her death in Dehradun.
Dehradun: The husband and sister-in-law of a government school teacher who was found dead under suspicious circumstances at her matrimonial home in Dehradun were arrested on Saturday in connection with her alleged dowry death, police said.
"On the basis of evidence, police arrested state secretariat official Saurabh Khatri, 36, and his sister, Surbhi Khatri alias Charu, 37, on Saturday," said Dehradun Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Pramendra Dobhal.
Police said the accused were arrested from their residence in Laxman Enclave in Harrawala, in Doiwala block of Dehradun.
The SSP said the incident triggered widespread outrage and drew national attention.
"During the investigation, police recorded the statements of the complainant and other witnesses. We also obtained a video that the deceased had sent to her mother before her death, in which she stated that she had been facing continuous harassment by her in-laws since her marriage," the SSP said.
"Our investigation into the matter is underway. Strict action will be taken against all culprits," he said.
Dobhal said they will request the court to ensure a speedy trial in the case.
The arrests came four days after the woman was found hanging under suspicious circumstances at her matrimonial home in Harrawala, Doiwala, on July 29.
Before her death, she recorded a video message addressed to her mother. In the video, she is heard saying through tears, "Sorry, Mummy, I am leaving like this... everything has become strange... I have been enduring this for the last six months... I cannot bear it anymore... their mindset will never change... they keep calling me cursed."
A first information report (FIR) in this regard was registered against the deceased's husband, mother-in-law Praveena Devi, and sister-in-law at Doiwala police station on July 29 under Section 80(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) on a complaint filed by the victim's mother, a native of Shrikot in Pauri Garhwal.
In her complaint, the deceased's mother alleged that her daughter had married Saurabh Khatri in November 2025 and was subjected to continuous mental and physical harassment by her husband, mother-in-law Praveena Devi, and sister-in-law Charu over dowry demands. She alleged that the three were responsible for her daughter's death.
Following the registration of the FIR, SSP Dobhal formed a special investigation team under Doiwala Circle Officer Vandana Verma and directed the immediate arrest of the accused.
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA from Devprayag, Vinod Kandari, on Friday urged Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami to order a high-level probe into the case.
Meanwhile, Uttarakhand State Commission for Women chairperson Kusum Kandwal has taken cognisance of the alleged harassment and the suspicious death of the newly married government school teacher, saying every effort would be made to ensure justice and that those found guilty would not be spared.
Kandwal spoke to SSP Pramendra Dobhal and Doiwala Circle Officer Vandana Verma over the phone and directed the police to conduct a fair and thorough investigation into every aspect of the case.
She said videos circulating on social media and other available evidence prima facie indicate that the victim was subjected to severe mental and physical harassment, and said that stringent legal action should be taken against all those responsible.
Kandwal also spoke to the victim's family and assured them that the commission stands with them in their fight for justice.
She said the commission would closely monitor the investigation and seek periodic progress reports from the police.
Kandwal asked women across the state not to remain silent if they face domestic violence or any form of harassment. "Enduring injustice is also a crime. Come forward and lodge a complaint without fear. The commission stands with every woman, and ensuring strict action against the guilty remains our priority," she said.

headline: Four killed in landslides as heavy rain triggers floods across Kerala
full_text:
Four killed in landslides as heavy rain triggers floods across Kerala
Idukki/Kottayam , Four people were killed while several others were rescued following separate landslides in Idukki and Kottayam districts on Saturday, as incessant heavy rain triggered floods and fresh landslides across Kerala, officials said.
The deceased was identified as Sumathi , a resident of the Adoormala area near Kudayathoor in Idukki district. Debris from a landslide struck her house in the early hours of Saturday, the district administration said.
Neighbours managed to rescue her husband, Ravi, and the couple's son, Ratheesh.
Both sustained injuries and were admitted to a hospital in Thodupuzha.
Authorities said the family's house was destroyed in the landslide.
Sumathi's body was recovered after a search operation carried out by personnel of the National Disaster Response Force , Fire and Rescue Services, police and revenue officials.
A youth died, and his mother was buried under debris in a landslide at Payyanithottam in Poonjar in Kottayam district.
The deceased is identified as Josephine , son of Johny, and his mother Rejina Johny , who were trapped under debris, officials said.
Even though Josephine was rescued, he succumbed to injuries while being shifted to the hospital.
The body of Rejina was recovered by around 10.30 am.
In another incident, a person identified as Prabhakaran Nair died after a landslide hit a house in the Vagamon area of Idukki district.
Officials said that Nair, a native of Vaikom in Kottayam, was sleeping in one of the bedrooms of his relative's house when the landslide took place.
Following an hours-long search, his body could be recovered, officials said.
Landslides and flooding were reported in various parts of the Idukki district.
At Upputhara, a parked police jeep was damaged in a landslide.
With the Pullakayar river overflowing, the Kokkayar low-level crossing has been submerged. Around six houses were inundated in the surrounding area, and the affected families were shifted to safer locations, officials said.
Heavy rain disrupted traffic at multiple locations as well.
The road between Kattappana and Vazhavara was blocked following a landslide, while rising water levels in the Chottupara stream at Vandiperiyar led to waterlogging on National Highway 183.
The road at Nellimala was also blocked, affecting vehicular movement.
Authorities have announced the opening of the shutters of minor dams in the district,
In the neighbouring Kottayam district, heavy rain triggered widespread flooding in Erattupetta, Kanjirappally, Koottickal and Erumeli, inundating residential areas, disrupting traffic and prompting large-scale rescue operations.
Four houses were damaged at Teekoy village following the landslide but residents managed to escape unhurt, officials said.
Erattupetta town witnessed a sudden rise in water levels overnight, forcing authorities to halt vehicular traffic.
Several houses in Erattupetta, including those in Nadakkal and Murikkoly, were inundated.
Rescue personnel, assisted by locals, evacuated people stranded on the upper floors of their homes to safer locations. Traffic in the area remained completely disrupted, according to officials.
In Koottickal and Mundakkayam, water levels continued to rise after the Manimala and Pullakayar rivers overflowed. The Koottickal causeway and low-level crossing were submerged, while water entered several houses.
Traffic was also affected after the Mundakkayam causeway went underwater.
More landslides were reported from the hilly areas of Pathanamthitta district.
Ranni MLA Pazhakulam Madhu, in a social media post, said heavy flooding had been reported in Ranni and adjoining areas. He urged people to remain cautious as river water levels had risen to dangerous levels and said floodwaters had entered several houses and shops.
Several parts of Ranni and nearby areas are cut off following the flood, and the district administration has deployed boats to rescue people trapped in their houses, officials said.
Authorities said heavy rain, accompanied by landslides, caused a sudden rise in the water level in the Pampa river.
Relief camps have also been set up in Pathanamthitta district, officials added.
Apart from central Kerala, heavy rain was reported in the hilly areas of Kollam district.
Also, floods and minor landslides were reported in Kozhikode, Malappuram, Kannur and Palakkad districts.
Engapuzha town in Kozhikode was completely inundated following heavy rain, with water from the river overflowing into the area.
Traffic on the Wayanad ghat road has been regulated considering the possibility of landslides in the area.
A four-year-old died after falling into a waterbody in Malappuram.
The India Meteorological Department has forecast continued heavy rainfall in parts of Kerala, prompting authorities to keep rescue teams on alert and advise people in vulnerable areas to remain cautious.
The IMD issued a red alert predicting very heavy rain in Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts.
An orange alert has been issued for Ernakulam, Thrissur and Palakkad districts.

headline: Tehseen Poonawalla claims house arrest ahead of hunger strike over E20 petrol: ‘Nitin Gadkari is scared’

Tehseen Poonawalla claims house arrest ahead of hunger strike over E20 petrol: ‘Nitin Gadkari is scared’
Tehseen Poonawalla shared a series of posts on social media showing police personnel outside his residence and claimed he had been confined to his home.
Tehseen Poonawalla, who describes himself as a political analyst and consultant, claimed on Saturday that Delhi Police had placed him under house arrest ahead of his planned protest march and hunger strike against the government's E20 petrol policy. On Friday, Poonawalla announced that he would walk to Delhi's Gandhi Smriti, where he would hold a silent protest and a hunger strike against the policy.
On Saturday, he shared a series of posts on social media showing police personnel outside his residence and claimed he had been confined to his home, while also criticising Union transport minister Nitin Gadkari.
Tehseen Poonawalla ‘put under house arrest’
In one of the videos shared on X, Poonawalla is seen questioning a police officer about how he could be detained without any official paperwork.
“Guys, Delhi Police has detained me!!! They have put me under house arrest with NO PAPERS!!” he wrote in an X post.
In another post targeting Gadkari, he wrote, “An entire battalion of Delhi Police, including women officers, has put me under house arrest! Nitin Gadkari is scared of ethanol.”
‘Orders from top’
In one post on X, Poonawalla claimed that a Delhi Police officer informed him that the force had received “orders from top to house arrest” him.
In another video he shared, the police officer can be heard saying there were “chances of law being broken” if large numbers of people gathered and joined the activist during the protest against the E20 policy.
Row over E20-blended petrol
After the Cockroach Janta Party's agitation over exam paper leaks, which led to the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, Poonawalla has attempted to channel the outrage over E20 petrol.
The government's introduction of E20 petrol, which contains 80% petrol and 20% ethanol, has drawn strong criticism from opposition parties as well as consumer groups.
One of the main demands raised by Poonawalla and his Team Bharat, which has been leading the campaign against E20, is that 100% petrol, E5 and E10 fuel should remain available so motorists have the freedom to choose.
Nitin Gadkari defends E20 policy
On Thursday, the Union minister informed Parliament that petrol blended with 20 per cent ethanol (E20) could lower fuel economy by 2 to 6 per cent, depending on the type and age of the vehicle.
In a written reply in the Lok Sabha, Gadkari said E20 offers better acceleration, improved ride quality and around 30 per cent lower carbon emissions than E10 fuel.
Protests over E20-blended petrol
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) had earlier announced a campaign against the policy beginning this month. At the same time, transport unions in Delhi are preparing to hold a protest march against the programme.
AAP national convenor and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal said last month that the party would hold a 'National Town Hall Against E20' at the Constitution Club of India in Delhi on August 1.
"We are inviting people to join in large numbers on this platform, where we will discuss how to create pressure on the central government to withdraw E20 petrol. Experts and people who have faced problems with their vehicles are all invited," he said, adding that those willing to join virtually can send a message to 85-88-833-212.
Delhi-based transport organisations have also announced a march to Parliament on August 4 to protest against the E20 policy.
“We want to give a wake-up call to the Members of Parliament who have been sleeping on this issue, as the problems in vehicles caused by ethanol blending are being reported from across the country," Sanjay Samrat, president of the Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association, said, as quoted by news agency PTI.
Meanwhile, Uttar Pradesh Congress chief Ajay Rai has reportedly written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging him to remove Union ministers Nitin Gadkari and Hardeep Singh Puri from their respective portfolios over the issue.

Sampath, a motorist.

headline: Ex-army chief General Sharma dies at 96
full_text:
Ex-army chief General Sharma dies at 96
Former army chief General Vishwa Nath Sharma passed away on Friday at the age of 96
Former army chief General Vishwa Nath Sharma passed away on Friday at the age of 96. He served as the army chief during 1988-90.
Sharma was the younger brother of Major Som Nath Sharma, the first soldier to be awarded the Param Vir Chakra, India’s highest wartime honour, posthumously. An alumnus of Indian Military Academy, Dehradun, General Sharma was commissioned into the 16 Light Cavalry in June 1950.
Offering his condolences on the former chief’s demise, defence minister Rajnath Singh said on X, “Deeply saddened by the passing of former Chief of the Army Staff, General Vishwa Nath Sharma. A distinguished military leader, General Sharma served the Nation with unwavering dedication, courage and honour. He carried forward the illustrious legacy of his family, including that of his elder brother, Major Som Nath Sharma, PVC, with great distinction.”
Major Sharma was among the four army heroes awarded the PVC for their uncommon courage in the 1947-48 Kashmir operations; the others were Lance Naik Karam Singh, Second Lieutenant Rama Raghoba Rane and Naik Jadunath Singh (posthumous).
The Indian Army also extended its condolences to his bereaved family and loved ones. “A distinguished soldier and visionary military leader, General Vishwa Nath Sharma dedicated his life to the service of the Nation. The younger brother of Major Som Nath Sharma, PVC, Independent India’s first Param Vir Chakra awardee, he upheld his family’s extraordinary legacy of courage and selfless service with distinction. His exemplary leadership, unwavering commitment and enduring legacy of honour, duty and military excellence will continue to inspire future generations,” it wrote on X.

headline: No GenZ disconnect, PM responded with action: Smriti Irani on NEET protest row
full_text:
No GenZ disconnect, PM responded with action: Smriti Irani on NEET protest row
Smriti Irani said the Centre answered the NEET paper leak protests with legislation, a task force and direct outreach by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She said the response showed engagement with students while drawing a line against violence during dissent.
Senior BJP leader and former Union Education Minister Smriti Irani has dismissed claims that the NEET paper leak protests exposed a widening disconnect between Generation Z (GenZ) and the Narendra Modi government. She asserted that the Centre responded swiftly through legislation, dialogue and direct communication by the Prime Minister.
In an exclusive interview with India Today, Irani said the passage of the anti-paper leak legislation in Parliament, coupled with Prime Minister Modi's recent appeal to students through an Instagram video, demonstrated that the government was responsive to the concerns of young people rather than indifferent to them.
'NO DISCONNECT BETWEEN GENZ AND GOVT'
Asked whether the student-led protests reflected a growing gap between the youth and the government, Irani rejected the premise, arguing that the government's response proved otherwise.
She said Parliament had passed the anti-paper leak Bill after extensive deliberations and described the Prime Minister's message to protesting students as evidence of constructive engagement.
"It is a great insult to Parliament when you say the issue has merely been papered over," she said, adding that the government had acted proactively by setting up a task force, passing the legislation and directly communicating with young citizens.
Irani also accused sections of the media of disproportionately focusing on the Jantar Mantar protests while ignoring similar student movements elsewhere, particularly in Jharkhand.
DEFENDS EDUCATION REFORMS, ANTI-PAPER LEAK BILL
Responding to concerns over whether previous reform committees had yielded tangible results, Irani said the new legislation "speaks for itself" and argued that examination-related challenges had existed long before the Modi government came to power.
Drawing on her tenure as Education Minister, she said the National Education Policy was framed after one of the most extensive consultation exercises in independent India's history.
According to her, the government consulted more than 2.25 lakh village education councils, district education officers, state education ministers, parent-teacher associations and student bodies before finalising the policy.
She also defended the composition of the newly constituted task force on examination reforms, saying it reflected the Prime Minister's willingness to involve experts and individuals across political and ideological lines rather than limiting participation to supporters of the government.
'RIGHT TO DISSENT, NOT TO ANARCHY'
Irani strongly defended the police response during the protests, saying democratic dissent was a constitutional right but violence against security personnel could not be justified.
She questioned why images of injured Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel had received relatively little attention and pointed to reports that individuals with criminal backgrounds had participated in the demonstrations.
"You have the right to debate, deliberate and dissent. You do not have the right to anarchy," she said, urging that conclusions be drawn only after official investigations are completed.
Rejecting attempts to portray the issue as a conflict between the government and GenZ, Irani argued that many young Indians serve in the armed forces, police and other public institutions, and should not be grouped together based solely on age.
"Don't bring age as a new division," she said, adding that patriotism and respect for democratic institutions transcended generational identities.
CREDITS PM MODI'S LEADERSHIP
Responding to criticism over the government's handling of the protests, Irani credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership for maintaining a balance between protecting students and preserving law and order.
She said then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down to prevent student protests from being "usurped by criminal forces" and described the government's actions as sensitive and timely.
Concluding the interview, Irani maintained that the Centre's response to the protests reflected a willingness to engage with students while ensuring that democratic dissent did not descend into violence or attacks on public institutions.

Amit Shah presented Lokmanya Tilak award to Ajit Doval and hailed his role in India's national security
NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday lauded National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval for his contribution to India's national security and foreign policy, saying the veteran intelligence officer has played a crucial role behind every major national security decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014.Speaking at a function in Pune after presenting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 to Doval, Shah said the NSA's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening India's security architecture and defence preparedness.He also said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him.
"NSA Ajit Doval has played a great role in strengthening India's foreign policy. In every decision of PM Modi for national security, Doval has had a 'role and advice' in the background," Shah said."Whenever history is written, if anyone analyses internal security and external security, then clearly, for Ajit Doval ji, a golden page will have to be kept reserved; there is no doubt about this," he added.
'First selection' after Modi became PM
Shah said one of the first decisions taken by PM Modi after assuming office in 2014 was appointing Doval as the National Security Advisor, a move he said transformed India's strategic posture.
"Today, India's foreign policy has become a foreign policy with a backbone of steel; no one can deny this. We have, along with self-respect, strengthened our position in the world," Shah said.Praising Doval's decades-long career in the Intelligence Bureau, Shah said India has emerged as a stronger and more confident nation under Modi's leadership, with Doval making a significant contribution to that transformation.
"After becoming NSA in 2014, Doval helped implement many strategic ideas on the ground and played a major role in modernising India's armed forces, strengthening technology, enhancing operational capability and improving the country's defence preparedness," Shah said.He added that the Modi government has fundamentally transformed both the defensive and offensive capabilities of the armed forces over the past 12 years, with Doval playing a key role in the process.Shah also noted that much of Doval's contribution can never be made public because of the confidential nature of intelligence operations.Recalling his tenure as Gujarat's home minister, Shah narrated how he first interacted with Doval following the Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts. He said then chief minister Narendra Modi had advised Gujarat Police to consult Doval while investigating the attacks."I remember Ajit ji had come to my house. The tips he gave resulted in Gujarat Police resolving not just the Ahmedabad bomb blast, but 13 bomb blasts across the country all at once. This was a very great achievement," Shah said.
Shah invokes Lokmanya Tilak's legacy
The Union home minister also paid tribute to Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, calling him one of the foremost architects of India's freedom movement.He said Tilak's iconic slogan, "Swarajya is my birthright, and I shall have it," gave a new direction to India's freedom struggle and inspired generations of freedom fighters.
Shah added that the slogan made Indians realise that self-rule was their right and not a favour bestowed by anyone.Describing Tilak as a fearless journalist, Shah said one could truly understand courage in journalism only by reading the articles published in Kesari, the newspaper founded by the freedom fighter."How fearless a journalist can be can only be experienced by reading the articles of Kesari," he said.
Referring to Tilak's role in mobilising people through the public Ganesh and Shivaji festivals, Shah said they laid the foundation for cultural nationalism and that India continues to follow the path envisioned by the freedom fighter."India is now moving firmly on the path of cultural nationalism laid down by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and no one can reverse that journey," he said.Shah further added that Tilak's ideas on nationalism, self-rule and social awakening continue to guide the country and remain relevant for nation-building, particularly for the younger generation.
Shah said honours such as the Lokmanya Tilak National Award are not merely ceremonial but recognise those who dedicate their lives to the country and inspire future generations."When such individuals are honoured, the feeling of gratitude of society towards them is discharged... Today, the Tilak Award that has been conferred upon Ajit Doval ji... for those who live for this country and work for this country, it will become a place of great inspiration," he said.
Doval accepts award with humility
Accepting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award, Doval thanked the organisers and said he was honoured to receive an award named after Lokmanya Tilak."I am thankful for this award named after Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and accept it with humility," Doval said.Doval also praised the country's leadership, saying, "We are very fortunate to have leaders like PM Modi and Amit Shah".

The BJP's Chhattisgarh unit had made a post comparing the state's students who make people proud and the ones who “dance on Babur's heritage”.
A student's response to a post targeting her for dancing during the recently-concluded student protest against the NEET paper leak has gone viral. The BJP's Chhattisgarh unit had made a post on Thursday, drawing a comparison between the state's students who make people proud and the ones who “dance on Babur's heritage”.
The BJP had shared a video of Gen Z protesters dancing and making a reel during a student protest against the NEET-UG paper leak and other exam irregularities. Parallely, the video featured a student receiving an award from President Droupadi Murmu. “Which mindset Gen Z will you choose?,” the BJP Chhattisgarh captioned the post.
Hours after the post, one of the students who featured in the protest reel shared by the BJP reacted and said that her content was used without her consent.
The student, identified as Urwashi Palandurkar, countered the video in a light-hearted manner and admitted that she “couldn't take it seriously”. Her candour and sarcastic yet witty reply to the video earned big praise on social media, including from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal.
Gen Z student's PPT to counter BJP clip
Urwashi had many notes on the caption and content of the video shared by BJP Chhattisgarh and she presented them all using a Power Point presentation. “Your caption game is very weak. Your ChatGPT is not giving you good responses,” the student began.
She further said that the ‘Babur ki Virasat" jibe was not relatable, and that “divide and rule” won’t work in 2026, especially on a generation that taught Gen Z terms to Parliamentarians.She was referring to the use of phrases like “clocked it”, “FOMO”, “MIA” and “Delulu” in Parliament recently.
"I scored 93% marks in both classes 10 and 12," Urwashi said, emphasising how academics and extracurriculars like dancing can go hand in hand.
Kejriwal, CJP heap praise, Rahul Gandhi shares video
Urwashi Palandurkar's video earned big praise online, including from AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal and the CJP. “You go, girl!,” the CJP commented on the student's Instagram video. Besides, Abhijeet Dipke called her a “legend”.
Arvind Kejriwal also commented on the clip: “God bless you beta. Loved your positivity.” The Gen Z student's video was also shared by Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi.
Urwashi was among the thousands of students who participated in students protests against the NEET paper leak. The protest was called off by the CJP on July 25, hours after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as education minister. However, the outfit later vowed to launch a new and bigger agitation if police action against protesters continued.
