headline: Unable to eliminate extortion despite being in power: Bengal BJP chief's admission
full_text:
Unable to eliminate extortion despite being in power: Bengal BJP chief's admission
BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said West Bengal could reverse the flight of capital only if partisan politics was kept out of business, and announced that the government would soon hold consultations before finalising a new industrial policy.
The BJP has not yet been able to eliminate extortion in West Bengal despite coming to power in the state, the party's state president Samik Bhattacharya said on Saturday, while admitting that a section within his own party was showing the same tendencies.
He said the government had been in office for only two months and that not everything had changed with the change in power.
Bhattacharya also warned party workers, supporters and newly inducted leaders against hurling eggs at opposition leaders, saying such acts could rebound on those now indulging in them. He said Bengal could reverse the flight of capital only if partisan politics was kept out of business, and announced that the government would soon hold consultations before finalising a new industrial policy.
Addressing the 'Udyami Samagam' event at the IIT Kharagpur Research Park in Rajarhat on the outskirts of Kolkata, Bhattacharya said, "Our government has come to power only two months ago. We have not been able to solve all problems. If I say on behalf of my party that we have been able to eradicate extortion from everywhere, then I will be making a false claim. There are deviations. People had become accustomed to passing through a system of making easy money through syndicates. Not everything has changed with the change in state power."
He added, "Some joined the ruling party within four hours, others had dormant wishes that have now surfaced. We are trying to control such tendencies within the party. Our CM Suvendu Adhikari is also trying to apply strict brakes on such tendencies." Bhattacharya said a section of workers in the party was trying to enter every sector, from education and health to business, with political flags.
Stressing the need to clean up the business environment, he said Bengal was at a point where it could move away from its difficult industrial past.
"We must keep partisan politics out of this system. We have become residents of a political society in West Bengal. We need freedom from it. Till such time Bengal is able to come out of the culture of infiltration of politics in every sphere of life, no government can bring about its effective change and attract investment," he said.
"We are making an earnest effort to build a government for West Bengal and not a BJP government," he added.
Bhattacharya said the party had achieved only partial success. "We haven't been able to provide you with an error-free atmosphere, but we have largely been able to deliver an investment climate that is fear-free. To set up a company, you can now buy your own brick, cement and sand. If someone approaches you, use the phone. He will either leave your premises or find himself inside lock up," he said.
Calling the BJP government in Bengal one that had "stepped into its adolescence", he said the business community should point out mistakes directly and protest if needed. "No system can function or be made to live for long by quashing protests. All autocracies across the world inevitably fall. If someone from our side sports a body language of having 207 MLAs and hits the road, then the consequence will be disastrous," he said.
He added, "The unwarranted egg-therapy we see now can turn on its head and start falling on the other side as well. All, including those in my party, must understand that. Those Sanatanis who have suddenly found a place in our party and are harbouring aspirations for influence and advantage must also remain careful because the trajectory of those eggs can change in no time."
Referring to the government's move to scrap the Urban Land Ceiling Act to unlock developable land and attract large-scale industrial and real estate investment, Bhattacharya said the next step would be wider consultation. "
Within the next few weeks, the government will sit in a meeting with the investors in this state, those who have set up start-ups, professors in different universities and our industrialists before drawing up our new industrial policy," he said.
Bhattacharya said the government was trying to curb extortionary practices, keep politics out of commerce and build conditions for investment, while also warning his own party against excesses.

full_text:
Nathula pass border trade resumes after 6 years; traders seek expansion of goods list
Nathula pass border trade resumes after 6 years; traders seek expansion of goods list
Edited by: Priyanka Jaiswal / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 01, 2026, 18:03 IST

Nathula Border gate (ANI image)
Border trade through the Nathula Pass in East Sikkim, a key segment of the ancient Silk Route connecting India and China, resumed on Saturday after remaining suspended for nearly six years. A formal reopening ceremony was held at Nathula, with officials from both countries participating in the event.The trade route had remained closed since 2020 due to the Covid-19 pandemic and subsequent border tensions between India and China.Welcoming the resumption of trade, Anil Gupta, General Secretary of the Indo-China Nathula Border Traders Welfare Association, thanked Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang for his efforts in facilitating the reopening.
"I extend heartfelt thanks to our Chief Minister, Prem Singh Tamang. This has become possible today solely due to his efforts. For traders who had outstanding dues or stocks stranded on the other side, this is a time of great joy, and everyone is happy," Gupta said.
Traders seek expansion of trade list
While welcoming the resumption of trade, Gupta said the existing list of goods permitted through Nathula needs to be updated to reflect present-day commercial needs.
"The current trading list includes items like horses, sheep and general goods. We believe industrial products relevant to today's times should be included. We have submitted a formal request to the department, and we are hopeful that the government will take a very positive view of this," he said.
Under the existing arrangement, only a limited list of traditional goods is allowed to be traded through the border route. Traders have long been seeking the inclusion of industrial and other commercially relevant products.
Around 300 traders await passes
Gupta said preparations for the resumption of trade were underway, with authorities verifying applications submitted by traders."Around five hundred traders collected forms, and approximately three hundred have submitted them. Verification is underway, and we hope all traders will receive their passes very soon," he said.
The reopening is expected to revive economic activity in the border region and provide relief to traders whose businesses had been affected by the prolonged suspension of cross-border trade. Nathula, located in East Sikkim, is one of the few officially designated border trading points between India and China and has historically served as an important corridor on the ancient Silk Route.

headline: Cabinet approves ₹84,084-crore ‘Samudra Manthan’ scheme for offshore energy exploration
full_text:
Cabinet approves ₹84,084-crore ‘Samudra Manthan’ scheme for offshore energy exploration
“Samudra Manthan” is expected to catalyse reserve accretion of over 600 MMT of oil equivalent (MMToE), substantially increase offshore exploration activity.
The Union cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday approved Samudra Manthan, a ₹84,084 crore national offshore exploration scheme that aims to boost depleting domestic oil and gas resources at a time when India’s crude oil import dependency has surged from 78.5% in 2014-15 to 88.7% in 2025-26.
The scheme draws on the Prime Minister’s vision, articulated from the Red Fort on Independence Day last year, of a modern-day “Samudra Manthan” — a reference to the churning of the ocean in India’s ancient epics — to unlock India’s vast offshore energy potential, an official statement issued by the cabinet said.
“It marks a landmark step towards strengthening India’s energy security, accelerating domestic exploration and production, promoting technological leadership, and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat,” the statement said.
Also Read | At CCS meet, PM Modi orders ‘whole of govt’ plan to protect oil supplies, Indians in West Asia
According to a spokesperson for the petroleum ministry, the scheme, which has an approved budget of ₹84,084 crore in its first phase up to March 31, 2031, has four key components: acquisition and processing of modern offshore seismic data with an outlay of ₹28,534 crore; drilling of 60 deepwater exploration wells (total outlay ₹43,200 crore, including government support of up to 50% of eligible drilling cost or ₹675 crore per well); development of common offshore infrastructure hubs ( ₹10,000 crore) to facilitate commercialisation of discoveries; and establishment of oil and gas manufacturing and services zones ( ₹2,000 crore) to promote domestic manufacturing and localisation of critical equipment and services.
Subject to exploration success, the scheme aims to increase India’s domestic oil and gas production from around 62 MMTOE (million metric tonnes of oil equivalent) to 80 MMTOE annually and expand the country’s hydrocarbon resource base from 1.6 billion TOE to 2.2 billion TOE. “The additional production has the potential to reduce crude oil imports by nearly ₹1 lakh crore annually, strengthening India’s energy security and reducing import dependence,” the spokesperson added.
India’s domestic oil and gas production
The policy comes at a time when India’s domestic oil and gas production from mature and ageing fields is declining. Some of the country’s major producing fields, such as the offshore Mumbai High and fields in Assam, have been in production for several decades and are well past what is known as the plateau production phase. India is the world’s third-largest oil consumer after the US and China, but its domestic energy output is low; it ranks around 20th in the world in terms of production. The country imported 189.4 million metric tonnes (MMT) of crude in fiscal 2015, which grew to 245.3 MMT in fiscal 2026. According to a statement made by minister of state for petroleum Suresh Gopi in the Lok Sabha on March 10, India’s domestic crude oil production is declining. Output from domestic fields fell from 36.9 MMT in 2015-16 to 28.7 MMT in 2024-25 despite the government auctioning 172 exploration blocks (3,78,652 sq km) in nine bidding rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP).
Also Read | Analysis-Drone strike in Egypt sparks security concerns about Suez oil exports
India also imports natural gas in large quantities to meet domestic requirements. Together with crude oil, India’s oil and gas import dependence was 80.7% in 2025-26. India’s total natural gas consumption in 2025-26 was 68,753 million metric standard cubic metres (MMSCM); gross domestic natural gas output that fiscal year was 34,776 MMSCM.
What government and industry experts said
Government and industry experts said the cabinet decision is a much-needed intervention as augmenting domestic energy output is a key requirement for a rapidly growing economy. The Prime Minister articulated this too in his speech on August 15, 2025, they said. “Samudra Manthan” is expected to catalyse reserve accretion of more than 600 MMT of oil equivalent (MMToE), substantially increase offshore exploration activity, promote higher domestic oil and gas production, generate large-scale employment, strengthen indigenous manufacturing under Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat, and foster a globally competitive ecosystem for offshore technologies and services. The scheme is also expected to stimulate significant investments across the exploration and production value chain, creating long-term opportunities for industry, innovation and economic growth.
In his speech last year, Modi said India spent a “huge part of the budget” on energy imports. “If we were not dependent on energy, that money would have been used for the future of the youth of my country, that money would have been used to help the poor of my country fight against poverty, that money would have been used for the welfare of the farmers of my country, that money would have been used to change the conditions of the villages of my country, but we had to give it to foreign countries.”
“Now we are working towards becoming self-reliant. To make the country developed, we are now moving towards ‘Samudra Manthan’ (churning of the ocean). Taking forward our Samudra Manthan, we want to work in a mission mode towards finding oil reserves, gas reserves under the sea and hence India is going to start the National Deep Water Exploration Mission. This is our important announcement to become energy independent,” he added.
Also Read | US grants Serbian oil firm another sanctions waiver
The scheme approved on Friday encompasses a comprehensive set of interventions across the offshore exploration value chain. It provides for large-scale acquisition, processing and interpretation of high-quality seismic data, accelerated deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploratory drilling, scientific drilling in frontier basins, development of common offshore production and evacuation infrastructure, and establishment of an integrated oil and gas manufacturing and services zone, a government statement issued after the cabinet meeting said. “It also includes dedicated provisions for digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach, creating an integrated ecosystem to accelerate offshore exploration and production in the country,” it added.
Rajnish Gupta, partner, Tax and Economic Policy Group at EY India said: “The Samudra Manthan scheme is a significant announcement of the seriousness of the Government in making India’s E&P sector stronger.” “Investments in large-scale seismic data acquisition and drilling of exploratory wells in deep and ultra deep waters will reduce geological uncertainty and derisk exploration and lay the foundation for future discoveries. Good results can catalyse greater private investments in the sector,” he added.
The emphasis on shared infrastructure for production and evacuation is also important, as it can improve project viability and create value by lowering costs for discoveries that may otherwise be considered marginal. This will support India’s efforts to reduce import dependence while building a more resilient energy ecosystem, Gupta said.

headline: Stating that the water situation in the Cauvery is “slightly better” in view of the rain, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Sunday (August 2, 2026) reiterated his appeal to the Kannada organisations to withdraw their State-wide bandh plan o...
full_text:
Stating that the water situation in the Cauvery is “slightly better” in view of the rain, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Sunday (August 2, 2026) reiterated his appeal to the Kannada organisations to withdraw their State-wide bandh plan on August 13.
However, Kannada Chaluvali leader Vatal Nagaraj, who is leading the protest, said the bandh will be held as planned.
At an all-party meeting, the Chief Minister said Karnataka is carefully assessing the Cauvery situation, including the petition of the DMK in the Supreme Court. A limited quantity of water is being released from the reservoirs in the light of rain, he said.
The meeting had been convened to address the concerns over the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA)’s directive to the State to abide by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee’s order to release 3,500 cubic metres daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days. The order set off protests in parts of Karnataka.
“(Four) reservoirs in the Cauvery basin are cumulatively receiving about 68,000 cusecs of water. Our dams were not full since there was no rain. There has been some rain (now) and the situation has become slightly better. Kabini (reservoir) is full,” he told presspersons here after the all-party meeting.
The data shared by the Water Resources Department shows that Karnataka was releasing water at the rate of 25,000 cusecs from the Kabini reservoir and 1,819 cusecs from the Krishna Raja Sagar on Sunday to Tamil Nadu.
The Chief Minister said: “We are releasing a limited quantity of water through canals only to fill lakes and tanks meant for drinking water purposes, and not for irrigation.”
‘Mekedatu is the solution’
Reiterating that the proposed Mekedatu project on the Cauvery is the long-term solution to the problems faced by both the States, he said, “Karnataka will respect the law and orders of the Supreme Court while protecting the State’s interest.”
On the petition filed by the DMK in the Supreme Court, Mr. Shivakumar said: “We are closely watching the situation. Individual petitions of political parties and organisations are treated differently. We have to utilise our experience and be careful.” He also said that a legal and technical team would fight the State’s case.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joesph Vijay has agreed to postpone his visit to Bengaluru to discuss the Cauvery issue on the request of the Karnataka government, he said. “Mr. Vijay intended to hold talks, but the meeting has been deferred. I requested from him that we meet later when a cordial atmosphere prevails. I do not want anyone shouting slogans against my friends. We should respect each other. We have to live together and work together. Ultimately, India is one,” said the Karnataka Chief Minister.
Asked if he would be able to convince Mr. Vijay of the situation, he said: “We will make him understand (the situation) and he will understand. Though he is new to politics, he is courageous. Whatever our political differences may be, he wanted to come to Karnataka.”
He said he will speak to the protesting farmers, Kannada organisations, and Opposition leaders. “Our Ministers will also speak. When the government is standing with you and nature is also with you, bandh is of no use. It will affect our schools and businesses. Ultimately, it will not help us. We are committed to farmers’ welfare and bound to protect the State's interest,” the Chief Minister said. “They [Opposition leaders] have pledged their support to the Government and have provided valuable suggestions. We will take the suggestions that will be discussed with the legal team before moving forward.”
However, in Mysuru, former MLA Vatal Nagaraj said the bandh had not been called on one issue. “More than 2,000 Kannada organisations have extended support to the bandh. Educational institutions, film chambers and hotel industries, among others, have extended support. Bandh is for various issues, including the Mahadayi river water dispute, employment for Kannadigas, and the development of the Mysuru-Hyderabad-Karnataka region, North Karnataka, Belagavi, Hubballi-Dharwad, and border areas. There is no question of withdrawing the bandh.”

headline: Pappu Yadav attacked with shoe in Delhi, MP claims attacker pulled out knife
full_text:
Pappu Yadav attacked with shoe in Delhi, MP claims attacker pulled out knife
Independent MP from Bihar's Purnea, Pappu Yadav, was attacked after a man identified as Sumit from Bulandshahr allegedly hurled a shoe at him during a press conference in Delhi, sparking chaos and a scuffle.
Independent MP from Bihar's Purnea, Pappu Yadav, was targeted after a person threw a shoe at him during a press conference in Delhi, triggering a commotion and a scuffle between his supporters and the attacker.
According to the information provided, the protest was linked to Yadav's statement on the law related to the theft of donations meant for the Ram Temple.
The incident led to chaos at the venue, with pushing and shoving breaking out between Yadav's supporters and the protester after the shoe was thrown. Police have started an investigation into the incident.
According to sources, the person who entered the venue and thrown the shoe at Yadav identified himself as Sumit, a resident of UP's Bulandshahr. He was overpowered and detained immediately after the incident.
Police are currently verifying the sequence of events at the press conference, including whether the accused had come armed with a knife.
According to police, when Sumit was handed over by Pappu Yadav's supporters, a knife was also handed over along with him. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the recovery of the knife.
Sources further said that Sumit told police he was upset over the alleged insult to saints, which he cited as the reason behind his actions.
Pappu Yadav claimed that the accused had come to kill him. "He came to kill me with a knife," Yadav alleged. The MP further alleged that there was a conspiracy to kill him.
"Every day, some religious figures are saying, 'Burn him, we will give Rs 51 lakh.' Everyone is saying, 'Kill him.' There was a conspiracy to kill me," Yadav said.
Pappu Yadav's media convenor, who was present at the spot, alleged that the attack escalated after the shoe was thrown.
"They first took off a slipper and threw it. When the knife was drawn to attack, our supporters and associates tried to restrain the assailant. I stepped forward and positioned myself between the attacker and Pappu Yadav, and I was beaten severely as a result," he said.
Following the incident Pappu Yadav alleged that the attacker had political links and sought an investigation into who was behind the alleged attack.
In a post on X, Yadav addressed Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, asking, "Prime Minister and Home Minister, tell me who gave him the contract to kill me? This youth was seen with the Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, and he carried out a murderous attack on me."
Yadav further alleged that people associated with the BJP were protecting the accused and demanded action.
"Tell me who is protecting such killers in your party. Do they have your direct patronage? If not, then action should be taken," he wrote.
One of Pappu Yadav's supporters also alleged that the attacker had pulled out a knife during the incident.
"Pappu Yadav is constantly serving the public. The moment he pulled out a knife from behind, we immediately acted together and overpowered him. Had we not restrained him at that moment, it is possible that our Pappu-ji might not have been with us today," the supporter said.
The media convenor further alleged that the Delhi Police failed to protect the MP despite prior warnings.
"I tried to help Pappu Yadav escape the scene. The Delhi Police stood by and allowed the beating to happen. The police seemed to be shielding the goons. These people had come to stage a 'Prayagraj Part Two'—they came to replicate the Atiq Ahmed incident today," he alleged.
Claiming that he was injured in the scuffle, he said, "I was beaten so badly while facing two or three individuals that I lost consciousness. My associates carried me away from the spot. The Delhi Police took the attackers away, so they would know the exact number."
He also claimed that he had alerted the police in advance about threats to the MP.
"I personally met the DCP this morning and filed a formal complaint stating that the MP was arriving today and has been receiving constant threats on social media. Despite knowing all this, they deployed only three or four police personnel here," he alleged.
The media convenor further claimed that no police personnel helped Pappu Yadav during the attack.
"Not a single policeman stepped forward to help Pappu Yadav escape. When the assault was taking place, they focused solely on saving the goons and whisked them away from the scene. There were people hiding behind the cameras, three or four of them. Suddenly, someone pulled out a knife, another a slipper. The MP was the target, no one else," he alleged.
Congress leader Pawan Khera also reacted to the incident, criticising the Delhi Police.
"The Delhi Police seems remarkably efficient when it comes to repressing students peacefully demanding their constitutional rights. But when it comes to protecting a vocal Opposition leader – even a sitting Member of Parliament – at his own residence, it suddenly falls short," Khera said in a post on X.
He further said, "Ever since Anurag Kumar took charge as Delhi's Police Commissioner, the force's record has gone from bad to worse."
Police are verifying the facts surrounding the incident, including the alleged use of a knife, and the investigation is underway.

headline: IIT Guwahati student dies in Brahmaputra drowning, another rescued: Police
full_text:
IIT Guwahati student dies in Brahmaputra drowning, another rescued: Police
Local sailors immediately came to the rescue, followed by the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) team
A third-year BTech student of the Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati (IIT-G) died after accidentally falling into the Brahmaputra near Guwahati’s Lathia Bagicha Ghat on Saturday evening, police said on Sunday.
Another student who fell into the river with her was rescued shortly after the incident, officers said.
Local sailors immediately came to the rescue, followed by the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) team.
“One of the students was rescued within around 20 minutes, while the body of the other student was recovered after nearly three hours of searching,” an NDRF official said.
“It is with profound grief and deep sorrow that IIT Guwahati informs of the untimely demise of a BTech 3rd Year student of the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE), who tragically lost her life in a drowning incident near Lathia Bagicha Ghat yesterday evening,” the institute said in a statement.
The authorities informed the student’s parents and asked them to visit the campus.
Also Read:IIT Guwahati Convocation 2026: 2265 degrees awarded, Saptarshi Mukherjee receives gold medal
“Police authorities are presently conducting a formal investigation into the circumstances of the incident. The institute remains in close communication with her parents and is extending full cooperation and assistance,” IIT-G said.
Additional superintendent of police (Kamrup), Kalyan Pathak, said police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. “We are investigating the matter further,” Pathak told HT on Sunday evening.
IIT-G urged students, faculty and staff to exercise caution around water bodies and avoid hazardous locations, particularly during the monsoon.
The institute said it would strengthen its safety communication and issue frequent advisories cautioning students against going to the river and other unsafe water bodies during the monsoon.

headline: Fake identities, phone numbers: How 5 men impersonated deceased owners in ₹2.29 crore land fraud in Navi Mumbai
full_text:
Fake identities, phone numbers: How 5 men impersonated deceased owners in ₹2.29 crore land fraud in Navi Mumbai
As per police, Shinde got his father and brother-in-law to impersonate the dead brothers by using fake identity documents.
A five-month manhunt in Navi Mumbai led to the arrest of five people accused of impersonating dead owners. As per the police, the five accused, led by mastermind Suraj Vasudev Shinde, faked their identities to carry out a land fraud of ₹2.29 crores.
As reported by HT earlier, the accused allegedly targeted a plot in Karanjade belonging to brothers Nathan Eliyahu Chincholkar and Shalom (Selim) Eliyahu Chincholkar, who had migrated to Israel and later died in the country.
Fake documents, new phone numbers
As per police, Shinde got his father and brother-in-law to impersonate the dead brothers by using fake identity documents.
Using these fake documents, Shinde and his accomplices managed to execute the sale of the plot for ₹2.29 crores.
Police added that the arrests came after a five-month manhunt for the accused as they kept changing their phone numbers, identities and hideouts to evade the police.
Shinde had lived in the states of Maharashtra, Goa, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh while trying to evade arrest. As per officials, Shinde fled with his relatives who were also involved in the scam.
Accused tracked using intelligence inputs
Suraj Shinde was tracked to Thivim in Goa, where he was arrested with his uncle, Satish Namdev Shinde, 41, and cousin, Tejas Pramod Surve, 26, using technical surveillance and intelligence inputs.
Police added that Manish More was arrested by Mapusa police in an unrelated theft case and was lodged in Colvale Central Jail, and Vasudev Shinde was arrested from Dombivli on July 27.
Following their arrest, police also recovered the forged PAN and Aadhaar Cards in the names of the deceased landowners.

headline: Tiger grabs woman by head, drags her 300 metres to death in Madhya Pradesh
full_text:
Tiger grabs woman by head, drags her 300 metres to death in Madhya Pradesh
A tiger entered Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat village and fatally attacked a woman sleeping in her hut. The killing has triggered fresh safety measures and renewed concern over repeated big cat incursions.
A woman in her 30s died after a tiger attacked her in Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat district in the early hours of Sunday, officials said. The woman, identified as Sugni Bai Dhurve, suffered grievous head injuries and was taken to a hospital in Baihar, where she died, Block Medical Officer Dr Anant Lilhare said.
The attack took place in Parrapur Baigatola village under the Khapa range of the Kanha National Park. Assistant Director of the Sijhora Buffer Zone Ashish Pandey confirmed the incident and said a detailed report would be prepared after an inquiry, while police said a case of accidental death has been registered and further investigation is under way.
According to villagers, Dhurve was sleeping in a hut when the tiger entered the village, around 80 km from the district headquarters, at about 1.30 am. They said the animal grabbed her by the head and dragged her away.
After hearing the family's cries for help, local residents rushed to the spot with torches. The tiger dragged her for about 300 metres before leaving her and disappearing into the forest, they added.
Forest officials said the village has seen several instances of tigers and leopards entering human habitations in recent months. They said the victim's family would be given financial assistance as per government norms.
The forest department also said it would install a cage in the area, step up patrolling, and urged residents to keep house doors shut at night, avoid going into the forest, and not leave children and elderly people unattended.
Local representatives claimed the woman's family lives in a hut without a door and alleged that it has not benefited from a central government scheme aimed at the socio-economic development of the most backward and vulnerable tribal groups.
The attack has prompted fresh measures in the area as officials investigate the incident and prepare assistance for the family.

headline: Stand-up comedian Kunal Kamra has cancelled his scheduled shows from Monday to Thursday at a venue in Whitefield and shifted them to another venue in Koramangala.
full_text:
Stand-up comedian Kunal Kamra has cancelled his scheduled shows from Monday to Thursday at a venue in Whitefield and shifted them to another venue in Koramangala.
The development comes after a Hindutva outfit, Hindu Rashtra Samanvaya Samiti, petitioned the Whitefield police, demanding that Mr. Kamra should not be permitted to perform.
They had contended that Mr. Kamra had disrespected Hindu deities.
A senior police official from the Whitefield Division told The Hindu that Mr. Kamra and the organisers of the shows visited the Whitefield Police Station on Sunday and informed that they had decided to cancel the shows. The decision, they said, was taken as the event had become controversial. No law and order incident was reported in connection with the scheduled performance.
Taking to social media platform X, Mr. Kamra on Sunday announced: “Shows for Monday - Tuesday - Wednesday - Thursday shifted to Underground Comedy Club in Koramangala.”
He further said that amount would be refunded to those who had already booked tickets for the Whitefield shows and requested them to book shows at the Koramangala venue afresh.
On Saturday, responding to the Hindutva activists objecting to his shows in Whitefield, Mr. Kamra gave an open invite on X that he would be at the Whitefield Police Station on Sunday to seek permission to perform and any objectors were free to join him to debate on “comedy and culture”. He later said only senior journalist Aakar Patel turned up.
Meanwhile, Mohan Gowda, spokesperson, Hindu Janajagruti Samiti, said that Mr. Kamra shifted the shows after facing strong opposition and appealed to the Koramangala police not to allow him to perform in their jurisdiction.
Sources in the government said that the shows would be not stopped.

headline: Over 1,200 children aged between 5 and 14 years showcased their mental arithmetic skills at the SIP Regional Prodigy 2026 — one of India’s largest mental arithmetic competitions for children — at CK Conventions in Mangalagiri on Sunday.
full_text:
Over 1,200 children aged between 5 and 14 years showcased their mental arithmetic skills at the SIP Regional Prodigy 2026 — one of India’s largest mental arithmetic competitions for children — at CK Conventions in Mangalagiri on Sunday.
The competition was inaugurated by AIIMS Mangalagiri Director Col. Shashikanth Thumma in the presence of SIP Academy India director Sibi Sekhar, New Franchisee Acquisition head Uma Swaminathan; Regional Business head – South and International Acquisition head Praveen E.G., and Andhra Pradesh head Jabeer Baig.
Addressing the gathering, Col. Shashikanth Thumma described the participants as ‘live supercomputers’. “You are human calculators, solving problems faster than calculators. This programme develops skills to solve not only mathematics problems but also life’s challenges,” he said.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Sibi Sekhar said that mental arithmetic was more relevant in the artificial intelligence (AI) era than ever before.
“While AI can provide answers, children still need strong cognitive abilities, logical thinking, concentration, memory and problem-solving skills. Mental arithmetic develops these foundational capabilities, enabling children to think independently and confidently.”
Meanwhile, Ms. Uma Swaminathan said, “We currently operate 25 centres in Andhra Pradesh and plan to double this number to 50 in the coming years,” she said.
SIP Regional Prodigy is the regional championship of the annual SIP Prodigy competition and serves as a qualifying event for the national finals. The winners of Andhra Pradesh regional competition will qualify for the National SIP Prodigy 2026 to be held in Kochi in November, where nearly 5,000 children from across the country will compete.

NEW DELHI: A press conference by Independent MP Pappu Yadav was disrupted in Delhi on Sunday after a confrontation broke out between his supporters and a group of men. Yadavâs media convenor alleged the MP was targeted with a knife in what he described as an attempt to replicate the Atiq Ahmed incident.The incident occurred while Yadav was seated and speaking to the media. According to his media convenor, three or four men suddenly approached the MP and an altercation broke out. He alleged that one of the men first removed a slipper and hurled it before another attacker pulled out a knife."The attackers first took off a slipper and hurled it. When the knife was drawn to attack, our supporters and associates tried to restrain the assailant. I stepped forward and positioned myself between the attacker and Pappu Yadav, and I was beaten severely as a result," the convenor said.
He alleged he was beaten so badly by two or three individuals that he lost consciousness. "My associates carried me away from the spot. I have no further information," he said.A supporter of Yadav who was present said he instinctively put his hand in front of the MP as the knife was swung, causing the blade to graze his finger.
The situation descended into a melee, with people falling and piling on top of one another.
The convenor also alleged that Delhi Police personnel present did not intervene to protect Yadav and instead focused on taking the alleged attackers away. "I tried to help Pappu Yadav escape the scene. The police seemed to be shielding the goons... Not a single policeman stepped forward to help Pappu Yadav escape. When the assault was taking place, they focused solely on saving the goons and whisked them away from the scene. We don't know where they took them," he alleged."These people had come to stage a 'Prayagraj Part Two' â they came to replicate the Atiq Ahmed incident today," the convenor said, referring to the 2023 killing of gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmed and his brother in Prayagraj while they were in police custody.
The convenor said he had met the DCP earlier in the day and submitted a formal complaint warning that the MP was arriving and had been receiving constant threats on social media. "Despite knowing all this, they deployed only three or four police personnel here, and even they were merely protecting the goons," he alleged.He further alleged that several people had been positioned behind the media cameras before the incident. "There were people hiding behind the cameras, three or four of them. Suddenly, someone pulled out a knife, another a slipper... The MP was the target, no one else," he said.According to people present at the scene, the confrontation began after some men allegedly accused Yadav of insulting Sanatan Dharma. The men argued with him before one of them removed a slipper and attempted to throw it. Yadav's supporters then intervened, leading to a scuffle.
Yadav and his supporters have alleged the men were carrying knives and had intentions to kill him. The Delhi Police have not yet issued an official statement on the incident.Yadav himself alleged in a later statementthat the confrontation was an attempt on his life and linked it to threats against his family.âI came here because last night, they went to my childrenâs home. Now, you are trying to intimidate my children too; that wonât happen,â Yadav said. âI was with the press, and a conversation was underway. Amid that, there was an attempt to kill me.âHe alleged that some of those involved were calling for him to be killed, adding, âSome âBabaâ was saying, âBurn him alive,â while others were saying, âKill him.â If people hadnât been here, I would have been finished.âYadav also connected the confrontation to the ongoing controversy over alleged discrepancies involving offerings at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.âI havenât said anything. I only asked Champat Rai or Giri Ji, where did the 200 kg of silver go? Where did the gold go?â he said.
On security concerns, Yadav said he had repeatedly sought protection. âThe Delhi Police is quite capable. I have been demanding security for a long time now. What crime have I committed?â he said.The confrontation comes days after Yadav was involved in a political controversy over a protest by opposition MPs concerning alleged theft of offerings made at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. Yadav, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad and other opposition parliamentarians staged a demonstration in Parliament premises in which they enacted a skit depicting the alleged theft of temple offerings.Yadav wore saffron during the protest and portrayed a temple priest who allegedly took offerings from a donation box. The demonstration drew criticism from seers and others, who accused the MPs of insulting Sanatan Dharma.

headline: In India, a towel draped over an office chair often became a symbol of power, associated with a govt job.
full_text:
In India, a towel draped over an office chair often became a symbol of power, associated with a govt job.
Long ago, my father told me a story about a certain âSunil ji. Nobody ever addressed him by his first name, it was always succeeded by a âjiâ, because his office chair was covered with a towel.He would often wear a safari suit & a stiff-upper lip at family weddings. The guy with a govt job, an Afsar (officer), top billing in the arranged marriage market, despite having the lowest basic pay. At one such wedding, his wife blurted out an issue they were facing. Due to some clerical mistake, the details of their salary account was not updated, and Sunil ji wasnât receiving his salary for over 2 years. They found this anomaly just last month. My family was grudgingly impressed, and hoped one of their kids turned out to be a towel-chair guy like Sunil ji.
For much of modern Indiaâs history, there wasn't enough. Jobs. College seats. Telephones. Gas cylinders. Batsmen with a good strike rate. We were short of everything. As if our nation came out of British rule like some of the TV reporters came out of the NEET protest, Gasping for breath, barely surviving the violence with almost all of the valuables stolen, but their morality, virtue and the associated pride intact.
This was India in 1947.Such was the muscle memory of the rule, that we kept presenting our Annual budget at 5 PM IST, so that our British overlords could tune-in after having their breakfast. This tradition continued till 1999, more than 50 years after independence, until the Finance minister Yashwant Sinha, changed it to 11 AM. Imagine. The trauma of British rule never went away, it showed up in our metabolic wiring, in our insulin resistance, in our early onset of diabetes. Primarily due to the British administered famines. The bodies of our ancestors rewired to store fat. When the Brits eventually went back, they left behind quite a few problematic things like bureaucracy, Pakistan & monumental scarcity.When our leaders took over, they knew our demand vastly exceeded the supply, so they had to control the access of resources. And who do you trust to do that?Another British inheritance - The Collectorate. A regiment of people specifically trained to extract from the population, to collect revenues and give it back to the overlords, for whom serving people was optional, a hobby. A lot of them were corrupt too, In contrast there was barely any corruption among British officers, because they were paid almost 70 times the Indian officers. Hence, the Indians had to compensate with corruption. As we know, they continued compensating beyond independence as well. This coterie was assigned to allocate resources to Indians.No wonder, they acquired tremendous power. People began paying to jump the queue. When the government decided who could manufacture, import or expand a factory, permissions themselves became valuable commodities. British raj was eventually succeeded by Inspector Raj. And the underpaid inspectors lived in the same bungalows the British lived in.Economist Robert Klitgaard famously summarized it as:Corruption = Monopoly + discretion - accountabilityWhenever one person has monopoly over a decision, wide discretion, and little accountability, corruption happens.Accountability was like Vitamin-D for the country. We were always deficient. Add to that a lethargic judiciary. Some even justified corruption saying it's an essential lubricant for files to move without friction. A tool to facilitate ease of doing business. Many of the Indian billionaires today, exist due to their ancestors greasing their file-folders with this lubricant generously.Corruption is a chronic illness, it has been embedded in the DNA of a drought-coded, resource starved nation like ours. A government comes to power riding a wave of public anger. The previous regime is portrayed as irredeemably corrupt. Files are opened. Committees are formed. Raids happen. People are content. Finally, someone is cleaning the system.For a while, it genuinely feels different. Time passes, Power stops feeling temporary. The government begins winning elections. The public approval remains high. Loyalists become more confident. Criticism starts sounding less like feedback and more like conspiracy. Every institution gradually fills up with people who think alike.Corruption creeps up again. Like a virus - a parasite that needs a host - like a mosquito or a bat or a pigeon.Parasites don't advertise themselves. They attach themselves to something stronger. In India's case, this host is often identity - caste, religion, language. Every political movement needs an emotional engine. That engine mobilises voters, creates loyalty and builds political capital. Most of the time these issues are legitimate and deeply important. But once emotions become intense enough, they also become excellent camouflage. People stop asking uncomfortable questions because larger battles appear to be underway.
If my religion is under threat, why discuss the waterlogged street near my house?If my caste is finally receiving justice, why focus on procurement irregularities?Not saying, Identity is not important. But we often forget to see whatâs lurking behind it. The virus keeps growing, and one day it becomes bigger than the host, voters can see it, and it gets overthrown. Exit pollsters get shamed. The power of democracy is lauded. Until a new host emerges. The cycle continues. Elections just change the wrapper of the age-old system.Corruption will go away when we make it high-risk and low-reward. High salaries & high conviction rate. A Singaporean minister earns more than a top investment banker. And their corruption watchdog has a conviction rate of 99%. Our ED has at ~1%. This is the crux, until we fix it - another Sunil ji will discover they have a salary account a decade later.

headline: The water level in the KRS and Kabini reservoirs in the Cauvery basin continued to rise on Sunday as the dams recorded heavy inflows following widespread rainfall in their catchment areas.
full_text:
The water level in the KRS and Kabini reservoirs in the Cauvery basin continued to rise on Sunday as the dams recorded heavy inflows following widespread rainfall in their catchment areas.
While the water level in the KRS reservoir was inching towards the 100-ft. mark, reaching 98.8 ft. against its Full Reservoir Level of 124.8 ft. on Sunday evening, the reservoir was receiving an inflow of 31,583 cusecs. The Kabini reservoir, meanwhile, had almost reached its maximum level.
According to a bulletin issued by the authorities, the water level in the Kabini reservoir stood at 2,282.43 ft. (above mean sea level) against its maximum level of 2,284 ft., with an inflow of 27,217 cusecs on Sunday.
Discharge from Kabini
The authorities were releasing 25,000 cusecs of water into the river through the four crest gates of the Kabini dam on Sunday. About 2,000 cusecs of water is being released into the canal system, the bulletin said.
The increased discharge from the reservoir submerged a low-level bridge near the dam while cutting off connectivity to a few villages in the vicinity.

headline: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday launched the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan', calling on the country's youth to stay physically and mentally fit and remain away from drug abuse.He said achieving the goal of a dev...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday launched the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan', calling on the country's youth to stay physically and mentally fit and remain away from drug abuse.He said achieving the goal of a developed India requires a healthy, confident and drug-free younger generation. During his address, PM Modi also highlighed how the drugs affect one's family and career.Launching the campaign through video conferencing, PM Modi said the initiative is not only for individuals, families and society but also for the nation. He added that the next 100 Sundays would represent 100 strong steps towards a drug-free India.
"Next 100 Sundays will mark 100 strong steps towards drug-free India," he said.PM Modi also warned that drug trafficking was part of a larger strategy by hostile forces to weaken India and called for greater public vigilance. "Hurting India's interests by supplying drugs part of enemy nations' terror plan," he said.
"Today, all countrymen have come together for a great and important resolve. The campaign we are witnessing is meant for individuals, families and society, but above all, it is for the nation. The campaign, 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat', clearly reflects this resolve. As the country moves towards the goal of a developed India, it is essential that our youth remain physically and mentally healthy and stay away from drugs and other such harmful substances."
"The campaign we are witnessing today is for the individual, the family, and society; above all, it is for the nation. The very name of this movementâthe 'Drug-Free Youth' initiative under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan â clarifies its resolve. As the nation sets its sights on becoming a Viksit Bharat, it is essential that our youth be healthy in body and mind, brimming with self-confidence, and forever free from the deadly habit of drugs. This is the objective of the campaign... This campaign was launched last year as a pilot project from Kashi... Over 125 spiritual organizations have joined us today for the welfare of crores of our fellow citizens."
"By being addiction-free, you need to protect your potential. You need to be aware that drugs get you high for a short time, but take your career and family to a new low/bottom.
From Varanasi to nationwide campaign
"As the MP from Kashi, I am happy that this campaign was launched last year from the sacred land of Kashi as a pilot project. Along with scientific clarity, it also carries spiritual energy. Social organisations and NGOs have joined this initiative for the welfare of crores of Indians. Together, they have prepared a roadmap through the Kashi Declaration. Today, we are witnessing how the welfare-oriented idea that emerged from Kashi has become a national project. From today, the Nasha Mukt Yuva campaign is being launched across the country."
"The 'Nasha Mukta Yuva Abhiyaan' is launching across the country today... There is immense power in collective action, and today, driven by that very strength, this campaign is set to touch the heart of every young person. Lakhs of youths across the nation took a pledge to stay free from drugs... The pledge taken today will continue to move forward steadily over the next hundred weeks."
"Drug use disturbs focus, takes you away from dreams. If a youth gets addicted to drugs, his aspirations take a hit, family gets shattered."
Govt's anti-drug drive and national campaign
"Today, the government stands firmly with the youth in the campaign against drugs. Strict action is being taken in the country against drug traffickers and drug abuse; there have been many times more arrests compared to before, and drugs worth thousands of crores of rupees have been seized. This shows how tough our government is against drugs."
"Today, thousands of students from schools, colleges and universities are connected online to this programme. Even lakhs of volunteers of MY Bharat are also connected. The NSS jawans too have joined us. People from different sectors, institutions and backgrounds--more than 1 crore youths are together today. I congratulate all of you for this big movement."
Youth key to Viksit Bharat, drugs part of enemy agenda
"You are India's Amrit Peedhi. You will shape your lives over the next 20-25 years, and you will lead the country to the goal of a Viksit Bharat in 2047, and you will be at the helm. You will be the ones to reap its full benefits."
"The country needs your energy, your imagination, and your talent, so staying drug-free is crucial for the country and for your own lives."
"When a young person falls prey to drug addiction, it is not just that individual who loses; a dream is lost. Hostile nations conspire and leave no stone unturned to drag our youth into the trap of addiction. Profiting from the supply of drugs while aiming to destroy a country like ours is part of their terror-driven agenda."
Parents, teachers and society must lead the fight
"We must always keep this in mind: if any child from our home has become a victim of addiction, do not hide it under the guise of social prestige. Seek help from whoever is needed."
"Make efforts to free your child from addiction with medical help."
"We should also foster a culture of open communication with children in the family, so that you can hold their hand before they get caught in such a whirlpool."
"Along with teaching the courses, please also discuss the dangers of drugs with the students. Launch a movement against addiction on your campus. Your efforts can bring big results."
"The support of society, the power of yoga and meditation--these strengthen our inner resolve against addiction. And today, we also have facilities like rehabilitation centres to help quit drugs." "I appeal to all of you that you are all the leaders of this great movement. You have further strengthened my belief that the youth of India is so aware, so sensible, and so serious about their duties."
The 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan' aims to encourage young people to stay away from substance abuse and become ambassadors of positive social change in their communities.
The launch marks the beginning of a 100-week nationwide Jan Bhagidari campaign, under which awareness programmes will be organised every Sunday across the country.Activities will include sports events, walkathons, meditation sessions, cultural programmes, street plays, discussions, art competitions and community engagement initiatives.The campaign brings together educational institutions, youth organisations, civil society groups, industry bodies and more than 125 spiritual organisations to build a collective movement against substance abuse.Youth from over 10,000 locations across the country are participating through schools, colleges, universities, MY Bharat volunteers, NSS volunteers, youth clubs, NGOs and industry associations.
Priyanshi Rastogi is a journalist with The Times of India. She primarily covers national and international news, along with business affairs. Her work focuses on the latest political events, in-depth explainers, features, offbeat articles and viral social media trending stories.

headline: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Sunday came under sharp criticism from the Opposition over flood management as well as his participation in private functions during the floods. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State secretariat said i...
full_text:
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Sunday came under sharp criticism from the Opposition over flood management as well as his participation in private functions during the floods. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State secretariat said in a statement on Sunday that the Chief Minister, who also heads the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority, should not stand aside and delegate responsibility to Ministers.
“The primary duty of an administrator is to protect the lives and property of the people. Not fulfilling that can only be seen as a defiant attitude towards the public. Pathanamthitta and Idukki districts, which received the most rainfall, had only an orange alert until Saturday morning. The fact that many areas were under water by the time the red alert was announced is evidence of mismanagement. No steps were taken to relocate people to safe places and evacuate them from danger-prone areas,” said the CPI(M).
The CPI(M) alleged that the Coastal Police arrived 13 hours late to rescue the fishermen whose boat capsized near Muthalapozhi in Thiruvananthapuram. A video shared by Muslim Youth League vice-president Faisal Bafaqui Thangal of Mr. Satheesan participating in a lunch at his house in Ponnani on Saturday as well as the reports of the Chief Minister using the government’s helicopter for private purposes also invited criticism from the Opposition.
“The fact that the helicopter rented by the government was used for a private purpose and that a feast was being held when the people were suffering has led to severe public criticism of the Chief Minister. The State rented the helicopter to use it for disaster-relief activities and in times of need. The then Leader of the Opposition who criticised the LDF government when it rented the helicopter and called it wasteful expenditure is now using it for private purposes,” said the CPI(M).
Don’t politicise: MLA
Congress MLA C. Noushad Ali of Ponnani said such issues should not be politicised to target the Chief Minister during times of disaster. “Shouldn’t the Chief Minister go anywhere or have food during the rainy season? Such campaigns against him are politically motivated,” he told press persons. Contrasting Mr. Satheesan’s conduct during the flood with that of Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan during his term as the Chief Minister, the CPI(M) said Mr. Vijayan and his office had stayed vigilant round-the-clock, coordinating rescue efforts.
“When journalists asked Mr. Satheesan about the flood situation on Saturday, he took an indifferent approach and said that his office would brief them. It is worth recollecting that during the LDF’s tenure, Mr. Vijayan used to interact constantly with the press during such crisis situations. Through this, it was possible to give confidence to the people and also make them alert,” said the CPI(M).
‘No warnings’
In a separate statement, Mr. Vijayan said it is unacceptable that the negligence and lack of coordination on the part of the government has worsened people’s sufferings amid the floods. “It is being alleged that proper warnings were not issued before the opening of a dam near Ranni. Traders did not even get time to secure the goods in their shops. The negligence in the relief camps is also worrying. The government agencies themselves have admitted that there was a lapse in food distribution. Due to the lack of coordination by the officials, volunteers, local people and political activists had to prepare and distribute the food. The government should also examine the lapses and prevent them from recurring,” said Mr. Vijayan.
