full_text:
Stone-pelting by CJP protesters happened even after Parliament march violence: Officials
The violence by protesters was contained with enforcement agencies exercising restraint despite servere aggravation.
Stone-pelting by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s protesters and political actiivists in the heart of Delhi carried on for over at least six days, but police acted with restraint to defuse the tensions, according to security officials aware of the developments.
The officials also shared details of locations that became flashpoints, as well as damaged or missing government properties during the protests over the alleged paper leak in the NEET-UG examination. HT has accessed the list.
According to the officials cited above, a section of people with vested political interests and political parties infiltrated the crowd of genuine students who had gathered at Jantar Mantar, and stoked violence.
On July 20, the day of the CJP's march to Parliament when the House was in session, clashes broke out, and law enforcement officials had to resort to a cane charge and tear gas amid allegations of police excesses. Security officials said the action against protesters should not be seen in isolation, and that it came after repeated warnings against provocation and aggression, including stone-pelting and the breaking of barricades in a high-security zone.
Also read: Jaish operative held in Bengal planned to target Suvendu, sabotage Jantar Mantar protest: STF
Stone-pelting incidents continued even after the Parliament march violence—right till July 25, when the CJP ended its protest after the government accepted its demands, including the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, the officials said. They added that police handled all incidents without any escalation, given the sensitivity of the matter.
According to the document accessed by HT, the flashpoints during the protest were concentrated within a roughly 2-kilometre radius, indicating that the incidents were spread across key roads and intersections near Parliament rather than being confined to a single location.
Also read: Day after 'forgive' remark, PM Modi praises youth for powering India's growth
The places of occurrence were Gol Dak Khana, the Tolstoy-Janpath Crossing (Restaurant Corridor and Parking), the Rafi Marg barricade near Rail Bhawan, Jantar Mantar, Outer Circle near the LIC Building in Connaught Place, multiple locations along the Tolstoy-Sansad Marg corridor, Sansad Marg near the SBI Building, Raisina Road near the Press Club of India, and the Regal Building towards the Sansad Marg-Tolstoy red light.
The location closest to Parliament was the Rafi Marg barricade near Rail Bhawan, while other locations ranged from 0.8 km to 2 km away, according to the document, which also said stone-pelting was reported at all the locations.
The document also detailed damage to and loss of government property during the violence. According to the list, 110 barricades and 171 ropes were damaged or went missing, along with operational equipment such as a wireless set, a body-worn camera, 10 handheld metal detectors (HHMDs), two public address systems, 15 loudhailers, 10 fire extinguishers, four wire cutters and an X-ray baggage scanner. Protective gear, including 355 helmets, 285 body protectors, 54 shields, 10 torches, 24 first-aid boxes and 12 blankets, was also reported missing or damaged.
In addition, 29 official vehicles (including cars, buses, motorcycles and tempos) were affected, along with a water tanker, a DTC bus and one public vehicle, the document said.
The document added that 244 police personnel and 209 civilians sustained injuries that were recorded as Medico-Legal Cases (MLCs).
Security officials had earlier told HT that the use of force during the CJP's march to Parliament was the culmination of escalation, repeated warnings, barricade breaches, vehicle damage, and continued unprovoked heckling of both police and the press.
According to a widely reported internal Delhi Police report submitted to the government, more than 100 people facing murder charges and hundreds accused in robbery, sexual offences, Arms Act and narcotics cases were identified through facial recognition technology during the violence at the CJP's march.

headline: SHIMLA/PITHIRAGARH: India and China resumed traditional border trade Saturday through Lipulekh in Uttarakhand and Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh after nearly six years, restoring two key Himalayan trade routes that had remained closed since the Covid-...
full_text:
SHIMLA/PITHIRAGARH: India and China resumed traditional border trade Saturday through Lipulekh in Uttarakhand and Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh after nearly six years, restoring two key Himalayan trade routes that had remained closed since the Covid-19 pandemic.At Lipulekh in Uttarakhand's Pithoragarh district, the first batch of 16 traders and four support staff crossed into Tibet without goods as the two sides began restoring trade operations. Chinese authorities restricted the inaugural batch to 20 people, citing infrastructure constraints at the Taklakot trade mart and sought detailed personal information of all traders in advance. They also asked that priority be given to those who had participated in the last trading season in 2019.Accordingly, the traders' association selected traders whose goods had remained stranded at Taklakot after trade was suspended in 2020. "Priority was given to traders who had participated in the 2019 trading season and had left their goods at Taklakot," Dharchula SDM and district trade officer Ashish Joshi said.Meanwhile, in Himachal Pradesh, revenue minister Jagat Singh Negi flagged off the first batch of 16 Indian traders as they set off with their horses towards Shipki village in Tibet through the 3,930-metre-high Shipki La Pass.
The trade, suspended since 2020 because of Covid, was scheduled to resume on June 1 but was delayed owing to security concerns and inadequate infrastructure at the trading post.Trade through Shipki La, which will remain open until Nov 30, will continue under the traditional barter system. Indian traders will be allowed to stay across the border for up to 72 hours, while the home department has cleared 53 traders after verification of their antecedents.Indian traders have been permitted to export 36 categories of goods, including dried fruits, spices, handicrafts and herbs, while Chinese traders can bring 20 categories of goods, including pashmina, wool, yak hair, sheepskin, goatskin and China clay. Officials said the overall list comprised 72 categories of tradable goods from the Indian side and 30 from the Chinese side.
Negi also inaugurated the Rs 1.7 crore Chhuppan Trade Mart at Namgya village in Pooh subdivision near the international border to facilitate border trade. Replying to a demand by local traders to expand the list of tradable goods, Negi said the proposal would be placed before CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and also with MEA.The routes were scheduled to reopen on June 1 but were delayed because of pending infrastructure and administrative preparations on both sides of the border. tnn (With inputs from Prem Punetha in Pithoragarh)

headline: From satire to sit-in is the most popular, and perhaps the easiest, explanation for the student protest movement that culminated in the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. This explanation is empowering in its simplicity. But ...
full_text:
From satire to sit-in is the most popular, and perhaps the easiest, explanation for the student protest movement that culminated in the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. This explanation is empowering in its simplicity. But it is incomplete.
By now, everyone knows how the story goes. On May 15, 2026, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant likened unemployed youth turning to activism and social media to “cockroaches”, triggering widespread backlash. Seizing on the remark, Abhijeet Dipke, an Indian student in Boston, launched a satirical online platform for fellow “cockroaches”, transforming an insult into a rallying cry for disaffected youth. Within the first 24 hours, 50,000 people signed up. That number swelled to more than a million within five days, while the movement’s Instagram account surged past 22 million followers.
Yet behind the viral posts, soaring follower counts and colourful symbolism stood a trio: Abhijeet Dipke (30), Ashutosh Ranka (30) and Saurav Das (27), whose skills complemented one another. They come from different parts of the country, different social backgrounds and possess markedly different temperaments.
Those who have spent time around Jantar Mantar since the movement began describe Mr. Dipke as politically intuitive, though at times a touch emotional, and the beating heart of the movement. On July 18, after activist Sonam Wangchuk was removed from Jantar Mantar, it was Mr. Dipke who argued that the movement should escalate its demands. Instead of limiting itself to seeking Mr. Pradhan’s resignation, he proposed demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Mr. Dipke loves discussing A.R. Rahman’s music and reciting Shah Rukh Khan’s dialogues from Swades. He brought a sense of lightness to the protest, spending time in the evenings talking to the protesters, posing for pictures with them and cracking a joke every now and then.
Mr. Ranka, meanwhile, has been described as decisive, though at times authoritarian, and quicker to lose his temper than others. He remains the mind of the movement and its principal strategist. Mr. Das, the youngest of the three, is known as much for his affable demeanour as for his outreach skills, though colleagues say he can occasionally be indecisive.
If Mr. Ranka and Mr. Dipke rave about Shah Rukh Khan starrer Swades and Aamir Khan’s Rang De Basanti, Mr. Das represents the other end of the social spectrum where his favourite series is Modern Family — a mockumentary about a multigenerational family based out of Los Angeles.
Association with AAP
One obvious thread connecting the three is their association with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), a link none of them has sought to conceal. Both Mr. Dipke and Mr. Ranka have worked for the party, while Mr. Das’s proximity to former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal is hardly a secret.
Mr. Dipke was born in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (formerly Aurangabad), Maharashtra, into a Dalit family, though his caste identity largely remained in the background during the protest. “He is a student leader who is also a Dalit and not the other way round,” a leader associated with the 36-day protest said. One occasion on which he publicly asserted his caste identity came after ink was thrown at him at Jantar Mantar on July 18. His response was brief: “Blue is my colour. Jai Bhim.”
He studied journalism at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth in Pune before moving to the U.S. in 2023 to pursue a Master’s degree in Public Relations at Boston University. Mr. Dipke worked in political communications and was associated with the AAP social media team between 2020 and 2023, working closely with senior leader Manish Sisodia.
Mr. Ranka’s journey to the CJP was unlike that of most protest leaders. Born and raised in Jaipur, he studied Materials Science and Engineering at IIT-Kanpur, where he was elected president of the Students’ Gymkhana, an early indication of his interest in public life.
He served as a Delhi Assembly Fellow during 2019-20, working closely with the team of former Delhi Chief Minister and current Leader of Opposition Atishi during the pandemic, before pursuing a Master’s in Public Administration at the London School of Economics. He subsequently worked with McKinsey & Company and with Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, before gradually moving away from the worlds of consulting and international policy in favour of Indian public life.
Mr. Ranka also worked on the AAP campaign for the February 2025 Delhi Assembly election, focusing exclusively on the New Delhi constituency, where Mr. Kejriwal was the candidate. He was part of the team examining voter deletions and continued to publicly defend Mr. Kejriwal and the party even after the election. His most recent article as AAP’s “national spokesperson” was published on March 16.
Unlike many political organisers, Mr. Ranka has never hidden his ambitions. He has often expressed a desire to focus on Rajasthan politics. Following the 2025 Assembly election, he turned his attention to the State, running campaigns to protect a 100-acre forest near Jaipur. More recently, he gave Rajasthan Education Minister Madan Dilawar a three-month ultimatum to address issues faced by students at Rajasthan University, warning that the CJP would otherwise seek the vice-chancellor’s resignation.
Saurav Das, the movement’s young spokesman, became its public face. A journalist before he became a protest leader, he understood how newsrooms functioned, how narratives were shaped and, more important, how to keep a movement in the headlines.
Mr. Das spent part of his childhood in Puducherry and speaks a smattering of Tamil. He studied Journalism and Mass Communication at Amity University, Noida, graduating in 2019. He is best known for his detailed profile of former Chief Justice of India D.Y. Chandrachud for The Caravan, and has also written for Frontline and other publications.
‘The language of Gen Z’
Mr. Das is also the co-founder of Climate Action Front, an initiative focused on climate governance, sustainability and environmental policy. Alongside journalism, he has been working on his debut book, Complicit Silence: The Court’s Role in India’s Quiet Suffering, which examines the judiciary’s role in contemporary India through a series of case studies involving citizens seeking justice. Videos of Mr. Das dancing after Mr. Pradhan’s resignation also went viral, attracting admiration as well as criticism. Mr. Das defended the celebrations as “the language of Gen Z”, arguing that young people express political victories differently.
None of the three had ever led a protest of this scale before they laid siege to the government near the 18th century observatory, Jantar Mantar. Nor had the majority of the protesters who took to the streets of Delhi, in response to their call. For now, the three insist that the CJP will continue to function as a pressure group rather than a political party.

headline: 36-year-old MNC employee found hanging in Gurugram, wife detained
full_text:
36-year-old MNC employee found hanging in Gurugram, wife detained
A Gurugram man was found hanging at home, and police have detained his wife for questioning. The death has triggered foul play allegations from his family as investigators await the postmortem report.
A 36-year-old associate operator at a multinational company was found hanging at his house in Gurugram's Surat Nagar area, police said on Saturday. Police identified him as Sanjeev Yadav, a native of Amritsar who lived there with his family.
The case is being investigated after Yadav's family alleged foul play and said there had been a dispute between him and his wife, who had sought a divorce. Police said his wife has been detained and the matter is being examined from every angle.
According to police, Yadav's body was found hanging on Thursday when only his wife, Manpreet Kaur, and their seven-year-old son were at home. Police said it was also reported that the child recorded a video on his mobile phone while watching his father hanging, while his mother screamed for someone to take him down. Manpreet then called her own family and Sanjeev's parents to inform them about the death.
Yadav's sister Kiran alleged that there had been a dispute between her brother and his wife and said that otherwise he could not have hanged himself. She also said the circumstances of his death must be investigated and described the video showing him hanging from the fan as suspicious, noting that her brother weighed more than 100 kg. Yadav's father Ramsevak Yadav said a dispute had been going on between the couple for some time and alleged that his daughter-in-law conspired with others to murder his son.
Police said Sanjeev and Manpreet, who is from Ambala, had a love marriage on April 29, 2018. They had met about eight years earlier while working at Denso in Gurugram and later got married. Sanjeev had been living in Gurugram since the wedding. Manpreet gave birth to their son in 2019 and left her job soon after.
Sub-inspector Mahender Singh, the investigating officer, said, "We handed over the body to kin after the postmortem and are investigating from every angle. The post-mortem report of the deceased is awaited, which will reveal the exact cause of death and action will be taken as per the law." The case centres on the death of Sanjeev Yadav, the family's allegations against his wife, and the police investigation now under way.

headline: In a series of changes for the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (Postgraduate) scheduled for August 30, the Centre is set to expand the choice of test locations, give candidates more time to plan travel to their examination cities, and give the...
full_text:
In a series of changes for the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (Postgraduate) scheduled for August 30, the Centre is set to expand the choice of test locations, give candidates more time to plan travel to their examination cities, and give them more time per question in the test.
The reforms are aimed at making the process more convenient for the candidates, according to the Union Health Ministry.
Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda on Saturday (August 1, 2026) reviewed the preparedness for NEET (PG) 2026 and directed all agencies to ensure the examination is conducted in a smooth, secure, transparent and technology-enabled manner. He assessed the readiness of National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS), technology partners, and other stakeholders and stressed that every effort must be made to ensure a fair and candidate-friendly examination.
"The end-to-end question paper preparation and delivery process has been further reinforced through multiple layers of encryption, secure offline preparation, time-bound finalisation of the question paper shortly before the examination, and controlled digital decryption only at the scheduled commencement of the test," the Ministry said in a statement.
The NBEMS has also operationalised a dedicated email address for reporting impersonation, touting, and other unfair practices while issuing regular advisories to candidates to promote awareness and vigilance.
The Ministry said that to strengthen the integrity of the examination process, Aadhaar-based authentication has been introduced during both the application process and on the examination day. Iris-based biometric verification will be used wherever fingerprint authentication is unsuccessful, it said.
Under the revised system, candidates will indicate three State preferences for their examination centre, with their correspondence State being the mandatory first preference, enabling allotment of centres closer to their place of residence, the Ministry said.
Earlier, exam cities were allotted on a first come, first-served basis prompting candidates to rush to submit their applications as soon as the registration window opened, a source explained. Those who delayed often found all nearby centres filled, forcing them to travel to other States to appear for the exam.
In another key change, candidates will be informed of their allotted test city nearly three weeks before the examination, giving them more time to plan travel and accommodation, the Ministry said.
The NBEMS has also rationalised the examination pattern to 180 questions to be answered in 210 minutes, allowing candidates more time per question while retaining the overall duration of the test, it said.
The exam previously had 200 multiple choice questions with a maximum score of 800 marks.
The source said that recently, the exam had been conducted in two shifts due to emergencies or postponements but the 2026 edition will be held in a single shift to ensure uniformity in the difficulty level and assessment of candidates.
Earlier, candidates often faced stress as the final venue and location details were released very close to the test date, leaving minimal time to book travel or accommodation, the official added.
A total of 2,73,183 candidates have registered for NEET (PG) 2026, an increase of over 12.5% compared with last year. The examination will be conducted in a single shift across around 340 cities and more than 1,300 examination centres.
Comprehensive security arrangements have been put in place for the examination, including advance sealing and verification of examination centres, CCTV surveillance, biometric authentication, candidate frisking, deployment of signal jammers, dynamic comput, live monitoring through central and regional command centres, and real-time supervision by independent observers and appraisers.
More than 60,000 examination functionaries will be deployed to ensure the smooth conduct of the examination, the ministry said.

headline: Supreme Court's Justice Bhuyan backs more transparency in collegium’s operation
full_text:
Supreme Court's Justice Bhuyan backs more transparency in collegium’s operation
Releasing a report on the Judicial Transparency Index, Justice Bhuyan said that not giving reasons is a disservice to many genuinely outstanding judges.
Justice Ujjal Bhuyan of the Supreme Court on Saturday observed that collegium resolutions are not being forwarded with reasons, questioning whether this was a “step back” from the principle of transparency that the judiciary has always embraced.
Releasing a report on the Judicial Transparency Index at an event in the Capital, justice Bhuyan said that not giving reasons is a disservice to many genuinely outstanding judges. Conversely, he said: “By withholding reasons, we also create space for individuals to enter the judiciary who may later describe groups of people as ‘ants’ and make other remarks that are wholly unconstitutional and contrary to the values of the Constitution.”
He was apparently referring to a controversial speech made by a former Allahabad high court judge at a VHP event in 2024 in a veiled reference to Muslims.
Also Read | ‘Collegium system well-suited for India': South Korea SC judge Justice Daeyup Chun | HT Interview
Justice Bhuyan said, “A judiciary that has embraced publicity in its adjudicative function has been markedly more cautious about extending the same principle to its own constitutive processes.”
He cited three recent Supreme Court collegium statements that do not contain any reason for recommending elevations as opposed to the earlier trend when detailed reasons accompanied resolutions forwarded by the collegium. “Is this a step back from the principle of transparency,” he asked.
Also Read | Collegium recommendation review will open ‘pandora’s box’: SC
He further observed that deliberations in the collegium remain confidential and reasons for rejecting or deferring a recommendation are rarely disclosed in full and the criteria applied are not codified in any publicly accessible instrument comparable to the Memorandum of Procedure.
Batting for open courts, he said, “There is no doubt that open courts make it possible for the public to develop reasonable perceptions about the judiciary, by enabling them to directly observe judicial behaviour, the processes and outcome of cases.”
Also Read | ‘Too important to discard, too imperfect to ignore’: The collegium system is flawed but necessary
On the recent SC hearing where use of judicial proceedings on social media was sought to be regulated, justice Bhuyan said the move by the CJI-led bench does not retreat from live-streaming. “Court’s concern is precisely that decontextualised fragments of oral exchanges, observations made by judges in the course of argument, not findings, are being circulated with sensational captions, causing reputational harm to judges, advocates, and litigants...”

SEEKS UNIFORM SOPs FOR POLICE ACTION

The restaurant owners acknowledged the mistake and assured the Indian boxing contingent that it would be corrected.The incident took place when the Indian boxing team visited Mister Singh's India, The Home of Curry for a celebratory dinner after securing a record 10 medals, seven gold and three silver, at the Commonwealth Games.Lovlina noticed that the restaurant's branding showed an incomplete map of India without the Northeast. Boxing Federation of India (BFI) president Ajay Singh, who was present at the restaurant, said there was no confrontation and that the issue was resolved amicably."There was no confrontation. headline: Major rivers in the district, including the Kadalundipuzha, the Chaliyar and the Bharathapuzha, remained swollen on Sunday (August 2, 2026) after two days of heavy rain. The rain stayed away during the day, with sunny spells providing temporary relie...
full_text:
Major rivers in the district, including the Kadalundipuzha, the Chaliyar and the Bharathapuzha, remained swollen on Sunday (August 2, 2026) after two days of heavy rain. The rain stayed away during the day, with sunny spells providing temporary relief. But but showers resumed in the evening.
The authorities kept 129 persons from 39 families in seven relief camps across Eranad, Kondotty and Nilambur taluks. The evacuees include 42 men, 51 women, and 36 children.
The Bakkikkayam regulator on the Kadalundipuzha remained above the warning level, prompting alerts at Vengara, Thennala, Ozhur, Oorakam, Parappur, Edarikode, Kannamangalam, A.R. Nagar, Othukkungal, Perumanna Klari, Tirurangadi and Kottakkal municipality.
Warnings were also issued for Angadippuram, Puzhakkattiri, Makkaraparamba, Kuruva and Koottilangadi after the Cherupuzha overflowed. Evacuations continued in flood- and landslide-prone areas based on vulnerability lists prepared by local bodies. The district administration warned of more rain over the next three days.
The recent rain caused flooding, landslips, and traffic disruption across the district. A compound wall of an anganwadi at Madarakundu, Kavanur, collapsed, damaging a nearby house. Landslides were reported from Kannamangalam and other areas, while a house under construction at Anchachavidi, Kalikavu, collapsed.
Overflowing streams flooded houses at Edavanna, forcing residents to move to safer places. Flooding disrupted traffic on the Pulikkal-Anthiyurkunnu road and caused congestion on the Kozhikode-Palakkad highway.
Sea erosion continued along the coast at Ponnani, Veliyankode, Perumpadappu and Parappanangadi. More than 100 houses were flooded in the Ponnani area, and several sustained partial damage. The authorities advised people to avoid travel to hilly areas.
District Collector Vinod Goyal has declared a holiday for all educational institutions, including professional colleges, on Monday (August 3, 2026) due to continuing heavy rain in the district. The holiday applies to madrasas, tuition centres and anganwadis as well. However, pre-scheduled university and PSC examinations will be conducted as planned.

headline: As relief and rehabilitation efforts continue across flood-ravaged Pathanamthitta, the focus is rapidly shifting from rescue to accountability, with allegations of administrative lapses and poor disaster management dominating the political discourse.
full_text:
As relief and rehabilitation efforts continue across flood-ravaged Pathanamthitta, the focus is rapidly shifting from rescue to accountability, with allegations of administrative lapses and poor disaster management dominating the political discourse.
The sharpest criticism came from CPI(M) Pathanamthitta district secretary Raju Abraham, who described the deluge as a `government-sponsored flood’. He accused the authorities of failing to issue timely red alerts and opening dam shutters without adequate public warning, and demanded compensation for all those who suffered losses.
“The authorities neither issued a proper red alert nor gave advance warning before opening the dam shutters. The lack of timely information from both the government and weather monitoring agencies caused widespread anxiety among the public and resulted in losses worth crores,” he alleged.
According to Mr.Abraham,the Moozhiyar and Kariyarkayam dams were opened at 1 a.m. Under the existing protocol, the authorities are required to inform elected representatives, local self-government institutions and the Public Relations Department before releasing water. Public announcements through loudspeakers should also have been made to alert residents. However, the government failed to follow any of these procedures. Had even a public announcement been made, people would have had time to move their belongings to safety and take the necessary precautions, he pointed out.
He also claimed that DYFI volunteers had to undertake cleaning operations because the official response was delayed.
Questions have also been raised over the government’s preparedness and the coordination of relief operations. Residents and public representatives alleged that relief camps lacked basic facilities, flood-hit areas did not receive adequate support and coordination among various departments remained patchy at a time when swift action was crucial.
Taking a serious note of the situation, Aranmula MLA, Abin Varkey urged the government to extend additional assistance to the constituency, saying it was among the worst-hit regions and required greater support. Ranni MLA, Pazhakulam Madhu likened the aftermath of the floods to `a battlefield after the battle’ and said local teams were doing their best with the limited resources at their disposal while appealing for more government assistance. Complaints also surfaced over inadequate facilities at a relief camp in Aranmula.
Even in Ranni, where post-flood cleaning operations were being coordinated under the leadership of the MLA, residents alleged that official support remained inadequate and inter-departmental coordination continued to be poor.
Responding to the criticism, Revenue Minister A.P. Anil Kumar said the government would step up rehabilitation efforts and improve facilities in the coming days. District in-charge Minister P.C. Vishnunath also remained in the district to oversee the relief and rehabilitation work in the flood-affected areas.

headline: Exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasrin on Sunday (August 2, 2026) called for all countries of the Indian subcontinent to implement a Uniform Civil Code (UCC), arguing that this was needed to protect women from discrimination.
full_text:
Exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasrin on Sunday (August 2, 2026) called for all countries of the Indian subcontinent to implement a Uniform Civil Code (UCC), arguing that this was needed to protect women from discrimination.
“Uniform Civil Code is a must. This is the first step for any civilised society,” Ms. Nasrin said, interacting with journalists in Kolkata. The Bengali writer said that she has been fighting for the UCC for the past 40 years and added that “if women come under religious laws, there is discrimination and persecution”. Delivering a speech in Kolkata on Saturday (August 1), she had said that India, Bangladesh, and Pakistan should have a uniform law for all their citizens.
“Due to religious laws, women are suffering. Hindus are being tortured in Bangladesh. During the Yunus regime, Hindus were tortured even more. In many madrasas and mosques, hatred is being taught against Hindus. Now we have Jamaat-e-Islami as an Opposition party. It is against women’s equality, and they want Sharia rule,” she said, reflecting on the situation in her home country.
The author’s remarks come at a time when the West Bengal government has announced plans to implement UCC in the State and has set up a committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge to look into the provisions of a draft UCC Bill.
Return to Kolkata
Ms. Nasrin arrived in Kolkata on July 31, almost 19 years after she was forced to leave the city due to violent protests by a mob upset with her writings during the Left Front government. Prior to this, she was exiled from Bangladesh in 1994.
Her return to Kolkata was celebrated by West Bengal’s first BJP government, even as she shared the stage with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Asked for her view on different governments in the State, she said, “One government had forced me out, another did not allow me to return, and one government has helped me to return,” she said.
‘Some madrasas produce jihadis’
Ms. Nasrin also came down hard against madrasas, saying that some of these “religious schools produce jihadis”. “In my opinion, madrasas should not exist. Not in all cases, but in some, it is seen that jihadis are being produced in madrasas,” the writer said. Alleging that “child abuse is going on there, rapes are happening, and imams and madrasa teachers are being held,” she opined that “there is no need for madrasas to exist.”
“No one does anything after passing out of madrasas. They beg, survive on charity. Madrasas should go, and secular schools should come up instead,” Ms. Nasrin said.
Freedom of speech
The Bengali writer also expressed anguish over an incident during Saturday’s (August 1) event, where the crowd prevented Bengali poet Joy Goswami from addressing the gathering. The poet is considered to be close to the Trinamool Congress regime. Ms. Nasrin had called Mr. Goswami to take his seat on the stage when the people gathered started shouting.
“Not only was Mr. Goswami insulted, but I was also insulted because I had invited him,” she said. “In my speech, I spoke about freedom of expression. Everyone should be allowed to speak. It is not right to stop anyone from expressing their views,” she said.

headline: Shame on Hemant Soren: Jharkhand students seek CBI probe into JPSC exams lapses
full_text:
Shame on Hemant Soren: Jharkhand students seek CBI probe into JPSC exams lapses
Jharkhand students have continued an indefinite sit-in in Ranchi against alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC exams. Their protest has sharpened pressure on the Jharkhand government for an independent probe and recruitment reforms.
Hundreds of students in Jharkhand continued their protest for the fifth consecutive day on Sunday over alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC examination, JSSC-CGL and other recruitment tests. They demanded a CBI probe into the alleged lapses and reforms in the state's recruitment agencies.
The protesters have been holding an indefinite sit-in at a stadium in Ranchi since July 29. They are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test held on April 19, an independent probe by central agencies including the CBI and Enforcement Directorate, and the introduction of a fifth option of 'not attempted' in OMR sheets.
During the protest, students raised slogans such as 'Order CBI probe in JPSC', 'Long live Students Unity' and 'Shame on Hemant Soren'.
JPSC aspirant Rahul Kumar Kranti said, "Paper leaks in JPSC have happened several times. This time, OMR sheets of candidates have been leaked. Chief Minister Hemant Soren has ordered a CID probe, but we are not satisfied." He alleged that earlier probes into the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission CGL paper leak had not led to action and claimed that the latest investigation could also be "covered up" after a few months.
Kranti said, "We have completely lost faith in the ongoing CID probe. We demand a CBI probe into all recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC over the past seven years. We also demand the chief minister's resignation on moral grounds."
Ankit Kumar from Giridih district said, "The careers of thousands of students and aspirants are at stake due to corruption in both agencies. Most of us come from farmers' families. We only want fair opportunities based on merit." Sneha, a tribal student from Ranchi, said the protesters wanted strict punishment for those involved in the alleged irregularities and cancellation of the 14th JPSC examination.
"I have been preparing for competitive examinations since 2023. But if an equal and fair chance is not given, how can I get a job? I urge CM Soren to listen to our demands," she said.
Archana Kumari from Palamu said the protesters would continue their agitation until the government addressed their demands and fixed accountability for the alleged irregularities. Shyam Bihari Gupta, a student from Balumath in Latehar district, said, "The state government is still in a sleeping mode. We are getting support from across the country. People from various cities are sending food items to the protest site. We are thankful to those helping us continue our protest."
The protest remained focused on demands for cancellation of the April 19 test, a wider independent investigation and changes in the recruitment process.

headline: Odisha Cabinet clears Bill for economic region authorities
full_text:
Odisha Cabinet clears Bill for economic region authorities
The Cabinet also approved the second phase of the state’s flagship tribal livelihood programme, the Mukhya Mantri Janajati Jeevika Mission
Odisha Cabinet on Saturday cleared a proposal to introduce the Odisha Development Authorities (Amendment) Bill, 2026 to amend the existing Odisha Development Authorities Act, 1982 for constituting Economic Region Development Authorities.
These Economic Region Development Authorities will be empowered to govern multi-district economic corridors, allowing the state government to seamlessly notify and establish future economic regions without the need to pass fresh legislative enactments every time.
Once the amendments are formally approved by the Odisha assembly, the state will constitute its first official City Economic Region: the Bhubaneswar-Kataka-Puri-Paradeep Economic Region (BKPPER).
Developed as a pilot project in collaboration with the federal think-tank NITI Aayog, BKPPER aims to integrate ports, industrial hubs, urban centers, logistics networks, and places of religious and cultural importance into a single, highly coordinated economic geography.
The Union Budget 2026-27 recently recognised BKPPER as one of four vital City Economic Regions in India poised to serve as engines of national economic growth, alongside Varanasi, Surat, and Vishakhapatnam.
Chief secretary Anu Garg said that regional master plans for these agglomerations will look beyond traditional municipal boundaries to leverage complementary economic potential, attract heavy investment, and improve overall public mobility and housing.
Other planned agglomerations under this phased development include Bargarh-Jharsuguda-Sambalpur, Berhampur-Chhatrapur-Gopalpur, and Jeypore-Koraput-Sunabeda.
The Cabinet also approved the second phase of the state’s flagship tribal livelihood programme, the Mukhya Mantri Janajati Jeevika Mission (MMJJM 2.0) to target eight lakh Tribal and Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) households, up from 1.5 lakh households in 13 districts in the first phase.
The expanded phase will span across 19 districts, encompassing 134 Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) and Micro Project Area (MPA) blocks, 23 Integrated Tribal Development Agencies (ITDAs), and 20 Micro Project Areas (MPAs).
The mission will be implemented over a five-year period, from 2026-27 to 2030-31, with a total financial outlay of ₹2,995 crore, fully funded by the state government. The government will provide financial assistance of ₹30,000 per household, transferred directly in two installments via the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system.
Under a beneficiary-centric model, each tribal household will have the flexibility to choose livelihood activities suited to their local resources. The programme supports a wide spectrum of activities, including agriculture, horticulture, livestock rearing, fisheries, sericulture, Non-Timber Forest Produce (NTFP) value chains, traditional arts and crafts, handlooms, and rural entrepreneurship.
The mission would carve out dedicated interventions for PVTG communities, recognising their unique needs. These include vital nutritional support for children, pregnant, and lactating mothers, as well as the establishment of creche facilities. A special Flexi Fund of ₹500 crore has been provisioned to address specific infrastructure needs within PVTG habitations using a bottom-up planning approach.

Ravneet Singh Bittu resigns from Union Council of Ministers
PM Modi inaugurates, lays foundation stone of several projects in Punjab
Corruption is rampant in Punjab: PM Modi targets AAP government
All these headlines, when looked at in isolation, appear to be one-off political developments separated in time. But one look at them together in the context of a wider long-term objective, they appear not just connected but also planned with a purpose. This is a perfect example of the BJP election playbook in action.
The BJP, which over the years played second fiddle to the Akalis in Punjab, contested the 2022 elections alone after snapping ties with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD). However, it could win only 2 seats with a vote share of 6.6%. Even the 2024 Lok Sabha elections were a huge disappointment. The BJP polled 18.65% of votes but could not win any seat. However, the BJP appears determined not to let the past numbers dictate its future strategy. And that explains the aggression with which the party has gone for the kill in Punjab.Punjab, which over the years alternated between the Congress and the Akalis, broke the duopoly in 2022 when it overwhelmingly voted for Arvind Kejriwalâs AAP.
And that perhaps gives BJP its biggest hope as it marshals its resources. Now, letâs analyze all these headlines as a part of one story to understand how the BJP is gearing up to add another state to its ever-expanding kitty.
The Ravidassia outreach
When Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Punjab on February 1 this year, the BJPâs election playbook was already in action. The visit was part of a well thought-out and planned outreach that could increase the partyâs base and presence in the state. The occasion was the 649th Birth Anniversary of Sant Guru Ravidas Ji. The Ravidassia community form an important electoral bloc of Punjabâs Scheduled Caste population, especially in the Doaba region. A slew of announcements were made, including renaming of Adampur Airport after Guru Ravidas and the launch of the Shri Guru Ravidas Ji Maharaj Express between Jalandhar and Varanasi. It was the start of a planned outreach. That outreach has continued with the Punjab BJP launching the statewide implementation of the 'Samrasta Sankalp Abhiyan' from July 29, the auspicious occasion of Guru Purnima, to commemorate the 650th birth anniversary year of Guru Ravidas Maharaj. Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon said the nationwide campaign will continue till February 20 (Magha Purnima) under the guidance of the BJP national leadership and aims to spread Guru Ravidas's timeless message of equality, dignity, social harmony and social justice across Punjab.
Targeted political acquisition
The BJP, enriched by its experience from victories in states like West Bengal and Odisha, perhaps knows the importance of organisational strength in winning states. So in Punjab, after breaking its alliance with the Akalis, the BJP has been on an overdrive to build a strong local leadership. After the 2022 elections, several prominent Congress leaders had joined the BJP. And now in the run up to the 2027 electoral battle, seven AAP members of Rajya Sabha from the state are already a part of the party. And this acquisition includes Raghav Chaddha, once the most trusted associate of AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal. Chadha has a good understanding of the electoral thinking of AAP that rules Punjab now and can help the BJP capitalise on its weaknesses. As the elections approach, we could see Raghav Chaddha play a greater role in crafting and implementing BJPâs Punjab campaign.
The âDhillonâ signal
When the BJP replaced one Congress export Sunil Jakhar with another Kewal Singh Dhillon as its state chief, the change was aimed to send across a message. Dhillon, who is a seasoned politician and a prominent industrialist, became the first Jat Sikh to head the BJP in the state. The purpose was clear: outreach among Sikh voters to help increase the acceptability of the party after its Akali alliance ended. The BJP would hope that Dhillon could help the party expand its rural footprint. Besides Dhillon's political base is in Barnala, which falls in the Sangrur-Malwa region. This region is considered a stronghold of Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party.
Ravneet Singh Bittu and Punjab focus
Ravneet Singh Bittu, who joined the BJP in March 2024 ahead of the general elections after ending his long association with the Congress, seems to have an important role in the saffron partyâs blueprint for Punjab. During the 2024 campaign, Bittu was projected as an important Sikh face for the BJP by none other than Amit Shah. For those who remember, the entire BJP had rallied in support of Bittu after Rahul Gandhi had referred to him as âtraitorâ. The BJP made Bittu a minister in the Modi government and a member of Rajya Sabha despite his Lok Sabha election loss from Ludhiana in 2024 to showcase his importance. But after his RS tenure ended in June this year, he quit as minister amid hints that he will play a key role in BJPâs Punjab plans. According to reports, in June, Bittu had expressed his desire to work for Punjab in the Vidhan Sabha after spending nearly 17 years in Parliament. Bittu had then said that the BJP made him the minister even though he had lost the 2024 parliamentary elections."People of Punjab are fed up (with other parties). People are very much aware of development and progress taking place in other (BJP-ruled) states and they want prosperity in Punjab as well," Bittu had then said.Ravneet Singh Bittu is the grandson of former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, who was assassinated in 1995. During his political career in the Congress, he was elected MP thrice and also served as the grand-old-party's leader in the Lok Sabha and as its whip in the Lower House.
PM Modiâs 'double-engine' promise
When Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Punjab for the second time on July 17, his focus was on development, youth and farmers. He pitched the BJPâs 'double-engine' model, arguing that a government of the same party at the Centre and in the state could bring investment, jobs and faster growth to Punjab.âOnly the BJP can bring real change in Punjab. Only the BJP will make Punjab developed. Only the BJP will make Punjab self-reliant,â PM Modi said, adding that the state needed new investment, employment opportunities and greater global reach for products made in Punjab.He also accused the AAP government of stalling development and merely rebranding central schemes. Citing BJP-ruled Delhi and Haryana, Modi argued that Punjab too needed a 'double-engine' government, while claiming that farmers in the state were being denied the support available elsewhere.
Rivals under fire
And while one part of PM Modiâs Punjab campaign was outreach, the other part was his fierce attack on the rivals in the state. Targeting the AAP government in Punjab over law and order and several other issues, PM Modi dubbed the ruling dispensation as a "Kattar Beiman" which neither has clean intentions, nor honesty.PM Modi then targeted the Congress, which has been in news more for factionalism than poll readiness. Taking a dig at infighting in the state unit over the chief minister's chair, the PM said "They are not fighting for people, they are fighting among themselves."Also under attack was the SAD, the BJPâs former ally. Taking a dig at the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the Prime Minister said it is not concerned about the welfare of the public as it is caught up with its own affairs.And finally, while the studentsâ protests against the NEET-UG paper leak forced Centre on the backfoot, the BJP is now using the same ammunition to target the Bhagwant Mann government over alleged paper leaks in Punjab.
Can BJP upset the AAP-Congress applecart in Punjab?
The BJP clearly has a plan for Punjab. It is bringing in leaders, strengthening its state organisation, reaching out to new social groups and sharpening its attack on both the AAP and the Congress. In the coming months, this push is likely to become more visible through political outreach, policy announcements and an aggressive campaign around governance, development and law and order.
But activity alone does not guarantee electoral success. The BJP may have increased its vote share and political visibility, but it still has to expand beyond its traditional urban base, build trust in rural Punjab and convert imported leaders into an effective ground organisation.So, can it upset the AAP-Congress contest? It is still too early to say. The BJP will leave no stone unturned to make Punjab the 23rd state in its kitty. The real test will be whether its carefully assembled strategy can finally translate into seats.

headline: A 22-year-old youth was arrested by Viruthampattu police in Vellore for selling narcotic-laced chocolates on Sunday.
full_text:
A 22-year-old youth was arrested by Viruthampattu police in Vellore for selling narcotic-laced chocolates on Sunday.
The police said the arrested person was identified as S. Manoj Kumar, a native of Bihar. He came to Vellore town to board a bus to Virudhunagar to meet his brother.
Initial inquiry revealed that based on orders of Superintendent of Police (SP) U.N. Sivaraman, searches have been conducted by special police teams in the district to prevent possession, selling and buying of narcotic items.
The police said as part of surveillance, a special police team was patrolling VIruthampattu area when they got an alert on the sale of narcotic chocolates near the bus stop. The team reached the spot and intercepted Kumar. They also checked his bag and found around 1,500 narcotic-laced chocolates in it. Kumar told them that he procured the contraband in Bihar. A case was registered and a probe is under way.

headline: Water released from the Kabini Dam in Karnataka is expected to reach the Tamil Nadu boundary on Monday (August 3, 2026) and flow into the Mettur Dam by Monday night or Tuesday (August 4), according to Water Resources Department (WRD) officials.
full_text:
Water released from the Kabini Dam in Karnataka is expected to reach the Tamil Nadu boundary on Monday (August 3, 2026) and flow into the Mettur Dam by Monday night or Tuesday (August 4), according to Water Resources Department (WRD) officials.
Following heavy rainfall over the past few days in Karnataka, the Karnataka government began releasing Cauvery water from the Kabini Dam on Saturday (August 1). Officials had initially expected the water to reach Tamil Nadu by Sunday (August 2) evening. However, the flow has been delayed as the water is moving slowly through the Cauvery riverbed.
WRD officials at the Mettur Dam said water was first released from the Kabini Dam at 500 cusecs on Saturday (August 1) morning. The discharge was gradually increased to 5,000 cusecs in the afternoon before reaching 25,000 cusecs by Saturday night. They attributed the delay to the dry riverbed, which has absorbed a significant amount of the released water, slowing its downstream movement. As a result, the water is now expected to reach the Mettur Dam on Monday (August 3) night or Tuesday.
“We expect the present discharge of 25,000 cusecs to continue for the next few days. If the Mettur Dam receives 25,000 cusecs of inflow for an entire day, the water level will rise by about four feet. Once the reservoir level crosses 90 feet, the government will decide on releasing water from the dam for delta irrigation,” WRD officials said.
Officials said Tamil Nadu is likely to receive a substantial quantity of Cauvery water only after the Krishna Raja Sagar (KRS) Dam fills up. The dam is yet to reach capacity. At present, the reservoir holds around 20 tmc ft of water against its storage capacity of 49.45 tmc ft.
“If the current spell of rain continues, the KRS Dam is expected to reach capacity within the next 10 days. Thereafter, surplus water from Karnataka is expected to flow into the Mettur Dam,” the officials added.
On Sunday (August 2), the water level at the Mettur Dam stood at 73.33 feet against its full reservoir level of 120 feet. The storage stood at 35.63 tmc ft, compared with the dam’s capacity of 93.47 tmc ft. Inflow into the reservoir increased to 47 cusecs from 42 cusecs, while the discharge for drinking water purposes into the Cauvery river was maintained at 1,500 cusecs.

headline: 'Grateful for a second chance': Mother of teen girl thanks PM Modi for forgiving her over abusive remarks
full_text:
'Grateful for a second chance': Mother of teen girl thanks PM Modi for forgiving her over abusive remarks
The remarks came a day after PM Modi's video, in which he said he forgives kids for hurling abuse at him during the recent anti-paper-leak protests in Delhi.
The mother of the 15-year-old girl against whom an FIR was registered for making abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a viral video has said she is grateful to the PM "for choosing to forgive" her daughter, adding that it has given the teen "a new life."
The remarks came a day after PM Modi, in a video message, said he forgave children for hurling abuse at him during the recent anti-paper leak protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). For the mother of the teenage girl who faced an FIR over the incident, the Prime Minister's statement has offered her daughter a second chance.
"PM Modi has shown his greatness by forgiving the child who used such filthy and obscene words. Today is her birthday, and PM Modi has given her the greatest gift: jeevandaan (the gift of life). Today, this girl has been reborn," she told news agency PTI.
The PM Modi video
PM Modi posted a video on Instagram on Friday, saying he forgives kids for hurling abuse at him during the protest, adding that he did not believe the answer lay in "anger or retaliation” against kids he called “misguided”.
"Sometimes our tongue comes under our teeth and blood comes out, but we do not break our teeth—because the teeth are ours, and the tongue is ours too. The children are also ours," he said.
Calling on the students to move on from the episode, Modi invited them to contribute to nation-building.
"Children, come, let us move forward together for the country. Let us learn something new, let us learn even from mistakes... I live for you, I toil for your bright future, so come, let us together take the country forward," he added.
The girl's apology
In her own video, the teen girl said she had gone to the protest with friends after visiting Connaught Place and was influenced by people around her who were raising abusive slogans against PM Narendra Modi.
Calling it her "first and last mistake," she added, “I apologise to the entire country. I am so ashamed. I can't even look at myself. Please forgive me.”
Despite the apology, a complaint had already been filed against the girl at a Noida police station for allegedly using derogatory slogans during the July 23 protest. Noida Police registered a Zero FIR, which was later transferred to Parliament Street Police Station in New Delhi.
The complainant alleged that the girl's remarks insulted the dignity of the office of the prime minister and had the potential to spread disharmony and disturb public peace.
Her mother said both she and her daughter had repeatedly apologised and appealed for the FIR to be withdrawn. She also claimed that the FIR incorrectly listed her daughter's age as 25, even though her daughter is a 15-year-old minor.
Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke lost no time in targeting the Prime Minister over the police action against the teen.
"Sirf reel par hi maaf karoge ya cases bhi vapas loge (Will you forgive them only in a reel, or will you also withdraw the cases)?" Dipke commented on PM Modi's Instagram video.

headline: 'Some madrasas produce jihadis, should not exist': Taslima Nasreen sparks row with remarks on religious schools
full_text:
'Some madrasas produce jihadis, should not exist': Taslima Nasreen sparks row with remarks on religious schools
Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen criticized madrasas in Kolkata, claiming they produce jihadists and enable child abuse.
Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday said that, in her opinion, madrasas "should not exist", alleging that some of these educational institutions were producing "jihadis" and witnessing cases of child abuse.
Speaking to reporters in Kolkata, Nasreen said, "In my opinion, madrasas should not exist... not in all cases, but in some it is seen that jihadis are being produced in madrasas."
She further alleged that "Child abuse is going on there, rapes are happening... imams and madrasa teachers are being held."
Nasreen argued that punishment alone was not enough and called for changes to the education system.
"They are going to jail, but just punishment won't help... this education system needs a transformation... I don't think there is a need for madrasas... no one does anything after passing out of madrasas... they beg, survive on charity... madrasas should go, and secular schools should come up instead," she said.
Some madrasas produce ‘jihadis’: Nasreen
She also alleged that "a lot of masjids have turned out to become jihad-producing factories", while adding, "not saying all, but some."
"If some money is made/collected, a masjid is built. So many masjids are not needed; the government should control this," Nasreen added.
However, she did not cite any specific instances or evidence to support her claims during the press conference.
Also Read: ‘Took me 19 years to say I have returned to Kolkata’: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasrin
Taslima's ‘homecoming’
Nasreen returned to Kolkata on Friday for the first time in nearly 19 years, describing the visit as an emotional homecoming to a city she still considers her own.
Ahead of her visit, Nasreen told PTI that returning to Kolkata felt like coming back to "my own country."
"I feel as though I am returning to my own country. Bengal has never been divided in my heart by a border or a barbed-wire fence. The door to the eastern part of Bengal remains closed to me, so for now, this part of Bengal is my home," she said.
Nasreen said she was returning "with joy, but also with pain", recalling that Kolkata had given her a home, friends, readers and a sense of belonging before she was forced to leave.
Her return marks her first visit to the city since November 2007, when she left following violent protests over her writings.
After fleeing Bangladesh in 1994 following death threats over her novel Lajja, she settled in Kolkata in 2004, describing the Bengali-speaking city as her cultural refuge in exile.
However, her stay ended in November 2007 after violent protests erupted over portions of her memoir Dwikhandito, which had been banned by the then Left Front government in 2003 for allegedly hurting the sentiments of sections of the Muslim community.
As the protests escalated and the Army was deployed in parts of Kolkata to restore order, the then Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee government asked Nasreen to leave the city. She was shifted to Jaipur and later Delhi before eventually moving abroad.
Over the years, Nasreen repeatedly expressed her desire to return to Kolkata, particularly to participate in literary events, but the visit did not materialise despite appeals from writers, civil society groups and occasional political interventions.
The issue resurfaced nationally last year when BJP Rajya Sabha MP and current West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya urged the Centre in Parliament to facilitate her return, describing Nasreen as a fearless voice against Islamist fundamentalism.

headline: A 35-year-old school teacher, whose family had earlier suffered substantial financial losses in cyberfraud, has once again fallen victim to online scamsters, losing ₹45 lakh in a fake investment scheme while attempting to recover her family’s financi...
full_text:
A 35-year-old school teacher, whose family had earlier suffered substantial financial losses in cyberfraud, has once again fallen victim to online scamsters, losing ₹45 lakh in a fake investment scheme while attempting to recover her family’s financial losses.
According to a complaint lodged with the East CEN Police, the teacher, a resident of Kamaraj Road, stated that her husband had previously been cheated in cyberfraud, leaving the family under heavy debt. To repay the earlier losses, they had availed a gold loan and were searching for investment opportunities that promised better returns.
In November 2025, the couple came across an online investment application through social media. The operators of the application assured them of exceptionally high returns. Believing the claims, the couple obtained additional personal loans and transferred money from the husband’s bank account to various beneficiary accounts specified by the fraudsters.
Between November 2025 and February 20, 2026, they allegedly transferred ₹45,00,000. When they later attempted to withdraw their investment and promised profits, they found themselves unable to access the application, while all contact numbers of the operators had been switched off or blocked.
Realising that they had been cheated, they registered a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. However, the complainant stated that due to mental stress and work pressure, she could not approach the police immediately to lodge a formal complaint.
Based on her complaint, the police registered a case on Friday and initiated a probe to identify the fraudsters, trace the money trail, and take appropriate legal action.
Further investigation is under way.
The case serves as a reminder that cybercriminals often target victims with promises of unrealistic returns, and even individuals who have previously experienced online fraud can become victims again when attempting to recover earlier financial losses, a senior cybercrime investigator said.

headline: Jharkhand man climbs 100 ft mobile tower after exam irregularities prevent wife from getting job
full_text:
Jharkhand man climbs 100 ft mobile tower after exam irregularities prevent wife from getting job
Students are protesting in Jharkhand against the alleged irregularities in the JPSC, JSSC and other recruitment exams over the last few days.
A 25-year-old man climbed a 100-foot-high mobile tower at the Jaipal Singh Munda stadium in Ranchi on Sunday morning and demanded Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren solve his problem.
Heeralal of Latehar district in Jharkhand was rescued by the police after hours of negotiations, senior police officer said, news agency PTI reported.
Also read: Stone-pelting by CJP protesters happened even after Parliament march violence: Officials
"We safely rescued the man after counselling him and assured him that his demands will be looked into. He climbed the tower around 12.30 am and was rescued around 7.30 am," Kotwali police station officer-in-charge Sanoj Choudhary was quoted as saying.
Hundreds of students from different parts of the Jharkhand are camped at Jaipal Singh Munda stadium over the past few days and are protesting against the alleged irregularities in the JPSC, JSSC and other recruitment examinations. The protesting students are demanding an impartial probe in the case.
A video of the incident has surfaced on social media where the police and other people around can be heard trying to convince the man to come down. “Heeralal come down. Electronic media is here. Your demands will be heard,” a police officer can be heard saying on a loudspeaker, though chatter about him climbing the wall for his wife can also be heard in the background.
HT could not independently verify the authenticity of the video
While the police are investigating the matter, the exact reason for climbing the tower is yet to be ascertained. Prima facie, it has come to light that the man was upset after his wife went to her parents' house.
Eyewitnesses were quoted as saying that Heeralal scaled the tower to protest the irregularities in recruitment examinations that prevented his wife from getting a job.
Also read: RTI activist seeks inquiry into how Abhijeet Dipke's father funded his US education
In a purported video of the incident, Heeralal can be heard saying that chief minister Hemant Soren should come and solve this problem.
Meanwhile, The BJP and its youth wing, Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM), on Saturday staged demonstrations in front of the collectorates of East Singhbhum, West Singhbhum, and Chatra, demanding a CBI probe into irregularities in theJPSC and JSSC examinations.
In Jamshedpur, BJP and BJYM workers took out an 'Akrosh' Rally in protest against corruption, irregularities in JPSC, Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC), CGL, Junior Engineer, Excise department constable examinations and question paper leak.
The rally started from the BJP office in Sakchi and culminated at the district collectorate here.

The BJP and BJYM leaders submitted a memorandum addressed to the Jharkhand Governor through the deputy commissioner in support of their demand for a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC examination, strict action against culprits and resignation of Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren.
They demanded an impartial probe into the irregularities.

headline: NEW DELHI: Even as exclusive breastfeeding rates have improved globally over the past decade, India continues to lag behind, with the proportion of infants exclusively breastfed for the first six months declining from 63.7% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) to 55....
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Even as exclusive breastfeeding rates have improved globally over the past decade, India continues to lag behind, with the proportion of infants exclusively breastfed for the first six months declining from 63.7% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) to 55.8% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).Ahead of World Breastfeeding Week (August 1-7), the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF called for stronger support systems for mothers, saying global exclusive breastfeeding has increased from about 37% in 2012 to over 47% today, driven by sustained investments in health systems, community counselling and maternity protection. However, the agencies said progress remains uneven and many countries continue to fall short of global targets.Responding to a question in the Rajya Sabha, the Union health ministry attributed the decline in India's exclusive breastfeeding rate to multiple factors, including socio-cultural practices, family customs, individual preferences, the use of pre-lacteal feeds and infant milk substitutes, and breastfeeding frequency.The ministry, however, highlighted improvements in other breastfeeding indicators.
Early initiation of breastfeeding within one hour of birth increased from 41.8% to 50.1%, while the proportion of infants below six months receiving any breast milk rose marginally from 95.1% to 95.6%.The Rajya Sabha question had sought to know whether the government had assessed the impact of rising Caesarean deliveries, inadequate postnatal lactation counselling and early return to work, particularly among women in the informal sector. While the ministry did not provide findings of any such assessment, it said the National Health Mission promotes exclusive breastfeeding through the Mother Absolute Affection (MAA) programme, lactation management centres, healthcare worker training, Poshan Tracker-based counselling and community awareness campaigns.
It also cited a 2025 NITI Aayog evaluation, which found that new mothers were receiving information on exclusive breastfeeding during the postnatal period.Calling breastfeeding one of the most effective public health interventions, WHO and UNICEF said it provides essential nutrition, protects children against infections, strengthens immunity, supports cognitive development and lowers mothers' risk of breast and ovarian cancers and type 2 diabetes. The agencies said scaling up proven interventions, including skilled breastfeeding support, community counselling, paid maternity leave, supportive workplace policies and stronger regulation of breast-milk substitute marketing, could prevent nearly 400,000 child deaths and 140,000 maternal deaths globally every year.

headline: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan is in the firing line from the Opposition for using a helicopter hired by the State government primarily as an air ambulance and for other emergencies for an alleged personal visit to Kochi.
full_text:
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan is in the firing line from the Opposition for using a helicopter hired by the State government primarily as an air ambulance and for other emergencies for an alleged personal visit to Kochi.
Mr. Satheesan reportedly flew aboard the helicopter from Golf Club in Thiruvananthapuram to Kochi on Friday to visit his father-in-law, who was undergoing treatment. However, inclement weather prevented the helicopter from landing, and it returned to Thiruvananthapuram. Reports suggest the journey was made later.
CPI(M) State committee member M.B. Rajesh slammed Mr. Satheesan for using the helicopter “for personal purposes, with prime-time actors in [his] lap remaining in silent mode”, in an oblique criticism of prime-time television anchors for not covering the issue. As Leader of the Opposition, Mr. Satheesan had criticised the then LDF government for its “extravagance” in hiring the helicopter.
Another State committee member of the CPI(M), V. Sivankutty, also mocked Mr. Satheesan’s flight as a ‘U-turn’ by the helicopter. Health Minister K. Muraleedharan defended the Chief Minister’s use of the chopper, saying modes of transport change with the times. He also contended that “nobody was criticised earlier for travelling by helicopter”.
However, social media was abuzz with criticism over the helicopter journey, with many users digging up old posts by Mr. Satheesan and other Congress leaders criticising the then State government and then Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan for hiring the helicopter. The Chief Minister’s Office did not respond to messages seeking clarification.

headline: Jaish operative, his girlfriend, honeytrap, and a plan to ‘target’ CM Suvendu, CJP protest: Bengal police's big case

Jaish operative, his girlfriend, honeytrap, and a plan to ‘target’ CM Suvendu, CJP protest: Bengal police's big case
The Bengal STF arrested the alleged Jaish operative – who had planned to target Adhikari and carry out sabotage at the recent students' protest – on Friday.
An investigation into an extortion plan and the social media handle of a Jaish operative's alleged girlfriend led the West Bengal Special Task Force to uncover an alleged plan to track chief minister Suvendu Adhikari's movements for Pakistan-based criminals, officials have claimed.
The West Bengal STF arrested the alleged Jaish-e-Mohammed operative who had planned to target Adhikari and also carry out sabotage at the recent students' protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar in the guise of a police official, news agency PTI cited a senior officer of the unit as saying on Saturday.
The accused has been identified as Mohammed Hamim Mondal, who was arrested from Purba Bardhaman district on Friday and brought to Kolkata later that night for interrogation, IG (STF) Gaurav Sharma said. The STF also arrested Arpita Sarkar, alleged to be Mondal's girlfriend, on Friday.
The STF claimed that the duo had hatched a plot to honey-trap the son of a minister of state in West Bengal, and later abduct him to extort money from his family.
How did STF unravel the Jaish operative's plot?
The probe began after investigators received inputs regarding a conspiracy to extort money from the minister and abduct his son, according to another STF officer cited by PTI. “A few days ago, we received information about a plan to extort money from a senior politician from Howrah and abduct his son through a honey-trap. We were told that an organisation was behind the conspiracy,” the officer said
A probe into that led the STF to a social media handle from Sahibganj operated by Arpita Sarkar. Investigation into Sarkar's social media account then led the officers to the Jaish operative, the IG said. Mondal and Sarkar had allegedly been in contact for the last four years after getting acquainted on Instagram and later meeting in person. The STF said the two had been in a relationship and that the officers were further probing whether Sarkar had been used to lure potential targets as part of the honey-trap plan.
‘Contacted Pak-based handlers through WhatsApp, Telegram’
IG STF Gaurav Sharma said the investigation had establised Mondal's links with Pakistan-based handlers, adding that he had been working for them. The probe further revealed that Mondal had allegedly been radicalised through social media before coming in contact with Pakistan-based operatives linked to the Shahzad Bhatti group, Sharma added.
“Hamim had been assigned by Pakistan-based handlers the task of keeping a watch on the CM's movements. He was asked to gather information on the places the chief minister could remain unguarded,” PTI cited Sharma as saying at a press conference. Sharma added that several police officers and politicians were also targets.
The accused was reportedly in contact with the Pakistan-based handlers through encrypted messaging platforms, including WhatsApp and Telegram as well as Element X and Session.
“During the investigation of his mobile phone and social media chat history, we have found some very serious information. He was in touch with several Pakistan-based handlers through encrypted platforms such as WhatsApp and Telegram,” Sharma said.
The Bengal STF sleuths said they had also recovered international SIM cards issued in the United Kingdom and Mexico from the accused. They said these SIM cards had allegedly been used “for encrypted communication with handlers operating from abroad and to facilitate the strengthening of sleeper cells and the terror network in different parts of the country.”

full_text:
Former Chief Minister of unified Andhra Pradesh and BJP leader N. Kiran Kumar Reddy wants the Andhra Pradesh Government to resume talks with Odisha and Chhattisgarh and complete the land acquisition for the Polavaram irrigation project so as to increase its storage capacity to the fullest level.
Addressing the media here on Sunday, Mr. Kiran Kumar Reddy said the task of completing land acquisition and grant of package by the Centre would be easy as the BJP was in the power in Odisha and Chhattisgarh as well.
As many as eight villages in Chhattisgarh and four in Odisha were falling in the Polavaram project submergence area, he said.
“The Centre will bear the R&R component for the Polavaram irrigation project in Chhattisgarh and Odisha as mentioned in the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014. The Andhra Pradesh government should consult the neighbouring two States to complete the land acquisition,” he said.
“Andhra Pradesh will not be able to store water in the project to the fullest level without completing the land acquisition in Odisha and Chhattisgarh,” said Mr. Kiran Kumar Reddy. Both the neighbouring States would also benefit if land acquisition was done, he added.

The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Chief Minister Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy on Sunday accused the TDP-led coalition government of misusing the police machinery to target Opposition leaders and workers. He alleged that those responsible for attacks were being protected while cases were being registered against the victims.
In a post on X, referring to the arrest of Alur MLA B. Virupakshi, Mr. Jagan questioned the deployment of a large police contingent to arrest the legislator and his son, Chandrasekhar, from their residence in the early hours of Sunday. He alleged that the manner in which the arrest was carried out raised serious concerns about the rule of law in the State.
Mr. Jagan said that the episode stemmed from an attack on the residence of a YSRCP leader at Nemakallu village in Chippagiri mandal. He said the local leader had contacted Mr. Virupakshi seeking protection for his family and argued that responding to such an appeal from a party worker could not be treated as a crime.
He further alleged that TDP workers attacked the MLA when he visited the village and that the legislator’s brother, Sriramulu, sustained injuries in the incident. Instead of taking action against those responsible for the attack, the government had allegedly registered attempt-to-murder cases against the MLA and YSRCP workers, he said.
Mr. Jagan also questioned the seizure of CCTV hard disks from the MLA’s residence and alleged that the move was intended to prevent the release of footage of the police action. He further claimed that several YSRCP leaders had been booked in different cases for opposing the government.
The former Chief Minister also alleged that former Guntur East MLA Shaik Mohammed Mustafa and his son had been implicated in a kidnapping case despite having handed over the person concerned to the police.
Asserting that the YSRCP would continue to stand by its workers, Mr. Jagan said arrests, police action and criminal cases would not deter the party from fighting what he described as political vendetta and injustice.
