headline: From Jan Suraaj's zero to Bankipur victory: What changed for Prashant Kishor in Bihar within months
full_text:
From Jan Suraaj's zero to Bankipur victory: What changed for Prashant Kishor in Bihar within months
Prashant Kishor's debut in Bankipur bypoll marked a political turnaround, ending BJP's 30-year dominance in seat last held by party president Nitin Nabin.
From a big zero for his Jan Suraaj Party in the 2025 Bihar assembly polls to a breakthrough win on his own electoral debut, Prashant Kishor has pulled off a swift political turnaround in less than a year. His Bankipur bypoll victory on August 3 has ended the BJP's three-decade hold over one of its strongest bastions in Bihar.
The bypoll was widely seen as the first real test of whether Kishor could convert more than a decade of political strategising into direct electoral success. Much changed in Bihar between Jan Suraaj’s rout in the 2025 polls and Kishor’s breakthrough win, from Nitin Nabin’s rise in the BJP and the vacancy it created in Bankipur, to Nitish Kumar’s exit as chief minister and the emergence of a BJP-led government in the state.
Also Read: 'Bankipur won't become Bengaluru overnight': Prashant Kishor after big win in Bihar
Dec 2025–Mar 2026: Nitin Nabin’s rise opens a window
The first turning point came with BJP leader Nitin Nabin’s elevation within the party. He was appointed BJP national working president in December 2025 and became the party’s national president in January 2026.
After being elected to the Rajya Sabha from Bihar in March 2026, Nabin resigned as MLA from Bankipur on March 30, triggering a bypoll in a constituency represented by him and, before him, his father Nabin Kishore Prasad Sinha for more than three decades.
For Kishor, the vacancy presented a new opportunity after he had decided not to contest in the assembly elections as he preferred to campaign statewide instead.
Track Bankipur bypoll election results here
Apr 2026: Nitish Kumar exits CM chair
The next major shift came in April, when Nitish Kumar resigned as Bihar chief minister after being elected to the Rajya Sabha, ending his decades-long tenure at the helm of the state.
Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary succeeded him, becoming the BJP’s first chief minister in Bihar.
Jul 5, 2026: Kishor decides to contest himself
Unlike the 2025 elections, when he stayed out of the electoral fray and campaigned for Jan Suraaj candidates, Kishor decided to contest the Bankipur bypoll himself.
The former election strategist repeatedly described the contest as “not just an election to choose an MLA” but a referendum on the Bihar government, arguing that he, even as a lone Jan Suraaj legislator, could amplify the Opposition’s voice inside the assembly.
Jul 10, 2026: BJP’s last-minute candidate switch
The BJP’s campaign took an unexpected turn just days before nominations closed. The party first fielded Abhishek Kumar Sinha, who filed his nomination papers in the presence of senior BJP leaders. Less than 30 hours later, however, Sinha withdrew, citing “family reasons”. The BJP then replaced him with Neeraj Kumar Sinha, but did not publicly explain the abrupt change beyond the withdrawal letter. The reason cited by his family was that his father was named in a case linked to the 1990s' fodder scam that was one of the major weapons for the BJP against RJD's Lalu Prasad Yadav.
Oct 2022 - Aug 3, 2026: From padyatra to political win
Kishor’s Bankipur victory capped a political journey that began well before the 2025 elections. In October 2022, he launched the Jan Suraaj Padyatra, a state-wide foot march that took him across Bihar over nearly two years. He eventually converted the movement into the Jan Suraaj Party ahead of the 2025 Assembly polls.
Addressing supporters after his victory, Kishor struck a measured note, saying his immediate priority was to improve Bankipur rather than make grand promises. “My becoming an MLA won’t turn Bankipur into Bengaluru, but you will see some improvements happening here over the next two to three months,” he said, adding that visible changes would begin soon with the support and trust that voters had placed in him.

headline: SC narrows caveat, says states can withdraw FIRs on protesters; CJP reacts
full_text:
SC narrows caveat, says states can withdraw FIRs on protesters; CJP reacts
The court, in its July 28 order, had said that cases could be withdrawn against student protesters, except those with criminal antecedents.
The Supreme Court on Monday reiterated and clarified aspects of its July 28 order on the release and withdrawing of police complaints against students who took part in the Cockroach Janta Party protest at Jantar Mantar.
The apex court held that the National Capital Territory of Delhi and other states were at liberty to withdraw the FIRs against student protesters, and clarified the scope of “criminal antecedents”, mentioned in its earlier order, news agency ANI reported.
The court had, on July 28, said in an interim order passed on student protest cases that cases could be withdrawn against protesters, except those with criminal antecedents. The court on Monday narrowed its scope to only grave and heinous offences.
“The NCT of Delhi or any other State shall be at liberty to close or withdraw any such criminal case, in accordance with law. 'Criminal antecedents' used in paragraph 8(5) would mean grave and heinous offences,” a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said while hearing a batch of petitions alleging police excesses during the recent student protests. This came after senior advocates appearing for one of the petitioners argued that the term ‘criminal antecedents’ was being interpreted in a broad manner, and had led to unnecessary arrests.
Responding to this, Solicitor General of India (SGI) Tushar Mehta, representing the Centre and Delhi, said peaceful protesters must not be equated with hardened offenders, while assuring that anybody who is not a hardened criminal would not face any legal action.
“Those who are protesting in a legally permissible way... except those who have criminal antecedents, everything can be taken care of,” he said, according to ANI.
‘SC has removed confusions, expect govt to honour assurances’: Saurav Das
Reacting to the SC clarification, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said that the states and government must now “honour” the assurances provided regarding the FIRs on students. “Now that the Supreme Court has removed confusions, we expect the Government of India and all BJP/NDA-ruled states to immediately honour the assurances given on 25 July to the young of this country,” Das said in a post on X.
He asserted that the CJP had “stood by every student and every protester”, adding that the outfit would also “closely monitor developments across states.” Das said that the CJP had provided “legal assistance, medical support, and every other form of help within our means”, and that this would remain unchanged in the future.
“We thank all lawyers across the country who continue to help the protesters. We also continue to closely monitor developments across states and remain in constant dialogue with senior representatives of the Union Government. We expect the assurances to be implemented in both letter and spirit,” Das added.
SC mulls single-member SIT, judge-led panel to probe police excesses
Meanwhile, while hearing the petitions against alleged police excesses and those seeking accountability for the use of force against protesters, the apex court said it was considering either a single-member SIT or a judge-led panel to probe the same. The SC bench signalled that it was mulling an independent mechanism to examine allegations of police excesses.
"We are thinking of two options... one is SIT by a sole senior police officer... the other... we don't want to have the nomenclature of SIT. Whatever we will constitute would be by a Judge. We won't call it an SIT," ANI cited the court as saying. CJI Surya Kant asserted that this proposed mechanism would examine allegations against both the authorities and the protesters.
The court further urged the devising of a mechanism on the issue of the closure of cases or criminal proceedings against those detained. The SC bench suggested gathering information on FIRs from all states, and then segregating them to determine those with and without any antecedents. “One mechanism... gather information on FIRs from all States and in Delhi. Then segregation, without antecedents and hardened criminals. After this categorisation, then take up some recourse,” the SC suggested.

headline: Odisha seeks Centre's help for UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity tag for Rath Yatra

Odisha seeks Centre's help for UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity tag for Rath Yatra
Bhubaneswar, The Odisha government has sought the Centre's support for nominating Puri's Jagannath Rath Yatra on UNESCO's List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, officials said on Monday.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has forwarded a proposal of the Shree Jagannath Temple Administration to the Centre and sought the intervention and support of the Union Ministry of Culture and Tourism for taking the nomination forward on priority.
In a letter to Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on August 1, Majhi said the Rath Yatra is not merely a religious festival but a timeless civilisational tradition.
"The Rath Yatra of Lord Jagannath is not merely a religious festival but a timeless civilisational tradition that embodies India's rich cultural diversity, inclusivity, spirituality, craftsmanship, music, dance and community participation".
The chief minister said the centuries-old festival attracts millions of devotees and visitors from across the world and remains one of the most enduring symbols of India's living heritage.
Its inscription on UNESCO's List would further strengthen global recognition of India's rich intangible cultural traditions and contribute significantly to their preservation and promotion for future generations, he said.
Majhi informed the Union minister that the SJTA had already submitted all supporting documents in the prescribed format.
"Considering the outstanding cultural significance of the festival and its universal message of harmony and human values, I request your personal intervention to kindly facilitate the examination of the proposal and extend necessary support of the Ministry of Culture for taking the nomination forward with UNESCO at the earliest," the chief minister said in the letter.
The chief minister also said the Odisha government and SJTA will be pleased to provide any further information or assistance that may be required by the Ministry during the process.
Over 50 lakh people participated in the annual Puri Rath Yatra held between July 16 and 27.

headline: An extremely rare pregnancy that developed outside the uterus, deep inside the abdomen near the kidneys (Representative image)
full_text:
An extremely rare pregnancy that developed outside the uterus, deep inside the abdomen near the kidneys (Representative image)
NEW DELHI: Doctors in Delhi have successfully treated a woman diagnosed with an extremely rare pregnancy that developed outside the uterus, deep inside the abdomen near the kidneys, using minimally invasive (keyhole) surgery.The woman, from Bengaluru, had initially presented for a routine pregnancy evaluation. During an ultrasound, doctors detected a 10-12 cm cystic structure, which was initially suspected to be a dermoid cyst because it appeared to contain fetal parts. However, an MRI revealed a far more unusual diagnosis.The scan showed uterine dehiscence, in which the uterine wall had ruptured, allowing the pregnancy to develop in the retroperitoneal space, close to the kidneys and major blood vessels, including the aorta and inferior vena cava. Doctors found a 12-week fetus measuring about 7-8 cm inside the cyst.Dr Mannan Gupta, Founder and Chairman, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Elantis Healthcare, said the pregnancy was neither inside the uterus nor in the fallopian tube or ovary, where most ectopic pregnancies occur.
"Initially, the ultrasound findings suggested a dermoid cyst. However, MRI revealed an exceptionally rare condition. The pregnancy was located in the retroperitoneal space near the kidneys and major blood vessels.
This is one of the rarest forms of pregnancy and the first such case I have encountered in my career," he said.Doctors performed the procedure laparoscopically, avoiding a major abdominal incision. Given the proximity of the pregnancy to vital organs and major blood vessels, the surgery required meticulous planning and precision. Doctors said the patient had an excellent postoperative outcome.According to the treating doctors, retroperitoneal pregnancy is estimated to occur in about one in 30,000 pregnancies. They said early diagnosis and timely intervention are critical, as delayed treatment can result in life-threatening complications because of the pregnancy's proximity to major blood vessels and vital organs.

headline: Multiple Delhi schools receive bomb threats, search ops on
full_text:
Multiple Delhi schools receive bomb threats, search ops on
Authorities said all safety protocols are in place and no suspicious objects have been found so far.
Multiple schools across Delhi received bomb threats on Monday, triggering security checks by Delhi Police.
Authorities said all safety protocols are in place and no suspicious objects have been found so far, news agency ANI reported.
The latest threats come just a few days after a similar hoax scare in Haryana. On July 31, the Gurugram Deputy Commissioner's office, district courts and several schools received a bomb threat email, prompting evacuation and extensive searches by bomb disposal and dog squads.
Police later declared the threat a hoax after no suspicious objects were found, though an investigation into the source of the email remains underway.
The email had also claimed that the DC office, a school and Haryana courts would be targeted at specific times during the day.

Safety deficiencies in Delhi schools
As many as 774 schools in Delhi have been found with safety-related deficiencies during a city-wide inspection drive launched under the Child Protection Month initiative, with private schools accounting for the highest number of cases, news agency PTI reported.
According to a statement from Lok Nivas, 1,677 schools were inspected between July 13 and 24 using a 'Student Safety Checklist' prepared in line with the guidelines of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), the Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights (DCPCR) and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.
The statement said the schools found deficient have been placed under corrective follow-up.
The inspection drive was launched following directions issued by Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu and Chief Minister Rekha Gupta during a review meeting on July 6, where they called for strict and time-bound implementation of Child Protection Month initiatives across the capital.

The exercise covers government, government-aided, MCD, NDMC, Delhi Cantonment Board and private schools.
Of the 1,677 schools inspected so far, 790 were government schools, 812 were private schools and 75 were government-aided schools. Safety deficiencies were found in 270 government schools, 463 private schools and 41 government-aided schools, it stated.
Schools where deficiencies have been identified are being directed to take remedial measures, following which verification will be carried out to ensure compliance rather than treating the exercise as "a one-time formality", it read.
The statement further said the inspection drive will continue until all 5,633 schools in Delhi are covered.

headline: FSSAI suspended a Tripura water company's license and banned a Punjab supplement. Inspections revealed serious food safety and regulatory violations at the water facility.
full_text:
FSSAI suspended a Tripura water company's license and banned a Punjab supplement. Inspections revealed serious food safety and regulatory violations at the water facility.
NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has suspended the licence of a packaged drinking water manufacturer in Tripura and prohibited the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of a dietary food supplement made by a Punjab-based company after inspections found serious food safety and regulatory violations.The licence of M/S Matri Drinking Water, Gomati, Tripura, was suspended with immediate effect following a complaint about foreign material in packaged drinking water. Inspectors found finished products stored outside the facility and on the floor alongside non-food materials, unhygienic processing and filling areas, rusted RO water storage tanks and chemical dosing containers, inadequate pest control and sanitation, and the absence of mandatory testing, maintenance and training records. A qualified technical supervisor was also not available during the inspection.In a separate action, FSSAI prohibited the manufacture, storage, distribution and sale of Venolex Forte, marketed by M/S Noble Healthcare, Mohali, saying the dietary food supplement contained ingredients not permitted under the Food Safety and Standards (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, Food for Special Medical Purpose, Functional Food and Novel Food) Regulations, 2022.
The regulator said the product contained pharmacologically active ingredients, including calcium dobesilate, diosmin and Euphorbia prostrata, which are not permitted in food supplements. It also found that the product contained 90 mg of vitamin C, which appeared to exceed the Recommended Dietary Allowance prescribed under the ICMR-NIN Guidelines, 2020.FSSAI also said the product's labelling was misleading, creating the impression of specific regulatory approval, and that it was manufactured and marketed beyond the scope of the firm's FSSAI licence. The prohibition order has been issued under Section 36(3)(b) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

headline: Ujjwal Nikam flags delay in acquittal appeals, seeks timely justice
full_text:
Ujjwal Nikam flags delay in acquittal appeals, seeks timely justice
Nikam cited a Supreme Court observation that as of March 25, 2025 more than seven lakh criminal appeals remained pending in high courts
Prominent public prosecutor and Rajya Sabha MP Ujjwal Nikam on Monday raised the concern of delays in hearing appeals against acquittals, arguing that the lack of timely justice can leave an innocent individual burdened by an unresolved case long after being cleared.
“If acquittal was erroneous, a dangerous offender will go to trial but if acquittal was sound, an innocent person continues to live under the shadow of an unresolved prosecution, unable to move forward with life,” said Nikam.
“The criminal justice system has two supporting pillars-- a fair trial and timely justice. If either pillar weakens the entire edifice begins to crumble,” he added.
Section 419 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 governs appeals in cases of acquittals. It allows both the state and the complainant to challenge a court order acquitting the accused in cases where the trial court has committed a grave error of law or in its appreciation of evidence.
Nikam cited a Supreme Court observation that as of March 25, 2025 more than seven lakh criminal appeals remained pending in high courts, of which thousands were appeals against acquittals.
“Scientific evidence and testimony of courageous witnesses can ultimately fail not because evidence was weak but because acquittal appeal remains unheard for too long,” Nikam said.
He further argued that the state bears responsibility in ensuring timely justice as a major litigant in criminal administration.

He is expected to assume charge shortly, the Ministry of External Affairs said.
The appointment comes weeks after the West Asia conflict triggered by Israeli and US strikes on Iran, during which India evacuated thousands of its nationals from the country.
Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh recently informed Parliament that the Indian Embassy in Tehran facilitated the return of 2,557 Indian nationals via Armenia and Azerbaijan since the hostilities began.
The government estimates that around 7,000 Indians, including seminary and medical students, workers, seafarers and fishermen, continue to reside in Iran.
The Centre has also taken up with Iranian authorities the issues faced by medical students who had to return during the conflict.
The Indian government has raised with Iranian authorities the ‘issues faced by Indian medical students studying in Iran, who had to return to India due to the conflict”, and is exploring ways to mitigate the situation, Singh said.
The government is closely monitoring the security situation in Iran and has issued timely advisories to Indian nationals depending on developments. The Indian embassy has a 24/7 emergency helpline and email for Indian nationals to stay in contact.
In the latest advisory issued on July 19, Indian nationals already in Iran were advised to consider temporarily exiting the country, using available flights. Indian nationals desiring to travel to Iran were advised to postpone their travel plans till the situation improves, Singh said in response to a question from Congress MP Jebi Mather Hisham.
US-Iran war: Latest updates
Donald Trump announced on Saturday night that the US will be holding off and halting its strikes on Iran. The US president stated that he was told a deal is in the works; however, he added that the deal's parameters must include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's denuclearisation.
"This would include the Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran’s nuclear threat. Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

headline: Security forces on Monday (August 3, 2026) claimed to have “foiled a terror conspiracy” after a local, carrying posters describing August 15 and August 5 as “black day” and August 14 as “Youm e azadi” (day of independence), was arrested from south Ka...
full_text:
Security forces on Monday (August 3, 2026) claimed to have “foiled a terror conspiracy” after a local, carrying posters describing August 15 and August 5 as “black day” and August 14 as “Youm e azadi” (day of independence), was arrested from south Kashmir’s Pulwama. He was also carrying a live grenade.
Officials identified the accused as Tousef Ahmad Dar, a resident of Drabgam Payeen, Pulwama.
“During checking, a suspicious person coming from Drabgam towards Pachar tried to flee on seeing the checkpoint set up by the Pulwama Police, Army’s 44 Rashtriya Rifles and CRPF’s 183 Battalion. The alert party chased and apprehended him near Fruit Mandi on Pachar Road,” said the officials.
One hand grenade, three anti-national posters and one mobile phone were recovered from his possession. The anti-national posters described August 15 and August 5, the day the Centre ended J&K’s special status, as “black day”. Another anti-India poster asked people to observe August 14, Pakistan’s Independence Day, as “Youm e Azadi”.
The police have filed a First Information Report under Sections 7 and 25 of the Arms Act and Sections 13, 18, 23 and 39 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.
“Investigation has been taken up to ascertain the source of the recovered material and identify any further linkages,” said the officials.
The Pulwama Police, in close coordination with the Army and CRPF, “will continue to take firm action against individuals involved in anti-national and unlawful activities,” a police spokesman said.
The latest arrest has come after two non-local labourers, and one policeman were killed in south Kashmir in two separate targeted killings since July 22 in south Kashmir. Meanwhile, many areas in Kulgam, where non-locals were killed, remain under the scanner of the security forces.

headline: Don't look at Bangladesh or Nepal, follow Gandhi: CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke
full_text:
Don't look at Bangladesh or Nepal, follow Gandhi: CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke
Abhijeet Dipke said Indian student protesters should follow Gandhi's peaceful path, not Bangladesh or Nepal. He used the interview to press for NEET relief, recruitment reforms and higher priority for education.
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has rejected comparisons between his group's recent student protest in Delhi and the upheavals in Bangladesh and Nepal, saying Indian students should draw inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi instead.
In an interview to PTI, Dipke defended the protest over alleged exam irregularities and insisted that the demonstrators had followed the Constitution and maintained peace despite police action.
"Protests in Bangladesh, Nepal are being used to defame us; we are different," Dipke said.
"We showed during the recent protest in Delhi that we were following the Constitution and holding our demonstration peacefully. Parallels to the protests in Bangladesh and Nepal are being used to defame us," he added.
Rejecting remarks by exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen linking the Delhi protest to the 2024 agitation in Bangladesh that led to the fall of Sheikh Hasina's Awami League government, Dipke said India did not need to look outside for models of protest.
"We don't need to look at Bangladesh or Nepal when we have Mahatma Gandhi from whom the world takes inspiration to protest," he said.
'STUDENTS DISPLAYED RESTRAINT'
Dipke said some people may have drawn parallels with protests in Bangladesh and Nepal because of the police action during the Delhi demonstration.
"The students in India were not violent or aggressive. They got their heads, arms and legs broken but displayed restraint and sat peacefully at Jantar Mantar," he said.
He also argued that education should become a central issue in electoral politics.
"If you don't make education the main agenda in election, it means you are not thinking about the future. Education is an investment for the future of the country," Dipke said.
DEMAND FOR NEET VICTIMS' COMPENSATION
Dipke criticised the government over what he described as a delay in compensation to families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide.
"They have money to topple government overnight. You can buy MPs and MLAs by spending hundreds of crores of rupees, but when it comes to the NEET victims and their kin, they look at the norms," he said.
He warned that CJP could launch another agitation if its demands were not addressed.
"The government should meet our demands as soon as possible, or else we will launch another agitation," he said.
Dipke also urged Gen Z protesters to maintain restraint and not imitate the conduct of politicians.
He said young protesters should "not reach the level of BJP leaders" who, according to him, abuse even in Parliament and at public rallies.
"There is some difference between us and the goons and that difference should always be there," he said.
SUPPORT FOR JHARKHAND STUDENTS
Dipke extended CJP's support to students protesting in Jharkhand over alleged irregularities in the state public service examination and other recruitment tests.
He backed their demand for a CBI probe and reforms in recruitment agencies, saying the movement was against the system rather than any political party.
"Their fight is not against any political party but against the system. We stand with their demands. If they want a CBI probe, we are going to support them in pursuing that," he said.
He said CJP would support student movements over education and recruitment issues irrespective of which party was in power.
"Wherever agitations will happen for education and wherever students come forward to demand their rights, we are going to stand with them, irrespective of the ruling party in that state," Dipke said.
"The rules are the same as our fight is not against any political party. It is against the system that has let down the students of the country," he added.
OPPOSITION LEADERS' SUPPORT
Asked about opposition leaders who visited Jantar Mantar to support the student protest, Dipke said they did not use the platform for political promotion.
"Everyone was sensitive towards the students' agitation. They were very sensitive towards the cause and the students. When they were on the stage at Jantar Mantar, none of these leaders spoke about their political party, but said they were there to support the students," he said.
CJP PLANS EXPANSION
Dipke said CJP would discuss its future roadmap at a meeting at his residence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on August 5.
Around 10 to 15 people are expected to attend the meeting, with other volunteers also expected to play a role in expanding the movement.
"The expansion of CJP will take place. Our responsibility has increased after the success of the recent protest. People's expectations about CJP have also gone up. In the meeting on Wednesday, we will discuss our future roadmap," Dipke said.
'EDUCATION MUST GET MAXIMUM SPENDING'
Dipke also criticised what he described as the gap between India's education system and those in other countries, particularly in infrastructure and practical learning.
"The biggest difference is that foreign countries have a good infrastructure when it comes to education," he said.
Drawing on his own experience in the US, Dipke said courses there were more practical and less theoretical, and argued that India needed to create greater scope for practical learning.
He also claimed that the present government was spending less on education than the previous regime.
"The maximum funds should go towards education. There is no dearth of funds with the government, so I don't understand why they are reducing expenditure on education. Education is something where the maximum spending should take place as it is the foundation of a nation," he said.
"We don't know how much money there is in the PM Cares Fund. I think the education department could really take some help from that fund," he added.
Dipke said education had become unaffordable and inaccessible for many people in India and called for greater government spending on the sector.

headline: No FIR against girl who abused PM Modi at Jantar Mantar protest by Delhi Police yet: Report
full_text:
No FIR against girl who abused PM Modi at Jantar Mantar protest by Delhi Police yet: Report
After the FIR was filed against the girl, she apologized on video and said that she “came under the influence of some people at the protest”.
No FIR has been filed by the Delhi Police against the 15-year-old girl who allegedly used abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during student protest at Jantar Mantar, news agency ANI reported citing Delhi police sources.
This comes Noida police filed a Zero FIR against the girl and forwarded it to Delhi Police. A Zero FIR can be filed at any police station in India, no matter where the crime happened.
The sources told ANI that the question of withdrawal of FIR against the girl does not arise because the it was never converted into a regular FIR in Delhi.
“A decision on regular FIR is yet to be taken in background of claim of minor,” they said.
However, some reports claim that the Delhi police has decided to not file an FIR against the girl. HT could not independently verify either of the reports.
After the FIR was filed against the girl, she apologized on video and said that she “came under the influence of some people at the protest”.
Also read: Mother of teen girl who abused PM Modi upset as 'FIR not withdrawn' despite apology, claims CJP
She called the incident her “first and last mistake” in the video widely circulating on social media.
“I apologise to the entire country. I am so ashamed. I can't even look at myself. Please forgive me,” she said.
While the Zero FIR alleged that she was 25-year-old, the girl in the video was heard saying that she is just 15.
HT could not independently verify the authenticity of the video.
Also read: 'Grateful for a second chance': Mother of teen girl thanks PM Modi for forgiving her over abusive remarks
The girl was booked by the Uttar Pradesh Police under Sections 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace), 353(1) (statements conducive to public mischief) and 356(1) (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The case was registered at the Expressway police station on the basis of a complaint filed by Ghaziabad-based lawyer Smriti Singh.
Also read: PM Modi forgives students amid abusive video row: 'Let's guide the misguided'
PM Modi ‘forgives misguided children’
In a video released on Friday, PM Modi said that he was “deeply hurt” that even his late mother was targeted with abusive remarks during the protest at Jantar Mantar. However, he decided to forgive the “misguided children”.
"Not only was I subjected to abusive language at Jantar Mantar, but even my late mother was abused there with filthy language. But abuses never solve anything; let's guide the misguided," he said in the video.
"I want to forgive them. People make mistakes, but it was a cultural shock that our daughters are using such abusive language. We must forgive our youth who were misguided; after all, they are our children. It's our duty to show them the right path," he added.

headline: NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) leader Atul Limaye has alleged that the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led protest over the NEET-UG paper leak evolved into an "experiment for alternative politics", claiming that several political, student,...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) leader Atul Limaye has alleged that the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led protest over the NEET-UG paper leak evolved into an "experiment for alternative politics", claiming that several political, student, labour and civil society organisations joined the agitation to propagate the idea of "subversion of democracy through democratic means."Addressing an ABVP event in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on July 30, Limaye said the protest should be "decoded" to understand its chronology, methodology, support system and ideological underpinnings. He also alleged that anti-Hindu and "anti-national" slogans were raised during the agitation and questioned how it transformed from a student-led protest into a broader political movement.
During his address, Limaye said, "In Today's times, CJP agitation should be studied as a case study. This has now come to the knowledge of everyone, but this was A phenomenon going on for years now. And if we have to study this whole agitation, we will have to see its full chronology, methodology and what their support system is, and the innovative system which they used and the ideology behind it. Of we see chronology, Abhijit Dipke was from our Marathwada itself. When he launched CJP, he got tremendous following (on social Media), and when he came back to India, he came back on 6th June and did his agitation on 7th."
Describing the course of the agitation, he added, "But he didn't receive the response which was expected. So, he roamed around the country from 7th to 19th. He started agitation in various cities of the country, or tried to start agitation, but even there did not get that kind of response. So, he started agitation, sit-in protest at Jantar Mantar from the 20th onwards, and gradually the face of the agitation got changed."According to Limaye, the movement later drew the participation of student organisations, labour unions, human rights groups, women's organisations, farmers' bodies and other civil society groups.He said, "What kind of things happened after that which changed the face of this agitation? What kind of support system did attach to this agitation? We need to see which organisations and institutions got attached to this agitation, and this will give us an idea of what kind of support system. This agitation obviously involved the youth, the students of the country. And that is why several student organisations got attached to it. Among the prominent organisations which were leading the stage in this protest was All India Student Association (AISA). And the second such Association was SFI."He further said, "Some human rights organisations, many tribal organisations, women organisations like Pinjra Tod joined them. Many Muslim organisations, Christian organisations, some institutions working in the legal sector, environment sector, journalistic associations also joined them. Some farmers' associations joined them, as Samyukta Kisan Morcha and Bharatiya Kisan Union joined them."Invoking Italian philosopher Antonio Gramsci's theory of cultural hegemony, Limaye argued that the protest was aimed at challenging democratic institutions and cultural values while operating within democratic processes.He said, "Why did the opposition to Hindus arise from the stage? Why were leaders from several political parties seen on the stage, and how did it convert from a student protest to a political protest? It was not limited to Delhi, but expanded in all the states. For this, we have to decode Yogendra Yadav's remark, 'Democracy's future now will not be decided in Parliament but on streets, elections will not decide, resistance will.' The cause of the protest was genuine, but who captured the movement? If we understand this, then we will understand this protest. There is a lot to learn. This protest was an experiment for an alternative politics."He added, "This theory states subversion of democracy through democratic means. This is well documented, and Italian scholar Gramsci gave the theory of cultural hegemony. He said that cultural hegemony needs to be destroyed for revolution. The deconstruction theory challenged Lord Ram and other figures. Alternative politics states that till there is a system, like our Parliamentary system, there cannot be revolution. All the systems, including the judiciary and police, need to be challenged."Claiming that such politics could be pursued either electorally or through weakening public faith in institutions, Limaye said, "There are two ways: one is election and the second is subversion of democracy through democratic means. There is infiltration in the judiciary, education system, and bureaucracy. Second is challenging the institutions and eroding faith in them. The results are so dangerous. Many police officers said the way the women were behaving, it was difficult to tolerate.
The way they were dressed and the language they used, we were ashamed. This was an attempt to degrade the culture."CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke rejected the allegations and said the RSS had no moral authority to describe others as anti-national. Responding to Limaye's remarks on Monday, Dipke referred to the period when the RSS was banned following Mahatma Gandhi's assassination.Abhijeet Dipke said, "People who murdered Mahatma Gandhi are calling us anti-national. The murderers of Mahatma Gandhi have no moral right to call anyone else anti-national. Nathuram Godse was the first anti-national."The CJP had led a 37-day protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak. The agitation was withdrawn on July 25 after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the organisation said it had received assurances on its other key demands.

headline: Delhi to open Ghazipur modern poultry market by December amid wider revamp
full_text:
Delhi to open Ghazipur modern poultry market by December amid wider revamp
From a Rs 193-crore poultry hub nearing completion to new grain market sheds, Delhi is expanding its agricultural infrastructure while planning a phased modern flower market at Ghazipur.
Delhi is set for a major overhaul of its agricultural markets, with a Rs 193-crore modern poultry market at Ghazipur due for completion by December, two new steel sheds planned at Narela and a modern flower market proposed at the Integrated Freight Complex in Ghazipur.
Chief Minister Rekha Gupta reviewed the progress of ongoing and proposed infrastructure projects at Ghazipur, Narela and the Integrated Freight Complex and directed officials to ensure that the works are completed within their deadlines, according to an official statement.
Gupta said agricultural markets are a vital link between farmers, traders and consumers and need modern infrastructure to keep pace with changing requirements.
RS 193-CRORE POULTRY MARKET AT GHAZIPUR
The modern poultry market at Ghazipur, spread across nearly 15 acres, has been under construction since March 2019 and is scheduled to be completed by December 31.
The facility will accommodate 100 wholesale traders and have 120 poultry processing units, according to the government.
The project is among the major infrastructure works being monitored by the Delhi government as part of its efforts to upgrade agricultural markets in the capital.
MODERN FLOWER MARKET PLANNED AT GHAZIPUR
The government also reviewed plans for a modern flower market at the Integrated Freight Complex in Ghazipur.
Around 10 acres of land acquired from the Delhi Development Authority in 2001 has been earmarked for the project. The proposed market will be developed in phases.
The project is intended to add modern infrastructure for the city's flower trade alongside the existing agricultural market facilities in the Ghazipur area.
DRAINAGE, SANITATION WORK AT GHAZIPUR
At the Ghazipur Fruit, Vegetable and Flower Market, work is underway to address waterlogging through the construction of a 200-metre bypass drainage pipeline.
The project has been approved at a cost of Rs 17 lakh.
Officials also told the chief minister that regular drives are being conducted to remove stray animals from the market premises as part of efforts to improve sanitation.
TWO NEW SHEDS FOR NARELA GRAIN MARKET
The government has also proposed two additional steel sheds at the Narela Grain Market at an estimated cost of around Rs 11 crore.
The new structures are expected to be completed by July 2027.
The projects at Narela, Ghazipur and the Integrated Freight Complex formed part of the review meeting, with the chief minister asking officials to keep the works on schedule.
The overall plan covers the completion of the Ghazipur poultry market, drainage and sanitation improvements at the Ghazipur market, new infrastructure at Narela and the phased development of the proposed flower market.

headline: Probe PM CARES Fund, Modi ji will forgive you: CJP takes swipe at RTI activist
full_text:
Probe PM CARES Fund, Modi ji will forgive you: CJP takes swipe at RTI activist
The Cockroach Janta Party has attacked an RTI activist who sought probes into founder Abhijeet Dipke's family finances and the outfit's funding. The exchange has sharpened questions over the group's legal status, donations and a Rs 1 crore legal aid fund.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has hit back at an RTI activist who sought an investigation into the finances of founder Abhijeet Dipke's family and the party's funding, accusing him of selectively targeting a private individual.
Reacting to the complaints filed by the Surat-based RTI activist Amit Tiwari, CJP spokesperson Vaishnavi Gaur said, "Those filing RTIs over a private individual's education expenses should also look at the PM CARES Fund. Modi ji will forgive you, don't worry."
Her remarks came after Tiwari on August 1 said he had filed complaints with the Election Commission of India (ECI), the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), and the Maharashtra government.
He has sought a probe into the finances of Dipke's father, Bhagwanrao Dipke, a retired Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC) junior engineer.
The activist questioned how a government employee earning around Rs 60,000-65,000 per month could allegedly afford to send his children to the US for higher education, and urged the Maharashtra government to investigate whether the case involved disproportionate assets.
While questioning the legal status of the CJP, saying that it is functioning like a political party without being registered, Tiwari urged the ECI to examine whether the outfit can legally accept donations despite not being a registered political party.
In a separate complaint to the CBIC, Tiwari sought the imposition of 18 per cent GST on the Rs 1 crore legal defence fund announced by veteran Congress leader Kapil Sibal for CJP protesters.
He further accused CJP leaders of crossing the line during the NEET paper leak agitation by allegedly using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, his late mother, and India's foreign relations, saying those remarks were also part of his complaint.
The controversy stems from Sibal's announcement on July 27 of a Rs 1 crore legal aid fund to support CJP protesters facing police cases following the nationwide agitation.
As questions over the outfit's funding and legal status intensified, the CJP dismissed the complaints as politically motivated.

headline: Madhya Pradesh woman strangles nephew-lover with dupatta over marriage pressure
full_text:
Madhya Pradesh woman strangles nephew-lover with dupatta over marriage pressure
The incident came to light on July 31 after Satyaprakash Gupta was found unconscious in a Maruti Suzuki S-Presso in Madhya Pradesh's Singrauli district.
A woman in Madhya Pradesh has been arrested for allegedly murdering her nephew, with whom she was in a relationship for two years. As per police sources, the woman, identified as Priya Gupta, strangled the victim with a scarf and left his body inside a car after being pressurised for marriage for a prolonged time.
The incident came to light on July 31 after Satyaprakash Gupta was found unconscious in the driver's seat of a Maruti Suzuki S-Presso in Singrauli district. His brother, Rahul Gupta alias Sanjay, alerted police after spotting him inside the vehicle.
The victim was taken to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
Following the murder, the local police registered a complaint, sent the body for a post-mortem, and launched an investigation shortly after. They visited the site and collected evidence for the investigation.
As part of the probe, the police soon discovered Satyaprakash’s link to Priya, his aunt and the widow of late Sunil Gupta. They found out that the two had been in a relationship and the victim was allegedly pressurising her for marriage. The proposals often led to severe disputes between the two.
According to the police, the two met on the day of the murder and had an argument which escalated further. As a result, Priya strangled Satyaprakash to death.
POLICE CRACK THE CASE WITH THE HELP OF CCTV
While investigating, the police found the CCTV footage on the day of the crime, which helped them crack the case.
It showed that Priya was taking Satyaprakash to his parked car around midnight. She later called the victim’s brother and informed him that Satyaprakash was inside the vehicle to divert suspicion after the murder.
Based on the evidence collected, police arrested Priya Gupta and registered a case at Morwa police station under Crime No. 420/26 under Sections 103(1) and 238(A) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). She was later produced before a court, while further investigation into the case is underway.

headline: Gurugram: Former Haryana chief minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda has demanded that the state’s Commonwealth Games gold medallists be appointed Deputy Superintendents (DSP) in the Haryana Police. Reviving a decade-old political argument over how the stat...
full_text:
Gurugram: Former Haryana chief minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda has demanded that the state’s Commonwealth Games gold medallists be appointed Deputy Superintendents (DSP) in the Haryana Police. Reviving a decade-old political argument over how the state should reward its athletes, Hooda used social media platform X to invoke the ‘Padak Lao, Pad Pao (get a medal, get a post)’ scheme that his Congress government ran between 2005 and 2014.
Accusing the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of tampering with the system to deny athletes their due once it came to power, Hooda said the policy had built Haryana into a sporting powerhouse, and credited it with laurels the state’s players continue to bring home.
“This is not the first time our players have raised the flag high at the Commonwealth Games, they did the same in 2010. Our players are extremely talented and we’re proud of their hard work. It is the result of the ‘Padak Lao, Pad Pao’ policy we introduced that Haryana’s players continue to bring glory to the country,” Hooda told ThePrint.
He further said: “We built the sports infrastructure, set up academies, turned Haryana into a sports hub, and gave the youth the right direction; the results are visible even today. The boxing academy in Bhiwani was opened during our tenure, and today our daughters from there are lighting up the world stage.”
He added that the BJP government had undone what Congress built. “They have tampered with the policy we made and denied players their rewards, their honours, their positions. Even the players we appointed as DSPs haven’t been promoted under this government,” he said.
The demand lands on the back of a rich Glasgow haul. Six of Haryana’s boxers won gold at the Commonwealth Games — Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria and Sakshi Chaudhary, all from Bhiwani, in the women’s draw, and Priya Ghanghas, also of Bhiwani, alongside Sachin Siwach and Ankush Panghal among the men. Hisar’s Narender Berwal took silver in the +90kg category. Panipat’s Neeraj Chopra added a javelin silver, his second Commonwealth Games medal after the 2018 gold at Gold Coast.
Haryana Police records back up the part of Hooda’s claim about his government’s track record. Between 2005 and 2014, some 13 sportspersons were recruited as DSPs on the state Cabinet’s recommendation, using powers under Rule 14 of the Punjab Police Service Rules, 1959, to grant relaxations for exceptional appointments. The list includes hockey players Mamta Kharab, Sardar Singh and Surinder Kaur; wrestlers Geetika Jakhar, Ramesh Kumar, Ravinder Singh Sangwan and Yogeshwar Dutt; boxers Jitender Kumar, Akhil Kumar, Vijender Singh, Vikas Krishan and Paramjeet Samota; kabaddi player Mamta Sodha; and cricketer Joginder Sharma.
Sandeep Singh left the force to contest the 2019 Assembly election from Pehowa, won, and was made sports minister — before being booked on a molestation complaint by a woman athlete and dropped from the Cabinet when Nayab Singh Saini took over as chief minister.
Yogeshwar Dutt tried the same route from Baroda in 2019 and lost to Sri Kishan Hooda. In 2020, Dutt was fielded yet again by the BJP in a byelection to Baroda Assembly seat necessitated by Sri Kishan Hooda’s death, but he lost to Congress candidate Induraj Narwal. The BJP didn’t field Dutt in in the 2024 Assembly elections, but he continues to be a BJP leader.
Boxer Vijender Singh quit his DSP’s job when he turned professional in 2015. He joined the Congress ahead of 2019 election. However, he quit Congress and turned up unannounced at the BJP office to join the party ahead of the 2024 Assembly elections.
Also Read: Bhiwani’s boxer factory delivers 5 golds in Glasgow—a reminder of why it’s dubbed India’s ‘mini Cuba
Post-Hooda era
Since 2014, the Khattar as well as the Saini governments have moved away from discretionary appointments toward a rules-based framework, the Haryana Outstanding Sportspersons Service Rules, alongside cash award slabs for medal winners that have themselves been revised more than once.
Under the revised norms, sportspersons can compete for jobs in Group A, B and C under the Outstanding Sportsperson (OSP) cadre based on their achievements in the sports.
A retired India Police Service officer, explaining the legal architecture behind the old appointments to ThePrint, said the underlying law leaves little room for a standing scheme of the kind Congress ran. Regular DSP appointments go through the Haryana Public Service Commission or fixed promotion quotas, 80 per cent by promotion, and 20 per cent direct recruitment, under rules framed under Article 309 of the Constitution. The Cabinet’s Rule 14 power, he said, was meant for genuinely exceptional cases, such as the appointment of K.K. Rao on compassionate grounds after his father, DSP Ranbir Singh, was killed by terrorists in March 1989.
That power, he said, was used more loosely after 2005. He cited Mamta Sodha, an Everester appointed DSP though mountaineering has no recognised competitive sporting body, and Joginder Sharma, a Rohtak cricketer given the post despite never having played an Olympic sport.
The officer added that the record of sports-quota DSPs inside the force has been mixed, with most of those appointed showing weak outcomes on professionalism, integrity and contribution to developing sport within the department itself.
He said that the sportspersons are normally busy in their sporting career and are hardly able to complete their training after induction into the police force. Also, the kind of expenditure a sportsperson has to incur on oneself for training and diet, cannot be logically met from the salary of a government officer even if one is a DSP. “Looking at their expertise, the government should make use of their talent at jobs where they can train the future generation of sportspersons,” he added.

headline: 80-year-old retired engineer killed in temple lift accident in Karnataka
full_text:
80-year-old retired engineer killed in temple lift accident in Karnataka
An 80-year-old retired engineer died after getting trapped beneath a lift at Dattatreya Swamy Temple in Karnataka's Shivamogga during Sunday morning prayers. Police have registered a case and are examining whether a mechanical fault or negligence led to the accident.
An 80-year-old retired engineer died after becoming trapped in a lift at Karnataka’s Dattatreya Swamy Temple in Shivamogga, during morning prayers on Sunday.
The deceased, identified as Kumaraswamy, had visited the temple in Vinayak Nagar for his regular prayers. According to police, the incident occurred when he pressed the lift button and attempted to board it. He was allegedly caught beneath the lift, leading to fatal injuries.
Fire and Emergency Services personnel responded to the scene, rescued Kumaraswamy from beneath the lift and rushed him to McGann Hospital. However, doctors declared him dead on arrival.
Police have registered an unnatural Death Report (UDR) at Jayanagar Police Station based on a complaint lodged by the deceased's wife, Lalitha Kumaraswamy. Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident, including whether any mechanical fault or negligence contributed to the fatal accident.

NEW DELHI: Improving court infrastructure and integration of technology in the justice delivery system with an outlay of more than Rs 9,800 crore since 2011 have had little impact on disposal of cases pending for several decades. More than 10,000 cases are pending in the Supreme Court for over 10 years â including 558 pending for over 20 years, and 26 cases for 30 years. In the 25 high courts across the country, over 80,000 cases are pending for over three decades.In a written response to a question in Parliament last week, law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal put the onus of disposal of cases on the judiciary, which has not fixed a time frame for their disposal.He further said: âTimely disposal of cases in courts depends on several factors which, inter-alia, include availability of adequate number of judges and judicial officers, supporting court staff and physical infrastructure, complexity of facts involved, nature of evidence, cooperation of stakeholders viz bar, investigation agencies, witnesses, litigants and proper application of rules and procedures.
âWhile the apex court has been prompt in appointing judges against vacancies, the situation in 25 high courts and subordinate courts is not the same. The HCs currently have 341 vacancies of judges against a sanctioned strength of 1,122. The subordinate courts have 7,311 vacancies against an approved strength of 30,868 judges.
The law minister blamed the respective HC collegiums for not following the timeline prescribed for initiating recommendation for appointments of judges for the HCs, the primary reason behind large vacancies. The HC collegium comprises the chief justice and two senior-most judges of the high court. For the SC, the recommendation for the appointment of judges is initiated by the Chief Justice of India.âArrears Committees have been set up in all 25 high courts and the district courts to clear cases pending for more than five years. The govt has also enacted the New Criminal Laws 2023, Negotiable Instruments (Amendment) Act, 2018, Commercial Courts (Amendment) Act, 2018, Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2018 with a view to reduce pendency,â Meghwal said.

headline: Rifle snatched, bullets fired, Jharkhand gangster killed in police encounter
full_text:
Rifle snatched, bullets fired, Jharkhand gangster killed in police encounter
Gangster Sujit Sinha was killed in a police encounter after an alleged escape bid during his transfer from Sahibganj Divisional Jail to Dhanbad Jail. Police have sealed the site and said standard legal procedures are under way.
One of Jharkhand's most wanted gangsters, Sujit Sinha, was killed in a police encounter late Sunday night after allegedly attempting to escape while being shifted from Sahibganj Divisional Jail to Dhanbad Jail.
According to police, the incident took place near the Jamtara border during the prison transfer. Officials said Sinha requested that the convoy stop so he could use the toilet. As the police vehicle halted, he allegedly snatched a rifle from one of the escort personnel and fled into the darkness.
Police claimed the gangster opened fire on the escort team while trying to escape, forcing officers to retaliate. During the exchange of fire, Sinha sustained serious bullet injuries.
He was immediately taken to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
The encounter marked the end of the gangster who had long been on the radar of Jharkhand Police and was facing multiple criminal cases.
Following the incident, the encounter site was sealed as senior police officers rushed to the spot and reviewed the sequence of events.
Police said all aspects of the encounter are being examined and standard legal procedures are being followed.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: For the first time since the Covid pandemic, fatalities on national highways (NHs) declined last year, even as overall road deaths rose in India. Govt data submitted in Lok Sabha last week shows that deaths on NHs, including Centre-run expressways, fell by 4.1% to 62,122 in 2025 from 64,772 in 2024.
Among states and UTs, 20 recorded a decline in fatalities on NHs while 15 reported an increase. Lakshadweep, with no national highways, was the only one to record âzero NH fatalitiesâ since 2022. 
Data shows UP registered the steepest decline in NH deaths, with fatalities dropping from 9,560 in 2024 to 7,573 in 2025. Madhya Pradesh also reported a significant reduction, from 4,644 to 3,610, along with Punjab, which logged a sharp fall from 1,562 to 1,022 during the same period. 
States that witnessed a rise in NH fatalities include Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.

headline: The agency has floated a tender estimated at Rs 7.5 crore to hire a security firm for its headquarters at Minto Road, regional office in Okhla and other notified locations.
full_text:
The agency has floated a tender estimated at Rs 7.5 crore to hire a security firm for its headquarters at Minto Road, regional office in Okhla and other notified locations.
NEW DELHI: After a paper leak exposed weak links in Indiaâs biggest entrance examination, National Testing Agency (NTA) is moving to put its premises, confidential records and examination material under round-the-clock watch. The agency has floated a tender estimated at Rs 7.5 crore to hire a security firm for its headquarters at Minto Road, regional office in Okhla and other notified locations.Issued on July 25, the tender is part of a procurement exercise covering security, housekeeping and examination-grade printing. Together, the bids signal an attempt to tighten controls across the examination chain â from printing and storage to access control and protection of digital infrastructure. The security contract will initially run for two years and may be extended twice by a year each. Bids can be submitted until 3 pm on Aug 17. The printing-services tender closes on Aug 20.The selected agency will watch over NTA employees, visitors, premises, confidential examination material, server rooms, strong rooms, warehouses, record rooms and other sensitive facilities. It will regulate entry and exit, verify staff and visitors, maintain logs and ensure that âonly authorised persons enter restricted areasâ.
The security apparatus will include door-frame and hand-held metal detectors, GPS-enabled guard patrol tracking, biometric attendance and digital incident-reporting systems.NTA has moved away from choosing a bidder mainly on cost basis. Citing the âsensitive nature of NTAâs examination ecosystem and confidentiality requirementsâ, it has adopted the quality-and-cost based selection model. Technical capability will carry 70% weightage and the financial bid 30%. Only agencies securing at least 70 marks in the technical assessment will reach the financial round.Bidders must have at least five yearsâ experience in professional security, an average annual turnover of Rs 10 crore in past three financial years and must have done prior work at high-security establishments such as central govt institutions, examination agencies, universities, airports, hospitals or metro systems.
Bidders for NTA tender will have to deposit 15 lakh as earnest moneyThe contract value excludes GST. Bidders must deposit Rs 15 lakh as earnest money, while the successful agency will furnish performance security equal to 5% of the contract value.Confidentiality is mandatory. The service provider and its personnel must protect information relating to examination material, security arrangements and IT systems even after the contract ends.The tender has been floated amid efforts to rebuild public confidence after the NEET controversy and have a foolproof system in place against paper leaks. The exercise suggests that NTA is treating security as a process in which every access point can become a vulnerability.

headline: Why Dharmendra Pradhan's homecoming has set the cat among pigeons in Odisha
full_text:
Why Dharmendra Pradhan's homecoming has set the cat among pigeons in Odisha
Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as a Union minister and a hero's welcome in Bhubaneswar have reignited speculation over his next political move. Will one of the most formidable leaders of the BJP become the CM? Experts suggest that the road ahead depends on several factors.
A resignation in New Delhi has resulted in the politics in Odisha hotting up. While it was watching the fast-paced developments in neighbouring West Bengal, the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union Education Minister and him receiving a hero's welcome have sparked speculation over the BJP heavyweight's next political move.
For the uninitiated, Dharmendra Pradhan, who's the Lok Sabha MP from Sambalpur, is credited for building the party's organisational muscles in Odisha. He commands the loyalty of a large number of MLAs and ministers, and is an alternative power centre in the state.
While the BJP projected Pradhan's Odisha homecoming as a show of strength, political observers in Bhubaneswar see it as the start of speculation about the leader's next role in the state where he built the saffron party from scratch. The reception at Bhubaneswar airport, attended by several Odisha ministers and MLAs, made many ask if the BJP was planning to assign the top job in the state to him. Just the buzz that Pradhan could be positioned for the CM's role has unnerved some in Odisha's political circles, say experts.
The circumstances of Pradhan's resignation in New Delhi and the political mood in Odisha, however, make these speculations far from straightforward. Two Odisha-based political observers and an insider in the BJP's political circle in Odisha say, while Pradhan remains one of the BJP's most formidable leaders in the state, the road ahead would be based on calculations of the party high-command. However, they see him as a rightful claimant to the CM's post.
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister after the CJP-led agitation over alleged examination irregularities demanded he quit from the post on the grounds of accountability. Pradhan's return to the east-coastal state has ignited speculation over whether the saffron party is scripting a role change for the leader who's been part of the Narendra Modi Cabinet since 2014. Though Pradhan has resigned as a Union minister, he continues to be the Sambalpur MP.
A Bhubaneswar-based journalist, who spoke to India Today Digital on condition of anonymity, says speculation about Pradhan's return to state politics has unsettled internal equations and "set the cat among the pigeons". We'll get into the explanation of why the journalist said so. But before that, let's first have a look at how Pradhan's resignation has gone down with people in Odisha.
A HERO'S WELCOME, BUT ALSO AN IMAGE RESET FOR PRADHAN?
Bhubaneswar-based senior journalist and political commentator Rajaram Satpathy says the optics of Pradhan's welcome at the Bhubaneswar airport were significant and noteworthy.
"Having relinquished his post as Union education minister in the face of fierce agitation over the NEET-UG question paper leak, Dharmendra Pradhan came home Tuesday [July 28] for the first time as an MP. There was, however, a good crowd at the airport to welcome him. The scene was reminiscent of the welcome NDA MPs gave him outside Parliament recently. Five of 16 ministers of the Mohan Charan Majhi-led government and 21 party MLAs were on hand to receive him," Satpathy tells India Today Digital.
Satpathy also says that he believes the reception carried a political message. "Observers view the heroic welcome accorded to Pradhan as a desperate image make-over bid to sustain him in politics in the days ahead," explains Satpathy.
Despite the setback, Satpathy argues that Pradhan's stature within the BJP remains significant.
"Close to the BJP top brass in New Delhi, Pradhan is rated an influential national Odia leader after [former Odisha chief ministers] Biju Patnaik and Harekrushna Mahatab. He is also credited with building the BJP's state unit almost from scratch to what it is today," says Satpathy.
However, he says Pradhan's resignation has altered some public perceptions in Odisha.
"Sadly, his public image belies his political standing. It certainly took a beating after the students' agitation that forced him to finally put in his papers after all efforts reportedly to retain him in the ministry failed," says Satpathy, adding that the public opinion on Pradhan in Odisha remains divided.
"People in Odisha, though, feel sad that an influential Odia in the Union government was sacrificed. However, they are divided," Satpathy tells India Today Digital. "His critics justify his resignation, saying he failed to foresee the approaching danger despite being so experienced in government functioning. Pradhan, they say, could have done more to check the recurring chaos in one exam after another."
The big question is where Dharmendra Pradhan goes from here. Interestingly, Pradhan was considered a frontrunner for the chief minister's post after the BJP won the Assembly elections in Odisha for the first time in 2024. However, the BJP high command chose Mohan Charan Manjhi, a four-time MLA from the tribal community representing the Keonjhar seat, to be the CM.
The move was seen by some as a signal from the BJP ahead of the Jharkhand Assembly polls, which the party lost.
WHAT NEXT FOR DHARMENDRA PRADHAN?
For now, Satpathy says there is little certainty about Pradhan's immediate future. But he points to two possibilities.
"There is speculation on two things. He may lie low for some time, or the BJP may give him some party post and use him in organisational work," Satpathy tells India Today Digital.
However, discussion around Pradhan's future inevitably circles back to Odisha's top post, given his journey from an ABVP leader to one of the principal architects of the BJP's organisation in a state long dominated by the Biju Janata Dal (BJD) led by former CM Naveen Patnaik.
Satpathy recalls that after the BJP's historic victory in 2024, Pradhan was seen as a contender. Asked whether that possibility could revive now, Satpathy remains unconvinced. "No. Distant possibility," he says.
He also dismisses comparisons between "a timid" Mohan Charan Majhi and the BJP's selection of firebrand leader Suvendu Adhikari in neighbouring West Bengal as the party's face.
"Whether Pradhan stands a chance to be the CM in view of the contrast in dynamism between the Odisha CM and his West Bengal counterpart is all speculation," Satpathy tells India Today Digital.
WHAT WORKS IN DHARMENDRA PRADHAN'S FAVOUR IN ODISHA?
Even though he has been in New Delhi for a considerable period of time (first as an MP since 2004 and then as a Union minister since 2014), Satpathy believes "Pradhan commands the support of a sizeable number of people in the party," Satpathy says, pointing to the airport reception in the state capital as evidence.
"Pradhan is a big force in Odisha politics, and he claims the loyalty of at least 40 BJP MLAs, especially the younger ones," says a Bhubaneswar-based journalist, who requested anonymity. He tells India Today Digital that Pradhan's organisational influence in Odisha remains formidable.
The BJP has 79 MLAs in the 147-member Odisha Assembly.
An insider from within the Odisha BJP spoke about a dinner that was attended by ministers and MLAs. "There was discussion on the Assembly seats that could be vacated for Pradhan to contest from," the person said.
The source said that there was a high possibility that the seat could be from Jharsuguda, which neighbours Sambalpur and is part of the Bargarh Lok Sabha constituency.
The journalist who didn't want to be named, however, believes that the BJP leadership, which might want Pradhan at the helm in Odisha in the long run, is unlikely to make any immediate leadership changes.
"The Delhi stint certainly has made Dharmendra Pradhan more experienced, but not an edge in Odisha politics, given the wind currently blowing against him," political commentator Satpathy tells India Today Digital.
ALL WELL WITHIN BJP IN ODISHA? IS RESURGENT BJD CATCHING UP?
Firstly, despite the goodwill of Odisha's first tribal Chief Minister, dissatisfaction over governance and crime has surfaced within political circles. CM Majhi's delivery is under scrutiny. The recent local body election in CM's Keonjhar did not go that well for the BJP. According to a report in The New Indian Express newspaper, out of the 21 wards of Keonjhar municipality, the BJD won 13 seats while the remaining eight went to the BJP.
CM Mohan Charan Majhi is the MLA from Keonjhar.
"There is a resurgence in pro-BJD sentiments for the first time since the BJP swept the polls in 2024... The BJP's setback in the Keonjhar municipality and the boost to the BJD following Sujata Rout Karthikeyan's entry into the party might prevent the BJP brass from promoting Pradhan immediately," the Bhubaneswar-based journalist says.
Sujata Rout Karthikeyan, a former IAS officer and wife of VK Pandian — the bureaucrat-turned-aide of BJD chief Naveen Patnaik — joined the party in June, almost two years after the regional party suffered a rout from the state it ruled for 24 years uninterrupted.
The party, needful of a robust second-rung leadership, found a helping hand in Sujata Rout's husband, VK Pandian. A person of Tamil origin, he wielded considerable influence as the CM’s private secretary, played a central role in governance, and was even called Patnaik's heir-apparent by many.
Pandian, following the BJD's defeat in the 2024 elections, faced backlash. He stepped away from politics, taking moral responsibility. With Rout entering politics, the BJD is rebuilding itself. Pandian's wife, Rout, is from Kendrapara district. Patnaik called her Sujata Rout instead of Sujata Rout Karthikeyan, according to a report in The Hindu.
WHY BJP MAY NOT BE IN A HURRY TO AWARD PRADHAN ODISHA's TOP POST
The journalist from Odisha who spoke on the condition of anonymity says that he believes replacing the current CM could create fresh complications. "Asking Manjhi to step down could become a 'tribal issue' while crowning Pradhan, who was forced to resign as a Union minister, might not go down well among the younger population," he says.
He adds that even speculation about Pradhan returning to state politics has unsettled internal equations in the state unit of the BJP. "The buzz of Pradhan returning to state politics had set the cat among the pigeons."
"Aparajita Sarangi, Baijayant Jay Panda and Manmohan Samal wouldn't be too excited," he says, pointing to the BJP heavyweights in Odisha. Manjhi, he explains, started from the Dharmendra Pradhan camp but has lately aligned himself with Manmohan Samal.
Sarangi is a former IAS officer-turned-politician and serves as an MP representing the Bhubaneswar Lok Sabha seat. Baijayant Jay Panda is an industrialist-politician and is the National Vice-President for the BJP. Samal leads the BJP's Odisha Unit.
"The BJP brass, if it has decided to make Pradhan the Odisha CM, might choose to wait for five to six months before going ahead with the plan," the journalist tells India Today Digital, adding that perceptions about the former Union minister differ across generations in the state.
"A big chunk of the people over 40 in Odisha think that Pradhan will bring about change. He will be a better CM than Majhi. Even those who don't support the BJP think Pradhan will do a better job," he says. The journalist said making Pradhan the CM immediately might make the BJP "the target of youth, especially Gen Z, ire. That's because of the baggage he carries from Delhi," the Odisha-based journalist adds.
To conclude, time will tell whether Pradhan's future lies in Bhubaneswar and when that time comes. The Delhi exit has certainly opened an opportunity for a chapter in Odisha. People on the ground say Pradhan could be an organisational strategist for the party with a pan-India role or could enter state politics. The question is how long the cooling-off period would be. The recent chain of events has definitely ignited debates over leadership even as Pradhan continues to enjoy New Delhi's backing. Will the BJP's next political move in Odisha determine Pradhan's future? The picture might be clear in a few months.

headline: Residents of the Scheduled Tribe settlement at Thoppilayi near Kakkanpara in Sreekandapuram municipality, Kannur, suspended their 17-day protest against a laterite quarry on Sunday (August 2, 2026) after the District Collector issued a temporary stop...
full_text:
Residents of the Scheduled Tribe settlement at Thoppilayi near Kakkanpara in Sreekandapuram municipality, Kannur, suspended their 17-day protest against a laterite quarry on Sunday (August 2, 2026) after the District Collector issued a temporary stop memo halting quarrying.
Protest committee convenor P. Bindu, who had been on a fast for nine days, and Uru Mooppan P. Aneesh, who continued the fast for three days, ended their hunger strike.
The protest committee alleged that a private individual had purchased land originally allotted to landless families for house construction under a surplus land scheme and obtained permission for laterite mining using fabricated documents. Residents of the tribal settlement said quarrying on the ecologically sensitive laterite hill posed a serious threat to around 50 Scheduled Tribe families living nearby. They also expressed concern that their cremation ground, community building, and drinking water tank, located close to the quarry site, could be endangered.
The quarry owners had resumed mining under police protection after securing a favourable order from the High Court. In response, the protest committee launched a relay hunger strike 13 days ago, with five people participating in different phases.
District Collector P. Vishnuraj issued the temporary stop memo after inquiries by the Department of Mining and Geology and other departments, following petitions submitted by the protest committee to the Collector and other authorities challenging the quarry permit.
The inquiry reportedly found that a public road lies within a 50-metre radius of the quarry, prompting the temporary suspension of mining.
Residents said attempts to start the laterite quarry had been made since 2023 but were abandoned following public opposition. After obtaining a favourable High Court order, the owners resumed quarrying, triggering protests by residents of the tribal settlement.
Earlier, P. Chandran and M. Remeshan, who had undertaken the initial phase of the hunger strike, were hospitalised after their health deteriorated. They were succeeded by P. Bindu and E. Shyamala. Ms. Shyamala was also admitted to hospital three days ago after her condition worsened, following which P. Aneesh continued the fast.
The Taliparamba Revenue Divisional Officer and the Tahsildar had earlier held discussions with the protesters and assured them that action would be taken against the quarry. On Saturday (August 3, 2026) afternoon, the Tahsildar reached the protest venue and read out the District Collector’s stop memo, after which the protest committee decided to suspend the agitation.
The protest committee said a public meeting would be held at the protest venue at 11 a.m. on Monday (August 3, 2026) to decide the future course of the agitation.

Give drug survivors a second chance, respect them: PM ModiPM Modi said society should instead respect those who overcome their drug addiction. âThey are real warriors whose incredible courage is their true identity,â he said in a virtual address, with a host of chief ministers, governors, spiritual figures and a large number of youngsters joining the event from across the country.As the nation has set the goal of âViksit Bharatâ, it is imperative that the countryâs youth remain physically and mentally fit, steering clear of destructive habits like drugs, he said, stressing the importance of support system offered by the society besides the help from yoga and meditation.He said, âEven if a youth has mistakenly fallen into the trap of addiction, it absolutely does not mean that all doors are closed for them.â
