Less than a year before the Punjab Assembly election, Congress leader Charanjit Singh Channi finds himself in a difficult position after locking horns with the party leadership over the recent organisation overhaul. With the party leadership clearly in no mood to relent, Mr. Channi’s options seem to have narrowed to two alternatives — accept a diminished role within the party or seek a political future elsewhere — neither of which may be favourable for him.
The discord was triggered by the All India Congress Committee’s organisational overhaul on July 1. While Amrinder Singh Raja Warring was retained as the State unit chief, Mr. Channi, Punjab’s first Dalit Chief Minister, was appointed chairman of the State poll campaign panel.
On July 3, the Lok Sabha member from Jalandhar and Congress’s most prominent Dalit face in the State convened a meeting of supporters at his Morinda residence, followed by another gathering in Mohali, in a clear show of strength aimed at persuading the high command to revisit its decision.
He was conspicuous by his absence from an event last week, where Congress general secretary for Punjab Bhupesh Baghel kicked off a nine-day mass mobilisation programme. He has stayed away from party events so far.
While Mr. Baghel has repeatedly ruled out replacing Mr. Warring as the Punjab Congress president, the faction led by the former CM has shown little sign of backing down.
Disruptions during the party’s ‘Har Booth Mazboot’ events in Patiala, Samana and Bathinda, where sections of workers were seen raising slogans in Mr. Channi’s support, have publicly exposed the fault lines. Mr. Baghel’s warning — urging party workers to stay alert against “traitors within the party who could cause serious damage” — seems to have had little effect in calming tempers.
Along with Mr. Channi, leaders such as Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa and Rana Gurjit are also believed to be upset with the revamp of the party unit, even as veteran leader Partap Singh Bajwa, the Leader of the Opposition in the State, is pushing for party unity to wrest power from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP).
Weighing options
“It appears that Congress factions are weighing their options and trying to outwit each other to gain a political edge. No faction can afford to go it alone. That would be self-destructive. But, if the situation fails to improve, I believe Channi could contest the election separately with leaders from his camp,” said Kehar Singh, former head of the Department of Political Science at Punjabi University.
While Punjab Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) chief Kewal Dhillon has said he would welcome the Jalandhar MP into the party, Mr. Kehar feels the chances of disgruntled leaders switching to the BJP are slim.
In January, Mr. Channi, who was also the party’s chief ministerial face in the previous poll in which the Congress suffered a crushing defeat, called for “greater Dalit representation” in the party, adding that the community is “not getting due representation”.
Dalit representation
His remark, which brought the internal discord within the Congress into public, assumed significance given that Dalits constitute nearly 32% of Punjab’s population — the highest proportion among Indian States — making them a decisive electoral constituency.
For the Congress, which had been emerging as a serious contender for the 2027 election, the continuing drama could result in loss of momentum. The infighting has, at least for now, shifted attention from its campaign against AAP towards its own infighting.

headline: Congress's shock Datia bypoll victory triggers BJP overhaul, district chief fired
full_text:
Congress's shock Datia bypoll victory triggers BJP overhaul, district chief fired
The BJP dissolved its entire Datia district organisation after losing the Assembly bypoll to Congress. The move followed a review of the defeat and revived tensions over Narottam Mishra's denied ticket.
The BJP has dissolved its entire district organisation in Madhya Pradesh's Datia after the party's defeat in the July 30 by-election, acting on the recommendation of a probe committee constituted to examine the setback.
Tuesday's action came a day after the Congress retained the Datia Assembly seat, with its candidate Ghanshyam Singh defeating his BJP rival Ashutosh Tiwari by 6,016 votes.
Singh secured 66,757 votes, while Tiwari polled 60,741. Azad Samaj Party candidate Damodar Yadav finished third with 22,527 votes.
In an order issued by BJP state office secretary Shyam Mahajan, the party announced the immediate dissolution of the entire Datia district unit.
District president Raghuveer Singh Kushwaha was removed from his post along with the entire district executive.
The order also dissolved all organisational divisions, fronts, cells, projects and departmental units operating in the district.
Earlier in the day, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav held a review meeting with senior BJP leaders from both the organisation and the government to assess the reasons behind the bypoll defeat.
Following the meeting, the party constituted a two-member committee to investigate the loss.
According to an official party statement, BJP State General Secretary Gaurav Randive and senior leader Ambaram Karada have been appointed to the panel.
The committee has been tasked with interacting with party office-bearers and senior leaders associated with the election, analysing the factors that led to the defeat and submitting its report to state BJP president Hemant Khandelwal.
The Datia by-election had already generated controversy within the BJP after the party replaced six-time MLA and senior leader Narottam Mishra with Ashutosh Tiwari as its candidate.
The decision to deny Mishra a ticket had triggered strong protests by party workers and supporters in his home district ahead of the bypoll.

headline: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) said he would discuss with the Centre the issue of mining in Nagaland as one of the causes of the devastating flood that has killed 87 people so far.
full_text:
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) said he would discuss with the Centre the issue of mining in Nagaland as one of the causes of the devastating flood that has killed 87 people so far.
A majority of the people died in three districts adjoining Nagaland — Sivasagar, Charaideo, and Jorhat. These districts hardly have a history of a major flood.
Touring the flood-hit districts, Mr. Sarma said the State government will begin assessing the damage to the houses from August 9 to fast-track relief and rehabilitation of the affected families.
He also addressed concerns about mining activities in Nagaland having contributed to the unprecedented flooding in the three districts, specifically Charaideo and Sivasagar. “I cannot stop mining in Nagaland. I will raise the issue with the Centre. We need a scientific study to determine the actual cause of the problem,” he said, insisting there was no illegal mining in Assam.
Many in the affected districts, including Sibsagar MLA Akhil Gogoi, have blamed illegal sand, stone, and coal mining along the foothills of Nagaland for the flood in Assam. They said such activities, along with rampant felling of trees, removed natural resistance to the floodwaters that rushed down the hills of Nagaland after bouts of extremely heavy rain.
Nagaland-based organisations, however, trashed “theories” that activities there were responsible for Assam’s flood.
Mr. Sarma said the government would drain out the floodwaters as quickly as possible, apart from rebuilding the houses under the government’s rehabilitation programme.
He said the highways obstructed the natural flow of floodwater in certain areas. “I will ask the National Highways Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited to construct additional cross-drainage structures,” he said.
He further said embankments would be constructed in vulnerable areas to prevent flood damage in future.
Higher compensation
Mr. Sarma concurred with Mr. Gogoi’s suggestion that the compensation to flood victims should be increased.
Donations have been pouring in from individuals, organisations, political parties, and social media influencers.
Many have touched hearts with ‘shram daan’ or voluntary labour. They include a group of Sikhs who have been cleaning up flooded namghars (prayer halls), temples, and other places of worship besides serving meals.
A group of daily wagers from western Assam, mostly Bengali Muslims and Koch-Rajbongshis, has been clearing silt from farmlands and house compounds, or removing livestock carcasses.
Members of a barbers’ association have been providing free haircuts to the flood-affected people. At the same time, car mechanics from other parts of Assam have pitched in to repair vehicles free of charge. “Visuals of hundreds of upturned, half-buried two-, three-, and four-wheelers made us reach out to the people. We do not have cash to spare, but decided we can make a difference by trying to restore these vehicles without any labour charge,” a mechanic from Nagaon said.

headline: In the first phase of the census â involving housing and houselisting operations â those opting for self-enumeration were not able to submit the form with blank fields
full_text:
In the first phase of the census â involving housing and houselisting operations â those opting for self-enumeration were not able to submit the form with blank fields
NEW DELHI: Census authorities are considering allowing persons self-enumerating for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 to submit a partially filled form online.In the first phase of the census - involving housing and houselisting operations - those opting for self-enumeration were not able to submit the form with blank fields. If any field was left blank - either accidentally or intentionally due to lack of clarity - the user could not advance to the submission window.Sources said that it was felt during discussions among census teams that this feature forced many to opt out of self-enumeration and rely on the enumerator's visit to record their replies to the questionnaire.There is now a realisation that even a partially filled form, provided a minimum number of questions are answered, would help in easing the task of the enumerator. Besides, self-declared data tends to be more accurate and reliable."Internal deliberations focused on why the self-enumeration option should not be made flexible, given that the data is to be entered digitally either by the respondent or the enumerator.
The census application anyway allows the enumerator to access the filled-up form and change any wrongly entered data. So why can't he access a partially filled-up form and fill in the few remaining fields during the house visit, saving time and effort?" an officer told TOI.The population enumeration exercise is set to be conducted nationwide in Feb 2027. However, the exercise, as per convention, is advanced for select states/UTs like Ladakh, J&K, HP and Uttarakhand that become wholly or partially snow-bound in Feb. These areas will witness population enumeration from Sept 1 to 30, preceded by a self-enumeration window of Aug 17-30.

headline: VIT Chennai has launched a dedicated centre to revive traditional Tamil knowledge and scientifically investigate the impact of traditional Tamil games and select teachings from traditional scriptures on cognitive abilities.
full_text:
VIT Chennai has launched a dedicated centre to revive traditional Tamil knowledge and scientifically investigate the impact of traditional Tamil games and select teachings from traditional scriptures on cognitive abilities.
The centre seeks to explore how traditional games such as Pallanguzhi, Thayam, Adupuli Attam, Paramapadham, and Aindhu Kal and select teachings of Thirukkural and Thirumandhiram can help improve concentration, memory, problem-solving skills, visuo-spatial ability, cognitive flexibility, and emotional regulation, a press release stated.
The centre has been developed under the Indian Knowledge Systems division of the Union Ministry of Education.
According to Vijayabanu U., Associate Professor of Psychology and the Co-Principal Investigator, the centre will examine specific cognitive abilities associated with different traditional games. Aindhu Kal will be studied in relation to visuo-spatial ability, Pallanguzhi with metacognition, Thayam with problem-solving skills and strategic thinking, Adupuli Attam with memory and cognitive skills, and Paramapatham to face life challenges.
Instead of assuming that ancient practices are beneficial simply because they are traditional, the researchers propose to test their effects using measurable scientific parameters, which makes the initiative quite unique, according to Ganesh N., Professor of Computer Science Engineering and the Principal Investigator.
The centre seeks to bring these traditional practices back into the lives of younger generations as knowledge systems whose potential benefits can help them, according to G.V. Selvam, Vice President, VIT.

headline: The Punjab Assembly on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) passed a resolution urging the Centre to review and suspend the mandatory rollout of E20 ethanol blended fuel for vehicles until all concerns are comprehensively addressed.
full_text:
The Punjab Assembly on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) passed a resolution urging the Centre to review and suspend the mandatory rollout of E20 ethanol blended fuel for vehicles until all concerns are comprehensively addressed.
The AAP government moved the resolution on a day party chief Arvind Kejriwal marched towards the Prime Minister's residence in the national capital with over 2.30 lakh petitions against E20 petrol but was stopped by Delhi Police and later held a sit-in on Firoz Shah Road as part of the agitation against the blended fuel policy.
On the second day of the Monsoon session of the Punjab Assembly in Chandigarh, Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema moved the resolution and e criticised the mandatory implementation of 20% ethanol blending (E20 petrol) from April 2026.
Mr. Cheema also questioned why the implementation of the E20 fuel policy has been advanced as against the earlier target of implementing it in 2030.
Highlighting that the U.S. produces 60% of the world's ethanol while India produces only 5%, Mr. Cheema accused the BJP-led central government of surrendering to the United States at the cost of Indian consumers and vehicle owners.
In its resolution, the House expressed serious concern over the decision of the Centre to mandate the nationwide supply of E20 fuel "without adequately safeguarding the interests of consumers, vehicle owners and the states".
"This House notes that while the objectives of reducing crude oil imports, enhancing energy security and promoting cleaner fuels are important national priorities, such policies must be implemented in a manner that is transparent, scientifically validated and sensitive to the concerns of citizens and state governments," it said.
The compulsory use of E20 raises legitimate concerns regarding engine compatibility, accelerated wear and tear of fuel system components, reduced fuel efficiency and mileage, increased maintenance costs, possible warranty disputes and diminished resale value, read the resolution.
It expressed concern that the increased operating and transportation costs would inevitably raise the cost of cultivation, movement of goods and essential commodities, thereby adding to the financial burden of ordinary citizens.
Through the resolution, the Union government was urged to review and suspend the compulsory nationwide rollout of E20 petrol for vehicles not originally designed or certified for E20 fuel until all concerns relating to vehicle compatibility, consumer protection, scientific evaluation and State-specific impacts are comprehensively addressed.
Consumers should be given the option to choose between ethanol-free petrol and E20 petrol, and owners of vehicles not originally designed or certified for E20 fuel should not be compelled, directly or indirectly, to use E20 until their vehicles are demonstrably certified as fully compatible with higher ethanol blends, it said.
The Centre should constitute an independent committee comprising automobile engineers, petroleum experts, environmental scientists, consumer organisations and representatives of state governments to undertake a comprehensive assessment of vehicle compatibility, fuel efficiency, maintenance costs, etc, and place its findings in the public domain, stated the resolution.
Cheema, while referring to "damage" to vehicles due to E20 fuel, said repairing such a car costs between ₹25,000 and ₹50,000.
He criticised the petroleum ministry for failing to provide alternative options for citizens with older vehicles, warning that delivery boys and small business owners risk losing their livelihoods if their vehicles break down every few months.
He claimed even Union Minister Nitin Gadkari admitted in Parliament to a 6% drop in fuel mileage, though actual efficiency losses are much higher.
"The unilateral imposition of policies without consulting domestic scientists, manufacturers, parliamentarians, or the general public is condemnable. The policy is selling out the country to corporate interests," he alleged.
Ethanol production consumes massive amounts of water, which poses a grave threat to Punjab's already depleted groundwater table, claimed Mr. Cheema.

headline: ‘Deeply worrisome’: India condemns attack on ship in Red Sea, Yemen blames Houthis for ‘terrorist attack’

‘Deeply worrisome’: India condemns attack on ship in Red Sea, Yemen blames Houthis for ‘terrorist attack’
Shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said the cargo vessel, MSV Faize Noore Oliya, capsized and sank after being hit by a “projectile” near Yemeni waters.
India has condemned the attack on an Indian-flagged merchant vessel carrying 13 Indian nationals that sank in the Red Sea after being attacked off the coast of Yemen on Tuesday.
In a statement released on Tuesday, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) called the repeated attacks on commercial vessels in West Asia “deeply worrisome”, and said that all the Indian crew members have been rescued.
Shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said that cargo vessel, MSV Faize Noore Oliya, capsized and sank after being hit by a “projectile” near Yemeni waters.
Meanwhile, Yemen’s internationally recognised government also condemned what it called a “Houthi terrorist attack”, saying the Indian-flagged ship was targeted by “an explosives-laden boat” off the country's western coast.

‘Deeply worrisome’: India on repeated attacks on commercial ships
The vessel, which had a 14-member crew comprising 13 Indian nationals and one Yemeni citizen, was rescued in a joint operation by the Yemeni navy and coast guard. The crew members were later taken to the port of Mokha in Yemen.
Expressing concern over the attack, the ministry of external affairs said the repeated attacks on commercial vessels in the region are “deeply worrisome”.
It also called for an immediate end to such attacks and reiterated its support for “free and unimpeded navigation and commerce” through international waterways in West Asia.
“The continuing incidents of attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply worrisome. The targeting of commercial shipping in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways in the region, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest,” the statement read.
The incident is the latest in a series of attacks on vessels operating in the Red Sea, a route reportedly used by some tankers after Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz in February.
A total of 10 Indian seafarers are among the 16 Indians who have died so far in the West Asia conflict, the MEA informed Parliament. It also said that another 5 Indian seafarers were killed in recent attacks on merchant ships in the Black Sea involving Russia and Ukraine.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, a day after the incident, Yemen's ministry of foreign affairs, as part of the internationally recognised government, condemned what it described as a “Houthi terrorist attack” on the Indian-flagged merchant vessel.
The ministry described the attack as a “flagrant violation of international law” and said it posed a “direct threat” to maritime safety, security and the freedom of trade along international waterways.
Yemen said the attack was part of an ongoing pattern of “crimes and assaults perpetrated by the Houthi terrorist militia”.
“The Ministry reaffirms the solidarity of the Republic of Yemen with the friendly Republic of India and its continued coordination with the relevant Indian authorities, while extending all necessary support and facilitation to the vessel’s crew members,” it added.
India’s MEA has thanked the Yemeni authorities for their assistance in rescuing the Indian nationals.

headline: The doctor certified her 90% disabled, but a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability
full_text:
The doctor certified her 90% disabled, but a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability
NEW DELHI: Holding that functional disability faced by a road accident victim should be the deciding factor for granting compensation and not doctor-certified medical disability, SC has granted compensation of Rs 83.3 lakh to a minor who met with an accident when she was just six months old and is now suffering from severe spinal cord and neurological injuries.Though the doctor certified her 90% disabled, a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability and quantified the compensation on that basis."...In the given facts of a case, a lesser physical disability may result in a much higher functional disability and in an appropriate case, even amount to complete loss of earning capacity," the bench said, adding it would be reasonable to assume that functional incapacity resulting out of a particular bodily injury may be higher and greater than what may be medically perceived."The present case concerns a child who has suffered permanent disability at a tender age and whose future stands altered on account of the injuries sustained in the accident. In such circumstances, the court is required to adopt an approach which is realistic, humane and consistent with the settled principles governing award of compensation under the MV Act," the bench said while increasing the amount of compensation to over Rs 83 lakh.
"Cases involving child victims suffering permanent or near total disability constitute a distinct and special category within the law relating to motor accident compensation. A child, by reason of age, vulnerability and complete dependence upon others, stands on an altogether different footing from an adult claimant. The consequences of a catastrophic injury suffered during childhood are not confined merely to the immediate physical impairment caused by the accident.
Such injuries alter the entire course of the child's existence and affect every subsequent stage of her life. The law, therefore, cannot evaluate claims involving injured children through the same lens that may ordinarily be applied in cases involving adults," it said.

headline: Heatwaves, lightning now a natural calamity in NDRF protocol, says Centre

Most heat stroke cases were reported from Telangana (915 cases), followed by West Bengal (733) and Chhattisgarh (660).

The current list of notified disasters has 12 entries: cyclone, drought, earthquake, fire, flood, tsunami, hailstorm, landslides, avalanches, cloudburst, pest attack, and frost and cold waves.
The latest inclusion will ensure states can use the SDRF fund for providing relief and assistance to people affected by heatwaves and lightning.
Welcoming the move, Anjal Prakash, a climate expert and an IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change) author, called it a significant policy shift.
“It’s an important step, given India’s rising exposure and fragmented response to it. By including these as notified calamities, states can now take central support for relief, which was previously hard to justify under the disaster finance tools,” he said.
“The 16th finance commission has also cited an increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events due to climate change. This brings India’s fiscal architecture closer to observed and projected risk, especially for urban and Agrarian population. Cities can also move away from ad-hoc solutions, to proper measures now,” Prakash further said.

headline: The Madhya Pradesh Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) evening disbanded its Datia district unit as part of disciplinary action following recommendations from a two-member review panel constituted earlier in the day to delve into...

The Madhya Pradesh Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) evening disbanded its Datia district unit as part of disciplinary action following recommendations from a two-member review panel constituted earlier in the day to delve into the reasons for the Datia byelection loss.
“On the directions of State president Hemant Khandelwal, and based on the recommendations of the committee constituted to review the results of the Datia Assembly by-election, the current organizational structure of the Bharatiya Janata Party, Datia District, is dissolved with immediate effect,” the party stated in an order.
The two-member panel of M.P. BJP general secretary Gaurav Randeeve and senior leader Ambaram Karada has been tasked with holding discussions with leaders and workers involved with the bypoll preparations and analyse the result.
The committee was set up shortly after a meeting of senior leaders at Chief Minister Mohan Yadav’s residence in Bhopal.
It was attended by Mr. Khandelwal, Deputy Chief Ministers Jagdish Devda and Rajendra Shukla, Datia candidate Ashutosh Tiwari, bypoll in-charge Bharat Singh Kushwaha, and other senior leaders and Ministers.
Mr. Tiwari’s 6,016-vote defeat at the hands of Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh has fuelled rumours of conflict within the BJP and allegations of internal sabotage by supporters of former State Home Minister Narottam Mishra, who was denied a ticket from the seat that he has represented thrice.
Accepting the mandate on Monday, Mr. Khandelwal also hinted, without taking any names, at action against those who may have worked against the party’s interests.
‘Find betrayers’
“First, we have to find out who the betrayer is,” Mr. Tiwari told reporters on a question about internal sabotage. A source in the State BJP unit said the meeting at the Chief Minister’s residence was “largely focused on allegations of sabotage”.
Political observes believe that the remarks were directed at Mr. Mishra.
Observers also recall a tearful Mr. Mishra at Mr. Tiwari’s nomination rally and attribute the BJP’s defeat in Datia town, a long-time BJP stronghold, to the discontent of his large supporter base there.
“Ashutosh Tiwari and the election in-charge [Mr. Kushwaha] both have made direct allegations. They have given some proof from there side but its not like the leadership was not aware of this already. And if there was actually sabotage, the State unit can only give its report to the high-command. Any action against those responsible will only be taken by Delhi,” a senior party functionary in Bhopal said.
Meanwhile, the Congress has targeted the BJP government over the bypoll result and said it indicates the “sentiment of the entire State”.
In a letter to Chief Minister Yadav, State Congress president Jitu Patwari sought white papers on the condition of various sectors like education, health, agriculture, youth employment, women’s safety and problems of the tribal and Dalit communities.
“We should not limit the mandate from Datia merely to a matter of political victory or defeat, but to view it as an opportunity for the state’s future. The government should issue a series of white papers on the key issues to present the true state of affairs to the public,” he said in the letter.

headline: The Gujarat health department has organised 6,868 medical camps, deployed more than 18,000 surveillance teams and administered preventive medicines to over 7.61 lakh people in flood-affected districts as part of an extensive drive to avert disease ou...
full_text:
The Gujarat health department has organised 6,868 medical camps, deployed more than 18,000 surveillance teams and administered preventive medicines to over 7.61 lakh people in flood-affected districts as part of an extensive drive to avert disease outbreaks following last week’s heavy rains, officials said on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).
According to officials, over 1.74 lakh people were examined and treated at the medical camps, while surveillance teams conducted daily door-to-door visits, distributing more than 1.05 crore chlorine tablets and 10.29 lakh ORS packets in affected areas.
The State government said a comprehensive Monsoon Action Plan had been implemented across all 34 districts and eight municipal corporations before and during the rainy season, helping prevent any major public health emergency despite widespread flooding.
Health authorities also conducted regular health check-ups in relief camps and shifted 675 pregnant women from vulnerable areas to healthcare facilities in advance, where 272 deliveries were carried out safely.
Round-the-clock health control rooms were established in all districts and municipal corporations, with each district receiving five additional emergency medical teams along with dedicated vehicles and staff. As many as 1,496 ambulances under the 108 Emergency Service and 816 ambulances attached to primary and community health centres have also been kept on standby.
The department said all government healthcare institutions have been stocked with more than 1.5 crore chlorine tablets, over 60 lakh ORS packets and 1,38,234 anti-snake venom injections.
Following the receding of floodwaters, preventive medicines against leptospirosis were administered to more than 7.61 lakh high-risk residents in 562 villages across Surat, Tapi, Valsad and Navsari districts. Additionally, 497 extra vector control teams were deployed in south and central Gujarat to undertake anti-larval measures and create public awareness against vector-borne diseases.
Torrential rain lashed several parts of south and central Gujarat on August 1, prompting authorities to evacuate around 27,000 people and rescue 53 others, particularly in Surat and Navsari districts, where flood-like conditions cut off several villages.
The India Meteorological Department has forecast light to moderate rainfall in parts of north, south and central Gujarat, as well as the Saurashtra region, during the week.

headline: Students belonging to SC/ST communities, who come under the post-matric scholarship scheme, have been asked to pay several lakhs of rupees in cash annually to private medical colleges towards “development fee” and under other heads every year so as t...
full_text:
Students belonging to SC/ST communities, who come under the post-matric scholarship scheme, have been asked to pay several lakhs of rupees in cash annually to private medical colleges towards “development fee” and under other heads every year so as to retain their seat in those colleges, affected parents have alleged.
At a press conference in Chennai on Tuesday, some of the affected parents said private colleges were collecting ₹6 lakh to ₹10 lakh from them in cash. No receipts were given to them after payment. “This has been the practice by almost all private medical colleges,” alleged M. Bharathan, state organiser, AKAM (Ambedkar Kalvi Centenary Movement) Foundation. “Out of the 2,500 medical seats available to SC/ST students in Tamil Nadu every year, only around 1,100 get filled due to these teething issues. As part of the post-matric scholarship scheme, both government quota and management quota students get their tuition fees paid by the government. This amount is demanded over and above that,” Mr. Bharathan alleged.
An affected parent, on condition of anonymity, said he was asked to pay ₹7.7 lakh cash at the time of admission which he mobilised after selling gold jewellery and borrowing money on usury. Before the first-year term-end exam, he was asked to pay the same amount for the next year without which his child won’t be able to appear for the exam. Another parent said that he had to sell his house to fund his child’s dream of studying medicine. The paperwork for loans disbursed by Tamil Nadu Adi Dravidar Housing and Development Corporation (TAHDCO), too, required endorsement by two government officials, putting the parents in a tight spot, they added.
“Almost all private colleges, whether the ones in Trichy, or Salem, or Kundrathur, collect this exorbitant fee and do not provide receipts to the parents. The Income Tax Department should carry out raids during the admission season,” Mr. Bharathan asserted.
In engineering colleges, the problem lies mostly with the government. As per G.O. 72 issued in 2018, the government sanctioned ₹50,000 as the scholarship payment towards meeting tuition fees for either government quota seats or the management quota. All private colleges have since increased their fees for popular courses like Computer Science and Engineering and AI-related courses, even for the government quota seats, said G. Chandramohan, state organiser, AKAM Foundation. Fees for the management quota seats and some of the government quota seats (depending upon the popularity of the course) have been increased to about ₹1.5 lakh per annum, he added. “We demand that G.O. 72 be withdrawn and scholarship amount be drawn up freshly keeping in mind the course fee,” Mr. Bharathan added. He also demanded the setting up of a fees fixation committee for Arts and Science colleges where SC/ST students get a scholarship amount of ₹1,500 per annum.

headline: Zepto, IndiGo, and Physics Wallah among 9 platforms penalised for deceiving consumers
full_text:
Zepto, IndiGo, and Physics Wallah among 9 platforms penalised for deceiving consumers
The CCPA issued an advisory in June 2025 asking e-commerce platforms to conduct self-audits to detect dark patterns on their platforms
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has penalised nine digital platforms, including IndiGo, Zepto, FirstCry, Physics Wallah and SpiceJet, for deploying “dark patterns”, or deceptive user interface designs that manipulate consumer choices, the government told the Rajya Sabha. The consumer affairs department has strengthened safeguards against unfair digital trade practices, it added.
The Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, identifies and regulates 13 types of deceptive interface designs, including false urgency, basket sneaking, subscription traps, drip pricing, confirm shaming and trick questions.
The CCPA issued an advisory in June 2025 asking e-commerce platforms to conduct self-audits to detect dark patterns on their platforms. The regulator has since then collected about ₹20 lakh in fines from those found violating the guidelines, the government told the upper House in a written reply on Tuesday.
Zepto Marketplace, a quick commerce outlet, was fined ₹7 lakh after the CCPA found that the platform initially displayed lower prices but added handling charges and membership fees. The CCPA noted that the handling charges amounted to drip pricing, while automatically adding the membership constituted basket sneaking.
The government informed the House that Zepto has discontinued the dark pattern.
The CCPA took suo motu cognisance and fined digital education platform Physics Wallah ₹5 lakh after the regulator found that a ₹10 donation to its “PW Foundation” was automatically pre-selected. It found emotionally persuasive messaging was displayed to nudge consumers into retaining the pre-selected donation amount.
The CCPA objected to free courses requiring mandatory disclosure of personal information before access. “The company deposited the penalty and discontinued the dark pattern,” the government told the Rajya Sabha.
The CCPA acted on complaints about IndiGo’s confirm shaming on its mobile application. The airline replaced the earlier opt-out message, “No I will take risk”, with the more neutral, “No, I will not add to the trip” after the regulator’s intervention.
BookMyShow, a movie ticket booking platform, was asked to remove a pre-ticked ₹1 contribution to its charitable initiative BookASmile after being pulled up for basket sneaking.
The regulator imposed penalties on FirstCry ( ₹2 lakh), PharmaEasy ( ₹1 lakh), McAfee ( ₹1 lakh), SpiceJet ( ₹1 lakh) and coaching platform Anuj Jindal ( ₹3 lakh), directing them to discontinue dark patterns ranging from hidden charges and forced subscriptions to misleading countdown timers and manipulative subscription renewal prompts.

headline: Ensure roads are stray cattle, encroachment-free, SC tells civic bodies
full_text:
Ensure roads are stray cattle, encroachment-free, SC tells civic bodies
The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed states and union territories to ensure public spaces and roads are cleared of stray cattle and encroachments as it pulled up civic agencies of state capitals to take time-bound action in this regard
The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed states and union territories to ensure public spaces and roads are cleared of stray cattle and encroachments as it pulled up civic agencies of state capitals to take time-bound action in this regard.
A bench of justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R Mahadevan said, “There is total anarchy on the roads. Rules are not being followed. The state of affairs of encroachment of public land is not only shocking but alarming.”
Issuing directions to civic agencies to come out with action taken reports against persons who indulge in such blatant misuse of building bye-laws, the court said, “We will see if your areas are encroachment-free. Even vehicles on roads are unable to move freely due to stray cattle. We direct all public areas to be kept free of stray animals as per law. This order shall apply to all public areas across the country.”
The order came while the court was considering a case from Tamil Nadu relating to a construction made in blatant misuse of land use and violation of building bye-laws. The court expanded the scope of the petition in March this year by issuing notices to civic bodies in major state capitals which included Delhi, Lucknow, Jaipur, Chennai, Kolkata among others.
On Tuesday, senior advocate Ajit Kumar Sinha along with advocate Govind Jee assisting the court as amicus curiae pointed out that several states and civic bodies have not filed compliance reports and those which have filed have not provided sufficient information.
Citing a news report which stated that 93% of buildings in Gurugram lack fire clearance, the bench said, “This is shocking. What are the authorities doing about it?” The Gurugram civic and land owning authority heads were present in court and said that the action against illegal constructions and encroachments is an ongoing exercise and the same will be completed within four weeks.
The court said, “Do you want this court to prod you on such an important matter. We will send a team to verify your claims. If we find your statement to be wrong, you will face perjury proceedings. We know all this is due to collusion of officials.”
The court found that several states were not parties in the proceedings and to get a pan-India status of action against encroachment and stray cattle, the court brought all states and UTs on board.
Turning to Lucknow, where a fire at a coaching centre claimed lives of 15 persons, the court was informed by top officials of Lucknow Development Authority that several officials have been suspended after it became known that several residential premises are being misused for commercial purpose. In Lucknow alone, notices have been issued to 51 such properties, the court was informed.
The bench said, “The public has no patience in this regard. It is time the states realise the court should not be taken for granted or we shall summon the chief secretaries of defaulting states.”
The court was further informed by the amicus that in Delhi, violations are of such a magnitude that there exists a serious threat of a major mishap or calamity, pointing to rampant illegal constructions in areas like Lajpat Nagar and Sarojini Nagar. The amicus report submitted to court showed that buildings have been constructed far beyond the sanctioned plans, with deviations exceeding the condonable limits and in blatant violation of the building bye-laws.
The report even pointed to the tragic and unfortunate incident that took place on May 30 in Saket where a five-storeyed building collapsed leaving at least 6 dead and 14 injured.
The court agreed to take up the matter concerning Delhi on Wednesday.

headline: UP has the highest number of traffic violations caught on e-challan: Centre
full_text:
UP has the highest number of traffic violations caught on e-challan: Centre
Nitin Gadkari said the Central Government has introduced the Central Motor Vehicles (Third Amendment) Rules, 2026
Uttar Pradesh is the state with the highest number of traffic violations caught via the e-challan system and also the one with the largest pool of unrecovered penalties in the country, the Parliament was told on Wednesday.
In fact, Uttar Pradesh has issued 20% of all e-challans issued in the country and when clubbed with Delhi, the two states account for over half of all unpaid traffic fines across states.
Between 2021 and 2026 (till July 30), Uttar Pradesh issued 78.9 million e-challans, followed by Tamil Nadu (63.7 million) and Delhi (47.1 million). Kerala stands fourth in the list with 45.8 million, while Gujarat, fifth, issued 19.9 million e-challans.
Uttar Pradesh ( ₹113,315 crore, 25.60%) and Delhi ( ₹110,760 crore, 25.02%) are the only states to cross the ₹100,000 crore mark in unpaid dues. Tamil Nadu sits at a distant third with ₹3,601 crore (8.14%), followed by Haryana ( ₹2,620 crore. 5.92%) and Odisha ( ₹2,167 crore, 4.9%).
Also Read:TDRF jawan dies in pothole crash on Mumbai-Nashik highway
At the other end of the spectrum, hilly regions and island territories reported the lowest enforcement activity. Ladakh sits at the bottom of the issuance list with only 598 challans since 2021. Nagaland (1,866), Arunachal Pradesh (2,120), Sikkim (5,533), and Mizoram (43,316) also recorded relatively low numbers.
The unpaid fine list reflects a similar trend. Ladakh has a mere ₹2,500 in pending fines, followed by Nagaland ( ₹53 lakh), Arunachal Pradesh ( ₹54 lakh), Sikkim ( ₹1.46 crore), and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands ( ₹1.99 crore).
Replying to a question by MP Sanjay Seth, Union road transport minister Nitin Gadkari said that to tackle the growing mountain of unpaid fines, the Central Government has introduced the Central Motor Vehicles (Third Amendment) Rules, 2026. Under these new rules, repeat offenders those committing five or more offenses in a year starting January 2026 will face the disqualification of their driving licenses.
Furthermore, the reply mentioned that government is leveraging the digital link between the e-challan system and vehicle records with owners being barred from processing any vehicle or license-related transactions until their pending e-challans are settled.

headline: IMA Headquarters termed the governmentâs August 3 Government Resolution (GR) âillegalâ.
full_text:
IMA Headquarters termed the governmentâs August 3 Government Resolution (GR) âillegalâ.
NEW DELHI: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has threatened a nationwide strike if the Maharashtra government does not withdraw its recent decision permitting registration of BHMS graduates (Homepathy) who have completed the Certificate Course in Modern Pharmacology (CCMP) with the Maharashtra Medical Council (MMC).In a letter to Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Wednesday, IMA Headquarters termed the governmentâs August 3 Government Resolution (GR) âillegalâ and urged its immediate cancellation, arguing that it undermines medical education, violates established legal principles and poses a risk to public health.The controversy centres on the stateâs decision to allow CCMP-qualified BHMS doctors to register with the Maharashtra Medical Council. The IMA has objected both to the CCMP course and to what it calls âdual medical council registration.ââThe CCMP course has not been approved by the erstwhile Medical Council of India (MCI), the National Medical Commission (NMC), or the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH). Such a course cannot be considered valid and should be discontinued immediately,â the association said in its representation.The doctorsâ body also argued that allowing practitioners to hold registrations under two different medical councils is unprecedented in India and could mislead patients regarding a doctorâs qualifications and scope of practice.
The IMA further pointed out that the issue is already pending before the Bombay high court in a petition challenging amendments to the Maharashtra Medical Council Act. It said the government should not proceed with registrations while the matter remains sub judice.Questioning the stateâs justification of addressing rural doctor shortages, the association claimed the circumstances have changed significantly since similar provisions were introduced over a decade ago.âThe Maharashtra government has already done away with the compulsory rural bond system for MBBS graduates because of the non-availability of vacant posts, indicating that there is no longer a shortage of qualified allopathic doctors,â the letter stated.
The association also said equating MBBS graduates, who undergo years of full-time medical education, with CCMP-trained practitioners who complete a part-time course would be unfair to students pursuing modern medicine.Citing the Supreme Courtâs landmark judgment in Poonam Verma vs Ashwin Patel (1996), the IMA reiterated that practitioners registered in one recognised system of medicine cannot prescribe medicines or practise another system without recognised qualifications and valid registration in that system.The IMA warned that if the GR is not withdrawn and the CCMP course is not discontinued, it will call for a nationwide strike involving doctors of modern medicine, including medical students, resident doctors and interns across the country.Copies of the representation have also been sent to the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister, Union Health Minister and the Chairperson of the National Medical Commission.

headline: Akhilesh Yadav reaches out to Brahmins, says Samajwadi's 'PDA' includes Pandits
full_text:
Akhilesh Yadav reaches out to Brahmins, says Samajwadi's 'PDA' includes Pandits
Akhilesh Yadav told a Brahmin gathering that the Samajwadi Party's PDA includes Pandits. He said the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh was targeting Brahmins, opposition workers and religious leaders.
Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday reached out to the Brahmin community, saying the party's 'PDA' formulation includes Pandits. He also accused the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh of targeting opposition workers, Brahmins and religious leaders, including a Shankaracharya.
Addressing a Brahmin Sammelan organised at the SP state headquarters on the birth anniversary of late socialist leader Janeshwar Mishra, Yadav said the state government had denied permission to hold the event at its proposed venue, Janeshwar Mishra Park in Gomti Nagar. He said this forced the party to shift the programme to its office premises.
'People keep talking about PDA and inventing new definitions of it. Ever since they lost to PDA, they have been trying to redefine it. But they have forgotten that the 'PD' in PDA also stands for Pandit. The more they inflict pain (peeda), the stronger PDA will become,' Yadav said. PDA is a term coined by Yadav during the 2022 Assembly elections for Picchda (backwards), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities).
Recalling Mishra's contribution to the socialist movement, Yadav described him as 'Chhote Lohia' and said the park named after him in Lucknow reflected his stature. The former Uttar Pradesh chief minister also accused the BJP government of persecuting opposition workers and claimed that several incidents involving SP members had been covered up. "They were already targeting our workers and us. Now they have also started targeting the Brahmin community. They are after the 'P' of PDA as well," he alleged.
Without naming anyone, Yadav also criticised the functioning of the state's health department, saying it had been 'completely ruined'. He further accused the government of insulting religious institutions and alleged that a Shankaracharya had been prevented from taking a holy dip during the Kumbh congregation.
"If there is any example in history where a government stopped a Shankaracharya from taking a holy dip, show us one. The Shankaracharya had to stage a protest, and the police misbehaved with his disciples. A false POCSO case was also filed to intimidate him, but he did not bow down," Yadav claimed.
Yadav was referring to Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, who made headlines over his confrontation with the organisers of the Magh Mela in Prayagraj, accusing them of preventing him from taking a bath on Mauni Amavasya. In his address, Yadav linked this allegation with his wider charge that the government was targeting opposition workers, Brahmins and religious figures.

For 19 years, Taslima Nasreen carried Kolkata in her memories, longing to return but unable to do so. The city that had become her âsecond homeâ after she left Bangladesh in 1994 remained out of reach. Forced to flee her country of birth and later compelled to leave the city where she had settled, Nasreen spent much of the past three decades moving from one place to another, not in search of adventure but of refuge, without quite recovering the sense of home she associated with Kolkata.That door finally opened nearly 19 years later.Nasreen set foot in the City of Joy on July 31 and received a civic felicitation at Rabindra Sadan on August 1. The visit was accompanied by a warm official welcome from West Bengalâs new government, with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari assuring the writer of security whenever she chose to visit.The author, who was forced to leave Kolkata in 2007, responded with gratitude. âItâs not just the city I return to; for me, itâs a homecoming to a lost chapter of my life,â she said.The change of government has given Nasreen fresh hope of spending more time in Kolkata, something that did not become possible under the previous two administrations. But it has also raised a more difficult question: Is her return merely a ceremonial visit, or could it be the first step towards once again making Kolkata her home?
Homecoming: Delayed, but not denied
In November 2007, Kolkata witnessed violent protests by groups opposed to Nasreen and her writings, including her memoir Dwikhandito. Amid concerns over her safety and the worsening law-and-order situation, the authorities moved her out of the city.
She was taken first to Jaipur and later kept under security in New Delhi before eventually leaving India for Europe. Her repeated appeals to successive governments to let her return to Kolkata did not produce a result.
Almost two decades and two changes of government later, her return became possible. âTaslima Nasreenâs return proves that Bengal is in good hands now. Threats and intimidation are in the past. Every pillar of the Constitution and fundamental rights are safe now,â Adhikari said at the felicitation.âYou can come to Kolkata whenever you want, as many times as you want, and stay as long as you want. As the chief minister and police minister of Bengal, I am personally responsible for your security.â Nasreen was equally effusive in her gratitude.âHistory remembers who shut the door. Now, history will also remember who reopened it,â she said. âThe opening of this door proves injustice can feel like a long night, but itâs never permanent.â But the cordial exchange also opened a larger conversation.Can Kolkata become a sanctuary to which Nasreen returns not merely as a guest but as a long-term resident? The answer is not straightforward. The chief minister can assure her of security within the state, but any longer-term residential arrangement would also depend on her visa status and decisions by the appropriate immigration authorities. Visa extensions and residential permits for foreign nationals are handled through the FRRO/FRO system and, in some cases, the Union home ministry.
Kolkata: Then and now
Nineteen years is a long time, particularly in a period of rapid political and social change. The Kolkata Nasreen knew in the early 2000s is not the city to which she has returned.For the writer, âevery year in banishment looked like a door heavily boltedâ. Meanwhile, although the government that moved her out of the city is no longer in power, her return has acquired a new and complicated political context.Nasreen has not forgotten how abruptly she had to leave Kolkata while the Left Front governed Bengal. She remains sharply critical of the Left, accusing sections of it of failing to defend free-thinkers while claiming to stand for secularism and progressive values.But the Kolkata of 2026 is governed by the BJP, and Nasreenâs return unfolded amid the symbols and slogans associated with its politics. Chief Minister Adhikari was welcomed at Rabindra Sadan with chants of âJai Shri Ramâ, a religious invocation that has also become a prominent political slogan.Nasreen has consistently argued that religion and the state should remain separate.âHumanity has to be bigger than any doctrine,â she said during her homecoming address.She also sought to draw a clear line between gratitude and political endorsement. âIâm thankful to this government for letting me return. But my gratitude doesnât warrant my allegiance to them. I havenât come here for any political party,â she said.The question, therefore, is not whether she is grateful to the government that facilitated her return. She plainly is. The harder question is whether Kolkata can protect her right to disagree with the same establishment if her views become inconvenient to it.The cultural composition of the felicitation offered another indication of how much the cityâs public life has changed. For a ceremony honouring one of the Bengali languageâs most internationally recognised writers, relatively few prominent members of the literary fraternity were present.Novelist Shirshendu Mukhopadhyay, who had been expected to attend, was absent. Poet Joy Goswami was present, but his appearance led to the most uncomfortable moment of the evening.When Nasreen invited Goswami to join her on the stage, a section of the audience erupted in protest, shouting slogans and objecting to his presence on the dais. Goswami, who had begun walking towards the stage, turned around and returned to his seat.The disruption continued for several minutes. Nasreen waited quietly before appealing to the audience to calm down and allow the programme to continue.The irony was difficult to miss. An event organised to celebrate a writer who had spent decades defending freedom of expression had briefly become a venue for preventing another poet from speaking.The hostility appeared to be connected to Goswamiâs perceived proximity to the previous Trinamool Congress establishment and criticism that prominent cultural figures had not done enough to defend Nasreen when she was made to leave Kolkata. Whatever the political grievance, however, it could not justify denying him the opportunity to speak after Nasreen herself had invited him.Goswami did not confront the protesters and later left Rabindra Sadan without reading the poem he had written for Nasreen.âEveryone has the right to speak. When someone speaks about freedom of expression, people support it; but when a poet is invited to speak, they do not want to hear him. That is not right,â Nasreen said the following day.âIt wasnât just Joy who was insulted. I was also insulted because I had invited him.âThe organisers also expressed regret over the incident. Nasreen subsequently spoke to Goswami by telephone after being unable to visit him during the trip.The episode showed how quickly cultural spaces can become arenas for political resentment. For all the celebration surrounding Nasreenâs homecoming, Kolkata is still negotiating the same difficult questions about dissent, ideological loyalty and the right to disagree that formed the background to her departure.The real test will not be how warmly the city welcomes her when her presence suits the political moment. It will be whether Kolkata continues to defend her when she says something those in power, or their supporters, do not wish to hear.
Where to next?
Kolkata has reopened its doors to Nasreen after nearly 19 years. Her own homeland, however, remains out of reach. After Lajja provoked widespread outrage among Islamist groups, Nasreen faced threats and criminal proceedings over her writings and public statements. Her Bangladeshi passport was revoked, and she left the country in 1994.Nearly 32 years later, she has still not been able to return permanently. Exile remains the defining condition of her life. âThe number of years Iâve been away from home has already surpassed the sum of time I was allowed to live there,â said Nasreen, who will turn 64 later this month.And yet she has supported former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasinaâs right to return to the country, even though Nasreen has said that Hasinaâs government opposed her own attempts to return to Bangladesh in 1999. âIâve criticised Sheikh Hasina in the past,â Nasreen said. âThe ban on the Awami League must be revoked since itâs undemocratic. Sheikh Hasina wants to return. I want her to return for the sake of democracy in Bangladesh.âHasina, who has been living in India since her government fell in August 2024, has said she intends to return to Bangladesh by December despite a death sentence handed down in absentia, which she rejects as politically motivated. She was scheduled to make her first public appearance since her ouster through a virtual address in New Delhi on August 5.Nasreenâs defence of Hasinaâs right to return is notable precisely because of their history. It is an argument that the right to go home should not depend on political sympathy or personal gratitude. âNo one wants my return. Sheikh Hasina did not. Neither did Khaleda Zia nor those who came to power subsequently,â Nasreen said, her disappointment over the repeated refusals unmistakable.But she refuses to abandon hope. âIt took me 19 years to be able to say, âKolkata, Iâve come back to youâ,â she said. âI have tears in my eyes, but I come with a heart full of love.âHer return to the City of Joy has renewed her belief that seemingly permanent barriers can eventually fall. âNineteen years stand between my exile and return. But the opening of this door proves injustice can be long-standing but never permanent.âPerhaps that is why Nasreen continues to dream of a day âwhen no writer has to live in exile from her own countryâ. She hopes Bangladesh will one day separate religion from the state and become a country where women have equal rights, minorities can live with dignity and free-thinkers and non-believers are not threatened for their views.In Indiaâs neighbouring country, that day may yet come. For now, Nasreen is grateful that she can at least return to Kolkata, revisit its familiar spaces and, she hopes, attend the Book Fair as she once did.
Her former address in the city no longer belongs to her. Kolkata has changed, and the pet that once helped make the city feel like home is no longer alive. But after nearly 19 years, Taslima Nasreen has returned, carrying with her hope, unfinished arguments and, perhaps, a few more lives in reserve.

headline: Man accused of kidnapping, raping schoolgirl lynched by mob in Jharkhand
full_text:
Man accused of kidnapping, raping schoolgirl lynched by mob in Jharkhand
Eight people were arrested in Jharkhand after an angry mob fatally beat a man who held a schoolgirl captive and raped her for two days.
A 32-year-old man accused of kidnapping and raping a girl died after being severely beaten by an angry mob in Jharkhand's Chatra district, police said, adding that eight people have been arrested in connection with the lynching.
According to locals, the man, Md Emroz, had kidnapped a schoolgirl and held her hostage inside his residence for two days.
The girl's family had been frantically searching for her but was unable to find any trace of her whereabouts. The situation reached a boiling point early Tuesday morning when the minor finally returned home. She recounted her ordeal to her family, alleging that she had been held captive by Emroz, who also threatened to kill her.
Enraged by the girl's statement, a large crowd of villagers gathered and surrounded the accused's house, subsequently launching an attack on him.
Police, who reached the scene, managed to rescue a critically injured Emroz from the crowd and transported him to a local hospital. After receiving primary treatment, he was referred to a higher medical facility, where he died during treatment.
Emroz's father, Sultan Miyan, also sustained injuries during the mob's attack.
Authorities have placed the girl under protection and initiated the mandatory medical examination process. The police have also recorded formal statements from the family members of the man.
Local villagers claim that this was not Emroz's first offence, alleging that he had a previous rape case registered against him and had served time in jail in 2023.
Police have confirmed that the allegations regarding the minor are being thoroughly investigated under due legal process. They added that further efforts are currently underway to identify and arrest other individuals involved in the mob violence.

full_text:
The Madras High Court, on Tuesday, adjourned to August 20, 2026, the hearing on a batch of cases, including the one filed by CREDAI-Chennai chapter, challenging the ban imposed by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) on new construction approvals on 8,584.44 acres of land located within a distance of 1 km around the boundaries of Pallikaranai marsh land, a Ramsar site.
First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan said they were inclined to set aside the blanket ban imposed by the NGT even before the determination of the ‘zone of influence’ around the wetland. They, however, did not want the lifting of the ban by the court to be mistaken as licence for indiscriminate constructions around the marshland.
The judges insisted there must be a balance between the need to preserve the environment by protecting the sources of water to the wetland and the need for infrastructure development. They directed Additional Advocate General P.V. Balasubramaniam to come up with suggestions on areas where constructions could be permitted and those where they could be banned until the final determination of ‘zone of influence.’
The judges granted two weeks’ time to submit the suggestions and said they shall pass further orders after analysing the matter in detail.

Two persons from Haryana was arrested by Kalavai police on Tuesday in connection with a robbery of ₹7 lakh from a private bank’s Automated Teller Machine (ATM) on the Cuddalore-Chittoor Road (NH 38) at Mulluvadi village near Arcot town in the district.
The police said that the arrested persons were identified as R. Sanjay, 25, and N. Rubin, 24. They are natives of Ferozepur Jhirka in Haryana. headline: India has achieved a remarkable milestone in clean energy, generating over one thousand billion units from nuclear power. This achievement helps avoid more than 860 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions. The government aims to increase nuclear p...
full_text:
India has achieved a remarkable milestone in clean energy, generating over one thousand billion units from nuclear power. This achievement helps avoid more than 860 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions. The government aims to increase nuclear power capacity to 100 GW by 2047, with an intermediate target of 22 GW by 2031-32. This expansion will involve multiple stakeholders and the introduction of new legislation.
NEW DELHI: In a milestone for Indiaâs clean energy production, Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) has cumulatively generated over 1,000 billion units of nuclear electricity.NPCIL said Tuesday, âSince commencement of commercial operation, NPCILâs nuclear power plants have cumulatively generated over 1,000 billion units of clean electricity, thereby avoiding over 860 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions into the environment.ââThis milestone reflects NPCILâs steadfast commitment to deliver safe, reliable and sustainable nuclear power, strengthening Indiaâs energy security while supporting the nationâs clean energy transition and climate goals,â it said on XTo give the scale of how much carbon emission is avoided, a typical passenger vehicle emits about 4.6 metric tonnes of CO2 per year. Avoiding 860 million tonnes is equal to taking roughly 187 million gasoline-powered cars going off the road for an entire year. At least 860 million tonnes is roughly equivalent to the total annual greenhouse gas emissions of a major industrial country like Germany or Japan for a full year.Govt has drawn up a roadmap for reaching the 100 GW nuclear power capacity in the next two decades by 2047, as announced in the Nuclear Energy Mission in the Budget 2025-26, thereby increasing the share of reliable, low-carbon base-load nuclear energy in the countryâs energy mix and reaching the goal of net zero carbon emissions by 2070.
The present nuclear power capacity of 8.78 GW is expected to reach about 22 GW by 2031-32 on progressive completion of projects presently at various stages of implementation. Another 32 GW of nuclear power capacity is envisaged to be set up beyond 2032 by NPCIL under the administrative control of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE).
This will comprise indigenous pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and light water reactors (LWRs) planned to be set up by 2047, taking NPCILâs nuclear power capacity to 54 GW.The balance of 46 GW comprising reactors of different technologies, is expected to be set up by other public sector enterprises, private sector and joint ventures in different business models. With the govt enacting the SHANTI Act (Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India Act, 2025) last year, the new law provides the legal framework that makes this 46 GW expansion possible.

headline: The flood doesn't end with the rain: What I witnessed in Kerala's worst-hit areas
full_text:
The flood doesn't end with the rain: What I witnessed in Kerala's worst-hit areas
The rain may have eased by the time we left Kerala's flood-hit Pathanamthitta, but for thousands of families, the ordeal was far from over. Homes had been inundated, businesses destroyed, roads swallowed by floodwaters and entire neighbourhoods emptied as residents sought refuge in relief camps.
"Chechi?" I called out to a woman standing outside her house along the road leading to the famed Aranmula Temple. We had reached the area to report on the severe waterlogging that had submerged the temple approach road and large parts of the premises, bringing movement to a standstill. I was desperately thirsty. Every shop nearby was shut because of the flooding.
"Yes?" she replied, stepping outside. I asked if I could have a glass of water. She smiled, said "of course" and invited me inside. I hesitated because I was drenched from hours of reporting in the rain, but she insisted.
Her house stood on slightly higher ground, with a sloping entrance. Looking at it, I assumed it had escaped the flooding. "The water wouldn't have entered this house, right?" I asked while drinking the water. "It did. Yesterday." Her answer caught me completely off guard. She pointed to the sofa where I was sitting. "In 2018, the water had reached this level."
For her family, this was the first time since Kerala's devastating floods of 2018 that floodwater had entered their home. Then she pointed towards the house opposite. "That belongs to our relatives. They've shifted to a relief camp. The water there rose to the level of the dining table."
As I stepped out, I turned around for one last look at the living room where I had just been sitting. I tried to picture muddy floodwater filling the space, swallowing the furniture and everything around it.
That's the strange thing about covering floods. You can stand waist-deep in water all day and still fail to comprehend what it means for those who live there. The real devastation begins inside people's homes.
From Aranmula, we headed to Ranni, one of the worst-hit towns after overnight torrential rain. I had seen drone footage before arriving, but nothing prepared me for the scene on the ground.
Police had barricaded the road leading into the flooded locality. Beyond the barricades, I waded through water that rose above my waist to report from the heart of the inundated neighbourhood.
A little further ahead, I saw a family taking shelter on the upper floor of their house. The ground floor had disappeared beneath murky floodwater.
"We don't want to leave everything behind and move to a relief camp," an elderly woman called out from upstairs. "Once the rain stops for a while, the water will go down."
It is a dilemma we encounter repeatedly while covering floods. Many residents hesitate to leave because they fear returning to find their homes looted or further damaged. Others simply cannot imagine abandoning everything they own.
For families living in Kerala's flood-prone low-lying areas, relief camps have become an unfortunate annual reality rather than an emergency measure.
Then came one of the most frightening moments I have experienced while reporting.
As I made my way back through the flooded street, I suddenly spotted a live snake cutting swiftly through the current just a few feet away. For a split second, I froze. Then instinct took over. I hurried through the water as fast as I could while keeping an eye on the snake. Thankfully, it slithered onto the gate of a nearby house before disappearing inside the compound.
Despite years of covering floods, this was the first time I had come face-to-face with a snake in floodwater. The fear is always there whenever you step into submerged streets. That day, it became real.
The neighbourhood itself was unnervingly silent. Every house was locked. Every family had left. With floodwater stretching across deserted lanes, the area felt abandoned.
A short distance away, I found a man hurriedly carrying goods to the first floor of a commercial building. He ran a business on the ground floor. "The stock downstairs is soaked. Most of it is damaged," he said without pausing. "We didn't get any warning or proper directions. Had we known earlier, we could have shifted everything to a safer place."
Like many others, he wasn't just counting financial losses. He was trying to salvage whatever little remained before the water claimed that too.
About two kilometres away, a relief camp had been set up at MS Higher Secondary School. Inside, families who had fled their homes just hours earlier were trying to settle into temporary lives. "We are 10 families, around 25 people, staying here," said Mini, who had arrived from a nearby apartment complex.
"We got a call from our panchayat member saying the water level was rising and asking us to leave immediately. We informed all our neighbours and rushed here. We came wearing only the clothes we had on. There wasn't even time to collect our belongings."
For Mini, displacement has become painfully familiar. "This happens almost every year," she said.
Then came the sentence that stayed with me long after we left. "I just hope there is a permanent solution. Going back, cleaning and making life normal again is a task."
That, perhaps, is the part of a flood most people never see.
Television cameras capture swollen rivers, submerged roads and dramatic rescues. But when the rain stops, another battle begins – scrubbing layers of mud from homes, salvaging damaged possessions, reopening shuttered shops and trying to rebuild routines that the water washes away every monsoon.
By the time we drove out of Ranni, the downpour had finally eased, and the floodwaters had begun to recede in parts. For us, the assignment was ending. For the people of Pathanamthitta, it was only the beginning. Their next few days would not be about surviving the flood, but about reclaiming their homes, their livelihoods and, somehow, a sense of normalcy.

headline: Haryana’s dominance at the recently concluded Commonwealth Games (CWG) in Glasgow has sparked a fresh demand from sportspersons and political leaders across party lines to make the State a co-host of the 2030 CWG scheduled to be held in Ahmedabad.
full_text:
Haryana’s dominance at the recently concluded Commonwealth Games (CWG) in Glasgow has sparked a fresh demand from sportspersons and political leaders across party lines to make the State a co-host of the 2030 CWG scheduled to be held in Ahmedabad.
Sportspersons from the agrarian State bagged seven of India’s 13 gold medals and 11 medals overall. Five of the seven golds in boxing came from Bhiwani alone, four of them won by women.
The performance has fuelled calls that the “Mini Cuba” of India, a tribute to the Caribbean island nation that has produced many famed boxers, deserves more than praise.
Bhiwani Boxing Club founder Jagdish Singh, who has trained several world-class boxers, said the demand is legitimate.
‘Strong claim’
“Haryana certainly has a strong claim; after all, we win the highest number of medals. The government renamed the existing stadium in Gujarat after Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and the facilities there are excellent. In terms of infrastructure, that venue is indeed deserving, but Haryana has a stronger claim in terms of performance on the ground,” he said.
Olympic bronze medallist boxer Vijender Singh, a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader, said while the final call rests with the government, “it would be good if they were held in Haryana”.
Will speak to PM: BJP MP
Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) Bhiwani-Mahendragarh MP Dharambir Singh said, “It is valid to say that boxing events — or at least some CWG events — should be held in Bhiwani. It is a hub for boxing in India.”
Mr. Singh said he would seek an appointment with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and raise the issue.
BJP leader and Olympic bronze medallist boxer Vijender Singh said while the final call rests with the government, “it would be good if the games are held in Haryana”. Former BJP Rajya Sabha member Kiran Choudhry said “If that happens, it would not only benefit budding sportspersons in Bhiwani but also those in neighbouring Hisar and Rohtak,” Ms. Choudhry said, adding she would take up the matter with the Prime Minister and Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini.
On Monday (Auust 3, 2026), Congress’s Haryana MPs — Deepender Hooda, Jai Prakash, Varun Mulana, Satpal Brahmachari, and Karmbir Baudh — staged a protest at the Parliament complex demanding that Haryana be made the host or a co-host for the 2030 games.
‘Centre shut the door’
Mr. Hooda alleged the Centre had already shut the door by announcing the Games would be held exclusively in Ahmedabad and that the 2036 Olympics bid was also being submitted only for Gujarat. He asked why Haryana, which wins 50% of the country’s medals at the CWG, Asian Games and Olympics with just 2% of India’s population, continues to face neglect. “Investments worth lakhs of crores of rupees for the games will now flow into Ahmedabad, where sports infrastructure will be developed. Had Haryana been made a co-host, this massive expenditure would have taken place in Haryana as well,” he said.
The Congress leader attacked the State government for not submitting a proposal to host the games and demanded that it immediately send a bid and that the Central government consider it seriously.

headline: NEW DELHI: If a food label says "100% pure", "100% natural" or "100% purity guaranteed", consumers may still need to read it with caution. In one of its strongest actions against misleading food labels, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (F...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: If a food label says "100% pure", "100% natural" or "100% purity guaranteed", consumers may still need to read it with caution. In one of its strongest actions against misleading food labels, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has ordered Dabur India to stop selling a range of products carrying such claims, saying they violated food labelling regulations and could mislead buyers.The order covers products that include organic honey, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, cow ghee, coconut water and coconut milk, marketed with claims such as "100% juice", "100% purity" and "100% original".According to FSSAI, the company had made unauthorised organic claims, creating an impression of regulatory endorsement.The regulator also found that some claims on the labels were not permitted under Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.FSSAI has directed the company to immediately stop the sale of the identified products, recall products already in the market within 15 days and submit a compliance report.In a statement, Dabur said it believes the declarations on its product labels comply with the prevailing legal and regulatory framework and are consistent with long-standing industry practices. It said it stands by the purity and quality of its products and has never made misleading claims.
Dabur said that it had begun removing the "100%" claims from product labels, advertisements and its website, in keeping with FSSAI's observations, adding that many products have already been updated while others are in the process of transition.It said that it is responding to the regulator, and will continue to engage constructively to resolve the matter.
