headline: India's youth is among the best, Sonam Wangchuk says in a video message
full_text:
India's youth is among the best, Sonam Wangchuk says in a video message
Sonam Wangchuk thanked supporters after ending his hunger strike and returning to his village. He said the protest renewed his faith in India's youth, democracy and the people.
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has shared an emotional message of gratitude nearly two weeks after ending his indefinite hunger strike, thanking supporters for standing by him and saying they had restored his faith in India's youth, democracy and the nation.
In a 4-minute, 34-second video posted on X, Wangchuk said it had been 12 days since he ended his fast and five days since he returned to his remote village.
"It's five days since I'm back in my remote village and 12 days since I broke my fast. I've regained six of the 11 kilos I lost. Thank you all for restoring my faith and hope in the youth, in the nation, and in democracy again," he wrote alongside the video.
Wangchuk said he had lost around 11 kg during the hunger strike but had already regained 6 kg and expected to return to his normal routine within a few weeks.
JANTAR MANTRA MEMORIES STAY WITH ME
Although he has returned home, Wangchuk said the memories of the protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar remain fresh.
"Whenever I close my eyes, the scenes from Jantar Mantar come back to me," he said. He praised Generation Z, saying the protest had disproved the perception that young people are lazy or self-centred.
"I have always believed that if young people are given respect and responsibility, there is no one better than them. What I witnessed at Jantar Mantar proved me right," he said.
According to Wangchuk, students and volunteers consistently put others before themselves, supported one another through difficult moments and showed extraordinary commitment during the protest.
INDIA'S YOUTH'S AMONG THE WORLD'S BEST
Drawing on his travels around the world, Wangchuk said India's young people were among the best he had encountered.
"I have travelled to many countries and met people from around the world. I can say with confidence that India's youth is among the best in the world," he said.
He added, however, that the country's real challenge lay with the older generation, particularly political leaders, saying he would speak about that at another time.
THANKS VOLUNTEERS, DOCTORS AND SUPPORTERS
Wangchuk thanked CJP volunteers, core committee members, doctors who monitored his health, student unions, donors, gurdwaras that provided accommodation and food, political parties, farmer organisations, media outlets, content creators, police personnel and government officials who supported or facilitated the protest.
He reserved special thanks for the people of India.
"You have shown that in a democracy, it is ultimately the people who hold the power," he said.
Reflecting on his role in public movements, Wangchuk said he saw himself as someone who gives a stalled vehicle an initial push before it starts moving on its own.
"I was with you until your vehicle started moving. Now I will probably help another movement," he said.
He ended his message on a hopeful note.
"We will meet again somewhere along the way. Wherever I am, I will never be far from you. Stay connected. Thank you once again. Jai Hind."
Earlier during the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day indefinite hunger strike after weeks of negotiations with the Centre, breaking the fast in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh. Wangchuk had launched the strike in support of students protesting irregularities in competitive examinations and demanding accountability for paper leaks.
During the fast, he was shifted to a hospital after doctors advised close monitoring of his health. The Centre assured him that the issue of accountability for paper leaks across India would be discussed by all political parties in Parliament.

The complainant knocked on the Commission’s door alleging that the local police were not keen to investigate the complaint.
A similar complaint alleged that a lender was not returning a 1.25-acre property mortgaged by an elderly person despite repaying the private loan.
Mr. Somaprasad said the Commission would seek report from the departments or agencies concerned on the complaints and summon the parties involved for hearing accordingly. Though two complaints received earlier were scheduled to be heard on Tuesday, neither of the opposing parties in one case turned up. Only the complainant appeared before the panel in the second case.

headline: New government schemes will offer significant financial support to Indian private space companies. These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology...
full_text:
New government schemes will offer significant financial support to Indian private space companies. These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology transfer, and access to ISRO facilities. The programs are designed to lower entry barriers and accelerate private sector growth. This support will make satellite data and infrastructure more affordable for Indian entities.
BENGALURU: Indian private space companies and non-government entities will receive govt support ranging from 30% to 100% on everything from launch services and technology transfer to satellite data and access to Isro facilities under two new schemes of the Department of Space (DoS).The incentives â Launch Services Price-support Scheme (LSPS) and the Price Support Scheme â being implemented by Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) are aimed at lowering entry barriers, making Indian space businesses globally competitive and accelerating private participation across the sector.The larger of the two initiatives is the Launch Services Price-support Scheme, with a budget of Rs 800 crore over five years until June 2031. The scheme seeks to boost domestic commercial launch operations and strengthen India's position as a global launch hub.IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka told TOI: âThe idea is to make the launches competitive. Therefore, we are trying to defray the cost of launch, thereby making the launch cost globally competitive. The ultimate beneficiary will be the satellite launch.âUnder Category A, eligible entities can receive up to 50% support for using Isro and DoS launch facilities.
The benefit extends to NGEs, government entities and launch vehicle providers.Category B offers a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower, for Indian small launch vehicles carrying satellites, experiments or payloads weighing up to 500 kg. The support is available to satellite owners and operators.The subsidy would apply to launches by Indian private entities from Indian soil too. âIt will be applicable to [Skyrootâs] Vikram also. Any satellite launch by an Indian company... from Indian soil... we will directly pay the satellite guys $3,000 per kg,â Goenka said. He added that the policy is focused on promoting small launch vehicles where private sector participation is growing.Category C provides the highest level of support, offering 100% funding for repurposed upper-stage platforms carrying payloads of up to 120 kg. The funding is capped at $13,000 per kg and limited to four missions. The category is aimed at NGEs, govt entities and launch vehicle providers.Category D extends launch incentives to satellites weighing up to 100 kg launched aboard PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 missions. Beneficiaries will receive a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower.Complementing the launch incentives is a separate Price Support Scheme for Indian entities, which will run for three years until Feb 2029. The programme is intended to reduce the cost of accessing Indiaâs space infrastructure, technologies and data.The scheme has three components. The first provides up to 50% support for the utilisation of DoS and In-SPACe facilities, along with technical expertise.
The second offers a 30% subsidy on Technology Transfer Fees (TTF) for technologies licensed from Isro, lowering the cost for companies seeking to commercialise govt-developed technologies.The third provides a 50% subsidy on standard Earth Observation data and data products, making satellite imagery and geospatial datasets more affordable for Indian companies developing applications in agriculture, urban planning, disaster management, climate services and other downstream sectors.
Chethan Kumar is a Senior Assistant Editor with the Times of India. Aside from specialising in Space & Science, he has reported extensively on varied topics, with special focus on defence, policy and data stories. He has covered multiple elections, too. As a young democracy grows out of adolescence, Chethan feels, there are reels of tales emerging which need to be captured. To do this, he alternates between the mundane goings-on of the Common Man and the wonder-filled worlds of scientists and scamsters, politicians and soldiers. In a career spanning nearly 18 years, he has reported from multiple datelines â Houston, Florida, Kochi, Hyderabad, Chennai, Sriharikota (AP), NH-1 (J&K Highway), New Delhi, Ahmedabad, Raichur, Bhatkal, Mysuru, Chamarajanagar, to name a few â but is based out of Bengaluru, Indiaâs science capital that also hosts the ISRO HQ.

headline: Marine researchers claimed to have solved a 150-year-old taxonomic confusion regarding the identity of the thorny seahorse, Hippocampus histrix.

Marine researchers claimed to have solved a 150-year-old taxonomic confusion regarding the identity of the thorny seahorse, Hippocampus histrix.
Scientific studies have identified a new species, Hippocampus amandavincentae, which was previously misidentified as Hippocampus histrix, they said.
Earlier, researchers had described Hippocampus jayakari, a lesser-known one, which was also previously wrongly identified as Hippocampus histrix, they said.
The new species, which was named after noted marine biologist Amanda Vincent, was collected from the fish bycatch at the Tuticorin fisheries harbour by Shalu Kannan, the lead author of the paper.
The species was described in a recently released research paper, according to the team of researchers from Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies (Kufos).
This is also the fifth known seahorse species from the Kerala coast, they said.
The study published in the taxonomy journal Zootaxa demonstrated that the thorny seahorse (Hippocampus histrix), historically believed to be widespread from the Red Sea and East Africa across the Indian Ocean to the western Pacific, was three distinct species, they claimed.
“Many museum specimens and online biodiversity records of spiny seahorses in the Indian Ocean have been assigned to Hippocampus histrix for decades,“ said Rajeev Raghavan, Assistant Professor at Kufos and a senior author of the study.
The new species was photographed alive during a survey held as part of the Ecomarine project at around 15-metre depth on the rocky reefs off Anchuthengu, said Kufos Vice-Chancellor A. Biju Kumar.

A 12-year-old tribal girl from Mancheeri hamlet in Karulai forest range of Nilambur sustained a thumb injury after she was allegedly beaten with a stick by her mathematics teacher at school. The Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has registered a case.
The Class VI student of S.V. Higher Secondary School, Palemadu, suffered swelling on her thumb after the alleged assault on July 21. The student is among the 16 Cholanaikan children from the Mancheeri tribal settlement studying at the school. She stays at a hostel run by Mahila Samakhya at Palemadu. According to sources, the teacher punished students for scoring poor marks in the examination.
Cholanaikans are a particularly vulnerable tribal group (PVTG) living deep inside the forests of Nilambur in Malappuram district. Traditionally, they lived in natural rock shelters and caves and are often described as among the last surviving cave-dwelling indigenous communities in Asia.
The child’s father Mani was killed in an elephant attack on January 4, 2025, while returning on foot to the hamlet after dropping his children at the hostel.
Mahila Samakhya district programme coordinator M. Rajeena took the child to a private clinic, where she was given a pain-relief injection. She was later taken to Eranad Hospital, Edakkara, where an X-ray ruled out a fracture.
Ms. Rajeena said the student entered school only in Class IV, without any primary education. “She is in Class VI now, but the learning gap still affects her studies,” she said.
Ms. Rajeena said she met the headmaster and teachers after the incident and warned them about the consequences of corporal punishment. She also reported the matter to her higher authorities.
According to sources, the school management informed the teacher that she would be held responsible for any consequences arising from the incident.
Representatives of Child Helpline (formerly Childline) visited the hostel on Monday and spoke to the girl. Child Rights Commission member Shajesh Bhaskar told The Hindu that a suo motu case was registered after seeing the video of the girl in sling, and a notice served on the school.

headline: Amid PM Modi video row, Meta’s global executives to meet MeitY officials today
full_text:
Amid PM Modi video row, Meta’s global executives to meet MeitY officials today
MeitY summoned the tech giant after a Facebook reel by the PM addressing nationwide protests over the NEET paper leak was removed from the platform.
Senior global executives from Meta, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, will meet officials from the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) on August 5 and 6 following the temporary takedown of a video posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, a government official said on Tuesday.
MeitY summoned the tech giant after a Facebook reel by the Prime Minister addressing nationwide protests over the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET-UG) paper leak was removed from the platform for about five hours on July 28.
Speaking on the sidelines of an event in New Delhi, MeitY secretary S Krishnan said the discussions will cover non-compliance with Indian laws, Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM), synthetically generated content, and safeguards for verified accounts, alongside the video removal.
Also Read | 'Stop them immediately': Centre orders Meta to remove Instagram ads promoting child sex abuse content
“There will be a range of issues…We know that the CSAM issue was raised…what measures have been taken regarding that? Synthetically generated information…to what extent that is being looked at? For prominent personalities, they have verified accounts. When content gets taken down, there have to be safeguards. We would like to understand from them as to why some of these things have not been working the way they are supposed to work and what are their challenges. After all, these are some of the world’s leading technology companies and they should have technology to make this work,” Krishnan said.
The August 5-6 meeting was convened after the ministry expressed disappointment with Meta’s India policy team, which it felt was not adequately conveying government concerns to the company’s US leadership, Hindustan Times reported earlier.
The secretary did not disclose the names of the executive delegation visiting India. Meta’s global public policy and global affairs leadership is headed by Joel Kaplan, chief global affairs officer, and Kevin Martin, vice-president and head of global policy. An emailed query sent to Meta seeking comment did not receive a response.
The upcoming meeting follows demands from Nishikant Dubey, chairperson of the parliamentary standing committee on Information Technology and Communications, for an apology from Meta chief executive officer and co-founder Mark Zuckerberg over the video removal.
Dubey stated that failure to issue an apology could result in Meta losing its safe harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act. Section 79 grants online intermediaries immunity from liability for third-party content hosted on their platforms, contingent upon compliance with due diligence requirements and lawful government directions.
However, legal protection under safe harbour is statutory and cannot be revoked unilaterally by the government. An intermediary’s entitlement to immunity remains a legal matter for determination by courts based on compliance with conditions specified under Section 79.
During the parliamentary committee meeting, a Meta executive apologised for the removal of the Prime Minister’s video, attributing the incident to an algorithmic error, according to people present at the meeting who spoke to Hindustan Times. The executive assured the panel that Meta would amend its algorithm to prevent recurrence.
A separate query sent to Meta regarding the committee chairperson’s demand for Zuckerberg’s apology also went unanswered.

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday backed students protesting over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand's recruitment examinations, saying his party stands with students and youth "whether it is Jharkhand, Punjab, Delhi or anywhere else".Additionally, he also demanded that the Union home minister come to Parliament and explain the alleged lathi-charge and use of pellet guns against protesting students in Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
"We want the Union Home Minister to come to the House and tell us who ordered the lathi-charge and the use of pellet guns on students," Kharge said while addressing a press conference in Delhi.Speaking on the protests in Jharkhand, which have entered their 13th day, Kharge said the Congress stands with students and youth across the country."We stand with the students, whether it is Jharkhand, Punjab, Delhi or anywhere else. "We will ask why this happened and whether any mistake was made on our part. We are also writing to each of them (allaince partners) to understand what happened. Whether it is our alliance partner or the Opposition, we stand with students and youth and will continue to fight to resolve their problems," Kharge said.The statements came as the LoP accused the Centre of refusing to respond to repeated demands for a statement in Parliament on the issue."We have been asking for a statement from him on this. headline: Centre deploys teams to combat outbreak of Chandipura virus
full_text:
Centre deploys teams to combat outbreak of Chandipura virus
The Union health ministry on Wednesday deployed a National Joint Outbreak Response Team (NJORT) to Gujarat and Rajasthan to strengthen the response to the ongoing Chandipura Virus Disease (CHPV) outbreak, which has claimed lives of at least 22 children in Gujarat, this monsoon
The Union health ministry on Wednesday deployed a National Joint Outbreak Response Team (NJORT) to Gujarat and Rajasthan to strengthen the response to the ongoing Chandipura Virus Disease (CHPV) outbreak, which has claimed lives of at least 22 children in Gujarat, this monsoon. The Centre has also stepped up disease surveillance, scientific investigations and testing in the affected districts to better understand and contain the outbreak, the ministry said in a statement.
Chandipura virus is an emerging arbovirus transmitted primarily by sandflies and is associated with outbreaks of acute encephalitis syndrome (AES), mainly among children under 15 years.
“The Union ministry of health and family welfare has deployed a National Joint Outbreak Response Team (NJORT) to Gujarat and Rajasthan to strengthen the response to the ongoing Chandipura Virus Disease (CHPV) outbreak. The deployment comes against the backdrop of sustained and intensified scientific investigations by a nationwide network of premier research institutions…,” the ministry said.
The multidisciplinary team, comprising experts from the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), will support the two states in outbreak investigation, epidemiological assessment, clinical management, laboratory coordination, vector surveillance and public health measures.
The ministry said disease surveillance is continuing under the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP), coordinated by the NCDC in collaboration with state surveillance units.
“These coordinated efforts aim to advance the understanding of the virus, including its transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum, epidemiology and potential treatment approaches, while guiding evidence-based public health interventions. The NCDC Public Health Emergency Operations Centre (PHEOC) has also been activated to support the NJORT,” it added.
The deployment comes as scientific investigations are already underway into Chandipura virus in recent years. Active surveillance has been intensified among patients with acute febrile illness (AFI) and acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) in affected districts. Community-based serosurveys are also being conducted to identify asymptomatic infections and assess the extent of virus transmission, along with mandatory testing of fever patients in the affected districts, the ministry said.
A key focus of the investigation is to unravel the virus transmission cycle. While sandflies are the established vectors of Chandipura virus, scientists are also examining whether other arthropods, including mosquitoes, ticks and mites, may have a role in transmission, the statement added.
Large numbers of vector samples collected from affected areas are being analysed, and officials aware of the matter said it is too early to identify the vector responsible for the current outbreak.
Animal surveillance has also been expanded to determine whether the virus is circulating among domestic animals that could act as reservoirs. Blood samples from cattle, buffaloes and goats, along with milk samples, have been collected for testing. Around 70 animal blood samples are currently being analysed, and the ministry said no conclusions can be drawn until laboratory investigations are completed.
“The ongoing investigations are also drawing upon lessons from the 2024 Chandipura virus outbreak in Gujarat. During that outbreak, several vector species, including sandflies, were collected and tested, but all samples were negative for CHPV, and no specific vector could be conclusively implicated,” the ministry said.
Besides tracking transmission, scientists are also carrying out whole-genome sequencing of virus samples at the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre in Gandhinagar to determine whether the virus has undergone genetic changes. Preliminary analysis has identified minor genetic variations, but officials said further studies are needed before drawing any conclusions.
“With the deployment of the National Joint Outbreak Response Team and parallel investigations by multiple national institutions, the Centre has significantly expanded scientific and field support to Gujarat and Rajasthan, reflecting a coordinated ‘One Health’ approach that integrates human, animal and vector surveillance to better understand and contain the Chandipura virus outbreak,” said the ministry.

headline: 21 MPs seek Tamil Nadu anthem to be sung first at state events, write to governor
full_text:
21 MPs seek Tamil Nadu anthem to be sung first at state events, write to governor
They said Raj Bhavan orders resulted in the ceremony opening with Vande Mataram, followed by the National Anthem, while 'Tamizh Thai Vaazhthu' was sung third.
Twenty-one members of parliament (MPs) have written to Tamil Nadu governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar amid a controversy over the state anthem, 'Tamil Thai Vaazhthu', being placed third during a convocation ceremony as well as at university and government events in the state.
In a letter dated August 5 (Wednesday), the MPs referred to the order followed during the 33rd convocation of state-run Manonmaniam Sundaranar University in Tirunelveli on July 28.
They said directions from Raj Bhavan resulted in the ceremony opening with Vande Mataram, followed by the National Anthem, while 'Tamizh Thai Vaazhthu' was sung third.
List of MPs who wrote to Governor
The letter carries the signatures of P Chidambaram, B Manickam Tagore, Karti Chidambaram, Thol Thirumavalavan, Durai Vaiko and 16 other members of parliament from Tamil Nadu.
The MPs said they were making the representation "not as a complaint, but as a respectful request" so that state institutions continue to function "with dignity and without avoidable controversy."
What MPs said in the letter
The MPs said many people in Tamil Nadu viewed the state anthem being sung third as "an unintended slight" to the Tamil people and to Manonmaniam Sundaranar Pillai, after whom the university is named and who wrote ‘Neeraarum Kadaludutha’.
They said that the song has been the official state anthem of Tamil Nadu since 2021 and has been performed at public events for more than 5 decades.
Referring to the Governor's own address to the Tamil Nadu Assembly in June 2026, the MPs said the proceedings had started with 'Tamizh Thai Vaazhthu', followed by the National Anthem.
They said the sequence followed at the university convocation was different from that practised. The letter also referred to similar traditions followed in other states, including Karnataka, where state anthems are rendered.
The MPs urged Raj Bhavan to issue "clear and advance guidance" to universities across Tamil Nadu so that 'Tamizh Thai Vaazhthu' is sung at the beginning of convocations and other official programmes, while the National Anthem is played at the end.
They also requested an assurance that there was no intention to show disrespect towards the state anthem or Manonmaniam Sundaranar.
Political slugfest over the controversy
Tamil Nadu higher education minister P Viswanathan boycotted the convocation ceremony, protesting what he described as the "disrespect" shown to the state anthem.
Criticising the revised protocol for songs at educational institutions, Tamil Nadu minister for electricity and energy resources CTR Nirmal Kumar said all state government functions would continue to give priority to the state anthem.
"In Tamil Nadu, absolute priority must be given to 'Thamizh Thai Vaazhthu'," he said, adding, "it is the established practice in all state government functions to sing the state anthem first."
DMK leader Kanimozhi wrote on her social media platform, "For the first time in a Tamil Nadu university, the convocation ceremony has begun with 'Vande Mataram', pushing the Tamil Thai Vaazhthu to the third place."
The issue had also surfaced during chief minister C Joseph Vijay's swearing-in ceremony on May 10, when the state anthem was placed third.

headline: Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam are in jail for years, I am one of them: Tarun Tejpal
full_text:
Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam are in jail for years, I am one of them: Tarun Tejpal
After the verdict, Tejpal claimed he had been targeted for over a decade because Tehelka's journalism offended vested interests and political forces, alleging a politically motivated campaign against him.
Tehelka founder and former editor Tarun Tejpal on Thursday described himself as a "political victim" after the Bombay High Court convicted him in the 2013 rape case involving a former junior colleague and sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment. Drawing parallels with people like Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam and Surendra Gadling who have been in jail for a few years without conviction now, Tejpal said that he was also one of them.
Speaking to reporters after the verdict, Tejpal alleged that he had been targeted for more than a decade because of the kind of journalism Tehelka practised and because "vested interests" and political interests were offended by its reporting.
On Thursday, the Goa bench of the Bombay High Court overturned a 2021 sessions court judgment that had acquitted Tejpal of all charges. The High Court convicted him under provisions dealing with rape by a person in a position of trust or authority, sexual harassment, and assault with intent to disrobe.
Soon after his conviction, Tejpal said he would challenge the judgment in the Supreme Court. "We will be appealing against this order. We feel the order is wrong. We will be moving the Supreme Court against the order," he said.
He maintained that the prosecution was driven by political vendetta rather than evidence. "We have no doubt that for the past 13 years they are after me because of my work with Tehelka," he said, adding that the trial court had acquitted him after years of proceedings and that he was now being pursued again.
Talking about former JNU student leaders, who have spent years in jail while facing criminal charges, Tejpal said, "Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam and Surendra Gadling have been in jail for years now. I think I am one of them".
Khalid, a former JNU student leader, is jailed under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case and has not been convicted.
Sharjeel Imam is also an accused in the same conspiracy case and remains in custody.
Lawyer-activist Surendra Gadling has been jailed in the Bhima Koregaon-Elgar Parishad case under anti-terror provisions and is awaiting trial.
Tejpal alleged that those who had spoken or written against people in power were being selectively targeted.
"The people who are with them, they are acquitted but the people who have done journalism against them or they have said something against them, they are after such people," he said.
He further claimed that the case had destroyed his professional life. "They have stopped my journalism, they have stopped Tehelka, they have stopped my books from being printed," he told reporters, while expressing faith that the judiciary would eventually vindicate him.
"There is so much material—if you were to look at the evidence presented in court, it is substantial enough to warrant acquittal ten times over, not just once. We will bring all that evidence before the public. There is no problem; we will present it all".
During sentencing, Tejpal sought leniency, saying he was 62-years-old and a father of two daughters.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Goa government, opposed any leniency and argued that the court should send a clear message that "no means no".
Tejpal was arrested in November 2013 and later released on bail. After his acquittal in 2021, the Goa government challenged the verdict before the Bombay High Court, which has now convicted him and imposed the 10-year sentence.
Tejpal is expected to pursue his appeal before the Supreme Court in the coming days.

headline: ‘Don’t approve of abusive language, but…': Sonam Wangchuk amid row over PM Modi remarks
full_text:
‘Don’t approve of abusive language, but…': Sonam Wangchuk amid row over PM Modi remarks
Abhijeet Dipke said that CJP will function as a “pressure group”, a decision backed by Sonam Wangchuk as well.
Scientist and activist Sonam Wangchuk said he did not support use of abusive language against political leaders, referring to videos of such language being used during the student protest at Jantar Mantar, but added that it was on the political leaders to understand what drove students to the point of such frustration.
"I do not approve abusive language at all. But for the government, it's more a signal of how frustrated our youth have become," he said while speaking to India Today.
He added that if he had been in place of the Prime Minister, he would question himself first and not take actions against students. "If I was in the place of the Prime Minister, I would first tell myself how bad I've been to invoke so much anger in them," Wangchuk said.
Also read: Listening to youth is ‘most powerful force’ to prevent protest violence: Supreme Court
"Take the message, don't kill the messenger," he added.
A zero FIR was filed against a 15-year-old girl over her abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the CJP protest, which was later withdrawn by he complainant saying that the teenager had apologised and the PM had forgiven her.
Sonam Wangchuk, who is now in Ladakh recovering after ending his 26-day hunger strike to support students during the Jantar Mantar protest, said that he has recovered 6kgs of the 11kgs of the weight he had lost.
‘Not a protest mascot’
While speaking on the students protests going on in Jharkhand over alleged exam irregularities, Wangchuk told India Today that he did not wish to be the face of every student protest but will continue supporting genuine movements. He said that ‘education’ and ‘environment’ were two subjects very close to him.
"I just want everybody to be their own heroes in their own places," he said when asked if he planned on travelling to Jharkhand to join the students protesting there.

"Education and environment are two subjects very close to my heart... I would like to support any place that is raising a just voice for these two subjects," Wangchuk said, adding that it was sign of a healthy democracy that people were raising their voices.
On Wednesday, Wangchuk spoke to student leader and Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JKLM) leader Devendra Nath Mahato, who is on a hunger strike in Ranchi, and adviced him to drink water.
Mahato clarified that he has not ended his hunger strike but has started to drink water on Wangchuk's advice.

The students in Jharkhand are demanding resignation of chief minister Hemant Soren over alleged exam irregularities. Soren, on Wednesday, offered talks with students to resolve the issue, saying that paper leaks was a nationwide issue.
CJP to travel to Jharkhand to support students
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke said on Wednesday that the satirical political outfit would travel to Jharkhand to support the ongoing students’ protest and added that Sonam Wangchuk would continue to serve as their mentor.
Dipke said that CJP will function as a “pressure group”, a decision backed by Wangchuk as well.
The remarks came as the CJP began its two-day core committee meeting on Wednesday to chalk out its future strategy, organisational expansion and the key public issues it plans to take up in the coming months.
The first day of the conclave took place at Dipke’s residence in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar.

Former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) president and BJP leader Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh on Thursday received a massive welcome from supporters on his return to his home district Gonda, marking his first visit after being acquitted in the sexual harassment case filed by wrestlers.
Singh reached Ayodhya’s international airport aboard a chartered aircraft, where a large number of supporters gathered to greet him with drums, music and slogans, news agency PTI reported. His convoy later moved towards Gonda, with thousands of people lining the route.

full_text:
South Africa recalls India envoy over presence at event with one of corruption-accused Gupta brothers
South Africa recalled India envoy Anil Sooklal after his presence at an event with former president Jacob Zuma and Gupta brother Ajay Gupta in Haridwar.
South Africa’s high commissioner to India, Anil Sooklal, has been recalled for being part of a meeting between former president Jacob Zuma and one of the Gupta brothers, who are wanted by South African authorities on charges of political corruption.
The move was announced by South African Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola weeks after photographs emerged of Zuma with Ajay Gupta and Sooklal at a ceremony at a temple in Haridwar on June 26. Zuma, who has long faced accusations of favouring the Gupta brothers’ business operations in South Africa, visited India in a personal capacity in June.
“We confirm that high commissioner Anil Sooklal has been recalled to the headquarters for further consultations,” Lamola told a media briefing in Pretoria on Wednesday. He did not give details but said the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO), or South Africa’s foreign ministry, has recommended that a new framework be adopted for protocol and diplomatic support for foreign visits by former presidents.
Sooklal joined the foreign ministry in 1995 and was South Africa’s longest-serving Brics sherpa. He was awarded the Pravasi Bharatiya Samman in 2019 for his contributions to diplomacy. He also served as South Africa’s G20 sherpa and ambassador to the European Union and Belgium during 2006-2012 before being appointed high commissioner to India in June 2024.
Who are the Gupta brothers?
The issue of the Gupta brothers remains a sensitive subject in South Africa as they were accused of using their connections with Zuma, who was president from 2009 to 2018, to win contracts, influence cabinet appointments, and siphon off state funds. Zuma and the Guptas have denied all wrongdoing.
The India-born brothers left South Africa after Zuma was unseated in 2018. A judicial inquiry established to examine allegations of graft during Zuma’s years as president recommended criminal charges against the Guptas. Ajay Gupta is in India, while Atul and Rajesh Gupta live in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), where a court dismissed South Africa’s request for their extradition in 2023 on technical grounds.
A departmental inquiry demand
The Democratic Alliance, South Africa’s second-largest political party and a key partner in the coalition government, has demanded a departmental inquiry into what it described as a “grave violation of diplomatic protocol which demonstrates the seeming political capture of South Africa’s foreign service”.
DIRCO had earlier launched an internal inquiry into Sooklal’s presence at the meeting between Zuma and Ajay Gupta, and a spokesperson said the department wanted an explanation from the envoy and that this would be the “subject of our discussions with him”.
During his visit to India, Zuma told the local media that Ajay Gupta was “a brother and friend of mine” who was forced to leave South Africa. “I haven’t had time to meet with him, so I decided that I should come [to India],” he said.

2 dead after dispute among brothers over loud music in Mumbai
Sunil allegedly played music at a high volume in the early hours, following which his brothers, Surendra and Suraj, objected, a senior police official said.
A dispute among three brothers over loud music allegedly escalated into an attack with sharp weapons in Mumbai on Thursday morning, leaving two family members dead and two others critically injured, police said.
The incident occurred at Rahul Nagar in the Parksite locality in Vikhroli, where four brothers shared a house.
Domestic dispute turns deadly
According to preliminary information, Sunil Vishwakarma (40) allegedly played music at a high volume in the early hours, following which his brothers, Surendra Vishwakarma and Suraj Vishwakarma, objected, a senior police official said.

A heated argument soon broke out among the brothers and escalated into a physical altercation. During the clash, Surendra and Suraj allegedly attacked Sunil and his family members with sharp weapons, the police said.
Sunil died on the spot, while his 14-year-old son, Shlok Vishwakarma, succumbed to injuries while being taken to hospital. Sunil's wife and younger son suffered serious injuries and were undergoing treatment at Rajawadi Hospital, officials said.
Police suspect deeper motives
Police detained Surendra and Suraj Vishwakarma in connection with the incident and were questioning them, they said.

headline: Following a surprise visit to Hampi last month, Upalokayukta Justice B. Veerappa has directed officials in Hampi to take legal and appropriate action against all the homestays running illegally within the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authorit...

Following a surprise visit to Hampi last month, Upalokayukta Justice B. Veerappa has directed officials in Hampi to take legal and appropriate action against all the homestays running illegally within the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority (HWHAMA) limits and clear them soon. They have been ordered to provide alternative accommodation to those living illegally within 100 metres of Janata Street in Hampi and to those who are running commercial businesses.
Suo motu case
Justice Veerappa told The Hindu that he found several violations of guidelines with respect to core zone, buffer zone and periphery zone owing to the allowance of commercial activities and homestays in the prohibited area of the Hampi World Heritage Area. He has booked a suo motu case over the violations.
As per details, around 200 homestays are being run illegally in the core zone, buffer zone and peripheral zones falling within the scope of HWHAMA. Similarly, 250 homestays are being run without any permission from the Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority (HWHAMA) in the Janata Colony near Hampi Temple.
Review ordered
Justice Veerappa has also instructed officials to submit details of the licenced and illegal homestays, bed and breakfast accommodations, resorts and lodges, along with the supporting documents and legal actions taken against those operating illegally. Officials have been asked to provide details of the total number of resorts, lodges and other types of accommodations being run officially and those that are run illegally without permissions or licences. Besides, the officials have been ordered to check if the owners of these properties have got land conversion documents, building plan approval, and official licences to sell liquor.
“In case property owners don’t have the permissions, I have asked officials to submit a detailed report on the action taken against such resorts, lodges and bed and breakfasts as per law. If the owners of the properties have licences, building plan approval, land conversion documents and others, the officials still have to submit those documents to us. I have also ordered them to submit a report on the legal action taken against the homestays where the owners are not residing on the properties as per regulations,” Justice Veerappa told The Hindu.
However, Vivekananda, Assistant Commissioner, Hospet taluk, denied that the total number of illegal homestays, lodges, resorts are as high as 200. “I agree that there are illegal homestays operating, and we will conduct a survey and submit a detailed report to the Upalokayukta.”

headline: 3 killed, 2 critical after toxic gas leak at pharma unit in Karnataka's Yadgir
full_text:
3 killed, 2 critical after toxic gas leak at pharma unit in Karnataka's Yadgir
Three contract workers died and two others were hospitalised after a toxic gas leak at a pharmaceutical manufacturing unit in Karnataka's Yadgir district.
Three contract workers were killed and two others were hospitalised after a toxic gas leak at a pharmaceutical manufacturing unit in Karnataka’s Yadgir district early Wednesday, police said.
According to police, the leak occurred between 2 am and 3.30 am at a private pharmaceutical plant in the Kadechur Badiyal Industrial Area under Saidapur police station limits in Gurmitkal Assembly constituency.
Also read: 2 dead, several hospitalised after suspected ammonia gas leak in Tamil Nadu's Tiruvallur
Scrubber leak triggers tragedy
Superintendent of police Prithvi Shankar said a chemical scrubber inside the factory developed a leak, exposing workers to hazardous gas. “According to preliminary information, the incident occurred between 2 am and 3.30 am inside the factory on Wednesday, where a chemical scrubber reportedly developed a gas leak. The workers are believed to have suffocated after inhaling the hazardous chemical, resulting in the deaths of three workers,” he said.
The workers who died were identified as Katla Ganesh, 23, from Telangana, and Vikram Singh Gond, 25, and Sanjay Singh Gond, 25, both from Madhya Pradesh. Two workers from Andhra Pradesh, Manchala Hemanth and Manchala Shivakumar, were admitted to the intensive care unit at Raichur Institute of Medical Sciences Hospital with serious injuries.
Police book company officials
Police registered a case at Saidapur police station under Sections 105 (culpable homicide) and 286 (negligent conduct with respect to poisonous substance) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The factory’s human resources manager, general manager and site in charge have also been booked and are undergoing treatment, according to the police.
Yadgir deputy commissioner Pandve Rahul Tukaram said an inspection found that thionyl chloride was being used in a stainless steel reactor and that sulphur dioxide produced during the manufacturing process escaped after a pipeline connected to the scrubber developed a leak.
“We inspected the factory and found that thionyl chloride was being used in a stainless steel reactor. During the process, sulphur dioxide gas is generated and is carried through a pipeline to the scrubber. The pipeline developed a leak, resulting in the workers inhaling the gas. Three people died due to the inhalation, while two others are undergoing treatment at RIMS Hospital,” he said.
Also read: 3 of a family dead, 1 injured in fire sparked by gas leak
Probe, compensation process begins
The district administration has directed the company to strengthen safety measures and provide details of compensation for the victims’ families. “The company will now be under police investigation, and those concerned will have to appear before the police. We have also directed the management to provide details regarding the compensation process for the victims’ families,” Tukaram said.
He said teams from the National Disaster Response Force and forensic experts had been deployed to determine the cause of the leak and identify any technical failures. “Further action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation,” he said.
The deputy commissioner added that pharmaceutical companies had been instructed during a pollution control and safety audit meeting last week to comply with all prescribed safety requirements, warning that violations would invite action.
Also read: Toxic gas leaks from Palghar chemical unit; 458 persons evacuated, some complain of eye irritation
Government orders safety review
Medical education minister Sharanprakash Patil, who visited the factory on Wednesday, described the deaths as a serious incident and said the government would proceed against those found responsible.
“It is unfortunate that workers who came here for employment have lost their lives. Legal action will be taken against those responsible without any leniency. Ensuring justice for the families of the deceased is the responsibility of the government,” Patil said.
He said the district administration would work towards providing appropriate compensation to the victims’ families and that a special team would inspect industries in the area to verify compliance with safety standards, labour laws and pollution control regulations.
Patil also said the government would examine whether chemical industries in the region were adhering to existing rules and that strict action would follow if violations were found.

headline: Kerala clears ₹8 lakh ex gratia for flood deaths
full_text:
Kerala clears ₹8 lakh ex gratia for flood deaths
The Kerala cabinet on Wednesday approved an ex gratia of ₹8 lakh for the families of those killed in the recent floods and landslides and ₹12 lakh for families that lost their homes and land in the disaster
The Kerala cabinet on Wednesday approved an ex gratia of ₹8 lakh for the families of those killed in the recent floods and landslides and ₹12 lakh for families that lost their homes and land in the disaster.
Chief minister V D Satheesan announced the decisions after a cabinet meeting in Thiruvananthapuram.
At least 26 people were killed in the rain-related incidents, while more than 27,000 displaced people are staying in 462 relief camps, mostly in Pathanamthitta, Kottayam and Alappuzha districts.
The government will provide ₹10,000 to the families of the deceased to conduct last rites. Families whose homes were inundated by floodwaters will also receive ₹10,000 to undertake cleaning and restoration work.
Families that lost both their homes and land in landslides will receive ₹12 lakh, while those requiring assistance to rebuild damaged houses will be given ₹6 lakh.
The government will also provide ₹300 a day to two members of each family staying in relief camps towards daily expenses. It will also bear rental expenses until their homes become habitable, Satheesan said.
Farmers who suffered extensive crop losses will receive 25% additional compensation over and above the existing government relief.
Preliminary estimates put crop losses at ₹67.44 crore, with damage reported across 1,882 hectares, affecting 23,537 farmers.
Traders affected by the rain-related incidents will receive ₹10,000 in assistance, the chief minister said.
Satheesan also announced the Ujjevana soft loan scheme for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) hit by the extreme rains. Under the scheme, the government will facilitate soft loans of up to ₹12 lakh for affected businesses.

headline: Yusuf Pathan asks Shah to step in, halt removal of Murshidabad loudspeakers
full_text:
Yusuf Pathan asks Shah to step in, halt removal of Murshidabad loudspeakers
Three rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who left the party and joined the NCPI, sought Union home minister Amit Shah’s “urgent intervention”
Three rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who left the party and joined the NCPI, sought Union home minister Amit Shah’s “urgent intervention” on Thursday to stop the removal of loudspeakers from mosques in Murshidabad district at the instance of the local police.
In a memorandum submitted to the home minister’s office, the MPs said that while they “fully respect” the law and the Supreme Court’s directions on noise regulation, the government must ensure “fair, uniform, and sensitive implementation without hurting religious sentiments.”
The three MPs, Yusuf Pathan (Baharampur), Abu Taher Khan (Murshidabad), Khallilur Rehman (Jangipur), won their seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha on a TMC ticket. The three were among the 20 MPs who left the TMC and joined the little-known NCPI, an unrecognised party that contested two assembly seats in Tripura and polled a few hundred votes, that backs the BJP.
The three Muslim MPs from Bengal’s Muslim-majority Murshidabad district, however, have, however, skipped National Democratic Alliance (NDA) meetings saying they would not support any legislation either that goes against the interest of Muslims.
The memorandum on Thursday comes against the backdrop of reports from Bengal that mosques were being forced to remove loudspeakers used for azan (call for prayers) by local police officers.
West Bengal Police officials have maintained in the past that the curbs were being enforced uniformly across all religious structures in line with Supreme Court and National Green Tribunal (NGT) orders on noise pollution, and were not directed at any one community.
The memorandum also flagged delays in deciding pending Electoral Photo Identity Card (EPIC) tribunal cases.
“A large number of genuine voters whose names have been deleted from the electoral rolls are awaiting tribunal decisions. The delay is causing difficulties in passport verification, land registration, and access to government welfare schemes,” the MPs said in the memorandum, seeking that all pending genuine cases be fast-tracked and disposed of by the end of this year.
The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls carried out by the Election Commission ahead of the 2026 West Bengal assembly polls, resulted in the deletion of about 4.55 lakh names in Murshidabad district alone, the highest among all districts in the state, according to Election Commission data.

headline: Delhi: IMD issues ‘orange alert’ as AQI remains ‘satisfactory’
full_text:
Delhi: IMD issues ‘orange alert’ as AQI remains ‘satisfactory’
An orange alert means “Be Prepared” for heavy to very heavy rain (typically 115.6 mm to 204.4 mm in 24 hrs) while a yellow alert means “Be Aware” (typically 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm in 24 hrs)
Delhi continued to receive light to moderate rainfall on Thursday with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing an ‘orange alert’ today and ‘yellow alert’ for Friday.
An orange rainfall warning means “Be Prepared” for heavy to very heavy rain (typically 115.6 mm to 204.4 mm in 24 hours) while a yellow rainfall warning means “Be Aware” (typically 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm in 24 hours).
Multiple parts of Delhi received light showers late Wednesday night and early Thursday morning. From 11:30pm on Wednesday to 8:30am on Thursday, Palam recorded the highest rainfall at 23.8mm, followed by Naraina 23.5mm, and Janakpuri at 17.5mm.
During the same period, Pusa recorded 6.5mm, followed by Chhatarpur at 4.5mm, and Mayur Vihar at 3.5mm. Safdarjung, the city’s base station for weather, recorded 3.1mm of rainfall during the same period.
At around 9:15am, the IMD issued a red alert for Shahdara, east, south east, central, and south Delhi, most parts of north east, central, along with parts of west, north west, and north Delhi, predicting heavy rain with thunderstorms and lightning in the same parts.
Multiple spells of very light to light rain at most places with moderate rain at a few places during the early morning to noon is predicted for Friday, while another spell of very light to light rain is likely towards evening or night.
The IMD categorizes rainfall up to 15.5mm as light, between 15.6mm to 64.4mm as ‘moderate’, between 64.5mm to 115.5mm as ‘heavy’, and between 115.6mm to 204.4mm as ‘very heavy’.
Also Read: Delhi under yellow alert as multiple spells of rain likely through the week, says IMD
Experts have stated that the increased rain over the past few days, after a number of days with no significant rain, was due to the monsoon trough returning to be positioned over northern India.
“The rains have picked up across Delhi as the excess of the monsoon trough that was over central and western India has started to move back to its position over the foothills of the Himalayas. Such scattered rain seen today is likely to be seen today as well, with only around 30% to 60% of NCR seeing strong showers, while other areas get light rain or remain completely dry. In the coming two weeks, NCR is likely to continue seeing days like today, with a few days with heavy rains in some parts of the region,” said Ashwary Tiwari, founder of Indiametsky weather.
AQI ‘satisfactory’
The city’s air quality index (AQI) was recorded at 80 around 11:05am, in the “satisfactory” category.
Due to the rain, the maximum temperature is expected to be between 31°C to 33°C, rising to 33°C to 35°C on Saturday. Thursday’s minimum temperature was recorded at 25.6°C.

Holding the Tricolour aloft and carrying what organisers described as an approximately 600-metre-long national flag, the students marched through Ranchi.
RANCHI: Undeterred by relentless rain, hundreds of students gathered at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi on Wednesday before setting out on a Tiranga March to Albert Ekka Chowk, intensifying an agitation that has entered its second week over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand's recruitment examinations.The march came amid an indefinite protest by students demanding a CBI investigation into the alleged paper leaks and recruitment irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) examinations.
The movement has also escalated on the hunger strike front. Alongside Devendra Nath Mahto, dubbed by protesters as "Sonam Wangchuk 2.0", four more students have joined an indefinite fast, pressing three principal demands: cancellation of all JPSC and JSSC examinations conducted during the Hemant Soren-led JMM government's tenure; a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities, paper leaks and delays in recruitment results instead of an investigation by the state's Criminal Investigation Department (CID), which the students say they no longer trust; and comprehensive reforms to Jharkhand's recruitment and competitive examination system.
As the march drew to a close, the rain intensified, but so did chants of "Jai Jharkhand".
The Tiranga March began with chants of "Jai Jharkhand" and slogans celebrating student unity. Organisers repeatedly instructed participants to refrain from using abusive language in slogans or on placards, stressing that the protest would remain peaceful and disciplined.The emphasis on restraint reflected the students' attempt to draw a clear distinction between their movement and political organisations.
Protesters pointed out that two separate demonstrations have been taking place in Ranchi: one led by students and another believed to be backed by local MLA Jairam Singh Mahato's party. Organisers also appeared mindful of the aftermath of the recent Jantar Mantar protest in New Delhi, where FIRs and complaints were lodged against some protesters over the use of profanities. Students said they were determined to ensure that no such controversy overshadowed their movement.Holding the Tricolour aloft and carrying what organisers described as an approximately 600-metre-long national flag, the students marched through Ranchi despite the downpour."Our flag march represents the moral spirit of India. It highlights our constitutional rights. Look at all these students getting drenched in the rain while waving the Tricolour. This is a symbol of our unity and a symbol of our constitutional rights," one protester said.As the march reached Albert Ekka Chowk, groups of students gathered at the intersection and continued raising slogans. Traffic disruption remained limited, largely because authorities had already closed one of the approach roads. Protesters also allowed vehicles to pass intermittently, saying they did not want to cause unnecessary inconvenience to commuters.Appealing directly to the Hemant Soren government, another protester said, "We are the children of Jharkhand. You speak about working for the indigenous and tribal communities. Please work in our interest too. Thousands of students are studying with the hope of securing jobs in their own state. We request the government to reform the JPSC and JSSC."Several protesters contrasted the Ranchi agitation with the earlier demonstrations at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, insisting that their movement had remained peaceful throughout. They also warned that any police action, including a possible lathicharge, would only intensify the agitation."We are protesting peacefully. If the police take action against us, it will only raise questions about the government's role because we have not indulged in any violence. Every evening we gather at our protest site and peacefully put forward our demands," one participant said.As the march drew to a close, the rain intensified, but so did chants of "Jai Jharkhand". Some protesters invoked the state's historical icons while asserting that Jharkhand's identity extended beyond sporting achievements."Our identity is not defined by MS Dhoni. Our identity is defined by Birsa Munda, Tilka Manjhi, Shibu Soren, Binod Bihari Mahto, Bisheshwar Prasad Keshari, Sidhu and Kanhu," a protester said.
Meanwhile, the Hemant Soren government has constituted a committee of ministers and senior officials to initiate talks with the agitating students. State minister Rajat said complaints regarding recruitment examination irregularities were already under investigation and that the agencies concerned were working on them with urgency.The students, however, rejected the proposal for closed-door discussions. They insisted that any dialogue with the government must be conducted transparently, in the presence of the media and television cameras, arguing that only an open process would inspire confidence among the protesters.

headline: AI can aid judges, not replace human judgment: CJI Surya Kant
full_text:
AI can aid judges, not replace human judgment: CJI Surya Kant
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said technology is making courts more effective and accessible. He stressed that AI can support judicial work, but justice still depends on human judgment.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Thursday said technology is helping courts discharge their constitutional responsibility more effectively, while stressing that it cannot replace human judgment.
Speaking at a function organised by the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association, he said the digitisation of court processes had gradually evolved into a truly integrated digital justice ecosystem.
At the same event, Justice Abha Nayar Patel, a judge of the Supreme Court of Zambia, said the future of justice delivery was a fundamental issue for all stakeholders.
She said courts across the world were using digital tools to improve access and case management, while underlining that delay in justice was itself a form of injustice.
CJI Kant said, "Over the last two decades, our endeavour has been to make the courts more accessible, more transparent and more responsive to every stakeholder who interacts with the justice delivery system."
He added, "Technology, in our understanding, is not an end in itself. It is an instrument that enables courts to fulfil their constitutional responsibility more effectively." The 53rd CJI said technology had also helped level the playing field and democratise professional opportunities within the legal profession.
He said litigants had perhaps gained the most from these changes. "Perhaps the greatest beneficiaries are the litigants themselves.
They are able to track the progress of their cases online, participate in virtual proceedings, and obtain essential legal information without undertaking costly and time consuming travel," he said.
On artificial intelligence, CJI Kant said it presented unprecedented opportunities for improving judicial administration, but drew a clear line on its role.
"Yet, as I have consistently observed in many of my lectures and addresses on the subject, artificial intelligence may augment judicial intelligence without replacing the judicial consensus. Technology can process information with remarkable speed. But justice ultimately demands wisdom, empathy, and the exercise of reasoned human judgment," he said.
He added that as judiciaries across jurisdictions continued to learn from one another's experience, efforts should be made to build justice systems that were innovative, accessible and worthy of the trust citizens placed in them.
Justice Patel, who delivered a lecture on "Future of Justice Delivery: Innovation, Inclusion and Integrity", said, "Across the world, judiciaries are experimenting with case management systems, e-filing, virtual hearings, AI-assisted legal research, and predictive analytics for case flow. Some jurisdictions have gone further still, piloting AI tools to assist but never replace judicial reasoning in high-volume, low-complexity matters." Referring to Zambia, she said, "In my own region, Zambia, we are taking slow but meaningful steps towards the digitisation of court records and virtual testimony, born partly out of necessity during the pandemic years, but now recognised as tools of genuine access." Supreme Court judges Justices Vikram Nath and V Mohana also spoke on the occasion, as the event focused on innovation, inclusion and integrity in justice delivery.

headline: 'Ties can't be severed, they can be on hold during conflict': Mohan Bhagwat's China-Pakistan example
full_text:
'Ties can't be severed, they can be on hold during conflict': Mohan Bhagwat's China-Pakistan example
Citing Pakistan and China as examples, Bhagwat said existing relationships could be put "on hold" during conflicts but should not be ended altogether.
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Thursday said that while India must stand with its government and armed forces during times of conflict, such situations should not permanently sever ties with other nations.
Citing Pakistan and China as examples, Bhagwat said existing relationships could be put "on hold" during conflicts but should not be ended altogether. Speaking at an event in Mumbai, he said, “In the times of conflict, we have to go with whatever our government and military does. But that should not sever the ties which are already there."
Also Read | ‘If GenZ is protesting, they are not anti-national’: Mohan Bhagwat
Referring to the two neighbours, he said, "China, people say that for 2,000 years, Bharat has given us some values, and Pakistan was Bharat not less than 100 years ago. This should not be forgotten."
Bhagwat added that "these ties cannot be severed; they can be put on hold till conflict is there," stressing that India's approach should not be one of "conquering or obliterating others" but of dialogue and harmonious coexistence. "Bharat's solution... requires dialogue," he said. “Humanity is one,” he said.
The RSS chief also said the grievances raised by student protesters recently were genuine and cautioned against branding young demonstrators as "anti-national", asserting that the country's youth deserve dialogue because they represent the next generation.
Also Read | 'We need to look into where the problem lies': Mohan Bhagwat on crackdown on protesters
“I'm saying, if Gen Z is protesting, they're not anti-national. They're our own people. They're our next generation. With this sense of belonging, along with dialogue, I said a sense of belonging is needed. A relationship is needed. That is our relationship. Its recognition is needed,” he said.
Bhagwat also endorsed the concerns voiced by the protesters, saying they reflected genuine issues within the education system. "Whatever has happened, the grievance is genuine. There is a lot that needs to be done in Indian education; since it's not happening, it's being talked about."
