headline: Tamil Nadu has increased its healthcare spending by about 6.6% this year, allocating ₹23,357 crore, and continuing its steady increase in public health allocations over the past few years. The announcements for the health sector include 1,000 Mobile ...
full_text:
Tamil Nadu has increased its healthcare spending by about 6.6% this year, allocating ₹23,357 crore, and continuing its steady increase in public health allocations over the past few years. The announcements for the health sector include 1,000 Mobile Geriatric Treatment Centres, maternity care and support centres and a Hub-and-Spoke medical system for cancer care.
There has been a year-on-year increase in Tamil Nadu’s health allocation, with the amount rising from ₹20,197 crore in 2024-2025 to ₹21,905 crore in 2025-2026. While the allocation increased by 8.45% in the previous year, the current year’s increase stands at 6.62%. Despite drawing differing views, the TVK government went ahead and allocated ₹560 crore in the Revised Budget Estimates for its “Thai Maaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam,” in which every newborn delivered in a government hospital will receive a one-gram gold ring.
The government allocated ₹33 crore for establishing mobile geriatric centres for senior citizens. To be introduced in phases across the State, each centre will have a team comprising a doctor, a nurse and a physiotherapist, who will visit every village panchayat to conduct free health check-ups and provide medicines for chronic conditions.
It will also set up “Thai Care”, maternity care and support centres for pregnant women. They can stay at these centres to receive care as their delivery date approaches. The centres will offer free meals, medical support, and continuous health monitoring. A total of ₹23 crore was allocated for the scheme. The government allocated ₹18.5 crore for a telemedicine system based on a “Hub-and-Spoke” hospital model to ensure access to specialised medical care for people in remote and rural areas. Five hubs staffed by specialist doctors will be linked to 200 spokes at Primary Health Centres and government hospitals through an online network. Over the next five years, this network will be expanded to 1,000 hubs and spokes.
Like previous years, cancer care continued to be a priority area. The government will establish a “Hub-and-Spoke” medical system for cancer care. Five zonal cancer care hospitals will be established as primary points of contact for patients and will also undertake research and development activities in cancer care. Financial allocation for medicines were increased by ₹100 crore to ensure uninterrupted supply of medicines.
However, the health announcements in the Budget fell short to address the need to increase manpower. The Tamil Nadu Nurses Empowerment Association expressed disappointment over the Budget, stating that it did not have any announcements benefitting government employees and healthcare staff, particularly nurses. It stated that there was no announcement on the regularisation of services of nurses currently working on consolidated pay nor on new recruitments.

BJP's Catch-22: With FCRA bill, it risks losing delimitation backers
For the passage of the delimitation bill, the government would need supporters beyond its NDA partners. However, many of these potential backers are vehemently opposed to the FCRA amendment bill.
The corridors of Parliament were abuzz on Wednesday afternoon with speculation over whether the government would push for the FCRA bill this week, or delay it to address the elephant in the room -- the delimitation bill. While the government needs a simple majority for the passage of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026, it is the constitutional amendment that could create a catch-22 situation for the ruling dispensation.
The BJP is believed to be reaching out to parties beyond the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) for passage of the ambitious delimitation bill which would be packaged under the 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill. However, many of these parties such as the DMK, NCP-SP are up in arms against the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill 2026. Others, such as YSRCP, are treading cautiously.
India Today spoke to top sources across parties including NCP-SP, DMK, YSRCP and even the BJP allies as to how they are placed when it comes to the FCRA Bill.
One of the regional parties from the south pointed out their concerns over the FCRA bill in its present format. They are worried about the impact the amendment would have on institutions which cater to their core vote bank.
“We are still in consultation with the government. If they agree for our amendments, we might consider coming on board. Else, we will have to oppose it,” the source said.
When asked if they could choose to abstain, the response was, "Abstaining is not a choice for us. We will either vote against it or support it. This issue would impact our core voter base. It touches upon on a sensitive issue related to them."
The Christian and minority voters form the core vote bank of this regional party. They fear the FCRA bill in its present form will trigger outrage amongst its core voters. While they are on-board with the government on the delimitation bill -- provided the BJP is ready to give 50% increase in parliament seats -- supporting the government on the FCRA seems unlikely.
Sources within the NCP-SP and DMK made it clear that they oppose the bill in its present format and would want it to be referred to the joint parliamentary committee.
"This FCRA bill needs more deliberation. Why suspect every donor?" a top NCP-SP source told India Today.
"The charity money is also being used for our children. There is no reason to suspect everyone, every donor and every institute...There are good institutions who are working in educational sector, running hospitals and other important welfare sectors. By bringing this bill, everyone is being suspected," the NCP-SP MP said.
When asked if the NCP-SP could support the delimitation bill, they asserted there was no way to come to a decision when the government hasn’t even shared a draft copy with lawmakers.
The DMK, which is at daggers drawn with the Congress post the Tamil Nadu polls, is also opposed to the FCRA bill. A senior leader told India Today that it could open the doors for "a witch-hunt of minority institutions”.
"This bill in present form will enable the targeting of minority institutions. It could open the gates for witch-hunt of educational institutions, charitable bodies and NGOs. There are clauses in this bill which would enable the government to attach properties owned by any institutes getting funds under the FCRA under dispute even if they have been bought in the past. You can't allow that to happen," the DMK leader said.
"The NGOs are doing a lot of good work. You can put them under ransom through these laws. If some changes are required, you can't open doors to penalise everyone or anyone," the DMK MP said. "We will ask for JPC. We don’t need further amendments to the bill."
Another DMK leader told India Today, "We will move certain amendments. We have strong reservations on the present form of the bill. Regional parties from southern India have issues with several clauses of the bill. We can’t support it."
It would also put parties like the DMK and YSRCP in a peculiar situation if they openly oppose the FCRA bill and then go on to side with the BJP on the delimitation bill. These optics are under consideration by them, the sources indicated.
Meanwhile, the INDIA bloc parties are preparing themselves for an entrenched fight over the FCRA in Parliament. Congress’s Rajya Sabha MP Syed Naseer Hussain told India Today that the party will oppose the FCRA bill for several reasons. His colleagues from Kerala pointed to how NGOs and religious organisations in the state will be affected by the proposed amendments. They said provisions allowing retrospective action against properties and granting sweeping powers to bureaucrats to act against institutions receiving FCRA funds were among their principal concerns.
A senior CPI(M) leader also argued that the powers proposed to be vested in bureaucrats under the bill were even broader than those under the Waqf amendments.
HOW THE DELIMITATION BILL FITS IN
The delimitation proposal, packaged as a constitutional amendment alongside the women's quota framework, was defeated by the united Opposition during the last session of Parliament.
However, the political arithmetic has shifted since the BJP's victory in West Bengal. The Trinamool Congress has witnessed a split, while the formation of the NCPI and the success of Operation Tiger have strengthened the NDA's numbers. With the numbers now appearing more favourable, the BJP could make another attempt to push the delimitation bill through Parliament within the next six months. The project now appears more achievable than ever before.

headline: The Kayastha Pathshala Trust has revoked permission for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' programme, scheduled to be held at K.P. Ground in Prayagraj on August 8, citing an Allahabad High Court order.
full_text:
The Kayastha Pathshala Trust has revoked permission for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' programme, scheduled to be held at K.P. Ground in Prayagraj on August 8, citing an Allahabad High Court order.
The trust also cited waterlogging at the venue for the cancellation.
The trust's acting president, Jitendra Nath Chaudhary, told PTI that the Allahabad High Court, in an order dated August 14, 2025, had directed that the KP College ground should not be used for purposes other than sports and educational activities.
He said the ground was also waterlogged after rain and was unsafe for a public event. Mr. Chaudhary said the permission granted to the Congress was conditional upon approval from the district magistrate.
The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha was scheduled to interact with students on alleged paper leaks and other matters affecting students at the gathering.
Appeal to government
On Wednesday, Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai visited Prayagraj to review preparations for the event.
Mr. Rai asserted that Mr. Gandhi will come to Prayagraj on August 8 and interact with students despite the KP Trust revoking permission for the venue.
Addressing reporters in the evening, Mr. Rai urged the state government and district administration to provide an alternative venue for the programme.
He alleged that the BJP government was "afraid" of Mr. Gandhi and claimed the event was being obstructed for political reasons.
Mr. Gandhi's programmes in Kota and Dehradun had similarly been cancelled, Mr. Rai claimed.

headline: During a tour of the flood-hit areas of eastern Assam, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) met the parents of the boy who died while trying to save his pet puppy. Sivasagar district was swamped so quickly by flood water i...
full_text:
During a tour of the flood-hit areas of eastern Assam, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) met the parents of the boy who died while trying to save his pet puppy. Sivasagar district was swamped so quickly by flood water in July that most people could not evacuate in time.
The floodwaters, triggered by extremely heavy rainfall in the hills of adjoining Nagaland, cut through Sivasagar and Charaideo districts on July 19. Nagaland’s Mon town bore the brunt of the water fury, with landslides claiming 11 lives.
“I can help build your house and help in every possible way, but I cannot bring back your son,” the Chief Minister said as 13-year-old Hridip’s parents, Deepak and Parbati Panika, cried on his shoulders.
The Panikas are residents of Bamun Pukhuri village in the Nazira area of Sivasagar district. Hridip, a Class 8 student, was swept away after he saved the puppy, which was struggling to stay afloat. His body was found a few days later, after the water subsided.
Although the number of affected people across 10 districts came down to 1.22 lakh by Wednesday (August 5), the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) has warned people to stay away from several rising rivers. The floods have claimed 89 lives since April.
Riverbank erosion
The ebb and flow of the rivers, primarily the Brahmaputra, have led to riverbank erosion in several parts of Assam. One of the worst hit areas is Lakhimpur district’s Bonpuroi-Jamuguri.
Assam’s Finance Minister Jayanta Mallabaruah inspected this erosion-hit area and promised to fortify the Jamuguri-Arimora embankment, a key flood-protection structure in the region.
He said the embankment came under severe pressure after rising water levels and strong currents in the Brahmaputra triggered intense riverbank erosion. A large crack developed along the embankment, raising fears of an imminent breach, with a substantial portion reportedly on the verge of collapsing into the river.
Officials warned that a breach of the embankment could inundate vast areas under the Bihpuria and Gohpur Assembly constituencies on the northern bank of the Brahmaputra, prompting concern among residents and the district administration.
In western Assam, reports of breaches in the embankments of rivers originating in Bhutan have caused widespread anxiety. There are also fears that excess water could be released from the Kurichhu Dam in the rain-battered Himalayan country, leading to a repeat of the 2023 deluge along the Beki River.
Nadda visit
Union Health and Family Welfare Minister J. P. Nadda visited flood-hit areas of Assam along with the Chief Minister and met with families of those who lost their lives in the disaster. He assured the victims of the Centre’s support.
“I assure everyone that there will be no lapses of any kind in the relief and rescue operations. Teams of Central Government representatives are conducting extensive assessments of flood damage, and financial assistance is being provided to the State,” he said.
Mr. Nadda also visited landslide-affected areas of Nagaland’s Mon district. According to Nagaland officials, the incessant rainfall washed away more than 800 houses and partially damaged 1,079 others.
Nagaland has been experiencing heavy rainfall over the past few days. Officials said the downpour triggered a major landslide on National Highway-29, blocking the crucial link between Kohima, the State’s capital, and Dimapur, its commercial hub on the border with Assam.
Incessant rainfall also triggered flash floods along the Laini River in adjoining Manipur’s Ukhrul district. Officials said freshly planted paddy in fields flanking the river has been damaged.

headline: After revolt by several legislators, whose supporters have taken to streets against their leaders not being inducted into the Cabinet, the Congress leadership went into damage control mode on Wednesday by reaching out to disgruntled leaders.
full_text:
After revolt by several legislators, whose supporters have taken to streets against their leaders not being inducted into the Cabinet, the Congress leadership went into damage control mode on Wednesday by reaching out to disgruntled leaders.
Party positions
The Congress is likely to offer certain party positions to key leaders to send a message to the communities important to the party in electoral matrix. Meanwhile, the party is expected to ask chairpersons of boards and corporations, appointed during the term of former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, to resign to accommodate disgruntled legislators and party workers, sources said.
On Wednesday, AICC general secretary in-charge of Karnataka Randeep Singh Surjewala arrived in Bengaluru and met senior Vokkaliga leader and former Minister M. Krishnappa and his son Priya Krishna. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Minister B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan also joined Mr. Surjewala in the meeting. Mr. Krishna defeated BJP heavyweight V. Somanna in Govindarajnagar in 2023, and the father-son duo were expecting one Cabinet berth between the two.
He also met former Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister H.K. Patil, who is learnt to be sulking at not being inducted.
Monsoon Session
Sources said that Mr. Surjewala’s outreach to senior legislators was to ensure smooth functioning for the party during the Monsoon Session starting next week. “The party does not want any jarring voices that could give ammunition to the Opposition. Mr. Siddaramaiah continues to be miffed at developments. Senior leadership is likely to approach him too.”
Meanwhile, several legislators who had announced resignation seem to have backtracked after stern warning from the Chief Minister.
Some mellow down
Party sources said Sagar legislator Belur Gopalakrishna has mellowed down while Indi legislator Yashwanthrayagoud V. Patil withdrew his resignation on Wednesday. Raichur Rural legislator Basanagouda Daddal has informed the KPCC president B.K. Hariprasad on Wednesday of his intention to work for the party and backed down from his resignation threat.
Mr. Hariprasad also visited the residence of Mr. Patil, and Dinesh Gundu Rao, another former Minister. He also met former Minister T.B. Jayachandra, and Ashok Pattan to discuss the current developments.
“Mr. H.K. Patil is a senior leader and he comes from the Congress’s family. He may be disappointed. Everyone may get an opportunity some times and may not get sometimes. In the coming days this will be set right,” Mr. Hariprasad told presspersons after meeting Mr. Patil.
When asked how the disgruntled legislators will be mollified, he said that they will be accommodated either in the government or in the party. “The Congress is a big party with 142 years of history. Everyone will get opportunity.”
Social justice angle
Earlier, he said that the legislators who met him have sought appointments to boards and corporations and some have sought party positions. When his attention was drawn to several former Ministers seeking reasons for being dropped, Mr. Hariprasad said, “The main reason is social justice and opportunity to those who had been denied it. The party has given priority to those from SC/ST/ OBC/minority communities. Brahmins could not be accommodated for some reasons. We are considering where they can be accommodated,” he said.

headline: The Tirupati Urban Development Authority (TUDA) and Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC) have jointly taken up the mammoth task of flood-proofing the temple city of Tirupati ahead of the ensuing monsoon season.
full_text:
The Tirupati Urban Development Authority (TUDA) and Tirupati Municipal Corporation (TMC) have jointly taken up the mammoth task of flood-proofing the temple city of Tirupati ahead of the ensuing monsoon season.
In 2021, the heavy downpour atop Tirumala hills made water gush down to leave the city marooned, providing ample proof of the absence of proper channels that were either encroached upon or filled with silt.
As part of the ambitious ‘City of Tanks and Lakes’ project, which was envisaged by the Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu, a joint team led by TUDA Chairman C. Divakar Reddy and TMC Commissioner Sarada Devi inspected Kapila Theertham and Malvadigundam waterfalls, which bring the gush of water from Tirumala into the city.
At Kapila Theertham, the team proposed conducting a hydrological assessment of peak flow, duration, and water availability using gauging and modelling, and using any surplus water for groundwater recharge by constructing a storage pond.
The team also assessed the hydrogeological profile of Malvadigundam and the recharge potential on the channel bed for a length of 150-200 metres immediately downstream of Divyaramam (or ‘Nagaravanam’, the urban park).
Mr. Divakar Reddy also contemplated constructing deep aquifer recharge structures on the middle of the bed, upstream of the existing check dams, besides developing vegetation and walking track in the existing park.
TUDA Secretary N.V. Sreekanth Babu and Water Resources Department Superintending Engineer P. Venkateswara Prasad were present.

headline: No complaints on Prasar Bharati autonomy, Centre tells Lok Sabha
full_text:
No complaints on Prasar Bharati autonomy, Centre tells Lok Sabha
The government told the Lok Sabha it received no formal complaints about Prasar Bharati's autonomy or editorial functioning in the past year. It said only seven appointment-related complaints came from applicants, while editorial feedback continues to be reviewed internally.
The government on Wednesday told the Lok Sabha that it had not received any grievances or formal representations in the past year from journalists, employees or media bodies on the autonomy, appointments or editorial functioning of public broadcasters. It said, however, that seven complaints related to appointments had been received from applicants.
In a written reply to a question by Samajwadi Party MPs Priya Saroj and Pushpendra Saroj, Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting L Murugan also said editorial matters at Prasar Bharati are regularly reviewed, and viewer complaints on content are sent to the relevant editorial teams for action. The government further informed the House that the Centre's Broadcasting Infrastructure and Network Development scheme has been extended till March 2027.
Murugan said, "In the last one year, no grievances or formal representations received from journalists, employees or media bodies concerning autonomy, appointments or editorial functioning of public broadcasters. However, 07 complaints regarding appointment were received from the applicants."
The MPs had sought details of editorial or content-related complaints alleging bias, lack of transparency or compromised independence, and the findings of internal reviews or oversight mechanisms at Prasar Bharati, which has Doordarshan and All India Radio as its constituents.
In response, the government said editorial matters are regularly reviewed by the Editor-in-Chief and senior editorial teams, and guidance and corrective steps are taken whenever required to improve the quality, accuracy, balance and presentation of news while ensuring compliance with Prasar Bharati's editorial policies and Programme Code.
The government also said viewer complaints or feedback, including those related to editorial content, are forwarded to the relevant editorial team for appropriate action under the established policy. It added that the BIND scheme for the development, modernisation and upgradation of Prasar Bharati's broadcasting infrastructure has been extended till March 2027.

headline: Targeted killings in Kashmir: Security forces hunt LeT's Lateef Bhat
full_text:
Targeted killings in Kashmir: Security forces hunt LeT's Lateef Bhat
Security agencies have announced a Rs 15 lakh reward and circulated posters to trace Mohammad Lateef Bhat after recent killings in south Kashmir. Investigators believe the Lashkar commander coordinated attacks on migrant workers and police personnel to spread fear.
Security agencies have stepped up efforts to track down Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorist Mohammad Lateef Bhat, believed to be the key conspirator behind a series of recent targeted killings in Jammu and Kashmir. Authorities have announced a cash reward of Rs 15 lakh for information leading to his arrest and circulated wanted posters across Srinagar and other parts of the Valley.
Posters carrying Bhat's photograph have been put up at prominent locations, including Srinagar's Press Enclave, urging the public to share credible information with security agencies.
Investigators suspect Bhat played a central role in the recent attacks that left a police officer and two migrant workers dead. On July 31, terrorists opened fire on two labourers from Chhattisgarh in Kulgam district. Deepak died on the spot, while Bhupender succumbed to his injuries during treatment. Days earlier, a head constable was shot dead in a targeted attack in Anantnag, triggering a major security crackdown across Kashmir.
According to preliminary investigations, both attacks were carried out using a small-calibre firearm, likely a pistol. Security officials say the method closely resembles attacks typically associated with The Resistance Front (TRF), a Lashkar-linked outfit that relies on locally recruited operatives and overground workers to execute swift targeted shootings before blending back into civilian populations.
Officials believe the attacks were aimed at creating fear, undermining the perception of normalcy in Jammu and Kashmir and targeting both migrant workers and security personnel.
Security agencies describe Bhat as a Lashkar commander who came into focus during a major encounter in Shopian, where he and senior LeT commander Zakir Ganai were trapped by security forces. While Ganai was killed during the five-day operation, Bhat managed to escape.
Since then, intelligence agencies believe he has been working to reactivate sleeper cells in south Kashmir and is allegedly coordinating attacks on non-local workers and security personnel on the instructions of handlers across the border.

The minister said the CJI had written to the PM on May 11, pointing to a substantial increase in the number of cases being filed in SC every day, leading to higher pendency, while there was a shortage of judges to hear regular matters.He cited the example of the Sabarimala case, which is being heard by a nine-judge Constitution Bench, leaving fewer judges available to hear other matters, including criminal appeals. âIncrease in number of judges in SC is a step towards improving judicial efficiency,â he said.Meghwal also said India would soon have its first woman CJI.

headline: Anti-quota voices get shriller: Protesters take to streets, Karni Sena vows no vote
full_text:
Anti-quota voices get shriller: Protesters take to streets, Karni Sena vows no vote
From Nagpur to Lucknow to Jaipur and Visakhapatnam, anti-reservation protests are being reported from several cities even as a parallel campaign against caste-based quotas is gathering pace online. With several Assembly elections approaching, the growing chorus against reservation could reopen India's most politically sensitive fault lines.
Remember the young man who, during a TV debate on the NEET paper leak, rose from his chair and passionately argued that caste-based reservation was driving student distress and even suicides? Harsh Dubey has since amassed thousands of followers on social media, reportedly given around two dozen interviews, and is now awaiting permission to stage a protest at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
Over the past few weeks, a series of seemingly unrelated incidents has hinted at the emergence of a broader sentiment.
Online, the anti-reservation campaign has found a growing rallying point. The Reservation Hatao Andolan (RHA) Instagram page, which began gaining traction as the CJP protests wound down, now has around 5.9 million followers, amplifying voices against caste-based quotas and calling for their rationalisation. The RHA also held its first on-ground protest in Maharashtra's Nagpur last week.
Days later, an agitation by the members of the Shri Rajput Karni Sena, a group of the Rajputs, in Jaipur turned tense. They took to the streets and clashed with police over the now-stayed UGC's caste equity regulations. One death has been alleged. Karni Sena leaders have sworn in the names of their revered deities not to vote for the BJP in the local body polls.
Put together, these developments suggest that anti-reservation voices are becoming louder and attracting supporters both online and offline. But the movement appears fragmented.
Harsh Dubey waits to enter Jantar Mantar and lead. The RHA is continuing to mobilise anti-quota voices on the internet. The Shri Rajput Karni Sena is waging its own battle on Jaipur's streets.
But it's clear that anti-reservation sentiment is growing stronger than ever, with prominent voices like academic-author Anand Ranganathan, journalist-creator Ajeet Bharti, and writer-director Anuradha Tiwari, joining in on the RHA platform that a student called Vedant started weeks ago.
A list of demands has also been floated by these voices.
Politicians, as always, are steering clear of the fast-boiling reservation debate. But on the ground, it is not just the Shri Rajput Karni Sena and Harsh Dubey who are trying to mobilise people against caste-based reservations in education, jobs and other domains.
Influencers, commentators and public intellectuals are split over reservations. Some favour the status quo, some want it scrapped entirely, while others support it only if they have a tighter eligibility criteria.
Online and offline, anti-reservation voices are steadily growing louder. The momentum threatens to widen one of India's most politically explosive and divisive debates on caste-based reservation. The timing is delicate and could unsettle multiple stakeholders.
The anti-quota momentum comes weeks after the weeks-long CJP-led protests culminated in the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and India saw nationwide unrest over the UGC equity regulations, which the "upper-castes" said was "unjustified, unjust, undermined merit", and would "deepen social divisions by enabling the unfair targetting of the savarna class". The "upper-castes" in February called the norms "kaala-kanoon".
These developments could also spell trouble for the government at the Centre, in the states, and the parties in power.
A packed election calendar lies ahead. Assembly elections are due in early 2027 in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa and Manipur, followed later by Himachal Pradesh and Gujarat. In several of these states — especially Uttar Pradesh, India's largest and politically most consequential state, through which the road to New Delhi is often said to pass — caste remains the most decisive electoral factor.
Electorally too, this is significant because, in the last election in Uttar Pradesh, when the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance outperformed the BJP, Rahul Gandhi's "jitni abaadi, utna haq" (rights proportional to population) pitch and Akhilesh Yadav's outreach to the Pichda, Dalit, Aadivasi (PDA) social coalition played key role in the campaigns. That was also reflected in the results.
ANTI-RESERVATION ANDOLAN's DEBUT RALLY IN NAGPUR. SAVARNAS WANT UGC NORM'S ROLL-BACK
In the past few days, as the anti-reservation narrative has gathered momentum online, the movement has also spilled onto the streets. Protests and demonstrations have been reported in Maharashtra's Nagpur, Uttar Pradesh's Lucknow, Rajasthan's Jaipur, and Andhra Pradesh's Visakhapatnam.
The Times of India reported that the Reservation Hatao Movement (RHM) on July 30 made its on-ground debut in Nagpur with a rally. The organisers had told the newspaper that around 1,000-2,000 people were expected to participate in the march. They described the Nagpur rally as the beginning of a nationwide campaign seeking changes to India's reservation system and drew parallels with how the CJP evolved from an online campaign into a street movement.
Days later, on August 3, members of Savarna Morcha and Swarn Samaj in Lucknow came out in the city's Shahid Smarak and Hazratganj area, reported Amar Ujala. They demanded a complete rollback of UGC rules and an end to caste-based reservation, alleging that they "gained nothing from democracy so far".
KARNI SENA PROTESTS IN JAIPUR, DEMANDS UGC NORMS ROLL-BACK
A day later, a rally of thousands of people belonging to the Shri Rajput Karni Sena, led by its chief Mahipal Singh Makrana, reached in Jaipur after what the outfit described as a 24-day, 800-km march demanding the rollback of the UGC's 2026 Equity Regulations, according to Dainik Bhaskar newspaper.
While the Sena mainly demanded the UGC norms be rolled back, they also sought "the review of caste-based laws, reservation for the economically weaker sections category in panchayat and municipal elections, and simplification of EWS reservation rules at the central level, among other demands," The Times of India reported.
Karni Sena's members marched towards the Collectorate and later attempted to move towards the BJP office and the Chief Minister's residence. The police used water cannons and carried out a lathi charge after clashes erupted and barricades were breached. Makrana alleged that women, children and women were hit, which led to the death of one of the protesters.
Following the police action, Makrana administered an oath asking supporters not to vote for the BJP in the upcoming urban local body and panchayat elections, reported Dainik Bhaskar. The Indian Express reported that Makrana warned that "if their demands weren't met, they would also oppose the BJP in the upcoming urban local body polls and later, the panchayat polls to ensure the ruling party's defeat".
Karni Sena has issued a seven-day ultimatum, threatening a Jaipur gherao and Rajasthan bandh. Former Rajasthan CM Ashok Gehlot accused the BJP government of a "dictatorial attitude", but didn't comment on the merits and demerits of the reservation.
Then, on August 3, NEET aspirants in Andhra Pradesh's Visakhapatnam, under the Jana Jagarana Samiti, held a silent protest in support of the RHA that we talked about. The young participants also wore black ribbons across their mouths and held placards, called for ending caste-based reservation, shifting to economic criteria, limiting quota benefits to a generation, minimum qualifying marks for all, incorporation of periodic reviews and sunset clauses, and ending election-time reservation promises, reported The Hindu.
While streets and roads across several states are witnessing demonstrations, the online space — where narratives are shaped, and mass mobilisation begins in the digital age — is seeing anti-reservation voices and demands grow even louder and more nuanced. Also, there is a caveat in the online mobilisation, which we'll come to shortly.
ONLINE MOBILISATION AGAINST QUOTA IN FULL SWING
The RHA, floated by a student named Vedant, now headed by influencer Ajeet Bharti, has now floated five policy proposals to replace caste-based quotas with "income-based reservations". The caveat is that while the RHA is concentrating on building a narrative online rather than rushing to the streets, Harsh Dubey [the face of the viral anti-reservation campaign] is still waiting for Delhi Police's permission to protest at Jantar Mantar.
In fact, after Dubey suggested on social media that permission had been granted to share an acknowledgement, the DCP of New Delhi had to publicly clarify that no approval had been issued.
Initially, many of the passionate anti-reservation voices had called for the scrapping of the entire reservation system. But many of these proposals would be difficult to implement, both politically and constitutionally, and would certainly clash with political will and would face judicial scrutiny. Moreover, in a post on X, Vendant said that he "started the RHA page on Instagram with one objective — to begin a national discussion on a subject that many people were hesitant to even talk about".
"One thing I also learnt is that many people expect immediate agitation, while my first goal was to encourage discussion. Lasting change begins when people are willing to talk, debate, and question. Agitation without dialogue rarely produces durable solutions," Vedant said in a post on X, where he was clarifying that the RHA handle had not been "hijacked" by Bharti, as critics were suggesting.
According to the RHA's proposal, the movement seeks to replace caste-based quotas with "income-based reservations." It argued that "poverty has no caste".
It also advocated "one family, one reservation, one time", a minimum qualifying mark for all categories, and the transfer of unfilled reserved seats to the general category. It has also suggested periodic reviews to move economically advanced communities off of the reservation list.
The proposal further called for a "sunset clause" to gradually phase out reservations as educational inequality narrows, while banning political parties from promising new or higher reservation quotas during elections.
Apart from its five-point policy proposal, the RHA has been using social media to build a broader narrative around reservation reform. The posts frequently criticise the existing caste-based reservation system, arguing that it disadvantages economically weaker students from the general category while privileging caste over merit.
The RHA, in one of its posts, strongly opposed the UGC's 2026 Equity Regulations, which saw fierce resistance from the "upper castes".
It claimed the UGC norms would further entrench reservations and adversely affect educational standards. The RHA also regularly shares videos and graphics to mobilise supporters and expand its online reach.
The RHA has framed the debate on merit, equality and economic justice, not caste identity.
At least for now, the RHA seems more focused on mainstreaming the debate on reservation that it believes has been avoided. It appears to be in no mood to launch nationwide street protests like Harsh Dubey, even though its messaging found resonance at the recent demonstration in Visakhapatnam.
So, that brings up to the question of whether the government has at all tried to rationalise reservations in India?
HAS THE GOVERNMENT TRIED TO RATIONALISE RESERVATION IN INDIA?
While the RHA is seeking a fundamental redesign of India's reservation policy, central government-appointed committees in the past have focussed on reforming the existing framework and were category-specific. The Justice G Rohini Commission, constituted in 2017, recommended sub-categorising the Central OBC quota so that benefits are distributed more evenly among backward communities. The BP Sharma Expert Committee (2019) suggested revising and simplifying the OBC creamy layer criteria.
Neither panel recommended replacing caste with income as the basis for reservation or phasing out affirmative action.
The creamy layer criteria have been periodically revised over the years. The Rohini Commission's recommendations on OBC sub-categorisation are yet to be implemented by the Centre. In that sense and perspective, the RHA's agenda is broader and more structural.
Meanwhile, posting an image of the RHA's Instagram page with a cross sign over it, MoS for Social Justice, Ramdas Athawale said anti-social elements were trying to incite India's youth against the country. Taking to X, he asserted that "no one can take away our reservation rights".
He warned that if anyone attempted to snatch away the reservation, those who had fought for it for generations knew how to defend it. He added that "Babasaheb Ambedkar's constitutional guarantee was completely secure".
Whether the momentum remains only an online conversation or morphs into a nationwide movement would depend on whether these disparate anti-reservation voices can find common leadership, a shared agenda and sustained public support. The political class is mum on this, as usual. The shrilling anti-quota voices, built on the CJP-led protests' momentum, have made that reservation rage spilling onto the streets.

headline: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday directed the officials to prepare comprehensive micro-level development plans for the Visakhapatnam Economic Region (VER), with a focus on balanced growth, infrastructure expansion, indu...
full_text:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday directed the officials to prepare comprehensive micro-level development plans for the Visakhapatnam Economic Region (VER), with a focus on balanced growth, infrastructure expansion, industrial development, tourism, and employment generation.
Reviewing the progress of the project at the Secretariat in Amaravati, Mr. Naidu said the development strategy should encompass every region and sector within the VER and align with the aspirations of local communities. The review covered proposed projects, Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) reclassification, the Visakhapatnam Bay City project, and the establishment of a Bay City Authority.
Investment potential
Officials informed the Chief Minister that the region had the potential to attract investments worth nearly ₹9.5 lakh crore. Of this, around ₹5.3 lakh crore is expected from the private sector, while government projects are estimated to require investments of ₹3.5 lakh crore to ₹4 lakh crore. They highlighted major projects such as the Google’s AI data centre and the ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel plant, which are expected to strengthen the region's industrial ecosystem.
Bay City Project
Officials said the Bay City Project has been identified as the anchor project for the region, complementing the existing information technology, data centre, manufacturing, logistics, and tourism infrastructure in and around Visakhapatnam.
The Chief Minister stressed the need to ensure that development initiatives comply with the CRZ regulations and coastal management plans. He said the proposed economic corridor should extend from Mulapeta Port in Srikakulam district to the Akhanda Godavari region in Rajamahendravaram and integrate tourism destinations, industrial hubs, townships, and experience zones.
Mr. Naidu directed the officials to utilise funds from multiple schemes, attract additional support from the Union government, and ensure the integrated development of the six urban development authorities within the VER.
He said the project should strengthen physical infrastructure while generating employment opportunities and improving the skills of local youth.
The Chief Minister also emphasised the importance of public-private partnerships and asked officials to explore the implementation of the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme wherever necessary. He instructed the administration to communicate the benefits of the project, including job opportunities and improvements in infrastructure, to the public regularly.
Calling for the involvement of academic institutions in the planning process, Mr. Naidu said the expertise of Andhra University should be fully utilised in preparing the development blueprint.
He also proposed the formation of a dedicated executive committee to oversee the implementation of the Bay City project. Emphasising the strategic importance of east-west connectivity, he said enhanced integration of roads, railways, ports, airports, logistics networks, global capability centres (GCCs), and financial technology infrastructure would accelerate economic growth.
Mr. Naidu said stronger connectivity between Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and western India would enhance trade and attract investments. Linking four airports and three ports in the region, he added, would significantly strengthen the area's economic potential.
The Chief Minister further directed officials to develop the Visakhapatnam zoo into a world-class tourist attraction, noting that the city's emergence as an international destination created new opportunities for tourism development.
Chief Secretary G. Sai Prasad and senior officials from the finance, industries, municipal administration, forest, energy, tourism, education, and health departments attended the meeting.

headline: The Kerala High Court has refused to suspend the sentence of Martin Antony, the second accused in the actor assault case of 2017.

Antony had contended that the prosecution had not adequately proved the charges against him, and that he was neither a passenger nor a witness or driver of the car in which the assault allegedly took place. He also contended that he had been arrested in 2017 and had undergone more than five years of imprisonment and had been serving his sentence since December 2025.
Six of the 10 accused were convicted by the Sessions Judge, Ernakulam, in 2025. Each accused was charged with two counts of gang rape, assault, use of criminal force on a woman with intent to disrobe, wrongful confinement, destruction of evidence, and taking and distributing obscene images.

headline: Noting the failure of replacement satellite NVS-02 in 2025, Jitendra Singh said that mecessary corrective measures have been incorporated
full_text:
Noting the failure of replacement satellite NVS-02 in 2025, Jitendra Singh said that mecessary corrective measures have been incorporated
NEW DELHI: The government is working to have the countryâs Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System or NaVIC up and running again as it plans to launch four satellites in the near future.âNVS-03 is ready for launch after incorporation of all corrective measures arising from the NVS-02 anomaly. It will be followed by the launch of NVS-04 and NVS-05. One more satellite is planned thereafter to complete the seven-satellite NavIC base layer constellation,â space minister Jitendra Singh said in a written reply in Lok Sabha on Wednesday.He, however, did not mention the timeline for these launches.Noting the failure of replacement satellite NVS-02 in 2025, Jitendra Singh said, âNecessary corrective measures have been incorporated and successfully implemented and tested in CMS-03 satellite. The same will be followed in subsequent satellites, including the NavIC series of satellites carrying bi-propellant systems.âCurrently, only IRNSS 1-B, IRNSS 1-L and NVS-01 are capable of providing navigation services. But for the NaVIC system to be operational effectively, at least four satellites with operational atomic clocks are required. So, NavIC is no longer providing standalone positioning services.
In March this year, the last atomic clock on board Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System-1F (IRNSS-1F) stopped functioning, paralysing NavIC.The first-generation satellites for NavIC were launched between 2013 and 2018. However, the constellation of satellites soon began to face issues, with the atomic clocks on board several IRNSS series satellites repeatedly malfunctioning.The NVS series represents the second-generation satellites for NavIC. While Isro successfully placed NVS-01 in the desired orbit in 2023, the 2025 launch of NVS-02 failed. This has delayed the launch of NVS-03, NVS-04 and NVS-05.

headline: 75% of 1st Agniveer batch to exit, 50% CAPF quota in place: MoS Rai to Rajya Sabha
full_text:
75% of 1st Agniveer batch to exit, 50% CAPF quota in place: MoS Rai to Rajya Sabha
The government told the Rajya Sabha that 75 per cent of the first Agniveer batch is expected to complete its four-year term and exit the Armed Forces. It said 50 per cent of Constable and Rifleman vacancies in CAPFs and Assam Rifles have been reserved for ex-Agniveers.
75 per cent of the first batch of Agniveers recruited under the Centre's Agnipath scheme are expected to complete their four-year tenure and exit the Armed Forces, the government informed the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday.
Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai, in a written reply, said the government has already provided for the reservation of 50 per cent of vacancies for the posts of Constable (General Duty) and Rifleman in the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Assam Rifles (AR) for Agniveers.
"Under the Agnipath scheme, 75% of the total Agniveers of the first batch are expected to complete their four-year engagement in the Armed Forces. The government has made provision for reservation of 50% vacancies for the post of Constable (General Duty)/Rifleman in CAPFs and Assam Rifles," Rai said.
He added that the first batch of Agniveers has not yet completed its term of engagement.
Earlier, Nityanand Rai informed the Lok Sabha that former Agniveers would be eligible for a 50 per cent reservation in recruitment to Constable (General Duty) and Rifleman posts in the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Assam Rifles. In a written reply, he said a separate "ex-Agniveer" category has been created for these recruitments, under which half of all vacancies will be earmarked for candidates who have completed service under the Agnipath scheme.
The Agnipath scheme, launched in 2022, recruits young men and women between the ages of 17.5 and 21 years for a four-year stint in the Army, Navy and Air Force.
Under the scheme, only up to 25 per cent of each batch is retained for permanent service based on merit, medical fitness and organisational requirements. The remaining personnel exit the forces after four years and receive a severance package, skill certificates and other support measures aimed at facilitating employment opportunities in the civilian sector.
The government's reservation policy in CAPFs and Assam Rifles is part of a broader effort to provide post-service career avenues for Agniveers completing their tenure under the scheme.

headline: The high court had refused to hear him on the technical ground and prolonged his stay in jail by 10 more years
full_text:
The high court had refused to hear him on the technical ground and prolonged his stay in jail by 10 more years
NEW DELHI: A trial courtâs failure to evaluate the evidence properly and the Odisha High Court remaining a mute spectator resulted in 22 years being erased from a personâs life as he was wrongly convicted and his appeal was not heard by the high court. Finally, the Supreme Court has come to his rescue and acquitted him.It is a classic case where a poor litigantâs fight for justice is frustrated at the altar of the judiciary itself, when the court refused hearing on technical grounds. The poor convict had already spent 12 years in jail when he approached the high court. The high court refused to hear him on the technical ground that there was a delay in filing an appeal, and it prolonged his stay in jail by 10 more years before he was acquitted by the Supreme Court, which had to admit that âaccess to justice still eludes the marginalised sections of our society and especially those convicted and imprisoned from among themâ.âWe are deeply dismayed, and equally perturbed by the order which rejected an application seeking condonation of delay of 3,157 days and as a consequence dismissed the âJail Memo of Appealâ against the order of conviction under Section 302, with sentence imposed of life imprisonment where the convict had, at the time of the impugned order suffered incarceration of 12 years and now a further period of 10 years; a total of 22 years,â a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said.
It said the high court ought to have also considered that it was an appeal through jail and the court ought to have taken a practical view, or rather a sympathetic view, of the matter and at least ought to have condoned the delay to give one opportunity to the petitioner to argue his criminal appeal on the merits.âWhen the three pillars of democracy consistently endeavour to bring legal aid to the doorsteps of every citizen, especially the poor...we...should sensitise ourselves in taking a liberal approach...Not a mere liberal approach but a pro-active one to condone delay, however large it is, when a convict knocks at the door of a Court...which in the present case raises some real concerns,â the bench said.
Examining the evidence, the court concluded that it was not a fit case of conviction on the basis of a sole eyewitness, which was not reliable and was shaky. It acquitted him in a triple murder case.â... a person taken into custody on mere suspicion from whom a confession, though not admissible, was extracted employing third-degree methods, the trial court fails to evaluate the evidence properly, and the high court remains a mute spectator...resulting in 22 years being erased out of a personâs life without any reliable evidence,â the court said.

headline: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) sought to expand his party’s ‘PDA’ constituency and include Pandits or Brahmins in its Pichhda-Dalit-Alpsankhyak (Backwards, Dalits and minorities) matrix ahead of the State ...

Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) sought to expand his party’s ‘PDA’ constituency and include Pandits or Brahmins in its Pichhda-Dalit-Alpsankhyak (Backwards, Dalits and minorities) matrix ahead of the State Assembly poll due early next year. The SP has used the PDA plank as a call for broader unity of forces of social justice since the 2022 Assembly election.
“People keep talking about PDA and inventing new meanings about it. Ever since they (BJP) lost to PDA, they have been trying to redefine it. But they have forgotten that the ‘PD’ in PDA also stands for Pandit. The more they inflict peeda (pain), the stronger PDA will become,” said the SP chief while addressing a ‘Brahmin/Prabuddh varg Sammelan’ at the party headquarters in Lucknow on the birth anniversary of late Socialist leader and MP Janeshwar Mishra.
Mr. Yadav hit out at the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh for “neglecting” Brahmins, other marginalised communities and religious leaders, and accused it of targeting Opposition workers and leaders. “They were already targeting our workers and us. Now they have also started targeting the Brahmin community. They are after the ‘P’ of PDA as well,” he alleged.
The SP chief referred to Swami Avimukteshwaranand being prevented from taking a holy dip during the Kumbh congregation earlier this year. “If there is any example in history where a government stopped a Shankaracharya from taking a holy dip, show us one. A false POCSO case was also filed to intimidate him, but he did not bow down,” he said.
In another signal to Brahmins, he said the SP, whenever it has got the chance, has done the work of giving respect to the community. He touched upon the embezzlement of donations at the Ram Temple as well: “Today, the biggest sin committed by anyone is that by the Bharatiya Janata Party, which stole even the offerings made to Lord Shri Ram… Lord Shri Ram will not let them win.”
‘Game changer’
Lucknow-based political analyst Asad Rizvi said the signal to Brahmins is aimed at securing a section of votes that could prove to be a game changer. “Brahmins, with a population of over 9%, are traditional BJP voters. The SP plans to align with the Brahmin community through Janeshwar Mishra’s birth anniversary. It knows that winning the community’s trust will significantly ease its path to power,” he said.

headline: Govt extends tenure of Cabinet, Home secretaries by one year
full_text:
Govt extends tenure of Cabinet, Home secretaries by one year
The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved one-year extensions for Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan and Home Secretary Govind Mohan.
The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Wednesday approved one-year extensions in service for cabinet secretary T V Somanathan and Union home secretary Govind Mohan, according to separate orders issued by the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT).
Somanathan gets another year
The ACC approved the extension of Somanathan, a 1987-batch IAS officer of the Tamil Nadu cadre, as cabinet secretary for one year beyond August 30, 2026.
“The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet has approved an extension in service of Dr T.V. Somanathan, IAS (TN:87) as Cabinet Secretary for a further period of one year beyond August 30, 2026,” the DoPT order said.
Somanathan was appointed cabinet secretary on August 30, 2024, succeeding Rajiv Gauba. Before taking over the country’s top bureaucratic post, he served as finance secretary and held key positions in the Prime Minister’s Office, including joint secretary and additional secretary.
Also read: Centre extends CBI chief Praveen Sood's tenure by one more year
Govind Mohan's tenure also extended
In a separate order, the ACC approved a one-year extension for Govind Mohan, a 1989-batch IAS officer of the Sikkim cadre, as Union home secretary beyond August 22, 2026.
“The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet has approved extension in the service of Shri Govind Mohan, IAS (SK:89) as Home Secretary, Ministry of home affairs for a period of one year beyond 22.08.2026 i.e. up to 22.08.2027 or until further orders, whichever is earlier, in relaxation of the provisions of FR 56 (d) and Rule 16 (1A) of the All India Services (Death-Cum-Retirement Benefits) Rules, 1958,” the order said.
The relaxation has been granted under provisions that allow the Centre to extend the tenure of certain key officials beyond the retirement age of 60 years. These include the cabinet secretary, home secretary, defence secretary, foreign secretary, the Intelligence Bureau director and the chief of the Research and Analysis Wing, among others.
Also read: Supreme Court okays 6-month extension for retiring members of tribunals
Mohan was appointed home secretary in August 2024, replacing Ajay Bhalla, who is now the governor of Manipur. Before assuming the post, Mohan served as secretary in the Ministry of Culture.
The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet comprises Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah.

headline: Ashutosh Ranka teases major CJP announcement today, nationwide expansion on agenda

Ashutosh Ranka teases major CJP announcement today, nationwide expansion on agenda
The Cockroach Janta Party will announce its next roadmap on Thursday after a strategy meeting in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. The group says it will expand nationally as a student pressure platform focused on education reforms, not electoral politics.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which emerged as a prominent voice during the nationwide protests against alleged examination paper leaks, is set to make a major announcement on Thursday regarding its future course of action and expansion plans.
In a video message shared on Instagram, CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the organisation's leadership had spent the past two days in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar preparing a roadmap for the movement's next phase.
“We have begun a massive fight for systemic change in this country,” Ranka said, adding that the movement had generated significant expectations among people across India.
According to Ranka, the leadership reviewed thousands of suggestions and messages received from supporters through social media platforms, including Instagram and WhatsApp, before finalising its strategy. He said a major announcement outlining the movement's future direction would be made on Thursday.
The announcement comes after CJP leaders held a nearly seven-hour strategy meeting at the residence of the organisation's founder, Abhijeet Dipke, in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. During the meeting, the leadership resolved to strengthen the group's presence across the country, build a nationwide network of student organisations and support ongoing education-related agitations in different states.
The organisation also discussed plans in the meeting to expand as a national student pressure group while keeping education reforms at the centre of its agenda. CJP leaders decided that the movement would continue functioning as a social and advocacy platform rather than entering electoral politics.
“Today we have gathered here to discuss the roadmap. How and where all can we contribute in other parts of the country, we will discuss,” Dipke said after the meeting. “We are not thinking about starting a political party. People of India don't trust the judiciary, politicians and the entire system. We will work as a pressure group,” he added.
Leaders present at the meeting said the organisation would remain focused exclusively on education-related issues, including examination reforms, transparency, accountability, student welfare and strengthening the education system.
The leadership also agreed to build the movement around the principles of Mahatma Gandhi and Dr BR Ambedkar, committing itself to non-violent and democratic methods while remaining independent of conventional political parties.
The strategy session followed what CJP describes as a major milestone in its anti-paper leak campaign — the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The organisation views the development as the beginning of a broader push for systemic reforms and has signalled that Thursday's announcement will outline the next stage of that campaign.

headline: Will Tarun Tejpal's acquittal be overturned in sex assault case? Big verdict today
full_text:
Will Tarun Tejpal's acquittal be overturned in sex assault case? Big verdict today
The case dates back to 2013, when an employee of Tehelka alleged that Tarun Tejpal sexually assaulted her in the elevator of a Goa resort. The judgment in the case will be closely watched, coming after days of hearings in one of the most high-profile trials involving a prominent journalist.
Will the acquittal of Tehelka founder Tarun Tejpal in the 2013 sexual assault case be overturned? The Goa bench of the Bombay High Court is set to deliver its verdict on the appeal by the Goa government on Thursday. The judgment in the case will be closely watched, coming after days of protracted hearings in one of India's most high-profile trials involving a prominent journalist.
The High Court reserved its order on July 30. At the centre of the appeal is whether the Goa sessions court erred in acquitting Tejpal in 2021 and whether his apology email to the complainant, a junior Tehelka employee, amounted to an admission that a sexual encounter took place. The High Court has directed the former Tehelka editor-in-chief to remain personally present in court on Thursday.
Before we go into what transpired during the High Court hearings, here's a flashback of what the case is all about.
WHAT IS THE TARUN TEJPAL CASE?
The case dates back to November 7, 2013, in Goa, where Tehelka magazine's annual Thinkfest event was being held. At that time, Tehelka was one of the most influential investigative magazines, and Tejpal had celebrity-like status. The woman alleged that Tejpal sexually assaulted her in the elevator of Grand Hyatt in Bambolim.
The matter came to light after a trail of emails between the woman, Tejpal, and Tehelka's then managing editor got leaked. Tejpal stepped down as editor six months after the incident and was also arrested later. He was released on bail in July 2014.
The trial in the case at the Goa sessions court began in 2017. Four years later, Tejpal was acquitted of all charges. In its order, the court said the complainant did not demonstrate any kind of "normative behaviour" that a survivor of sexual assault "might plausibly show".
However, the acquittal invited widespread criticism and backlash, following which the Goa government challenged the verdict before the Goa bench of the Bombay High Court.
The final arguments were heard by a bench of Justices Dr Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar over three days - which saw the prosecution and defence cite numerous WhatsApp chats, CCTV footage, emails, and testimonies of witnesses to push their case.
While Solicitor General Tushar Mehta represented Goa, senior advocate Aabad Ponda argued on behalf of Tejpal.
DAY 1: WHAT HAPPENED AT LIFT OF GOA RESORT?
The first day of the hearing centred around the survivor's key claim - the alleged assault inside the lift of the resort.
Tejpal's lawyer argued that the woman's allegation that the Tehelka founder kept the elevator moving by pressing buttons to keep it in a "continuous loop", which prevented the doors from opening, was mechanically impossible. To buttress his claim, Ponda submitted the testimony of an expert and CCTV records.
"When the emergency stop button is pressed, the lift goes to the closest landing or the floor and stops, and the doors open automatically," Ponda said, quoting the expert's testimony.
Quoting the expert, Ponda further said that even if the "close" button was continuously pressed, the doors "will automatically open to the fullest" whenever the lift reached a floor.
Tejpal's lawyer also said the CCTV footage did not back the woman's allegation that she was pulled back into the lift when she tried to exit. He said the footage showed Tejpal walking ahead of the woman after they exited the lift.
Solicitor General Mehta, however, maintained that the survivor was a "credible witness" whose testimony withstood extensive cross-examination.
DAY 2: SURVIVOR'S 'CONDUCT' AFTER INCIDENT
The survivor's conduct following the alleged incident formed the crux of the second day's hearing at the High Court.
Tejpal's lawyer argued that the woman's actions contradicted her claim that she was distressed or was in a state of trauma after the incident. Ponda submitted that the complainant continued to participate in social gatherings after the alleged incident.
In one incident, Ponda said, the woman texted Tejpal and asked him to join her for a photograph with Hollywood actor Robert De Niro, whom she was chaperoning at the event.
The lawyer argued that it countered the prosecution's claim that the woman was "fearful" of Tejpal and was trying to avoid him.
He also placed WhatsApp texts between the survivor and her friends before the court. Ponda said the woman, in one of the messages, stated that she wanted to create a "reign of sexual terror".
Ponda further submitted that the complainant had a "propensity to lie". "Amnesia and trauma are her answers to every piercing question," he said.
TARUN TEJPAL'S APOLOGY EMAIL
One of the key issues before the High Court was an email Tejpal sent to the woman after the alleged incident.
The prosecution argued that the email was an "admission of guilt". However, Tejpal's lawyer argued that it was sent under "institutional pressure" to protect Tehelka's reputation.
"An internal apology email cannot be treated as a voluntary confession of sexual assault... it was allegedly engineered under pressure by Tehelka's then managing editor," Tejpal's lawyer told the High Court.
He also argued that Tejpal was under immense emotional pressure at that time, particularly due to his mother's illness.
DAY 3: MOTIVE AND RS 1 LAKH GRANT
On the final day of the hearing, the defence sought to bring into focus the alleged motive behind the woman's claims.
Tejpal's lawyer claimed the sexual assault narrative was made up by the woman to secure a Rs 1 lakh fellowship grant to write a book on violence against women.
He said much before the incident, the woman was exploring other employment opportunities. Ponda claimed the woman had received an offer linked to the TV show Satyamev Jayate. She also applied for a year-long fellowship to write a book on violence against women, he claimed.
"Can someone who is writing about violence against women not go to the police?" Ponda argued in concluding arguments. He submitted that rather than going to the police, the woman was more inclined towards a settlement with Tehelka.
HOW GOA GOVT COUNTERED ARGUMENTS?
Countering Tejpal's lawyer, the Goa government argued that there could not be any universal standard for a survivor's conduct.
SG Mehta said the trial court, while acquitting Tejpal, adopted stereotypical assumptions on how a sexual assault survivor should behave.
The Solicitor General also underscored that the woman's decision to continue with her "professional duties" after the alleged incident could not be used to undermine her credibility.
He also said the trial court attached undue importance to minor inconsistencies in her testimony. The complainant's core allegations had remained consistent throughout, SG Mehta said.
On Thursday, the High Court will decide the fate of Tejpal's acquittal in a case that has been in the spotlight for over a decade.

headline: The allocation for the Higher Education Department in Tamil Nadu Revised Budget 2026-27 has dropped by ₹101 crore compared to last fiscal year prompting sharp response from educationists and activists.
full_text:
The allocation for the Higher Education Department in Tamil Nadu Revised Budget 2026-27 has dropped by ₹101 crore compared to last fiscal year prompting sharp response from educationists and activists.
The total outlay for the department has been put at ₹8,393 crore. In his Budget speech, State Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson highlighted allocation of ₹2,000 crore for the “Vetri Laptop Scheme” for college students and the proposal to establish a specialised government law college in Madurai with an intake of 300 students.
He also announced the setting up of Tamil Nadu Student Housing and Infrastructure Corporation to build 200 integrated students’ hostels with one lakh beds through a Public-Private Partnership model at a total capital outlay of ₹3,200 crore with a State grant of ₹640 crore. Although the Finance Minister’s speech did not mention much else, budget documents indicate that the government has allocated ₹1,807 crore as a grant to universities, which is an increase from ₹1,678 crore last fiscal. Besides, there has been a marginal increase in the amount allocated for the payment of fees for students admitted to colleges under the 7.5% horizontal reservation scheme (preferential allotment for students who studied in government schools from Class VI to Class XII).
Reacting to the budget, G. Thiruvasagam, former vice-chancellor of University of Madras, said that Tamil Nadu’s 20-odd universities have over 50% vacancies in faculty positions. If the government seeks to fill up the vacancies, the allocation will not be enough. The shortfall in faculty members is being managed with part-time faculty, which has impacted research and publication, not to mention pedagogy and instruction.
Although Tamil Nadu universities and colleges have fared better than others in the country in NIRF rankings, poor funding from the government has begun to take a toll. “All universities are low on resources. The allocation would not even meet a fraction of their requirement,” Dr. Thiruvasagam asserted. Elaborating, he said that public universities in the State were losing students to private universities because of better infrastructure, laboratory facilities, and technology-oriented teaching materials there. “If we are to attract better and more students to our universities, we need to increase funding several times,” he added.
Meanwhile, P.B. Prince Gajendra Babu, general secretary, State Platform for Common School System-Tamil Nadu, raised concerns over the cost of accommodation and food at the students’ hostels built under the PPP model. He said there was significant risk that it would impose a heavy financial burden on both students and parents, especially first-generation learners and women students. The decrease in allocation to Higher Education at a time when universities were facing a financial crisis contradicts the government’s stated policy of strengthening higher education, he added.

headline: ‘Nambikkai Illam’, a centre for persons with intellectual disabilities, will be coming up on the Girivalam path near Arunachaleswarar temple in Tiruvannamalai town as revenue officials have identified land for the new facility.

‘Nambikkai Illam’, a centre for persons with intellectual disabilities, will be coming up on the Girivalam path near Arunachaleswarar temple in Tiruvannamalai town as revenue officials have identified land for the new facility.
Along with health and revenue officials, Collector Vandana Garg and District Revenue Officer (DRO) A. Siva Subramanian has identified land near Government Arts and Science College along the path in the town.
The ‘Nambikkai Illam’ initiative was announced by State Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson during the presentation of the Annual Budget for 2026-27 on Wednesday. “The new government facility will be a model one stop centre where all facilities and training for persons with intellectual disabilities will be provided. The identified land is located along a bus route and can be accessed easily,” M. Saradha, District Disabled Officer (Tiruvannamalai), told The Hindu.
Officials of Welfare of Differently Abled Persons Department, which will maintain the facility, said that the new centre will provide special education, early intervention services, including physiotherapy, rehabilitation, and vocational training for children aged three and above. “The new government centre in Tiruvannamalai town will be the largest facility in terms of space with modern facilities,” Ms. Saradha said.
Officials said initially, the new facility would function as a day school between 9. 45 a.m and 5 p.m on all days, except Sundays. On an average, around 50 students would be enrolled at the centre which would have 13 staff led by the chief coordinator. Around 20 cents of government land have been identified for the purpose with a budgetary allocation of ₹4 crore.
At present, persons with intellectual disabilities, including children are taken care of in government-aided homes in the district. Officials had undertaken door-to-door visits to identify persons with intellectual disabilities and around 53,000 persons with disabilities have been identified in the district.
Officials also said that other Panchayat Unions such as Arani, Chengam, Kilpennathur, Vandavasi, Cheyyar, Polur, Jamunamarathur, and Chetpet would have small centres for persons with intellectual disabilities in the coming months. These small centres would mostly operate at government hospitals in the area. headline: Crackdown on fake dairy grows as Gujarat joins Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh
full_text:
Crackdown on fake dairy grows as Gujarat joins Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh
Gujarat has banned the production and sale of analogue paneer, cheese and butter across the state. The move follows lab findings, with officials citing consumer protection, food safety and misleading labelling.
The Gujarat government has imposed a statewide ban on the production, storage, transportation, distribution and sale of analogue paneer, cheese and butter, citing public health concerns and consumer protection. The decision comes after food safety inspections and laboratory tests found several products being sold as dairy items despite not meeting prescribed standards.
Announcing the move, Gujarat Health Minister Praful Pansheriya said restaurants, hotels, dairy parlours, supermarkets, caterers and traders across the state have been directed not to manufacture, sell or transport such products. Authorities have warned that violations could attract legal action under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
Analogue dairy products are designed to resemble traditional paneer, cheese or butter but are often made using vegetable oils, starches and other non-dairy ingredients. Officials say such products can mislead consumers when marketed as genuine dairy products and also hurt the interests of dairy farmers and milk-based food manufacturers.
The state's Food Safety Department carried out extensive sampling and laboratory testing before recommending the ban. Investigators found instances where products were being sold as dairy items despite failing to conform to established standards. The government said the ban aims to ensure that consumers receive safe, authentic and high-quality food products.
All food business operators have been instructed to use and sell only genuine dairy-based paneer and related products in accordance with regulatory norms.
OTHER STATES TIGHTEN CURBS
Gujarat's move follows similar action by Maharashtra, which recently prohibited the manufacture, storage, transport, distribution and sale of analogue paneer and other artificial dairy substitutes. Violators can face penalties, including imprisonment and fines under food safety laws.
Reports also indicate that Chhattisgarh had earlier imposed restrictions on analogue paneer, making it one of the first states to crack down on such products amid growing concerns over food adulteration and misleading labelling.
The crackdown comes amid a broader regulatory push by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which has directed manufacturers and food service establishments not to sell cheese analogues as paneer and to clearly disclose the use of non-dairy substitutes to consumers.

headline: Collective failure: SC acquits Odisha man after 22 years for crime he didn't commit
full_text:
Collective failure: SC acquits Odisha man after 22 years for crime he didn't commit
Arjun Jani was arrested largely on suspicion and subjected to third-degree methods to extract a confession. The police failed to produce reliable evidence establishing his guilt.
The Supreme Court has acquitted an Odisha man who spent 22 years in prison after being wrongly convicted in a triple murder case, calling his prolonged incarceration a "collective failure" of the country’s criminal justice system.
The man, Arjun Jani, was convicted in the 2004 murder of three women in Odisha’s Nabarangpur district and spent more than two decades behind bars after being subjected to third-degree methods during interrogation.
A three-judge bench of the Supreme Court expressed serious concern over the miscarriage of justice, observing that Jani had been deprived of his liberty for 22 years despite the absence of credible evidence against him.
The court said the loss of more than two decades of an individual’s freedom without sufficient proof reflected a "collective failure" of the criminal justice system.
The case dates back to 2004, when three women were murdered in Nabarangpur district. Jani was subsequently arrested after an alleged eyewitness claimed to have seen him at the crime scene.
According to the Supreme Court, the police arrested Jani largely on suspicion and allegedly subjected him to third-degree methods during interrogation to extract a confession. The purported confession became a key part of the prosecution’s case and eventually led to his conviction.
Re-examining the evidence and the manner in which the investigation was conducted, the Supreme Court held that the prosecution had failed to establish Jani’s guilt beyond reasonable doubt. The Bench found that his conviction could not be sustained in the absence of reliable and legally admissible evidence.
The Supreme Court subsequently acquitted Jani of all charges, bringing an end to his 22-year incarceration. The court also flagged serious shortcomings in the investigation and the criminal justice process that resulted in his prolonged loss of liberty.
