As part of the reforms, the existing route-wise categorisation of licences will be abolished
NEW DELHI: Container Train Operators (CTOs) will now be able to operate across the entire Indian railways network with a single licence by paying a one-time fee, in a move akin to the National Permit system for trucks. The reform aims to boost containerised cargo movement by rail, reduce road congestion and cut air pollution, especially as nearly the entire railway network has been electrified and rail freight remains significantly cheaper than road transport.Introducing the major overhaul of the CTO licensing framework in nearly two decades, the railway ministry has approved a uniform all-India licence fee of Rs 25 crore, replacing the existing system under which operators paid Rs 10 crore or Rs 50 crore depending on the category of licence.Under the existing regime, concession agreements are valid for 20 years and may be extended by another 10 years. Under the revised framework, operators will instead be eligible for a fresh 20-year licence after successfully completing the initial 20-year concession period, with no additional renewal fee."The changes will be notified through a Gazette notification," the railway ministry said.As part of the reforms, the existing route-wise categorisation of licences will be abolished.
The ministry said the simplified framework would lower compliance costs and provide greater operational flexibility. There are currently 22 CTOs in the country, and the ministry expects the new policy to attract more private operators.
Existing operators will be allowed to continue under their current licence category until the end of their concession period. However, they may opt for an early migration to the new all-India licence by paying Rs 15 crore.The ministry said the uniform registration fee and the removal of renewal charges would reduce regulatory and compliance costs while simplifying the approval process."The amendments are aimed at establishing a simplified and uniform licensing framework for CTOs across the Indian Railways network. The reforms are expected to facilitate a streamlined approval mechanism while providing a common regulatory framework for container train operations under the Model Concession Agreement," it said.

headline: Cranes and earthmovers dominate Amaravati’s skyline as Andhra Pradesh’s greenfield capital, where towering government complexes and landmark infrastructure, takes shape. But behind the rapid construction is a quieter story of migrant workers, local c...
full_text:
Cranes and earthmovers dominate Amaravati’s skyline as Andhra Pradesh’s greenfield capital, where towering government complexes and landmark infrastructure, takes shape. But behind the rapid construction is a quieter story of migrant workers, local communities, women exploring entrepreneurship and skill development opportunities, and the people whose lives are being transformed alongside the city.
Among the thousands of workers contributing to Amaravati’s transformation is 46-year-old Deepak Maiti from Purba Medinipur district of West Bengal, who has spent the past year amid cranes, concrete, and steel helping build the capital city.
Maiti is among 1,900 migrant labourers, mostly from West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, and Odisha, engaged in constructing the sprawling multi-storied NGO housing project at Nelapadu village under Thullur mandal in Guntur district. His workday begins early and stretches for nine hours. Despite demanding schedule, thoughts of home are not far away. “My old mother awaits me back home. I visit her whenever possible,” he says softly.
As dusk settles over the workers’ camp, the atmosphere begins to shift. After a long day at the construction site, labourers gather around carrom boards and ludo games, sharing laughter and enjoying moments of camaraderie. Yet, conversations often drift back to families waiting thousands of kilometres away.
Maiti’s story is echoed by many others at the site, each carrying a similar tale of migration, sacrifice and hope. One of them is 35-year-old Indrabhan, a farmer from Bharatpur in Uttar Pradesh, who arrived in Amaravati four months ago in search of additional income, while the crop on his farm awaits harvesting.
“Like many seasonal migrant workers, I plan to return once the farming season demands my attention,” he says. On a lighter note, he adds that five fellow workers from his home State are also at the site. “I don’t feel out of place, and adapting to life in the camp has been easier,” he says.
Inclusivity
To make life away from home easier for these migrant workers, the contractor has put in place facilities to cater to their diverse cultural and daily needs. Separate kitchens and dining areas allow them to prepare meals according to their culinary preferences, while a grocery store within the camp stocks daily essentials, lending a sense of familiarity and routine to life far from home.
The camp site is equipped with bunk beds, sanitation facilities, safe drinking water, kitchens, dining halls, first-aid centres, CCTV surveillance, emergency response systems and recreational spaces for sports and weekend movie screenings.
Even with these facilities, the emotional burden of migration remains difficult to overcome. For 32-year-old Ramswamy from Odisha’s Rayagada district, separation from family remains the hardest part of life away from home. Having arrived in Amaravati six months ago in search of work, he left behind his wife and two young children, an eight-year-old son and a two-year-old daughter. After a long day at the construction site, one ritual remains non-negotiable. “I make video calls every day after returning to my room. Seeing my children refreshes my body and heart,” he says, a gentle smile lighting up his face. “The facilities here do not lessen the pain of separation from the family,” he adds.
Life at the site is not entirely defined by work and separation. Community celebrations, including birthday events, provide workers with relief from the rigours of construction.
Welfare at the camp extends beyond accommodation and recreation. ”Welfare measures complement a safety programme that begins even before a worker enters the site,” says Nilanchala Hotta, Occupational Health and Safety Manager at Larsen and Toubro, the multinational conglomerate company implementing the NGO housing project.
Highlighting the mandatory medical examinations, safety induction, and continuous training, Hotta says the project has recorded four million safe work hours while maintaining full compliance with environmental and social safeguard standards.
Beyond work
The scale of these measures becomes evident when viewed against the backdrop of Amaravati’s massive construction activity, stretching over expansive tracts of land. The rich alluvial plains, once known for their fertile agricultural fields nourished by the River Krishna, now bear the unmistakable marks of large-scale excavation and earthwork.
Every few kilometres, fleets of earthmovers, excavators, bulldozers, graders, dump trucks, and compactors dot the landscape, their steady movement underscoring the scale of activity under way. The roads tell the story of a city being built from the ground up. Traffic slows as signboards caution motorists with messages of “go slow”, “deep excavations in progress,” “heavy machinery at work,” and “construction zone ahead.”
Beyond the heavy machinery and construction sites, efforts have been made to support the families who have migrated with the workforce. Snaking around excavation sites will lead to a crèche set up at a labour camp in Thullur, where P. Swathi, the caretaker, is surrounded by nearly 30 children in the 3- to 10-year age group.
Bridging the language gap with the children is a challenge, shares Swathi, who is a native speaker. “I try to communicate with them in my broken Hindi,” she says with a sheepish smile and a shrug.
Caring for children is only one part of the broader social support system. Persuading mothers to send their children to the crèche is a difficult task, says Ch. Nithisha, a gender specialist deployed by the Social Welfare wing of the Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA). “Attendance remains an uphill task,” she adds.
Beyond childcare, efforts are also being made to address gender concerns, enhance safety, and create opportunities for women through dedicated welfare and empowerment initiatives. Describing her role, Nithisha says it entails preparing and implementing a Gender Action Plan, conducting awareness programmes, and providing training on gender issues and gender-based violence prevention.
She is also responsible for establishing grievance redressal mechanisms, supporting women’s livelihoods and entrepreneurship, and ensuring that the project’s benefits are inclusive, equitable, and responsive to the needs of women and vulnerable groups. “We have established Internal Complaints Committees at all levels of the projects,” she says, adding that she visits camps where women migrant workers live to see if they feel comfortable.
“Women take time to open up, and it is important to ensure their welfare while they work far away from their homes,” she says.
Bridging the gender gap
While migrant workers play a key role in Amaravati’s construction, the city’s development is also reshaping the lives of local communities that once heavily depended on agriculture. For generations, farming was the primary source of livelihood for families across the villages that now make up the Amaravati Capital Region.
Even as many landowners voluntarily pooled their land for the construction of the new capital, the need for alternative sources of income became increasingly important. Employment opportunities remained limited, particularly for women, owing to low literacy levels, early marriages, and socio-cultural norms that largely confined them to their homes.
Recognising this gender gap, the APCRDA has been working to make local women active participants in Amaravati’s growth story. “The CRDA’s Entrepreneurship Development Programme equips women with vocational skills, business training, and market linkages, enabling them to establish micro-enterprises and generate sustainable livelihoods,” says Col. V. Ramulu, Group Director of CRDA Social Development Wing.
“Through this programme, we are helping women become economically independent,” says Ramulu. The initiative aims not only to improve household incomes but also to empower women to become stakeholders in the development of the State’s future capital.
One such outcome of these efforts is the promotion of women-led entrepreneurship through “Amaravati Amma Vanta” initiative—a community-based food brand developed by the CRDA to promote local livelihoods and the culinary heritage of Andhra Pradesh. “This initiative supports women Self Help Groups (SHGs), local producer groups, and micro-entrepreneurs by providing training, quality standardisation, branding, packaging, and market access for traditional food products such as millet-based foods, pickles, sweets, snacks and other value-added local specialties,” Ramulu says.
The impact of the initiative is reflected in the journey of Adineni Mahalakshmi, a 21-year-old from Mandadam village, who had no understanding of the concept of financial independence. A Class VII dropout, she is now considered one of the successful micro-entrepreneurs. Mahalakshmi says, “I never thought I could contribute meaningfully to my family income.” As a homemaker, Mahalakshmi sells millet malt, which is in great demand among CRDA employees and people visiting the office for grievance redressal.
Mahalakshmi’s success story is one among many that highlight the programme’s wider impact on women’s livelihoods in the capital region. The initiative began with millet-based food processing training for 161 community members, leading to the establishment of 26 women-led micro-enterprises, with each entrepreneur now earning an average monthly income of ₹12,000. Encouraged by this success, APCRDA plans to expand into dairy products, culinary powders, pickles and other traditional foods under the “Amaravati Amma Vanta” brand.
“We are also exploring partnerships with corporate market facilitators such as HESA Global to connect these enterprises with organised retail outlets and wider markets, ensuring long-term commercial sustainability and improved livelihoods,” says Mr. Ramulu.
“Amaravati Amma Vanta” is only one among several livelihood initiatives being promoted in the capital region. The focus is also on equipping women with marketable skills that can pave the way for self-employment and entrepreneurship.
This is evident in the beautician training classes being conducted at an auditorium on the SRM University-AP campus. The classroom buzzed with enthusiasm as participants eagerly learnt professional beauty and grooming techniques, many nurturing dreams of setting up home-based salons or small enterprises that could provide them with a steady source of income.
Nearly 100 women from villages across the Amaravati Capital Region sat engrossed as trainer G. Vasavi demonstrated beauty and skincare techniques. The beautician course, offered by APCRDA in collaboration with SRM University-AP, is one of several skill development programmes designed to equip local residents with employable skills and encourage entrepreneurship.
“I would love to start my own beauty business from home after completing this course,” says Kaithepalli Sravani, a homemaker from Thulluru. Then, breaking into laughter, she adds, “Even if I don’t get any customers, I can at least use what I’ve learned to enhance my own beauty.”
For Borra Sri Durga Shanti, a young mother of two from Malkapuram, the training represents an opportunity to contribute to her family’s income. “I can’t wait to start my own beauty parlour and support my husband financially,” she says.
“These women are quick learners and constantly ask questions that go beyond the course curriculum,” says Vasavi, a cosmetologist and makeup artist. As part of the tie-up, SRM University is also conducting training programmes in Fitness and Nutrition Science, GST and Tally, cybersecurity, digital marketing, embedded systems, and Very Large Scale Integration technology for various sections of the local community. Additionally, a free weekly Ayurvedic medical camp, organised at the APCRDA Project Office with the support of the Department of AYUSH, provides consultations and medicines to employees and farmers visiting the capital region.
Social and environment
The focus on inclusive development transcends livelihoods and extends to the environment as well. The officials’ effort to ensure that urban development goes hand in hand with environmental conservation is exemplified by the centralised tree translocation facility, which has been developed on 15 acres of land in Anantavaram.
This facility preserves mature trees that would otherwise be lost to infrastructure development. Nearly 10,000 trees representing 54 species are being scientifically relocated, rehabilitated, and nurtured before being replanted across Amaravati’s future parks and avenues. Instead of waiting decades for new saplings to mature, the initiative safeguards existing canopy cover, biodiversity, and carbon sequestration, ensuring that the city’s green heritage grows alongside its urban infrastructure.
From protecting decades-old trees to creating spaces for remembrance and farewell, Amaravati’s development story is rooted in a broader vision of care, sustainability, and human dignity. A multi-faith funeral campus in Amaravati is a first-of-its-kind integrated facility designed to provide dignified, affordable, and environmentally sustainable funeral services for people of all faiths.
The campus addresses the lack of adequate funeral infrastructure in the capital region by offering religion-specific spaces and common amenities such as prayer halls, cremation and burial facilities, a mortuary, waiting halls, a dining area, parking, and landscaped grieving spaces. “The project was planned after extensive consultations with religious leaders and community representatives and aims to cater to the city’s needs for the next 15 years while serving as a model that can be replicated elsewhere,” says Mr. Ramulu, noting that the ₹13-crore project, built on 6.89 acres in Thulluru, has been completed and is ready for inauguration.
While construction machinery continues to dominate the skyline of Amaravati, officials are ensuring that development remains socially and environmentally accountable. In many ways, the foundations for the new capital are being laid not just with concrete and steel but also with the aspirations of the people building it.

headline: Another 15% chose "applying for job" as their next step, without indicating whether the job would be in India or overseas
full_text:
Another 15% chose "applying for job" as their next step, without indicating whether the job would be in India or overseas
NEW DELHI: The foreign degree may be global, but the career plan is largely homeward-bound: 81% of Indian study-abroad aspirants surveyed by Oxford International said they planned to return to India after completing their courses. Nearly nine in 10 were the first in their family to pursue education overseas, while almost half said the decision to go abroad was their own.The findings are part of the third edition of Student Global Mobility Index, which combines 17,925 responses to core questions with about 2,400 responses to additional questions on courses, family background, information sources and post-study plans. Another 15% chose "applying for job" as their next step, without indicating whether the job would be in India or overseas.The biggest shift over three survey cycles is in who drives the decision. Self-motivated students rose from 29% in 2023-24 to 34% in 2024-25 and 49% in 2025-26. Family influence fell from 59% to 37% and then 36%. Younger students were more likely to rely on family guidance, while older applicants tended to decide independently. Self-motivation was highest in north and south India; family influence was strongest in the west and central region.
Academic choices were heavily concentrated. Seven in 10 were applying for postgraduate courses, and 75% identified business and management as their main field. Health and medicine was a distant second at 8%. Sciences accounted for 2% and engineering 1%.Google searches led 39% of students to their institution, followed by agents (35%). But Google's lead widened on trust: 56% named it their most trusted source for education information, compared with 20% for college events and 9% for Instagram. AI tools were trusted most by 6% and YouTube by 5%.
Manash Pratim Gohain is a seasoned journalist with over two decades at The Times of India, where he has built a rich body of work spanning education policy, politics, and governance. Renowned for his incisive coverage of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, accreditation reforms, and skilling initiatives, he has also reported on student politics, urban policy, and social movements. His political reportageâboth reflective and news-drivenâadds depth to his writing, bridging policy with public impact. Through his 2,500 articles and related outlets, he has emerged as a trusted voice in national discourse, particularly in linking education reform to broader societal change.

headline: Rahul said students in the country are protesting against a flawed education system.
full_text:
Rahul said students in the country are protesting against a flawed education system.
NEW DELHI: Flooded with queries on Instagram about his stand on the ongoing Jharkhand studentsâ protests, Rahul Gandhi on Thursday said every government should try to change an education system that has âcollapsedâ and is âexpensive and oppressiveâ, be it government of Congress or national government or of Jharkhand.He said students in the country are protesting against a flawed education system.The remark is significant as his party, Congress, is part of the JMM-led governing coalition in Jharkhand. Congressâs state unit and student wing NSUI have already met CM Hemant Soren espousing the cause of students.Rahul replied on Instagram, where he, in a novel youth outreach, opened himself to questions Thursday. Rahul launched a page saying, âStudents, Gen-Z - Iâm here to listen. Ask me anything on Instagram, and Iâll answer as many questions as I can.âThe initiative came a day after Rahul held an interaction with youngsters who were part of the recent NEET agitation in Delhi and other parts of the country, with whom he then held a news conference. The youngsters included Rhiya Ahir whose photo went viral for blocking a Mumbai police van, and Muskaan Sharma, who was the victim of a cop âjabbing a baton in her buttocksâ at Jantar Mantar on July 20.
As Rahul stood next to the protesters at the news conference, Farah Naaz alleged that in police detention, she faced communal barbs, with a cop even calling her âanti-nationalâ. Muskaan said she was assumed to be a Muslim, which makes an Indian âfair gameâ, though she is a Hindu. Nutan Toppo said a pellet gun was fired at her.Rahul alleged the governing party is sending goons to the homes of students and forcing them to apologise, with those apologies being subsequently accepted by PM Modi. â They defended the Constitution and protected the idea of India and its future... They are so young and standing before the media. But PM and home minister (Amit Shah) have no courage to stand before the press,â Rahul said.

headline: Some BJP workers began raising anti-women slogans during 7th anniversary âcelebrationsâ of Article 370âs abrogation
full_text:
Some BJP workers began raising anti-women slogans during 7th anniversary âcelebrationsâ of Article 370âs abrogation
SRINAGAR: BJP distanced itself Thursday from slogans raised by some of its workers during âcelebrationsâ marking the seventh anniversary of Article 370âs abrogation the previous day after backlash over their alleged anti-women content.âThe party firmly believes in respecting the dignity of women and remains committed to Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs vision of women empowerment. BJP has been at the forefront of empowering women and the historic decision to provide 33% reservation for women reflects that commitment,â BJP general secretary (organisation) Ashok Koul said.During Wednesdayâs event in south Kashmirâs Anantnag, the BJP workers altered a well-known slogan of J&Kâs governing National Conference (NC) associated with Article 370. For decades, the NC slogan has been â...Aze hund izat te Faze hund izat 370 (the honour of Azi and Fazi is Article 370)â. Azi and Fazi are names of women in the Valley.The BJP workers modified the slogan to â...Moklev Fazi hund te Azi hund izat (the honour of Fazi and Azi has ended)â. This ran counter to the NC sloganâs emphasis on dignity and respect in its discourse on Article 370.Images of BJP workers dancing to these slogans evoked sharp social media criticism with people decrying them as derogatory to women, forcing the party to issue the clarification.
âSome individuals may have raised slogans based on their personal thinking or emotions, but those slogans do not represent BJPâs official stand or the views of the leaders who led the rally. The party does not endorse any defamatory or derogatory remarks against anyone,â BJP spokesperson Altaf Thakur said.
Rivals were not convinced. âSome insults are not directed at individuals but at an entire society. Azi and Fazi are not merely names. They symbolise the respect, affection and dignity with which Kashmir has always regarded its mothers and sisters. The day they chose to turn those names into a joke, they crossed a line,â NC spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq said.PDP spokesperson Syed Tajamul Islam echoed the sentiment. âIdeological differences are a natural part of public life. But there are certain boundaries that should never be crossed. Fazi and Azi symbolise our mothers. Regardless of political ambition, personal interests, or ideological beliefs, no one should insult, ridicule, or demean what they represent,â Islam said.

headline: Sonam said the government has about one month to address these issues, otherwise they shall be compelled to launch another movement in Ladakh
full_text:
Sonam said the government has about one month to address these issues, otherwise they shall be compelled to launch another movement in Ladakh
SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body functionaries Sonam Wangchuk and Chering Dorjay Lakrook gave Union government a one-month deadline to withdraw criminal cases against around 80 protesters charged during last yearâs agitation for Sixth Schedule status and statehood for Ladakh, compensate families of four demonstrators killed in police firing, and provide relief to those seriously wounded, warning of a fresh movement if their demands remain unmet.âPeople in Ladakh are deeply hurt as four unarmed civilians lost their lives last year and dozens were wounded. We hope government will review what happened and provide compensation to the families of those killed (on Sept 24 last year in Leh) and withdraw all cases against those who were arrested and jailed,â Wangchuk said Thursday in Leh.âWe are giving government about one month to address these issues. If it fails to do so, we will be compelled to launch another movement in Ladakh,â he said, adding Ladakh âshould be governed with trust and respect, not fearâ.Lakrook condemned the recent police action against NEET paper leak protesters at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi but called the crackdown in Leh far harsher. He alleged the response from media, people and political parties to the use of force in Ladakh was far weaker. âEvery citizen deserves the same concern and justice, whether they live in Ladakh or elsewhere in India.â
Lakrook said LAB and Kargil Democratic Alliance had pursued their four-point agenda for years, but talks with Centre had yielded little progress.
âThere has been some progress but there is still no decision on our core demands,â he said, describing Ladakh as a strategically sensitive region whose concerns should not be pushed to the back burner.After the firing on Sept 24, authorities imposed curfew-like restrictions, suspended mobile internet and arrested more than 70 people, including Wangchuk, who was accused of inciting protesters. Wangchuk was held under NSA in Jodhpur jail until Centre revoked his detention in March. Talks resumed after his release and he described the May 22 meeting with Centre as positive after it agreed to discuss Article 371-like protections for Ladakh.

headline: Why Congress MP Manish Tewari wants Parliament to debate the Anti-Defection law
full_text:
Why Congress MP Manish Tewari wants Parliament to debate the Anti-Defection law
Manish Tewari has repeatedly sought a Lok Sabha debate on reforming the anti-defection law during the Monsoon Session. He says defections betray the public mandate even as the wider Opposition remains focused on student protest issues.
While the Opposition has largely focused on student protests and other contentious issues during the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament, senior Congress leader and Chandigarh Lok Sabha MP Manish Tewari has been relentlessly pressing for a discussion on one issue — the Anti-Defection law.
According to official Lok Sabha records, Tewari has submitted 14 adjournment notices so far during the ongoing session. Thirteen of them sought a comprehensive discussion on reforms to the Anti-Defection law. The only exception came on July 28, when he moved an adjournment notice seeking a discussion on the use of pellet guns against unarmed protesters.
An adjournment notice enables a Member of Parliament to seek suspension of the House's scheduled business to discuss a matter of urgent public importance, subject to the Speaker's approval.
Speaking to India Today Digital, Tewari said comprehensive reform of the Anti-Defection law was essential as it lay at the heart of many of the problems confronting India's parliamentary democracy.
Calling defections "a betrayal of the people's trust," Tewari said legislators are elected on the mandate of one political party but later switch allegiance, undermining the electoral verdict.
"It's a betrayal of the people's trust. Legislators win elections on the ticket of one political party and later join another. Today's Parliament is fundamentally at variance with the mandate of the 2024 general election. The current polity and Parliament are increasingly being governed by the whims of those in power," Tewari told India Today Digital.
Asked why he continued to pursue the issue while the Opposition was simultaneously targeting the government over the recent Gen Z protests, the former Union minister said every MP has the right to raise issues they consider important through adjournment notices.
He said repeatedly moving notices on the Anti-Defection law was a conscious attempt to draw the attention of the Speaker and the public to what he described as a growing menace requiring urgent parliamentary debate.
While Tewari has remained firm on his demand for a discussion on the Anti-Defection law, both Leaders of the Opposition — Rahul Gandhi in the Lok Sabha and Mallikarjun Kharge in the Rajya Sabha — have been leading the Opposition's attack on the NDA government over student issues and the alleged police excesses against protesting students on July 20.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday said the Opposition had been demanding for the past 15 days that Union Home Minister Amit Shah make a statement in Parliament on the alleged police excesses against students, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi should apologise to the affected students. He alleged that both leaders had stayed away from Parliament.
Addressing reporters at his residence, Kharge said the Prime Minister and the Home Minister were either ignoring Parliament or were afraid of answering the Opposition's questions in the House.

headline: 57,000 names to be dropped from Bengal housing scheme beneficiaries list after SIR
full_text:
57,000 names to be dropped from Bengal housing scheme beneficiaries list after SIR
At least 57,000 names will be removed from the list of beneficiaries of Awas Yojana because they were already struck off from the electoral rolls during SIR.
At least 57,000 names will be removed from the list of beneficiaries of Awas Yojana (housing scheme) in West Bengal because they were already struck off from the electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR) in 2025, state panchayat and rural development minister Dilip Ghosh said on Thursday.
“Around 9.1 million names have been struck off from the voters’ list during SIR in the state. Of these, around 57,000 people received assistance under the awas yojana. They are not eligible to avail this fund and their names will be struck off,” said Ghosh.
Also Read | West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh targets Mamata Banerjee over Shaheed Diwas: ‘You stand alone’
He was speaking at an administrative programme at the state secretariat where chief minister Suvendu Adhikari handed over cheques and transferred funds directly to the bank accounts of around 1.02 million beneficiaries of the state’s housing scheme.
“Of the three million beneficiaries, who have received the funds, around 12,500 individuals are not eligible for the scheme. They received the funds illegally. Action is being initiated against them and further enquiry is being done. We have already started the process to recover the funds from around 1,000 such beneficiaries,” said Ghosh.
The Centre had stopped releasing funds to the state under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) following allegations related to nepotism and financial irregularities in 2022. The previous TMC government headed by Mamata Banerjee launched a parallel scheme “Banglar Bari” with its own funds in 2024.
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) after coming to power in May this year, conducted a survey to weed out fake names. On Thursday, 1,020,370 beneficiaries were handed over the second instalment of ₹60,000 each. Verification for the remaining beneficiaries was underway, officials said. The name of the scheme was also changed from Banglar Bari to Paschim Banga Awas Yojana.

headline: Violation of natural justice: Dabur goes to court over FSSAI ban over 100% claims
full_text:
Violation of natural justice: Dabur goes to court over FSSAI ban over 100% claims
FSSAI directed Dabur to immediately stop selling food products carrying '100 per cent' claims, terming them ambiguous, unverifiable and potentially misleading to consumers.
Dabur India on Thursday moved the Delhi High Court challenging the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) order barring the sale of several of its food products, including honey, cow ghee and edible oils, over the use of claims such as "100 per cent natural", "100 per cent pure" and "100 per cent organic".
The challenge comes days after the food safety regulator issued a prohibition order against the fast-moving consumer goods company over what it described as misleading "100 per cent" claims on a range of products, including honey, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, cow ghee, coconut water and coconut milk.
Dabur, however, has argued that the FSSAI order was passed in "violation of the principles of natural justice and statutory provisions", claiming that the regulator did not issue a prior show-cause notice or provide the company an opportunity to be heard before imposing the prohibition.
The company has also questioned the FSSAI’s authority to issue such a prohibitory order, contending that the regulator does not have the power to impose such restrictions in the manner adopted in the present case.
The company has further termed the order "non-speaking, ambiguous and without application of mind", also objecting to the FSSAI making its enforcement order public, arguing that the move has painted a "negative image" of the company and its brand.
Dabur's petition in the High Court said expressions such as "100 per cent" are widely used across several categories of food products by other major market players and questioned why it was subjected to the prohibition and public disclosure in these circumstances.
The company has sought judicial intervention against the regulator’s directive and the restrictions imposed on the sale of the products concerned. The petition is scheduled to be heard on Friday by Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma.
WHAT FSSAI DIRECTED
Announcing its action earlier this week, the FSSAI said food products being sold on Dabur’s website were found carrying claims of "100 per cent" purity and such claims violate the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, because they are ambiguous, unverifiable and potentially misleading to consumers.
The regulator said Dabur Himalayan Organic Apple Cider Vinegar and Dabur Organic Honey were also found displaying the Jaivik Bharat logo without a valid FSSAI organic endorsement.
It additionally flagged Dabur Hommade Coconut Milk, which was marketed with the claim "100 per cent purity". According to the FSSAI, such a claim is not permissible for compound foods under the regulations.
NOTICE ISSUED EARLIER: FSSAI
The regulator has said it had earlier issued a notice to Dabur directing it to discontinue misleading "100 per cent" claims, but satisfactory corrective action was not taken by the company.
Following this, the FSSAI directed Dabur to immediately stop the sale of the food products identified in its notice, as well as other food products carrying what it considers misleading claims.
The company was also directed to submit an Action Taken Report (ATR) within 15 days detailing the steps taken to comply with the order.
The prohibition covers products across several categories, including honey, cow ghee, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, coconut water and coconut milk.
The action against Dabur comes amid increased scrutiny by the food safety regulator over advertising, labelling and health-related claims made by food and beverage companies.
In recent months, it has increasingly used its social media platforms to publicly announce enforcement action against food business operators and e-commerce platforms selling products that allegedly violate food safety and advertising regulations.

headline: Farmer accepts woman's friend request on Facebook, ends up losing Rs 6.3 lakh
full_text:
Farmer accepts woman's friend request on Facebook, ends up losing Rs 6.3 lakh
Three people, all from different African countries, have been arrested in connection with the case. As part of the group's elaborate scheme, the woman allegedly told the farmer that she wanted to send him and his family gifts from Germany.
Three Africans, including a woman, have been arrested for allegedly cheating a farmer of Rs 6.31 lakh using social media in Gujarat's Rajkot district. The accused have been identified as Josephine alias Angel from Ghana, and her purported associates, Mgenjeli Imani Dennis from Tanzania and Philip Batista Joseph Valentine from South Sudan.
The complainant in the case had purportedly accepted a friend request on Facebook sent by the woman accused, who later introduced herself as a single mother. As part of the group's elaborate scheme, Josephine allegedly told the farmer she wanted to send him and his family gifts from Germany. She later told him the parcel contained valuables, including 30,000 euros in cash, a gold chain, a laptop, a watch and an iPhone.
Soon afterwards, the man allegedly received calls from a woman posing as a customs officer at the Delhi airport, who demanded customs duty and other charges to supposedly release the parcel. The accused subsequently sought additional payments on various pretexts, including currency conversion, customs clearance and processing fees.
Believing the claims to be genuine, the farmer transferred a total of Rs 6.31 lakh in multiple online transactions from his two bank accounts. However, the promised parcel never arrived. When the accused continued demanding more money, the man realised he had been duped and approached the cyber crime police in Rajkot.
During the investigation, police carried out technical analysis of social media accounts, mobile numbers, WhatsApp chats, bank transactions, IP logs and other digital evidence. The probe traced the alleged cyber fraud operation to Greater Noida in Uttar Pradesh, leading to the arrest of the three accused from Delhi and Noida.
Police said they have initiated the process of freezing 15 bank accounts allegedly used in the fraud. Preliminary investigation also revealed that two of the accused had entered India on student visas, while the third had arrived on a short-term visa. The visas of all three have since expired.
Investigators further said that African nationals allegedly involved in such cyber frauds often remain in India after their visas expire because ongoing court proceedings prevent them from returning to their home countries, enabling them to continue operating similar scams. The investigation into the case is ongoing.

headline: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has arrested four accused persons, including the “mastermind”, who were part of a syndicate that ran a tech-support fraud and extortion racket through call centres and offices across Punjab and Delhi. The gro...
full_text:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has arrested four accused persons, including the “mastermind”, who were part of a syndicate that ran a tech-support fraud and extortion racket through call centres and offices across Punjab and Delhi. The group primarily targeted U.S. nationals, the agency said on Thursday (August 6, 2026).
The CBI raided 10 locations across Punjab and Delhi, including a call centre operated from the premises of the main accused in Mohali in the intervening night of August 5 and 6, and arrested the accused. It seized communication devices, storage drives, cash, and details of cryptocurrency wallets.
Those arrested include Sourabh Rana, the prime accused, and his alleged associates Indermohan Singh, Harneet Singh, and Jappandeep Singh. The agency alleged that they posed as representatives of Microsoft, financial institutions, and law enforcement agencies to cheat victims.
In one case, in 2022, the syndicate allegedly extorted $4.40 lakh from a Florida resident by threatening her that her personal and financial information had been compromised and that illegal material had been planted on her computer. She was coerced into making multiple transactions into a Bitcoin ATM. The funds were routed to a specific wallet address for further transfer to the accounts controlled by the accused.
Another case was reported in 2023, in which a New Jersey resident was misled into believing that unknown entities had gained access to her banking details. She deposited around $1.30 lakh into Bitcoin ATMs.
Explaining the modus operandi, the CBI said the accused sent pop-ups to the computers of prospective targets, displaying bogus warnings about serious technical issues. The pop-ups carried fake Microsoft toll‑free numbers that directly connected victims to fraudulent call centres run by the syndicate. The victims were then persuaded to make payments for repairing their systems.
The syndicate also allegedly extorted money through cryptocurrency ATMs by convincing the victims that they had been implicated in serious crimes such as child pornography. The proceeds were routed through multiple cryptocurrency wallets and later laundered via operators based in Delhi.

headline: Ladakh supports more than 38 mammal species, 340 bird species and 1,800 vascular plant species
full_text:
Ladakh supports more than 38 mammal species, 340 bird species and 1,800 vascular plant species
SRINAGAR: In a bid to prevent illegal off-roading and disturbance to wildlife, Ladakh administration Thursday approved the introduction of Indiaâs first-ever high-altitude wildlife safari on popular snow leopard and bird-watching trails in the Union Territoryâs upper reaches.Ladakh is home to Indiaâs largest snow leopard population â 477 of the countryâs estimated 718 snow leopards. The UT also supports more than 38 mammal species, 340 bird species and 1,800 vascular plant species, which have drawn significant tourist attention over the years. Under this sustainable eco-friendly tourism initiative, visitors will get a rare, guided opportunity to witness the regionâs distinctive flora and fauna, a government spokesperson said.The decision was made in the first governing body meeting of the newly constituted Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature (SHAN) Conservation Society, chaired by Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena, the spokesperson said. Saxena directed the forest department to introduce guided jeep safaris on the lines of popular national parks like Kaziranga, Ranthambore, and others, using specially designed open-back vehicles driven by trained local drivers and guides.
Apart from including areas like Nubra, Zanskar, Sham, Kargil and Drass â known to have sizeable populations of the elusive snow leopard and avian diversity â Saxena told the department to explore possible safari routes across Hemis National Park, Changthang and Karakoram wildlife sanctuaries, the spokesperson said. Govt will appoint 20 local youths and train them in bird-watching, bird identification, and spotting skills.
They will be provided with all necessary equipment.SHAN Society, constituted by Saxena on June 16 this year, seeks to formulate a comprehensive roadmap for community-led wildlife conservation and waste management, and to promote plastic-free tourism, sustainable livelihood generation, and responsible eco-tourism across Ladakh through environmental education and empowerment of local communities.âThese efforts aim at conserving Ladakhâs natural heritage so that future generations inherit an ecosystem that is richer, healthier and more resilient. Our vision is to establish Ladakh as a global example of community-led conservation and responsible high-altitude mountain tourism,â Saxena said.

headline: The deal is made, the buyer has been found, the price has been agreed upon, the documents are in order. Then comes the final step: registration. But for an increasing number of property owners, that is precisely where everything falls apart.
full_text:
The deal is made, the buyer has been found, the price has been agreed upon, the documents are in order. Then comes the final step: registration. But for an increasing number of property owners, that is precisely where everything falls apart.
Many say they only discover that their land has been included in the prohibited list under Section 22A of the Registration Act when they walk into a Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) to complete what they believed would be a routine transaction. One of them is 40-year-old mason Udayagiri Prasad of Narapally in Medchal-Malkajgiri district, near Hyderabad.
Prasad had purchased a 66.8-square-yard residential plot in Survey No. 58 at Kachavanisingaram village in the district several years ago. When his niece’s wedding approached, he decided to sell the property to repay the ₹10 lakh he owed to his elder brother. But when he approached Narapally SRO, officials refused to register the sale, informing him that the land was included in the prohibited list maintained under Section 22A of the Registration Act. “I have all ownership documents but cannot sell my own property. I had to mortgage the property’s title documents to secure a private loan,” he says.
Across Hyderabad and surrounding districts, owners of residential plots, apartments, independent houses and private patta lands say they are facing similar hurdles after discovering that their properties have been brought under the prohibited list. The restriction often comes to light only after a buyer has been identified, a sale agreement signed and the parties approach the SRO to complete the registration.
Mekala Harshavardhan, 28, of Boduppal, ran into a similar problem. His sister and brother-in-law, a defence official posted in Kashmir, had purchased residential plots measuring 200 and 100 square yards in Survey No. 44 of Peerzadiguda village in Medchal-Malkajgiri.
He says the Uppal SRO refused to register the properties after finding that the entire survey number was categorised as Urban Land Ceiling (ULC) land under the prohibited list.
On July 29, the Sub-Registrar wrote to the District Collector seeking clarification on whether plot no.13 (Part) in Survey No. 44 could be registered or whether it was covered under Section 22A(1)(d). Verification of the Prohibition Watch Register reportedly showed that the entire extent of about 1.58 lakh square yards in Survey No. 44 stood notified as ULC land in the name of D. Malla Reddy. The registration process has been kept on hold, pending clarification from the Collector.
The problem extends beyond vacant plots. A resident of Peerzadiguda approached the Medchal-Malkajgiri District Collector after registration of her apartment in Survey No. 43 was refused because the entire survey number had been classified as ULC land. Following her representation, the Uppal SRO advised her to obtain a no objection certificate (NOC) from the Collector’s office before registration could be permitted.
Residents in several parts of the district, including Alwal, say similar issues have affected apartments and independent houses.
What is Section 22A?
Section 22A of the Registration Act was introduced to prevent the illegal registration of government lands, water bodies, forest lands, endowment properties, waqf lands and other protected public assets. It empowers the government to notify lands where registrations are prohibited, preventing fraudulent transfers and safeguarding public property.
Property owners and real estate representatives, however, contend that poor land records and weak coordination between departments have resulted in genuine private lands also being included in the prohibited list.
Officials familiar with the process said district administrations were asked to update records of prohibited lands about three-and-a-half months ago. In several cases, revenue authorities reportedly furnished only survey numbers instead of identifying the exact extent under government ownership. As a result, entire survey numbers were brought under Section 22A, rendering privately owned lands within them non-transferable despite owners possessing registered sale deeds, approved layouts and municipal permissions.
Developers cite a residential layout near Shamirpet police station that received approval from Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority (HMDA) in 2022 but was later included in the prohibited list, forcing the developer to seek denotification.
“Even buyers of plots in HMDA-developed and auctioned layouts are facing similar hardships, as those lands have also been included in the prohibited list,” says R. Srisailam, a realtor.
For affected families, the issue goes far beyond paperwork. Farmers who depend on land as collateral, middle-class families, retirees and NRIs say they are unable to sell or mortgage properties despite holding registered ownership documents. Many owners say the lack of prior intimation has compounded their problems. “There was no notice informing us that our property has been included under Section 22A,” says one property owner. “We came to know only after identifying a buyer, signing agreements and paying advance.”
Applications for NOCs, they say, often remain pending for months, forcing repeated visits to Revenue offices, submission of historical ownership records and considerable expenditure on legal assistance.
Realtors seek review
The Telangana Realtors Association (TRA) has urged the State government to undertake a comprehensive review of the prohibited list.
TRA State president Naragoni Praveen Kumar alleges that legally owned private patta lands had been wrongly included because of administrative lapses and inadequate verification of records. Registrations that were permitted earlier were now being refused in several areas, he says.
The association also alleges that registrations in some newly developed colonies were being withheld because the lands had been classified as waqf properties.
While supporting the government’s efforts to protect public lands from encroachment, it demanded the immediate removal of genuine private lands from the prohibited list, fixation of responsibility for wrongful inclusion, district-level grievance redressal centres, a time-bound mechanism for issuing NOCs, an online application tracking system with SMS and e-mail alerts, and greater accountability among departments responsible for maintaining land records.
The Telangana government introduced the Bhu Bharati portal after widespread complaints over lapses in the Dharani portal launched by the previous Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) government.
However, problems relating to lands classified under Part B of the prohibited list continue, with complaints from both rural and urban areas over the wrongful inclusion of private properties. Over 18 lakh acres of agricultural land are included in Part B, while fresh additions of urban lands continue to expand the list.
The Part-B category, primarily governed by Section 22A of the Registration Act, originates from a 2006 State amendment to the Central Act following the recommendations of the Koneru Ranga Rao Committee on land reforms. It empowers the government to prohibit the sale, gift, transfer or mortgage of specified land parcels through SROs.
However, the government that introduced the amendment did not frame detailed guidelines for identifying prohibited lands, resulting in the present imbroglio. Officials say the absence of clear guidelines, inclusion of patta lands, removal of the ‘enjoyment’ column from registration records and reliance on outdated land records have led to mismatches between official records and the actual extent of land on the ground.
The use of outdated records for categories such as Bhoodan, waqf, ceiling surplus and assigned lands is another reason for the mismatch, experts say. Land laws expert M. Sunil Kumar says Telangana follows a deeds registration system rather than a title registration system, unlike what it is followed in over 90 countries. “Placing lands in the prohibited list does not necessarily reflect the ground reality,” he says, citing Kharij Khata lands that are restored to owners once tax dues are cleared.
Although the Congress government replaced the Telangana Rights in Land and Pattadar Pass Books Act, 2020, with the Telangana Bhu Bharati (Record of Rights) Act, enabling corrections at different levels instead of only through the Chief Commissioner of Land Administration (CCLA), issues relating to prohibited lands remain unresolved. Experts say District Collectors face a conflict of interest as they are tasked with protecting government land while also deciding ownership disputes, which are further complicated by unreliable land records and technical registration errors.
Although lands have periodically been removed from the prohibited list, they reportedly reappear because speaking orders confirming their clearance were never issued. The problem is said to be particularly acute in urban areas, especially Ranga Reddy and Medchal-Malkajgiri districts surrounding the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation limits.
The way forward
The growing number of complaints has revived demands for greater transparency in the preparation of the prohibited list. Experts call for recording the reasons and documentary evidence for including any land under Section 22A and suggest introducing a ‘community audit’ mechanism, enabling residents of villages or wards to verify ownership claims.
Displaying the list of prohibited lands in Gram Panchayat offices and inviting claims and objections, they say, could offer a cost-effective way of resolving disputes.
They have also suggested that the government resolve disputes category-wise to make lands litigation-free in a phased manner. “The government can first clear disputes relating to lands assigned before 1956 and gradually move to subsequent categories,” Sunil Kumar says.
He also stresses the need for a proper adjudication mechanism at different levels so that disputes do not escalate to the office of the Chief Commissioner of Land Administration or the judiciary.
Meanwhile, Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy has reiterated that the government is committed to ensuring that no poor person or genuine landowner suffered because of lands included in the Section 22A prohibited list.
Chairing a high-level review meeting on August 5, the Minister said the government is pursuing the twin objectives of protecting the rights of eligible citizens while safeguarding government lands. He maintained that not even one cent of land had been deliberately added to the Section 22A prohibited list since the Congress government assumed office in December 2023.
The Minister has also directed officials to dispose of all Section 22A applications and complaints within the stipulated time, ensuring that no file remains pending. Every case, he says, should be examined on its merits, based on records and legal provisions, so that eligible landowners receive justice.
Referring to Telangana High Court’s directions, he said all Section 22A disputes should be resolved within the stipulated 45-day period. He also reminded Collectors that they were the final authority to review lands included in the prohibited list and urged them to strike a balance between protecting public rights and safeguarding government interests.
As the government promises time-bound resolution, thousands of property owners continue to wait for a certainty they believed they already had: the right to freely sell, mortgage or transfer land they legally own.

headline: Bengal govt reaches out to Tata Group, seeks to resolve ₹765.78 crore compensation dispute over Singur
full_text:
Bengal govt reaches out to Tata Group, seeks to resolve ₹765.78 crore compensation dispute over Singur
The BJP-led Bengal government initiated talks to set up new industries and resolve a dispute over compensation of ₹765.78 crore that previous govt didn't pay.
The West Bengal government has initiated talks with the Tata Group to set up new industries and resolve a legal dispute over compensation of ₹765.78 crore that the previous government under the Trinamool Congress (TMC) did not pay to Tata Motors for losses suffered in aborting the Nano car project at Singur in 2008 following a two-year agitation by then-opposition leader Mamata Banerjee, officials aware of the matter said.
“Our officers went to Mumbai this week and talked to the Tata Group. Of course, we want them to return to Bengal. Had Mr Ratan Tata been alive I would have touched his feet and requested him to set up an industry here,” industry minister Tapas Roy said.
Also Read | Centre keen on investing to develop tea, textile sector in Bengal: CM Suvendu Adhikari
“Our state is saddled with debts piled up by the former government. The court ordered that a compensation of around ₹766 crore be paid to the Tatas. All these issues are being discussed,” Roy added.
Officials aware of the matter said if the initial talks bear fruit then finance minister Swapan Dasgupta and Roy may visit Mumbai.
Known for multi-crop farming, Hooghly district’s Singur made headlines in 2006 when Tata Motors set its sights on the land to build its ₹1-lakh car, the Nano. The Left Front government acquired 997.11 acres along the NH-2 and handed it over to the company. However, Mamata Banerjee, then in the Opposition called a hunger strike demanding the return of 347 acres of farmland that she alleged was “forcibly” acquired.
Following a two-year agitation by Banerjee and several litigations, the Tatas moved out in October 2008 and shifted the project to Gujarat’s Sanand.
The Tata Group moved the Calcutta high court seeking compensation for the losses and the matter was referred to an arbitration tribunal which directed the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) in October 2023 to pay a compensation of ₹765.78 crore along with 11% annual interest to the Tatas. The state challenged this order at the Supreme Court but its appeal was rejected.
“On May 7, three days after the BJP won the Bengal polls, the Calcutta high court turned down WBIDC’s prayer for an unconditional stay on the arbitration tribunal’s order and directed WBIDC,” a senior state official said. “Efforts are being made to reach an out-of-court settlement with the Tata Group,” he added, asking not to be named.

headline: Zero tolerance for attempts to disrupt Kanwar Yatra: Adityanath
full_text:
Zero tolerance for attempts to disrupt Kanwar Yatra: Adityanath
Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday directed officials to adopt a zero-tolerance approach against anyone attempting to disrupt the ongoing Kanwar Yatra, saying the pilgrimage reflects faith, discipline and social harmony and any attempt to disturb communal harmony or spread rumours must be dealt with firmly.
Adityanath said misinformation should be countered immediately with factual clarification and asserted that lawlessness during religious events would not be tolerated.
He said the Kanwar Yatra had emerged as an example of social harmony at a time when attempts were being made to spread caste-based hatred.
According to an official statement, the ADG, Meerut, informed the chief minister during a review meeting that authorities were receiving full cooperation from neighbouring states, while the Ghaziabad Police Commissioner said around 70,000 Kanwar pilgrims had passed through the district so far and the number was expected to rise over the next two days.
The chief minister directed officials to maintain special vigil in Bareilly in view of the simultaneous Kanwar Yatra and Ala Hazrat Urs.
He welcomed arrangements made by members of the Muslim community to distribute vegetarian food during the Urs and said limiting celebrations out of respect for Kanwar pilgrims was a commendable example of communal harmony and mutual respect.
Reviewing fertiliser availability, Adityanath said there was no shortage of urea, D or other fertilisers in the state but directed district magistrates to ensure transparent distribution, prevent black marketing and distribute fertilisers only after verification of land records. He also ordered enhanced vigilance in districts bordering Nepal.
Expressing concern over recent crimes against women, the chief minister said women's safety remained the government's highest priority and directed officials to strengthen implementation of Mission Shakti.
He ordered increased deployment of women police personnel, intensified patrolling in sensitive areas, strict action against negligent officials and public identification of eve-teasers and snatchers.
Reviewing the flood situation in eight affected districts, including Ballia, Barabanki and Unnao, Adityanath directed officials to ensure there was no shortfall in relief operations and that residents of marooned villages received immediate assistance.
He also ordered urgent measures to prevent erosion of river embankments in Siddharthnagar, Shrawasti, Kushinagar, Muzaffarnagar and Ballia, and directed that families displaced by erosion in Ballia be provided land pattas and houses at the earliest.
The chief minister further directed authorities to ensure that only school vehicles meeting prescribed fitness standards operate and ordered mandatory verification of drivers of school vehicles, taxis and e-rickshaws to enhance passenger and student safety.

headline: Farmers in villages near Sathanur dam protested in front of the Office of the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) near the Old Collectorate Office in Tiruvannamalai on Thursday against the land acquisition for the proposed Nandan Link Canal project, whi...
full_text:
Farmers in villages near Sathanur dam protested in front of the Office of the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) near the Old Collectorate Office in Tiruvannamalai on Thursday against the land acquisition for the proposed Nandan Link Canal project, which will be executed by Water Resources Department (WRD).
Farmers said that the identified land for the multi-crore project covers a large tract of agricultural land in the villages near Sathanur dam. Acquisition of agricultural lands would deprive farmers of their livelihood. “The new canal should not be laid by destroying agricultural lands in the area. We have been cultivating our lands for generations. Where will we go and what alternative work do we know?” asked G. Suresh Babu, a farmer and an organiser of the protest.
Farmers said that identified land owners in the villages were asked to submit objections against land acquisition. Despite submitting objections to the project, residents said that the preliminary works for land acquisition, including survey of the villages and marking of identified lands, are being done by revenue officials.
WRD officials said that around 355 acres of land in 14 villages between Sathanur dam and Samudram village, a distance of 28.95 kms, have been identified for land acquisition for the project. “The aim of the project is to rejuvenate the existing defunct Nandan Canal with surplus rainwater during Northeast monsoon. Water in the Nandan Canal will help to increase groundwater level, thereby expanding the total acres under cultivation in the region,” S. Sakthi Selvam, Assistant Engineer (AE), WRD (Kilpennathur), told The Hindu.
WRD officials said the proposed project consists of construction of main canal and link canal between Sathanur dam and Samudram village near Cheyyar town. The Samudram lake is the confluence of Aliyar and Thurinjal rivers, tributaries of Then Pennaiyar river. The British era Nandan Canal originates near the confluence of these two rivers. The new Link Canal will be connected to Nandal Canal at Samudram lake. Excess rainwater will help rejuvenate the old Nandan Canal back to life.
Divided into two phases, the main Nandan Link canal will be constructed in the first phase. It will cover 12.45 kms between Sathanur dam and Pachal village near Chengam town along the Then Pennaiyar river. It will also help to connect Palar and Cheyyar rivers by discharging excess rainwater into it. The new main canal will be around 12 metres wide and 1.5 metres in depth.
WRD officials said that a new branch Link Canal, covering a distance of 16.5 kms, will be built under the second phase. The new branch canal will vary in its size due to topography. It will be connected to Samudram lake.
The Nandan Canal was once the lifeline of 120 villages in Villupuram and Tiruvannamalai districts. Built in the late 18th century by the British, the canal originates from the Thurinjalaru River in Tiruvannamalai and covers a distance of 10.40 km in Tiruvannamalai district and 25.46 km in Villupuram district.
During its splendour years, the canal discharged water to 36 tanks in the region, helping farmers to irrigate around 1,500 acres and 5,000 acres in Tiruvannamalai and Villupuram district respectively.

headline: Rahul Gandhi reveals his favourite BJP leader: 'Get along with him, he's cool'
full_text:
Rahul Gandhi reveals his favourite BJP leader: 'Get along with him, he's cool'
The Congress leader added that he likes Amarinder Singh because of his expertise in military history.
Congress MP and leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi on Thursday revealed who is his favourite BJP leader in an ‘Ask Me Anything’ session on Instagram. The feature allows an Instagram user to respond to questions through their Instagram stories.
Responding to a question about who his favourite politician is from BJP, Rahul quipped that he gets along well with Captain Amarinder Singh. “Captain Amarinder Singh, definitely. I get along with him. He’s cool.” Rahul was seen saying this in a video posted by the handle of Congress on X.
The Congress leader added that he likes Singh because of his expertise in military history.
“And… he is an expert on military history,” he added, ending the video with, “Hello, Uncle Amarinder.”
Singh is a former soldier, a royal, a military historian and former chief minister of Punjab. He joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 2022 after resigning from the Congress, saying he had been humiliated by the party.
After Congress’s Charanjit Singh Channi became the chief minister, he quit the party and formed a new party, which merged with the BJP later in 2022.
Singh said he still felt hurt by the manner in which he was removed as chief minister when he was with the Congress.
“The question of joining Congress does not arise,” he said in an interview with PTI Videos last year.
However, he said he would always help Congress leader Sonia Gandhi if she asked, although “not politically”.
Gandhi's 'Ask Me Anything' on Instagram
Gandhi on Thursday launched an "Ask Me Anything" session on Instagram, in his fresh outreach to the GenZ. He answered several questions, including one on the student protest in Jharkhand, India’s education system and others.
Posting a link to his Instagram initiative on X, Gandhi said, “Students, Gen-Z -- I'm here to listen. Ask me anything on Instagram, and I'll answer as many questions as I can.”
Responding to a question on what his favourite meme from the Jantar Mantar protest was, Gandhi said, “I think the videos that came out of the PM's house at midnight. Those were the best. Showing a new panicked Prime Minister.”
On Jharkhand protests, Gandhi said, “The student protests that are happening in the country are against the education system. I have stated it clearly in Kota and Dehradun, and will say it in Allahabad, that our education system has collapsed; it is unaffordable and oppressive.”
“Every government, be it the central government, Congress government or Jharkhand government, should listen to what students are saying and take action to change the education system,” he said.
The protest in Jharkhand, which began on July 25 under the banner of the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, entered its 14th day on Friday.
In another question, Gandhi was asked about his message to young women fighting for their right to study, to which he said, "India's women are our strength, our biggest asset and frankly I do not appreciate the way women are treated in society, the way our education system treats our women and the way our corporate system treats our women. Women deserve equal space in every sphere of life. In fact I believe they deserve more than equal space in every sphere of life."
Asked whether the education system in India is producing enough thinkers, Gandhi said the education system is busy destroying thinkers.
"The USP of our education system now, especially since the RSS has captured it, is how not to make young Indian people think for themselves," he said.
Gandhi's batman response
On a lighter note, one participant asked Gandhi if he was Batman. Gandhi replied, "Let's just say that no one has ever seen me and Batman in the same room together!"
The initiative comes a day after Gandhi met a group of students who had staged protests last month demanding the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak.
In recent weeks, Instagram has become an increasingly important platform for political outreach, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi leading a coordinated push to engage Gen Z voters.

Foreign Ministry makes Snapchat debut amid PM Modi's Gen Z push
The development came as Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged his cabinet colleagues to bolster their social media presence by engaging with young minds through the use of interactive content like reels.
The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Thursday launched its official Snapchat account, becoming one of the first ministries to expand its footprint on the digital platform that is dominated by the Gen Z population.
The development came as Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged his cabinet colleagues to bolster their social media presence by engaging with young minds through the use of interactive content like reels.
Briefing on the latest development, Randhir Jaiswal, the spokesperson for the MEA, posted a video on X. “You followed us on X, on Instagram, and on LinkedIn. Follow us on Snapchat to hear more about what the Ministry of External Affairs does. Both in India and through our missions and posts abroad,” Jaiswal was heard saying.
He also shared the video with the caption, “We're now on Snapchat! Add us and stay connected for exclusive stories, updates, engaging content and more. Let's Snap!”
Nearly two weeks ago, Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked several other ministers to use Instagram actively as the platform is home to a vast section of Indian youth. He also asked his colleagues to post reels and engage with the young minds through other interactive content.
"Young audiences are on Instagram. This is a large section of citizens that all of us need to stay connected with," the Prime Minister told ministers, according to sources close to the development.
PM Modi further said that simply posting updates about government initiatives was not enough. Instead, they should use Instagram to interact directly with young people and communicate in a more engaging and accessible manner.
The instructions came in the wake of a month-long protest by the Cockroach Janta Party over the paper leak of the NEET examination. The protest, which saw massive participation of the youth, led to the resignation of Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

The Gen Z in India were being "created" as someone who rebelled, while the Gen Z in Europe, Japan and America wanted to listen to the music of 1970s and 80s and read the books of 1960s, Editor of Thuglak and chairman of Vivekananda International Foundation S. Gurumurthy said on Thursday.
Delivering the Dr. (Mrs.) YGP Centenary Year Memorial Lecture 'Indian Civilisation Past Glory or Future Guide' organised by by Padma Seshadri Bala Bhavan Group of Schools in Kamarajar Arangam on Anna Salai in Chennai, Mr. Gurumurthy referred to a study of Gen Z abroad.
"But, Gen Z is being created in India, as someone who rebels; rebels against the system, rebels against the society, rebels against parents, rebels against tradition, rebels against religion. This is how a new Gen Z is being created. Gen Z is being told that you are not a Gen Z, if you don't do it. This is a very peculiar, consumerist approach of western communication experts."
Mr. Gurumurthy, however, also pointed out that many young people in India went to temples and visited Kumbh Mela in large numbers and they included software engineers, chartered accountants, teachers, businessmen, company executives, among others. He further noted that "there is a civilizational connect" in each of these activities.
Referring to the study that compared Indian savings with that of a few other countries, he said: "Unlike in the west, in India, people save for their grandchildren," and further noted that that thought was "not there in countries which we have iconized or made examples of."
He said, "Civilization means continuity. Civilization means the memory of the people."
Mr. Gurumurthy said that recalling the past was a matter of pride and also was a matter of self confidence. The country's civilization is still guiding it, he said. "The entire answer to how the universe originated, how climate changes are taking place and how human beings are affected by the things happening in the universe - all these secrets will be unraveled only by studying the Indian civilization."
Earlier in the day, veteran actor A.R. Srinivasan, Founder of Ramcons K. Ramanujam and ophthalmologist Mohan Rajan, Chairman and Medical Director of Rajan Eye Care Hospital, were honoured on the occasion.
Dean, Director and Correspondent of the PSBB Group of Schools Sheela Rajendra said that under late Mrs. YGP's leadership, PSBB grew to be a confluence of Indian tradition and progressive thinking, combined with academic excellence where learning extended beyond textbooks to develop character, conviction and compassion.

headline: Continuing its tradition of showcasing the State’s rich heritage through giant kites, the Tamil Nadu International Kite Festival (TNIKF) will unveil a Poikkal Kuthirai themed kite this year.
full_text:
Continuing its tradition of showcasing the State’s rich heritage through giant kites, the Tamil Nadu International Kite Festival (TNIKF) will unveil a Poikkal Kuthirai themed kite this year.
Poikkal Kuthirai (dummy horse dance) is a traditional folk dance where performers wear a lightweight, decorated dummy horse frame around their waist, creating the illusion of riding a horse while dancing. This dance is quite popular at village festivals and cultural events in Tamil Nadu.
According to details shared by Tamil Nadu’s Director of Tourism, V.P. Jeyaseelan, this year there are participants from Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam. They will present an aerial display featuring over 200 giant show kites.
“The Department of Tourism envisions the TNIKF as a flagship tourism event that will further strengthen Tamil Nadu’s position on the global tourism map. The long term objective is to develop this into one of the world’s leading international kite festivals by attracting participants from more than 30 countries, filling the skies with over 1,000 kites, and introducing an International Aerobatic Kite Flying Championship,” he said.
“We want to promote Tamil Nadu’s cultural icons through the kite festival. That is why we began with designs inspired by the Jallikattu bull and the Thanjavur doll, which are vibrant and visually appealing. This year we are bringing Poikkal Kuthirai kite. Next year, we plan to introduce a kite inspired by the Nilgiri tahr, Tamil Nadu’s State animal,” said Benedict Savio, founder and curator of the Tamil Nadu International Kite Festival and Director of Global Media Box. It takes two months to make a kite.
The event is being organised by the Tamil Nadu Tourism Department in collaboration with Global Media Box. What began as a festival that attracted around 5,000 visitors has now grown into one that draws more than 40,000 people. To further boost footfall, entry to this year’s festival will be free for the public. The event will be held from August 14 to 16.
Through this event, the Tourism Department aims to increase international tourist arrivals, encourage domestic travel during the Independence Day holiday, extend visitor stays along Tamil Nadu’s coastline, generate economic opportunities for local businesses and communities, and establish Tamil Nadu as a preferred destination for international cultural and tourism events.

The Directorate of Enforcement (ED), Patna Zonal Office, has conducted search operations on Thursday (August 6, 2026) at 5 locations in Munger District, Bihar, under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, in connection with investment fraud committed by M/s Jollywood Music Industries Pvt. Ltd. and M/s DLMS Jollywood Music Pvt. Ltd.
As per ED, these entities are controlled by a family of Munger (Bihar), headed by Jitendra Kumar Rajeev and his associates.
In a press statement, ED stated that the scam enticed individuals with promises of a “digital job” and doubling their investment.
“The potential investors were lured that by investing ₹2,56,500 and watching 4800 audio/videos on the company’s website per month, they would earn ₹15,000 monthly, with promises of additional bonuses for more engagement. The company also offered additional money for recruiting new investors, even promised bikes and cars to those who brought in many people,” ED said in the press note.
The federal agency further stated, “After collecting investments, the software engineer of the company intentionally slowed down the website. This made it technically impossible for users to complete the required tasks of watching 4800 audio/videos per month. This deliberate manipulation prevented investors from meeting the conditions needed to receive payouts. The cumulative investment in the scheme amounted to around ₹11.67 Crore. Investors were asked to deposit “security money” by investing in one of two main slabs offered for investment.”
ED initiated an investigation based on FIR registered under various sections of BNS, 2023 against Jitendra Kumar Rajeev, Dheeraj Kumar and others, who were found to have enticed individuals with promises of a “digital job” and doubling their investment in Jamalpur, Munger and nearby regions.
Accordingly, ED Patna took up the investigation in the matter in the year 2025. During the investigation, it was gathered that the investments grabbed by the accused were diverted and used for the acquisition of various immovable properties. Accordingly, search operations have been conducted in the residential premises of the Directors, technical/software experts, singers and others, who lured poor investors for high returns and grabbed their investments.
During the search operations, various incriminating documents about immovable property, bank account details, agreements, investment details, list of investors, etc were recovered and seized, which are being scrutinised to proceed further under the provisions of PMLA, 2002. Further investigation is in progress.
