headline: ‘Ready to face insults’: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay amid face-off with Udhayanidhi over Cauvery dispute
full_text:
‘Ready to face insults’: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay amid face-off with Udhayanidhi over Cauvery dispute
CM Vijay said he was "prepared to bear insults" if it meant opening talks on the Cauvery issue in the interest of the people of Tamil Nadu.
Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay said on Friday that he was the one who suggested holding discussions with neighbouring Karnataka over the Cauvery issue, hoping the move could lead to a positive outcome.
Addressing the Tamil Nadu assembly, Vijay said he was "prepared to bear insults" if it meant opening talks on the Cauvery issue in the interest of the people of Tamil Nadu.
ALSO READ | Cauvery crisis sparks farmers’ protest in Tamil Nadu
CM Vijay's big remark on Cauvery issue
The chief minister told the assembly that he was willing to face “insults” if it helped initiate dialogue with Karnataka over the Cauvery issue for the benefit of the people of Tamil Nadu.
Responding to the leader of the opposition and DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin, who raised the Cauvery issue, Vijay recalled how Tamil Nadu's approach to the dispute had evolved since 1969, moving from dialogue to pursuing legal remedies.
He said that, in the present situation, his government remained committed to resolving the Cauvery issue through legal channels and that its position had not changed.
However, he also said he had planned to visit Karnataka to discuss the Cauvery issue. "I thought, what if talks are held with the neighbouring state, as even nations that are sworn enemies hold dialogue to solve issues," he said.
Vijay vs Udhayanidhi in assembly
During the assembly proceedings, Udhayanidhi Stalin demanded that the government convene an all-party meeting regarding Karnataka's proposal to build the Mekedatu Dam on the Cauvery River.
"In Tamil Nadu, all political parties are urging the government to convene an all-party meeting on the Mekedatu Dam issue. Everyone is asking why the Tamil Nadu government is avoiding convening an all-party meeting on this matter," Stalin said in the Assembly.
Vijay, however, said there was "no need" for such a meeting and assured the assembly that his government remained fully committed to protecting the state's interests.
He criticised the Opposition and said the TVK-led government would "not compromise on the rights regarding the Cauvery water issue".
The Cauvery issue, explained
The Cauvery dispute is a decades-old disagreement over sharing river water between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The conflict intensifies in years when water availability is low, with both states seeking a larger share.
The issue has again come into focus over Karnataka's proposed Mekedatu balancing reservoir project, which has remained a major point of disagreement between the two states.
Tamil Nadu has consistently opposed the project, saying it could reduce the flow of water reaching the downstream areas.
Meanwhile, Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar described the proposed Mekedatu balancing reservoir as a long-term solution to the Cauvery dispute. He also said that Tamil Nadu would receive most of the project's benefits.

headline: Kerala: 469 fishermen died, 160 went missing over 11 years: Govt
full_text:
Kerala: 469 fishermen died, 160 went missing over 11 years: Govt
Thiruvananthapuram, A total of 469 fishermen died and 160 others went missing off the Kerala coast over the last 11 years, according to figures released by the state Fisheries Minister's office on Friday, as protests erupted among the coastal community over the recent disappearance of two fishers.
As per the data released by the office of minister V E Abdul Gafoor, 23,000 patrolling operations and 5,072 sea rescue missions have been conducted during the period from 2015-16 to 2025-26 under the Kerala Marine Fisheries Regulation enforcement.
As many as 47,773 fishermen were rescued over the 11 years.
The highest number of fishermen deaths was reported in 2017-18 at 79, followed by 55 in 2025-26 and 54 in 2023-24.
Further, the highest number of fishermen reported missing in a single year was 29 in 2017-18, while 26 fishermen each went missing in 2016-17 and 2021-22, the figures showed.
The latest data for 2025-26 showed that 2,107 patrolling operations and 560 sea rescue missions were carried out, resulting in 6,556 fishermen being rescued.
During the year, 55 fishermen died and three were reported missing, according to the figures released by the minister's office.
The Fisheries minister's office released the figures at a time when protests erupted among the coastal community over the recent missing of two fishermen, including a 26 year-old man in the state.
The Coastal Police on Friday intensified the search for the man who went missing after a fishing boat capsized near Puthenthura here on July 31, officials said.
Officials at the Neendakara Coastal Police Station said additional boats and personnel have been deployed to search for Gautam Krishna of Puthenthura here. Gautam's father, Radhakrishnan , and grandfather, Rajeevan , who were also on the fishing boat, died in the mishap.
The Vizhinjam Coastal Police are continuing the search for John of Pulluvila, who went missing in a separate boat mishap off the Thiruvananthapuram coast on July 31.
John's family recently staged a protest outside the Vizhinjam Coastal Police Station, alleging that the search operation was not being carried out effectively.

headline: NHRC sends notice to MP govt over assault on Dalit student by teacher

NHRC sends notice to MP govt over assault on Dalit student by teacher
New Delhi, The NHRC on Thursday said it has sent notices to Madhya Pradesh government and police authorities over reports that a class 4 student was allegedly assaulted and subjected to "casteist slurs" by a teacher at a government-run primary school in a village in Shivpuri district.
The National Human Rights Commission observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights.
The rights panel said it has taken suo motu cognisance of a media report about the incident that took place in Ukawal village on July 28.
Reportedly, the teacher was enraged seeing the boy from a Dalit community drinking water from his bottle, therefore, it has issued notices to the state chief secretary and Shivpuri's superintendent of police, seeking a detailed report within two weeks, it said.
The report is expected to include the status of the statutory relief to the victim, it added. According to the media report carried on August 1, the boy narrated the incident to his parents, following which the matter was reported to the police.
In a separate statement, the NHRC said it has taken suo motu cognisance of a media report that a 12-year-old girl died due to jaundice caused allegedly by consumption of contaminated drinking water in Shahzadpur in Ambala district of Haryana.
Several other children have also been diagnosed with jaundice in the locality. The residents have alleged that the drinking water being supplied through a public tap in the area is "contaminated," it said.
Accordingly, it said it has issued a notice to Haryana's chief secretary, seeking a detailed report on it in two weeks. It is expected to include the health status of the victim children undergoing treatment, as well as steps being taken by the administration to address the issue, it said.
According to the media report carried on August 3, the girl was initially treated for jaundice at a local hospital. As her health condition deteriorated, she was referred to PGIMER, Chandigarh, where she succumbed.

headline: SC said in court monitored investigations, sanctions for prosecution should be granted promptly
full_text:
SC said in court monitored investigations, sanctions for prosecution should be granted promptly
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has put a spoke in efforts of defaulting realtors to escape CBI probe by settling with a few homebuyers. The court said these builders would continue to be investigated for cheating homebuyers and siphoning off their deposits till the last of the flat purchasers get their property or refund.Many homebuyers had become parties to petitions filed by groups of homebuyers pleading similar cause â enormous delay in project completion by builders who have already received money through banks under subvention and the banks insisting on repayment in disregard of the fact that the flats are yet to be delivered.
Many bank officials found to have colluded with realtors, Supreme Court told
Advocate Pranav Sachdeva told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the court may allow those homebuyers, with whom defaulting builders has settled, to withdraw from petition and continue proceedings for the remaining homebuyers left high and dry by builders.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for CBI, informed that the agency had completed probe in 18 of 50 cases in which CBI registered FIRs on SCâs orders. A total of 17 chargesheets and a closure report have been filed before competent courts.She said the chargesheets name several bank officials who were found to have colluded with builders. The agency has invoked provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act against them and CBI has sought sanction to prosecute the officials from State Bank of India, Bank of India, Uco Bank, HDFC and ICICI.
SC said in court monitored investigations, sanctions for prosecution should be granted promptly and directed these banks to give necessary permissions within two weeks for prosecution of the accused bank officials. âFailure to accord sanction within two weeks would require banks to submit explanations to the court,â it said and asked CBI to share documents on money trail to ED for initiation of inquiry under PMLA.On some complaints regarding alleged defaulting builders in other states, across states, the bench directed the CBI to conduct a thorough investigation into the allegations of misrepresentation and other irregularities by entities such as Ozone group in Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu; Vivansaa in Bengaluru; Rudra Buildwell Pvt Ltd in Greater Noida, and Omaxe group in Chandigarh. A separate status report in respect of investigations into these builders and related banking institutions shall be submitted to the court.
The main allegation, as crystallized by amicus Rajiv Jain, against these builders is that they donât have ownership title over the land and have partnered leaseholders to construct housing projects. However, they advertised as if they owned the land, entered into agreements with homebuyers and financial institutions without the lessee being a part thereof and remained unaccountable for delay and default.Given the expanding workload, Bhati informed SC that CBI had sought additional hands from states for expediting the investigations but none of the states have responded to the CBI directorâs request. The bench directed the DGPs of UP, TN, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Punjab to send on deputation required number of personnel, as requested by CBI, within 10 days.

headline: Days after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) swept the West Bengal Assembly poll in 2026, winning 207 of the 293 seats, West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya made a bold political claim. “Our doors are closed for Trinamool. There will be no ‘Tr...
full_text:
Days after the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) swept the West Bengal Assembly poll in 2026, winning 207 of the 293 seats, West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya made a bold political claim. “Our doors are closed for Trinamool. There will be no ‘Trinamoolification’ of the BJP,” Mr. Bhattacharya had said. The 62-year-old leader, who had been a foot soldier of the party when its vote share was in single digits in West Bengal was among the first to use the phrase, ‘Trinamoolification of the BJP’.
He didn’t know then that on the afternoon of July 9, he would be handing out lotus-insignia party flags to three former Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs at the BJP office in Kolkata’s Salt Lake area. The three MPs were Sukhendu Sekhar Ray, Sushmita Dev, and Prakash Chik Baraik. They had been nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the Trinamool Congress, and had resigned after the party suffered an electoral setback in the Assembly poll. When in the Trinamool, they had publicly criticised the BJP.
Within hours of Mr. Bhattacharya welcoming the Trinamool leaders into the BJP fold, the party announced that the former Trinamool MPs were to be renominated to the Upper House with the support of newly elected BJP legislators. Mr. Bhattacharya tried to defend opening doors for the Trinamool leaders by saying that the decision was in national interest.
“Syama Prasad Mookerjee has taught us that the party is bigger than an individual, and the nation is bigger than the party,” he said, trying hard to say that inducting the three leaders into the party was an “exception”.
The Bengal BJP president who had spoken about the party’s doors being closed for Trinamool members, is now saying that those in the Trinamool who could not raise their voices in the party are now knocking on BJP doors and the party may consider opening its doors at an opportune moment.
Feeling the heat of the Trinamoolification
A month after this incident, Mr. Bhattacharya admits that the anger among the BJP rank and file was so much that those supporters who were singing his praises during the election are putting a garland of shoes around his photograph. “Usually the garland is made of old shoes, but I saw that the shoes were all new,” the BJP leader quipped. Several BJP leaders, such as State Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta, said they found it difficult to participate in the flag handing-over event.
To many, the Trinamoolification of the BJP started even before the party won the 2026 Assembly poll. Former West Bengal BJP president Dilip Ghosh, now a prominent Minister in the West Bengal government, took a swipe at Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari by saying that it was not new for Trinamool leaders to join the BJP. “Where is it written in the BJP that people from other parties cannot join. Our Chief Minister is also a former Trinamool (leader),” Mr. Ghosh said.
Mr. Ghosh’s reference to Mr. Adhikari points to the unease in BJP’s rank and file. Mr. Adhikari, once a key Trinamool leader and Minister in Mamata Banerjee’s government, defected to the BJP in December 2020. Mr. Adhikari, who defeated Mamata Banerjee twice at Nandigram in 2021 and Bhabanipur in 2026, was chosen to lead the BJP government in West Bengal, five years after joining the party.
Good TMC vs not-so-good TMC
After the defeat in the West Bengal Assembly poll in 2026, the Trinamool Congress has been torn apart by rebellion and desertions. The majority of Lok Sabha MPs and party MLAs decided to part ways with party chairperson Mamata Banerjee.
Despite being the beneficiaries of the Trinamool Congress’s politics, these MPs and MLAs have blamed the party chairperson for favouring her nephew Abhishek Banerjee and allowing corruption and misrule to persist.
Of the 28 Lok Sabha MPs of the Trinamool Congress, 20 have merged with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), and have become a part of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA).
Of the 80 MLAs of the Trinamool Congress who were elected to the 18th West Bengal Legislative Assembly, 65 legislators decided to support the claim of Ritabrata Banerjee as the Leader of the Opposition, against the writ of Mamata Banerjee. One of the reasons behind the rebellion of both the MPs and MLAs of the Trinamool Congress is the opportunity to cosy up to the BJP, the party in power both at the Centre and in the State.
The BJP leadership in West Bengal, which is perceived as being soft on the rebel MPs and MLAs, has come out with a theory of “bhalo (good) Trinamool”. The Lok Sabha MPs, who have decided to join the NDA, have allegedly been told that after delimitation, when the seats increase, so will their chances of returning to Parliament in 2029.
On August 4, Chief Minister Adhikari met the NCPI MPs in Delhi. He was joined by Union Minister Bhupender Yadav, who was election-in-charge of West Bengal, and BJP MP Nishikant Dubey. If the photograph of Samik Bhattacharya handing over party flags to the three Rajya Sabha MPs created discomfort in the BJP’s rank and file, the Chief Minister’s photograph with the NCPI MPs was reason for heartburn.
The “good Trinamool” is the rebel camp led by Leader of the Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee. Mr. Banerjee, who was a Communist Party of India (Marxist) nominee to Rajya Sabha, joined the Trinamool Congress in 2020 after the CPI(M) expelled him. The Trinamool Congress re-nominated him to Rajya Sabha for a second term in 2024. In 2026, he resigned from the Upper House to contest the Assembly poll from Uluberia Purba.
The rebel MLAs led by his camp are claiming to be the “original Trinamool” and have sought the party’s symbol from the Election Commission and laid claim to hundreds of crores of party funds.
After the change of regime, hundreds of local-level Trinamool Congress workers have been arrested by the police on charges of corruption, extortion, and electoral violence. Many were attacked with eggs when they were being taken into custody or being produced before courts. However, the MPs and MLAs of the “good Trinamool” have not faced police action after warming up to the BJP.
Among the handful of loyalists left by Mamata Banerjee’s side is Beleghata MLA Kunal Ghosh. After an under-construction warehouse collapsed in Kolkata’s Taratala area on June 24 burying 16 workers, Chief Minister Adhikari blamed it on the former Trinamool Congress regime.
Mr. Adhikari held up a document in the West Bengal Legislative Assembly with the signature of former mayor of Kolkata Municipal Corporation Firhad Hakim, and said no one would be spared. Ghosh dared the Chief Minister to act against Hakim to prove that the State government was serious about taking action against those responsible for the deaths. Hakim, who was one of the key Ministers during Mamata Banerjee’s regime, joined the Ritabrata Banerjee camp, and despite the Chief Minister blaming him for the tragedy, the only high-profile arrest was his former personal assistant.
The reverse ‘egg therapy’
With the majority of the Trinamool leaders now part of the “good Trinamool” camp, it is Mamata Banerjee and a handful of her loyalists who are being blamed by the BJP for they say was “misrule and corruption” over the past 15 years. The BJP government in West Bengal is yet to complete 100 days. It is already faced with something it had accused the Trinamool Congress leadership of over the past several years: extortion and political corruption.
In the past three months several businesses have alleged that BJP leaders have demanded money from them and they have had to reach out to the police seeking protection.
Sources in the BJP said that the party has suspended 22 functionaries, including several mandal presidents, over allegations of extortion and indiscipline.
Senior leaders of the BJP, including party president are warning its workers against extortion. While former State BJP president and Minister Dilip Ghosh said that many leaders are becoming addicted to this “honey of extortion”, the current State BJP chief has warned party members to mend their ways.
“The unwarranted egg therapy we see now (referring to Trinamool leaders being attacked with eggs) can turn on its head and start falling on the other side as well. Everyone, including those in my party, must understand that. Those ‘Sanatanis’ who have suddenly found a place in our party and are harbouring aspirations for influence and advantage must also remain careful because the trajectory of those eggs can change in no time,” Bhattacharya said.
It is the BJP workers in the districts who are most upset with Trinamool leaders warming up to the BJP, but only a few have mustered the courage to speak about it publicly. Nikhil Ranjan Dey, a former BJP MLA from Cooch Behar, came out in public against the nomination of the three former Trinamool Congress MPs to Rajya Sabha by his party.
“We do not know what our central leadership is thinking. They want to increase numbers in Parliament. But why will (former) Trinamool leaders be nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the BJP? Are there not enough qualified and educated people in the BJP?” the former MLA said.
Mr. Dey said that several BJP workers have suffered at the hands of the Trinamool Congress and are still languishing behind the bars after being booked under what he claims are false charges during the Trinamool Congress regime.
In fact, former Trinamool leaders had once even allegedly called for violence against BJP members. One such example is of former Trinamool Congress MP and actor Nushrat Jahan, who represented the Jadavpur Lok Sabha seat from 2019 to 2024.
She was photographed with BJP leaders at an event to honour exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasrin. The photo went viral and was criticised by several right-wing online portals.
The portals highlighted how, before the election, the actor-turned-politician had been heard telling the electorate to beat up BJP leaders with bamboo sticks if they came seeking votes.
Personal versus the political
Sudip Bandyopadhay is an MP from the Kolkata North Lok Sabha seat. After parting ways with Mamata Banerjee, he is the senior-most MP of the NCPI, and is now holding meetings with the BJP leadership in the national capital.
While Mr. Bandyopadhay is meeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Adhikari, BJP’s Tapas Roy, now Minister of Industries and Commerce in the West Bengal government, is fuming. “I will never have anything to do with him. I hate him, because of what he did to me,” Mr. Roy said.
The Manicktala MLA left the Trinamool Congress and joined the BJP in 2024. That year, he lost the Lok Sabha polls to Mr. Bandyopadhay. Mr. Roy has publicly said that Mr. Bandyopadhay was the reason he had to quit the Trinamool Congress, and join the BJP. He claims that Mr. Bandyopadhay was behind a raid at his residence when he was with the Trinamool, a charge Mr. Bandyopadhay has vehemently denied.
The only thing that is keeping the 70-year-old BJP leader happy: “It is very comforting to see the Trinamool Congress crumbling.”

headline: Passenger vehicle retail sales increased 19% year-on-year to 4.1 lakh units, crossing the four-lakh mark for the first time in July
full_text:
Passenger vehicle retail sales increased 19% year-on-year to 4.1 lakh units, crossing the four-lakh mark for the first time in July
NEW DELHI: Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles are on the verge of overtaking petrol-powered models in India, with CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles accounting for 40.6% of passenger vehicle retail sales in July, just behind petrolâs 41.7%, according to data released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) Thursday. The gap has narrowed sharply from 13.2 percentage points a year ago to just over a percentage point, reflecting a rapid shift in buyer preferences.The trend came as Indiaâs automobile retail market recorded its strongest-ever July performance, with overall registrations rising 25.8% year-on-year to a record 25.9 lakh units. For the first time, all six vehicle categories â two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers, tractors and wheeled construction equipment â posted their highest-ever July retail volumes, underscoring broad-based demand across the industry.
Passenger vehicle retail sales increased 19% year-on-year to 4.1 lakh units, crossing the four-lakh mark for the first time in July. Within the segment, CNG vehicles accounted for 24.6% of sales, hybrids for 8% and electric vehicles for 7.9%. While hybrid vehicles continue to use petrol as their primary fuel source, automakers classify them as alternative-fuel vehicles because they combine an internal combustion engine with an electric powertrain to improve efficiency and reduce emissions.
Petrolâs share, meanwhile, declined to 41.6% from 47.6% a year earlier. FADA said fresh model launches, affordability gains following GST changes and consumersâ increasing focus on lower running costs supported demand for alternative powertrains. The dealersâ body also noted that uncertainty surrounding the transition to E20 fuel appears to have nudged some buyers towards CNG, hybrid and EVs.
The transition was equally evident in the two-wheeler market. Electric two-wheelers accounted for a record 11.2% of retail sales in July, up from 7.7% a year earlier.Overall EV retail registrations across all vehicle segments climbed to an all-time high of 3.28 lakh units during the month, taking EV penetration to about 12.7% of total vehicle retail sales from 9.6% a year ago. Maruti Suzuki retained its lead in the PV market in July, retailing over 1.6 lakh units.

headline: As per figures shared by home ministry last month, 2024-25 witnessed 16,200 NGOs receiving foreign contributions worth Rs 22,963 crore
full_text:
As per figures shared by home ministry last month, 2024-25 witnessed 16,200 NGOs receiving foreign contributions worth Rs 22,963 crore
NEW DELHI: Notwithstanding the progressive tightening of laws governing foreign contributions under Modi govt, their inflow has grown even though the total number of NGOs registered under Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2020, has declined.As per figures shared by home ministry last month, 2024-25 witnessed 16,200 NGOs receiving foreign contributions worth Rs 22,963 crore. During the three years from 2019-20 to 2021-22, Rs 55,741 crore was received in foreign funding by 13,250 NGOs/associations through FCRA route, as per data cited by the ministry in Parliament in Dec 2023. This translates to an average of Rs 18,580 crore per year.As reported earlier by TOI, barely 28% of NGOs and associations ever registered under FCRA are currently active, with licences of the other 72% either deemed cancelled or deemed expired. As of Aug 6, 2026, only 14,434 NGOs were active. FCRA registration of 22,496 NGOs has been cancelled so far, mostly after 2015 when nearly 10,000 NGOs lost their licences.In a recent statement, the ministry had addressed the criticism directed against the FCRA bill, particularly by Christian organisations. It underlined that "FCRA-registered associations are a small fraction of all NGOs operating in India. "The active FCRA database stands at 14,500 against several lakh registered NGOs," it said while asserting the proposed amendments target a specific, foreign-funded channel, "not civil society at large".
The ministry also tried to allay fears that the proposed amendments would give govt unbridled powers to seize an NGO's assets, clarifying the designated authority shall manage only assets created from the foreign contributions and only once the organisation's FCRA registration has lawfully ceased."Vesting is initially provisional, with full restoration if registration is renewed, and places of worship retain their religious character by law in all cases," it clarified and added that the designated authority's orders would not be final but subject to appeal before the court of the district judge.As regards fears that the amendments specifically target a particular religion or community, the ministry clarified that it applies uniformly to all organisations regardless of religion, community or ideology.

headline: Facing public outcry, the BJP on Thursday (August 6, 2025) distanced itself from the slogans, which allegedly berated women of Kashmir, raised during a celebratory rally held in south Kashmir’s Anantnag on the seventh anniversary of abrogation of Art...

Facing public outcry, the BJP on Thursday (August 6, 2025) distanced itself from the slogans, which allegedly berated women of Kashmir, raised during a celebratory rally held in south Kashmir’s Anantnag on the seventh anniversary of abrogation of Article 370 on August 5.

“The party has always upheld the dignity and honour of women and that the 33% reservation for women reflects its commitment to women’s empowerment. The BJP remains committed to political decorum, issue-based politics and strengthening the participation of women in public life,” said Mr. Thakur.
He said the party’s policies and public conduct are guided by the principles of respect, democracy and constitutional values.
Ruling National Conference said the apology tendered by the BJP spokesman “was not enough”. “Aazi and Fazi are not just names; they are our mothers, our sisters, our identity. Mocking them was an insult to every Kashmiri and to our culture. Leader of Opposition Sunil Sharma should tender a public apology,” said NC leader and legislator Tanvir Sadiq.

headline: The number of cases reported under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act in Kerala continues to rise, underscoring the vulnerability of children despite the presence of various protection mechanisms.
full_text:
The number of cases reported under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act in Kerala continues to rise, underscoring the vulnerability of children despite the presence of various protection mechanisms.
In 2024, the number of POCSO cases reported in the State was 4,607. This increased to 4,765 in 2025, according to the annual report of the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights for 2025-26.
In 2013, the year the commission came into being, the number of POCSO cases reported was 1,002. The increase, however, cannot be interpreted as a rise in the number of crime alone.
Better reporting
Improvement in legal literacy, strengthening of awareness activities, and lesser hesitation in reporting sexual crime against children have led to better reporting of incidents, says the report.
Data provided by the State Crime Records Bureau to the child rights panel show that the highest number of cases was reported in Thiruvananthapuram district—689. This is up from 602 in 2024.
Kollam was next with 502 cases. Malappuram and Kozhikode followed with 465 and 460 cases, respectively. The higher number of cases in some districts is attributed to access to POCSO reporting mechanisms, population density, urbanisation, and better awareness.
86% girls
As many as 86% (4,167) of the 4,818 child survivors in 4,765 cases were girls. In 2024, the figure was nearly 85%. The number of boy survivors was 13% (618), while in 1% of the cases the gender was not known.
Children in the 15-18 age group remain the most vulnerable with 55% (2,666) of the survivors in that age bracket.
As many as 33% were in the 10-14 bracket, 9% in the 5-9 bracket, and 2% in the 0-4 age group. Among the survivors, 3% (154) were differently abled children, up from 2% (104) the previous year.
In familiar spaces
As per the statistics, sexual crime against children occurs mostly in private and familiar spaces. Most of the offenders are family members or those familiar to the children. This underscores the need to provide children with life skill training to understand sexual crime, says the report.
As many as 1,032 (22%) of the offences took place in the houses of the survivors and 615 (13%) in the houses of the offenders.
As much as 10% of the offences took place in public spaces, 4% in multiple places, 3% in vehicles, and 2% in schools and 14% of the offences occurred in hostels, cyberspace, and houses of relatives of either survivors or offenders. In 27% of the cases, the place of occurrence was unclear.

headline: Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) national working president Tejashwi Yadav on Thursday dissolved all organisational units in Bihar, including district, block, and panchayat committees as well as units associated with various cells and other affiliated bodi...
full_text:
Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) national working president Tejashwi Yadav on Thursday dissolved all organisational units in Bihar, including district, block, and panchayat committees as well as units associated with various cells and other affiliated bodies, with immediate effect.

headline: CRPF suicides hit five-year high in 2025, with most deaths on duty
full_text:
CRPF suicides hit five-year high in 2025, with most deaths on duty
The CRPF recorded 59 suicides in 2025, the highest in five years. Most cases involved lower ranks and occurred on duty, sharpening concern over service stress and family pressures.
The CRPF recorded 59 suicide cases in 2025, the highest in the last five years, official sources said on Thursday. More than 80 per cent of those who ended their lives over this period were from the constabulary and other non-gazetted ranks.
Data for 2021-25 showed that in more than 77 per cent of the cases, the deaths took place while the personnel were on duty. Of the 262 cases recorded during this period, 202 happened when personnel were on duty and the rest took place while they were on leave, the sources said.
While there was no official response from the force, CRPF officials told PTI that several steps had been initiated to ensure the physical and mental well-being of troops, and that the process was ongoing. Officials said it had largely been found that most suicide cases were linked to issues at home, along with the rigours of service and hard duties.
The CRPF, with a strength of about 3.25 lakh personnel, is the country's lead internal security force. Officials said that at any given time, about 95-97 per cent of its operational strength remains on duty tackling terrorists and insurgents or performing law and order duties.
The year-wise figures shared by the sources showed 59 cases in 2025, 46 in 2024, 57 in 2023, 43 in 2022 and 57 in 2021. In the five-year breakup by method, 128 personnel died by hanging, 118 shot themselves, 12 consumed poison, and in two cases each, personnel jumped before a train or cut their veins or throat.
The sources said that of the total 281 personnel who died by suicide in the last five years, including 19 till July 2026, 237 were from non-gazetted ranks, 43 were subordinate officers and one was a gazetted officer. They said the data showed that non-gazetted officials made up about 84 per cent of those who ended their lives during this period.
Non-gazetted officials hold the ranks of constable and head constable, while subordinate officers include Inspector, Sub Inspector and Assistant Sub Inspector. Gazetted officers are those of Assistant Commandant rank and above.

headline: Parliamentary panel seeks faster uranium mining nod to secure nuke fuel supply
full_text:
Parliamentary panel seeks faster uranium mining nod to secure nuke fuel supply
The recommendations are part of the Parliamentary panel's report on regulatory enablement for strategic minerals. The government has submitted interim replies, while its final response is still awaited.
A Parliamentary committee has recommended sweeping regulatory reforms for uranium mining, including time-bound single-window clearances and provisions for contiguous lease extensions to compress project timelines and ensure a reliable fuel supply for India's Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) fleet.
The recommendations are part of the panel's report on regulatory enablement for strategic minerals. The government has submitted interim replies, while its final response is still awaited.
The committee noted that newly identified or deeper ore bodies sometimes extend beyond existing lease boundaries.
However, current provisions under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act (MMDR) do not permit seamless lease-area extensions, forcing fresh leases and separate regulatory clearances.
It said this affects the techno-economic viability of projects, particularly for deposits located at depths beyond 600 metres, such as those at Narwapahar.
The panel also observed that the Uranium Corporation of India Ltd (UCIL) must obtain approvals from multiple agencies, including the Ministries of Environment and Forests, the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB), the Directorate General of Mines Safety (DGMS), the Pollution Control Board, as well as secure land and water permissions.
In addition, projects face social licence requirements and site-specific challenges such as tailings disposal and water availability.
"These multi-agency approval pathways can extend project timelines, with possible implications for fuel supply planning for PHWR reactors," the committee said.
To address these issues, the panel recommended amending relevant provisions of the MMDR Act and associated rules to allow contiguous lease extensions for strategic minerals such as uranium when ore bodies extend beyond existing boundaries, subject to stringent safety and environmental safeguards.
It also recommended operationalising a single-window clearance mechanism with statutory timelines for uranium mining and milling projects by integrating Central and State approvals and enabling parallel processing of permissions.
Further, the Committee proposed a State-level framework covering land acquisition, project-affected persons (PAP) rehabilitation and resettlement (R&R), assured industrial water supply, and off-site emergency planning.
It also suggested creating a coordination platform chaired by the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) to resolve inter-ministerial bottlenecks within defined service-level agreements.
According to the panel, these reforms would significantly compress the "permit-to-production" cycle and improve UCIL's reliability in supplying uranium to the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd (NPCIL).
The Ministry has submitted interim replies to the Committee's recommendations.
However, final action on amending MMDR provisions, establishing the single-window clearance mechanism, and creating the DAE-led coordination platform is still awaited.
With India expanding its nuclear power capacity, the Committee stressed that greater regulatory predictability is essential to de-risk uranium production and ensure the long-term fuel requirements of the country's domestic nuclear reactor programme are met.

headline: Same Sangh, different vocabulary: Priyank Kharge mocks RSS chief's Gen Z outreach
full_text:
Same Sangh, different vocabulary: Priyank Kharge mocks RSS chief's Gen Z outreach
During an interaction, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat made a strong pitch for engaging with young people, saying members of Gen Z who protest should not be branded "anti-national" and that their concerns are genuine.
Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge on Friday took a sharp swipe at Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat's outreach to the Gen Z, accusing the organisation and the BJP of merely changing their vocabulary without changing their ideology.
Responding to Bhagwat's remarks backing the concerns of young people and calling for dialogue, the Congress leader said in a post on X, "RSS and BJP are desperately updating their vocabulary, but unfortunately, it won't update their ideology. The truth remains the same, dividing people, misguiding youth and dressing up hatred in new packaging."
"Same Sangh, just different slang," he added.
Kharge also shared a caricature mocking Bhagwat's interaction with Gen Z and Gen Alpha students. The illustration carried the caption: "Flex the saffron, ghost the Constitution, let Manusmriti live rent-free, that's the whole vibe."
The Congress leader's remarks came a day after Bhagwat made a strong pitch for engaging with young people, saying members of Gen Z who protest should not be branded "anti-national" and that their concerns are genuine.
His interaction is being viewed as the RSS' most significant outreach to Gen Z and Gen Alpha since the nationwide agitation over the NEET paper leak, which culminated in the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan last month.
Addressing around 2,000 Gen Z and Gen Alpha participants at the 15th anniversary event of India's International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN) in Mumbai, Bhagwat said protest is a legitimate form of dialogue in a democracy and should ultimately help build consensus rather than create divisions.
"If Gen Z members are agitating, they are not anti-national; they are our people. It is our next generation. You need a dialogue and rapport with them," the RSS chief said.
He maintained that if concerns were not addressed through dialogue, people may resort to agitation, but stressed that the objective should remain consensus-building.
"The Gen Z grievances are genuine, and I believe in their honesty," Bhagwat said, while reiterating that dialogue should always be the first step.

headline: 'Prime Influencer': Dipke takes a dig at PM Modi's National Handloom Day Instagram video
full_text:
'Prime Influencer': Dipke takes a dig at PM Modi's National Handloom Day Instagram video
PM Modi promoted National Handloom Day online, while CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke reacted with a comment and later appealed for youth-focused announcements.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has kicked off this year’s National Handloom Day campaign with a social media push that also drew an unexpected reaction from Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke.
On August 6, Modi shared an Instagram reel asking people to celebrate National Handloom Day on August 7 by posting videos of their favourite handloom products, including GRWM-style content, with #NationalHandloomDay.
Soon after, Dipke commented “prime influencer” on Modi’s Instagram post. He later shared a separate video urging the Prime Minister to address India’s youth in his Independence Day speech.
Narendra Modi asked people to post handloom and GRWM videos
In his August 6 X post, Modi wrote: “Tomorrow, 7th August is National Handloom Day. Let’s make India’s handloom diversity popular. Share your videos with your favourite handloom products, including GRWM videos on social media. Don’t forget to use #NationalHandloomDay.”
The Instagram reel carried the same message. Speaking directly to viewers while displaying colourful handloom fabrics, Modi said, “Friends, we must not forget August 7, 1905.
He also asked people to celebrate National Handloom Day with the same enthusiasm as Friendship Day.
Modi added, “Celebrating Handloom Day means supporting every poor family and every weaver family that creates clothes on looms with their own hands from their small homes. There are countless new varieties and designs available in handloom products…”
He further added, “Our goal is to build an Atmanirbhar Bharat. For that, even the smallest and poorest families must become economically prosperous.”
Abhijeet Dipke reacts to PM Modi’s reel
Among the many reactions on Instagram, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke left a short comment that read, “prime influencer.”
It came under Modi’s reel promoting National Handloom Day and encouraging social media users to create and share videos highlighting India’s handloom products.
National Handloom Day has been observed every year since 2015. It marks the beginning of the Swadeshi Movement on August 7, 1905, and aims to support weavers, preserve India’s textile traditions and encourage rural livelihoods.
Abhijeet Dipke urges PM Modi to speak about youth
In a separate reel posted later, Dipke appealed to Modi to use his Independence Day address from the Red Fort to speak directly to young people.

headline: The All India United Trade Union Centre (AIUTUC) on Thursday organised a district-level protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner’s office in Kalaburagi, demanding the immediate implementation of the revised minimum wages for contract workers and u...

The All India United Trade Union Centre (AIUTUC) on Thursday organised a district-level protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner’s office in Kalaburagi, demanding the immediate implementation of the revised minimum wages for contract workers and urging the State government to reject any proposal to keep the final minimum wage notification issued on May 22, 2026, in abeyance.
Contract workers employed in various government departments, local bodies, public sector undertakings, private establishments, wind energy and solar energy companies participated in the demonstration. After the protest, the agitators submitted a memorandum addressed to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar through the Deputy Commissioner.
The protesters alleged that the reported proposal by the Finance Department to suspend the implementation of the revised minimum wages was anti-worker, unconstitutional and contrary to the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act. They contended that the issue was not confined to any particular department, but concerned lakhs of contract workers across Karnataka whose livelihood and statutory rights depended on the timely implementation of the revised wage structure.
The memorandum pointed out that although the minimum wages were due for revision in 2021, the notification was issued only in May 2026 after a delay of nearly five years. Any further postponement, it said, would inflict additional hardship on workers who had already been waiting for nearly a decade for the revision.
The AIUTUC maintained that the Karnataka High Court had declined to grant any interim stay on the revised minimum wage notification despite petitions filed by employers’ associations. Under such circumstances, the memorandum argued, the Finance Department could not administratively keep the notification in abeyance, as such a move would amount to interference with the judicial process.
The workers also contended that the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, does not empower any department to suspend a final notification once it has been issued. They pointed out that several government departments had already begun paying the revised wages and that withdrawing the notification now would create administrative confusion, industrial unrest and grave injustice to workers.
Rejecting the argument that higher wages would force industries to shift out of Karnataka, the protesters said sectors such as construction, security services, housekeeping, sanitation, municipal services, government outsourcing, wind energy and solar energy were location-specific and could not be relocated to other States merely because of revised wage rates.
The memorandum also stated that financial constraints could not be cited as a valid reason for denying minimum wages, referring to Supreme Court rulings which held that employers, including governments, were legally bound to pay statutory minimum wages irrespective of financial difficulties. It also argued that withholding the revised wages would violate Articles 21 and 23 of the Constitution as well as the spirit of ILO Convention No. 131 on minimum wage fixing.
The AIUTUC demanded that the State government immediately reject the proposal to suspend the May 22 notification, enforce the revised minimum wages in all government departments, boards, corporations, local bodies, private establishments and outsourcing agencies, release additional funds required for implementation, clear wage arrears, strengthen enforcement by the Labour Department through inspections and awareness drives, initiate stringent action against employers violating the law and strongly oppose any fresh attempts to obtain a stay against the notification before the High Court.
Labour leaders Raghavendra M.G., S.M. Sharma, Santosh Kumar Hirave, Sharanu Herur, Basavaraj Hulgol, Sharanamma Kattimani, Pavan Kumar Benakanalli, Mallinath Patil, Santosh Kumar Doddamani, Isamma Nalwar and others participated in the agitation.

headline: The SC said that compulsory retirement is open to judicial scrutiny if the order is mala fide, arbitrary or perverse
full_text:
The SC said that compulsory retirement is open to judicial scrutiny if the order is mala fide, arbitrary or perverse
NEW DELHI: It is not punitive to hand out compulsory retirement to someone, particularly in the armed forces, whose performance is slackening over the years, the Supreme Court said Thursday while rejecting the plea of a CISF officer challenging his removal from service on the ground of poor performance.A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar said compulsory retirement should not be seen as punitive but as a measure needed to ensure a high standard of efficiency and discipline in the force. "The object underlying compulsory retirement is to weed out the dead wood so as to maintain a high standard of efficiency and integrity in public service," the bench said, adding such an order is "not punitive in nature", carries no stigma and is passed in public interest on the government's subjective satisfaction.
It, however, said compulsory retirement is open to judicial scrutiny if the order is mala fide, arbitrary or perverse.Rejecting the officer's plea, the bench noted his performance had declined in the two years preceding the retirement order, with gradings dropping from "Good" to "Average". Members of disciplined forces are expected to maintain consistently high standards of efficiency, vigilance and discipline, it said.

headline: The High Court of Karnataka on Thursday ordered issue of notice to State government on a PIL petition questioning the project that envisages constructing a 2.2 km long three-lane, short transitory twin tunnel from Hebbal junction to the Karnataka Vet...
full_text:
The High Court of Karnataka on Thursday ordered issue of notice to State government on a PIL petition questioning the project that envisages constructing a 2.2 km long three-lane, short transitory twin tunnel from Hebbal junction to the Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries University (KVAFSU) at an estimated cost of ₹1,130 crore.
Also, the Court orally warned of staying the project if the Government and its authorities failed to file its response to the issues raised in the petition in writing before the next date of hearing on August 24.
A division bench comprising Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice K.S. Hemalekha passed the order on the petition filed by Guruprasad R.K, a technocrat, Rishvanjas Raghavan, founder of Bengaluru Nava Nirmana Party’s youth wing, and Elizabeth Soumya, founder of Hebbal Nature Society.
Any study conducted?
Apart from responding to the issues raised in the petitions, the Bench directed the Government to file affidavit specifying if any study has been conducted on the impact of the project on Hebbal lake, and stating that whether studies have covered the question whether tunnel would cause any obstruction to lake’s inflow or outflow of water. The Bench also ordered issue of notice to M/s Rithwik Projects Pvt. Ltd., the contractor of the tunnel road project.
Contending that the project poses a severe threat to the ecologically sensitive Hebbal lake and has been approved by violating various provisions of the law, it has been pointed out in the petition that the Detailed Project Report (DPR) itself acknowledges the hydrological sensitivity of the area, noting groundwater movement and the need for a watertight structure near the lake.
Stating that the DPR admits that the tunnel will be just 8-12 metres from the lake boundary, the petition contends that this distance from the lake violates even the reduced buffer zones under the amended provisions of the Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority Act.
Constitutional validity
Also, the petitioners have challenged the constitutional validity of the Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority (Amendment) Act, 2025, which drastically reduced buffer zones around lakes.
The amendment replaced a uniform 30-metre buffer with a graded system based on a lake’s size, allowing for buffers as small as 0 to 1 metre for smaller lakes and reducing the buffer to 30 metres only for lakes over 100 acres, the Court said while contending reduction in buffer zone is scientifically unsound and a deliberate attempt to facilitate the tunnel project. Karnataka High Court asks State’s response to plea complaining about impact of tunnel road project to Hebbal lake.
The litigation also challenges Rule 24 of the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority (BMLTA) Rules, 2026. The petition terms amended rule a ‘colourable exercise” that attempts to retrospectively validate projects, including the Hebbal tunnel, initiated without the mandatory prior approval from the BMLTA.
Impact assessment
The petitioners have also sought a direction to restrain the authorities from proceeding with the project until comprehensive and independent hydrological, hydrogeological, groundwater, stormwater, flood-risk and cumulative environmental impact assessments are conducted by competent expert agencies and disclosed publicly, while seeking direction for constituting an independent panel of experts to assess impact on Hebbal lake, groundwater recharge, drainage, flood resilience and mobility.

headline: Children under 13 could be barred from making accounts on social media, gaming platforms: Bill in Parliament
full_text:
Children under 13 could be barred from making accounts on social media, gaming platforms: Bill in Parliament
As per the proposal, children under the age of 13 could be barred from creating accounts without parental consent along with limits on personalised advertising.
Children under 13 could be barred from creating accounts on social media and online gaming platforms without verified parental consent, while platforms could be prohibited from tracking, profiling or targeting minors with personalised advertising, according to a proposed private member’s bill.
The Safeguarding Healthy Internet Environments for Little Digital-Natives (SHIELD) Bill, 2025, also proposes mandatory age-verification systems for platforms accessible to minors and parental-control dashboards that would allow guardians to monitor activity, manage privacy settings and restrict screen time.
Also Read I PM Modi ‘fears people’: Kejriwal alleges Centre using new law to silence critics on social media
The bill, proposed by BJP MP Baijayant Panda, was among two private members’ bills that were scheduled to be introduced in the parliament on Friday but could not be taken up because of adjournments of the House. The second bill is a proposed law seeking to regulate the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) to create realistic imitations of people. However, private members’ bills rarely make it into law, with only about a dozen having cleared parliament since Independence.
Online gaming, pornography and advertising
The SHIELD Bill defines a child as anyone below 18 and seeks to impose a dedicated set of safety obligations on social media services, online gaming platforms and other digital intermediaries. It proposes to prohibit platforms from tracking, profiling or using personalised advertising for children.
Also Read I Govt reduces 'unlawful' content removal deadline for social media firms from 36 hours to 3 hours
Platforms would also have to take steps to prevent children from being exposed to pornography, gambling and simulated betting, violent or extremist material and drug-related content. Platforms violating the proposed law could face penalties of up to ₹10 crore. Repeated or wilful violations could result in temporary suspension or blocking of services under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act.

headline: Rahul Gandhi's 'dard, data, daulat' message to Gen Z; BJP says should've gone to Jharkhand
full_text:
Rahul Gandhi's 'dard, data, daulat' message to Gen Z; BJP says should've gone to Jharkhand
Rahul Gandhi's event in Prayagraj came as political parties step up outreach to young voters, with recent student-led protests over paper leaks and examination irregularities pushing Gen Z into the political spotlight.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday pitched India’s 40 crore young people as the country’s “greatest strength”, but said they had been trapped in a “chakravyuh” of expensive education, shrinking job opportunities and paper leaks.
The BJP immediately hit back, asking why Gandhi was addressing students in Prayagraj instead of visiting protesting aspirants in Congress-ruled Jharkhand.
“Rahul Gandhi should have gone to Ranchi instead of Prayagraj,” BJP leader Amit Malviya said, as the Congress leader addressed students and competitive exam aspirants at the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme at KP Ground.
The Leader of Opposition built his speech around three themes: “dard, data and daulat” — pain, data and wealth — arguing that India possessed an unmatched advantage in its young population but was failing to convert that potential into jobs and economic opportunity.
“If this country moves forward, it will do so because of your strength. India has the world’s largest youth population – 40 crore energetic young people. This is the strength of the country,” he said.
The event was part of the Congress’s 40-day nationwide ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ campaign, launched in June to highlight paper leaks, recruitment irregularities and unemployment and to press for reforms in the examination system.
‘DEGREES HAVE NO MEANING IF THEY CANNOT GET YOU A JOB’
Gandhi argued that families were spending lakhs of rupees on higher education only for young people to discover that their degrees did not guarantee employment.
“You study engineering, medicine, postgraduate courses or whatever you choose. Lakhs of rupees are taken from your families and then you are given a certificate,” the 56-year-old leader said.
“But today that certificate has no meaning in India because it cannot give you employment.”
He claimed that only 12 out of every 1,000 young Indians secured permanent jobs.
Gandhi also referred to a competitive exam aspirant who said he worked for Blinkit for nearly 10 hours a day before studying for government examinations and had missed clearing an Indian Army test by one mark.
The Congress leader used the example to argue that young people were being forced to work long hours simply to fund their preparation, only to face the added uncertainty of paper leaks.
According to Gandhi, years of effort could be wiped out if someone with money was able to “buy” access to a leaked examination paper.
‘YOUTH PLUS DATA EQUALS 21ST-CENTURY ECONOMY’
Gandhi then shifted to what he described as India’s second major advantage after its youth population — data. “Youth plus data is equal to the 21st-century economy,” he said.
Drawing a comparison with petroleum in the previous century, the Rae Bareli MP argued that data was the raw material driving artificial intelligence.
“If I gave you a petrol engine in the 20th century but refused to give you petrol, you would say the engine was useless. In the same way, AI has no meaning without your data,” he said.
Gandhi said the huge volumes of data produced by Indians constituted a national asset.
“This data is India’s and it is yours. You create it. It comes from your imagination. It is India’s capital, strength and asset,” he said.
He alleged that this data was instead benefiting large corporations, naming Jio, Adani, Facebook and Google.
‘REELS ARE THE ADDICTION OF THE 21ST CENTURY’
Gandhi also took aim at the social media economy, calling endless consumption of reels the “addiction of the 21st Century”.
He said young Indians were encouraged to spend hours consuming and creating content on Instagram and WhatsApp while secure employment remained out of reach.
“You are told to watch as many reels as you want, send as many WhatsApp messages as you want and make as many Instagram Reels as you want,” Gandhi said.
“This is the addiction of the 21st century. But then you are told that you cannot get a job or employment in this country.”
Towards the end of his speech, Gandhi said his political fight was against the system rather than individuals.
Referring to images of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, industrialist Gautam Adani and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat that he had displayed during the address, Gandhi said there was no need to hate anyone.
“We only have to change the system. We have to spread love,” he said, before signing off with his familiar “Tata, bye-bye”.
BJP QUESTIONS RAHUL OVER JHARKHAND PROTESTS
The BJP sought to turn Gandhi’s student outreach back on the Congress, pointing to the ongoing protests by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand, where the Congress is a junior partner in the JMM-led government.
BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan accused the Lok Sabha MP of “two-faced political hypocrisy”, saying he had found time to attend the Prayagraj programme but not to meet students protesting and fasting in Ranchi.
“Today is the anniversary of the Quit India Movement, and it is high time Rahul Gandhi quit his two-faced political hypocrisy,” Kesavan said.
“He has no empathy, nor does he find the time to meet students in Jharkhand who are on a hunger strike, some of whom have even fainted. Yet today, Rahul Gandhi is attending his ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme in Prayagraj,” he added.
The BJP’s criticism came as protests in Jharkhand over alleged irregularities in government recruitment examinations continued, with aspirants demanding action over JPSC and JSSC examinations.
GEN Z BECOMES NEW POLITICAL BATTLEGROUND
The Congress leader's event came as political parties step up outreach to young voters, with recent student-led protests over paper leaks and examination irregularities pushing Gen Z into the political spotlight.
Hours before the Prayagraj programme, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also addressed young people at IIT Delhi’s 57th Convocation.
Modi urged graduating students to question accepted ideas and break larger challenges into smaller, manageable parts rather than feel overwhelmed by them.
“Keep curiosity alive in life. Keep your learning instinct awakened,” Modi told over 3,000 students and 587 PhD scholars present at the venue.
The parallel outreach reflects the growing political importance of young voters as parties increasingly view Gen Z as a potential vote bank.

headline: Hospitals can’t show negligence in treating crime victims, says SC
full_text:
Hospitals can’t show negligence in treating crime victims, says SC
New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday said hospitals cannot show negligence in treating victims of serious crimes requiring immediate medical attention, as it decided to frame broad guidelines for hospitals and law enforcement agencies to ensure that such lapses do not recur
New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday said hospitals cannot show negligence in treating victims of serious crimes requiring immediate medical attention, as it decided to frame broad guidelines for hospitals and law enforcement agencies to ensure that such lapses do not recur. The apex court directed two private hospitals in Ghaziabad to pay a total compensation of ₹12 lakh to the family of a four-year-old rape victim who died after allegedly being denied emergency treatment.
A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said the case exposed serious failures on the part of both the police and hospitals.
“Both law enforcement agencies and medical institutions have been found lacking. We want to lay down the law. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita has certain safeguards but there exists a gap between the normative law prescribing the statutory mechanism and the law in real which exists at the ground level. Our effort is to bridge that gap,” the bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said.
The court added, “We are further inclined to lay down guidelines for timely medical assistance to victims in such cases.”
The bench was hearing a petition filed by the victim’s father, a daily wage labourer, seeking a court-monitored probe into the March incident. The court had earlier constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT), which found lapses in both the police investigation and the medical response.
According to the SIT, the four-year-old girl was raped by her neighbour and remained alive for nearly five hours after sustaining grievous injuries. She was taken to two private hospitals, including a multi-speciality facility, but was allegedly denied treatment before being shifted to a district hospital, where she was declared dead. The SIT also found that the delay in treatment contributed to her death.
Accepting the findings, the court directed St Joseph (Mariam) Hospital to pay ₹10 lakh and Khajan Singh Manvi Healthcare to pay ₹2 lakh to the victim’s family.
“On going through the SIT report, it was our prima facie opinion... that it was a clear case of sheer negligence on part of the hospitals,” the bench said.
Senior advocate N Hariharan, appearing for the victim’s family, argued that the police had also failed in their duty. He said there was a delay of nearly 30 hours in registering offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and sought directions for video recording of complainants’ statements at police stations.
“There was a 30-hour gap in registering the POCSO offence. Even the hospitals wasted five hours. The child could have been saved during this time. It is high time we call the Hippocratic oath taken by doctors a hypocratic oath,” Hariharan said.
A Hippocratic oath is an ethical code followed by doctors worldwide emphasising their duty towards treating any patient to the best of their skill and ability.
The bench underlined that timely medical intervention could make the difference between life and death.
“When a victim is haemorrhaging, the time is crucial. It has also been seen that the initial hours are always crucial in saving burn victims,” it observed.
Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Uttar Pradesh government, told the court that the police registered the POCSO offence within 24 hours of the SIT’s recommendation and that disciplinary proceedings had been initiated against the officials responsible for the lapses.
The court said the guidelines it proposes to frame would address training, accountability and supervision of both police personnel and medical institutions.
“It is extremely important that police officials at a particular level have to be periodically sensitised. As human beings they deal with one or the other crime every day. There is sensitivity involved in every matter. This involves human emotions, how to take care of victims. This is completely up to them how they manage it,” the bench said.
Hariharan also submitted that both hospitals had the necessary facilities and doctors on call but neither admitted the child nor summoned emergency doctors despite her critical condition.
Counsel for one of the hospitals said it was willing to pay ₹10 lakh as a voluntary contribution instead of compensation and requested the court to consider dropping the criminal case against it. The bench said it would consider the request while passing its final order.
The incident took place on March 16 in Ghaziabad’s Nandgram area, where the child was allegedly lured away by her neighbour, raped and brutally assaulted. The post-mortem report recorded severe injuries to her private parts, indicating aggravated sexual assault under the POCSO Act.

headline: Explainer: What changes as Parliament passes Registration of Births and Deaths Bill
full_text:
Explainer: What changes as Parliament passes Registration of Births and Deaths Bill
Kanchan Yadav / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 09, 2026, 07:16 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
The Parliament passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
The Parliament passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026, amid a wider logjam that has repeatedly disrupted the Monsoon Session. The Rajya Sabha cleared the legislation on Tuesday by voice vote days after the Lok Sabha passed it on July 31 amid opposition protests without a debate.Both Houses witnessed repeated adjournments during the session, with several Bills being passed amid disruptions. The Monsoon Session began on July 20 and is scheduled to conclude on August 13.The new legislation focuses on a seemingly routine but important part of government records like registering births and deaths. A birth certificate records a person's entry into the official system, while a death certificate formally records their departure.Together, these documents help establish identity, maintain public records and provide proof for a range of legal and administrative purposes. The amendment seeks to tighten the process when such events are reported long after they occur.
What does the Bill change?
Under the existing system, delayed registration already requires additional verification. If information about a birth or death is submitted after one year but within two years, the amended law will require an order from a district magistrate, sub-divisional magistrate or an executive magistrate authorised by the district magistrate.
For cases reported more than two years after the event, the threshold becomes higher. The registration will require an order from a judicial magistrate of the First Class having jurisdiction over the place where the birth or death occurred.The magistrate will have to verify the correctness of the information before permitting registration. A prescribed fee will also have to be paid, according to a document released by the government.The amendment also updates the reference to an "Executive Magistrate" in the 1969 law to align it with the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which replaced the earlier Code of Criminal Procedure.The government says the primary objective is to ensure that births and deaths are registered promptly and that delayed registrations are subjected to stronger scrutiny.The Registration of Births and Deaths Act makes registration mandatory. According to the government's statement of objects and reasons, birth and death certificates provide legal identity and can be used as evidence of a person's birth or death.The government argues that the integrity of these records is particularly important because birth certificates can be used for several official purposes, including processes involving identity and citizenship-related documentation.Tighter scrutiny of delayed registrations, it says, can help prevent fraudulent or questionable entries and improve the reliability of official records.BJP IT cell head Amit Malviya said, âThe objective is straightforward: encourage timely registration, prevent fraudulent or dubious entries, and preserve the credibility of birth and death certificates, the foundational documents that establish a personâs legal identity.âThe government has also pointed to a significant rise in registration rates over the past decade.Union minister of state for home Nityanand Rai said birth registration increased from 86.6% in 2014 to 99.1% in 2024, while death registration rose from 72.5% to 99.4% during the same period. He also said around 3.5 lakh registration centres have been established across the country.The government's argument is that as registration coverage approaches universal levels, the focus must increasingly be on ensuring that the remaining delayed or questionable cases are properly verified.
What is the significance of a birth certificate?
A birth certificate is often the first formal document linking an individual to the state. It records details such as a person's date and place of birth and can be required for a range of official purposes, including education, employment, passports and other government documentation.The government has also highlighted the role of birth records in establishing identity and in processes where proof of birth or citizenship-related documentation is required.That makes the accuracy of the registration system important beyond population statistics.A fraudulent birth certificate, for instance, could potentially affect records across several government systems. Similarly, failure to register deaths can leave outdated information in official databases.The government has also linked accurate death registration with keeping records, including electoral rolls, updated.
What happened in the Parliament?
The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on July 31 by voice vote amid opposition protests. Several opposition MPs entered the Well of the House demanding the presence of Union home minister Amit Shah, and the legislation was cleared without a debate.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju criticised the opposition for not participating in the proceedings and said the government wanted a discussion on the "important Bill".âIt is unfortunate. Please do not repeat this in the future. People who sent you to Parliament will seek answers from you,â Rijiju said, urging MPs to participate in debates rather than disrupt proceedings.The legislation was passed amid continued sloganeering, with the opposition MPs demanding the presence of Union home minister Amit Shah and his response on the "police action" against student protesters on July 20 at Jantar Mantar.The Rajya Sabha later took up the Bill amid similar disruptions.Moving the Bill in the Rajya Sabha, Rai said the government wanted every birth and death to be properly recorded. He said, âThe country wants that anyone born in the country, it is important that he or she is registered. Anyone who has died, cannot continue to remain in the voter lists to benefit some parties.âRai also linked the legislation to concerns over people who have died continuing to appear on electoral rolls.
The country now wants to get rid of ghosts. There are govts in some states that look for an opportunity and welcome those (who were not born in India) and register their births who are not eligible to be registered here. Now, we will not allow this to happen.
Union minister of state for home Nityanand Rai
He also cited the rise in registration rates as evidence of the government's efforts to improve the system.Some NDA members supported the legislation. YSRCP member M R Reddy, AIADMK's M Thambidurai and BRS member Ravi Chandra Vaddiraju backed the Bill. BJP member Biswajit Sinha, meanwhile, accused the Congress of opposing the legislation because it did not want proper registration of births and deaths.Sinha also referred to the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in West Bengal, claiming that people who had died years earlier remained on voter lists.He alleged that some parties were helping illegal Bangladeshi and Pakistani infiltrators obtain birth registrations and voter identities, and said the proposed changes would help prevent such practices.Leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge said, âThe prime minister and the home minister should come. we want discussion.âDespite the protests, the Bill was taken up for consideration and passage.
What is the significance of the bill
Why did the opposition say
Opposition members did not reject the need for accurate birth and death records but questioned the practical implications of requiring a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class to approve registrations delayed by more than two years.UPPL member Pramod Boro said the objective of the Bill was important but questioned whether an administrative responsibility should be shifted to the judiciary.He warned that the provision could add to the workload of courts, increase costs and make registration more difficult for migrants, homeless people, poor families and those living in remote areas.BJD member Santrupt Misra also questioned why registrations are delayed in the first place. He suggested that the government should identify the reasons behind late registration and consider dedicated registration offices, particularly in tribal areas, to improve access.CPI(M) member V Sivadasan supported the need for proper registration but said the government should also focus on the circumstances surrounding deaths, including malnutrition and student deaths.
The passage came amid a wider logjam in the Monsoon Session, with repeated adjournments in both Houses and several Bills being cleared amid disruptions.With Parliament having passed the Bill, the legislation will now go through the remaining constitutional process before coming into force. The Bill, therefore, seeks to strike a balance between two objectives: ensuring that births and deaths are recorded promptly, while subjecting unusually delayed registrations to greater scrutiny.
Kanchan Yadav is a writer at The Times of India, where she covers business, politics, international affairs and social issues. Her reporting also focuses on policy, governance and economic developments, with a close lens on how decisions in corridors of power affect everyday lives and community well-being.

headline: Vijay’s wife withdraws petition to divorce him
full_text:
Vijay’s wife withdraws petition to divorce him
Sangeetha, the wife of Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay, on Friday withdrew her divorce petition filed before the family court in Chengalpattu, near Chennai
Sangeetha, the wife of Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay, on Friday withdrew her divorce petition filed before the family court in Chengalpattu, near Chennai.
Judge D Sujatha allowed Sangeetha to withdraw the plea after the latter appeared through video conferencing and confirmed that she did not wish to pursue the proceedings.
The court issued notice to Vijay’s counsel, who said they had no objection to the request. The court therefore, allowed Sangeetha to withdraw the petition and granted her liberty to file a fresh petition in future, if required.
Sangeetha had filed the divorce petition in February under Section 27(1)(a), (b) and (d) of the Special Marriage Act, alleging adultery and mental cruelty. She had told the court at the time that she had tried to resolve their differences amicably but failed. She had also said she delayed legal proceedings to protect her children’s studies and emotional well-being.
She had also sought maintenance and the right to live in the couple’s Neelankarai residence.
At the previous hearing on June 20 this year, both Vijay and Sangeetha had failed to appear before the court. Their lawyers had then sought permission for their clients to appear virtually, citing security concerns and procedural difficulties arising from their status as public figures.
On Friday, after recording Sangeetha’s statement and noting Vijay’s lack of objection, judge Sujatha dismissed the petition as withdrawn and allowed Sangeetha to initiate fresh proceedings, if necessary.
