headline: JPSC, E20, anti-reservation: The issues India is talking about
full_text:
JPSC, E20, anti-reservation: The issues India is talking about
Aastha Jha / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 08, 2026, 19:08 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
CJPâs success may have opened the door for the next big youth movement, but what issue can turn online anger into real-world action?
India just witnessed the 'reel' generation make the 'real' world listen. July 2026 saw something Indian parents have dreamt of for years: Gen Z looked up from its screens. But it was for a cause. They turned memes into megaphones and forced the country to pay attention to exam reforms. In their own language, they ate and left no crumbs.Exam paper leaks weren't new. Student protests weren't either. What was different was how a "cockroach" remark snowballed into a meme, then into the Cockroach Janata Party, and eventually into a nationwide movement that dominated headlines.Now comes the bigger question: What other issues is India talking about?
Eyes on Jharkhand
While the CJP protest has ended, the demand for a system overhaul has not. As Jantar Mantar went quiet, Jharkhand emerged as the new battleground as students demand accountability over JPSC-JSSC exam irregularities.Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto has been on a hunger strike since August 2, while protesters are seeking an independent probe and reforms in the recruitment process.
E20
Then there is E20, a policy that directly affects vehicle owners.The nationwide rollout of 20% ethanol-blended petrol has sparked a political and online debate over mileage, older vehicle compatibility and whether the Centre followed the phased roadmap laid out by NITI Aayog.
After the NEET protests, calls for Union minister Nitin Gadkari's resignation began circulating, while leaders including Arvind Kejriwal and Rahul Gandhi also raised the issue.Vivek Rajput, a CA at a top government firm, says that although he has never attended a protest, this might become his first. âIf there is a protest over E20, I will definitely go. My vehicleâs mileage has gone down compared to before.âCJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka agrees that E20 deserves attention, but questions whether the government has adequately addressed concerns around its impact and benefits. âObviously, E20 is an important issue that needs to be addressed. I don't think the government has very scientifically backed data to suggest whether the vehicles would be impacted or not,â Ranka said.âNeither has there been any clarification on why the prices haven't dropped as it was promised to us. So what exactly has ethanol E20 petrol achieved in the country? There is no sort of clarity on that.â
Containers displayed as purported fuel samples are seen during an Indian Youth Congress (IYC) protest against E20 fuel policy (PTI)
Lack of jobs
Indiaâs job crisis is particularly acute among its growing pool of educated young people. According to the State of Working India 2026 report, the number of young graduates rose nearly 13-fold from about 5 million in 1983 to 63 million in 2023, but graduate unemployment among those below 25 remains close to 40%. The number of unemployed graduates has also surged 16-fold, from less than 1 million to around 11 million over the same period. Government data points to continued pressure: youth unemployment among 15-29-year-olds reached 16.2% in June 2026, even as their labour force participation rate fell to 40.3%. The figures highlight a widening gap between the number of young people entering the workforce and the availability of secure, quality jobs.Also read: Inside India's broken jobs market and why the 'cockroaches' are fed upAnger has also been growing over the increasing tax burden on common people. âAs the finance minister, Nirmala Sitharaman is not giving enough tax benefits to salaried people. Under the old tax regime, at least people could save money and also save on taxes. Now, neither are we able to save, nor are we getting tax benefits," said Rajput.
Anti-reservation movement
Reservation Hatao Andolan (RHA) recently gained nearly 6 million followers on Instagram. âBacked by citizens who feel left behind by reservation politics and driven by merit. The brave earn respect through their character and perseverance. Only the cowardly and the cruel keep shouting about caste,â the Insta bio of the page reads.The page was formed in October last year and the first post was made in March this year. Since the CJP protest, the account became more active.
RHAâs Insta page has gained significant followers
But quota has been a divisive issue in India. Unlike the paper-leak issue, which is an offence and affects students across categories, reservation is a constitutional policy rooted in questions of representation, historical disadvantage and unequal access â and does not attract a unified opinion.The merit debate also gets complicated when cut-offs enter the picture. In 2023, when the NEET-PG qualifying percentile was reduced to zero for all categories amid thousands of vacant seats, candidates who had fallen below the original cut-off became eligible for admission. General-category candidates accounted for the largest share of those admitted after the reduction â over 56%, compared with 26% OBC, 11% SC and 6% ST. The skew was sharper in private colleges, where General-category candidates accounted for around 70% of those who secured clinical specialities after the cut-off was lowered. The data does not suggest that General-category candidates were given a special concession; rather, it shows that they formed the largest share of those who benefited from the relaxation.Caste-based reservation in education has been part of India's affirmative-action framework for decades. Before independence, several rulers and institutions had experimented with measures to uplift historically disadvantaged communities. After independence, the Constitution formally provided for reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, which was later expanded to other backward classes and, in a different form, economically weaker sections.Those advocating against the existing quota system argue that it compromises merit and should be replaced or reworked around economic disadvantage.
CJP's spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka brings focus on lack of jobs
RHA has posted five broad demands:Income-based reservation: Under this, they demand that the reservation should purely be based on the income.One family, one reservation, one time: Under this, it demands that once a family has benefited from reservation, the next generation should compete on merit.Minimum standards for everyone: Under this, it demands that every exam should have minimum qualifying marks within 10-20% of the higher quota cut-off. If reserved seats fall vacant, it wants them allotted to the General category.No reservation politics: Under this, it demands:
Political parties be barred from promising new or higher reservation quotas during elections.
The 50% limit on caste-based reservation should not be breached.
The sunset clause: Under this, it demands that no policy should run forever.
Set a time-bound roadmap to improve government schools, teachers and educational infrastructure.
As educational inequality reduces, reservation should be gradually phased out.
Reservation should be reviewed every 10 years using updated socio-economic data.
Reservation lists should be updated periodically, moving communities that have progressed to the General category.
CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka, however, believes the reservation debate itself risks taking attention away from a larger problem: the shortage of opportunities.âI think the reservation-hatao movement, I just don't get the idea,â Ranka said. âThe focus every time the debate is brought on reservation, that really means that people, there is a distraction from the broader issue.âFor Ranka, that broader issue is jobs and seats. âThere are only 2% of the jobs which are government jobs in this country, 98% of the jobs in this country are private sector jobs,â he said. âWhy are there not enough jobs in this country? Why are there not enough government seats, medical seats, engineering seats in this country?ââReservation, the topic of reservation is always a distraction on the broader structural issues which no one is ready to address. We need more jobs, we need more seats in colleges. That's what people should be asking,â he said.Others, however, see reservation itself as the issue that needs to be challenged.The matter has gained even more attention after the UGC rules. The UGC equity regulations have also become a potential flashpoint, with the 2026 rules aimed at addressing discrimination in higher education.
Members of Swarn Samaj and Brahman Parivar stage a protest against the UGC's new caste-based equity rules at Hazratganj, in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh in January (PTI)
The Supreme Court stayed the regulations in January, citing ambiguities and the possibility of misuse, but the issue has resurfaced amid growing anti-reservation sentiment online and could emerge as another potential trigger for youth mobilisation.But whether online traction can become a street movement remains an open question.Rajput said his brother sent him the Reservation Hatao Andolan page on Instagram and he started following it only last week. He said there were 21 people on his team with eight or nine belonging to the General category while the others benefited from reservation.For Rajput, however, the online movement has not yet translated into a willingness to protest on the ground. That distinction could prove crucial. After all, CJP's success was not simply about getting people to watch, like or share.But there is a counter-argument to the idea that reservation could become the next universal youth cause. Many SC/ST communities and other socially disadvantaged groups still lack equal access to quality education, particularly in rural areas where caste-based discrimination and social inequalities continue.So, unlike the paper-leak issue, where the grievance could unite students across categories, an anti-reservation movement begins with a built-in fault line.It may have the followers. It may have the slogans. It may even have people ready to take the fight to the streets. But whether it can replicate CJP's cross-sectional appeal is another question altogether.
Pollution
Diwali is just a couple of months away. And, as predictable as the festival itself, the annual debate will return: to burn or not to burn crackers.But for Delhi-NCR, pollution is not just a seasonal social-media debate. When the air turns toxic, the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) kicks in, bringing curbs that can affect everything from construction and traffic to office timings and schools. A study by IITM-Pune and CAQM found that without GRAP, Delhi could see 60% more severe-AQI hours, while the measures could reduce PM2.5 levels by up to 42 Âµg/mÂ³, depending on the stage.
Anti-pollution protest: Protesters last year showing posters of Maoist commander Madvi Hidma, who was killed in an encounter (PTI)
In Mumbai too, pollution has emerged as a growing urban challenge, with construction and road dust, vehicle emissions and industrial activity among the key contributors to poor air quality. Pollution spikes have become a recurring concern, with several parts of the city recording AQI levels above 200, raising concerns over prolonged exposure to harmful particulate matter such as PM2.5. The problem adds to the wider challenges of rapid urbanisation, infrastructure growth and increasing vehicular traffic in the city.So, could pollution become the next rallying point, or is an issue with no single villain simply too difficult to turn into a movement? âIf there is a protest over pollution, Iâll go for that too. I think we can raise our voice over issues that directly affect us. I would even join a protest over taxes,â said Rajput.The logic is simple: if an issue hits your lungs, your wallet or your everyday life, it may be easier to turn outrage into action.
So, what actually makes people protest?
For Ratna Singh, CJPâs legal head, the answer isn't simply the issue itself. It is how that issue is packaged, communicated and mobilised.She believes CJP gained momentum because it was a Gen Z protest around education â an issue that extends well beyond NEET aspirants to competitive-exam candidates, school and college students, graduates and young people looking for jobs.Education, she said, allowed both Gen Z and Gen Alpha â and even their parents â to relate to the movement. âA lot of people in the crowd, when they were coming, they were like, you know, my parents were not letting me be here. But now I'm here. So they're also supporting,â Singh said.And then comes the part that may matter most for the next protest. âSomething can trend on Instagram, but on ground, how you are planning it, how you are strategising it, that's also important,â Singh said.She added that people may relate to an issue online but still not turn up physically. How organisers convey the importance of an issue â and how they plan to keep an agitation going â can determine whether it survives beyond a social-media trend.
Why CJP clicked with Indiaâs youth: Anger, accessibility and a platform to be heard
That is perhaps the biggest lesson from CJP.Going viral can get an issue noticed. Mobilising people can turn it into a movement.
Singh believes unemployment could be the next major youth issue. CJP is planning a nationwide âKya Bolti Publicâ campaign in September to hear from young people across states about the problems they face.She said the organisation wants unemployment and education to become a more central part of the public conversation and wants to understand youth concerns and push for reforms. âWith the success of Cockroach Janata Party, this wave has started, where people will come forward, people will talk about issues, people will also talk about unemployment and youth-related, youth-centric issues,â Singh said.Reservation has the Instagram audience. Pollution has the lived experience. E20 has the everyday grievance. Unemployment has the scale. But whichever issue wins the race will need to clear one final hurdle. It has to make people look up from their screens â and then actually leave them.
Aastha Jha is a writer at The Times of India, covering politics. She also writes on business, global affairs, social issues, with a focus on policy, governance and their impact on everyday lives. Her work brings together reportage and analysis, tracking developments in India and abroad while examining the broader social and economic currents shaping public discourse.

headline: Govt asks Meta to revamp algorithms, curb spread of propaganda: Report
full_text:
Govt asks Meta to revamp algorithms, curb spread of propaganda: Report
The government has sought these specific changes as part of efforts to strengthen the detection and removal of harmful and manipulated content.
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has asked Meta to revamp its algorithms and provide a compliance roadmap to curb the spread of deepfakes, propaganda and other manipulated or illegal content across its platforms, according to government sources.
The government has sought these specific changes to Meta's algorithms as part of efforts to strengthen the detection and removal of harmful and manipulated content, the sources said.
MeitY officials have also asked the company to strengthen its content moderation systems, act faster on takedown requests received from authorised government agencies and comply with data localisation requirements.
The government has further sought closer coordination with Meta to speed up the detection and removal of deepfakes, morphed images and misleading posts, according to the sources.
The directions followed a meeting between Meta's technical team and MeitY officials on Friday, during which the company explained how its existing systems identify and handle harmful content online.
Government officials, however, pushed for specific algorithmic changes aimed at restricting the spread of what they described as propaganda, deepfakes and manipulated media on Meta's platforms.
The latest discussions follow a series of meetings between the government and Meta over the handling of harmful and illegal content on its platforms.
During the discussions, Meta acknowledged gaps in its existing systems and outlined technical measures it could take to tackle deepfakes and other forms of synthetic content, the sources said.
Both sides have agreed to continue the discussions, with another meeting expected next week.
The government's scrutiny of Meta has intensified in recent days over concerns related to deepfakes, Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) and other harmful content on its platforms.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg had earlier apologised over errors related to CSAM and deepfake content on the company's platforms after concerns were raised by the Indian government.
The latest discussions also come as India has tightened its regulatory framework for synthetically generated content, including deepfakes.
The government earlier this year amended the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules to bring synthetically generated information under a specific regulatory framework and place additional due-diligence requirements on online intermediaries.
The rules seek to strengthen accountability for AI-generated and manipulated content, including through identification and labelling requirements.
The government's ongoing engagement with Meta is also focused on whether online platforms are adequately meeting their responsibilities under Indian law, including their obligations related to harmful and illegal content.
Government sources have maintained that social media platforms operating in India are required to comply with Indian laws and have a responsibility towards users and society.

headline: Meta has restricted access to a report in India on Kashmir pellet victim Insha Mushtaq from its platform, Instagram.
full_text:

Assam flood: Over 1.55 lakh people hit, toll at 98; damage assessment from Sunday
Guwahati, More than 1.55 lakh people remained affected by Assam floods, with the toll in this year's deluge reaching 98 with one more fatality, officials said on Saturday.
Even as 13 districts remained affected, the government will, from Sunday, launch an assessment of damage caused by the deluge to expedite release of funds for permanent rehabilitation in the four worst-hit districts in the eastern part of the state.
Officials said one death was reported from the Mahmora revenue circle in Charaideo district, taking the toll to 98.
Thirteen districts Sivasagar, Golaghat, Nagaon, Hojai, Sonitpur, Dhemaji, Darrang, Biswanath, Kamrup , Lakhimpur, Udalguri, Jorhat and Charaideo remained affected on Friday.
A total of 1,55,849 people were reeling under the deluge, with Golaghat being the worst-hit district, where 58,750 were affected, followed by Sivasagar and Jorhat . On Thursday, over 1.68 lakh people in 15 districts were affected.
The administration was operating 55 relief camps, sheltering over 10,000 displaced people. Another 18 relief distribution centres were also functional. A crop area of 10,748.64 hectares remained submerged, while over 47,000 animals have been affected.
Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Friday said his government will conduct a door-to-door assessment of flood damage in the worst-hit districts of Jorhat, Sivasagar, Golaghat and Charaideo from August 9 to 30.
He asserted that no affected household will be left out and the government will provide maximum relief permissible as per norms.
He further said after the first assessment list is compiled, it will be re-verified with the affected families, and by September 10, it is expected that the government will have an estimation of funds required for rehabilitation purposes.
"Once we have the estimate of the funds, we can start providing the requisite financial assistance for permanent rehabilitation," he added.

headline: 7 killed, 11 injured in Himachal bus accident; PM Modi expresses sorrow
full_text:
7 killed, 11 injured in Himachal bus accident; PM Modi expresses sorrow
Seven people were killed, and eleven were injured after a private bus skidded off the road and met with an accident in Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday condoled the lives lost in the road accident near Chalunj Mor in Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district and prayed for the recovery of the injured.
Seven people were killed, and 11 were injured after a private bus skidded off the road and met with an accident at 7.15 am under Patwar Circle Bairagarh, according to the State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC).
"The loss of lives due to a mishap in Chamba, Himachal Pradesh, is deeply saddening. My thoughts are with the families who have lost their loved ones. May those injured recover at the earliest," the Prime Minister's Office posted on X.
Also Read I Vehicles torched, stones pelted as violence breaks out in Patna over man's death in road accident
Himachal Pradesh CM condoles
Earlier today, Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu also expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and instructed the district administration to make proper arrangements for the treatment of the injured.
Sukhu posted on X, “The news of the demise of 7 people and injuries to 11 others in the bus accident near Chaluj Morh on the Tisa-Bairagarh route in Chamba district is extremely heartbreaking. I extend my deepest condolences to the families who have lost their loved ones in this tragic accident. May God grant a place at His divine feet to the souls of the departed and bestow strength upon the bereaved families to bear this immense sorrow.”
Also Read I Nitin Gadkari stresses good training for drivers to curb road accidents
"Instructions have been issued to the district administration to ensure that all the injured are immediately admitted to the nearest hospitals and proper arrangements are made for their treatment. I pray to God for the swift recovery of all the injured," he added.
Police recalls the incident
Chamba Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP), Dinesh Sharma said, "We received information about this accident at 7:15 AM today. A private bus that was coming from Bairagarh to Chamba met with an accident just after covering 5 kilometers. There were a total of 18 people on board, out of which 7 died on the spot. The other 11 injured individuals were sent for treatment with the help of local people. Postmortem of the deceased is being conducted. Further enquiry is ongoing."
Meanwhile, in the wake of heavy rainfall in Himachal Pradesh, Meteorological Centre Shimla Director Shobhit Katiyar warned the public of slippery roads, reduced visibility and damaged structures as well as agricultural and horticultural crops.

headline: PM speaks to JD Vance, discusses India-US ties, congratulates him on son's birth
full_text:
PM speaks to JD Vance, discusses India-US ties, congratulates him on son's birth
Interestingly, Vance's last publicly known phone call with PM Modi was in May 2025, during Operation Sindoor against Pakistan, a conversation the Prime Minister later disclosed in the Lok Sabha.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday spoke to US Vice President JD Vance over the phone and discussed ways to further deepen the India-US Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership across key areas.
PM Modi also congratulated Vance and Second Lady Usha Vance on the birth of their son and conveyed his best wishes to the family. Further details of the conversation were not immediately available.
Vance’s call to the Prime Minister comes amid a series of global and domestic developments that could have ramifications for India-US relations.
On the geopolitical front, the call came days after Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a mutual defence pact, widely seen as signalling a new regional alignment amid the conflict in West Asia.
The agreement, signed on Friday by Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman, and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, states that an armed attack on any one of the three countries will be treated as an attack on all three.
The call also comes against the backdrop of concerns raised by US Congressman Riley Moore over the proposed changes to the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA), which he alleged could allow the Indian government to take over churches and religious charities.
Responding to Moore’s remarks, the Ministry of External Affairs on Thursday said legislative matters were India’s internal affairs, while noting that several countries, including the United States, have laws regulating foreign funding.
MODI-VANCE PREVIOUS CALL
Interestingly, Vance’s last publicly known phone call with PM Modi was in May 2025, during Operation Sindoor against Pakistan, a conversation the Prime Minister later disclosed in the Lok Sabha.
Modi told the House that he had noticed around four missed calls from the US Vice President and returned the call. According to the Prime Minister, Vance warned him that Pakistan was planning a major attack on India.
PM Modi said he responded by telling Vance, “Our response will be even stronger.”
PM MODI CONGRATULATES VANCE FAMILY
PM Modi also congratulated Vance and his wife on the birth of their son.
The US Vice President and his wife recently welcomed their fourth child, a baby boy named Alec Neel Vance, who was born at the Walter Reed National Military Medical Center in Maryland.
Announcing the birth on X, Vance said Usha and the baby were “happy and healthy” and that their other children were overjoyed to meet their younger brother.
The birth was also historically significant, since it was the first time in over 150 years that a sitting US Vice President welcomed a child.
INDIA-US COMPREHENSIVE GLOBAL STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP
While the exact details of the call are not yet in the public domain, PM Modi mentioned that both leaders discussed ways to expand the India-US Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.
The India-US partnership was formally elevated to a Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership during President Donald Trump’s visit to India in February 2020. It now covers defence and security, trade and investment, critical technologies, space, energy, healthcare, education and people-to-people ties, alongside cooperation through the Quad.
In 2025, India and the US launched the COMPACT and TRUST initiatives to expand cooperation in defence, commerce, AI, semiconductors, quantum technology and other emerging sectors, while setting a target of $500 billion in bilateral trade by 2030.
The two countries have also been negotiating a broader trade agreement, making the partnership one of India’s most wide-ranging strategic relationships.

headline: The Union government is considering a separate legislation to protect the rights of women farmers, on the lines of the Maharashtra Women Farmers Empowerment Act, 2026, S. Mahendra Dev, Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, ...
full_text:
The Union government is considering a separate legislation to protect the rights of women farmers, on the lines of the Maharashtra Women Farmers Empowerment Act, 2026, S. Mahendra Dev, Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, said in Chennai on Friday (August 7, 2026).
Speaking at the inauguration of a conference on ‘Building Gender-just Food, Land, and Water Systems’ at the M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation (MSSRF), Professor Dev described the Maharashtra law as a landmark legislation and said other States could draw inspiration from it. “The Centre is also discussing something similar,” he said.
Highlighting the need to place women at the centre of agrifood systems, he said agriculture should shift from being production-centric to income-centric. This, he said, could be achieved through crop diversification, better post-harvest marketing, food and agro-processing, and institutional support to enhance farmers’ incomes.
Aditi Sunil Tatkare, Maharashtra Minister for Women and Child Development, said the legislation reflected the government’s commitment to recognising women farmers through policy measures. She said the Bill received support across party lines, when it was introduced in the Assembly. “It was an optimistic moment. Implementation will begin this year,” she said, adding that women farmers should also be equipped with financial and digital literacy.
The ongoing Census exercise should capture the contribution of women, particularly their unpaid household work, C. Chandramouli, former IAS officer and member of the MSSRF Board of Trustees, said. He urged enumerators to ensure the collection of gender-disaggregated data, cautioning that gender-blind laws could have far-reaching consequences.
Soumya Swaminathan, Chairperson of MSSRF, said the Foundation’s programmes are built around the three pillars of poverty reduction, gender equity and sustainability. Noting that 2026 has been designated the UN International Year of the Woman Farmer, she said she was pleased that the legislation, first proposed by M.S. Swaminathan in 2011, had finally become a reality.
The Foundation also released its Annual Report for 2025-26.

headline: Manipur govt announces free movement on NH, Imphal-Dimapur bus service to resume
full_text:
Manipur govt announces free movement on NH, Imphal-Dimapur bus service to resume
As part of the government’s ongoing peace-building and reconciliation efforts, the CM visited Kangpokpi district headquarters
Manipur chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh, deputy chief minister Nemcha Kipgen, and Saitu MLA Haokholet Kipgen on Saturday jointly announced the immediate reopening of National Highways for free movement of all communities in the state and announced that the Imphal-Dimapur bus service will be resumed.
The announcement was made at the Kangpokpi district headquarters in Manipur, a district predominantly inhabited by the Kuki-Zo community. Since the Kuki-Zo–Meitei conflict erupted on May 3, 2023, various Kuki-Zo civil bodies, including Kuki-Inpi Manipur (KIM) and the Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU), have prohibited Meiteis from using NH-2, the Imphal-Dimapur highway that passes through Kangpokpi.
Deputy CM Nemcha Kipgen and Haokholet Kipgen are among the 10 Kuki-Zo legislators, including late Vungzagin Valte (victim of the Manipur crisis), who are demanding ‘separate administration’ in the form of a Union territory.
The Manipur crisis between Kuki-Zo and Meitei claimed over 260 lives and more than 60,000 were displaced.
As part of the government’s ongoing peace-building and reconciliation efforts, the CM visited Kangpokpi district headquarters and held meetings with various community leaders. He also inaugurated several development projects and distributed welfare benefits to beneficiaries under different government schemes.
The Chief Minister further said that the boundaries of Manipur were formed by all communities and have been protected by everyone. He added that people from all communities have made sacrifices to safeguard the state’s territory. He said it was unfortunate that some vested interest groups were trying to create confusion among people, but stressed that there is a solution to every crisis.
Also Read:Tapes implicating Biren in violence manipulated, Manipur govt tells SC
Khemchand Singh urged all communities to trust and support each other. He said people should first consider themselves Indians and then Manipuris. He expressed concern that people are now hesitant to identify themselves as Manipuris.
He emphasised that the development of India will remain incomplete without the development of the North East, and that the development of Manipur will be incomplete without the development of Kangpokpi district.
Following Union home minister Amit Shah’s directives for free movement on all highways in Manipur with effect from March 8, 2025, Manipur government had attempted twice for free movement along NH-2 however, protestors in Kangpokpi district disrupted the attempt.
Deputy CM Nemcha Kipgen said that the day marked a historic occasion for everyone. She said the present Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led government has been consistently working to bring development to the state. She added that Manipur can achieve complete development only when both the valley and the hill areas progress equally.
She further said that peace in the state can be ensured through mutual love and trust among communities. She also sought the support of Civil Society Organisations, public leaders, intellectuals and others to bring lasting peace to the state.
Besides, MLA Haokholet Kipgen said he was happy to meet his MLA colleagues after four years. He appealed to all communities and to those who were involved in the conflict to forget the past and return to normalcy.
He also said that National Highway-2 has been the lifeline of all communities in the state.
During the visit, the CM inaugurated a Dialysis Unit at the Community Health Centre and a District Blood Storage facility at Kangpokpi District Hospital. He also handed over ambulances to the chief medical officer, Kangpokpi.
Khemchand Singh also distributed benefits and incentives under various government schemes including PM-JAY, TB Mukt Bharat, Mission Vatsalya, sprayers under the Agriculture Department, PM-Kisan cards, PM Surya Ghar, cheques to IDPs and dialysis patients and solar pumps under PM-KUSUM.

headline: CCTV, security audits: Parliament panel calls for tighter security at J&K tourist spots
full_text:
CCTV, security audits: Parliament panel calls for tighter security at J&K tourist spots
The panel’s suggestions come a year after 25 tourists and a pony operator were killed by three Pakistani terrorists in Pahalgam’s Baisaran meadow last year.
A parliamentary panel on home affairs has recommended developing an integrated security and surveillance framework, incorporating comprehensive CCTV coverage, centralised monitoring facilities, regular vulnerability assessments and periodic security audits at all major tourist destinations in Jammu and Kashmir.
The panel’s suggestions come a year after 25 tourists and a pony operator were killed by three Pakistani terrorists in Pahalgam’s Baisaran meadow on April 22, 2025, triggering a four-day armed conflict between India and Pakistan.
The panel has further asked the government to prescribe and review clear inter-agency standard operating procedures (SOPs) before every peak tourist season to ensure a coordinated and timely response to any security-related incident.
A delegation of department related standing committee on home affairs, led by Dr Radha Mohan Das Agrawal, visited Gulmarg on May 13 and Sonmarg on May 14 to undertake an on-the-spot assessment of the security arrangements at major tourist destinations and to review the preparedness measures in place for ensuring the safety and convenience of tourists.
“The committee appreciates the comprehensive security arrangements put in place by the Union Territory administration and the Jammu and Kashmir Police at Gulmarg and other major tourist and religious destinations...The committee, however, recommends that an integrated security and surveillance framework be developed for all major tourist destinations, incorporating comprehensive CCTV coverage, centralised monitoring facilities, regular vulnerability assessments and periodic security audits,” the panel said in its 260th report, tabled in Parliament on Friday.
Also Read: 3 dead in 10 days: Two terror attacks rock J&K despite high security alert
“The committee further recommends that clear inter-agency standard operating procedures be prescribed and reviewed before every peak tourist season to ensure a coordinated and timely response to any security-related incident,” the report states.
The panel further recommended that the “existing inter-agency coordination mechanism be further institutionalised through a unified command-and-control framework, clearly defined responsibilities and real-time information-sharing protocols”. “Periodic joint security audits and vulnerability assessments should also be conducted, particularly before the commencement of the tourist season and the Yatra, to identify and address emerging security concerns,” it said.
Security at border
Committee members also visited Drass and Kargil on May 15 to assess border security management and operational preparedness of the armed forces.
At Post 43 in Kargil, the committee members interacted with army personnel and obtained a first-hand understanding of border management practices, terrain and other operational contingencies.
For these sensitive sectors, the panel has recommended “sustained investment in integrated intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities, counter-drone systems, secure communication networks and indigenous high-altitude technologies”.

It has further asked the ministry of defence to ensure their “timely procurement, deployment and periodic technological upgradation in all strategically important sectors”. It also recommended accelerated development of all-weather roads, tunnels, bridges, advanced storage facilities, forward logistics hubs and alternative supply routes.

headline: Cost huge political credibility: Omar Abdullah fumes over J&K statehood delay
full_text:
Cost huge political credibility: Omar Abdullah fumes over J&K statehood delay
Omar Abdullah said the delay in restoring Jammu and Kashmir's statehood has triggered anger and hurt his credibility. He urged the Centre to set a clear timeline, saying the Union territory arrangement is unworkable.
Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Saturday expressed deep frustration over the delay in the restoration of statehood to the Union territory, saying the issue has led to widespread anger and disappointment. He said the discontent is not directed only at the PM Modi government, and added that he himself has lost a "huge amount" of political credibility because of the delay.
In an interview, Abdullah said he had tried to build a constructive working relationship with the Union government in the hope of securing the early return of statehood. He said that approach had come at a political cost, and urged the Centre to clearly spell out the conditions and timeline for restoring statehood.
"I put a huge amount of my own political credibility at stake for this. I know for a fact that I've eroded a large part of it," Abdullah said. "I will pay the price for sins that are not mine, and again, I will carry that cross because it's mine to bear," he added.
Criticising the Centre's position that statehood would be restored at an "appropriate time", Abdullah said the process had become like a shifting finish line. "It's like running a marathon. Instead of completing it in 42 km, every time you reach near the finishing line, they keep shifting it," he said. He called on the Centre to define clear parameters so that his administration has a concrete goal.
Abdullah also rejected the argument made in some quarters that statehood cannot be restored until terrorism is fully eradicated. He said his elected government has no control over the security apparatus in Jammu and Kashmir. "The problem with this argument is that you're effectively punishing a government that has no role in this. Militancy does not exist in Jammu and Kashmir because there's an elected government. In fact, we have absolutely nothing to do with the anti-terror mechanism that is in place in J-K right now," he said.
He said such an argument effectively shifts the decision outside India. "You are effectively saying that when Pakistan stops sponsoring terror, you will restore statehood – effectively transferring the decision from our capital to Islamabad," he said.
Highlighting what he called administrative paralysis under the Union territory arrangement, Abdullah described a Union territory with an Assembly as an "abomination". He said institutions such as the JK Power Development Corporation and the Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences remain under the lieutenant governor's control. "There is no worse form of government than a Union territory with an Assembly. Please, by all means, have Union territories, but don't give them assemblies," he said, adding that his Cabinet cannot even choose its own administrative secretaries or appoint an advocate general.
Responding to criticism that he has softened his stand on Article 370, Abdullah said statehood must come first because it is a legal prerequisite for any division of constitutional powers. "Article 370 was basically the division of powers between the Union government and the state government. How can you have a state list when you are not a state? Statehood has to come before (Article) 370 can be restored," he said.
Abdullah also referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public commitment on the issue, saying the prime minister had personally backed the promise during visits to the region. "The prime minister put his personal credibility behind it. He said the restoration of statehood is not just any other promise, it's a 'Modi Ka Wada'. Obviously, he holds that promise to a higher standard, giving it greater weightage," he said.
Reiterating that he has lost "huge political capital" by trusting the Centre's assurances, Abdullah said the disappointment in Jammu and Kashmir is palpable. He urged the Modi government to honour the commitments made to Parliament, the judiciary and the people of the region, and said his government would continue to press for statehood through political dialogue, street protests and demonstrations in the national capital.

headline: Rotten meat, fungus on veggies: Bengaluru's 3-star, 5-star hotels in soup over food safety violations

Rotten meat, fungus on veggies: Bengaluru's 3-star, 5-star hotels in soup over food safety violations
An inspection across 26 hotels uncovered the stark food safety violations in Bengaluru as expired milk, bakery items among other rotten food items were found.
Several luxury hotels in Bengaluru are reportedly under the scanner after the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FDA) department flagged multiple food safety violations ranging from unhygienic storage, fungal growth on vegetables and inadequate segregation of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food items.
The department's Food Safety Wing has launched action against several three-star and five-star hotels in Bengaluru as a special inspection drive across 26 hotels uncovered the stark food safety violations.
Also read: FSSAI cracks down on misleading food and alcohol claims; Dabur Honey, Old Monk and more banned
Rotten meat, chicken, fish and expired bakery products are among some items seized from hotels under scanner, news agency ANI reported, citing FDA statement.
During the inspections, officials found several food safety violations, including non-compliance with FSSAI labelling requirements, improper labelling and misbranding of food products, storage of expired food items, and unhygienic food handling and storage conditions.
The regulatory body has now sent notices to the concerned Food Business Operators (FBOs). Adjudication proceedings under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 will be initiated before the Adjudicating Officer, the report added.
Food samples collected, sent for analysis
The department said that food samples collected during the drive included tea powder, chicken, mutton, fish, edible oil, chilli powder, turmeric powder, tomato sauce, lemon juice, cheese, papad, cashew nuts, ginger, pepper powder, spice powder and milk, among other food products.
Also read: Delhi high court stays FSSAI ban on Dabur selling food products with '100 per cent' claims
The Karnataka Health and Family Welfare Department constituted 30 special teams to conduct surprise inspections at hotels, restaurants and food outlets across Bengaluru and other major locations in the state following a rise in complaints over poor food quality, hygiene and food safety violations.
The inspection drive was launched on the directions of Karnataka Health and Family Welfare Minister UT Khader following several complaints from members of the public, including those shared on social media, alleging unhygienic practices and the sale of substandard food at various eateries.
Hotels under scanner: Check list
The following hotels, according the Food Safety and Drug Administration, are under scanner for violating food safety norms:
- The Lalit Ashok (Annex South): The authorities seized 32 litres of expired milk. They also seized 76 kg of meat and 200 kg of vegetables. -
- Shangri-La Bengaluru: 15 kg of meat seized.
- Four Seasons Hotel Bengaluru: 19 kg of meat seized.
- Vivanta Bengaluru Whitefield: 3 kg of expired bakery products.
- Taj Yeshwantpur: 72 kg of meat/fish seized.
- The Radisson Blu (The Atrium): 105 kg of expired food articles, comprising 50 kg of chicken, 25 kg of meat, 23 kg of fish, and 7 kg of vegetables, seized.
Concerns have been raised over food safety in Karnataka, Over the past few months, several videos and posts shared on social media have alleged unhygienic kitchen conditions, poor food handling and the use of artificial colours in popular dishes such as gobi manchurian, kebabs and other prepared foods. These complaints have prompted the department to step up enforcement measures.
The state government had also carried out a similar enforcement drive last year under "Operation Eat Right" after reports of food poisoning and the use of artificial colouring in food products. During that campaign, several hotels and food establishments were inspected, notices were issued to violators and penalties were imposed for non-compliance with food safety standards.

The defence panel urged the Centre to subsidise Sainik School fees for EWS students and introduce scholarships for girl cadets, citing gaps in the ministry’s response.
The parliamentary standing committee on defence has reiterated its recommendations to make Sainik Schools more affordable and inclusive, after noting that the defence ministry had “not furnished any reply or comment” on key proposals, including extending tuition fee reimbursement, scholarships for girl cadets, and greater financial support for economically weaker students.
In its report on the analysis of the action taken by the ministry regarding its March 2026 recommendations, tabled in Parliament on Friday, the committee reiterated that the Centre should extend reimbursement of tuition fees for Sainik School cadets joining the National Defence Academy (NDA) and Naval Academy (NA) from the current Classes 11 and 12 to Classes 9 to 12, arguing that the move would “motivate” the cadets of Sainik Schools to join the NDA, NA and other defence-related establishments and “benefit” in increasing the intake for the NDA and NA.
The report comes nearly five months after the panel, in its March report, urged the ministry to address the issue of rising fees in Sainik Schools on a priority basis. At the time, it had recommended creating a dedicated fund to provide financial assistance or special concessions for students from middle-class, lower middle-class and low-income families so that deserving candidates are not denied admission because of an unaffordable fee structure. It had also sought reforms aimed at greater inclusivity, fee rationalisation and wider access to Sainik Schools.
Reviewing the ministry’s response, however, the 31-member committee headed by BJP MP Radha Mohan Singh said several of its recommendations had gone unanswered.
“The Ministry has not furnished any reply or comment” on enhancing the Central government’s share in scholarship and incentive schemes, the committee noted, asking the Centre to increase its contribution “wherever possible” to provide “holistic support” to Sainik School students. It also observed that the ministry had not responded to its recommendation for introducing a special scholarship scheme for girl cadets and asked it to review the existing scholarship policy to encourage more girls to join the armed forces. The ministry had said scholarships are currently administered by state governments, with varying rates across states, and that it has requested states and UTs to adopt a uniform scholarship structure.
The committee also renewed its push for greater financial support to economically weaker students. While the ministry maintained that the existing reservation policy was “satisfactory” because there is no reservation for economically weaker sections (EWS) in Kendriya Vidyalayas or Navodaya Vidyalayas, the panel was unconvinced.
Acknowledging “the social background of the students”, the committee reiterated that the ministry should review the Sainik Schools Society Rules & Regulations, 1997, to introduce provisions for exemption, minimisation or subsidisation of fees for students from the EWS category. Such a step, it said, “will certainly create a milestone by way of enabling desirous students getting an opportunity to serve the nation.”
The report also flagged the ministry’s response on girls’ education in Sainik Schools.
While welcoming progress in hostel infrastructure—21 schools now have girls’ hostels and construction is underway in nine others—the committee noted that the ministry had “not furnished any reply or comments regarding steps taken for incrementally increasing the number of all-girls Sainik Schools.” It reiterated that more all-girls Sainik Schools would “surely pave the way for intake of more female officers in the NDA course along with other areas of defence-related institutions/organisations” and sought details of the ministry’s plans in the next action taken statement.
The committee also reviewed progress in the government’s ambitious plan to establish 100 new Sainik Schools under the public-private partnership (PPP) model. It welcomed the increase in the number of schools signing Memorandums of Agreement—from 64 in March to 80 now—and noted that 58 schools are operational in PPP mode. However, it again asked the ministry to establish a dedicated mechanism for faster disposal of pending applications, set up a high-powered committee to remove implementation bottlenecks, and prepare a comprehensive action plan to ensure at least one new Sainik School is established in every state and Union Territory.
There are 91 operational Sainik Schools in the country, including 33 traditional institutions run under the Sainik Schools Society and 58 new schools established under the Centre’s PPP-based New Sainik Schools initiative. Both run classes from Class 6 to 12. According to rules, traditional Sainik Schools raise fees by 10% annually, with 2025-26 annual charges at several schools ranging from about ₹1.7 lakh to ₹2 lakh, including boarding and other expenses. New Sainik Schools under the PPP model have no uniform fee structure, but the Centre provides 50% fee support, capped at ₹40,000 a year, to up to half the students in Classes 6 to 12 on a merit-cum-means basis.

headline: Anantapur MP Ambica Lakshminarayana has urged Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari to expedite various works related to national highways in the district.

Anantapur MP Ambica Lakshminarayana has urged Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari to expedite various works related to national highways in the district.
The MP submitted representation to Mr. Gadkari on various issues pertaining to development of road connectivity in the district, including expansion of National Highways, and construction of service roads, link roads, and underpasses.
Mr. Lakshminarayana sought priority to be given to expansion of Hyderabad–Bengaluru National Highway (NH-44). He said that the NH-44 connecting Hyderabad and Bengaluru is one of the busiest national highways in the country and explained that traffic congestion and accidents frequently occur on this route as the volume of traffic exceeds its capacity.
Although detailed project reports (DPRs) for widening the road were prepared in the past, work has not yet commenced, the MP said and requested the immediate granting of administrative and financial sanctions so that expansion work could begin on a priority basis. The MP requested Mr. Gadkari to expedite the tendering process for the Gooty-Guntakal National Highway and initiate the work as soon as possible.
He said that local residents are facing severe difficulties due to the absence of a service road along a stretch of approximately 750 metres from the Sakshi office underpass to the Prasannayapalli underpass within Anantapur town limits. He explained that this situation increases the risk of accidents, as people are forced to cross the main highway. Similarly, the MP suggested that the proposed vehicular underpass at Prasannayapalli be relocated from its currently designated site to a spot near the main crossroads.
Mr. Lakshminarayana also urged the Central government to sanction funds for the construction of an “East Bypass” connecting NH-44, NH-42, and NH-544D, aiming for a permanent solution to Anantapur city’s traffic issues. The proposal involves connecting the Anantapur–Tadipatri road with the Anantapur–Chennai road which would enable the diversion of cement lorries and other heavy transport vehicles away from the city center reducing traffic congestion and improving transportation efficiency.
The MP said his primary objective is to provide safe and modern transportation facilities to the people of the Anantapur parliamentary constituency. He expressed optimism that the Central government would favorably consider these proposals and take immediate action as the implementation of these projects would provide a permanent solution to traffic issues in Anantapur city, improve commuting facilities for the public, and pave the way for industrial, commercial, and economic development.

Supriya Sule said foreign funding should not automatically be treated with suspicion
NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule on Saturday opposed the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 in its present form, urging the Centre either to withdraw the proposed legislation or refer it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) for wider discussion.Sule, the Lok Sabha MP from Baramati, said all political parties should be given an opportunity to examine the contentious legislation before Parliament takes it up for consideration. She cautioned the government against rushing the bill through Parliament, amid reports that it could be discussed and passed next week.âWe reject and disagree with the present form of the FCRA bill. If the government is not ready to withdraw the bill, then it should send it to a JPC. In a strong democracy, merely opposing something is not enough; we also have to sit together and discuss it,â she said.
The proposed legislation seeks to establish a designated authority for the vesting, supervision, management and disposal of foreign contributions and assets in cases involving cancellation, surrender or expiry of an organisationâs FCRA registration.The bill also provides for provisional and permanent vesting of such assets.
Critics have argued that the proposed changes could give the government greater control over organisations receiving foreign contributions.
âForeign funding cannot always be viewed with suspicionâ
Sule said foreign funding should not automatically be treated with suspicion, arguing that overseas contributions can support legitimate work in areas such as healthcare and education.She said action should be taken if foreign funds are linked to illegal activities such as drug trafficking or terrorism, but questioned the rationale for viewing every foreign-funded organisation negatively.âThere are organisations such as the Gates Foundation and USAID that have been doing good work for many years. Why should we look at every foreign-funded organisation with a bad eye?â she said.She also compared foreign funding with money sent home by Indians living abroad, arguing that the source of money alone should not determine whether it is viewed negatively.According to official figures, 13,520 entities received foreign remittances totalling Rs 55,741 crore between 2019 and 2022.As of July 15, 2026, there were 14,449 active FCRA registrations, while 22,498 registrations had been cancelled and 15,212 had expired.The FCRA regulates the receipt and utilisation of foreign contributions by NGOs, charitable institutions, educational bodies, religious trusts and other organisations.
Sule backs youth protests, questions party symbol decisions
Sule also commented on the ongoing protests by students, saying young people should not face such treatment while seeking education.âWhat happened at Jantar Mantar should not happen anywhere in the country. Our children want to study and this is happening to them. I read that ministers from Jharkhand have ordered an inquiry into it,â she said.She also backed Uddhav Thackeray in the dispute over the Shiv Sena's name and election symbol, arguing that party organisations and constitutions should be considered while deciding control of political parties.On the NCP dispute, Sule said the legal battle remained unresolved and alleged that her party had been waiting for a hearing.âSharad Pawar is the founder president of the NCP and injustice has been done to him. We have been asking for a date for a long time, but why are we not getting a date?â she said.
Sule also criticised the Maharashtra government's approach to farm loan waivers and called for political criticism to remain focused on issues rather than becoming personal.On the proposed delimitation legislation, Sule said it would be premature to comment before the bill was introduced. She added that the NCP (SP) would discuss the legislation with its alliance partners once it came before Parliament.Sule further said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had agreed to meet NCP (SP) MPs on Monday to discuss issues concerning their constituencies, amid the opposition's contention that Parliament was not functioning properly.

headline: âNaturalâ, âhealthyâ, âorganicâ, âheart-friendlyâ, âhigh proteinâ and âzero maidaâ often persuades a shopper before the packet is even turned over. In a spate of notices sent in the past month, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has...
full_text:
âNaturalâ, âhealthyâ, âorganicâ, âheart-friendlyâ, âhigh proteinâ and âzero maidaâ often persuades a shopper before the packet is even turned over. In a spate of notices sent in the past month, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has asked several brands whether their front-of-pack promises say more than the product can support.FSSAI has issued notices to food businesses across categories including breads, chocolates, juices, cooking oils, noodles, supplements, packaged water and caffeinated drinks. The claims questioned range from â100% naturalâ and âorganicâ to immunity, detoxification, disease reduction and energy-boosting promises. Since these are notices rather than final rulings, the issues remain subject to the companiesâ replies and regulatory examination. TOI reached out to FSSAI over e-mail, but was yet to receive a response.The scrutiny comes as Indiaâs health-and-wellness food market expands and brands compete for shoppers seeking healthier choices. Experts say the front of a packet increasingly functions as advertising, while the information needed to judge the product â ingredients, sugar, fat, sodium and additives â is usually on the back.
Former FSSAI CEO Pawan Kumar Agarwal says consumers rarely read or fully understand the mandatory information panel.
Marketing teams therefore have a powerful incentive to foreground attractive words, sometimes stretching the meaning permitted by regulation. For large companies, he argues, penalties may need to be linked to turnover or the commercial gain from a misleading claim rather than treated as a routine cost.Nutrition experts call this the âhealth haloâ effect: one positive phrase can make the entire product appear healthier and reduce the buyerâs inclination to examine it critically. A packet labelled ânaturalâ can still be high in sugar or sodium. âSugar-freeâ does not automatically mean low-carbohydrate. âOrganicâ requires certification; it is not merely a lifestyle description. Disease-treatment or prevention claims require scientific and regulatory support.AIIMS dietician Monita Gahlot advises shoppers to start with the ingredient list, which records ingredients in descending order by weight. The nutrition panel should then be checked for total and added sugars, saturated and trans fats, sodium, protein and carbohydrates. Serving sizes deserve particular attention: a modest-looking number can be based on a portion far smaller than what people normally consume.
The clearest warning sign, food-testing expert Ashwin Bhadri says, is a bold front claim that is not supported or adequately explained elsewhere on the label. The simplest consumer rule is therefore to turn the packet over before deciding.Food author Krish Ashok argues that companies are not acting in a vacuum. Consumers increasingly seek a purchasable shortcut to good health. Products labelled âhigh proteinâ, âlow GIâ, âA2â or âheart-healthyâ can offer the feeling of making a healthy choice without the slower work of eating fewer ultra-processed foods, increasing fibre and protein, exercising and sleeping well.That is why tighter enforcement alone will not end the health halo. Brands must make precise, evidence-backed claims, but consumers must also stop treating the front of a packet as nutritional advice.

She specializes in health and heritage reporting, expertly simplifying complex health information to make it engaging and understandable for readers. Her deep dives into heritage topics are well-researched, resulting in captivating narratives that resonate with her audience. Over the years, she has worked in Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh and West UP, gaining diverse on-ground experience that shapes her storytelling.

headline: Centre mulling framework to check ‘offensive’ OTT content via review panel
full_text:
Centre mulling framework to check ‘offensive’ OTT content via review panel
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting is considering a statutory framework to regulate OTT content considered offensive to society’s moral standards.
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB) is considering a statutory framework to regulate OTT content considered offensive to society’s moral standards, according to a parliamentary committee report tabled in the Lok Sabha by BJP MP Satish Kumar Gautam on Friday. The proposed framework may also provide for an independent post-release review panel to examine flagged content and recommend corrective action.
The development was disclosed by the Home Ministry on August 7 in its response to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs, which had examined the regulation of OTT platforms and the protection of children from inappropriate content.
Also Read I Tourism ministry's partnership with Netflix, YouTube can create wonders: Shekhawat
Regulation of programmes on OTT platforms
According to the report, seen by HT, a “comprehensive statutory framework mechanism” to regulate programmes aired on OTT platforms that are offensive to societal moral standards is under consideration.
The committee has recommended setting up an independent “post release review panel” comprising experts from child development, education, law, social sciences and civil society.
Explaining the panel’s role, the committee report said, “...the Post Release Review Panel will watch the flagged or trending content post release based on user complaints submitted through a standardised grievance mechanism. The Committee recommends that the Panel shall devise suitable norms and guidelines keeping in view the cultural ethos and sensitivity of the country. The Committee further recommends that the panel may also workout suitable penalties in case of infringement of these norms/guidelines.”
Also Read I ‘Dhurandhar was the most-watched non-English movie in the world this year’: Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos
Age verification and parental controls
The committee has also recommended that the proposed statutory framework include technology-enabled age verification and stronger parental controls that go beyond simple self-declaration to prevent minors from accessing age-inappropriate content. It has also suggested penalties for non-compliance.
The report, however, does not specify a timeline for introducing the proposed framework or indicate whether the government has finalised its structure.
The committee noted that the current regulatory framework under the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, relies largely on self-regulation and a three-tier grievance redressal mechanism.

headline: Attempt to murder charge against passenger who tried to open flight exit midair
full_text:
Attempt to murder charge against passenger who tried to open flight exit midair
Police added an attempt to murder charge against a Batik Air passenger accused of trying to open an emergency exit on a Kochi-bound flight. Investigators are now examining his mental condition, motive and the risk posed to passengers and crew.
Police have added an attempt to murder charge against a passenger accused of trying to open the emergency exit of a Kuala Lumpur-Kochi flight, damaging its window panel and threatening fellow passengers and cabin crew, officials said on Saturday. Investigators are also carrying out a detailed probe into what led to the incident.
The passenger, identified as Jamsheer Athanikkal of Koottanad in Palakkad, was travelling on Batik Air flight OD231 from Kuala Lumpur to Kochi on Wednesday. Police said his actions on board endangered the safety of those on the flight before the cabin crew intervened and restrained him. He was arrested after the flight landed at the airport on Thursday.
Officials at the Nedumbassery police station said the case was first registered under Section 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for criminal intimidation, Section 11A of the Aircraft Act for violating safety or security directions, and Section 118(e) of the Kerala Police Act for acts endangering public safety. "However, as the act of the accused could have endangered the lives of the co-passengers, we have evoked an attempt to murder charge against him. He has to be questioned in detail as part of the probe," an officer said.
Police said they would move the Angamaly Judicial First Class Magistrate on Monday, seeking Athanikkal's custody for further questioning. "We will also file a petition to conduct a test to ascertain his mental condition," an officer said. During the initial interrogation after his arrest, Athanikkal allegedly told police that he had felt like dying while travelling on the flight.
According to the police, there was no apparent provocation during the flight that could have triggered his behaviour. Officials said his health history and that of his relatives were also being examined as part of the probe. "The statements of other passengers on the flight will be recorded. We are also trying to obtain the statement of the cabin crew members, who are currently abroad," the officer said. Police also said Athanikkal had turned violent when he was produced before the magistrate.
Police said Athanikkal had been working in Malaysia at a company owned by his friend for the past 10 years and was travelling to Kerala to see his newborn child. Officials said other state and central agencies were also collecting information about him.
"If any evidence emerges during the investigation, we will invoke fresh charges and refer the matter to other agencies for a detailed investigation," the officer said. The case now centres on the added attempt to murder charge as police continue to examine the motive, his condition and the events on board the flight.

headline: HT archives: ‘Quit India’ begins, British crack down with tear gas squibs, lathis, arrests
full_text:
HT archives: ‘Quit India’ begins, British crack down with tear gas squibs, lathis, arrests
Yet, the crackdown failed to dampen the spirit of the movement, instead inspiring a new generation of young leaders.
By the summer of 1942, India’s patience with its colonial masters appeared to have run its course. Lord Linlithgow had plunged India into World War II without consulting Indian political representatives or provincial ministries, triggering tremendous unrest and the en-masse resignation of Congress-ruled provincial governments.
Successive debacles by Allied Powers in East Asia had brought Japanese troops to the gates of erstwhile Burma, British promises of eventual self-governance had repeatedly dissolved into stonewalling, and the failure of Sir Stafford Cripps – who only offered dominion status after the war, expressly ruled out independence, and refused to commit to a clear timeline – had frustrated even the moderates within the Congress and convinced its leadership that further negotiation with London or the viceroy was futile.
Against this backdrop, the mood in the Congress was hardening. It was clear that drastic action was the only recourse for the nationalist movement. On August 8, 1942, the All India Congress Committee met in erstwhile Bombay and passed the Quit India resolution, demanding immediate British withdrawal from the country. That evening, Mahatma Gandhi delivered his memorable call, “Do or Die.”
The British response was immediate. Within hours, the entire Congress leadership — including Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel — was arrested, and the party banned. “The police in Bombay opened fire about a dozen times in different localities on August 9, 1942. Five persons have been killed and twenty others received bullet wounds, while thirty-five more, including police, received injuries resulting from stone-throwing. The demonstrations marked the start of the “Quit India” movement against British rule, launched after the Congress resolution adopted in Bombay on August 8,” this newspaper reported on August 10, 1942.
The repression was not limited to Maharashtra but quickly spread across the country even as the second-rung leadership of the Congress – people like Ram Manohar Lohia, Jayaprakash Narayan, and Sucheta Kripalani — took over coordination and running the movement. Hundreds of strikes and hartals, walkouts and mass demonstrations crippled major cities.
“Curfew has been enforced in Bombay…In the city, 149 persons, including Mrs. Kasturba Gandhi and Mr. Pyarelal, have been arrested so far, while elsewhere in the country Dr. Rajendra Prasad and Mr. Vinoba Bhave were also taken into custody. The police had to resort to firing in Poona and Ahmedabad also. In Poona, one man was killed and another seriously injured when the police opened fire near the Congress House, and in Ahmedabad the military was called out to deal with the crowd which had gathered on Gandhi Road, where one man was killed and another injured as the result of firing,” HT reported.
Yet, despite the absence of front-tier leadership, ordinary people rose to the occasion, fighting against the colonial police force and often deploying novel agitation tactics. One such instance unfolded at the famous Shivaji Park.
“Police parties and large crowds were engaged in outwitting each other for over four and a half hours at Shivaji Park on August 9, where originally it was announced that Mahatma Gandhi would address a public meeting that evening. Despite his arrest thousands of people streamed into the park, where a posse of armed police, tear gas squads and some lathi police were stationed to prevent the holding of any public meeting. The park was too big to be cleared of the crowds that repeatedly dodged the police, and frequent use of tear gas squibs did not result in their complete dispersal. With buckets of water and sand the dispersed crowds re-entered the park and smothered the tear gas squibs that were thrown on them. There were a few minor clashes between the police and sections of the crowd that kept on shouting Congress slogans, and the police, it is stated, fired a few shots, one person being removed to hospital with a bullet wound. At about 8.30 p.m. the crowd had completely left the park and the police also withdrew,” HT reported.
Yet, the crackdown failed to dampen the spirit of the movement, instead inspiring a new generation of young leaders. In the absence of central leadership, resistance turned local. Students walked out of colleges. Workers struck in mills and factories. Protestors blocked railway lines, cut telegraph wires, and torched police stations and government offices.
By the time Gandhi was released one May morning in 1944, the tide had turned, both globally and nationally. The Allied Powers had their boots on the neck of the Axis Powers. And in India, the question was no longer whether the British would leave India, but when.

headline: The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) says its spending on power purchases in 2026-27 could see an increase by ₹1,596.28 crore. As per a revised claim made by the power utility before the Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission, the estima...
full_text:
The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) says its spending on power purchases in 2026-27 could see an increase by ₹1,596.28 crore. As per a revised claim made by the power utility before the Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission, the estimate on power purchase spending in 2026-27 has been revised to ₹13,344.11 crore. Earlier, the Commission had given provisional approval for making power purchases for ₹11,747.83 crore in 2026-27 while clearing a multi-year tariff (MYT) petition.
The latest projection is part of a petition on mid-year performance review and revised forecast for the period from 2024-25 to 2026-27 which the KSEB has submitted to the Commission for approval. The Commission has scheduled a hearing on the KSEB’s petition on August 18 in Thiruvananthapuram.
The spotlight is back on KSEB’s power purchase expenses as Kerala was passing through a crisis in meeting the peak demand just before the southwest monsoon regained strength over the State. Kerala’s internal generation meets about 30% of the demand. The balance requirement is met through power purchases from multiple sources including central generating stations (CGS), independent power producers (IPP), power traders and power exchanges.
1,187.66 mu deficit
The KSEB has noted in the petition that it expects to face a deficit of 1,187.66 million units (mu) in 2026-27. While the total energy requirement of the State is estimated at 33,813.53 mu, the availability from all sources is likely to be 32,625 mu. Over the years, the power utility’s spending on power purchases has increased, especially with Kerala experiencing higher demand during the evening peak hours. The power purchase expenditure of the KSEB in 2023-24 stood at ₹12,982.59 crore
The projected spending for 2026-27 includes ₹1,109.07 crore on short-term purchases through the Union Power Ministry’s Discovery of Efficient Electricity Price (DEEP) e-bidding and e-reverse auction portal for meeting the peak deficit.

headline: ‘Degree means nothing in India today’: Rahul talks of ‘dard’, ‘data’ and 'daulat' at ‘Chhatron ki Goonj’ event
full_text:
‘Degree means nothing in India today’: Rahul talks of ‘dard’, ‘data’ and 'daulat' at ‘Chhatron ki Goonj’ event
Rahul Gandhi said a degree certificate “means nothing in India today” because it does not lead to a job.
Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on Saturday spoke about “dard” (pain), “data”, and “daulat” (wealth) at the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj, saying that degree certificates “mean nothing” in India today.
Gandhi spoke before a large gathering of students and competitive exam aspirants, who turned up at Kayastha Pathshala (KP) Ground despite waterlogging and muddy patches.
“This evening I want to speak to you about dard (pain), data, and daulat (wealth)…. Data aapka, dard aapka aur daulat inki (Your data, your pain, but their wealth),” he said.
The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha said India's 40 crore youths constitute its "greatest strength", adding that while there is much talk about America, China and Russia, "India's youths are unparalleled."
Rahul Gandhi also raised his concerns about the debasement of educational credentials in the country. He said a degree certificate “means nothing in India today” because it does not lead to a job.
“All doors of employment are closed in India,” Gandhi said.
"People's Data is snatched away and handed over to big companies. Then you're told—Make reels and content. But know this—reel is the new addiction of the 21st century. After all this, the youth are told: 'Work at Blinkit, Uber. Do labour, make reels, but you can't get a job in this country,'" he added.
A warm welcome
Before his address in the evening, Rahul Gandhi was given a warm welcome at Prayagraj airport by party leaders and workers, including Ujjwal Raman Singh, the MP representing the Allahabad parliamentary constituency.
The KP Ground, where the interaction took place, was waterlogged after overnight rain. Party workers were seen using buckets to drain the accumulated water in preparations for the event, news agency PTI reported.
JCB machines were also deployed to spread limestone and sand across the waterlogged patches, while a road roller was used to level the ground.
