Stalin, speaking on the Cauvery-Mekedatu issue, asked, “What is your fear and hesitation in holding the all-party meeting? He said Karnataka had shown unity, held an all-party meeting on the issue and considered stakeholders’ representations.
On the CM’s comments that the Kuruvai cultivation relief package had been granted, Stalin said: “The special package you provided to farmers is ₹134 crore which is a standard special package provided. Now, the farmers are asking for drought relief funds, one must understand the difference between these two.”

headline: Chhattisgarh horror: 65-year-old man held for rape-murder of woman, killing her infant daughter
full_text:
Chhattisgarh horror: 65-year-old man held for rape-murder of woman, killing her infant daughter
The cops arrested the accused, identified as Bhikariram Nagvanshi, on August 6 after weeks of intensive probe, an official said on Saturday.
The Chhattisgarh police arrested a 65-year-old man for the brutal rape and murder of a 35-year-old woman, and for killing her 10-month-old infant daughter, days after the crime.
The cops arrested the accused, identified as Bhikariram Nagvanshi, on August 6 after weeks of intensive probe, an official said on Saturday. The crime had taken place on July 15 on a remote farm in Chhaparani village in Raigarh district under the Lailunga police station limits, PTI news agency reported.
The woman's cousin lodged a complaint at Lailunga police station on July 16, after she was found critically injured and her daughter dead at the spot, Raigarh Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Shashi Mohan Singh said. The SSP said that the crime had occurred in an isolated location with no eyewitnesses, posing a major challenge to the investigation.
Also Read | Chhattisgarh: 8 juveniles escape Mahasamund observation home; search underway
Suspicious injury marks on accused's body led to arrest
SSP Singh said that police had camped in Chhaparapani village for the probe, questioning residents and deploying informants to gather intelligence. Meanwhile, teams from the police, Forensic Science Laboratory, and the dog squad had also been brought un to inspect the crime scene and collect physical evidence.
The Raigarh police cracked the complex case through suspicious injury marks on the alleged accused, following which they pieced together forensic evidence, leading to the arrest of Nagvanshi, a resident of Kodasiya village. Evidence has begun pointing towards the accused during the investigation early on, but he had initially denied any involvement in the crime, according to PTI.
However, officers later noticed a suspicious injury mark on his hand, an official said, and he confessed to the crime upon further interrogation. The accused was on Friday produced before a local court, which remanded him to 14 days in judicial custody.
Woman sustained severe injuries to head, face; was attacked with heavy object
The victim was found with severe injuries to her head and face, indicating that she had been attacked with a heavy object. The 35-year-old, who was a widow allegedly suffering from mental health issues, lived on the farm with her infant daughter, Raigarh SSP Singh said.
She was rushed for medical assistance but succumbed to her injuries during treatment, Singh said, adding that a case was initially registered under section 103(1) (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), PTI reported. According to police, the accused entered the victim's house on the night of July 15 and found her asleep next to her daughter. When she resisted his attempt to rape her, Nagvanshi repeatedly struck her on the head and face with a brick until she lost consciousness, following which he sexually assaulted her.
When the infant started crying, the accused allegedly strangled her and struck her too with the brick, killing her on the spot, PTI cited police as saying. After the crime, Nagvanshi fled to his hideout through the fields, and changed his bloodstained dhoti, which was later recovered by the police. Nagvanshi has been held on charges of rape and double murder.

headline: ‘Most passengers discharged, DGCA investigating’: Ram Mohan Naidu on Air India flight turbulence
full_text:
‘Most passengers discharged, DGCA investigating’: Ram Mohan Naidu on Air India flight turbulence
Speaking on the medical status of those affected, the Minister noted that the majority of injured passengers were treated and released shortly after landing.
Union Minister of Civil Aviation Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu on Saturday provided an update following the severe air turbulence encountered by an Air India Phuket-Delhi flight on August 4, assuring the public that the situation is being handled with urgency and care.
Speaking on the medical status of those affected, the Minister noted that the majority of injured passengers were treated and released shortly after landing.
"The turbulence incident that happened, most of the passengers in the first few hours only, were discharged from the hospital," Naidu stated. "Around 24 passengers were facing some kind of medical inconvenience. So they were taken to the hospital; thorough check-ups have been done for them, and most of them have been discharged."
While most passengers have returned home, four crew members remain hospitalised under medical observation. "4 crew members are still there, and we are continuously watching their medical condition and the hospitals. Air India: Everyone is providing full support," he added.
Also Read: Why always Air India: Misinformation takes flight as airline meets turbulence
Addressing the cause of the mid-air scare, Naidu confirmed that the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has stepped in to determine how the incident occurred.
"As far as how the incident happened, the DGCA is investigating it, and we still have to know the final report on that. So we are waiting for that," the Minister explained.
Highlighting broader aviation safety and regulatory reforms, Naidu emphasised that the government is proactively addressing modern industry needs rather than relying on reactive measures or lagging behind Western standards.
"We have created different committees within the working groups within DGCA to look into different ones. Safety is also an important aspect. Navigation is one. Vertiports are one," Naidu said, noting that regulators are continuously engaging with industry stakeholders as technology evolves.
"The statement I want to make is that we are not waiting for other countries or the West to look at what guidelines they are making and replicate them. We are moving ahead at our own pace and looking at how the innovation is happening in India. So I feel the timelines are going to be reduced for us," he said.
Meanwhile, on Friday, a passenger on board an Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi has filed a complaint with the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), alleging that the aircraft suffered a sudden drop during the flight and that two elderly members of his family sustained injuries.
Also Read: ‘Flight dropped 300 feet’: Woman recalls terrifying Air India Phuket-Delhi turbulence
According to the complaint filed through the AirSewa portal, the Air India flight operating from Phuket to Delhi on August 4 was carrying the passenger's family of six when the aircraft experienced a sudden drop of around 300 feet at about 9:30 am IST.
The passenger alleged that passengers were thrown against the cabin ceiling during the incident. He said his 62-year-old mother-in-law, Renu Raniwala, suffered a rib injury and a suspected spinal injury, while his 64-year-old father-in-law, Mukul Raniwala, sustained bruises
The flight encountered turbulence during cruise on August 4, resulting in a brief change in altitude and leaving a small number of passengers and crew members with minor injuries.
Visuals from the airport showed ambulances stationed outside the terminal gate, with several passengers seen being assisted out in wheelchairs, while others appeared with bandages on their heads before being taken for medical evaluation.

headline: Former Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan on Saturday (August 8, 2026) said he had personally sought permission from Prime Minister Narendra Modi to concede the demands of the protesters led by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) recently at the Jan...
full_text:
Former Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan on Saturday (August 8, 2026) said he had personally sought permission from Prime Minister Narendra Modi to concede the demands of the protesters led by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) recently at the Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. Who are Gen Zs? I believe they are our own. It was never a matter of personal prestige for me,” he said, addressing a gathering attended by Padma Shri awardees in Sambalpur, Odisha.
“If around two crore children are born in India every year, there will be nearly 20 crore young people in the 15-25 [years] age group over a decade. They carry the responsibility of making India a ‘Vishwaguru’ and ensuring global welfare,” Mr. Pradhan said.
“I come from a land where many eminent personalities have made great sacrifices, and I have inherited those values. Holding the responsibility of Education Minister is nothing in comparison,” he said.
“I met the Prime Minister and sought his permission to accept [the protesters’ demands]. The Prime Minister agreed and later interacted with the youth. Nothing is above the nation’s interest. Fulfilling the hopes and aspirations of the younger generation is part of the values upheld by the great personalities from this land,” the MP from the Sambalpur Lok Sabha constituency said.

headline: Kerala should become a model State that can ensure equality, dignity, and equal opportunity for all the children with disabilities, the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has said.
full_text:
Kerala should become a model State that can ensure equality, dignity, and equal opportunity for all the children with disabilities, the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has said.
The recommendation has been made in a report on challenges — physical, emotional, intellectual, and developmental — faced by disabled children. It was was submitted by the commission to the government earlier this year.
The report, prepared following consultations with functionaries at State and district levels, urges the State to adopt a rights-based approach, calling for viewing them not just as beneficiaries of services but also recognising them as citizens with rights.
The commission has recommended a single-window system to ensure that schemes for children with disabilities and benefits —including social security pension, scholarships, treatment-rehabilitation aid, travel allowance, and distribution of assistive devices— reach them in a transparent and time-bound manner. At present, these are implemented through various departments, leading to lack of coordination, delays, complications in documents, and lack of information.
The report underscores the importance of early detection of disabilities in children to provide comprehensive treatment and rehabilitation. Services of experts such as paediatricians, clinical psychologist, psychiatrist, and therapists should be ensured permanently in taluk hospitals
Mobile screening teams should be formed for direct screening of children in anganwadis and schools in areas that are remote or difficult to access such as hilly regions.
Home care, palliative care, and other services should be ensured at the doorstep of children who have severe disabilities or are bed-ridden.
Disability certificates and UDID (Unique Disability Identification Card) card should be made available to eligible children. Steps should also be taken to organise camps at the panchayat level to avoid delays in this respect, the report adds.
The report calls for appointing special educators in all government, aided, and recognised unaided schools to ensure school participation and social inclusion of differently abled children. Need-based support will prevent them the children from dropping out of school, it says.
It moots an inclusive evaluation system that considers each child’s abilities, individual education goals, and reasonable accommodation.
Another recommendation is setting up of district disability centres in order for services such as early identification, therapies, counselling, educational support, and training for parents can be provided under a single umbrella.
It stresses the need for police stations that have personnel who have received training in accepting complaints related to children with disabilities, taking their statements, and conducting investigations. Steps should also be taken to provide the services of sign language interpreter, special educator, and support persons to help them in investigations related to them, the commission recommends.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the organisation stood in “complete solidarity” with the protesting students in Jharkhand as a party delegation arrived in the state to extend support to the protesters.
He said the delegation, led by Mukesh and Akshay Shinde, would provide “all forms of support” to the students.
A CJP delegation arrived in Jharkhand to extend support to protesting students.
Govt holds talks with students
The Jharkhand government on Saturday held talks with various outfits amid the massive agitation over the alleged paper leaks in recruitment exams, but failed to break the deadlock as the protesting aspirants decided that their stir would continue until all their demands are met.
A five-member panel of the government, which included state ministers, first met the faction of protesters led by JLKM leader Devendra Nath Mahto, whose fast over the issue entered its seventh day. They then separately met delegations of the Congress-backed NSUI, ACS and JCM.

On Friday night, the government had held similar talks with a delegation of the JPSC/JSSC Reforms Manch.
"Demands of protesting aspirants are genuine; we will place these before Chief Minister Hemant Soren," state minister Sanjay Prasad Yadav, who is a member of the panel set up by the government, said after the back-to-back meetings.
The ruling JMM's students' wing Jharkhand Chhatra Morcha (JCM) placed five demands before the government panel, including the cancellation of the 14th Jharkhand PSC Civil Services Examination.
The NSUI placed six demands before the government, including a CID probe into all JPSC and JSSC examinations under doubt within 90 days and the setting up of Jharkhand Testing Agency (JTA) on the lines of the National Testing Agency, its spokesperson Sanjiv Shah said.
Adivasi Chatra Sangh leader Kartik Oraon said, "We demanded inclusion of tribal and regional languages as qualifying papers in the recruitment examinations, besides cancellation of the tests in which irregularities were found..
The government panel's first meeting was with Mahto's grouping, JPSC JSSC Candidates' Forum, and it lasted around two hours.
"The government assured us of a quick decision to resolve the issues raised by us. However, our protests will continue until all our demands, including cancellation of the 14th JPSC exam, are met," a leader of the forum said.

headline: 'Modi understands language of votes only': Kejriwal reveals plan to pressure Centre over E20 policy
full_text:
'Modi understands language of votes only': Kejriwal reveals plan to pressure Centre over E20 policy
Arvind Kejriwal comments come as part of his solution to pressure the Modi govt to roll back E20 fuel policy.
Aam Aadmi Party leader Arvind Kejriwal on Saturday launched an attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging that he only understands the “language of votes,” and urged everyone to vote BJP out of power in the 2027 Goa assembly polls.
Kejriwal comments come as part of his solution to pressure the Modi govt to roll back E20 fuel policy.
Addressing AAP volunteers in Margao, Kejriwal urged people to unite, saying the BJP's defeat would “shatter PM Modi's arrogance”. He said the drubbing of the BJP in Goa will force the Prime Minister to withdraw the E20 policy.
"Modi ji doesn't listen to anyone. He thinks he will win anyway. He thinks people will vote for him no matter what he does," Kejriwal said.
He had made a similar appeal to the public on Friday at a press conference, stressing that losing the Goa assembly polls would force BJP to withdraw E20 within five days.
“Come together to defeat the BJP in the Goa election and break their overconfidence. I guarantee the government will withdraw E20 within five days of the election result,” he said.
"This time, if the people of Goa come together and defeat the BJP, the results will come on March 10 (2027). And you can quote me on this: 'by March 15, Modi ji will withdraw E20'," he said.
Referring to a conversation he claimed to have had with a person in Goa, Kejriwal said the coastal state's voters could "make Modi sweat" by defeating the BJP, news agency PTI reported.
"If this time Modi ji thinks that the BJP will win Goa....If the people of Goa come together and defeat the BJP, then Modi ji's arrogance will be shattered," he said.
Citing the student protests in New Delhi that forced then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign, Kejriwal underlined that the Centre was compelled to act because it felt public support turning away.
"When it comes to votes, only then will Modi ji understand. He understands only the language of votes, and he does not understand any other language," the AAP national convener said.
‘If you want to save your vehicle…’
Kejriwal hinted that his party will make E20 as one of its mail poll planks, saying, “The key is in your hands. If you want to save your vehicle, your motorcycle, your car, your scooter, then break Modi ji's arrogance once. This time, defeat Modi ji in Goa."
Kejriwal has been one of the most vocal critics of the E20 fuel policy. He had led a march to the prime minister's house with 100 people to submit petitions against ethanol-blended fuel.
The AAP chief alleged that India had “yielded” to US President Donald Trump to purchase “ethanol from the United States,” suggesting a “hidden agenda” behind the government’s continued push for ethanol-blended petrol.

RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s remarks defending Gen Z protesters as “not anti-national” triggered sharp political reactions on Friday, with the Congress accusing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of running the government from behind the scenes, while Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah welcomed Bhagwat’s distinction between opposing the government and opposing the nation. The BJP, meanwhile, backed the RSS chief’s comments and said they should be viewed positively.
Bhagwat made the remarks on Thursday while addressing more than 2,000 students in Mumbai, days after student-led protests over the alleged NEET paper leak led to the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. “If Gen Z is protesting, they are not anti-nationals. They are our own people, our next generation,” he said, adding that the “new generation, Gen Z and Gen Alpha, is more honest than the existing generation” and that an “honest appeal of patriotism and service” resonates with them.
Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said Bhagwat’s remarks only reinforced the Opposition’s allegation that the RSS, and not the elected government, was calling the shots.
“RSS is controlling the government. If he has any sincerity towards Gen Z, let him ask the home minister to resign. Otherwise, at least come to Parliament and apologise to the students and to the Prime Minister also,” Venugopal said.
He also questioned Bhagwat’s silence during the protests. “If he has any sincerity towards the students, he has to contemplate the atrocities that happened against the students. Why is he keeping mum on that? These are all eyewashing,” he added.
Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said students did not require Bhagwat’s endorsement. “They don’t need a certificate from RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat ji,” she told reporters outside Parliament, adding that the youth had raised genuine concerns on their own.
Congress leaders linked Bhagwat’s remarks to Rahul Gandhi’s recent allegation in the Lok Sabha that the RSS controls the education system. During the debate on the Public Examinations (Amendment) Bill, Rahul Gandhi had said, “He never ran the Education Ministry. The RSS runs it.”
Other Congress leaders also questioned the timing of Bhagwat’s outreach. Congress MP Rajeev Shukla said, “Bhagwat ji is saying that students are not traitors... The entire BJP is running a campaign against students and Gen Z, calling them traitors, goons and criminals. Bhagwat ji should express his views to the government.”
Congress MP Manickam Tagore alleged that the RSS had “captured educational institutions”, while MP Imran Masood claimed the leadership realised the issue “far too late” after students had already faced police action. Congress MP Amar Singh accused the BJP of damaging the education system over the past decade.
Samajwadi Party MP Ram Gopal Yadav alleged the BJP had turned to Bhagwat only after being “completely cornered” politically and had sent him to “handle the situation”. Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge said the RSS and BJP were “desperately updating their vocabulary” even though their attitude towards young people remained unchanged.
CPI MP P Sandosh Kumar said the RSS appeared “confused” about its stand, alleging that several BJP leaders had attempted to “tarnish the students’ movement”. He said the protests were not only about the NEET paper leak but reflected wider concerns affecting young people.
In contrast, Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah welcomed Bhagwat’s remarks, saying they recognised an important democratic principle.
“Mohan Bhagwat hasn’t said anything that isn’t true. Opposing the administration or government is not the same as opposing the country. Often, opposing the government turns out to be beneficial for the country because it allows mistakes to be corrected,” Abdullah said.
He urged authorities to stop action against students who participated in the protests, saying, “The youth must be heard and engaged with, rather than being vilified. They have done nothing against the country.”
Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis also backed Bhagwat’s remarks, saying his message was in the interest of the entire country and not confined to any particular political party or organisation. “What RSS Sarsanghchalak says is not just for one party, one group or one organisation. He speaks for our country. I feel that whether it is the ruling side or the Opposition, what he said is in the interest of this nation, for everyone,” Fadnavis said.
The BJP defended Bhagwat’s remarks. Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao said they should be “taken in a very positive spirit”, adding that while young people have the right to protest, they also have a responsibility to respect the law and law enforcement agencies. He also accused the Congress of backing protesting students only after facing public backlash, in Jharkhand and Kerala.

headline: Access to justice begins with dialogue, must ensure dignity and inclusion: CJI Surya Kant
full_text:
Access to justice begins with dialogue, must ensure dignity and inclusion: CJI Surya Kant
The CJI said access to justice cannot be considered meaningful if it is hindered due poverty, disability, language or lack of awareness.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Saturday said public access to justice rests on dialogue, dignity and inclusion, which are also the key objectives of legal aid. The CJI was addressing the Western Zone Regional Conference of the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) in Indore.
CJI Kant said legal aid works with the understanding that people are spoken to and not merely spoken at. It ensures that they are treated as citizens and not mere case numbers. The aim of legal aid is reach the people "wherever they are", rather than expected them "to find their own way to us".
"Access to Justice has never been built by laws alone. It begins with a conversation. Before justice can be delivered, people must feel heard," he was quoted as saying by Bar and Bench.
ALSO READ: Listening to youth is ‘most powerful force’ to prevent protest violence: Supreme Court
Explaining why ensuring dignity matters, the CJI said, "For the ordinary citizen, the experience of justice begins the moment they walk into a legal aid clinic. Long before a judicial order is passed, they have already formed an opinion about the justice system from the manner in which they are received, heard and treated." Hence, it is important to offer a patient explanation and have a respectful conversation.
Stressing on the need for inclusion, the CJI said access to justice cannot be considered meaningful if it is hindered due poverty, disability, language or lack of awareness. "The real test of an institution is not how well it serves those who are able to reach it, but how effectively it reaches those who never can," he said.
To further ease access, the grievances and hardships of different communities should be heard in their own languages, the CJI said.
The Chief Justice termed legal services volunteers as part of "judicial army", who play essential role in taking the government schemes to the grassroots level.
The inaugural session of the conference was attended by Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal, Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, and judges from the Supreme Court and High Courts.
Addressing the event, CM Yadav said the justice system has undergone significant transformations driven by modern technology. "The judicial framework is being revamped through systems such as e-filing, digital records, the 'One Data-One Case' approach, virtual hearings, and modern judicial management," he said.

headline: Cricketer Rishabh Pant seeks land in Uttarakhand, CM Dhami directs officials to help
full_text:
Cricketer Rishabh Pant seeks land in Uttarakhand, CM Dhami directs officials to help
Uttarakhand CM Dhami promises to assist cricketer Rishabh Pant with land acquisition after his three-year struggle to relocate from Delhi.
Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Saturday directed officials to assist cricketer Rishabh Pant with his request to acquire land in the state, after the cricketer said he had been trying for three years to shift his base from Delhi.
“Dear Rishabh, you are the pride of Uttarakhand. Through your brilliant performance and achievements, you have brought glory to Devbhoomi across the country and the world. Your love for your motherland and your desire to return here and contribute is highly commendable. Regarding the matter raised by you, the concerned officials are being directed. They will contact you soon and ensure all possible assistance as per the rules,” Dhami posted on X.
Dhami said Pant belonged to the state and had brought recognition to both Uttarakhand and the country. “Rishabh Pant is from our state. He has brought glory to the country and the state. He is welcome here. Our officials will discuss everything with him. If he requires anything, we will certainly provide it,” Dhami said.
Pant had made the appeal in a late-night post on X, saying he had been trying for the past three years to acquire land in Uttarakhand and shift his base from Delhi, but couldn’t find it.
“It’s a long time for me, especially being local from Uttarakhand. I have been trying to buy land to shift my base from Delhi to Uttarakhand and I couldn’t find anything facilitating and big to live here. I love my Uttarakhand,” Pant wrote.
He said he wanted to return to his native state, build a home and contribute to its development.
“My humble request to you is please help me in land acquisition because nowadays it has become a nightmare with clarity. I want to move back to my native place to help and build around Uttarakhand and I want to shift back to my Pahadi people,” he said.
He requested Dhami to allow him to purchase land from the government so that he could build his first house in his home state.
“It’s been three years, didn’t get any land. Awaiting your answer,” Pant wrote, tagging Dhami.

headline: RSS-linked BMS ‘Yagna’ at Jadavpur University sparks political row
full_text:
RSS-linked BMS ‘Yagna’ at Jadavpur University sparks political row
The ‘yagna’ was performed in the afternoon in front of the administrative building, Aurobindo Building, while classes were being held
A ‘yagna’ performed inside the Jadavpur University (JU) campus on Friday by supporters of the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh (BMS), a trade union affiliated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), has triggered a row in the state.
The ‘yagna’ was performed in the afternoon in front of the administrative building, Aurobindo Building, while classes were being held. However, JU officials clarified that they gave no permission to organise the ‘yagna’.
“No permission was given for the event. The ‘yagna’ was performed under the portico, in front of the main gate of the Aurobindo Building. It is a heritage structure. Also, the university’s visually impaired students regularly come to the building. This is illegal. I will write to the vice-chancellor of the university on Monday,” said Selim Box Mandal, acting registrar of JU.
This comes three months after the BJP came to power in the state, ousting the 15-year-old Trinamool Congress (TMC) regime.
The organisers, however, said that they have been holding protests inside the campus over the past few weeks against various alleged irregularities and the ‘yagna’ was performed so that good sense prevails.
“We have been holding protests against ongoing irregularities in the university. We have written to the high authorities but to no avail. Hence, we performed the ‘yagna’ so that good sense prevails on the authorities and the university campus is purified,” said Asim Mitra, one of the organisers and the working president of the association of university employees in the state.
At least 10 organisations, including those of students, teachers and non-teaching staff, have raised objections against the event alleging that such events would vitiate the academic ambience of the university.
The Jadavpur University Teachers’ Association (JUTA), in a statement, opposed holding the ‘yagna,’ saying it could encourage other religious groups to hold similar events inside the campus.
“There is a paucity of research funds and the buildings need repair. There is funding and will. Those who are trying to divert attention from these problems and created a new one by performing a ‘yagna’ don’t want the development of the university,” the JUTA said in a statement.
The TMC said that attempts to impose the RSS and the Bharatiya Janata Party’s Hindutva agenda will not be accepted.
“BJP has no connection with the values of education or the ethos of Bengal. Does BMS have permission from the University administration to organise such a Yagna? Attempting to impose the RSS/BJP’s Hindutva agenda on the progressive campus of Jadavpur University will not be accepted by the students and stakeholders of the University,” said Nilanjan Das, TMC spokesperson.

headline: Rijiju defends Shah amid Oppn persistent demand for HM’s statement
full_text:
Rijiju defends Shah amid Oppn persistent demand for HM’s statement
Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju strongly defended Union home minister Amit Shah amid the Opposition’s persistent demand for the latter’s statement Shah on the use of pellet guns against students, triggering disruptions and discord for the second straight week in both Houses of Parliament
Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju strongly defended Union home minister Amit Shah amid the Opposition’s persistent demand for the latter’s statement Shah on the use of pellet guns against students, triggering disruptions and discord for the second straight week in both Houses of Parliament. The government blamed the Congress and Opposition MPs for the unruly behaviours but refused to accept the anti-NDA group’s demands.
In the Lok Sabha, Rijiju slammed the Opposition and said Shah is a person whose name makes terrorists and extremists tremble in fear.
“Since this morning, these people have been raising slogans while repeatedly invoking the name of the Home Minister. I wish to state very emphatically that these people create a ruckus and then disappear. Home Minister Shri Amit Shah arrives at Parliament early in the morning and leaves late at night. He remains in Parliament throughout the day. Therefore, their manner of raising slogans is inappropriate,” Rijiju said.
“Secondly, Home Minister Shri Amit Shah is a person whose very name makes terrorists and extremists tremble. On the day the discussion takes place here and the Hon’ble Home Minister delivers his reply, you will not even be able to listen. You dare to invoke the Home Minister’s name! The Minister concerned with the scheduled business is required to be present in the House. You cannot dictate or demand which Minister should attend or who should provide the reply; that is decided by the Government and the Chair,” Rijiju added.
The minister later said, the government’s attempts to pass bills after discussion have not yielded results because the Opposition has not allowed both Houses to function. “The Monsoon Session of Parliament has passed many critical and important Bills so far. But Congress and Opposition MPs are unable to speak due to their own unruly behaviors. I feel sorry for the first time MPs who are losing great opportunities. So, do not blame the government,” he said.
The Lok Sabha cleared the MSME development bill amid din. The bill has already been cleared by the Rajya Sabha on August 3.
The amendments in the MSMED Act have been made to strengthen the legal framework governing the development of the MSME sector, improving the ease of doing business, creating an enabling business environment through decriminalisation, providing institutional mechanisms for promotion of MSMEs and addressing delayed payment issues faced by the Micro and Small Enterprises.
This amendment is aimed at aligning the Act with the changing MSME landscape. The MSME classification based on twin criteria of “Investment in plant/machinery” and “Turnover” has been incorporated in the Act. The Bill provides permanence to the Udyam Registration Portal as a Digital, free, and voluntary registration platform for MSMEs. The registration for MSMEs is voluntary.
On Friday Rajya Sabha was adjourned for the day after the opposition did not budge from its demand for a statement from Shah. In the Lok Sabha Opposition leaders rushed to the Well of the House to press for Shah’s statement.
Birla reminded the Opposition of the significance of August 9—a historic day in the Quit India movement led by Mahatma Gandhi—and said, “The contribution of Mahatma Gandhi is acknowledged not only by India but by the entire world; that is why the world draws inspiration from him. You, too, should draw inspiration from him. Engage in discussion and dialogue, and express your views here to strengthen democracy within the country. Question Hour is a crucial time.”
The government has been reaching out to the opposition parties to support the FCRA and the Delimitation Bills although it is becoming increasingly clear that the bills may not be taken up for discussion in the coming week, said people aware of the details.
On Thursday, Shah had informed Mizoram chief minister Lalduhoma that the FCRA bill will be taken up for discussion on August 12.
“The government has made several attempts to reach out to the opposition, it has heard their concerns about both the FCRA and the Delimitation Bills, but it seems the Opposition does not want the bills to be taken up…” said a senior BJP lawmaker.
Opposition parties such as the Congress, the DMK, the NCP (Shardchandra Pawar),and the Samajwadi Party have dug in their heels that the government should give in writing the assurance that proportional representation of states in the Lok Sabha will be maintained.
“We are clear that the government must give it in writing that the seats will increase by 50%...We cannot speculate on the basis of verbal assurances,” said a DMK lawmaker.

headline: Mumbai 3.0 takes off: 323 sq km new city planned across 124 villages
full_text:
Mumbai 3.0 takes off: 323 sq km new city planned across 124 villages
MMRDA has appointed Surbana Jurong to prepare the vision document and master plan for Mumbai 3.0 in Raigad. The proposed new town across 124 villages is intended to become a major growth centre between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai.
Maharashtra has moved a step closer to creating a new urban and economic hub outside Mumbai, with a global urban planning firm tasked with designing the master plan for the proposed 323 sq km Mumbai 3.0 project.
The proposed development, also known as the Karnala-Sai-Chirner (KSC) New Town, will come up across 323.44 square kilometres in Raigad district and cover 124 villages in Uran, Panvel and Pen talukas.
The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) has appointed Singapore-based Surbana Jurong Infrastructure Pte Ltd to prepare the vision document, master plan and comprehensive planning framework for the ambitious new urban area.
The appointment marks the beginning of the detailed planning phase for Mumbai 3.0, which Maharashtra is positioning as a new growth centre for the Mumbai Metropolitan Region.
124 VILLAGES TO FORM NEW URBAN HUB
The proposed KSC New Town will bring 124 villages across Uran, Panvel and Pen talukas into a planned urban development zone.
The government plans to develop the area as a new economic and urban centre between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai, with modern townships alongside commercial zones, logistics parks, employment centres and other economic activities.
The project is also expected to create space for institutions and businesses linked to education, healthcare, technology, innovation and commerce.
ATAl SETU, NAVI MUMBAI AIRPORT TO DRIVE CONNECTIVITY
The project's location is central to the government's plans for its development.
Mumbai 3.0 lies close to the influence zones of the Atal Setu, also known as the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, and the Navi Mumbai International Airport.
The proposed urban hub is expected to benefit from road, metro, rail, airport and logistics connectivity, helping it emerge as a new growth centre within the Mumbai Metropolitan Region.
LAND ACQUISITION PROCESS UNDERWAY
The MMRDA began the land acquisition process for the area in April 2026.
Landowners have been offered multiple compensation options as part of the process, including monetary compensation, compensation through Floor Space Index and Transferable Development Rights, and a land pooling model.
Under the land pooling arrangement, eligible landowners can receive a portion of the developed land in return for contributing their land to the project.
PLAN TO EASE PRESSURE ON MUMBAI
Mumbai 3.0 is being planned as more than a new township. The project forms part of Maharashtra's broader strategy to expand the Mumbai Metropolitan Region and create new centres of employment and economic activity.
The government aims to reduce the growing population and infrastructure pressure on Mumbai and Navi Mumbai by developing a new urban centre with modern infrastructure and economic opportunities.
With the Atal Setu and Navi Mumbai International Airport providing major connectivity links, the area between Mumbai and the airport is expected to become an important development zone in the coming years.
The Maharashtra government has already outlined its vision of developing Mumbai 3.0 as an international-scale urban and economic centre. The preparation of the vision document and master plan by Surbana Jurong will now shape how the proposed 323.44 sq km development takes form.

headline: Allahabad High Court grants deceased UP employee regularisation rights
full_text:
Allahabad High Court grants deceased UP employee regularisation rights
The Allahabad High Court ordered that a deceased work-charge employee be treated as regularised from his due date. It said the accrued right survived his death and warranted consideration of his son's compassionate appointment.
The Allahabad High Court has directed Uttar Pradesh government authorities to treat a deceased work-charge employee of the Rural Engineering Department as regularised from the date he became eligible, saying his death could not end his accrued right to be considered for regularisation. The court also asked the authorities to consider his son’s claim for compassionate appointment under the Uttar Pradesh Recruitment of Dependants of Government Servants Dying in Harness Rules, 1974.
Justice Indrajeet Shukla of the Lucknow bench, while allowing a writ petition filed by Hasan Ahmad on Friday, said the exercise must be completed within two months of the production of a certified copy of the order. The court also described the conduct of the authorities as "ex-facie contemptuous" and awarded Rs 50,000 as costs to the petitioner.
The petition said Ahmad’s father, Rifakat Hussain, was engaged as a junior assistant in the work-charge establishment of the Rural Engineering Department in Hardoi on November 1, 1985. He died on August 11, 2012 after serving the department for over 18 years. His name was listed at serial number 58 in a seniority list prepared for regularisation in 2005.
The court noted that 172 Group-C posts had been sanctioned in 2012 for the regularisation of daily-wage, work-charge and court-case employees. However, Hussain died before the process could be completed, while other similarly placed employees were regularised. The bench said the authorities had repeatedly rejected the claim despite earlier court directions, and observed that the impugned order dated March 17, 2023 had been passed in defiance of an earlier binding direction.
The court held that the right to consideration for regularisation, once accrued, does not disappear merely because the employee dies before the process is completed, and that such a right can survive through legal representatives. It directed that its order be communicated to the secretary of the Rural Engineering Department and the department’s director and chief engineer, while reiterating that the petitioner had been forced into prolonged litigation because of repeated non-compliance by the authorities.
In sum, the court ruled that Hussain must be treated as regularised from the date he became eligible, ordered consideration of his son’s claim for compassionate appointment, and asked the authorities to complete the process within two months.

headline: Bengaluru: As its proposed Sharavathi pumped storage project (PSP) continues to face rejection by experts and opposition from the people, the Karnataka Power Corporation Limited (KPCL) has approached the Forest department with an offer that ostensibl...
full_text: Bengaluru: As its proposed Sharavathi pumped storage project (PSP) continues to face rejection by experts and opposition from the people, the Karnataka Power Corporation Limited (KPCL) has approached the Forest department with an offer that ostensibly reduces the damage caused to the environment..The activists, however, have expressed concern over the disclosure and questioned the assumptions..KPCL had sought 131.81 acres of forest land in the Sharavathi Valley Lion Tailed Macaque Sanctuary to build an underground powerhouse between two reservoirs for generating 2000 MW. A joint committee of experts, led by members of the National Board of Wildlife, had declared that the project has no merit and should be rejected..Expert Committee did not approve Sharavathi Project, Centre tells Karnataka High Court .In a new proposal, the KPCL said it has reduced the forest land required for the project by nearly 30%, to 96.33 acres. “The total number of trees proposed for felling has been reduced from 16,041 to 6,377,” it said, adding that the wildlife mitigation plan submitted earlier has been revised to enhance the mitigation measures..Major changes.The Corporation said it has made several changes to the original proposal following discussions with an expert from the National Institute of Advanced Studies. Among the major tweaks is the decision not to widen the Nagarabastikere to Begodi village but only strengthen it. This, the company said, will avoid the felling of 4,074 trees..The KPCL said it has also eliminated two other major components: a new road from Gerusoppa dam and a surge shaft that required 25 acres and the felling of over 2,500 trees have been eliminated. Other tweaks include the relocation of intermediate adit tunnel and provision of tunnel connectivity for operation and maintenance instead of using village roads, to reduce disturbance..“Due to the above modifications, the overall environmental footprint of the project has been substantially reduced...Further, the extent of the surface level disturbance within the forest has also been minimised,” the document said..Opposition from early days.The project has been facing headwinds ever since authorities conducted preliminary tests five years ago. Over 30,000 people had opposed the project during the public hearing in September 2025. Most recently, the high court had ordered an interim stay on the project..Wildlife conservationist Veeresh G, however, said the revised plan has several wrong assumptions and also fails to provide crucial details. “It has become a trend these days to propose all manner of projects underground. Even though the Wildlife (Protection) Act recognises land as core part of the habitat, the underground is treated as a vacuum chamber,” he said..He noted that any development work that touches the ground in the Sharavathi valley will create disturbance and damage the ecosystem.

Air India salary hikes salaries of pilots by up to 15%

Air India is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb levels next month
NEW DELHI: Air India on Friday hiked pilot salaries by 8% to 15%, with commanders getting the biggest hikes and increases tapering by rank. Going ahead, first officers or co-pilots will get command upgrades in AI Express, which has single-aisle aircraft, then move to AI, which has wide-body aircraft with higher pay, to build progression within the group. Air India has tried to make Air India Express more attractive through better pay and to address shortages on the B737 fleet.Air India pilots have for years been facing a 40-hour guaranteed pay â meaning they get minimum pay for these hours irrespective of actual flying, while flying more means more pay â while IndiGo has fixed pay for 70 hours. Under the revised framework, Air India will continue to provide guaranteed pay for 40 flying hours but has enhanced flying allowance rates. Rates beyond 40 hours have been increased, aligning compensation with industry benchmarks while rewarding productivity.Air India is restoring international flights that were slashed post the West Asia crisis and will return to Jan-Feb levels next month. Pakistan airspace closure means longer routes, higher flying time and greater pilot requirements.
A senior commander flying 55 hours a month will get Rs 8.3 lakh, up from Rs 7.5 lakh, while a first officer will get Rs 3.3 lakh, up from just over Rs 3 lakh.
Privilege leave has been reduced from 30 to 24 days, though weekly offs will not be counted as leave.Since Tata Group took over Air India and Air India Express in Jan 2022, it has grown from around 100 to 300 aircraft. Under the new framework, Air India Express will serve as the âprimary pathwayâ for command upgrades. They can then progress to Air India for wide-body flying. A fleet allowance is being offered to pilots supporting the B737 fleet in Air India Express.

The report also suggested prescribing clear inter-agency SOPs ahead of the peak tourist season to ensure a coordinated and timely response to any security-related incident
NEW DELHI: A parliamentary committee has recommended an integrated security and surveillance framework for all major tourist destinations in Jammu & Kashmir, incorporating comprehensive CCTV coverage, centralised monitoring facilities, regular vulnerability assessments and periodic security audits.In its 260th report tabled in Parliament on Friday, the department-related standing committee on home affairs also suggested clear inter-agency SOPs be prescribed and reviewed ahead of the peak tourist season to ensure a coordinated and timely response to any security-related incident.The recommendations, which followed the panel's visit to J&K in May 2026 to assess the security arrangements at tourist destinations, come in the wake of last year's Pahalgam terror attack in which 25 tourists were gunned down.The committee noted that sustained growth in tourist arrivals has been facilitated by improved connectivity, stronger security arrangements, better tourist infrastructure and a renewed sense of confidence among visitors."In this context, security management at tourist destinations assumes special importance, as it directly affects the perception of safety, the quality of visitor experience and the continued growth of the tourism sector," it said.
Appreciating security arrangements at Gulmarg and other major tourist and religious destinations, the committee noted the deployment of security personnel, surveillance mechanisms, crowd-management measures and coordination among police, tourism department, district administration, development authorities and other agencies.

headline: The panel, it said, shall devise suitable norms and guidelines 'keeping in view the cultural ethos and sensitivity of the country'
full_text:
The panel, it said, shall devise suitable norms and guidelines 'keeping in view the cultural ethos and sensitivity of the country'
NEW DELHI: The information and broadcasting (I&B) ministry has told a parliamentary committee that it is mulling a comprehensive statutory framework to regulate the airing of programmes on OTT platforms, "which are offensive to moral standards of society", without infringing upon the rights and freedom of individuals.The department-related standing committee on the ministry of home affairs, in its recommendations in the 259th report tabled in Parliament on Friday, said the proposed comprehensive statutory framework for regulating OTT content must incorporate robust technology-enabled age verification mechanisms, effective parental controls and suitable penalties for non-compliance.While observing that the existing framework continued to rely largely on self-regulation by OTT platforms, the committee - in its recommendations on the action taken on its 254th report - reiterated that the government examine the feasibility of establishing an independent post-release review panel - comprising experts from fields like child development, education, law, social sciences and civil society - to review flagged OTT content and lay down appropriate corrective measures.The panel had, in its 254th report, said, "OTT platforms have emerged as a primary source of entertainment in India, with a reach that surpasses traditional cinema, including a substantial audience of minors." The committee pointed out that unlike films, which require mandatory pre-certification under the Cinematograph Act, OTT content operates under a self-classification system with post-release grievance redressal as per the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021.
The panel said that although the aforesaid rules require age ratings, parental controls and a grievance mechanism, the lack of pre-release checks and weak age verification still leaves minors exposed to harmful content. Accordingly, it recommended that the government consider establishing a recognised panel of experts who will monitor new OTT releases.
It suggested that the post-release review panel watch the flagged or trending content based on user complaints submitted through a standardised grievance mechanism.The panel, it said, shall devise suitable norms and guidelines "keeping in view the cultural ethos and sensitivity of the country". It recommended that the panel also work out suitable penalties for infringement of these norms/guidelines.

Several of the named sites on the map carry the weight of India-China conflict.
GUWAHATI/NEW DELHI: The updated Survey of India map has assigned standard place and feature names to 27 Arunachal Pradesh sites, including four mountain passes and a high-altitude lake, as part of the Union governmentâs strategy to remove any ambiguity on demarcation of territory and counter Chinaâs repeated attempts to rename places on this side of the McMahon Line.The MHA said on Friday that the names were finalised in consultation with the Arunachal Pradesh government. âIdentifying them formally on the Survey of India map is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public.âOf the 27 sites identified on the map, one is a monument. Three of the rest â Longju, Maja & Bisa â are strategically important border villages in Upper Subansiri district. There are also three passes along the McMahon Line, Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La, in the same district. Thag La pass, a 1962 battleground, lies on the border in Tawang district.âThese places are already marked on Indian military maps, even those of 1962 vintage. Identifying them on Survey of India maps is a bold counter to China,â a source said.Several of the named sites carry the weight of India-China conflict. Longju was one of the earliest flashpoints in the boundary dispute and was occupied by Chinese troops in 1959.
Thag La overlooks Namka Chu valley, where the 1962 conflict began after Chinese forces crossed the McMahon Line.Jaswant Garh, in Tawang, commemorates Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat, one of the most celebrated heroes of 1962 war. The Sher-e-Thapa Memorial in Upper Subansiri honours Hav Shere Thapa, whose resistance at Rio Bridge significantly delayed the Chinese advance in 1962. The lone lake named is Sambho Sarovar, a high-altitude glacial lake.
The remaining land areas include Bara Kundun, Chhota Kundun and Dhan Bari in Anjaw district; Pritnagar, Buddhamandir, Jairampur, Teritnagar and Ramnagar in Changlang; Sagar, Padma, Jyotinagar and Baisakhi in West Kameng; Chhota Ropuk and Bara Ropuk in Upper Subansiri; and Shivaji Nagar, Sunpura and Kamlang Nagar in Lohit.In April, China announced Chinese names for 23 locations in Arunachal Pradesh, which Beijing refers to as âSouth Tibetâ. The external affairs ministry then said assigning âfictitious namesâ wouldnât alter the reality that Arunachal Pradesh âwas, is, and will always remain an integral and inalienable part of Indiaâ. China has carried out similar renaming exercises periodically.McMahon Line demarcates the boundary between India and China in the eastern sector, separating Arunachal from Tibet.

headline: After meeting PM Modi, Sukhbir Singh Badal’s SAD backs women’s quota, delimitation bills
full_text:
After meeting PM Modi, Sukhbir Singh Badal’s SAD backs women’s quota, delimitation bills
The Shiromani Akali Dal demanded the immediate implementation of the Women’s Reservation Bill, SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal said in a post on X.
A day after meeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal announced the party’s support for the Women’s Reservation Bill and the Delimitation Bill.
The Shiromani Akali Dal, at a meeting of its senior leaders in Chandigarh on Saturday, demanded the immediate implementation of the Women’s Reservation Bill, SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal said in a post on X.
“The Shiromani Akali Dal draws inspiration from the teachings of the Sikh Gurus, who championed the dignity, equality and equal rights of women. The Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (@SGPCAmritsar) has already set an example by providing for women’s reservation in its House,” he said.
The party also extended its support to the Delimitation Bill. According to Badal, after detailed deliberations on key issues before Parliament, the Shiromani Akali Dal demanded a fair and equitable delimitation process that ensures equal representation to all states.
The Shiromani Akali Dal supported the proposal put forward by the Government of India on the floor of the House for a uniform 50% increase in the number of seats for all states. The party emphasised that both women’s reservation and delimitation should be implemented immediately.
Party senior leader Naresh Gujral said the decision was “a very logical thing” for the party to do.
“We have one member in the Parliament and we cannot just oppose the two bills for the sake of it,” said Gujral, party vice-president and former Rajya Sabha member.
“We have been supporting women reservation in the Parliament and delimitation is need of the hour,” he further said.

headline: Don't pay toll on NICE Road: HD Kumaraswamy gives Karnataka govt 10-day deadline
full_text:
Don't pay toll on NICE Road: HD Kumaraswamy gives Karnataka govt 10-day deadline
H D Kumaraswamy urged Bengaluru motorists to stop paying toll on NICE Road and gave the government 10 days to act. The demand follows sharp Karnataka High Court observations on the BMIC project and has triggered a political clash.
Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy on Saturday appealed to people in Bengaluru not to pay toll on the NICE Road corridor, saying the JD(S) would seek to stop what he called the government "robbing people through toll".
He also set a deadline of a week to 10 days to stop toll collection on the Nandi Infrastructure Corridor Enterprises (NICE) Road.
Kumaraswamy said his party had been opposing the project since its inception, alleging illegalities and deception. He also cited recent observations by the Karnataka High Court on the Bengaluru-Mysuru Infrastructure Corridor (BMIC) project and said the state government should act immediately to take over the NICE project and halt toll collection.
"I appeal to the people of Bengaluru to stop paying toll on NICE Road. We have decided to stop the government that is robbing people through toll. We are giving a deadline of a week or 10 days," Kumaraswamy told reporters. He said he had appealed to members of both the JD(S) and the BJP to raise the issue in the Karnataka Assembly.
KUMARASWAMY ALSO OPPOSES BIDADI TOWNSHIP PROJECT
He said the party had also decided to oppose the AI Powered Bidadi Township project. "If the government does not take any action, we will launch our fight to stop this toll collection. I have appealed to the people with folded hands not to pay from today itself," he said.
Referring to the High Court's observations, Kumaraswamy said, "The High Court has observed that the BMIC project appears to be one of the biggest scams in the state."
He said that, in view of the judgment, motorists should not pay toll on the road.
"The state government must wake up to the serious observations made by the High Court regarding the NICE project. The Court has pointed to serious irregularities in the implementation of the project and has questioned the manner in which toll is being collected from motorists," he said.
KUMARASWAMY CALLS IT A BIG SCAM
Kumaraswamy referred to the judgment delivered by a Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court on July 29 in connection with alleged irregularities in the NICE project.
According to a statement issued by the JD(S), the High Court said the BMIC project "appears to be one of the biggest scams in the state" and that the matter was fit for an independent investigation by a team of experts into allegations of fraud and other offences, along with a forensic audit of the project accounts.
"These observations of the High Court make it clear how serious the situation surrounding this project is. The people of Karnataka must understand what the judgment says and what it reveals about the manner in which the project has been implemented," Kumaraswamy said.
Questioning the state government's silence, Kumaraswamy said it should respond to the Court's observations. Reacting to his remarks, Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge said no BJP leaders had ever protested when toll rates were increased across the country.
"If the Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) increases the Metro fare by even one rupee, the entire BJP comes and stages a protest, asking how and why the fare was increased. Toll rates have been increased. Who is responsible for that?" he said.
He also asked why BJP leaders who had been protesting against the Metro fare hike had disappeared.
The NICE Road, a private tolled peripheral expressway in Bengaluru that was initially conceived as the BMIC, has again come under political focus, with Kumaraswamy demanding an end to toll collection and the state government facing questions over the High Court's observations on the project.

headline: On day 3, MeitY-Meta technical teams hold talks on platform algorithms
full_text:
On day 3, MeitY-Meta technical teams hold talks on platform algorithms
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) on Friday held a third round of discussions with Meta, this time with their technical team, focusing on technical aspects of the social media giant’s platform algorithms, two people aware of the matter said
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) on Friday held a third round of discussions with Meta, this time with their technical team, focusing on technical aspects of the social media giant’s platform algorithms, two people aware of the matter said. These discussions on technical grounds are expected to continue over the next couple of days, a senior MeitY official had told HT on Thursday.
The meeting was held in the morning at Electronics Niketan and was presided over by MeitY Secretary S Krishnan, one of the people quoted above said. The discussions are part of the government’s continuing engagement with Meta following the temporary restriction of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Facebook Reel on July 28, which had triggered concerns within the government over the company’s content moderation systems and safeguards for high-profile accounts.
The meeting after a global delegation of Meta led by chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan met Union electronics and IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Wednesday and Thursday, and apologised for the temporary restriction of Modi’s post. Meta had attributed the incident to an error in its automated systems, which incorrectly matched the Prime Minister’s Reel with another video, resulting in the post being inaccessible for around five hours.
The government has since sought a deeper understanding of Meta’s algorithms, content moderation policies and compliance mechanisms, particularly the checks and safeguards that determine what content is restricted or removed in India.
A senior IT ministry official had told HT that while the global delegation accompanying Kaplan was expected to return after its meetings with Indian officials, Meta’s technical team would remain in India and engage with MeitY over the next three to four days.
It is understood that the global delegation has now returned, while the company’s technical team has stayed back for the continuing discussions with the ministry. Meta and MeitY did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Punjab Policeâs âGangstran Te Vaarâ Completes 200 Days of Sustained Crackdown
Punjab Policeâs flagship anti-gangster campaign âGangstran Te Vaarâ has completed 200 days, with the force claiming a major crackdown on organised crime networks across the state.During the campaign, police conducted 1,09,087 raids, arrested 1,532 proclaimed offenders and initiated action against 58,212 criminals and their associates, according to official sources.
Launched under the Bhagwant Mann government, the intelligence-driven campaign has focused not only on gangsters but also on their associates, financial networks, weapons supply, logistics and overseas handlers.Police said preventive action was taken against 28,201 people, while another 18,514 were verified and released. Overall, the campaign covered 1,04,927 persons, including gangsters, their associates and wanted criminals.DGP Gaurav Yadav said the operation had evolved into a multi-dimensional campaign aimed at dismantling the ecosystem supporting organised crime.âOur strategy goes beyond arrests to dismantling the ecosystem that enables organised crime by targeting associates, finances, logistics, communication channels and overseas linkages,â Yadav said.
Weapons, drugs and criminal infrastructure seized
The campaign also targeted the firepower and financial networks of organised gangs. Punjab Police recovered 990 illegal firearms, 242 sharp-edged weapons, 2,739 rounds of ammunition, 315 magazines, 2.5 kg of explosives and 15 hand grenades.In its action against the crime-drug nexus, police seized 774.38 kg of heroin, 480.23 kg of opium, 7,266.26 kg of poppy husk and more than 26.91 lakh intoxicant tablets.Authorities also seized Rs 1.73 crore in drug money, Rs 1.80 crore in cash and 413.85 grams of gold.
Overseas gangsters brought back
The Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF) also pursued fugitives operating from abroad. Police highlighted the deportation of gangster Bhuvnesh Chopra alias Ashish Chopra from Central Asia and Jobanjit Singh alias Joban Billa from Jakarta, Indonesia.
AGTF chief Pramod Ban said the campaign increasingly combines field operations with financial investigations, digital intelligence and coordination with central agencies to track foreign-based handlers and criminal networks.
Tipline launched for public intelligence
Punjab Police said 4,978 mobile handsets, 1,781 vehicles and 61 drones linked to criminal activities were also seized, while 64,402.77 litres of illicit liquor was recovered and destroyed.To strengthen public participation, the AGTF has launched a dedicated anonymous tipline at 93946-93946 for information about gangsters, wanted criminals and related activities. A reward policy has also been introduced for credible information leading to action against wanted criminals, with authorities promising confidentiality for informants.

headline: At the ancient Adoor Mahalingeswara temple in Kasaragod district, every visit offers a journey into history. Alongside its deity, centuries-old inscriptions, and unique architecture, two old cannons preserved in the temple courtyard stand as a silent...
full_text:
At the ancient Adoor Mahalingeswara temple in Kasaragod district, every visit offers a journey into history. Alongside its deity, centuries-old inscriptions, and unique architecture, two old cannons preserved in the temple courtyard stand as a silent reminder of a turbulent past, adding another layer to the temple’s rich historical legacy.
The temple, located in Delampady Gram Panchayat, is already renowned for its 10th-century origins, its three-tiered Gajaprishta (elephant-back) style architecture, the famous Adoor inscription, an intricately carved Balikkal (sacrificial stone), and the Sathyakallu (oath stone). The presence of the historically significant cannons has further enhanced the site’s archaeological importance.
The cannons drew scholarly attention when Nandakumar Koroth, Head of the Department of History at Nehru Arts and Science College, Kanhangad, visited the temple to study the Adoor inscription.
According Dr. Koroth, both are made of an alloy that may date to the 18th century or even earlier. One cannon measures 96 centimetre in length, including its handle for directional movement, while the second is 90 centimetre long. Each has side trunnions designed for mounting on wheeled carriages, while a small opening on the top was used for loading gunpowder.
“The comparatively small size of the cannons suggests that they were probably mounted on wheels and used as mobile field artillery during military campaigns,” Dr. Koroth said.
He noted that the cannons bear no visible foreign insignia, manufacturer’s mark, or date of production. The absence of European markings indicates they may have been locally manufactured and probably predate British rule in South Canara, which was established around 1800, he said.
The origin of the cannons, however, remain a mystery. No inscription or historical record directly links them to any ruler or military campaign.
Temple renovation committee volunteer Balakrishnan Adoor said local tradition associates the cannons with the military expedition of Tipu Sultan in the late 18th century.
“According to oral tradition, Tipu Sultan reached the temple during one of his campaigns against local rulers. He is believed to have intended to plunder the temple after defeating a regional chieftain and expanding his kingdom,” Mr. Balakrishnan said.
There are no written records to authenticate the legend or establish that the cannons belonged to Tipu Sultan. They are believed to have been abandoned here during that period, but there is no evidence to prove it, he said.
Mr. Balakrishnan said the heavy cannons were originally found elsewhere within the temple compound and were later shifted to their present location for protection. Local residents also recall that large iron balls, believed to be cannonballs, were unearthed during excavation works around the nearby temple and school premises several years ago.
Kannada scholar and historian N. Radhakrishna, who has studied the temple’s inscriptions, said the temple’s epigraphs document donations made by rulers of the Kumbla dynasty, including Kattillamma and King Gunyappa Rasa, particularly to the temple’s sacrificial stones.
“The inscriptions are well documented, but there is no inscription or historical record explaining how the cannons reached the temple. We only know that they are old,” he said.
Mr. Radhakrishna said the temple itself dates back to the 10th century, while some inscriptions belong to the 17th or 18th century, probably marking later renovations.
“There is no documentary evidence linking these cannons to Tipu Sultan or any particular battle. Similar traditions exist in other temples, but historical proof is absent,” he said.

headline: The Supreme Court on Friday (August 7, 2026) directed the Union government to share the latest report by the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) with the petitioner-NGO Kuki Organisation for Human Rights in a case seeking probe into the alle...
full_text:
The Supreme Court on Friday (August 7, 2026) directed the Union government to share the latest report by the National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) with the petitioner-NGO Kuki Organisation for Human Rights in a case seeking probe into the alleged involvement of former Manipur Chief Minister N. Biren Singh in the ethnic violence in the northeastern State.
According to the report, the leaked audio clips alluding to Mr. Singh have been “clearly manipulated”.
Appearing before a Bench headed by Justice Sanjay Kumar, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, representing both the Centre and the State of Manipur, said even the first-generation copy of the audio clippings outed by a whistleblower showed alterations.
Ms. Bhati asked the top court to dismiss the petition.
Advocate Prashant Bhushan, representing the NGO-petitioner, strongly objected to the report, saying tests of the audio clippings done at Truth Labs had shown a 93% match with Mr. Singh’s voice. Agreeing to keep the report confidential, Mr. Bhushan said he would nevertheless counter its findings in court on the next date of hearing.
Select clippings
The court, in an earlier hearing, had asked the petitioner-NGO to hand over to the national forensics lab a ‘first generation copy’ of the full audio tapes.
On December 15 last year, the court had questioned why the entire available leaked audio clips were not sent for forensic examination. The court had conveyed its unease at the affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioners on November 20, 2025, that stated that “only select clippings were sent” for forensics.
The petitioner has sought an independent SIT probe into the matter.
More than 260 people were killed and thousands displaced since the ethnic violence broke out between the Imphal valley-based Meitei and neighbouring hills-based Kuki communities in May 2023.
The court listed the case next for hearing on October 5.

The Bihar government on Friday (August 7, 2026) announced that four new minority residential schools will start academic activities from August, taking the total number of such schools to six in the State.
While addressing the press in Patna, Minority Welfare Department Minister Mohammad Zama Khan said the department has given the nod to build new minority residential schools in 24 districts.
“The construction of four new schools at Jamui, Nalanda, Kaimur and Muzaffarpur has been completed, and the academic session is likely to start from August 17,” Mr. Khan said. He added that this will be in addition to the existing two such schools which are already operational at Darbhanga and Kishanganj.
The department has implemented “Bihar State Minority Residential School Scheme” in the State since 2018-19, he said, adding that at least one minority residential school will be opened in each district under the scheme.
A minority residential school provides high-quality residential education from Class 9 to Class 12 for meritorious minority students, besides offering free boarding, lodging, and books, the Minister said.
With a view to improve educational standards of madrasas, especially located in bordering districts of the State, the department is carrying out “online/smart classes” in association with Maulana Mazharul Haque Arabic and Persian University, Patna and Bihar State Madrasa Education Board, Patna, the Minister said.
“We have made arrangements for providing ‘skill development’ to the students of madrasas so that they can get jobs in different fields,” Mr. Khan said, adding that the skill development programme in madrasas will be run in association with National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), a public enterprise under India’s Ministry of MSME.
The madrasa students are being taught subjects like Hindi, English, Social Science, Science and Mathematics to make them competitive in today’s world, he added.
The department has sent the requisition to Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) to fill the 288 posts of teachers to be appointed through TRE 4.0 in ‘residential minority schools’ of the State, Mr. Khan said. He added that the government has approved 481 posts of teaching and non-teaching staffers to operate 13 minority residential schools.
In order to promote entrepreneurship and self-employment among the youth of the minority community in the State, Mukhya Mantri Udyami Yojana (Chief Minister Minority Entrepreneur Scheme) was launched in 2023, Mr. Khan said. Loans amounting to ₹100 crore were disbursed among 1,247 beneficiaries under the scheme in 2025-26. So far, a total of 3,741 beneficiaries have received loans worth Rs 270 crore.
He also said that the Bihar State Haj Committee has been constituted to facilitate and assist Haj pilgrims, and a total of 2,526 pilgrims undertook the Haj pilgrimage through the committee during 2025-26 while the registration process has been completed for a total of 3,637 applicants for the Haj pilgrimage for 2026-27.

headline: A Kashmir Pandit organisation on Sunday (August 9, 2026) expressed concerns over purported online threats issued by terrorists to Pandits living in the valley and demanded a probe. It said the threats have “forced many minority community employees” w...
full_text:
A Kashmir Pandit organisation on Sunday (August 9, 2026) expressed concerns over purported online threats issued by terrorists to Pandits living in the valley and demanded a probe. It said the threats have “forced many minority community employees” working in the in the Muslim-majority Jammu & Kashmir to “go on leave”.
Kashmiri Pandit killings: J&K Police’s special cell reopens 1990 case; searches multiple locations
A spokesperson of Panun Kashmir, one of the Jammu-based organisations of Kashmiri Pandits, said a purported threat communication dated August 7, 2026 and issued in the name of the United Liberation Council “has specifically named members of the Kashmiri Pandit community and disclosed their telephone numbers”.
“The communication represented a serious escalation because it went beyond generic threats and appeared to identify individuals as potential targets while claiming access to information about their families, locations and places of work,” said Agnishekhar, convenor of Panun Kashmir.
Mr. Agnishekhar demanded an investigation into the authenticity of the claims made in the letter. He also urged J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha “to immediately direct the police and security agencies to undertake a comprehensive threat assessment of all persons named in the communication and their immediate families”.
Official sources said scores of Kashmiri Pandits working in Kashmir under the Prime Minister’s package have left the valley in the face of the fresh threat. They said departments in “volatile and sensitive locations” in Kashmir have allowed Pandit employees to go on leave till August 20. However, there has been no official communication from the government.
The Pandit organisation also sought appropriate security measures for the individuals identified in the communication and a review of the security of Kashmiri Pandit employees working in sensitive government departments.
Referring to the letter, Mr. Agnishekhar said it needed to be established whether the perpetrators actually possessed such information or were “attempting psychological warfare”. “The authorities must investigate the source of the information, the digital trail behind the communication and whether any surveillance, profiling or reconnaissance of the targeted persons has taken place,” he added.
A sense of fear returned to Kashmir after terrorists killed one policeman and two non-local labourers in south Kashmir in the past 20 days in two separate targeted killings. According to police sources, a local Lashkar-e-Taiba militant could be involved in these targeted killings.
JeI premises searched
Meanwhile, the J&K police conducted coordinated searches at 26 locations across Sopore in north Kashmir in connection with the cases registered under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against the banned socio-religious organisation Jamaat-e-Islami (JeI).
“The searches were carried out at residential and other premises linked to the JeI leaders, members and activists across different areas of Sopore. During the searches, incriminating documents, literature and electronic devices were recovered and seized from various premises. The seized material is being examined as part of the ongoing investigation to ascertain further linkages and activities connected with the proscribed organisation,” said the police.
The police said the operation forms part of sustained efforts to dismantle networks and ecosystems associated with proscribed organisations and separatist activities and to take firm action against activities “prejudicial to the security, sovereignty and integrity” of the nation.
