headline: Rented bike, informed fiancée: Indore man who went for trek at Karnataka's Shivgange missing since two days; search on
full_text:
Rented bike, informed fiancée: Indore man who went for trek at Karnataka's Shivgange missing since two days; search on
Advaith Upadhyay is a resident of the Begur area and works at a finance firm in Whitefield. He went for trekking at Shivagange and has been reported missing.
A morning trek turned into chaos for a 31-year-old man, identified as Advaith Upadhyay, who went missing at Shivagange in Nelamangala taluk on the outskirts of Bengaluru. Police launched an extensive search for him after a missing person complaint.
A native of Madhya Pradesh's Indore, Upadhyay is a resident of the Begur area and works at a finance firm in Whitefield. He went for trekking at Shivagange and has been reported missing, news agency PTI reported, citing police.
The police have informed that an extensive search operation has been launched to trace Upadhyay.
Also Read | 2 teenage girls among 3 go missing in Kapurthala
What happened before Upadhyay went missing?
The man reached the hill around 6:30 am on Friday and parked his rented bike at the foothills, the report added.
Before his trip, Upadhyay had reportedly informed his fiancée of his plan for Shivagange trekking and had also hired a motorcycle for the same.
The review of CCTV footage confirmed about him climbing the hill. However, all trace of his whereabouts ends there, and his mobile phone has remained switched off.
Also Read | Woman missing for over two weeks; family stages protest outside police station in Ludhiana’s Dehlon
Search operation and missing person case
Following a complaint, a missing person case has been registered at the Kadugodi police station.
According to a police official, subsequently, a search operation has been launched at Shivagange and its vicinity.
Also Read | Indian Navy joins search for three fishermen missing after boat mishaps in Kerala
Family expresses concerns about kidnapping
Upadhyay's family has expressed suspicion that he may have been kidnapped or harmed by robbers who noticed he was trekking alone.
Investigation underway into the matter
A senior police official also confirmed that the authorities are exploring every possible angle to trace the man.
"An extensive search operation continues, and further investigation is underway. We are looking into all angles," a senior police officer said.
Similar inciden in Wayanad
In a separate incident, earlier, two young trekkers who lost their way on Ponmudikotta hill near Ambalavayal were successfully rescued.
The incident unfolded on an afternoon when Mubashir and Mohammed Mundhir, who are natives of Kalloor, trekked to Ponmudikotta hill. However, they lost their way while descending from the other side of the hill.
They had also tried to return to the peak but were further disoriented.
According to a PTI report, officials said that in the evening, when mobile phone connectivity was restored, the stranded trekkers were then able to place a call to the Fire and Rescue Services.
Following this, the authorities launched a joint search operation and the young trekkers were subsequently rescued.

headline: ‘Could have been killed’: Mamata Banerjee's vehicle attacked with ‘stones, mud’ in North 24 Parganas
full_text:
‘Could have been killed’: Mamata Banerjee's vehicle attacked with ‘stones, mud’ in North 24 Parganas
Mamata Banerjee remained unhurt as she did not leave the car when the incident unfolded.
Angry residents of Halisahar in West Bengal's North 24 Parganas district hurled shoes, mud and stones at Trinamool Congress (TMC) chief and former chief minister Mamata Banerjee's car on Sunday afternoon when she went to meet the family of a TMC worker who died in police custody on Saturday.
Banerjee remained unhurt as she did not leave the car when the incident happened.
The agitators, who did not carry any party flag and claimed to be local residents, said they got angry because Banerjee had never visited that area while in power. Slogans such as "go back" and "thief" were raised.
Banerjee targeted the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), and said, "We would have died if any of the stones had hit us. This was planned by the BJP as it did not want me to talk to the family of our party worker."
Mobs had earlier hurled eggs and verbally abused several top TMC leaders, including Abhishek Banerjee and Mahua Mitra, since the party's defeat in the assembly polls in May, this was the first time Mamata Banerjee faced such a situation.
TMC Lok Sabha member Kalyan Banerjee accused the state administration for allowing BJP workers to hurl shoes and mud at a former chief minister's car.
"This was a conspiracy to murder Mamata Banerjee. One of our workers was killed by police in custody and today Mamata Banerjee was attacked. The director general of police must resign immediately," Kalyan Banerjee said.
BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya condemned the incident saying workers of his party were not involved.
"The way they (TMC leaders) are saying that there was an attempt to kill a [former] chief minister it seems they have not gotten over the hangover of power. This was mass outrage. Our party workers were not involved in the incident but we condemn such gross misconduct. Mamata Banerjee is a former chief minister. People can show black flags and shout slogans but nobody can treat her like this. This is not Bengal's culture," Bhattacharya said.
Urban development minister Agnimitra Paul said, "If anyone thinks that he has done a great job in the name of the BJP, then he is wrong. He will be punished. How can a woman, who is a former chief minister, be treated in this manner? We condemn it."
A political row erupted on Saturday after a local Halisahar TMC leader died in police custody. His arrest was based on an August 1 complaint by a woman.
The victim, Birju Keot, was the husband of Jenny Sharma Keot, a former councilor of the TMC-led Kanchrapara municipality.
“My husband was arrested on Friday and taken to Halisahar police station. During the day he was taken to a hospital for a mandatory medical checkup and brought back to the police station in the evening. I met him around 9pm to give him some clothes. He was fit at that time,” Jenny Sharma Keot said.
“He was beaten up inside the police station later at night. The body bore injury marks on the hand, back and legs. Blood had oozed out of his ears," she said.
The local police said Birju Keot was booked under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Indian Arms Act and was charged with cheating, assaulting and outraging the modesty of a woman.
“He fell ill on Saturday morning and was rushed to the JNM Hospital at Kalyani in Nadia district where the doctors declared him dead. An enquiry by a judicial magistrate has been ordered,” a senior Barrackpore city police officer said.

headline: Andhra CM calls for mass movement to make every citizen partner in nation building

Andhra CM calls for mass movement to make every citizen partner in nation building
Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to design the Partners in Nation Building programme as a mass movement, with active public participation in achieving the goals of Viksit Bharat and Swarna Andhra by 2047.
Reviewing the design of the programme, the Chief Minister said the initiative would be launched from August 15 as the country completes 79 years of Independence and enters its 80th year.
"The Partners in Nation Building programme should involve every citizen in nation building and create awareness about the responsibility of contributing to the country's development. People should be encouraged to set goals and contribute towards achieving the 2047 vision," Naidu said in a press release issued on Saturday.
He directed officials to ensure that the national flag is hoisted at every home from August 13 to 15 and that the feeling of "My Nation, Nation First" reaches every household.
Naidu said programmes should be designed to encourage youth and students to play a key role in building the future of Andhra Pradesh and the country.
He suggested creating platforms for leadership to emerge in various fields from the village level.
The chief minister also called for reviving the spirit of voluntary service that once existed in villages and said the Partners in Nation Building programme should provide a platform for such activities.
He stressed that the ideas, energy and capabilities of youth should be channelled towards nation building. People, he said, should not remain merely beneficiaries of government welfare schemes but should become stakeholders in shaping the future of the state.
Naidu directed officials to prepare programmes with public participation and said progress achieved towards the 2047 goals should be reviewed and reports submitted every August 15.
He said the initiative should create awareness among people about their role in nation building and ultimately develop into a mass movement involving citizens across the state.

headline: Raja Raghuvanshi’s two brothers booked for selling liquor without licence in MP
full_text:
Raja Raghuvanshi’s two brothers booked for selling liquor without licence in MP
Assistant Commissioner of Police Nidhi Saxena said the action followed the discovery that liquor was being served to customers without the mandatory licence.
Two brothers of Indore businessman Raja Raghuvanshi, who was allegedly murdered during his honeymoon in Meghalaya last year, were among five people arrested by police in Madhya Pradesh on Saturday for allegedly serving liquor without a licence at their eatery.
The two brothers, Sachin Raghuvanshi and Vipin Raghuvanshi, own the food establishment in the Rau police station area. Three employees working at the eatery were also taken into preventive custody, police said, according to news agency PTI.
Assistant Commissioner of Police Nidhi Saxena said the action followed the discovery that liquor was being served to customers without the mandatory licence.
The five were arrested as a preventive measure under Section 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which allows police to arrest a person without a warrant or a magistrate's order if they have information that the person is planning to commit a cognisable offence, the report further added.
Police have also registered a case against the eatery under the Excise Act for allegedly serving liquor illegally, Saxena said.
A separate case has been filed under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for allegedly disobeying an order issued by a public servant and failing to provide information sought by police, she added.
Also Read: Supreme Court cancels Sonam Raghuvanshi's bail, gives her 3 weeks to surrender
What happened to Raja Raghuvanshi?
The preventive arrests come in the wake of the sensational murder case involving Indore businessman Raja Raghuvanshi, who travelled to Meghalaya with his wife, Sonam, for their honeymoon in May 2025.
The couple went missing after checking out of a homestay in Nongriat on May 23. Raja's body was recovered on June 2 from a deep gorge near Weisawdong Falls in Sohra, while Sonam was traced days later in Uttar Pradesh.
Meghalaya Police subsequently arrested Sonam, her alleged lover Raj Kushwaha and three alleged hired killers, Vishal Singh Chauhan, Akash Rajput and Anand Kurmi, in connection with the case. A chargesheet of more than 700 pages alleged that the murder was part of a pre-planned conspiracy.
Also Read: 'I am innocent, falsely implicated': Sonam tells Supreme Court in Raja Raghuvanshi murder case
The case has continued to see developments in the courts. The Meghalaya High Court had upheld Sonam's bail in June 2026, but the Supreme Court later cancelled the bail and directed her to surrender.
The top court, while hearing the Meghalaya government's challenge, had expressed reservations about the High Court's reasoning for granting her bail.

headline: ‘It’s their internal matter': Supriya Sule on Sunetra Pawar-led NCP's talks with Prashant Kishor
full_text:
‘It’s their internal matter': Supriya Sule on Sunetra Pawar-led NCP's talks with Prashant Kishor
Supriya Sule stressed that Prashant Kishor worked independently in his professional capacity and that deciding whom to work with was entirely his call.
NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule on Saturday said it was up to the rival Nationalist Congress Party faction to decide whether it wanted to work with political strategist-turned-politician Prashant Kishor, calling it their “internal” matter.
Earlier this week, Kishor met Nationalist Congress Party chief and Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar and her son, MP Parth Pawar, in Mumbai.
Sule, the Baramati MP, said Kishor had been her personal friend for several years and that she had never hidden their association. However, she stressed that Kishor worked independently in his professional capacity and that deciding whom to work with was entirely his call, news agency PTI reported.
“Prashant Kishor has been a good personal friend of mine for several years. I have closely followed his work, and I have never hidden our friendship,” Sule told reporters.
“But he works independently in his professional capacity, and with whom he wanted to work was his decision,” she said.
“Whether the Ajit Pawar-led NCP wants to work with Prashant Kishor or not is their internal matter,” Sule added.
Sule also praised Kishor for his electoral debut in Bihar, where his Jan Suraaj Party won the Bankipur assembly bypoll, defeating the BJP in one of its strongest bastions.
Also Read: Prashant Kishor’s meeting with Sunetra Pawar sparks churn in NCP, unease in BJP
Why Kishor met Sunetra Pawar
The meeting took place three days after Kishor opened Jan Suraaj’s electoral account with his Bankipur victory. NCP spokesperson Suraj Chavan said the discussions focused on strengthening the party’s organisation and ensuring that government development programmes reached the grassroots.
Kishor, who is advising the party on organisational rebuilding, attended the meeting with Sunetra Pawar, Parth Pawar and other senior NCP leaders, Chavan said.
It was the second meeting between Kishor and Sunetra Pawar since the death of her husband and then Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar in a plane crash in Baramati in January this year. After their first meeting a few months ago, Parth Pawar had said Kishor was known to the family.
Kishor's Bankipur win sparks speculation
Kishor’s meeting with the NCP leadership, however, triggered speculation within the party and among its Mahayuti allies, according to HT's earlier report.
Following the Mumbai meeting, speculation emerged that Kishor could be advising the NCP on organisational and electoral matters, with reports also suggesting that he had recommended replacing Maharashtra unit chief Sunil Tatkare.
Tatkare questioned Kishor’s appointment as the party’s election strategist, pointing out that Kishor himself heads a political party. He argued that the NCP did not need a poll strategist and said elections were won through the ability to connect with the masses rather than advice or campaign themes.
“I don’t know what was discussed. We are practical people and don’t believe in theories. Frankly, I don’t need strategists because I’m a field person. A visit to a village tells me about the mood of its people,” said Tatkare, who represents the party as a Lok Sabha MP in Raigad.
“How can he (Kishore) be appointed as the strategist of a party when he is already heading a political party? I am not aware of such an appointment being made. Had the leadership taken such a decision, I would certainly have been informed,” he added.
Tatkare also stressed that the NCP operates under a system of collective leadership and that decisions such as appointing a poll strategist could not be taken unilaterally.
“This tradition has existed since Pawar Saheb (Sharad Pawar) led the undivided NCP, and it was continued by Ajit Dada (Ajit Pawar) after he took over the reins of the party,” he said.
Tatkare has been the party’s Maharashtra unit chief since the NCP split in June 2023.
BJP unhappy too
Kishor’s engagement with the NCP leadership has also raised concerns within its BJP ally in Maharashtra, particularly given his recent electoral battle against the BJP in Bihar and his past criticism of the party.
“They have the right to take decisions within their party. However, no one should take any step that creates doubts, misgivings or causes harm,” BJP leader and Maharashtra Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule said.

headline: East Godavari Superintendent of Police D. Narasimha Kishore said on Sunday that the police would file a petition before the court seeking the custody of Suravarapu Daswanth and Andrew Joseph Edwards for further investigation into the death of medico ...
full_text:
East Godavari Superintendent of Police D. Narasimha Kishore said on Sunday that the police would file a petition before the court seeking the custody of Suravarapu Daswanth and Andrew Joseph Edwards for further investigation into the death of medico K. Priyanka.
On August 7, the two accused were remanded in judicial custody till August 21 for allegedly hitting Dr. Priyanka with a car in an inebriated condition at a mall in Rajamahendravaram on August 3.
The accused allegedly hit Dr. Priyanka twice with the car before running over her while she was riding pillion on a two-wheeler. She was declared brain dead at G.S.L. Hospital in Rajamahendravaram on the same day and died on August 7 at a private hospital in Secunderabad, according to the G.S.L. Hospital management.
A native of Kurnool district, Dr. Priyanka had enrolled in the Doctor of Medicine (MD) course at G.S.L. Medical College, Rajamahendravaram, in February 2026.
Speaking to reporters at a press conference here on Sunday, Mr. Narasimha Kishore said the police would seek the custody of the two accused for further investigation. “As per the preliminary probe, Dr. Priyanka and the accused were not known to each other,” he said.
Mr. Daswanth, who was driving the car that hit Dr. Priyanka, holds an engineering degree and was preparing to go abroad, while Mr. Edwards operates lorries on hire, the SP said.
“The case was registered under the charge of culpable homicide not amounting to murder as of August 9. The charges will be altered based on the findings of the further investigation,” Mr. Narasimha Kishore said.
₹20 lakh financial assistance
Meanwhile, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu expressed anguish over Dr. Priyanka’s death and directed officials to extend ₹20 lakh financial assistance to her family. He assured the family of the government’s continued support and directed the authorities to provide all possible assistance.
Mr. Naidu, who had earlier reviewed the incident with the District Collector and SP, directed the authorities to ensure stringent legal action against those responsible. He also assured the family of a speedy investigation and trial.
Tourism Minister Kandula Durgesh said the State government would bear the medical expenses incurred by Dr. Priyanka since August 3. He said the Chief Minister had assured the family of justice.
Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan and Home Minister V. Anitha also expressed grief over Dr. Priyanka’s death and assured the family of government support. Ms. Anitha said strict action would be taken against those responsible.

headline: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is facing considerable flak over the shoddy condition of service road stretches on either side of the 17-km-long Edappally-Aroor NH 66 bypass, considered the busiest national highway (NH) corridor in Ke...
full_text:
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is facing considerable flak over the shoddy condition of service road stretches on either side of the 17-km-long Edappally-Aroor NH 66 bypass, considered the busiest national highway (NH) corridor in Kerala.
The situation is particularly bad on either side of the Edappally overbridge-Edappally Junction-Palarivattom stretch, where the agency has been constructing a pair of flyover-cum-underpasses for well over a year.
“Motorists and pedestrians have been hard hit by the inordinate delay in completing the flyovers, unscientific diversion of vehicles, severely potholed service roads and the resultant traffic chaos on Kerala’s busiest NH corridor,” said D.G. Suresh, acting president of Ernakulam District Residents Associations’ Apex Council (EDRAAC) and a resident of Palarivattom.
“There are inadequate direction boards around work sites, while the service roads merge with the main carriageway in a confusing manner. The situation becomes even worse whenever a nearby mall announces a discount sale, as the additional influx of motorists to Edappally Junction, where NH 66 converges with NH 544, adds to the traffic congestion.”
“In this situation, the NHAI ought to urgently repair potholed service roads, raise road shoulders to the level of the tarred carriageway, and fast-track work on the pair of flyovers and underpasses. headline: Violations in 'deep burial' of medical waste by 17 states, UTs: CPCB to NGT
full_text:
Violations in 'deep burial' of medical waste by 17 states, UTs: CPCB to NGT
New Delhi, The Central Pollution Control Board has informed the National Green Tribunal that it will take action against states and Union territories not complying with some rules for disposal of biomedical waste.
The green body is hearing a matter regarding violations in the handling, treatment and disposal of biomedical waste by treatment facilities.
In an order dated August 5, a bench of NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and expert member Afroz Ahmad noted that CPCB had filed a report regarding the "deep burial" of biomedical waste which was practised across 17 states and Union territories in the country.
Deep burial remains a limited disposal method under the Biomedical Waste Management Rules, permissible only in rural or remote regions where a Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facility is unavailable. Such practice requires prior approval of the prescribed state authority.
The tribunal noted that out of 9,178 Healthcare Facilities using deep burial, only 5,715 were compliant with standard provisions, with the most frequent violations including failure to maintain a minimum groundwater table level of six metres below the burial pit and operating without proper authorisation from prescribed authorities .
It noted that the report showed significant gaps in compliance across various parameters by the states and UT's concerned. For instance, in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, all 111 and 33 HCFs, respectively, were found non-compliant.
The tribunal said, "Counsel appearing for the CPCB has informed that presently the communications have been sent to the concerned State Pollution Control Boards /Pollution Control Committees of the violating states and UTs and, if the compliance is not done within eight weeks, then the directions under Section 5 of the Environment Act, 1986 will be issued."
The provision grants the Centre enforcement powers to issue binding directives, including to regulate or shut down industrial operations and terminate utility services.
In its order, the tribunal directed the CPCB to file a further progress report at least one week before the next date of hearing on October 28, 2026.

headline: In a unique blend of traditional faith and modern water management concerns, the Telangana government will conduct a grand Varuna Yagam at Nagarjunasagar on Monday (August 10), seeking abundant rainfall across the Krishna and Godavari river basins to...

In a unique blend of traditional faith and modern water management concerns, the Telangana government will conduct a grand Varuna Yagam at Nagarjunasagar on Monday (August 10), seeking abundant rainfall across the Krishna and Godavari river basins to ensure water security for the State.
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy is scheduled to participate in the special Vedic ritual, while Irrigation and Civil Supplies Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy will lead the programme. The event will be held at the Vijay Vihar premises in Nagarjunasagar, where 108 priests and Vedic scholars will perform elaborate rituals around 11 homa kundams throughout the day.
The yagam comes at a crucial time for Telangana. Although the southwest monsoon has crossed the halfway mark, inflows into the Krishna and Godavari river systems remain below expectations. Authorities point out that Telangana’s water security depends not only on rainfall within the State but also on precipitation in the upper catchment areas of Maharashtra and Karnataka, which contribute a major share of flows into both river basins.
Officials said the ritual is being conducted with the collective prayer that reservoirs, tanks and rivers receive adequate inflows, groundwater levels improve, and farmers are assured sufficient irrigation water during the ongoing agricultural season.
Current reservoir figures underline the concern. Nagarjunasagar, which has a gross storage capacity of 312.045 TMC, currently holds only 145.65 TMC of water, leaving 166.39 TMC of vacant storage. The reservoir level stands at about 518 feet, significantly below its full reservoir level of 590 feet. On the same date last year, the project held around 310.25 TMC, almost reaching full capacity.
At the same time, inflows in the Krishna basin are gradually improving. Almatti is receiving over 1.05 lakh cusecs of inflow, while releases continue downstream through Narayanpur, Jurala and Srisailam. However, irrigation experts maintain that sustained rainfall across upstream regions is essential for ensuring steady river flows and filling major reservoirs.
Minister Uttam Kumar Reddy said the government’s objective is clear: to secure abundant rainfall, healthy river flows, full reservoirs and prosperity for Telangana’s farming community. While scientific monitoring of rainfall and reservoir levels continues, the Varuna Yagam symbolises a collective appeal for nature’s support in safeguarding the State’s water resources.

full_text:

Edited by: Ayush Pandey / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 09, 2026, 14:14 IST

Meta must follow Indian law, not just global rules: Govt after MeitY talks (Mark Zuckerberg)
NEW DELHI: Meta's platforms must comply with Indian law and cannot be governed solely by the company's global policies, news agency ANI reported quoting government sources said on Sunday.This follows a series of meetings between the social media giant and the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY). Officials also clarified that it would be factually incorrect to say the government had "directed Meta to completely overhaul its algorithm".The governmentâs focus, is on ensuring that Metaâs content policies, platform guidelines and moderation systems are aligned with Indian law. While concerns remain, officials said the discussions are aimed at securing concrete changes from the company rather than simply seeking assurances, ANI reported quoting sources.
Sources told ANI that India's cultural context is not always fully understood by teams based outside the country. They said Meta needs greater local input, including stronger understanding of Indian languages and cultural nuances, to improve content moderation in India.
The latest clarification came after a meeting on Friday between Meta's technical team and MeitY officials, during which the company explained its existing systems for handling harmful content online. Technical discussions between the two sides remain underway, with another round of meetings expected next week, sources said.On child sexual abuse material (CSAM), government sources told ANI that there is zero tolerance and zero compromise.Officials said allowing such material to remain on Meta's platforms would amount to a serious violation of rules. They said the company needs to adopt stronger and more proactive measures, with concrete action expected instead of assurances.The issue was also raised during earlier meetings between Meta's global team and government officials, amid wider concerns over the company's content moderation systems.The government has also raised concerns over deepfakes involving prominent personalities.Sources told ANI that content posted from authorised or verified handles should not be incorrectly identified as deepfakes. Officials said such sensitive cases cannot be left entirely to automated detection systems and called for a "human-in-the-loop" mechanism to ensure content is properly reviewed before any takedown.The government has also questioned Meta over synthetically generated content that reappears after being identified and removed as a deepfake.Officials have sought details from Meta on the concrete steps it is taking to prevent such content from resurfacing after removal.Meta's recommendation and virality algorithms have also come under scrutiny during the discussions.The government questioned why users are frequently shown content unrelated to their stated interests and whether this points to shortcomings in Meta's recommendation systems, ANI reported.Officials also asked why synthetically generated content continues to be amplified through the company's algorithms.The government has insisted that once such content is flagged, it should not be recommended further or repeatedly resurface on the platform, sources said.The issue of Meta's recommendation systems had also figured in earlier meetings with IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and senior ministry officials, when the company's global team was questioned about its algorithms and compliance with Indian laws.The latest discussions follow several rounds of engagement between Meta and the Indian government over deepfakes, CSAM, bot accounts, synthetic content and the company's compliance with Indian laws.According to earlier reports, Meta's technical team had explained its proposed measures to address the concerns raised by the government and said it had solutions to tackle deepfakes, CSAM and bot accounts.
The government has also been examining Meta's compliance with intermediary provisions under Indian law, including the conditions governing safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act.The Centre had earlier sought action against deepfake content and was examining whether Meta's role in determining what content users see could have implications for its status as an intermediary.The latest discussions, however, have focused on the technical functioning of Meta's systems and how its global policies are implemented in India.
As the talks continue, government sources said the objective is not to demand a complete overhaul of Meta's algorithm but to ensure that its platforms, content policies and moderation mechanisms comply with Indian law and adequately account for India's linguistic and cultural context.

headline: Ladakh LG disburses Rs 1.10 crore incentive to over 1,200 Pashmina herders
full_text:
Ladakh LG disburses Rs 1.10 crore incentive to over 1,200 Pashmina herders
Ladakh has transferred Rs 1.10 crore to more than 1,200 Pashmina herders under a first-time production incentive. The move, along with an Rs 8 crore revolving fund, aims to raise incomes and speed up payments.
Ladakh Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena on Sunday disbursed Rs 1.10 crore to more than 1,200 Pashmina goat herders as a production-based incentive, describing it as a major step towards strengthening the Pashmina sector and supporting nomadic herders. The incentive, introduced for the first time, is aimed at raising the income of herders and improving the profitability and sustainability of the sector.
The 25 per cent production-based incentive was announced after the first meeting of the Ladakh Pashmina Development Board last month. Speaking at the Changthang Nomadic Festival on the banks of Tso Moriri in Korzok, Saxena also announced a revolving fund of Rs 8 crore for the All Changthang Pashmina Growers Marketing Cooperative Society to ensure timely payments to growers.
Saxena said the incentive had already led to a rise in the collection of raw Pashmina, with 19 tonnes gathered till July this year, compared with 16 tonnes in the whole of 2025. Under the scheme, Rs 1.10 crore has been transferred through direct benefit transfer to over 1,200 herders, mostly from Samad, Kharnak and Korzok villages in Changthang district, which is known to be the largest producer of Pashmina wool.
Herders in Samad received about Rs 44 lakh, while those in Kharnak and Korzok received Rs 28 lakh and Rs 23 lakh respectively, making up the largest share of the incentive.
The Lieutenant Governor said 60 per cent of the incentive received by beneficiaries would be reinvested in scientific breeding of Pashmina goats, 20 per cent would go towards modern combing equipment and other infrastructure, and the remaining 20 per cent could be used for household and personal needs. He said this would help ensure the financial sustainability of herders.
On the revolving fund, Saxena said it would help the cooperative society, which runs a Pashmina dehairing plant in Leh, make faster payments to growers for their produce. Under the arrangement, 50 per cent of the cost of Pashmina will be paid immediately to producers, while the remaining amount will be cleared within two months, ending earlier delays of eight to 10 months.
Calling for wider use of scientific practices, Saxena urged herders to raise average fibre production from 200 grams per goat at present to at least 350 grams per goat. He also encouraged an increase in the Pashmina goat population from around two lakh to at least four lakh over the next three years through scientific breeding. He stressed the need to improve the cleanliness and quality of raw Pashmina to reduce wastage and secure better prices.
The Lieutenant Governor described Pashmina as a timeless heritage of Ladakh and the Changpa nomadic community, which he said had mastered goat rearing over centuries. He said the Changpa community was a living example of resilience, sustainability and harmonious coexistence with nature. He said, "Pashmina is not merely a product; it is part of Ladakh's cultural identity and the livelihood of thousands of our pastoral families. Our objective is to ensure that those who have preserved this heritage for generations, receive a greater share of its economic value." He added, "The Ladakh administration's decision of 25 per cent production-based incentive and the Rs 8-crore revolving fund is strengthening the Pashmina value chain and improving returns to nomadic pastoral communities."
The Changthang Nomadic Festival drew more than 10,000 people, including a large number of foreign tourists. Saxena said the festival, which began as a local celebration a few years ago and has now grown into an international event, had become an important platform for showcasing Changpa culture, traditional pastoral practices, handicrafts, music, dance, cuisine and way of life to audiences in India and abroad. The announcements made at the festival focused on raising herders' incomes, improving production and ensuring faster payments across the Pashmina value chain.

headline: Shoeshine boy outside schoolIn 1959, on his first day to school as a five-and-a-half-year-old in Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh, Kailash Satyarthi (he was Sharma then) spotted a shoeshine boy sitting quietly outside the gate. Curious and confused, he asked ...
full_text:
Shoeshine boy outside schoolIn 1959, on his first day to school as a five-and-a-half-year-old in Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh, Kailash Satyarthi (he was Sharma then) spotted a shoeshine boy sitting quietly outside the gate. Curious and confused, he asked a teacher, âWhy is a child sitting outside the school?â He was told that it is not uncommon for poor kids to work.Satyarthi was not satisfied. Every day, he would see the boy, roughly his own age, sit there with his father until one day he gathered courage and asked his father why his son was not at school. The man spoke with a deep hopelessness, recalls Satyarthi. He said, âBabu, school jaane ke liye aap log to hain. Hum to yehi kaam karne ke liye paida hote hain (There are people like you who go to school. We are born to do this kind of work).âAs a child, Satyarthi felt there was something wrong in this, but he couldnât understand what. âI was taught that God has made us all equal. Why this inequality, I wondered,â he recalls.This encounter gave him a different perspective on life at a very early age.Friend who dropped outSatyarthi was just 11 when he found that his best friend and some other students had stopped attending classes in the new session. He was told that such dropouts happened because the poor could not afford even nominal fees and textbooks.Satyarthi wanted to do something. He got an idea and shared it with a friend. âMy father had given me some money to buy sweets after I had cleared the examination. We went to a vegetable vendor, gave him the money and rented his pushcart,â he says.They went around the neighbourhood, urging people to donate the used books of their children, so that the needy could use them. âWithin a few hours, the cart was full and we had to take a second turn. We collected 2,300 books that day,â he remembers.Soon, another idea â a permanent book bank for needy kids â was born, in which even headmasters and bookstore owners joined in. About 10,000 books were collected.Decades later, when Satyarthi went to Vidisha after winning the Nobel in 2014, he heard someone call out his name during an open-jeep parade. âThe gentleman said, âI am a retired headmaster. I had almost quit my studies due to lack of money. But your book bank initiative allowed me to continueâ,â Satyarthi recalls.It was quite a moment for both.Wasal Khan and SaboAt 27, Satyarthi had started a journal, âSangharsh Jaari Rahegaâ, which spoke up for the marginalised and oppressed. The office was near Mandi House in central Delhi. One day, a sickly person in a lungi knocked on his door and passed out after a few words. He was carrying a copy of the magazine.When he regained consciousness, the man started whimpering, âBabuji, please save my daughter.â His name was Wasal Khan. Over the next few minutes, he poured out his life story. His wife and he were lured away from a village in Aligarh district, taken to Punjabâs Sirhind, where they had been enslaved in a brick kiln for 17 years. They worked without pay, given just food and used clothes to wear. âHe said the owners were planning to sell Sabo, his 15-year-old daughter, to brothel agents from Delhi,â says Satyarthi. Wasal had escaped on the back of a truck and reached Chandigarh, where a magazine subscriber had given him an old copy and asked to go to Delhi for help.Satyarthi was faced with a tough choice: write an article or take action. He opted for the latter. He organised a truck and, on reaching the spot, he and his friends from Punjab â one of them had a camera â boldly told the lone gun-wielding chowkidar that they were journalists from Delhi. The watchman ran away. âWe were about to leave with 36 men, women, and children when a police jeep arrived with the owners. They started slapping us and forcing the labourers to get down from the truck,â Satyarthi recalls. The truck driver had run away. Satyarthi and his friends too had to flee. âOur slippers were lost, our clothes torn.âSomehow they reached Chandigarh and then Delhi. âThey had taken away the camera. But two reels, which vividly captured the labourers on camera, were with us. We had good evidence,â he says. Satyarthi approached Swami Agnivesh and, through him, renowned lawyer Gobinda Mukhoty, who filed a habeas corpus petition in Delhi high court. Since nobody knew the name of the brick kiln owners, a notice was sent to Punjab Police and the state. Eventually, Wasal Khan, Sabo and the rest were produced in court and freed.The children, who had grown up inside the brick kiln, had no idea of life outside. âAs we walked from the high court towards our office, they were jumping like frogs released from a bucket, oblivious to the traffic. That day, I realised what true freedom really meant. I could feel God in their joy. We also knew this was the field where we have to work. Over the decades, our organisation, Bachpan Bachao Andolan, has rescued over 1,40,000 men, women and children,â he says.Compassion and AI ethicsThis is the age of AI and Satyarthi believes that technology should factor in compassion (karuna), which he defines as âa force born from feeling the suffering of others and drives us to take action.â Satyarthi feels that AI technology must be governed by a sense of responsibility during its designing, development and deployment. âAI should have a moral compass. It cannot just be profit-hungry,â he says.

headline: 96 pc Indian travellers opt to adapt, not cancel amid disruptions: Report
full_text:
96 pc Indian travellers opt to adapt, not cancel amid disruptions: Report
New Delhi, As many as "96 per cent" of Indian travellers are willing to adapt their travel plans rather than cancel them when disruptions occur, highlighting their resilient approach to travel, according to a new report by online travel agency Booking.com.
The inaugural "Travel Happiness Index", based on a survey of over 10,000 travellers across 10 Asia-Pacific markets, found that travel continues to be a major source of happiness and wellbeing for Indians.
"As many as 96 per cent say they would rather adapt their travel plans than cancel when disruptions occur," reads the report.
"Among those adapting their plans, 28 per cent would opt for an alternative destination, 19 per cent would postpone their trip and another 19 per centwould change the timing or duration," reads the report.
Similarly, as per the report, an overwhelming "99 per cent" per cent of Indian travellers associate travel with positive emotions, while "90 per cent" say having a trip to look forward to lifts their mood.
About "82 per cent" consider travel essential to their overall happiness and wellbeing, while happiness , relaxation and excitement were the top emotions associated with travel.
The study also found that Indian travellers are increasingly prioritising meaningful experiences over packed itineraries.
Around "78 per cent" prefer local food and meaningful experiences, while "68 per cent" said family trips are the most enjoyable.
Despite concerns over extreme weather and health and hygiene risks , crime , inflation and political instability , travel remains a priority.
Around "70 per cent" state they feel more confident about their ability to afford travel than before.
"Travel is increasingly becoming more than just a break from routine, it is an investment in wellbeing, relationships and personal enrichment.
"What's particularly encouraging is their resilience, rather than putting their plans on hold during uncertainty, most are choosing to adapt and make the most of their trips," Santosh Kumar, regional head, South Asia at Booking.com, said in a statement.
The research was commissioned by Booking.com and independently conducted among 10,136 respondents aged 21 years and above across 10 Asia-Pacific countries.
The online survey was conducted in May 2026, with 1,015 respondents from India.

headline: Leaders of the Puducherry- based All India N.R. Congress (AINRC) on Sunday announced the party has plans to expand its footprint in Tamil Nadu.
full_text:
Leaders of the Puducherry- based All India N.R. Congress (AINRC) on Sunday announced the party has plans to expand its footprint in Tamil Nadu.
The party celebrated birthday (August 4) of the AINRC founder and Puducherry Chief Minister N Rangasamy, in Chennai on Sunday.
Former Minister and senior party leader K. Lakshminarayanan said many people from Tamil Nadu especially youngsters “who were impressed by Mr. Rangasamy’s leadership”, had expressed their desire to contest in Tamil Nadu on behalf of the party. “We have plans to contest in the next elections,” he said.
Puducherry Minister P. Rajavelu, said he was “amazed to see the kind of support that Mr. Rangasamy had in Tamil Nadu”.
The party also celebrated the birth anniversary of former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister K Kamaraj in advance. Former MLA and Member, Pondy Backward Classes Commission, M. Ilango recalled he and Mr. Rangasamy had met Kamaraj at the same time in 1974 during the elections. “We went as a group. We both became first time MLAs at the same time.”
Leaders including V. P. Sivakolundhu, N. S. Jayapal and Khaliyan Kandaswamy participated in the celebrations.

headline: For 74-year-old K.K. Xaviour, a settler farmer from Poozhithode near Chakkittappara, the State government’s decision to confer the Kera Kesary Award-2025 on him is a recognition of a farming practice he has followed for nearly three decades.
full_text:
For 74-year-old K.K. Xaviour, a settler farmer from Poozhithode near Chakkittappara, the State government’s decision to confer the Kera Kesary Award-2025 on him is a recognition of a farming practice he has followed for nearly three decades.
Mr. Xaviour has been selected for the award for his independent efforts to promote organic coconut farming using high-yielding Kuttiyadi coconut saplings. His two-acre coconut plantation, nurtured over the years through organic methods, has been the mainstay of his agricultural activities.
“I planted nearly 100 coconut saplings about 30 years ago. I have been earning a good income from the plantation ever since. Coconut farming can be a profitable enterprise if one is committed to working independently,” says Mr. Xaviour.
He follows only organic farming methods and makes effective use of rainwater to meet the water requirements of his farm. Cow dung and cow urine are used as organic manure to maintain the fertility of the soil without depending on chemical fertilisers.
A recipient of several regional awards for his contributions to farming, Mr. Xaviour belongs to a family that migrated to Chakkittappara from Kottayam district several decades ago. His wife, Alice, has been a constant companion in his agricultural pursuits.
“My three children are abroad now. Alice is my main support. We undertake most of the agricultural work together without relying on external labour,” he says.
Mr. Xaviour’s farm is not confined to coconut cultivation. A keen follower of traditional farming practices, he also cultivates a variety of fruits, different varieties of pepper and arecanut. He manages a one-acre rubber plantation as well for additional income.
For this upland resident, farming is more than a livelihood even at this age, as he is healthy and passionate about carrying out all agricultural jobs in the field. When pursued with dedication and care for the land, it can always be a positive and profitable enterprise for a decent standard of living,” he adds.
Rasma Nair, Agricultural Officer at Chakkittappara Krishi Bhavan, says that Mr. Xaviour has emerged as a model farmer in the village through his innovative approach.

headline: 'Bid to silence him': Tarun Tejpal's daughter says he was targeted for investigative journalism after his conviction
full_text:
'Bid to silence him': Tarun Tejpal's daughter says he was targeted for investigative journalism after his conviction
Bombay high court sentenced Tarun Tejpal to 10 years in jail for raping a junior colleague in 2013.
Days after former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal was convicted in a rape case by Bombay High Court, his daughter Cara Tejpal has decried foul play. Cara has reportedly claimed that Tarun was targeted because of Tehelka magazine's investigative journalism, with the rape allegation being used as a means to "silence" him.
Cara, in a statement on Saturday, said she did not care if she was labelled a "rape apologist" or the “child of a rapist” as she linked the rape case against Tarun to Tehelka's investigative journalism and the “controversies surrounding the magazine's reports on corruption” and the alleged wrongdoing by those in power, news agency PTI reported.
‘Examined evidence for 13 years’
"I'm not that 23-year-old anymore. I'm 36 and I couldn't care less about being called a 'rape apologist' or 'child of rapist' or whatever vile slur is used against me," she was quoted as saying.
She said she had examined the evidence in the rape case against her father for 13 years and was convinced that he was ‘innocent.’
"I was 23 years old when my father was arrested. I was 31 when he was acquitted, and today, at 36, I stand by him as he is convicted by the Bombay High Court on the basis of a false allegation of rape filed suo moto by the state of Goa," she said, adding that she had initially been "terrified of speaking the truth".
She further claimed that the media coverage surrounding the case deeply affected her, but was no longer willing to remain silent despite the criticism she could face for supporting her father.
"Tarun Tejpal was more than a thorn in the side of the BJP government, and what better way to silence him than to portray him as the most reviled of all sinners-a rapist," Cara was quoted as saying.
Also read: AAP's Saurabh Bharadwaj alleges ‘ ₹22,000 crore rice scam plan’ by Delhi govt
She further alleged that the case was accompanied by a strong public narrative that discouraged people from questioning the allegations.
"The truth is the truth. No court, no prime minister, no godi media can take that from us," she said, urging people to read the "actual facts of the case" rather than relying on headlines and what she described as uninformed public discourse.
Tarun Tejpal convicted
On Thursday, the Bombay high court at Goa overturned a trial court’s 2022 acquittal and sentenced Tejpal to 10 years in jail for raping a junior colleague during the ThinkFest conference at a five-star hotel in Goa in 2013.
A bench of justices Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar held that the trial court’s appreciation of evidence was not only unreasonable but perverse, and that its evaluation of the testimony exhibited multiple fatal flaws stemming from “preconceived notions” and reliance on how an "ideal" victim should physically resist or emotionally react.
The high court sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment and a ₹5 lakh fine under section 376(2)(f) of the Indian Penal Code (rape by a relative, guardian or teacher, or a person in a position of trust or authority towards the woman), 10 years of rigorous imprisonment and ₹5 lakh fine under section 376(2)(f) (rape by a person in position of control or dominance over a woman), one year in prison and ₹10,000 fine under section 354 (criminal force to outrage modesty of woman), one year jail under section 354A (sexual harassment), three years rigorous imprisonment and ₹10,000 fine under section 354B (using criminal force to disrobe a woman), a fine of ₹500 each under sections 341 and 342 (wrongful restraint and punishment for wrongful confinement).
The complainant had alleged that Tejpal raped her on November 7 and attempted to assault her again on November 8.
Following the allegations, Tejpal resigned from his position and issued an email to staff apologising for the incident. While he did not specifically refer to the allegations, he referred to the incident as a “shameful lapse of judgement.”

headline: UP man hacked to death, cops suspect revenge over accused's cousin's murder
full_text:
UP man hacked to death, cops suspect revenge over accused's cousin's murder
Shivkumar Tripathi was attacked at a brahm bhoj in Gorakhpur and later killed on the way to hospital. Police suspect the assault may have been driven by revenge over a 2024 murder case.
A 52-year-old man was hacked to death in Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur district, with police suspecting the killing may have been carried out in revenge for a murder last year, an official said on Sunday.
Police said Shivkumar Tripathi was attacked on Saturday evening and later killed despite efforts by villagers to take him to hospital. A case has been registered, and several people have been detained as investigators probe the motive and the role of those involved in the attack.
According to police, Tripathi was attending a 'brahm bhoj' or funeral feast in Ahirauli village under the Sikriganj police station area when he was allegedly attacked from behind with a 'banka' or cleaver by Rahul Chaudhary, a resident of the same village. Eyewitnesses told police that Tripathi suffered serious injuries and collapsed on the spot.
Villagers then rushed him towards a hospital in an autorickshaw. However, police said the accused, along with his brother Rohit, allegedly intercepted the vehicle on the way. Despite resistance from locals, the two allegedly forced Tripathi out of the vehicle, dragged him nearly 200 metres away and attacked him repeatedly with swords, killing him on the spot.
Police said the preliminary investigation suggests the murder may have been committed to avenge the killing of the accused's cousin about a year ago. According to villagers, Rahul's cousin Adesh Chaudhary was murdered in 2024, and some members of Tripathi's extended family were named as accused in that case. Investigators are examining whether Saturday's killing was an act of vengeance.
Superintendent of Police (South) Dinesh Kumar Puri said on Sunday that a case has been registered in connection with the murder. Three named accused, and seven others have been detained for questioning, and police are probing the exact motive and the role of those involved in the attack.
Tripathi worked as a contractor for the electricity department, and his son Aditya Tripathi is an advocate practising in Gorakhpur civil court. The body has been sent for post-mortem.

headline: 'Pellet guns strictly for...': Ranchi police 'fully prepared' as Jharkhand students announce ‘Vidhan Sabha gherao’
full_text:
'Pellet guns strictly for...': Ranchi police 'fully prepared' as Jharkhand students announce ‘Vidhan Sabha gherao’
Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said precautionary force deployment would be carried out effectively as a large number of students are expected.
Ranchi Police on Sunday said it was “fully prepared” to deal with the planned “Vidhan Sabha gherao” by JPSC-JSSC aspirants, while assuring that no action would be taken against protesters as long as the demonstration remained peaceful.
Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said precautionary force deployment would be carried out effectively as a large number of students are expected to take part in the protest.
“Precautionary force deployment will be carried out effectively; the Ranchi Police is fully prepared. There will be a large number of students. Instructions have been issued to all Ranchi Police personnel that if the protesters conduct themselves peacefully, no inconvenience will be done to anyone. However, if anyone attempts to resort to violence, appropriate legal action will be taken against them...” Rana told news agency ANI.
Police clarify pellet gun video
Rana also addressed concerns over a viral video showing what appeared to be a pellet gun being carried by security personnel.
“If a pellet gun is being carried, it is strictly for emergency situations. Regarding the viral video—what is being mistaken for a pellet gun is actually a paintball gun; it fires soft, colored balls used to mark and identify troublemakers. It is not a pellet gun...” he said.
The clarification came as student aspirants prepared to march towards the Jharkhand Assembly on Monday amid their ongoing agitation over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.
Also Read | All 3 JPSC members quit amid CID summons; Jharkhand Governor accepts resignations
Students reject govt offer on CGL probe
The police statement came after a fresh round of talks between student representatives and a Jharkhand government delegation on Sunday.
Student leader Ravindra Paswan said the government had agreed to consider cancelling the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) Civil Services Examination, JPSC Backlog 2023 and JPSC Backlog 2025 examinations.
“This was the second round of talks with the government delegation. Regarding the specifics-specifically the 14th JPSC, JPSC Backlog 2023, and JPSC Backlog 2025 exams, the government has decided to consider cancelling all three,” he said.
Paswan said the government had also agreed to several demands linked to recruitment reforms. However, issues such as age relaxation remained unresolved.
On the Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, the students had sought a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe. The government, however, proposed a judicial inquiry headed by a retired judge instead.
'Vidhan Sabha gherao will continue'
Another student leader, Kunal, said the planned Assembly march would go ahead but stressed that protesters would maintain peace.
“Let me clarify that our Vidhan Sabha gherao will continue peacefully. Our demand is for a CBI inquiry; we will not compromise on that,” Kunal said.
The student groups have been protesting over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC examinations and are seeking action against those responsible.
Three JPSC members resign
Meanwhile, Jharkhand Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar accepted the resignations of three members of the JPSC Commission on Sunday, according to a statement issued by the Lok Bhavan.
The resignations of Ajita Bhattacharya, Anima Hansda and Jamal Ahmed were accepted following a recommendation from the state government.

headline: Amid taunts over no woman in Karnataka Cong cabinet, change in offing as Shivakumar heads to Delhi
full_text:
Amid taunts over no woman in Karnataka Cong cabinet, change in offing as Shivakumar heads to Delhi
Union minister Rijiju had asked about Karnataka as Rahul, in a social media AMA, said “no country can be successful if women are not expressing themselves”.
With focus on his assurance that women “will certainly” have a place in his cabinet, Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar is headed for Delhi for meetings with the Congress leadership. The assurance gained significance after a sharp exchange between Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Union minister Kiren Rijiju of the BJP over women's representation.
Shivakumar is scheduled to leave for Delhi on Sunday evening and is expected to meet Congress general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal and other senior leaders over Sunday and Monday, reports said. The discussions are reportedly expected to cover allocation of portfolios to the 19 ministers inducted earlier this month — two months after DKS, 64, became CM in place of veteran leader Siddaramaiah, 79 — plus pending changes in the ministry, including the possibility of inducting a woman.
Shivakumar took over as CM in June after the Congress high command agreed to the change of leader. His initial council of ministers was formed with 14 ministers, before the expansion of August 3, when 19 more took oath. The expansion took the ministry's strength to 33, including Shivakumar, against the constitutional ceiling of 34. One berth therefore remains vacant — and that is now the slot that could go to a woman amid a wider debate on gender representation.
Rahul-Rijiju exchange on woman representation
Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi had, on Friday, while arguing that the Women's Reservation Act of 2023 be implemented without being linked to delimitation, said, “The energy of India’s women is trapped, is not allowed to express itself, is not allowed to imagine.” He had argued in response to an ask-me-anything session on social media: “For me, no country can be successful if the women in the country are not expressing themselves… Our country is stunted and incomplete without the expression of our women.”
Minister Rijiju had hit back, remarking there was a “visible change of heart” in Gandhi's position and urging the Congress to support women's reservation “unconditionally”.
Gandhi responded that Congress had already supported the law, which was passed unanimously in 2023, and said the party had a problem only with its being linked to delimitation, that is, a change in number and boundaries of the constituencies. “Implement the 2023 law. Without any conditions,” Gandhi said.
It was then that Rijiju turned the argument towards Karnataka. “There's no woman in Karnataka DK Shivakumar's Cabinet! This raises serious questions over Congress's stand on the 33% Women quota,” the minister posted on X.
Rahul Gandhi did not react specifically to that.
What DKS said
However, Shivakumar responded by saying Congress had itself piloted and passed the women's reservation law. “So, in Karnataka, definitely we are sorting out that issue. Rijiju may not worry about the Congress party,” the CM said in Bengaluru on Saturday. In PM Narendra Modi's central government, seven of the 71 ministers are women.
A day later, DKS gave an even clearer indication that the omission could soon be corrected. “There will certainly be a place for a woman in our cabinet. We are committed to giving greater representation to women,” Shivakumar said.
Who may get berth
The assurance came as 19 ministers were sworn in on August 3, with no woman among them. The absence drew immediate criticism from the BJP as well as sections of the Congress, particularly given the party's emphasis on women's political representation.
The next question is, who could get the berth. One name that has gained prominence is Gayathri Shantegowda, a member of the Karnataka Legislative Council. She was excluded from the list at the last minute for the August 3 swearing-in, TOI had reported citing unnamed sources.
Former minister Laxmi Hebbalkar is considered another prominent possibility. The Belagavi Rural MLA was the lone woman minister in Siddaramaiah's previous government.
Roopakala Shashidhar, the Kolar Gold Fields (KGF) MLA, and Kaneez Fatima, the Gulbarga North MLA, are among the names that have repeatedly figured in reports on possible women inductees. MLC Arathi Krishna is seen as another contender, as per The New Indian Express.
The choice, though, depended not only on gender representation but also on calculations over region, caste and political factions. Shivakumar's Delhi meetings are expected to address these concerns at large too.
The Karnataka legislature's monsoon session begins on August 13.

headline: Assam govt begins flood damage survey, compensation to start by mid-September
full_text:
Assam govt begins flood damage survey, compensation to start by mid-September
The survey, which will continue until August 30, will take stock of damages to affected families to provide compensation for loss
Three weeks after heavy flooding caused extensive damage in four districts of Assam, the state government on Sunday began a survey to assess the damage caused by the deluge that has claimed 99 lives, destroyed hundreds of houses and killed thousands of livestock.
The survey, which will continue until August 30, will take stock of damages to affected families to provide compensation for loss and assistance towards rehabilitation.
Revenue and disaster management minister Keshab Mahanta said the survey would take place in Sibsagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Golaghat, which were ravaged by flooding on July 19 and continue to remain inundated and affected.
“Government officials will visit each affected family to assess the loss of lives and damages. Once this process is complete, the survey will be reviewed to ensure no one is left out. We hope to start providing monetary compensation by mid September,” he said.
Giving details of the compensation structure, minister for cultural affairs Bimal Borah said that the compensation could range from ₹1.78 lakhs per family to over ₹3.5 lakhs.
“Those whose houses are completely damaged will get ₹1.20 lakhs, severely damaged ones where appliances and items inside the house are also ruined will also get a similar amount,” he said.
Also Read:What is happening in Assam? Floods batter villages, over 4 lakh impacted, 60+ dead
Borah informed that compensation for each cattle will be around ₹37,500, for damaged handlooms they will get ₹5,000 each, those who have lost goats, sheep or pigs will get ₹4,000 for each animal (up to a maximum of 30 animals per household).
“Compensation will also be paid for loss of poultry and damage to crops. If everything is taken into account each affected family could get a minimum compensation of ₹1.78 lakhs and a maximum sum of somewhere above ₹3.5 lakhs each,” he said.
The Assam government had earlier paid ₹15,000 each to around 70,000 affected families as immediate relief. It was also decided that ₹9 lakh would be given to the family of each person who lost their life in the flooding. Other announcements included a six-month moratorium on loans, an extension of the loan repayment tenure by one to two years, and an additional ₹2,500 each to families in flood-affected districts covered under the flagship Orunodoi poverty alleviation scheme. Flood-affected families will not have to pay land taxes for a year, and their electricity bills for July have been waived.
According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), till Sunday 101 people had lost their lives in floods while over 137,000 people in 10 districts continued to remain affected. A total of 8000 persons displaced by flooding are taking shelter in relief camps in 6 of the affected districts.

headline: As part of intensifying protests demanding a comprehensive inquiry into the death of Yogi (Jogi), who was reportedly killed in police firing during the 2003 Muthanga land agitation and the alleged human rights violations in connection with the stir, ...
full_text:
As part of intensifying protests demanding a comprehensive inquiry into the death of Yogi (Jogi), who was reportedly killed in police firing during the 2003 Muthanga land agitation and the alleged human rights violations in connection with the stir, an Adivasi-Dalit convention and Declaration of Rights were held at Sulthan Bathery in Wayanad on Sunday (August 9) on the occasion of the International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples.
The gathering was inaugurated by Bommi Amma of Cheeral, the oldest surviving participant in the Muthanga struggle.
Several people who participated in the land stir shared their experiences at the meeting, organised by the Adivasi Gothra Mahasabha (AGMS) and the Ambedkarite Democratic Front (ADF). In the evening, a cultural procession was taken out through the town under the leadership of the Adi Shakti Summer School, followed by a public meeting at the Municipal Town Hall. It was inaugurated by ADF State working chairperson K. Ambujakshan.
AGMS general secretary P.G. Janardhanan made the Declaration of Rights. The resolution demanded a fair investigation into Jogi’s death, implementation of the direction issued by the National Human Rights Commission calling for a comprehensive inquiry into the human rights violations during the Muthanga agitation and adequate compensation for all those affected by the violence.
Sivan Yogi, son of Jogi, and others attended.
The Muthanga land agitation has returned to the limelight after the Kalpetta Principal Sessions Court, on July 31, acquitted all the accused who stood trial, including social activist M. Geethanandan, in the case relating to the murder of police constable K.V. Vinod. However, the court convicted Geethanandan and three others on other charges related to the case and sentenced each to five years of rigorous imprisonment.

headline: संसद का मानसून सत्र इस समय चल रहा है. इस बीच चर्चा है कि सरकार इस सत्र में विदेशी अंशदान नियमन अधिनियम (FCRA) में संशोधन करने के लिए नया बिल ला सकती है. कांग्रेस पार्टी ने इस बिल का पुरजोर विरोध करने का मन बना लिया है.
full_text:
संसद का मानसून सत्र इस समय चल रहा है. इस बीच चर्चा है कि सरकार इस सत्र में विदेशी अंशदान नियमन अधिनियम (FCRA) में संशोधन करने के लिए नया बिल ला सकती है. कांग्रेस पार्टी ने इस बिल का पुरजोर विरोध करने का मन बना लिया है.
कांग्रेस का कहना है कि यह बिल 'ईसाई विरोधी' है. इस बिल से देश में काम कर रहे अल्पसंख्यक संगठनों को बहुत नुकसान होगा.
कांग्रेस नेताओं का मानना है कि एफसीआरए के नए नियमों से देश के दूर-दराज, ग्रामीण और आदिवासी इलाकों में चल रहे ईसाई संगठनों, स्कूलों और अस्पतालों पर बुरा असर पड़ेगा.
कांग्रेस सांसद हिबी ईडन का कहना है कि देश के कई मुश्किल इलाकों में ये संगठन शिक्षा और स्वास्थ्य सेवाएं दे रहे हैं. लेकिन, सरकार इन्हें दबाना चाहती है.
उन्होंने आरोप लगाया कि नए बिल के नियमों के तहत जिला मजिस्ट्रेट (DM) या उप-जिला मजिस्ट्रेट (SDM) नियमों के उल्लंघन पर किसी भी संस्था की संपत्ति को अपने कब्जे में ले सकते हैं. वे पुराने मामलों में भी जांच कर ऐसा कर सकते हैं.
कांग्रेस महासचिव केसी वेणुगोपाल ने भी साफ कह दिया है कि अगर सरकार इन दो-तीन दिनों में जल्दबाजी में यह बिल लाना चाहती है, तो उनका यह सपना पूरा नहीं होने दिया जाएगा.
राजनीतिक फायदा उठाने की तैयारी
राजनीतिक जानकारों का मानना है कि कांग्रेस इसे सिर्फ एक राजनीतिक मुद्दा नहीं मान रही, बल्कि इसके जरिए अल्पसंख्यक वोटर्स को अपने पाले में लाने का बड़ा मौका देख रही है. केरल और पूर्वोत्तर के राज्यों में ईसाई आबादी अच्छी खासी है. इसके अलावा आंध्र प्रदेश और पंजाब जैसे राज्यों में भी इनकी संख्या है.
विपक्ष को लगता है कि इस मुद्दे के जरिए इन वोटर्स को एकजुट किया जा सकता है. पार्टी को लगता है कि हाल ही में केरल विधानसभा चुनावों के दौरान भी इसी मुद्दे से उन्हें फायदा मिला था.
पहले भी बजट सत्र के दौरान केरल चुनावों से ठीक पहले कांग्रेस ने इस पर खूब हंगामा किया था. तब भारी विरोध को देखते हुए सरकार ने साफ कर दिया था कि अभी ऐसा कोई बिल लाने का इरादा नहीं है. हालांकि, तब तक इस मुद्दे की चर्चा जनता के बीच पहुंच चुकी थी.
समाजवादी पार्टी भी करेगी बिल का पुरजोर विरोध
सिर्फ कांग्रेस ही नहीं, बल्कि समाजवादी पार्टी (SP) ने भी कड़ा कदम उठाया है. पार्टी ने अपने लोकसभा और राज्यसभा के सभी सांसदों को पत्र जारी कर कहा है कि वे 10, 11 और 12 अगस्त को संसद में अनिवार्य रूप से मौजूद रहें.
माना जा रहा है कि जब केंद्र सरकार इन तारीखों में एफसीआरए बिल संसद में पेश करेगी, तो पूरा विपक्ष एकजुट होकर इसका कड़ा विरोध करेगा. इसे देखते हुए सभी विपक्षी दलों ने अपने सांसदों की उपस्थिति सुनिश्चित करनी शुरू कर दी है ताकि सदन में सरकार को घेरा जा सके.
क्या है FCRA बिल
फॉरेन कंट्रीब्यूशन रेगुलेशन एक्ट (FCRA) एक ऐसा कानून है जो भारत में गैर-सरकारी संगठनों (NGOs), चैरिटेबल ट्रस्टों, शैक्षणिक संस्थानों और धार्मिक निकायों द्वारा विदेशी फंडिंग को लेने और उसके इस्तेमाल को नियंत्रित करता है. इसके तहत विदेशी चंदा पाने के लिए गृह मंत्रालय से रजिस्ट्रेशन कराना होता है. इसे हर पांच साल पर रिन्यू कराना पड़ता है.
प्रस्तावित एफसीआरए संशोधन बिल में यह प्रावधान किया गया है कि अगर किसी संस्था का लाइसेंस रद्द हो जाता है, सरेंडर कर दिया जाता है या समय पर रिन्यू नहीं होता तो विदेशी फंड से बनाई गई उसकी संपत्तियों और बची हुई राशि के प्रबंधन और नियंत्रण के लिए सरकार एक 'नामित प्राधिकारी' (Designated Authority) नियुक्त करेगी.
सरकार का तर्क है कि इससे विदेशी फंडिंग में पारदर्शिता आएगी और नियमों का कड़ाई से पालन होगा. वहीं आलोचकों और विपक्षी दलों का मानना है कि इससे सरकार को संस्थाओं की संपत्तियों पर नियंत्रण करने की अत्यधिक शक्तियां मिल जाएंगी, जिससे दूर-दराज के इलाकों में अल्पसंख्यक समुदायों के चलाए जा रहे स्कूल और अस्पताल प्रभावित हो सकते हैं.

headline: 'Rapid, rigorous investigations': NTA revamps top ranks, creates new roles to probe exam malpractices
full_text:
'Rapid, rigorous investigations': NTA revamps top ranks, creates new roles to probe exam malpractices
NTA has advertised senior roles in cybersecurity, exam-centre operations and vigilance as part of its institutional overhaul after exam controversies.
The National Testing Agency (NTA) has stepped up recruitment for specialised leadership roles covering cybersecurity; test-centre operations; and vigilance, investigation and forensics, with the latter tasked with probing examination malpractice and coordinating with agencies such as CBI, IB, ED and state police.
In its latest advertisement notifications issued on July 25, NTA has advertised individual notifications for hiring General Manager–Test Centre Network & Operations (GM-TCNO), General Manager–Information Security (Chief Information Security Officer/CISO), and General Manager–Vigilance, Investigation & Forensics (GM-VIF) at its New Delhi headquarters.
The recruitment is part of NTA’s ongoing institutional overhaul following controversies surrounding its examinations, including the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. The agency had earlier said the creation of specialist positions was the first concrete step in rebuilding its institutional capacity and reducing dependence on contractual and outsourced manpower.
Also read: 3 NTA experts named in CBI's NEET paper leak probe chargesheet, may face life term if proven guilty
Vigilance role to probe exam malpractice
The GM-VIF will be expected to lead “rapid, rigorous investigations” into reports of paper leaks, impersonation and fraud and build a “robust digital forensics ecosystem” to trace cyber threats, analyse social-media intelligence and financial trails.
The officer will also serve as NTA’s principal liaison with the CBI, IB, ED, cybercrime units and state police and travel to investigation sites, partner agencies, courts and stakeholder offices across India as case work demands. “If you have a distinguished background in intelligence, investigation, or anti-fraud operations (CBI, IB, ED, Police, or as a CVO), this is a unique opportunity to build NTA’s internal defense mechanisms and dismantle examination malpractice networks,” NTA said in a post on X.
Also read: From NTA's Delhi building to Pune: How NEET questions made it out
NTA seeks zero-disruption exam delivery
For the GM-TCNO, NTA has listed “zero-disruption exam delivery” across hundreds of centres as a key deliverable.
The officer will also expand the test-centre footprint into Tier-3, Tier-4 and aspirational districts, improve candidate facilities and coordinate with state and district administrations and law-enforcement agencies.
The GM-CISO will be tasked with architecting an “impenetrable security posture” across NTA’s technology systems and operationalising a 24x7 Security Operations Centre (SOC). The position will also oversee compliance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, CERT-In directions and MeitY guidelines and strengthen security monitoring of technology vendors.
Recruitment drive expands across specialist roles
The latest advertisements follow a series of recruitment drives this year. On May 17, NTA advertised three specialist leadership positions — Chief Technology Officer (CTO), Chief Finance Officer (CFO) and General Manager-Human Resources (GM-HR)— as part of efforts to modernise the agency.
On July 15, it invited applications for nine senior posts, including three joint directors, two deputy directors, two assistant directors, a research scientist and a senior superintendent (Accounts).
On July 25, NTA had also announced four newly created general manager positions covering assessment research and psychometrics, test-centre network and operations, information security, and vigilance, investigation and forensics, besides 16 young professional positions through the UPSC’s Pratibha Setu portal.

headline: 'Dialogue, not batons': Jharkhand CM warns parties against misleading youth, politicisation
full_text:
'Dialogue, not batons': Jharkhand CM warns parties against misleading youth, politicisation
"Dialogue, not batons, can solve problems; weapons for enemies at the border," CM Hemant Soren said.
Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Sunday warned political parties against allegedly misleading students protesting over recruitment examination irregularities, saying the ongoing stir should not be politicised.
Soren said the government was committed to addressing the protesters' concerns through dialogue and transparency. He stressed that force was not the answer to the students' demands.
"Dialogue, not batons, can solve problems; weapons for enemies at border," the chief minister said, promising justice to exam protesters through a transparent process, reported news agency PTI.
Soren also referred to the treatment meted out to protesting youths during the Jantar Mantar agitation, saying they had faced force while raising their demands.
"All saw how youths were tortured, had to face pellet guns, baton charges, declared traitors," the Jharkhand chief minister said.
The comments came as the Jharkhand government has begun fresh talks with the protesting aspirants, who have been on agitation for the 16th consecutive day. However, a prominent student faction has described the government's latest outreach as “political manoeuvring”.
Soren further said that his government remained committed to ensuring justice for the protesting aspirants and promised strict action against anyone found responsible for irregularities in the recruitment process.
"Committed to justice for protesting youth; those guilty of irregularities to face strictly action," Soren said while speaking at the Adivasi Mahotsav.
Soren warns against politicising students' stir
The Jharkhand CM also accused political parties and vested interests of attempting to exploit the students' movement for political gains.
"Political parties trying to mislead youth by spreading lies, misinformation; intellectuals also involved," Soren said.
He also alleged that certain vested interests were attempting to disrupt the functioning of the state and its democratic processes.
"Unable to accept state's self-reliance, vested interests working at full force to disrupt democracy here," PTI quoted the chief minister as saying.
He also urged the protesters not to seek political backing for their agitation, saying their demands could be addressed through the democratic process.
"Urge youths not to seek political patronage (for their stir); justice is your right, govt committed to delivering it," Soren said.
Soren reiterated that the students' movement should not be turned into a political campaign and warned those with political ambitions against misleading the protesting youths.
