headline: Woman arrested for killing husband in Mathura; daughter, her lover also involved
full_text:
Woman arrested for killing husband in Mathura; daughter, her lover also involved
Mathura , A woman drugged her husband with sedative-mixed milk and killed him with an iron pestle, later dumped his body in a forest because he opposed their daughter's relationship with a delivery boy, police said on Sunday.
According to police, the woman identified as Naina Soni allegedly conspired with her minor daughter and the daughter's lover, Vimal Chaudhary, a delivery boy, to abduct the deceased, Manoj Soni , with the intention of killing him. Following a probe, all three were arrested on Saturday, police said.
They were produced before a court, which sent Naina to judicial custody and the minor to a juvenile home, police said.
During questioning, Naina allegedly told police that on April 18 they gave Manoj a sedative mixed in milk and, after he fell asleep, they killed him by repeatedly striking him with an iron pestle.
Police said the daughter and Vimal then allegedly wrapped the body in a blanket and took it on a scooter to the forest near Akrur village along the Yamuna. They allegedly burnt the body and buried the remains near the river. However, the rising water level in the Yamuna made it difficult for police to recover the remains, officials said.
A blanket was recovered from the spot, while police found ashes of burnt clothes and documents outside the house. Since the body has not yet been recovered, police are currently treating the case as one of abduction with intent to murder.
Police said the case will be altered to include murder charges if sufficient evidence, including the recovery of the body or other material evidence, is found.
Police are digging in several places in a forest area to locate it and collect evidence.
So far, police have recovered the scooter allegedly used to transport the body, a blanket in which it was wrapped and evidence indicating that the victim's clothes and documents were burnt in an attempt to destroy evidence, officials said.
Station House Officer of Govind Nagar, Ajay Verma, said Manoj, a resident of Ganesh Dham Colony in Jaisinghpura under the Govind Nagar police station, went missing after a quarrel at his home on April 18. His elder brother Rambabu lodged a missing-person complaint on July 11 after Manoj, his wife and their minor daughter had suddenly disappeared.
During the investigation, police found Naina and her daughter suspicious.
On August 7, Rambabu lodged a case under Section 140 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Police said the investigation revealed that Manoj's daughter was allegedly in a relationship with Vimal Chaudhary, son of Ramveer Singh. Manoj allegedly opposed the relationship, was angry with his wife and daughter, and would assault them, police said.

headline: Patna HC orders CBI probe into man's disappearance after police detention
full_text:
Patna HC orders CBI probe into man's disappearance after police detention
The Patna High Court has handed the Sanoj Kumar disappearance case to the CBI after questioning the excise police account. The order underscores judicial concern over bias, delay and possible influence in the state probe.
The Patna High Court has ordered a CBI probe into the disappearance of a man who went missing after being detained by Excise Police officials in Bihar's Bhojpur district one year ago. The court said the police investigation was biased and that investigators failed to show urgency after an FIR was registered.
The case relates to Sanoj Kumar, a centring mason, who was allegedly detained on August 13, 2025, on the charge of consuming liquor near a Kali temple. His father, Gauri Shankar Ram, moved the high court seeking a CBI investigation. Police had claimed that Sanoj jumped from a police vehicle and fled during transit.
In its August 7 order, a division bench of Justices Rajeev Ranjan Prasad and Alok Kumar Sinha directed the CBI to take over the investigation.
According to the order, Sanoj called his family on the evening of August 13, 2025, and said police had caught him on allegations of consuming liquor near a Kali temple. He called again and told them police personnel were beating him "mercilessly", after which the call got disconnected.
His father lodged a complaint at Bihiya police station the next day to find out his son's whereabouts. The court noted that Sanoj's motorcycle was later found abandoned near the spot where he was allegedly detained. Excise Department SI Deeraj Kumar, ASI Raju Kumar, home guards Dharmendra Paswan, Umesh Kumar Yadav and Raju Kumar, and drivers Raju Kumar Singh, Vikash Kumar and Surendra Kumar Singh were marked as suspects by the police.
Describing the matter as one of the "rare and exceptional cases", the court said it required transfer to an independent agency such as the CBI, particularly as several Excise Police officials were suspects and progress over the past year had been slow.
"Bias on the part of the state investigating agency may be clearly deduced from their inaction," the bench observed, adding that two accused ASIs were in a "position to influence the investigation". The court said it had "no iota of doubt" that the state agency had failed to act with urgency after the FIR was lodged.
The court said local witnesses were not examined promptly, material witnesses were not produced before a magistrate, and meaningful steps to question suspects and collect scientific evidence were not taken for a considerable period.
It also recorded that Excise officials repeatedly changed their version before finally stating that five people had been detained, two of whom were released after a breath-analyser test. According to that version, the remaining three were taken towards Bihiya Chaurasta in a police vehicle, but one of them jumped out and escaped.
The bench observed that the doors of the vehicle were closed from the outside and said nobody could have jumped out unless the rear door had been opened. The order also noted that the investigation found there had been a scuffle involving Sanoj and the excise vehicle's private driver, who had put a towel around the detainee's neck and pulled him.
The high court has directed the CBI to form a team of reputed officers and said the agency would be free to question police officials linked to the earlier investigation. The CBI has been asked to submit an action-taken report at the next hearing on September 11, as the court seeks an independent probe into Sanoj Kumar's disappearance.

headline: JNU cancels booking for event on jailed activist Umar Khalid's book, organisers say university admin lying
full_text:
JNU cancels booking for event on jailed activist Umar Khalid's book, organisers say university admin lying
Student union said no particular reason was given for cancelling venue. JNU on X later cited “non-disclosure of the full facts about the program” as the reason.
A book discussion on ‘Fractured Communities: Adivasi Histories and the Politics of Power’, authored by jailed activist Umar Khalid, scheduled for Monday, August 10, in an auditorium at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) in New Delhi, has been moved out of its originally designated venue, after a row erupted over the permission granted and withdrawn.
The book happens to be Khalid's PhD thesis when was a scholar at JNU.
“The event was supposed to take place in the auditorium of the School of Social Sciences, but the venue has now been cancelled,” the JNU Students' Union (JNUSU) general secretary said, adding that the alternate venue would be announced separately.
JNU on why permission cancelled
While the union asserted that no particular reason was given for cancelling the original venue, the JNU official handle on X later cited “non-disclosure of the full facts about the program” as the reason.
The university admin shared the permission letter in which the student applicant mentioned the event as “Public Talk for Adivasi Diwas (Book Discussion)”.
The X post by JNU tagged Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan, PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah's official and personal handles; finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, external affairs minister S Jaishankar, and education minister Pralhad Joshi and his ministry.
What organisers said
However, Professor Avinash Kumar, who had submitted the requisition for booking the venue, said, “The stated reason for the cancellation of the booking of the SSS auditorium is false. The Dean, School of Social Sciences, was fully informed that the event was going to discuss Umar Khalid's book ‘Fractured Communities’.”
“The JNUSU before reaching out to me had already met and spoken to the Dean and the requisition form was filled as per his advice. So there is no question of lack of full disclosure. And if the full disclosure was not made, then why was permission for the auditorium booking approved and granted in the first place?” asked Avinash Kumar, who is an assistant professor of Political Studies at the Centre for Informal Sector and Labour Studies (CISLS) under the School of Social Sciences (SSS), JNU.
‘Real reason’
He added, “As regards the real reason for cancellation, the administration should come out clean. Why cannot they permit a discussion on this book in the SSS Auditorium? Isn't this book based on the PhD thesis submitted by Dr Khalid at CHS/SSS/JNU and subsequently was he not granted a PhD degree by JNU for that thesis?”
He noted that the book has been published by “a leading publisher” (Juggernaut) and “there is no reason why a book discussion cannot be held”.
“Instead of making false claims and hollow statements about democracy, the administration should declare under which rule of the University they have unilaterally cancelled without any consultation at any level the venue for the event,” he asked.
What event was about
The event was to feature a discussion on Khalid's book that examines Adivasi histories and the politics of power, and was organised by the JNUSU on the occasion of the International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples (or Vishva Adivasi Diwas). It was scheduled to take place at the School of Social Sciences-I (SSS-I) auditorium at 3 pm on Monday.
According to the event poster, speakers at the discussion include Professors Prabhu Mahapatra and Uma Chakravarti, writer and journalist Shuddhabrata Sengupta, social activist Harsh Mander and scholar Banojyotsna Lahiri, who also happens to be Khalid's partner.
Umar Khalid has been imprisoned since September 2020 under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) regarding the 2020 northeast Delhi riots conspiracy case. He continues to await the start of his trial. The violence erupted during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) and the proposed National Register of Citizens (NRC), leaving 53 people dead and over 700 injured.
What Umar Khalid's book is about
Umar Khalid completed his PhD thesis on the history of the Adivasi tribes of the Singhbhum region of Jharkhand, which has formed the basis of the book. The thesis was submitted at Jawaharlal Nehru University’s Centre for Historical Studies in July 2018, and he was awarded his PhD the following year.
Historian-writer Ramachandra Guha has called it “one of the most accomplished doctoral dissertations by an Indian that I have read”.
The publisher's note on the book's Amazon listing says, “In Fractured Communities, published in book form for the first time, Khalid combines archival rigour with analytical clarity to illuminate the history of Singhbhum’s tribal societies under British rule. The book is both a valuable work of history and a critique of histories written from positions of power, which tend to flatten differences among and, more crucially, within communities.”
It adds, “At a time when public debates are increasingly shaped by simplistic versions of the past, the inquiry at the heart of Fractured Communities acquires a contemporary relevance that few historical works can match. And running through the narrative is a political philosophy grounded in democratic values and genuine concern for the marginalised.”

headline: UP woman accuses trainee IPS officer's father of firing at house to take possession
full_text:
UP woman accuses trainee IPS officer's father of firing at house to take possession
A Sitapur woman has accused the father of a trainee IPS officer of getting her house fired at during a land dispute. Police have recovered empty cartridges and begun investigating rival ownership claims and the alleged intimidation.
A woman in Uttar Pradesh's Sitapur district has accused the father of a trainee IPS officer of allegedly getting her house fired at as part of an attempt to take possession of a disputed plot of land, police said on Sunday.
Police said the woman has filed a written complaint and empty cartridges were recovered from the spot. Officers said several suspects have been detained for questioning and that all allegations, including the firing, are being investigated.
According to Shobhana Shukla, she bought a plot on the Adhauri Bypass in 2018 for around Rs 1.5 crore and has been living with her family in a house built on part of that land. She said the remaining portion of the land is also in her possession.
Shukla alleged that Vipin Bajpai, the father of the trainee IPS officer, is also claiming ownership of the land through a sale deed registered by his father in 2022. She said the dispute over the property has continued since then. She further claimed that a decision by Maholi tehsil authorities about two months ago had gone in her favour, but alleged that people from the other side had continued trying to take possession of the land.
On Sunday, around 24-25 people arrived at her house in a vehicle and, after abusing her, allegedly opened fire, Shukla claimed. In a video circulated among the media, she alleged that Vipin Bajpai had orchestrated the firing incident. She claimed the group had been sent to intimidate her and help in an attempt to take possession of the disputed land.
Maholi Circle Officer Nagendra Choubey said police reached the spot after receiving information about the firing and recovered empty cartridges from the scene. Several suspects were detained for questioning. "The woman has submitted a written complaint. A case will be registered. Police recovered empty cartridges from the spot. All allegations, including firing, are being investigated," Choubey said.
He said the matter relates to a land dispute between two parties and that cases regarding the property have already been filed in court. "A thorough investigation into all aspects is being conducted by the Maholi police station in-charge. Further action will be taken based on the investigation," the officer said.
The case centres on rival claims over the Sitapur land, with the woman alleging an armed attempt to seize it and police saying they have begun action on her complaint while examining all aspects of the dispute.

headline: Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president B. Manickam Tagore on Sunday said there could be no “fair delimitation”, and criticised certain political parties “for changing their tune in their opposition to the delimitation Bill in just a matter of...
full_text:
Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president B. Manickam Tagore on Sunday said there could be no “fair delimitation”, and criticised certain political parties “for changing their tune in their opposition to the delimitation Bill in just a matter of months”.
Speaking at the anti-delimitation march held at Medavakkam in Chennai, Mr. Tagore said, “When Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Kamarajar, and Vallabhbhai Patel called for the Quit India Movement on August 8, 1942, two groups did not take part in it: one, sanghis, and the other, everyone knows who they are.”
He further said those who did not participate in the meeting of MPs from Tamil Nadu were now “talking about fair delimitation”. The DMK, AIADMK, and their allies had stayed away from the delimitation discussion meeting chaired by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Saturday.
“This is a fraud — how can there be a fair and an unfair delimitation when it is a fraud? The [Prime Minister Narendra] Modi government is denying Tamil Nadu its financial share and schemes. We have 39 MPs from Tamil Nadu. In April this year, we defeated the Bill [on delimitation] by voting against it. But those who said ‘no to delimitation’ are now calling for a ‘fair delimitation’. What is fair delimitation? They may increase the seats of Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh by 50%. But, the 40 seats will become 60, and 80 will become 120. The difference in the number of seats between Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh will be 60 after the delimitation. ‘Fair’ delimitation is a scam,” he said.
Congress Rajya Sabha member Praveen Chakravarthy said, “Tamil Nadu’s rights and freedom are in danger. The delimitation Bill will suppress its voice in Parliament. The share of MPs from Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh should remain the same. That’s our demand. But the BJP is trying to increase the representation of north Indian States. They are trying to defraud us by showing some numbers… if they increase our seats by 20, they will increase Uttar Pradesh’s by 40. We have to oppose this. All parties in Tamil Nadu should oppose the Bill… if they don’t, it is a betrayal. As Chief Minister Vijay said, we should oppose the Bill in one voice.”
On the Mekedatu dam issue, Mr. Tagore said, “The Tamil Nadu Congress is very clear that the Mekedatu dam should not be allowed to be constructed. Who can give clearance? Only Prime Minister Modi, Chief Minister Vijay, and [Karnataka] Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar can. Just like how we are fighting for Tamil Nadu’s interests, the Chief Minister of Karnataka will fight for Karnataka’s interests.”
TNCC district president Vijay Sekar said the party’s district office-bearers held marches against delimitation across Chennai.
Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi general secretary D. Ravikumar said any delimitation Bill, including the proposal that there would be a uniform increase of 50% for each State, would render the idea of parliamentary democracy in India “meaningless”.
Speaking to The Hindu, he urged political parties to eschew the traditional view that the delimitation exercise would drive a wedge between the northern and southern States in terms of political representation in Parliament.“After delimitation, there could be close to 850 Members of Parliament. In the current Parliament, in which there are 543 seats, majority of parliamentarians hardly get on people’s issues. If the strength is increased to 850 MPs, there would hardly be any meaningful debates,” he said.
Mr. Ravikumar said, “It is obvious that the BJP finds a great advantage in bringing in this delimitation at this moment. They could simply pass the Bills and amendments without any debate.”

Kharge demands PM Modi's reply in Parliament over alleged Ram Mandir donation embezzlement (ANI image)
NEW DELHI: Congress president and Rajya Sabha leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge on Sunday demanded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi respond in Parliament to allegations of embezzlement of donations and missing valuables linked to the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya.Kharge said the issue concerns the faith of devotees and claimed the Prime Minister should explain the functioning of the temple trust.Speaking to ANI in Rudrapur, Kharge said the opposition had raised the issue on behalf of people who have faith in the temple and Lord Ram."We were the first to raise the issue of theft of the assets inside the temple... Who appointed that trust of caretakers? It was our Prime Minister. Who inaugurated it? He did. Who started the worship? He did. Who hoisted the flag at the Ram Mandir? He did. Who selected the trust members? He did. That is precisely why we want that, since he orchestrated everything, to come to the House and provide a reply," Kharge said.Kharge alleged that jewellery, gold, silver, money and other valuables kept inside the temple were among the assets in question. He also referred to allegations involving gold bricks and a gold Ramcharitmanas book.
He questioned the composition and functioning of the trust responsible for the temple's affairs and sought an explanation from the Prime Minister over the allegations.Kharge said devotees who have faith in the Ram Temple and Lord Ram were distressed by the allegations and that the issue had affected their religious sentiments.He also said people expected opposition parties to raise the matter in Parliament and asserted that the Congress had taken up the issue on their behalf. The allegations are already under investigation.The Uttar Pradesh government told the Supreme Court on July 27 that it had constituted a fresh Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by Inspector General of Police Kiran S, to investigate the alleged embezzlement of donations made at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.According to the information provided by ANI, eight accused have so far been arrested in connection with the case. Investigators are tracing the money trail to identify additional assets and alleged beneficiaries.Earlier, several Samajwadi Party MPs also raised the issue in the Parliament premises and displayed posters carrying the slogan "Chanda chor, gaddi chhod" (Donation thieves, step down).The allegations concern the handling of donations and other valuables associated with the Ram Temple, with the investigation continuing to establish the extent of the alleged financial irregularities and identify those responsible.During his Uttarakhand visit, Kharge also said the Congress would oppose the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill and that opposition parties would discuss their strategy at a meeting of floor leaders on Monday."We will oppose the FCRA-related move. We will take a decision (about strategy) tomorrow after a meeting of floor leaders," he said.The FCRA Amendment Bill is expected to be introduced in the Lok Sabha during the final week of the monsoon session. The proposed legislation seeks to amend the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, with the stated objective of increasing transparency and accountability in the regulation of foreign contributions.Several opposition parties have opposed the proposed amendments.
Congress leader KC Venugopal had earlier said the party would "vehemently oppose" the Bill and that the government "cannot bulldoze this type of bill".Kharge is in Uttarakhand as part of the Congress' preparations for next year's Assembly elections. He said his visit was aimed at energising party workers and expressed confidence that the party would form the government in the state."I am the AICC President. I cannot come here every day, but our army is present here... Does PM Modi come here every day? Does Amit Shah come here? Does Nadda, even though he hails from this very region, come here? Does the new BJP President come here? We visit when and where it is necessary to energise our party workers. That does not mean we simply arrive and leave like tourists," he said.

headline: Advocate claims PGIMER's heritage furniture listed for auction in US, seeks govt intervention
full_text:
Advocate claims PGIMER's heritage furniture listed for auction in US, seeks govt intervention
Chandigarh, A member of the Heritage Protection Cell, Chandigarh, on Sunday claimed that a piece of furniture that belonged to PGIMER was going under the hammer in the US and urged hospital authorities and the Union Health Ministry to intervene.
In a representation to PGIMER Director Vivek Lal, with a copy to Union Health Minister J P Nadda, advocate Ajay Jagga claimed that a "day bed" carries markings of the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research and the Nehru Hospital is listed for auction on August 13 by Chicago Auction House.
The item carries an estimated price of USD 8,000 to USD 10,000, or approximately ₹7.62 lakh to ₹9.52 lakh.
There was no immediate response from PGIMER on the matter.
Jagga has sought immediate intervention to determine how the item reached the United States and whether it was lawfully sold or exported from India.
"The decision to challenge the proposed auction of a PGIMER heritage item, or at least formally raise an objection, is not merely an administrative choice but a responsibility to preserve institutional heritage," Jagga said in his representation.
He described the furniture associated with Chandigarh's post-Independence architectural heritage as part of the country's institutional and cultural legacy and said such objects should be preserved for future generations.
He has urged PGIMER to immediately raise a formal objection to the proposed auction, order an inquiry into the origin and ownership of the article and take steps, if it is established that the item was unlawfully removed from India, to facilitate its recovery.
According to the details shared by Jagga, the item is listed as Lot No. 165 and described as a teak day bed with upholstery, measuring 28 x 72 x 36 inches.
The advocate also referred to an earlier auction in the US in June this year in which, he claimed, another item associated with PGIMER was auctioned.
He sought a detailed inquiry into whether PGIMER had sold any of its heritage furniture and, if not, what steps were being taken to protect and preserve such articles.
Jagga also invoked Articles 49 and 51A of the Constitution, arguing that institutions and authorities have a responsibility to protect objects of historical and artistic importance.
He requested PGIMER and the Union Health Ministry to ascertain the ownership and provenance of the furniture and, if necessary, approach US authorities through the Indian Embassy to determine how the article reached the Chicago Auction House.
The advocate also sought verification of whether Indian and US laws relating to the export and import of heritage objects were followed, including whether the seller was in lawful possession of the furniture.

'Anti-people': Congress vows to oppose FCRA Bill, Venugopal accuses Centre of targeting NGOs

NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday stepped up its opposition to the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, with AICC general secretary KC Venugopal warning that the party and other opposition parties would strongly protest if the legislation is introduced in Parliament.Venugopal, speaking to reporters in Alappuzha, alleged that the proposed legislation was aimed at targeting minorities and NGOs and said the Opposition would not allow it to be passed."If the Central Government thinks they can cook up and introduce the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill within these two or three days, they should keep that wish to themselves," Venugopal said.He described the proposed legislation as "unconstitutional and anti-people", adding, "We will not allow such an anti-people and unconstitutional bill to be passed."
The FCRA Amendment Bill, which seeks to amend the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, is expected to be taken up in the final week of the Monsoon Session.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also said on Saturday that the party would oppose the measure and that its strategy would be discussed at a meeting of Opposition floor leaders on Monday.
Congress raises questions over student protests, Amit Shah
Venugopal also sought answers from Union home minister Amit Shah over the alleged use of force against students protesting in Delhi against irregularities in competitive examinations.
He asked Shah to respond to allegations concerning the use of pellet guns, lathi charges and tear gas during the protests, and questioned his absence from Parliament."When students in India ask the crucial question of who ordered the use of pellet guns, lathi charges and tear gas shells against them to suppress their protest, Amit Shah would not come forward to answer it," Venugopal said.His remarks came amid a broader opposition campaign over the July 20 protests in Delhi, during which student protesters have alleged excessive use of force.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had also raised the issue during an interaction with protesters earlier.
Opposition prepares for key Bills in Parliament
The Congress' opposition to the FCRA Bill comes ahead of the final three days of the Monsoon Session, with the party issuing a whip asking its MPs to remain present in both Houses on August 10, 11 and 12.Congress chief whip in the Rajya Sabha Jairam Ramesh said the party wanted to ensure that "history should not repeat itself", recalling the suspension of 146 Opposition MPs during the 2023 Winter Session.Ramesh said that after the suspensions, several major pieces of legislation, including the three new criminal laws, were passed with minimal Opposition presence.The Congress has also asked its INDIA bloc allies to ensure their MPs remain present during the final days of the session.The FCRA Bill requires a simple majority for passage, while any Constitution amendment bill on delimitation would require a two-thirds majority, according to the background information provided by the party.
Venugopal also questioned the proposed restrictions on organisations receiving foreign contributions and raised the issue of foreign funding received by organisations associated with the RSS."If you have the courage, try controlling the RSS," he said.He also opposed the proposed delimitation legislation, arguing that it could disadvantage states that had successfully implemented population-control measures."This bill effectively chokes states that have successfully implemented population control," Venugopal said, referring to the proposed legislation.On the FCRA Bill, several Opposition parties have expressed concerns. NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule has called for the legislation to either be withdrawn or referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee, while DMK president MK Stalin has also urged the Centre to withdraw it.
The proposed FCRA legislation has also drawn regional concerns. Mizoram chief minister Lalduhoma said after meeting Shah that he had raised six issues concerning the Bill and received an assurance that the legislation would not be retrospective.Venugopal further criticised the Kerala Police over an alleged defamatory statement by RSS ideologue T G Mohandas concerning the protests, saying an FIR should be followed by an investigation and appropriate action.

headline: Mamata Banerjee's convoy attacked, shoes and stones thrown, mud smeared on cars
full_text:
Mamata Banerjee's convoy attacked, shoes and stones thrown, mud smeared on cars
The protest followed the death of Trinamool Congress worker Birju Keot, who died after falling ill in police custody. While police attributed his death to a heart attack, his family alleged custodial torture, triggering political controversy and demands for an independent investigation.
Tensions flared in West Bengal's Halishahar on Saturday after former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's convoy was attacked by protesters while she was on her way to meet the family of party worker Birju Keot, whose death in police custody has become the centre of a political confrontation.
According to reports, demonstrators surrounded Banerjee's vehicle and staged a protest, smearing the car with mud and hurling water bottles, shoes and other footwear at the convoy.
Protesters also raised slogans against the Trinamool Congress (TMC) leader, calling her a "thief" and the "queen of dacoits" as the situation turned chaotic.
The protest was triggered by the death of a TMC worker, whose family has alleged that he died after being assaulted in police custody. The family has accused the local police of beating him to death, allegations that have intensified public anger and sparked demonstrations in the area.
Banerjee had travelled to Halishahar to meet the bereaved family amid the growing controversy surrounding the custodial death allegations.
However, before she could reach the residence, protesters blocked her convoy, leading to a brief stand-off.
POLICE INTERVENED TO CONTROL THE SITUATION
Police personnel rushed to the spot and intervened to bring the situation under control. Security officials escorted Banerjee's convoy out of the area to ensure her safety and prevent any further escalation.
Banerjee alleged that her vehicle was attacked while she was on her way to meet the family of TMC worker Birju Keot in Barrackpore, North 24 Parganas.
"Large stones were hurled at my car by anti-social elements,right in front of the police. The attack on the vehicle was so severe that if the windows had been open, my head would have been split open," she said.
She claimed the attack was severe enough to have caused fatal injuries had the vehicle's windows been open.
Accusing the police of failing to intervene, Banerjee alleged they were "providing protection to the BJP".
TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee alleged that the attack on the convoy was a "pre-planned attempt to murder". He claimed BJP workers hurled large stones at the former Chief Minister's vehicle as she was on her way to meet the family of Keot.
"Stones were thrown to assault Mamata Banerjee... The stones were thrown to kill her. It is an attempt to murder case. Hundreds of BJP workers were there and police were a silent spectator... Of course there was a direction given by the CM Suvendu Adhikari," he alleged.
BJP DENIES INVOLVEMENT
Reacting to the incident, BJP's West Bengal unit president Samik Bhattacharya condemned the attack and denied any involvement of party workers.
He said the BJP did not support stone-pelting, throwing mud or footwear at the former Chief Minister's convoy, adding that such incidents tarnish West Bengal's image. He said those responsible should face action.
West Bengal minister Agnimitra Paul also condemned the attack, saying such acts had no place in the BJP's political culture.
While criticising Mamata Banerjee's tenure, she said neither the party nor the government supported assaulting, manhandling or throwing mud, ink or footwear at political opponents.
"We do not endorse this... If anyone is carrying out such acts while claiming to represent the BJP, they are in the wrong," she confirmed.
Stressing that Banerjee was both a woman and a senior political leader, Paul said anyone indulging in such behaviour in the BJP's name was "in the wrong" and should not be associated with the party.
DEATH OF TMC WORKER
The protest comes in the wake of the death of Birju Keot, a Trinamool Congress worker who died after falling ill while in police custody.
Keot had been arrested on charges of corruption and extortion and was shifted to a hospital after his health reportedly deteriorated, where he was declared dead.
While police have maintained that he suffered a heart attack, his wife has alleged that he was brutally tortured in custody, triggering demands for an independent investigation.
The incident has sparked a political confrontation in West Bengal, with the TMC accusing the police of custodial abuse and seeking accountability, while the BJP has called for a transparent probe into the circumstances surrounding Keot's death.

headline: 2 Kanwariyas die in separate hit-and-run accidents in Haridwar: Police
full_text:
2 Kanwariyas die in separate hit-and-run accidents in Haridwar: Police
Police teams in both cases are examining CCTV footage from the accident areas and investigating to trace the vehicles and their drivers
A 45-year-old man, travelling as part of the annual Kanwar pilgrimage was killed in a road accident on Sunday morning after an unidentified vehicle hit him near Libberhedi in Uttarakhand’s Haridwar, superintendent of rural police, SC Suyal said.
The deceased identified as Manga Kumar was from Uttar Pradesh’s Badaut, police said, adding that the driver fled the spot after hitting the pilgrim. Further investigation is underway, police said.
In a separate incident late on Saturday night, another man travelling for Kanwar pilgrimage was killed after an unidentified vehicle allegedly hit him near the Lord Shiva temple in Hardiwar’s Manglaur, under the jurisdiction of the Gurukul Kangri police post.
Police officers said the deceased’s identity was yet to be established. The deceased was estimated to be between 25 and 30 years old.
Also Read:23-year-old Kanwariya killed, 2 injured as motorcycle collides with bus in Haridwar
Police teams in both cases are examining CCTV footage from the accident areas and investigating to trace the vehicles and their drivers.
Cases have been registered against the unidentified vehicle drivers under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for rash driving and causing death by negligence, officers said.
On Sunday a Kanwariya’s motorcycle caught fire on the highway stretch near Patanjali Yogpeeth. Firefighters reached the spot and managed to douse the flames.
The Kanwariya escaped unhurt after jumping off the motorcycle immediately after flames erupted from the engine. Police and emergency personnel reached the spot and ensured that the situation was brought under control.
The incidents come amid the ongoing Shravan Kanwar pilgrimage, during which a large number of devotees are travelling through Haridwar and other parts of Uttarakhand to collect holy Ganga water.
With the number of Kanwariyas rising sharply, police and administration officials have stepped up traffic management and surveillance measures along major routes.

Timely action by the Fire and Rescue Service helped contain the fire that could have spread to another 30 cars that were parked on the basement of the apartment.
An official at the Club Road Fire and Rescue station said a total of four fire tenders from there and from Gandhinagar station strove for well over an hour to contain the fire. headline: Cheruvayal K. Raman, popularly known as the ‘guardian of native paddy,’ has been selected for the first Oommen Chandy memorial award for outstanding contributions to Kerala’s farm sector.
full_text:
Cheruvayal K. Raman, popularly known as the ‘guardian of native paddy,’ has been selected for the first Oommen Chandy memorial award for outstanding contributions to Kerala’s farm sector.
Agriculture Minister T. Siddique announced his name while announcing the 2025 Kerala State Farm Awards in Thiruvananthapuram on Sunday (August 9, 2026).
The award carries ₹5 lakh in cash prize, citation and plaque. Mr. Raman, who was conferred the Padma Shri in 2023 for his “contribution to sustainable agriculture and preservation of biodiversity,” underscored the need to encourage farming and farmers.

headline: Video: Liquor bottles, chairs fly as two groups clash at UP nightclub, 3 injured
full_text:
Video: Liquor bottles, chairs fly as two groups clash at UP nightclub, 3 injured
A fight between two groups at a Jhansi nightclub left three people injured. CCTV footage of the brawl is being examined as police investigate the assault and alleged rule violations.
A violent clash broke out between two groups inside a nightclub in Uttar Pradesh's Jhansi, leaving 3 people injured after liquor bottles and chairs were allegedly used during the assault. The entire incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed inside the venue, with the footage now going viral on social media.
The incident took place at Ibiza Night Club, located under the Nawabad police station limits in Jhansi. According to police, a written complaint has been received, and an investigation has been initiated based on the CCTV footage.
One of the injured, Shivam Shukla, alleged that he had gone to the nightclub with his friends for dinner when the altercation broke out.
He claimed that a group of men, who were already consuming alcohol at the venue, began abusing another individual. When he and his friends objected, the group allegedly turned on them and attacked them with liquor bottles and physical force.
Shivam alleged that one of the accused struck him on the head with a liquor bottle, causing a serious head injury. Two of his friends also sustained injuries in the incident.
The CCTV footage purportedly shows members of the two groups engaging in a violent brawl, with bottles, chairs and other objects being used during the fight. The incident created panic among other customers present at the nightclub.
POLICE LAUNCHES INVESTIGATION INTO THE MATTER
The complainant further alleged that the nightclub routinely remains open beyond the permitted hours and that similar incidents have occurred at the establishment in the past. He urged authorities to take strict action against those involved in the assault.
Responding to the incident, Nawabad police said they had taken cognisance of the complaint and were examining the CCTV footage to identify those involved in the violence.
Station House Officer Ravi Srivastava said a case would be registered after verifying the facts and appropriate legal action would be taken against the accused.
Police are also looking into the circumstances that led to the clash and whether there were any violations of operational rules by the nightclub. Further investigation is underway.

headline: 86-year-old on evening walk killed as car hits 4 in Kolkata township
full_text:
86-year-old on evening walk killed as car hits 4 in Kolkata township
An eyewitness said that the car shot out of the parking area and hit the pedestrians at considerable speed.
An 86-year-old man died in the early hours of Wednesday after being hit by a car while he was out for his evening walk inside the Uniworld City residential complex in New Town, Kolkata. Three others were also injured in the accident.
The deceased was identified as Sribas Chandra Ojha, India Today reported. He was taking his daily walk with the assistance of an attendant when the accident occurred around 6.45 pm near a parking area inside the complex.
The car was allegedly being driven by a woman who runs a shop at the adjoining Downtown Mall, the Telegraph reported.
An eyewitness said that the car shot out of the parking area and hit the pedestrians at considerable speed, the report added.
The FIR lodged at Techno City police station stated that the car “was allegedly being driven in a rash and negligent manner and struck the deceased and the others” head-on. Police have registered a case of causing death by negligent driving and an investigation is underway.
Police have not confirmed whether the driver possessed a valid driving licence, India Today reported.
Also Read: Six killed as container truck rams into car in Madhya Pradesh's Dhar
What happened after the accident?
Nilendu Chakraborty, additional chief health director of BR Singh Railway Hospital and Ojha’s son-in-law, described the moments after the accident.
“I had just returned home from the hospital when I was called downstairs. His denture had lodged in his airway. I removed it and inserted a bottle into his mouth to create an airway before we rushed him to Ohio Hospital. A CT scan revealed bleeding in the brain. We shifted him to Apollo Hospital around 11.30pm. He succumbed to his injuries there,” Chakraborty said, according to The Telegraph.
Ojha’s grandson Nilabhro Chakraborty said, “The impact threw my grandfather off his feet. Three others were also injured. We cannot describe what we are going through. I never imagined that he would go out for his evening walk and never return,” India Today reported.
An autopsy was conducted at NRS Medical College and Hospital, following which Ojha was cremated later that day.
Also Read: Training plane skids while landing at Baramati, where Ajit Pawar died in crash
Three others injured
Ojha’s attendant suffered a fractured shoulder and remains hospitalised, India Today reported. Another youth sustained a skull fracture and is undergoing treatment in the ICU of a private hospital in Kolkata.
The young man remains under treatment for a fractured skull, while the third injured person, a resident of a neighbouring housing complex, was given first aid and discharged.

headline: 40 people injured as bus collides with truck, falls off bridge in Andhra Pradesh
full_text:
40 people injured as bus collides with truck, falls off bridge in Andhra Pradesh
At least 40 passengers were injured, including 10 critically, after a Volvo bus collided with a truck and plunged off a bridge in Andhra Pradesh’s Anantapur.
At least 40 passengers were injured, some critically, after a private bus collided with a truck and plunged off a bridge on the Hyderabad-Bengaluru national highway (NH-44) in Andhra Pradesh’s Anantapur district early Sunday, police said.
The accident occurred near Pogururu village in Pamidi mandal around 4 am when the Hyderabad–Bengaluru Volvo bus was crossing the Pogururu bridge.
“The bus rammed into an Eicher truck, and as a result, both vehicles fell off the bridge, leaving them severely damaged,” an officer from the Pamidi police station said, adding that many passengers were trapped inside the mangled bus.
“Around 10 passengers are in critical condition,” the police officer said.
Police said that the bus driver was among those seriously injured. “With the help of the excavator, we managed to extricate the bus driver after a prolonged operation,” the officer said.
The injured were initially shifted to the Pamidi government hospital. Those with serious injuries were later referred to the Government Hospital in Anantapur for advanced treatment.
The police cleared the wreckage and regulated traffic flow.
A case was registered under Section 125(A) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for causing injuries through rash and negligent driving. “Authorities have launched an investigation to ascertain the exact cause of the accident,” the officer said.

headline: Kerala school teacher suspended for Savarkar question amid 'freedom quiz' row
full_text:
Kerala school teacher suspended for Savarkar question amid 'freedom quiz' row
The education minister's office said the question was framed in a manner that could lead to spread of misleading and historically unsupported information.
After a political row erupted over a school quiz in Kerala, a teacher from Kumbla sub-district was held responsible for preparing the question paper and suspended amid an ongoing enquiry. The controversy broke out after a quiz question described Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar as a freedom fighter "who received the most severe punishment from the British".
The role of Guru Prasad, a teacher at AUPS Pallathadka, has come under the scanner for formulating the questions of the 'Freedom Quiz' competition held at schools in Kasaragod, Kumbla and Manjeshwaram sub-districts on August 6.
Announcing the step taken against the teacher, general education minister N Samsudheen's office said, "Following the directions of the General Education Minister, the Director of General Education suspended Guru Prasad, a teacher at AUPS Pallathadka in Kumbla sub-district, pending an inquiry."
The office further said the question was allegedly framed in a manner that could lead to dissemination of "misleading and historically unsupported information".
Earlier, the minister directed the Director of General Education to take stringent action against those responsible. The minister’s office said the controversial quiz was not included in the official activity calendars of either the Social Science Club or the General Education Department. Neither body had authorised anyone to independently prepare the questions or conduct the competition. "The person who included the historically incorrect question holds a prejudiced view," the statement said.

The disputed question asked which freedom fighter received the “most severe punishment” from the British, with Vinayak Damodar Savarkar listed as the answer.
The question drew strong criticism from the CPI(M) and Left student and youth organisations, which accused the Congress-led UDF government of promoting a "sangh parivar agenda" in education.
Senior CPM leader and former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan accused the UDF government of "colluding" with the RSS to hide Savarkar's "real history" and glorify him. Vijayan accused the Centre and the RSS of "attempting to rewrite history", while raising concerns over the Centre's efforts to implement its new education policy in Kerala.
Former General education minister V Sivankutty alleged attempts at "saffronising" the state's general education sector and distorting the history of India's freedom struggle.

headline: ‘Distorting it’: Shashi Tharoor says remarks on Rahul Gandhi's ‘Chhatron ki goonj’ campaign not an attack on Congress
full_text:
‘Distorting it’: Shashi Tharoor says remarks on Rahul Gandhi's ‘Chhatron ki goonj’ campaign not an attack on Congress
Shashi Tharoor said he was stressing that political parties must open their doors and create paths for the next generation to gain the power to shape politics.
Following his remarks that Congress's student outreach did not resonate with the students as much as the Cockroach party's paper leak protests did, Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Saturday sought to explain his stand, decrying that the media was interpreting it as "an attack on my own party or its leadership".
Tharoor insisted that he was stressing that political parties must open their doors and create pathways for the next generation to gain the power to shape politics.
Also read: ‘No one has seen us in same room’: Rahul Gandhi's cheeky AMA response to ‘are you Batman’ question
This comes after Tharoor said during an event in Maharashtra that all opposition parties have to be conscious of the fact that they didn't "provide a route into our parties for the kinds of people who are at Jantar Mantar last month".
The established parties will cease to be relevant unless they can listen to the new voices that they haven't heard so far, he remarked.
Tharoor noted that Rahul Gandhi's 'Chhatron ki goonj' programme had raised the issue of paper leaks and other issues central to students even before the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) announced the mass protest.
Agreeing on the fact that Congress' student outreach programme did not ‘resonate’ as much as the CJP's protest, Tharoor said, “We need to ask ourselves what did we fail to do? Did we fail to listen? Was our finger missing from the pulse of the Gen Z?”
But Tharoor later claimed that his remarks had been distorted in the media.
"It takes a particular combination of incompetence and malice for some media to interpret my conversation with Rishabh Shah at @iimunofficial as an attack on my own party or its leadership.
"Here is the entire video, uncut and unexpurgated, in full, of the conversation. Watch it and judge for yourself, as clearly none of the Journalists distorting it have done," Tharoor said in a post on X.
Tharoor, the Lok Sabha member from Thiruvananthapuram, also shared his entire conversation at the India's International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN) in Mumbai on August 7.
Tharoor's office also shared a video of a part of his conversation and said, "Context is often more instructive than commentary. Beyond the noise lies Dr Shashi Tharoor's point: India's young people must not remain spectators to politics. Parties must open their doors, create pathways to leadership and give the next generation the power to shape our politics".
Rahul Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, launched the Chhatron Ki Goonj campaign from Rajasthan's Kota on June 17. The initiative later moved to Dehradun, where Gandhi interacted with students and families affected by alleged examination irregularities.
Gandhi has held the Chhatro ki Goonj campaign in several cities across the country since then, in parallel to the CJP's protest against paper leaks which it announced on June 20.
While the protesters camped at the Jantar Mantar protest site till Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as the Union education minister, the Congress also held a protest outside the PM's residence.

headline: AI is not intended to replace doctors but to multiply specialist capacity by assisting in diagnosis
full_text:
AI is not intended to replace doctors but to multiply specialist capacity by assisting in diagnosis
NEW DELHI: India's healthcare system is coming under growing pressure from an ageing population, rising burden of chronic diseases and shortages of doctors, nurses and hospital beds, according to a knowledge paper released by Union Health Minister J P Nadda on Saturday. The report says artificial intelligence (AI) can help bridge this widening gap by extending specialist expertise, improving diagnosis and expanding access to quality healthcare, particularly in smaller hospitals and underserved areas.Nadda released the knowledge paper, "AI in MedTech: Revolutionizing Healthcare Through Artificial Intelligence," at the 9th edition of India Medical Device 2026, organised by the Department of Pharmaceuticals in association with FICCI.The report estimates India's population at 1.47 billion in 2026 and says more than 65% of deaths are now due to non-communicable diseases such as heart disease, diabetes and cancer. It projects the population aged 60 years and above to cross 230 million by 2036, further increasing demand for long-term healthcare.Despite expansion in healthcare infrastructure and medical education, shortages persist. India has 9.6 doctors per 10,000 population, compared with the global average of 18.3.
It has 27.2 nursing personnel per 10,000 against 40.5 globally, 15.9 hospital beds per 10,000 compared with 33, and only 4 MRI scanners per million people, against the global average of 19, the report says.According to the report, AI is not intended to replace doctors but to multiply specialist capacity by assisting in diagnosis, clinical decision-making and screening. AI-enabled diagnostics are expected to be the first large-scale application, helping extend specialist expertise to primary and secondary healthcare, improve productivity and reduce inequalities in access to care.
The report says India has already built the foundations for AI in healthcare through initiatives such as the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, IndiaAI Mission, SAHI, BODH and the National Medical Devices Policy, 2023. It says the next challenge is to move AI from successful pilot projects to routine clinical use by creating AI-ready health data, a predictable regulatory framework and reimbursement mechanisms for AI-enabled technologies.

headline: Laser light disorients Malaysia Airlines pilot approaching Kolkata airport; flight circles before landing
full_text:
Laser light disorients Malaysia Airlines pilot approaching Kolkata airport; flight circles before landing
When the aircraft was around eight nautical miles from the runway, the pilot reportedly noticed a bright laser beam flashing towards the cockpit.
A Malaysia Airlines flight carrying 159 passengers faced a problem while approaching Kolkata airport for landing after the pilot was distracted by a laser beam.
Flight MH-184, operating from Kuala Lumpur to Kolkata, was scheduled to land at 11.20 pm on Saturday.
When the aircraft was around eight nautical miles from the runway, the pilot reportedly noticed a bright laser beam flashing towards the cockpit from the Madhyamgram-Barasat side, PTI reported, citing sources.
The aircraft eventually landed safely at around 11.25 pm. All passengers and crew members were reported safe.
The aircraft could not land at the scheduled time and had to circle in the sky after the laser flash reportedly affected the pilot's vision, momentarily disorienting him.
Also Read: Training plane skids while landing at Baramati, where Ajit Pawar died in crash
Complaint lodged
Following the incident, the Kolkata airport authorities lodged a complaint with the NSCBI Airport Police Station.
Kolkata airport director Vikram Singh said the use of laser lights around the airport is prohibited, but such incidents occur occasionally and can potentially affect aircraft operations, PTI report added.
He said the matter has been brought to the notice of police authorities, who are investigating the case.
Earlier laser beam incidents
Pilots have previously raised concerns over laser beams affecting their vision during take-off and landing.
During the 2025 Durga Puja festivities, laser lights used near the Sreebhumi Sporting Club pandal reportedly raised concerns among pilots, following which the laser show was stopped.
Intense laser beams can temporarily impair a pilot’s vision, causing distraction and even effects similar to temporary blindness, posing a safety risk during the critical stages of take-off and landing.
Training aircraft skids in Baramati
A training aircraft operated by a private company crash-landed near the Baramati airstrip in Maharashtra's Pune district on Sunday, police said. No casualties were reported, they said.
The mishap occurred around 12:30 pm, it is learnt. This comes seven months after the then Maharashtra deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar of the NCP was killed in a crash during a landing attempt at the Baramati airstrip.
“We are investigating whether the aircraft developed a technical snag or if there were any other problems. It is too early to comment on anything,” a senior police official said on the training aircraft mishap, as per news agency PTI.
At the same airstrip, in January, Ajit Pawar and four others were killed as their Learjet 45 aircraft crashed in what was the second attempt at landing.

headline: OBC representation below quota in postal dept, parliamentary panel flags shortfall
full_text:
OBC representation below quota in postal dept, parliamentary panel flags shortfall
A parliamentary panel flagged OBC under-representation in several postal cadres and sought steps to meet the 27% quota, fill 207 backlog vacancies and raise GDS pay.
The Parliamentary Committee on Welfare of Other Backward Classes (OBCs) has flagged under-representation of OBCs across several cadres in the Department of Posts and recommended filling backlog vacancies, enhancing the remuneration of Gramin Dak Sevaks (GDS) and strengthening welfare measures for OBC employees in a report tabled in the Lok Sabha on Friday.
Committee chairman and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) lawmaker Ganesh Singh said the objective of the reservation system “is not merely to fulfil the prescribed percentage, but to ensure that eligible youth and employees belonging to the Other Backward Classes receive equal opportunities, due representation in employment and effective benefits of their rights.”
The report examined OBC representation in the Department of Posts, implementation of the reservation policy, the backlog of reserved vacancies, remuneration of GDS, welfare of OBC employees, and expansion of postal services in rural areas, according to the panel, which functions under the Ministry of Communications. The committee noted that despite the reservation policy being “implemented for more than three decades,” representation in several cadres has “not yet reached the prescribed level.”
As per data placed before the committee, OBC representation stood at approximately 7.2% at the Junior Time Scale level in Group A, 19.5% among Inspectors of Posts and 21% among Stenographers in Group B, and 25.2% among Postal Assistants/Sorting Assistants and 26.1% among Postmen/Mail Guards in Group C, all short of the prescribed 27% quota. The panel recommended that “concrete and effective measures” be taken to close this gap across all groups, and that it be kept updated on the progress.
On remuneration, the committee noted that more than 2.5 lakh GDS are currently employed in the Department of Posts, with minimum basic pay ranging between ₹10,000 and ₹12,000 a month for roughly four to five hours of daily work. Besides delivering postal articles, GDS also extend “India Post Payments Bank deposit and withdrawal facilities, banking services and other financial services” to rural areas, the report said, recommending an “appropriate enhancement” in their pay.
The panel was informed that 207 backlog vacancies reserved for OBCs remain unfilled in Group C, including one in Chhattisgarh, two in the North East, and 204 in West Bengal. It has asked the department to fill these “at the earliest” and to undertake “Special Recruitment Drives” where necessary to reach the 27% benchmark.
The committee also took note of the absence of “regular/periodic meetings” with OBC employees’ welfare associations, and asserted that OBC is “a social category recognised under the Constitution” and should not merely be viewed as “a group of castes.” It recommended that “necessary basic facilities” be extended to such associations functioning across the department’s circles.
On rural outreach, the report said 1.39 lakh of the country’s 1,64,987 post offices are in rural areas, of which around 28,000 currently operate from Gram Panchayat Bhawans. The department told the committee that roughly 10,000 additional rural post offices “could be accommodated” in such buildings, and the panel asked the government to coordinate with states and panchayati raj institutions to expand this arrangement, including new construction where required.
The committee has also directed the Department of Posts to ensure “strict compliance with the reservation provisions” for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and OBCs in all temporary and contractual appointments lasting 45 days or more, citing a Department of Personnel and Training office memorandum dated May 15, 2018.
Singh said the recommendations are aimed at “strengthening the effectiveness of the reservation system, filling backlog vacancies, strengthening the welfare of OBC employees and further expanding access to postal and financial services across rural India,” and are in keeping with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of “inclusive development, equal opportunities and the empowerment of every section of society, particularly the Other Backward Classes.”

headline: BSF firing kills Bangladesh national in Tripura during alleged smuggling attempt
full_text:
BSF firing kills Bangladesh national in Tripura during alleged smuggling attempt
The Bangladeshi national, suspected of involvement in smuggling Burmese cigarettes, was allegedly carrying out smuggling activities at midnight on Saturday
A 20-year-old Bangladeshi national was found dead on Sunday after Border Security Force (BSF) personnel fired at him on Saturday at Magruli in Tripura’s Unakoti district, said police.
The deceased, identified as Tara Miah was a resident of Muraicharra in Bangladesh’s Moulvibazar district. Police said his body was taken to Kailasahar district hospital for a postmortem.
According to police, the Bangladeshi national, suspected of involvement in smuggling Burmese cigarettes, was allegedly carrying out smuggling activities at midnight on Saturday in the IBB area at Maguruli.
When on-duty officers spotted a group of smugglers and attempted to stop them, the smugglers allegedly tried to attack the BSF personnel. The personnel then fired two rounds from their rifles, injuring the Bangladeshi national and causing his death.
Earlier this June, a Bangladeshi man was shot dead by the BSF at the Latiapura border outpost in Unakoti district during an alleged smuggling attempt.
Last November, a person was arrested in connection with an incident where two BSF personnel sustained minor injuries after being allegedly attacked by smugglers at a bordering area of Bishalgarh in Sepahijala district.
In another incident in January last year, an on-duty BSF team was attacked by a group of Bangladeshi smugglers near the India-Bangladesh international border under Magroli in Tripura’s Unakoti district, however no one was injured on either side in the incident.
Later in March last year, a Bangladeshi smuggler was killed and two BSF personnel sustained injuries during a clash at Magroli in the district.
Tripura has an 856 km international border with Bangladesh, most of which is covered by a barbed wire fence, but a few patches remain unfenced.

headline: Man performs ‘tantric ritual’ with Chhattisgarh chief justice's photo in effort to get bail for kin; held at crematorium
full_text:
Man performs ‘tantric ritual’ with Chhattisgarh chief justice's photo in effort to get bail for kin; held at crematorium
Police recover a fish, some lemons, vermilion and photographs of Chhattisgarh HC CJ Ramesh Sinha from the spot
A man was caught in Chhattisgarh's Bilaspur while allegedly performing a “tantric ritual” with a photograph of the chief justice of Chhattisgarh High Court in his efforts to secure bail for a relative, an official said on Sunday.
According to the official, the incident took place at a cremation ground in Devri village under Sipat police station limits on the intervening night of Friday and Saturday, news agency PTI reported.
The accused has been identified as Rishikesh Kumar, and was performing the ritual with three other people. Kumar was apprehended after the villagers in Devri saw four men engaging in suspicious activities late at night, and confronted them on the alleged ritual. Thereafter, three of them ran away, but Kumar was caught and handed over to the police, superintendent of police (SP) Rajnesh Singh said, according to PTI.
Also Read | Chhattisgarh Christian Forum office-bearer held over ‘objectionable’ Lord Shiva post
The accused, when questioned, allegedly told the cops that his relative, Priyanshu Bole, was under police custody along with a few others in a case of stabbing. SP Singh warned that strict action would be taken against anyone performing such rituals, saying those who had committed crimes must work on reforming themselves. “Bail can not be obtained by performing any ritual. Criminals should reform themselves,” SP Rajnesh Singh further said.
Fish, lemon recovered from site; accused watched ‘tantrik’ video before ritual
After Kumar was detained for questioning, cops recovered some ritual materials from the cremation ground. These included a fish, lemons, vermilion and photographs of Chhattisgarh HC chief justice Ramesh Sinha and two other persons, the SP said. One of the photographs recovered from the spot was of Priyanshu Bole, while another was that of the victim in the stabbing case.
Also Read | Class 12 student stabbed outside Delhi school in case of ‘mistaken identity’
Kumar and his friends had further watched a video of a “tantric”, who claimed that a ritual could be conducted to help secure bail, before they visited the cremation ground, he told the police. He said that in the case his relative was arrested for, one accused had got bail, while the applications of the others were pending before the court. The SP said further investigation in the matter was underway.

headline: BJP-JD(S) urge Governor to reject Horatti's resignation, seek probe into pressure
full_text:
BJP-JD(S) urge Governor to reject Horatti's resignation, seek probe into pressure
A BJP-JD(S) delegation met Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot seeking rejection of Basavaraj Horatti's resignation. The opposition alleged coercion by ruling party leaders and sought a constitutional inquiry.
A BJP-JD(S) delegation on Sunday met Karnataka Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot and sought constitutional action over the resignation of Legislative Council Chairman Basavaraj Horatti. The opposition leaders alleged that Horatti was forced to resign under pressure from ruling party leaders and asked the Governor to reject what they called an unconstitutional resignation.
The delegation, led by Leader of Opposition in the Legislative Council Chalavadi Narayanaswamy, also demanded a constitutional and legal inquiry against DK Shivakumar, KPCC president BK Hariprasad, MLCs Saleem Ahmed and S Ravi, and others. They alleged that the resignation was obtained through "goondaism" and unlawful pressure, and said the autonomy of the legislature had been undermined.
In a petition submitted to the Governor, the leaders said, "We wish to bring to your attention a very serious and alarming development in the State of Karnataka, where the democratic system and constitutional values have completely deteriorated, and the leaders of the ruling party are behaving like goondas." They alleged that though Horatti had said he would resign on August 14, Shivakumar, Hariprasad, Ahmed, Ravi and others went to his office and "exerted intense political pressure on him for more than one-and-a-half hours".
"They threatened him like goondas, and forcibly and unconstitutionally obtained his resignation. This incident is a grave affront to the dignity of the legislature and the sanctity of the Constitution," the petition alleged.
Horatti resigned on Friday and said he had been asked to step down by the Congress dispensation. According to him, Congress leaders had told him they would move a no-confidence motion against him if he did not resign.
The BJP and JD(S) leaders further alleged that the ruling party ignored procedure during the episode. "Disregarding the rules, they called the Chairman's Personal Secretary and ordered him to bring the chairman's official letterhead," they said. "The ruling party leaders themselves got the resignation letter typed on that letterhead and forcibly and unconstitutionally obtained the chairman's signature on it," they claimed.
Calling it one of the darkest days in the history of the Constitution, they said, "This is a direct attack on the basic principles and spirit of the Constitution."
They asked the Governor to intervene as the constitutional head of the state, reject the resignation, order an inquiry and take strict action under the Constitution against those allegedly involved. "We hereby request the governor to intervene immediately and take appropriate and stringent decisions to uphold the rule of law and protect the Constitution in the State," they said.
Horatti's resignation came days after the Congress high command wrote to DK Shivakumar on Monday approving Saleem Ahmed as its nominee for chairman of the Legislative Council and Umashree for deputy chairperson. The letter also contained the list of ministers sworn in on August 3.
The BJP also released a letter that Horatti wrote to the Governor on August 7 about the developments in his office before his resignation. In it, Horatti said that after he reached his official chamber for the oath-taking ceremony of a newly elected MLC, the CM, the KPCC president and certain members of the Karnataka Legislative Council came there and asked him to resign the same day.
"As per your Excellency's order convening the ensuing Monsoon Session, I had expressed my intention to tender my resignation only after conveying my thanks and gratitude to the Hon'ble Members of the Legislative Council in the House on 14th August, 2026," Horatti wrote. "I had already informed my intention of resignation to the Chief Minister of Karnataka, and the same matter had also been reported in several media across the State," he said.
He added, "The Hon'ble CM instructed me to tender my resignation on this day itself. Such a sudden development in my official chamber surprised me. Therefore, on his request at that moment to calm down the situation, I considered it my duty to take such a step." The opposition has now asked the Governor to reject that resignation and initiate action against those it accused of forcing it.

headline: Ladakh, one of the country’s two youngest Union Territories, is set to lead the way in demonstrating how caste will be enumerated for the first time in Independent India. The second phase of the Census—the Population Enumeration (PE)—which starts on ...
full_text:
Ladakh, one of the country’s two youngest Union Territories, is set to lead the way in demonstrating how caste will be enumerated for the first time in Independent India. The second phase of the Census—the Population Enumeration (PE)—which starts on August 17 in Ladakh and other snow-bound areas, is likely to ask questions on 40 parameters and provide an open-ended column for caste enumeration.
Open-column methodology
As reported by The Hindu on July 6, the rehearsal, or the “pre-test” for the PE phase, was conducted from July 1 to 20 in 16 States and Union Territories, where respondents, other than Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes, recorded their castes in an “open column”, or the enumerator noted a resident’s caste as declared by them. The methodology is likely to be retained in the final form.
While the ongoing Census is India’s first digital Census, officials are making an exception for Ladakh by printing a sufficient number of paper schedules. The move takes into account the presence of large defence establishments in the region bordering China and Pakistan, whose locations cannot be geo-tagged because of security concerns. The digital Census mandatorily requires enumerators to geo-locate the structures on a mobile App. Respondents who self-enumerate on Census portal are also required to do the same.
Though the questionnaire or the schedule is yet to be notified by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI), preparations have begun in Ladakh and snow-bound areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand to conduct Population Enumeration—the second phase of Census—from August 17-September 30, ahead of the rest of the country, where the exercise will be conducted in February 2027.
The Directorate of Census Operations, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, has concluded a three-day Master Trainers’ Training Programme for Census 2027 population enumeration, marking the next phase of field preparedness ahead of operations scheduled to begin on August 17 with the self-enumeration phase.
According to Chief Principal Census Officer Amit Sharma, the three-day programme provided comprehensive training on all aspects of Census 2027 population enumeration, covering census concepts, caste and demographic data collection, digital tools, self-enumeration, interviewing techniques and hands-on use of the mobile application.
Ladakh’s case is peculiar as it was not among the 16 States and UTs where a “pre-test” or rehearsal of the questions to be asked during the second phase, was held in July.
A senior government official said that, in the absence of the pre-test, the master-trainers are being trained based on tentative questions, around 40, which are likely to be notified this week.
“The broad contours have been conveyed to us. This time the questions are descriptive and will also include caste. The caste column will be open-ended, and enumerators will record the name of the caste as provided by the respondent,” said the official.
The official added that since the Census envisages counting all structures and buildings, enumerators are being told to exercise caution and record defence structures along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) as “special charges” on paper schedules.
The open-column methodology had resulted in the 2011 Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) returning over 46 lakh different “caste names”, largely owing to the differences in what people understand by caste. Significantly, the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led government has consistently maintained over the last decade that the 2011 SECC’s caste data was unreliable because of “errors” in data collection.
The total number of castes recorded during the 1931 Census was 4,147. The SECC was conducted as a survey and was outside the purview of the Census Act, 1948, and had no statutory backing. The data was never released by the government.
On August 3, the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India notified in the gazette of India that “the conduct of Census of the population shall be undertaken in the Union territory of Ladakh and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the States of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, from 1st September, 2026 to 30th September, 2026 with a revisional round from 1 October, 2026 to 5th October, 2026”.
An option for self-enumeration will be available from August 17 to 31, before the start of house-to-house population enumeration, the notification said.

headline: Four detained in UP's Bareilly as police raid shops selling non-veg food on Kanwar Yatra route

Four detained in UP's Bareilly as police raid shops selling non-veg food on Kanwar Yatra route
This came after authorities had directed traders not to sell meat, chicken, fish and other non-vegetarian food along the routes to be travelled by Kanwariyas.
Four people were detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bareilly after police raided two shops allegedly selling non-vegetarian food along a designated Kanwar Yatra route, officials said on Sunday.
This came after authorities had directed traders not to sell meat, chicken, fish and other non-vegetarian food along the routes designated to be travelled by Kanwariyas during the pilgrimage. The officials had warned of legal action if the orders were violated.
The police action came amid heightened police and administrative surveillance on Kanwar routes during the ongoing Sawan month, PTI news agency reported. Monitoring along the Bareilly-Bahedi route and other major Kanwar routes has been increased to check the sale of meat, chicken and fish in restricted or designated areas.
Also Read | Yogi showers flowers on Kanwariyas, hails Kanwar Yatra as symbol of unity
Shop found running despite earlier warning, its roof razed
The police received information on Saturday evening that chicken biryani was being sold at a shop near the old Roadways bus stand in Bahedi in Bareilly district, according to the PTI report.
When the cops raided the shop, it was found operating despite an earlier warning. The police then detained the shopkeepers, identified as Salman and Raees. The former is a resident of Lodhipur.
Following this, a JCB machine was brought to the spot and the shop's tin shed and counter were removed, Bahedi circle officer Arun Kumar Singh said, PTI reported. In a second incident, the cops raided another shop near the bakery area and detained two other persons.
Police said that these traders had already been given a warning earlier to stop the sale of non-vegetarian food during the Kanwar pilgrimage, but had allegedly continued to operate. Circle officer Singh reiterated that directions regarding the sale of non-vegetarian food along major routes during Sawan month had been issued earlier on, adding that further violations of the instructions could invite legal action.
Unauthorised meat shops along Kanwar Yatra route ordered shut in Delhi too
Meanwhile, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) had also, in June, ordered a crackdown on all illegal and unlicensed meat shops operating along the Kanwar routes and near the 308 Kanwar camps, senior municipal officials said.
The office memorandum, dated June 27 and issued by MCD additional commissioner Arun Mishra, stated, “During the said meeting, it was deliberated that Karwar Camps shall primarily be established at 308 original sites besides some new sites, as the case may be, and will become fully operational from July 30, the first day of Shravana month till Shivratri on August 11.”
