full_text:
Prime suspect in Bulandshahr girl’s rape-murder killed in encounter: UP Police
The prime suspect in the rape and murder of a 12-year-old girl in Bulandshahr, was killed in a police encounter in Gulawathi early Sunday.
The prime suspect in the rape and murder of a 12-year-old girl in Bulandshahr was killed in a police encounter in the Gulawathi area of Uttar Pradesh early Sunday.
Police on Saturday had announced a bounty of ₹50,000 on the prime suspect, identified as Monu, who allegedly abducted the Class 4 student from outside her home in Bulandshahr district on August 1, sexually assaulted her and killed her before dumping her body in bushes near Vair railway station, police said.
The minor went missing from her home in the Kakod area on July 31 around 3pm and her family had been searching for her since then. On Saturday evening, locals spotted an unclothed body near Vair railway station in the bushes and informed the police.
According to police officers, the girl had injuries on her face, shoulders, hands, abdomen, chest and legs.
Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Dinesh Kumar Singh said a joint team of the SWAT and local police was conducting checking in the Gulawathi area around 4 am on Sunday when they spotted two men travelling on a motorcycle without a number plate.
“The suspects opened fire at the police team when they were asked to stop. In the retaliatory firing, Monu sustained bullet injuries. He was taken to hospital, where doctors declared him dead,” the SSP said.
A second suspect accompanying Monu allegedly escaped, taking advantage of the darkness. Police teams are conducting a combing operation to trace him, Singh said.
Special Operations Group (SOG) sub-inspector Sandeep Kumar and constable Narendra Kumar sustained bullet injuries during the exchange of fire, an officer said, adding that inspectors Shailendra Kumar from Sikandrabad and Dharmendra Sharma from Gulawathi were hit by bullets on their bulletproof jackets and escaped unhurt.
Police recovered a pistol, two magazines, cartridges and the motorcycle without a number plate from the encounter site.
Police said CCTV footage from the area showed the accused taking the girl away. The footage helped investigators identify Monu and led to the formation of teams to track him down.
After the recovery of the girl’s body, SSP Dinesh Kumar Singh and local MLA Lakshmi Raj Singh visited the victim’s family and assured them that the accused would be arrested at the earliest.

headline: US Russia sanctions bill could tighten oil markets, put India’s energy security at risk, says Kpler: Report
full_text:
US Russia sanctions bill could tighten oil markets, put India’s energy security at risk, says Kpler: Report
US Senate sanctions bill targeting Russian energy buyers could disrupt crude supplies, tighten global oil markets and raise pressure on India’s energy security.
A US Senate vote to advance tougher sanctions on Russia raises the risk of disruption to Russian crude supplies but is unlikely to immediately alter oil flows to India and China, according to Kpler analyst Sumit Ritolia.
The US Senate on Friday passed a bipartisan Russia sanctions bill that would give President Donald Trump authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on imports from countries that are among the world's largest buyers of Russian oil and gas. The Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026 targets the five biggest purchasers of Russian energy and is aimed at cutting Moscow's revenues from oil and gas sales.
Also read: US Senate passes Russia sanctions bill; India risks tariffs over Russian oil
The measure still needs to clear the US House of Representatives and faces further legislative and administrative steps before it could take effect.
According to Ritolia, the measures still face further legislative and administrative hurdles, while their impact will depend largely on how aggressively the US administration implements them, including whether it grants exemptions or waivers.
"Recent experience suggests that when physical supply security becomes a concern, policymakers retain an incentive to avoid measures that could unnecessarily disrupt crude availability," he said.
Also read: 100% tariffs on India soon? US Senate clears bill for sanctions over Russian oil
The timing of any curbs is critical as global crude markets remain relatively tight and uncertainty over Middle Eastern supplies has increased the importance of alternative sources, Ritolia said. A significant restriction on Russian oil could therefore tighten global balances rather than simply redirect existing trade flows.
India's dependence on Russian crude has surged since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, when Western sanctions and an exodus of European buyers left Moscow offering deep discounts to Asian refiners. Russia supplied less than 100,000 barrels per day to India in 2021, or about 2.5 per cent of its crude imports, according to the US Energy Information Administration. The volume rose to about 740,000 bpd in 2022 and nearly 1.8 million bpd in 2023, making Russia India's largest crude supplier with about 39 per cent of imports that year.
The dependence has since grown further. Kpler data show Indian refiners imported a record 2.8 million bpd of Russian crude in July 2026, accounting for about 55.5 per cent of total crude imports of just over 5 million bpd. That compares with roughly 1.8 million bpd on average in 2024, according to Kpler-based data.
Ritolia said Russian crude has become an important supply hedge for Indian refiners, reducing their exposure to disruptions along traditional Middle Eastern supply routes.
This reliance became particularly evident during the recent period of heightened Middle East supply risks, when the US provided temporary sanctions flexibility that allowed Russian barrels to continue flowing to India, he said.
Also read: How US bill proposing 100% tariffs over Russian oil purchase could hurt India
Replacing Russian crude at current volumes would be difficult, if not impossible, in the short term, Ritolia said. A rapid curtailment of Russian supplies to India or other Asian buyers could therefore tighten global oil balances and put upward pressure on crude prices.
For India, the impact would extend beyond refinery procurement costs, potentially increasing the country's overall crude import bill, widening pressure on the current account and raising concerns over energy security.
The key question, Ritolia said, is not simply whether Russian barrels can be redirected to other buyers, but whether sufficient alternative supplies are available to replace them without further tightening the global market.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of civil aviation (MoCA) said on Sunday that a team from aviation regulator, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), is being sent to Maharashtraâs Baramati airfield, where a Cessna training aircraft was involved in a runway excursion earlier in the day.âThe air safety team from the DGCA is going to the site to conduct a preliminary investigation and ascertain the circumstances and contributing factors leading to the incident,â the ministry statement read.MoCA further noted that the plane appeared to have sustained damage to its propeller, engine cowling and nose landing gear, while no fatalities or injuries were reported.âThere were no injuries or fatalities reported. The aircraft has sustained prima facie damage to the propeller, engine cowling and nose landing gear. A detailed assessment of the damage will be carried out by the competent authorities,â the statement added.According to the ministry, the incident occurred around 12:25 pm when the Cessna C172, bearing registration VT-SEX and operated by flying training school Academy of Carver Aviation, veered off the runway at Baramati airfield.The aircraft was being operated for a Circuit and Landing Emergencies (CL Emergencies) training exercise.
It was under the command of flight instructor Captain Chirag Shashikant Doifode, with trainee Abhijeet Jundre on board.The plane had taxied out at around 12:09 pm for the scheduled training exercise.âDuring the exercise, the aircraft entered the runway through Link Bravo and lined up at the threshold of runway 29, where a rejected take-off exercise practice was carried out.
âSubsequently, the aircraft lined up at the threshold of runway 11 and another rejected take-off exercise was carried out,â the statement noted.During the exercise, the aircraft was unable to stop within the paved runway surface and subsequently veered off the extended paved surface beyond the threshold of runway 29 towards the right side, resulting in a runway excursion, according to the ministry.(With PTI inputs)

headline: A planned procession by Green Visakha, an environmental NGO, to raise concerns over proposed hyperscale AI data centres in the city was denied permission by the police on Sunday.
full_text:
A planned procession by Green Visakha, an environmental NGO, to raise concerns over proposed hyperscale AI data centres in the city was denied permission by the police on Sunday.
Residents gathered near the Bhagat Singh statue at YMCA junction around 6 p.m. for a procession from the statue to RK Beach. For nearly an hour, police personnel engaged in discussions with the gathering, during which the residents were asked not to raise banners or slogans.
Senior officials arrived at the spot and spoke with the organisers, who maintained that they intended no protest but sought only to hold a discussion and take a photograph at the statue. The police permitted the group for a photograph at the site before dispersing.
Speaking to The Hindu, Circle Inspector L. Appala Naidu said, “No protest had been permitted on Beach Road, and that citizens wishing to demonstrate should do so at the designated protest site near the Gandhi statue close to the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation building.”
Green Visakha president Raja Rama Mohan Roy said the procession had been intended to sensitise citizens to concerns over water scarcity, groundwater depletion, rising electricity demand, waste heat, and pollution linked to large-scale data centre projects. He said the organisation would approach the police again to seek permission.

headline: 'Attempt to murder': TMC MPs blame BJP for attack on Mamata Banerjee's car, claim CM Suvendu link
full_text:
'Attempt to murder': TMC MPs blame BJP for attack on Mamata Banerjee's car, claim CM Suvendu link
Edited by: Yashasvi Vasistha / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 09, 2026, 20:02 IST

Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee speaks to the media following the attack on her vehicle, while she was on her way to meet a TMC worker in North 24 Parganas, in Barrackpore
NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs Kalyan Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee on Sunday accused the BJP of being behind an alleged attack on former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee's vehicle, after stones and other objects were reportedly hurled at her car in North 24 Parganas.Mamata Banerjee was travelling to meet the family of a TMC worker who allegedly died in police custody when the incident took place. TMC MPs Kalyan Banerjee and Dola Sen were accompanying her.Kalyan Banerjee described the incident as an "attempt to murder" and alleged that the attack was targeted at Mamata Banerjee. He also accused the police of remaining silent spectators while the incident took place."The entire car, there was not a single second when stones were not thrown. Stones were thrown every moment, targeting Mamata Banerjee to assault her," Kalyan Banerjee said, as cited by news agency ANI.He alleged that hundreds of BJP workers were present at the spot and claimed that the incident took place in the presence of police personnel."Hundreds and hundreds of BJP workers were there, and police were remaining silent spectators, absolutely silent spectators," he said.
Kalyan Banerjee also alleged that there was a direction from West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari behind the incident.
"Of course there was a direction given by the CM Suvendu Adhikari," he said.
Abhishek Banerjee alleges 'political violence'
TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee also accused the BJP of unleashing political violence in West Bengal and alleged that Mamata Banerjee was "brutally attacked" while travelling to meet the family of the deceased party worker.In a post on social media, Abhishek Banerjee alleged that the incident reflected a wider law-and-order failure in the state."And now, a former Chief Minister of the state, who was on her way to meet the grieving family, is brutally attacked by goons planted by BJP," he said, as reported by ANI.He questioned the police response and said the incident represented a "failure of governance"."This is not merely a failure of the state police. This is a failure of governance," Abhishek Banerjee said.He also alleged that the police had failed to protect TMC workers and the grieving family, and questioned whether political violence had become a tool of governance in the state.
Dola Sen questions law and order
Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen said Mamata Banerjee had gone to meet the family of the TMC worker who allegedly died in police custody and questioned whether she should have been prevented from making the visit."Our worker died in police custody, an incident akin to a lockup death. His wife is a councillor. You tell me, as a matter of simple, natural justice, should our leader, Mamata Banerjee, not go to meet that family?" Sen said.She alleged that stones and half-bricks were thrown at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle and claimed that BJP workers and police personnel were present at the spot."They attacked her in a targeted manner... BJP goons and police stood in front, throwing half-bricks and stones, cracking the glass of Didi's car," she alleged.Sen also said Mamata Banerjee's visit was not a political programme but an attempt to meet the family of the deceased worker.
Mamata alleges attack could have caused serious injuries
Mamata Banerjee herself alleged that large stones were hurled at her car in front of police personnel and said the attack could have resulted in serious injuries or death."Large stones were hurled at my car by anti-social elements, right in front of the police. The attack on the vehicle was so severe that if the windows had been open, my head would have been split open. We could have all been killed," she said.
She also alleged that the police were providing protection to the BJP and said she had never witnessed such an incident before."This happened right in front of the police. I have never seen anything like this. What is going on?" she said."Chor bhagao" slogans were also heard from the crowd, according to ANI.
BJP denies involvement, condemns incident
West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya denied any BJP involvement in the alleged attack and condemned the throwing of stones or other objects at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle.
"Let me be clear: the BJP has absolutely no connection to the incidents where mud, stones, or slippers were thrown at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle," Bhattacharya said, according to ANI.He said the BJP did not endorse such behaviour and called for police action against those responsible."It is between the public and TMC," he said, while maintaining that the BJP condemned the incident.State minister Agnimitra Paul also condemned the alleged attack and said neither she nor the BJP supported such actions."Mamata Banerjee may have committed many wrongs or made many mistakes, but we can never support this kind of behaviour, especially against a woman, and an elderly woman. We do not endorse this. If anyone is carrying out such acts while claiming to represent the BJP, they are in the wrong," Paul said.

headline: Bengal tea farmer abducted from field, taken across Bangladesh border
full_text:
Bengal tea farmer abducted from field, taken across Bangladesh border
A Jalpaiguri tea farmer was allegedly taken into Bangladesh from a border tea garden on Saturday. The case has raised tensions after his family linked it to a foiled infiltration and BSF-BGB talks.
A 35-year-old tea farmer from West Bengal’s Jalpaiguri district was allegedly abducted by a group of Bangladeshi men from a tea garden near the India-Bangladesh border on Saturday.
The farmer, identified as Dipankar Gope, lives in Tasar Para village in the Chaulhati border area. His family believes he was taken away in an act of revenge after an earlier attempt to cross the border illegally was stopped.
According to local sources, on August 6, a Bangladeshi man allegedly tried to enter India by cutting the barbed wire fence along the Chaulhati border.
Villagers and Border Security Force (BSF) personnel caught him and handed him over to the police. Locals suspect that the man was linked to a cross-border smuggling network.
Two days later, on Saturday morning, Gope went to his six-bigha tea garden near the border to spray pesticides. The garden is located beyond the barbed wire fence.
Gope was working alone when around 20 Bangladeshi men allegedly crossed the border and surrounded him. He reportedly tried to escape but was overpowered.
The group then allegedly took Gope across the international border into Bangladesh’s Panchagarh district.
BSF ATTEMPTS NEGOTIATION BUT IN VAIN
The incident sparked panic across nearby border villages, with residents expressing concerns over the safety of people who regularly work in fields and tea gardens located close to the international boundary.
Following the alleged abduction, BSF personnel rushed to the spot and initiated efforts to secure Gope's release. Officials also held a flag meeting with the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB).
However, the farmer had not been released till Saturday night and was reportedly in BGB custody.
Meanwhile, a video purportedly showing Gope has surfaced on social media, in which he allegedly says he would only be released if the Bangladeshi national arrested by Indian authorities is freed.
The authenticity of the video has not been independently verified.
Gope's father appealed for his son's safe return, alleging that the abduction was an act of revenge linked to the recent arrest at the border.
The BSF remains in constant contact with Bangladeshi authorities to secure the farmer's safe release, while investigations are underway to determine the circumstances behind the incident and examine the possible involvement of organised cross-border smuggling groups.

headline: Delhi tribunal awards ₹44 lakh to children of couple killed in UP road accident
full_text:
Delhi tribunal awards ₹44 lakh to children of couple killed in UP road accident
New Delhi, A Delhi Motor Accident Claims Tribunal awarded over ₹44 lakh in compensation to the five children of a couple killed after a car allegedly rammed their motorcycle from behind in Uttar Pradesh in 2021.
Presiding Officer Aparna Swami directed IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company to pay a total compensation of ₹44.09 lakh, along with interest at 7.5 per cent per annum from the date of filing the petitions.
In an order dated July 30, the tribunal said, "The respondent number 1 was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner at the time of the accident. The mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle also corroborates the version of the petitioners."
The tribunal passed separate awards of ₹19.86 lakh and ₹24.23 lakh for the deaths of Brijnandan and his wife Rajkumari, respectively.
According to the claim petitions, the couple was travelling on a motorcycle in Bulandshahr district on July 2, 2021, when a WagonR car allegedly hit their vehicle from behind at high speed. The impact threw them onto the road, and the car subsequently ran over them. Both were declared brought dead at a hospital.
The driver, owner and insurer contested the claim.
The insurance company argued that the offending vehicle's registration number did not initially appear in the FIR and investigation records. Rejecting this contention, the tribunal held that the investigation later traced the vehicle and established its involvement through the mechanical inspection report, registration certificate and insurance policy.
The court relied on the testimony of an eyewitness who said he saw the car overtake his motorcycle, violently hit the victims' bike from behind, and then flee the scene.
Holding that the accident occurred due to the driver's rash and negligent driving, the tribunal said minor lapses in the investigation could not outweigh reliable oral and documentary evidence.

headline: Chhattisgarh to provide ₹5 crore aid to flood-hit Assam: CM Vishnu Deo Sai
full_text:
Chhattisgarh to provide ₹5 crore aid to flood-hit Assam: CM Vishnu Deo Sai
Sai spoke to Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma over the phone and took stock of the situation arising from the floods
Chhattisgarh chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai on Sunday announced ₹5 crore assistance for relief and rehabilitation efforts in flood-hit Assam and said the people of the state stood firmly with those affected by the natural calamity.
Sai spoke to Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma over the phone and took stock of the situation arising from the floods, according to an official statement.
Sai expressed concern over the difficulties faced by people in the flood-affected areas and conveyed the solidarity of the people of Chhattisgarh with Assam.
“In this difficult time, the people of Chhattisgarh stand with their brothers and sisters in Assam with deep empathy and solidarity,” Sai said.

He said the Chhattisgarh government decided to provide ₹5 crore to assist the ongoing relief and rehabilitation efforts in Assam.
The assistance is aimed at supporting the state government’s efforts to provide relief to families affected by the floods and help in rehabilitation and restoration work, the statement said.
Sai’s announcement comes as Assam continues to grapple with the impact of flooding, which has disrupted normal life and affected families in several areas.
The Chhattisgarh CM also expressed concern for the safety of the affected people and prayed for an early return to normalcy in the state.
“I pray to Maa Kamakhya to protect all families affected by the floods and for peace, prosperity and normalcy to return to Assam at the earliest,” he said.
Sai also assured that Chhattisgarh will stand with Assam in this difficult period, underlining the spirit of cooperation and mutual support between the two states during a natural disaster.

headline: Milk prices in Maharashtra set to increase by ₹2 per litre from August 11, association cites rising cost pressure
full_text:
Milk prices in Maharashtra set to increase by ₹2 per litre from August 11, association cites rising cost pressure
The decision to increase milk prices in Maharashtra by ₹2/litre follows discussions on protecting dairy farmers' interests while safeguarding consumers.
In a key development for consumers, the prices of both cow and buffalo milk across Maharashtra are set to increase by ₹2 per litre from August 11, Tuesday.
This comes after a decision taken by the Milk Producers and Processors Welfare Association, news agency ANI reported.
Also Read | Maharashtra’s daily milk collection drops by 750k litres after FDA crackdown
Why a price rise in milk and dairy products?
As the prices rise, the association explained that packaging and procurement steps are facing significant cost pressures.
The association stated that diesel prices have increased by ₹10 per litre.
It added that the expenses incurred in packaging have also increased by around 30 per cent.
The procurement price of milk has also increased.
Thus, the association has increased the selling price of milk by ₹2 per litre, according to news agency PTI. Furthermore, the prices of dairy products would be up to 10 per cent.
Also Read | Karnal: NDRI commercialises eight rapid milk quality assessment technologies
Govt rules out MSP for milk?
The decision to increase milk prices in Maharashtra follows discussions on protecting dairy farmers' interests while safeguarding consumers.
Addressing milk pricing at the national level, Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Rajiv Ranjan Singh (alias Lalan Singh) clarified in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha that the government has no proposal to fix a Minimum Support Price (MSP) for milk.
According to the government, the rates will continue to be determined by cooperatives and private dairies based on market conditions.
However, as per ANI, the minister emphasised that the authorities are implementing several measures to safeguard dairy farmers, consumers, stabilise market rates, and maintain quality control.
Infrastructure and processing capacity expansion
In order to integrate more dairy farmers into the organised sector, the government outlined infrastructure developed by March 2026:
Dairy cooperative societies: 36,283 new village-level societies were established, and 31,150 societies were strengthened.
Quality assurance: 168 lakh litres per day of milk chilling capacity were created, and the distribution of 76,748 quality testing devices.
Processing capabilities: Projects with a milk processing and value-addition capacity of 418 lakh litres per day have also been approved.
Also Read | 930,000 farmers to begin getting loan waiver benefit from Tuesday
India's milk production
India produced 248 million metric tonnes (MMT) of milk in 2024-25, up from 146 MMT in 2014-15, registering an increase of about 69 per cent, according to the government.
The government attributed this expansion to livestock initiatives, including breed development, genetic improvement, free artificial insemination (AI), sex-sorted semen, and in-vitro fertilisation (IVF).

headline: Ahmedabad PG security guard ties wire around student's neck, rapes her on terrace
full_text:
Ahmedabad PG security guard ties wire around student's neck, rapes her on terrace
A security guard at a paying guest accommodation in Ahmedabad was arrested after a student alleged he raped her on the terrace. Police formed 10 teams, examined CCTV footage and continued investigating the circumstances around the case.
A woman living in a paying guest accommodation in Gujarat’s Ahmedabad was allegedly raped by a security guard after she went to the building’s terrace for a walk, with police arresting the accused within hours of the incident.
The incident took place at a PG in the Anandnagar area on Saturday, August 8. The woman, who is studying interior designing, had gone to the terrace at around 10 pm when the security guard was also present there.
According to the preliminary information, when the woman tried to leave the terrace to get away from the guard, he allegedly tied a wire around her neck and raped her. She was later taken to hospital, where she is undergoing treatment.
The accused has been identified as Dharm Singh, a security guard at the PG. Police arrested him on Sunday morning after launching a large-scale search operation.
Following the incident, Anandnagar police, the Local Crime Branch and the Crime Branch formed 10 teams to track down the accused.
The teams searched for Singh through the night before police managed to apprehend him in the morning.
Police have also shared CCTV footage showing the accused moving between the floors and the terrace using the lift. The footage is part of the evidence being examined as part of the investigation.
Preliminary information suggests that Singh is a native of Hardoi district in Uttar Pradesh. He had reportedly started working as a security guard at the PG only a few days before the alleged rape.
Police are continuing their investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident and are examining the CCTV footage and other available evidence.
The woman remains under medical treatment following the alleged assault.

headline: 'Couldn't bring to complete stop': Why trainer aircraft ran off Baramati runway
full_text:
'Couldn't bring to complete stop': Why trainer aircraft ran off Baramati runway
The aircraft reportedly crossed the threshold of Runway 29 at the Baramati airfield, reaching around 20 feet beyond the end of the runway.
A private trainer aircraft crashed at the Baramati airstrip after it skidded off the runway on Sunday. The plane, operated by a private aviation academy, was part of a training exercise being held in Baramati, which falls in Pune district of Maharashtra.
Pune Rural Superintendent of Police (SP) Sandeep Singh Gill said the VT-SEX aircraft went off the extended paved surface to the right side beyond the runway. Captain Chirag Shashikant Doifode and cadet Abhijeet Jundre, who were on board, escaped safely and no injuries were reported.
WATCH: Trainee aircraft crashes at Baramati airstrip
ALSO READ: Training plane skids while landing at Baramati, where Ajit Pawar died in crash
Explaining the reason behind the mishap, the police officer said a failure to bring the aircraft to a complete stop while taxiing along the runway led to the incident. The aircraft reportedly crossed the threshold of Runway 29 at the Baramati airfield, reaching around 20 feet beyond the end of the runway.
"The aircraft initially entered the runway through Link Bravo, lined up at the threshold of Runway 29, and carried out a rejected take-off. Thereafter, the aircraft was lined up at the threshold of Runway 11, where another rejected take-off was carried out. During the course of this exercise, the aircraft could not be brought to a complete stop on the runway and continued beyond the threshold of Runway 29," he said.
ALSO READ: Training aircraft makes hard landing in Baramati; pilot safe
The aircraft was owned by Carver aviation, a private flying school in Baramati.
The Baramati airfield saw a major tragedy earlier this year when a private charter plane carrying then Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar and four others crashed on January 28, leading to the death of all on board.
In another recent mishap, a trainer aircraft of a different private company crash landed near the Baramati airstrip following a technical snag. No casualties were reported in the incident which occurred on May 13.

headline: ‘Bid to saffronise': Question on VD Savarkar in primary level quiz triggers row in Kerala | What we know
full_text:
‘Bid to saffronise': Question on VD Savarkar in primary level quiz triggers row in Kerala | What we know
Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan accused the Congress-led UDF government in the state of “colluding” with the RSS and “glorifying” Savarkar.
A political row erupted in Kerala over a question on Hindutva ideologue V D Savarkar, asked in a school quiz that supposedly praised him, with the Left student organisations and leaders saying that the state government was promoting "sangh parivar agenda".
On August 6, a "Freedom Quiz" was organised for lower primary students in Kasaragod, Kumbla and Manjeshwar schools.
In the quiz, a question was asked — "Who is the freedom fighter that received the most severe punishment from the British?"
The expected answer? VD Savarkar.
This led to a controversy in the state, following which, Kerala's education minister N Samsudheen ordered a probe and directed the Director of General Education to investigate the matter and present a report, news agency PTI reported.
Also read: Kerala Lower Primary School Teacher rank holders eat grass in protest over delay in appointments
He also directed the education department to take strict actions against those found responsible.
‘Historically inaccurate’
The statement released by the education minister's office called the question “historically inaccurate” and said that the quiz was not authorised to be conducted independently.
The minister's office said that the ‘freedom quiz’ was not part of the activity calendar of either the Social Science Club or the General Education Department. It added that no one was authorised to prepare the questions or conduct the competition independently by either of the departments.
"The person who included the historically incorrect question holds a prejudiced view," the statement read.
CPI(M), left student organisations attack govt
The question and its alleged implication triggered criticism from the left student organisations such as the Students' Federation of India and leaders of the Communist Party of India (Marxist).
Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan accused the Congress-led UDF government in the state of “colluding” with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh and “glorifying” Savarkar.
He alleged that the Centre and the RSS were attempting to “rewrite history”.
V Sivankutty, former education minister of the state said that this was an attempt to "saffronise" Kerala's education and distort the history of India's freedom struggle.
He also demanded an apology from the general education department of the state to the students and public.
CPI state secretary Binoy Viswam said that “to smuggle in people like Savarkar as the heroes of freedom movements, it is not accidental, it's a conscious attempt by the BJP-RSS forces to impress the young generation that India's freedom movement is a movement led by such kind of people, which is contrary to the fact.”
“What's the fact? The fact is that they had no role at all the freedom movement. They were not even spectators. But they want to tell the young generation that Savarkar is the hero of the freedom movement. Not Mahatma Gandhi, not Jawaharlal Nehru... They want to tell that Savarkar is the hero. Savarkar is the person who wrote letters after letters to the British authorities. They were all letters for apology. He wrote 4-5 letters to the British tendering apology for whatever he did. BJP-RSS was always keen to depict him as a national hero,” he told news agency ANI.
SFI state secretary PS Sanjeev alleged that the quiz sought to portray Savarkar as a freedom fighter. "Under the UDF government in Kerala, with the IUML handling the general education portfolio, an attempt is being made to create a role for the Sangh Parivar, which betrayed the freedom struggle," Sanjeev said in a social media post, reported PTI.
MK Muneer, a leader of IUML which is part of the current UDF government in the state, also said that portraying Savarkar as a patriot was part of the agenda of RSS and BJP.
BJP State President and MLA Rajeev Chandrasekhar warned the Congress and IUML, which holds the education portfolio in Kerala, to not make the issue political.
“This is India. This is Keralam. The history of India and the history of Kerala is well understood by every Indian, every Malayali… Veer Savarkar was an important and significant figure in India's independence movement, and the Muslim League and Rahul Gandhi cannot change that. I would caution them not to make this a political issue because otherwise the BJP will have to come out and expose the Muslim League and their politics. In the name of secularism, you should not try and defame important leaders of the Indian freedom movement,” he said.

The doctor said while the protesters should be taken to the hospital, they are refusing to move. The required treatment was being provided on the spot.
The protests over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jharkhand continued for the sixteenth day on Sunday morning as talks held over the past two days failed to end the deadlock. The Hemant Soren government will hold fresh discussions with the protesting job aspirants at 12 pm today as student leaders carry on their indefinite hunger strike for seventh straight day at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Stadium.
Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has emerged as one of the prominent faces leading the protest, saw his health deteriorate last night with blood glucose level falling to 53 around 3 am. One of the protesters alleged that efforts were made to remove Mahto during night as a medical team visited repeatedly.
ALSO READ: JPSC row: Govt talks with another faction of protesters end without breakthrough, stir to continue
The agitating students have vowed to continue their protests. Student protester Umme Hani said, "If the government doesn't accept our demands, we will continue our protests. Because we want a reform in the system. We are not just fighting for ourselves. This is a fight for the next generation."
Union Minister Sanjay Seth and Jharkhand BJP President Aditya Sahu met the protesters at the protest site and spoke to them.
What doctor says on health of fasting leaders
Sharing latest update on the health of the fasting student leaders, which include Mahendra and Kush Mahto, Doctor AP Sinha said their condition was stable. “Their weights have dropped. But they are alert. Their vitals are fine.”
The doctor said while they should be taken to the hospital, the protesters are refusing to move. Hence, the required treatment was being provided on the spot.
The protests broke out few days after the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) declared the preliminary examination results of the 14th Combined Civil Services Examination on July 2. There were allegations of irregularities in the exam taken by 3.5 lakh people. The agitating students have been demanding the cancellation of the exam and reforms in both JPSC and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).
Five rounds of talks fail
So far, the Soren government has held five rounds of talks with protesting students. On Friday night, the state ministers first met JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, one of the groups spearheading the agitation, and heard their demands. On Saturday, talks were held with Mahto-led JPSC-JSSC Abhyarthi Nyay Manch, NSUI, Jharkhand Chhatra Morcha (JCM) and Adivasi Chhatra Sangh (ACS). A sixth round of talks is set to be held today noon.
ALSO READ: ABVP members scuffle with police near Jharkhand CM residence, 8-10 detained
Unimpressed by the Jharkhand government's move to hold separate talks with various student groups, the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch called it "political manoeuvring" which was meant "to create a divide among students and divert attention" from core demands. "But they should know that all students are united," said Ravindra Paswan, a leader of the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch.
The All India Students' Association (AISA), led by Neha Bora and Ranchi unit chief Vijay Kumar, also joined the protests and expressed solidarity with the fasting student leaders.
The members of Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), who also held protests, clashed with police while attempting to break through barricades near the chief minister's residence.
What are Jharkhand protesters demanding
The protesters have been demanding the cancellation of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination, and a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), CID or by a panel of retired high court judges from outside the state.
ACS leader Kartik Oraon has further demanded inclusion of tribal and regional languages as qualifying papers in recruitment examinations.
What Jharkhand govt said
Rural Development Minister Dipika Pandey Singh said the panel had apprised the chief minister of the demands and concerns raised by student delegations during the discussions. "It was decided in the meeting with the chief minister that a final round of talks with the protesting students will take place at 12 pm on Sunday," she said.
Jharkhand Minister Sanjay Prasad Yadav said the government would continue discussions with the agitators demanding comprehensive. Higher and Technical Education Minister Sudivya Kumar said the government had issued an email ID to seek suggestions from aspirants on reforms in the recruitment process.
As many as 19 people have been arrested and the former panel chairperson L Khiangte has been questioned four times since July 28.

headline: Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar B. Khandre directed officials to ensure effective implementation of the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) scheme in Ballari district to provide employment...
full_text:
Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar B. Khandre directed officials to ensure effective implementation of the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) scheme in Ballari district to provide employment to eligible workers locally and prevent distress migration.
Chairing a review meeting on the progress of schemes of the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department at the new Abdul Nazir Sab auditorium of the zilla panchayat in Ballari on Sunday (August 9), Mr. Khandre said inadequate rainfall had affected agricultural activities in the district, increasing the possibility of people migrating to cities in search of employment.
He directed officials to ensure that every eligible worker in rural areas was given employment under the scheme.
Expressing dissatisfaction over the district achieving only 46% of the person-day generation target set up to June, the Minister said that Ballari has a target of generating 51.3 lakh person-days during the current year. He directed officials to accelerate employment generation and create at least five to six lakh person-days every month.
The officials informed the meeting that there were 1.84 lakh active job cards covering around 4.6 lakh workers in the district, of which e-KYC was completed for about 1.3 lakh job cards. The Minister then instructed officials to complete the remaining e-KYC process at the earliest.
‘No excuses for delay in providing work’
Mr. Khandre expressed particular displeasure over the performance of Ballari taluk, where there are around 48,000 active job cards, but only about 11,000 workers are being given employment per day.
The taluk panchayat executive officer attributed the delay to the completion of earlier works and the time taken to prepare an action plan for new works. The Minister, however, directed officials not to offer excuses and immediately take up individual and community-based works.
Officials to be held accountable for migration
Mr. Khandre said that preventing the migration of poor people and members of Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Backward Class communities in search of work was a major priority of the government.
“If people migrate from any area because they have not been given employment, the executive officer and panchayat development officer concerned will be held responsible,” Mr. Khandre warned, directing officials to continuously monitor the employment guarantee programme and ensure that wages were credited regularly to workers’ bank accounts. Timely payment, he said, would increase workers’ confidence in the scheme.
‘No shortage of funds’
Mr. Khandre said there was no shortage of funds for the scheme and that more than ₹1,000 crore had already been released to zilla panchayats. “During the first quarter, the State government has provided ₹1,200 crore and the Union government ₹1,700 crore. The officials should maintain complete transparency and strictly follow the rules. They should personally inspect worksites. Technical supervisors, executive officers and IEC coordinators, besides senior officials, should actively participate in field-level implementation. Merely showing works on records without actually executing them will not be tolerated,” he warned.
Clean drinking water a priority
Mr. Khandre said ensuring clean and safe drinking water to every rural household was a major priority of the government and that delays or negligence in implementing projects would not be accepted.
Criticising the failure to properly restore roads dug up for Jal Jeevan Mission works, Mr. Khandre said that the contractors and engineers were responsible for restoring roads to their original condition immediately after laying pipelines.
E-Swathu records to be delivered at doorsteps
Taking note of citizens repeatedly visiting government offices for e-Swathu related work, Mr. Khandre made it clear that officials and staff must make arrangements to visit households and distribute e-Swathu and khata records at their doorsteps.

headline: Two years since RG Kar rape-murder, West Bengal medical institutions to observe 2-min silence today
full_text:
Two years since RG Kar rape-murder, West Bengal medical institutions to observe 2-min silence today
RG Kar Medical College and Hospital rape and murder case dates back to August 9, 2024, when the body of a trainee doctor was found in a seminar room on campus.
The West Bengal Health and Family Welfare Department has directed all establishments under its control to observe two minutes of silence on Sunday in memory of "Abhaya," marking two years since the rape and murder of a postgraduate trainee doctor at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital.
According to a notice issued by the department on August 8, all establishments under the Health and Family Welfare Department will observe two minutes of silence from 11:00 am to 11:02 am on August 9.
Also Read | Bengal govt sanctions prosecution of ex-RG Kar principal Sandip Ghosh in graft case
"I am directed to request all the establishments under the control of Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of West Bengal shall observe 2 (two) minutes' silence in memory of 'Abhaya', from 11.00 AM till 11.02 AM on 09/08/2026," the notice read.
The RG Kar Medical College and Hospital rape and murder case dates back to August 9, 2024, when the body of a 31-year-old postgraduate trainee doctor was found inside a seminar room on the hospital campus.
The incident triggered nationwide protests by doctors, medical students and civil society groups, who demanded a transparent investigation into the case and stronger safety measures for healthcare professionals. The victim came to be referred to as "Abhaya" during the protests and subsequent proceedings.
Last year, in 2025, the students and Bharatiya Janata Party leaders held a 'Nabanna Chalo Abhiyan' protest march, demanding justice for the victim.
Also Read | ‘Vox populi, vox dei’: TMC MP resigns, cites RG Kar rape-murder case as Bengal crack reaches Delhi
Meanwhile on May 21, the Calcutta High Court directed an investigation into the alleged destruction of evidence and to revisit the issue raised by the family of the victim regarding the RG Kar incident.
In an order issued today, a bench comprising Justice Shampa Sarkar and Justice Tirthankar Ghosh stated that a three-member Special Investigation Team (SIT), led by the Joint Director (Eastern Zone) of the CBI, shall conduct this investigation.
The CBI has been directed to re-investigate the sequence of events that transpired from the time dinner was consumed on the night of the incident until the cremation took place the following day. To this end, the CBI is authorised to interrogate anyone it deems necessary.
Also Read | K'taka: Three arrested for gang-rape of tribal woman from West Bengal
On November 29, 2025, the CBI filed a chargesheet concerning financial irregularities at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital. The chargesheet named Sandip Ghosh and others, including Dr. Ashish Kumar Pandey, Biplab Singha, Suman Hazra, and Afsar Ali Khan, for their involvement in financial misconduct. This investigation was initiated following an order by the Calcutta High Court.

headline: ‘We condemn such incidents’: BJP's Samik Bhattacharya denies party role in alleged attack on Mamata Banerjee's car
full_text:
‘We condemn such incidents’: BJP's Samik Bhattacharya denies party role in alleged attack on Mamata Banerjee's car
Reacting to the incident, suspended TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee alleged that stones were repeatedly hurled at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle.
A political row erupted in West Bengal on Sunday after former Chief Minister and Trinamool Congress (TMC) supremo Mamata Banerjee's vehicle was allegedly attacked with stones and other objects, with the ruling BJP and TMC trading allegations over the incident.
Reacting to the incident, suspended TMC MP Kalyan Banerjee alleged that stones were repeatedly hurled at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle and claimed that the incident was a targeted attack.
"The entire car, there was not a single second when stones were not thrown. Stones were thrown every moment, targeting Mamata Banerjee to assault her," he alleged.
Also Read: ‘Could have been killed’: Mamata Banerjee's vehicle attacked with ‘stones, mud’ in North 24 Parganas
Watch his statement here:
He described the incident as an "attempt to murder" and alleged that hundreds of BJP workers were present at the spot while the police remained a "silent spectator".
"Hundreds and hundreds of BJP workers were there, and police were remaining silent spectators, absolutely silent spectators," he said.
On the incident, TMC leader Dola Sen said Mamata Banerjee had gone to meet the family of a party worker who allegedly died in police custody and questioned whether she should have been prevented from visiting the family.
"Our worker died in police custody, an incident akin to a lockup death. His wife is a councillor. You tell me, as a matter of simple, natural justice, should our leader, Mamata Banerjee, not go to meet that family?" Sen said.
She alleged that the incident reflected a deterioration in the law-and-order situation in West Bengal and accused the administration of allowing such incidents to take place.
"They attacked her in a targeted manner... BJP goons and police stood in front, throwing half-bricks and stones, cracking the glass of Didi's car," she alleged.
She also claimed that Mamata Banerjee's visit was not for a political programme but to meet the family of the deceased party worker.
Sen added that the incident should prompt the administration to reflect on the law-and-order situation in the state.
Meanwhile, BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya dismissed TMC's allegations of the party's involvement and condemned the reported stone-pelting on Banerjee's vehicle.
"Let me be clear: the BJP has absolutely no connection to the incidents where mud, stones, or slippers were thrown at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle. Regardless of whether it involves a Chief Minister or any other female leader, the BJP does not endorse the throwing of stones at anyone's vehicle; we condemn such incidents," Bhattacharya said.
He said that if such incidents occurred, the police would take appropriate action, while accusing the TMC of being involved in a conflict with the public.
Bhattacharya stated, "What is happening here is a conflict involving the Trinamool, a clash between the public and the Trinamool. Regardless of whether it involves a Chief Minister or any other female leader, the BJP does not endorse the throwing of stones at anyone's vehicle; we condemn such incidents"
State Minister Agnimitra Paul also condemned the alleged attack and said neither she nor the BJP or the state government supported such acts.
"Mamata Banerjee may have committed many wrongs or made many mistakes, but we can never support this kind of behaviour, especially against a woman, and an elderly woman. We do not endorse this. If anyone is carrying out such acts while claiming to represent the BJP, they are in the wrong," Paul said.
The former CM was allegedly attacked when she was on her way to meet a TMC worker's family in North 24 Parganas. Kalyan Banerjee and Dola Sen were also accompanying Mamata Banerjee. "Chor bhagao" slogans were heard from the crowd.

headline: 20,000 security personnel, NDRF force, CCTVs: Preparations in full swing for Independence Day at Delhi's Red Fort
full_text:
20,000 security personnel, NDRF force, CCTVs: Preparations in full swing for Independence Day at Delhi's Red Fort
The security arrangements include Delhi Police units, paramilitary forces, commandos and NSG teams, including snipers and specialised ‘hit teams’.
With Independence Day just days away, Delhi has stepped up security around the Red Fort, deploying around 20,000 personnel and a multi-layered surveillance network to secure the venue for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s August 15 address.
The security arrangements include Delhi Police units, paramilitary forces, commandos and NSG teams, including snipers and specialised ‘hit teams’, while over 1,000 CCTV cameras, facial recognition and number plate detection systems have been deployed around the Red Fort and adjoining areas, news agency PTI reported.
DCP North Raja Banthia said the security deployment would include Delhi Police personnel from the Traffic Unit, North District teams, local police, PCR, Special Branch and Special Cell, along with general security personnel.
“Personnel from all these divisions will be deployed. Additionally, numerous paramilitary companies, commandos, and NSG teams, including ‘hit teams’ and snipers, will be stationed here,” he said.
He added that an NDRF force will also be present to respond to any potential contingencies. Furthermore, our Quick Reaction Teams (QRTs) will be deployed at strategic points, including on watchtowers.
Also Read: Defence ministry issues Independence Day invites with Vande Mataram lyrics
CCTVs, body-worn cameras and more
On technical deployment, Banthia said over a thousand cameras have been installed at the Red Fort and surrounding areas specifically for Independence Day. "We have control rooms staffed by highly trained personnel dedicated to monitoring these feeds, and we have established specific points for on-ground response teams to act quickly", he added.
The police have incorporated video analytics, such as Facial Recognition Systems (FRS), number plate recognition, and intrusion detection, at various locations based on specific needs.
Additionally, some police personnel will be equipped with body-worn cameras. Anti-drone systems are in place to counter any drone threats, and are actively monitoring online social media chatter. "We are fully prepared on all fronts, with all briefings and training sessions completed. We are on track," Banthia said.
Counter-terrorism exercise
In addition to the security deployment, to assess preparedness for possible terror attacks, Delhi Police and the National Security Guard (NSG), along with several central and state agencies, conducted a joint counter-terrorism exercise across the national capital.
The fifth edition of "Sudarshan Shakti-V" was conducted from 10 am on August 7 to 4 am on August 8 under the aegis of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Delhi Police said, according to news agency PTI.
Multiple simulated terror scenarios, including simultaneous blasts, indiscriminate firing, hostage situations, an aircraft hijacking and CBRNE attacks, were created at prominent locations, including ISBT Kashmiri Gate, Connaught Place, Nehru Place, IGI Airport, Red Fort Metro Station and Kalkaji Mandir.

headline: CID probe, fast-track courts: Jharkhand govt's promises to student protesters; minister says ‘98% demands met’
full_text:
CID probe, fast-track courts: Jharkhand govt's promises to student protesters; minister says ‘98% demands met’
The Jharkhand government on Sunday began fresh talks with the students after three days of inconclusive meetings.
After more than two weeks of protests over alleged irregularities in recruitment exams in the state, the Jharkhand government on Sunday said it “decided to address” the protesters' demands. The state government agreed to the cancellation of the 14th JPSC preliminary exam, the JPSC Backlog 2023, and the JPSC Backlog 2025.
The JMM-Congress government, which has RJD and Left among allies, also extended certain promises to the protesters, including probes by the state police's Crime Investigation Department (CID) in criminal cases, and the setting up of fast-track courts.
The government had on Sunday began fresh talks with the students after three days of inconclusive meetings, with chief minister Hemant Soren assuring them that “justice will be delivered.” Education minister Sudivya Kumar, after a meeting with the aspirants' delegation, said the government would address irregularities associated with the 14th GPSC and the 2023-25 backlog recruitments.
What has the Jharkhand government promised?
📌'Two-pronged approach': CID, ED probe
Addressing reporters, Kumar said the government would address the irregularities, and refer cases to central agencies as and when required. The minister said the government would take a “two-pronged approach”, according to a video released by news agency ANI. He said the CID would probe criminal cases, while the financial implications and related matters would be investigated by the ED.
📌Fast-track courts to be set up
Minister Kumar also said that after the investigations are initiated, fast-track courts would be set up, adding that chargesheets against the accused would be filed within 90 days of the probe's beginning.
📌Experts from IIT, XLRI to work on reforms
The minister said that experts would be called in to work on reforms.
“Regarding necessary reforms, the government stated that a committee comprising experts from IIT-ISM, IIM Ranchi, and XLRI would be formed to guide the process,” Kumar stated.
📌Monitoring committee headed by retired judge
The state government also offered to constitute a committee to oversee the investigation into the irregularities. This proposal was rejected by the students.
“The government offered to oversee the investigation by constituting a monitoring committee headed by a retired judge; however, the students refused to accept this proposal,” Kumar said.
State govt lacks authority to cancel CGL exam, 98 per cent demands met: Jharkhand minister
Minister Sudivya Kumar claimed “98 per cent” of the points raised by the aspirants and students had been agreed to. However, he said that the state government “lacks the authority” to cancel the CGL examination, a demand posed by the protesters. Kumar stated that the examination was being conducted on the directives and oversight of the high court and Supreme Court.
“The government cannot unilaterally cancel an exam conducted under court orders, where results have been published and successful candidates are already employed,” the minister said.
The fresh round of talks on Sunday came after a series of meetings between the government and student groups on Friday night and throughout Saturday, which had not brought about any substantial conclusion.
However, while the state government displayed optimism after the talks, saying they had held a “positive dialogue”, the students have refused to back down unless a CBI probe on the irregularities is announced. The JMM government is apparently reluctant for a CBI probe as the central agency reports to the BJP-led central government in New Delhi.
The protesters said they would march to the Jharkhand assembly on Monday (August 10), and were not ready for any compromise.

headline: Who is Juan Antonio March Pujol? Spain's India ambassador set to be replaced over spending row
full_text:
Who is Juan Antonio March Pujol? Spain's India ambassador set to be replaced over spending row
The move comes as Juan Antonio March faces scrutiny over his handling of cultural events linked to the Spanish embassy.
Spain is set to bring a new ambassador in New Delhi, with diplomat Juan Antonio March Pujol likely to be replaced amid controversy over cultural events allegedly being organised without Madrid's approval and questions about the use of embassy funds.
March, who took charge as Spain's ambassador to India in September 2024, is expected to be replaced within the next few weeks, Spanish digital daily The Objective reported. The Spanish government has already begun seeking an agreement with India for his successor.
Who is Juan Antonio March?
Juan Antonio March is a veteran Spanish diplomat with around 30 years of experience in international relations. He has served in several prominent diplomatic positions, including as Spain's ambassador to the United Nations in Geneva from 2004 to 2007 and ambassador to Russia from 2007 to 2011.
According to London Speaker Bureau, he also served as ambassador to Armenia, Belarus, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan during his diplomatic career. His career has included postings in London, Rome and Mexico, alongside his senior ambassadorial assignments and work on international cooperation and multilateral affairs.
March has held senior positions within Spain's foreign affairs establishment.
He has also held positions in the private sector and international affairs organisations. He was a member of the International Advisory Board of multinational company Abertis from 2015 to 2019 and has been a Partner of Counsel at ECIJA since 2012.
March has written books on international relations and future perspectives, including Power & Future: 20 World Leaders and Tomorrow and Momentum, on the Edge of the New World.
Why is March being replaced?
The move comes as March faces scrutiny over his handling of cultural events linked to the Spanish embassy.
The controversy surfaced earlier this year over plans for concerts in Rajasthan featuring Bengaluru-based STEM Dance Kampni and tenors Joan Laínez and Zhu Huiling. The controversy has since spiralled beyond the proposed concerts, with questions being raised over public funds and procurement.
Spain's Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office received a report in May from a foreign ministry official concerning March. The report said certain details regarding the ambassador, which “if true, could have criminal relevance in the area of public procurement and the management of funds”, The Objective reported.
Opposition lawmakers and UGT, a major Spanish trade union, have called for March's dismissal.
The case also involves Zhu Huiling, who has dual Chinese and German nationality. Zhu received €18,000 from the Spanish embassy in New Delhi last year for concerts organised by March, according to the media report.
Zhu was hired for two concerts in New Delhi and Kathmandu in July, and another in Bhutan in October, when March travelled there to present his credentials.
The matter came to light after the Spanish embassy's cultural attaché sent a report to Madrid about plans to raise funds for concerts in 2026 without informing the foreign ministry.
The hiring of Zhu also stood out because Spanish embassies are obligated to promote the country's culture with Spanish artists or local performers who have artistic ties to Spain, according to The Objective.
Who is replacing March?
Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares has asked the government to begin the process of appointing Alfredo Martínez Serrano, currently Spain's ambassador to Canada, as the country's next envoy to India.
Madrid has sent a communication to the Indian side seeking agrément, or formal approval, for Martínez Serrano's appointment as ambassador in New Delhi, according to the report.

headline: Tamil Nadu may offer childbirth incentives as fertility rate falls below 1.4
full_text:
Tamil Nadu may offer childbirth incentives as fertility rate falls below 1.4
Tamil Nadu Health Minister K G Arunraj said the state may consider incentives for couples to have more children. The remark spotlights concerns over a low fertility rate, an ageing population and changing maternity care patterns.
Tamil Nadu Health Minister KG Arunraj on Sunday said the state government could consider incentives for couples to have more children as it looks at the impact of a falling fertility rate and an ageing population. He said the state’s Total Fertility Rate had fallen below 1.4, well below the replacement level of 2.1, and described the trend as a major public health challenge.
Addressing the mid-year workshop of the Obstetrics and Gynaecological Society of South India, Arunraj said nearly 16 per cent of Tamil Nadu’s population was aged above 60.
Referring to steps taken elsewhere, he said the government could examine measures similar to those in Andhra Pradesh. ‘We were told that in places like Andhra Pradesh, there are government schemes providing incentives for couples to have a third child. Therefore, in the future, there could definitely be such things (here) too,’ he said.
The minister said 99 per cent of childbirths in the state take place in hospitals, but the share of deliveries in government facilities had fallen steadily from 65.8 per cent in 2017-18 to 51 per cent now. He attributed this to private medical colleges offering free maternity care and to the extension of the Muthulakshmi Reddy Maternity Benefit Scheme to private hospitals.
He said the government had recently launched the ‘Thaai Maaman Thangam’ scheme to reduce the financial burden on poor and middle-class families seeking private healthcare.
Arunraj said the health department would carry out a detailed study to find out why deliveries at government hospitals were declining despite the availability of quality care through Comprehensive
Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care centres. Responding to reports of pregnant women facing long queues at outpatient registration counters, he said an Aadhaar card was not mandatory and that no government hospital could deny treatment in its absence. He also referred to a scheme that allows patients to generate an outpatient receipt from home using a smartphone.
On medical education, Arunraj criticised the previous administration for allowing three private medical colleges to get Deemed University status, alleging that this had affected social justice and the 7.5 per cent quota for government school students.
He said the present government had quickly met the National Medical Commission’s requirements and secured 150 additional seats across three government medical colleges this year.
He added that the state’s medical counselling schedule and merit list would be published on August 10. He also warned of strict action against private medical colleges accused of illegally collecting fees beyond the stipulated period, and said a newly formed committee was looking into complaints.
On the political front, Arunraj rejected opposition charges that the ruling government was only renaming schemes started by earlier administrations, and said policy continuity was necessary for good governance.
He also accused the opposition of compromising on social justice and state rights by aligning with the BJP to protect its leaders from past corruption allegations. Reiterating the state’s stand on the Cauvery water dispute, he said the government and Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay would not yield to pressure from the Centre and would stay united in opposing Karnataka’s proposed Mekedatu dam project while protecting Tamil Nadu’s federal rights.
In sum, Arunraj used the event to flag concerns over Tamil Nadu’s falling fertility rate and ageing population, outline steps being considered in maternal healthcare, announce measures in medical education oversight, and restate the government’s position on key political and inter-state issues.

headline: The Bengaluru police on Saturday launched a citywide verification drive to identify foreign nationals allegedly staying illegally in the city, deploying more than 500 personnel under “Operation Mukta”. The drive covered more than 30 locations in the ...
full_text:
The Bengaluru police on Saturday launched a citywide verification drive to identify foreign nationals allegedly staying illegally in the city, deploying more than 500 personnel under “Operation Mukta”. The drive covered more than 30 locations in the Whitefield division and several areas in Electronic City.
In the Whitefield division, teams led by DCP Saidulu Adavath conducted simultaneous checks in Whitefield, Varthur, Kadugodi, Balagere Road, Bellandur, Marathahalli and Mahadevapura. Police verified identity documents, passports, visas and other records of people residing in the areas.
Whitefield DCP Saidulu Adavath said the operation was being conducted across Bengaluru on the directions of the city police commissioner and was part of a continuous exercise.
“We have carried out similar operations in the past and deported foreign nationals found staying illegally. If we find anyone without valid documents, their details will be forwarded to the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO). Based on the verification report, legal proceedings for deportation will be initiated,” he said.
Police sources said around 40 suspicious people were taken into custody for verification in the Whitefield division, while four were identified as Bangladeshi nationals based on documents recovered from them. Verification of the others is continuing.
“If we find an identity card or any other document indicating that they are from another country, we will write to the FRRO. Once we obtain the deportation order, we will follow the legal procedure and deport them to their respective countries,” the DCP said.
The searches also covered makeshift settlements where people from Bangladesh, West Bengal, Assam, Bihar and Nepal were found residing. Residents were asked to produce identity and citizenship documents, including Aadhaar cards and voter IDs. Those unable to provide documents or found suspicious were taken to police stations for further questioning.
At one location, police found around 150 sheds, while another settlement had more than 100 sheds. Police sources said the sheds were allegedly being rented out for around ₹2,000 to ₹3,000 each, and the role of landowners and others facilitating such accommodation was also being examined.
Asked about landowners, Adavath said, “We will look into that as well. As you know, in many places, local people construct these sheds and provide them on rent. There are people working as construction labourers here, including those who have come from different states and different districts within Karnataka. Such construction labourers stay in these sheds.”
According to police sources, several of those found in the settlements appeared to be working as construction labourers, domestic help, drivers and delivery personnel.
The DCP also warned property owners against renting premises without verifying tenants’ credentials. “Owners who provide houses or accommodation to illegal immigrants without verifying their documents will also face legal action. We have already registered 10 such cases in the Whitefield division,” he said.
The Electronic City division also reported significant findings. Police detained 1,909 suspected persons and examined their nationality and identity documents. Detailed verification of passports, visas and other records led to the detection of 15 Bangladeshi nationals allegedly staying illegally.
Of the 15, eight were detected within Begur police station limits and seven under Parappana Agrahara police station limits. They have been taken into custody for further legal proceedings.
Electronic City DCP Narayan said 23 special teams comprising 295 police officers and personnel were deployed for the operation. The teams searched 29 identified locations, including construction sites, temporary shelters and other suspected hideouts.
“We have so far identified 15 Bangladeshi nationals during the verification. An official report is being submitted to the FRRO, following which further action will be taken according to the prescribed procedure,” Narayan said.
State home minister Priyank Kharge said the Karnataka government was conducting a serious and continuous search for illegal immigrants, irrespective of their country of origin, and had already detected around 1,000 such migrants over the past three months.
“Illegal immigrants could be from Bangladesh, Africa or any other country. We are conducting a strict and serious search. There will be no compromise on this issue. Among immigrants many of them are coming from northern India,” Kharge said.
He said the state government was in regular touch with the Border Security Force (BSF) and Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) officials. “This cannot be an operation for one week and then stopped. It has to be a continuous exercise. If necessary, we will constitute a special team to monitor the situation,” he said.
Kharge pointed out that Karnataka does not share an international border with Bangladesh, Nepal or any other country. “If people from other countries are entering Karnataka despite the state having no international border, the question is where they are coming from and how they are reaching here,” he said.
He also sought greater assistance from the Centre, saying border security was primarily a Central government responsibility. “If people are travelling this far, it raises questions about the effectiveness of border and interstate checks,” he said.
The drive was part of a continuing exercise to identify illegal immigrants from different countries and initiate deportation proceedings wherever required.
The operation comes amid a recent Karnataka High Court intervention in a case involving a doctor who identified a Bangladeshi national allegedly residing illegally in Bengaluru. Police had registered a case against the doctor on the complaint of the migrant. The High Court stayed further investigation in the criminal cases registered against the doctor-activist.
Justice M Nagaprasanna, who heard the case, questioned the police action and observed that the system should not support illegal immigration by prosecuting those who report it.
