headline: 'Shoot first, ask questions later' won't work in law: Bombay HC raps Maharashtra FDA
full_text:
'Shoot first, ask questions later' won't work in law: Bombay HC raps Maharashtra FDA
A bench of Acting Chief Justice RV Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad was hearing a petition filed by Cadila challenging the FDA's recent directives to seize stocks and halt the sale and distribution of several of its medicines.
The Bombay High Court on Tuesday granted relief to Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd and rebuked the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) over its stop-sale orders against the drugmaker, saying that “shooting first and asking questions later” may be “a rule of the Wild West but does not apply in law”.
Following the court’s sharp observations, the Maharashtra FDA agreed to revoke its existing stop-sale orders against Cadila and assured the bench that it would follow due process before taking any fresh action. The FDA is headed by Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe.
A bench of Acting Chief Justice RV Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad was hearing a petition filed by Cadila challenging the FDA’s directives to seize stocks and halt the sale and distribution of several of its medicines.
The bench criticised what it viewed as the FDA’s trigger-happy approach to regulatory action. “Shooting first and asking questions later is a rule of the Wild West which does not apply in the arena of law,” the court observed.
It said such an approach could not be followed in the legal and regulatory system. “Even when it comes to hotels, you shoot first, then ask questions. The same is happening in this case,” the court said.
The FDA had seized stocks and stopped the sale and distribution of several Cadila medicines. Cadila’s lawyer, senior advocate Birendra Saraf, sought cancellation of the orders, arguing that they had caused substantial financial losses to the pharmaceutical company.
The High Court's criticism of the FDA came after weeks of high-profile inspections by the regulator, which has suspended the licences of nearly 100 food establishments across Mumbai and elsewhere in Maharashtra over hygiene and food safety violations.
Mundhe has emerged as the public face of the crackdown, drawing praise from consumers while facing criticism from sections of the hospitality industry.
The High Court said it had no doubt about the FDA’s statutory powers but questioned the manner in which they were exercised. “We have no doubts about your powers. You only display your powers, but the problem is you have the power to use the sword, but you use it to kill a mosquito,” ACJ Ghuge told FDA lawyer Neha Bhide.
The bench stressed that the issue was not whether the regulator had the authority to act, but whether it exercised that power with adequate propriety.
WHAT FDA SAID
The FDA defended its action by alleging that some Cadila products had similar branding despite containing different active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).
The High Court, however, said its primary concern was not the company’s financial losses but the impact of the stop-sale orders on patients. “The drug was not sold for 20 days. We are not concerned with the loss of Senior Advocate Saraf’s client,” ACJ Ghuge observed.
“We are concerned that the drug was not available to the patients for 20 days, effectively 32 days till today,” he added.
According to the FDA, the similarity in branding could create a serious risk of medication errors if consumers or healthcare providers confused one medicine with another.
While acknowledging the FDA’s statutory mandate to regulate medicines and protect public health, the court questioned whether the manner in which its powers were exercised was proportionate.
The bench also warned that the regulator could face heavy costs in future cases if similar orders continued to be passed without following due process.
MAHARASHTRA FDA TO REVOKE CADILA STOP-SALE ORDERS
Following the court’s observations, the Maharashtra FDA agreed to revoke the existing stop-sale orders against Cadila. The regulator also assured the bench that it would follow the statutory procedure before taking any fresh action.
This would include issuing fresh show-cause notices to Cadila, giving the company adequate time to submit written responses to the alleged violations and conducting proper hearings before passing any final orders.
The court’s intervention came after it questioned the manner in which the FDA had exercised its regulatory powers, while stressing that protecting public health must go hand in hand with following due process.
With the stop-sale orders being revoked, Cadila will get an opportunity to respond to the allegations before the regulator takes any fresh decision.

17 children escape narrowly as school bus catches fire in Rajasthan’s Jaisalmer
Police said the bus driver immediately stopped the bus and evacuated all the children safely before the flames engulfed the vehicle and burnt it completely
Seventeen children had a narrow escape on Tuesday after the school bus they were travelling in caught fire near Dhauwa village in Rajasthan’s Jaisalmer. Police said the bus driver immediately stopped the bus and evacuated all the children safely before the flames engulfed the vehicle and burnt it completely. No one was injured. Bags, books and other belongings kept inside the bus were destroyed.
Police said three fire tenders were rushed to the spot. Preliminary investigation suggested that a short circuit in the bus wiring may have caused the fire.
Mahendra Kumar Sirvi, a local police officer, said the bus was carrying children from Pithla village to a private school, around 12 km away. When the bus reached near Dhauwa, its front wheel suddenly hit a pothole. A short circuit reportedly followed, after which smoke began emerging from the engine and the bus caught fire. Locals rushed to the spot and helped move the children to a safe distance from the burning bus.
On October 14 last year, a private sleeper bus travelling from Jaisalmer to Jodhpur caught fire, leaving 19 passengers dead on the spot. One more person died while being taken to Jodhpur. The death toll later rose to 26, with the remaining victims succumbing to their injuries during treatment. The tragedy raised concerns over fire safety and emergency preparedness in buses.

headline: MEA hits back at Chinese criticism over naming of 27 Arunachal sites: ‘Indisputable reality’
full_text:
MEA hits back at Chinese criticism over naming of 27 Arunachal sites: ‘Indisputable reality’
Arunachal is an inalienable and integral part of India and this is a fact which is self-evident, India said.
The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Tuesday said nothing can change the “indisputable reality” that Arunachal Pradesh is an inalienable and integral part of India, days after China termed India’s move to identify 27 places and features in the northeastern state by their standard names as “null and void”.
"Arunachal is an inalienable and integral part of India and this is a fact which is self-evident. At the same time, let me also underline that nothing can change this indisputable reality,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told a press briefing.
The spokesperson made the remarks in response to China’s condemnation of the Indian government’s move to formally identify 27 places and features in the northeastern state by their standard names on the official Indian map.
On Friday, India issued standard names for 27 places and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh located along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), a move officials described as a riposte to China’s efforts to rename dozens of locations in the Indian state in recent years. This is the first time India has issued the names on a cartographic map.
Among the places included in the list is the border village of Longju, which has been controlled by China since 1959 but is within the Indian claim line, they added. The move is aimed at reinforcing India’s absolute sovereign and legal jurisdiction over these territories.
Also Read | Renaming places in Arunachal is part of China's cultural expansion
An official familiar with the development said: “There has been a lot of ambiguity regarding the maps. China uses this to give fictitious names to Arunachal Pradesh’s territories, which are part of sovereign India.
He added: “Putting these 27 locations on the Survey of India map provides clarity, makes our claim status strong and strengthens the official documentation of geographical features.”
China termed the move “illegal, null and void”. "China does not recognise the so-called 'Arunachal Pradesh' illegally set up by India," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun on Monday said while answering a question on India's recent announcement.
"India's move of attempting to replace names long been used by China with its so-called 'standard names' is illegal, null and void," he said in a reply posted on the official website of the Foreign Ministry. "Still less will it change the fact that Zangnan region belongs to China," he added.

headline: Harbhajan Singh shares second Punjab drugs video, AAP alleges smear
full_text:
Harbhajan Singh shares second Punjab drugs video, AAP alleges smear
The former cricketer, who quit the AAP and joined the BJP in April, said the issue was not about targeting any individual but about making Punjab drug-free.
BJP Rajya Sabha MP Harbhajan Singh on Tuesday shared another video purportedly showing men standing motionless and asked the AAP government in Punjab to address the state’s drug problem, a day after he drew criticism for posting a clip that Punjab Police said was from Rajasthan.
Singh, the former cricketer who quit the AAP and joined the BJP in April, said the issue was not about targeting any individual but about making Punjab drug-free.
AAP leaders, including Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema, accused him of sharing misleading content to defame the state, while Punjab Police again urged social media users to verify facts before posting such material.
In the video shared on Tuesday, Singh posted a compilation of separate clips in which a few men could be seen standing motionless.
He asked the AAP government, "Are these also pictures from Rajasthan? The issue is Punjab’s drug problem." He added, "Your paid troll won’t be able to hide this issue. Work will have to be done on this. Running away from responsibilities will not solve the problem."
Singh also said, "This is not about targeting any particular individual. For anyone in Punjab and across the entire country who consumes narcotic substances, whatever efforts are made to free them from addiction should be carried out. Instead of pulling each other down, the Punjab government should work on how to make Punjab drug-free."
Speaking to reporters in Delhi, he said the focus should be on whether Punjab had become drug-free. "Has Punjab become drug-free? If so, then speak about it. If Punjab is to be made drug-free then focus on the work you are doing towards it, rather than targeting any other individual," he said.
He further said, "If I do not speak on Punjab’s issues, then I feel that there is no point being here. I feel that these are serious issues concerning Punjab and the government should work on them."
Singh added that he would continue to raise issues linked to Punjab’s welfare, its youth, making the state drug-free and promoting sports.
The fresh exchange came a day after Singh shared a video clip of two apparently intoxicated men and said Punjab’s youth deserved better.
The clip showed two men standing in a strange, motionless state on a road and was widely circulated on social media, with several users claiming they were under the influence of a "zombie drug".
Sharing the clip on X, Singh had said, "Very sad to see the situation of Punjab." He added, "Punjab and its youth deserve better. This issue needs honesty, accountability, and urgent action - not denial."
He also wrote, "What have the governments done to Punjab and its Punjabi youth? Where have they brought Punjab to? The Punjab that was once known for its high spirits, courage and bravery, today that same Punjab’s youth has been engulfed by drugs. There is still time... save my Punjab."
AAP leaders and Punjab Police said the first video was from Sri Ganganagar in Rajasthan and had no link with Punjab. AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal accused BJP leaders of spreading falsehoods and asked, "Many BJP people spread this lie together yesterday. Did the order come from the PMO? Does the PMO spread lies in the country?"
Cheema accused Singh of "peddling BJP’s lies" and demanded an apology. He said that while Singh was with the AAP, he had never raised issues concerning Punjab’s youth in Parliament and had remained "mum".
"Today he is releasing BJP’s fake videos to defame Punjab’s youth," Cheema alleged. Asked whether any action would be taken against Singh, he said a legal team was examining the matter and legal action would also be taken against him.
Cheema said Singh had been sent to the Rajya Sabha by the AAP to represent Punjab’s interests and work for the state’s youth, but was now amplifying BJP propaganda.
"Harbhajan Singh should have used his platform to encourage Punjab’s youngsters to take up sports and raise issues concerning their future, rather than sharing misleading content that tarnishes the image of Punjab," he said.
Referring to the first video, Cheema said Punjab Police had traced it to Sri Ganganagar in BJP-ruled Rajasthan. "Instead of checking the facts, the BJP’s IT machinery is picking up videos from other states and presenting them as incidents from Punjab to malign our state and its youth," he alleged.
Cheema also attacked the BJP over Punjab’s drug problem and alleged that the menace had intensified during the 10 years of the SAD-BJP government from 2007 to 2017.
He said terms such as "chitta" and "smack" became widely associated with Punjab during that period, with countless young lives destroyed by addiction. He added that the AAP government was strengthening sports infrastructure to give youngsters positive alternatives.
Punjab minister Baljit Kaur also criticised Singh and said he had shared a Rajasthan video while falsely presenting it as one from Punjab.
"Look at the desperation to please his political bosses. He is sharing a video from Rajasthan and lying that it is from Punjab," she said in a post on X. She added, "You will do anything for 'BJP ki dalali', even if it means ruining Punjab’s image. The people of Punjab will never forgive you for this."
Punjab Police, which tagged Singh in its post, also said the video was from Rajasthan. In a post on X, it said, "The video being circulated is from Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan – not Punjab. We urge users and social media accounts to verify the facts and location before posting misleading content or tagging Punjab Police. Responsible sharing matters."
The row has now widened, with Singh insisting that Punjab’s drug problem must be addressed and the AAP government accusing him of using misleading videos to target the state.

headline: CAG detects irregularities in PMAY-G, Jal Jeevan Mission, MGNREGA implementation in Jharkhand
full_text:
CAG detects irregularities in PMAY-G, Jal Jeevan Mission, MGNREGA implementation in Jharkhand
Over 6.32 lakh eligible households remained uncovered under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) due to deficient planning.
Major irregularities were detected in the performance audit of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin), Jal Jeevan Mission and MGNREGA in Jharkhand, according to the latest CAG reports tabled in the Assembly on Tuesday.
Over 6.32 lakh eligible households remained uncovered under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) due to deficient planning.
"The state identified 22.34 lakh eligible households by November 2022 under the scheme. However, inaccuracies in the priority list, inability of the state to utilise the targets and a two-year delay in finalising Awaas beneficiaries resulted in the Centre allocating only 16.02 lakh houses. As a consequence, 6.32 lakh eligible households could not be covered under the scheme," the report on implementation of PMAY-G in Jharkhand said.
The state sanctioned 15,92,124 houses from 2016 to 2024 and constructed 15,62,249 houses as of January 2025, it added.
Also Read | CAG report flags irregularities in NPA payment, govt doctors paid above prescribed maximum limit in UP
"Financial management under the scheme was inadequate. Total expenditure under PMAY-G in the state was ₹14,113 crore against the total available funds of ₹20,199.98 crore with funding utilisation ranging between 55 and 83 per cent from 2019 to 2024," the report said.
The report on implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) said that the "state government approved 98,067 schemes under JJM at an estimated cost of ₹24,360 crore. Of these, 97,535 schemes had been taken up for execution at an agreed cost of ₹24,665.29 crore".
"However, only 27,249 schemes could be completed as of December 2024," the report stated.
There were 52,27,214 rural households in Jharkhand when the scheme was launched in August 2019. Of these, 3,45,165 households had already been covered with tap water connections.
Also Read | BJP's Pravesh Verma says CAG report flagged ₹3,500 crore-worth irregularities under AAP government
"As of March 2025, as many as 34,31,115 (55 per cent) out of 62,53,471 households had been provided with functional household tap connections (FHTC). The FHTC coverage in the state was, however, below the national coverage of 80 per cent," the report added.
A discrepancy between the NREGASoft portal data and the certified financial accounts maintained by the department was detected in the report on implementation of MGNREGA.
Besides, wages to unskilled labour amounting to ₹321.84 crore for the period from 2019-20 to 2023-24 were outstanding, it added.
Also Read | CAG raises concerns over declining capex in Delhi
"Out of total 1,02,68,484 works proposed to be executed during 2019-24, only 27,96,044 (27 per cent) were completed and 50,21,492 (49 per cent) were lying incomplete as of March 2024 after incurring an expenditure of ₹2,633 crore," the report added.

headline: Prakash Raj claims name dropped in Bengaluru voters' list after SIR: 'Kya kya kaagaz dikhana padega'

Prakash Raj claims name dropped in Bengaluru voters' list after SIR: 'Kya kya kaagaz dikhana padega'

Actor Prakash Raj claimed that his name has been deleted from the Bengaluru electoral roll amid the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Karnataka.
In a video shared on X, Raj called the development a “joke” and said he was born and raised in the constituency, where he attended school and college and worked in theatre.
“I am one of the 65 lakh voters whose vote right has been deleted from Bangalore constituency after SIR. Nice joke, no?” he said, questioning what documents he would now need to submit to get his name back. “Kya kya kaagaz dikhana padega?” he said.
Raj, who had also contested the Lok Sabha election in 2019 from the Bengaluru Central Lok Sabha constituency, said he would find out the process to get his voter ID back. “Game on. Let me see what is the process I have to go through to get back my voter ID is,” he said.

He further questioned whether authorities could stop citizens from exercising their political power, saying, “You can use your powers to deny a few of the citizens the right to vote who may not elect you. But can you stop us, my dear friend, from our power of bringing you down?”
Raj on protest in Jharkhand
Raj earlier reacted to the use of force against protesting students marching towards the Jharkhand legislative assembly in Ranchi on Monday.
Prakash took to his X account and reposted a video allegedly taken from the protest site, which showed visuals where tear gas and lathi charge were used to disperse students. In the caption, the actor wrote, “Why .. Why .. Why. This brutality will not work anymore.. it will only bring the arrogant power down.”
Karnataka SIR
The publication of Karnataka’s draft electoral roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has been deferred to August 24, and the final electoral roll will now be published on October 27, according to a revised schedule issued by the Chief Electoral Officer’s office.
The revised schedule follows an August 7 letter from the Election Commission of India and retains October 1, 2026, as the qualifying date for the electoral roll revision.

headline: Wife of liquor chain owner held for assaulting domestic help at Gurugram's Camellias
full_text:
Wife of liquor chain owner held for assaulting domestic help at Gurugram's Camellias
The matter came to light after a video of the incident, reportedly shot by an occupant of an adjacent flat in Camellias, was widely shared on social media.
A 52-year-old woman – a resident of the upscale DLF Camellias high-rises in Gurugram – was arrested on Monday for allegedly assaulting her 22-year-old house help and confining her at the residence, police said.
The matter came to light after a 90-second video of the incident, reportedly shot by an occupant of an adjacent flat, was widely shared on social media.
Police took suo motu action based on the video and registered a first information report (FIR) against an unnamed woman early on Monday at Sushant Lok police station under Sections 115 (voluntarily causing hurt) and 127(2) (wrongful confinement) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
HT has accessed a copy of the FIR.
Who is the accused
“The accused is a housewife, and her husband is the proprietor of a chain of liquor outlets,” a police officer aware of the details of the case said, adding that the house help is a Nepal national.
“In the video, the employer is seen assaulting the house help repeatedly, pulling her by hair, choking her, and shoving her inside the kitchen which was visible through a glass window,” the officer said. The officer added the police are examining if such incidents took place in the past.
HT could not independently verify the authenticity of the video
“The accused has been identified as Ruchira Sachdeva (aged 52), a resident of Camellias Apartments, Sector 42, Gurugram,” said Sandeep Turan, public relations officer of Gurugram police.
Kumar added that Sachdev told police that the incident occurred on the night of July 24. “It was a work-related dispute over which the woman assaulted the 22-year-old. Following the incident, the house help returned to Nepal on July 27,” Turan said.
HT made multiple attempts to reach out to the family of the accused, but they did not respond.
According to investigators familiar with the case, who asked not to be identified, the couple also presented to police with a document signed by the victim requesting that no legal action be taken against her employers.
Police said it would be clear only after investigation whether the victim signed the document willingly or was coerced.
Woman banned from leaving house, using phone
Investigators also said it had emerged that the woman was not allowed to use a phone or leave the house. These allegations are now being investigated, they added.
Turan said there was strong preliminary evidence against Sachdeva as her face was clearly visible in the video, which also helped police establish her identity when police team reached Camellias for investigation.
A police team approached her on Monday and arrested her after questioning her at the station.
Police have the victim’s details and will contact her to record her statement, Turan said.
Afterwards, it will be clear if the house help was repeatedly assaulted or only once and if she willingly signed the document urging no legal action against her employer, officers, associated with the investigation told HT.

headline: UP temples reverberate with 'Har Har Mahadev' as devotees throng shrines on Sawan Monday
full_text:
UP temples reverberate with 'Har Har Mahadev' as devotees throng shrines on Sawan Monday
Lucknow, Temples across Uttar Pradesh reverberated with chants of 'Har Har Mahadev' and 'Bam Bam Bhole' as large numbers of devotees and kanwariyas thronged Shiva shrines on the second Monday of the holy month of Sawan, officials said.

In Varanasi, devotees began arriving at the Kashi Vishwanath temple since Sunday night. Kanwariyas took a holy dip in the Ganga, collected water and proceeded towards the temple in queues.
The temple premises echoed with bells, drums and chants as devotees offered milk, curd, honey, bel leaves and other traditional offerings to Lord Shiva.
In Prayagraj, devotees queued up at the major Shiva temples, including the Mankameshwar temple, after taking a dip at the Sangam.
Kanwariyas in saffron carrying decorated kanwars were seen chanting 'Jai Bholenath', the statement said.
In Ayodhya, large crowds gathered at temples, including Nageshwarnath, Kshireswarnath, Panchmukhi Mahadev and Jharkhandeshwarnath.
The devotees also thronged the Ram Janmabhoomi and Hanumangarhi areas. After bathing in the Saryu, many offered Ganga water at the Nageshwarnath temple.
The Kanwar pilgrimage also remained in full swing across the state, with devotees travelling on foot, bicycles and decorated vehicles.

headline: The special investigation team (SIT) inquiring into the alleged ₹15.85-crore microfinance scam involving Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam general secretary Vellapally Natesan has filed final reports in 17 cases.
full_text:
The special investigation team (SIT) inquiring into the alleged ₹15.85-crore microfinance scam involving Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam general secretary Vellapally Natesan has filed final reports in 17 cases.

The committee is led by former Supreme Court judge Justice Prakash Prabhakar Naolekar (retd.), who is not part of the visit.
Also Read | Demography panel to study population changes post 2011 Census, prepares detailed questionnaire for States
The committee is likely to meet civil society members on Tuesday and visit settlements along the Pakistan border in Kathua and Samba districts over the next two days. Organisations that have received invitation from the panel include Brahmin Sabha; Team Jammu, which works on anti-narcotics programmes; Pannun Kashmir, an organisation of displaced Kashmiri Pandits; Jammu State Morcha; Transporters Association; and Private Schools Association. The panel is meeting groups shortlisted by the district administration, an official said.
The panel members are likely to visit a detention centre in Hiranagar where around 450 Rohingyas are lodged. As per the Ministry’s estimate in 2017, around 13,000 Rohingyas have settled in Jammu.
Also Read | Demography panel chief says subject new to him, will consult experts
Rohingyas are an ethnic group from Myanmar, mostly Muslims, who are based in the Rakhine province of West Myanmar. The country has not granted them full citizenship and they are classified as “resident foreigners” or as “associate citizens”. They left Myanmar in large numbers in two distinct waves – first in 2012 and again in 2017.
Census Commissioner Mritunjay Kumar Narayan, former IAS officer Durga Shanker Mishra who served as the Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary, former IPS officer Balaji Srivastava who retired as Director General Bureau of Police Research and Development, and Shamika Ravi, who is part of the Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council, are members of the vising committee. The Joint Secretary (Foreigners-I), Home Ministry, is the Member Secretary of the panel.

Last year, on Independence Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had announced the High-Powered Demography Mission. On May 26, the Home Ministry constituted the committee to study demographic changes arising from illegal immigration and other reasons, and to suggest measures to deal with these changes.
The Minsitry’s notification said that the panel, which has to submit its report in the next one year, will also recommend “a well-organised and permanent operational system for the legal, fair and time bound identification, detention, and deportation of illegal immigrants already residing in the country.”

headline: The aircraft plunged 300ft, injuring many on board
full_text:
The aircraft plunged 300ft, injuring many on board
NEW DELHI: European aerospace major Airbus and France's Bureau of Enquiry and Analysis for Civil Aviation Safety will join the probe to establish what caused the Air India A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi with 145 aboard to suddenly lose altitude by about 300ft last week, injuring many on board.Led by India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), the investigation is examining the twin aspects of the aircraft's mechanical issues and pilot behaviour. Everyone TOI spoke to said what happened mid-flight was indeed "a close shave". Luckily, the aircraft (AI 2379) landed safely at its destination, but 17 people had to be hospitalised.The captain's psychoactive substance screening test was not negative, and the confirmatory test result is not yet officially known. His behaviour on board is under the scanner. "One of the pilots fell in the cockpit and had to be assisted by cabin crew to get back on his seat," said a source. The flight data recorder will reveal mechanical failures, if any, and the cockpit voice recorder will reveal what transpired on the flight deck."Airbus is sending its team to India, and they will reach by Wednesday to inspect the aircraft and work with Air India and AAIB.
Being a serious incident, the investigator of the original equipment manufacturer's country (France in this case) is also coming," said a source. An Airbus official said it is "providing technical assistance to the investigating authorities. We are actively supporting the airline and will provide further information as it becomes available".Industry executives said the A320 (VT-EXO) may have suffered a triple hydraulic failure for a few seconds, which is rare. This system uses a fluid under pressure to drive machinery or move mechanical components to power critical elements like wheel brakes, nose wheel steering, landing gear retraction/extension and flight control surfaces. It is also learnt the autopilot became disengaged during that tumultuous time for a few seconds, and the aircraft even got a stall warning.
A pilot then steadied the aircraft by pushing the nose down.AI said it can't "comment on any findings or observations related to the investigation" as it "is being conducted by AAIB" and that the airline "will continue to extend our full cooperation to authorities as required". The flight data recorder will reveal the timestamps of the sequence of events - whether the alleged transient hydraulic failure occurred because of the aircraft's rapid descent or whether the aircraft first entered an air pocket and subsequent turbulence caused hydraulic failure.

headline: Three-day Bengaluru hotel checks seize 640 kg meat, 276 kg rotten vegetables
full_text:
Three-day Bengaluru hotel checks seize 640 kg meat, 276 kg rotten vegetables
Karnataka's food safety department inspected 60 Bengaluru hotels over three days using 30 teams, collecting 77 samples. Officials seized 640 kg of meat, 276 kg of rotten vegetables and other expired food, while several kitchens faced enforcement action over serious safety violations.
Karnataka food safety officials have intensified their crackdown on food safety violations in Bengaluru, inspecting 60 hotels and collecting 77 food samples during a three-day special drive from August 7 to 9.
The Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration deployed 30 teams to inspect 3-star and 5-star hotels, along with restaurants, food storage facilities and warehouses supplying major establishments.
The inspections uncovered several violations, including expired food products, mislabelling, unhygienic food handling, improper meat storage and inadequate segregation of vegetarian and non-vegetarian items.
Officials seized 640 kg of mutton, chicken and fish, 276 kg of rotten or mould-affected vegetables, 45 litres of expired milk and curd, 12 kg of expired bakery products, 67 kg of mislabelled or expired cereals and other food products, and 49 litres of used or non-compliant cooking oil.
The kitchen at Skyye Lounge in UB City was ordered shut after officials found rotten chicken and beef, with fungus reportedly growing on the meat. Expired milk and curd were also found. Officials disposed of 51 kg of food articles, including 45 kg of rotten meat and 6 kg of vegetable cutlets, along with 15 litres of used cooking oil.
Enforcement action was also taken at Hotel Sky, UB City, and Pegs & Bottles, while several other eateries faced seizure and disposal of food products.
At Royal Chain Hotel, officials seized 50 kg of duck and 5 kg of fish. Madras Kitchen and Tescon Hotel had 5 kg each of green peas and mushrooms seized, respectively. At Senchez Hotel, 3 kg of fish was seized and another 7 kg of cake, potatoes and tacos was discarded.
The department also inspected food storage and distribution centres operated by Coldman Logistics and Radhakrishna Foodland, which supply food products to hotels and caterers across Bengaluru. Around 70 kg of soy sauce and other sauces nearing expiry were seized, while about 10 litres of beverages nearing their expiry dates were also confiscated.
Special inspections were additionally conducted at KFC, McDonald's and Subway outlets and their supplying warehouses. At McDonald's Brigade Road, officials found Magnesium Sulfite being used in connection with the treatment of used frying oil. A notice has been issued and further legal action is expected.
Officials collected five meat samples and 13 other food samples from the inspected facilities and sent them for laboratory analysis.
The inspections formed part of a wider food safety drive across Bengaluru Urban district and BBMP zones. The department said legal action would be initiated against food business operators found violating food safety and quality requirements under the Food Safety and Standards Act.

headline: Sukhbir Singh Badal challenges Kejriwal to debate Punjab paper leaks and job scams
full_text:
Sukhbir Singh Badal challenges Kejriwal to debate Punjab paper leaks and job scams
Sukhbir Singh Badal challenged Arvind Kejriwal to an open debate on alleged paper leaks and recruitment scams in Punjab. He coupled the attack with demands for resignations, a CBI probe and fresh promises on jobs and education.
Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Monday challenged Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal to an open debate over alleged paper leaks and recruitment scams in Punjab, accusing the state government of failing to hold anyone accountable.
Addressing a protest at Government Rajindra College in Bathinda as part of the Students Organisation of India’s (SOI) ‘Bhavikh Bachao Morcha’, Badal demanded the immediate resignation of Punjab ministers Harjot Bains and Balbir Singh and a CBI probe into 10 alleged paper leak cases.
Badal claimed that the examination leaks had affected more than 10 lakh students across Punjab and questioned why no senior official or minister had resigned over the issue.
BADAL CHALLENGES KEJRIWAL OVER STUDENT PROTESTS
Taking aim at Kejriwal, Badal questioned why the AAP leader had protested for students in Delhi but had not held a similar demonstration for students in Punjab.
“Are they not your children? Why are you betraying Punjabi students like this?” Badal asked.
He challenged Kejriwal to an open debate at any university in Punjab, saying he would present what he described as facts and figures on alleged paper leaks, recruitment of candidates from outside the state and the exclusion of Punjabi youth from government employment.
BADAL ALLEGES RECRUITMENT OF OUTSIDERS
Badal alleged that more than half of the 60,000 jobs claimed to have been provided by the AAP government had gone to candidates from outside Punjab.
He cited recruitment figures to allege that 24 candidates from Haryana and 12 from Rajasthan were appointed among 68 Veterinary Inspectors. He also claimed that 600 candidates from Haryana and 100 from Rajasthan were recruited for 2,100 Lineman posts.
Badal further alleged that 60% of newly created posts in the Punjab Health Systems Corporation had gone to candidates from outside the state.
100% GOVERNMENT JOBS FOR PUNJABIS
Badal announced that the SAD would reserve 100% of government jobs in Punjab for Punjabis if the party returned to power in 2027.
He said the previous SAD government had introduced legislation aimed at securing jobs for Punjabis, but alleged that the AAP government had subsequently overturned it.
“We will bring back legislation to secure jobs in Punjab for Punjabis,” Badal said.
He also announced that a future SAD government would provide industrial incentives only to companies that employ at least 75% Punjabis.
EDUCATION REFORMS AND INTEREST-FREE LOANS
Badal said the SAD would amend the education law to reserve 50% of seats in private universities for poor Punjabi students, with the government bearing half of their fees.
He said the same formula would be extended to medical and veterinary colleges.
Badal also promised to establish a World Skill University in Punjab to train young people in partnership with major companies and facilitate their employment.
He further announced Rs 10 lakh interest-free loans for young people seeking to start their own businesses.
STUDENT LEADERS DEMAND PROBE
Student leaders at the protest demanded an investigation into the alleged financial transactions linked to the Pharmacy paper leak.
SOI leaders claimed that Rs 13 lakh to Rs 15 lakh had changed hands in connection with the alleged leak and sought a probe into the matter.
Other student leaders demanded free education for girls in Punjab and accused the AAP leadership of compromising the interests of students.
Badal said the SAD would continue its agitation until those responsible for the alleged irregularities were held accountable and the ministers facing demands for resignation stepped down.

headline: Anthropic Software, a Belagavi-based tech firm, has cautioned the State and Union governments against entering into formal engagements with California-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic PBC until an ongoing legal dispute over the use of ...
full_text:
Anthropic Software, a Belagavi-based tech firm, has cautioned the State and Union governments against entering into formal engagements with California-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic PBC until an ongoing legal dispute over the use of the “Anthropic” brand name is resolved, citing what it describes as “serious risks arising from brand confusion, email misrouting and potential exposure of confidential information.”
Anthropic Software Pvt. Ltd., founded in 2017 in Belagavi, operates through the domain anthropic.in, while Anthropic PBC uses anthropic.com.
Mohammad Ayyaz Mulla, founder and managing director of Anthropic Software, told The Hindu that the similarity in the business name and domains has led to increasing confusion among customers and organisations in India and overseas, particularly after the U.S. company announced its entry into India.
He said his company had received over 700 emails over the past four months that were intended for its namesake in the U.S. and vice versa. He said the concern went beyond missed business enquiries because some of these misdirected communications contained sensitive information.
“Some of the emails have come from government departments, including the police, judiciary and other financially and operationally sensitive departments,” he cautioned, adding that his company had not examined the contents of such emails but considered their misdirection itself a potential security concern.
According to Mr. Mulla, his company has developed an automated email misrouting system to track such messages with minimal human intervention. When an email is identified as being intended for Anthropic PBC, the system automatically alerts and routes it to the designated leadership and data-protection officials, while maintaining logs and following what the company describes as data-minimisation principles. More than 700 such emails have reportedly been redirected through this system, he claimed. “We have also put a clarification on our website stating that the two entities are separate,” Mr Mulla added.
He said the issue had acquired greater significance with the Karnataka government considering engagements involving the U.S.-based Anthropic entity. He added that his company had also urged the State government to take note of the existing brand confusion and potential data-security implications before proceeding with initiatives involving multiple government departments.
“We are urging the government to take note of this. Unless the court verdict comes and these issues are sorted out, the government should pause business proposals with American Anthropic,” Mr Mulla cautioned, arguing that wider government adoption could magnify the consequences of any existing data-security or identification problems.
The Belagavi company has also raised the issue before Indian and U.S. regulatory and cybersecurity agencies. Mr. Mulla said complaints had been submitted to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the U.S. Federal Trade Commission and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, besides India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and CERT-In. The company has asked regulators, among other things, to consider the material risks associated with brand confusion and email misrouting in the context of the U.S. company’s proposed public offering.

9 of family killed in Madhya Pradesh's Rajgarh as flooded drain sweeps van away
Chief minister Mohan Yadav announced a compensation of ₹4 lakh to the families of each of the deceased.
Nine members of a family, including four children, were killed after the vehicle they were travelling in was swept away while crossing a flooded drain in Madhya Pradesh’s Rajgarh district on Monday, police said, adding that two of the passengers were rescued by local residents.
Chief minister Mohan Yadav announced a compensation of ₹4 lakh to the families of each of the deceased.
“...My condolences go out to the bereaved families. Instructions have been issued to provide financial assistance,” the CM said.
According to police, the incident took place in Padana town around 9 am when the Eco van was travelling from Dewas to Kadnavad village in Sarangpur tehsil for a religious visit. The victims include four women, a man and four children, all residents of Satwas village in Dewas, while the two rescued men were admitted to Sarangpur hospital.
“As the vehicle reached the Padana bypass, water from the swollen Jhiri drain had spilled over the road. Despite repeated warnings from locals, the driver tried to cross. The strong current swept the van into the drain,” said Arvind Singh, sub-divisional officer of police (SDOP).

Rescue teams from police, administration, and SDRF, along with villagers, launched operations using ropes and cranes.
A witness, Mahendra Parmar said, “The water level was so high that the driver could not distinguish between the road and the drain. We urged him to wait until the water receded, but he ignored the warnings.”
Sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) Rohit Bamhore said, “A total of 11 people were involved; two of them were rescued. The bodies of nine people have been recovered; among the deceased...Two people were rescued by residents.” “Heavy rains had submerged the road, but despite warnings, the driver drove ahead, leading to the tragedy,” he added.
Meanwhile, high alert has been issued in 21 districts of MP. In Bhopal, water has inundated railway tracks, temples, police stations, and homes. Many roads in Sehore and Shajapur are closed due to flooding, and a bridge was washed away in Raisen.
Bhopal recorded the highest rainfall of 7 inches in the last 24 hours. In Vidisha, 17 people, including children, were rescued after getting stranded in floodwaters. Temples in Sehore’s Sevaniya village have been submerged due to heavy rains. Meanwhile, water is flowing over a bridge, disrupting transportation.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the state has received 17.8 inches (453 mm) of rainfall so far.

GUWAHATI: China has hit back sharply at India for assigning standard names to 27 geographical locations in Arunachal Pradesh, with the state-run Global Times claiming these areas are in China's 'Zangnan' region - Beijing's term for Arunachal Pradesh and adjoining areas that it claims as part of Tibet Autonomous part.The daily reiterated that Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a routine press briefing on April 14 that the Zangnan region is China's territory and "China does not recognise the so-called 'Arunachal Pradesh' illegally set up by India. It is fully within China's sovereign rights for the Chinese govt to issue standard names for some of the places in Zangnan."
The reaction came three days after India's Survey of India updated its official map to identify 21 land areas, four passes, a high-altitude glacial lake and a 1962 war hero monument in Arunachal Pradesh, which govt said was an exercise to ensure the "correct identification" of places and enhance public awareness of their geographical and historical significance.Global Times reported on Sunday night that the mapping by India came shortly after the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on China-India Border Affairs (WMCC), held on Aug 6 in New Delhi, where officials from both sides discussed issues including boundary delimitation, border management and control, mechanism building and cross-border cooperation."India's latest move is essentially an attempt to reinforce its claims over disputed territory and counter China's sovereignty position," Guo Xuetang, a professor at Shanghai International Studies University, said.The latest "war of names" adds another layer to an already complex border dispute, even as both sides seek to keep military and diplomatic channels open.

headline: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday (August 11, 2026) in Gorakhpur said ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign is a tribute to the sacrifices of freedom fighters and urged people to display the national flag at their homes with pride and resp...
full_text:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday (August 11, 2026) in Gorakhpur said ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign is a tribute to the sacrifices of freedom fighters and urged people to display the national flag at their homes with pride and respect.
“Our Tricolour is a symbol of India’s honour, pride and glory. Throughout the freedom movement, our freedom fighters, at various times and in diverse manners, displayed different flags and infused new energy into the struggle. In 1905, the Swadeshi movement emerged as the fundamental principle of India’s quest for freedom. Subsequently, during the 1930s, the charkha positioned at the centre of the Tricolour symbolized the banner of the freedom fighters. Following the achievement of independence, the national flag was officially adopted, featuring the chakra that represents all states alongside the Tricolour.,” Mr. Adityanath said, addressing the gathering before inaugurating the Yatra.
The nearly two-and-a-half-kilometre-long yatra started from the Nagar Nigam premises to Railway Station Chowk, with the CM undertaking the padyatra carrying the Tricolour in his hand with the sentiment of ‘Nation First’. Mr. Aditayanath also paid floral tribute and offered flowers at the statue of Veerangana Maharani Lakshmibai located in the Nagar Nigam premises, paying homage to her contribution and sacrifice in the freedom struggle.
The CM added “Earlier, citizens had to engage in legal battles to raise the national flag, Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji associated this act with the rights of every individual. This Tiranga Yatra is part of Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji’s call to hoist the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’. The ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign, which began in 2022, is moving towards its peak every year. Great personalities and revolutionaries are sources of inspiration for the youth,”.
Speaking about sacrifice of great freedom fighters Mr. Adityanath added, “once, this Tricolour had become the mantra of India’s independence. Mangal Pandey had ignited the spark of freedom in Barrackpore. In Gorakhpur, Bandhu Singh, in Jhansi, Rani Lakshmibai, in Bithoor (Kanpur), Tatya Tope, and in Meerut, Dhan Singh Kotwal gave direction to the freedom movement. A very heavy price had to be paid for independence. In 1922, the historic incident of Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur shook the foundations of British rule.”
The U.P. CM alleged revolutionaries didn’t receive the respect they deserved due to neglect of earlier governments. “The revolutionaries could not receive the respect they deserved. Under the previous governments, memorials were not built in their names, and institutions and roads were not named after them. At that time, institutions were named after one family and schemes were run in their names. Today, freedom struggle martyrs are being honoured in India. They are also being honoured through Har Ghar Tiranga.”
Mr. Adityanath urged the people to put up the Tricolour they were carrying in their hands at their homes after the Tiranga Yatra and upload a selfie with it. “The state government has set a target of hoisting the Tricolour at five crore homes this year. Along with this, the Tricolour will be hoisted on the buildings of all government, semi-government, private, commercial and business establishments. This is a symbol of our respect for the brave martyrs who made the supreme sacrifice for the nation,” added the U.P. CM.

headline: Tamil Nadu Assembly to pass separate resolutions against NEET, FCRA Bill
full_text:
Tamil Nadu Assembly to pass separate resolutions against NEET, FCRA Bill
The Tamil Nadu Assembly is set to move separate resolutions against NEET and the FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026. The measures frame the debate around social justice in admissions and autonomy for charitable institutions.
The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly is set to pass separate resolutions opposing the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026.
Health Minister Ma Subramanian will move a separate resolution urging the Union government to amend relevant central laws to abolish the uniform NEET system for undergraduate medical admissions.
The resolution argues that NEET undermines social justice and equality and adversely affects students from rural and socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, particularly those educated in Tamil. It also criticises the growing dependence on expensive coaching centres and says the examination has shifted students' focus away from the school curriculum.
The resolution points out that the Tamil Nadu Assembly had unanimously passed the Tamil Nadu Admission to Undergraduate Medical Degree Courses Bill, 2021, seeking exemption from NEET, but the Bill has not received presidential assent.
It also cites repeated question paper leaks and irregularities in the examination system, including the cancellation of NEET-UG 2026 and the subsequent re-examination. The resolution says these developments have caused severe mental distress among lakhs of students and eroded public confidence in the examination system.
The Assembly will urge the Centre to amend the National Medical Commission Act, 2019, the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine Act, 2020, the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020, and other relevant laws to discontinue NEET at the national level.
The Tamil Nadu government has proposed that admissions to medical courses in the state be based on Class 12 examination marks.
Separately, the School Education, Tamil Development, Information and Publicity Minister will move a resolution opposing the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, in its present form.
The resolution expresses concern over provisions that could allow the government to take over, manage, dispose of or sell assets of charitable organisations following the expiry, non-renewal, refusal, cancellation or surrender of FCRA registration.
The state Assembly will argue that the provisions could undermine the autonomy of charitable organisations, particularly educational and social welfare institutions run by minorities.
The resolution will urge the Union government to withdraw the Bill in its current form and hold comprehensive consultations with state governments and stakeholders, including charitable, religious, educational, medical and social organisations.
It will also call for any amendment to safeguard natural justice, proportionality, property rights, legitimate expectation and federalism while ensuring transparency and accountability in foreign contributions.

Data showed the number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26
NEW DELHI: The number of govt elementary schools across the country fell by nearly 10,000 in a year, with Meghalaya, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh recording the steepest declines, according to data tabled in the Lok Sabha on Monday.UDISE+ data showed that the number of elementary-level govt schools declined from 8,89,806 in 2024-25 to 8,79,940 in 2025-26 - a reduction of 9,866 schools, or about 1.1%.The govt data was provided in response to a question from DMK MP T R Baalu on whether a large number of elementary schools had been closed because of insufficient student strength and the steps being taken to prevent dropouts. However, the education ministry did not specify how many of the schools were actually closed due to lack of students, while furnishing the overall number of govt elementary schools in the two academic years.Meghalaya recorded the biggest numerical decline, with the number of govt elementary schools falling from 7,633 to 5,459, a drop of 2,174. Telangana followed with a reduction of 1,961 schools, from 22,983 to 21,022, while Andhra Pradesh saw its count decline by 1,446, from 37,449 to 36,003.Madhya Pradesh had 1,043 fewer schools, Karnataka 615, West Bengal 587, Rajasthan 473 and Maharashtra 357. Himachal Pradesh recorded a decline of 259 schools, while Assam had 209 fewer.
Uttar Pradesh, which continues to have the largest network of govt elementary schools, saw the number fall marginally from 1,34,115 to 1,33,948.Not every state recorded a decline. Bihar's count rose from 66,803 to 66,915, while Chhattisgarh increased from 43,836 to 43,853. The numbers remained unchanged in Jammu & Kashmir, Puducherry and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
The ministry said opening, closing and rationalisation of schools fall within the jurisdiction of state and UT govts since education is on the Concurrent List.At the same time, it said access to schooling had improved. The Gross Access Ratio rose between 2018-19 and 2025-26 from 96.49 to 98.14 at upper-primary level, from 88.24 to 95.05 at secondary level and from 65.05 to 94.79 at higher-secondary level.The Centre said states were being supported through Samagra Shiksha and PM POSHAN, besides assistance for school infrastructure, residential schools and hostels, transport facilities, enrolment drives, textbooks and uniforms to curb dropouts and improve enrolment.

The deceased was identified as Jaiwanti, who worked as a house help, they said, adding that the car driver has been apprehended.
A 48-year-old woman on her way home was run over by a speeding luxury car when she was crossing the road in Delhi Cantonment area on Tuesday afternoon, police said. The woman later died at the hospital.
Deputy commissioner of police (south west) Amit Goel said that the victim was identified as Jaiwanti, a resident of Mehram Nagar, and the accused was identified as Deepak, a resident of Mandoli, who drove a BMW. Police, however, refused to share details of the BMW owner.
According to the family, Jaiwanti was a contractual employee of the Delhi Cantonment Board and worked as a house help in the Mehram Nagar police colony.
Police received a PCR call about a road accident at 12 pm. “The police staff immediately reached the spot and found that the injured woman had already been shifted to DDU Hospital, where she was declared dead,” Goel said.
Police said Jaiwanti was hit by a car while crossing the road, and the driver fled the scene. Locals then reached the spot and took her to the hospital, where she was declared dead.
Her family said locals informed them about the accident, after which they blocked the road opposite the Mehram Nagar police colony, demanding immediate arrest.
Sandeep, 25, who drives an ambulance at a private hospital, said, “My mother was on her way home for lunch when the accident happened. The driver of the BMW drove at a very high speed and didn't stop after hitting my mother. He left her bleeding on the road. The least he could do was take her to the hospital.”
The family members blocked the road for about three hours, demanding to meet the BMW's driver. The son said, “After about two and a half hours, police came to inform us that the driver had been arrested and was at the police station. But we wanted to see him for ourselves to ensure they had arrested the right person. Some people had seen the driver, but they have not shown him to us.”
Her relatives said Jaiwanti was the family's primary breadwinner and was taking care of her son and three married daughters.
Sonu Prajapati, 45, a relative, said, “Her husband passed away many years ago and the son works on and off. Who will run their house now? The son should now get a permanent job, and the family should receive heavy compensation from the driver.”
Police said a case has been registered on charges of causing death by negligence and rash driving.
“Deepak was traced and arrested within two hours, and further investigation is underway. His medical examination has been conducted to verify if he was drunk at the time of the incident, and reports are awaited,” a senior police officer said.
Police said Deepak lives with his wife and children in East Delhi’s Mandoli. He has been working as a driver for the last six months. Police said he was returning from the airport and was alone in the car when the accident occurred.

headline: Amit Shah will reply to student protests debate, says govt; Opposition demands specific reasons, Ram temple discussion
full_text:
Amit Shah will reply to student protests debate, says govt; Opposition demands specific reasons, Ram temple discussion
NEET protest debate: Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju made the offer during a BAC meeting in a bid to end the two-week-long logjam in the Lok Sabha.
The government on Monday offered to debate students’ issues and police action in Parliament with a reply by Union home minister Amit Shah, in a last-ditch effort to end the two-week-long logjam, but the Opposition insisted on specific responses and a second debate on donation theft in the Ram Temple.
In a meeting of the Lok Sabha’s Business Advisory Committee (BAC) chaired by speaker Om Birla, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju made the offer. Birla, too, appealed to the Opposition to cooperate in the smooth conduct of proceedings, pointing out that the government agreed on the main demand of the Opposition — a statement by Shah.
'We are ready for discussion': Kiren Rijiju
“We have made it clear to the BAC of the Lok Sabha that the government is ready for a full-fledged discussion on the student and youth agitations that have been going on in different parts of the country as well as police action. The home minister will give point-by-point reply to the debate on behalf of the government,” Rijiju said after the BAC meeting.
Pointing out that the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi had demanded that Shah make a statement in Parliament on the student protests. Rijiju said, “We have made our offer. Now, there appear to be some differences between the Congress and the Samajwadi Party — which they need to resolve. As for the student issue, we are ready for a discussion. We have stated our position. Now, it is up to the Samajwadi Party and the Congress to sort out the differences between them.” Both the Congress and the SP said debates on both issues were non-negotiable.
'Don't want fantasy statements': Rahul Gandhi
“The question was never that Amit Shah would come and speak on some general topic. Neither we nor the nation is interested on his view on education. We are not interested in any fantasy statements from Shah. He has to clarify who authorised the shooting at youngsters in Delhi. Students were fired at. They were beaten with lathi with nails. Shah is guilty of either negligence of culpability and he must resign,” Gandhi said.
Over the past two weeks, the ongoing monsoon session has been largely washed out because the Opposition demanded a statement from Shah in the House over allegations of police excesses and the use of pellet guns at the July 20 protest demanding the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
ALSO READ | No direction from Rajya Sabha Chair to Amit Shah to attend House: Rijiju amid Oppn uproar
To be sure, the supplementary list of business stated earlier in the day that Shah was going to introduce two bills – one to formally change the name of Kerala to Keralam, and another to amend the National Co-operative Development Corporation Act. Eventually, the first bill was introduced by Union minister of state (MoS) Nityanand Rai and the second by MoS Murlidhar Mohol.
Demand for Ram temple donation ‘theft’ debate
For the SP, which faces the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections scheduled early next year, the controversy around Ram Mandir collections has been the top issue in the monsoon session, which ends on August 13.
“The Opposition have been demanding from the very first day that the home minister make a statement. The government is not ready to do so. There are still two days left, and the government has time to discuss both issues. It is not an ordinary matter that the offerings made to Lord Ram have been stolen. The faith of crores of people has been hurt. People who donated money, offerings and dakshina with faith and devotion...were government or BJP leaders involved in it? Who will ultimately answer for this?” SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said.
ALSO READ | 'Opposition is anti-Lord Ram': Kiren Rijiju attacks Congress, SP over Ram Temple donation row protest
Yadav alleged that the BJP formed governments by playing with people’s faith and devotion. “Why does the government not want a discussion on this issue? And the second issue is the lathi-charge on young people and the way the children, youth and students were humiliated. They were not only NEET aspirants. Along with NEET students, all those who appeared for examinations across the country and in Uttar Pradesh, including those who could not take their exams because of paper leaks, were present there...”
Hours later, Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge and Gandhi said that Shah’s statement on police excesses and Ram Mandir theft were non-negotiable for the party.
Kharge and Gandhi both said the Opposition’s first demand was the home minister’s statement on allegations of police overreach, including the use of pellet guns and shock batons on July 20. The second demand was that the prime minister reveal the truth about the ‘offering theft’ and take the strictest possible action against the culprits. The two leaders said that the third demand was apologies from the PM and home minister.
ALSO READ | ‘Amit Shah gave firing order’ vs ‘No shots fired’: Rahul Gandhi, Centre in war of words as anti-paper leak bill passed
Kharge argued that for two weeks, the government didn’t agree to a debate on students. “This means that Shah didn’t want the debate. The PM played a big role in setting up Ram Mandir trust. He picked members who were close to him. But when people raised questions on theft and Modi’s trusted trustee—he didn’t reply. We wanted the PM to apologise to the nation because millions of people have faith in Ayodhya. Both the PM and HM are silent on these issues, which are non-negotiable. These are non-negotiable issues,” Kharge said.
Gandhi alleged that people close to the PM stole from the Ram Mandir collections and criticised Shah and Narendra Modi for not coming to the House for the past 15 days. According to a senior non-Congress MP, the presser was an attempt to avoid any fissures in the Opposition camp.
Congress general secretary KC Venugopal has written to Birla to urge him to demand Shah’s statement on the police brutalities on students on the floor of the House.
'Rahul Gandhi, don't run away': JP Nadda
Hours later, Union minister JP Nadda accused Gandhi of deliberately disrupting Parliament for the last 15 days and misleading the country. “Gandhi was demanding a statement from home minister Amit Shah on the Jantar Mantar protest. When the home minister agreed to his demand, the Congress leader changed his goalpost and started demanding a discussion on the alleged embezzlement of Ram temple donation,” Nadda said. “Why are they running away from the discussion? I want to state clearly: Rahul Gandhi, do not run away from the discussion. We are ready. We are prepared to discuss every issue inside the House. Do not run away,” he added.
