headline: Ladakh has planned to introduce guided wildlife safaris on popular snow leopard and bird-watching trails.
full_text:
Ladakh has planned to introduce guided wildlife safaris on popular snow leopard and bird-watching trails.
SRINAGAR: A safari car can roll past a rhino in Kaziranga. In Ranthambore, it can track a tiger. Put that car in Ladakh. For its elusive snow leopards â masters of camouflage in a landscape where survival depends on staying unseen â the question is whether tourism can get close enough to see them without making them disappear for good.Ladakh has planned to introduce guided wildlife safaris on popular snow leopard and bird-watching trails, triggering warnings from conservationists that turning a fragile high-altitude wilderness into a tourist circuit could disturb wildlife, commercialise off-roading and open the door to roads, eateries and other tourism infrastructure.âYou cannot see a snow leopard from a jeep unless you do something illegal like placing bait or a sheep to lure it,â said Dr MK Ranjitsinh, emeritus member of Wildlife Trust of India, who has spent nearly 50 years shaping conservation strategies and played a key role in framing the Wildlife (Protection) Act of 1972 and Project Tiger.âKaziranga is not Ladakh and Ranthambore is not Ladakh. The ecology is completely different,â he added.In Ladakhâs open valleys, vehicles can be visible from miles away. Vegetation is concentrated along valley bottoms, drawing animals there to feed and drink. âAre you taking a safari there?â he asked.Ladakh is home to 477 of Indiaâs estimated 718 snow leopards â the countryâs largest population. It also supports more than 38 mammal species, 340 bird species and 1,800 vascular plant species.
But spotting a snow leopard is a needle-in-a-haystack affair. Its thick, mottled coat melts into rocky slopes, while steep, remote terrain gives it a vast natural advantage.The Ladakh govt spokesperson said lieutenant governor Vinai Kumar Saxena has directed the forest department to introduce guided safaris modelled on national parks such as Kaziranga and Ranthambore, using specially designed open-back vehicles operated by trained local drivers and guides. According to govt, the move is aimed at preventing illegal off-roading and disturbance of wildlife.The plan was cleared at the first governing body meeting of Snow Leopard and High-Altitude Nature Conservation Society, chaired by Saxena. Forest officials have been asked to explore routes across Hemis national park, Changthang and Karakoram wildlife sanctuaries, besides Nubra, Zanskar, Sham, Kargil and Drass.Ranjitsinh fears a different road ahead. âWildlife safari may be good in principle but in practice it could be a disaster,â he said, warning that tourism and hotel lobbies could eventually overwhelm govt controls. âThere will be demands for more roads, eating places and other infrastructure. Eventually, the whole landscape could turn into a festival.â
A wildlife official said safaris work best where animals occur in large concentrations or herds â unlike Himalayan and Trans-Himalayan terrain. Ladakh already has roads across its protected areas, with tourist vehicles accessing most zones except some restricted border regions.âWhat they actually plan is to regularise and commercialise off-roading,â the official said, warning that vehicles could be allowed into fragile meadows for a price.Kaziranga and Ranthambore were built into Indiaâs safari imagination. Ladakhâs proposed safari would venture into an entirely different world. Its snow leopards are scattered across an unforgiving landscape where the first rule of spotting one is knowing where not to look.

headline: Parliament's Monsoon Session heads for a washout as key bills remain stuck
full_text:
Parliament's Monsoon Session heads for a washout as key bills remain stuck
NDA began the Monsoon Session on the front foot, but student protests and Pradhan's exit have left key bills hanging in balance.
When Parliament's Monsoon Session began on July 20, the BJP-led NDA appeared to have the numbers, the Opposition appeared divided, and the government seemed well-placed to push through an ambitious legislative agenda. Three weeks later, that script has been upended.
The session, which was expected to focus on major proposals including women's reservation, delimitation and tighter regulation of foreign funding, has instead been dominated by the NEET controversy, student protests and a widening confrontation between the government and the Opposition over police action against demonstrators.
The resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan on July 25 was the first major political fallout of the protests. But rather than drawing a line under the controversy, it shifted the battle to the Home Ministry, with the Opposition now demanding that Amit Shah explain who authorised the alleged police action against protesting students in Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
The immediate trigger for the disruption was the Opposition's campaign over the NEET paper leak and the treatment of students who took to the streets. What began as a demand for accountability in the examination system widened after allegations of police excesses against protesters. Pradhan's resignation gave the Opposition fresh political ammunition, but did little to ease the standoff in Parliament.
The focus has since shifted to the Home Ministry. Opposition parties have been demanding an explanation from Amit Shah over the alleged police action against protesting students in Delhi, including allegations of pellet guns and lathi-charge. The government has now offered a discussion on student protests, with Shah agreeing to respond, but the Opposition wants him to specifically address who authorised the action.
This difference in approach has become the immediate obstacle to restoring normal proceedings. The government argues that it has offered the Opposition a forum to raise its concerns and has agreed to put the Home Minister in the House to respond. The Opposition, however, wants a direct answer on the Delhi police action before it agrees to move on to a broader discussion.
THE POLITICAL EQUATION HAS CHANGED
That standoff matters because it has consumed a session in which the government had hoped to concentrate on legislation.
When the session began, the NDA's improved numbers and divisions within the Opposition had strengthened expectations that the government could advance some of its more ambitious proposals. The political arithmetic, however, has proved less useful in practice as the Opposition has found common ground around student protests and the demand for accountability.
The first major test is the proposed legislation on women's reservation and delimitation.
The government wants to provide 33 per cent reservation for women from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections and link its implementation to the redrawing of parliamentary constituencies. The proposals carry political consequences well beyond the current session because delimitation could alter the representation of states in the Lok Sabha.
The government also needs the numbers to pass a constitutional amendment. An earlier Constitution amendment connected to the exercise was defeated in April, with 298 members voting in favour and 230 against. The NDA's strength has since improved, but it remains short of the two-thirds majority required for such a constitutional amendment.
That is where Opposition differences become important. The DMK has strongly opposed delimitation, while Congress and several of its allies have objected to the government's approach. The Shiromani Akali Dal, however, has backed both women's reservation and delimitation.
The positions are therefore not neatly divided along government-versus-Opposition lines. For the government, the challenge is not simply to improve its numbers but to build a sufficiently broad political consensus around legislation that could reshape the composition of Parliament.
FCRA COULD BECOME ANOTHER FLASHPOINT
The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, presents a separate challenge.
Introduced in the Lok Sabha on March 25, the Bill proposes tighter oversight of organisations receiving foreign funding. It also provides for a new authority with powers to seize and manage the assets of non-profit organisations that lose their licence.
Congress has strongly opposed the Bill, calling it "unconstitutional and anti-people" and alleging that it could target minorities and NGOs.
The Opposition has made clear that it does not intend to allow the legislation to pass without a fight. Congress general secretary KC Venugopal has warned against any attempt to introduce and pass the Bill in the remaining days of the session. NCP-SP leader Supriya Sule has called for the legislation to be withdrawn or referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee, while DMK chief MK Stalin has also demanded its withdrawal.
For the government, therefore, the FCRA Bill could open another political front at a time when Parliament is already struggling to function.
PARLIAMENT HAS PASSED BILLS, BUT DEBATE HAS SUFFERED
The picture is not one of complete legislative paralysis.
The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, dealing with examination malpractice and paper leaks, was passed by both Houses following a debate. Other legislation has also cleared Parliament.
But the manner in which several Bills have been passed has raised a separate question about the quality of parliamentary scrutiny.
The Lok Sabha has so far cleared nine Bills, according to the information available, but debate could be held on only two. The others were passed amid Opposition protests and sloganeering.
The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, passed by the Lok Sabha on Monday, was the latest example. Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said the legislation seeks to reform the appointment and service conditions of tribunal chairpersons and members and establish a National Tribunals Commission. The government argued that the proposed system would improve transparency, uniformity and efficiency in tribunal appointments.
But Opposition MPs continued to protest during the minister's speech. The Bill was eventually passed without debate.
That leaves both sides with a political argument. The government can point to legislation that has been cleared despite sustained disruptions. The Opposition can argue that passing Bills amid sloganeering does not substitute for detailed parliamentary debate and scrutiny.
GOVERNMENT REACHES OUT; BREAKTHROUGH REMAINS ELUSIVE
The government has made several attempts to end the impasse.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju has held meetings and spoken with Rahul Gandhi, while government floor managers have also sounded out other Opposition parties on women's reservation and delimitation.
But the outreach has not yet produced a broad political agreement.
Rahul Gandhi has sought an all-party meeting on the proposed legislation. The issue has also played out publicly between Gandhi and Rijiju, reflecting the wider political divide over delimitation and the proposed implementation of women's reservation.
Outside Parliament, political alignments have added another layer to the government's calculations.
The SAD's support for women's reservation and delimitation came shortly after party president Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi, prompting speculation about a possible political realignment ahead of the Punjab Assembly election next year.
Tamil Nadu has taken the opposite position. A meeting attended by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and a section of the state's MPs adopted a resolution opposing delimitation and demanding that the strength of the Lok Sabha remain frozen at 543.
These developments underline the difficulty before the government. Its improved numbers may give it greater room for manoeuvre, but they do not automatically translate into the numbers or political consensus required for every major piece of legislation.
THE FINAL THREE DAYS
The Congress has issued a whip asking its MPs in both Houses to remain present on August 10, 11 and 12, describing the issues expected to come up as "very important". It has also asked its INDIA bloc allies to ensure that their MPs remain present.
The government now has very little time to change the trajectory of the session.
The immediate challenge is to decide whether the offer of a discussion, with Amit Shah responding, is enough to bring the Opposition back into the debate. If the confrontation continues, the government may have to choose between bringing legislation before a disrupted House or carrying some of its most politically significant proposals into the next session.
That would be a very different outcome from what appeared possible on July 20.
The NDA entered the Monsoon Session with improved political arithmetic and hopes of using a divided Opposition to advance its legislative agenda. The student protests changed that equation. Pradhan's resignation gave the Opposition an early political victory, while the continuing dispute over police action has kept the confrontation alive.
The final days will therefore test more than the government's ability to pass Bills. They will test whether it can regain control of the political agenda inside Parliament.
The government may still salvage some legislative business before August 13. But unless the standoff over the student protests is resolved, the defining image of the Monsoon Session could be one of a government with the numbers to legislate, but not the political space to do so.

headline: Opposition parties in Punjab lashed out at the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government after nine Bills were passed in the House on Monday, describing the exercise as a “display of majoritarian arrogance”.
full_text:
Opposition parties in Punjab lashed out at the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government after nine Bills were passed in the House on Monday, describing the exercise as a “display of majoritarian arrogance”.
The State Assembly passed nine Bills pertaining to various sectors, including education, infrastructure, taxation, and employment, rural development and environmental protection.
The Bill included the Punjab Common Infrastructure (Regulation and Maintenance) Amendment Bill, 2026, the Punjab Regulation of Fee of Un-aided Educational Institutions (Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Punjab Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Punjab State Outsourced Personnel (Transition to Contractual Engagement) Bill, 2026, the Punjab Panchayati Raj (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the Punjab Protection of Trees Bill, 2026.
The House also passed three Bills pertaining to universities, including the Cloud University, Hoshiarpur Bill, 2026, the MS Digital University, Patiala Bill, 2026 and the Physicswallah Digital University, Patiala Bill, 2026.
‘Gross insult’
Bharatiya Janata Party’s Punjab president Kewal Singh Dhillon called it “a gross insult to Punjab’s legislative system and democracy”. He said passing Bills that could have far-reaching consequences for the lives of the people of Punjab without giving legislators adequate time to read, understand, and scrutinise is not law-making. “Rather, it is a display of the arrogance of the majority,” he said.
“If nine Bills are introduced in the House and passed immediately on the same day, when will any legislator read their provisions, when will they understand them, and when will they discuss them with the people of their respective constituencies?,” he quipped.
Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring in a post on X said: “On the very last day of the Assembly session, Congress MLAs were handed nine Bills this morning. This is nothing short of a joke with democracy. The government expects the Opposition to study, scrutinise and debate nine bills without even giving us adequate time to read them. This is not legislation, this is an attempt to bypass democratic scrutiny. Why is the Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann so scared of debate? We strongly oppose this hypocrisy and this blatant disregard for democratic legislative procedure.”

headline: Chirag Paswan's LJP to enter UP poll battle, alliance call still open
full_text:
Chirag Paswan's LJP to enter UP poll battle, alliance call still open
Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), led by Chirag Paswan, will contest the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The party will remain with the NDA if a satisfactory seat-sharing deal is reached, but is prepared to contest independently if negotiations fail.
The Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas), led by Union Minister Chirag Paswan, has decided to contest the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, while keeping open the possibility of fighting either as part of the National Democratic Alliance or independently.
The decision was taken at the party’s national executive committee meeting in New Delhi on Monday, chaired by Chirag Paswan. Senior party leaders and executive members discussed organisational expansion, electoral preparations and the party’s strategy for upcoming Assembly elections.
Uttar Pradesh emerged as a key focus of the meeting as the LJP (Ram Vilas) seeks to expand its political presence beyond Bihar. Party leaders said the organisation is working to strengthen its network across several states and sees political and social space in Uttar Pradesh as an opportunity to increase its footprint.
While the party remains committed to the NDA, sources said it is preparing for an independent contest if seat-sharing negotiations do not meet its expectations. The party has not yet finalised the number of seats it plans to contest in Uttar Pradesh.
Chirag Paswan asked party workers and office-bearers to make the organisation stronger and more effective and intensify political activities in states heading for elections. He also called for the party’s ideology and policies to be taken to all sections of society.
The national executive reviewed membership campaigns, booth-level expansion, grassroots outreach and preparations for upcoming elections. The leadership also discussed strengthening the party’s organisational structure in states where its presence remains limited.
The party reiterated its commitment to the ideas and ideals of its founder, late Ram Vilas Paswan, and said it would continue to focus on public service and issues affecting ordinary people. It also reaffirmed its slogan, “Bihar First, Bihari First”, while highlighting the expansion of the organisation under Chirag Paswan.
The decision to enter the Uttar Pradesh electoral contest marks an effort by the LJP (Ram Vilas) to expand its political footprint and project itself as a force beyond Bihar. The party’s final electoral strategy in Uttar Pradesh is likely to depend on seat-sharing talks with NDA allies and the wider political arithmetic in the state.

headline: A man once tasked with saving Maharashtra’s daughters has now been unmasked as one of their most prolific predators.
full_text:
A man once tasked with saving Maharashtra’s daughters has now been unmasked as one of their most prolific predators.
For decades, Dr. Chandrakant Gunda Gaikwad sat comfortably within the upper echelons of the State health establishment, serving as a district civil surgeon and assistant director. He was also part of the government’s ‘Save the Girls’ campaign for years.
Retirement did not signal an end to his medical career, but marked the expansion of a dark underground enterprise. Dr. Gaikwad was arrested by the Kolhapur police on July 31 for allegedly orchestrating a sophisticated female foeticide ring. During interrogation, he allegedly admitted to performing around 200 to 250 illegal abortions, the police said.
The racket operated out of Kolhapur in western Maharashtra, the home district of State Health Minister Prakash Abitkar. The Minister called it a “serious matter” that a former health official was involved in such a crime. He announced that the State will soon introduce a new law to invoke the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act against female foeticide, ensuring that doctors, family members, pharmacists, and anyone else supporting the crime face prosecution.
However, when mediapersons pressed the Minister about how implicated doctors and individuals routinely escape punishment and continue running their rackets after securing bail, he had no concrete answer. It underscored a grim reality: culprits easily slip through the cracks and accountability remains elusive.
According to Sunanda Patil, an octogenarian and resident of Kolhapur, female foeticide “is nothing new”. She said women face two choices: empty their wombs if it is a girl, or keep giving birth until a son is born. She chose the second option, delivering three daughters before finally having a son. She considers herself lucky that her husband stopped there.
Quiet tragedies
For daily wage worker Maloji Kharat and his agricultural worker wife Lankabai, the reality was starkly different. By 38, Ms. Lankabai had 21 pregnancies and struggled to recall the names of all her children. Of her 11 surviving children, nine are girls. The other 10 died either shortly after birth or during delivery. When their story was reported a few years ago, the couple vanished from public view.
Beed district in the Marathwada region has long carried a dark reputation for illegal abortion rings. The most notorious was run by Dr. Sudam Munde and Dr. Saraswati Munde from Parali who operated a sex determination racket for years.
In one of the most chilling revelations, investigators found that the Mundes fed aborted female foetuses to a pack of dogs to hide the evidence, reportedly aborting up to 20 female foetuses a day for decades.
Beed-based activist Manisha Tokale noted that it has been over a decade since the Munde case, yet illegal abortion networks continue to operate in secret. The issue makes headlines briefly when a case is uncovered, she said, before things slip right back to normal.
This generational pressure drives quiet tragedies across the State. After delivering two sons, Renu (name changed) became pregnant a third time. Her husband, a daily wage worker, expected another boy. Fearing that her family history of having only daughters meant she would carry the same genes, he routinely took her for ultrasound tests.
“We went, had a sonography, and the family suggested abortion,” Ms. Renu said, without needing to specify that the third child was a girl. Phrases like “khali karun ye (empty it and come back)” or “tapasun baghu (let us check)” echo across both rural and urban Maharashtra. When she went to a private clinic in Beed for the abortion, the doctor botched the procedure. She said the clean-up was not done properly, leaving her with lasting physical pain and nowhere to turn for justice.
According to Roopa Shah, founder of the Kolhapur-based Dilasa Samajik Vishwast Sanstha, female foeticide happens everywhere in the State without exception.
Society’s mindset has not changed, regardless of whether people live in rural or urban areas, or are rich or poor, she said.
Having spent three decades fighting crimes like child marriage and female foeticide, Ms. Shah feels conventional measures have utterly failed. Because the police, courts, administration, and government have not been able to stop these atrocities, she believes the time has come for women to take a stand themselves. “It is not easy though,” she said.
Deep-rooted bias
The National Family Health Survey 2019-21 offers a window into the mindset of this social fabric. Maharashtra has shown a strong preference for sons. While 9% of women and 12% of men express a desire for more sons than daughters, only 4-5% of women and men want more daughters. A large majority of women and men wish to have at least one son while fewer desire at least one daughter. These figures capture a deep-rooted gender bias in the State, one that starts at birth and follows girls throughout their lives.
“Those who survive have to carry the burden of being a girl forever,” said Dhondabai Ningule, a resident of Dharashiv district.
In Marathi households, names like Dhondabai, derived from dhonda (stone), or Nakushi (unwanted) are often given to girls born merely as stopgap arrangements until a son arrives, serving as a constant, grudging reminder from their families of their unwanted existence.

headline: Boxer Narender Berwal recalled his encounter with a Pakistani opponent at the 2015 World Military Games, where he had defeated him.

Boxer Narender Berwal recalled his encounter with a Pakistani opponent at the 2015 World Military Games, where he had defeated him.
NEW DELHI: A Pakistani boxer who had "started hating" the name 'Narendra' after discovering that his Indian opponent, his coach and India's PM all shared the name drew laughs as Narendra Modi interacted with India's Commonwealth Games medallists Sunday.Boxer Narender Berwal recalled his encounter with a Pakistani opponent at the 2015 World Military Games, where he had defeated him. headline: Cops fact-check Harbhajan Singh over viral zombie drug clip: ‘From Rajasthan, not Punjab’
full_text:
Cops fact-check Harbhajan Singh over viral zombie drug clip: ‘From Rajasthan, not Punjab’
BJP Rajya Sabha MP Harbhajan Singh re-shared a video that purportedly showed two men standing motionless, calling the situation “very sad.”
A political slugfest erupted on Tuesday after BJP MP Harbhajan Singh shared a video showing two people under the influence of drugs and claimed that Punjab was “besieged by addictions”.
The video went viral on social media, with many claiming that the two youth visible in the clip were under the influence of “zombie drug”. However, this particular term was not used by Singh as he shared the clip.
While Harbhajan Singh claimed that the clip was indicative of the state of drug addiction in Punjab, the Punjab Police was quick to fact-check him, saying the video was from Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan and not Punjab.
Who said what
BJP Rajya Sabha MP Harbhajan Singh re-shared a video that purportedly showed two men standing motionless, calling the situation “very sad.” He added that the youth of Punjab deserves better and called for urgent action.
“Very sad to see the situation of Punjab. Punjab and its youth deserve better. This issue needs honesty, accountability, and urgent action—not denial,” he said on X.
In a separate post on X, Singh shared the video himself and blamed the government for “ruining” Punjab and its youth. He added that the Punjab – which was once known for its rising fortunes, courage, and bravery – is today besieged by addictions.
Also Read: Punjab Police hold over 39k meetings in 17 months to combat drug abuse: DGP
“The evil eye has struck, my friend, on our Punjab. The governments have ruined Punjab and its Punjabi youth. It makes me want to cry seeing all this. Forgive my Punjab... Excuse Punjab,” he wrote.
“Where have they brought Punjab to? The Punjab that was once known for its rising fortunes, courage, and bravery—today, that same Punjab's youth is besieged by addictions. There's still time—save my Punjab. Save Punjab's youth.”
Kejriwal, Punjab Police react
His post triggered a backlash from AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal, who accused the BJP of spreading lies. He wondered if the order had come from PMO to say such things.
“Many BJP people spread this lie together yesterday. Did the order come from the PMO? Does the PMO spread lies in the country?”
Also Read: Saini urges Haryana youth to lead anti-drug fight
Punjab Police also took to X, clarifying that the video shared on social media, was not from Punjab but Sri Ganganagar in Rajasthan and said that it has no connection with Punjab Police.
It added that putting Punjabi music over the video doesn't make it from the state and urged users and social media accounts to verify the facts and location before posting what is described as “misleading” content.
“A Punjabi audio track does not make an incident a Punjab incident. We urge users and social media accounts to verify the facts and location before posting misleading content or tagging Punjab Police,” it wrote on X.
The police also tagged the BJP MP and said, “Responsible sharing matters.”
Punjab Cabinet Minister Dr Baljit Kaur also hit back at Singh almost immediately, accusing him of trying to “please his political bosses.” She added that the people of Punjab would never forgive him for doing what she called “BJP ki dalali.”
“Look at the desperation to please his political bosses. He is sharing a video from Rajasthan and lying that it is from Punjab. You will do anything for BJP ki dalali, even if it means ruining Punjab's image. The people of Punjab will never forgive you for this,” she wrote on X.
Punjab Public Works (B&R) Minister Harbhajan Singh ETO also criticised the BJP MP, calling it the “BJP’s standard modus operandi.” He accused the BJP of using its MP to constantly defame Punjab and added that the people of the state see right through this “dirty propaganda.”
“This is the BJP's standard modus operandi: manufacture lies and use sell-outs like Harbhajan to constantly defame Punjab. This video is from Rajasthan, but he lies to ruin the image of the state that gave him his entire career. Punjabis see right through this dirty propaganda,” he wrote on X.
What did the video show?
The video featured two men wearing turbans and standing motionless in a hunched back position. It appeared as they were struggling to stand on a roadside or move ahead. The video has been shared on social media, with many claiming that the two men appear to be under the influence of drugs, particularly the “zombie-drug.”
While the BJP MP claimed the video to be from Punjab, its origins lie in Rajasthan’s Ganganagar. There is no confirmation if the two men actually are under the influence of the alleged “zombie-drug.”
The incident has once again put the spotlight on Punjab, where political parties continue to clash over the state’s drug crisis. The BJP has repeatedly accused the AAP government of failing to curb the persistent rise in drug abuse in the state.

3 Bidar factories to be shut amid water pollution charges
The state government on Monday ordered the immediate closure of three industrial plants in Humnabad Industrial Area after residents alleged that untreated chemical waste was being discharged into local water bodies, including the Guruganga and Manjra rivers
The state government on Monday ordered the immediate closure of three industrial plants in Humnabad Industrial Area after residents alleged that untreated chemical waste was being discharged into local water bodies, including the Guruganga and Manjra rivers.
State rural development minister Eshwar Khandre, who is in charge of Bidar district, ordered the deputy commissioner to issue closure orders against M/s 6H Industries, M/s Sathyadeepthi K. Industries and M/s Himalaya Industries. He also sought a compliance report within 24 hours.
The minister took note of complaints of foul-smelling effluents entering a stream at Maniknagar and subsequently the Guruganga and Manjra rivers.
Residents also alleged that the contamination has caused illnesses among people and livestock. Protests, rallies and public meetings have been held under the “Save Guruganga” campaign.
The stream eventually flows into the Karanja backwaters, Khandre said, raising concerns over the possible contamination of a source of drinking water. He directed the administration to act against industries found to be releasing waste into the water sources and referred to Section 152 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which provides for urgent measures to prevent public nuisance.
The latest order follows directions issued by Khandre on August 5 after reports brought the pollution issue to his attention. In that communication, he had asked the district administration to test the water, take legal action against industries found discharging waste, protect the affected water sources and submit an action taken report within 48 hours.
Khandre also referred to earlier action taken when he wasserving as the state forest minister. Following complaints from residents, an inquiry was conducted and action was ordered under the applicable rules. On July 29, 2024, the Deputy Commissioner directed the Humnabad Tahsildar to seal nine industries allegedly responsible for pollution.
Humnabad BJP MLA Siddalingappa Patil said residents of his constituency had been dealing with industrial pollution for nearly 15 years and that he had repeatedly sought government action. “In my constituency, people have been suffering from chemical factory pollution for nearly 15 years, and I urged the government to take strict action,” Patil said.
He said that when Khandre was serving as the state forest minister, a committee had been formed and more than 14 chemical factories were shut down. Patil said the pollution had since spread to nearby villages.

headline: Coaching centres boom, charging huge fees: Why CM Vijay's govt wants NEET abolition
full_text:
Coaching centres boom, charging huge fees: Why CM Vijay's govt wants NEET abolition
State health minister KG Arunraj said the examination had “diverted focus of students” from the curriculum followed by schools to coaching.
A resolution for abolishing the NEET system for undergraduate medical admissions was passed by the Tamil Nadu legislative assembly on Tuesday.
Citing the reasons for urging the abolition of NEET, state health minister KG Arunraj said the examination had “diverted focus of students” from the curriculum followed by schools to coaching, ANI news agency reported. Arunraj alleged that it had further resulted in the “proliferation of coaching centres that charge exorbitant fees.”
The resolution comes days after the students' protest in Delhi and other parts of the country over the alleged irregularities in NEET and the paper leak row around it, which led to the resignation of union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
‘NEET against social justice, equality, state rights’, single exam decides
Arunraj, while speaking in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, said NEET was against “social justice, equality and state rights”. “This test gravely undermines medical education opportunities of rural, socio-economically disadvantaged students,” the minister added.
The Tamil Nadu government has earlier too alleged that the examination adversely affects students from rural and economically disadvantaged backgrounds, particularly those who study from Tamil medium, according to ANI. It had also raised concerns over the growing dependence of students on expensive coaching centres to clear the test.
The state government had also highlighted the pressure on the students to clear a single entrance examination to secure a seat in medical colleges after Class 12.
What does the resolution propose? Which parties supported it?
The resolution primarily calls for the amendment of relevant central laws and urges the BJP-led union government to abolish the NEET for admission to undergraduate medical courses. The chief minister Vijay-led Tamil Nadu government has proposed that admissions to medical courses in the state be based on Class 12 examination marks – a stand similar to the one the previous DMK government took.
Along with TVK and its ally Congress, the main opposition DMK, AIADMK, PMK, DMDK, left parties and other smaller parties also supported the resolution. The lone BJP MLA in the Assembly staged a walkout. DMK MLA Muthuraja said his party supported the resolution, with AIADMK also saying it remains “firm in its anti-NEET policy.”
Meanwhile, BJP MLA M Bhojarajan, opposing the resolution, said NEET was an “encouragement for the people of Tamil Nadu,” while citing an example from Pollachi. “In Pollachi, 10 students from the same school have cleared the exam,” the BJP MLA said. He further questioned why the state government was not focusing on providing coaching facilities to students instead of asking for the abolition of NEET.

headline: ‘Zealots overlooked human nature’: Tharoor's ‘12 minutes’ question as new law for Vande Mataram okayed by President
full_text:
‘Zealots overlooked human nature’: Tharoor's ‘12 minutes’ question as new law for Vande Mataram okayed by President
Congress MP Shashi Tharoor questioned the underlying premise of the law itself: “Can respect and patience be legislated?”
Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Tuesday raised questions over the practical implications of the newly enacted Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026, hours after President Droupadi Murmu gave her assent to the legislation extending status and protection to the National Song, Vande Mataram, on par with the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana.
In a post on X, the Thiruvananthapuram MP noted that the amendment had been passed without discussion in Parliament. He said it requires the singing of the National Song in full at the start and ending of any official function, in addition to the National Anthem.
“As one who greatly respects both, and can sing the first two stanzas of the former (but not the other four, which were never required till now) as well as the entire anthem, i would like to point to just one practical consideration our zealots appear to have overlooked: human nature,” he wrote.
He then laid out a timing-based argument: “'Jana Gana Mana' requires audiences to stand respectfully and focus their attention for a reasonable 52 seconds… The National Song in full takes 3 minutes and 10 seconds.”
He also mentioned state-level protocol, such as in Tamil Nadu, which has decided that both Vande Mataram and Jana Gana Mana will be preceded by the State Song in Tamil “for another 2 minutes”.
“Do we really expect audiences to stand still and respectfully for six minutes before and after every function, a total of 12 extra minutes?” Tharoor wrote.
He questioned the underlying premise of the law itself: “Can respect and patience be legislated?… I fear that the intent of the Bill, to promote greater respect for the National Song, will not be achieved, but its opposite may well be.”
What are the law and rules on Vande Mataram now?
The new law amends the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, by substituting Section 3 to explicitly include Vande Mataram alongside the National Anthem.
Under the amended provision, any person who intentionally prevents the singing of the National Song, or causes disturbance to an assembly engaged in its rendition, is liable to imprisonment for up to three years, a fine, or both. This is the same rule applied to the National Anthem since 1971.
However, the amendment does not, on its own, make the singing of the National Song compulsory. That had come before it via a government circular. The requirement for all six stanzas to be rendered at official functions stems from a Union home ministry circular issued earlier this year. The amendment in law now attaches criminal liability to deliberate disruption of the National Song's singing.
This means that if Vande Mataram is made compulsory by an authority in charge of a function, anyone objecting to that can be jailed. Some states ruled by parties other than the Centre's ruling BJP – such as Kerala – have stood against mandating the singing of Vande Mataram in full.
The amendment bill was introduced in the Rajya Sabha on July 24, passed by it on July 29, and cleared by the Lok Sabha on July 30 amid Opposition protests, before receiving Presidential assent on Tuesday.
Earlier, only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram were traditionally sung at official events, since the remaining four contain imagery invoking the nation as a Hindu goddess, seen as excluding non-Hindu citizens. The BJP-led government of PM Narendra Modi, which describes itelf as “Hindu nationalist”, argued that Vande Mataram was central to India's freedom struggle.

headline: A day after the police action on students, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) launched a scathing attack on the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and called them a “parasite” during a speech in the Assembly.
full_text:
A day after the police action on students, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) launched a scathing attack on the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and called them a “parasite” during a speech in the Assembly.
On the last day of the Assembly’s monsoon session, which was adjourned sine die a day before the scheduled date, Mr. Soren asserted that he had been under the impression that nothing was left in the Opposition to raise a banner.
‘Students as shield’
“I was observing the chain of events of the past few days. It seemed that the Opposition had nothing left. Yet, they were attempting to demonstrate their strength by using students as a shield. Through various guises, they sustain themselves through different sources, much like a parasite survives,” Mr. Soren said in the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly.
He, however, added that over time, whatever little substance remained in the Opposition would also disappear. Throughout the session, the ruling coalition and the Opposition continuously attacked each other over student protests and alleged irregularities in Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) examinations.
In his address, Mr. Soren said that TDPL, the company responsible for irregularities in the examinations, is based in Lucknow, the capital of Uttar Pradesh. He alleged that a conspiracy was being hatched from there, involving people from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, to mislead the youth of Jharkhand.
“The government’s intention is absolutely clear. We have already clarified our stance regarding the 14th JPSC examination as well as the backlog examinations for 2023 and 2025,” Mr. Soren said.
On the other hand, a mixed response was witnessed during the Jharkhand Bandh call given by the BJP over the police action on the students. All top leaders of the Jharkhand unit of BJP came out onto the streets to protest, including State president Aditya Sahu.
BJP workers and leaders registered their protest by burning tyres in several areas, while shops were also forcibly closed in some places. Vehicular traffic was disrupted due to road blockade by the protesters.
ABVP members detained
Also, hundreds of Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) members were detained by the Jharkhand police when they held a protest march from Old Vidhan Sabha to New Vidhan Sabha in Ranchi.
Later in the day, while addressing a press conference at the BJP State office, Mr. Sahu held Congress leader Rahul Gandhi responsible for the police action on students.
“To crush and suppress the student movement, barbed wire was used, tear gas shells were fired, and students were subjected to atrocities involving lathi-charges and water cannons. All of this was done by the State government at the behest of Rahul Gandhi,” Mr. Sahu alleged.
He stated that Mr. Gandhi demanded the resignation of BJP leader Dharmendra Pradhan as Union Education Minister but never demanded a similar ouster of Jharkhand’s Education Minister.
The manner in which students protesting democratically were treated by officials meant August 10 turned out to be a ‘black day’ for Jharkhand, Mr. Sahu added. The BJP State president termed the ‘Jharkhand Bandh’ called by the party to protest against the police excess as a success.
Meanwhile, the agitating students continued their peaceful protest at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in the State capital.
The Congress alleged that some members of the BJP’s Yuva Morcha were being brought in from West Bengal in trucks to Jharkhand, and an attempt was being made to give a “different colour” to the ongoing non-violent student movement.
Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal shared a video clip purportedly showing youth allegedly being sent by the BJP to participate in the Jharkhand student protest against exam irregularities.
In a post in Hindi on X, Mr. Venugopal said: “Behold another example of the petty politics of Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. Some boys from the BJP Yuva Morcha are being transported from West Bengal in trucks to Jharkhand, and an attempt is being made there to give a different colour to the ongoing non-violent student movement.”
“They think that if a fake crowd is sent to the Jharkhand movement to make it look bigger, then the public outrage that has arisen against them will die down. Modi ji, stop thinking of and treating the people of India as fools,” the Congress leader said.

Along with Bansal, who is posted as as a city superintendent of police, assistant sub-inspector Praveen Kumar Rathore and constable Anshul Sharma have been accused of demanding and accepting a bribe of ₹1 crore to cover up a cyber fraud case, according to a report by Live Hindustan.

headline: Driver couldn't see unfinished bridge: 9 of family killed in MP as van swept away
full_text:
Driver couldn't see unfinished bridge: 9 of family killed in MP as van swept away
The van was swept away attempting to cross an unfinished bridge. The driver allegedly couldn't tell the bridge was unfinished despite warnings from passersby.
Nine members of a family were killed after a van they were travelling in was swept away as they tried to cross over flooded drain near Padana village of the Rajgarh district, Madhya Pradesh, on Monday morning.
The van, carrying eleven passengers, was driving on an unfinished bridge over Jhiri drain,Times of India said in a report. According to the publication, the heavy rain made it difficult for the driver to see incomplete portion of the bridge while crossing, causing the accident.
Seven of the victims were identified as Shankar Singh (50), his wife Sagarbai, Rinu (28), wife of Hukum Singh, their three-year-old son Rajveer, another son Jaspreet, Vishal Chauhan and his wife Pooja (27). Two passengers, Hukum Singh and driver Mukesh Singh, swam out and survived. The two were admitted to Sarangpur hospital and reportedly were in shock due to the incident. All passengers were residents of Satwas village.
According to the police, the incident took place around 9am on Monday when the Eco van was travelling from Dewas to Kadnavad village in Sarangpur tehsil for a religious visit.
Also Read | Body of teen, who was swept away in Delhi drain amid heavy rain, found in Agra canal after 40 hours
“As the vehicle reached the Padana bypass, water from the swollen Jhiri drain had spilled over the road. Despite repeated warnings from locals, the driver tried to cross. The strong current swept the van into the drain,” said Arvind Singh, sub-divisional officer of police (SDOP) according to a report by HT earlier today.
A witness, Mahendra Parmar, “The water level was so high that the driver could not distinguish between the road and the drain. We urged him to wait until the water receded, but he ignored the warnings.”
A bridge is under construction over the Jhiri drain. Due to heavy rain and flooding, the driver was reportedly unable to see the unfinished part of the bridge. Moreover, there were no railings.
Police, administrative officials and SDRF personnel, assisted by villagers, launched rescue operations using ropes and cranes. The van was pulled out with the help of a crane with police reporting that no bodies were found in the vehicle.
Also Read | Uttarakhand rains trigger landslides, boulder crashes into govt residential unit
Madhya Pradesh Chief minister Mohan Yadav announced an ex-gratia payment of ₹4 lakh to the families of each of the deceased.
“...My condolences go out to the bereaved families. Instructions have been issued to provide financial assistance. I pray to Baba Mahakal that he grant place at his divine feet to the departed souls and bestow strength upon the grieving families to bear this sorrow,” the CM said in an X post.
A high alert has been issued across 21 districts of Madhya Pradesh. In Bhopal, rising water levels have submerged railway tracks, temples, police stations and residential areas. Several roads in Sehore and Shajapur have been shut due to flooding, while a bridge in Raisen was washed away.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the state has received 17.8 inches (453 mm) of rainfall so far.

headline: Dhruv Rathee’s video allegedly disparaging deities withheld, Google tells HC
full_text:
Dhruv Rathee’s video allegedly disparaging deities withheld, Google tells HC
The Grievance Appellate Committee directed the video’s removal months after YouTuber Dhruv Rathee uploaded it on March 21
Google withheld a video of YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in India over allegations that it disparaged Hindu deities after the government’s online dispute resolution body directed its removal on July 15, the platform informed the Delhi high court on Tuesday. It told a bench of Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma that the video could not be removed globally as the issue remains pending before a division bench.
The Grievance Appellate Committee directed the video’s removal months after Rathee uploaded it on March 21.
Google’s submission on Tuesday came as the court heard lawyer Amita Sachdeva’s plea seeking directions for the removal of the video. In her plea, Sachdeva said the committee had ordered the video’s removal on July 15, but Google had failed to comply with the direction.
She claimed that the video contained harmful content. Sachdeva called it hurtful and defamatory, since Rathee allegedly said that Hindu gods had meat and alcohol. Her petition will be next heard on September 3.
The committee’s order came after the high court on July 3 directed the government to decide within 15 days the petition seeking removal of Rathee’s video.
Sachdeva also filed a complaint against Rathee in a Delhi court seeking registration of a case. She alleged that the video insulted Sanatan Dharma, distorted Hindu scriptures, spread anti-Hindu sentiment, and incited religious disharmony, all of which are grave offences requiring urgent attention.

headline: The Federation of Karnataka State Private Transport Associations has urged the Karnataka government to address a range of issues affecting the private transport sector, including bike taxis, app-based aggregators, the Shakti scheme and competition fr...
full_text:
The Federation of Karnataka State Private Transport Associations has urged the Karnataka government to address a range of issues affecting the private transport sector, including bike taxis, app-based aggregators, the Shakti scheme and competition from State-run transport corporations.
In a memorandum submitted to the government on Tuesday (August 11), the federation sought a clear policy on bike taxis and strict action against unauthorised app-based transport services. It alleged that private operators and drivers were facing financial difficulties due to high commissions, arbitrary fare structures and increasing competition from app-based companies.
The federation also raised concerns over the impact of the Shakti scheme on private transport operators and sought an alternative mechanism to compensate or support the sector. It suggested measures such as reducing road taxes for contract and stage carriage vehicles.
It also called for a scientific, cost-based fare revision mechanism, with a permitted variation of 20% from government-fixed fares. The federation in a release stated it has given the government 15 days to respond to its demands, failing which it said it would decide on the next course of “democratic and legal action”.

headline: Disease outbreak in MP’s Balaghat kills 6 children, over 100 sick: Officials
full_text:
Disease outbreak in MP’s Balaghat kills 6 children, over 100 sick: Officials
Experts are now supervising treatment, with acute nutritional deficiencies also detected among children
At least six children died and 101 others fell ill in four Baiga tribe-dominated villages of Madhya Pradesh’s Balaghat district in the past month, officials said on Tuesday.
“The children died of multiple infections. Blood samples have been sent to the ICMR-National Institute of Research in Bacterial Infections, Kolkata, and the ICMR-National Institute of Virology, Pune to ascertain the exact cause,” said Paresh Upalap, chief medical health officer (CMHO), Balaghat.
The district administration has set up temporary health camps in the affected villages.
Officials said children between the ages of one and 13 in Adori, Kundeksa, Bondari, and Korka villages were suffering from high fever, rashes, red spots, stomach ache, and ulcers since July. Six of them died, 47 are admitted to the hospital, while 54 are being treated at home.
“Initially, villagers relied on faith healing and rituals. When conditions worsened, they rushed to hospitals in Baihar and Balaghat. The delay in proper treatment cost lives,” said a doctor on condition of anonymity.
Also Read:9 of family killed in Madhya Pradesh’s Rajgarh as flooded drain sweeps van away
Villagers, however, blame the delayed action of the health department. “Children were falling ill for weeks. In the absence of health facilities, six died. Only now has the health department started camps,” said Parasram Dhurve, head of Adori village.
A team from Jabalpur Medical College, led by epidemiologist Dr Ravindra Vishnoi is investigating the outbreak in the villages.
Experts are now supervising treatment, with acute nutritional deficiencies also detected among children. A report has been sent to the health department in Bhopal, the CMHO confirmed.

headline: Family members of railway employees belonging to the erstwhile Waltair Division, currently posted in the Rayagada (RGDA) Division under East Coast Railway, staged a demonstration outside the Divisional Railway Manager’s (DRM) office in the city on Tu...
full_text:
Family members of railway employees belonging to the erstwhile Waltair Division, currently posted in the Rayagada (RGDA) Division under East Coast Railway, staged a demonstration outside the Divisional Railway Manager’s (DRM) office in the city on Tuesday, demanding the release of the Joint Procedure Order (JPO) and a review of postings made in Visakhapatnam since June 1, when South Coast Railway came into existence as a separate zone.
In a representation submitted to the DRM, the employees said Para 9.3 of the DPR provided for willingness/options to be obtained from staff for postings in the Visakhapatnam and Rayagada divisions. They alleged that the process has not been extended to them.
They protestors sought protection of seniority and lien, and demanded a halt to fresh postings pending finalisation of the JPO.
Family members also visited the South Coast Railway (SCoR) zonal headquarters in the VMRDA Deck Building, Siripuram, and submitted a similar representation to the authorities.
Bholanath, divisional secretary of the All India Loco Running Staff Association, Visakhapatnam Division, said the bifurcation between South Coast Railway and East Coast Railway had left many employees stationed away from their families.
“When employees belonging to safety category are placed under such stress, it is not good for railways safety,” he said.
Senapati Kalavathi, a resident of Pendurthi whose husband is posted in Koraput, alleged that senior staff had been retained at outstation locations while some junior employees were posted to Visakhapatnam along with promotions. “We only want the same justice to be done to us,” she said.
Chalasani Gandhi, senior retired railway trade union leader, said that employees who once were part of a single seniority group now stood divided. He demanded immediate issuance of a JPO or a mutually agreed MoU to bring clarity on seniority, promotions and transfer policies for employees of both divisions.
“There should be a meeting at the Railway Board level, with the All India Railwaymen’s Federation (AIRF) and National Federation of Indian Railwaymen (NFIR) presenting the employees’ case alongside the two general managers,” he said.

headline: Chandra Kumar Bose, Netaji's grandnephew, plans Azad Hind Party inspired by Gen Z
full_text:
Chandra Kumar Bose, Netaji's grandnephew, plans Azad Hind Party inspired by Gen Z
Chandra Kumar Bose says he will launch the Azad Hind Party, drawing inspiration from the Gen Z-led Jantar Mantar protests and seeking to channel growing youth frustration over corruption through Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's inclusive and secular ideology.
Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s grandnephew Chandra Kumar Bose, who recently resigned from the Trinamool Congress after an earlier stint with the BJP, has announced plans to launch his own political outfit inspired by the recent Gen Z-led protests at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar.
The move marks another turn in Bose’s political journey. He had joined the TMC ahead of the West Bengal Assembly elections after quitting the BJP and describing his decision to join the saffron party as a “mistake”. He subsequently left the Mamata Banerjee-led party as well, citing personal reasons.
Speaking to India Today, Bose said the proposed Azad Hind Party would be built around young people and follow what he described as Netaji’s inclusive and secular ideology.
“Nearly 80 years after Independence, the youth are once again stepping forward. We saw that spirit in the Jantar Mantar protests,” Bose said.
He alleged that widespread corruption in politics and institutions had left young Indians frustrated with the existing system.
“There’s rampant corruption across the country. All political parties are involved. In education, health infrastructure and industry, corruption has become a way of life,” he said.
Bose said young people were “fed up” with governments, the administration and other institutions and needed political space to fight for their rights.
“What could be better than fighting under the banner of Netaji’s Azad Hind Fauj, the Azad Hind Party?” he said.
FROM BJP TO TMC, AND NOW HIS OWN PARTY
Bose joined the BJP in 2016 and remained with the party for around seven years. He claimed he had been assured that an Azad Hind Morcha would be created within the BJP to promote Netaji’s ideology.
According to Bose, he was expected to lead the proposed platform and take its message across the country.
“I waited for seven years, patiently waited. But the Azad Hind Morcha was not formed,” he said.
“Why wasn't it formed? Only the BJP leadership can answer that question. They had made a commitment. Otherwise, I would have never joined BJP,” Bose added.
After quitting the BJP, he joined the Trinamool Congress ahead of the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections, saying the party had offered him another opportunity to work around Netaji’s political legacy.
“In April 2026, I was told that they believed in Netaji’s ideology and that I could work in the party and spread his ideology,” Bose said.
He later resigned from the TMC, citing personal reasons. Bose has also criticised what he described as “mundane, low-level politics” within mainstream parties.
‘PARTY OF THE YOUTH’
Bose said the Azad Hind Party would seek to bring together young people who identify with progressive, inclusive and secular politics.
“All progressive, inclusive, secular people, particularly the youth, I think, would support the Azad Hind Party,” he said.
He added that the outfit would seek to contribute to nation-building based on Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s ideology.
For Bose, the recent Gen Z protests provided the immediate trigger for attempting to create an independent political platform after his stints with both the BJP and TMC.
Whether the Azad Hind Party can convert that youth discontent and the appeal of Netaji’s legacy into electoral support will be its first major test.

headline: Number of injured on Air India Phuket-Delhi flight that dropped 300 feet rises to 24
full_text:
Number of injured on Air India Phuket-Delhi flight that dropped 300 feet rises to 24
It was earlier reported that fourteen passengers on board the flight were injured after it dropped about 300 feet due to turbulence before landing safely.
The number of injured people on the Air India Phuket-Delhi flight that dropped 300 feet has risen to 24, four crew members, a Press Information Bureau release said on Tuesday.
On August 4, the Phuket-Delhi flight AI2379 experienced a sudden 300-foot drop in altitude during cruise, injuring passengers and crew members. An initial statement from Air India had cited turbulence as the reason.
The aircraft was carrying 137 passengers, including three infants, and eight crew members comprising two pilots and six cabin crew. It was earlier reported that fourteen passengers on board the flight were injured after it dropped about 300 feet due to turbulence before landing safely.
Soon after the incident, the aircraft stabilised and landed safely in Delhi. As part of prescribed procedures, both pilots underwent a screening for psychoactive substances after the flight landed. The pilot-in-command (PIC) of the flight tested positive for a psychoactive substance, HT had earlier reported.
“The pilot in question has tested positive in the confirmatory test. He has tested positive for Marijuana,” an official aware of the details in the report told HT.
Technical glitch responsible for the incident?
Earlier, people familiar with the matter cited a preliminary defect report (PDR) prepared by the pilots, suggesting that the incident was preceded by multiple technical glitches, including an autopilot disconnection.
Also Read | ‘Flight dropped 300 feet’: Woman recalls terrifying Air India Phuket-Delhi turbulence
Two people aware of the matter said the pilots mentioned technical issues with the aircraft in the PDR. “The PDR mentioned that the autopilot disconnected. It also mentioned a stall warning and a flight control ECAM (Electronic Centralised Aircraft Monitor) message,” said one of these persons, requesting anonymity.
A second official said the matter “is being investigated considering all the angles, including suspected technical glitch.”
The airline’s spokesperson, however, did not comment on the development, citing the ongoing probe. “As the investigative process is ongoing, Air India cannot comment on any findings or observations related to the investigation. We will continue to extend our full cooperation to relevant authorities as required,” the spokesperson said.
On Wednesday, civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu said two crew members who suffered spinal injuries in the incident remained admitted at Fortis Hospital.
The AAIB is investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident, while the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is responsible for regulatory action based on the investigation's outcome and the prescribed testing process.

headline: Rainwater accumulates in Noida Airport, authorities say ‘cleared in 30 minutes’
full_text:
Rainwater accumulates in Noida Airport, authorities say ‘cleared in 30 minutes’
The Noida Airport statement added that there was no impact on flight operations or the overall functioning of the airport.
Rainwater accumulated on Tuesday in a part of the Noida International Airport in Uttar Pradesh's Jewar, less than two months after it started operations.
The airport saw its first flight take off and land on June 15, while the airport was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on March 28.
Videos of water running inside the airport premises went viral on social media.
According to a statement from the Noida Airport, the water was cleared within 30 minutes.
“Following extremely heavy rainfall over a short time period, rainwater temporarily entered the passage connecting the terminal with the parking area. Airport teams responded promptly, clearing the water under 30 minutes,” the NIA statement said.
The statement added that there was no impact on flight operations or the overall functioning of the airport.
“We continue to monitor the situation closely and remain prepared to ensure seamless passenger movement,” it further said.
Delhi’s August rainfall crosses normal mark in just 10 days
The quantum of showers this August in Delhi has gone past the weather department’s long-period average for the month, which still has three weeks to go, underscoring what has been an unusually wet spell for the Capital deep into the monsoon.
The Safdarjung station – considered Delhi’s representative weather gauge – clocked just 4mm of rain on Monday, enough to drive the month’s total to 234.5mm, past the India Meteorological Department’s (IMD) long-period average (LPA) of 233.1mm for the month.
This is the earliest rains in Delhi have crossed the mark in at least 15 years, with just seven days of showers in the first 10 days of the month. Last year, Delhi clocked a significant rain surplus, with 400.81mm of precipitation between August 1 and 31, but it crossed the LPA only on August 15, after 11 days of rain.
In 2024, the city took one more day to reach the same mark, crossing the LPA on August 16, after 13 days of rain.

headline: IMD gets its rain data wrong, then quietly fixes it. Delhi yet to cross its average for August showers
full_text:
IMD gets its rain data wrong, then quietly fixes it. Delhi yet to cross its average for August showers
Delhi rain news: IMD had also updated rainfall data for August 5-6 to 18.77mm in the current chart, in comparison to the earlier 56mm.
A brief spell of showers in Delhi on Monday helped push the quantum of rain this August past the long-period average for the month. Or did it?
On Monday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said Delhi had received 234.5mm of rain in the first 10 days of August this year, more than the month’s total expected quantum of 233.1mm.
On Tuesday, IMD quietly cut this month’s rain figure to 197.2mm in its bulletin.
Hours later, IMD, in response to a query from HT, said the cumulative August rain numbers it released on Monday were “incorrect” and that the Capital was still about 36mm short of its expected August rain quota.
ALSO READ | Delhi traffic cripples as rain causes waterlogging amid Kanwar Yatra chaos
“That (the earlier figure) was incorrect. 197.2mm is the correct figure being displayed now,” said an IMD official in the agency’s WhatsApp group for national media.
Another official confirmed the error.
IMD officials declined to pinpoint the cause of the error.
August 6 rain data ‘corrected’
HT compared the weather agency’s monthly online weather chart for Delhi which details the daily rain and maximum-minimum temperatures for the month with an earlier version of the same chart.
It found that the entry for rainfall between 8.30am on August 5 and 8.30am August 6 was updated from 56mm in the earlier version to 18.7mm in the chart currently visible on the site.
The difference – 37.3mm – corresponds to the shortfall in IMD’s rain readings for August this year between its logs on Monday and Tuesday.
An IMD official confirmed the discrepancy.
“Safdarjung’s cumulative rainfall data displayed yesterday was 230.5mmwhich happened due to incorrect rainfall entry of 56 mm instead of 18.7 mm for August 6 in the table...However it was correctly displayed in the Delhi bulletin issued every day in August. This has been corrected and 197.2mm is the correct figure, which is being displayed currently,” said Krishna Mishra, regional meteorological scientist, IMD.
IMD has ‘gone wrong’ before
IMD has often gone wrong with its predictions of rain, Tuesday being a case in point. Monday was an occasion the weather agency was also wrong with its logs.
The agency at 2:30pm on Tuesday issued an orange alert, predicting light or moderate rain for most parts of the city, with heavy showers in some pockets. The IMD categorizes rainfall up to 15.5mm as light, between 15.6mm to 64.4 mm as moderate, between 64.5mm to 115.5mm as heavy, and between 115.6 to 204.4 as very heavy.
ALSO READ | Kanwar Yatra, rain trigger long snarls on Delhi-Gurugram roads
By 5.30pm, Safdarjung was the wettest part of Delhi with 4mm of rain. Delhi Ridge recorded 3.7mm, followed by Mayur Vihar and Pusa at 3mm each. Chhatarpur and Narayana both clocked 2mm of rain, followed by Ayanagar (1.6mm), Lodi Road (1.5mm), and Palam (1.4mm). Najafgarh got 1.5mm, with Jafarpur (1mm) and Jharoda Kalan (1mm) next. Pushp Vihar recorded no rain during the same period.
The IMD has predicted “very light to light rain” on Wednesday and Thursday.

headline: Man kills 2 daughters, attempts suicide at 5-star hotel near Bengaluru airport
full_text:
Man kills 2 daughters, attempts suicide at 5-star hotel near Bengaluru airport
The police said that a note purportedly referring to a dispute over an alleged extramarital relationship was found in the Bengaluru hotel room.
A 35-year-old man allegedly murdered his two daughters, aged five and 10, before attempting to die by suicide at a five-star hotel near Bengaluru’s Kempegowda International Airport on Monday, police said.
Investigators said the girls were found dead inside a room at the hotel. The man, who was lying unconscious with severe throat injuries in the same room, was rushed to a private hospital, where his condition is stated to be critical, police said.
Also read | Bengaluru delivery boy abused in Hindi by girls, beaten by male friends; incident caught on cam
CCTV footage, digital evidence being examined
“We are also examining CCTV footage, digital evidence and other material collected. Once the accused is medically fit, his statement will be recorded,” said deputy commissioner of police (DCP) GK Mithun Kumar.
The premises are being examined by forensic personnel, who are expected to collect samples and other material that could help establish the sequence of events and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.
“Further action will be taken based on the evidence,” the deputy commissioner added.
Also read | Bengaluru man, 24, slits grandmother's throat after repeated arguments over having no job
What was mentioned in the note?
The officer said that a note purportedly referring to a dispute over an alleged extramarital relationship was found in the room. However, it has not been established if the alleged dispute was linked to the deaths.
“The contents of the note are being examined, and we are verifying the allegations mentioned in it. At this stage, it would be premature to arrive at any conclusion regarding the motive,” said Kumar.
Police said the man worked as a manager with a private firm. The room in question is on the fourth floor of the hotel.
Investigators said they were verifying the booking details and the bodies were sent to a mortuary for post-mortem examination to determine the exact cause of death.

headline: Bay low-pressure system to bring heavy rain to Bengal; fishermen warned
full_text:
Bay low-pressure system to bring heavy rain to Bengal; fishermen warned
The Regional Meteorological Centre, Kolkata, said an upper-air cyclonic circulation is currently lying over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas.
West Bengal is likely to see another spell of heavy rain as a low-pressure area is expected to develop over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas on Wednesday, August 12, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
The system is likely to strengthen rainfall activity across south Bengal, with several districts expected to receive heavy to very heavy showers over the next few days.
READ ALSO | Ambenali Ghat closed till Aug 16 amid IMD’s heavy rainfall warning: Officials
Heavy rain forecast in south Bengal
Most parts of south Bengal may receive light to moderate rain or thundershowers on Wednesday. Heavy rainfall of 7 to 11 cm is likely at isolated places in Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly and Bankura.
North 24 Parganas, South 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur and Paschim Medinipur could receive 7 to 20 cm of heavy to very heavy rain.
Jhargram, Purulia and Paschim Bardhaman are also expected to receive heavy rain through August 15.
Kolkata and neighbouring districts may witness thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 30 to 40 kmph. Rainfall is likely to remain active across south Bengal through the week, with heavy showers forecast in several districts on Thursday and Friday.
READ ALSO | Multiple spells of rain expected in Delhi on Tuesday, IMD issues yellow alert
What is driving the rainfall?
The Regional Meteorological Centre, Kolkata, said an upper-air cyclonic circulation is currently lying over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas. It extends up to 7.6 km above mean sea level and tilts southwestwards with height.
Under its influence, a low-pressure area is likely to form over the same region on August 12, increasing rainfall across Bengal.
ALSO READ | Delhi traffic cripples as rain causes waterlogging amid Kanwar Yatra chaos
North Bengal to see fresh spell of rain
North Bengal, which received some relief after heavy rain last week, is likely to turn wetter again from August 14.
Heavy rainfall is expected in Jalpaiguri and Alipurduar on Thursday, while Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Cooch Behar and other northern districts may receive heavy spells over the following days. The wet spell is likely to continue through August 17.
Kolkata records heavy overnight rain
Kolkata remained cloudy on Tuesday, with light to moderate rain still expected in parts of the city.
Heavy rain lashed northern parts of Kolkata on Monday night, inundating several roads and slowing traffic during the Tuesday morning commute.
Dum Dum recorded 101 mm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending at 8.30 am on Tuesday, while Alipur received 62 mm, according to IMD data.
Fishermen advised against venturing into sea
The developing system has also prompted a warning for the coastal areas.
Squally weather with winds of 35 to 45 kmph and gusts reaching 55 kmph is likely along and off the West Bengal and Odisha coasts and over the north Bay from August 11 to 15.
The IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into the sea during this period.

headline: UP hospital claims lab-grown cell therapy used for urethral stricture treatment
full_text:
UP hospital claims lab-grown cell therapy used for urethral stricture treatment
Lucknow, A 30-year-old man has been treated for urethral stricture using lab-grown cells in what a Lucknow hospital has claimed is the "first such procedure" in Uttar Pradesh.
The patient, a Lucknow resident, had a three-centimetre-long bulbar urethral stricture, a narrowing of the urinary passage.
Doctors on Monday claimed the cell-based technique could offer a minimally invasive alternative to conventional procedures for selected patients.
Traditionally, such patients may undergo buccal mucosa graft urethroplasty, in which tissue is taken from inside the cheek, or endoscopic urethrotomy, which carries a risk of recurrence and may require long-term self-catheterisation in some cases, they said.
In the new procedure, doctors said they removed a tiny tissue sample measuring 10 mm by 5 mm from the patient's cheek and sent it to a specialised laboratory in Pune.
Over two weeks, the sample was expanded into nearly 50 lakh living cells. Since the cells remain viable for only about 72 hours, they were transported to Lucknow under a maintained cold chain, the hospital added.
The cells were then mixed with liquid thrombin and delivered endoscopically to the treated area after an incision was made over the stricture, allowing the cells to attach to the wound and promote tissue healing while potentially reducing recurrent scar formation.
Dr Mayank Mohan Agrawal, Director and Head of Urology and Kidney Transplant, Apollomedics Hospital, Lucknow, said, "The entire surgical process was completed in just 15-20 minutes. We do not make any big cut in the mouth, nor is there any cut made on the lower part of the body below the scrotum, unlike what we do in BMGU."
"With this new technique, the tube will be removed after just one week," he said.
Dr Ved Bhaskar, Associate Director, Urology, said the procedure's claimed success rate was 70-80 per cent, comparable to open surgery.
He said it could particularly benefit elderly patients and those with multiple health conditions by avoiding large incisions and reducing recovery time.
The patient was discharged the following day, according to the hospital.
