headline: Cal HC extends interim protection from arrest to Abhishek Banerjee till August 31
full_text:
Cal HC extends interim protection from arrest to Abhishek Banerjee till August 31
Kolkata, The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday extended till August 31 the interim protection from arrest granted to TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee in three criminal proceedings pending against him.
The court also fixed August 25 for passing its final order on Banerjee's petition seeking quashing of the three FIRs registered against him.
Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya extended the interim protection granted to the Diamond Harbour MP till August 31 or until further orders, whichever is earlier.
Refusing to accept one of the complainant's contentions that Banerjee is "super-influential" and that granting interim protection to him will affect the probe and subsequent trial, the court verbally observed that the situation in West Bengal had altered following the change in the ruling dispensation.
On July 30, Justice Bhattacharyya granted interim protection to Banerjee till August 17 in connection with three FIRs against him, lodged at Bhowanipore on May 27, Kalitala on June 16 and Bishnupur on June 16.
On a prayer by Banerjee's lawyer, the court directed the police authorities to supply copies of all the FIRs registered against the Diamond Harbour MP.
The state informed the court on August 6 that a total of 16 FIRs were pending against Banerjee in different police stations across the state over various allegations.
Opposing the prayer for interim protection from coercive action, complainant Abhijit Das' counsel Jayanta Narayan Chatterjee claimed that Banerjee is "super-influential".
He claimed that if the petitioner is not taken into custody, witnesses will be intimidated and prevented from deposing before the trial courts.
Chatterjee also prayed for police protection to his client if Banerjee is granted interim protection, claiming that Das may get "murdered" otherwise.
Justice Bhattacharyya verbally observed that following a change in the government, the situation in the state has changed.
He also asked if Banerjee is so influential even now, then how demolition of his MP office at Amtala was undertaken, regarding which a petition is pending before the high court.
Justice Bhattacharyya noted that the demolition was stalled by the high court during a special sitting on a Sunday, pointing out that this does not support Chatterjee's contention.
The court asked whether the demolition of Banerjee's party office could have been taken up before the current dispensation came to power, maintaining that this goes to show the situation has changed.
Justice Bhattacharyya noted that the demolition was also taken up on a Friday, requiring the court to sit on a weekend.
During the hearing of a petition on Monday seeking permission for a rally in Kolkata on Tuesday, Justice Bhattacharyya had expressed anguish that refusal by police of permission is generally being communicated on Friday evenings, forcing the court to hold special sittings on weekends to hear challenges to those decisions.
Advocate General Surojit Nath Mitra stated that the building on Diamond Harbour Road where Banerjee's MP office was located did not have any sanctioned plan and that the ownership of the property is not in the name of the TMC leader.
Seeking protection for Banerjee in the quashing application, his lawyer Gopal Sankaranarayanan referred to the quashing of 13 FIRs by the high court in October 2025, against Suvendu Adhikari, who was then the leader of the opposition in the Assembly.
The senior advocate stated that Banerjee is cooperating with the investigation and will continue to do so.
Additional Solicitor General SV Raju opposed the prayer for quashing criminal proceedings against Banerjee and interim protection from coercive action, arguing that if an FIR discloses cognisable offence, it cannot be quashed at the threshold stage.
He stated that the investigation is at a nascent stage.

headline: RAW chief meets Bangladesh PM's defence advisor amid strain in bilateral ties
full_text:
RAW chief meets Bangladesh PM's defence advisor amid strain in bilateral ties
RAW chief Parag Jain met Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's defence affairs advisor in Dhaka on Monday. The visit came as both sides try to steady strained bilateral ties.
Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chief Parag Jain met Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's Defence Affairs Advisor Brig Gen (retd) Dr AKM Shamsul Islam in Dhaka on Monday, as India and Bangladesh seek to manage strained bilateral ties and work towards a reset.
According to The Daily Star, Jain led a four-member Indian delegation that arrived in Dhaka on Sunday on an official visit at the invitation of Bangladesh's Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI), the country's spy agency. The delegation included Ashwin Mukund Kotnis, Rahul Negi and Shaibal Roy Chowdhury.
Jain's meeting with Shamsul Islam coincided with Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi's meeting with Tarique Rahman, The Daily Star reported.
The Indian delegation also met the chiefs of other law enforcement agencies and Bangladesh Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed during its stay in Dhaka before returning to New Delhi.
A diplomatic source cited by The Daily Star described Jain's visit as “routine”, saying DGFI delegations visit India while RAW officials visit Dhaka every other year. The visits involve sharing observations and perspectives on the security situation and other matters, the source said.
The visit comes amid efforts to reset India-Bangladesh ties, which deteriorated during the tenure of former chief advisor Muhammad Yunus. Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) won a decisive mandate and took office in March.
The bilateral relationship has also been affected by the issue of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh in 2024 following massive student protests.
Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition to face legal proceedings in the country. India has said it is examining Dhaka's request in accordance with its legal obligations and applicable procedures.
RAW CHIEF'S DHAKA VISIT COMES DAYS AFTER HASINA'S DELHI PRESSER
The RAW chief's visit also came days after Hasina made her first public appearance before international media since fleeing Bangladesh two years ago. During a virtual interaction from Delhi on August 5, she rejected the official account of the 2024 uprising, describing it as a “planned regime change” rather than a peaceful student-led movement.
Hasina also said she would return to Bangladesh in December, despite facing multiple criminal cases and a death sentence handed down in absentia.
Her remarks triggered a sharp response from Dhaka, which accused India of allowing its territory to be used to undermine Bangladesh's sovereignty. Bangladesh described the event as “an affront to the sovereignty of Bangladesh” and said India's decision to allow Hasina's live media interaction had hurt bilateral ties and insulted those killed in the 2024 uprising.
Dhaka said it had conveyed its concerns to New Delhi before the event and warned of its possible impact on bilateral ties.
India had distanced itself from the programme even before it was held. The Ministry of External Affairs said the event was organised by the Foreign Correspondents' Club of South Asia, a private entity, and that the Indian government had no role in hosting or facilitating it. New Delhi also made clear that it did not endorse any views expressed during the event.

headline: On final day on Yatra, relay race-like ‘Daak Kanwar’ takes spotlight
full_text:
On final day on Yatra, relay race-like ‘Daak Kanwar’ takes spotlight
The last days of 'Kanwar Yatra' are dominated by 'Daak Kanwar', an intense practice requiring the pilgrims to carry holy water without stopping midway.
If you happen to cross one of the key transit routes of ‘Kanwariyas’ — devotees who perform the revered Kanwar Yatra — chances are you saw groups of people engaged in a relay race of sorts, passing baton-like objects to each other in coordinated clothes and being assisted by trucks carrying their team memmbers— a practice known as 'Daak Kanwar' that is mostly undertaken on the last two days of the pilgrimage, i.e, 48 hours leading to Shivratri.
The Kanwar Yatra is a yearly holy walk by worshippers Lord Shiva that takes place during the Hindu month of Sawan or Shravan (July to August), in which pilgrims — mostly in saffron clothes — walk to holy rivers, and fill pots with Ganga water while making sure the pots don't touch the ground on the way.
The pilgrims carry these pots on their shoulders using a special bamboo pole called a ‘Kanwar’ and either walk back home or travel in vehicles to pour the water on a ‘Shivling’ at a local temple.
Watch | Kanwar DJs shake car windows
Given the key ritual of fetching holy water from the Ganges, Kanwar Yatra takes place primarily across northern India, moving through states like Uttarakhand where Haridwar is the main hub of Kanwariyas.
The Kanwar movement is also seen in other states like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Jharkhand, where the holy river flows.
What is ‘Daak Kanwar’
On the yatra routes, last two days of the pilgrimage are dominated by Daak Kanwars — pilgrims who do not stop to rest or sleep until reaching their destination after fetching holy water from the Ganges.
In a regular Kanwar Yatra, the Kanwariyas walk to collect holy water from the Ganges River and carry it back to offer on a Shiva temple. Daak Kanwars, on the other hand, complete the journey as quickly as possible, often by running or jogging.
The word "Daak" comes from the Hindi/Urdu word for mail or post, referring to the old postal runners who carried messages rapidly without long breaks.
The 'Daak Kanwar' yatra is mostly done in groups wherein members complete the trip in a relay, passing the kanwar between each other so that it is continuously moving.
Because Daak Kanwar participants often travel at higher speeds and through the night, it is considered more physically demanding than the regular Kanwar Yatra and requires significant endurance and planning.
Why do people undertake a ‘Daak Kanwar’?
Many devotees are believed to undertake the Daak Kanwar to fulfill a mannat (religious vow), many others do it merely as an act of devotion and penance to Lord Shiva.
Rules commonly followed during regular Kanwar Yatra and Daak Kanwar Yatra vary by region and tradition but motly include maintaining the purity of the kanwar and the sacred water, avoiding intoxicants as well as non-vegetarian food and remaining barefoot or wearing simple footwear, depending on local custom.
The most critical ritual of Kanwar Yatra is ensuring the kanwar, the pot carrying holy water, is not placed directly on the ground without a proper stand.
Pilgrims undertaking the Kanwar Yatra gather holy water from the Ganges River at sacred sites like Haridwar, Gaumukh, Gangotri, and Rishikesh in Uttarakhand, or Sultanganj in Bihar, Tarakeshwar in West Bengal.
Devotees walk back carrying the water to offer it at local Shiva temples or major shrines on Shivratri, which is being observed on August 11 this year.
HT report on Kanwar Yatra window-rattling music
While most Delhi residents have been dealing with traffic snarls and disruption as hundreds of devotees participating in the annual Kanwar Yatra traverse the city, those living next to temporary camps for Kanwariyas have borne a more immediate brunt: days of blaring music, rattling windows, disrupted sleep and clogged neighbourhood roads.
Through Monday, HT visited B-Block in Ramesh Nagar – a west Delhi neighbourhood between Kirti Nagar and Rajouri Garden – with a sound meter to track the sound levels there and found that the levels of exposure were high enough to cause long-term hearing damage. Residents there said the steady movement of devotees and two Kanwar camps set up below the Ramesh Nagar metro station had turned daily life into a struggle. Read full report here

headline: A 24-year-old driver who was assaulted allegedly by a group of kanwariyas died at a hospital in New Delhi on August 4.
full_text:
A 24-year-old driver who was assaulted allegedly by a group of kanwariyas died at a hospital in New Delhi on August 4.
The victim, Mohd Azeem, hailed from Moradabad in Uttar Pradesh. According to an FIR filed on a complaint from his father, Mohd Intezar, Azeem was driving a mini-truck from Moradabad towards Delhi for work on July 31 when it collided with an autorickshaw in Hapur district. The autorickshaw was being driven by 19-year-old Mohd Farman and was carrying several passengers who, according to the complaint, were kanwariyas.
Kanwariyas are devotees of Lord Shiva and carry water from the Ganga to their hometowns across north India during the Hindu month of Shravan.
“Following the collision, the autorickshaw driver and the passengers, Manish, Ankit, Lokesh and Shivam, and two others, assaulted my son severely,” the FIR states. Azeem sustained serious injuries and was taken to a nursing home in Garhmukhteshwar, from where he was referred to a higher medical centre.
Azeem was subsequently shifted to SS Hospital in Meerut, where his condition remained critical and he slipped into a coma. He was later taken to Delhi, where he died on August 4 without responding to treatment, according to his family.
His father told The Hindu on Monday (August 10, 2026) that Azeem was the sole breadwinner of a family of five. He is survived by his wife, one-year-old son, and his elderly parents.
According to the Hapur police, the autorickshaw driver also suffered serious injuries and is in a critical condition. Garhmukteshwar Station House Officer Devendra Singh said another FIR was lodged on August 3 on a complaint from Mr. Farman’s father, who alleged that it was Azeem who tried to kill Mr. Farman.
“His father said Azeem ran down Farman, not once but twice. He then drove over Farman’s abdomen and chest, before fleeing the scene. But now as Azeem is dead, we are initiating the process of filing a closure report in the the FIR against him,” said the police official.

headline: 'Well done': After Gen Z, Alpha get into protest arena in UP; CJP's Dipke, Das give a shoutout
full_text:
'Well done': After Gen Z, Alpha get into protest arena in UP; CJP's Dipke, Das give a shoutout
Schoolchildren marched several kilometres from Chandupur and nearby villages to the Collectorate, demanding a proper road.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has endorsed a ‘Gen Alpha’ protest in Uttar Pradesh’s Hamirpur, where schoolchildren blocked the main gate of the district Collectorate on Tuesday to demand a proper road connecting their villages.
The ‘Gen Alpha’ schoolchildren marched several kilometres from Chandupur and nearby villages to the Collectorate. They were seen carrying the tricolour, placards and banners. They were accompanied by their parents and other residents, HT has learnt.
“Well done,” CJP spokesperson Saurav Das, reacting to the video, said.
The kids were protesting the poor condition of a roughly 1.5-km road serving several settlements along the Yamuna belt. The stretch has turned into mud and slush following the rains, making it difficult for residents to travel.
Abhijeet Dipke lends support
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke later also endorsed the protest. Sharing the video on his Instagram Stories, he said, “This Independence Day, let’s pledge to improve government schools in our villages.”
On X, he wrote, "Salute to these kids who are fighting for their future! All they are asking for is a road to their school. Is that too much to ask after nearly 80 years of Independence? This should have been done decades ago. This 15th August, let’s pledge to work for the children and schools of rural India."
ALSO READ | CJP's Abhijeet Dipke kicks off nationwide 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign to gauge public concerns
Nearly 3,000 residents affected
The road is the main access route for nearly 3,000 residents living in Chandupur and surrounding deras, including Brahma ka Dera, Banvasi ka Dera, Athbhaiyan ka Dera, Bachchi ka Dera, Bhikhua ka Dera, Gusai Baba ka Dera and Gangwa ka Dera.
Residents said the condition of the road made it difficult for children to get to school and has also created problems in taking sick people to hospitals.
Children block main gate
As the protesters marched towards the Collectorate on Tuesday morning, SDM Sadar Abhishek Kumar and CO Yashpal Singh, accompanied by police personnel, reached the route and attempted to stop them.
The children still reached the Collectorate and blocked its main gate. Officials tried to persuade them to withdraw the protest, but the children refused to move. Officials and employees inside were left unable to exit.
CJP’s education push
This came a day after Dipke announced a campaign to improve government schools in villages. The 30-year-old, now leading a ‘pressure group’ against the government, asked sarpanches and parents to take up the “social and moral responsibility” of ensuring better basic facilities for children.
Dipke called on people to pledge to the cause on August 15, India’s 80th Independence Day. He said he would begin the campaign from his own village, Hingoli, in Maharashtra’s Marathwada region, by approaching the sarpanch and requesting improvements to the government schools there.
In a video message posted on social media, Dipke said government schools in villages had been “neglected and ignored” over the past 80 years and questioned why children in rural areas continue to lack facilities that are available to students in bigger cities.
Dipke said children in villages still had to walk long distances to attend school and often do not have access to basic facilities such as drinking water and washrooms.
“How difficult it must be for small girls. So, I feel that this August 15, if we should pay attention to anything, it should be to making a new start, and we must begin by correcting our government schools,” he said.
He appealed to village heads across the country to take up the issue and improve schools in their respective villages. Dipke said the CJP would showcase their efforts on its social media platforms, along with credits and visuals.
CJP expands focus beyond student protests
The campaign is another step in the CJP’s expanding youth-focused activities. What began as an online satirical platform launched by Dipke from the US later moved to street protests, including an agitation over the NEET paper leak and issues affecting students.
The movement’s protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar drew students and parents from different parts of the country. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk also joined the agitation.
The protests forced the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister. After the demonstrations ended on July 25, the CJP held a two-day strategy meeting in Maharashtra and announced that it would continue as a youth movement, with Wangchuk as its mentor.
Last week, Dipke also announced the nationwide “Kya Bolti Public” campaign to understand people’s concerns. He said education would be the first focus of the outreach initiative.

headline: FCRA bill may impact Christian groups, Nagaland CM tells Amit Shah
full_text:
FCRA bill may impact Christian groups, Nagaland CM tells Amit Shah
Nagaland CM Rio requested the Centre to reconsider the FCRA amendments, highlighting potential negative effects on Christian groups and humanitarian efforts.
Nagaland chief minister Neiphiu Rio wrote to Union home minister Amit Shah expressing concerns over proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA), becoming the third CM from the Northeast to flag the controversial proposals.
The developments came on a day the Centre said it has not yet received additional suggestions from church representatives who met Shah last week to discuss their concerns about the proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026.
There is no clarity on whether the government will take up the FCRA bill for discussion in the current session. Mizoram CM Lalduhoma said last week that the bill was likely to be debated on August 12. But the business advisory committee – which met last week and on Monday – did not take up the issue of time allocation for the FCRA bill, triggering speculation that the government might not push for its passage in the current session.
In his three-page letter dated August 9, Rio said he had in-depth discussions with Christian leaders and representatives of the Nagaland Baptist Church Council (NBCC) and the Bishop of Kohima, who conveyed their concerns and challenges being faced by churches and Christian organisations in carrying out various activities and humanitarian services.
“The proposed amendments, if implemented in their present form, are likely to further compound these challenges and could adversely impact a number of ongoing welfare, educational, healthcare and social-service programmes in the State. The difficulties are particularly acute for smaller institutions working at the grassroots level, many of which operate with limited resources while serving people in remote, underserved and economically disadvantaged communities,” he said in an X post on Monday.
Rio requested the Centre to consider referring the legislation to a joint parliamentary committee – a demand first made by Lalduhoma after he met Shah last week. Meghalaya CM Conrad Sangma also met Shah with a delegation of Church leaders last month.
Nagaland is 87.93% Christian, Meghalaya is 74% Christian, and Mizoram is 87% Christian.
As part of the government’s outreach to build consensus on the bill, the home minister has already assured the FCRA laws will not be implemented retrospectively. “The government has already assured that the provisions of the bill will not adversely impact any faith or community…it will not be implemented retrospectively. Some groups had said they will send in their additional concerns and suggestions but have not done it so far…” said a senior minister.
Also Read | Maharashtra CM Fadnavis says FCRA bill aims to curb anti-national activities, not target any religion
Shah holds meetings to build consensus
Shah held detailed meetings with several delegations, including church representatives, to build consensus on the FCRA bill, which was introduced during the budget session in March.
Asked whether the government was confident that the outreach will alleviate concerns, the minister quoted above said, “…If there is political intention, then there will be no consensus. We have asked them for suggestions and we are yet to receive those even though reminders have also been sent.”
FCRA Bill may not be taken up this session
Though Lalduhoma said last week that the bill was likely to be debated on August 12, the business advisory committee, which met last week and on Monday, did not take up the issue of time allocation for the FCRA bill, triggering speculation that the Centre might not push for its passage in this session.
The bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in the previous session but was not brought for passing after protests by the Opposition and controversy in then poll-bound Kerala. The bill had evoked sharp reactions from Opposition leaders, particularly Kerala lawmakers, as Christian groups alleged they might be targeted under the new law.
The bill provides for the cessation of the FCRA certificate of an organisation upon expiry, non-renewal or refusal of renewal by the government. The amendments also establish a designated authority for “a comprehensive framework for vesting, supervision, management and disposal of foreign contribution and assets, including provisional and permanent vesting.” A provision stated that the government can appoint a “designated authority” to take over, manage, or sell assets created from foreign funds by an non-governmental organisation whose licence under FCRA was cancelled, suspended, or simply not renewed.
Last Thursday, Lalduhoma – accompanied by a delegation of senior Christian leaders, including representatives from the Council of Churches in Mizoram (CCM) and the Mizoram Kohhran Hruaitute Committee (MKHC) – met Shah and submitted a memorandum about the bill. “We raised six issues with him. Out of those, we were assured that this bill will not have retrospective effect. As for the remaining points we raised, he said he would respond to them in writing and send us his comments. We will have a clear picture only after we receive that reply…,” Lalduhoma said after the meeting.
Opposition seeks JPC review, withdrawal of Bill
Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam’s Rajya Sabha MP P Wilson – who is also the Chairman of the Joint Action Forum on Minorities – also met Shah with a delegation of religious heads representing all denominations on the same day.
He said the delegation requested withdrawal of the bill in its present form. “In the alternative, we said the bill should be referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee for comprehensive stakeholder consultation and a detailed examination of its constitutional, legal and practical implications. And the third demand was to repeal Section 15 of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, so that no provision permitting the vesting of foreign contribution or charitable assets survives in any form,” Wilson said.
The delegation said the proposed amendments would fundamentally alter the existing regulatory framework by introducing provisions on the automatic cessation of registration, the vesting of charitable assets, the government’s management of institutions, and the permanent transfer of assets. “We said these provisions would have far-reaching consequences for educational institutions, hospitals, orphanages, homes for the elderly, healthcare facilities and other charitable institutions serving vulnerable communities across the country.”
Also Read | 'Our internal matter': India rebuffs US lawmakers’ criticism of FCRA bill
Meghalaya CM urges protection of minority rights
Sangma had also urged the Union government to “safeguard” the rights of the minorities, according to a person aware of the details. “The CM urged the government to safeguard the constitutional rights of minority institutions while preserving the objectives of transparency and regulatory oversight. He submitted copies of amendments made by churches from Meghalaya,” said the person quoted above.

headline: In a huge relief to students of ILS Law college in Pune barred from appearing for their semester-end law exams for attendance shortfall, Bombay high court on Monday permitted them to appear for the exams.
full_text:
In a huge relief to students of ILS Law college in Pune barred from appearing for their semester-end law exams for attendance shortfall, Bombay high court on Monday permitted them to appear for the exams.
MUMBAI: In a huge relief to students of ILS Law college in Pune barred from appearing for their semester-end law exams in the academic year 2025-26 for attendance shortfall, Bombay high court on Monday permitted them to appear for the exams as a âstrictly one-time measureââ. Justices Riyaz Chagla and Farhan Dubash relied on a recent July 21 Supreme Court order that permitted students as a one-time relief to appear for their examinations in the academic year 20-26.The HC clarified that its relief would apply to all similarly barred students of the college who had not filed petitions, as it said the SC order had carved out similar placed students as a âprotected classââ. But the bench clarified its order was âconfined to the academic session 2025â26ââ.The HC said its order cannot be construed as diluting the attendance rules for any other academic session. âStudents pursuing legal education shall continue to remain bound by the attendance requirements otherwise applicable to them,ââ the bench said.The HC order came in a batch of petitions filed by 41 students pursuing different years of the 3-year and 5-year law courses conducted at ILS, Pune affiliated to the Savitribai Phule Pune University.
The University said their attendance was tween 46 to 54 % while minimum attendance was 75 %.The petitions said an earlier 70 % rule with 20 % additional waiver rule ought to apply to them and also cited a November 3 2025 Delhi HC order to argue their case.The Delhi HC High Court directed that no student enrolled in a recognised law college in India should be detained or prevented from appearing for examinations or from pursuing academic progression solely on account of shortage of attendance.The SC then stayed the Delhi HC order, prospectively in May. But in July protected students across colleges against a lost academic year of 2025-26, with a one-time reprieve to appear for the final exam in that academic year when the Delhi HC order was passed. The SC order does not prescribe any minimum attendance for the protected class of last academic year student, HC noted.On Monday, disposing of the batch of petitions the Bombay HC clarified that the Delhi HC order did not bind it, but the July SC order did.Six different HCs had differed with Delhi HC.The Pune University and the law college argued that the SC order would apply only to final examination students of the 3 year and 5 year LLB courses. But disagreeing, the HC reasoned and the SC meant âconcluding exam for that academic sessionââ hence the petitioners who were students of first, second, third- or fourth-year stand included.
The HC said, âA student studying in an earlier year who is prevented from appearing for the semester-end examination may equally lose the academic session and, consequently, be unable to progress to the succeeding academic yearââ If the apex court â intended to protect only students in the final year or final semester of the law course, it could readily have said so,ââ the HC explained.The HC clarified it has not dealt with the controversy raised by the students of whether the maximum condonation of 20% contemplated under Ordinance 70 was required to operate upon the minimum attendance requirement of 70% prescribed under Rule 12 of the Legal Education Rules or upon the requirement of 75% prescribed under Ordinance 68. This issue is left open.The HC had earlier granted interim protection to the Petitioners who appeared for their examinations and confirmed the relief. The HC directed the University to conduct supplementary exams within 4 weeks for academic year 2025-26 for those who could not appear.

headline: Nagaland CM urges Shah to reconsider FCRA amendments, seeks parliamentary panel review
full_text:
Nagaland CM urges Shah to reconsider FCRA amendments, seeks parliamentary panel review
Kohima, Nagaland Chief Minister Neiphiu Rio wrote to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, urging him to reconsider the proposed amendments to the FCRA, and stated that the changes in the legislation could lead to a burden on churches and Christian charitable organisations and affect educational, healthcare and social welfare programmes in the state.
Rio proposed that the Foreign Contribution Act amendments be referred to a parliamentary committee for comprehensive examination, with representatives of stakeholders concerned given an opportunity to present their views.
Such a process, he said, would help address genuine concerns, remove apprehensions and build public confidence while protecting transparency, accountability and national interest.
The move would demonstrate the "inclusive and positive approach" of the NDA government and reaffirm India's commitment to constitutional values, secular ethos and respect for the rights and contributions of all communities, the chief minister said in the letter to Shah on Monday.
In June this year, the government notified amended FCRA rules for receiving foreign funds, requiring non-governmental organisations to choose from a predefined list of purposes and areas of operation.
While allowing a range of faith-based activities, the rules explicitly excluded proselytisation from several categories eligible for registration under the Foreign Contribution Act .
The FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026, was introduced in the Lok Sabha on March 25 this year and is likely to be taken up for discussion during the ongoing Monsoon session of Parliament.
Rio said various sections of society, particularly the Christian community, had expressed concerns over the proposed amendments to the law.
He said the Nagaland Baptist Church Council and the Bishop of Kohima had also submitted representations to the union home minister, highlighting difficulties faced by churches and associated charitable organisations.
Rio requested that their representations be considered with due sensitivity, keeping in view Nagaland's unique social, historical and developmental circumstances.
The CM said he had held consultations with Christian leaders, and on August 9, held another round of discussions with the NBCC leadership and representatives of the Bishop of Kohima, who conveyed concerns over challenges faced by churches and Christian organisations in carrying out their activities and humanitarian services.
Pointing out that more than 90 per cent of Nagaland's population is Christian, Rio said churches have historically played a vital role in the state's spiritual and community life as well as in education, healthcare, poverty alleviation, social welfare, livelihood support and assistance to disadvantaged and vulnerable sections.
He said many educational, healthcare, humanitarian and social-service activities, particularly in remote and economically weaker areas, have been supported by legitimate foreign contributions, partnerships and assistance.
According to Rio, increasingly stringent FCRA regulatory and compliance requirements have already imposed considerable financial and administrative burdens on churches and charitable organisations.
The proposed amendments, if implemented in their present form, could further compound these difficulties and adversely affect ongoing welfare, educational, healthcare and social-service programmes.
Rio said smaller grassroots institutions with limited resources could be particularly affected while serving remote and underserved communities.
The chief minister also raised concerns over reports that FCRA renewal applications of some Christian organisations had been declined on grounds relating to the alleged utilisation of foreign contributions for religious conversion.
Given Nagaland's demographic context, he said such cases deserved careful and sensitive examination based on the actual nature and purpose of the organisations' activities.
He stressed that legitimate charitable, educational, healthcare and social-welfare activities should not be inadvertently affected by broad or generalised assumptions, particularly where organisations have otherwise complied with applicable laws.
Rio urged that cases where renewal had been denied be reviewed and examined seriously, objectively and individually, so that genuine welfare activities are not adversely affected.
Highlighting the humanitarian role of churches, Rio said Christian organisations have provided assistance during natural calamities, disasters and emergencies.
He cited their substantial relief work for people affected by the floods and landslides and recalled their contribution during the COVID-19 pandemic, when churches and Christian institutions mobilised resources, infrastructure and volunteers in support of communities and government efforts.
Rio also underlined the more-than-150-year history of Christianity and the Church in Nagaland and its longstanding links with the global Christian community.

headline: Kerala student injured in Maharashtra taekwondo event; family alleges referee negligence
full_text:
Kerala student injured in Maharashtra taekwondo event; family alleges referee negligence
The family alleged that the referee failed to follow rules requiring the official to move along with the contestants.
A 17-year-old Kerala student was seriously injured after being kicked in the head by an opponent during a recent CBSE South Zone Taekwondo competition in Maharashtra, with his family alleging serious lapses on the part of the referee.
Faiz Abdul Jalal, a plus two student of a private English-medium school in Thrissur, is currently on ventilator support at a private hospital here, his family said.
The incident occurred on August 3 during a competition held in Nagpur.
According to his paternal uncle Mujeeb, Jalal was kicked in the groin by his opponent during the bout, following which he moved aside and gave a signal to withdraw from the competition.
Jalal had signalled with his head that he wanted the bout to be stopped, and the referee should have immediately intervened after seeing the signal, Mujeeb told reporters here.
The family alleged that the referee failed to follow rules requiring the official to move along with the contestants and remain within a distance of two metres of them.
The opponent had kicked Faiz in the groin initially, but the referee failed to intervene even after the first foul, the family alleged.
"Instead, the match was not stopped. After Jalal withdrew from the competition and was standing outside the court, the opponent delivered a powerful kick to his head. He was thrown off balance, fell and hit his head on the concrete floor," he alleged.
School authorities immediately rushed the injured teenager to a private hospital in Nagpur, where he underwent emergency surgery on the same day.
"The emergency surgery helped save his life," Mujeeb said.
Later, He was brought to Kochi by air ambulance on Sunday for further expert treatment
The student continues to remain on ventilator support at the hospital here, and his health condition has shown some improvement according to doctors, the family said.
The family has lodged a complaint with the CBSE authorities alleging negligence and an irresponsible approach on the part of the referee.
The family has also decided to pursue legal action in the matter.
"We have lodged a complaint with the CBSE. We will continue our legal fight until he gets justice," Mujeeb said.

headline: Pankaj Yadav, 28, lay on the road, 1 km away from the Jharkhand Assembly, with a swollen foot, trying to explain to those around him where the police baton had struck him. His knees and leg were hurting, he said, and there was pain near his stomach t...
full_text:
Pankaj Yadav, 28, lay on the road, 1 km away from the Jharkhand Assembly, with a swollen foot, trying to explain to those around him where the police baton had struck him. His knees and leg were hurting, he said, and there was pain near his stomach too.
Jharkhand students protest: Follow LIVE updates on August 10, 2026
Yet even as he sat amid the chaos outside the Vidhan Sabha on Monday (August 10, 2026) evening, Mr. Yadav was talking about the examinations that had brought him there.
A JPSC and JSSC aspirant, Mr. Yadav had appeared for the State-level job recruitment examinations four times. Each time, he said, the process had been marred by irregularities. On Monday (August 10, 2026), he joined thousands of other aspirants marching towards the Assembly, carrying with them a frustration that had long outgrown any single examination.
For Sonali Agrawal, a JPSC-CGL aspirant, the march was about the years students were losing while waiting for a recruitment system they could trust. “As students, we are constantly dealing with exam cancellations and paper leaks. Since the formation of Jharkhand, this has been a consistent issue for 26 years,” she said. “These exams are a lifeline for this State’s youth and this is the reason why the issue is still alive.”
The march called by the JPSC-JSSC Reform Manch and the JLKM began at the old Vidhan Sabha around 10.30 a.m. The protesters came demanding the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, accountability for the alleged examination irregularities and an CBI investigation into them.
As the crowd moved closer to the Assembly, police baton-charged the protesters and used tear gas and low-pressure water cannons on them. Later in the evening, the police used heavier force and baton charge to disperse those who remained.
Around 8.30 p.m., YouTuber Parth Kumar told The Hindu that his camera had been destroyed by the police personnel near the Vidhan Sabha complex. “They forced me to delete the footage of lathi charge and then pushed me to the ground with my camera and it broke,” he said.
The police action deepened the anger among the aspirants. “They should directly hit us with a gun. The government is already sucking our youth years,” said 32-year-old Shubam Kumar, an aspirant.
‘Are we terrorists?’
For many in the crowd, the barricades themselves had become part of the message they felt the government was sending them.
Binod, a protester, pointed to the barbed wire around the barricades. “We see these barbed wires on the border with Pakistan. Does the government think that we are terrorists in our own country?” he said.
The anger intensified after the first round of lathi charge. Anand Sagar, 26, suffered an arm injury in the police action. “This dictatorial government is beating us students, but we will give an answer for this treatment through our votes,” Mr. Sagar said. “We came to wish the Chief Minister on his birthday but they beat us black and blue. I can’t even stand up.”
Jitendra, who was present during the baton charge, questioned the government’s response to the students. “This government says that students are like its family. Is this the way to treat family?” he said. “If we are protesting as per the laws, then why is the government beating us like criminals?”
For Ms. Agrawal, the march was ultimately not about a political party or a single day of confrontation. It was about whether students could believe that the years they spend preparing for government jobs would lead to a fair examination. “We demand a CBI investigation because we do not trust the State authorities,” Ms. Agrawal said. “We are not against any party, we just want reforms in the system.”
For some protesters, Monday’s march also brought back memories of earlier demonstrations. Manu, 24, from Ramgarh, had attended the CJP’s July 20 march to Parliament in Delhi, where he suffered a head injury.
“The Delhi Police was much more aggressive. Here the police have let us move forward. We couldn’t even leave the Jantar Mantar site,” he said.
Mr. Manu said he saw a difference in how the two police forces handled the protests. “The Delhi Police should learn from Jharkhand police. They are doing their duty but also supporting the aspirants. Many of them have given the exams we are now giving,” he said.
But the use of force, he added, was still difficult to justify. “Lathi charge was wrong and people got angry, but we reached the Vidhan Sabha premises, even while the police were there,” he said.

headline: Members of Parliament of Nationalist Congress Party Sharadchandra Pawar group met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Monday. While commenting on the meet, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said there was “Nothing wrong with meeti...

Members of Parliament of Nationalist Congress Party Sharadchandra Pawar group met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Monday. While commenting on the meet, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said there was “Nothing wrong with meeting PM”.
“The Prime Minister is of the country and not just of a party. I am also Chief Minister, people from different parties meet me for their work. If they have met, it is good,” Mr Fadnavis said while addressing media persons.
The remarks came following NCP-SP’s eight MPs delegation meeting led by working president Supriya Sule on Monday (August 10, 2026) to discuss several issues related to Maharashtra.
“At the meeting Maharashtra related issues were discussed,” said Mr. Sule, adding that PM assured of positive and concrete measures on all these issues.
According to NCP leader Amol Kolhe, the delegation demanded to award Bharat Ratna to Mahatma Jyotirao Phule, Savitribai Phule, Shahir Anna Bhau Sathe and Tukdoji Maharaj.
“All of eight MPs had some pending matters in their respective constituencies. We have been unable to present these matters in the parliament. Nothing is wrong in presenting these matters to the PM if they could get resolved,” said Mr. Kolhe.
NCP-SP also submitted a memorandum citing their demands. On Saturday, Ms Sule opposed the FCRA Amendments Bill and pointed out that the Centre should either refer it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) before tabling it or withdraw it.
This is the second time that Ms. Sule met the PM in a month. The last meeting was held on July 22, when NCP (SP) chief and her father, Sharad Pawar, met the PM to discuss students’ demands regarding the NEET paper leaks.

headline: A three-member inquiry committee constituted by the Lok Sabha Speaker has found the charges “proved” against Justice Yashwant Varma over the discovery of cash at his official residence, holding that his explanations were “evasive and unsatisfactory”.
full_text:
A three-member inquiry committee constituted by the Lok Sabha Speaker has found the charges “proved” against Justice Yashwant Varma over the discovery of cash at his official residence, holding that his explanations were “evasive and unsatisfactory”.
The committee’s report, tabled in both Houses of Parliament on Wednesday, said Justice Varma had failed to provide a satisfactory explanation regarding the presence, source or ownership of the cash found in the storeroom of his official residence.
Justice Yashwant Varma’s withdrawal from probe cannot end statutory inquiry, says Lok Sabha panel
The committee was headed by Supreme Court judge Justice Aravind Kumar, with Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court, Justice Shree Chandrashekhar, and senior advocate of the Karnataka High Court B.V. Acharya being the other members.
The panel also found that material evidence at the site had not been properly secured or preserved, and that the evidentiary condition of the storeroom had been disturbed before it was lawfully sealed and inspected.
“Evasive and unsatisfactory“
The committee said Justice Varma’s explanation did not demonstrate the “candour, transparency and institutional responsibility” expected of a judge in such circumstances. “It remained evasive and unsatisfactory when tested against the evidence of independent official witnesses and corroborative material,” the committee said.
In its consolidated findings on the three articles of charge, the panel recorded: “The Committee therefore records its final findings that Articles of charges I, II and III are proved.”
The report, submitted in two volumes, contains the oral and documentary evidence gathered during the inquiry. Earlier, the panel submitted its findings to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla in May.
The inquiry committee was constituted under the Judges (Inquiry) Act after allegations emerged following the discovery of burnt currency at Justice Varma’s official residence.
A fire had broken out at the residence of Justice Varma, then a judge of the Delhi High Court, on the night of March 14, 2025. Firefighters responding to the blaze allegedly found large quantities of burnt currency in a storeroom. Nearly 200 MPs subsequently moved a motion seeking his removal from office.
Also read: Justice Yashwant Varma row: The future of inquiry amid his resignation
Justice Varma has since resigned, but his resignation has not yet been notified by the Union Law Ministry. His name continues to appear on the Allahabad High Court website, although the resignation of a judge of the higher judiciary is deemed to be accepted.
If the resignation is taken as accepted, the removal proceedings against Justice Varma would virtually become infructuous.

headline: CBI judge rejects Nirav Modi’s sister’s plea, says accused can’t dictate probe
full_text:
CBI judge rejects Nirav Modi’s sister’s plea, says accused can’t dictate probe
Purvi has been listed as accused no. 31 in CBI’s second supplementary charge sheet. Like her husband, she had earlier applied to become an approver in the case
A Mumbai court has rejected a request by Purvi Modi, sister of fugitive diamantaire Nirav Modi, to appear before the Central Bureau of Investigation via video conference, observing that her physical presence was necessary for detailed questioning and confrontation with the “voluminous” documents, accounts and transactions involved in the case.
Purvi has been listed as accused no. 31 in CBI’s second supplementary charge sheet. She had earlier applied to become an approver in the case, like her husband, Maiank Mehta.
In his order on Monday, special CBI judge SK Karhale noted that Purvi, a Belgian citizen, had failed to respond to a notice issued by the investigating officer in June 2022.
This, the court said, prima facie showed that she had not cooperated with the investigation. The judge also stressed that under Indian criminal law, the investigating officer (IO) of a case exercises complete control over its investigation and “an accused or an approver cannot dictate how the IO should conduct the investigation.”
Also Read | UK court orders Nirav Modi to pay ₹100 cr to Bank of India in loan recovery case
In his request, Purvi told the court that she was settled in Belgium and had been cooperating with the agency. Her lawyer argued that the law and the rules of the high court and the CBI manual permitted statements to be recorded through video conferencing.
CBI opposed the request, saying Purvi was a beneficiary of the alleged fraud and hadn’t cooperated with the investigation. The agency said it wanted to question her in person and that provisions allowing video conferencing did not give her a right to insist on being examined remotely.
The court agreed with the CBI. “In these kinds of serious cases, when the Investigating Officer is insisting on physical presence of the proposed accused, Mrs Purvi Modi, because of her crucial role in the alleged crime, the opportunity of making a fair investigation has to be given to him,” the court said.
Nirav Modi is the prime accused in the ₹13,850 crore fraud at PNB and was declared a fugitive economic offender in December 2019. Modi and his uncle, Mehul Choksi, are accused of defrauding PNB by obtaining fraudulent LoUs, enabling them to secure overseas loans without proper collateral.
The fraud, uncovered in 2018, allegedly involved officials from PNB’s Brady House branch in Mumbai who issued the unauthorised LoUs to Modi’s firms. The total loss to PNB was estimated at ₹6,498 crore. The transactions went unnoticed for several years due to collusion by bank officials. Modi, the mastermind behind the PNB scam, has been fighting his extradition process from the UK, where the authorities arrested him in 2019.
Also Read | Ex-ED officer Satyabrata Kumar who probed Nirav Modi, Vijay Mallya cases takes VRS
The judge pointed to the scale of the case, noting that it involves thousands of crores of rupees and a large volume of documents, accounts, entries and transactions.
Purvi’s physical presence was “just, fair and reasonable,” the court said, as it would allow investigators to confront her with the material, which requires detailed interrogation.
The court also noted that Nirav Modi’s brother Neeshal Modi is another accused and a Belgian citizen. Belgium has rejected the CBI’s plea for his extradition, citing restrictions on extraditing its citizens for offences committed in other countries.

Suspected Pakistani nationals arrested near Bangladesh border by Bengal STF
Two suspected Pakistani nationals were arrested by the Bengal STF near the Bangladesh border in North 24 Parganas and charged with espionage, lawyers said.
Two suspected Pakistani nationals were arrested by the West Bengal Police’s Special Task Force (STF) near the Bangladesh border in North 24 Parganas district on Wednesday and charged with espionage, lawyers for the state said.
“The two men, identified as Rana Rauf Khalid alias Wahab Alam and Md Aziz, were arrested by the STF near the Benapole border when they were trying to enter Bangladesh with the intention of going to Nepal, where they have lived intermittently since 2012. headline: Kuki group ends counter-inter-district economic blockade, highway shutdown
full_text:
Kuki group ends counter-inter-district economic blockade, highway shutdown
The group launched a counter-economic blockade on July 27 in retaliation for a Naga group’s inter-district economic blockade on all national highways
A Kuki organisation ended an indefinite counter-inter-district economic blockade and shutdown of the National Highway (NH) 202 connecting ethnic violence-hit Manipur with neighbouring Nagaland in Ukhrul following a meeting with the state government representatives on Tuesday.
The Working Committee of the Kuki Civil Society Organisation said the counter-blockade was lifted effective from 4.30pm on Tuesday after a meeting with state home minister Govindas Konthoujam and ruling Bharatiya Janata Party lawmaker Thokchom Radheshyam in Ukhrul. The committee said a handwritten agreement was signed with the government delegation, under which it agreed to ensure the safety and security of NH-202 and prevent any group from imposing blockades or disrupting traffic along the vital highway.
The assurances included the “free and non-discriminatory” movement of essential commodities, a key demand amid concerns over restrictions on supplies and movement.
The Kuki body launched a counter-economic blockade on July 27 in retaliation for a Naga group’s inter-district economic blockade on all national highways in Manipur. The counter-blockade intensified the shutdown from August 5.
The Naga group imposed the blockade demanding justice for six Nagas whose mutilated bodies were found on June 10 after Kuki groups allegedly abducted them on May 13.
There was no word from the United Naga Council on lifting its ongoing economic blockade.
Naga and Kuki-Zo tensions escalated after May 13 twin ambushes left four people, including three church leaders, dead. On the same day, Kuki-Zo and Naga groups captured 48 people. On May 15, 14 captives each from the two communities were released. The remaining 14 Kuki-Zo hostages were freed unharmed on June 9. Mutilated bodies of the six Nagas were found the next day.
The ethnic violence in Manipur first began in 2023 between the Meitei and Kuki communities before involving almost every community. The state’s Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities have shut each other out of the areas they dominate.
The Meiteis, mostly Hindu, live largely in the Imphal valley. The Kukis, predominantly Christian, reside in the hills. The state government has maintained that there are no buffer zones dividing communities in the state, but it has identified certain sensitive areas.
A new government was formed in February, nearly a year after the imposition of President’s Rule. It includes representatives from all three major communities as part of an attempt to maintain ethnic balance. But sporadic violence has continued and has left over 260 people dead and displaced 60,000.

Tamil Nadu assembly backs 543 Lok Sabha seat freeze
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu assembly on Wednesday passed a special resolution in the urging the Centre to permanently retain the Lok Sabhaâs strength at 543 seats.Days after convening a meeting of parties supporting his government, including the Congress and the Left parties that extend support from outside, CM Vijay moved the resolution in the assembly urging the Centre to maintain the Lok Sabha-Rajya Sabha seat ratio at 2.2:1.The government-sponsored resolution urged the Centre to implement 33 per cent reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections without delay, based on the existing strength of 543 seats.
"The 33% reservation for women should be implemented in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections itself, based on the existing 543 constituencies. The 33% reservation for women should not be delayed any further. In Tamil Nadu, more women have voted than men. Providing reservation for women is not a concession; it is a matter of social justice. The 33% reservation for women must be implemented without any further delay," Vijay said in the assembly.The resolution noted that the population of states, including Tamil Nadu, and the Union Territories has not been counted for more than five decades, with the next census scheduled for 2026."All the states including Tamil Nadu and the people / elected representatives of the union territories have not had their population counted for more than 50 years.
The next census to count the population was supposed to be held in 2026. Therefore, since the delimitation of constituencies has not been carried out for the last 50 years, based on the 2011 population census, the constituencies should be delimited and the number of Lok Sabha and Assembly members should be increased from 550 to 850 by bringing in a constitutional amendment Bill," the resolution stated.Last week, a meeting convened by Vijay with Tamil Nadu MPs from alliance and friendly parties decided to oppose the Union governmentâs proposed delimitation exercise in its entirety.The meeting was boycotted by the main opposition DMK and the AIADMK, with the former calling the deliberations a âfarceâ and the latter describing them as a âhurriedly staged dramaâ.The MPs had demanded that the ratio of seats between the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha be maintained at 2.2:1. They also unanimously agreed to adopt a resolution in the state Assembly to permanently safeguard the interests of Tamil Nadu and other southern states in the delimitation process.Meanwhile, the AIADMK called the meeting a âhurriedly staged dramaâ, pointing out that no fresh delimitation Bill had been introduced in Parliament and that there had been no official announcement on the exercise.While the Congress and other opposition parties have supported the Women's Reservation Bill, they have opposed linking its implementation to the delimitation exercise and have demanded that the two be delinked.
The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, was passed by both Houses of Parliament. However, its implementation has not moved forward after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill fell in the Lok Sabha on April 17, failing to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting.

headline: After anti-NEET bill, Vijay-led Tamil Nadu govt votes to freeze Lok Sabha strength at 543
full_text:
After anti-NEET bill, Vijay-led Tamil Nadu govt votes to freeze Lok Sabha strength at 543
The resolution also called for the immediate implementation of the 33 per cent women's reservation in the existing 543 seats in the Lok Sabha.
A day after a bill seeking the removal of the NEET examination was moved in the Tamil Nadu assembly, Chief Minister Vijay moved a resolution on the delimitation and women's reservation bill.
As per reports, the TVK leader's resolution urges the Centre to maintain the Lok Sabha-Rajya Sabha ratio at 2.2 : 1 by keeping the seats fixed at 543.
The resolution also called for the immediate implementation of the 33 per cent women's reservation in the existing 543 seats in the Lok Sabha.
"All the states including Tamil Nadu and the people / elected representatives of the union territories have not had their population counted for more than 50 years. The next census to count the population was supposed to be held in 2026. Therefore, since the delimitation of constituencies has not been carried out for the last 50 years, based on the 2011 population census, the constituencies should be delimited and the number of Lok Sabha and Assembly members should be increased from 550 to 850 by bringing in a constitutional amendment Bill," the resolution stated.
The state government is all set to argue that in case the delimitation is carried out by the Centre based on any census taken after 1971, the parliamentary representation of southern states, including Tamil Nadu, which have effectively controlled their population, will be permanently affected.
“Even though Tamil Nadu has built a strong Tamil Nadu by effectively implementing population control measures on the basis of the 1971 population census, the representation of the southern states, including Tamil Nadu, in Parliament will be permanently affected. This is an undeniable truth,” the resolution added.
Tamil Nadu's push against NEET
On Tuesday, the state assembly passed two separate resolutions against the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET).
The TVK government, led by Vijay, called for the abolition of the NEET exam, stating that it was against social justice and state rights.
"This examination has completely lost the trust of students across the nation. Therefore, this examination system must be abolished,” he told the assembly.
The government also moved a resolution against the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bill.
Both the resolutions were passed in the House amid a walkout from the opposition Bharatiya Janata Party.

headline: Video shows pitbull attacking couple on house hunt in Patiala; woman undergoes surgery
full_text:
Video shows pitbull attacking couple on house hunt in Patiala; woman undergoes surgery
A video of the incident shows the pet dog dashing out and attacking Shifali the moment the gate of the house was opened.
A couple suffered multiple grievous injuries in an attack by a pitbull dog outside a house in Patiala on Tuesday evening, an incident that has raised fresh concerns over the safety of residents amid repeated cases of dog attacks in the city.
The incident, CCTV footage of which has gone viral, took place when the couple – Ankit Sabharwal and his wife Shifali – went to Ghuman Nagar along with a property dealer to view a house for rent.
A video of the incident shows the pet dog dashing out and attacking Shifali the moment the gate of the house was opened. The dog is seen attacking her arm and other parts of her body, causing deep injuries. Gradually, the pitbull is seen attacking Ankit in a similar manner, leaving him with deep injuries on his legs and back while trying to protect his wife.
A woman emerges from the house with a stick but fails to control the dog. Subsequently, a few local residents wielding sticks and wipers are seen approaching the dog as the couple tries to escape.
“We had gone to check out a property we were planning to rent. The pitbull suddenly came and attacked us. My wife suffered multiple injuries and had to undergo a surgery at Amar Hospital,” Ankit said.
Ankit said the police have been informed about the incident and sought action against those responsible for allegedly allowing the dog to roam freely.
Patiala police said a First Information Report (FIR) will be registered against the pet owner under section 291 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita on the basis of the victims’ statements.
Earlier, on August 9, a girl was allegedly mauled by a stray dog while passing through Guru Nanak Nagar area.
Taking note of the latest incident, a senior official at Patiala Municipal Corporation said keeping of ferocious breeds, including pit bulls, as pets is banned by the civic body. However, enforcement of such restrictions on the ground remains a challenge.
When contacted, Patiala Municipal Corporation Commissioner Pooja Grewal said pit bulls, considered to be one of the ferocious dog breeds, cannot be kept as pets as per rules. “It is very unfortunate. Our teams have already approached the victims. We are checking all the records and will also take action in the matter,” she said.
Punjab is witnessing a massive surge in cases of dog bites. From 1.10 lakh cases in 2020, the state reported 3.34 lakh dog bite cases in 2025 — the highest ever recorded in a single year.

headline: Trump aide who called India ‘maharaja of tariffs’ says faced ‘nasty attacks’ for remarks. Who is Peter Navarro?
full_text:
Trump aide who called India ‘maharaja of tariffs’ says faced ‘nasty attacks’ for remarks. Who is Peter Navarro?
Peter Navarro has repeatedly attacked India's trade policies involving Russia and has accused the country of helping fund Russia's "war machine" in Ukraine.
White House trade adviser Peter Navarro, who has repeatedly criticised India's trade policies, particularly its purchase of Russian oil, said on Tuesday that he got “firebombed” by New Delhi through “nasty little attacks” online following his remarks against the nation.
“I actually got firebombed by the Indian continent on the internet with all sorts of nasty little attacks. And all I would say is, don't do that. That's not how we resolve problems here in America,” he told reporters at the White House.
ALSO READ | Trump aide says he got ‘firebombed’ by India over remarks against its Russian oil purchases: ‘Don't do that’
Deep Dive
Notably, Navarro has repeatedly criticised India's trade relationship with Russia and has previously accused New Delhi of helping fund Moscow’s "war machine" in Ukraine.
In September last year, India rejected Navarro's remarks on its purchases of Russian oil, calling them “inaccurate and misleading”.
Who is Peter Navarro?
A Harvard University graduate with a PhD in economics, Navarro currently serves as an adviser to US President Donald Trump on trade and manufacturing matters.
A Trump loyalist since his first presidential campaign in 2016, he has long supported tariffs as a tool of economic policy.
He is believed to have had a major influence on Trump's views on tariffs, including his decision to impose duties on Chinese imports during his first term.
He was among those who pushed for higher duties on Chinese goods during Trump's first term and backed a 45 per cent tariff on imports from China. He argued that the move was needed to address what he described as Beijing's use of illegal export subsidies, manipulation of its currency, intellectual property theft and poor worker safety and environmental standards.
Notably, Navarro had also tried to enter politics but failed, including during a stint as a Democratic Party candidate. He first crossed paths with Trump while he was campaigning nearly a decade ago and later became part of the first Trump administration.
He spent four months in prison after being found guilty of refusing to comply with a congressional subpoena from a committee probing the January 2021 US Capitol riots. He was released in 2024.
When Trump announced his appointment in 2025, he defended Navarro, saying he was “treated horribly by the Deep State, or whatever else.”
Apart from his work in government and politics, Navarro has authored several books, including Death by China, Seeds of Destruction, Always a Winner, The Coming China Wars, If It’s Raining in Brazil, Buy Starbucks, and The Well-Timed Strategy.
ALSO READ | ‘Trump, Modi have good working relations; will work it out’: US official amid 100% tariff threat
Navarro’s tirade against India
The White House official has repeatedly attacked India's trade policies involving Russia and has accused the country of helping fund Russia's "war machine" in Ukraine.
‘India’s oil laundering’
In an opinion piece for the Financial Times, he described India's oil trade with Russia as “opportunistic” and “corrosive” to international efforts aimed at isolating the Russian economy.
“As Russia continues to hammer Ukraine, helped by India’s financial support, American (and European) taxpayers are then forced to spend tens of billions more to help Ukraine’s defence. Meanwhile, India keeps slamming the door on American exports through high tariffs and trade barriers. More than 300,000 soldiers and civilians have been killed, while Nato’s eastern flank grows more exposed and the west foots the bill for India’s oil laundering,” wrote Navarro.
'Maharaja of tariffs'
Navarro has repeatedly used this term for India, first making the remark just days after Trump's tariff announcement. He had defended the US decision not to impose similar penalties on China, Russia's biggest oil buyer.
"It's important to understand that the rationale for the Indian tariffs are very different from the reciprocal tariffs. This was a pure national security issue associated with India's abject refusal to stop buying Russian oil," Navarro said as he called India the 'Maharaja of tariffs'.
'Laundromat for Kremlin'
Last year, Navarro stepped up his attacks on India and called New Delhi a "laundromat for the Kremlin".
While he described Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a "great leader" and said he had "love" for India, he also asked the country to reconsider its role in the global economy. "What you're doing right now is not creating peace. It's perpetuating the war," he had said.
He had also alleged that India's trade with Russia was "a refining profiteering scheme".
'Modi's war in Ukraine'
He referred to the Russia-Ukraine conflict as "Modi's war", claiming that the money Moscow earns through oil sales is used to fund "its war machine" in Ukraine.
“Everybody in America loses because of what India is doing. The consumers and businesses and everything lose, and workers lose because India’s high tariffs cost us jobs, and factories, and income and higher wages. And then the taxpayers lose because we got to fund Modi’s war,” he said during an interview on Bloomberg TV's Balance of Power.
