headline: China denying Indian forces access to key patrolling points in Arunachal Pradesh?
full_text:
China denying Indian forces access to key patrolling points in Arunachal Pradesh?
The People's Party of Arunachal, a regional political outfit in Arunachal Pradesh, has alleged that China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) troops are blocking Indian forces from accessing key patrolling points in the Taksing sector. Government sources junked the claims, while China said that the border situation was "stable".
Reports have emerged suggesting that China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) was denying Indian forces access to key patrolling points along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh's Taksing area. The PLA is steadily expanding its control over traditional Indian grazing and hunting grounds, according to a fact-finding committee (FFC) of the People's Party of Arunachal (PPA). Government sources, however, on Wednesday rejected the claims.
The PPA is a regional political party founded in Arunachal Pradesh in 1977. It currently has two MLAs in the state's 30-member legislative assembly.
The PPA committee, headed by former minister and PPA chief adviser Kahfa Bengia, visited Taksing on July 10, 2026. It also comprised PPA vice-president Kaling Jerang and secretaries Sorang Kiokam and Narah Jimmy.
The party's findings have emerged amid renewed concerns over Chinese activities along the LAC in Upper Subansiri district. Itanagar-based The Arunachal Times newspaper reported on August 10 that a four-member PPA's FFC had found that PLA troops were effectively blocking Indian access to designated patrolling points and that Chinese "incremental intrusions" were being consolidated on the ground.
The PLA, the PPA found, had been denying access of one of the patrolling points since 2023.
"The FFC described this as a clear illustration of how incremental Chinese intrusions are being consolidated on the ground," The Arunachal Times report said.
A day later, The Times of India, in its August 11 report, said the PPA described reports of Chinese intrusions in the Taksing sector as "inexplicable yet irrefutable", alleging that the intrusion followed a "well-calculated, gradual and persistent" pattern refined over several years.
ARMY JUNKED REPORTS OF PLA INTRUSION IN JUNE
Earlier in June, Nah Welfare Society (NWS), a community-based organisation from Taksing in Arunachal Pradesh's Upper Subansiri district, submitted a memorandum to the Deputy Commissioner alleging that the PLA had established camps inside Indian territory near the India-China border.
The Indian Army refuted the claims made by NWS on June 29 and called the allegations "incorrect and without any basis".
Arunachal Pradesh shares a long border with Tibet along the Great Himalayan range. China was never India's neighbouring country. The annexation of Tibet by the People's Republic of China that began in 1950 made the communist country India's neighbour.
ARUNACHAL HOME MINISTER JUNKS CLAIMS AS JUST RUMOURS
Videos have surfaced on social media, purportedly featuring residents of Arunachal Pradesh, in which they claim to have witnessed Chinese Army troops intruding near their villages. One of them featured a young man with a guitar saying "goodbye in advance".
The claims of Chinese encroachment was refuted by Arunachal Pradesh Home Minister Mama Natung on Sunday (August 9), reported news agency ANI. Natung rejected the claims as "just rumours".
"Regarding the Chinese encroachment claims being shown on social media, I would request media friends to verify whether such statements are true or not. The reality is that there is no Chinese encroachment in Arunachal Pradesh. Our soldiers are standing 24x7 on the borders to protect Mother India," said Natung.
"I can say with confidence that China doesn't dare to cross even one inch of Indian territory," he added.
A day later, on August 10, The Arunachal Times reported that the denial by the government and Natung had "further infuriated" people living in the border areas like Taksing and Limeking.
"Many citizens have taken to social media to support the NWS claim and allege that the Chinese PLA is slowly advancing towards Taksing circle headquarters," it said.
TOP CABINET MINISTERS MEET OVER ARUNACHAL CLAIMS
Amid the growing clamour over the Chinese intrusion claims, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh held a meeting at the Defence Minister's office in Parliament house.
Government sources on Wednesday rejected social media claims of "slow encroachment" by China in Arunachal Pradesh, asserting that the Indian Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) are "geared up to dominate the border, monitor and check Chinese activities," according to India Today TV's Manjeet Negi.
The PPA's FFC comes at a time even as India on Tuesday (August 11) rejected China's objection of New Delhi formally marking 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh on its official maps, asserting that the northeastern state is an "inalienable and integral part of India" and that nothing could change that reality.
Responding to Beijing's criticism of the mapping exercise, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said: "India's position on Arunchal Pradesh remained unequivocal".
INDIA'S PATROL ROUTE ABANDONED SINCE 2023: PPA FINDINGS
The most serious allegations by the PPA panel concern Shera 5 Point, a designated patrolling location of India.
According to The Arunachal Times, the PPA committee was told by local residents that Indian and Chinese troops had "a physical confrontation at the point in 2023".
Indian forces subsequently withdrew and have not returned, The Arunachal Times report said.
The PLA then allegedly dismantled the remaining Indian markers at the site and began preventing Indian patrols from accessing the area.
The Times of India's report similarly noted that Shera 5 Point had remained "completely abandoned" since 2023 following a confrontation between PLA troops and the Arunachal Scouts.
According to the TOI, Chinese personnel subsequently removed symbolic Indian structures from the location and have since prevented Indian troops from accessing the area.
The PPA committee described this intrusion as "a familiar Chinese strategy — gaining ground incrementally until temporary restrictions become an established reality on the ground".
NO INDIAN FORCES' PRESENCE IN WINTERS?
The PPA panel's concerns extend beyond a single patrolling point.
During the PPA committee's visit, the team interacted with local leaders, elders, intellectuals and residents of Taksing, Maza and Galemo, besides speaking to senior defence personnel and Army jawans deployed in the sector.
According to The Arunachal Times, one of the biggest vulnerabilities identified by the committee is the seasonal nature of Indian patrolling. Regular Army patrols are largely restricted to the April-October period because heavy snowfall and extreme weather make movement difficult during the remaining months.
The PLA, however, continues its activities throughout the year, the Itanagar-based newspaper's report said.
The committee also pointed to the role of local porters who ferry supplies for Indian troops. Their services are generally suspended during the winter months, which, according to the panel, indicates a significant reduction in the Indian military presence during the period.
The PPA panel warned that there is a seasonal vacuum along a strategically sensitive stretch of the LAC.
HAVE TRADITIONAL HUNTING GROUNDS BECOME PROHIBITED FOR ARUNACHALIS?
Another concern flagged by the committee is Nanga Pahar, traditionally used by the indigenous Nah and Mara communities for hunting and yak rearing.
The area has now become a strictly prohibited zone for local residents, according to the PPA's findings reported by both newspapers.
The Arunachal Times reported on August 10 that the restriction had effectively provided the PLA with greater freedom to push forward, describing the nature of the alleged intrusions as "calculated, gradual and persistent".
The Times of India, in its August 11 report, said the restriction on local access had enabled PLA forces to deepen their alleged encroachment activities towards the Indian side.
"... Restriction has effectively enabled PLA forces to push their encroachment activities deeper into the Indian side," the TOI reported.
For communities living in the remote frontier, the issue therefore extends beyond military patrols. Traditional access to hunting grounds, grazing areas and routes used by local residents is also at stake.
PPA DEMANDS ROADS, BASES AND BETTER CONNECTIVITY IN THE REGION
The committee has called for a major strengthening of India's infrastructure and military presence in the Taksing region.
Among its principal recommendations is the acceleration of the ongoing Border Roads Organisation (BRO) road from Nacho to Taksing on a war footing. The PPA has also called for the proposed 68-km BRO road connecting Galemo and Pokorla to be prioritised.
The Taksing-Pokorla road via Yaja and Huri should also be completed under a strict, time-bound schedule, the panel recommended.
The Times of India reported that the PPA described the progress of the Nacho-Taksing road as sluggish and its condition as "pathetic", arguing that inadequate road infrastructure hampers the rapid movement of troops and equipment towards the frontier.
The panel has further sought the construction of a helipad at Sipi 2 (Rest Point) and permanent Army base camps at Sipi 4 and Sipi 6.
It has also called for reliable grid power to replace diesel generators and improved telephone and network connectivity at forward locations such as Maza and Galemo.
According to the PPA's FFC, poor electricity and communication facilities are major demotivating factors for both soldiers and local residents.
The Times of India quoted that the PPA president and Doimukh MLA Nabam Vivek urged the authorities to ensure that the proposed frontier highway project is not diverted away from Taksing, stressing the town's strategic importance along the LAC.
CHINA SAYS BORDER SITUATION STABLE, INDIA JUNKS CLAIMS
Amid the claims, the Chinese Foreign Ministry said that the situation along the Sino-Indian border is "generally stable at the moment".
Beijing's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the comments while responding to media queries about whether the Chinese military has stepped-up its activity near the Arunachal border. "The China-India border situation is generally stable at the moment," Guo said on Wednesday.
Government sources dismissed the claims of "slow encroachment" by China in Arunachal Pradesh, saying the Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) were "geared up to dominate the border, monitor and check Chinese activities".
The PPA's findings do not represent an official assessment by the Indian Army or the central government, but they have drawn attention to Arunachal Pradesh's most remote frontier sectors. The Indian government is yet to make any official statement on the reports.

headline: Working on framework for hill cities amid growing disaster risks, govt tells LS
full_text:
Working on framework for hill cities amid growing disaster risks, govt tells LS
The government told Lok Sabha that climate change had increased the intensity and frequency of extreme rainfall events in the region
The government is working on a new planning framework for the rapidly growing Himalayan cities as climate change and human activity are increasing disaster risks in the region, it told the Lok Sabha on Tuesday.
In its reply to a question on whether climate change and unscientific construction were contributing to the rise in cloudburst incidents and other disasters in Himachal Pradesh, the government said that anthropogenic factors had also contributed to disaster risk. It added that climate change had increased the intensity and frequency of extreme rainfall events in the region.
The government’s public policy think tank NITI Aayog is working on a planning framework for hill cities. On July 13, NITI Aayog and the North Eastern Council held a consultation on the Hill City Regions Planning Initiative for Sustainable Urban Development in the Indian Himalayan Region. The proposed approach will cover ecological carrying capacity, climate resilience, sustainable infrastructure, governance and financing.
There have been calls for more integrated Himalayan planning. In June, the CP Kukreja Foundation for Design Excellence, a platform for aspiring designers, students and amateurs, released a framework, noting that roads, hydrology, tourism, settlements, forests and disaster management were being planned separately despite their interconnected impact on mountain systems. It called for a shift towards a more integrated approach, saying that “mountains do not function in fragments”.
The foundation’s framework said that a single road project could affect slope stability, drainage, rivers, forests, settlement growth and disaster vulnerability. It argued that many Himalayan disasters could no longer be treated as isolated natural events.
The foundation’s framework pointed to destabilised slopes, poor drainage, excessive cutting and construction in hazard-prone areas as factors linked to cumulative planning failures. It proposed scientific carrying-capacity assessments for Himalayan towns and tourism corridors, covering population, tourism, water availability, waste, traffic and ecological stress, with development approvals calibrated to these limits.
The foundation’s framework proposed multi-hazard zoning that would incorporate landslides, seismic vulnerability, flooding, erosion, and hydrological instability before infrastructure and settlement approvals are granted. It said the broader objective is to move planning from reactive disaster response towards predictive resilience, including continuous monitoring of slopes, drainage and infrastructure after construction.

headline: Leader of Opposition in Jharkhand Assembly Babulal Marandi on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) condemned the late night visit by two top officials at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where the agitation by job aspirants over alleged irregularities in the State...
full_text:
Leader of Opposition in Jharkhand Assembly Babulal Marandi on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) condemned the late night visit by two top officials at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where the agitation by job aspirants over alleged irregularities in the State recruitment examinations entered its 19th day
Ranchi’s Deputy Commissioner (DC) Manjunath Bhajantri and the Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Rakesh Ranjan reached the protest site late at night, Mr. Marandi said.
Sharing a post on X he wrote: “This morning, as soon as I checked my mobile, I learned from the tweet posted by Amit Malviya ji, the party’s central social media coordinator, at 1:30 AM, and ANI’s social media post that late at night, Ranchi’s DC and SSP reached the protest site at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium and attempted to forcibly remove the students by cutting off the electricity.”
He strongly condemned the “undemocratic and reprehensible attitude” of the Ranchi district adminstration and the Hemant Soren-led governement.
“The officials stated that the government has cancelled the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) exam, so the protest should now be ended. As soon as the students received the information, BJP leaders arrived at the protest site late at night. Upon seeing the BJP leaders arriving there, the administrative officials left the spot,” he added.
The senior BJP leader, who also visited the site on Wednesday morning (August 12, 2026), asserted that the government can no longer tolerate even the peaceful struggle of students fighting for their rights and future. He added that the students’ demand is absolutely clear: there should be a fair CBI investigation into the selling of jobs and irregularities in the JPSC and JSSC exams.
“The students have already trusted the government’s assurances in the name of a CID investigation, and now they no longer have faith in that investigation. Simply cancelling the JPSC exam will not resolve the entire matter. The government should immediately order a CBI investigation and take concrete action on all the legitimate demands of the students,” Mr. Marandi said.
The former Chief Minister alleged that instead of suppressing the students’ voice by force of the police and administration, the government should resolve their demands.
“I warn the Hemant government not to make the mistake of challenging the power of the students. If an attempt is made to suppress this voice that has arisen in Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, its spark will reach every village in Jharkhand,” Mr. Marandi said.
He also demanded that the Ranchi district administration should ensure proper arrangements for electricity, water, sanitation, and other basic facilities at the protest site, rather than attempting to disrupt the peaceful movement at the government’s behest.
Ranchi DC, SSP on purpose of visit
On the purpose of the visit, DC Bhajantri said they had come to check on the protesters. “We have come here to ask whether the protesters are not facing any difficulties. Three students are on hunger strike over here, so we requested them to eat something so that their health does not deteriorate,” he said.
“We also have a request from the students to think about a practical and implementable next step, and accordingly we will cooperate,” the DC added.
Mr. Bhajantri was also found asking students whether they had appeared for the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission-Combined Graduate Level (JSSC-CGL) exam.
Ranchi SSP Mr. Ranjan appealed to the students not to allow any outsiders or anti-social elements to become part of their movement. He also urged the students to verify the identities and origins of all individuals at least once at night.
Reacting to the visit of the officials, student leader Kunal Singh said that it was humanly not possible to identify the outsiders and that it was the job of the special branch. He also alleged that during their visit, the officials tried to separate the JPSC and JSSC students.

headline: Search on for Indore techie who went missing during trek near Bengaluru: Police
full_text:
Search on for Indore techie who went missing during trek near Bengaluru: Police
A resident of Begur area, Advait Upadhyay reportedly informed his fiancée of his Shivagange trekking plan.
Bengaluru Police on Wednesday said efforts are underway to trace a 31-year-old Indore man who went missing during a solo trek near the Karnataka capital last week.
“The operation to trace the missing man, Advait Upadhyay, is underway,” Bangalore Rural Superintendent of Police MV Chandrakant told HT.
The officer’s comment was in response to reports that Upadhyay was feared dead after a drone spotted a possible human body in dense vegetation.
According to the police, Upadhyay, who worked at a financial firm in Whitefield, was reported missing on August 7. A resident of Begur area, he reportedly informed his fiancée of his Shivagange trekking plan. He had also hired a motorcycle for the same.
Upadhyay, the police said, reportedly parked his rented bike at the foothills before proceeding uphill. CCTV footage showed him climbing the hills, the police said.
The man’s family suspects that he may have been kidnapped and harmed by robbers, keeping in mind he went for the trek alone.
A missing case has been registered at Kadugodi police station, and a search operation has been underway at Shivagange and its vicinity to trace him, a senior police officer earlier said. "An extensive search operation continues, and further investigation is underway. We are looking into all angles," the officer said, seeking anonymity.
Over 70 personnel from the police, forest department, fire and emergency services and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) have been roped in for the search operation.
Investigators earlier said they are examining the man’s digital activity in the days leading up to the trek. They said during the examination, they found a query made to an AI tool regarding the hill’s height and what could happen to someone in the event of a fatal fall.
“These searches are significant from the investigation point of view. We found queries relating to Shivagange, including its height and what could happen if someone fell from the hill. There was also a search through an AI tool concerning the consequences of such a fall,” inspector B Govardhan said.
The Madhya Pradesh Police have offered to assist Karnataka authorities in their effort to trace the man. "We received information from social media that Advait Upadhyay, originally from Indore, had gone missing while trekking in Shivagange near Bengaluru. We have contacted the Karnataka police in this matter and offered necessary assistance in the investigation," Indore Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Rajesh Dandotiya said.
The Indore police will immediately assist if any assistance is needed in the investigation, the officer said, adding that they have not yet received any information from Upadhyay's family.

headline: PM Modi remembers his mother at ex-president's autobiography launch: ‘Even today, I feel the void’
full_text:
PM Modi remembers his mother at ex-president's autobiography launch: ‘Even today, I feel the void’
At the launch of Ram Nath Kovind's book, Modi said his life showed how determination could help a person overcome adversity.
At the launch of former president Ram Nath Kovind's autobiography, Prime Minister Narendra Modi remembered his late mother while he was talking about the sacrifices that mothers make for raising their children. He was referring to a particular incident quoted from Kovind's book where the former president mentioned how his mother died in a fire accident at their house while trying to save household belongings when he was a young child.
“Kovind ji has written in his book about an incident where a fire broke out in their home during the summer. His mother, setting aside concerns for her own safety, tried to save the household belongings; after all, for an ordinary family, every single item is essential for raising the children. Tragically, while making this effort, she became trapped in the fire and lost her life. Just imagine—experiencing such a tragedy at a tender age, losing one's mother in this manner. How agonizing that must have been,” Modi said at the book launch event.
He remembered his mother and said, "I have been fortunate; my mother lived for over a hundred years and continued to bless me. Yet, even today, I deeply feel the void left by her absence."
Also read: Amit Shah sets condition for debate on student protests, Rahul Gandhi says 'not interested'
Speaking at the launch of Kovind's autobiography "Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles", Modi said Kovind's life showed how determination could help a person overcome adversity and rise to the highest constitutional office.
Modi urges youth to read
Urging the youth to read autobiographies, Modi said they offer an opportunity to understand a particular period through the life of someone who experienced it.
"Today is the era of reels; social media influencers draw you somewhere. But in this age too, remember what's written in railway stations: Shortcut will cut you short," he said, news agency PTI reported.
Modi's remarks come amid the government's efforts to connect to the the youth particularly after the NEET paper leak protests that came to be known as the Gen Z protests. In the aftermath of the NEET protests, Modi had asked his ministerial colleagues to actively use Instagram and post reels to connect with young people.
In recent weeks, Modi himself has posted reels more frequently, addressing young people.
Kovind recalls childhood, association with BJP
Kovind recalled his childhood hardships and the values he imbibed from his surroundings.
"I come from a village at Kanpur Dehat in Uttar Pradesh. I learnt mutual compassion and love from the villagers," he said, recalling how rainwater used to leak through the roof of his home and the family would wait for the rain to stop.
Kovind said crores of poor families had got a roof over their heads under government housing schemes, receiving an opportunity to live with dignity.

headline: On June 29, SIA filed a chargesheet in the abduction, torture and killing of Bhat
full_text:
On June 29, SIA filed a chargesheet in the abduction, torture and killing of Bhat
SRINAGAR: Sarvanand Kaul Premi was a poet. Sarla Bhat was a nurse. Both were Kashmiri Pandits who stayed behind when militancy erupted and were killed in 1990. More than three decades later, J&K policeâs SIA revived unresolved cases from the Valleyâs darkest years. The agency searched Wednesday nine locations in its probe into the abduction-murder of Premi and his younger son, weeks after filing a chargesheet in Bhatâs killing.Premi, 66, a poet, teacher and Gandhian, and Verinder were abducted from their village, Soaf Shali near Kokernag, on Apr 30, 1990. They were shot dead the next day. Five days later, the grief-stricken Kaul family left Kashmir, never to return.State Investigation Agencyâs searches were linked to FIR No. 45/1990 registered at Dooru police station in Anantnag. SIA is pursuing militancy-era cases that had lain cold for decades.On June 29, SIA filed a chargesheet in the abduction, torture and killing of Bhat, 27, a staff nurse in the neonatology ward at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences in Srinagar. She was allegedly abducted by JKLF from SKIMS Habba Khatoon Hostel on Apr 18, 1990, and taken to Illahibagh-Lal Bazar, tortured and shot dead.
Her bullet-riddled body was found the next day at Omer Colony Malabagh in downtown Srinagar.Born in Soaf Shali in 1924, Premi joined Khadi Bhandar after completing his education and became associated with Mahatma Gandhiâs Swadeshi movement. His association with Kashmiri poet Ghulam Ahmad Mahjoor inspired his literary career. He translated Rabindranath Tagoreâs âGitanjaliâ into Kashmiri and the Bhagavad Gita and Ramayana into Kashmiri and Urdu, and advocated secularism and interfaith harmony.
J&K govt under then-CM Farooq Abdullah posthumously awarded Premi a gold medal in 1997 for his contribution to Kashmiri literature and communal harmony.The killings from Kashmirâs violent spring of 1990 were part of a wider wave of hostility against Kashmiri Pandits after militancy erupted, driving a mass exodus of the community from the Valley. In 2010, J&K govt under then-CM Omar Abdullah told the assembly that 209 Kashmiri Pandits had been murdered since 1990.

headline: Ghaziabad-Jewar corridor may link Noida airport with Namo Bharat, metro
full_text:
Ghaziabad-Jewar corridor may link Noida airport with Namo Bharat, metro
NCRTC has proposed a 72.44-km Ghaziabad-Jewar corridor with Namo Bharat and metro services. The link could cut travel time to Noida International Airport and improve regional connectivity.
Ghaziabad, Greater Noida and Noida International Airport are among the proposed stations on the 72.44-km Ghaziabad-Jewar corridor, according to station details shared by the National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC). The corridor is planned to offer both Namo Bharat and metro services, giving commuters a public transport link between Ghaziabad, Noida and the airport.
An official said the project is still at the Detailed Project Report stage. Once developed, the corridor is expected to cut travel time between Ghaziabad, Noida and Noida International Airport to about 40 to 50 minutes, with a planned maximum operational speed of 180 kmph.
The corridor will connect Ghaziabad station on the Delhi-Meerut Namo Bharat corridor with Noida International Airport at Jewar. Of the total length, around 71.5 km will be elevated and 1.29 km underground, the corporation said. The route is planned with 11 stations for Namo Bharat services and 18 stations for metro services, allowing passengers to use both regional rapid rail and local metro along the corridor.
The proposed Namo Bharat stations are Ghaziabad South, Greater Noida Sector 2, Greater Noida Sector 3, Greater Noida Sector 12, Surajpur, Alpha-I, EcoTech-VI, Dankaur, YEIDA North (Sector 18), YEIDA Central (Sector 21) and Noida International Airport. The proposed metro stations are Siddharth Vihar, Greater Noida Sector 16C, EcoTech 12, Greater Noida West (Sector 4), Greater Noida Sector 10, Knowledge Park V, Police Lines Surajpur, EcoTech-2, Knowledge Park III, Omega-II, Phi-III, EcoTech-1E, EcoTech VIII, Dadupur, Junedpur, YEIDA Sector 17, YEIDA Sector 15 and YEIDA Sector 33.
The project aims to strengthen public transport connectivity across the National Capital Region by linking Ghaziabad to Greater Noida, the Yamuna Expressway area and the upcoming Noida airport, the official said. He added that the corridor will provide an additional public transport option for passengers travelling between Ghaziabad, Noida and Noida International Airport, while improving connectivity to residential, commercial and upcoming infrastructure hubs along the route.
In sum, the proposed Ghaziabad-Jewar corridor is planned as a dual-service route with Namo Bharat and metro stations, linking key parts of Ghaziabad, Greater Noida and the Noida airport area, though it remains at the DPR stage.

headline: Gen Alpha protests bus fare hike in MP, govt assures schoolgirls of action
full_text:
Gen Alpha protests bus fare hike in MP, govt assures schoolgirls of action
Schoolgirls in Madhya Pradesh's Vidisha district protested against a bus fare hike and sought restoration of old rates. The administration promised talks with private operators as students said higher fares were hurting attendance.
Schoolgirls in Madhya Pradesh's Vidisha district staged a protest in Sironj on Wednesday against a recent increase in bus fares, saying the hike had made their daily commute to school a financial burden on their families. A large number of students from the Girls' Higher Secondary School, many of whom travel to Sironj from nearby rural areas, gathered at the bus stand and raised slogans for around half an hour, demanding that the increased fares be reduced.
The students said fares on routes they use to travel to school had earlier ranged between Rs 10 and Rs 15 but had now been increased. They said the additional cost was particularly difficult for families with limited incomes.
The protesting students said their families already bear the expenses of household needs and education, and the fare hike had added to their monthly financial burden. They demanded that students be allowed to travel at concessional fares so that the increased cost does not affect their regular attendance.
STUDENTS APPEAL TO MLA FOR INTERVENTION
During the protest, the students also appealed to local representatives, including MLA Umakant Sharma, to intervene and help reduce the fares.
They said affordable transportation was essential for students travelling from rural areas to attend school in Sironj and urged the authorities to ensure that the earlier fares were restored.
OFFICIAL REACHES SPOT, ASSURES STUDENTS
The protest continued for around 30 minutes before SDM Om Narayan Badkul, SDOP and the local police station in-charge reached the bus stand and spoke to the students.
The SDM listened to their concerns and assured them that the administration would discuss the matter with private bus operators and explore the possibility of allowing schoolgirls from rural areas to travel at the earlier fares.
"We have heard the students' problems and will make every effort to ensure that girls travelling from rural areas can commute to school at the old fare. We will call a meeting of bus operators and discuss the issue to resolve it at the earliest," Badkul said.
Following the SDM's assurance, the students agreed to end their protest.
The students, however, maintained that their main demand was restoration of the earlier bus fares so that those travelling from rural areas can continue attending school without facing an additional financial burden. The next step will depend on the outcome of the administration's discussions with the bus operators.

headline: Rashtrapati Bhavan, the official residence and office of the President of India, will host the Independence Day Reception (At Home) on August 15 as a celebration of the country’s cultural diversity and traditions of environmental stewardship.

Rashtrapati Bhavan, the official residence and office of the President of India, will host the Independence Day Reception (At Home) on August 15 as a celebration of the country’s cultural diversity and traditions of environmental stewardship.
The Hindu Independence Day Edition
“Under President Droupadi Murmu, Rashtrapati Bhavan has increasingly served as a national platform for showcasing India’s artistic traditions through State Receptions, banquets for foreign dignitaries and programmes such as the Artists-in-Residence initiative. The 2026 reception will focus on the living cultural traditions of Chhattisgarh, Goa, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, highlighting the relationship between communities, culture and nature,” said a release issued by the President’s House.
Folk dances, music
Around 35 artists from the four States will present folk dances and musical traditions, including Maharashtra’s Lavani and Songhi Mukhawate, Chhattisgarh’s Gedi and Gaur Madiya, Madhya Pradesh’s Bhagoria and Baiga Karma, and Goa’s Samai and Ghode Modni.
The performances reflect diverse community traditions. Gedi, performed on bamboo stilts during Chhattisgarh’s Hareli festival, showcases agility and balance, while Gaur Madiya of Bastar reflects tribal valour. Bhagoria and Baiga Karma embody social, agricultural and nature-linked traditions. Samai features performers balancing brass lamps, while Ghode Modni recalls the bravery of Goan warriors.
The musical programme will unfold as a cultural journey through forests, villages, temples and coastal landscapes, culminating in a shared performance by musicians from all four States. It has been curated by Chhattisgarh folk artist Rakesh Kumar Tiwari, a Sangeet Natak Akademi Award recipient.
The theme will extend to décor and cuisine. Table runners will feature Bagh Print, Khunn, Kunbi textiles and Soura traditions. The menu will include regional specialities such as Indori Poha, Patoleo, Mini Farra, Bafauri, Khamang Kakdi, Dodol and Kodo Millet Kheer.
The reception seeks to demonstrate how India’s cultural heritage and environmental traditions continue to reinforce one another.

headline: SC refuses deadline extension for Aravalli panel submissions
full_text:
SC refuses deadline extension for Aravalli panel submissions
The Supreme Court refused to extend the deadline for submissions to the committee defining the Aravalli hills, citing potential misuse to delay the process.
The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to extend the deadline for submitting representations to the high-powered committee (HPC) tasked with defining the Aravalli hills, saying any such judicial extension could be misused by vested interests to delay the process.
Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said the court would not extend the deadline through a judicial order, while indicating that representations could still be submitted to the committee.
“We will not extend time through a judicial order. We know people with vested interests having deep-rooted interests who will try to delay this process, if any extension is granted,” the CJI said.
The matter was mentioned for urgent listing by senior advocate Devashish Bharuka, who said the deadline for suggestions and representations ended on August 11 and the committee would not accept submissions unless the court permitted it.
Bharuka said he represented a non-profit organisation working with tribal communities in Gujarat, many of whom were digitally illiterate and unaware of the committee’s online notice. He also alleged that the committee had overlooked Gujarat and conducted site inspections only in Delhi, Haryana and Rajasthan.
The CJI rejected the criticism, saying the court would wait for the committee’s report.
“We do not want such piecemeal criticism of the committee. We will wait for the report. It is not that they have closed site visits,” he said.
The bench also said the committee’s notice had been widely publicised and rejected the suggestion that stakeholders were unaware of the exercise.
“It is very difficult to believe that people did not know. However, you can submit your suggestions. If they do not take it, come to us. This is not like any limitation period that they will not consider beyond a date,” the bench said.
The court had in June constituted the five-member HPC, headed by Kanchan Devi, director general of the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE), to arrive at a uniform definition of the ecologically fragile Aravalli hills and ranges and recommend measures to regulate future mining.
The committee has been asked to submit its report by August 31, with recommendations for conserving the Aravalli ecosystem across Gujarat, Haryana, Rajasthan and Delhi.
Other members are former Forest Survey of India (FSI) director general Subhash Ashutosh; former Geological Survey of India (GSI) director Rajendra Kumar Sharma; former joint secretary in the environment ministry Brij Mohan Singh Rathore; and former Delhi University botany professor Ashok K Bhatnagar.
The court will consider the committee’s report on September 7, when it is also expected to decide whether to lift its stay on mining across the Aravalli region.
The HPC was constituted after the Supreme Court, on December 29, 2025, recalled its November 20 order laying down a uniform definition of the Aravalli hills. The court said the committee should assess the short- and long-term environmental impact of the proposed definition and consider the “varied and competing considerations” involved.
It directed the panel to consult environmentalists, non-profit organisations, mining lease holders, project proponents, villagers, particularly farmers, and local communities whose livelihoods are linked to the Aravalli ecosystem.
The Aravalli range is considered a key ecological barrier separating the arid northwestern desert from the fertile northern plains and acts as a “green lung” for northwestern India. The Supreme Court has regulated mining in the region since 2002. A 2018 FSI report found evidence of extensive illegal mining, including the disappearance of 31 hillocks across 3,000 sites in Rajasthan and Haryana.

headline: The Himachal Pradesh government has imposed a cess of 60 paise per litre on petrol and high-speed diesel to fund welfare measures for widows and orphaned children.The ‘Orphan and Widow Cess’ came into effect from midnight on August 11, according to a...
full_text: The Himachal Pradesh government has imposed a cess of 60 paise per litre on petrol and high-speed diesel to fund welfare measures for widows and orphaned children.The ‘Orphan and Widow Cess’ came into effect from midnight on August 11, according to a notification issued by the State Taxes and Excise Department. The levy will be collected at the first point of sale of petrol and high-speed diesel in the State.The money collected through the cess will be credited to an Orphan and Widow Welfare Fund and used for the welfare of widows and orphans.The levy follows the passage of the Himachal Pradesh Value Added Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2026, by the State Assembly in March. The amendment inserted a provision allowing the government to impose a cess of up to Rs 5 per litre on petrol and high-speed diesel.The government has currently fixed the cess at 60 paise per litre, well below the maximum permitted under the amended law. The rate can be changed through a government notification, subject to the Rs 5-per-litre ceiling..Himachal Pradesh to legalise cannabis cultivation for medical, industrial purposes.The bill had faced strong opposition from BJP legislators when it was introduced in the Assembly. BJP members protested against the proposed levy and staged a walkout during its passage.Leader of the Opposition Jai Ram Thakur criticised the government for seeking to raise revenue through a levy named after widows and orphans. He argued that increasing fuel prices could make petrol and diesel more expensive in Himachal Pradesh than in neighbouring States, prompting consumers in border districts to buy fuel elsewhere.Other BJP legislators also warned that a fuel cess would increase the cost of transportation and have a cascading effect on prices. The party described the proposal as an additional burden on the public.The BJP also raised concerns about the potential impact on petrol pumps in districts bordering Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh, where consumers could choose to refuel in neighbouring areas if fuel prices were lower.Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu defended the bill, saying the government needed a stable and dedicated source of revenue for welfare measures for economically weaker widows and orphans. He had also pointed out during the Assembly debate that Rs 5 was only the maximum permissible limit and that the government could fix a much lower rate.

Amit Shah 'ready to answer any question'; Rahul Gandhi says 'not interested in him giving us lecture'

Amit Shah says 'ready to sit through, take notes and respond to anything' in Parliament.
NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday offered to sit in Parliament from "3pm today till 3pm the next day" to hear the opposition's concerns and respond to every point, amid protests over his "absence" from the Houses. Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, however, rejected the offer saying they "seek answers, not lectures."Shah's offer came amid opposition protests demanding that he make a statement in Parliament on the police action against students during their July 20 march over the NEET paper leak issue.Speaking to reporters, Shah rejected opposition allegations that he had been absent from Parliament and said the government was ready for a detailed discussion on the issue."First of all, terms like 'laapata', 'bhaag gaye' are the kind of language increasingly being heard in India's public and parliamentary life. I have been coming to Parliament regularly since the session began; I sit in my chamber, but since the opposition is not allowing Parliament to functionâin either Houseâwhat is one supposed to do?" Shah said.He said Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju had already made it clear that the government was ready for a full discussion on the student protests.
"We asked for a time to be fixed and for the Opposition to be ready. That was their initial demand, and we agreed to it. I, too, have stated that I am ready to answer any question in Parliament, yet they simply do not want the discussion to take place," Shah said."Now, let the public decide who is running away. Let them submit a letter to the Speaker by 3:00 pm today. We are ready for a discussion on all aspects from 3:00 pm today until 3:00 pm tomorrow. I will sit in the House; I will listen to everyone and respond to every point. The government has nothing to hide," he added.Shah said he was even willing to discuss why the opposition had not allowed the debate to take place. "The NDA governmentâunder Modi ji's leadership is ready to discuss anything; they just need to let Parliament function," he said.Elaborating on his offer, Shah said, "I want to tell the opposition: submit a letter to the Speaker by 2.00 pm, we will start the discussion at 3.00pm, and I will provide answers to everything by 3:00 PM tomorrow.""There are established rules and procedures for parliamentary discussions. Yet, some ask me to simply make a statement. Such a serious issue cannot be discussed in that manner. That may be your method, but it is not the parliamentary way. In Parliament, discussions are held at length," he said."In Parliament, discussions are held at length. I am ready for the debate to continue from 3:00 PM today, sitting late into the night and continuing until 3:00 PM tomorrow; I am even prepared to suspend the Question Hour if the Speaker grants permission," Shah said."I am ready for the discussion to go on until 3:00 PM tomorrow. I will sit through it myself, take notes on everything, and respond to every point so that the entire matter becomes clear to the people of the countryâso that the truth is fully revealed. Now, the Opposition must decide whether they want to engage in a discussion or create an uproar," he added.
Rahul Gandhi hits backCongress leader Rahul Gandhi rejected Shah's offer, saying the opposition was seeking answers on the alleged police action against students rather than a lecture from the home minister."The opposition has clearly said that we are not interested in Amit Shah giving us a lecture. When I say 'we', I mean the younger generation of this country. Who shot the students? Who gave the order to beat up the students with lathis with nails? Did Amit Shah give this order to shoot our children? If he did, then he should resign. For the last 20 days, Amit Shah has been missing. The Home Minister of India has no courage; he cannot come to the House," Rahul said."Did home minister Shah give orders to shoot our children or not; if he did, he is culpable and if he did not, he is incompetent," he added.
The leader of opposition also took to X, sharing a video of his remark saying "When a man lacks the courage to speak the truth, his silence speaks for him. Amit Shahâs silence is his confession."Centre vs oppositionThe opposition has been demanding Shah's presence in Parliament and a statement on the "police action" against students during the Jantar Mantar protest.Earlier in the day, opposition MPs, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and party general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, staged a protest in the Parliament House Complex over the alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya and the alleged police excesses against student protesters.Priyanka also questioned the government over the alleged use of force against students.The INDIA bloc has been protesting for more than three weeks, demanding Shah's presence in the House and a statement from him.Earlier on Monday, Kiren Rijiju said the government was ready for a detailed discussion on the student protests and urged the opposition not to disrupt proceedings when Shah responds."The offer made by the government is very clear that it is ready to have a full and detailed discussion on students' movement and activities related to it," Rijiju said.
"My only point made to the opposition is that while the discussion and a reply are being made, the opposition should not create disturbances to prevent the statement of the home minister," he said, adding that, "They must listen to the reply of the home minister and the government. Once discussion begins, we must have a threadbare discussion."Rijiju's remarks came after Rahul criticised the Centre over the alleged police action during the July 20 student protests at Jantar Mantar and demanded a court-monitored probe. Parliament proceedings have repeatedly been disrupted during the Monsoon Session, with several Bills passed by the Lok Sabha amid the continuing deadlock.

headline: Haryana health minister calls for greater adoption of AYUSH healthcare systems
full_text:
Haryana health minister calls for greater adoption of AYUSH healthcare systems
Chandigarh, Haryana Health Minister Arti Singh Rao on Wednesday said AYUSH healthcare systems play an important role in the management and prevention of chronic diseases and appealed to people to consider and adopt these traditional systems of medicine.
In a statement released here, the minister said that with lifestyle-related diseases increasing, there has been a growing interest in AYUSH systems, including Ayurveda, Yoga and naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and homoeopathy not only in India but also globally. Keeping in view the growing relevance of these systems, the state government recently organised the Rashtriya Poshan Maah/Seva Pakhwada on a large scale, she said.
During the campaign, the AYUSH department organised around 1,771 health camps across the state, providing free check-ups and medical consultation to more than 10,900 people, according to the statement.
Highlighting the steps being taken to strengthen the state's healthcare infrastructure, she said the government is committed to providing better healthcare facilities, quality medical education and health awareness, particularly to people living in rural and remote areas.
In this direction, the state has four major Ayurvedic hospitals a 100-bed hospital in Kurukshetra, a 25-bed hospital in Bhiwani, a 10-bed hospital at Imlota village in Charkhi Dadri and a 100-bed hospital in Narnaul. Besides, one Unani hospital has been established at Sihol in Palwal and one homoeopathic hospital at Chandpura in Ambala, the minister said.
She further said the AYUSH infrastructure is not limited to major hospitals and has also been expanded at the primary level. Six Ayurvedic Primary Health Centres are functional in Haryana, including two in Kaithal and one each in Panipat, Rohtak, Sirsa and Jind.
To make Panchakarma treatment more accessible, six centres are being run by the state government, two each in Ambala and Panchkula and one each in Karnal and Jhajjar, while 21 Panchakarma centres are being operated under the National Health Mission.
Additionally, 515 Ayurvedic, 16 Unani and 24 homoeopathic dispensaries are providing healthcare services across the state, Rao said, adding that the Institute of Indian Medical Systems and Research in Panchkula is also functioning as a key centre for research and innovation.
Giving details of healthcare facilities established under the National AYUSH Mission, the health minister said 21 AYUSH wings in district hospitals, 102 AYUSH IPDs in community health centres and 106 AYUSH OPDs in primary health centres are currently providing healthcare services to citizens.
Most of these facilities are located in rural and remote areas, helping extend healthcare services to people in underserved regions, the statement read.
Highlighting Haryana's efforts in medical education, Rao said the state is giving a new dimension to AYUSH education through Shri Krishna AYUSH University, Kurukshetra. One government Ayurvedic college and 12 private Ayurvedic colleges are currently functioning in the state and providing medical education.
Rao said that Ayurveda, Yoga and naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and homoeopathy have been practised in India since ancient times.
She said these systems have a long history of use and continue to contribute to healthcare and wellness.
She further appealed to the people to incorporate healthy practices into their daily lives for a healthier and longer life.

headline: Amit Shah sets condition for debate on student protests, Rahul Gandhi says 'not interested'
full_text:
Amit Shah sets condition for debate on student protests, Rahul Gandhi says 'not interested'
Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi said he was “not interested” in Amit Shah's “lecture” and sought answers over the police action against the protesters.
Union home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday said that the government was prepared for a detailed discussion in Parliament on the student protests at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi and the police crackdown that followed, provided the Opposition submitted a letter to the speaker.
In response, leader of the opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said that the Opposition is not interested in Shah's “lecture”.
Follow Parliament monsoon session live updates here.
Shah's condition for discussion on student protests
Deep Dive
Speaking to reporters in the Parliament House complex, Shah said the government was willing to discuss all matters in Parliament, including the students' protests, and called on the Opposition to allow the House to function.
He said he would respond to the debate and asked the Opposition to submit a notice to the Lok Sabha Speaker by 2 pm on Wednesday seeking a discussion on the issue.
"We are ready to discuss all the issues in Parliament, including students' protests; let the House function," the home minister said.
"If opposition gives it in writing to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla by 2 pm today, we can start a discussion at 3 pm today until 3 pm tomorrow," Shah said.
Rahul Gandhi hits back, says ‘not interested’
The Lok Sabha LoP and Congress MP said the Opposition was “not interested” in Shah's “lecture” and sought answers over the police action against the protesters.
He asked who had ordered the alleged firing and lathicharge against the student protesters and demanded that the home minister be held accountable. He also alleged that Shah had been absent from Parliament and said the home minister did not have the courage to face the House.
Speaking to reporters outside the Parliament complex, Rahul Gandhi said, “The Opposition has clearly said that we are not interested in Amit Shah giving us a lecture. When I say 'we', I mean the younger generation of this country. Who shot the students? Who gave the order to beat up the students with lathis with nails? Did Amit Shah give this order to shoot our children? If he did, then he should resign.”
He added, "For the last 20 days, Amit Shah has been missing. The Home Minister of India has no courage; he cannot come to the House."
Parliament deadlock over crackdown on student protesters
The Monsoon session, which began on July 20, has been repeatedly disrupted as the Opposition protests over issues including the student protests over the NEET paper leak and allegations of theft of Ram temple donations.
Amid the ruckus, Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said on Monday that the government was prepared for a full-fledged discussion in the Lok Sabha on the student protests and the police action that followed.
Rahul Gandhi said the issue was not whether Shah could deliver a speech in Parliament on "general issues".
"The question was that Home Minister Shah has to make it clear who authorised the shooting of our children in Delhi. He is the home minister; pellet guns were fired," Gandhi said, adding that Shah must clarify whether he had ordered the firing.
Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Wednesday appealed to Opposition members protesting in the House to allow proceedings to continue. He said it was not appropriate for them to damage the image of Parliament by staging protests and raising slogans.

headline: Odisha DGP selection delayed amid procedural, integrity concerns
full_text:
Odisha DGP selection delayed amid procedural, integrity concerns
The UPSC’s empanelment committee was expected to shortlist three officers, from whom the state government will choose the next DGP
Odisha is without a new director general of police (DGP) even four months after the state government initiated the selection process which is currently entangled in procedural deadlocks, integrity concerns, last-minute promotions and judicial scrutiny. The incumbent YB Khurania is set to retire on August 16.
In April this year, the state government submitted a panel of three DGP-ranked officers to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC): Dr Sudhanshu Sarangi (1990 batch), Susanta Kumar Nath (1993 batch) and RP Koche(1993 batch). In May, the state government added eight more ADG-ranked officers’ names.
The UPSC’s empanelment committee was expected to shortlist three officers, from whom the state government will choose the next DGP under guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court in its 2006 Prakash Singh judgment.
The guidelines require the state to choose its police chief from among the three senior-most officers empanelled by the UPSC, based on length of service, service record and relevant experience. An officer must also have at least six months of residual service.
On August 7, when the UPSC was supposed to decide on the panel, the state government withheld the integrity certificate of Susanta Kumar Nath, a DGP-ranked officer who heads the prisons department.
A home department official aware of the development said Nath faced adverse feedback from the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) over a sub-inspector recruitment examination controversy when he was the chairman of the Odisha Police Recruitment Board. The examination was cancelled following allegations of a question-paper leak and the CBI subsequently investigated the matter.
The government withdrew its original proposal from the UPSC after it raised questions about including ADGP-rank officers in the panel. Under the UPSC guidelines, officers below the DG rank can be considered only when there are not enough eligible DG-rank officers.
On August 10, the state government promoted Sanjeeb Panda and Yeshwant Kumar Jethwa from additional DGP rank to DGP rank, to make them eligible for UPSC consideration. Panda heads anti-Maoist operations and Jethwa is the director of vigilance.
The move changed the seniority list and officials said it aimed at the state government submitting a revised proposal to the UPSC.
A public interest litigation filed in the Supreme Court argued that promoting ADGPs and seeking their inclusion could undermine the requirement that the UPSC consider the senior-most eligible officers already in the zone of consideration.
The officials said that the UPSC is expected to consider the state government’s revised list on Thursday. The state government can select one of the shortlisted officers as Odisha’s next police chief.
According to state government officials the revised list includes 1990-batch IPS officer Sudhanshu Sarangi, 1993-batch IPS officer RP Koche, and 1994-batch officers Sanjeeb Panda and Yashwant Jethwa.
Former Mumbai police commissioner and Biju Janata Dal leader Arup Patnaik said the uncertainty reflected the unusually powerful position of the DGP.
“The post of DGP is exceptionally powerful because the entire police force functions under the DGP,” said Patnaik.
“Chief ministers therefore rarely give up control of the home department and often want a police chief they can work with. The empanelment process gives governments considerable influence because only officers empanelled by the Union Home Ministry can be considered by the UPSC. The UPSC recommends three names, but the final choice is made by the state government,” Patnaik said.

headline: Hyderabad: 26-year-old constable found dead in LB Nagar Police Station restroom
full_text:
Hyderabad: 26-year-old constable found dead in LB Nagar Police Station restroom
A 26-year-old police constable was found dead at the L B Nagar ACP office in Hyderabad. Police suspect suicide, while his family alleges foul play.
A 26-year-old police constable was found dead in the restroom of a police station in L B Nagar, Telangana’s Hyderabad, in the early hours of Wednesday, police said, adding that prima facie, it appeared to be a death by suicide, even as his family members suspected foul play.
The constable, who was on electronic computerised operations for police services (e-COPS) duty and was working night shifts, was found dead in the restroom of the L B Nagar assistant commissioner of police (ACP) office at around 2.30 am.

“The other police personnel who noticed him immediately shifted him to nearby Kamineni Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival,” a senior police officer of the L B Nagar police station said.
Police said the deceased was from Bandalemuru village in Manchal mandal of Ranga Reddy district and was staying in a room with his friends at Karmanghat, about a kilometre away from the police station.
“He was a quiet person and there were no indications of the deceased experiencing any kind of stress. Inquiries also revealed that he did not have any family-related problems. He attended duty on Tuesday as well without any complaints,” the police officer said.
His body was shifted to Osmania General Hospital for postmortem and a case was registered at the L B Nagar police station.

Tension prevailed outside the L B Nagar police station on Wednesday, with the family members and villagers staging a protest.
“There were bloodstains in the rest room where he was found hanging. We want an explanation from the police what exactly led to the death of my son,” he demanded.
A large number of police personnel were deployed at the station to bring the situation under control. L B Nagar deputy commissioner of police (DCP) Anuradha inspected the police station and made inquiries about the possible cause of the constable’s death.

headline: Lok Sabha inquiry panel indicts ex-HC judge Yashwant Varma in cash-at-home case
full_text:
Lok Sabha inquiry panel indicts ex-HC judge Yashwant Varma in cash-at-home case
TOI News Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 12, 2026, 16:39 IST
Comments
Share

Text Size

The panel found Justice Varmaâs explanation over the discovery of unaccounted cash at his official residence "evasive" and "unsatisfactory".
NEW DELHI: A Lok Sabha inquiry committee on Wednesday indicted former Allahabad High Court judge Yashwant Varma in the cash-at-home case.The panel found Justice Varmaâs explanation for the discovery of unaccounted cash at his official residence "evasive" and "unsatisfactory". Its report, tabled in both Houses of Parliament, said all three charges against Varma were proved.The committee said the charges are threefold - firstly, discovery and possession of unexplained Indian currency notes within official premises; secondly, failure to preserve and causing interference with material evidence; and thirdly, furnishing evasive and misleading explanations.The committee examined documentary and electronic material and recorded evidence from witnesses. It also noted that Varma was given an opportunity to respond to the charges and present his defence."The statement of grounds accompanying the charges records the occurrence of fire, discovery of cash, location of the storeroom within the Government-allotted residence, the alleged conduct after the fire, and the explanation offered by the Judge," the inquiry report said."Article I is proved. Substantial unexplained Rs 500 denomination currency notes were found in the storeroom situated within the official residential premises at 30, Tughlaq Crescent, New Delhi.
The Judge failed to furnish a satisfactory explanation regarding the presence, source or ownership thereof," it said.On the third charge, the committee said Varmaâs explanation, including his March 22, 2025 response and subsequent statements, did not demonstrate the "candour, transparency and institutional responsibility" expected in the circumstances. It remained evasive and unsatisfactory when tested against evidence from independent officials and other corroborative material.
A large amount of unaccounted, partially burnt cash was discovered in the outhouse of Varmaâs official residence following a fire in March 2025. The discovery triggered allegations of judicial corruption, which Varma denied.Following an in-house inquiry ordered by the then Chief Justice of India, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla constituted a three-member panel headed by Supreme Court judge Aravind Kumar under the Judges (Inquiry) Act. The motion for the inquiry was backed by MPs from different political parties.Varma resigned during the inquiry. It remains unclear whether Parliament will proceed with the committeeâs findings, as some legal experts have argued that the Judges (Inquiry) Act can be invoked only against a serving judge.

headline: Rajya Sabha passes bill to rename Kerala as ‘Keralam’
full_text:
Rajya Sabha passes bill to rename Kerala as ‘Keralam’
The bill seeks to amend the First Schedule of the Constitution to change the name of the southern state to “Keralam”
The Rajya Sabha on Wednesday passed the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 by voice vote amid the din to rename the southern state as ‘Keralam’, completing the parliamentary process for the change. The Lok Sabha passed the bill without discussion on Tuesday.
“The name of a state is not merely about changing its name, or simply changing the name of a geographical area to ‘Keralam’. It certainly is that as well, but in the Malayalam language, ‘Keralam’ represents the culture, civilisation and emotions of Kerala. Therefore, making ‘Keralam’ the name of Kerala is a matter of pride, honour and self-respect for all of us, for all Indians,” said minister of state for home affairs Nityanand Rai, who piloted the legislation on behalf of Union home minister Amit Shah.
The bill seeks to amend the First Schedule of the Constitution to change the name of the southern state to “Keralam”.
Deep Dive
The move follows a resolution passed by the Kerala assembly in 2024, which noted that “since the time of the country’s independence struggle, there has been a strong demand for the formation of United Kerala for the people speaking the Malayalam language,” and that the state legislature had “unanimously appealed to the Central government to take urgent steps as per Article 3 of the Constitution for modifying the name as Keralam.”
Opposition MPs demanded that Shah pilot the bill in the House since the list of business mentioned his name but the government rejected the demand. “The minister of state Nityanand Rai is here and he is piloting the bill and that is very much within the parliamentary democracy that is being followed here,” said senior minister JP Nadda.
The Opposition has been demanding that Amit Shah make a statement on the July 20 police action against student protesters at Jantar Mantar.
Sasmit Patra, who was in the chair at the time, asked MPs to confine themselves to the general principles of the Bill in their speeches and avoid “irrelevant points and repetition of arguments”.
”These guidelines are provided under Rules 110, 124 and 240 of the Rules of Procedure. Anything said in violation of the Rules shall not form part of the records, and you don’t have to repeat it again and again,” he said.

headline: Parliament's Monsoon Session nears end with political tango as FCRA Bill goes to JPC
full_text:
Parliament's Monsoon Session nears end with political tango as FCRA Bill goes to JPC
One side wanted Parliament to function and offered a debate. The other wanted a specific answer before entering a broader discussion.
The final stretch of Parliament's Monsoon Session saw the government and Opposition trade offers, counter-offers and political barbs, with a proposed 24-hour discussion on the July 20 incident failing to break the deadlock.
The government offered an extended debate on the violence surrounding the students' protest on July 20, with Home Minister Amit Shah saying he was ready to speak, listen to the Opposition and answer its questions.
The Opposition, however, wanted a more specific answer.
Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition did not want a lengthy speech from the Home Minister. It wanted to know one thing: Who ordered the firing of pellet guns on the protesting students?
That effectively kept the July 20 issue unresolved.
AMIT SHAH OFFERS 24-HOUR DEBATE
The Home Minister said he had been coming to Parliament and sitting in his chamber while the Opposition was preventing the Houses from functioning.
He said the government was ready for a discussion if the Opposition gave the Speaker a letter by 3 pm. The proposed discussion could run from 3 pm that day to 3 pm the following day, he said.
Shah also used the Opposition's recent “laapata” and “bhaag gaye” rhetoric to challenge it to let the public decide who was actually avoiding a debate. His message was that the government had nothing to hide and was ready to respond if Parliament was allowed to function.
Rahul Gandhi, however, rejected the broader proposition. He said the Opposition wanted an answer to a specific question about the July 20 incident rather than an extended speech.
FCRA BILL BECOMES THE NEXT FLASHPOINT
As the dispute over the July 20 incident remained unresolved, Parliament turned to the contentious Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, or FCRA, Bill.
The government moved to refer the Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee. Interestingly, referring the legislation to a JPC had also been demanded by sections of the Opposition.
The Home Minister's name was listed for moving the motion, but Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai moved it when the House took up the matter at around 2.18 pm.
As Rai finished speaking, Congress leader KC Venugopal called for the Bill to be withdrawn.
Venugopal argued that the legislation targeted minorities and NGOs. He also accused the government of applying a double standard by scrutinising foreign donations received by NGOs while pointing to foreign contributions received by the RSS.
RIJIJU CHALLENGES OPPOSITION TO NAME A CLAUSE
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju rejected the Opposition's objections and pointed out that Congress had itself demanded that the Bill be referred to a JPC.
Rijiju challenged the Opposition to identify a provision in the Bill that was against minorities.
“Show me one clause,” he said, questioning the basis of the Opposition's allegation.
He argued that objections to the legislation could be examined by the JPC and accused the Opposition of creating a political controversy around the Bill.
Rijiju also said the government was ready to respond to the Opposition's concerns if the House was allowed to function.
AKHILESH JOINS THE DEBATE
At around 2.30 pm, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav intervened in the exchange.
Yadav said he had expected the promised discussion at 3 pm and questioned Rijiju over the government's position on minorities.
“I thought there would be a debate at 3 pm. But I don't see anyone here. Kiren Rijiju ji, tell us, which bill have you brought without mentioning minorities?” he said.
At 2:32pm, Rijiju responded by asking the Opposition to identify even one clause in the Bill that was against minorities. “Show me even one clause that is against minorities. First read the bill,” he said.
The exchange reflected the broader political divide over the legislation, with the Opposition questioning its implications for NGOs and minorities and the government insisting that its provisions should first be examined by the parliamentary committee.
FCRA BILL SENT TO JPC
At around 2.34 pm, the FCRA Bill was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee through a voice vote.
The committee will have 21 members from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha. Lok Sabha members will be nominated by Speaker Om Birla, while Rajya Sabha members will be nominated by Chairman C P Radhakrishnan. The committee has been asked to submit its report to the Lok Sabha by the last day of the first week of the Winter Session this year.
The referral created an unusual political situation. The Opposition had demanded a JPC, but once the government agreed to send the Bill to the committee, Congress called for the legislation to be withdrawn instead.
A DAY OF OFFERS AND COUNTER-OFFERS
The day's proceedings captured the political dynamics of the Monsoon Session. The government offered a lengthy discussion on the July 20 incident. The Opposition insisted that the Home Minister answer a specific question instead.
The FCRA Bill then became the next flashpoint, with the government sending it to a JPC and the Opposition questioning its provisions.
In the end, Parliament got a committee to examine the FCRA legislation, but the political deadlock over the July 20 incident remained.
One side wanted Parliament to function and offered a debate. The other wanted a specific answer before entering a broader discussion.
The result was another day of political confrontation in the final stretch of the Monsoon Session.

headline: ‘Time to move on’: Bombay high court seeks ED view on Vijay Mallya’s 2020 plea
full_text:
‘Time to move on’: Bombay high court seeks ED view on Vijay Mallya’s 2020 plea
Vijay Mallya’s 2020 petition challenged a court order allowing an SBI-led bank consortium to use ED-confiscated assets to recover unpaid dues.
The Bombay high court on Wednesday observed that a long-running dispute over the recovery of dues from Vijay Mallya needed to “be brought to an end” after being told by Mallya’s lawyer that his 2020 petition against asset seizures was now redundant due to developments over the last six years.
Mallya’s original 2020 petition challenged an order passed by a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court, which had allowed a consortium of lender banks led by the State Bank of India (SBI) to utilise assets confiscated by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to recover his unpaid dues.
ALSO READ | Can’t say when I will return to India, Vijay Mallya tells HC
On Wednesday, senior advocate Amit Desai, appearing for Mallya, told the court that the 2020 petition was filed when settlement talks were ongoing and sought protection for specific assets. However, Desai argued that the application no longer survives as most of the mentioned assets have already been attached and dealt with.
‘Issue needs to be put to an end’: HC
The bench appeared to agree. “Actually, this issue needs to be put to an end. The idea is to move on… otherwise the relations and the economy of the country suffer,” justice Jadhav said.
The court directed ED to file an affidavit clarifying whether the settlement process has concluded and if “everything is done and dusted,” while emphasising that this would not impact the criminal prosecution against Mallya, which must still be “taken to its logical end.”
The high court said it would decide on the further course of action after hearing from ED’s deputy director concerned.
ALSO READ | Haryana: CBI court denies bail to ex-bank official in ₹550 crore fraud case
Mallya claims banks recovered ₹15,000 crore
Desai had argued that Mallya’s civil liabilities were over now. “Public sector banks keeping this matter pending is unfortunate,” Desai said, claiming that banks have already recovered around ₹15,000 crore from Mallya against the original claimed dues of ₹6,203.35 crore plus interest.
“The RBI audit itself says it’s an airline’s business failure and nothing else. Banks have taken away ₹15,000 crore and now they say sorry. That’s not good enough,” he added.
ED had allowed liquidation of confiscated assets
In February 2019, ED informed the special PMLA court that it had no objection to the SBI-led consortium liquidating Mallya’s confiscated assets to recover the debts. Mallya was declared a fugitive economic offender in January 2019.
Mallya’s legal cases and extradition
Mallya has been facing multiple legal cases in India related to alleged loan defaults, fraud, money laundering and financial irregularities in connection with those loans. In July 2015, the Banking Securities & Fraud Cell of the Central Bureau of Investigation registered an FIR against him in connection with alleged irregularities in loans taken by Kingfisher Airlines from a consortium of banks led by IDBI Bank. He was charged with criminal conspiracy, criminal breach of trust and criminal misconduct.
Mallya left India in March 2016 amid mounting legal pressure and has remained in the United Kingdom since then. He has been resisting extradition to India to face criminal charges. After the enactment of the FEO Act in 2018, proceedings were initiated against Mallya under the law, prompting him to file a petition in the high court. Although UK courts have approved his extradition to India, Mallya has utilised what has been termed a “confidential legal matter” to stay on in the UK. This is widely understood to mean an application for political asylum.

headline: ‘Compromised PM sold India’s interest': Rahul Gandhi after US court's relief to industrialist Gautam Adani
full_text:
‘Compromised PM sold India’s interest': Rahul Gandhi after US court's relief to industrialist Gautam Adani
A US court dismissed criminal charges against Gautam Adani and associates, ending a legal saga.
Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday raised doubts over the dismissal of criminal charges against industrialist Gautam Adani by a US court and launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the development.
In a post on X, the Congress leader said, “There is much more to this than meets the eye. A compromised PM was forced to sell India’s interests. India is paying a huge price.”
Rahul Gandhi’s remarks came after a US court on Monday ended the long-running legal saga involving Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and their associate Vneet Jaain by dismissing the criminal charges against them at the request of the US government.
Also read | US court ends all criminal charges against Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and associate Vneet Jaain
In its judgement, Judge Nicholas Garaufis of the district court for the Eastern District of New York dismissed criminal charges against the Adanis related to securities and wire fraud with prejudice.
The district court also finalised a settlement between the Adanis and the US Securities and Exchange Commission, which will see the Adanis pay the US government $18 million without admitting guilt and formally settle the civil securities fraud charges against them.
Adani reacts to the development
Reacting to the legal relief, Gautam Adani took to the social media platform X and welcomed the judgement.
Also read | Gautam Adani welcomes big legal relief by US court: 'Deep respect for judiciary'
"I welcome the US court’s decision with humility and deep respect for the judicial process. Throughout this challenging period, our faith in truth, fairness and the rule of law remained unwavering," Adani wrote on X.
"My deepest gratitude to those who never lost faith in us, in the system and in India’s capacity for justice," he wrote, adding that the Adani name will work towards "building for our nation."
What were the charges?
In 2024, the US Justice Department unsealed an indictment against the Adani group and its associates, alleging that the group had been involved in a $265 million bribery scheme to win solar energy contracts with Indian government entities.
Furthermore, the Adanis were also accused of participating in an effort to defraud American and international investors by lying about the company's anti-corruption activities.
Also Read | Not aware of any quid pro quo offer: Adani
In addition to the case by the Justice Department, the US Securities and Exchange Commission also filed civil charges against Gautam and Sagar Adani.
Ahead of Monday's judgement, the Department of Justice told the court in May that it would decline to pursue further legal action against Gautam Adani and his associates.
US Principal Associate Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter also stated later in July, that the charges against the Adani group should not have been brought in the first place.

Karnataka bandh: Will schools be open tomorrow during shutdown over Cauvery water-sharing row?
Banks, hospitals, pharmacies and public transport and other essential services are likely to remain unaffected during the bandh.
As the Cauvery water-sharing row between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka intensifies, several Kanada organisations have given a call for a Karnataka Bandh on Thursday, August 13.
The bandh comes after the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) directed Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days from August 12.
"We will observe Bandh at any cost. I appeal to everyone to support our call for strike," Vatal Nagaraj, convener of Kannada Chalavali Vatal Paksha was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.
