The Mandya District Farmers' Welfare Protection Committee also announced a protest near the Visvesvaraya statue in Mandya on Wednesday as it urged the farmers, Kannada organisations, workers, women and citizens to participate in the demonstrations.
"The government should not release water under any circumstances," a farmer leader was quoted as saying as he called the CWMA direction a threat to the Karnataka's water security.
Will schools remains open?
Yes, the schools will operate per normal on August 13 during Karnataka Bandh, The News Minute reported, citing Karnataka Associated Managements of Schools (KAMS). The body had earlier called for the closure of schools, but later rolled back the call, saying that it would impact the academic schedules.
Also read: Karnataka weighs Cauvery order amid water stress
However, the KAMS has said it would extend moral support to the bandh. School managements, teaching staff and non-teaching employees have been asked to wear black ribbons or black strips as a mark of solidarity, the report added.
What about banks, public transport and hospitals?
Banks, hospitals, pharmacies and public transport and other essential services are likely to remain unaffected during the statewide bandh that will remain in effective from 6 am to 6 pm on August 13.

What CM DKS said
As the protests broke out in the Cauvery region, Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar said the state government has the duty to protect the state's farmers and abide by court orders, and the government will decide on it after assessing the situation.
"I know that 12,000 cusecs orders have come. I'm also monitoring our inflow. Considering our situation, I have the duty to protect our farmers. We must protect our farmers and also abide by the court orders. Keeping both these aspects in mind, I will discuss with the irrigation minister and officials," Shivakumar said, news agency PTI reported.

full_text:
For a very long time, anyone considered particularly good at studies in India was almost automatically tipped to become a doctor or an engineer. 3 Idiots made a joke of that national fixation years ago, showing a world in which parents and professors seemed convinced they knew what success ought to look like.Alternative streams of education have slowly gained popularity since then. The race to become a doctor or engineer, however, has hardly become easier. As the pool of aspirants expands beyond the metros, competition for a coveted seat has only become harder. Many tuition centres, almost like factories, in Kota and other places train students rigorously to pass these coveted exams.The May 3 NEET-UG examination was cancelled after the paper-leak controversy and nearly 20 lakh candidates returned for a re-examination on June 21. The anger travelled from coaching rooms to Jantar Mantar and towards Parliament, propelled by the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party. Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister on July 25. The CBI chargesheet has since named 13 accused, including three subject experts associated with NTA, while CJP has demanded that the testing agency itself be replaced. Similar protests over exam leaks have now erupted in Jharkhand.The anger that erupted at Jantar Mantar after the leak is merely a reflection of the deeper anxiety over competition for quality jobs and the yearning for a stronger CV, which for many begins with studying at a hallowed institution. How difficult, then, is it to get into a top-tier engineering or medical college in India?
The IIT-NIT funnel
Engineering here means the route to the country's most sought-after public engineering institutions, particularly the IITs and NITs, not every engineering college.
The pathways are slightly different. JEE Main is the direct gateway to the 31 NITs participating in JoSAA 2026, while it also acts as the screening stage for candidates hoping to reach the IITs through JEE Advanced.NTA recorded 15,38,468 unique candidates appearing for JEE Main 2026. Of the 1,87,389 who registered for JEE Advanced, 1,79,694 appeared in both papers and 56,880 qualified. The JoSAA 2026 matrix provides 18,826 IIT seats.Put another way, the original Main candidate pool is roughly 82 times the number of IIT seats. Even after reaching JEE Advanced, there were 9.5 test-takers and almost exactly three qualifiers for every IIT place.
How competitive is the field
Not every JEE Main candidate is a serious IIT contender, so the 82-to-one comparison is largely academic. It is a measure of the scale of the field, not an individual's admission probability. Seats are allocated across categories and other reservation rules. But in both IITs and NITs, the fight is not only for a seat, but also for a preferred stream and college.Interest in admission wanes considerably as one goes down the value chain. That distinction becomes clearer when one looks at the rest of India's engineering system. The latest Rajya Sabha disclosure by the ministry states that BTech/BE enrolment in AICTE-approved institutions rose to 13.56 lakh in 2025-26. Yet adding up the state-wise vacancies in the same annexure produces 2,52,914 empty seats. In the same year, 67 AICTE-approved engineering and technology institutions applied for closure or were listed as closed. So India does not lack engineering seats. What it lacks are the seats students value most in IITs, top NITs and other highly sought-after institutions.
What government told in Parliament
The engineering race does not necessarily end with a BTech for all. For those aiming for an MTech from an IIT, NIT or another premier institution, GATE becomes another competitive gate.The numbers are substantial. In GATE 2026, 2,11,020 candidates appeared for the Computer Science and Information Technology paper, while 95,752 appeared for Electronics and Communication, 76,385 for Civil Engineering and 69,242 for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence.Those figures cannot simply be converted into applicants-per-MTech-seat ratios. Candidates can sit more than one GATE paper. For NITs, the pool is still broader. CCMT 2026 accepts valid GATE scores from 2024, 2025 and 2026. So candidates for these seats can effectively be competing with more than one year's GATE cohort. However, suffice to say, the odds are tough for aspirants.
Medicine has its own hierarchy
Medical education runs on the same preference for high-value seats. For the valid June 21 NEET re-examination, 22,79,743 candidates were registered, 19,99,895 appeared and 11,21,185 qualified. The cancellation itself affected the denominator, with 2,79,848 registered candidates not sitting the re-test.Against this pool, the NMC's July matrix lists 1,36,939 MBBS seats for 2026-27, excluding Institutes of National Importance such as AIIMS. The NEET test-taker pool is about 14.6 times the listed MBBS capacity, while the number of qualified candidates is about 8.2 times the capacity. These are broad national comparisons, not individual admission odds, since seats are divided across quotas, categories and state eligibility rules. But the headline number conceals another hierarchy.Of those 1,36,939 NMC-listed seats, 63,296 are in government colleges and 73,643 are private. Private colleges account for about 54% of the listed capacity. If we compare the NEET re-test pool only with NMC-listed government seats, the candidate pool is roughly 31.6 times the available government capacity.
Level of competition
Government seats are prized because of substantially greater affordability, the reputation of established institutions and, in many large public hospitals, the prospect of extensive clinical exposure. This year's expansion makes that distinction sharper. NMC approved 9,911 additional MBBS seats for 2026-27. Of these, 7,800 are private and only 2,111 government.
Skewed nature of growth of MBBA seats
Nearly four out of every five newly approved seats were added on the private side. So medicine and engineering are more alike than they look. In both, the real contest is increasingly over which seat, in which institution, and at what cost. There is, however, an important difference between the engineering and medical journeys.An engineer can enter another fierce competition through GATE for MTech, but postgraduate study remains an optional route for most. For doctors who want to specialise, postgraduate training is much closer to another necessary career gate.The latest completed NEET-PG examination makes the scale clear. More than 2.42 lakh candidates appeared for NEET-PG 2025, according to the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences. NEET-PG 2026 is yet to be held and is scheduled for August 30.And the postgraduate pool is much smaller than the undergraduate universe. The Centre said in July that India had 86,360 postgraduate medical seats in 2025-26. Earlier this year, it said 8,967 additional PG seats, including those in AIIMS and other Institutes of National Importance, had been approved for 2025-26. For some who pursue super-specialisation, there may still be another competitive gate beyond that.
Governments have tried to build capacity
Governments have tried to accommodate more students in quality institutions. Seven IITs have been established since 2014, while approved expansion at five newer IITs is intended to create capacity for another 6,500 students. In medicine, 157 government medical colleges have been approved under one central scheme, with 137 already functional. Separate government programmes have also expanded undergraduate and postgraduate capacity.But adding seats does not automatically solve the problem. The latest figures placed before Parliament show 15.35 lakh registered allopathic doctors and 7.52 lakh AYUSH practitioners and, assuming 80% availability in both groups, a government-estimated combined practitioner-population ratio of 1:778. Yet the existence of incentives for hard-to-serve areas underlines another problem. Doctors and specialists are not distributed evenly. So hierarchy exists beyond educational institutions too, which makes the work of policymakers even harder in a large country like India.
How other countries filter their best
In the US, 54,699 people applied to MD-granting medical schools in 2025 and 23,440 matriculated, but candidates generally apply after or during undergraduate study and typically take the MCAT. In England, medicine remains one of the most competitive university routes, with a sizeable socioeconomic gap in acceptance rates.France pushes much of the filter inside university, with two in five students entering its PASS or L.AS health routes in 2022 reaching medicine or another major health discipline within two years. China's Gaokao had 1.29 crore registrations in 2026, but admissions are distributed across provinces, universities and programmes rather than through a single NEET-style medicine pool. Russia uses another lever altogether, with targeted state-funded medical training linked to future employment and workforce.
Every country has tried different approaches based on the reality of the land. Whether a test like NEET is the best way forward is still being intensely debated. However, for policymakers, the only feasible solution seems to be building more institutions of comparable quality, ones students believe can offer strong education, credible employment prospects and a better quality of life. Simply multiplying seats is unlikely to be enough if aspirants continue to see only a small proportion of them as worth fighting for.

headline: BBMB share dispute: Punjab very close to amicable settlement, Centre to SC
full_text:
BBMB share dispute: Punjab very close to amicable settlement, Centre to SC
New Delhi, The Centre on Wednesday told the Supreme Court that the Punjab government is very close to agreeing to its proposal on the issue of payment of dues to Himachal Pradesh arising out of the Bhakra Beas Management Board projects since 1966.
On July 30, the Centre had told the apex court that an amicable settlement can be reached on a new cashless formula between the partner states for payment of arrears.
The top court had then recorded that the governments of Himachal and Haryana have in principle agreed to the Centre's proposal but the Punjab government has objected.
The apex court had pulled up the Punjab government for not agreeing to the proposal, observing that it has the habit of not following the decree of the court.
On Wednesday, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for the Himachal Pradesh government, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the apex court has listed the matter for finding out whether the Punjab government is agreeable to the Centre's proposal or not.
"I must say now today we speak in a joint voice. Punjab is coming very closer," Attorney General R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre, told the bench.
"I think we are going to iron out the creases," Venkataramani said and requested the bench to list the matter for hearing next week.
The bench posted the matter for hearing on August 20.
According to sources, BBMB is paying 7.19 per cent share of Himachal Pradesh's electricity from Bhakra Beas projects after November 1, 2011, while Punjab and Haryana have not paid the outstanding dues of BBMB projects for the previous period, which is 13,066 million units.
Under the proposal, since no consensus was reached among the parties on the rate of electricity to be applied, the Centre has suggested payout to Himachal by Punjab and Haryana in energy terms.
It was also decided that Himachal will not pay the dues of ₹420 crore to Punjab and Haryana and the amount will be adjusted from 13,066 million units of electricity.
According to the Centre's proposal, the payout to Himachal by Punjab and Haryana will not be in monetary terms but on an energy scale for over 12,000 million units out of 13,066 million units of electricity arrears.
Besides, the hilly state from which the river Beas flows does not have to pay over ₹400 crore towards capital cost to Punjab and Haryana.
On July 30, Venkataramani had told the bench that the government has suggested a total cashless settlement because if the parties go by the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, there will be no settlement.
Senior advocate Nidesh Gupta, appearing for the Punjab government, had told the bench that they have a problem with the rate at which arrears are to be paid.
He had said the rate of ₹2.5 per unit of electricity is very high and it should be a reasonable rate, otherwise, the state will incur a loss of around ₹2,000 crore.
The bench had told Gupta that if Punjab does not agree to amicable settlement, then the court would examine the issue on merit and pass orders.
The Himachal Pradesh government had said the state was entitled to the arrears on the terms decided by the apex court in 2011.
After failing to settle an inter-state dispute about allocation of assets for decades following the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, Himachal had moved the apex court in 1996 through an original suit, pleading that as a successor state, it was entitled to 7.19 per cent share in the BBMB projects.
After the central government failed to settle the dispute between the states out of court, the top court on September 27, 2011 passed a decree.
According to the decision of the apex court of 2011, the share of Himachal was fixed at 7.19 per cent, while that of Punjab and Haryana at 51.80 per cent and 37.51 per cent respectively.
Rajasthan's share largely remained unaffected, while the share of Union Territory of Chandigarh was fixed as 3.50 per cent.
According to the 2011 decision of the court, Himachal was to get a share in the Bhakra project from November 01, 1966, the Dehar project from November 1977 and the Pong Dam project from January 1978.
On July 13, Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said that nearly 15 years ago, the Supreme Court had clearly recognised the state's entitlement to 7.19 per cent share in BBMB projects and the benefits arising from them.
He said that despite this, Himachal had been deprived of its share of 13,066 million units of electricity and the associated financial benefits for more than a decade.
Sukhu said the state was taking all necessary legal and administrative steps to recover approximately ₹4,200 crore pending dues from the BBMB.

headline: Telangana SIR: 73 lakh voters may be excluded from draft electoral rolls
full_text:
Telangana SIR: 73 lakh voters may be excluded from draft electoral rolls
The draft rolls will be published on August 17, revealing significant discrepancies and potential voter reductions across districts.
Around 7.33 million names, accounting for 21.7% of the total 33.8 million electors, are likely to face deletion in the draft electoral roll following the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Telangana, chief electoral officer (CEO) C Sudharshan Reddy said on Tuesday.
The enumeration process under the SIR concluded on Monday and the draft rolls are likely to be published on August 17.
Of the 33,826,448 electors registered in the current rolls, enumeration was completed and digitised for 26,487,214, or 78.3% electors, the CEO said. “The enumeration forms of as many 7,339,234 electors, accounting for 21.70% could not be collected and uploaded,” Reddy added.
Hyderabad records lowest digitisation rate at 58.89%
According to data uploaded on the Telangana CEO website, Hyderabad recorded the lowest progress with only 58.89% of the total forms being digitised, while Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri district topped the state with 94.31% digitisation of forms.
Rangareddy and Medchal-Malkajgiri districts — adjacent to Hyderabad and accounting for 28 of the state’s 119 assembly constituencies — recorded 65.16% and 63.97% of enrolment, respectively, the data said. The two districts collectively are likely to see the total number of electors fall from around 11.4 million to 7.1 million after the completion of SIR, an official familiar with the matter said.
“This means that more than one out of every three electors included in the earlier electoral rolls is currently not reflected in the provisional figures,” the official said.
Over 4.5 million voters identified as permanent migrants
According to the CEO, at least 4,518,961 electors have permanently shifted their residence and they have been categorised as migrants.
“These voters were found to be no longer residing at the addresses mentioned in the present electoral rolls. In several cases, field-level verification indicated that voters had moved permanently to other locations,” Reddy said.
Among other districts, Kamareddy recorded 89.61% enrolment, followed by Kumuram Bheem Asifabad 89.43%, Karimnagar 88.59%, Nirmal 87.89%, Rajanna-Sircilla 87.7%, Adilabad 86.46%, Nizamabad 85.28%, Peddapalli 83.69% and Mancherial 82.56%, according to the Election Commission of India (ECI) data.
SIR flags deceased, untraceable and duplicate voters
Booth-level officers (BLOs) also identified 922,230 electors as dead, 1,125,546 as untraceable and 670,203 as already enrolled in other places. Another 1,02,294 electors had not submitted their enumeration forms, the CEO said.
The SIR exercise also identified around 318,000 duplicate electors in possession of voter identity cards of more than one places. These duplicate entries are also likely to be removed from the draft rolls.
There has also been considerable variation among districts in the digitisation of around 6.1 million enumeration forms collected.
“Notices will be issued to such voters after draft rolls are published on August 17. Such voters will have an opportunity to appear before the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) and establish their eligibility by producing any one of the identity documents specified by the Election Commission,” the CEO said.
Hyderabad constituencies face voter declines of over 40%
Of the 15 assembly constituencies in Hyderabad district, 10 have recorded a decline of more than 40% in the number of voters. In Rangareddy district, three of the eight constituencies have witnessed a reduction of over 40%. In Medchal-Malkajgiri district, Uppal has recorded a decline of 39.95% among the five constituencies in the district, according to the ECI data.
“After the draft electoral rolls are published on August 17, voters will be able to check whether their names have been included, whether there are errors in their personal details and whether their names have been correctly mapped to the respective polling stations,” the official cited above said.
After examining all claims, objections, applications and corrections, the final electoral rolls are scheduled to be published on October 19.

headline: Delhi HC asks Meta to explain its access policy on copyright management tool
full_text:
Delhi HC asks Meta to explain its access policy on copyright management tool
“Why does everybody not have access to it then? It is like giving the key to the robber and not to the owner of the house,” Justice Bhambhani remarked
The Delhi high court on Wednesday told Meta to explain the criteria to grant users access to its copyright management tool that lets people protect and manage their original content on Facebook and Instagram.
A bench of Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani was hearing a petition by a content creator Mohit Kumar who complained that some people downloaded his content and used their access to Meta Rights Tool to claim copyright over his videos.
Kumar said he could not have claimed copyright over the videos because Meta hadn’t given him access to the tool.
“Why does everybody not have access to it then? It is like giving the key to the robber and not to the owner of the house,” Justice Bhambhani remarked.
The court made the observation in a suit filed by Kumar, an Indian e-commerce and AI business coach who creates educational content on social media under the handle “Rise with Mohit”.
Also Read:Govt asks Meta to revamp algorithms, curb spread of propaganda: Report
Kumar said he applied for access to the tool thrice, but his applications were rejected without clear reasons, while individuals with only a few hundred followers appeared to have secured access.
He further argued that fraudulent copyright strikes could result in a genuine creator’s account being taken down overnight, wiping out years of work, monetisation, brand collaborations and business opportunities.
Meta’s counsel submitted that the fraudulent strikes issued against Kumar were reversed and that content removed pursuant to those strikes had been reinstated.
The court, however, issued summons in Kumar’s suit and listed the matter for September 24.
It observed that the issue arose in several cases involving content creators and therefore warranted closer scrutiny.
“There are some chinks in the armour, some loopholes have been noticed. We better sort it out,” the court remarked.
The court’s direction came days after it agreed to examine on September 24 whether social media platforms can suspend or delete user accounts solely on the basis of copyright strikes.
The same judge is considering the issue in a petition filed by content creator Saurabh Maurya, whose Instagram account was suspended following a copyright strike that was subsequently found to be false.

headline: H1N1 flu cases swell in Delhi: Symptoms, precautions and who is at risk
full_text:
H1N1 flu cases swell in Delhi: Symptoms, precautions and who is at risk
The government has said that the hospitals are "fully prepared" to handle patients with separate wards and dedicated rooms for H1N1 and dengue patients.
Delhi's swine flu cases have gone up this monsoon season with the capital recording 1,349 confirmed cases of H1N1 virus this year so far. The government has said that the hospitals are "fully prepared" to handle patients with separate wards and dedicated rooms been set aside for H1N1 and dengue patients.
Hospitals have reported a rise in the number of patients with symptoms like cold, cough and fever over the past few weeks.
Also read: Virulent dengue strain circulating in Delhi: Officials
"Over the past 3-4 weeks, hospitals have witnessed a rise in patients presenting with cough, cold and high fever. Testing has revealed a significant increase in H1N1 (swine flu) cases, with doctors reporting that they are seeing around 7-10 such patients daily in the OPD. There has also been a slight increase in COVID-19 cases," Dr Satish Koul, Principal Director and Unit Head of Internal Medicine at Fortis Memorial Research Institute, Gurugram, was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.
Also read: Yamuna sludge may be behind ammonia spikes: Central pollution board study
People on social media have also posted how more and more people in Delhi are falling sick with flu-like symptoms. However, doctors have said that most H1N1 cases are mild and symptoms subside within three to five days.
Swine flu symptoms
- Fever or chills
- Persistent cough
- Sore throat
- Body aches and muscle pain
- Headache
- Runny or stuffy nose
- Nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea
While the above symptoms are manageable, patients should look out for symptoms such as difficulty in breathing or shortness of breath, chest pain, bluish pain, bluish lips.
Health experts on sharp surge in swine flu cases
While the doctors have reported a sharp rise in the number of H1N1 cases being reported, health experts have said the sudden change in temperature can be a cause of flu outbreak.
Also read: 5 days on, Kanwar rush, heavy rain, traffic brings Delhi to standstill
"During monsoon, there's a decrease in temperature. So, because of the temperature change, the influenza virus is more common nowadays. They have a sore throat, nasal discharge, dry cough and headache," Dr Sanjeev Sinha, professor of medicine, department of medicine, AIIMS, Delhi told ANI.
Vulnerable groups at risk
Dr Sinha said that vulnerable groups, including the elderly and those suffering from diabetes, hypertension and chronic kidney disease, are more prone to infections.
"In our OPD, there is an increased number of patients who are suffering from upper respiratory tract infections, and we found that they are positive for influenza, especially H1N1 and influenza A," he was quoted as saying.
Delhi recorded 229 H1N1 cases during this time last year, as compared to 1,349 cases this year, marking six fold rise, according to NDTV.
What to do if you test positive for H1N1
Those diagnosed with H1N1 should isolate at home for two or three days and use a face mask, according t Dr Sinha . If you get the infection, immediately contact the doctor about the treatment.
Dr Atul Kakar, Chairperson, Internal Medicine, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, told ANI that Delhi is witnessing a seasonal increase in viral respiratory infections, with many patients reporting flu-like symptoms. "Many of them have high-grade fever, which has been running for a few days. A few of them have cold and cough; many of them complain of joint pains, muscle pain, extreme weakness, runny nose and throat pain. This is a type of trend which we are now seeing, especially during this post-rainy season. So, the number of patients is definitely much more," he said.

headline: Lok Sabha probe panel finds Justice Yashwant Varma guilty in cash-at-home case
full_text:
Lok Sabha probe panel finds Justice Yashwant Varma guilty in cash-at-home case
The incident came to light after a fire broke out in the official residence of Justice Varma on the night of March 14 last year.
The three-member inquiry committee probing allegations against Allahabad High Court judge justice Yashwant Varma has found all three articles of charge against him proved, holding that his explanation regarding the discovery of a large quantity of unaccounted currency at his official residence was “evasive” and “misleading”.
The report, tabled in both Houses of Parliament on Wednesday, stopped short of holding that the currency belonged to justice Varma for want of substantial evidence establishing personal ownership. But it rejected his defence that he had no knowledge of the cash or responsibility for what happened to it after it was discovered following a fire at his official residence in Delhi on March 14, 2025.
Also Read | Can Parliament act against a judge who has already resigned? Constitutional puzzle in ex-judge Varma's case
“The cumulative record therefore establishes the presence of substantial currency notes within the official premises, failure to satisfactorily explain its presence, failure to preserve the material, later non-availability of the currency notes, and absence of any substantiated defence capable of displacing the evidence led before the Committee,” the 126-page report said.
The committee comprised Supreme Court judge justice Aravind Kumar, then Bombay high court chief justice Shrikrishna Chandrashekhar, who has since been elevated to the Supreme Court, and senior advocate BV Acharya.
Also Read | ‘For cheap publicity’: SC junks plea for criminal probe against Justice Varma
The panel rejected justice Varma’s contention that the storeroom where the cash was found was beyond his control. It noted evidence concerning a locked cabinet containing his personal articles in the room and held that the circumstances established a sufficient connection between the judge and the premises. The first article of charge was consequently held proved.
The committee was also critical of the failure to preserve the burnt currency after the fire.
While it did not find direct evidence that justice Varma himself physically removed the cash, it held him responsible for failing to ensure preservation of material evidence from premises under his institutional control. It also examined the role of people attached to his household and establishment in the handling of the storeroom and currency. The second article of charge was held proved.
Also Read | ‘Deep anguish...’: Inside justice Yashwant Varma's resignation letter to President
The panel was particularly critical of justice Varma’s explanation during the inquiry. It examined his initial denial of any knowledge of the currency and his subsequent allegations of conspiracy, planting of cash and deficiencies in the collection and preservation of evidence. The committee found that these explanations failed to account for the presence of the cash or displace the evidence before it.
It also drew an adverse inference from justice Varma’s decision not to enter the witness box and subject himself to cross-examination. The committee said his defence was “false” in parts and found his overall explanation evasive and misleading. The third article of charge was also held proved.
Also Read | ‘Inquiry marked by unfairness': Justice Yashwant Varma withdraws from cash-pile probe after resignation
The findings follow an earlier in-house inquiry ordered by then Chief Justice of India Sanjiv Khanna after the controversy erupted in March 2025. After that panel found justice Varma’s explanation unsatisfactory, CJI Khanna asked him to resign or face the constitutional process for his removal. Justice Varma declined and the report was forwarded to the President and Prime Minister.
Parliamentary removal proceedings followed, with the Lok Sabha admitting a motion against him and constituting the statutory inquiry committee. Justice Varma, however, resigned from judicial office on April 9, 2026, while the parliamentary inquiry was underway.
It remains to be seen whether the tabling of the report marks the end of the matter, or whether Parliament can still consider the implications of the findings and explore the possibility of pursuing proceedings for justice Varma’s removal through impeachment despite his resignation.

headline: ‘Unbearably hot’: SpiceJet passengers suffer for hours after AC fails on Delhi-Pune flight
full_text:
‘Unbearably hot’: SpiceJet passengers suffer for hours after AC fails on Delhi-Pune flight
The passengers protested after the aircraft was moved towards the runway despite the problem, prompting the airline to return.
More than 100 passengers travelling from Delhi to Pune on a SpiceJet flight were left distressed for several hours after the aircraft developed an air-conditioning problem soon after boarding, with passengers alleging that the cabin became unbearably hot and humid.
The passengers protested after the aircraft was moved towards the runway despite the problem, prompting the airline to return. The replacement flight eventually took off around 5 am — nearly seven hours after the scheduled 9.55 pm departure.
The incident occurred on Tuesday night, and passengers later raised concerns over the airline’s handling of the technical problem and its communication with them.
Also Read: Number of injured on Air India Phuket-Delhi flight that dropped 300 feet rises to 24
“On August 11, 2026, SpiceJet flight SG 105, scheduled to operate from Delhi to Pune, encountered a last-minute technical issue. An alternate aircraft was arranged, and the flight subsequently operated to Pune. SpiceJet deeply regrets the inconvenience caused to the passengers,” a SpiceJet spokesperson said in an official statement.
Leshpal Javalge, a passenger who was travelling on the flight and was among those who protested at Delhi airport, said the trouble began after passengers boarded the aircraft at around 10.30 pm.
“The flight was scheduled for 9.55 pm, but we boarded at around 10.30 pm. Initially, we thought the AC would take some time to start, as sometimes happens after boarding. But nearly half an hour passed and the cabin became extremely hot. The aircraft was completely full and, with the doors closed, the heat and humidity became unbearable. Everyone was sweating heavily,” he said.
Javalge said the conditions were particularly difficult for children, elderly passengers and pregnant women.
Also Read: Full emergency briefly declared at Chennai airport after left engine issue on IndiGo flight
“They told us that they would start the AC and fix everything within two minutes. But when they finally switched it on, hot air started coming directly from the blowers. Instead of cooling the cabin, it became even hotter. It literally felt like a gas chamber inside the aircraft,” he said.
“We had to shout and tell them to switch off the blowers. At least if they stopped, the hot air would stop coming into the cabin. It was at that point that we realised something was technically wrong with the aircraft,” he added.
Despite the discomfort, the aircraft was subsequently moved towards the runway at around 11 pm, prompting passengers to raise stronger objections.
“The aircraft was taken towards the runway even though the problem had not been properly resolved. We asked them to change the flight. We were not prepared to take a risk with our lives,” Javalge said.
Another passenger, who requested anonymity, said, “The biggest problem was that nobody was clearly telling us what had gone wrong. We were sitting inside an extremely hot aircraft with children and elderly people around us. When we questioned the staff, we did not get a satisfactory response. We had no confidence that the aircraft was fit to fly.”
The protest intensified as passengers collectively demanded that the aircraft be changed. Javalge said the airline eventually called its technical team to inspect the aircraft.
He also recalled the presence of a large number of CISF personnel during the protest.
“There were around 100 to 150 CISF personnel carrying weapons around us. Naturally, that made the situation even more tense,” he said.

headline: Mumbai biker, 24, killed after motorcycle hit by heavy vehicle in Chhattisgarh
full_text:
Mumbai biker, 24, killed after motorcycle hit by heavy vehicle in Chhattisgarh
The accident took place around 6 am at Markatola Ghat under Purur police station limits on National Highway 30, roughly 100 km from state capital Raipur.

headline: The first indication of the Union Government’s softening of stance on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, emerged on August 9, when several Christian organisations launched coordinated appeals on YouTube, Facebook and WhatsApp...
full_text:
The first indication of the Union Government’s softening of stance on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, emerged on August 9, when several Christian organisations launched coordinated appeals on YouTube, Facebook and WhatsApp, urging the Centre to either refer the Bill to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) or withdraw it altogether.
The appeals were seen as an attempt to provide the government with an honourable route to step back from pushing the legislation through Parliament.
On Wednesday, Minister of State for Home Nityanand Rai moved a motion in the Lok Sabha to send the Bill to a JPC. Amid din, the motion was adopted, giving Parliament more time to examine the contentious provisions in the Bill.
Ever since the Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on March 25, Opposition parties have protested the legislation. It was among the bunch of legislations listed for passage in the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament, which concludes on August 13.
The Bill makes way for the appointment of a ‘designated authority’ to take over, manage, or dispose of assets created from foreign funds when an NGO’s FCRA registration is suspended, cancelled, or not renewed. This authority will have the powers of a civil court and can order the transfer or sale of assets owned by NGOs to either the government or any other body.
Since July 6, Union Home Minister Amit Shah has held at least four meetings with various Christian groups to allay their concerns. The latest meeting was held on August 6 in the Parliament House complex when he met an 18-member delegation comprising all Christian denominations — Catholic, Protestant and Orthodox.
Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam MP P. Wilson, who led the delegation called the Joint Action Forum on Minorities, said the Home Minister granted an audience after they wrote a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
“We had given a representation to the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister’s Office forwarded it to the Home Minister, and we were called by the Home Minister for a meeting,” Mr. Wilson said.
Government sources said the subsequent decision to refer the Bill to a JPC was also a conciliatory move aimed at breaking the parliamentary deadlock, with Opposition parties continuing to demand a discussion on the police action against Jantar Mantar protesters on July 20.
U.S. pressure
The statement made by U.S. Congressman Riley Moore, a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, on August 4 on X, where he alleged that the Bill could permit government takeovers of churches and religious charities, was also one of the reasons for the rethink, sources said.
In the post, the Republican politician described the Bill as a “clear attack against Christians” and warned that the issue could become a concern in India-U.S. relations.
On Wednesday, the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of India (CBCI) and the National Council of Churches in India (NCCI) welcomed the move, saying it was a “positive step”.
Jonathan Lalremruata, advisor to the CBCI, told The Hindu that the legislation should differentiate between major and minor offences before the assets built by an NGO are taken over.
“Regulation of foreign funds is a must. Action should be taken against those NGOs which indulge in anti-national activities. If a building has been made at a cost of ₹100 lakh, and ₹50 lakh is foreign funds and the rest is domestic contribution, which part is going to be tagged as foreign funds?” Mr. Lalremruata said, adding that they will be deposing before the committee with their suggestions.
He said by next week, as decided during the meeting with Mr. Shah on July 10, the CBCI will send a list of Christian institutions whose registrations have either been cancelled or delayed arbitrarily. FCRA registration is mandatory to receive foreign funds.
After his meeting with the Home Minister on August 6, Mizoram Chief Minister Lalduhoma had said the Bill would likely be discussed in the House on August 12.

headline: Why road accident death figures differ in govt reports, Gadkari tells Rajya Sabha
full_text:
Why road accident death figures differ in govt reports, Gadkari tells Rajya Sabha
The Centre said differences in India’s road crash death figures across MoRTH and NCRB reports stem from varying state and UT reporting methods.
The variation in India’s official road crash death figures in the government’s “Road Accidents in India”, “Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India” and “Crime in India” is due to differences in reporting methodologies adopted by some states and Union territories, the government told the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday. It said the Centre is working with states and UTs to improve the quality, consistency and harmonisation of road crash reporting.
According to a ministry of road transport and highways (MoRTH) report, 177,175 people died in road accidents in 2024. The NCRB’s Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India reported 175,142 deaths, while Crime in India recorded 162,500 deaths under “deaths due to negligence relating to road accident”.
Replying to a question by Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) Manoj Jha, road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari said the differences may be attributed to methodologies used by states and UTs, including reporting through police departments and State Crime Records Bureaus.
The Crime in India report has narrower coverage because it records road accident deaths that are registered under the relevant provisions of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) or the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The government said that not every road accident needs to involve a violation of penal law, resulting in lower figures in that dataset.
The government said a unified national road-crash database has already been established through the Electronic Detailed Accident Report (eDAR) portal, formerly known as the Integrated Road Accident Database. It serves as a central repository for road accident data and is integrated with VAHAN, Sarathi, PM Gati Shakti, NHAI’s Data Lake and the National Health Authority’s Transaction Management System. Data on eDAR is entered and verified by police, transport and health departments, road-owning agencies and insurance companies, Gadkari said.

Meth worth ₹9.4 cr seized from Mumbai, Greater Noida Israeli national; two foreign women held

The Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), with assistance from the local police, busted an inter-state drug racket, seizing ₹9.4 crore worth of 'Methamphetamine' from Mumbai and Greater Noida.

Meth tablets worth ₹45 cr seized from ambulance in Mizoram

A joint team of the Assam Rifles and the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) conducted the raid in Seling area on Thursday (August 6)last week, acting on a tip-off, the official said. headline: Karnataka bans sale of gutkha, pan masala containing tobacco or nicotine for 1 year
full_text:
Karnataka bans sale of gutkha, pan masala containing tobacco or nicotine for 1 year
Karnataka imposed a one-year ban on the manufacture, storage, distribution, transport, and sale of gutkha and pan masala containing tobacco or nicotine.
Karnataka on Wednesday banned the manufacture, storage, distribution, transportation and sale of gutkha and pan masala containing tobacco or nicotine across the state for a period of one year.
The notification, dated June 15, 2026, issued by the Commissioner of Food Safety, Karnataka State, said the ban has been imposed under clause (a) of sub-section (2) of Section 30 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, read with Regulation 2.3.4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulation, 2011.
Order cites health concerns
The order was issued citing public health concerns, and it prohibits gutkha and pan masala containing tobacco or nicotine across Karnataka with effect from the date of the notification.
Deep Dive
Also read | FSSAI bans plastic, foil packaging for pan masala under new rules
It also covers other products marketed separately that contain tobacco or nicotine in the final product, regardless of their name, whether packaged or unpackaged and whether sold as one product or packaged separately in a manner that facilitates mixing by consumers.
“Gutkha /Pan masala which contains tobacco and nicotine…”
“Any other products marketed separately having tobacco or nicotine in the final product by whatever name called, whether packaged or un-packaged and/or sold as one product, or though packaged as separate products, sold or distributed in such a manner to easily facilitate mixing by the consumer. Gutkha /Pan masala which contains tobacco and nicotine as ingredients, which are packed in sachets/pouches/package/containers etc., or by whatever name it is called in the entire State of Karnataka for a period of one year with effect from the date of notification,” the notification read.
Earlier, India’s food safety regulator, FSSAI, had updated its packaging rules to ban plastic and foil packaging for pan masala. Under the new Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Amendment Regulations, 2026, manufacturers can no longer use plastic-based materials, plastic laminates, aluminum foil, or metallised layers to pack pan masala.
Moving forward, pan masala can only be sold in eco-friendly packaging or traditional rigid containers.
The new rules have been notified as the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Amendment Regulations, 2026, and will come into force from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette, according to a press release.
Under the amended regulations, pan masala can be packed using paper, paper board, cellulose or other naturally derived materials.

headline: Air India pilot who tested positive for marijuana says he had sleep issues, was on prescribed medication
full_text:
Air India pilot who tested positive for marijuana says he had sleep issues, was on prescribed medication
On August 4, the Phuket-Delhi flight AI2379, an Airbus A320neo, lost 300 feet of altitude while cruising.
The pilot-in-command (PIC) of an Air India Phuket-Delhi flight that plunged 300 feet last week was on medication over “sleep difficulty”, people familiar with the matter told HT on Wednesday.
The development came a day after a confirmatory drug test said the PIC had tested positive for marijuana during a post-flight screening – a finding that raises questions over passenger safety.
The latest revelation was made by the PIC before a team of the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) during the course of investigation, the people cited above said.
“In his statement to the AAIB, the PIC said he was experiencing sleep difficulty over a preceding period related to personal circumstances for which he was prescribed medication by a family doctor,” one of the persons said, seeking anonymity.
“He also claimed that he struggled to sleep during his layover as well,” the person added.
There was no immediate comment from Air India at the time of filing this report.
On August 4, the Phuket-Delhi flight AI2379, an Airbus A320neo, lost 300 feet of altitude while cruising. The airline, in an initial statement, blamed the drop on turbulence. The government, in an earlier statement, said 14 passengers on board the flight – which was carrying 137 passengers, six cabin crew and two pilots – were injured.
However, the Press Information Bureau (PIB) in a statement on Tuesday increased the number of injured to 24 – four cabin crew members and 20 passengers.
As part of prescribed procedures, both pilots were checked for psychoactive substances after the flight landed in Delhi. The PIC’s preliminary drug test had returned a “non-negative” – an inconclusive finding – according to a government release on Sunday.
“The pilot in question has tested positive in the confirmatory test. He has tested positive for marijuana,” said a central government official aware of the development on Tuesday. To be sure, it is not clear when the marijuana was ingested.
The two pilots have been off-rostered pending a probe.
The incident, initially under investigation by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), was referred to the AAIB after being classified as a “serious” incident.
The AAIB is investigating the circumstances surrounding the occurrence, while the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is responsible for regulatory action based on the outcome of the investigation and the prescribed testing process.

headline: India’s long-term urban transition requires strategic planning: Parl panel report
full_text:
India’s long-term urban transition requires strategic planning: Parl panel report
The ministry instead cited AMRUT 2.0, Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) 2.0, PMAY-U 2.0, metro rail projects and PM e-Bus Sewa as initiatives addressing infrastructure, service delivery
The Union ministry of housing and urban affairs (MoHUA) will not commit to preparing a unified long-term urban strategy for India’s cities through 2047, especially in light of the government’s Viksit Bharat 2047 goals, a parliamentary standing committee report tabled in Parliament on Tuesday said.
In the action-taken report on the recommendations made by the Standing Committee on Housing and Urban Affairs regarding the ministry’s budgetary exercise, the ministry instead cited AMRUT 2.0, Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) 2.0, PMAY-U 2.0, metro rail projects and PM e-Bus Sewa as initiatives addressing infrastructure, service delivery, climate resilience and urban governance.
It also said that, with “urban development” being a state subject, the Centre plays a “catalytic role” through centrally sponsored schemes, sectoral missions, policy frameworks and financial support.
Also Read: Over 141,000 houses sanctioned under PMAY-Urban 2.0; total approvals cross one million
The committee had sought to ascertain whether the ministry had prepared a long-term strategy covering infrastructure creation, governance reforms, climate resilience, economic growth and social inclusion across metropolitan, Tier-II and Tier-III cities, with the previous such exercise done only in 2011, when the High Powered Expert Committee had assessed urban infrastructure requirements up to 2031.
‘Substantial investment‘
In its response, MoHUA said, “India’s long-term urban transition requires substantial investment and strategic planning,” and cited a World Bank estimate that India would need about $840 billion in urban infrastructure investment over 15 years to 2036, or an average of $55 billion a year. It also pointed to the ₹1 lakh crore Urban Challenge Fund and existing City Action Plans, State Annual Action Plans and convergence frameworks as tools for integrated planning.
However, the committee said the ministry’s interventions were “largely scheme-driven and sector-specific” and that no updated national-level assessment had been undertaken to estimate infrastructure demand, financing gaps and institutional requirements beyond 2030 in a holistic manner. It recommended constituting a new High-Level Expert Committee to assess urban infrastructure requirements, financing needs, governance reforms and capacity-building requirements up to 2047.
Budget utilisation
On budget utilisation, the committee flagged the nearly 40% reduction in the ministry’s 2025-26 Budget
Estimate, from ₹96,777 crore to ₹57,203.78 crore at the Revised Estimate stage, along with uneven scheme performance and unspent balances. MoHUA, however, said it had utilised 99.78% of its final Revised Estimate, spending ₹57,075.19 crore against ₹57,203.78 crore, and said it was taking steps to improve the accuracy of its Budget and Revised Estimate assessments.
On PMAY-U, the committee flagged the gap between houses sanctioned and completed and called for a review and suitable enhancement of central assistance. MoHUA said the scheme is demand-driven, with beneficiary selection and project formulation and execution undertaken by states, Union territories and public or private entities.
Also Read: Over 53k PMAY-U houses for urban poor remain unfinished in Punjab
The committee flagged delays in grounding projects and uneven utilisation under AMRUT 2.0 as the mission enters its final phase. MoHUA said 8,736 projects worth ₹1,95,422.52 crore had been approved under State Water Action Plans as of May 5, 2026, but contracts had been awarded for 7,402 projects worth ₹1,45,666.71 crore.
The ministry said it was providing states and Union territories with technical support and handholding, while regularly reviewing progress through meetings, video conferences, workshops and site visits.
With schemes such as Industrial Housing and National Urban Digital Mission remaining a non-starter, MoHUA cited delays in approval and said the same is responsible for slow implementation of the flagship 1 lakh crore Urban Challenge Fund.

headline: How Corporate India Is Investing In Climate & Environmental Resilience
full_text:
How Corporate India Is Investing In Climate & Environmental Resilience
TNN / Aug 12, 2026, 14:54 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
For years, environmental CSR in India was largely associated with tree plantation drives, cleanliness campaigns and occasional conservation projects. While those initiatives continue, companies are increasingly directing their CSR efforts towards something far more strategic. Theyâre strengthening climate resilience, securing water resources, promoting circular use of materials, and helping communities adapt to a warming world.The change reflects a growing realisation that environmental sustainability is no longer just about protecting nature. It is about protecting livelihoods, businesses, and the economy itself.Climate change is already affecting water availability, agriculture, supply chains, and industrial operations. As these risks intensify, Corporate India is beginning to see environmental CSR not as philanthropy but as an investment in long-term resilience.The scale of the challenge is enormous. India's draft Climate Finance Taxonomy estimates that the country will require around $2.5 trillion (Roughly an estimated Rs 2,50,00,000 crore or Rs 250 trillion) to meet its climate commitments by 2030, while climate adaptation alone could require investments of nearly Rs 56.7 trillion during the same period.
These figures underline why resilience has become a business imperative as much as an environmental one.Increasingly, companies are aligning their CSR programmes with this new reality. Water has emerged as one of the biggest priorities.According to the Central Ground Water Board, India extracts 245.6 billion cubic metres (BCM) of groundwater annually, with 751 assessment units already categorised as over-exploited, 206 as critical and another 711 as semi-critical. Agriculture accounts for 87% of groundwater extraction, making water scarcity a concern that extends far beyond farms to industries, cities and supply chains.For CSR programmes, this has meant a shift from isolated water projects towards landscape-level interventions. Infosys, for instance, reports creating 40 lakes across its campuses with a combined rainwater storage capacity of 430 million litres, supported by 409 deep injection wells and complete recycling of wastewater.
UltraTech Cement says its operations became 4.9 times water positive during FY2024-25 through rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, watershed management and recycling initiatives. Hindustan Zinc reports achieving 3.3 times water positivity while targeting a 50% reduction in freshwater consumption by 2030. ITC, meanwhile, has expanded watershed restoration and river basin stewardship programmes alongside improvements in water-use efficiency.The common thread running through these initiatives is that they benefit both communities and businesses. Restoring watersheds improves groundwater availability for nearby villages while also reducing water-related risks for industrial operations. Wastewater recycling lowers pressure on freshwater resources while helping industries operate more sustainably.The focus is also widening beyond water. Another emerging area for CSR is the circular economy, where companies seek to minimise waste and maximise the productive use of resources. Rather than viewing waste simply as something to be disposed of, businesses are increasingly investing in recycling, reuse and resource recovery.India's policy framework now covers plastics, batteries, e-waste, waste tyres, construction waste and several other waste streams under Extended Producer Responsibility rules. As of March 2026, registered recyclers had processed 417.6 lakh metric tonnes of waste, generating nearly 342 lakh metric tonnes of EPR certificates. The government has also introduced a Rs 1,500 crore incentive scheme to promote recycling of critical minerals such as lithium, nickel and cobalt.Corporate initiatives are increasingly reflecting this transition. Tata Steel reported recycling around 4.2 million tonnes of scrap during FY2024-25. Infosys diverted 98% of its waste away from landfills, while Hindustan Zinc is working towards achieving near-zero waste to landfill by 2030 through greater reuse and recycling. These examples demonstrate how environmental investments can reduce raw material consumption, lower disposal costs, and improve resource security.CSR is also beginning to support innovation rather than only funding conventional projects. Technology-led solutions are emerging as an important area of investment. Digital Paani, featured in NITI Aayog's Frontier Tech Repository, uses Internet of Things-based automation to optimise wastewater treatment plants. The platform has been deployed at more than 40 facilities, treating over 90 million litres of wastewater every day.In agriculture, Kheyti's "greenhouse-in-a-box" model has demonstrated how climate-smart farming can improve resilience. According to the study cited in the report, participating farmers recorded a 73% increase in income, 58% lower crop losses, 67% lower water consumption, and significantly lower fertiliser use. Satellite-enabled platforms such as SatSure are also helping govts, financial institutions and agribusinesses assess climate risks and improve decision-making using artificial intelligence and Earth observation data.
The evolution of environmental CSR reflects a broader shift in corporate thinking. Earlier, environmental spending was often evaluated through the number of trees planted or awareness campaigns organised.
Today, companies are increasingly asking whether their investments improve water security, strengthen ecosystems, reduce resource consumption, and help communities withstand climate shocks.The approach also aligns more closely with business priorities. Healthier watersheds mean more reliable water supplies. Circular resource use reduces dependence on virgin materials. Climate-resilient agriculture strengthens rural livelihoods while improving supply-chain stability. Investments in environmental resilience, therefore, generate benefits that extend beyond compliance or corporate reputation.

Tripura college student allegedly abducted, raped while returning home: Police
A college student was allegedly abducted and raped by unknown people while returning home from college in West Tripura, police said. No arrests have been made.
A college student was allegedly raped on Tuesday while she was on her way home from college in West Tripura district, police said on Wednesday.
Police lodged a First Information Report (FIR) based on the complaint at a local police station.
Police said the survivor, who is married, was allegedly abducted by unknown people, who later raped her before abandoning her a few kilometres away from the place.

In 2024, a total of 724 cases related to crimes against women were lodged, among which 180 were rape cases, followed by 108 molestation cases.

India’s pharma exports grew 6.8% in Q1 FY27: Pharmexcil
India’s pharmaceutical exports rose 6.8% to $8.1 billion in April-June FY27, with the US remaining the top market, Pharmexcil data showed.
India’s pharmaceutical exports grew by 6.8% to USD 8.10 billion during April–June financial year (FY) 2026-27, compared with USD 7.58 billion in the corresponding period of the previous financial year, despite recent concerns that US tariffs might negatively impact India’s pharma exports.
The growth indicates the continued strength of India’s pharmaceutical exports in global markets, said the Pharmaceuticals Export Promotion Council of India (Pharmexcil), which released the export data on Wednesday.
Also Read: India’s next trade frontier for pharma is regulation
Pharmexcil is the authorised export promotion council for the pharmaceutical and healthcare sector under the Union Ministry of Commerce and Industry. It works to promote exports of pharmaceuticals, bulk drugs, drug intermediates, formulations, vaccines, biologicals, herbal products, nutraceuticals, surgical products and other healthcare products from India.
“Export momentum strengthened further in June FY27, with pharmaceutical shipments increasing by 7.13% to USD 2.81 billion, compared with USD 2.62 billion in June FY26. June exports were also 6.86% higher than the USD 2.63 billion recorded in May FY27, indicating sustained month-on-month momentum and a positive start to the financial year,” said the council in a statement.
Drug formulations and biologicals continued to lead India’s pharmaceutical exports during the quarter, contributing USD 5.98 billion and accounting for 73.85% of total exports.
Also Read: The brain may be about to have its Ozempic moment
“The category recorded a growth of 4.14% over the corresponding period last year and continued to dominate India’s pharmaceutical exports. Similarly, bulk drugs and drug intermediates, the second-largest export category, grew by 13.84% to USD 1.36 billion, while vaccine exports emerged as the fastest-growing segment, rising by 35.68% to USD 0.39 billion. Meanwhile, exports of surgical products also registered healthy growth of 11.95% to USD 0.21 billion during the quarter,” it added.
The broad-based growth across product categories reflects sustained global demand for affordable generic medicines, increasing procurement from regulated and emerging markets, and India’s growing strength as a pharmaceutical manufacturing and export hub, said the council. The performance also highlights the country’s diversified export portfolio, with multiple product segments contributing to overall export growth, it added.
In terms of region-wise exports, NAFTA (North American Free Trade Agreement), Europe, Africa, and Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) continued to be the key destinations for India’s pharmaceutical exports during the quarter, collectively accounting for nearly 75% of the country’s total pharmaceutical exports, the data showed.
Also Read: Faridabad: Fake cough syrup chemical supply racket busted, 1 held
“This reflects the continued strength of Indian pharmaceutical products across both mature and emerging markets. Among these regions, NAFTA remained the largest export market, contributing 34.28% of India’s overall pharmaceutical exports, underlining its strategic importance for the industry.”
By country-wise export share, the United States remained India’s largest pharmaceutical export destination during April–June FY27, followed by Brazil, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and France. The list includes both developed and emerging markets, indicating the geographical spread of India’s pharmaceutical exports. During the quarter, the top 25 export destinations together accounted for nearly 70% of India’s pharmaceutical exports, with shipments valued at USD 5.65 billion. Exports to these 25 countries recorded year-on-year growth of 5.50% during April–June FY27.
“India’s pharmaceutical export performance demonstrates that the sector continues to combine scale in established markets with growing momentum across a wider set of geographies,” chairman of Pharmexcil Namit Joshi said.
He added that The United States remained India’s largest export destination, with shipments valued at USD 2.50 billion and a 30.89% share, while the strong performance of Brazil, the Netherlands, France and several emerging markets reflects the expanding global footprint of Indian pharmaceutical companies.
Also Read: India’s next pharmaceutical revolution
The double-digit growth recorded across Europe, Africa, Latin America, ASEAN and South Asia is particularly important in the present global trade environment. India must continue consolidating its leadership in generics while building a stronger presence in complex generics, biosimilars, peptides and other innovation-led segments. Our ability to combine quality, regulatory credibility, manufacturing scale and market diversification will determine the strength of India’s next phase of pharmaceutical export growth,” said Joshi.
Bhavin Mehta, vice chairman, Pharmexcil, added, “The growth recorded across vaccines, bulk drugs and drug intermediates reflects the increasing depth of India’s capabilities across the pharmaceutical value chain. Vaccine exports increased by 35.68%, while bulk drugs and drug intermediates grew by 13.84% during the quarter. Sustaining this momentum will require continued investments in advanced manufacturing, stronger quality systems, specialised production capabilities and regulatory preparedness. It will also be important to enable Indian MSMEs to upgrade their capabilities, meet international compliance requirements and participate more meaningfully in regulated and emerging global markets.”
With exports registering steady growth across product categories, regions and key markets, the performance during the first quarter of FY27 reflects continued demand for Indian pharmaceutical products in global markets, they said. Going forward, sustained focus on product diversification, regulatory compliance, market expansion and manufacturing capabilities will remain important to maintaining the growth momentum, they added.

headline: Russia appoints former CJI DY Chandrachud as arbitrator in investment treaty dispute with Ukrainian bank: Report
full_text:
Russia appoints former CJI DY Chandrachud as arbitrator in investment treaty dispute with Ukrainian bank: Report
Oschadbank claims that it lost assets and operations in the regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia after Russian military actions in Ukraine.
Russia has reportedly appointed former Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud as its arbitrator in an investment treaty dispute with Ukraine's state-owned bank, Oschadbank.
Cost Rican arbitrator and former trade minister Dyalá Jiménez has been chosen to preside over the three-member tribunal, Global Arbitration Review reported.
Jiménez was jointly selected as President by both Russia and Ukraine.
Stavros Brekoulakis, a Greek arbitrator and professor at the National University of Singapore, has been appointed as the third arbitrator by Ukraine's Oschadbank.
What the Ukraine bank claims
Oschadbank claims that it lost assets and operations in the regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia after Russian military actions in Ukraine, especially after Moscow's full-scale invasion of Kyiv in February 2022.
Oschadbank's claim is reportedly worth hundreds of millions of dollars.
The Ukrainian bank initiated the arbitration proceedings after a notice of dispute served to Russia in July 2025 allegedly went unanswered.
ALSO READ | Child among 13 killed as Ukraine launches one of the deadliest attacks on Russian oil-refining city
The arbitration has been initiated in accordance with the 1998 bilateral investment treaty between Ukraine and Russia, the report said.
Russia is represented by Pinna Goldberg partner Andrea Pinna, counsel Pratyush Panjwani and senior associate Dimitrios Papageorgiou.
On the other hand, Ukraine's Oschadbank is represented by Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan partners, Epaminontas Triantafilou and Alex Gerbi, along with Asters partners Oleksiy Didkovskiy, Andrii Pozhidayev and Oksana Legka.
Russia-Ukraine investment treaty dispute
Oschadbank had earlier pursued Russia for losses in Crimea after Moscow annexed the territory in 2014.
The Ukrainian bank was awarded approximately US$1.1 billion by a Paris-seated tribunal, formed under the UNCITRAL Arbitration Rules, in 2018.
ALSO READ | Ex-CJI Chandrachud says bail should be a right if speedy trial not possible
However, the award has been the subject of prolonged proceedings before the courts in France.
In 2021, the award was set aside after a French court accepted Russia's argument that the treaty's offer to arbitrate applied only to investments made after the opening of Oschadbank's Crimean branch, reported LiveLaw Business.
The very next year, the French Court of Cassation reinstated the award, stating that the French courts could not review the relevant provision.
In 2023 and 2024, the Paris-seated tribunal issued two further decisions, rejecting Russia's request to revise the award on the basis of new evidence. The tribunal reportedly directed Moscow to bear the costs of the revision proceedings.
Recently, the Paris Court of Appeal annulled the tribunal's decision on Russia's request to revise the award, and the cost order. This is because the court found that an amicus curiae brief, co-signed by arbitrator Charles Brower, created reasonable doubts about his fairness.
Therefore, Russia's revision request remains undecided, with the need for a fresh arbitral tribunal's adjudication.
Russia approached Chandrachud earlier as well
Notably, Justice Chandrachud was previously approached by Russia to serve as its arbitrator in treaty claims brought by German energy company, Wintershall Dea.
ALSO READ | Former CJI DY Chandrachud to mediate Sunjay Kapur estate case between Rani, Priya Kapur
The German company had initiated the arbitration proceedings against Russia under the Energy Charter Treaty, Bar and Bench previously reported.
However, Chandrachud had declined the approaches, as they were made on the same day that the Permanent Court of Arbitration designated him as the appointing authority in the Wintershall proceedings.
Chandrachud later stepped down from the appointing authority role after disclosing the communications with Russia.

headline: ‘Ready to talk at 3pm’: Amit Shah's big remark amid Opposition uproar in Parliament over his ‘silence’

‘Ready to talk at 3pm’: Amit Shah's big remark amid Opposition uproar in Parliament over his ‘silence’
Home minister Amit Shah asked the Opposition to submit a letter to the Lok Sabha Speaker at 2pm if they want a discussion, provided ‘they let the House run.’
Union home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday said the government is ready for a discussion on the student protests and the subsequent police action, provided the Opposition allows the House to run, even as he maintained he has been coming regularly to Parliament amid demands for his presence and statement there on the issue.
Shah insisted he is ready to answer any questions in Parliament but the Opposition does not want the discussion to take place. He added that the Opposition should submit a letter to the Speaker by 2pm to begin the debate from 3pm (Wednesday). Follow Parliament monsoon session LIVE updates
“Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led NDA [National Democratic Alliance] government is ready for discussions. The House should be allowed to run. We are ready to start discussion at 3pm,” he said in a rare statement to journalists outside Parliament.
Parliament's ongoing monsoon session has largely been washed out over the past two weeks with the Opposition insisting on a statement from Shah in the House over allegations of police excesses and the use of pellet guns at the July 20 protest, demanding then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.
On Monday, the supplementary list of business stated that Shah would introduce bills to change the name of Kerala to Keralam, and to amend the National Cooperative Development Corporation Act. Union ministers of state Nityanand Rai and Murlidhar Mohol introduced the bills.
ALSO READ | ‘No firing at Jantar Mantar’: Nadda slams Rahul Gandhi; claims Congress leader ‘changing goalpost’
The Opposition has targeted Shah for being “missing” from the House. The government has rejected the description.
‘What’s the point of going inside when…?'
Shah slammed the Opposition, saying words such as "missing" and "fugitive" have recently begun to be heard in India’s public and parliamentary discourse. "Ever since the Parliament session began, I have been coming regularly and sitting in my chamber. But the Opposition is not allowing Parliament to function. So, what is the point of anyone going inside when the proceedings are not being allowed to run?”
He said parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju has made it very clear that the government is ready for a discussion on all aspects of the students’ protests related to the paper leak issue.
“The Opposition had initially demanded that time be allotted for a discussion and that the government should agree to it. I have also made it clear that I am ready to answer any questions in Parliament. But they simply do not want the discussion to take place," Shah said.
He said the government is ready for all kinds of discussions from 3pm Wednesday until 3pm the next day. “I will remain in the House, listen to everyone and answer every question. The government has nothing to hide.”

headline: Samik Bhattacharya seeks Paschim Banga name amid Keralam Bill debate

Samik Bhattacharya seeks Paschim Banga name amid Keralam Bill debate
During the Rajya Sabha debate on renaming Kerala as Keralam, BJP MP Samik Bhattacharya demanded West Bengal be renamed Paschim Banga. He said the existing name reflects Partition-era history and opposed any shift to Bengal.
BJP Rajya Sabha MP Samik Bhattacharya on Wednesday demanded that West Bengal be renamed Paschim Banga, saying the state's name is tied to its history and the circumstances of its creation in 1947. He made the demand while taking part in a Rajya Sabha debate on the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, which proposes renaming Kerala as Keralam.
Bhattacharya welcomed the Bill and said the people of the southern state had struggled for the change for decades. He congratulated the people of Keralam and credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah for facilitating the move.
During his speech, Bhattacharya criticised attempts to rename West Bengal as Bengal, saying these were made by the previous Trinamool Congress government because it had a majority in the state assembly.
He said, "West Bengal was born on June 20, 1947, under the leadership of Syama Prasad Mukherjee. Even the Congress had said that for the sake of Bengali Hindus, a separate state was required".
He said changing the name of West Bengal to Bengal would insult those who had fought for a separate state for Bengali Hindus. "West Bengal is not just a name; it has a history. We want the name to be changed to Paschim Banga," Bhattacharya said.
Bhattacharya also raised the issue of Vande Mataram, saying Bengal had seen both its birth and opposition to it.
Referring to CPI founder member Muzaffar Ahmed's autobiography, he said Ahmed had described Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's Vande Mataram and Anandamath as being full of hatred. "Vande Mataram and Anandamath are full of hatred. It is unacceptable for a Muslim like me," Bhattacharya said.
He also backed a demand raised by another NDA member for renaming Bihar's capital as Patliputra and a railway station in Nalanda district that is currently called Bakhtiyarpur.
During the debate, Rashtriya Lok Morcha member Upendra Kushwaha also sought the renaming of Patna as Patliputra, saying Bihar has a glorious historical legacy and that Patliputra was once the capital of an ancient and prosperous empire. Kushwaha supported the Bill and said he hoped the proposal would be considered quickly.
TDP member Vijay Chintakayala, CPI(M)'s A A Rahim, BJP members Sudhanshu Trivedi and Lahar Singh Siroya, KC(M)'s Jose K Mani, CPI member Sadosh Kumar P, IUML's Harish Beeran, UPP(L)'s R Narzary and DMDK's L K Sudhish also took part in the debate.
Ministers of State Ramdas Athawale and Suresh Gopi also participated in the discussion, which centred on the proposal to rename Kerala as Keralam and wider demands for changes in place names.

headline: Madhya Pradesh bans analog paneer production, sale and use over health concerns
full_text:
Madhya Pradesh bans analog paneer production, sale and use over health concerns
Madhya Pradesh has banned the production, sale and use of analog paneer, citing health concerns, with officials ordered to seize the product.
The Madhya Pradesh government on Wednesday banned the production, sale and use of analog paneer, citing health concerns and seeking to promote natural dairy products, officials said.
Chief minister Mohan Yadav announced the decision during a meeting with officials of the food and civil supplies department.
Madhya Pradesh became the fourth state after Maharashtra, Gujarat and Chhattisgarh to ban analog paneer. The product is made as a cheaper substitute for natural-milk paneer, using vegetable fats and starch either in place of milk or mixed with it. Its production and consumption have increased because of its lower price.
“We are banning analog paneer in Madhya Pradesh, just as other states have done. We will boost natural milk production and produce paneer naturally,” Yadav said.
MP's analog paneer consumption
According to a Food Safety Department official, around 9,000 to 12,000 quintals of analog paneer are consumed every month in Madhya Pradesh, particularly in restaurants.
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has also expressed concern over the sale of analog paneer. Commission member Priyank Kanoongo wrote to all state governments last month, urging them to ban the product and describing its use as hazardous.
Following the chief minister’s directive, the Food Safety Department instructed district officials to test paneer being produced at different factories across Madhya Pradesh and immediately seize analog paneer.
On Wednesday, a team in Indore raided a dairy factory and seized 450 kg of paneer.
