headline: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) searched 13 locations in Tamil Nadu and Mizoram on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) in connection with the seizure of over 6,016 kg of methamphetamine from a Myanmarese boat near the Barren Islands in the Bay of Ben...
full_text:
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) searched 13 locations in Tamil Nadu and Mizoram on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) in connection with the seizure of over 6,016 kg of methamphetamine from a Myanmarese boat near the Barren Islands in the Bay of Bengal in November 2024.
Five locations in Mizoram and eight in Tamil Nadu were searched, leading to the seizure of several digital devices, ₹71 lakh in cash, $53,500, and 1,50,000 Myanmar Kyat in Chennai. Additionally ₹22.38 lakh and ₹20.73 lakh was recovered from Champhai and Aizawl.
“The case originated in the seizure of the methamphetamine along with a satellite phone and other articles from the Myanmarese boat near Barren Islands in November 2024, which prompted the Andaman & Nicobar police to register a case,” the agency said.
Six Myanmar nationals were arrested and charge-sheeted by the police on March 27, 2025, under various provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act and the Foreigners Act. The NIA took charge of the investigation on August 11, 2025; the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act was also invoked. The accused persons are currently in judicial custody.
“The searches form part of ongoing efforts to unravel a larger transnational narcotics trafficking network and identify other individuals involved in the conspiracy. The investigation aims to establish connections between the seized methamphetamine and wider international drug syndicates,” the NIA said.

headline: SC rejects plea for national policy for demolition rehab, leaves it to states
full_text:
SC rejects plea for national policy for demolition rehab, leaves it to states
The Supreme Court said the petitioners could directly approach the states and union territories since such issues fall within the policy domain
The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to entertain a petition seeking a uniform national rehabilitation policy for people displaced by demolition drives against unauthorised constructions, observing that this was a policy matter that falls within the domain of states and union territories,
“It would be difficult and not prudent for this court to lay down a uniform policy framework to be applied across various states,” a bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said, underlining that such issues essentially fall within the policy domain
The bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said the petitioner, non-profit organisation Centre for Law and Good Governance, could directly approach the states and UTs, which would be at liberty to consider the issues raised for formulating or revisiting their existing policies.
The petitioner, represented by advocate Surat Singh, had reasoned that the top court protected the right to shelter as part of the right to dignity and right to live under Article 21 of the Constitution. At the same time, he pointed out that contradictory orders have been passed by the court in this context.
The bench said, “The circumstances may vary from state to state and may, therefore, warrant variations in their respective policy frameworks.”
Singh said Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Delhi have settlement and regularisation policies but such policies do not exist in other states where unauthorised colonies are suddenly ordered to be demolished.
He stated that neither due process was followed and even if notice was served, there was no rehabilitation scheme to ensure the affected persons were provided an alternative site. Demolition was an extreme and irreversible measure, he said, adding that the same ought to be balanced with the right to shelter, livelihood and dignity of citizens.
The bench said, “On one hand there are rank illegal constructions. At the same time, there are also people, largely belonging to economically marginalised sections, who occupy tracts of public land and require alternative accommodation. We cannot fetter the state from taking any suitable policy decision. If the policy is arbitrary, unreasonable or does not accommodate due process, it will be open to judicial review.”
The court also observed that its judgments in the past have laid down “guardrails” beginning with Olga Tellis judgment which recognises that a person in a settled possession cannot be dispossessed without due process. In the suo motu case on bulldozer demolitions, the court held that notice before demolition is mandatory, provided it is not an occupation on public land or space.
The petitioner sought the appointment of a court-appointed committee to monitor this issue but the bench was not keen since a court-appointed committee could not substitute the power vested in the state or municipal authority.
“These issues must be examined case by case. They cannot be addressed through a collective policy framed by this court,” the bench reiterated, asserting that it hoped the government would give due consideration to the issues involved.

headline: Kangana Ranaut slams Rahul Gandhi over remarks on Amit Shah: ‘He makes mockery of the country’
full_text:
Kangana Ranaut slams Rahul Gandhi over remarks on Amit Shah: ‘He makes mockery of the country’
Kangana's comments came after Rahul said he was not interested in hearing Shah’s response following the latter’s ‘prolonged absence’ from Parliament.
Kangana Ranaut has hit out at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on Union home minister Amit Shah. The BJP MP on Wednesday accused him of “making a mockery of the country” and refusing to listen to answers to the questions he raised.
Her comments came after Rahul said he was not interested in hearing Shah’s response following the home minister’s ‘prolonged absence’ from Parliament following police crackdown on student protesters last month.
“I heard his interview earlier and initially could not believe that he was actually saying those things,” Ranaut said of Rahul. “But when I listened to it again, I felt that even talking about growing potatoes on the Moon or selling jalebis in other countries pales in comparison,” she said.
ALSO READ | Amit Shah sets condition for debate on student protests, Rahul Gandhi says 'not interested'
Kangana questions Rahul Gandhi's approach
Ranaut accused Rahul of mocking the people of the country and said his remarks had crossed a line. “The way he mocks the people of this country has gone beyond all limits,” she said.
She also questioned Rahul's demand for answers from the government while refusing to hear Amit Shah's response.
“In the same breath, he says, ‘I don't want to listen to anything Amit Shah has to say; I want answers from you on this and that, including what happened to the students.’”
Ranaut asked how Rahul expected to get answers if he did not listen to the government's response.
“On the one hand, he says he does not want to hear anything, and on the other, he demands answers. How will he get answers if he refuses to listen?” she said.
‘Come to Parliament and raise questions’
Ranaut said Rahul should raise his questions in Parliament instead of seeking answers through the media. “If he has questions, he should come to Parliament and raise them,” she said. She also questioned Rahul's approach to the allegations surrounding the student protests.
ALSO READ | ‘Compromised PM sold India’s interest': Rahul Gandhi after US court's relief to industrialist Gautam Adani
“He is asking the media whether bullets were fired, whether anyone was injured, whether tear gas was used, and demanding answers,” Ranaut said.
“But when answers are being given, he does not listen, nor does he come to Parliament,” she added. “I would say that while comedy has its place, the way he is making a mockery of the country is highly condemnable,” she said.
Why Ranaut used the ‘Generation gutter’ label
Ranaut has also explained why she earlier referred to some young Gen Z protesters as “Generation gutter”. The actor-politician on Wednesday said her remarks were directed at the “filthy” language and behaviour seen in videos from the student-led protests in Jantar Mantar last month.
Ranaut said Gen Z was initially seen as more sensitive and vocal about issues. She now says the generation has created its identity and faces struggles like every generation before it.
ALSO READ | ‘Coming regularly to Parliament’: Amit Shah attacks Opposition over ‘laapata’, ‘bhaag gaye’ remarks
“Gen Z was given this name because, when this generation first emerged, they were considered to be more sensitive and had louder reactions to issues,” she said.
She added that young people had always gone through a rebellious phase. Ranaut cited movements such as the Flower Power movement and armed revolutions as examples.
“In the beginning, every generation tends to be rebellious, but eventually, they settle into the mainstream of life, just as previous generations have,” she said. Ranaut said Gen Z should no longer be judged by old stereotypes. She praised young Indians for their ambition, confidence and talent.
“We are now seeing that Gen Z has moved beyond the stereotypes associated with it. I would say that today’s Gen Z is ambitious and fiery by nature,” she said.
“They are taking the country forward, and there is no shortage of talented and confident young people,” Ranaut added, pointing to young entrepreneurs, startups and other talented youth. She said the talent and confidence of young Indians is increasingly being recognised around the world.
Ranaut's clarification come after she faced criticism for targeting protesters involved in the CJP-led agitation.
In an earlier social media post, she criticised videos from the protests, calling them “puke inducing” and objecting to the language used by some participants.
She had also targeted women protesters, saying, “Here is a new generation of so-called westernised Indian women. I call them generation gutter.”
Ranaut later clarified that she was referring to “obscene and unethical” conduct by some protesters and not to Gen Z as a whole.

She also objected to alleged abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his late mother during the protests.

Bhubaneswar: A woman was allegedly gang-raped by four to six men in Odisha’s Cuttack district late Tuesday night while she was travelling with a male friend, police said.

"A DSP-rank officer and a woman police officer were assigned to lead the investigation. Multiple teams have been formed to trace and arrest the accused. We are conducting raids at various locations and are hopeful of making arrests soon,” the SP said.

headline: He called a Rs 500 bribe 'very bad'. Now IPS trainee faces Rs 1 crore charge
full_text:
He called a Rs 500 bribe 'very bad'. Now IPS trainee faces Rs 1 crore charge
The contrast between what Rahul Bansal said while preparing to enter the civil services and the allegations he now faces has given the old mock interview a fresh, ironic relevance.
Years before he found himself accused in a Rs 1 crore bribery case, Rahul Bansal sat before a mock interview panel and spoke about corruption from the other side of the table.
The then civil services aspirant recalled how uncomfortable he had felt when a panchayat official allegedly demanded Rs 500 to urgently issue his brother’s birth certificate.
“I felt very bad paying the bribe of Rs 500,” Bansal said in the old video.
The clip has now resurfaced and gone viral for an uncomfortable reason.
Bansal, a 2022-batch IPS officer of the Chhattisgarh cadre, has been named along with two police personnel in a complaint alleging that Rs 1 crore was sought and received to settle a cyber fraud case.
The contrast between what Bansal said while preparing to enter the civil services and the allegations he now faces has given the old mock interview fresh, ironic relevance.
‘YOU CAN’T BLAME THE WHOLE SYSTEM’
In the video, Bansal speaks at length about corruption, inefficiency and the need for police reforms.
“There are some corrupt and inefficient people. But you can’t blame the whole system,” he is heard saying.
He then recounts his own experience of allegedly being asked for a bribe.
According to Bansal, his brother was studying at IIT Kanpur and was due to travel to the United States for a paper presentation. He urgently needed a birth certificate to apply for his visa.
Bansal alleged that a panchayat official sought Rs 500 to issue the certificate at short notice. The experience, he told the interview panel, left him deeply uncomfortable.
He also stressed the need for reforms in policing and public administration.
Years later, the same interview is being viewed through a very different lens.
NOW, A RS 1 CRORE ALLEGATION
A complaint before a special CBI court in Delhi has named Bansal, Assistant Sub-Inspector Praveen Kumar Rathore and constable Anshul Sharma in connection with an alleged Rs 1 crore bribe.
The complaint alleges that the money was sought and received to settle a cyber fraud case.
The special court has sought an Action Taken Report from the Chhattisgarh Director General of Police and the Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation.
The complainant has also submitted what he claims is digital evidence linked to the alleged transaction, including WhatsApp conversations and call recordings.
Before joining the Indian Police Service, Bansal worked as an Income Tax inspector.
His first field posting as an IPS officer was as City Superintendent of Police in Chhattisgarh’s Surguja district. The allegations linked to the cyber fraud case surfaced during this posting.
TWO RS 50 LAKH PAYMENTS ALLEGED
According to the complaint, the alleged Rs 1 crore payment was made in two instalments rather than as a single transaction.
It claims that two payments of Rs 50 lakh each were routed through hawala channels in May 2026.
The complainant has placed alleged communications and other material before the court in support of the claims.
The Action Taken Report sought by the court is expected to indicate what action, if any, has been taken by the state police or the CBI and whether an investigation is underway.
VIDEO RETURNS TO HAUNT BANSAL
Against that backdrop, the resurfaced mock interview has acquired a significance it never had when it was first recorded.
In the video, Bansal presents himself as someone troubled by even a Rs 500 bribe and argues that policing needs reform. Today, he faces allegations involving Rs 1 crore, an amount 20,000 times larger.
That contrast does not establish the allegations against him, which will have to be tested through investigation and due process. But the resurfaced video has brought the irony into sharp focus.

headline: Gujarat’s Deesa to get ₹542-cr zoo, desert-themed night safari: Official
full_text:
Gujarat’s Deesa to get ₹542-cr zoo, desert-themed night safari: Official
The Gujarat Forest Department will develop the project on 103 hectares of government land at an estimated cost of ₹542.14 crore
The Central Zoo Authority (CZA) approved the proposal for the Desert Zoological Park and Night Safari at Deesa in Gujarat’s Banaskantha district to develop Asia’s first desert-themed drive-through night safari, an official said on Wednesday.
The Gujarat Forest Department will develop the project on 103 hectares of government land at an estimated cost of ₹542.14 crore.
“The proposed Desert Zoological Park and Night Safari is being developed over about 103 hectares of government land at Deesa. The project has been prepared in accordance with Central Zoo Authority guidelines and has an estimated cost of ₹542.14 crore. It has now received approval from the Central Zoo Authority,” forest and environment minister Arjun Modhwadia said.
The zoo is planned to house around 2,700 native and exotic animals and birds representing nearly 83 species. It will include a day zoo and five dedicated night safari enclosures, allowing visitors to see nocturnal animals after sunset.
Minister of state for forests and environment Pravin Mali said the project would also focus on conservation breeding, wildlife rescue and rehabilitation, environmental education and scientific interpretation.
“The project will not only provide visitors with a unique wildlife experience but will also serve as a centre for conservation breeding, wildlife rescue, rehabilitation, environmental education and scientific interpretation of nature,” Mali said in a statement.
The park will be designed around a desert ecosystem with arid landscapes. According to Jaipal Singh, principal chief conservator of forest (wildlife) and chief wildlife warden, Gujarat, Indian species planned for the facility include chinkara, blackbuck, Indian wild ass, Asiatic lion, leopard, Indian porcupine, Indian hare, hedgehog, sloth bear, caracal, Indian wolf, golden jackal, striped hyena and Indian desert fox.
The proposed park will also house species from other desert ecosystems. African species listed in the plan include Angolan giraffe, Grevy’s zebra, scimitar oryx, African kudu, springbok, addra gazelle, black rhinoceros, chimpanzee, meerkat, African cheetah, African lion, fennec fox, bat-eared fox and ostrich. Kangaroos, emus and wallabies are among the Australian species planned for the park. The facility will also include a reptile safari, rainforest biome, aquarium, aviary, reptile house and butterfly park.
Visitor facilities will include an interpretation centre, food court, souvenir shop and golf cart services.
Forest officials said the site was selected because of its 103 hectares of land, natural sand dunes, proximity to the Banas river and road and railway connectivity.

headline: Full emergency briefly declared at Chennai airport after left engine issue on IndiGo flight
full_text:
Full emergency briefly declared at Chennai airport after left engine issue on IndiGo flight
The full emergency was declared shortly before the aircraft was scheduled to land at Chennai airport at 11:30 pm.
A full emergency was declared at Chennai airport for IndiGo flight 6E-723 travelling from Kolkata to Chennai after the aircraft reported a left engine failure, Chennai airport sources said on Wednesday.
In a statement, an IndiGo spokesperson confirmed the incident and said that the aircraft experienced a technical snag before landing at Chennai airport.
Full emergency at Chennai airport
The full emergency was declared shortly before the aircraft was scheduled to land at Chennai airport at 11:30 pm. It was later lifted.
The aircraft, carrying 224 people on board, faced a left engine failure after which a full emergency was declared at the airport, sources told HT.
The aircraft was later declared Aircraft on Ground (AOG) at 1:50am, meaning it was grounded due to technical issues, they added.
IndiGo also said that the aircraft is currently undergoing necessary checks and maintenance.
IndiGo's statement on the incident
In the statement, IndiGo confirmed that the flight experienced a technical snag shortly before landing in Chennai.
“Following standard operating procedures, all relevant authorities were immediately informed, and the pilots made a priority landing at the Chennai International Airport,” the statement read.
IndiGo said that all customers and crew safely disembarked the aircraft and that the aircraft is currently undergoing necessary checks and maintenance.
It will resume operations after receiving the relevant clearances, the airline said.
Similar incident in March
In March this year, a full emergency was declared for an IndiGo flight approaching Delhi after the aircraft reported an engine failure shortly before landing, officials aware of the matter said.
All passengers and crew members landed safely despite the technical problem, they said. The incident took place at 10.39am.
Officials identified the flight as IndiGo 6E 579, operating from Visakhapatnam to New Delhi, with 161 people on board.
The aircraft landed safely at Indira Gandhi International Airport at 10.54am. The Boeing 737-800 was given priority to land on Runway 28 after the alert was received during the flight, officials said.

Lucknow-Delhi Tejas Express, India’s ‘first private train’ flagged off
After IRCTC awarded advertisement rights through train branding of the Lucknow-Delhi-Lucknow Tejas Express to M/s Sprite for a period of six months, the North Eastern Railway was told that Train 82501/82502 Lucknow-Delhi-Lucknow IRCTC Tejas Express should be announced as the ‘Sprite’ Tejas Express from August 19, 2026 to November 11, 2026, sources in the Railways said.

The country’s first private train was flagged off by Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on December 3, 2021.

full_text:
The Opposition Left Democratic Front (LDF) on Wednesday accused the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government of clamping down an “undeclared social media emergency” by allegedly removing several posts as well as news reports related to the arrest of Youth Congress leaders on synthetic drug peddling charges. Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan on Thursday posted screenshots of the removal of news reports of his own statements on one of the accused being close to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan.
All posts and news reports which were removed were from platforms managed by Meta. As per the screenshots, access to the news reports from the Facebook pages of News Malayalam 24X7, Reporter Live, Kairali News and Deshabhimani were restricted in India as per “legal requirements” under the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021. Such regional blocking of posts are usually carried out under demands from the government. Some social media users also posted that their earlier posts with videos and photographs of one of the MDMA case accused with the Chief Minister were removed.
Mr. Vijayan said that the Opposition has supported the government’s ‘Operation Toofan’ to clamp down on drug peddling networks. However, when a person who claims to be the Chief Minister’s social media coordinator was caught in the operation, the government has intervened to hide the news from the public.
“The Chief Minister and the UDF are trying to suppress the freedom of expression of the media and the Opposition just like how it was done during the Emergency. Even the statement of the Leader of the Opposition is being prevented from reaching the people. Is the government trying to protect drug traffickers through such measures? The Home Minister should respond,” he said.
Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] Central Committee member P. Rajeeve accused the UDF government of misusing the Union government’s IT Act 2021 to suppress criticism.
“The law provides for the removal of posts that affect national security, fake news and those that cause law and order disruption through hate propaganda. But what is happening in Kerala? The government is encroaching on press freedom through the back door by blocking their social media posts, without directly banning the media. Some media outlets are also reporting that this is being implemented using the Modi government. If this is true, it is clear how carefully the Modi government is protecting the UDF government,” said Mr. Rajeeve.
CPI(M) Central Committee member K.K. Shailaja said the fact that even criticisms that naturally arise in a democratic society against an elected government are being suppressed using loopholes in the law raises suspicions that an emergency-like situation has been created in the State.
“It has been 48 hours since the person who claims to be the Chief Minister’s social media coordinator was caught with MDMA. The Chief Minister or the Chief Minister’s office has not yet given any explanation on this issue, but news related to this is being widely deleted,” she said.

headline: ‘Frustrated, disappointed’: Kiren Rijiju slams Opposition for ‘running away’ from debates in Parliament
full_text:
‘Frustrated, disappointed’: Kiren Rijiju slams Opposition for ‘running away’ from debates in Parliament
Kiren Rijiju remarked that he is witnessing this for the first time where the government wants a discussion in Parliament, yet the opposition is running away.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday expressed frustration and disappointment with the Opposition for allegedly avoiding debates in Parliament, saying it was “unthinkable” that the government was ready for discussion while the Opposition was not.
“I am really frustrated that the Opposition is running away from debates in Parliament. It is unthinkable and incomprehensible that, in a parliamentary democracy, the Opposition is running away from debate while the government is insisting on a full-fledged discussion and is also ready to respond.”
"How can Parliament function if there is no discussion? The government cannot present its views or respond in Parliament if the Opposition does not want to listen. Holding placards, raising slogans and even hurling abuses has now been normalised by the Congress party. Congress MPs seem to think that their only job is to raise slogans, hold placards and abuse people. They have forgotten that Parliament is meant for debate and discussion..."
Deep Dive
Rijiju, responding to the Opposition’s question over home minister Amit Shah writing to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla a day before the Monsoon Session ends, said the move came because the Opposition was continuing to disrupt Parliament.
Shah wrote Birla, saying the government is ready to discuss the student protest, urging him to consult with the Opposition on when they want the discussion and to allocate as much time as he deems appropriate.
He cited Rijiju’s statement at the Business Advisory Committee meeting that the government was ready for a discussion in Parliament on the student agitation and the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (Undergraduate) or NEET (UG) paper leak.
“Amit Shah is writing today only because they are not listening. I have been making an appeal from the first day. I am the representative of the government as the Parliamentary Affairs Minister. I am the person conveying the government’s position. I informed the Business Advisory Committee and the House that the government is ready for a full-fledged discussion on the NEET exam paper leak,” Rijiju said.
What Amit Shah said in the letter
In the letter, Shah said that the government is ready for a discussion on the student protests and the subsequent police action, provided the Opposition allows the House to run.
He insisted he is ready to answer any questions in Parliament but the Opposition does not want the discussion to take place. He added that the Opposition should submit a letter to the Speaker by 2pm to begin the debate from 3pm (Wednesday).
“Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led NDA [National Democratic Alliance] government is ready for discussions. The House should be allowed to run. We are ready to start discussion at 3pm,” he said in a rare statement to journalists outside Parliament.
Shah also slammed the Opposition for using words like "missing" and "fugitive" over his absence from the Lok Sabha, saying such words have recently begun to be heard in India’s public and parliamentary discourse. "Ever since the Parliament session began, I have been coming regularly and sitting in my chamber. But the Opposition is not allowing Parliament to function. So, what is the point of anyone going inside when the proceedings are not being allowed to run?”
Why is the Opposition denying discussion?
Even though the Opposition has continued to attack Shah over his absence in the Parliament and demanded answers from him on the alleged police violence during the Jantar Mantar protests, Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said that the Opposition is not interested in Shah's “lecture”.
The Congress MP said the Opposition was “not interested” in Shah's “lecture” and sought answers over the police action against the protesters.
He asked who had ordered the alleged firing and lathicharge against the student protesters and demanded that the home minister be held accountable. He also alleged that Shah had been absent from Parliament and said the home minister did not have the courage to face the House.
Speaking to reporters outside the Parliament complex, Rahul Gandhi said, “The Opposition has clearly said that we are not interested in Amit Shah giving us a lecture. When I say 'we', I mean the younger generation of this country. Who shot the students? Who gave the order to beat up the students with lathis with nails? Did Amit Shah give this order to shoot our children? If he did, then he should resign.”
The situation intensified on July 20 during the Sansad Chalo march organised by the Cockroach Janta Party, with reports alleging that police used force against protesting students.
The Opposition has since been demanding an explanation from the government and Home Minister Amit Shah over the incident. The Monsoon Session of Parliament also saw repeated disruptions, with the Opposition demanding Shah’s presence in the House.

headline: Private hospital room cost must not exceed 3-star hotel room tariff in cities: Parl panel
full_text:
Private hospital room cost must not exceed 3-star hotel room tariff in cities: Parl panel
New Delhi, A private hospital room in a metropolitan city should not cost more than the average tariff of a three-star hotel room in the vicinity, a parliamentary committee has recommended as part of a series of measures to make healthcare more affordable and curb out-of-pocket expenditure.
The 176th Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare, titled "Affordability and Accessibility of Healthcare Facilities in Public and Private Sector" said room charges in private hospitals, particularly in metropolitan cities, need to be rationalised on an "emergent basis".
The report was presented in the Rajya Sabha and tabled in Lok Sabha on August 7.
The panel recommended making the three-star hotel tariff benchmark mandatory for all private hospitals in large metropolitan cities. Resident doctor, nursing, disposable consumable, meal and laundry costs may be added to the basic room tariff, it said.
It also recommended that the government mandate all tertiary care hospitals to provide patients with a comprehensive and legally binding upfront cost estimate before starting any complex or prolonged medical intervention.
Hospitals should also deploy dedicated financial navigators to help patients and their families understand treatment costs, available philanthropic assistance and health assurance limits, it said.
The committee noted that households continue to face significant financial stress while accessing private healthcare, with average out-of-pocket expenditure per hospitalisation episode pegged at ₹34,064.
It also flagged medical inflation of 10-13 per cent and differential billing practices linked to room categories.
The panel recommended eliminating room-rent-linked inflation models for standard procedures across private hospitals and putting in place standardised treatment guidelines and mechanisms to cap arbitrary price variations.
It further called for "continuum of care" packages that bundle preventive screening, diagnostics, curative treatment and palliative care under a single capped financial umbrella, saying financial protection should extend beyond acute treatment and surgery to follow-up, rehabilitation and end-of-life care.
For expensive cancer and rare-disease therapies, including immunotherapy, genomic and targeted treatments, the committee proposed creation of a regulated National or State Healthcare Corpus Fund by pooling CSR contributions, philanthropic donations and charitable grants.
The corpus should be used to subsidise or fully fund high-cost therapies for eligible patients, it said.
The committee also recommended that psychological counselling, emotional support and patient support groups be made mandatory, zero-cost components of approved treatment protocols and capped packages for severe, chronic and terminal diseases in both public and private sectors.
On medicines and medical devices, it recommended mandatory AMRIT and Jan Aushadhi pharmacies within all hospitals empanelled under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY. Private empanelled hospitals should also adopt transparent, tender-based procurement and cap mark-ups on life-saving consumables and devices, it said.
The committee further called for a "Zero-Stockout Policy" in government hospitals, backed by digital inventory systems, to ensure uninterrupted availability of high-value consumables and surgical implants.
On health insurance, it recommended universal onboarding of private hospitals and healthcare providers onto the National Health Claims Exchange and expedited deployment of the Public Insurance Registry to improve transparency, reduce claim disputes and curb fraudulent billing.
The panel also stressed the need to expand healthcare infrastructure beyond urban centres, recommending mobile diagnostic units, hub-and-spoke telehealth services across districts and use of the postal network for transportation of diagnostic samples and essential medicines to remote areas.
India currently has about 1.3 hospital beds per 1,000 population, compared with the WHO norm of 3.5, with the public sector accounting for only 0.79 beds, the report noted.
The committee also recommended strengthening rural and Tier 2 and 3 healthcare infrastructure, encouraging public-private partnership clinics for middle-income populations and promoting domestic manufacturing of medical devices to reduce import dependence and treatment costs.

headline: ‘Pilot seemed high, eyes were red’: Passenger after pilot of turbulence-hit Air India plane tests positive for marijuana
full_text:
‘Pilot seemed high, eyes were red’: Passenger after pilot of turbulence-hit Air India plane tests positive for marijuana
Air India flight turbulence: A passenger reportedly revealed that after landing in Delhi, the pilot also asked them not to record anything.
A passenger of the Air India Phuket-Delhi flight that suddenly lost altitude, dropped 300 feet and injured 24 people, reportedly said on Tuesday that the pilot "seemed high" before the plane took off.
The passenger was quoted in an NDTV report, which also said that the claim came after the pilot-in-command (PIC) tested positive for marijuana, a psychoactive substance.
The August 4 incident, in which 20 passengers and four crew members of flight AI2379 were injured, was deemed serious, prompting a probe by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB).
Deep Dive
As part of the standard operating procedure (SOP), both pilots of the flight had to undergo screening for psychoactive substances after landing in Delhi.
The initial test of the PIC turned up an unconfirmed result, with a government release earlier stating that the drug test had returned "non-negative." The results indicated that confirmatory testing was required. Following this, the pilot's sample was sent to a designated laboratory.
"The pilot in question has tested positive in the confirmatory test. He tested positive for Marijuana," an official aware of the details in the report told HT.
In line with this revelation, a passenger, who was travelling on the Phuket-Delhi Air India flight with his brother, told NDTV that the PIC appeared visibly high before the plane took off. He also revealed that after landing in Delhi, the pilot asked passengers not to record anything, saying that a small thing would turn into a full-blown controversy.
"My brother and I were the last passengers to board the flight, and the pilot boarded with us. I spoke to him and asked him whether the flight was on time or if we were late. He was very slow to respond, and his eyes were red. I told my brother then that he seemed high, and you all know what happened after that," the passenger told the news channel.
ALSO READ | ‘Flight dropped 300 feet’: Woman recalls terrifying Air India Phuket-Delhi turbulence
The passenger said there was no way to be sure whether the matter was serious enough to avoid boarding the flight.
He also recalled how people made fun of him when he spoke to the media at Delhi airport after the incident, telling them that the pilot seemed to be high.
What happened on Phuket-Delhi flight?
Several passengers were injured to the head and back after the Air India Phuket-Delhi flight experienced heavy turbulence during cruise, dropping 300 feet after a sudden loss of altitude.
Speaking to news agency ANI, a passenger revealed that during the early morning hours, when most passengers were asleep, the flight suddenly stopped and flipped around, and it kept doing so for 2-3 minutes.
"Around 15-20 passengers got injured. Somebody's head was hit, a baby was injured, and my lower back was injured. My brother's shoulder was hit, and his eardrums are also damaged," the passenger revealed.
He further stated that around 70 to 80 per cent of the passengers on board the flight were injured, adding that they will seek 100 per cent action against Air India for the incident and the damages incurred.
Pilot's shocking remarks after landing
The passenger who spoke to NDTV also revealed how the pilot-in-charge stepped out of the cockpit after landing in Delhi and asked passengers not to record anything. According to him, the PIC said, "baat ka batangad ban jayega."
"We were in a life-and-death situation. Who is so worried about being recorded? His major concern was not how he could ensure medical treatment for everyone. His thing was to land in Delhi, so he didn't have to answer any questions or anything like that. So he did not make any emergency landing elsewhere," the passenger told the news channel.
He also reportedly mentioned that the pilot spoke about Lucknow as a closer landing option but decided against it, landing in Delhi, as the city in Uttar Pradesh "lacked good medical infrastructure."
AAIB probes Phuket-Delhi flight
After the incident, the civil aviation ministry had said that both the pilots were taken off the roster by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), pending investigation and completion of the prescribed procedure. The incident is now being investigated by the AAIB.
ALSO READ | Airbus team to assist AAIB probe into Air India Phuket-Delhi turbulence case
A government release on Tuesday revealed that the AAIB is engaged in the systematic collection, preservation and examination of all relevant evidence. It said that the process also included the examination of the aircraft and its systems, recorded flight data, relevant operational and maintenance records, medical information, and an interview with persons concerned.
Conclusions would be drawn only after the complete examination of all material evidence.
An Air India spokesperson refused to comment on the development, citing the ongoing investigative process. "As the investigative process is ongoing, Air India cannot comment on any findings or observations related to the investigation. We will continue to extend our full cooperation to relevant authorities as required,” the spokesperson said.

headline: Police to verify viral video claiming to be of Atiq Ahmed's son's fatal car crash

Police to verify viral video claiming to be of Atiq Ahmed's son's fatal car crash
The viral video purportedly shows the moment the fatal car crash happened. The driver seemed to have lost control of the vehicle and rammed into a road divider.
Uttar Pradesh Police on Wednesday said they are verifying a video that is going viral on social media showing footage of the car accident in which Aban Ahmad, the youngest son of slain gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmad, and his friend were killed.
"A video is going viral on social media platforms, which is being linked to a recent accident. As per the instructions of the Senior Superintendent of Police, Jhansi, the authenticity of the said video is being verified,” Moth circle officer said.
“We humbly request all of you to share or circulate the said video only after its verification and confirmation,” he added.
What does the video show?
The viral video purportedly shows the moment the fatal car crash happened. The driver seemed to have lost control of the vehicle and rammed into a road divider.
The video was allegedly shot by a car behind them.
HT could not independently verify the authenticity of the video.
What had happened?
The driver of the vehicle in which Abaan Ahmed was travelling, suffered “a momentary blackout” before crashing into the side of a road in Uttar Pradesh's Jhansi on Thursday.
According to Jhansi Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) BB GTS Murti, the car had five occupants, out of which two, including 20-year-old Abaan, died in the crash, while three others are undergoing treatment.
“I have also spoken to the three survivors and the driver, Zaid. He stated that he experienced a momentary blackout or dizziness, which led to the accident,” the officer was quoted by news agency ANI as saying.
The fatal crash occurred around 10:30 am on Thursday, when Abaan Ahmed, who was the younger son of Atiq Ahmed, was travelling to meet his elder brother, Ali Ahmed.
Their destination was the Jhansi district jail, where Ali is currently lodged in connection with criminal cases.
According to police, the accident occurred in the Poonch police station area when the speeding car Abaan was travelling in reportedly went out of control and rammed into a road divider.
The impact of the collision was so severe that the vehicle's front end was completely mangled. Local residents and police personnel helped rescue the occupants trapped inside the wreckage.
Abaan and the other occupants of the car were taken to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared Abaan and Sonu, a resident of Prayagraj, dead on arrival. The condition of the three injured is stable, the Jhansi SSP said in his statement.

headline: The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. (Representative Image)
full_text:
The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. (Representative Image)
NEW DELHI: The domestic medical device industry, along with hospitals and healthcare providers, has urged govt to re-examine the Draft Drugs, Medical Devices & Cosmetics Bill, 2026."The Bill in its present form, does not provide the regulatory foundation required for India's medical devices sector to grow, innovate, and compete globally", an industry expert told TOI.The draft aims to repeal the existing Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and consolidate laws related to import, manufacture, distribution and sale of drugs, medical devices and cosmetics, to ensure their quality, safety and efficacy.In a letter to govt, the associations say that the draft bill, in its current form, treats medical devices as an adjunct to pharmaceuticals, despite clear scientific, engineering, and regulatory distinction between the two.Medical devices are engineering products, and should not be clubbed with pharmaceuticals, the letter says, adding the draft Bill continues to use drug-centric terminology such as "adulterated", "spurious".
"misbranded", and applies pharma-style criminalisation to engineering deviations.Globally, medical devices are regulated through risk-based conformity assessment and quality management systems.Further, the Bill does not provide for a dedicated regulatory authority for medical devices, despite repeated recommendations.In 2023, the Association of Indian Medical Device Industry argued that proposed overarching legislation (such as the Drugs, Medical Devices and Cosmetics draft) fails the domestic sector by continuing to regulate medical devices as "drugs" under a joint framework, instead of establishing an independent, specialized regulatory body.Administrative enforcement including recalls, corrective actions, civil penalties-- should replace imprisonment for technical lapses, the letter by 11 associations including Aimed, AHPI (Association of Healthcare Providers India), ADMI (Association of Diagnostics Manufacturers) and Patient Safety and Access Initiative, says.
The Bill 2026 applies uniform penalties across all device classes, from low-risk surgical instruments to high-risk implants, contrary to global norms.It does not clearly recognise key medical device standards covering areas such as biocompatibility, usability and software safety.While the draft has been circulated to various ministries and departments, key stakeholders, including industry associations, manufacturers and hospital bodies, have not been adequately involved in the process, the industry executive said, adding it appears inconsistent with the pre-legislative consultation process.

headline: A remand prisoner allegedly attempted to end his life by slashing his throat with a vegetable-cutting knife inside the kitchen of the Repalle Sub-Jail on Wednesday.
full_text:
A remand prisoner allegedly attempted to end his life by slashing his throat with a vegetable-cutting knife inside the kitchen of the Repalle Sub-Jail on Wednesday.
The prisoner, V. Srinivasa Rao, was arrested on July 5 in connection with the murder of an elderly woman and was subsequently remanded in judicial custody. Police said he had surrendered at a police station in connection with the murder case.
According to the police, Mr. Srinivasa Rao entered the jail kitchen in the morning to open a bag of rice. He allegedly picked up a vegetable-cutting knife kept there and slashed his throat. Jail staff noticed him bleeding heavily and immediately shifted him to the Repalle Government Hospital.
After preliminary treatment, he was referred to the Tenali Government Hospital as his condition was serious. Doctors there later advised that he be shifted to the Guntur Government Hospital for better medical care.
Police said Mr. Srinivasa Rao was reportedly distressed over not getting bail. His wife and son had also visited him, officials said.
Based on a complaint lodged by the jail authorities, the Repalle Town police registered a case and launched an investigation.
Superintendent of Police B. Umamaheswar said the police had been closely monitoring the murder case, which was why the accused had not been granted bail. As the crime was committed against a woman, the case had been accorded top priority, he said.
Through the district court monitoring cell, the police were closely following the case, and all bail petitions filed by the accused had been contested in court, Mr. Umamaheswar said.

NEW DELHI: The parliamentary standing committee on social justice and empowerment has brought into focus the failure of the National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities (NAP-SDP) to meet setout targets and highlighted that the continued shortfall in achieving even 25% of the set targets is a matter of serious concern.The panel in its latest report tabled in Parliament on Monday yet again raised the issue which it had flagged in its earlier report in March saying that the performance of the action plan remained significantly below the set targets over the last three years.In the report on the action taken by the government on the observations and recommendations made in March on âDemands for Grants (2026-27)â of the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, the panel said that it has not accepted the reply of the govt on NAP-SDP and added that it requires reiteration.The Committee, in its original report, had observed with concern that under the (NAP-SDP) the performance data reveals a widening gap. The Committee had further suggested that the targets for the 2026â27 fiscal year be monitored quarterly to ensure that the transition to the new Yojana results in a measurable improvement in both the number of beneficiaries trained and their subsequent placement in sustainable employment.The Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities in its reply to the Commission dated June 18 said that âthe recommendations of the Committee have been notedâ. âThe new skilling scheme is being designed to address diverse skilling needs and aspirations of all types of Persons with Disabilities, through industry-linked and outcome-based livelihood models. headline: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan released literary critic M. Leelavathi’s new work Bharathalokam at her residence in Thrikkakara, Kochi, on Wednesday.
full_text:
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan released literary critic M. Leelavathi’s new work Bharathalokam at her residence in Thrikkakara, Kochi, on Wednesday.
Stating that he is proud to have released the book, Mr. Satheesan praised her for presenting her own interpretation of the characters and moments in the Mahabharata at the age of 98.
“I am lucky to have released the book after having read her various works from my student days. Though there have been numerous works based on the Mahabharata in various languages, a work like this that takes a critical look at the characters and episodes in the epic is rare. Critics like Kuttikrishna Marar and P.K. Balakrishnan had penned such books. But Leelvathi teacher’s work is different. She has carried out extensive research for her new book,” he said in a communication.
Ms. Leelavathi said that the Mahabharata intended to convey a strong message against war. She recalled how Vedavyasa had stated that he cried out with his arms raised, though no one listened to him. “That feeling of nobody listening to the call for an end to war still remains. Women and children, who are never connected to wars, are forced to bear the brunt of it. War destroys everything,” she was quoted as saying in the release.
The Chief Minister released the book by handing over a copy to literary critic N.E. Sudheer. Minister for Fisheries V.E. Abdul Gafoor, Uma Thomas, MLA, and Jamal Manakkadan, chairperson of Kalamassery municipality, were present.

headline: Bengal assembly clears delimitation bills, Kolkata to have 209 municipal wards
full_text:
Bengal assembly clears delimitation bills, Kolkata to have 209 municipal wards
West Bengal assembly passes bills to increase Kolkata civic wards from 144 to 209 and Howrah wards from 50 to 68 ahead of municipal elections.
The West Bengal assembly on Thursday passed two bills proposing to increase the number of civic wards in the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) from 144 to 209 and in the Howrah Municipal Corporation (HMC) from 50 to 68.
Presenting the bills in the assembly, state urban development and municipal affairs minister Agnimitra Paul said that delimitation would lead to the creation of smaller wards with lower populations, making faster delivery of civic services to citizens easier.
“We decided to increase the number of wards on the basis of population. Citizens will get better services,” Paul said.
In mid-July, the KMC launched the exercise to redraw the boundaries of the city’s 144 municipal wards based on population density so that each of the new wards would have around 16,000-18,000 voters. A similar exercise was launched in Howrah.
Civic body elections in both cities are scheduled to be held later this year, along with their counterparts in the districts.
Also Read: BJP workers repaint Kolkata’s Academy of Fine Arts ticket counter saffron
Although the state’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party won only three of the 144 wards in the last KMC election in 2021, it now controls six of Kolkata’s 11 assembly seats, including Bhabanipur, where chief minister Suvendu Adhikari defeated his predecessor and Trinamool Congress (TMC) chairperson Mamata Banerjee in April.
The delimitation exercise may help the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ahead of municipal elections likely to be held later this year, in November or December, political leaders said. While some wards in the KMC have only 8,000-10,000 voters, some in areas with a large Muslim population have 50,000-60,000 voters.
“The number of voters is even higher in some pockets. For example, Ward 66, represented by TMC councillor Faiz Ahmed Khan, has around 80,000 voters. The ward covers parts of Topsia, Tangra and Tiljala,” a KMC official, requesting anonymity, said.
Also Read: Azan loudspeakers removed from several Bengal mosques through ‘unwritten’ orders
The split in the TMC in June — following which Mamata Banerjee loyalists and the rebels led by MLA Ritabrata Banerjee are fighting for the right to the party’s election symbol and funds — could lead to triangular contests in the KMC polls.
Former Rajya Sabha member and spokesperson of the rebel TMC group, Santanu Sen, said that the Mamata Banerjee-led faction may not matter in the November KMC elections because more than 60 of the TMC’s 80 MLAs and 20 of the 29 Lok Sabha members have left her.
“Also, the Election Commission of India will declare well before November which group is the real TMC,” Sen, a former KMC councillor, said.

headline: SC defers Cauvery water plea to Aug 17 as judge recovers from viral fever
full_text:
SC defers Cauvery water plea to Aug 17 as judge recovers from viral fever
Justice Vikram Nath, who was to head the bench hearing Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking directions to Karnataka to release Cauvery water, fell ill
The Supreme Court has deferred to August 17 the hearing on Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking directions to Karnataka to comply with the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s (CWMA) decision on the release of Cauvery water, after Justice Vikram Nath, who was to head the bench hearing the matter, fell ill with viral fever.
Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Wednesday said that the matter, which was earlier scheduled to be heard on Thursday, will now come up before a bench headed by Justice Nath, who is expected to resume judicial work next week.
Senior advocate P Wilson, appearing for the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and some farmers, mentioned the party’s application before the CJI and sought that it be taken up along with Tamil Nadu’s plea. Wilson pointed out that the CWMA had since passed a fresh order directing Karnataka to release water, but the direction was not being complied with.
The CJI informed Wilson that Justice V Mohana had recused herself from hearing the matter and that the case would consequently be placed before a bench headed by Justice Nath. However, with Justice Nath down with viral and likely to return only next week, the matter will now be heard on August 17.
The development comes a day after the CWMA, which met in Delhi on Tuesday, endorsed the decision of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) directing Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs of water per day for 15 days from Wednesday to Tamil Nadu.
At 12,000 cusecs a day, Karnataka would have to release around 15.55 TMC ft of water over 15 days, based on the conversion that 11,574 cusecs flowing for 24 hours amounts to one TMC ft.
Tamil Nadu approached the Supreme Court saying Karnataka had wilfully failed to comply even with the earlier direction to release 3,500 cusecs per day. The state had sought directions to ensure that the stipulated flow reaches the inter-state border point at Biligundlu and that Karnataka makes good the accumulated shortfall in releases.
According to Tamil Nadu, the earlier 3,500-cusecs direction would have required Karnataka to release 4.536 TMC of water by August 12. The state, however, claimed that actual flows recorded at Biligundulu between July 29 and August 2 were substantially below the mandated quantum, ranging between 158 cusecs and 530 cusecs.
Tamil Nadu had also sought an additional release of 26.954 TMC, contending that this represented its pro-rata entitlement between June 1 and August 12 under the distress-sharing formula.
The DMK’s application, which was filed separately ahead of the state government’s plea, similarly seeks immediate directions to Karnataka to ensure the release of Cauvery water at Biligundulu. The party has stressed the importance of the current period for farmers in the Cauvery Delta, particularly for the Kuruvai paddy crop and preparations for the Samba crop.
The fresh 12,000-cusecs direction by the CWMA has, meanwhile, triggered another round of deliberations in Karnataka.
Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar said the state would decide its next course of action after assessing the availability of water, while stressing that the interests of Karnataka’s farmers would have to be protected alongside compliance with the CWMA and CWRC directions. He is expected to meet legal experts and senior bureaucrats on Wednesday to discuss the possible legal options.
Karnataka had urged the CWMA to defer any decision on further releases until the end of the south-west monsoon, arguing that a decision should be based on the actual hydrological position at that stage. Alternatively, it had sought reduction of the proposed release from 12,000 cusecs to 10,000 cusecs a day.
The state told the authority that the Cauvery basin was “reeling under severe hydrological distress”, pointing out that its four reservoirs had received cumulative inflows of only 77.746 TMC ft during the current water year — about 47% below the 30-year average. Karnataka also said inflows into the reservoirs were rapidly declining.
The dispute assumes significance for Tamil Nadu’s Cauvery Delta, where water flows into the Mettur reservoir are crucial for the standing Kuruvai crop as well as preparations for Samba cultivation.
Karnataka and Tamil Nadu have repeatedly contested the hydrological data and the quantum of water to be released during periods of deficient rainfall. The CWRC on July 28 directed Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs per day for 15 days from July 29. The CWMA endorsed that recommendation on July 30 after considering the hydrometeorological conditions in the basin.

headline: SC sets aside protection from arrest granted to Future Group director in GST case
full_text:
SC sets aside protection from arrest granted to Future Group director in GST case
The bench however, clarified that GST authorities are obligated to communicate to an individual the reasons for arrest recorded under Section 69 of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act
The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside a Bombay High Court order granting Future Group non-executive director Sunil Biyani one week’s protection from arrest in a Goods and Services Tax (GST) investigation, holding that the high court could not have granted such relief after concluding that his anticipatory bail plea was premature.
A bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu, however, clarified that GST authorities are obligated to communicate to an individual the reasons for arrest recorded under Section 69 of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act. The court said such communication could also be made through email.
The ruling came on an appeal by the Union government against the Bombay High Court’s February order, which had held that Biyani’s anticipatory bail plea was premature since no order authorising his arrest under Section 69 of the CGST Act had been issued, but nevertheless directed that if such an order was passed subsequently, he would not be arrested for one week from the date it was communicated to him.
The Supreme Court found this course of action impermissible.
Also Read: Haryana starts process to regularise contractual staff under 2014 policies
The bench had during the hearing questioned the legal basis for the high court granting protection after finding that there was no immediate apprehension of arrest and that the anticipatory bail plea was therefore not maintainable.
The case arose from Biyani’s apprehension of arrest in connection with a GST investigation. He had approached the Bombay High Court in February after being summoned by GST authorities under Section 70 of the CGST Act.
Section 70 empowers GST officers to summon a person to give evidence or produce documents during an investigation. Section 69, meanwhile, empowers the Commissioner to authorise the arrest of a person where there are grounds to believe that the person has committed specified offences under the GST law, including certain cases involving fraudulent input tax credit or tax evasion.
The Centre had told the high court that no arrest order under Section 69 had been issued against Biyani. The high court consequently held his anticipatory bail plea to be premature, but proceeded to provide him limited protection in the event an arrest order was issued later.
The Union government challenged this part of the high court’s order before the Supreme Court.
During the proceedings, Biyani’s counsel had argued that an arrest under Section 69 could be authorised only after the Commissioner recorded the requisite “reasons to believe” and that an affected individual ought to be informed of such an order to enable him to exercise his legal remedies.
The argument was based on the concern that Section 69 arrest authorisations were not ordinarily available to the affected person and that an individual could otherwise be arrested without knowing the basis on which the Commissioner had authorised the arrest.
The Supreme Court has now accepted the importance of communicating the reasons for arrest, while rejecting the high court’s decision to grant advance protection from arrest.
The bench made clear that communication of the arrest authorisation and the reasons supporting it is distinct from granting interim protection in anticipatory bail proceedings that have been found to be premature.
The Centre had during the earlier proceedings also maintained that an order passed under Section 69 could be communicated to the person concerned and that the individual would retain the right to challenge the arrest order if the statutory requirement of recording reasons to believe had not been met.

headline: 2020 riots: HC seeks Delhi Police stand on appeals in IB official murder case
full_text:
2020 riots: HC seeks Delhi Police stand on appeals in IB official murder case
The bench sought Delhi police’s response in an appeal filed by Nazim and Kasim against trial court’s orders and application for seeking suspension of the sentence
The Delhi high court on Wednesday issued notice in an appeal filed by two persons against trial court’s order convicting and awarding them life imprisonment in connection with the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) official Ankit Sharma during the Northeast Delhi riots in 2020.
A bench of justices Prathiba M Singh and Vikas Mahajan sought Delhi Police’s response in an appeal filed by Nazim and Kasim against trial court’s orders and application for seeking suspension of the sentence.
During the hearing, Delhi Police’s counsel, Rajat Nair, accepted notice and informed the court that the police were also in the process of filing an appeal against the order, as the trial court had acquitted six accused.
The trial court on July 13 convicted former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) councillor Tahir Hussain and four others for Sharma’s murder, holding that Hussain, along with an “armed” mob, had carried out a “savage” and “relentless” attack. It had however acquitted six other accused.
On July 31, the trial court sentenced Hussain, along with four others including Nazim and Kasim to life, ruling that while the crime was “horrendous” and “sickening”, the prosecution had failed to prove that the convicts were beyond the possibility of reform.
The court rejected the Delhi Police’s plea for capital punishment. The court observed that although the murder fell within the “rarest of the rare” category on account of its brutality, the prosecution had not established that the convicts’ continued existence in prison “would pose a menace to society”.
Emphasising the severity of the crime, the court held, “The crime was brutal, with a murderous mob baying for the blood of the victim… the manner and the utmost brutality with which the victim was killed was done solely on account of religion. He was sucked in by a murderous mob and strapped like an animal… and as if the hatred had still not been satiated, the dead body was thereafter thrown into the nala.”
Nazim and Kasim then moved the high court against the verdict.
In their appeal, they argued that no test identification parade was conducted and the conviction was based on the testimony of the sole witness, which was not corroborated.
The matter will be heard on December 2.

headline: Was asked for bribe, girl says in front of Uttarakhand CM, cameras. Then, a twist
full_text:
Was asked for bribe, girl says in front of Uttarakhand CM, cameras. Then, a twist
Shayra, a Class 12 student of CNI Girls School, raised the issue during Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami's 'Mukhyamantri Yuva Vidyarthi Manthan' programme in Dehradun on August 10.
A Class 12 student's emotional account of missing an international Taekwondo tournament sparked a political row in Uttarakhand after the Congress alleged that she had been asked for a bribe. In a later video, however, the student gave a fuller account and did not describe the money as a bribe.
Shayra, a 17-year-old student of CNI Girls School, raised the issue during Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami's 'Mukhyamantri Yuva Vidyarthi Manthan' programme in Dehradun on August 10.
She told the gathering that she had won gold at a national Taekwondo competition and was selected for an international event, but could not participate because she was unable to arrange Rs 1.5 lakh.
Shayra became emotional while speaking, prompting Dhami to comfort her and direct officials to collect details about her school and look into the matter.
CONGRESS ALLEGES BRIBE DEMAND
The Congress interpreted Shayra's remarks as an allegation that Rs 1.5 lakh had been demanded as a bribe for her participation in the international competition.
In a post on X, the party accused the BJP government of corruption and claimed the student had been prevented from competing internationally despite winning at the national level.
The Congress also alleged that the live broadcast of the programme was later removed from the government's, the Chief Minister's and the BJP's social media platforms.
Shayra, however, did not explicitly identify the Rs 1.5 lakh as a bribe in her remarks at the event or name anyone who had allegedly demanded the money.
STUDENT'S LATER VIDEO OFFERS FULLER ACCOUNT
Shayra later released another video, saying she had been unable to complete her account before the Chief Minister.
In the video, she said she had travelled to Jammu for the national championships and was selected for an international tournament in Romania.
She said the organisation involved in the event agreed to cover around Rs 1.70 lakh of the expenses, while she had to arrange the remaining Rs 1.5 lakh herself.
Shayra said she had not informed her school or anyone else about the opportunity and was therefore unable to arrange the remaining money and travel to Romania.
Her later account did not describe the Rs 1.5 lakh as a bribe or allege that any government official had demanded the money. Instead, she described it as the amount she was required to contribute towards the cost of participating in the international tournament.

headline: Sedative, electric shocks: Delhi woman kills husband, promised ₹50 lakh to lover to plot murder
full_text:
Sedative, electric shocks: Delhi woman kills husband, promised ₹50 lakh to lover to plot murder
The accused, identified as Manju alias Nazia, allegedly mixed a sedative in water and gave it to her husband, Munna Lal, so that he loses consciousness
A Delhi woman allegedly plotted the murder of her 55-year-old husband with her lover, allegedly promising the latter ₹50 lakh for the crime. The incident took place at the couple's house in south Delhi's Sangam Vihar area, police said on Wednesday, according to PTI news agency.
The accused, identified as 45-year-old Manju alias Nazia, allegedly mixed a sedative in water and gave it to her husband, Munna Lal, so that he loses consciousness. Following this, her lover, 20-year-old Chaman, and his associate, 28-year-old Kishan, attacked Munna.
The accused allegedly strangled Munna with a rope, gave him electric shocks, and hit him with a wooden stick, before dumping his body near the house, according to the police.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Anant Mittal said it was Chaman who allegedly gave Nazia the sleeping pills to administer to Munna Lal on the night of the murder. When he fell asleep, the 55-year-old was strangled, electrocuted, and beaten with a stick to ensure he was dead.
The body was found reported to have been lying in south Delhi on August 10 at 5.15 am. “Munna Lal was found dead at the spot, with several injury marks on his body,” PTI cited the DCP as saying at a press conference.
Woman promised ₹50 lakh to lover, ‘staged burglary’
The accused wife had reportedly convinced Chaman to help her kill her husband, promising a sum of ₹5 lakh for the murder. She also gave him ₹20,000 right after the crime. Nazia also initially tried to mislead investigators by claiming that burglars had killed her husband, and staging the spot with things strewn around. She had further removed some items in the house to support her claim, PTI reported citing Mittal.
However, upon checking the CCTV camera mounted outside the house, police saw that a masked male had entered the couple's house at 1.45 am and left at about 3.15 am. The investigators also found other evidence pointed to a pre-planned murder, according to PTI.
The cops then confronted Nazia with the evidence, following which she confessed to the crime.
‘Domestic disputes, physical assault, extra-marital affair’ led to murder
DCP Mittal said frequent domestic disputes, physical assault and humiliation faced by Nazia, and financial troubles had led to Nazia plotting the murder. Her affair with Chaman had also contributed to the disaffection with her husband, according to police.
Following her confession, the police took Nazia into custody, along with the two others accused, and recovered ₹15,000 from them.

headline: 'BJP threatening to hang Delhi hall owners upside down': Dipke's big claim after cancelled meet
full_text:
'BJP threatening to hang Delhi hall owners upside down': Dipke's big claim after cancelled meet
Dipke said a meeting of CJP volunteers was cancelled after the banquet hall where it was to be held revoked the booking.
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of threatening hall and banquet owners in the Capital against renting out their spaces for his party activities.
Speaking to reporters, Dipke said a meeting of CJP volunteers in Naraina was cancelled earlier in the day after the banquet hall where it was to be held revoked the booking at the last minute due to "pressure" from the ruling party.
“We were scheduled to hold our volunteers’ meet in Delhi today. We were looking for a hall but no one agreed to rent out one to us. Everyone kept saying there was pressure from above and that they cannot give a hall to the CJP. At least 10 places refused to give us space, saying if they did so, they would invite trouble,” Dipke told reporters.
He said the organisers eventually reserved a venue but when they reached there, they were told that they could not be given the hall because of "pressure".
“It was after a lot of difficulty that we managed to get a hall. We also have a receipt of the booking. But the people who gave us the hall were also threatened and told that if they allowed a CJP meeting to take place there, they would be turned upside down and hung,” he alleged.
Also Read | ‘School Thik Karo’: Dipke announces CJP campaign for Independence Day, says rural kids failed ‘in worst way’
“The people are being threatened in this manner. Efforts are being made to prevent us from holding such meetings. All this is being done by the BJP... Their actions and words clearly reveal that they are afraid of the country's youth... If they think such petty actions will frighten us, they are purely mistaken,” he added.
CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka also hit out at the BJP, saying “Don’t worry BJP, tumhare baccho k bhi schools thik karwayenge!” The remarks were an apparent reference to the CJP’s upcoming nationwide campaign ‘School Thik Karo’ to be launched on Independence Day.
The developments came hours after Dipke announced an upcoming protest similar on the lines of the student protests in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar last month, which he termed "Season 2 of Jantar Mantar".

“Many people were commenting on Instagram when Season 2 of 'Jantar-Mantar' will begin. I want to tell them that Season 2 of 'Jantar-Mantar' is going to start very soon,” he said.
Dipke led the protest, which continued for 36 days and drew massive support, and the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.
It also came days after the CJP announced its national team, with Dipke named its national convener, as the outfit moved to build an organisational structure.

headline: ‘School Thik Karo’: Dipke announces CJP campaign for Independence Day, says rural kids failed ‘in worst way’
full_text:
‘School Thik Karo’: Dipke announces CJP campaign for Independence Day, says rural kids failed ‘in worst way’
In a post shared on social media platform X, Dipke said, “Kids in villages shouldn’t be pleading for basic facilities at school after 80 years of Independence.”
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will launch a campaign titled “School Thik Karo” on Independence Day to improve the condition of government schools in villages, founder Abhijeet Dipke said on Wednesday.
Dipke had announced the nationwide campaign on Monday, while its name was revealed on Wednesday.
In a post shared on social media platform X, Dipke said, “Kids in villages shouldn’t be pleading for basic facilities at school after 80 years of Independence.”
“As a country, we have failed rural kids in the worst possible way. This Independence Day, CJP will launch the ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign to improve Govt schools in villages,” he added.
Campaign to improve government schools in villages
Dipke on Monday announced a campaign to improve government schools in villages. The 30-year-old, now leading a ‘pressure group’ against the government, asked sarpanches and parents to take up the “social and moral responsibility” of ensuring better basic facilities for children.
Dipke called on people to pledge to the cause on August 15, India’s 80th Independence Day. He said he would begin the campaign from his own village, Hingoli, in Maharashtra’s Marathwada region, by approaching the sarpanch and requesting improvements to the government schools there.
In a video message posted on social media, Dipke said government schools in villages had been “neglected and ignored” over the past 80 years and questioned why children in rural areas continue to lack facilities that are available to students in bigger cities.
“How difficult it must be for small girls. So, I feel that this August 15, if we should pay attention to anything, it should be to making a new start, and we must begin by correcting our government schools,” he said.
Protest in UP
A day after Dipke announced a campaign to improve government schools in villages, the kids protested in Uttar Pradesh’s Hamirpur over the poor condition of a roughly 1.5-km road serving several settlements along the Yamuna belt. The stretch has turned into mud and slush following the rains, making it difficult for residents to travel.
Nearly 3,000 residents affected
The road is the main access route for nearly 3,000 residents living in Chandupur and surrounding deras, including Brahma ka Dera, Banvasi ka Dera, Athbhaiyan ka Dera, Bachchi ka Dera, Bhikhua ka Dera, Gusai Baba ka Dera and Gangwa ka Dera.
Residents said the condition of the road made it difficult for children to get to school and has also created problems in taking sick people to hospitals.
Children block main gate
As the protesters marched towards the Collectorate on Tuesday morning, SDM Sadar Abhishek Kumar and CO Yashpal Singh, accompanied by police personnel, reached the route and attempted to stop them.
Also read | 'Well done': After Gen Z, Alpha get into protest arena in UP; CJP's Dipke, Das give a shoutout
The children still reached the Collectorate and blocked its main gate. Officials tried to persuade them to withdraw the protest, but the children refused to move. Officials and employees inside were left unable to exit.
CJP expands focus beyond student protests
The campaign is another step in the CJP’s expanding youth-focused activities. What began as an online satirical platform launched by Dipke from the US later moved to street protests, including agitation over the NEET paper leak and issues affecting students.
The movement’s protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar drew students and parents from different parts of the country. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk also joined the agitation.
The protests forced the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister. After the demonstrations ended on July 25, the CJP held a two-day strategy meeting in Maharashtra and announced that it would continue as a youth movement, with Wangchuk as its mentor.
Last week, Dipke also announced the nationwide “Kya Bolti Public” campaign to understand people’s concerns. He said education would be the first focus of the outreach initiative.
