headline: Fire breaks out at a private school in Manesar; no casualty reported: Officials
full_text:
Fire breaks out at a private school in Manesar; no casualty reported: Officials
The official added that the non-teaching staff rushed and broke the window panes present in all classrooms
A fire broke out at a private school in Manesar in Gurugram district on Wednesday morning due to an electrical short circuit, fire department officials said.
According to officials, the fire broke out at Kautilya Academy around 7.40am, and they received the information at 7.55am, when school authorities contacted the fire helpline. School officials said an electrical short circuit in the school’s kitchen caused an explosion and led to fire and smoke on the ground and first floor.
“After receiving the call, we immediately dispatched three fire tenders to the venue. Unfortunately, two of the fire tenders were stuck in a traffic jam for a long time, but the third fire tender reached there within 15 minutes after diverting its route,” said Manesar fire station fireman Surinder.
“It took us another 15-20 minutes to completely douse the fire,” he added.
According to school administration around 150 students were in the school when the fire broke out.
“Around 150 students were on campus when the staff noticed the fire. The teaching staff immediately evacuated the campus, and two buses were stopped at the school gate due to the fire,” a senior school administration official told HT adding that all students were safely evacuated and no casualties were reported.
The official added that the non-teaching staff rushed and broke the window panes present in all classrooms to ensure smoke does not accumulate inside the premise of the school.
“Our in-house electrician was present at the school site to oversee the work, and once he noticed the smoke, he immediately cut the school’s main electricity supply to ensure no further damage,” a school official told HT.
The school will remain shut until a proper inspection of the incident is done and precautionary safety measures are taken to avoid such incidents in the future.

headline: As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements (representative image)
full_text:
As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements (representative image)
NEW DELHI: The Congress spent a total Rs 248.6 crore on its campaign for the recent assembly elections in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry, even as its total receipts between the date of announcement and completion of these polls stood at Rs 207.1 crore.According to Congress's election expenditure statement for the five state/UT polls, filed on July 31 with the Election Commission, the party received Rs 104 crore in cash and Rs 103.1 crore via cheque or draft between March 15, 2026, when the elections were announced, and May 6, 2026, when they had concluded.
The Congress's full poll expense statement shows its total opening balance of cash in hand (including at the level of its central headquarters and the state/district/local level units of the 5 states/UTs) at Rs 22.9 crore and its cash in bank at Rs 146.1 crore. At the end of the polls, its cash in hand was marginally lower at Rs 22.6 crore while its bank balance had declined by 45% to Rs 80.6 crore.On the expenditure side, the party declared a total spend of Rs 143 crore on general party propaganda and Rs 105.6 crore on candidates. The latter includes Rs 95.5 crore given by the party as lump-sum payments to its candidates across the five poll-gone states/UT; while the central party headquarters bore Rs 95.3 crore of expenditure under this head, the state/district/local units disbursed only Rs 23 lakh among the candidates.

Another Rs 8 crore funded public meetings, processions and rallies, while Rs 11.5 crore was spent on badges, posters, cutouts, hoardings etc and nearly Rs 2 crore on miscellaneous propaganda items.Poll surveys and campaigns for the five assembly elections cost the Congress Rs 4.8 crore.A total Rs 23.5 crore was spent by the grand old party on the travel and lodging of its star campaigners (Rs 21.8 crore) and other leaders. The aircraft and helicopters were sourced from Air Charter Services Pvt Ltd, Aircab Aviation, A R Airways, GMP Air Charter, Lima Tang Aviation Service, Devigo Data Systems and Global Vectra.

headline: New Delhi: Union Home Minister Amit Shah Wednesday wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, urging him to consult the Opposition and allocate time for a debate on the NEET paper leak protests. This came soon after he dismissed the Opposition’s claim that...
full_text:
New Delhi: Union Home Minister Amit Shah Wednesday wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, urging him to consult the Opposition and allocate time for a debate on the NEET paper leak protests. This came soon after he dismissed the Opposition’s claim that he has been avoiding Parliament, asserting that he is ready to answer any questions on the topic.
This comes amid an intense tug-of-war between the Opposition and the Modi government. The Opposition has focused its attack on Shah, indicating that it was unwilling to back down and was not interested in listening to a “lecture” from the Home Minister. Meanwhile, the BJP has said that it is the Opposition now which is running away from discussions when Shah has already offered to discuss the matter. Parliament has seen repeated disruptions due to the deadlock.
In his letter to Birla, Shah stated that the government is ready for a detailed discussion on the paper leak protests and has prepared to answer all questions raised by the Opposition.
In a democracy, solutions emerge through discussion and dialogue, he wrote, adding that he has an “unwavering faith in democracy and democratic institutions”, and that “this House is meant for discussion and dialogue”.
“You are aware that the Honorable Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju, has agreed on behalf of the Government at the Business Advisory Committee meeting to discuss the student protests regarding the NEET exam in Parliament. I would also like to mention that, at the request of the Opposition, the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 has already been discussed in the current session of Parliament, where no Honorable Opposition MP expressed any views regarding the NEET exam. Despite this, the government is ready to discuss this issue again,” Shah said in his letter to the Speaker.
“I request you to discuss this with the Opposition and, by mutual agreement, allocate as much time as you deem appropriate starting today. I intend to be present in the House during the allotted time, participate in the discussion on this issue, and am prepared to answer all questions from the opposition,” he added.
“Therefore, you are requested to discuss this important issue with the opposition leaders and arrange a discussion in a conducive atmosphere so that all the honourable members of the ruling and opposition parties can present their valuable opinions and views on this issue,” he further wrote.
Not interested in Amit Shah’s ‘lecture’: Oppn
Earlier in the day, the Opposition maintained that it is not interested in listening to Amit Shah’s “imagination” or “lecture”, and demanded his resignation.
“Did Mr Amit Shah give the order to shoot the students? If he did, he should resign because he is culpable. And if he did not, he should resign because he is incompetent. For the last 20 days, Amit Shah has been missing. The Home Minister of India has no courage; he cannot come to the House,” said the Congress MP.
Shah meanwhile alleged that the Opposition is not interested in having a discussion. Reacting to the Opposition’s claim, Shah, told media persons outside the Parliament complex: “First of all, terms like ‘laapata’, ‘bhaag gaye’ is the kind of language increasingly being heard in India’s public and parliamentary life. I have been coming to Parliament regularly since the session began; I sit in my chamber, but since the Opposition is not allowing Parliament to function—in either House—what is one supposed to do?”
The Opposition has been demanding that Shah make a statement in the House on who authorised the violent crackdown on protesting students at Jantar Mantar.
Shah further said that as far as holding a discussion is concerned, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju has made it “very clear” that the government is ready for a full discussion regarding the NEET protests.
“We asked for a time to be fixed and for the Opposition to be ready. That was their initial demand, and we agreed to it. I, too, have stated that I am ready to answer any question in Parliament, yet they simply do not want the discussion to take place. Now, let the public decide who is running away. Let them submit a letter to the Speaker by 3 pm today. We are ready for a discussion on all aspects from 3:00 PM today until 3 pm tomorrow. I will sit in the House; I will listen to everyone and respond to every point,” said Shah.
He further said that the government has nothing to hide. “I will even discuss why they did not want the discussion to happen. The NDA government—under Modi ji’s leadership is ready to discuss anything; they just need to let Parliament function.”
Speaking to the media earlier, Rahul said: “Kharge ji and I have held press conferences, and the other opposition parties have also made it clear that we are not interested in listening to Amit Shah’s imagination. We are not interested in him giving us a lecture or a discussion. We are interested in one simple thing.”
He added: “And when I say ‘we’, I mean the younger generation of this country: Who shot those students (in Delhi)? Who gave the order to shoot those students? Who blinded one of the students? Who gave the order to beat the students with lathis with nails? Who gave that order? That order was implemented by the Home Ministry.”
The Delhi police and RAF, Rahul said, are under the Home Ministry. “For the last 20 days, Amit Shah has been missing. The Home Minister of India has no courage; he cannot come to the House.”

headline: 40 seconds to fame: 3 schoolgirls get village road fixed, become local heroes
full_text:
40 seconds to fame: 3 schoolgirls get village road fixed, become local heroes
Three 15-year-old schoolgirls from Kondivade village in Maharashtra's Karjat turned a potholed road they travelled on every day into the subject of a short, satirical piece of "ground reporting". The video travelled far beyond their village, clocked millions of views and eventually forced the administration to take note.
They did not organise a protest, sit on a dharna or approach a politician. They did not even upload their video on social media themselves.
All it took was a 40-second clip.
Three 15-year-old schoolgirls from Kondivade village in Maharashtra’s Karjat turned a potholed road they travelled on every day into the subject of a short, satirical piece of “ground reporting”. The video travelled far beyond their village, clocked millions of views and eventually forced the administration to take note.
Soon afterwards, the road was resurfaced.
For Neha Ghare, Jyotsna Mukane and Mansi Pawar, all Class 10 students of Nyan Makarand Vidyalay in Khandape, what began as a simple video shot on a mobile phone became an unexpected lesson in the power of a camera — and of Gen Alpha speaking for itself.
“We did not post it on social media,” Neha told India Today. “One of our classmates had kept it as a status. From there, it was downloaded and shared on social media.”
India Today travelled to Kondivade, around 90 km from Mumbai, to meet the schoolgirls whose improvised reporting managed to do what repeated complaints often fail to achieve: get a broken village road repaired.
PHONE AS MIC, SCHOOL LESSONS AS CAMERA TRAINING
The video itself was simple.
Neha played the reporter, holding her mobile phone like a microphone as she questioned Jyotsna about the state of the road. Mansi stood behind the phone, shooting the video.
There was no production crew, no professional equipment and no prepared political speech.
“We learnt some camera work in our school and implemented it in the video,” Neha said.
Jyotsna, meanwhile, borrowed one of the most memorable lines in the clip from a teacher who travelled to school on a motorcycle.
“I used a line saying, ‘potatla pani pan halat nahi’,” she said, roughly referring to the ride being so rough that even the water inside one’s stomach would not stay still.
She said their teacher, who travelled from a distance every day, had often used the expression while complaining about the condition of the road.
The humour worked because the problem was familiar to everyone in the village.
MONSOON MADE DAILY SCHOOL JOURNEY WORSE
The Karjat-Kondivade road is among several roads in Maharashtra’s Raigad district that deteriorate during the monsoon.
For the three girls, the potholes were not an abstract civic problem.
They were part of their daily journey to school.
Vehicles passing through waterlogged stretches would splash muddy water onto their white uniforms. At other times, the students would get drenched while walking kilometres to school and then spend the rest of the day in wet or stained clothes.
The road had become a regular source of frustration for students and other residents.
Instead of simply complaining, the three friends decided to document it.
Their video did not directly attack the government or name a politician. It simply showed the condition of the road, using humour and the format of a television news report.
That was enough.
THE VIDEO THEY NEVER POSTED WENT VIRAL
Once the video was picked up from a WhatsApp status and began circulating on social media, its reach expanded rapidly.
Millions watched the clip of the teenage “reporter”, “interviewee” and “cameraperson” highlighting a problem that residents had been living with for months.
The attention eventually reached the administration.
The road was resurfaced.
For the girls and their families, that was the biggest result.
“We are proud of what our daughters did. The government needs to take cognisance of such issues,” Neha’s father, Atmaram Ghare, said.
The girls have since received praise from villagers, their families and political leaders.
Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray is also likely to meet them, while Cockroach Janata Party leader Abhijeet Dipke praised the students, saying there was “nothing more inspiring than watching Gen Alpha expose the system”.
NO DHARNA, NO SLOGANS, JUST A CAMERA
What makes the Kondivade episode stand out is not merely that three schoolgirls made a viral video.
It is what they did not do.
They did not call for a bandh. They did not sit on the road. They did not launch a political campaign.
They simply turned the camera towards the problem.
The format was familiar to a generation that has grown up consuming short-form videos: a reporter asks a question, someone on the ground answers, and the camera shows the evidence.
But this time, the “reporters” were 15-year-old students and the subject was the road they used every day.
Their satire did what conventional complaints had not.
It made people look.
GEN ALPHA'S 40-SECOND WAKE-UP CALL
The girls say they never expected the video to travel as far as it did.
Nor did they set out to become social media personalities.
Their immediate concern was far more basic: getting to school without muddy water being splashed across their uniforms and without navigating potholes during the monsoon.
Yet the episode has turned the three students into unlikely local voices of civic accountability.
A phone became a microphone. A school lesson in camera work became a tool for documenting a public problem. A teacher’s complaint became the punchline.
And a 40-second video that its creators did not even upload themselves ended with a village road being repaired.
For Kondivade, the message from its youngest reporters was simple: sometimes, all it takes to make the administration listen is to show the problem clearly enough.

She was taken to Etawah, where she was confined for nearly three months and repeatedly raped by the two brothers, the ADGC added.

headline: Recovered & Returning Home: Hospital text 42 days after cop's death adds to grief; kin seek probe
full_text:
Recovered & Returning Home: Hospital text 42 days after cop's death adds to grief; kin seek probe
Raipur/Ambikapur, A seemingly routine hospital message meant to reassure patients brought fresh anguish to the family of a Chhattisgarh police constable who died weeks earlier as it received a text saying he had "recovered" and was "returning home".
While the hospital authorities attributed the embarrassing lapse to a daily-wage data entry operator and said he has been removed, the constable's family demanded an inquiry and stringent action against those responsible.
Health officials also denied allegations that the patient's Ayushman card was misused after his death, and said deductions were made only for his actual five-day hospital stay.
The hospital administration has now written to the state nodal agency, urging that auto‑generated messages on discharge, referral or death be sent only after verifying the patient's actual status.
Devnarayan Ram, 39, a constable from Jashpur district, was admitted to the government medical college hospital in Ambikapur, the headquarters of Surguja district, on June 26 and died during treatment on June 30, officials said.
His last rites were subsequently performed, and the hospital issued a death certificate, said Ram's wife Seema Kujur, a nurse at a government hospital in Jashpur.
But on August 6, more than a month after his death, Kujur received an auto-generated message under the Ayushman Bharat scheme on her husband's registered mobile number, saying: "Dear Devnarayan Ram, We are happy that you have recovered and are returning home. We hope that you will be satisfied with the free healthcare services provided under the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana."
The message listed June 26 as the date of admission and August 6 as the date of discharge, showing the patient remained admitted for 42 days.
For Kujur, who had already lost her husband and performed his last rites, the message came as a painful reminder of her loss.
"You can imagine what it means for a family to receive such a message for a person who has died. It causes immense pain," she said in a video message that went viral on social media on Tuesday.
She demanded a high-level inquiry and strict action against those responsible.
"I am a hospital employee, and even then this happened to me. You can easily imagine what could happen to ordinary people, particularly poor and tribal families," she said.
Kujur also questioned how such a major technical lapse could occur and said action was necessary to restore people's faith in the healthcare system and ensure that such an incident is not repeated.
The hospital administration, however, said the message was generated because of a delay in closing the Ayushman claim on the portal and that there was no misuse of the patient's Ayushman card after his death.
The constable was treated in the Intensive Care Unit under the surgery department from June 26 to 30 and remained admitted for only five days. During this period, only ICU and blood transfusion-related packages of ₹16,700 were blocked under the Ayushman Bharat scheme, the hospital said in a statement on Tuesday.
No additional package was blocked after his death, it said, adding that ₹4.74 lakh remained available in the patient's Ayushman card account.
Queries are generated at various stages of the Ayushman claim process, and the hospital has to upload documents and respond to them before the claim can be closed. In this case, the data entry operator responsible for monitoring the claim delayed the process, resulting in the claim closure being updated on the portal on August 6, the hospital said.
The update automatically triggered the message indicating that the patient had recovered and was being discharged.
Dr Shailendra Gupta of the Surguja district health department said the allegation that the Ayushman card was used for 42 days was "completely incorrect".
"The amount was deducted only for the treatment provided during the patient's actual stay in the hospital. No additional amount was deducted," he said.
Acknowledging that the matter was sensitive, Gupta said the data entry operator should have closed the case promptly but failed to do so.
The data entry operator, who was a collector rate employee, has been removed, he said.
The hospital administration has also written to the state nodal agency in Nava Raipur, seeking measures to ensure that auto-generated messages concerning discharge, referral or death are sent only after the patient's actual status is verified.

headline: SC asks Karnataka to provide infrastructure for special UAPA court
full_text:
SC asks Karnataka to provide infrastructure for special UAPA court
New Delhi, Observing that the state "cannot have the luxury of prolonging trials for years", the Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Karnataka government to provide infrastructure for an additional special court to exclusively deal with cases under the UA on a day-to-day basis.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the directions while hearing a plea filed by Shahid Khan, an accused in a PFI conspiracy case in which the prosecution proposes to examine 707 witnesses, including a few protected witnesses.
"We direct the State of Karnataka to immediately provide the requisite infrastructure, including the creation of one additional post in the Karnataka Higher Judicial Service, along with the requisite staff and other allied facilities as per the norms fixed by the High Court. The necessary sanctions shall be accorded within two weeks," the CJI said in the order.
Once the state sanctions the requisite infrastructure, staff and posts, the chief justice of the Karnataka High Court will spare a judicial officer to preside over the special court to deal exclusively with Unlawful Activities Act on a day-to-day basis, the court said.
"The present case shall also be entrusted to the special court. The Presiding Officer shall first examine the three protected witnesses, followed by the other vital witnesses, to ensure that the material evidence for the prosecution is recorded within a maximum period of three months," the bench ordered.
After the examination of material witnesses, the petitioner shall be at liberty to apply afresh for release on bail, it said.
"Such an application shall be considered on its own merits without being influenced by the observations made in the impugned order," it said.
The court also took note of the existing workload of the special court.
The state informed the bench that the existing court has around 97 trials pending and that repeated interim bail applications by different accused were also consuming considerable judicial time.
The bench noted that following its earlier order, special courts have been set up in Karnataka to try the UA cases, with each court expected to deal with not more than 12 to 15 cases.
"If that has not been done, compliance with our earlier order shall also be ensured. In that scenario, the Presiding Officer of the special court is expected to deal with only 12 to 15 cases, including the case in hand," the bench said.
Referring to the delay, the bench said, "The state cannot have the luxury of prolonging this trial for years."
Justice Bagchi observed that with 97 trials pending in special courts, even if the other cases involved substantially fewer witnesses, their completion could take years. He told the state its understanding of interim bail applications and the examination of witnesses was "faulty", emphasising that examination of witnesses forms part of the trial and should not ordinarily stop merely because an accused has filed an interim bail application.
"When a witness is present, nowhere in India is the witness sent back because a bail application has been filed," he said.
Referring to the present case, the bench noted that only around 50 of the 707 prosecution witnesses were stated to be material and only three protected witnesses were required to be examined in the immediate phase.
"Unless the trial is taken up on a day-to-day basis, it will be practically impossible to conclude it within a reasonable time," the CJI said.
The CJI also criticised the length of an order passed by the trial court rejecting an accused's interim bail application.
"Look at the order passed on the interim bail application. The trial court has spent about 12 pages declining interim bail to one accused. This exercise could probably have been completed in a one-page order," the CJI said.
"If the trial court passes orders of this length, half of the day will be consumed in writing orders," he added.
Senior advocate Aditya Sondhi, appearing for Shahid Khan, submitted that his client had been in custody for nearly four years. He also contended that nine other accused facing IPC offences arising from substantially similar allegations were already on bail.
Sondhi said his client had moved only one interim bail application, following the death of his father-in-law, and that too was rejected.
He urged the court to consider the petitioner's right to a speedy trial under Article 21.

Amit Shah, rejecting “missing” and “fugitive” labels, said he stayed out of the House as Opposition disruptions prevented proceedings.
Union home minister Amit Shah on Wednesday hit back at the Opposition over allegations that he was avoiding Parliament. The BJP MP said he had been attending the session regularly but saw no point in entering the House when proceedings were repeatedly disrupted. Track Parliament proceedings live here
“Ever since the Parliament session began, I have been coming regularly and sitting in my chamber,” Shah told reporters. “But the Opposition is not allowing Parliament to function in either House. So, what is the point of anyone going inside when the proceedings are not being allowed to run?”

Shah rejects ‘missing’, ‘fugitive’ claims
The Opposition, since the beginning of the Parliamentary session, has been demanding Amit Shah's presence in Parliament. They have staged protests and marches in the Parliament House complex to address police action against student protesters in Delhi's Jantar Mantar on July 20.
Shah told reporters on Wednesday, “words like 'laapata', 'bhaag gaye' are terms that have only recently begun to be heard in India’s public and parliamentary discourse.”
Shah also said the government was ready for a discussion on all issues, including protests by students over paper leaks and the alleged police brutality on protesters. He has asked the Opposition to submit a written notice to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla so that a discussion could be held Wednesday through Thursday.
The home minister said parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju had already made the government's position clear on holding a discussion over the students' protests.
“It was the opposition's demand. We agreed to it... From my side, I conveyed that I am also ready for any questions in Parliament. But they do not want to allow any discussion. Now people should decide who is running away,” Shah said.
Rahul Gandhi rejects Shah’s offer
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, said Shah's proposal was a last-minute effort to revive the home minister's public image.

Speaking to reporters, Gandhi said the Opposition was not interested in hearing Shah's “imagination” or a lecture in Parliament. He said the focus should instead be on identifying those responsible for the alleged use of force against protesting students.
Gandhi questioned who ordered the alleged firing on protesting students and police action, pointing to the Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force (RAF), both under the home ministry.

What is a solar eclipse: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon moves directly between the Sun and Earth, casting a narrow shadow across the planet. The phenomenon creates an unusual twilight, with temperatures dropping, shadows appearing at unusual angles and some animals going to sleep. Such strange occurrences once led ancient civilisations to believe eclipses were signs of the apocalypse or messages from the gods.
‘Cosmic coincidence’: In reality, the phenomenon is the result of a "cosmic coincidence", according to Nasa. "Even though the Sun is about 400 times bigger than the Moon, it is also about 400 times farther away," the US space agency says. As a result, people in the right location can see the Moon completely cover the Sun, revealing its outer atmosphere, known as the corona.
Where will the eclipse be visible? According to Nasa, total solar eclipse will sweep across Greenland, Iceland, northern Russia, the Atlantic Ocean, Spain, and a small corner of Portugal. Many other places in the Northern Hemisphere will experience a partial solar eclipse that day, including parts of the northern US (from Alaska to North Carolina), most of Canada, much of Europe, and northwestern Africa.
Will the solar eclipse be visible in India: No, the solar eclipse will not be visible in India, either as a total or partial eclipse. The main reason is the eclipse's visibility path does not extend over India. A solar eclipse can only be seen from the part of Earth where the Moon's shadow falls. For this eclipse, the Moon's shadow will sweep across the Northern Hemisphere, with the path of totality passing through parts of northern Russia, Greenland, Iceland, Spain and Portugal. Other parts of Europe, North America and northwest Africa will see a partial eclipse.

headline: Parliamentary panel flags 56% vacancies at NCERT, 44% at CBSE
full_text:
Parliamentary panel flags 56% vacancies at NCERT, 44% at CBSE
The Tenth Report of the Committee on Estimates for 2026-27, tabled in Lok Sabha, examines affordable quality education, budgetary and policy issues, and reviews the functioning of CBSE.
A parliamentary committee has flagged major staff shortages at two key school education bodies, saying more than half the sanctioned posts at the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) are vacant, while 44 per cent of positions at the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) remain unfilled.
The findings are part of the Tenth Report of the Committee on Estimates for 2026-27 on budget and policy aspects of providing affordable and quality education in the country, including a review of the CBSE, which was presented in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.
The panel said the vacancies need urgent attention, especially as NCERT is central to education policy and curriculum work, and CBSE conducts major national board examinations. It warned that shortages of permanent staff at CBSE could affect the safety, quality and smooth conduct of these exams.
The committee noted that NCERT has played a key role in shaping education policy in India, including the National Education Policy 2020.
The Education Ministry informed the panel that NCERT has developed the National Curriculum Framework for Foundational Stage and the National Curriculum Framework for School Education, and has begun work on syllabi and textbooks based on these frameworks in line with NEP 2020.
At the same time, the committee expressed concern over vacancies across NCERT. It said that as of October 2025, against a sanctioned strength of 2,844 posts across NCERT branches, the actual strength was 1,248, leaving 1,596 posts vacant.
These included 145 academic posts, 131 school teaching posts, 916 ministerial posts and 404 ancillary posts.
"The Committee are of the view that having so many posts vacant in NCERT which is an apex body instrumental in rethinking and reshaping education in a manner that is national in scope, deserve urgent attention of the Ministry," the report said.
It added that "sincere effort should be made by the Ministry for filling up of various vacancies", given the role of education as a transformative force and NCERT’s importance in that process.
On CBSE, the committee said there was a “major shortage” of permanent staff. Out of 2,117 approved positions, 933 posts, or 44 per cent, are vacant, with the biggest gap in Group C support staff, where 595 posts are unfilled.
The panel said CBSE is relying on temporary contractual staff for day-to-day work and warned that "such shortage of permanent staff may put the safety, quality, and smooth running of major national board exams at serious risk".
It strongly recommended that CBSE “should stop relying on temporary contractual workers for sensitive exam works” and fill all vacant posts through fast-track recruitment in a time-bound manner.
The report also noted that CBSE is a self-funded autonomous body that does not receive grant-in-aid from the ministry. It said the number of CBSE-affiliated schools rose from 3,787 in 1992-93 to 31,234 in 2024-25, as on October 8, 2025, and that the board now operates through 25 regional offices and five sub-regional offices.
By 2025, the number of students had risen to over 1.70 million in Class XII and over 2.38 million in Class X, underlining the committee’s concern over staffing gaps at both NCERT and CBSE.

headline: UP to run extra buses from August 26 for Raksha Bandhan travel rush
full_text:
UP to run extra buses from August 26 for Raksha Bandhan travel rush
The Uttar Pradesh government has ordered extra state-run buses from August 26 to 31 for Raksha Bandhan travel. The move aims to ease festival rush, improve passenger safety and cut waiting time.
The Uttar Pradesh government has directed the state transport corporation to run additional buses from August 26 to 31 to ensure safe and smooth travel during Raksha Bandhan, Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh said on Wednesday. The move is aimed at handling the expected rise in passenger traffic during the festival period.
All corporation buses have been asked to remain on the road during the six-day period, with services to be increased on routes where demand rises, especially towards eastern Uttar Pradesh. Officials said extra buses will be deployed on major routes, including those linking Lucknow and Kanpur, and connectivity from Delhi to eastern UP through Moradabad-Bareilly and Aligarh-Kanpur will also be strengthened.
Singh said providing safe and convenient transport to women travelling to meet their brothers during Raksha Bandhan is a priority of the Yogi Adityanath government. Transport Corporation Managing Director Prabhu N Singh has directed regional and assistant regional managers to increase bus operations in line with passenger demand.
Officials said existing restrictions on services from Delhi towards eastern UP through Moradabad-Bareilly and Aligarh-Kanpur will be relaxed wherever needed. The government has also asked authorities to ensure cleanliness, drinking water, adequate lighting and fans at bus stations and inside buses.
A 24-hour control room will monitor bus operations and help passengers, while supervisors will remain posted at busy bus stations. Depot and regional-level officials will also oversee the arrangements. The government has announced special incentives for drivers, conductors and technical staff deployed during the festival period.
Eligible drivers and conductors who complete 1,800 km of bus operations during the six days will get an incentive of Rs 1,200, subject to prescribed conditions. Contractual drivers and conductors will receive an additional 55 paise per km for operations beyond 1,800 km. Eligible technical staff attending depots and regional workshops on all six days will get a one-time incentive of Rs 500. Eligibility for drivers and conductors will also depend on a load factor of more than 64 per cent. An amount of Rs 90,000 has been sanctioned to incentivise employees and supervisors responsible for maintaining arrangements at designated bus stations.
The special arrangements are meant to ensure enough buses are available and to prevent long waiting times for passengers during the Raksha Bandhan rush from August 26 to 31.

full_text:
Chandigarh Administration’s Heritage Items Protection Cell on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) sought urgent intervention from Vice-President and Panjab University (PU) Chancellor C.P. Radhakrishnan to stop the proposed auction of heritage furniture items associated with Panjab University, to be held in the U.S. on August 13.
In a letter to the Vice-President, advocate Ajay Jagga, who is a member of HIPC, has asserted that heritage items belonging to Panjab University had been listed for sale by a Chicago-based auction house, which includes a set of eight dining chairs, described as student residence chairs of PU, with an estimated price of $12,000-$15,000. Besides, there’s a writing chair from PU, with an estimated price of $3,000-$4,000.
“As a premier national institution, Panjab University has a corresponding moral and institutional responsibility to safeguard its own heritage. Therefore, the Panjab University should immediately lodge a formal objection to the proposed auction scheduled for August 13, 2026 in the United States, in which two items belonging to Panjab University are proposed to be auctioned. Such timely intervention may help prevent the alienation of India’s institutional heritage and chances of bringing it back and reaffirm the nation’s commitment to preserving its cultural legacy for future generations,” he wrote in the letter.
Pointing out that it was astonishing to learn who sold Panjab University’s articles in violation of the Constitution of India, and who took them to the U.S. for sale, he said “There is an urgent need to stop this auction or at least put it on hold. Beyond doing our best to reclaim our heritage items, we also need a probe into how, why and by whom the heritage of Panjab University was sold, despite a ban by the Ministry of Home Affairs.”
Mr. Jagga said the representation has been filed in accordance with Article 51A(f) of the Constitution, which calls upon citizens to value and preserve India’s rich cultural heritage, and Article 49, which relates to protection of monuments, places and objects of national importance.

headline: 110 decibels of devotion and the asuras in Kanwar Yatra
full_text:
110 decibels of devotion and the asuras in Kanwar Yatra
The Kanwar Yatra brings lakhs of devotees onto roads across north India each Sawan. It's not just some of the hooligans among the kanwariyas who are a problem. Their music can leave commuters with palpitations. Here's what the kanwariyas said about themselves and their gigantic DJ sets.
"Who was the first Kanwar?" one of the young men from a group of Kanwariyas asked as I hesitantly approached them on the outskirts of Delhi. I guessed Shiva. They laughed at the answer. "No. Ravana. Ravana was the first Kanwar. And who was Ravana?" A Shiva bhakt, I said. "Yes, but what else?" they asked rhetorically, adding, "He was a Brahmin. He was also an asura. We are also asuras. Have you seen any educated, employed person carrying the waters in a Kanwar? It is just us. We are paying for our past sins."
The words were rather poignant, coming from a group of youths who could pass off as ruffians, or to some, kabaddi players. These young men, all of them in their 20s, seemed to have found asura as a way to appropriate their place in the Kanwar Yatra. The thumping bass from their Mad Max trucks was seemingly a sign of Shiva devotees' arrival, as they travelled from Har Ki Paudi in Haridwar to their villages, "seeking redemption".
On the streets of Kalkaji in South Delhi, the music from their trucks registered 93 to 110 decibels on the Decibel Meter app. Legally, normal daytime levels of noise sit around 55 decibels in a residential area. A jet engine operates in the same range as the Kanwariyas' Mad Max trucks. A shotgun blast is around 120 decibels. The bass is deliberate. "Dhammak honi chaahiye, sheesha hilne chaahiye (The earth must shake. Windows must rattle)," one of them said.
"That is the measure of arrival for us Shiv bhakts," the Kanwariya added.
For people stuck behind these trucks for hours, the constant bass and nerve-racking can trigger palpitations and anxiety. The trucks often move slowly, or stop without warning. The men on them are sometimes high on alcohol or other substances. The combination turns ordinary traffic scary, sometimes deadly.
This is not to say that Kanwar Yatra is about hooliganism and chaos. It's just that the high-powered DJ systems and chest-thumping participants make some in the Kanwar Yatra stand out.
Kanwar Yatra is the annual pilgrimage in which devotees carry Ganga water from Haridwar to offer at local Shiva temples in their villages, towns and cities.
In recent years, large sections of it have taken the form of processions built around sound systems, Mad Max-style trucks, and open displays of intoxication.
Kanwariyas India Today Digital spoke to said police in some stretches now restrict speaker size to 10X12 feet, and allow them only on the front sides of vehicles. The groups treat these limits as a "challenge".
"We pool money, around Rs 25,000 for two days in one group of 15-20, and hire DJs known for volume. DJ Kasana, DJ Ravan, DJ SarZen," they pointed out, saying, I should check out their Instagram pages. For a group that size, the cost comes up to roughly Rs 1,700 per person.
"In fact, the kanwariyas also compete during the Kanwar season, and whoever is the loudest wins," he said.
Surprisingly, most of the DJ names mentioned by the kanwariyas have lakhs of followers.
WHAT 110 DECIBELS CAN DO TO THE BODY
Noise at the levels recorded around the Kanwar trucks is dangerous in multiple ways. The WHO identifies environmental noise as a health risk associated with cardiovascular disease, hypertension, sleep disturbance, cognitive impairment, hearing impairment and mental-health effects.
The body's response to loud noise can involve stress pathways that affect the cardiovascular and metabolic systems.
At 110 decibels, that we recorded around Kanwar trucks in Delhi, the exposure was well above the 85 dBA threshold at which repeated or prolonged exposure can cause noise-induced hearing loss.
The US National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders says that at 100 dBA, hearing damage can occur after around 14 minutes, while at 110 dBA it can occur after about two minutes, depending on the exposure.
"Loud sound I hear behind the Kanwar trucks all day while driving the cab causes ringing or buzzing in my ears," said Ajeet Rajput, the cabbie I went around with.
The effects are not confined to just ears. Research cited by WHO links environmental noise with increased cardiovascular risk, including hypertension and ischaemic heart disease.
People who have been stuck around these trucks producing sustained low-frequency bass in traffic have reported palpitations, heightened stress or a sense of panic.
THE KANWAR GROUPS AND THEIR MAD MAX TRUCKS
The first group I met was resting under open truck flaps in the rain. No DJs because they were resting, but the residue of the night before was there in the form of booze breath.
The second group I encountered moved on foot with dhols. Not very loud, but visibly very high, most likely on bhaang or other marijuana derivatives.
The third matched the image that has come to define Kanwar Yatra in the National Capital Region. Speakers that can make your ears bleed, gym rats aboard the truck and flanking it, and if you moved closer to the group, the cross-faded smell of alcohol and marijuana.
The scene matched the exact image the young man had told me earlier: the procession was the declaration that they are asuras, "seeking Shiva's favour, so their lives might improve". Most were between 20 and 25. Many admitted they were unemployed. This self-description was consistent across groups India Today Digital spoke to.
"In Haridwar the police enforce restrictions more tightly. Once the water is collected and the journey towards villages in Haryana or Uttar Pradesh begins, the music becomes louder," a Kanwar told India Today Digital.
The consequences of lax control by the administration fall on everyone else. On August 10, schools across large parts of Uttar Pradesh remained closed because of Kanwar Yatra. Private schools shifted to online classes. For students, the academic calendar paused unexpectedly. The reason given was safety and traffic management.
Processions of this scale and temperament make ordinary movement and ordinary business difficult.
Small collisions, or even perceived disrespect, such as someone's car brushing a truck, a pedestrian crossing at the wrong moment, have escalated into attacks by Kanwariyas, and even schoolchildren have not been spared.
In south Delhi's Kalkaji, a group travelling from Haridwar towards a village called Harkesh Nagar blasted, "Agle janam mujhe paida keejo Gujjar jaat mein". The sound meter on my phone climbed to 110 decibels next to their truck.
The problem with Kanwar trucks is not only that they are loud, they also move slowly through roads that are already struggling with traffic. National highways and city arteries fill with these trucks in Sawan every year, and the bass continues.
The men I met did not see themselves or their music as a threat. They saw themselves as devotees. They spoke about Shiva, Ravana and redemption, and an appropriated identity. For everyone else on those roads, there was no choice but to listen.

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) ordered that the licence of the residential tribal school, where three girls died due to snake bite, be cancelled permanently. The administration said that it was in the process of issuing a notice regarding the matter. The CM also said that the official who had inspected the school earlier and had submitted a report, should be placed under suspension.
Maharashtra Tribal Affairs Minister Ashok Uike is learnt to have said in the Cabinet meeting on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) that the government should take strict action against the private organisation which receives government aid to run the residential school for tribal girls.
“The tribal residential schools need to be inspected properly. Instead of looking at only such schools which are on the main roads, the schools in the interior areas too need to be inspected properly. This school had no teacher, no warden. No facilities were provided though this school received government aid,” the CM is learnt to have said during the meeting.
Meanwhile, a 14-year-old girl continued to be critical and remained under treatment. Another girl, 11, is stable, district health officials told The Hindu. Officials said that the snake bit five girls, and not six, as reported earlier in the media. Several girls felt scared and said they had symptoms like stomach ache and vomiting. “They were all admitted and later discharged after found to be stable,” Dr. Pratap Shinde, District Health Officer, Gadchiroli, told The Hindu.
The incident took place in the intervening night between August 9 and August 10. approximately between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m.. At the residential tribal school for girls in Japtalai in Dhanora taluka, some girls were sleeping on the floor in a large hall. The total number of girls in the tribal school is 233.
Political reactions
The Opposition slammed the government and asked that the culprits be booked for culpable homicide. “This is a murder by the system,” NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar said. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut asked how the girls could die of a snake bite in Maharashtra. The BJP said that the school was being run by the organisation owned by Congress leader Marotrao Kowase, who was an MLA for three terms and an MP for one term.

Former Haryana Chief Minister and the Leader of Opposition in Assembly, Congress’s Bhupinder Singh Hooda, on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) said the party would corner the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in the monsoon session of the State Assembly over poor law and order, rising organised crime and tax hikes based on property tax and collector rates in the State.
“We will submit a calling attention motion during the assembly session, to seek answers from the government regarding the breakdown of law and order, rising organized crime and tax hikes based on property tax and collector rates,” said Mr. Hodda, addressing a press conference in Chandigarh.
He said the Congress MLAs will also move motions in the Assembly to raise issues surrounding waterlogging in urban and rural areas due to rains, compensation for farmers, demands of electricity department employees, the privatisation of power services in Gurugram and the grievances of guest teachers, sanitation workers and other staff.
“The Congress would move an ‘adjournment motion’ as well to discuss the alleged scams involving IDFC Bank, AU Small Finance Bank, etc in the session,” he said.
Mr. Hooda accused the BJP government for being insensitive towards farmers. “The government has failed to lift the full stock of urea and other fertilizers allocated to Haryana by the Centre. The Centre had allocated 9.59 lakh metric tonnes of urea to Haryana up to August, yet the government has lifted only 8.14 lakh metric tonnes. Similarly, 2.53 lakh metric tonnes of di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) were allocated, yet the government lifted only 1.15 lakh metric tonnes. This implies the government intends for farmers to face hardship by having to stand in long queues for fertilizer,” he said.
On the issue of Sutlej-Yamuna Link (SYL) canal, the center of a decades-long water-sharing dispute between Punjab and Haryana, Mr. Hooda said, “The incumbent Chief Minister of Haryana remains frequently active in Punjab, yet never raises the matter of the SYL canal while he is there. Ministers from the Centre regularly visit and announce decisions regarding the transfer of water from Haryana to Rajasthan via pipeline, but no one speaks about securing Haryana’s rightful share of water from Punjab.”
Mr. Hooda announced that the Congress party will hold a protest demonstration on August 19 regarding the demand for the regularisation of ‘Haryana Kaushal Rozgar Nigam’ workers and other issues. “During the 2024 assembly elections, the BJP had announced the regularisation of 125,000 ‘Kaushal’ workers to garner their votes. However, even after nearly two years, these contractual employees have not received any law or official notification regarding their regularisation,” he alleged.

headline: In a representation to PMO in July, a parent sought uniform implementation of the SC judgement
full_text:
In a representation to PMO in July, a parent sought uniform implementation of the SC judgement
NEW DELHI: More than a year after Supreme Court ruled that residence or domicile cannot be the basis for postgraduate medical admissions under the state quota, parents of NEET-PG aspirants say admission rules still vary across states, leaving students with unequal opportunities despite having taken the same national entrance examination.The concerns stem from SCâs Jan 29, 2025, judgement in Dr Tanvi Behl vs Shrey Goel case, which held that residence-based preference in postgraduate medical admissions is not permissible. The court said admissions should be based on NEET-PG scores while allowing only limited institutional preference, meaning a student may receive preference for having graduated from a particular medical college â and not because he or she is a resident or domicile of a state.
. Some states appear to have implemented the judgement, while others continue with different eligibility conditions.
The dispute primarily concerns private medical colleges, where admissions are conducted through state counselling. Several states prescribe domicile or other state-specific eligibility conditions. âThe intention of the SC judgement was to replace residence-based preference with institutional preference. Some states appear to have implemented the judgement, while others continue with different eligibility conditions.
If these policies are challenged, the courts will decide whether they are consistent with the judgement. The Centre can still review the issue and issue uniform guidelines to states,â a health ministry official said.State counselling brochures for the NEET-PG admission process, reviewed by TOI, indeed show differences in eligibility rules. Gujarat requires additional state-specific eligibility conditions for some candidates who completed MBBS outside the state. Maharashtra allows only certain Maharashtra domicile candidates who studied outside the state to apply, while Karnataka permits candidates from other states to participate in counselling, though without Karnataka reservation benefits.
Parents say these differences mean students with the same NEET-PG score may not have equal opportunity to compete for PG seats.In a representation to PMO in July, a parent sought uniform implementation of the SC judgement, a common national counselling portal and biannual NEET-PG examinations, arguing that students continue to face unequal admission opportunities across states. PMO has acknowledged the grievance, but no final decision has been communicated.Parents say the system also increases costs as candidates must register separately for multiple counselling processes, each with its own eligibility rules, timelines and security deposits. In response to one representation, NMC said domicile or residence-based reservation under state quota falls within the statesâ jurisdiction and advised the complainant to approach the state or UT concerned. A similar representation to PMO in 2022 seeking uniform rules was closed after noting the concerns.
Anuja Jaiswal is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Times of India, with an impressive 18-year career in narrative journalism. She specializes in health and heritage reporting, expertly simplifying complex health information to make it engaging and understandable for readers. Her deep dives into heritage topics are well-researched, resulting in captivating narratives that resonate with her audience. Over the years, she has worked in Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh and West UP, gaining diverse on-ground experience that shapes her storytelling.

NEW DELHI: The Centre should scrap all existing inter-state border check posts within six months and replace the All India Tourist Permit with a unified All India Passenger Permit within a year, a parliamentary panel has recommended, pitching for a sweeping overhaul of the countryâs bus transport system.The committee headed by JD(U) MP Sanjay Kumar Jha made the recommendations after consultations with govt departments, bus operators, passengers and other stakeholders to identify key hurdles facing the sector, which transports more passengers daily than Indian Railways.The panel noted that India has around 4.4 lakh buses, but only about 1.1 lakh are owned by govt entities, mainly state road transport undertakings. Ten states account for nearly 90% of these govt-owned buses, including Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.Calling for an overhaul of the permit regime, panel urged road transport ministry to replace the All India Tourist Permit with an All India Passenger Permit. The new permit should reflect the number of passengers actually carried, ensuring that enforcement does not hinge on whether a traveller qualifies as a âtouristâ.
âThe rights of the permit holder, including the right to halt, to board and set down passengers at notified points, and to enter public terminals on payment, should be stated exhaustively on the face of the permit,â panel said.It also asked Centre to prevail upon six states to close border check posts that they are still operating.
Panel further recommended that all bus terminals provide private operators ânon-discriminatory accessâ to pick up passengers on payment of an entry fee, following the model at Delhiâs ISBT.It also proposed establishment of a National Bus Terminals Authority to develop and standardise terminal infrastructure and, where states agree, manage bus terminals and intermodal passenger hubs.Panel further recommended a unified online ticketing platform covering state-run and private bus operators for passenger convenience.It has proposed a citizen vigilance channel, modelled on Election Commissionâs cVIGIL app, allowing passengers to file geo-tagged, time-stamped complaintsâwith photos or videosâabout overloading, unsafe transport of schoolchildren, faulty safety equipment and poor sanitation in buses, terminals and halting points.Complaints would be automatically forwarded to the enforcement authority concerned for action within a prescribed timeframe, it said.

headline: Kerala Higher Education Minister Roji M. John has said the centralised spot admission process for vacant B.Tech seats in the State’s government and aided engineering colleges has been made more student-friendly. Until last year, centralised spot admi...
full_text:
Kerala Higher Education Minister Roji M. John has said the centralised spot admission process for vacant B.Tech seats in the State’s government and aided engineering colleges has been made more student-friendly. Until last year, centralised spot admissions were conducted at the Government Engineering College (GEC), Thrissur. Under the system, students could secure admission to vacant seats in any of the nine government engineering colleges and three aided engineering colleges from the centre alone.
This year, the Technical Education department had initially decided to conduct separate spot admissions at individual colleges. However, following concerns raised by students, the Minister has issued directions to make the process more convenient for applicants.
According to the revised arrangement, candidates participating in the centralised spot admission scheduled for August 13 will not have to travel to GEC Thrissur. Instead, applicants can report at any one of the 12 participating government or aided engineering colleges. A centralised software system will allot the available seats based on the candidates’ rank.
The students must report at any one of the 12 colleges before 12 p.m. on August 13 to be considered for admission to vacant seats. The arrangement is expected to eliminate the need for students to travel to Thrissur for the centralised spot admission.
The same team of software experts that coordinated the centralised spot admission process at GEC Thrissur during the previous years will coordinate the process.
Students participating in the spot admission must produce their Transfer Certificate (TC) or No Objection Certificate (NOC). However, the requirement does not apply to students who are already admitted to government engineering colleges.

headline: An internal government task force has recommended several amendments to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, including raising the relief and rehabilitation amounts that governments are mandated to pay victims o...
full_text:
An internal government task force has recommended several amendments to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Rules, including raising the relief and rehabilitation amounts that governments are mandated to pay victims of atrocities under the law to adjust for inflation. Among other recommendations made by this task force are measures to introduce counselling for the accused and the victims and their dependents.
Further, the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) has separately suggested amendments to the Atrocities Act, mainly focusing on introducing a provision to protect the livelihoods of Scheduled Tribe communities who are alienated from their land and are involved in prolonged court battles over it. The NCST has also called for measures to check the registration of “counter FIRs” against those who end up reporting atrocity cases to the police.
In a report submitted to the government on July 31, the task force, headed by the Secretary, Social Justice and Empowerment, drafted suggested amendments to the rules framed under the SC/ST Act, which was last amended in 2018 in response to widespread protests from SC and ST communities across the country against a Supreme Court ruling that held that prior permission was required to make arrests in such cases and that anticipatory bail could be granted.
According to government officials, the recommendations also include measures to establish special relief and rehabilitation cells in States and Union Territories. One official told The Hindu that the idea under discussion at the task force meetings was to increase the relief and rehabilitation amounts in accordance with inflation.
Currently, the relief and rehabilitation amount ranges from ₹85,000 to ₹8.25 lakh, depending on the seriousness of the crimes under the Atrocities Act and the degree of injuries and harm suffered by the victims and their dependents. These amounts were set in 2016. Apart from provisions related to relief and rehabilitation, the task force has also suggested amendments that require FIRs and chargesheets in such cases to be sent to government officials concerned within 24 hours.
The move to initiate discussions on possible amendments comes as the anti-reservation movement under the “reservation hatao andolan” banner is growing to also campaign for other issues faced by the “general category” in India, including the alleged “misuse” of the Atrocity Act. General category activists and anti-reservation campaigners have argued that the law “incentivises fake cases”, among other things.
However, a senior government official said the recommendations have been submitted to the Social Justice Ministry and are subject to review by the government. More information will be made public if the amendments are accepted, the official said.
No means of livelihoods
On the NCST suggestions, another government official said that in several cases, tribals fighting court battles after being dispossessed of their lands have no recourse for livelihoods as they lose access to the land in the meantime. “One suggestion was made to include a provision that allows the local official, like the DM, to intervene and allow the tribals to use the land for livelihood while the court dispute continues,” the official said.
The official added that “counter FIRs” were another important issue that needed to be addressed. In many cases, victims are intimidated through registration of counter FIRs after they report an atrocity to the police, the official said. “There should be a measure to randomly check the final reports filed by the police when they close an atrocity FIR and the final reports in the counter FIRs to check if the procedure was followed,” the official said.
The current set of recommendations was made by a task force constituted with the approval of Union Social Justice Minister Virendra Kumar in December, 2025. This task force had representation from the Law Ministry, the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Tribal Affairs Ministry, the National Commissions for SCs and STs, and Social Justice Department officials of Bihar, Assam, Tamil Nadu, Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh.
In response to a question in the Lok Sabha on Tuesday, the Ministry of Social Justice said the task force’s recommendations will be discussed with State and Union Territory governments, and other stakeholders “as appropriate” before finalising such amendments. It went on to note that any amendments to the rules will be considered only in accordance with the Act, adding that care would be taken to “ensure that such amendment does not dilute the protective framework, investigation procedures, or the provisions relating to relief and rehabilitation guaranteed under the Act”.

headline: Over 50 writers, thinkers and activists have written to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar against Vishnu Vardhan, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Horticulture Sciences, Bagalkot, for inviting the public to a religious ceremony in his official resid...
full_text:
Over 50 writers, thinkers and activists have written to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar against Vishnu Vardhan, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Horticulture Sciences, Bagalkot, for inviting the public to a religious ceremony in his official residence, on his official letter pad.
They objected strongly to this act and sought disciplinary action against the Vice-Chancellor. They alleged that the invitation made attendance mandatory.
The Vice-Chancellor has invited all the officers, teaching and non-teaching staff, and students of the main campus of the university, on behalf of his family, to the Sri Satyanarayana Puja, Navagraha Shanti Homa, and Sri Mahaganapati Puja Programme in his official residence on the campus. The Vice-Chancellor has signed the letter. A copy of the invite was attached to the email sent to the Chief Minister.
An individual’s faith and the functioning of a public institution are different issues. There should be no attempt to mix them by public officials, it said.
If Satyanarayana Puja and Navagraha Homa are all personal beliefs of an individual, then there can be no objection to it. But making the same belief public through an invitation made mandatory for all staff and students using the official letterhead of the university, the official signature of the Vice-Chancellor, and the name of the Vice-Chancellor is condemnable.
India is a secular and democratic country. The Constitution asks each citizen to promote the spirit of inquiry and the scientific spirit. Universities are centres of knowledge. They are supposed to transcend caste, religion, and beliefs. It is against the spirit of the Constitution and the State government service rules for the head of such an institution to impose a particular religious practice on the institution by using the power of his position. Following such a letter, subordinate employees and students will not have the courage to reject the invitation from the Vice-Chancellor. This is an indirect imposition, the email said.
It is alarming that such practices are becoming “normal” in all the universities of the State in recent days. It is regrettable and condemnable that the Chancellors appointed by the government are acting like priests of religious practices, they said. They demanded that the government suspend the Vice-Chancellor and issue orders to all universities and colleges that no religious ceremony should be held in the name of the institution or in government buildings.

headline: Dr. M.P. Parameswaran, fondly called M.P. by his numerous friends, is no more. His going is certainly a loss to many in Kerala and the rest of India who knew him or of him.
full_text:
Dr. M.P. Parameswaran, fondly called M.P. by his numerous friends, is no more. His going is certainly a loss to many in Kerala and the rest of India who knew him or of him.
A young nuclear engineer-turned-political and social activist during the second half of the 1960s, M.P. got attracted and then immersed in building up a small organisation of writers of science called Kerala Sastra Sahitya Parishad into a people’s science movement. Of course, there were forerunners like P.T. Bhaskara Panicker who had already opened a way for mobilising young teachers, professional experts and students. M.P. electrified the imagination of the youth especially in rural areas by his book, rather booklet, titled Nature, Science and Society. KSSP activists conducted more than thirty thousand classes during 1974-76 based on this booklet talking about the interrelationship between nature, science and society.
Marx to Gandhi
Then followed a book on Kerala’s economy prepared by a collective for which I was invited to contribute. That set off a personal relationship that lasted half a century. M.P. started, as was the case with many youth in Kerala, as a Marxist to understand the socioeconomic problems afflicting one’s society. But his young Marx grew into a dynamic Gandhi over time. He then wrote, lectured and acted to formulate a decentralised governance system, applying it to Kerala, to attain what he called sustainability in all spheres, ecological , economic and social. His party punished him with expulsion for straying away from the officially adopted Marxist path. He did not rebel or complain. He worked tirelessly and published a large number of books and articles on how to translate his dream of decentralised development for sustainable living.
Despite impressive awareness about environmental sustainability and a rather passive and patchy awareness of the desirability of decentralised governance, Kerala is miles and miles away from the dreams of the like of M.P.
I feel fortunate to have closely associated with him for about half a century in pursuing our common dreams, howsoever inconsequential it may seem.
(The author is a development economist and Honorary Fellow, Centre for Development Studies, Thiruvananthapuram)

headline: The Kerala High Court has orally questioned the basis on which two bodybuilders were appointed as sub-inspectors in the State’s armed police force, despite failing the physical test.
full_text:
The Kerala High Court has orally questioned the basis on which two bodybuilders were appointed as sub-inspectors in the State’s armed police force, despite failing the physical test.
The court was acting on a petition seeking Vigilance inquiry into the appointment of bodybuilding champion Chitharesh Natesan and Shinu Chowwa, who had won the silver medal in the South Asia World Bodybuilding Championship, in the armed police force by creating two supernumerary posts.
Justice A. Badharudeen was considering a statement by Director General of Prosecution T. Asaf Ali on behalf of the Home Secretary, asserting that the bodybuilders — Chitharesh Natesan and Shinu Chowwa — had been called for a physical examination, during which the former did not show up and the latter had failed. Later, they underwent the mandatory medical examination and police verification, during which Mr. Natesan was found medically unfit.
It was also reported that even though appointment orders had been issued to the sportspersons, neither candidate had been admitted to training and no proposals from the police department recommending their appointment had been forwarded to the government.
Additionally, the court was informed that none of the officers assailed in the petition could have committed an offence warranting an approval for a Vigilance probe since the decision to appoint the two sportspersons in question was not made by an individual official, but as part of a policy decision.
The petition challenging the appointments was filed by lawyer K.M. Shajahan, contending that the bodybuilders had been appointed after failing the physical test, that DGP S.Sreejith had taken an undue interest in the matter, and that then Home Secretary Biswanath Sinha and then political secretary to the Chief Minister, P. Sasi, had intervened in the matter of their appointment, and sought a Vigilance inquiry.
