NEW DELHI: The tiny plastic sachet that has become synonymous with pan masala may finally be on its way out. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has notified plastic-free packaging norms for the product, a move experts say could further enforcement of an existing ban by allowing the food regulator to act directly against violators.The amended Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2026, require pan masala to be packed only in paper, paperboard, cellulose or other naturally derived materials free from plastic, or in tin or glass containers. The notification prohibits use of materials containing polyethylene, polypropylene, polyester, PVC, synthetic polymers, laminates, aluminium foil and metallised layers, and also makes the packaging subject to Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016.
The rules came into force upon their publication in the gazette
A senior FSSAI official told TOI that pan masala has been specifically included under Schedule IV of packaging regulations to provide Food Business Operators with clear guidance on suitable packaging materials, given the widespread use of small single-use packs and the environmental concerns arising from their disposal. However, environmental experts said the notification primarily furthers enforcement rather than imposing fresh prohibition.
âThe Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, had already placed an explicit legal ban on plastic sachets for gutka, tobacco and pan masala. The FSSAI notification reinforces that mandate through food safety regulations,â said Siddharth G. Singh, programme manager, solid waste management and circular economy, Centre for Science and Environment.He said enforcement of Plastic Waste Management Rules has remained patchy because it largely depends on state pollution control boards and local bodies. Bringing the requirement under the ambit of food safety regulations will allow FSSAI to act directly against Food Business Operators, plugging an enforcement gap that environmental laws alone struggled to address, he said.Singh said pan masala was specifically targeted because the sector relies heavily on use of small single-use sachets, which have a high littering potential and among the lowest collection rates.
Anuja Jaiswal is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Times of India, with an impressive 18-year career in narrative journalism. She specializes in health and heritage reporting, expertly simplifying complex health information to make it engaging and understandable for readers. Her deep dives into heritage topics are well-researched, resulting in captivating narratives that resonate with her audience. Over the years, she has worked in Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh and West UP, gaining diverse on-ground experience that shapes her storytelling.

headline: MP High Court seeks funds for Indore girl's Rs 9.55 crore treatment
full_text:
MP High Court seeks funds for Indore girl's Rs 9.55 crore treatment
The Madhya Pradesh High Court has asked the Centre and the state to help fund SMA treatment for a three-year-old Indore girl. The court said about Rs 1 crore is still needed so treatment can begin without delay.
The Madhya Pradesh High Court has said it expects the Centre and the state government to find a way to provide financial assistance for the treatment of a three-year-old girl suffering from Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) Type-2, a rare medical condition. The court noted that about Rs 1 crore more is needed for the treatment even after central government assistance and money raised through crowdfunding.
Hearing the matter on Tuesday, the Indore bench said the treatment should begin at the earliest and fixed the next hearing for August 18. The case relates to Anika Sharma, a three-year-old from Indore, whose petition said the injections required for SMA treatment cost about Rs 9.55 crore.
Justice Sandeep N Bhatt noted that financial assistance of up to Rs 50 lakh is available under a central government scheme. Counsel for the petitioner, Chanchal Gupta, told the court that about Rs 8 crore had been raised through campaigns run by various non-governmental organisations and charitable institutions.
Gupta told the court that the amount collected through these campaigns is currently with the concerned institutions. The high court directed the petitioner's lawyer to submit all relevant details from these institutions and an affidavit stating that they are willing to pay the treatment amount to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, once the bill for the injection is raised.
The court also said the bill from Novartis, the company that manufactured the injection, must be made available to AIIMS for necessary action. It noted that even after adding the Centre's assistance of Rs 50 lakh to the nearly Rs 8 crore raised through crowdfunding, an additional Rs 1 crore is still required.
In its order, the high court said, "It is also expected that looking to the special circumstances, the government can also find out some way to consider such cases under exceptional case to provide further financial assistance which is also to the tune of Rs 1 crore after adding Rs 50 lakh as by the government and Rs 8 crore which are already collected through crowd funding by various institutions." The court added, "It is also open for the state government to find out some way to provide some financial assistance. It is also expected probably by the next date that the further amount can be received from other organisation/ institution so that the treatment of the said child who is suffering from rare disease can be started at the earliest."
Spinal Muscular Atrophy is a genetic neuromuscular disease in which motor neurons in the spinal cord are gradually destroyed, causing muscles to weaken and degenerate. Motor neurons are specialised nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord that carry messages from the brain to the body's muscles for functions including breathing, swallowing and speaking.
In sum, the high court has asked for documents linked to the crowdfunding amount, said the bill should be placed before AIIMS, and expressed the hope that the Centre, the state government and other institutions will help bridge the remaining Rs 1 crore so that the child's treatment can start soon.

headline: Residents of Valayambattu village in Tirupattur have been opposing the setting up of a Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) by neighbouring Vaniyambadi municipality along Palar River due to fear of groundwater pollution.
full_text:
Residents of Valayambattu village in Tirupattur have been opposing the setting up of a Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) by neighbouring Vaniyambadi municipality along Palar River due to fear of groundwater pollution.
Residents said that more than 4,000 families reside in Valayambattu village that comes under Alangayam Panchayat Union in the district. Most of the families depend on agriculture and weaving. “The proposed treatment plant can be established away from farming areas and water bodies. Alternative sites for the facility should be identified,” said M. Karthigeyan, a resident.
Residents said that the village has a few water bodies. It is located on the confluence of Kallar and Palar rivers along Chennai - Bengaluru Highway (NH 48). Paddy is the chief crop cultivated in the village and adjoining hamlets. Farmers also cultivate green chilli, brinjal, groundnuts, greens and mango. Farmers said that the proposed 10-acre plot that had been identified for the new treatment plant could be used for grazing cattle by farmers. It could also store excess rainwater during monsoon, thereby preventing inundation of houses.
Residents said that setting up of the sewage treatment plant near water bodies and farmlands will affect water quality in the area. Such pollution to groundwater and surface water will impact farming in surrounding villages.
As municipal officials of Vaniyambadi town, which has over one lakh residents, were unable to find land within its limits due to high cost, civic officials said that they identified land in Valayambattu village. The village is also located downstream of the river that will help discharge household wastewater to the proposed treatment plant.
The STP will be built to treat sewage generated in houses within the Vaniyambadi municipality, two km from Valayambattu village. Recycled water will be used to water plants on roads. At present, existing stormwater drains in Vaniyambadi are used to discharge sewage which flows into nearby lakes and ponds, resulting in pollution. The new plant will end illegal discharge of sewage into drains and pollution of water bodies, the officials said.

headline: The Jaipur zonal office of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested an accused, Subhash Chandra Bijnoriya, in connection with a money laundering investigation related to the alleged fraud case against Nexa Evergreen, in which ₹2,676 crore were c...
full_text:
The Jaipur zonal office of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested an accused, Subhash Chandra Bijnoriya, in connection with a money laundering investigation related to the alleged fraud case against Nexa Evergreen, in which ₹2,676 crore were collected from a large number of investors.
Mr. Bijnoriya, one of the principal architects and operators of Nexa Evergreen Group, has been accused of carrying out fraudulent operations along with another partner in the firm. The two accused allegedly floated and operated a web of companies and proprietorship concerns in the names of associates and investors for layering and routing the proceeds of crime.
The ED arrested Mr. Bijnoriya under Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, on Monday (August 10, 2026) and produced him in a PMLA special court here, which remanded him to the custody of the financial investigation agency till August 13.
The ED launched investigation in the case on the basis of multiple first information reports and chargesheets filed by Rajasthan Police against Nexa Evergreen Group. An ED spokesperson said here that the accused had lured investors by claiming that the funds would be invested in land development and plotting projects at Dholera Smart City in Gujarat.
“Investors were induced on the promise of assured weekly returns of 3% for 60 weeks or allotment of plots, while additional commissions and rewards, including laptops, motorcycles and cars, were offered for enrolling new investors under a multi-level referral scheme,” the ED spokesperson said.
The entities floated as part of the alleged fraud and their bank accounts were systematically used for collection of investors’ funds, inter-account transfers, payment of returns to earlier investors in the nature of a Ponzi scheme, and acquisition of immovable properties, according to the ED. All of this was done while concealing the true source and ownership of funds.
The ED’s Jaipur zonal office had earlier conducted searched under Section 17 of the PMLA in June 2025 at 25 locations in Jaipur, Sikar, Jhunjhunu and Ahmedabad, which resulted in the seizure of cash amounting to Rs.2.04 crore along with various incriminating records and digital devices.
An amount of ₹15 crore lying in the bank accounts and crypto accounts linked with various Nexa Group entities and associates were also frozen, according to the ED.

headline: Shivraj Singh Chouhan informed the Lok Sabha that the VB-G RAM G scheme has been implemented in rural areas of the entire country.
full_text:
Shivraj Singh Chouhan informed the Lok Sabha that the VB-G RAM G scheme has been implemented in rural areas of the entire country.
NEW DELHI: Over 9.69 crore person-days have been generated in approximately a month of the rollout of the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act (VB-G RAM G) which replaced MGNREGA, the govt informed Lok Sabha on Tuesday.When VB- G RAM G Scheme was rolled out from July 1, revised wage rates were notified by the govt with a new interim base wage rate of Rs 300 per day. With this the national average notified wage increased from Rs 298.8 per day under MGNREGA to Rs 327.4 under VBâG RAM G, representing an average increase of Rs 28.6 per day. Prior to this notification, wage rates in several states were below Rs 300, with the lowest notified wage being Rs 241 per day.Meanwhile, the parliamentary standing committee on rural development and panchayati raj in its report submitted in Parliament on Tuesday recommended a comprehensive review of the wage-determination methodology including the appropriateness of the 2011 base year and the adequacy of CPI-AL and consider instituting a minimum wage floor of Rs 400 per day with regional differentiation and ensure systematic and meaningful indexation to a robust inflation indicator that reflects actual rural living costs.
âPending structural revision, necessary fiscal space should be sought for a significant upward adjustment in the current cycle,â the panel chaired by Congress MP Saptagiri Sankar Ulaka recommended. The Committee in its report, on the action taken on the recommendations contained in its earlier report submitted in Parliament in March on 'Demands for Grants (2026-27) related to the department of rural development, has sought an action taken report on the fresh recommendations within three months.In a written response to a question asked by Congress MPs Vijayakumar Alias Vijay Vasanth and Manickam Tagore, rural development minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan informed the Lok Sabha that the VB-G RAM G scheme has been implemented in rural areas of the entire country.
The VB-G RAM G scheme provides for a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work against 100 days of guaranteed wage employment available under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS.In response to the question on whether the govt has taken note of concerns raised by several State Governments regarding the financial structure of VB-G RAM-G and details of the reasons for shifting financial burden to states up to 40% under VB-G RAM-G. âPresently almost all centrally sponsored schemes (CSS) across sectors are being implemented on the 60:40 sharing model. The 60:40 pattern adopted under this Act is therefore consistent with the broader framework of Centrally Sponsored Schemes,â the minister said and shared that regular consultations were being held with states. The fund sharing pattern is 90:10 with the Centre bearing 90% of the expenditure incase of union territories and northeastern and Himalayan states.

headline: IGP Kashmir VK Birdi said the police were probing the threat letter, believed to have been released on social media on Aug 7.
full_text:
IGP Kashmir VK Birdi said the police were probing the threat letter, believed to have been released on social media on Aug 7.
SRINAGAR: J&K police have tightened security in areas of the Valley where Kashmiri Pandits live and allowed some employees to work from home temporarily after Panun Kashmir claimed a purported threat letter from Lashkar affiliate United Liberation Council naming several community members and listing their phone numbers.âAuthorities must investigate the source of the information, the digital trail behind the communication and whether any surveillance, profiling or reconnaissance of the targeted persons has taken place,â Agnishekar, convenor of Panun Kashmir said, adding it was important to establish whether the âperpetrators actually possessed the information or were using it as a form of psychological warfareâ.IGP Kashmir VK Birdi said the police were probing the threat letter, believed to have been released on social media on Aug 7. Divisional commissioner Anshul Garg said some Pandits had been allowed to work from home, but there was no blanket order. Education officials said the department had not issued any such work-from-home order for all Pandit staff.According to Panun Kashmirâs Agnishekar, âthe letter represented a serious escalation as it went beyond generic threats and appeared to identify individuals as potential targets while claiming access to information about their families, locations and places of workâ.
âThe publication of names and personal contact details, accompanied by explicit threats to pursue the individuals and their families, is a matter of grave concern. This is not something that can be dismissed as mere rhetoric. It has the unmistakable potential to intimidate the targeted individuals and terrorise the wider Kashmiri Pandit community,â Agnishekar said.The threat was particularly disturbing in view of the communityâs history of being victims of targeted killings, intimidation and forced displacement from Kashmir, Agnishekar pointed out. Jammu-based Panun Kashmir seeks a separate homeland for Pandits in the Valley with Union territory status.Kashmiri Pandit Sangarsh Samiti, another community group representing those who stayed back in the Valley after 1990sâ migration, called the new threat a conspiracy to sabotage their existence. âRecent terror attacks in south Kashmir, followed by fresh threat posters naming Kashmiri Pandit employees, have once again exposed the chilling sense of vulnerability,â KPSS said.
In 2008, the Manmohan Singh-led UPA govt introduced a rehabilitation package for the Pandits who had to leave the Valley in the 1990s in the face of terror. Among other measures, the package provided 6,000 govt jobs and created new posts. Such people are posted in various departments across Kashmir and are called âPM package employeesâ.

headline: The petitioner said that post-May 15, there has been a quantum increase in clips of selectively edited judicial proceedings.
full_text:
The petitioner said that post-May 15, there has been a quantum increase in clips of selectively edited judicial proceedings.
NEW DELHI: Three months after CJI Surya Kant's 'cockroach' remark sparked a storm and gave birth to Cockroach Janta Party that led a Gen Z protest against NEET-UG paper leak, Supreme Court Tuesday sought responses from govt and CBI on a PIL seeking action against those who commercially exploited the remark through clever editing of virtual court proceedings and draped it with a meaning that was never intended.During a half-an-hour long debate on the issue before a bench comprising CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, petitioner-cum-advocate Raja Choudhary said it requires a deeper investigation as to how the word 'cockroach', used in a completely different context during judicial proceedings on May 15, was selectively picked, cleverly edited and commercially exploited to undermine judicial dignity and hurt institutional integrity. The petitioner sought a direction to authorities "to examine and take action in accordance with law against persons/entities allegedly involved in commercial exploitation, trademark appropriation, monetized circulation, or unauthorised commercial use of oral courtroom observations/metaphors, including activities of CJP, while recognising that fair criticism, democratic dissent, satire, and free speech remain permissible within the constitutional framework without undermining institutional dignity".
Referring to the May 15 hearing before a CJI-led bench on a petition 'Sanjay Dubey Vs Registrar General of Delhi HC', Choudhary emphasised the CJI had made the "cockroach" remark in the specific context of fake advocates, as he expressed "concerns regarding misuse of court process, deterioration of professional standards and how it impacted the institution itself".He said post-May 15, there has been a quantum increase in clips of selectively edited judicial proceedings. The distorted versions and oral observations made during court proceedings are turned into memes and are circulated in social media for profit, said Chaudhary.He complained there is no mechanism against these sinister designs aimed at diminishing public faith in the institution and judges by showing them in poor light.

headline: Lawyers belonging to the Kerala High Court Advocates’ Association have declined a suggestion of the High Court to let the Kerala Chief Justice hoist the national flag on the court premises on Independence Day.
full_text:
Lawyers belonging to the Kerala High Court Advocates’ Association have declined a suggestion of the High Court to let the Kerala Chief Justice hoist the national flag on the court premises on Independence Day.
The association has resolved to continue with, what it termed as, the three-decade-old practice of its president hoisting the national flag on August 15 at the portico of the court complex. The honour of hoisting the tricolour on Republic Day will continue with the Chief Justice.
Govt. orders
The High Court had initiated an informal conversation with the association representatives regarding the proposed change of practice a few weeks ago. The court had also cited government orders regarding the observance of Independence Day, which stipulated that the heads of departments shall hoist the national flag at the respective institutions. The Chief Justice of the Kerala High Court, being the head of the institution, was entitled to hoist the flag on Independence Day, argued the High Court sources.
However, the suggestion did not find favour with the members of the association. The general body meeting of the association held on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) was not convinced of the need to change the custom. The meeting resolved to continue with the decades-old practice of its president hoisting the flag. The decision of the association was duly conveyed to the Registry of the court, sources said.
Mutual respect
While all the judges of the High Court would attend the ceremony on August 15, organised by the association, the lawyers also reciprocate the gesture by attending the function of January 26 in good numbers. It is a case of mutual respect between the Bar and the Bench, which shall continue uninterrupted, according to lawyers.
With the lawyers’ forum refusing to entertain the request of the High Court, the annual celebration will continue without change. However, a full court of the Kerala High Court may deliberate on the issue later, sources indicated.

The family alleged that the DMO had been informed about her condition, but the official failed to give it due consideration and deliberately proceeded with the transfer. The relatives and the NGO union are planning to submit a complaint to the Health Minister seeking an inquiry into the circumstances leading to her death and action against those responsible.
Deepa Lekha had sustained a leg injury in a scooter accident a few months ago and had undergone treatment for nearly three months. She had difficulty walking and had only recently returned to duty after leave.
According to her relatives and colleagues, her health condition had been brought to the DMO’s attention. She was included in the draft transfer list prepared after the change in government and was initially proposed for transfer to the Mattannur health centre. She had reportedly sought permission to continue at Chokli, citing her health issues, but was instead transferred to Pinarayi. Her colleagues said she had been under mental stress over the transfer and alleged that the transfer-related stress contributed to her death.

headline: Residents of 18 villages surrounding the Girivalam path near Arunachaleswarar temple protested against the merger with Tiruvannamalai Corporation at the Office of Collectorate in town on Tuesday.
full_text:
Residents of 18 villages surrounding the Girivalam path near Arunachaleswarar temple protested against the merger with Tiruvannamalai Corporation at the Office of Collectorate in town on Tuesday.
Agitated residents said that the merger deprived residents in these affected villages, especially women, of getting work under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) scheme for the past several months.
Each affected village, on an average, has nine wards with around 5,000 residents. “The merger of villages with the Corporation has also increased taxes on basic amenities like water supply, garbage removal, and houses. Despite the increase in taxes, civic amenities in affected villages around the town have not improved,” Arul Arumugam, a social activist and organiser, said.
Some of the affected villages include Adi Annamalai, Endal, Nochimalai, Devanandal, Navalanpalayam, Chinnakangiyanur, Vegaikaal, Adaiyur, Savalpoondi, and Athiyandal around Girivalam path.
Of the total 14 km of the Girivalam path, six kilometres come under the limits of the Adi Annamalai panchayat that takes care of the daily maintenance of the path, while the remaining areas belong to Tiruvannamalai Corporation.
Despite their closeness to the temple town, affected villages depend on agriculture and related activities. Most of the residents are farmers and petty traders. They were also employed as workers under the MGNREGA scheme to dig ponds and water channels.
As the villages were located near reserve forests (RFs), women workers were roped in to create water facilities inside the forest for animals in the wild. Residents said that despite the merger of the villages with the Corporation in January, basic facilities like water supply, bitumen roads, streetlights, daily garbage removal, and health care have not been on par with core areas in Tiruvannamalai town.
Agitated residents gave petitions to revenue officials at Collectorate and dispersed peacefully after assurance from officials that necessary steps will be taken. Corporation officials said that around 20 surrounding villages were merged with the civic body to upgrade itself into a corporation from the erstwhile municipality status. It could help the corporation seek additional funds from international banks to undertake various civic and infrastructure works within its limits.

headline: The Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights and Sreenarayanaguru Open University (SGOU), Kollam, are together set to launch certificate and diploma courses on child rights and laws related to them.

The Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights and Sreenarayanaguru Open University (SGOU), Kollam, are together set to launch certificate and diploma courses on child rights and laws related to them.
A memorandum of understanding (MoU) was signed in this regard by commission chairperson K.V. Manoj Kumar and SGOU Vice Chancellor Jagathy Raj V.P. in the Vice Chancellor’s chamber on Tuesday.
Later, addressing a press meet in the State capital, Mr. Manoj Kumar said a curriculum was proposed against the backdrop of a rise in crimes against children and feedback of inadequate awareness of child rights that was received by the commission during its programmes.
Following talks with SGOU, a decision was taken to launch two courses – Certificate in Child Rights and Advocacy and Diploma in Child Rights and Protection Studies. The certificate course will be of six months’ duration and the diploma of one year comprising two semesters. The minimum qualification for the certificate course is SSLC (class X) and that for the diploma is Plus Two. These are credit-based courses which enable transfer of credits as per the National Education Policy. Learning material will be made available in Malayalam and English and learners can appear for the examinations in the two languages.
The courses, perhaps the first such in the country, would focus on child rights and related laws, those related child labour and child marriage, child protection, child pyschology, skill development, nutrition, Mr. Manoj Kumar and Prof. Jagathy Raj said.
The curriculum for the courses was ready. It would include theory and practical and would benefit anganwadi workers, teachers, school counsellors, juvenile home staff, lawyers, and social activists. The courses were designed to bring about a positive change in society, Prof. Raj said. Awareness programmes, training, and workshops would be held in the future, he added.

headline: Kaziranga eco-sensitive zone to be cut from 10km to 1km as per SC guidelines: Assam CM
full_text:
Kaziranga eco-sensitive zone to be cut from 10km to 1km as per SC guidelines: Assam CM
Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said the Kaziranga ESZ would be reduced from 10km to 1km in line with Supreme Court guidelines.
Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Wednesday said the state government’s move to reduce the eco-sensitive zone (ESZ) around Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve (KNPTR) from 10 km to 1 km would follow Supreme Court guidelines.
On August 8, the CM had commented that the ESZ around the UNESCO World Heritage Site, which is the largest habitat of the endangered one-horned rhinos, was 10 km ‘by default’ and the Assam government would send a proposal to the Centre within two months to reduce the limit to 1 km. He stated that it was needed for development activities in the area, including constructing a stadium.
“The SC itself had stated that the ESZ would be of 1 km. But till the state government’s doesn’t notify the ESZ, the limit of that zone would be 10 km. Once the state notifies the ESZ properly, it will come down to 1 km, which is what the apex court had specified,” Sarma said.
“If we have to maintain that 10 km limit around KNPTR than towns like Kaliabar, Doboka, Jakhalabandha, Bokakhat would not remain. The SC guidelines specifies that the ESZ should be 1 km, but it can extend to 3 km depending on circumstances. There’s no wildlife sanctuary in the world which has an ESZ of 10 km surrounding it,” he added.
In June 2022, the SC had ordered that ESZs of a minimum of 1 km should be declared around protected forests, national parks and wildlife sanctuaries.
But in April 2023, following submissions from states and the Centre that such a uniform practice was not feasible, the SC modified its order, stating that a stringent observance of its earlier order was not feasible as it could lead to more man-animal conflict and hamper the day-to-day activities of citizens. It, however, stipulated that no mining activity would be allowed within the 1 km boundary of the protected areas.
The Assam government’s proposal to reduce the ESZ has evoked negative reactions from wildlife activists and conservationists in the state.
“Kaziranga is not just Assam’s pride, but its a world heritage site. The proposal, if implemented would have a drastic effect on wildlife in the national park,” said Jadav Payeng, wildlife conservationist.
“During the annual floods, animals like rhinos, deer, elephants from Kaziranga leave the park and head to higher altitudes nearby for safety. If the ESZ is reduced, they won’t be able to move freely and get trapped. What’s the need to reduce the ESZ for construction activities near the national park?” questioned the Padma Sri awardee known as the Forest Man of India.
“Supreme Court in its earlier judgement has made it very clear that if a national park doesn’t declare ESZ, then the apex court will assume ESZ is up to 10 km from park boundary. Further the apex court in its June 2022 judgement held that every national park and wildlife sanctuary must have a mandatory ESZ of atleast 1 KM from demarcated boundary,” said Bibhab Talukdar, secretary general of Aaranyak, a wildlife conservation organisation.
“What is important is the spirit of the ESZ for proper implementation, whether is 10 km from the park boundary of whether even one km from the park boundary for long term conservation future of Kaziranga or in that matters all other national parks and wildlife sanctuaries. At the same time there has to be a balance between conservation and livelihood needs of local people living around such protected areas,” he added.

J'khand: Raghubar Das threatens hunger strike if CBI probe into exam irregularities not recommended
The BJP leader accused JMM-led government of playing with the fate of lakhs of students in the state.
Former Jharkhand chief minister Raghubar Das on Wednesday threatened to sit on a hunger strike if the JMM-led dispensation failed to recommend a CBI probe into alleged recruitment examination irregularities in the state within a week.
Thousands of students in Jharkhand have been agitating over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in the state for the past 19 days under the banner of the 'JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch'.
"If the state government fails to recommend a CBI probe into recruitment examination irregularities within a week, I will be forced to sit on a hunger strike here," Das, who was also the governor of Odisha, said while addressing agitating students at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium.

The BJP leader accused JMM-led government of playing with the fate of lakhs of students in the state.
"If the government is clean and has no involvement, it should recommend CBI probe into the irregularities. Otherwise, people of Jharkhand will consider there is involvement of top politicians and bureaucrats in the irregularities," he said.
Das alleged that massive recruitment scams took place in the last six years under the JMM-led regime.
He also demanded ₹1 crore compensation each for the next of kin of 19 people who died during physical tests for excise constable recruitment in 2024.
Over 15 aspirants lost their lives while undertaking physical tests during the drive in 2024.
The BJP has been attacking Hemant Soren's government over the deaths, alleging they were victims of the administration's mismanagement and negligence.
He alleged that the Ranchi district administration attempted to forcibly remove students from the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where they have been demonstrating against "irregularities" in recruitment examinations.
"I caution administrative officers that power comes and goes but you should be worried about your careers. Your careers are tied to the Government of India and Ministry of Home Affairs and you draw your salaries from taxpayers' money in Jharkhand.
"I strongly condemn the pressure tactics employed yesterday by these officials, which aimed at breaking students' morale and forcing them to call off the protest," he said.

headline: What is N Chandrasekaran's net worth? Report shows he got ₹671.4 crore in 5 years

What is N Chandrasekaran's net worth? Report shows he got ₹671.4 crore in 5 years
While his exact personal net worth is not publicly disclosed, his Tata Sons remuneration has run into hundreds of crores.
N Chandrasekaran’s decision to step down as Tata Sons chairman has put the spotlight on the wealth and earnings of one of India’s most highly paid corporate leaders.
While his exact personal net worth is not publicly disclosed, his Tata Sons remuneration has run into hundreds of crores.
N Chandrasekaran’s salary: ₹158.66 crore in FY26
According to the Tata Sons FY26 annual report, Chandrasekaran received a total remuneration of ₹158.66 crore for the financial year ending March 31, 2026, compared to ₹155.81 crore in FY25.
ALSO READ | Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran steps down, says will complete term; firm's stocks tumble
This was his highest remuneration since Tata Sons began disclosing executive compensation in FY22, the annual report said.
His FY26 remuneration included ₹17.97 crore in salary and other benefits and ₹140.69 crore as profit-linked commission.
The commission, therefore, accounted for the overwhelming majority of his annual remuneration, with the ₹140.69 crore profit-linked component making up about 89% of his total FY26 pay, based on the figures disclosed in the annual report.
₹671.4 crore earned over five years
Tata Sons’ disclosed executive remuneration figures show that Chandrasekaran earned a cumulative ₹671.4 crore from FY22 to FY26, according to a Business Standard report based on the company’s annual report.
That figure represents remuneration paid by Tata Sons, not his total personal wealth or net worth.
His net worth would also depend on his assets, investments, properties and liabilities, details of which are not available in a public wealth statement.
From TCS to the Tata Sons boardroom
Chandrasekaran joined Tata Consultancy Services in 1987 and went on to become its chief executive officer and managing director in 2009, as per Tata’s official biography and company records.
The Tata Sons board appointed him executive chairman in January 2017, with his tenure beginning on February 21, 2017. Tata said at the time that he had demonstrated leadership as TCS chief executive and managing director.
He was later reappointed for a second term, and he has now decided not to seek another extension. This decision followed a prolonged disagreement involving Tata Trusts and a lack of unanimous board support for his reappointment.
Chandrasekaran’s departure will now make way for Tata Sons to select a new chairman after nearly a decade under his leadership. Reuters reported that the group’s succession process is being closely watched as Tata Trusts, which owns about 66% of Tata Sons, remains a major part of the company’s governance structure.

headline: 'In absence of unanimous support...': N Chandrasekaran steps down as Tata Sons Chairman. Full resignation statement
full_text:
'In absence of unanimous support...': N Chandrasekaran steps down as Tata Sons Chairman. Full resignation statement
N Chandrasekaran in his resignation statement said that Tata Trust's recommendation to extend his tenure was vetoed by one of the board members.
Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran has stepped down from his post and will not be seeking an extension of his tenure beyond February 2027. Chandrasekaran announced the move on Wednesday as he cited lack of board approval for his reappointment. This comes amid tensions with the charity arm that controls the salt-to-aviation Tata Group
In a statement detailing the move, Chandrasekaran said the Tata trust had unanimously recommended the extension of his tenure for another five years after his term was due to end in February 2027. However, ‘in absence of unanimous support’, Chandrasekaran said he was deferring the decision.
Chandrasekaran said that after Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust had recommended the extension of his tenure, the proposal was vetoed by one of the board members, stalling his extension.
“The resolution was tabled in the Tata Sons Board on Feb 24, 2026. However, the proposal was not carried through because one of the Board Members did not support it, and in the absence of unanimous support, I chose to defer the decision,” he wrote.
Here is the full text of Chandrasekaran's statement after he announced his resignation:
"My current tenure as the Chairman of Tata Sons comes to an end on Feb 20, 2027. Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust had unanimously resolved and recommended the extension of my next term for a period of five years, which was recorded and recommended by the Tata Sons Nomination and Remuneration Committee and the Board. Subsequently, the resolution was tabled in the Tata Sons Board on Feb 24, 2026. However, the proposal was not carried through because one of the Board Members did not support it, and in the absence of unanimous support, I chose to defer the decision.
It has been 6 months since that Board meeting, and no resolution has been reached till date. Tata Sons is a very large institution and there are many strategic projects that are under critical stages of execution. It is not only necessary to have a leader in place to lead the Group beyond Feb 2027, but also clarity on leadership is important for employees, investors, partners and other stakeholders.
Under these circumstances, earlier today, I have communicated to the Tata Sons Board, that I have decided not to offer myself for reappointment when my term ends on Feb 20, 2027. I have asked the Board to decide on the succession soon to ensure a proper transition.
I am grateful for the support of all stakeholders.
With warm regards,
Chandra"
Disagreements between Chandrasekaran and Tata Trusts
Tata Sons encompasses over 30 companies, including Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Tata Motors and Air India, but is in turn 66% owned by Tata Trusts, the group's charitable arm.
Disagreements have been brewing between Chandrasekaran and Tata Trusts over the past few months, with the two sides clashing over board representation, strategy, losses at group company Air India and how to handle the planned exit of a minority shareholder, Reuters reported.
In February, Tata Sons postponed a decision on reappointing Chandrasekaran as chairman after Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts, opposed the move.
Tata has also been entangled in several controversies over the past one year after the fatal Air India crash in Ahmedabad, pricing pressure at TCS and a cyberattack at Jaguar Land Rover that disrupted production and weighed on Britain's economic output.

headline: Cara Tejpal rejects survivor's 'father figure' claim in Tarun Tejpal rape case
full_text:
Cara Tejpal rejects survivor's 'father figure' claim in Tarun Tejpal rape case
Cara Tejpal has rejected claims that the complainant was a family friend who saw her father as a father figure. Her statement comes after the Goa High Court convicted Tarun Tejpal, reviving scrutiny of the case narrative.
Tarun Tejpal's daughter Cara has rejected as "an absolute untruth" the "narrative" that the complainant in the rape case against her father was a childhood friend of hers and her sister, and that she therefore regarded Tejpal as a "father figure".
In a statement on Wednesday, Cara said the claim was false and said the issue had already been examined during the trial before the Sessions Court in Mapusa.
Her statement came after the Goa bench of the Bombay High Court last week set aside Tejpal's acquittal, convicted him and sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment.
"Yes, it is true that my father and the complainant's father briefly worked in the same office in the 90s. What is untrue is that they were close comrades or that we were family friends to any degree," she said.
Cara said she had not even known of the "complainant's existence" until she was an adult, and claimed that the complainant was older than both her and her elder sister. She also said the "father figure" characterisation had been tested during the trial before the Sessions Court at Mapusa.
Tejpal, the former editor-in-chief of Tehelka magazine, was arrested by Goa Police in November 2013 after the complainant, then a junior journalist, accused him of sexually assaulting her inside a lift at a luxury hotel in Goa during the magazine's annual ThinkFest event.
A sessions court in 2021 acquitted him of all charges, saying the prosecution had failed to establish the charges beyond reasonable doubt.
The state government challenged that ruling in the High Court, which last week overturned the acquittal, convicted Tejpal and sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment.
Tejpal has said he will challenge the High Court verdict in the Supreme Court and has maintained that the order was erroneous.
The case has returned to focus after the High Court's ruling, with Cara disputing the claim that the complainant was a family friend who saw her father as a father figure, while Tejpal has said he will challenge his conviction in the Supreme Court.

headline: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday directed the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to grant a hearing to pharmaceutical companies before taking action against their products, observing that the regulator was using “a sword to kill a mosquit...
full_text:
The Bombay High Court on Tuesday directed the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to grant a hearing to pharmaceutical companies before taking action against their products, observing that the regulator was using “a sword to kill a mosquito”.
A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad made the observation while hearing a plea filed by Cadila Pharmaceuticals Limited challenging the FDA’s decision to bar the sale and distribution of some of its medicines and seize stock worth ₹2.45 crore across the State over branding similarities.
It accepted the statement of government pleader Neha Bhide that the FDA would revoke its orders against the petitioner, issue show-cause notices, and grant a hearing before passing a reasoned order.
Warns of imposing costs
The Bench, while warning of imposing costs on the FDA, said it was coming across several cases of such action by the regulator in the State.
“You have the power to use a sword, but the problem is you are using it to kill a mosquito. Power has to be exercised with restraint. It has to be used properly. Even in cases of hotels and restaurants, you shoot first and then ask questions,” the Bench said.
The government pleader told the court that there was confusion between the said medicines and the decision was taken as a preventive measure. “It was a preventive measure and not high-handed action,” she said.
After Bhide submitted that the FDA would revoke its orders against the petitioner and grant a hearing, the High Court accepted the statement and disposed of the petition.

headline: No response yet on invite to Brics Summit for Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman
full_text:
No response yet on invite to Brics Summit for Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has been invited to the Brics Summit in New Delhi in his capacity as the chair of the Bimstec grouping
The Bangladesh government is yet to convey its formal acceptance of India’s invitation to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to attend the Brics Summit next month amid a recent downturn in bilateral relations, people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.
Rahman was invited to the Brics Summit to be held in New Delhi during September 12-13 in his capacity as the current chair of the Bimstec grouping. India’s envoy Dinesh Trivedi is understood to have reiterated the invitation at a meeting with Rahman in Dhaka on August 10.
With barely a month to go for the Brics Summit, the Bangladesh side is yet to inform India about its acceptance of the invitation, the people familiar with preparations for the event said on condition of anonymity.
Besides Rahman, India has invited the leaders of Bahrain, the chair of the Gulf Cooperation Council; Burundi, the chair of the African Union; the Philippines, the chair of Asean; and Uruguay, the chair of the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States (CELAC), for the outreach session of the Brics Summit.
Similarly, the people said, there has been no word from Dhaka so far on the Indian government’s invitation to Rahman for a bilateral visit. That invitation was extended through a letter sent by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Rahman at the time of his swearing-in in February.
A day ahead of the meeting between Trivedi and Rahman, Bangladesh’s Prothom Alo newspaper had reported, citing its sources, that it was “almost certain” the Bangladesh Prime Minister would not attend the Brics Summit because of “fresh tensions” in bilateral ties after former premier Sheikh Hasina addressed a virtual news conference from New Delhi on August 5.
At the meeting between Rahman and Trivedi, the Bangladesh side urged India to expedite the extradition of Hasina, who has lived in India since she fled Dhaka in August 2024. The Indian side responded by saying that the extradition request, which was made in late 2024, is being examined in line with established processes.
The people said the Brics Summit may not be the ideal venue for a bilateral meeting between the Prime Ministers of the two countries, especially since a lot of hopes are riding on such a meeting to reset the bilateral relationship. “There will be bilateral meetings with all the leaders of Brics member states and the leaders of other countries, and there may not be time for a substantive meeting,” one of the people said.
“A bilateral visit from the Bangladesh side may be a better opportunity for the two leaders to have more substantial discussions on all the important issues between India and Bangladesh,” the person said.
Besides Hasina’s presence in India, which is currently the main irritant in bilateral ties, Dhaka has raised issues such as the alleged killing of Bangladeshi nationals in firing by India’s border security forces and the so-called “pushback” of undocumented migrants from the states of Assam and West Bengal. The two sides are also yet to begin the substantive work for renewing the Ganga Waters Treaty, which is set to expire at the end of the year.

headline: Public capital must act as catalyst, not substitute for pvt investment: Sitharaman
full_text:
Public capital must act as catalyst, not substitute for pvt investment: Sitharaman
Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said public capital must act as a catalyst for private investment, citing VGF, HAM, InvITs, NIP and PM Gati Shakti.
The government believes that public capital must act as a catalyst, not a substitute for private investment, Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Wednesday.
She said policy measures have been taken to support this principle, citing examples such as viability gap funding (VGF), the hybrid annuity model (HAM), infrastructure investment trusts (InvITs), the National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) and PM Gati Shakti.
VGF supports financially constrained but socially desirable projects, HAM ensures balanced risk-sharing in road infrastructure, and credit enhancement mechanisms help improve project bankability, she said while delivering the keynote address at a seminar on ‘The Role of the New Development Bank in Mobilising Private Capital in Member Countries’ on the sidelines of the BRICS Finance Ministers’ and Central Bank Governors’ (FMCBG) meeting in Jaipur.
Also Read: No transaction charge on UPI for users, small merchants: Nirmala Sitharaman
She said InvITs help recycle capital and attract long-term institutional investors, while NIP provides long-term visibility to investors. PM Gati Shakti — the National Master Plan for Multimodal Connectivity — is improving coordination and efficiency, she added.
Building on this foundation, the Union Budget 2026-27 introduced several targeted measures to facilitate private sector investment, such as new dedicated freight corridors, new high-speed rail corridors, new national waterways and a coastal cargo promotion scheme, she said.
Also Read: Sitharaman introduces tax amendment Bill to attract global capital, strengthen manufacturing
While BRICS economies represent major growth engines of the global economy, they also face common structural constraints in mobilising private capital at scale, she said. The challenge is not merely the availability of capital, but the creation of confidence, stability, predictability and credible long-term frameworks, which are essential to unlock sustained private participation across member countries, she added.
Sitharaman also delivered the inaugural address at the 1st BRICS Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors’ (FMCBG) meeting under India’s BRICS 2026 chairship in Jaipur on Wednesday. Emphasising the importance of collective action and practical cooperation, she highlighted India’s BRICS 2026 chairship theme, “Building Resilience and Innovation for Cooperation and Sustainability”.
She underscored the need for BRICS members to work together towards resilient, inclusive and sustainable growth, while translating cooperation into practical outcomes across the finance track.

headline: New Delhi: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi has questioned the government over the situation along the Line of Actual Control with China in Arunachal Pradesh, alleging that Chinese forces had entered Indian territory, blocked Indian patrols and pitched t...
full_text:
New Delhi: AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi has questioned the government over the situation along the Line of Actual Control with China in Arunachal Pradesh, alleging that Chinese forces had entered Indian territory, blocked Indian patrols and pitched tents.
“The Narendra Modi government needs to come clear on what is happening on the border in Arunachal Pradesh. The information it has provided so far is inadequate and meant to obfuscate. If Chinese forces have entered our territory, blocked our patrols from going to areas they always went to, and pitched tents, our people need to be told the truth. The current situation is unacceptable,” Owaisi said in a post on X.
Owaisi also invoked the earlier border standoffs in Doklam and Ladakh.
“We have seen what happened in Doklam and Ladakh earlier and do not want a repeat now. PM Modi said that no one had entered our territory in Ladakh but our soldiers can’t still patrol so many areas there. In Doklam, the Chinese have built a permanent base and alternative roads. When will the Narendra Modi government learn?” he said.
He further questioned the government’s China policy in the backdrop of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to New Delhi for the upcoming BRICS Summit.
“While all this is happening on the border, we are inviting Chinese President Xi Jinping to New Delhi next month. Is this our policy on how to deal with Chinese troops pitching tents on our territory and blocking our patrols? Or have we accepted all the terms that Beijing has placed before us for ‘normalcy’ in bilateral ties?” Owaisi added on X.
Owaisi’s remarks come amid a reported face-off between Indian and Chinese patrol parties in late July in Taksing, a remote border village in Arunachal Pradesh’s Upper Subansiri district.
ThePrint earlier reported that Indian and Chinese patrol parties came face-to-face in the area, about 2.5 km inside the Line of Actual Control. The usual banner protocol, under which both sides claim they are in their area, was carried out and the Chinese patrol subsequently pulled back.
However, the Chinese returned in early August and set up two-three tents in the area, ThePrint reported. Sources in the defence and security establishment told ThePrint that the “situation was well under control”. The Army is yet to respond to queries on the reported tents.
The Ministry of External Affairs, meanwhile, said Tuesday that the state of affairs along the India-China border would have a bearing on broader bilateral ties.
Responding to a question on the military situation and whether the standoff had been taken up diplomatically, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India had “always emphasised” in discussions with China that border issues were “most serious” and that maintaining peace and tranquility in these areas was “of the utmost importance”.
“We have also stated that the state of border affairs will reflect on the state of our larger bilateral ties,” Jaiswal said.
Jaiswal said this was also reiterated at the 36th Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs meeting held on 6 August.
The two sides, he said, engaged in “frank discussions” and reviewed the situation along the Line of Actual Control.
The Indian side again maintained that peace and tranquility in the border areas was essential for the overall development of bilateral relations.
“It was agreed to continue to use existing mechanisms, diplomatic and military channels including the WMCC local commander level meetings and other agreed mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC,” Jaiswal said.
(Edited by Viny Mishra)

headline: Senior Maoist leader carrying ₹20 lakh bounty surrenders before Telangana DGP, recieves reward
full_text:
Senior Maoist leader carrying ₹20 lakh bounty surrenders before Telangana DGP, recieves reward
A former senior Maoist, Kakarala Samatha, surrendered to Telangana police after a lengthy career in the CPI (Maoist).
A 60-year-old senior Communist Party of India (Maoist) member who served in the Andhra Pradesh state committee of the banned outfit surrendered to Telangana director general of police (DGP) CV Anand late on Monday, said police.
The former Maoist leader was identified as Kakarala Samatha, wife of senior Maoist leader and CC member Patel Sudhakar Reddy alias Suryam, who led the party’s Central Military Commission before police shot him dead on May 24, 2009. Samatha carried a reward of ₹20 lakh on her head and the DGP said the amount would be handed over to her. “As an immediate relief, she has been given ₹25,000. She will also get other financial benefits as per the norms,” Anand said.
Samatha and her elder sister Kakarala Sunitha were both active in the movement. Sunitha served as a member of the Dandakaranya Special Zonal Committee and gave up arms on August 21, 2025. Their father is Telugu film industry veteran Kakarala Satyanaraya, whose filmography spans over 300 films. The family hailed from Rajamahendravaram in Andhra Pradesh.

Samatha served in Ganapathy’s core team from 2009 to 2015
Samatha’s career as a Maoist began in 1984 when she joined the Radical Students Union (RSU), a student wing of the CPI (ML) People’s War and subsequently became a full-time member of the party. Between 2009 and 2015, she served in the core team of then- party general secretary Muppala Lakshmana Rao alias Ganapathy.
She later moved to the party’s Southern Regional Bureau and was entrusted with the responsibility of women’s issues and intelligence propaganda in the urban areas. “With the Maoist movement getting wiped out completely, she decided to surrender before the police,” the DGP said.

Telangana DGP says only three Maoist leaders remain underground
The DGP said at present, only three Maoist leaders from Telangana were still underground— Ganapathy, Jade Ratna Bai alias Sujatha and Vartha Sekhar alias Mangthu.
“We appeal to them to surrender to the police at the earliest and join the mainstream,” added the senior police officer.

headline: Assam-Arunachal resolved most issues, disputes only in 52 villages: Himanta
full_text:
Assam-Arunachal resolved most issues, disputes only in 52 villages: Himanta
Arunachal Pradesh CM Pema Khandu said that he attended a meeting with several organisations to solve the matter
Assam and Arunachal Pradesh have resolved most boundary issues, with only 52 areas across five zones are remaining, said Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, adding that the two neighbours must not indulge in conflicts.
Sarma on Wednesday wrote on X, “Assam and Arunachal Pradesh have resolved most boundary issues, with only 52 areas remaining, for which Regional Committees have been reconstituted.”
Responding to Monday’s firing incident along the inter-state border where 11 people from Assam were injured, Sarma said, “We should not fight or indulge in conflict because ultimately we have to stay together.” He added, “This was an unfortunate incident. I appeal Arunachal CM, you must order an enquiry, find the culprits and punish them.”
The incident happened in Mingmang Badati area under the Gogamukh Revenue Circle of Dhemaji district along the inter-state border. Police said those injured were taken to a local hospital and later shifted to the Assam Medical College and Hospital (AMCH) in Dibrugarh.
According to locals in the area, the clash started following a dispute over alleged encroachment by people from Arunachal Pradesh on land in Assam.
Himanta said that he believed this was a local land dispute issue and not a matter between the two states. He also asked the director general of police (DGP) and other senior officials to intervene and investigate.
“I have instructed the DGP, chief secretary and other officials to look into it and they’ll also talk to their counterparts in Arunachal Pradesh. But I think we are in a peaceful situation,” he said on Monday.
Police also said on Monday that they were investigating the matter and deployed force to prevent the situation from escalating.
Arunachal Pradesh CM Pema Khandu said that he attended a meeting with several organisations to solve the matter.
In a post on X, Khandu said, “Held discussions on the situation arising from the recent incident at Hime village, near the Assam border, with AAPSU and representatives of the Galo Welfare Society, Galo Students Union and Dolok Bango Welfare Society.”
“The priority is to facilitate dialogue, and restore normalcy at the earliest. All concerned stakeholders are being engaged to maintain peace, and uphold mutual trust,” Khandu added.
The two states share over 800km of border, parts of which are disputed and the source of localised clashes, triggered by allegations and counter-allegations over land encroachment.
The two states signed the Namsai Declaration on July 15, 2022, in Arunachal Pradesh to resolve the issues. Under the pact, both states agreed in principle to restrict the number of contested border villages from 123 down to 86, paving the way for structured regional committee talks to demarcate the boundary.
The state government reconstituted Regional Committees during a cabinet meeting in Guwahati on Tuesday to strengthen the efforts.

headline: Food safety officials find expired ingredients at Arogya Soudha canteen, ‘problems with products’ at Zomato warehous
full_text:
Food safety officials find expired ingredients at Arogya Soudha canteen, ‘problems with products’ at Zomato warehous
Expired food was found at Arogya Soudha canteen on Magadi Road, where food storage practices did not comply with FSSAI requirements.
Food safety and drug administration officials found expired ingredients and unhygienic conditions at the canteen of the Karnataka health department headquarters, while inspections at Zomato’s Hyperpure facility in Bengaluru uncovered licensing, labelling and storage violations.
Officials found expired idli rava and coconut powder at the Arogya Soudha canteen on Magadi Road, where food storage practices did not comply with Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) requirements and pest control had not been carried out, according to inspection findings.
The department’s inspection of the Hyperpure by Zomato warehouse at Sakalawara Nagar on Tuesday found problems with several products, although the premises itself was described as clean.
Deep Dive
Also Read: Luxury hotels, eateries raided in city over food safety issues
Officials found 146 kg of chicken without the manufacturer’s FSSAI licence number and 40 kg of garlic for which the manufacturer’s FSSAI licence was not in force. They also recorded mislabelling involving 300 kg of rice, 20 kg of dry fruits and 15 kg of masala.
Another 10 kg of imported radish pickle was not stored in a refrigerated area as required by the labelling conditions, according to the department’s findings.
The inspection team collected 40 samples from the warehouse, comprising five legal samples and 35 survey samples. The Food Safety and Drug Administration subsequently issued a notice to the Zomato Hyperpure unit and said further legal action would follow under the prescribed provisions.
HT contacted Zomato for its response to the findings, but the company did not respond at the time of publication.
The Hyperpure inspection brought the department’s checks to another major point in the food supply chain. The warehouse was described by the department as a major supplier to hotels, and officials examined products there for compliance involving licences, labelling, refrigeration and food handling.
The Hyperpure inspection was carried out under the guidance of health and family welfare minister U.T. Khader. According to the department, the exercise was intended to examine food quality, safety, storage, labelling and handling practices under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and its rules.
The action at the two facilities followed a week of food safety inspections across Bengaluru that began with raids on restaurants and hotel kitchens.
At Skyye Lounge in UB City, officials found 45 kg of rotten meat, 6 kg of mould-affected vegetable cutlets and 15 litres of used cooking oil. The kitchen was shut after the inspection found food that officials considered unfit for consumption.
The department also inspected Royal Chain Hotel, Madras Kitchen, Tescon Hotel and Sanchez. Food products were seized or discarded at those establishments. Across Skyye and the four other establishments, the Food Safety and Drug Administration said 132 kg of food articles and 15 litres of used cooking oil were seized or discarded.
The enforcement drive then moved beyond restaurants and hotel kitchens to facilities involved in storing and supplying food. Officials inspected a Zepto warehouse in Hoskote before turning to other food-handling establishments.

headline: A third of skilling scheme trainees remain unplaced
full_text:
A third of skilling scheme trainees remain unplaced
The panel also questioned the performance of the RSETIs, under which only 4.5 million of 6.2 million trained beneficiaries had been “settled” in self-employment.
Since the Union government launched its flagship rural skilling programme in 2014, more than 1.8 million rural youth have been trained under it, but nearly one in three did not secure a reported placement, according to a parliamentary standing committee report tabled on Tuesday.
The Standing Committee on Rural Development and Panchayati Raj, headed by Congress MP Saptagiri Sankar Ulaka, questioned the Ministry of Rural Development on why only 1.2 million of the 1.8 million candidates trained under the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) had been placed in employment.
The panel also questioned the performance of the Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs), under which only 4.5 million of 6.2 million trained beneficiaries had been “settled” in self-employment.
Launched in September 2014, DDU-GKY aims to move rural youth aged 15 to 35 from poor households into regular wage employment through industry-linked training.
The ministry told the committee that the overall placement rate of about 65% varied significantly across states and argued that the headline numbers did not capture the full impact of the programme.
“Overall, the country’s current placement ratio of 65% is a fact, but it varies from state to state,” an official told the committee.
The government also attributed part of the apparent decline to changes introduced under DDU-GKY 2.0, which came into effect in April 2025. The revamped scheme doubled the minimum period for a job to qualify as a placement from three months to six months.
The scheme also expanded eligible outcomes to include self-employment and gig work, ended advance payments to training providers and shifted to milestone-based funding.
However, reported placements fell sharply in 2025-26, with the placement rate dropping to 47.7%, from an average of 77.7% over the preceding three financial years. The decline coincided with the rollout of the revamped scheme.
Experts, however, cautioned against assuming that skills training alone determines employment outcomes. “Unemployment may not be because of lack of skills,” said Ajay Gudavarthy, associate professor of political science at the Centre for Political Studies, Jawaharlal Nehru University. “The supply of employment opportunities is independent of the supply of skills.”
States show disparity
The committee data shows significant differences in placement rates. Tamil Nadu recorded a 95.3% placement rate among 80,214 trained candidates, followed by Andhra Pradesh at 82.9%, Odisha at 81.2%, Haryana at 75% and Telangana at 70.7%.
Uttar Pradesh, which trained the largest number of candidates at 2.55 lakh, placed 1.10 lakh, giving it a 43% placement rate. Jharkhand, Punjab, Rajasthan, Kerala and Bihar also recorded rates below the national average.
A conversion gap
Women accounted for 52.5% of all DDU-GKY trainees, well above the scheme’s one-third participation mandate. But their share fell slightly among those placed: 9.65 lakh women were trained, compared with 6.03 lakh placed.
“The data suggests that the scheme has been successful in bringing women into training, but that success is not translating into employment at the same rate,” said Harshil Sharma, a labour economics and public policy expert.

headline: Centre redefines Ganga floodplain, drops 'construction-free zone' provision
full_text:
Centre redefines Ganga floodplain, drops 'construction-free zone' provision
New Delhi, The Centre has redefined the "active floodplain" of the Ganga and its tributaries and introduced regulatory and warning zones based on flood return periods.
The Jal Shakti Ministry, through a notification issued on August 7 and published in the Gazette on August 10, has amended the River Ganga Authorities Order, 2016.
The latest amendment removes the "construction free zone" wording and instead says that the banks of the Ganga and its tributaries and their floodplains shall be maintained to reduce pollution sources and pressures, and preserve their natural groundwater recharge functions through necessary measures.
At the same time, the government has introduced a specific definition of "active floodplain", meaning an area of the Ganga or its tributaries coming under water due to floods corresponding to a one-in-five-year return period.
The amended definition of "flood plain" includes the active floodplain, a regulatory zone covering areas inundated between one-in-five-year and one-in-25-year floods, and a warning zone covering areas inundated between one-in-25-year and one-in-100-year floods.
Under the 2016 order, construction of permanent or temporary structures for residential, commercial, industrial or other purposes was prohibited in the Ganga, its banks, its tributaries and the active floodplain, subject to specified exceptions and permissions.
The 2026 amendment does not amend that provision, but defines the active floodplain as the area corresponding to a one-in-five-year flood.
The notification itself does not specify any construction permission or prohibition for the newly defined regulatory and warning zones.
The amended definition also includes areas of the Ganga or its tributaries that come under water on either side due to floods corresponding to their greatest flow or a flood with a frequency of once in 100 years.
The 2016 order had defined "flood plain" as the area of the Ganga or its tributaries that comes under water on either side due to floods corresponding to its greatest flow or a flood with a frequency of once in 100 years.
The latest amendment also substitutes the provision relating to maintenance of the river banks and floodplains.
It says they shall be maintained to reduce pollution sources and pressures and preserve their natural groundwater recharge functions through necessary measures.
The order, called the River Ganga Authorities Order, 2026, came into force on the date of its publication in the official Gazette.
The principal order was notified on October 7, 2016, and was last amended on May 7, 2026, according to the notification.

headline: "Engagement of SPOs is not of a permanent nature but only to take care of a particular contingency,â the HC noted.
full_text:
"Engagement of SPOs is not of a permanent nature but only to take care of a particular contingency,â the HC noted.
Srinagar: Only God can save this country if a police officer, of whatever rank, gets frightened by terroristsâ threats and refuses duties, J&K high court has said while dismissing a copâs petition for reinstatement.âThe justification provided by the petitioner for not attending his duties is unacceptable, to say the least,â a single bench of Justice Sanjay Dhar said in its Monday order. The judge rejected special police officer (SPO) Hemo Hamid Waniâs argument that he was entitled to the âsame powers, privileges and protections available to ordinary officers of police under Police Actâ. The HC pointed out that âSPOs do not hold any civil posts regulated by statutory rulesâ.Residents of a neighbourhood are appointed SPOs âfor specific purposes when the force ordinarily employed for preserving peace is not sufficientâ. âThus, engagement of SPOs is not of a permanent nature but only to take care of a particular contingency,â the HC noted.Wani was engaged as an SPO in 2012. In 2015, he was posted at Reshipora in south Kashmirâs Shopian. While at home on medical leave at one point then, he received life threats from terrorists and failed to report back to duties.
When he returned after some time to his posting, he was not allowed to join duty, forcing him to take the matter to senior officers.When no action was taken, Wani moved the HC. In Aug last year, the court directed the J&K police DGP to take a decision on Waniâs plea. The DGP turned it down, forcing Wani to move the HC again.In his HC petition, Wani argued that J&K Police had disengaged him without inquiry, formal charges or hearing. The action, he said, violated the Constitutionâs Articles 16 (equality of opportunity in public employment), 21 (right to life and livelihood) and 311 (protection against arbitrary dismissal), besides provisions of J&K Police Rules.
The HC rejected the contentions, saying Wani, as an SPO, was not entitled to any hearing or inquiry in view of the temporary nature of his engagement. Even if it is assumed that Wani had the right to such a hearing, his failure to perform duties in the face of terror threats is enough reason to remove him, the HC held.âGranting an opportunity to the petitioner to present his case prior to disengagement would have been an empty formality. The DGP has rightly rejected the petitionerâs representation. The order does not call for any interference,â Justice Dhar observed.

headline: As part of a campaign against drugs, phrases like ‘Say No To Drugs’ and ‘Stop Drugs’ are being painted on the recently opened rail overbridge (ROB) in Navalpur village by Public Works Department.

As part of a campaign against drugs, phrases like ‘Say No To Drugs’ and ‘Stop Drugs’ are being painted on the recently opened rail overbridge (ROB) in Navalpur village by Public Works Department.
PWD officials said that the drive, which was initiated by District Collector Priya Ravichandran, was part of a ‘Drug-Free Tamil Nadu’ campaign that was launched by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay in Chennai on Tuesday. “Among four to five ROBs in the district, the bridge is the longest facility located in congested Ranipet town. As many schools and other public facilities are located on both sides of the bridge, the idea to use its pillars for the campaign was mooted,” a PWD official told The Hindu.
Jointly built by the National Highways (NH) wing of the State Highways Department and the Southern Railway, the ₹26.65-crore bridge was opened in September 2025. It brought relief to residents as prior to its construction, they had to take a de-tour of eight km to reach Ranipet town from surrounding villages.
Highways officials said that the two-lane bridge is 921-metre-long and 12-metre-wide with at least 15 pillars. Each pillar, on an average, has a height of 10 ft. The awareness campaign against drugs in the pillars is part of the beautification of open space below the bridge and a few parks in the town. Beautification work, that costs around ₹4.5 crore, has been supported by Tata Group under CSR initiative.
“Such innovative awareness campaigns should be done in other public places where crowds gather in large numbers. The idea of converting pillars for such awareness helps prevent its misuse for wall posters,” said R. Sugan, a motorist.
As part of beautification, identified open space below the bridge will be converted into a small children’s play area, seating arrangements, and a walking track. The entire space will be fenced, and visitors will be allowed at specific timings. The entire painting work of the pillars will be done in the coming weeks. Once completed, the space below the bridge will be maintained by the Ranipet municipality.

Calcutta High Court on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) extended the interim protection of Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee till August 31 and said that his custodial interrogation is not required in the 16 cases registered after May 4, the day when the result of the Assembly election was out.
Justice Saugata Bhhattacharyya was hearing a plea by Mr. Banerjee claiming that a spate of politically motivated FIRs was registered against him shortly after the BJP government came to power on May 4.
