headline: India blocks over 3,700 apps, flags 32 lakh mule accounts in cybercrime crackdown
full_text:
India blocks over 3,700 apps, flags 32 lakh mule accounts in cybercrime crackdown
India has expanded its cybercrime crackdown by blocking thousands of apps, SIM cards and devices linked to fraud. The move is paired with faster complaint handling and new tools to freeze and restore stolen funds.
India has blocked 3,718 mobile applications, including fake loan apps, as part of a nationwide crackdown on cybercrime, the Ministry of Home Affairs said in Lok Sabha. The action was taken through the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) in coordination with various government agencies and technology platforms.
Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar said that more than Rs 11,158 crore involved in cyber fraud had been saved through the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS) as of June 30, 2026.
According to the ministry, 32.80 lakh cybercrime complaints had been registered through the system by the same date. The CFCFRMS enables authorities to coordinate with banks, payment gateways and financial institutions to stop or freeze suspicious transactions after a fraud is reported.
The government has also intensified action against mule bank accounts used by cybercriminals to route and conceal stolen money. As many as 32.08 lakh suspected mule accounts have been identified, while transactions worth Rs 25,698 crore have been stopped, the ministry said.
Authorities have further blocked 15.75 lakh mobile SIM cards and 5.77 lakh IMEI numbers linked to suspected cybercrime activities. The measures are aimed at preventing criminals from using fraudulent connections and devices to carry out cyber fraud.
The Ministry of Home Affairs has also introduced a new Standard Operating Procedure for the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP) and CFCFRMS to speed up complaint resolution, improve coordination between agencies and expedite the freezing and restoration of defrauded funds.
Two new modules, the Money Restoration Module and Grievance Redressal Module, were introduced in April 2026. The Money Restoration Module is intended to streamline the process of returning recovered funds to victims, while the Grievance Redressal Module helps monitor complaints where action or resolution has been delayed.
The NCRP allows citizens to report a wide range of cyber offences, including online financial fraud, fake investment schemes, digital arrest scams, sextortion, identity theft, social media crimes, online blackmail and fraud involving fake websites and mobile applications. Citizens can also report financial cyber fraud by calling the 1930 helpline.
The government has simultaneously stepped up cyber awareness campaigns through SMS messages, television and radio advertisements, social media, digital platforms, railway stations, airports, schools and colleges. Awareness campaigns have also been conducted during major sporting events, including the IPL.
The I4C serves as the central coordinating agency for tackling cybercrime, bringing together state governments, law enforcement agencies, banks, financial institutions and technology companies.
With the rapid expansion of digital payments, UPI, internet banking and online services, cybercriminals have increasingly turned to methods such as fake investment schemes, digital arrest scams, OTP fraud, fake KYC updates, fraudulent customer care services and loan app scams.
The latest figures indicate that the government's strategy is focused not only on blocking fraudulent applications but also on disrupting the financial and digital infrastructure used by cybercriminals while improving mechanisms to help victims recover their money.

NEW DELHI: Tribunal Reforms Bill, piloted by govt in Parliament, is seen as a move that reinforces the constitutional position in appointments: ensuring primacy of the judiciary in deciding top positions. At the same time, it seeks to maintain a three-tier architecture between the tribunal, the secretariat and the administrative ministry with clear roles mapped out for each.In the bill â passed by RS Tuesday and LS Monday â govt has sought to ensure the independence of National Tribunals Commission (NTC) that will supervise the appointment, functioning, discipline and administrative needs of tribunals. To be headed by a retired judge of the Supreme Court or chief justice of a high court, the proposed NTC will have two judicial members drawn from among retired HC judges apart from two technical members. The chairperson and judicial members will be appointed by govt in consultation with the CJI.The commission, through its search and selection committee, has been tasked to streamline selection of chairpersons and members of tribunals. Unlike the current system, where a panel of names is sent, the committee will recommend a single name for each vacancy, along with a waiting list. Strict timelines have been proposed for recommending names to govt and for the Centre to approve them.
It addresses a constant complaint that ministries have in appointments getting delayed.Besides, govt has decided to fix the retirement age of chairperson of tribunals at 70 years, with members to retire at 67, unless they complete their five-year terms.The commission will be assisted by a secretariat with the administrative ministry having no role in either advertising for the post or scrutinising the candidates. headline: Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult
full_text:
Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult
The legal availability of marijuana for either medicinal or recreational use in places like Thailand and Amsterdam has made life difficult for airlines flying there. The reason: Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult. The only way to deter their consumption by flight crew members, say officials across multiple airlines, is to increase random dope testing, as there substances usually remain present in the body for much longer than alcohol.The concern across airlines globally to check this stems from the fact that operating a flight âunder the influence of any psychoactive substance might render (licensed personnel like pilots) unable to safely and properly exerciseâ perform their duty, as per the International Civil Aviation Organisation.Possibly the most infamous case of this was a US carrierâs off-duty pilot travelling on the jump seat (extra seat behind pilots) in the flight deck trying to shut down the engines. This off-duty pilot had reportedly taken psychedelic mushrooms two days before the incident and hadnât slept in 48 hours. âThis is a challenge globally. Often the tests are not conclusive if taking some medicine leads to detection of psychoactive substances.
However, recent consumption of drugs does show up in tests,â said officials.DGCA rules on âprocedure for examination of the aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substancesâ says: âIn case the confirmatory test is found positive, the medical in charge of the organisation shall consult a medical review officer to determine if the result was due to a legitimate therapeutic treatment or some other innocuous source (for example pain relief medication containing codeine may trigger a positive result for opiates).
âAirlines try to create awareness and encourage employees to anonymously report addiction so that the same can be addressed. But mostly people avoid reporting the same, so this virtually remains a non-starter, said many officials. Officials running operations across airlines say the focus in India is primarily on self-reporting and de-addiction.âBut given the easy availability of psychoactive substances, we need to make the consequences a bit tougher and act as deterrent. We have to increase random testing, thatâs the only way out,â said an official. Under DGCA rules, all scheduled commercial airlines and air navigation service providers need to test at least 10% of their flight crew members and air traffic controllers every year.

NEW DELHI: A patientâs hospital room in a private hospital could soon cost no more than a room in a nearby three-star hotel if a key recommendation of the parliamentary standing committee on health and family welfare is accepted. In an effort to rein in soaring medical bills, the panel has proposed linking room rents in private hospitals in major metropolitan cities to the average tariff charged by three-star hotels nearby.The recommendation is part of the committeeâs report on the affordability and accessibility of healthcare facilities in public and private sector, which says the absence of a transparent mechanism for fixing room charges has led to wide variations in bills. It recommended benchmarking room rents to nearby three-star hotels, while allowing hospitals to levy separate charges for resident doctors, nursing care, consumables, meals and laundry.
Beyond room rents, the panel, headed by SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav, proposed standardised package rates for common medical and surgical procedures.
Citing the 80th National Sample Survey (Jan-Dec 2025), the panel said average cost of hospitalisation was Rs 6,631 in govt hospitals compared with Rs 50,508 in private hospitals. For childbirth alone, the average out-of-pocket expenditure was Rs 37,630 in private hospitals against Rs 2,299 in govt facilities.
Hospital administrators, however, questioned the comparison. âHotel room tariffs should not be the yardstick for hospital room rents because medical infra, staffing and support services are different,â said Dr Vinoy Kumar Upadhyay, CMD of Hope Hospital in Greater Noida.
Noting the sharp difference in treatment costs, the panel said reducing out-of-pocket expenditure should be a key priority. It called for a legal mechanism to standardise and cap charges for essential treatments and routine procedures in private hospitals, mandatory disclosure of treatment costs before admission, and a fast-track grievance redressal mechanism for complaints related to billing.Beyond room rents, the panel, headed by SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav, proposed standardised package rates for common medical and surgical procedures. It also recommended advance cost estimates for complex treatments, financial navigators to guide patients on treatment costs and insurance, and âContinuum of Careâ packages covering screening, treatment and palliative care under a single capped payment. It urged the Centre to raise public health spending to 2.5% of GDP, strengthen govt hospitals, expand affordable medicines, and ensure stricter implementation of the Clinical Establishments Act.

headline: Nagaland’s NSF asks students to skip I-Day events over Vande Mataram row
full_text:
Nagaland’s NSF asks students to skip I-Day events over Vande Mataram row
NSF has been critical of MHA’s 28 January 2026 communication that laid down a detailed protocol for the observance of the national song at official events
An influential students’ organisation in Nagaland has asked educational institutions not to send students to participate in Independence Day celebrations this weekend, during which the complete version of the national song Vande Mataram will be sung.
According to the Naga Students’ Federation (NSF), the complete version of the national song was not in keeping with the country’s secular principles.
In a statement on Wednesday, NSF said its concern was solely with the compulsory participation of students in Vande Mataram, particularly where its devotional and religious imagery conflicts with the conscience and sincerely held beliefs of students belonging to non-Hindu communities.
“India as a secular democratic republic, its Constitution guarantees freedom of conscience and freedom of religion. No student should therefore be compelled to participate in any religiously sensitive expression contrary to his or her sincerely held beliefs,” the NSF said.
NSF has been critical of the Union home ministry’s 28 January 2026 communication that laid down a detailed protocol for the observance of the national song at official events, including the stipulation that it should be rendered before the national anthem when both are played together.
NSF has cited the constitutional safeguards under Article 371A of the Constitution of India, particularly in relation to the religious and social practices of the Nagas.
“Accordingly, all Federating Units and Sub-ordinate Bodies are notified to enforce this position to concerned schools and institutions within their respective jurisdictions and to ensure that no student is subjected to disciplinary action, discrimination, intimidation or academic consequences for declining to participate in Vande Mataram on grounds of conscience or religious belief,” the directive said.
The NSF is an apex youth body that seeks to safeguard student interests and advocates for Naga solidarity across Nagaland, Manipur, Assam, and Arunachal Pradesh.

Former Delhi chief minister (CM) Arvind Kejriwal and ex-deputy CM Manish Sisodia have moved the Delhi high court seeking dismissal of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI’s) appeal challenging trial court’s order discharging them in the excise policy case.
In their application filed on Wednesday, days before the high court scheduled hearing CBI arguments on August 17, Kejriwal and Sisodia argued that the agency filed the appeal with “unprecedented haste” and in a manner that reflected a lack of seriousness.
They contended that the appeal was filed within four hours of the trial court’s discharge order, which runs into more than 500 pages.
According to the two leaders, the speed with which the CBI preferred the appeal “manifestly shows” that the agency could not have properly appreciated or considered the detailed findings and reasoning contained in the discharge judgment.

“That the entire Revision Petition is sans pointing out any specific finding/paragraphs of the discharge order which according to CBI show the perversity. Hence the present Petition fails the test of a Revision Petition being filed under Section 442 BNSS. The present Petition is nothing but an Appeal which is filed in garb of the Revision Petition,” the application stated.
It further submitted that the CBI’s petition fails to make specific allegations against each accused, including how the discharge order was passed without evidence, what material evidence was allegedly ignored in relation to a particular accused or which specific finding, paragraph in the judgment reflects an arbitrary or perverse exercise of judicial discretion.
“The CBI has also failed to produce any evidence, materials or documents with the present revision petition to show the perversity in the order of discharge. The present petition is incomplete as it is without the material being relied upon and the specific averments in the order of discharge and hence it is liable to be dismissed in the present form,” the application added.

headline: Delaware has proclaimed August 15, 2026, as âIndia Dayâ, joining New York and New Jersey in recognising India's Independence Day and the contributions of the Indian-American community ahead of the country's 80th Independence Day.
full_text:
Delaware has proclaimed August 15, 2026, as âIndia Dayâ, joining New York and New Jersey in recognising India's Independence Day and the contributions of the Indian-American community ahead of the country's 80th Independence Day.
The proclamation was issued by Delaware Governor Matthew Meyer, who highlighted the state's growing Indian-American community and its contributions to the state's social and economic life.
The development was shared by the Consulate General of India in New York on August 13.
According to the proclamation, Delaware is strengthened by the many cultures and traditions represented across its communities, including its Indian-American population.
Delaware honours Indian-American community
The proclamation said Delawareans of Indian heritage have enriched the state through their work, leadership and service, contributing to shared prosperity and creating opportunities for future generations.
It also highlighted India's diversity of languages, traditions, faiths and customs, noting that generations of Indian Americans have carried these traditions forward while building communities in the US.
The proclamation said India Day would provide an opportunity to honour India's independence, celebrate the heritage and achievements of Delaware's Indian-American community and recognise the enduring connections between Delaware and the people of India.
Governor Meyer encouraged residents to participate in the observance and recognise the contributions of the state's Indian-American community.
New York, New Jersey also recognise August 15
Delaware's proclamation follows similar declarations by New York and New Jersey, which recognised August 15, as India's Independence Day.
New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill issued a proclamation recognising Indian Independence Day across the state. According to the Consulate General of India in New York, the proclamation highlighted the Indian-American community's contributions to New Jersey in areas including education, healthcare, research, technology, business, public service and community leadership.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul also proclaimed August 15 as India Independence Day across the state.
The Consulate said New York's proclamation recognised the Indian-American community's contribution to the state's cultural, economic and civic life, while also highlighting the enduring ties between India and the US.
The Consulate thanked Hochul for the recognition, saying the proclamation celebrated India's journey of independence and the democratic values shared by the two countries.
How US communities celebrate India's Independence Day
India's Independence Day is marked across the US each year through flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, cultural programmes and community events.
Indian diplomatic missions, including the Embassy of India in Washington and Indian consulates, hold special programmes on August 15. The Indian mission to the United Nations also participates in commemorative events.
Indian-American communities across states organise cultural performances and public celebrations, with local political leaders often participating and highlighting the community's contributions to American society.
Prominent landmarks have also joined the celebrations in previous years, including the Empire State Building in New York and the Space Needle in Seattle, which have been illuminated in the colours of the Indian tricolour for Independence Day events.
India marks 80th Independence Day with focus on youth
The proclamations come as India prepares to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026.
This year's celebrations will also focus on the commemoration of 150 years of âVande Mataramâ, while placing particular emphasis on âYuva Shaktiâ or youth power.
The celebrations are expected to combine the historical significance of India's freedom movement with recognition of the achievements and contributions of its younger generation.
The growing number of US states formally recognising India's Independence Day also underlines the visibility of the Indian-American community and the broader social, economic and cultural ties between India and the United States.

headline: YSRCP’s assembly boycott to continue in monsoon session
full_text:
YSRCP’s assembly boycott to continue in monsoon session
HyderabadOpposition YSR Congress Party on Wednesday decided to continue its boycott of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in the upcoming monsoon session, while raising issues linked to public interest and highlighting the failure of the Telugu Desam Party-led coalition government in the state legislative council meetings
Hyderabad
Opposition YSR Congress Party on Wednesday decided to continue its boycott of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in the upcoming monsoon session, while raising issues linked to public interest and highlighting the failure of the Telugu Desam Party-led coalition government in the state legislative council meetings.
Addressing the party MLAs and MLCs at the office at Tadepalli, YSRCP president and former chief minister Y S Jagan Mohan Reddy reiterated that there was no point in attending the assembly session as speaker Chintakayala Ayyanna Patraudu was unwilling to give the status of leader of opposition to the party.
Deep Dive
“The government is against recognising the YSRCP as the leader of opposition only to gag its voice. I shall continue to highlight the public issues through regular media conferences to show people the other side of the coin,” he said.
The YSRCP chief, however, said since the party had enough strength in the legislative council, it would act as the voice of the people and highlight the burning public issues,” Jagan said.
The YSRCP chief asked the party MLCs to raise the issues like irregularities in Mega DSC-2025 teachers’ recruitment. “We took up 10 different types of protests on the issue in the last 74 days, placing all the evidence to establish a viewpoint. We exposed various irregularities, including leakage of question papers, outsourcing scandal and irregularities in sports quota appointments, and demanded a CBI inquiry into the role of education minister Nara Lokesh,” he said.
Jagan also asked the MLCs to raise issues like failures in the implementation of fees reimbursement and Vasathi Deevena schemes. He announced that the party would represent the farmers’ voice on lack of minimum support price to the crops and suspension of free crop insurance scheme.
The YSRCP also decided to fight against new public-private-partnership policy, repeal of Disha Bill, witch-hunt of OBC leaders of the party, junior doctors’ strike and dissatisfaction among the employees.
Meanwhile, Jagan announced MLC Thumati Madhava Rao as the party’s candidate for the vacant post of deputy chairman of the legislative council.
NO ATTENDANCE, NO SALARY: SPEAKER
Meanwhile, state assembly speaker Chintakayala Ayyanna Patraudu expressed dissatisfaction over the decision of the YSRCP MLAs to boycott the state assembly proceedings.
Speaking to reporters, the speaker questioned why salaries should be paid to YSRCP MLAs who decided not to attend assembly sessions. “Legislators are elected to discuss public issues and raise the concerns of their constituencies in the assembly. What is the rationale behind their continued absence from the House?” he asked.
Ayyanna Patrudu said MLAs who failed to attend assembly sessions should not be paid salaries and added that he had already brought the issue to the attention of the Central government. He suggested that the matter should be discussed in Parliament and that appropriate legislation should be enacted to deal with legislators who remain absent from the House.
“Why should those who do not attend the assembly continue as MLAs?” Ayyanna Patrudu asked. He said a face-recognition system had been introduced in the Assembly to prevent proxy attendance and the alleged use of forged signatures by some members.
The speaker also said a proposal to disqualify MLAs who remained absent from the assembly for six months was currently at the discussion stage. “We are waiting to see what guidelines the Central government will issue on the matter,” he said.
He further said the issue of allotting government quarters to MLAs who do not attend assembly sessions would be examined in consultation with the General Administration Department before a decision was taken.

headline: Muzaffarnagar riots case: MP-MLA court acquits 25 BJP leaders, Hindu activists
full_text:
Muzaffarnagar riots case: MP-MLA court acquits 25 BJP leaders, Hindu activists
The accused faced trial for allegedly violating prohibitory orders, obstructing public servants and inciting communal tension through speeches at a 2013 mahapanchayat in Nagla Mador.
A special MP-MLA court has allowed the prosecution to withdraw a case against 25 BJP leaders and Hindu activists, including Uttar Pradesh minister Kapil Dev Agarwal, former Union minister Sanjeev Balyan and former state minister Suresh Rana, in connection with a 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots-related case.
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate/MP-MLA court judge Devendra Kumar Faujdar allowed the prosecution's application seeking withdrawal of the case on Wednesday, prosecution officer Rahul Singh said.
The accused were facing trial for allegedly violating prohibitory orders, obstructing public servants in the discharge of their duties and inciting communal tension through speeches at a mahapanchayat held at Nagla Mador in the district on July 31, 2013, Singh told PTI on Thursday.
The accused included Agarwal, Balyan, Rana, former Uttar Pradesh minister Ashok Kataria, former BJP MPs Bhartendu Singh and Sohanvir Singh, former BJP MLAs Ashok Kansal and Umesh Malik, VHP leader Sadhvi Prachi and Narsinghanand of Dasna Shiv Temple, among others.
The prosecution moved the application following the Uttar Pradesh government's decision to withdraw the case, Singh said.
The 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots and subsequent violence in neighbouring districts left more than 60 people dead and displaced over 40,000, according to official figures.

headline: Centre agrees in principle to rail travel concessions for acid attack survivors
full_text:
Centre agrees in principle to rail travel concessions for acid attack survivors
Have agreed in principle to give railway travel concessions to acid attack victims, Centre tells SC
The Centre on Thursday told the Supreme Court that it has agreed in principle to formulate a policy for granting railway travel concessions to acid attack survivors to enable them to travel to well-equipped hospitals in cities for periodic treatment.
The top court asked the Centre to consider the issue of granting travel concessions to acid attack survivors "liberally".
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the submissions of Additional Solicitor General Archana Pathak Dave, appearing for the Ministry of Railways, and asked her to file the draft policy on record within six weeks.
Also Read | Acid attack survivors with internal injuries to get RPwD benefits: Centre to SC
At the outset, the law officer said that a meeting has been held and it has been decided in principle that the acid attack survivors can be given railway concessions.
She said the Centre proposes to extend the benefit under the "patient category" as it has reservations about placing acid attack survivors in a separate category among persons with disabilities.
"I can inform that they will put the acid attack victims in the patient category… because they have some reservations about putting them under the disabled category as others in that disabled category are not given railway concessions," she added.
Also Read | At a cafe in Viman Nagar, acid attack survivors find work, acceptance and a new beginning
"Putting them in the disabled category, that has now been statutorily resolved, with the amendment through another petition before us," the CJI said.
"They are in the disabled category, but we will give them concession under the patient category because they require it for the purpose of going to the doctor and for their treatment. We are still deliberating, but under the disabled category, because we are not giving this concession to all disabled persons, then the other categories would also come and say that the concession should be given to them as well," the law officer said.
She said the Railways will not be able to differentiate amongst each disabled person.
"We will give them, but under the patient category. How and how it would be given, those modalities, I would seek some time," the law officer said.
The CJI said that the relief should be given in a time-bound manner.
On July 16, the bench had sought the views of the Centre on the plea seeking concessional air-conditioned class rail fare for acid attack survivors to enable them to travel to well-equipped hospitals in cities for treatment.
It had asked Dave to take requisite instructions from the Ministry of Railways on the issue.
Dave had earlier said that there are 21 categories of persons with disabilities (PwDs) and the railways is already providing travel concessions to them. She said the railways is also contemplating providing an emergency travel quota for all categories of PwDs.
The counsel, appearing for PIL petitioner Atijeevan Society, which has sought railway reservations for acid attack victims, said such survivors have to undertake multiple visits to super-speciality hospitals for treatment for almost four to five years.
He said that persons who have been forced to ingest acid face difficulty in getting medical certificates to seek a railway reservation.
Moreover, they are asked to get such certificates from the treating hospitals to claim reservation, which is difficult, he added.
The bench asked the law officer to see whether acid attack victims can be included in the category of patients like thalassemia and cancer to ensure that they can also avail the concession in rail tickets to get treatment.
The bench asked the law officer to take instructions and listed the plea for further consideration.
Earlier, the bench had issued a notice to the Centre on the PIL seeking a separate reservation quota and concessional railway fares for acid attack survivors.
"Due to the nature of the burn injuries, persistent itching, and especially after undergoing surgery, acid attack survivors often need to travel by train in AC coaches. However, they cannot afford the high cost of AC tickets for frequent travels and due to the existing framework, they can neither avail themselves of the earmarked quota otherwise available to PwDs nor the concessional railway fare facility," the PIL said.
It said their rehabilitation necessitated multiple reconstructive surgeries, advanced ophthalmic interventions and prolonged post-operative care, which are available only at a handful of elite tertiary institutions in metropolitan cities like Delhi, Chennai and Hyderabad.
It pleaded for inclusion of acid attack survivors within the PwD category to make them entitled to a concession in rail fare.

headline: SC expresses concern over pendency of cases at NCDRC, bats for regional, circuit benches
full_text:
SC expresses concern over pendency of cases at NCDRC, bats for regional, circuit benches
New Delhi, The Supreme Court on Thursday took serious note of the pendency of cases in the National Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission and asked the Centre to consider setting up regional and circuit benches to clear the backlog.
The top court also called for performance audits of state and district consumer commissions. The forums should not become rehabilitation centres for retired judicial officers, it said.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the Centre to consider setting up regional and circuit benches of the national consumer forum, saying a consumer must not be made to travel all the way to Delhi, instead, the forum must go to them.
The bench asked the chairman of the NCDRC to furnish a status report on total pending cases, total complaints filed, average rate of disposal of cases, estimated time likely for disposal of a pending case and need for increasing the strength of members of the commission.
The top court, which is monitoring the functioning of consumer commissions, including appointments, service conditions and infrastructure. said the report must be filed in two weeks.
The top court was informed that pendency of case is huge in NCDRC as the matters which are being taken up for hearing at present are from 2018-19.
While some lawyers informed the bench that if a matter is listed in June this year, then the next date of listing of the matter is almost next year while others said that 30-40 matters are normally listed in post-lunch session, which does not get disposed of.
The bench then told Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for Centre in the matter that if the arrears are piling up in the NCDRC, then the only option left is to increase the maximum strength of the commission.
"We have a consumer friendly jurisprudence and pendency of cases can be reduced by increasing the number of benches," CJI Kant said.
The top court, however, said the quality of orders passed by NCDRC, which come up in appeal before the top court are very good, which shows that the problem is with filling vacancies of members of commission.
It asked the amicus curiae in the matter to also furnish data on pendency in state consumer commissions, vacancies and the information about the oldest case pending in the commission.
The bench asked the state consumer commission to furnish evaluation reports of district consumer forums for the last three years and posted the matter after three weeks.
Last month, the top court said that states with fewer than 1,000 pending consumer disputes may abolish some district consumer forums and transfer those cases to regular courts with approval from the jurisdictional high courts.
"All those states where the total pendency is less than 1,000 cases shall be at liberty to abolish some of the district forums and entrust the cases to the serving judicial officers, with the prior concurrence of the jurisdictional high court," the top court had said.
The clarification came during the court's current exercise to ensure compliance with its earlier directions governing the constitution of state and district consumer commissions and the service conditions of their chairpersons and members.
In its February 11 order, the apex court had noted submissions from several smaller states, especially the northeastern states and Union territories, that maintaining separate consumer commissions despite very low pendency was financially unviable.
It referred to such states as Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Tripura, Mizoram, Manipur and Goa, as well as the UTs of Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where only a limited number of consumer disputes were pending.
The court also observed that some states did not have constituted state consumer commissions headed by a sitting or a former high court judge. The bench thus directed that pending matters from certain states be transferred to the registrars general of the jurisdictional high courts.
A single judge of the high court, sitting with the existing technical members, would hear those cases as a deemed state consumer commission, it then said.
In February, the top court also permitted states and UTs with fewer than 1,000 pending complaints and appeals to submit alternative proposals to ensure effective consumer dispute resolution.
It asserted that states with below the 1,000-case threshold may also rationalise their district consumer forums by transferring cases to serving judicial officers, provided the arrangement receives the prior concurrence of the concerned high courts.

headline: Defence ministry issues ₹1 lakh-crore tender for 60 medium transport aircraft to boost Air Force capabilities
full_text:
Defence ministry issues ₹1 lakh-crore tender for 60 medium transport aircraft to boost Air Force capabilities
The IAF, the world’s fourth largest, is looking for a new transport aircraft with an 18- to 30-tonne cargo carrying capacity to meet its growing airlift needs.
The defence ministry on Wednesday issued a tender worth around ₹1 lakh crore to buy up to 60 medium transport aircraft (MTA) to boost the Indian Air Force’s (IAF) airlift capabilities, officials aware of the development said.
The tender has been issued to five Indian companies, including Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL), Mahindra Group, Adani Defence & Aerospace, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited and Reliance Defence, the officials said, asking not to be named. The IAF, the world’s fourth largest, is looking for a new transport aircraft with an 18- to 30-tonne cargo carrying capacity to meet its growing airlift needs.
Also Read | CBI books ex-defence ministry official, wife in ₹3.05 crore DA case
TASL has tied up with US firm Lockheed Martin, which has offered its C-130J Super Hercules aircraft for the MTA contest, and the Mahindra Group has teamed up with Brazilian plane maker Embraer, which has pitched its KC-390 Millennium aircraft to India. The three other Indian firms have not yet announced partnerships to advance the project. The MTA contest aligns with the government’s Make in India initiative to boost self-reliance in the defence manufacturing sector; the winner will set up a production line for the planes in India.
India is likely to conclude several big contracts in the financial year 2026-27 to sharpen the air force’s combat edge, including deals for the new transport planes, additional airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) systems, and 114 Rafale fighter jets.
Also Read | Defence ministry issues Independence Day invites with Vande Mataram lyrics
France recently responded to a letter of request (LoR) sent by the defence ministry with a techno-commercial offer for the 114 Rafale fighter jets sought by the IAF, marking the next step in a deal expected to be worth ₹3.25 lakh crore. The French government submitted its proposal to the defence ministry on July 29, paving the way for negotiations on the government-to-government deal to begin.
In February, the Defence Acquisition Council (DAC)—India’s apex military procurement body—cleared the purchase of military hardware worth ₹3.6 lakh crore, including 114 Rafale jets under the MRFA (multi-role fighter aircraft) programme. The council’s acceptance of the necessity for new fighters was the first step in the procurement process.
Under the MRFA model being considered, the Rafales will be made in India by French plane maker Dassault Aviation and a local partner. France is expected to supply 20 Rafale jets in fly-away condition while the remaining will be made in India. Discussions have been held with France regarding the localisation of the Rafales to be manufactured in India, the integration of local weapons and other India-specific requirements.
Also Read | India advances deal for 114 Rafale fighters from France
The IAF already operates 36 Rafale fighter jets bought from France at a cost of ₹59,000 crore. Also, India ordered 26 Rafale Marine fighter jets from France in April 2025 for the navy, which will operate them from its two aircraft carriers. The first deliveries of the Rafale Ms under the ₹63,000-crore contract will take place in 2029 and be completed by 2031.

headline: The 2027 Pirelli Calendar is dedicated to India. For the first time, it features an all-India cast and is shot entirely in the country, built around the idea of Indian identity. So alongside glamorous portraits of celebrities like television host and...
full_text:
The 2027 Pirelli Calendar is dedicated to India. For the first time, it features an all-India cast and is shot entirely in the country, built around the idea of Indian identity. So alongside glamorous portraits of celebrities like television host and author Padma Lakshmi, actress Aditi Rao Hydari, sitarist Anoushka Shankar and supermodel Bhavitha Mandava are some 200 ordinary Indians, from dancers and street artists to musicians and craftspeople.
One half of the 2027 Pirelli Calendar features Indian celebrities photographed by Norwegian photographer SÃ¸lve SundsbÃ¸ I Picture credit: Alessandro Scotti
The project began as a collaboration between Norwegian photographer SÃ¸lve SundsbÃ¸ and Raghu Rai, modern India's most celebrated photojournalist known for chronicling the country's many faces and contradictions over several decades. Rai died in April shortly after the project began. His daughter, photographer Avani Rai, stepped in to complete it and in doing so changed its direction. What had been conceived as a studio shoot moved outdoors into the neighbourhoods her father spent his career documenting, from Kinari Bazar and Yamuna Ghat to the streets of Old Delhi.When asked how a project like the Pirelli Calendar sits alongside her reportage-driven practice, Avani, speaking to TOI, gently rejects the premise of the question. Genre, she argues, describes where a photograph ends up, not how it is made. What remains constant, whether in documentary work or a fashion commission, is the attempt to stay honest to what is in front of the camera. "Curiosity, presence and empathy are not specific to one genre of photography. The Pirelli Calendar asked me to bring those values into a different context. I wasnât interested in making images that simply looked beautiful. I wanted them to feel alive. To hold the same emotional honesty that I search for in every photograph I make," says Avani whose mother, conservation architect Gurmeet Rai, also appears in the calendar.Even to this day, The Cal's physical copies are not sold publicly; Pirelli limits production to roughly 20,000 copies annually and they are sent as corporate gifts to monarchs, CEOs, prime ministers, top celebrities, fashion icons and the like.But why India? SundsbÃ¸ says it was a long-held ambition within Pirelli. His contribution came from a very different vantage pointâthat of an outsider conscious of his own limitations. "The fact that Avani and Raghu Raiâs images would be one half of the Calendar enabled me to concentrate on portraits. That's a smaller and more realistic task for a visitor than capturing the whole soul of a nation.I didnât try to decide what âIndiannessâ should mean. Especially not as the guest that I am. I tried to cast people I admire, women who have inspirational talent," says SundsbÃ¸.The edition also marks the first time Pirelli has commissioned two photographers to share a calendar. What makes the India edition notable is not simply that it swaps eroticism for cultural identity; the calendar has been moving in that direction for years. Rather, it is the first edition shaped by two intertwined perspectives: an outsider looking in and a daughter completing her father's final project in the streets he loved.
"I used to think inheritance was about continuing someoneâs work. Now I think itâs about continuing their way of being in the world. The patience they lived with. The integrity they carried. The generosity with which they met people. Those are the things that survive," says Avani."Completing the calendar gave me a sense of continuity. It wasnât about recreating him or holding onto the past. I understood that what he had really left me wasnât an archive or even a body of work. It was a practice of being alive to the world," she adds.
Sneha Bhura is an Assistant Editor with The Times of India. She loves exploring stories at the intersection of culture and technology. She is also a published poet and podcaster. Her debut poetry collection 'Velvet Grapes' was released in 2021.

headline: 2 attacks in 2 years, 2 escapes: Sukhbir Singh Badal attack in Nanded reminiscent of close call in Amritsar
full_text:
2 attacks in 2 years, 2 escapes: Sukhbir Singh Badal attack in Nanded reminiscent of close call in Amritsar
Sukhbir Singh Badal survived an assassination attempt while performing sewa at the entrance of the Golden Temple in Amritsar on 4 December, 2024.
The former Punjab deputy chief minister and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Thursday survived another attack, this time outside a gurdwara in Maharashtra.
The incident comes less than two years after Badal survived an assassination attempt at the Golden Temple in Amritsar in December 2024.
Badal was reportedly attacked by a Nihang at Gurdwara Mata Sahib Kaur on the outskirts of Nanded district. He sustained an injury to his hand and was rushed to the nearby Yashosai Hospital for treatment.
2024 assassination bid at Golden Temple
Deep Dive
The latest incident is the second reported attack on Badal in less than two years.
On December 4, 2024, Badal survived an assassination attempt while performing sewa at the entrance of the Golden Temple in Amritsar. He was serving a religious punishment, or tankhah, pronounced by the Sikh clergy over “mistakes” during the SAD's 2007-17 rule in Punjab.
The shooter, former militant Narain Singh Chaura, allegedly approached Badal and fired at him from close range.
As reported by HT at that time, the bullet missed Badal after a security volunteer intervened and grabbed Chaura's hands, causing the shot to hit a wall around six feet from where Badal was sitting. No one was injured in the incident and Chaura was overpowered and arrested.
Badal was serving religious punishment
At the time of the 2024 attack, Badal was carrying out his punishment as a sewadar, or volunteer, outside the Golden Temple.
He was seated in a wheelchair and wore the blue sewadar uniform while holding a spear in one hand. Badal had been serving the punishment after the Sikh clergy pronounced a tankhah against him over decisions taken during the Akali Dal's tenure in Punjab.
Also Read | Nihang in 60s, worked as 'sewadar': What we know about Sukhbir Singh Badal's attacker
The 2024 attack was captured on cameras covering the second day of Badal's penance. Footage showed Chaura walking towards Badal before pulling a gun from his pocket. A volunteer standing near the SAD chief quickly intervened and grabbed him as he fired, allowing Badal to escape unharmed.
Badal, who had a fractured leg at the time, continued with his religious duty after the failed assassination attempt.
Attacked outside Nanded gurdwara
The latest attack took place around 15 km from Gurdwara Nanded Sahib, one of the five Takhts, or temporal seats, of Sikhism. Badal was reportedly heading towards the langar hall after paying obeisance when a Nihang attacked him with a kirpan.
The gurdwara is controlled by a Nihang samparday and is not managed by the board that oversees the main Nanded Sahib gurdwara.
Badal had arrived in Nanded on Wednesday with his family and a group of close associates for a three-day visit. He was inside the gurdwara with his wife, Harsimrat Kaur Badal, who is also a SAD MP, when the incident took place.

headline: Ruckus in Parliament over attire: John Brittas and Sushmita Dev trade barbs
full_text:
Ruckus in Parliament over attire: John Brittas and Sushmita Dev trade barbs
Communist Party of India (Marxist) MP John Brittas alleged that the Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP’s) Sushmita Dev had made a disparaging remark about his attire and moved a motion of privilege against her.
The Rajya Sabha witnessed a ruckus on Wednesday as the ruling side and the Opposition locked horns over the alleged remarks on a House member’s attire.
Communist Party of India (Marxist) MP John Brittas alleged that the Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP’s) Sushmita Dev had made a disparaging remark about his attire and moved a motion of privilege against her. Brittas was wearing a Mundu, a garment worn by men in Kerala. However, Dev later clarified in the House that she did not cast aspersions on any state’s attire.
Soon after the House proceedings began, Brittas said the BJP MP had on Monday “repeatedly” disturbed him while he was speaking and proceeded to comment on his attire. “Verbal duel is okay… We fight each other… But she repeatedly made derogatory remarks over my attire...,” Brittas said in the House.
Deep Dive
The MP who represents Kerala in the Upper House said he is proud of his Malayali identity, culture and traditional attire and disparaging remarks on the Mundu was objectionable.
Speaking to HT outside Parliament he said, “While I was moving the statutory resolution, she came from her seat and was disturbing me…So I said, you see these turn coats are more enthusiastic in criticism… then she started calling me lungi walla …which is highly derogatory.” Brittas had soon after filed a notice for moving a privilege motion against her.
Following Brittas’s statement in the House, Rajya Sabha chairman, CP Radhakrishnan said, certain instances have come to his notice regarding discourteous and undignified comments being made by Members interrupting the speech of other Members in the House. “...I would advise that Hon’ble Members should be careful not to hurt the sentiments and feelings of fellow Members. Our culture is unique and inclusive of diverse regional cultures. There should be no disrespect to the cultural traditions and regional identities of our colleagues,” he said, adding that he would speak to both sides.
Union minister JP Nadda who is also the leader of the House said his party does not subscribe to such statements. “...We do not call it lungi; we call it dhoti,” he said.
As the two sides locked horns over the issue, the House was adjourned till 2 p.m.
Speaking outside Parliament Dev said she had not used the term and also accused Brittas of instigating her by using the term turncoat. Dev also submitted a notice to move a motion of privilege against Brittas for making a reference to “religion and a party’s allegiance”.
Later when the House reassembled she said, “I would like to say on record, no message from this should go that any member wants a division in India culturally or on the basis of religion. I’m from Assam… I’m a Bengali from Assam… I have seen various states of the north east where different attires are worn…Neither I nor any member has cast any aspersion on any state’s attire.”
According to a person aware of the details, Dev’s statement in the House came after the short video clip of the incident was shown to both the Chairman and the parliamentary affairs minister. “It was made clear that Brittas did not use any reference to any religion…as was alleged by Dev. Several lawmakers had urged Dev on Monday to clear the air with Brittas and AAP’s Sanjay Singh has even offered to mediate…” said a person aware of the details.

headline: NEW DELHI: Revenue earned from foreign patients and affluent Indians should help fund treatment for poorer patients, a Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare has recommended, proposing that corporate hospitals adopt a cross-sub...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Revenue earned from foreign patients and affluent Indians should help fund treatment for poorer patients, a Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare has recommended, proposing that corporate hospitals adopt a cross-subsidisation model to make advanced healthcare more affordable.The panel said hospitals that benefit from government concessions such as subsidised land, tax incentives and 100% foreign direct investment (FDI) should earmark part of the revenue generated from medical tourism and high-paying patients to provide advanced tertiary care to economically weaker Indians.The recommendation is part of the committee's report on the affordability and accessibility of healthcare, which noted that India's corporate hospital sector has recorded strong growth driven by high-value procedures, rising medical tourism and increasing revenue per occupied bed. While acknowledging India's emergence as a global healthcare destination, the panel said the benefits of this growth must also reach patients who cannot afford expensive treatment.Observing that private health insurance penetration in India remains low and out-of-pocket expenditure continues to push many families into financial distress, the committee said a structured cross-subsidy mechanism could improve access to life-saving tertiary care for poorer patients.
It said hospitals receiving government support should share part of the gains from medical tourism and premium-paying patients with economically weaker sections.The panel also recommended that corporate hospitals reserve a defined quota of beds under government-funded health insurance schemes such as Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY at standard package rates to ensure that beneficiaries have access to advanced treatment at leading private hospitals.
To address the uneven distribution of healthcare infrastructure, the committee proposed linking government incentives, including subsidised land, tax benefits and FDI facilitation, to investment in tier-2, tier-3 and rural areas. It also recommended expanding public-private partnerships and extending financial and technology support to smaller hospitals in underserved regions.The recommendations form part of a broader roadmap to make healthcare more affordable. The committee has also proposed capping private hospital room rents in major metropolitan cities at the average tariff of nearby three-star hotels, standardising treatment package rates, improving price transparency and expanding government health spending to reduce out-of-pocket expenditure.

headline: No tolerance towards digital offences: Naidu
full_text:
No tolerance towards digital offences: Naidu
Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday directed the police to adopt a zero-tolerance approach towards political crimes, digital offences, obscene social media posts and crimes against women, while calling for stricter and more effective policing to deal with the changing nature of crime
Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday directed the police to adopt a zero-tolerance approach towards political crimes, digital offences, obscene social media posts and crimes against women, while calling for stricter and more effective policing to deal with the changing nature of crime.
Addressing a video conference with nearly 1,650 police officers, ranging from the Director General of Police (DGP) to Station House Officers (SHOs) from around 1,200 police stations across the state, Naidu said political affiliations should not be allowed to shield criminals or encourage anti-social activities.
He specifically questioned the motorcycle stunts reportedly performed on public roads during a political party rally at Ibrahimpatnam and said no political party should be permitted to conduct such activities at the cost of public safety. He also pointed to instances in which police personnel had allegedly come under attack.
The chief minister said political parties had a responsibility to ensure that their programmes did not inconvenience the public. While condolence visits or meeting affected families were legitimate activities, he said, demonstrations that block public roads for prolonged periods could cause serious hardship to citizens.
Citing an incident in Visakhapatnam in which roads were reportedly blocked for nearly three hours, Naidu said such disruptions could create difficulties for ambulances transporting patients to hospitals as well as people travelling to work.
He warned that even a minor lapse in maintaining law and order could have consequences for the entire police system. Referring to incidents involving deaths and accidents that had subsequently resulted in counter-allegations against police personnel who had attempted to save lives, he stressed the need for greater professionalism and vigilance.
Naidu said the nature of crime was changing rapidly, with digital crimes, “digital arrests”, obscene online campaigns and personal abuse emerging as major challenges. He directed the police to make greater use of technology in crime prevention and investigation.
He said cognizable crimes had declined by 14% over the past two years, but stressed that the police could not afford to be complacent. Technology, he said, was being used both by law-enforcement agencies to detect criminals and by offenders to commit new forms of crime.
The chief minister said 14,770 CCTV cameras installed by the government across the state had been integrated with privately installed cameras, creating a network of around one lakh cameras. Facial recognition systems and DNA-based technologies were also increasingly being used in investigations, he said.
“If police officers effectively implement technology, knowledge and best practices, law and order can be brought under control,” Naidu said.
He called for the implementation of the “Invisible Police, Visible Policing” approach and said the police must win the trust of the people through effective and friendly policing. At the same time, the police should command respect among citizens and instil fear among anti-social elements.
Naidu alleged that some individuals were encouraging ganja users and “blade gangs” under the guise of political affiliations. He said disturbances that were earlier allegedly fuelled by alcohol were increasingly being associated with ganja use.
He also expressed concern over the manner in which some rowdies and criminals were being portrayed as heroes on social media. He called for a wider social discussion on crimes committed by individuals with serious behavioural and mental issues and stressed the need to prevent social media platforms from glorifying criminal behaviour.
The chief minister said the government was working towards establishing a national-level organisation aimed at creating a drug-free and ganja-free society. He directed officials to take the anti-drugs campaign to a wider audience as part of efforts to prevent drug and ganja abuse.
Naidu reiterated that there should be zero tolerance towards crimes against women. He also directed the police to pay special attention to obscene campaigns, personal abuse and other objectionable content circulating on social media.
“When the conviction rate increases, crime comes down,” he said, emphasising the importance of effective investigation and prosecution. He asked the police to take successful investigations and achievements in important cases to the public so that people were aware of the department’s performance.
He said the coalition government would provide the police with complete freedom to perform their duties and take measures to enhance the dignity and respect of police personnel.
Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha, DGP Harish Kumar Gupta and other senior police officials participated in the meeting.

headline: 100 skeletons, medieval settlement found near India-Pakistan border in Kutch
full_text:
100 skeletons, medieval settlement found near India-Pakistan border in Kutch
Archaeologists have uncovered a medieval settlement near the Kutch border with structures, artefacts and a cemetery of about 100 skeletons. The finds suggest the now desolate border landscape was once a connected centre of agriculture, trade and movement.
Archaeologists have uncovered the remains of a medieval settlement in a remote part of Kutch, close to the India-Pakistan border, revealing large brick structures, ancient artefacts and a cemetery containing around 100 human skeletons.
The site was first spotted by Border Security Force (BSF) personnel during patrols in the desolate border region. Soldiers noticed several structures scattered across the landscape and began referring to the place as an abandoned village.
A joint research project by Krantiguru Shyamji Krishna Verma Kachchh University and the University of Oxford has since begun investigating the site, which has been provisionally named Barbadi Gaon.
Preliminary findings suggest the settlement was inhabited mainly between the 11th and 14th centuries, during the Soomra period.
Excavations have unearthed large brick structures, earthen household vessels, oil lamps, a copper coin, a camel figurine and tools believed to have been used for removing rice husks. The findings point to a settled community engaged in agriculture and possibly trade.
Researchers have also identified a cemetery containing around 100 skeletons, many of them found with their heads facing west. Researchers suspect that seismic activity, including a major earthquake in the past, may have contributed to the remains becoming exposed.
The settlement may also have stood near a waterway linking the inland region to the Arabian Sea, potentially giving its inhabitants access to important trade routes.
The discovery offers a glimpse into a landscape that today appears barren and remote. Centuries ago, the same region may have been a thriving centre of settlement, agriculture and trade, connecting communities to wider commercial networks around the Arabian Sea.

headline: NCDC bill passed in Upper House amid Opposition walkout
full_text:
NCDC bill passed in Upper House amid Opposition walkout
The bill amends the National Co-operative Development Corporation Act, 1962, to broaden the Corporation’s mandate and enable it to extend loans and grants directly not only to cooperative societies but also to other organisations engaged in cooperative development, provided the funds are ultimately used for the benefit of cooperatives.
The Rajya Sabha passed the National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, by voice vote on Wednesday, a day after the Lok Sabha approved it. Opposition parties staged a walkout before the House took up the Bill for voting.
The bill amends the National Co-operative Development Corporation Act, 1962, to broaden the Corporation’s mandate and enable it to extend loans and grants directly not only to cooperative societies but also to other organisations engaged in cooperative development, provided the funds are ultimately used for the benefit of cooperatives.
“It is proposed to enable the corporation to provide loans and grants directly to the cooperative societies or any entity engaged in cooperative development to the extent such funds are used for cooperative societies, subject to furnishing security as may be required by the corporation,” the statement of objects and reasons of the bill said.
Deep Dive
The changes come because the government believes that the cooperative sector has “expanded and diversified considerably” over the years. According to the statement of objects and reasons accompanying the bill, statutory bodies, state government agencies and other specialised organisations now provide infrastructure, technology, processing, marketing and financial services to cooperatives. As many of these organisations are not themselves registered as cooperative societies, NCDC cannot finance them directly under the existing law, resulting in “procedural delays and limited uptake” as proposals have to be routed through state governments or cooperative societies.
Replying to the debate on the bill, minister of state for cooperation Murlidhar Mohol said, “This bill does not have any provision for additional budgetary financial assistance by the government. The proposed amendment only expands the mandate and financial scope of NCDC”.
Besides widening the funding net, the bill also seeks to expand the definition of foodstuffs to include additional food items notified by the Centre, removes geographical restrictions on financing industrial goods, updates obsolete statutory references, empowers the corporation to collect and share credit information with banks and other financial institutions, and grants it incidental powers to carry out its functions more effectively.
The bill also authorises NCDC to acquire equity in entities engaged in cooperative development, subject to prior approval of the Centre.
(With inputs from PTI)

headline: Chennai: The TVK government has passed four high-profile resolutions in the Tamil Nadu assembly in the last three days—on state song Tamizh Thai Vazhthu, NEET abolition, the FCRA Amendment Bill, and delimitation. All received substantial cross-party ...
full_text:
Chennai: The TVK government has passed four high-profile resolutions in the Tamil Nadu assembly in the last three days—on state song Tamizh Thai Vazhthu, NEET abolition, the FCRA Amendment Bill, and delimitation. All received substantial cross-party support, including from key opposition party DMK, and drawing criticism mainly from lone BJP MLA M. Bhojarajan.
These moves lead to the question—is the ruling TVK, under Chief Minister Vijay, is following the DMK template of asserting state rights and Tamil identity as a challenge to the Union government, or is it trying to establish itself as the new flag-bearer of federalism and regional pride?
On 10 August, CM Vijay moved a resolution making it mandatory for the Tamizh Thai Vazhthu to be sung before any events at educational institutions, universities, government offices, PSUs etc. In May, the DMK had attacked the TVK over the state song being relegated to the third position in the assembly after the Governor’s address, accusing the party of having compromised on state pride.
This week, Vijay described Tamil as “not only a language but also our life and emotions” and “as pure as our mother,” framing the issue as a matter of state rights and cultural identity amid friction with a Union Home Ministry advisory on the sequence of national and state songs.
On 11 August, Tamil Nadu Health Minister K.G. Arunraj moved another resolution urging the Centre to abolish NEET for undergraduate medical admissions and allow selection based on Class 12 marks. It cited social justice concerns, disadvantages for Tamil-medium, rural and socio-economically weaker students, coaching centre proliferation, paper leaks and student distress that have led to suicides in the state. DMK, AIADMK, Left parties and PMK supported it but the BJP MLA walked out.
In 2021, the then DMK government under MK Stalin had passed the Tamil Nadu Admission to Undergraduate Medical Degree Courses Bill in assembly, seeking Tamil Nadu’s exemption from NEET and proposing that undergraduate medical admissions be based solely on Class 12 marks. The Bill was reserved for the President’s consideration and remains without assent.
The DMK has repeatedly adopted assembly resolutions demanding NEET’s abolition, framed it as anti-federal and a driver of coaching centre commercialisation and consistently campaigned against it as a core issue of education autonomy and equity.
Also on 11 August, state School Education Minister A. Rajmohan moved a resolution opposing the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, in its current form, arguing it could undermine the autonomy of charitable, educational and minority-run social welfare institutions. It too passed with broad support in the state assembly, while the BJP opposed it.
Earlier on 8 August, DMK president M.K. Stalin held a meeting with several Christian bishops and minority organisation representatives who thanked the party for its opposition to the FCRA Amendment Bill. Stalin described its provisions as a threat to the autonomy of charitable, educational, medical and social welfare institutions, particularly those run by minorities.
DMK had written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi calling the Bill “draconian” and a “legalised assault on minority-run institutions” and urged its complete withdrawal. The party has demanded that the Centre either withdraw the Bill entirely, repeal Section 15 of the existing FCRA Act, or refer both the amendment and a full review of the 2010 law to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
A delegation of Christian leaders headed by Rajya Sabha MP from DMK P. Wilson met Union Home Minister Amit Shah on 6 August to press these demands. In the Tamil Nadu assembly, DMK members supported the resolution moved by the TVK government opposing the FCRA Bill in its current form.
On 12 August, Vijay moved a special resolution seeking a permanent freeze on Lok Sabha strength at the existing 543 seats, retention of current inter-state allocation to protect southern states that controlled population growth, maintenance of the present Lok Sabha-Rajya Sabha ratio, and implementation of 33 percent women’s reservation in the 2029 elections on the basis of the existing 543 seats. DMK and Left parties backed it, while BJP opposed it. AIADMK and DMDK questioned the timing while supporting the women’s reservation component.
Throughout the debates, DMK leaders repeatedly said that these were long-standing positions of their party. On delimitation, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin said, “The movement that first told India what the impact of delimitation would be is the DMK.” He added that the previous DMK government under M.K. Stalin had passed an assembly resolution, convened an all-party meeting, written to chief ministers of other states and formed a joint action committee.
“Our firm stand is that Tamil Nadu’s representation must not be diminished. We welcome the assembly resolution and reiterate that Tamil Nadu’s existing 7.18 per cent share of Lok Sabha seats must be protected,” he said.
A calculated move by TVK?
Political observers see a calculated approach by TVK when moving these resolutions to position itself as the one raising the classic Dravidian or state-rights issues. TVK has picked language and cultural primacy, education autonomy, federal balance in parliamentary representation, and protection of minority institutions.
Academician and political analyst Ramu Manivannan told ThePrint that TVK is fighting the DMK more than the Centre. “TVK is raising all these issues from nowhere without any reference in earlier times and without any presence in the Parliament. This is like being everywhere and ultimately nowhere. This suits their politics and their ties with all including the Congress and BJP. TVK must resist DMK and by this crossfire, TVK will diminish the cutting edge advantage of DMK on all these issues.”
Analysts also say that the broad support to the government on these issues demonstrates consensus, allowing Vijay to claim credit for “protecting Tamil Nadu” without appearing isolated. It also creates optics of a “people’s government” willing to confront Delhi on matters of principle, after being criticised for not attacking the BJP directly on state matters.
Political analyst Sunil Kumar said that the TVK’s strategy serves multiple purposes as it will help the party occupy the moral and political high ground traditionally associated with the DMK on Centre-State issues, and make it harder for the opposition to portray the TVK government as soft on federalism or Tamil identity.
“TVK is trying to replace the AIADMK completely by diminishing its role by following the DMK playbook. They want to hold the power and cultivate the political messaging as State first and the TVK versus DMK narrative. Even the usage of words while moving the resolutions says ‘Union’ instead of Centre, which was something DMK popularised. The party wants to ensure that they are seen as a State party that is also supportive of minorities, such as in the case of FCRA bill,” Sunil told ThePrint.
(Edited by Gitanjali Das)

headline: FSSAI warns influencers of legal action over unverified food claims

FSSAI warns influencers of legal action over unverified food claims
NEW DELHI: From "boosts immunity" to "rich in nutrients", food claims endorsed by celebrities and social media influencers are now under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) scanner. In a significant move aimed at curbing misleading promotions, the regulator has warned influencers and celebrities that endorsing unverified food claims could invite legal action, even as it cracked down on manufacturers selling unsafe food products.The advisory comes at a time when food brands are increasingly relying on digital creators and celebrities to market health drinks, protein supplements, snacks and packaged foods to millions of consumers online. FSSAI has asked influencers to verify that every claim made by a brand is truthful, scientifically substantiated and compliant with food safety regulations before lending their name or credibility.The regulator said endorsements are more than advertisements because consumers often trust the people promoting them. It cautioned influencers against amplifying claims such as "boosts immunity" or "rich in nutrients" unless they are backed by evidence and permitted under food laws.
Misleading food advertisements and endorsements, it said, can attract action under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.Alongside the advisory, FSSAI prohibited the manufacture, sale and distribution of food products made by M/s Shree Shyam Foods, M/s Bharat Food Products and M/s KDP Food Industry after government laboratories found their ghee and mustard oil products unsafe for consumption.
The regulator also penalised Dharwad Mishra Pedha and Food Processing Industry in Karnataka after its Motichoor laddoos were found to contain Tartrazine at 2,670.5 mg/kg, more than 26 times the permissible limit of 100 mg/kg. Shree Chemfood Pvt Ltd of Gujarat was similarly penalised after samples of iodised salt were found to be substandard and misbranded.FSSAI has also urged consumers to report misleading food advertisements and celebrity endorsements through its Food Safety Connect platform.

headline: Woman dies while learning to drive as new car plunges into pond near Kolkata
full_text:
Woman dies while learning to drive as new car plunges into pond near Kolkata
Locals told the media that some people jumped into the pond to save her immediately after the car fell into the pond, but failed
A 42-year-old woman died after her new car plunged into a pond while learning to drive at Keshtopur near Kolkata on Wednesday, police said.
The woman, Sumitra Das, used to stay with her husband Krishnendu and their daughter in a flat near Prafulla Kanan West off the VIP Road in the northern fringes of Kolkata. While Krishnendu runs a business, Sumitra worked in a private firm.
“The family recently purchased a car and Sumitra was learning to drive it. She had to appear for a driving test for her license and was practising. She might have pressed the accelerator instead of the brakes and the car plunged into the 10–12 feet deep pond,” said a police official.
Also Read: Mohali: Zimbabwean student killed as two-wheeler crashes into parked truck
Locals told the media that some people jumped into the pond to save her immediately after the car fell into the pond, but failed. The police and fire brigade were alerted. The car was fished out after around an hour and a half. She had died by then. The victim was rushed to the hospital where doctors declared her dead.
“When the car was fished out of the water and the doors were opened, it was found that the victim had tried to reach the back door. Her head was towards the back seat and her legs were towards the driver’s seat, suggesting that she might have desperately tried to open the door,” Sujoy Das, a local resident, told media persons.
According to family members, Sumitra had gone to drop off her daughter at the bus stop in the morning. While returning she went to the garage where the car was parked. The garage was located at a distance from their residence and there was a pond nearby.
“Soon after bringing out the car from the garage, it plunged into the pond. A few local residents jumped into the pond but couldn’t save her,” said Anish Pal, another local resident.

headline: Delhi court flags ‘criminal breach of trust’ by 3 experts in NEET-UG paper leak
full_text:
Delhi court flags ‘criminal breach of trust’ by 3 experts in NEET-UG paper leak
A Delhi court said three subject experts accused in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak prima facie committed criminal breach of trust with the NTA.
A Delhi court has observed that three subject experts accused of leaking the NEET-UG 2026 question paper prima facie committed criminal breach of trust with the National Testing Agency (NTA), which had engaged them to translate the examination paper after they undertook not to disclose its contents.
The observation was made by Fast-track court special judge Ajay Gupta of Rouse Avenue Courts while taking cognisance of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)’s 20,000-page chargesheet filed earlier this month against 13 people in the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case.
The court order specifically focused on the role of PV Kulkarni, a Chemistry subject expert, in “taking advantage” of the lack of an adequate security apparatus at the NTA’s headquarters to leak the question paper.
“It prima facie seems from the chargesheet that A-2 (PV Kulkarni) was fully aware that there was no practice of frisking of the subject experts at the designated place, therefore, he took advantage of the situation and took along with him chits/short notes prepared by him discreetly while doing the translation work for his subject,” it said.
Also Read: NEET paper leak: Delhi court dismisses plea by accused to undergo lie detector test
The court said that the three subject experts, Kulkarni for Chemistry, Manisha Mandhare for Biology and Manisha Havaldar for Physics, had clearly given an undertaking before the translation work that they would not divulge examination-related material to anyone else.
“This prima facie shows that these accused persons have committed the criminal breach of trust with the NTA authority which engaged them for the purpose of translation of NEET (UG) 2026 exam question paper of their respective subjects,” the court observed.
The judge further underlined how the questions were leaked through the subject experts and subsequently travelled to students through intermediaries.
“...it is also prima facie clear from the record that all these subject experts, in active conspiracy with other co-accused persons, have in order to obtain the illegal monetary gain, sold the exam related material to the co-accused persons as well as several candidates in the guise of providing coaching to them,” it said.
The court also noted that the accused persons disposed of the leaked questions and destroyed their electronic devices in order to hide evidence, thereby making them liable to be prosecuted under the relevant sections of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.
Also Read: ‘FIFA’ group, small chits: How 3 NTA experts at centre of NEET leak probe ‘abused’ positions
“It is prima facie clear from the overwhelming incriminating material collected by the CBI through an extensive investigation that all the accused persons, in one manner or the other, formed part of NEET (UG) 2026 Exam leak syndicate and each one of them have played an active role in the dissemination and circulation of the exam question paper of all three subjects,” the court said.
The matter is now at the stage of scrutiny of documents and has been listed for arguments on charge to begin from next week.
The CBI had earlier this month filed a chargesheet against all 13 arrested accused in the alleged NEET-UG 2026 question paper leak case, saying its investigation had traced the leak from the paper setters to the beneficiary candidates and uncovered the entire chain of the alleged conspiracy.
The chargesheet invokes charges of criminal conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust, destruction of evidence, and offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.
The agency said it has relied on 360 witnesses, 422 documents and 43 material objects to support the prosecution. All 13 charge-sheeted persons are currently in judicial custody.
Among those charge-sheeted are three subject experts contracted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) to set the Chemistry, Biology and Physics papers, several alleged middlemen and two persons linked to coaching institutes.
According to the chargesheet, no government official, including any office bearer of the NTA, was involved in the leak. Investigators concluded that the question paper was leaked by teachers contracted to set the examination.
