headline: CJI invite row: Bar Council warns no NALSAR student will be lawyer, makes U-turn
full_text:
CJI invite row: Bar Council warns no NALSAR student will be lawyer, makes U-turn
The BCI said all students from the graduating batch can now enrol with State Bar Councils, while it awaits an inquiry report from NALSAR's Vice-Chancellor. The council also claimed that a "handful of teachers and outsiders" had instigated the students.
The Bar Council of India (BCI) on Thursday withdrew its decision to stop the enrolment of NALSAR University of Law’s 2026 graduates with State Bar Councils, just hours after issuing the directive amid a row over students opposing the invitation to Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant as the chief guest at the university’s convocation.
In a fresh communication issued after an emergency discussion, the BCI said all NALSAR students graduating in 2026 would be entitled to enrol with the State Bar Council of their choice. It said no student would be made to suffer "without any fault on his part."
The council, however, has not closed the matter and said it would await the inquiry report from the NALSAR Vice-Chancellor before deciding on any further action.
BCI MODIFIES ENROLMENT BAN
The reversal came hours after the BCI chairman directed that no NALSAR student who obtained a law degree in 2026 would be enrolled as an advocate by any State Bar Council "till further orders." The move triggered criticism and social media backlash over its potential impact on the professional prospects and placements of the graduating batch.
In its fresh letter, the BCI said it had “thoroughly discussed and deliberated” on the earlier communication issued by its chairman to the NALSAR Vice-Chancellor and the secretaries of all State Bar Councils. “After thorough discussion, the Members are of the unanimous view that as per the latest report, the vast majority of the students of NALSAR (2026 pass out students) are innocent, and they were not inclined to take part in the move of disrespect,” the letter said.
“Accordingly, the Council modifies the order of Chairman with regard to the ban on the enrolment of NALSAR Students with the State Bar Councils. All the students will be entitled to get enrolled with the State Bar Councils of their choice,” it added.
'TEACHERS, OUTSIDERS INSTIGATED STUDENTS'
The council also claimed that “a handful of teachers and outsiders” had been instrumental in instigating the students. “It has further been reported by some reliable sources that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in instigating the innocent students,” the BCI said.
The council did not name the teachers or outsiders or provide further details of the allegation. It said it would wait for the inquiry report of the NALSAR Vice-Chancellor before taking any further action.
OVER 450 STUDENTS OPPOSE CJI’S INVITATION
The controversy arose after a section of outgoing NALSAR students objected to the invitation extended to CJI Surya Kant to preside over the university’s 2026 convocation.
More than 450 students from the Batch of 2026 signed a representation addressed to the Vice-Chancellor, Registrar, professors and other university authorities, urging them to reconsider the decision.
The students said the date of the convocation and the choice of chief guest had not yet been formally finalised, but wanted to place their concerns on record before any decision was taken.
STUDENTS REFER TO JANTAR MANTAR PROTEST HEARING
In their representation, the students cited recent judicial developments, particularly Justice Surya Kant's handling of a hearing concerning alleged police action against protesters during a Parliament march from Delhi's Jantar Mantar on July 20, 2026.
According to the students' representation, during the July 23 hearing, the CJI declined to watch video evidence allegedly showing police excesses, saying, “We are not interested in videos; we don't have time to watch.” The students also alleged that submissions by the petitioner's counsel were subsequently cut short.
The students also raised concerns over remarks attributed to the CJI regarding the Jantar Mantar protest and his alleged comparison of Indian youth to “cockroaches”. “We, the undersigned students of [redacted] (2025-2026), share the concerns of the graduating batch regarding inviting the Hon’ble CJI, Justice Surya Kant, as our convocation’s Chief Guest,” the letter said.
“From referring to the youth as ‘cockroaches’ to making insensitive statements about not having time to watch videos of police brutality, the CJI has shown apathy towards students like us. Inviting him to our college to hand us degrees that hold so much academic and emotional importance does not sit right with us,” it added.
STUDENTS CITE CONSTITUTIONAL VALUES
The students said their objection was not directed at the office held by the CJI, but at whether his reported conduct in recent proceedings was consistent with the values they believe a university convocation should represent. “As students of law, our concern is narrow and more specific to us as a graduating batch,” the representation said.
The students argued that a convocation should reflect NALSAR's commitment to constitutional rights, access to justice and reasoned engagement with grievances.
They said receiving their degrees from a dignitary whose recent reported conduct appeared dismissive of allegations of police brutality against protesting citizens would be inconsistent with the values taught at the law university.

headline: No GST arrests without communicating order, ‘reasons to believe’: Supreme Court
full_text:
No GST arrests without communicating order, ‘reasons to believe’: Supreme Court
Supreme Court mandates GST authorities to communicate arrest orders, asserting it is essential for anticipatory bail applications.
The GST authorities cannot arrest a person without first communicating the order authorising the arrest and the “reasons to believe” recorded by the commissioner, the Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday, stressing that withholding such reasons could have “drastic consequences” for an accused’s right to liberty.
A bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said an arrest order under Section 69 of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act must be communicated to the affected individual because the order is a “sine qua non” (an essential condition) for seeking anticipatory bail. The court said such communication would not impede an ongoing GST investigation and, instead, would reinforce an accused’s right to seek legal protection.
Also Read | SC sets aside protection from arrest granted to Future Group director in GST case
“The order under Section 69 of the CGST Act, as held, being a sine qua non to seek anticipatory bail, it would be an anomaly to hold that the order need not be communicated at all,” it said.
The court held that disclosing the reasons behind the arrest authorisation was crucial as such an order is open to judicial review by constitutional courts. The accused must be in a position to challenge both the order and the “reasons to believe” recorded by the commissioner.
“If Section 69 were read as it is, without there being any requirement of disclosure of the ‘reasons to believe’, withholding of reasons could have drastic consequences on the right to liberty of the accused,” it noted.
Arrest order must be shared before arrest, court says
The judgment also clarified that communication of the arrest order need not wait until after the person is arrested. “Without such communication, question of arrest would not arise,” it said.
Also Read | GST collections cross ₹2.11 lakh crore in July
The judgment came even as the bench set aside a Bombay high court order granting Future Group non-executive director Sunil Biyani one week’s protection from arrest in a GST probe, holding that the high court could not have granted such relief after concluding that his anticipatory bail plea was premature.
The top court found this course of action impermissible, but at the same time directed the GST commissioner to communicate the Section 69 order to Biyani, after which he could pursue whatever legal remedy was available to him. It said that the order could be communicated electronically, including through email, in addition to the modes permitted under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and other permissible methods.
Also Read | Cut GST on smartphones below ₹25,000 to 5%: GT Bharat-PWIF report
Referring to Rule 8 of the CGST Rules, the bench noted that a person seeking GST registration is required to provide an email address and mobile number. “This would enable an accused to seek remedy that the law provides to him, if so advised,” it said.

headline: Nihang in 60s, worked as 'sewadar': What we know about Sukhbir Singh Badal's attacker
full_text:
Nihang in 60s, worked as 'sewadar': What we know about Sukhbir Singh Badal's attacker
Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked while he was walking towards the langar hall after paying obeisance at the gurdwara.
Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked with a kirpan by a Nihang at Gurdwara Mata Sahib Kaur on the outskirts of Nanded Sahib in Maharashtra on Thursday.
Badal suffered an injury to his right hand and was shifted to a nearby hospital. He is now out of danger, HT has learnt.
READ ALSO | Ex-Punjab deputy CM Sukhbir Singh Badal attacked with 'kirpan' outside gurdwara in Maharashtra's Nanded
Who attacked Sukhbir Singh Badal?
The attacker was a Nihang dressed in blue attire and is reportedly in his mid-sixties. His identity has not yet been revealed. Security personnel accompanying Badal overpowered him and handed him over to the local police for questioning.
According to Jaimal Singh Dhillon, a functionary at Takht Nanded Sahib, the gurdwara is under the control of a Nihang Samparday and the attacker is said to be from Punjab.
The historic Nanded gurdwara is managed by a splinter group of Shiromani Panth Akali Budha Dal 96 Crori, a major Nihang organisation headed by Baba Maan Singh. The local jathedar is Baba Teja Singh. The accused Nihang was reportedly serving as a sewadar at the gurdwara.
Where was Sukhbir Singh Badal attacked?
The attack took place at Gurdwara Mata Sahib Kaur on the outskirts of Nanded, around 15 km from Takht Nanded Sahib, one of the five temporal seats of the Sikhs.
Badal was attacked while he was walking towards the langar hall after paying obeisance at the gurdwara. The shrine is controlled by a Nihang sect and is not managed by the board that oversees the main Nanded Sahib Gurdwara.
ALSO READ | PM Modi inquires about Sukhbir Singh Badal's health after ‘kirpan attack’ in Nanded
Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis sought details of the incident from the Nanded Superintendent of Police and directed authorities to investigate the motive behind the attack.
‘Attack on Punjab’s unity’: SAD leader
SAD national vice-president Sanjeev Talwar called the attack on party chief Badal a serious security lapse.
“Sukhbir Singh Badal is a promoter of Hindu-Sikh unity, he speaks of Punjab and Punabiyat,” Talwar said. “This is not a direct attack on Sukhbir Singh Badal but an attack on the unity and integrity of Punjab,” he added.
“Such attack on someone who has Z+ security and is a former Deputy CM will certainly be considered a security lapse,” he said.
Why was Sukhbir Badal in Nanded?
Badal reached Nanded on Wednesday with his family and a group of close associates for a three-day visit. He organised an Akhand Path at the gurdwara.
Earlier on Thursday, Badal was offered a siropa by the head priests at Sachkhand Nanded Sahib, the main gurdwara in Nanded and one of the five temporal seats of the Sikhs. Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal and other family members were also present.
Gurdwara Mata Sahib Kaur is located around 15 km from the main Nanded Sahib gurdwara and is under the control of a Nihang Samparday.
Badal’s second attack in less than two years
The Nanded incident is the second attack on Sukhbir Badal in less than two years. On December 4, 2024, former militant Narain Singh Chaura allegedly attempted to assassinate Badal at the entrance of the Golden Temple in Amritsar.
Chaura fired at the SAD chief from close range, but the bullet narrowly missed after a security officer grabbed his pistol. The bullet struck the shrine wall.
No one was injured in that incident. Chaura was overpowered and arrested.

headline: The Chief Judicial Magistrate Court in Coimbatore, which is the Special Court for CBI cases, on Thursday convicted four persons in two cases of electrocution of wild elephants in Erode and Coimbatore districts.
full_text:
The Chief Judicial Magistrate Court in Coimbatore, which is the Special Court for CBI cases, on Thursday convicted four persons in two cases of electrocution of wild elephants in Erode and Coimbatore districts.
Chief Judicial Magistrate K. Sivakumar awarded the punishments in the cases, which were taken over and investigated by the CBI from the Forest Department, based on Madras High Court direction.
In the first case, the court sentenced Mathappa (38) and his father Kalayya (78) to three-and-a-half years of imprisonment for electrocuting a male wild elephant in Thalavadi in Jeerahalli forest range in Erode district in 2020.
The father-son duo cultivated crops such as ragi and paddy in six acres. They powered the iron cable fence around the farm by illegally connecting it to an overhead low tension powerline, resulting in the electrocution of a 10-year-old tusker on December 19, 2020.
The court found the two persons guilty for the crime and awarded a fine of ₹25,000 each along with the punishment.
In another case, the court sentenced Aruchamy (64) and his wife Thilagavathy of Thennamanallur near Thondamuthur in Coimbatore district to five years of imprisonment for the electrocution of a male elephant within the jurisdiction of the Boluvampatti forest range in 2021.
The couple cultivated paddy and other crops in a little over seven acres at Semmedu. They used the electricity connection given for agricultural purposes to power a fence in the farm illegally, leading to the electrocution of a 25-year-old tusker on January 5, 2021. The court also slapped a fine of ₹25,000 each on them.
Pronouncing the judgements, the judge observed that the crime committed by the convicts for their personal selfishness resulted in the death of a voiceless creature - elephant. When farming is done in forest areas where elephants naturally roam, it is normal for them to feed on nearby crops to satisfy their hunger. Hence, the act committed by the convicts was not one that warrants a reduction in punishment, he observed.
Public Prosecutor V. Surendra Mohan appeared for the CBI in the two cases.

headline: BCI halts enrolment of NALSAR 2026 graduates amid row over CJI Surya Kant in convocation, withdraws move later
full_text:
BCI halts enrolment of NALSAR 2026 graduates amid row over CJI Surya Kant in convocation, withdraws move later
The BCI has also sought a factual report from the university on the persons allegedly instrumental in initiating and organising a campaign concerning CJI
In a dramatic turn of events, the Bar Council of India (BCI) on Thursday evening withdrew its order freezing the enrolment of the entire 2026 graduating batch of NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad, just hours after directing all state bar councils not to enrol any student from the batch pending an inquiry into a campaign opposing Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s participation in the university’s convocation.
In a communication issued late on Thursday evening, BCI Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra said the Council had “thoroughly discussed and deliberated” on his earlier letter and modified the direction imposing the enrolment ban. The Council, he said, was of the unanimous view that, according to the “latest report”, the vast majority of NALSAR’s 2026 graduating students were innocent and had not intended to participate in any move to show disrespect.
“Accordingly, the Council modifies the order of chairman with regard to the ban on the enrolment of the NALSAR students with the State Bar Councils. All the students will be entitled to get enrolled with the state bar councils of their choice,” the amended order said.
BCI to continue factual inquiry over CJI row
The BCI, however, has decided to continue with the factual inquiry into the controversy. The fresh letter said the Council had received reports from “reliable sources” that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in “instigating the innocent students”.
“The Council will wait for the inquiry report of the learned vice-chancellor and the further action will be taken after receipt of the report,” Mishra said.
To be sure, the Advocates Act, 1961 leaves no room for a blanket freeze of enrolment by an administrative order of the BCI chairman. Sections 24 and 24A prescribe eligibility and disqualifications, while Sections 25 and 26 lay down the statutory process for enrolment and consideration of any refusal. The Act contemplates an individualised determination of eligibility or disqualification, not collective punishment of an entire graduating batch. Experts say that Section 48B’s supervisory power over state bar councils cannot be used to create a new ground of disqualification or a power to indefinitely suspend enrolment which Parliament has not conferred.
The quick reversal came within hours of the BCI’s first communication, also dated August 13, in which Mishra had directed all state bar councils not to enrol any student who obtained a law degree from NALSAR in 2026 “till further orders”.
The first order had sought an authenticated report from the university identifying those who had initiated, organised, coordinated or mobilised the campaign against the CJI’s proposed participation in the convocation. It had also sought details of representations, signatories, meetings, social-media groups, media interactions and any calls for boycott or disruption, besides information on the involvement of faculty members, research scholars, alumni, student organisations or outsiders.
The first communication had said the interim freeze was necessary because permitting enrolment while the inquiry was pending could frustrate the process. It had also made strong observations about the suitability of those who, according to the BCI, showed disregard for the highest judicial office and linked such conduct to the dignity, discipline and ethical standards of the legal profession.
Also Read | Access to justice begins with dialogue, must ensure dignity and inclusion: CJI Surya Kant
The amended order now makes clear that the blanket restraint will not continue. “No student shall be made to suffer without any fault on his part,” Mishra said.
What is the NALSAR students-CJI row?
The controversy arose after a section of NALSAR students opposed the proposed participation of CJI Kant as chief guest at the university’s convocation. The university had confirmed that Justice Kant had been invited as chief guest, although the convocation dates had not yet been finalised and it was awaiting a response to the invitation.
Also Read | 'Strongly reconsider': Hyderabad law university students object to CJI Surya Kant's invite for convocation
The first representation was submitted on July 23 by 70 members of the outgoing LLB batch. Students from several subsequent batches later expressed solidarity with the representation. The students’ objections followed remarks made by CJI Kant in the Supreme Court while dealing with a plea concerning alleged police excesses during student protests in Delhi.
In their representation, the students said they were concerned by the refusal of the bench led by the CJI to urgently entertain the plea and by remarks made when a lawyer sought to place videographic material of the alleged police action before the court.

It has sought details of those involved in organising meetings, communicating with the media, administering social media or organised groups used for coordination, or proposing or mobilising any call for boycott, obstruction, disruption or organised non-participation in the convocation or any programme connected with the CJI.
The bar council has also sought information on whether any student body, student bar council, studentsâ union or other recognised student organisation was involved in initiating, approving, coordinating or circulating the campaign. The university has also been asked to specify whether any faculty member, research scholar, alumnus or outsider participated in initiating, drafting, coordinating, advising or facilitating the campaign.In addition, the council has requested copies of relevant resolutions, minutes, agendas or other official records of meetings connected with the matter, and details of whether permission was sought or granted for any protest or organised activity and whether university rules governing student conduct or official functions were invoked.At the same time, the bar council clarified that participation in the representation or campaign would not automatically result in disqualification from enrolment. It said a distinction must be maintained between those who merely signed or supported a representation and those who organised or coordinated the campaign or proposed or mobilised an actual boycott, obstruction or disruption.The bar council said that where material concerning the conduct of a particular applicant is under statutory examination, completing enrolment during the pendency of such examination could create a fait accompli and render the examination ineffective.Accordingly, it directed that where the BCI specifically communicates the name of a person for further statutory consideration, no enrolment order should be passed in respect of that person and, if an application is already pending, the final decision should remain deferred during the inquiry.
State bar councils have also been instructed to ensure that any person whose name is communicated by the bar council does not circumvent the pending examination by seeking enrolment before another state bar council. The council clarified that such communication at the preliminary stage would not itself constitute a conclusive finding of misconduct or disqualification.The bar council said any final adverse decision would be taken in accordance with the Advocates Act, 1961, the applicable rules and principles of natural justice.The communication further emphasised that legal education permits critical reasoning, debate and analysis of judicial decisions, but said there is a distinction between reasoned criticism and conduct which, if established after due examination, may involve intimidation, obstruction, organised disruption or disregard of institutional responsibilities attached to the legal profession.The communication has been issued to NALSAR University of Law as well as the secretaries of all state bar councils for necessary compliance.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: The Govt of NCT of Delhi has notified 20% horizontal reservation for ex-Agniveers in direct recruitment to the posts of warder and matron in the prison department.The 20% quota he has been provided by the Delhi Lieutenant Governor (LG) in exercise of powers conferred by the proviso to Article 309 of the Constitution of India, read with the relevant recruitment rules governing the posts of warder and matron in the Delhi prison department. It fits in with the policy of the govt of India for rehabilitation of ex-Agniveers, as communicated in a letter of the Union Home Secretary dated March 25, 2026.The home ministry has already reserved 50% of the posts at the constable (general duty) and rifleman level in all the Central armed police forces (CAPFs) and Assam Rifles, for ex-Agniveers.
Ex-Agniveers shall be granted a three-year age relaxation above the prescribed upper age limit in the relevant/applicable recruitment rules. headline: Ex-district judge, 90, kept under ‘digital arrest’, cheated of ₹2.5 cr in Jaipur
full_text:
Ex-district judge, 90, kept under ‘digital arrest’, cheated of ₹2.5 cr in Jaipur
A 90-year-old retired district judge in Jaipur was allegedly kept under ‘digital arrest’ for 15 days and duped of ₹2.5 crore by fake CBI, RBI officials.
A 90-year-old retired district judge in Rajasthan’s Jaipur was allegedly kept under “digital arrest” for nearly 15 days and cheated of around ₹2.5 crore by unidentified people posing as Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) officers and Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officials, police said.
Police officers said that the fraudsters allegedly threatened to arrest Ganpat Singh Bhandari in connection with a purported ₹50-crore hawala transaction and kept him under constant surveillance through video calls, pressuring him to transfer money to multiple bank accounts.
Bhandari’s nephew, Ravindra Singh Mohanaut, lodged a complaint with the Jyoti Nagar police station.
Also Read: Reel creator held in ₹10.74 crore ‘digital arrest’ fraud
Received phone call from ‘cop’
According to the complaint, Bhandari received a WhatsApp video call on July 28 from a man dressed in a police uniform who introduced himself as a CBI officer posted in Mumbai.
The caller claimed that a ₹50-crore hawala transaction had been detected in Mumbai and that ₹40 lakh from the proceeds had been deposited into Bhandari’s State Bank of India (SBI) account.
The caller allegedly threatened Bhandari with arrest and told him that he would be taken to Mumbai if he failed to cooperate with the investigation. The fraudsters also threatened to implicate one of his family members, creating fear of arrest and public embarrassment.
The accused allegedly remained in constant contact with him through video calls. At different stages, they posed as CBI officers and RBI managers and told him that his bank accounts were being investigated in connection with a serious financial crime.
Also Read: CBI court denies bail to mule account holder in ₹2-crore digital arrest fraud case
‘Delete chats, call logs’
Bhandari was allegedly instructed to follow their directions until the purported investigation was completed and warned against discussing the matter with his family or anyone else. He was allegedly warned that disclosing details of the purported investigation or communicating with family members could lead to legal action against him.
He was also asked to delete WhatsApp chats, call logs and other messages after every interaction. Under pressure, Bhandari allegedly complied for several days.
The complaint further mentions that Bhandari transferred around ₹2.5 crore to different bank accounts specified by the callers between August 3 and August 10. When the former judge reached SBI’s Johri Bazaar branch on Wednesday morning to transfer the funds, the bank manager grew suspicious.
After questioning him about the transaction and learning the circumstances, the manager stopped the transfer and alerted Bhandari that this might be a cyber fraud. The former judge then contacted his nephew.
Jyoti Nagar Station House Officer (SHO) Gunjan Verma said, “We received a complaint in this regard on Wednesday and have recorded the victim’s statement. We have also succeeded in putting around ₹14 lakh on hold.”
“We are investigating the remaining amount to ascertain how the money was transferred and subsequently withdrawn. Further investigation is underway,” she added.
Police are examining the bank accounts used in the transactions and attempting to trace the people behind the alleged cyber fraud.

headline: Kurukshetra man stabbed to death in Germany, had planned to visit home on Diwali
full_text:
Kurukshetra man stabbed to death in Germany, had planned to visit home on Diwali
The deceased’s sister Noni said she had already sent a Rakhi for her brother and Vishu had promised to give her a ring on Raksha Bandhan.
A 25-year-old man from Kurukshetra was allegedly stabbed to death in Frankfurt, Germany, by a group of three men on Tuesday, his family said on Thursday.
The motive of the murder is yet to be ascertained. The man, who was identified as Vishu Sharma from Mahadev Mohalla, last spoke to his family on Monday.
Vishu’s father Neeraj Sharma, who works at a jewellery shop, said: "We did not hear from him on Tuesday and learnt of his death on Wednesday morning from his roommate Gaurav. He said Vishu had injuries on his body. After some time, Gaurav switched off his phone. Then, we sent one of our relatives living in Germany to the hospital to identify him.”
He added: “I was told that on Tuesday, a group of three men called Vishu outside his room and stabbed him to death, after which Gaurav rushed my son to the hospital.”
Vishu’s family said he had left for Portugal in November 2022 and was due to come home this Diwali. They added that they spent approximately ₹20 lakh and sold a plot of land to send him to Portugal in search of a good job.
After a year, Vishu shifted to France, where he underwent six months of military training and served in the French Army for about a year. After leaving the French Army, he moved to Germany and began working in the delivery sector, his family said.
Neeraj said his son had formed a team of delivery workers who worked under his supervision.
The deceased’s sister Noni said she had already sent a Rakhi for her brother and Vishu had promised to give her a ring on Raksha Bandhan.
Vishu's uncle and former councillor Nitin Bhardwaj said the family is now completing formalities to bring his mortal remains to India.

headline: Bihar CM announces job, compensation for Bharat Tiwari's family after interim probe
full_text:
Bihar CM announces job, compensation for Bharat Tiwari's family after interim probe
Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced financial assistance and a government job for Bharat Tiwari's family after an interim judicial inquiry report. The relief comes while the probe into Tiwari's Bhojpur encounter death continues amid conflicting claims by his family and the police.
Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has announced financial assistance for the family of Bharat Tiwari and a government job for one of his family members, based on the interim findings of a judicial inquiry into his death during a police encounter in Bhojpur.
The decision comes as a judicial probe headed by retired Patna High Court judge Justice Vinod Kumar Sinha continues to examine the circumstances surrounding Tiwari's death in the June 17 encounter.
According to the Bihar government, the financial assistance and government employment will be provided on the basis of the interim report submitted by the inquiry commission.
Justice Sinha has been leading the inquiry into the incident, during which the commission has recorded statements from Tiwari's family members and other witnesses, besides examining evidence related to the encounter.
GOVT TO GIVE FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE: BIHAR CM
Announcing the relief, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said the state government had decided to extend financial assistance to the bereaved family and provide a government job to one eligible family member in line with the interim findings of the judicial inquiry.
The circumstances surrounding Bharat Tiwari's death have remained under scrutiny since the June 17 encounter in Bhojpur. While his family has alleged that the encounter was staged, the police have maintained that their actions were lawful and have stood by their version of the incident.
The judicial inquiry was constituted to independently examine the sequence of events and ascertain the facts surrounding the encounter. The commission is expected to submit its final findings after completing its examination of evidence and witness testimonies.
The government's announcement is expected to provide interim relief to Tiwari's family while the inquiry remains underway. Officials said any further action in the case would depend on the conclusions and recommendations contained in the final report of the judicial commission headed by Justice Vinod Kumar Sinha.

headline: Former Punjab deputy CM Sukhbir Singh Badal attacked with kirpan from 'close range' outside Nanded gurdwara
full_text:
Former Punjab deputy CM Sukhbir Singh Badal attacked with kirpan from 'close range' outside Nanded gurdwara
Former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhbir Singh Badal was rushed to Yashosai Hospital in Nanded after being attacked by a Nihang.
Shiromani Akali Dal president and former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhbir Singh Badal was reportedly attacked by a Nihang at Gurdwara Mata Sahib Kaur on the outskirts of Nanded, Maharashtra, on Thursday. Badal sustained an injury to his hand and was rushed to a nearby hospital for treatment.
The incident took place around 15 km from the main Gurdwara Nanded Sahib, one of the five Takhts, or temporal seats, of Sikhism. Badal was reportedly heading towards the langar hall after paying obeisance at the gurdwara when he was attacked with a kirpan.
The gurdwara is controlled by a Nihang samparday and is not managed by the board that oversees the main Nanded Sahib gurdwara. Following the attack, Badal was shifted to the nearby Yashosai Hospital.
Deep Dive
A viral video following the incident showed Badal walking inside a building with a saffron-coloured cloth wrapped around his right hand.
Badal had arrived in Nanded on Wednesday with his family and a group of close associates as part of a three-day visit. He was inside the gurdwara with his wife, Harsimrat Kaur Badal, a Shiromani Akali Dal MP.
SAD calls it ‘close-range’ attack
The Shiromani Akali Dal described the incident as a “close-range” attack and said Sukhbir Singh Badal was doing fine and remained in “Chardi Kala”, or high spirits, after the incident.
SAD spokesperson Arshdeep Singh Kler said the attacker, dressed in Nihang attire, attempted to target Badal but was stopped by security personnel accompanying the SAD chief. Badal is a Z-category security protectee.
Kler said Badal suffered a minor injury to his arm and was undergoing treatment at a hospital. “Badal sustained a minor injury on his arm and is undergoing treatment at a hospital. He is completely fine and in 'Chardi Kala' (high spirits),” he said.
A local official in Nanded said Badal received two to three stitches on his hand.
Kler said Maharashtra Police would investigate the incident as it took place in the state and determine whether there was any conspiracy behind the attack.
Alleging that “panthic leaders” were being targeted repeatedly, Kler said, “Some 'panth virodhi' (anti-panth) forces are hatching such conspiracies.”
BJP condemns incident
BJP spokesperson RP Singh condemned the attack, calling the incident “completely unacceptable” and saying that violence has no place in a democratic society.
Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has ordered an inquiry into the reported attack on Shiromani Akali Dal chief and former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhbir Singh Badal at a gurdwara in Nanded, reported news agency PTI.
In a post on X, he wrote, "Punjab and the Punjabi community have already suffered immensely during the dark and painful years of violence and militancy. Generations of Punjabis have borne the deep scars left by that period. We cannot, under any circumstances, allow those dark days to return. Peace, brotherhood, constitutional values and the rule of law must always prevail.
I pray for the good health, safety and speedy recovery of S Sukhbir Singh Badal Ji."
2024 assassination bid
This is the second reported attack on Sukhbir Singh Badal in less than two years. On December 4, 2024, Badal survived an assassination bid when former militant Narain Singh Chaura allegedly fired at him from close range at the entrance of the Golden Temple in Amritsar.
The bullet narrowly missed Badal after a security officer intervened and grabbed the pistol, causing the shot to hit the shrine wall. No one was injured in the incident, and Chaura was overpowered and arrested.

headline: Onion procurement lags after system overhaul
full_text:
Onion procurement lags after system overhaul
A major overhaul of India’s onion procurement system this year slowed government purchases for weeks despite an early start to stock-building, forcing authorities to relax quality specifications and repeatedly raise procurement prices to accelerate buying.
This has troubled the consumer affairs ministry so much so that the ministry had recently for the sixth time raised procurement prices to ₹23.35 per kg.
The government, as of July 7, had procured only around 13,000 tonnes of onion against a target of 200,000 tonnes, even though procurement began on May 15, a senior government official told HT on the condition of anonymity. However, after relaxing the quality grade norms, procurement rose to 115,000 tonnes as of Thursday.
According to officials, the slow pace was largely driven by changes introduced this year to curb irregularities in procurement and storage.
Until last year, procurement and storage were both handled by the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India (Nafed) and the National Cooperative Consumers’ Federation of India (NCCF) through local agencies. This year, however, storage responsibility was shifted to the Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC).
“CWC initially enforced quality norms very strictly and rejected a large quantity of onions offered at procurement centres. This affected procurement,” the senior official stated above said.
Consumer affairs secretary Nidhi Khare, however, told HT that the change was aimed at eliminating an inherent conflict of interest in the system.
“Till last year, both procurement and storage of onions were handled by Nafed and NCCF through local agencies selected by them. This had an inherent problem of conflict of interest. CWC has been roped in to handle storage primarily to resolve this issue,” Khare said.
The changes were introduced after repeated concerns over procurement irregularities. Officials familiar with the matter said issues ranged from middlemen inflating prices and only “on paper transactions” to genuine farmers being excluded from procurement operations.
The stricter scrutiny, however, coincided with quality challenges in this year’s crop. Unseasonal rains during harvesting in Maharashtra resulted in a larger share of onions with single skins, partial discolouration and sunburn damage, leading to higher rejection rates at procurement centres, Khare said.
Faced with poor procurement, the government was eventually forced to dilute its quality requirements. The government had initially allowed procurement only of Grade A onions, which are premium-quality bulbs suitable for long-term storage. But as procurement lagged, authorities eased the specifications.
“Slight relaxation has been provided in Grade A specifications and we call it Grade-URS (Under Relaxed Specification). Grade-URS is far superior to what is generally considered Grade B,” Khare explained.
Rising prices pushed onion inflation to 22.5% in July, up from the 4.7% it stood at in June.

headline: NHPC flagged methane risk months before Sikkim's Teesta VI blast that killed 25, show documents
full_text:
NHPC flagged methane risk months before Sikkim's Teesta VI blast that killed 25, show documents
NHPC documents show methane was flagged as a risk months before the Teesta VI blast killed 25 workers in July.
NHPC Ltd had flagged methane as a risk at the Teesta VI hydropower project in Sikkim months before a methane explosion in an under-construction tunnel killed 25 workers on July 20, documents on the company’s website show. The documents record a methane leak in January and show that safety measures and equipment to monitor the gas were subsequently recommended and sought.
The blast occurred in the head-race tunnel (HRT) of the 500-MW Teesta VI project in Namchi district. NHPC said it was caused by a “sudden burst of suspected methane gas” trapped inside the rocks, leading to an explosion, dense fumes and toxic gases. Twenty-five workers trapped after a rockfall blocked the tunnel died. A detailed investigation into the incident is still underway.
Also read: 12 dead, 13 still trapped after suspected methane explosion in Sikkim tunnel; toll may rise
Methane leak reported months before fatal blast
An NHPC document prepared to justify nomination-basis contract awards for April-June 2026 records that on January 14 there was “a sudden leak of flammable methane gas during heading excavation at HRT Face 4A”.
“Several personnel from the executing agency….suffered burn injuries in the incident. Consequently, excavation work was suspended with immediate effect..” the document said.
A subsequent safety audit by CSIR’s Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research (CSIR-CIMFR) recommended strict implementation of handheld, rugged methanometers for real-time monitoring. “The CSIR-CIMFR team advised that tunnelling may proceed safely if the effective protocols viz effective ventilation management, continuous monitoring, procurement of DGMS approved, handheld rugged methanometers for real-time site assessment are strictly implemented,” it stated.
It is not clear from the documents whether all these recommendations had been fully implemented before work resumed.
Also read: Rescue on as 27 workers trapped in Sikkim tunnel after landslides
Equipment procurement, calibration timeline unclear
NHPC documents show that the Ministry of Power issued a tender on June 17 for quarterly calibration of three methanometer-cum-toximeter units for two years at the project. The documents do not establish when the equipment was procured or whether all three units were operational on July 20.
More significantly, an expression of interest (EOI) issued by NHPC on July 10, just 10 days before the explosion, sought expert agencies to address challenges affecting excavation, including “seepage, ingress of water/slush, cavity formation, face collapses, and the presence of methane gas”.
Also read: Toxic gases slow rescue ops in South Sikkim tunnel blast, toll reaches 15
Experts question preparedness, seek independent probe
Experts said the documents raise questions about whether adequate safety measures were in place despite NHPC being aware of the methane risk, and sought independent and transparent investigation.
“If the details of methane gas leaks and its problems were well known, it shows NHPC has once again failed in basic monitoring and preparedness. Such incidents will continue as long as there is no accountability established through independent investigation,” said Himanshu Thakkar, Coordinator at South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers & People (SANDRP).
HT reached out to NHPC for comment, including on the implementation of the safety recommendations, availability of methane-monitoring equipment and preparedness at the site, but no immediate response was available.
“A detailed investigation will be undertaken to ascertain the cause of the incident. We remain committed and are extending full support to the rescue agencies and the affected families..” NHPC had said in a statement after the incident.

headline: Andhra:2018 Andhra Group-I exam riddled with irregularities, say SIT probe
full_text:
Andhra:2018 Andhra Group-I exam riddled with irregularities, say SIT probe
Amaravati, An SIT probing the 2018 Andhra Pradesh Group-I recruitment examination has uncovered alleged irregularities across multiple stages of evaluation, including the use of unauthorised evaluators, purported manual evaluation at a private resort and widespread alterations in OMR evaluation sheets.
The probe pertains to Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission's recruitment of 169 Group- I posts through a notification issued in 2018. It attracted more than 1.14 lakh applications.
"An SIT probing the 2018 Andhra Pradesh Group-I recruitment examination, the state's premier civil services examination has uncovered serious irregularities across multiple stages," said a press release.
The SIT was constituted by the Andhra Pradesh government in February 2026, following directions from the High Court to scientifically examine allegations of tampering and irregularities in the recruitment process.
According to the SIT, alleged irregularities had occurred during three separate evaluation exercises - the original digital valuation in 2021, a purported manual valuation conducted at a private resort following a High Court order, and a second manual valuation conducted at Vijayawada in 2022 during the erstwhile YSRCP government.
During the digital evaluation, the SIT alleged that unauthorised evaluators, private e-mail and mark discrepancies had occurred, adding that the first major irregularities arose during digital evaluation of the mains stage of the examination.
"The SIT found that the decision to introduce digital evaluation, as well as the panel of evaluators engaged for the exercise did not carry the mandatory approval of the PSC Chairman," said the press release.
Out of a secretary-approved panel of 158 evaluators, only 72 actually evaluated the answer scripts while another 25 persons who were not on the approved panel also evaluated answer scripts and were paid, the SIT claimed.
The approved panel itself predominantly consisted of teachers and lecturers from private schools and colleges instead of the university-level subject experts contemplated by the PSC Office Manual, it said.
The digital evaluation was coordinated through an unofficial private e-mail account, personal email accounts and Google Drive links, said the SIT.
The probe noted alleged differences between marks originally entered by the evaluators and the marks reflected in the final digital-result database.
The SIT noted that the second-evaluation marks were allegedly entered in several cases without an independent second examiner, with one freelancer, Mahamkali Raghuram, making such entries himself.
The SIT observed that the PSC paid ₹1.38 crore to Stone Media Advisory Services and TrueGrader for the digital evaluation exercise, adding that Raghuram received approximately ₹10 lakh towards evaluation and coordination work.
Following candidates challenging the digital evaluation in the High Court, it ordered a manual evaluation, observing that the notified methodology to digital valuation was contrary to the recruitment notification.
Later, the SIT noted that manual evaluation was undertaken at a private resort, which was not a government office but a private space, where "manual evaluation" amounted to only allegedly re-entering the earlier digital marks.
According to the SIT, answer scripts had remained in a private agency's custody for 84 days and accused the then PSC secretary PSR Anjaneyulu over the manual evaluation irregularities.
Further, it noted that the second manual evaluation was conducted in Vijayawada after D Gautam Sawang took charge of the PSC in February 2022.
However, the SIT alleged that there was no documentary record supporting the policy decision of the then PSC chairman, Sawang, to conduct the second manual evaluation.
In the second manual evaluation, the SIT claimed that there were several discrepancies, such as alleged 95 percent alterations or over-writings, different inks and handwritings and others.
Highlighting that forensic material was examined by Central Forensic Science Laboratory in Hyderabad, New Delhi, Shimla, Pune, Bhopal, Kolkata and Guwahati, the SIT raised concerns over the custody and surveillance of confidential examination material.
It found that there was allegedly no CCTV coverage over the PSC Confidential Sections or the Strong Room during the original examination period.
"During the fresh manual valuation in 2022, cameras were initially installed only in two confidential-section rooms. The Strong Room itself came under CCTV only on April 11, 2022 17 days after valuation began," said the press release.
Even after cameras were installed, the SIT found multiple alleged inconsistencies between CCTV footage and the official Guard Register.
The SIT additionally found that most examiners were allegedly using mobile phones inside the manual evaluation camps and another inconsistency was the unusually large number of answer scripts that required a third evaluation.
According to PSC, only 0.45 percent of scripts required third evaluation in the previous Group-I recruitment, compared with alleged 10.2 percent in the 2018 recruitment process.
"The SIT said that while this alone could not establish wrongdoing, the dramatic increase, taken together with over-writing, unauthenticated corrections, signature mismatches and other forensic irregularities, indicated serious inconsistency in the evaluation process," the release said.
A criminal case was registered in April 2025 under Sections 409, 477-A, 420 and 120-B read with Section 34 of the IPC.
Camsign Media Director P Madhusudhan Rao was arrested in May 2025, while Anjaneyulu was secured on a Prisoner Transit Warrant for investigation.
The SIT examined 173 witnesses, and the investigation includes forensic reports, financial records, WhatsApp communications, electronic data, valuation records, videos and reconstruction of the evaluation processes at both the resort and Vijayawada.

‘What if all legal cockroaches came together?’: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke recalls first post amid CJI-NALSAR row
Abhijeet Dipke has teased a possible campaign seeking the resignation of BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra.
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has brought back the slogan that launched his satirical movement, this time turning to the legal fraternity amid the ongoing row between the Bar Council of India (BCI) and NALSAR University of Law.
The BCI on Thursday directed state bar councils not to enrol any of the NALSAR 2026 graduates after students opposed Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant’s invitation as chief guest at the university’s convocation.
“What if all legal cockroaches come together?” Dipke posted on X, reacting to the BCI’s decision to halt the enrolment of law graduates as advocates.
The council withdrew the blanket enrolment ban hours later.
From ‘all cockroaches’ to ‘legal cockroaches’
Dipke’s latest post carries a reference to the origins of the CJP movement. The movement began in May after CJI Surya Kant, during a hearing, referred to the youth of the country as “cockroaches”.
Dipke, located in the US at the time, posed online the now-famous question: “What if all the cockroaches come together?” The post evolved into the Cockroach Janta Party, a satirical youth movement that went on to attract a large following and eventually organise protests across the country.
Massive student-led demonstrations over paper leaks, student suicides and reform in the examination system ultimately forced the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.
Dipke had earlier publicly thanked CJI Surya Kant for the remark that inspired the movement. He said at a Jantar Mantar protest that he would not have returned to India or started the campaign had he not been called a “cockroach”.
With the BCI-NALSAR controversy once again involving CJI Surya Kant, Dipke seems to have returned to the same metaphor.
ALSO READ | ‘Jantar Mantar Season 2 going to start very soon’: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke's big remark
Dipke also appeared to tease a possible campaign seeking the resignation of BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra. “Time for Manan Mishra isteefa do? (resign)," he wrote on X.
‘Legal cockroaches unite’: CJP
The founder's post also saw a response from CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das. “Much needed,” he said.
"The Bar Council of India needs to be looked into. Manan Mishra has been its Chairman since 2012. What has he done? Needs to be accounted for. All legal cockroaches, your task is cut out. Let’s fix BCI’s accountability. Let’s fix Mishra’s accountability. #LegalCockroachesUnite,” Das wrote on X.
CJP on the CJI-NALSAR controversy
Das separately criticised the BCI's action against the NALSAR graduates. He said it was “grossly disproportionate, deeply troubling, and prima facie indefensible”.
“Students cannot be collectively penalised for expressing dissent over a ceremonial invitation. The Cockroach Janta Party condemns this order,” Das said.
He also warned that if BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra did not withdraw the order, CJP would mobilise law students, advocates, senior lawyers and its supporters to protest outside the BCI office and Mishra’s official residence.
Mishra later responded to the protest threat: “Council has already withdrawn that letter.”
Das, though, claimed the order had not been fully withdrawn. He said the BCI’s new letter still sought the names of students and called for an inquiry against them.
“IMMEDIATELY withdraw that entire letter,” Das wrote on X and demanded no NALSAR student face an inquiry for expressing dissent against CJI Surya Kant.
He also said the CJP’s protest call would remain in place until the BCI withdrew the letter completely and assured that no action would be taken against the students.
The CJP also demanded the BCI withdraw, rather than modify, its order. On X, the CJP said the BCI initially barred the entire 2026 graduating batch from practising law after around 70 students wrote a letter questioning the invitation to CJI Surya Kant as convocation guest.
While the BCI later modified the order and allowed the students to enrol, the party pointed out that the inquiry into the students and teachers involved was still continuing.
Calling it a “witch hunt”, the CJP demanded that the BCI withdraw the letter completely and guarantee that no student would face action for peacefully expressing dissent. It also said that BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra was a sitting BJP Rajya Sabha member, and said, “We will NOT stay silent.”
What is the BCI-NALSAR row?
The row began after a section of NALSAR students objected to CJI Surya Kant being invited as chief guest for the university’s convocation.
A group of 70 final-year LLB students first submitted a representation on July 23, with students from other batches later supporting it. The students cited concerns over remarks made by the CJI during a Supreme Court hearing on alleged police violence against student protesters in Delhi.
On Thursday, the BCI responded by directing all state bar councils not to enrol any of NALSAR’s 2026 graduates and sought a report identifying those behind the campaign.
This triggered vast criticism over the collective enrolment freeze. Hours later, BCI chairman Mishra withdrew the blanket ban and said the vast majority of students were innocent and should not suffer for the actions of a few.

headline: The Kochi Corporation will recommend to the State government a Vigilance probe into the alleged lapses in the construction of G. Memorial, built in memory of poet G. Sankara Kurup, and the P&T Apartment Complex, which have led to their present squali...
full_text:
The Kochi Corporation will recommend to the State government a Vigilance probe into the alleged lapses in the construction of G. Memorial, built in memory of poet G. Sankara Kurup, and the P&T Apartment Complex, which have led to their present squalid condition.
Mayor V.K. Minimol announced this while responding to a discussion at the Corporation council meeting on Thursday, where ruling United Democratic Front councillors launched scathing criticism over alleged corruption, particularly in the case of the G Memorial. The memorial, set up at a cost of nearly ₹6 crore, was inaugurated by former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan in February 2024.
Ms. Minimol said the Public Works department had submitted a report denying that construction activity in the neighbourhood had caused the memorial to tilt, while the consultancy concerned claimed that increased vehicular movement during construction was responsible. “Those accountable for the inferior construction cannot be spared, as it will send a wrong message to future endeavours. They should also be made to bear the cost of the rectifications required,” she said.
V.A. Sreejith, LDF parliamentary party leader, said that while shortcomings must be addressed, the issue should not be reduced to an attempt to blame the previous LDF council and former Mayor M. Anilkumar, who had taken the initiative to construct the memorial, as ruling councillors tried to do during the discussion. Earlier, UDF parliamentary party secretary M.G. Aristotle alleged that the memorial had been reduced to a symbol of corruption. He questioned why the original design was altered to include an open-air stage in a State where it rains for nearly six months a year. He further alleged that the memorial had one of the highest construction costs per square foot in the country, at over ₹8,000.
Ms. Minimol also pointed out that the Compressed Biogas (CBG) plant at Brahmapuram has been processing an average of 50 tonnes of waste per day, against its promised optimum capacity of 150 tonnes a day since commissioning. BPCL-KR, which funded the project, has asked the Corporation to ensure waste of 97% purity, free of plastic and other non-biodegradable components. She said the sanitation committee must ensure proper segregation at source by holding meetings with residents’ associations. The tendency to mix food waste with other refuse, such as sanitary napkins, should be identified and traced to the health circles concerned.
“Even then, it will take time before the plant achieves its optimum capacity, as BPCL will have to tackle issues such as arranging land for handling residues and disposing of slurry left behind after treatment,” she added.

headline: Kudumbashree is set to add flavour to the Onam celebrations through its Onasadya this year too.
full_text:
Kudumbashree is set to add flavour to the Onam celebrations through its Onasadya this year too.
Nearly 400 women entrepreneurs running canteen and catering units across the State will prepare the Onasadya. Customers can choose the dishes and payasams they want if they order the sadya in advance.
The sadya will comprise rice, sambar, aviyal, koottu curry, thoran, olan, kalan, pachadi, kichadi, pulinji, rasam, buttermilk, pickle, sarkaravaratti, banana chips, pappadom, banana, and payasam. The prices start from Rs.170. The minimum order is five sadyas.
Orders can also be placed for ada prathaman, palada prathaman, and parippu payasam, beginning with half a litre.
Bookings have begun in all districts through a call centre and the Kudumbashree community development society (CDS) concerned. The sadya will be supplied by the Kudumbashree entrepreneur in the vicinity of the person placing the order.
Orders will also be accepted for sadyas as part of Onam celebrations organised by government and quasi government organisations, private organisations, banks, schools, residents’ associations and so on.
For orders, contact the Kudumbashree district mission offices or CDS offices concerned.

headline: Congress, SP, TMC boycott customary meet with Speaker after acrimonious session
full_text:
Congress, SP, TMC boycott customary meet with Speaker after acrimonious session
A Congress leader said they have nothing against the Speaker but avoided joining the meeting as nothing substantial was discussed
The Congress, Samajwadi Party (SP) and Trinamool Congress (TMC) boycotted the customary meeting with Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla after the acrimonious monsoon session of Parliament ended on Thursday.
A Congress leader said the three parties decided not to attend the courtesy meeting. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and other top leaders attended the meeting. “We have nothing against the Speaker. But we wanted to avoid joining the meeting as nothing substantial was discussed in the session. Bills were passed in din. Our demand for debates on police excess against students and donation theft in Ayodhya remained unfulfilled,” said the leader.
Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition, has not attended these meetings over the past few sessions. In December, Congress lawmaker Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined the customary meetings over tea and interacted with Modi over issues of Kerala and Wayanad, her parliamentary constituency, in the southern state.
The TMC boycotted the Thursday meeting as its petitions to Birla for the disqualification of the 20 defectors remain pending. The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam attended the meeting.
The monsoon session was largely washed out, with the Opposition insisting on Shah’s statement in the House over allegations of police excesses and the use of pellet guns during the July 20 protest march, demanding then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.

headline: Engaged couple, working in same bank, found dead hours apart in two different states
full_text:
Engaged couple, working in same bank, found dead hours apart in two different states
P Anushree, 25, and her fiancé V Amal, 26, were planning to marry in December.
A young couple who worked for the same bank were found dead in Kerala and Karnataka within hours of each other, police said on Thursday.
P Anushree, 25, from Poochakkad in Kasaragod, and her fiancé V Amal, 26, from Iritty in Kannur, had just gotten engaged and were planning to marry in December, PTI reported. Anushree was posted at a bank branch in Karnataka, while Amal was working at the bank's Ernakulam branch.
ALSO READ | Till death do us part: African couple found dead in each other's arms in Delhi hotel fire
Woman found dead in Hunsur, husband in Ernakulam
Anushree was found dead at her accommodation in Hunsur, Karnataka, police said. Her body was taken to her Kasaragod home after a post-mortem and cremated on Wednesday evening.
Amal had been staying in Ernakulam with friends. Police said he appeared to have checked into a lodge on Wednesday after learning about Anushree's death.
He was later found dead in a hotel room. Ernakulam North police suspect he died by suicide. No suicide note was found, and investigators said the exact circumstances surrounding the deaths would be known only after a detailed probe.
Police will also examine Amal's mobile phone as part of the investigation, PTI reported.
Similar incident
In a separate incident, a 24-year-old woman died after falling from the 16th floor of a high-rise in Sector 110, Noida, on Sunday. Her 28-year-old husband was arrested on charges of dowry death after her family accused him of demanding dowry.
READ ALSO | 24-yr-old newlywed jumps to death in Noida; husband arrested over dowry charges
Police said the couple belonged to different faiths and had been in a relationship for around two years before getting married on July 11. They had moved into their Sector 110 residence from another housing society in Noida only last month.
The woman, a resident of Etah, worked at a call centre, while her 28-year-old husband, who is from Dehradun, Uttarakhand, worked as a video editor at a private company in Noida.
The incident took place at around 5:30pm on Sunday. A security guard alerted the police after the woman fell from the building, following which officers reached the residential society and identified her with the help of residents.
An investigator said police went to the couple's flat after the incident and found the husband asleep.
“When we approached her flat, her husband, who was asleep, opened the flat. He was shocked to learn of the incident,” the investigator said, requesting anonymity.
After being informed about the death, the woman's family members allegedly accused her husband of demanding dowry.

headline: House panel criticises Union government’s flagship welfare support for fisherfolk
full_text:
House panel criticises Union government’s flagship welfare support for fisherfolk
The panel said only about 2.1% of the estimated 28 million fisherfolk received assistance during the annual fishing ban between 2020 and 2025
A parliamentary panel has criticised the Union government’s flagship welfare support for traditional fisherfolk, noting that only about 2.1% or 595,000 of the country’s estimated 28 million fishers received financial assistance during the annual fishing ban between 2020 and 2025.
An annual 61-day fishing ban is enforced along India’s coastal waters to protect fish during their peak breeding and spawning seasons. The period differs for the country’s east and west coasts.
The Standing Committee on Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Food Processing said the performance of the livelihood and nutritional support component under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) was “dismally low”, despite the scheme being intended to cushion income loss during the ban.
Under the current PMMSY design, the Union government provides ₹3,000 annually for each enrolled beneficiary. The beneficiary contributes ₹1,500, taking the total annual assistance to ₹4,500, which is disbursed by the respective states or Union territories.
The committee said it was “very disheartening” that such a small proportion of fisherfolk had benefited despite the scheme being operational for five years. It rejected the argument that low coverage was primarily because many were not registered under the scheme.
The panel cited the current economic parameters and inflation and recommended an increase in the financial assistance during the fishing ban to at least ₹10,000 per fisher per year without any annual contribution from fishermen. It urged immediate measures to significantly expand the reach of the scheme.
In its action taken report, the fisheries department said a proposal to enhance financial assistance had been prepared for implementation from financial year 2025-26. It added that it depended on the availability of fiscal space and approval of the competent authority or the Union Cabinet. The department did not indicate the proposed amount of enhanced assistance.
The panel flagged the slow pace of investment in fisheries infrastructure. It noted that India has 1,547 notified fish landing centres, but only 379 have been selected for development as fishing harbours or fish landing centres since 1964. The panel said just 287 of them had been completed by June 2025.
The panel said existing facilities can accommodate 148,000 fishing vessels, against 238,000 active vessels operating in the country. It called the gap significant, and the panel urged the fisheries department to select more landing centres for modernisation, consider relaxing some selection criteria, and speed up project implementation.

headline: As Mayawati's base shrinks, BJP, SP and Congress intensify fight for Dalit votes in UP
full_text:
As Mayawati's base shrinks, BJP, SP and Congress intensify fight for Dalit votes in UP
NEW DELHI: Dalit politics in Uttar Pradesh is at a crossroads. For a very long time, Mayawati and her Bahujan Samaj Party were synonymous with the idea of Dalit vote in UP. Not any more. Mayawatiâs BSP today is a much weaker force. The last three elections in the state have pushed Mayawati, the four-time chief minister of UP, to the margins of state politics. This has opened up the Dalit space and triggered an interesting scramble among political parties for a slice of the Dalit pie in the 2027 assembly elections.So, we have the BJP playing the name-change game in Bhadohi and organising a 7-month campaign to honour 15th-century saint-poet Sant Ravi Das. Then we have Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav announcing 14 extra seats for the Dalits to cement his PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) politics. Congress too is trying to win back voters it lost decades ago. Then there is Chandrashekhar Azad, who is trying to consolidate his own space in the state.As Uttar Pradesh heads towards 2027, the question is: if the BSP continues to lose ground, where does Mayawatiâs old support base go and which of her rivals stands to gain the most?
From 206 seats to one: How BSP lost ground
The BSPâs rise in UP politics was as dramatic as its fall. The party was founded by Kanshi Ram in 1984 with the idea of giving Dalits and other marginalized communities an independent voice.
Mayawati, who emerged as his political successor, took the BSP to great heights in Uttar Pradesh. Under her leadership, the BSP won a majority on its own in the 2007 assembly elections, winning 206 seats with a vote share of 30.43%.Dalits, who constitute around 21% of UPâs population as per the 2021 census, have for years been the core base of Mayawatiâs Bahujan Samaj Party. But that dynamic has now changed.BSP is a much weaker force today. Mayawati has failed to mobilise Dalit support for her BSP in the last two elections in the state, thereby opening up the space for other political contenders. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BSP could win just 1 seat with a vote share of 12.88%. This was a sharp decline from the 19 seats and a 22.23% vote share that Mayawati had got in 2017.The 2024 Lok Sabha elections went on to showcase that Mayawatiâs dismal 2022 performance was not an aberration. The BSP supremo failed to win even one Lok Sabha seat, while her partyâs vote share dipped to 9.4% from 19.43% in 2019. Clearly, the results reinforced the gradual decline in BSPâs influence among Dalits.As Mayawati gears up for the 2027 assembly challenge, she faces an uphill road. The BSP chief has not just lost support of voters, but also control over her party. So, when Mayawati issued a stern message that all the candidates for the upcoming poll will be finalised by her and not by her nephew Akash Anand, it was an indication of the internal tussle in her party.Akash Anand, who has been in and out of Mayawatiâs favour in the past, launched the partyâs 2027 assembly poll campaign from Sadabad in Hathras this week.Mayawati, who has often been accused of helping the BJP, has ruled out any pre-poll alliance. She has claimed that some candidates have already been finalised for the upcoming assembly elections. Mayawati has asked party cadres to start rebuilding the party and drum up OBC support ahead of the polls. The cadres have apparently been asked to remind people of the party's past governance and convince them that the real benefit and welfare of the OBC community lie with the BSP and its "iron lady government".Mayawati, however, must consider that it will be difficult for the BSP to come back to power only by holding on to its core Dalit vote alone. It will have to recreate the Dalit-OBC combination that originally carried Mayawati to power in Lucknow with a majority of her own.
BJP's Dalit outreach gets sharper ahead of 2027
One interesting fallout of BSPâs decline has been the BJPâs aggressive outreach to woo the Dalits. When Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath announced the renaming of Bhadohi district as Sant Ravidas Nagar last month, he put the BJP right at the middle of the Dalit outreach battle ahead of 2027 polls.The move also revived an old political contest over name-change politics. Mayawati was the one who had renamed Bhadohi as Sant Ravidas Nagar in December 1997. Akhilesh Yadav restored the old name in 2014. Now, by bringing Sant Ravidas Nagar back, Yogi sought to make a bigger political point, accusing the SP of erasing a Dalit symbol while positioning the BJP as a party willing to restore it.Mayawati publicly welcomed the decision, a rare moment of agreement with the ruling party. She was quick, however, to remind voters that it was her government that had changed the district's name in the first place and that the decision was later reversed under Akhilesh.The party realises that Dalit votes are up for grabs and hence is going all out to woo them. The partyâs 'Samrasta Sankalp Abhiyanâ appears planned to coincide with assembly elections in two key states, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, early next year.Both these states have a sizeable population of Dalits who play an important role in many constituencies. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BJP and its ally Apna Dal (Soneylal) together bagged 63 Scheduled Caste (SC) seats compared to 20 won by the then Samajwadi Party-led opposition alliance. But the 2024 Lok Sabha polls changed the dynamics, with the SP and the Congress winning 43 of the 80 seats in the state and pushing the BJP to make an aggressive outreach. The loss of Faizabad seat to SP's Awadhesh Prasad, a Pasi leader, was particularly significant and gave Akhilesh Yadav fresh ammunition for his PDA pitch.Earlier this year, the Yogi Adityanath government approved the âDr B R Ambedkar Murti Vikas Yojna" under which Rs 1 crore is to be allocated to each of the state's 403 assembly constituencies for the beautification and development of statues of social reformers.The BJP's efforts to woo Dalits has also been visible in its recent Cabinet expansion. Of the six new ministers inducted into the Yogi government, two were Dalits, Krishna Paswan from the Pasi community and Surendra Singh Daler from the Valmiki community. Three others were from OBC groups. Two non-Yadav OBC ministers were also given independent charge.The BJP's primary task ahead of 2027 would be to hold on to the non-Jatav Dalit support it built over the past decade and prevent a repeat of 2024.
SPâs Dalit outreach
The 2024 Lok Sabha elections also showed that the Dalits in UP were ready to back other political parties who wooed them. Dalit support played a key role in the spectacular success of Akhilesh Yadavâs Samajwadi Party, which won 37 seats in 2024.Together with its alliance partner Congress, the INDIA bloc won 43 of the 80 seats in the state, pushing the BJP on the back foot. Akhilesh Yadav, who has centred his politics around PDA (Pichhde, Dalits and Aplasankhyaks), gained from his Dalit outreach in the 2024 elections. His Samajwadi Party fielded two Dalit candidates from general seats. While one of them went on to win the all-important Faizabad seat, the other lost by just 10,585 votes to the BJP in Meerut.
How Samajwadi Party performed when they contested independently
Little wonder, in the run-up to the 2027 assembly elections, Akhilesh has already announced plans to field 14 Dalit candidates from general seats. Uttar Pradesh has 84 seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and two for Scheduled Tribes. With 14 more candidates on general seats, the total tally of reserved candidates for SP will increase to 100. This will help reinforce his message to the Dalits in line with his PDA politics. The move will also help the SP shed the narrative of being a Muslim-Yadav party.
Congress tries to reclaim lost ground
Rahul Gandhi has made it clear that Dalits would now play a 'central role' in Congress. Before Mayawati and the BSP built their massive Dalit vote bank in the 1990s, Congress was the primary choice for Uttar Pradesh's Dalits. For nearly three decades after that, Congress was almost pushed out of UP politics.Rahul Gandhi has started his road to the UP election by acknowledging that the party had failed to take the right steps for the community in the 1980s and 1990s. He even praised Kanshi Ram for bringing Dalits together and giving the community a sense of confidence.Rahul has also made the Constitution a regular part of his social justice pitch. He is often seen carrying the red book of the Constitution while warning that constitutional rights and reservation are under threat. He has repeatedly invoked BR Ambedkar in the same pitch, asserting that Congress wants to position itself as a guardian of the Constitution.The party has also put a Dalit leader in charge of Uttar Pradesh. Rajendra Pal Gautam, who heads the Congressâs Scheduled Castes Department, has been appointed UP in-charge ahead of the 2027 polls. Interestingly, Gautam had also made an unsuccessful attempt to meet Mayawati at her Lucknow residence earlier this year.Whether the party will be able to translate this outreach into votes remains to be seen.
Chandrashekhar Azad adds another claimant
Then there is Chandrashekhar Azad, whose 2024 victory from Nagina made him a prominent figure in UPâs Dalit politics. Unlike BJP, SP or Congress, Azad is trying to build an independent space outside the BSP. His challenge now is to take that appeal beyond one constituency and build an organisation strong enough to matter across the state in 2027.
That is what makes the coming assembly election in Uttar Pradesh interesting. For decades, politics in Uttar Pradesh has revolved around caste. Political parties build their electoral strategies around social coalitions, loyalty of communities and traditional vote base.Mayawati may no longer command the Dalit vote the way she once did, but that vote bank has not disappeared. It simply has more claimants. And in 2027, where those voters eventually move could make a significant difference.

headline: Students of a state-run school blocked a road for nearly seven hours on Thursday in Jharkhand's Garhwa district to protest the transfer of their headmaster, officials said.
full_text:
Students of a state-run school blocked a road for nearly seven hours on Thursday in Jharkhand's Garhwa district to protest the transfer of their headmaster, officials said.
Garhwa District Education Officer (DEO) Jagarnath Lohra said Malay Kumar Singh had been serving as headmaster on deputation at the Kandi Plus-2 High School for nearly two months.
On August 12, Singh was directed to report back to his parent institution, Lawahi Kala High School in Dandai block of the district, he said.
"The students did not want the headmaster to leave the school and staged a protest. Considering their demand, the department has decided not to send him back to his parent institution and allow him to continue serving on deputation at the Kandi Plus-2 High School," Lohra told PTI.
The students ended their protest after receiving the assurance, he said.
Garhwa SP Ashutosh Shekhar said the students initially demonstrated near the school premises, carrying banners and posters demanding that the headmaster be retained.
They later blocked the Kandi-Bhawnathpur Main Road, disrupting traffic for several hours, he said.
"There are also allegations that some students vandalised nearby shops, but no case had been registered as police had not received any complaint," he said.
