headline: What our histories owe to the food that we eat
full_text:
What our histories owe to the food that we eat
Given that we celebrate Independence Day in August, it becomes fashionable to villainise the British
Given that we celebrate Independence Day in August, it becomes fashionable to villainise the British. However, even the most ardent nationalist in this state will doff their Mysore peta to Benjamin Lewis Rice, the administrator-turned antiquarian/ historian in whose memory stands a church on Avenue Road in the heart of Bengaluru, the city where he was born all the way back in 1837.
Rice was educated in England, and held many posts in the Kingdom of Mysore. It was a land he loved and wrote about. Consider this paragraph in his monumental 1897 Mysore Gazetteer: “If there be any truth in the observation that small countries with diversified and distinctive physical characteristics have played the greatest part in the world’s history, and given rise to its most distinguished men, Greece, Palestine, England and others being quoted as instances, Mysore, it seems to me, may fairly claim a place in the category. She is the peculiar home of the sandal and also of teak, a special haunt of the elephant, rears a famous and superior breed of horned cattle, supplies as the staple food of her people the nutrient grain of ragi, was the cradle in India and is still the chief garden for coffee cultivation. Thus in every department of the natural world she may claim some pre-eminence.”
Rice’s records detail a sudden, massive agricultural fluctuation in the ragi-growing belt of Southern Karnataka (including Bangalore and its environs) between 1871 and 1873. It was an abrupt relinquishment of wet rice cultivation in favour of ragi and oilseeds. This wasn’t a culinary whim, but an administrative side effect. The control of irrigation channels and tanks was transferred from local Revenue officers to the Public Works Department to enforce repairs and curb water waste. When the new Revenue Survey rendered all occupied lands liable for tax whether they were actively cultivated or not, the area under wet rice dropped drastically from 1.32 million acres to just half a million. The fields reverted to dry-land ragi, a crop managed with staggering precision, and more importantly, less dependent on water. As the historical chronicler Mark Wilks famously noted, “The whole world does not, perhaps, exhibit a cleaner system of husbandry than that of the cultivation of ragi in the home fields of Mysore.”
Both Rice and Wilks chronicled agriculture. However, if you want to look at the historical zenith of regional gastronomy, you must open the ancient Sanskrit and Kannada shastras. In the 12th-century text Manasollasa, written by the Kalyani Chalukya King Someshvara III, the only sweet deemed worthy of mention is the payasam. The text includes topics on poetry, art, music, dance and all good things including perfumes and food. In his royal kitchen, cooking was done exclusively with pure ghee, tamarind provided the sourness, and chilies had not yet arrived to disrupt the palate. The king was clearly an aesthete, as he gave specific instructions about food preparation, including a technique that my grandmother and aunts still use: soaking hingu or asafoetida in water.
Even earlier, the 1025 A.D. Kannada text Lokopakara by King Chavundaraya laid down the rules of Soopashastra (culinary science). It reads like an ancient domestic manual, breaking down ingredient substitutions, methods for seasoning butter, and cookware selection. The first chapter describes the preparation of 35 breads, sweets and snacks. The second chapter describes the preparation of various soft drinks salty, sour and sweet in taste. The third chapter is on nine types of sweet payasam (pudding), eight types of cooked rice, and 24 types of mixed rice dishes. The remaining three chapters are on dishes made with various vegetables. These include recipes for 28 dishes with eggplant, 16 dishes with jackfruit, 25 dishes made with raw bananas and banana flowers. The last chapter contains recipes using bamboo shoots and myrobalan, along with preservation methods for pickles and papads.
All of this reminds us that before we became obsessive modern dieters, the traditional idea of a good meal was beautifully uninhibited. As anthropologist MN Srinivas observed in The Remembered Village, a satisfying meal meant eating until the stomach could hold no more, punctuated by a necessary, resounding post-meal belch, which gratified the hostess and signalled satisfaction.
(Shoba Narayan is Bengaluru-based award-winning author. She is also a freelance contributor who writes about art, food, fashion and travel for a number of publications.)

headline: Police constable found dead in ACP office, kin suspect foul play
full_text:
Police constable found dead in ACP office, kin suspect foul play
Hyderabad A 26-year-old police constable was found dead in the restroom of a police station at L B Nagar in Hyderabad in the early hours of Wednesday, the police said, adding that prima facie, it appeared to be a death by suicide, even as his family members suspected foul play
Hyderabad A 26-year-old police constable was found dead in the restroom of a police station at L B Nagar in Hyderabad in the early hours of Wednesday, the police said, adding that prima facie, it appeared to be a death by suicide, even as his family members suspected foul play.
The body of the constable was found hanging in the rest room of the L B Nagar assistant commissioner of police (ACP) office at around 2.30 am. The constable had been attached to the office for e-COPS duty and was working on night shifts.
“The other police personnel who noticed him immediately shifted him to nearby Kamineni Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival,” a senior police official of the L B Nagar police station.
The official said the deceased hailed from Bandalemuru village in Manchal mandal of Ranga Reddy district and had been staying in a room along with his friends at Karmanghat, about a km away from the police station.
“He was a quiet person and there were no indications of the deceased experiencing any kind of stress. Inquiries also revealed that he did not have any family-related problems. He attended the duty on Tuesday as well without any complaints,” the police official said.
His body was subsequently shifted to Osmania General Hospital for post-mortem examination and a case of suspicious death was registered at the L B Nagar police station.
After receiving information about the incident, senior police officials reached the station and enquired into the circumstances surrounding the constable’s death. Police informed the family members of the deceased, who rushed to the police station on Wednesday morning.
Tension prevailed outside the LB Nagar police station with the family members and their villagers staging a protest. At one point, some protesters allegedly entered the police station and damaged a computer and a printer.
As the situation turned tense, a large number of police personnel were deployed at the station to bring the situation under control. L B Nagar deputy commissioner of police Anuradha inspected the police station and made inquiries about the possible cause of the constable’s death.
Speaking to reporters, the deceased constable’s father refused to believe that his son had died by suicide. “There were bloodstains in the rest room where he was found hanging. We want an explanation from the police what exactly led to the death of my son,” he demanded.
His mother alleged that his son might have been tortured. “Why did they kill my son? Why did they kill him and then hang him? Why was there no CCTV camera in that room? Why was his phone switched off? Why did they not show my son to us until we arrived? We want justice,” she alleged.
Ibrahimpatnam MLA Malreddy Ranga Reddy, who represents the constituency, reached the LB Nagar police station and spoke to the bereaved family.

headline: Man's eye forced open for KYC scanning: Nagaland minister shares eye-opener clip
full_text:
Man's eye forced open for KYC scanning: Nagaland minister shares eye-opener clip
Nagaland Tourism and Higher Education Minister Temjen Imna Along shared a video showing a KYC eye scan repeatedly failing on a Naga man. The humorous post by the BJP leader highlighted, with a touch of wit, a relatable struggle faced by people from the northeastern states.
Mongoloid facial features, including narrow eyes, have been used to stereotype people from India's northeast. Nagaland Tourism and Higher Education Minister Temjen Imna Along once again used humour to destroy racial stereotyping, while highlighting the limitations of some technology.
Temjen Imna Along, a BJP MLA, used a video captioned just "Struggle is real", highlighting the difficulty of some in getting biometric verification done.
In a video shared on X, a person (who's not in the frame) repeatedly struggles to scan the eyes of a Naga man on the KYC biometric application. As the system fails to scan his iris, a group of people are seen trying to hold the Naga man's eyes open to make the scan possible.
People are heard laughing in the video.
Behind the humour, however, lies a real problem. That of technology being non-inclusive in design.
Biometric technologies are increasingly used for KYC, authentication and accessing digital services, but systems designed around standardised facial and biometric parameters can sometimes create difficulties for people from certain communities whose physical features might not fit these broader parameters and assumptions.
Temjen Imna Along's post brought that problem into focus without turning it into a technical or political lecture. Instead, he chose mirth, which is a style that has become closely associated with his social media presence. Even if the clear intention of sharing the video was not mentioned by Temjen, the post has done its job.
"We should create alternative methods. If people are facing problems nobody should suffer due to their natural biological traits," one person wrote on X, reacting to Temjen's post.
"Who said technology doesn't exercise racism! I'm sure China, Japan and other south east Asian nations must have invented something for this. Why is Indian government not adopting something similar?" another user reacted on X.
The Nagaland minister himself has repeatedly used humour to address stereotypes directed at people from India's Northeast, particularly the popular perception that they have "small eyes".
This theme of Temjen Imna Along went viral in 2022 when he spoke about the supposed advantages of having smaller eyes during a public event.
Acknowledging the stereotype head-on, he joked that people from the northeast do indeed have smaller eyes, but claimed they also have a sharp vision.
"Because of smaller eyes we don't get much dirt inside the eyes. And we can easily sleep when some long programme is going on," he said, drawing applause and laughter from the audience.
The video quickly travelled across social media and was also shared by Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma. "My brother Temjen is in full form," Sarma wrote on X.
Temjen responded in his trademark playful manner. "My eyes may be small, but I can see the camera from a mile. Always pose ready. Also I can see you smile as you reading it! Good Morning," he wrote.
Temjen's latest KYC post follows the same playbook of taking a familiar experience or stereotype, turn it into a joke and use the humour to make people notice the larger issue.
The biometric video, however, carries an additional layer. What appears at first to be a funny struggle with an eye scanner also raises questions about how technology interacts with India's enormous diversity.
For people in the northeast, where facial and physical features can differ from the assumptions built into some technologies, a seemingly routine process such as biometric authentication can become an unexpected obstacle.
Temjen has made a political style out of addressing such subjects without sounding overtly political. His posts often turn everyday experiences into moments of humour, allowing him to connect with audiences beyond conventional political messaging.
And this time, the joke is quite literally in the eye of the scanner. The video might be funny. The problem it points to is not. It's indeed eye-opening.

headline: Noel Tata, TV Narendran: Who could take Chandrasekaran's mantle at Tata Sons?
full_text:
Noel Tata, TV Narendran: Who could take Chandrasekaran's mantle at Tata Sons?
Tata Trusts said the trustees of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust have passed a resolution to set up a selection committee to recommend a new chairman for Tata Sons.
Natarajan Chandrasekaran's announcement that he will step down as Tata Sons chairman at the end of his term has sparked speculation over who will get the baton.
Chandrasekaran's term is scheduled to end in February. On Thursday, Tata Trusts said the trustees of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust – a group of charities that wields indirect control of the Tata Group – have passed a resolution to set up a selection committee to recommend a new chairman for Tata Sons.
As the Trust begins the process of finding a successor to lead the diversified conglomerate's holding company, several big names have been doing the rounds.
Also read | N Chandrasekaran's decision to step down creates immediate succession challenge for Tata Sons
Noel Tata
Late industrialist and former Tata Sons chairman Ratan Tata's half-brother Noel Tata is one of the serious contenders, according to The Hindu Businessline. His chances shouldn't be discounted, especially given the central role the Trusts play in the group's governance.
"Noel Tata should not be ruled out for a larger role on grounds of experience, pointing to similar doubts surrounding Ratan Tata when JRD Tata was choosing his successor," former Tata Sons senior executive Mukund Rajan was quoted as saying by the website.
Long overshadowed by Ratan Tata, the public face of the conglomerate for decades, Noel, 68, rose through less prominent corners of the business, building credentials in retail and trading rather than the group's flagship companies. Noel spent years serving on boards across the group. Unlike Ratan Tata, Noel largely shunned publicity. He emerged as a central figure only after Ratan's death in October 2024, Reuters reported.
Also read | How Tata Sons will pick N Chandrasekaran's successor and who will choose him
Trustees unanimously appointed him as chairman of Tata Trusts and he subsequently joined the Tata Sons board as a non-executive director.
TV Narendran
Tata Steel Limited chief executive officer and managing director TV Narendran is being considered as a lead contender and possible successor to Chandrasekaran, according to a report by The Times of India.
He is a Tata veteran who joined the group in 1988. Narendran has spent his entire career in the company, and has led it for years. He has over 37 years of experience in the mining and metals industry, according to the Tata Steel website. He is currently on the boards of Tata Steel Limited and Tata International Limited and he is the chairman of Tata Steel Europe.
A person close to Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata said Narendran "could be part of Noel's inner team", The Times of India reported.
Also read | What is N Chandrasekaran's net worth? Report shows he got ₹671.4 crore in 5 years
Saurabh Agrawal
Tata Sons Private Limited (Tata Sons) chief financial officer Saurabh Agrawal could also be in the race to replace Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman, Business Standard reported. The company is the holding firm of the Tata group of companies. He joined Tata Sons in June 2017.
Agrawal is on the boards of Tata Steel, Voltas and Tata Digital. He chairs the boards of Tata Capital, Tata Play, Tata AIA Life Insurance, Tata AIG General Insurance, Tata Power Renewable Energy Limited, Tata 1mg and Big Basket, according to information available on the Tata Power website.
In a career spanning over 30 years, he has served as head of investment banking in India for Bank of America Merrill Lynch, head of corporate finance for India and South Asia at Standard Chartered Bank, and head of strategy at the Aditya Birla Group.
Also read | ‘Respect his decision’: Tata Trusts on Chandrasekaran’s call to step down
Shailesh Chandra
According to the Business Standard, Tata Motors' Passenger Vehicles Limited and Tata Passenger Electric Motor Limited's chief executive officer and managing director Shailesh Chandra may also be considered for the top post.
Information available on the company's website says Chandra joined Tata Motors in 1995 as a production manager and steadily rose through the ranks, taking on pivotal roles across multiple functions, including a stint at the Group Strategy Office of Tata Sons between 2013 and 2016.
He spearheaded corporate strategy and business transformation, laying the foundation for future readiness and operational excellence.
P Venkatesalu
Trent CEO P Venkatesalu, who is close to Noel, is likely to find his name in the list of contenders, The Hindu Businessline reported.
Information available on the company's website says he joined Trent in 2008 and has been with the company since then. Prior to Trent, he was associated with Tata Administrative Services since 2001 and was formerly with Tata Sons Limited as a part of the Group Finance team.
Harish Bhat
Tata veteran Harish Bhat, who is the brand custodian at Tata Sons, is also among the contenders, The Hindu Businessline reported. He joined the Tata Group in 1987, as an officer in the Tata Administrative Service (TAS).
Currently, he is the chairman of Tata Coffee Limited, according to the company's website. He is a director on the boards of several other Tata companies, including Trent, Tata Starbucks, Infiniti Retail, and Tata AIA Life Insurance.

headline: 'Do you not want India to stay healthy?' Top court grills Centre, FSSAI over food labels
full_text:
'Do you not want India to stay healthy?' Top court grills Centre, FSSAI over food labels
The bench was particularly concerned by minutes of a recent meeting of the food regulator suggesting continued hesitation over front-of-pack warning labels.
The Supreme Court on Thursday questioned the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) over its reluctance to introduce front-of-pack warning labels on foods high in sugar, salt and saturated fat, asserting that consumers, especially children, need to know what they are eating.
“You don’t want people of this country to remain healthy? More particularly growing children?” a bench of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran asked the Centre and FSSAI, while underlining that India must not compromise on public health or settle for lower standards merely because Indian foods may differ from those consumed in developed countries.
The bench was particularly concerned by minutes of a recent meeting of the food regulator suggesting continued hesitation over front-of-pack warning labels, despite the Supreme Court having already asked it to consider the measure. “Are you taking the court for a toss?” asked the bench, questioning whether pressure from food manufacturers was influencing the regulator.
“There is immense pressure at the end of all these corporate houses on you. And you are succumbing to that pressure! We are doing this in public interest. Keep it in mind. We are not doing it for ourselves,” it added.
The court gave the Centre and FSSAI two weeks to place their final decision on record, warning: “This is your last chance. Next time we will dictate the judgement,” it said.
The bench made clear that it was not seeking to ban any particular food or dictate what consumers should eat. What it wanted was for people to have clear information before making that choice.
“In this country, how many people can afford dry fruits? And how many children buy Kurkure? That makes all the difference. We are not against any particular product. We only want the person purchasing it to know what he is consuming,” it said.
The exchange came during the hearing of a public interest litigation filed by non-profit 3S and Our Health, seeking warning labels on packaged foods to indicate high levels of salt, sugar and saturated fats.
The government sought to explain the reluctance to impose such warnings by pointing to the composition of Indian foods. Additional solicitor general Brijender Chahar, appearing for the Centre and FSSAI, said traditional Indian foods tend to contain more salt, sugar and fat than what he described as “bland” food in developed countries.
“The difficulty is that each of our traditional foods will have the red symbol on it. Whether it is namkeen etc warning that it is very harmful,” argued Chahar, adding that even foods such as eggs could cross the proposed thresholds for fat. He also submitted that such a system could adversely affect micro, small and medium enterprises, with about a third of MSME revenue coming from traditional foods.
But the bench was unconvinced.
“Even without a red label, everybody knows there is sugar, fat, carbs etc. no? This is to create public awareness,” it said, stressing the need to protect children who are increasingly consuming such products.
The court also rejected the argument that manufacturers could be affected by warning labels. “Manufacturers may not like this because it may affect their business. Even after these warnings, it’s the discretion of the person who purchases it. He may still purchase it or he may not purchase. Why are you reluctant to do this?” it asked.
The confrontation over the issue comes after the Supreme Court previously expressed dissatisfaction with FSSAI’s handling of the matter.
In its August 4 order, the court recorded that it was not satisfied with FSSAI’s compliance affidavit and specifically asked the authority to consider front-of-package labelling, noting that such a system was “internationally prevalent”, and directed it to revert within four weeks.
The issue has been pending for more than a year. The original public interest litigation (PIL) was disposed of in April 2025 after FSSAI told the court that an expert committee would recommend amendments to food labelling rules. The regulator’s proposed Indian Nutrition Rating (INR) system envisaged a 0.5-to-5 star rating for packaged foods based on factors including sugar, salt, saturated fat, energy, protein and fibre, aimed at helping consumers make healthier choices.
But the process has dragged on. FSSAI said it received more than 14,000 comments on the proposal and its expert committee held five meetings, but later reported a lack of consensus on the INR format. It subsequently proposed further amendments, research, consumer surveys and wider stakeholder consultations, while the matter was deferred by the Food Authority.
The Supreme Court, however, appeared unwilling to let the consultation process become an indefinite exercise. It also rejected the Centre’s suggestion that India should not necessarily seek to match international standards on food labelling.
“We do not approve the stance of the Union when it says that it’s not possible to match the international standards, more particularly developed countries. Should India remain as an undeveloped country? The world should know that India is concerned about the health of its citizens and more particularly children,” it said.

headline: Rapido secures five-year cab licence in Karnataka, to operate till 2031
full_text:
Rapido secures five-year cab licence in Karnataka, to operate till 2031
The company said the licence will provide greater continuity to its users while allowing Rapido to expand its cab services within the state.
Rapido has received a five-year licence from the Karnataka State Transport Authority for its cab services in the state, valid until August 2031, giving the mobility platform a longer-term regulatory framework for its operations in its home market.
Roppen Transportation Services Private Limited, which operates Rapido, said the licence has been issued under the Karnataka On-Demand Transportation Technology Aggregators Rules, 2016.
The company said the licence will provide greater continuity to its captains and commuters while allowing it to expand its cab services within the state's regulatory framework.
Deep Dive
Rapido operates across 21 Karnataka cities
Rapido currently operates across 21 cities in Karnataka, supporting more than 3.14 lakh captains and over 2.04 crore registered customers, according to the company. More than 69 lakh customers in the state have taken cab rides through the platform.
The company said the licence will strengthen its ability to support Karnataka's urban transport ecosystem, with a focus on safe, reliable and technology-enabled mobility.
ALSO READ | Delhi woman books Rapido bike at 11 pm, says rider arrived in car and insisted she get in. Company responds
Rapido joins Karnataka's Urban Mobility Mission
Rapido said it has also been made part of the Urban Mobility Mission announced by the Karnataka government, through which it will work with the state on priorities including commuter access, urban travel, technology integration, safety and service reliability.
Pavan Guntupalli, Co-founder, Rapido, said the licence would allow the company to strengthen its cab offering while continuing to work with the Karnataka government and Transport Department.
"Karnataka is our home state and one of our most important markets," Guntupalli said, adding that the company aims to operate in full compliance with the state framework.
He said clear and predictable regulation benefits commuters, captains, platforms and the government, while Rapido's priority would remain safety, service reliability and earning opportunities for captains.
Rapido's presence across Karnataka
Rapido said its presence spans major and emerging mobility centres including Bengaluru, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Belagavi, Davangere, Shivamogga, Ballari, Kalaburagi and Tumakuru.

headline: Kharge raises Uttarakhand post-rally ‘purification’, Rajya Sabha chair seeks probe
full_text:
Kharge raises Uttarakhand post-rally ‘purification’, Rajya Sabha chair seeks probe
Kharge said he is not making it a political issue, but a case under the Untouchability (Offences) Act should be filed and the accused should be arrested
Rajya Sabha chairman CP Radha Krishnan on Thursday instructed the government to conduct a thorough inquiry into the alleged “purification of a site” where Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a gathering in Uttarakhand and said action must be taken against the guilty.
The instruction came after Kharge spoke about the issue in the Upper House. He said some “BJP [Bharatiya Janata Party] people” carried out the purification at Haldwani’s Ram Lila Maidan, where he addressed the gathering.
The BJP is in power in Uttarakhand, which is due to go to polls next year.
Track Parliament monsoon session LIVE updates
Kharge said he did not take the name of any religion, and only referred to problems being faced by people. “…but some BJP people conducted a havan at the stage and shuddikaran [purification]…is this the way in a democracy… I am the leader of the Opposition [in Rajya Sabha],” he said.
Kharge said he is not making it a political issue, but a case under the Untouchability (Offences) Act should be filed against the accused, and they should be arrested.
Untouchability is outlawed, and practising it in any form is a punishable offence.
Kharge said he has been in this House for years and never said he is a Scheduled Caste, a Dalit, and needs protection. “I am capable of fighting …” he said.
Also Read | ‘No firing at Jantar Mantar’: Nadda slams Rahul Gandhi; claims Congress leader ‘changing goalpost’
Amid shouting from both sides, Union minister and the House leader JP Nadda said the BJP condemns the incident. “The BJP does not subscribe to such activities. The incident is painful not just for the Congress but for all of us…”
As the Opposition continued to protest, Nadda said an investigation will be conducted and assured the House that action will be taken. “We condemn this, and this is a regrettable issue for all of us,” Nadda said. He objected to Kharge using the term “you people” while referring to the incident.
Krishnan said an insult to Kharge was an insult to everyone. “If untouchability is not a sin, then there is no sin in the world… we all condemn untouchability…all are purified and no need for anyone to purify us again and again…” He then directed the government to investigate and punish the guilty.
Congress Uttarakhand’s unit on Wednesday alleged that people linked to the ruling BJP carried out the purification ritual on the stage after Kharge’s address.

headline: Rs 13,355 crore released for 6 nuke projects in 5 years, Centre tells Parliament
full_text:
Rs 13,355 crore released for 6 nuke projects in 5 years, Centre tells Parliament
The projects are expected to add 8,000 MW to the national grid upon commissioning. The government cited supply delays, Covid-19, geopolitical conflicts and site-related challenges among the reasons for project delays.
The government has sanctioned Rs 13,355 crore as equity for six nuclear power projects currently under construction over the past five years, with the entire amount released so far fully utilised, the Ministry of Atomic Energy informed the Rajya Sabha. Minister of State for Atomic Energy Dr Jitendra Singh, in a written reply, said the six projects, once progressively commissioned, will add a cumulative 8,000 MW of nuclear power capacity to the national grid.
The government, however, acknowledged that several nuclear projects have faced delays in construction and commissioning in recent years. The reasons include extensive design changes following the Fukushima nuclear accident in Japan, delays in the supply of critical equipment and disruptions caused by the Covid-19 pandemic.
Other challenges cited by the government include delays in supplies from Russia for the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant (KKNPP), financial and cash-flow problems faced by contractors after the pandemic, difficult soil conditions at the Gorakhpur Haryana Anu Vidyut Pariyojana (GHAVP) site and a shortage of skilled manpower.
The government also flagged the impact of ongoing geopolitical conflicts, including the Russia-Ukraine war and the US-Israel-Iran conflict, on project execution and supply chains.
GOVT STEPS UP MONITORING TO PREVENT FURTHER DELAYS
To address these challenges and ensure timely completion, the government said the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd (NPCIL) and the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) are conducting periodic reviews and closely monitoring project progress.
Measures include identifying constraints early, making mid-course corrections, holding frequent meetings with vendors and contractors, resolving execution-related issues and re-sequencing construction activities wherever possible.
The government has also delegated greater powers to NPCIL executives and constituted a Board sub-committee to monitor project implementation.
In addition, bulk ordering of long-delivery equipment has been adopted for reactors being implemented under the fleet-mode approach. Several critical items are already under manufacturing or being progressively delivered to ensure timely availability of long-lead equipment for future projects.
The government said these measures are aimed at reducing supply-related delays and ensuring that upcoming nuclear reactors are completed within their targeted timelines.
With 8,000 MW of additional capacity expected from the six projects under construction, the government said their commissioning would provide a significant boost to India's nuclear power capacity and its clean-energy objectives.

headline: Copy-pasted from US: Tehseen Poonawalla shares Gadkari video on E20 petrol
full_text:
Copy-pasted from US: Tehseen Poonawalla shares Gadkari video on E20 petrol
Did the government simply copy ethanol standards from the US? Activist Tehseen Poonawalla has raised the question after sharing a video of Nitin Gadkari speaking about how India framed ethanol standards.
The controversy over E20 petrol took a fresh turn on Thursday after activist Tehseen Poonawalla shared a video of Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and accused the government of "copy-pasting" ethanol standards from the US. Poonawalla, who has been spearheading the campaign against E20 petrol, said Gadkari's speech ran counter to his claim in courts that he had nothing to do with the ethanol program.
Seeking the immediate sacking of Gadkari, Poonawalla tweeted, "This man copy-pasted the ethanol standards policy from the US. He lied to the courts that he has nothing to do with ethanol. He needs to be sacked ASAP." Poonawalla and his Team Bharat have demanded the rollback of E20 petrol - a blend of 80% petrol and 20% ethanol - amid a raging debate in the country on its impact on vehicles.
WHAT NITIN GADKARI SAYS IN THE VIDEO?
In the undated video shared by Poonawalla, Gadkari is seen lamenting the long time taken by departments in India to frame standards. "They take at least 3-4 years. I got tired of it. We had to prepare standards for ethanol," Gadkari says.
The minister then goes on to describe a quick fix he suggested to officials instead of "wasting" five years on research.
"One day, I said, 'Keep your research to yourself. If it is an American law, then cut the header from above, put our details, put our stamp on it, make the necessary corrections and declare it'," the minister says.
He also explains the reason behind his diktat, saying he only has five years to get the work done.
"The US must surely be better than us, and Europe must be even better than us. They must also be thinking about safety, perhaps much more than we do," Gadkari says in the video.
"I will be a minister for five years... I have to get the work done within these five years. If you take five years just to set a standard, then when will the work actually happen?" he further says.
However, in the same vein, Gadkari stresses that the government would not "compromise on safety".
"Now, standards for everything are being prepared -- 100% ethanol, electric vehicles and even hydrogen. My only suggestion is: do not compromise on safety," the Transport Minister says.
It is not known where and when Gadkari made the remarks. From the video, it appears that the minister was speaking at a GatiShakti event. Neither the government nor Gadkari has so far reacted to Poonawalla's criticism. We will update you when Gadkari responds.
NITIN GADKARI FACES FLAK
However, Gadkari's remarks have opened a can of worms and invited criticism on social media.
"A rare gem in politics. Wish all politicians were as honest and transparent. A new standard in lowering them," quipped satirist Kamlesh Kishore Singh, popularly known as 'Tau'.
Journalist Umashankar Singh posted, "Nitin Gadkari could only see his own and his government's term, not the lifespan of the bikes and cars bought with the hard-earned money of common people."
"Nobel Prize for this explanation," political commentator Gaurav Pradhan said in a cryptic post.
Several experts claimed Gadkari's remarks in the video ran counter to his recent statement in Parliament.
Last month, the Transport Minister, in a written reply, stated that the E20 program was launched after extensive scientific testing and multi-year research by bodies like ARAI (Automotive Research Association of India).
A key concern raised by several vehicle owners (pre-2023) is that E20 petrol has resulted in a reduction in mileage and increased wear and tear. It has led to higher maintenance costs.
While the government has admitted that E20 may marginally reduce fuel efficiency, extensive testing has found no proof of engine failures linked to the fuel blend.
The trade-off, Gadkari has argued, is improved acceleration, better ride quality and around 30% lower carbon emissions than E10 fuel.

headline: Prayers, walk to gurdwara langar hall, then strike: Blow-by-blow account of ‘kirpan’ attack on SAD's Sukhbir Singh Badal
full_text:
Prayers, walk to gurdwara langar hall, then strike: Blow-by-blow account of ‘kirpan’ attack on SAD's Sukhbir Singh Badal
Badal arrived in Nanded for a three-day visit with wife Harsimrat Kaur and close associates. He was attacked at a gurdwara in Nanded by a Nihang, a day later.
Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president and former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked with a sharp-edged weapon during a visit to a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded on Thursday.
He suffered an injury to his hand and was rushed to a nearby hospital.
The attack was allegedly carried out by a Nihang Sikh while Badal was on his way to the langar hall of the gurdwara.
Here is a blow-by-blow account of what happened
Badal arrived in Nanded on August 12
Deep Dive
Sukhbir Singh Badal arrived in Nanded for a planned three-day visit. He was accompanied by his wife and Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal, besides close associates.
Also Read | Ex-Punjab deputy CM Sukhbir Singh Badal attacked with 'kirpan' outside gurdwara in Maharashtra's Nanded
Thursday morning: Visit to Sachkhand Nanded Sahib gurdwara in Nanded
Badal first visited the main gurdwara, Takht Nanded Sahib, one of the five Takhts, or temporal seats, of Sikhism. Visuals reviewed by Hindustan Times showed Badal offering prayers inside the shrine, with Harsimrat Kaur Badal also present.
After paying obeisance, Badal was honoured with a siropa by the head priests of the gurdwara.
Below is the video of Badal offering prayer at Takht Nanded Sahib.
Next stop: Gurdwara Mata Sahib Kaur
From the main gurdwara, Badal travelled to Gurdwara Mata Sahib Kaur, located on the outskirts of Nanded, around 15 km from the main Nanded gurdwara.
The gurdwara is associated with a Nihang Sikh sect and is not managed by the board overseeing the main Hazur Sahib shrine.
Also Read | Nihang in 60s, worked as 'sewadar': What we know about Sukhbir Singh Badal's attacker
The attack
After offering prayers at Gurdwara Mata Sahib Kaur, Badal was walking towards the langar hall when the attack took place.
An assailant suddenly moved towards him and attacked with a Kirpan, a sharp-edged weapon carried by Sikhs. Badal sustained an injury to his right hand.
The attacker was reportedly a Nihang. He was dressed in the blue attire that nihangs wear and is reportedly is in mid-sixties.
Badal rushed to hospital
Following the attack, Badal was taken to Yashosai Hospital in Nanded for treatment. The attacker was detained, and police began investigating the circumstances and motive behind the assault.
Second attack on Badal in less than two years
Thursday’s incident is the second major attack on Sukhbir Badal in less than two years. On December 4, 2024, Badal survived an assassination attempt outside the Golden Temple in Amritsar. Former militant Narain Singh Chaura allegedly approached him and opened fire from close range.
The bullet narrowly missed Badal after a security officer intervened and grabbed the assailant’s pistol. The bullet struck the wall of the shrine instead. No one was injured in that incident, and Chaura was overpowered and arrested.
The Nanded attack has once again raised questions over the security of the SAD chief during visits to religious sites.

headline: ‘My election as President shows greatness of our democracy’: Kovind writes in his autobiography
full_text:
‘My election as President shows greatness of our democracy’: Kovind writes in his autobiography
In the early years of Independence, Dalit students at a primary school in Paraunkh village of Uttar Pradesh were not free to drink water as they pleased
In the early years of Independence, Dalit students at a primary school in Paraunkh village of Uttar Pradesh were not free to drink water as they pleased. They had to inform their teacher, who would then ask another student to give them water. This protocol was not required for students from savarna families.
On July 25, 2017, one of those students, Ram Nath Kovind, took charge as India’s second Dalit president, tracing a stunning arc – “of a village lad from the rural hinterlands of Uttar Pradesh to the Central Hall of Parliament to be sworn in as the First Citizen of India”.
The former president details this broad journey in his memoir, Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles, released on Wednesday by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi.
“I believed that my elevation to the highest post in the country symbolized the greatness of our democracy,” he writes in the 334-page book, published by Rupa Publications.
Kovind also leaves insights into his life after demitting office in July 2022 and offers personal accounts of his interactions with and experiences of Modi, Atal Bihari Vajpayee and LK Advani. It offers a glance into his interaction with Opposition leaders through his political career – as a BJP worker, as an MP, as governor, as President, as well as head of the high-level committee to take a call on simultaneous elections.
At the launch event, at Vigyan Bhagwan, Modi said Kovind’s life was a case study in how a person should treat society as “an equal partner in his success” rather than blame it for difficulties.
Modi recalled that Kovind lost his mother in a house fire when just four years old, saying the tragedy made him stronger. A neighbour helped raise him, while his father became his “hero”.
Drawing a parallel, Modi said he was fortunate his mother Heeraben “lived beyond 100,” but he could still “feel her absence”. Heeraben died on December 30, 2022.
The 80-year-old throws his weight behind the “One Nation, One Election” plan, drawing on experiences through his career.
“ONOE…is aimed at enhancing the efficiency of our electoral system, reducing the cost of elections, and enabling the government to focus on development without the frequent interruptions of staggered elections,” writes Kovind.
“While it is a challenging endeavour, I believe it is essential for a more stable and cohesive democratic process,” he adds.
He says the panel held 65 meetings over 191 days, consulting political parties, constitutional experts, political leaders and the public.
Of 62 political parties approached, 47 responded: 32 supported ONOE while 15 opposed it. The BJP and a clutch of regional parties – including the BJD, Shiv Sena, JD(U), SAD and AIADMK – supported the proposal, while the Congress opposed it.
Kovind’s account of his entry into the BJP is closely linked to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.
He recalls attending a massive VHP rally at Delhi’s Boat Club on April 4, 1991, organised in support of the construction of the Ram temple in Ayodhya. Atal Bihari Vajpayee and VHP leader Ashok Singhal were present, as was Modi, then a volunteer in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Kovind says Modi was instrumental in a 1991 signature campaign for the temple.
Kovind describes Vajpayee’s speech on an inclusive society, tolerance and peaceful coexistence as a “powerful catalyst” in his decision to join the BJP. He eventually joined the party in April 1991.
He also writes that the BJP’s support for the Ram Janmabhoomi movement represented “a burning issue of cultural nationalism” and a struggle between “pseudo-secularism and real equal respect to every religion”.
The former president also discusses BR Ambedkar’s influence on his life and work.
He recalls that former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, at the 2001 Dalit Sangam rally at the Red Fort, declared that his government would function on the basis of “Bhim Smriti” rather than “Manusmriti”.
Kovind’s Modi account stretches back to the latter’s days as BJP general secretary (organisation). He describes Modi as “meticulous and methodical”, recalling working with the Prime Minister on the 2001 rally.
Through his decades in the political space, Kovind recalls his interactions with the Opposition.
He speaks warmly of former prime minister Manmohan Singh.
“Dr Manmohan Singh was one of those rare politicians in our country whose humility, modesty and gentleness uniquely defined his persona... One had so much to learn from the erudite and soft-spoken Dr Manmohan Singh,” he writes.
At the same time, Kovind recalls his time canvassing support during his presidential campaign, when he met leaders across the political spectrum. He recalls support from several opposition or regional parties, while noting that former Uttar Pradesh chief ministers Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati ultimately did not vote for him, “perhaps guided more by political interests”.

headline: Telangana school principal found dead with 27 stab wounds at home: Police
full_text:
Telangana school principal found dead with 27 stab wounds at home: Police
Kallu Roopa Reddy, principal and director of Nagarjuna Grammar English Medium School in Kondamallepally, suffered around 27 stab wounds in the attack
A 48-year-old school principal was stabbed to death by unidentified people at her residence in Telangana’s Nalgonda district on Wednesday, police said, suspecting that people known to the victim could be behind the murder.
Kallu Roopa Reddy, principal and director of Nagarjuna Grammar English Medium School in Kondamallepally, suffered around 27 stab wounds in the attack. Police said no cash or valuables were missing from the house, ruling out theft as an apparent motive at this stage.
“She lived with her husband, Kallu Rajender Reddy, at their own house in the Colony. The couple also owned a house in Hyderabad, where their son Abhinav Reddy was pursuing engineering, and they frequently travelled between the two places,” Devarakonda deputy superintendent of police M V Srinivas Rao said.
Also Read | 6 farm labourers killed in lorry-auto collision in Telangana’s Sangareddy district
According to the police, Roopa Reddy had gone to Hyderabad with her husband on a three-day holiday on Saturday. As Rajender Reddy had some work in Hyderabad, she returned alone to Kondamallepally on Tuesday morning and attended school.
“She remained at the school until around 5.30 pm and returned home, which is closer to the school, telling her colleagues that some friends were expected to visit her. However, she did not come to the school on Wednesday and when her husband called her, he could not reach her,” Rao said.
He then contacted tenants staying in their house and asked them to check on his wife, but they also received no response.
Also Read | T’gana govt mulls land pooling for infra works
Rajender contacted Chintapalli sub-inspector Rammurthy, who lives next to their house, and requested him to check the residence. The SI, accompanied by neighbours, went to the house and found Roopa lying in a pool of blood.
Police subsequently examined the premises with a dog squad. “The victim had suffered about 27 stab wounds, indicating the brutality of the attack. No cash or valuables were missing from the house, ruling out theft as an apparent motive at this stage,” Rao said.
The police are examining the possibility that persons familiar with Roopa may have committed the murder. Family disputes and other possible motives are also being investigated.
A case was registered based on a complaint lodged by the victim’s son, Abhinav Reddy, and further investigation is under way, Rao said.

headline: Woman, 35, dies after husband allegedly sets her ablaze in Rajasthan: Police
full_text:
Woman, 35, dies after husband allegedly sets her ablaze in Rajasthan: Police
A 35-year-old woman died after her husband allegedly poured petrol on her and set her ablaze at her parental home in Rajasthan’s Sri Ganganagar.
A 35-year-old woman died after her husband allegedly poured petrol on her and set her ablaze at her parental home in Rajasthan’s Sri Ganganagar district, police said.
The woman, identified as Pooja, suffered burns over nearly 80% of her body and died on Tuesday while being taken to a higher centre in Bikaner for treatment. Her husband, Sultan Ram, 40, was also injured in the incident and is undergoing treatment at a district hospital, police said.
Also Read: Rajasthan court acquits 40 in 2015 murder of 5 Dalits, cites probe lapses
Circle officer of Sri Ganganagar Vishnu Kumar Khatri said the incident took place around 2.30am on Monday.
According to the complaint, Pooja had been staying at her parental home for around three months following repeated disputes with her husband. Police officers said Ram allegedly entered the house through the terrace, went to the room where Pooja was sleeping and poured petrol over her before setting her on fire. He then fled on a motorcycle.
Family members rushed to the room after hearing her screams and managed to put out the flames before taking her to the district hospital. She was referred to PBM Hospital in Bikaner with serious burn injuries but died on the way.
Also Read: Father of minor girl held for murder of Rajasthan athlete in Faridabad
Police said the couple had been married for around 15 years and had three daughters. The woman’s family has alleged that Ram frequently assaulted her and suspected her of having an extramarital relationship.
Police recovered a five-litre petrol can allegedly used in the crime from the spot.
Based on the initial complaint by the woman’s brother, an attempt to murder case was registered with the Sadar police station, which was converted into a murder case after her death. police said.

headline: Fourth rail line approved through strategic 'Chicken's Neck' corridor: official
full_text:
Fourth rail line approved through strategic 'Chicken's Neck' corridor: official
Katihar, A fourth railway line through the strategically important 'Chicken's Neck' corridor has been approved by the Centre, a senior official said.
Northeast Frontier Railway General Manager Chetan Kumar Shrivastava said the Malda-New Jalpaiguri section is a crucial rail corridor connecting the Northeast with other parts of the country.
"A third line had earlier been proposed for the section, but approval has now been accorded for a fourth line as well. In addition, the nearly 29-km double-line underground project between Tinmai Ghat and Bagdogra is another important infrastructure initiative," he said, addressing a press conference on Wednesday night.
Given the strategic importance of the region, the railways is laying special emphasis on enhancing the capacity of the corridor, he said.
The 'Chicken's Neck', also known as the Siliguri Corridor, is a narrow stretch of land about 20-22 km wide and nearly 60 km long in north Bengal that connects the northeastern states with the rest of India. It is considered a critical and sensitive lifeline from both security and logistical perspectives.
Shrivastava said once the projects are completed, the entire rail corridor will undergo a major transformation, and the area will develop in a more organised manner.
He said work on doubling the line in the Barsoi section was also underway, while infrastructure was being expanded across the Katihar division to cater to growing passenger and freight traffic.
As many as 42 new trains had been introduced on different routes during the previous year, while around 250 new stoppages had been provided to improve passenger convenience, he said.
Shrivastava said redevelopment of the New Jalpaiguri station was progressing rapidly and it will be completed by April 2027.
"Efforts are also underway to introduce new local train services from Jogbani, Radhikapur and Balurghat soon. The services are expected to improve connectivity for passengers in border and remote areas," he said.
He said 100 per cent electrification of the NFR network had been completed and work was being accelerated to further expand the operation of electric trains.
"There are plans to extend Vande Bharat train services beyond Guwahati to Tinsukia and Agartala, with services operating in both directions. It would provide passengers in the Northeast with faster and more comfortable rail travel," he said.

headline: FSSAI has suggested a tabular declaration of the recommended daily requirement of added sugar, saturated fats and salt.
full_text:
FSSAI has suggested a tabular declaration of the recommended daily requirement of added sugar, saturated fats and salt.
Citing industryâs opposition to warning labels on food packets, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has suggested a tabular declaration of the recommended daily requirement of added sugar, saturated fats and salt.The FSSAIâs affidavit filed in the Supreme Court only mentions the food industryâs opposition but has ignored the evidence in favour of warning label to help discourage consumption of foods high in added saturated fats, sugar and salt submitted by civil society representatives.FSSAIâs âcomplianceâ affidavit in response to the Supreme Court order directing it to frame Front of Pack labelling regulation states that a âmajority of industry organizations were against the inclusion of âwarning labelsâ on the product,â and goes on to suggest a nutrition table giving âthe daily allowance for added sugar, added saturated fat and salt vis a vis their presence in per serve of packed food productâ on the front of the pack.âThe proposed numerical table format being suggested by FSSAI would force consumers to do math at the supermarket shelf. The FSSAI has called it a âcomplianceâ affidavit but in reality, it is defiance. The Supreme Court had explicitly said that the exercise so far had not yielded any positive or good result and it had given FSSAI four weeks to revert. And six months later, FSSAI has filed an affidavit that abandons warning labels altogether and avoids defining HFSS (high fat, salt and sugar) foods.
Clearly, FSSAI has bowed to food industryâs interests,â said Dr Arun Gupta of Nutrition Advocacy in Public Interest (NAPi).FSSAI stated in the affidavit that it had held a stakeholder consultation on March 19, 2026 involving consumer groups, food industry representatives and farmer organisations. It stated that industry bodies argued that âconsumers should be able to make an informed decision without creating fear amongst the consumersâ. The affidavit was silent on the input given by consumer organisations, which had sought warning labels that have been shown to be the most effective in reducing consumption of junk food high in salt, sugar and saturated fats in several countries. NAPi had also given FSSAI evidence generated from studies conducted in India and other countries showing how effective warning labels are.

headline: Bangladesh turns to India for help as power crisis forces 8pm shutdown for malls, shops
full_text:
Bangladesh turns to India for help as power crisis forces 8pm shutdown for malls, shops
Bangladesh government has directed shops, markets and shopping malls to shut shop by 8 pm amid ongoing power crisis in country.
Bangladesh is facing one of its worst power crisis in years as a severe shortage of natural gas has hit electricity generation in the country, prompting the government to direct closure of shops, markets and shopping malls as early as 8pm.
Bangladesh has now turned to India for help.
New govt order forces commercial establishments to shut shop early
Under a government directive that took effect on Thursday, shops, markets and shopping malls have been directed to shut shop by 8pm, according to a Reuters report. Commercial establishments are now permitted to operate only between 11am and 8pm while hospitals, pharmacies and food-related businesses have been exempted.
Also Read | No response yet on invite to Brics Summit for Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman
B'desh turns to India for help
The worsening crisis has also prompted Bangladesh to seek additional diesel supplies from India to help manage the shortages of power and gas.
Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi met Bangladesh's Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood to discuss cooperation in the power and energy sectors, three days ago.
"High Commissioner Trivedi paid a courtesy call on Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood," the Indian High Commission said in a post on X.
They "exchanged views on further strengthening India–Bangladesh cooperation in the power and energy sectors," it said.
Also Read | ‘Will update when there is one’: India on Dhaka’s Hasina extradition request
Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Mahmood said the diesel shortage had directly affected gas-fired power generation, triggering widespread load-shedding.
"We have a pipeline with India through which diesel is supplied. We have asked them to provide more," he told reporters, according to PTI.
The energy minister said additional diesel supplies from India through the existing cross-border pipeline were needed to help manage Bangladesh's ongoing power and gas shortages.
"India is our neighbouring country, so we have many areas of mutual interest, and those issues were discussed," he added.
Iran crisis has impacted gas supply
Limited gas supplies have reduced electricity generation, leaving Bangladesh's national grid facing a shortfall of several hundred megawatts during peak hours and triggering load-shedding in different parts of the country, Reuters reported.
The situation has been further aggravated by the Iran crisis, which has disrupted energy markets and increased volatility in global fuel and LNG prices, according to the report.

headline: Laying the foundation stone for Indiramma Towers in Kukatpally on Friday evening in Hyderabad, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy took a swipe at the opposition parties even as he listed out the achievements of his government to benefit the urban poor.
full_text:
Laying the foundation stone for Indiramma Towers in Kukatpally on Friday evening in Hyderabad, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy took a swipe at the opposition parties even as he listed out the achievements of his government to benefit the urban poor.
“Telangana has seen a rapid burst of growth that is not limited to urban areas over the past two years that outpaces that of the previous 10 years. Nearly 55 lakh families are benefiting from the free 200 units of electricity which translates into savings for their families,” said Mr. Reddy addressing a public meeting after laying the foundation stone.
The Indiramma Towers scheme envisages affordable housing for poor with four 10-storey towers coming up with each tower having 120 houses with 12 flats on each floor.
“The earlier government promised houses for the poor but built them 40-50 km away from the city. People live in the city; they have businesses, shops and offices here. How will they survive if they have to commute for long hours? This 11-acre land parcel is very expensive but we want to build houses here for one lakh families so that they have a better life in the city. I don’t care about expenses,” said Mr. Reddy as a large number of women seated in the audience cheered.
“As your brother, I will stand by you to make your dream of owning a home a reality,” the Chief Minister told the women.
Highlighting the schemes launched for the empowerment of women, the CM said that distribution of ‘Indiramma Saris’, free bus travel for women on RTC buses, bank linked loans worth ₹65,000 crore for self-help groups, ownership of buses through Self-Help Groups, establishment of petrol bunks and solar plants by women groups and stalls at Shilparamam for self-help groups to sell their products brought a big transformation in the lives of the women in the State. “We are also providing fine-quality rice to 3.28 crore people, supplying 200 units of free electricity to every poor family and cooking gas for just ₹500,” said Mr. Reddy.
Referring to the disputes about lands under Section 22, Mr. Revanth Reddy assured that no one would lose their ownership of lands and there is no need to worry. The Chief Minister appealed to people not to believe in the false propaganda spread by some on social media on the prohibited lands.

headline: Chennai: The appointment of Archana Kalpathi Aghoram, creative producer of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s films Bigil and The Greatest of All Time, as a member of a state-level committee has raised eyebrows in political circles.
full_text:
Chennai: The appointment of Archana Kalpathi Aghoram, creative producer of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s films Bigil and The Greatest of All Time, as a member of a state-level committee has raised eyebrows in political circles.
Archana, who is CEO of AGS Entertainment, will be part of a seven-member reconstituted panel under the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department. This panel will shortlist applicants for appointment as non-hereditary trustees of temples with annual incomes exceeding Rs 10 lakh. The order for her appointment was issued by HR&CE Secretary J. Kumaragurubaran.
Critics have questioned a film producer’s domain expertise in temple administration, religious endowments, or the legal and customary nuances of trustee selection.
AIADMK leader and former Tamil Nadu minister R. B. Udhayakumar told media persons, “If government posts are given only to those who have made films with Vijay, how is this democracy?”
He added that people close to the CM have been appointed as government advisers (possibly referring to Vijay’s close aide Vishnu Reddy and political strategist John Arokiasamy), and sarcastically asked whether actor Trisha would be appointed deputy CM next.
This is not the first time Vijay has faced such criticism. In May, Vijay’s astrologer Radhan Pandit was appointed as Officer on Special Duty (OSD) to the CM. The appointment was later recalled amid massive backlash.
In June, Bengaluru-based businessman K Venkata Narayana, who produced Vijay’s film Jana Nayagan, was appointed as the Tamil Nadu government’s Special Representative in New Delhi. The move too triggered a sharp political backlash and Opposition attacks over qualification, conflict of interest, and non-Tamil Nadu roots.
HR&CE Minister S. Ramesh defended Archana’s appointment. “If one looks at Archana Kalpathi’s appointment merely as that of a film producer, it will appear wrong and the question will arise as to why she got this post. But Archana Kalpathi has undertaken renovation (thiruppani) works in more than 10 temples. Her father-in-law Srinivasan has spent several crores on temple renovation works. The responsibility given to Archana will serve as an encouragement to those who come forward to undertake temple renovation works.”
From entrepreneur to govt role
Archana Kalpathi is the daughter of Kalpathi S. Aghoram, who with his brothers built AGS Entertainment and the associated multiplex chain AGS Cinemas. The Kalpathis, an entrepreneur family, also saw earlier success in software education and training.
Archana holds an engineering degree from College of Engineering, Guindy, and got her Master’s degree in Computer Science with Management Studies at the State University of New York.
Archana joined the family business around 2006, initially focusing on cinema exhibition before moving to movie production. She took up the role CEO/creative producer of AGS Entertainment later and is also a non-executive director of Veranda Learning Solutions.
She has worked as creative producer for Vijay’s films Bigil and GOAT. She was also the producer for the actor Pradeep Ranganathan-starrer AGS projects Love Today and Dragon. Archana has maintained a relatively low public profile outside entertainment industry circles until recent appointments.
Who else is in this committee
The committee’s two-year term took effect from 24 July following the expiry of the previous panel’s tenure. It is headed by Thavathiru Sivagnana Balaya Swamigal of Bommapuram Adheenam, Mayilam, with retired District and Sessions Judge Dr K. Ramanathan as deputy chairman and vice-chairperson.
Other members include retired IAS officer P.R. Sampath, spiritual speaker M. Sumathi, and playback singer Dr T. Velmurugan. The HR&CE Commissioner serves as ex-officio member and secretary.

headline: Lucknow: Jagdambika Pal, the BJP MP from Domariyaganj, holds the unenviable record of being ‘chief minister for a day’ of Uttar Pradesh. That was 28 years ago. The BJP leader has arguably set another record. He is now the only Presiding Officer of th...
full_text:
Lucknow: Jagdambika Pal, the BJP MP from Domariyaganj, holds the unenviable record of being ‘chief minister for a day’ of Uttar Pradesh. That was 28 years ago. The BJP leader has arguably set another record. He is now the only Presiding Officer of the Lok Sabha whose remarks, delivered from the Chair, were expunged twice by the Speaker.
Speaker Om Birla Wednesday expunged from the official record remarks Pal made when he was presiding over the House. This was the second time during the Monsoon Session that Pal’s remarks were expunged. The remarks were directed at Samajwadi Party MP Chotelal, who represents Robertsganj. Pal, trying to restore order in the House after it resumed at 2 PM following an adjournment, was asking opposition MPs to return to their seats.
This was not the first time that Birla expunged remarks made by Pal from the chair.
On 5 August, Birla directed that Pal’s remarks be expunged ahead of the passage of the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026. At the time, Pal had commented on SP MP Ruchi Vira and Congress MP K.C. Venugopal, who were protesting against Delhi Police action during ‘Sansad Chalo’ protest march called by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on 20 July. Pal had made the remarks while reprimanding opposition MPs for disrupting the proceedings.
According to former Lok Sabha Secretary General P.D.T. Achary, “This is the first time that remarks made by a presiding officer have been expunged twice. This is quite surprising. A presiding officer should be careful while conducting Lok Sabha proceedings. This does not set a good example.”
But Pal has another, far more unusual, record to his name. He was chief minister of Uttar Pradesh for only about 31 hours. The episode dates back to 21 February, 1998. Then Uttar Pradesh Governor Romesh Bhandari dismissed Kalyan Singh’s government and appointed Pal in his place. Pal, who was then a minister in the Kalyan Singh-led BJP government, was sworn in as the state’s 17th chief minister at around 10 PM that night.
The dramatic change followed withdrawal of support by Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati to the BJP government. Mayawati backed Pal, who was then leader of the Akhil Bharatiya Loktantrik Congress legislature party, and urged the Governor to invite him to form the government, claiming that Kalyan Singh had lost his majority.
The BJP challenged the Governor’s decision in court. The following day, the Allahabad High Court ordered the restoration of Kalyan Singh’s government, bringing Pal’s stint as chief minister to an end within about 31 hours. The dispute later reached the Supreme Court which ordered a floor test to determine who enjoyed majority support in the Assembly.
Kalyan Singh secured 225 votes, while Pal received 196.
The episode had also led to criticism of then Assembly Speaker Kesri Nath Tripathi over his decisions concerning the disqualification of 12 legislators under the anti-defection law. Even after the votes of the 12 MLAs were excluded, Kalyan Singh still had a majority. Before the floor test, he had offered to prove his majority, but the Governor rejected the proposal.
Pal’s political journey
Jagdambika Pal began his political career with the Congress in the 1980s. He became a member of the UP Legislative Council twice, between 1982 and 1993.
He was elected as an MLA in 1993 from Uttar Pradesh’s Basti constituency and later joined the All India Indira Congress (Tiwari), led by N.D. Tiwari.
In 1997, Pal joined Naresh Agarwal, Rajeev Shukla, Shyam Sundar Sharma and Bacha Pathak to form the Akhil Bharatiya Loktantrik Congress and was made transport minister in the Kalyan Singh-led BJP government.
Pal re-joined the Congress in 2003 and was appointed president of the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee (UPCC), a position he held until 2004.
He was elected to the Lok Sabha for the first time in 2009. Pal parted ways with the Congress and joined the BJP in the run-up to the 2014 general election.
He won the Domariyaganj seat in 2014, 2019 and 2024, and is currently a member of the 18th Lok Sabha.
According to a senior Congress leader, “Pal was in Rahul Gandhi’s good books until 2014. He then sensed the mood on the ground and switched to the BJP.”
“Recently, he taunted Rahul Gandhi by saying, ‘Aapne meri suni hoti toh main idhar kyun aata?’ (If you had heard me out, why would I have switched sides?) But the reality is that he understands the political winds and chooses his party accordingly. Though he is now with the BJP, he is not communal. That is his style of politics. In UP’s circles he is commonly called as ‘ek din ka CM’,” the Congress leader added, requesting anonymity.

headline: Landslide, then influx of debris, water: What happened at Uttarakhand tunnel mishap
full_text:
Landslide, then influx of debris, water: What happened at Uttarakhand tunnel mishap
The landslide trapped workers inside the tunnel and prompted an urgent rescue operation.
A landslide caused a sudden surge of debris and water inside an under-construction THDC India tunnel near Pipalkoti in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district on Thursday evening, trapping 22 workers inside, officials said.
As many as 18 workers have been rescued so far, while a search and rescue operation is underway for the remaining workers.
The debris and water entered the 3-km-long tail-race tunnel (TRT) at a point around 1.5 km from its mouth, officials said.
Also Read | 6 workers trapped, 16 rescued as debris, water enter tunnel in Uttarakhand's Chamoli after landslide
DM's statement on landslide
Chamoli District Magistrate Gaurav Kumar said the incident occurred when a large volume of debris and water suddenly surged into the tunnel while workers from the shift on duty were inside.
He said, “This is a tunnel under construction for a hydropower project belonging to THDC. Around 6:30 or 6:45 PM, a large volume of debris and water surged into the tunnel".
“Workers from the shift on duty got trapped inside. About 14 or 15 people have already been rescued. NDRF and SDRF teams, along with all our machinery, are currently engaged in operations for the remaining individuals, and we are hopeful that we will be able to rescue everyone within the next few hours.”
According to police, the incident occurred around 7:05pm when 22 workers were inside the tunnel. A sudden influx of water and debris following the landslide trapped those on shift, HT earlier reported.
Also Read | 6 workers trapped, 16 rescued as debris, water enter tunnel in Uttarakhand's Chamoli after landslide
CM Dhami directs officials to oversee rescue efforts
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami expressed concern over the incident and said teams of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) had been dispatched to the site “considering the seriousness of the incident”.
“Instructions have been issued to all relevant agencies, including the district administration, to carry out relief and rescue operations at a war footing,” he said.
Dhami said he was in touch with senior officials and receiving real-time updates on the situation. He stressed that the government's top priority was to safely evacuate every person trapped inside the tunnel and that all necessary resources had been deployed for the operation.
The chief minister also directed officials to ensure there was no laxity in the rescue efforts and that all possible assistance was provided to the affected workers and their families.
Vinod Kumar Suman, secretary, disaster management and rehabilitation, said all agencies concerned had been directed to work in close coordination and expedite relief and rescue operations to ensure the safe evacuation of those trapped inside the tunnel.
“The priority is to safely evacuate all the people trapped inside the tunnel,” Suman said, adding that additional resources and specialist teams would be deployed as required to strengthen the rescue operation.
The district administration and all agencies involved in the relief and rescue operation are working in coordination at the incident site, officials said.

headline: India, Indonesia launch project to restore 9th-century Prambanan Temple
full_text:
India, Indonesia launch project to restore 9th-century Prambanan Temple
India and Indonesia have launched a landmark project to restore the 9th-century Prambanan Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site near Yogyakarta.
India and Indonesia have launched a landmark project to restore the 9th-century Prambanan Temple near Yogyakarta, one of Southeast Asia’s most important Hindu heritage sites and a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its exquisite Ramayana sculptures.
The temple, which houses three grand shrines dedicated to Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, is also home to a famed Ramayana tradition that continues through its elaborate dance ballet performances.
This beautiful temple dates to the 9th century and is the second-largest Hindu temple in Southeast Asia, after the Angkor Wat Temple in Cambodia.
The Parmanand Temple (widely known as Prambanan) was originally built around 850 CE during the reign of King Rakai Pikatan of the Sanjaya Dynasty in Java, Indonesia. It was later expanded by subsequent kings and is today a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Ramayana Ballet at the Prambanan Temple is a spectacular traditional performance.
It brings the Hindu epic to life with over 200 professional dancers and gamelan musicians against the backdrop of the illuminated temples. The epic story is performed over 150 times every year and keeps the grand tradition alive.
The Prambanan Temple also has exquisite sculptural reliefs depicting the story of the Ramayana. In terms of the quality of the art, this is one of the finest depictions of the Ramayana story anywhere in the world.
(Benoy K Behl is a filmmaker, art historian and photographer who has taken over 53,000 photographs of Asian monuments and art heritage and made 146 documentaries. He is known for having documented the Ramayana tradition in 10 countries of South and Southeast Asia)

Despite efforts to break the deadlock on the penultimate day, repeated disruptions have kept the two sides at odds. The standoff came into sharper focus on Wednesday when Union home minister Amit Shah offered to hold a discussion on the student protests and police action....Read More
“Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led NDA government is ready for discussions. The House should be allowed to run, the Opposition should submit a letter to the speaker by 2pm today. We are ready to start discussion at 3pm today,” Shah said in a rare media interaction outside Parliament.
Shah also wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla conveying the government's readiness to participate in the discussion. The Opposition, however, rejected the proposal.
Rahul Gandhi calls it ‘last-minute attempt’
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi described Shah's offer as a “last-minute attempt” and said the Opposition was not interested in listening to a lecture from the home minister.
The disagreement has centred on the Opposition's demand for statements from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Shah over police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak. The Opposition has alleged that students faced pellet guns, lathi charges and tear gas during protests at Jantar Mantar.
The government has maintained that it is willing to discuss the issue, but differences over the scope and format of the debate have repeatedly led to disruptions.
FCRA bill sent to JPC
Amid the continuing standoff, the Lok Sabha on Wednesday moved the controversial Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill to a 31-member joint parliamentary committee.
The panel will have 21 members from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha, with a BJP member expected to head it.
The bill, which was introduced in the previous session but held back, has faced opposition from several political parties, church delegations and chief ministers of three Christian-majority states. Critics have raised concerns over its proposed changes to India's foreign contribution law.
Minister of state for home affairs Nityanand Rai moved the resolution to constitute the JPC. The Opposition said it would participate in the committee but continue to oppose the legislation.
‘RSS getting foreign donations,’ says Venugopal
“Even in the JPC, we will continue to strongly oppose this bill and will not allow these unconstitutional and coercive provisions to become law,” Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said.
“On one side, the RSS is getting donations from foreign countries, while on the other side, the government is trying to target minorities and NGOs. The government should withdraw this bill,” he added.
Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju defended the decision to refer the bill to the JPC, pointing out that the Opposition had itself been seeking such a move.
“Yet, even when we are referring such an important bill (to a panel), these people have objections. If KC Venugopal or a member of any other party finds anything objectionable in this bill, or if there is any point they wish to oppose, they can present their views in the JPC. The JPC will have sufficient time; hearings will be held, and other people will also be invited to participate. Instead of being pleased about this, they are speaking against it.”
Rijiju also rejected suggestions that the government had been pressured into referring the bill to a parliamentary panel, saying the move was intended to facilitate a detailed examination of the legislation.
What lies ahead on the final day
With only hours left before the session ends, the key question is whether the government and Opposition can find common ground to allow Parliament to function on its final day.
The student protests have remained one of the biggest flashpoints of the session. The Opposition has repeatedly sought accountability over alleged police action against students protesting the NEET paper leak, while the government has maintained that it is ready for a discussion.
The two sides, however, remain divided over the terms of that discussion.
The Lok Sabha also passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, on Wednesday. The legislation seeks to facilitate mineral exploration, particularly of critical and strategic minerals, and gives mining lease holders greater flexibility to seek the inclusion of additional minerals in existing leases.
