Parliament monsoon session LIVE: Lok Sabha Monsoon Session among least productive in over two decades
Parliament monsoon session LIVE:The Lok Sabha recorded one of its lowest productivity levels in more than two decades during the Monsoon Session that ended on Thursday, with the House functioning for just 15% of its scheduled time, according to data compiled by PRS Legislative Research.
The figures covering the past 22 years show significant fluctuations in the functioning of Parliament, with some sessions extending well beyond their scheduled hours, while others saw disruptions and political confrontations consume much of the time available for legislative business.
The just-concluded Monsoon Session ranks among the Lok Sabha's least productive sessions in this period. At 15%, its functioning matched the Winter Session of 2016 and was higher only than the Winter Sessions of 2010 and 2013.
The House functioned for just 5% of its scheduled time during the Winter Session of 2010, while it worked for 8% during the Winter Session of 2013, according to data shared by PRS with PTI.

headline: Truckers stopped operations on National Highway-37 in Manipur on Thursday (August 13, 2026) following the death of a stranded driver on the highway, even as the State government pushed for the reopening of other highways in the State.
full_text:
Truckers stopped operations on National Highway-37 in Manipur on Thursday (August 13, 2026) following the death of a stranded driver on the highway, even as the State government pushed for the reopening of other highways in the State.
NH-37, the least blockade-prone highway in Manipur, connects State capital Imphal with Silchar in southern Assam. Truckers have been stranded on this highway for almost a month due to sporadic blockades and landslides in Manipur.
A loose associationof truck operators called a 24-hour strike on the movement of goods on NH-37 on Thursday (August 13, 2026) after Nagina Kumar Mahto, a driver from Narayanpur in Bihar, died near Labankhal in Jiribam district in the State.
The truckers said Mahto did not respond to calls on his mobile phone and was later found unconscious in his vehicle on Wednesday. He was rushed to the Jiribam Primary Health Centre, where the doctor on duty declared him dead.
“We want the governments of India, Assam, and Manipur to address our concerns and compensate the deceased driver’s family adequately,” one of the striking drivers said.
Manipur government announces reopening of National Highways
The drivers also accused the authorities of ignoring their prolonged ordeal. “We have to be on the roads for weeks without proper food, drinking water, or medical assistance. We are paying a heavy price and risking our lives to transport essential commodities to a State in conflict,” a trucker in Jiribam said. Jiribam is close to the Assam-Manipur border.
The truckers warned that their strike could be extended if the government failed to address issues they faced. Officials in Jiribam said the cause of Mahto’s death could be ascertained after an autopsy.
On August 8, Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh announced the reopening of the State’s arterial highways for all communities. While tribal organisations responded by lifting their blockade on NH-202 (connecting Imphal and Naga-dominated Ukhrul district), there has been no such move on NH-2, which links Imphal and Nagaland’s capital Kohima.
Movement on NH-2, the most preferred lifeline of Manipur, remains restricted for members of certain communities since the ethnic conflict between the Kuki-Zo and Meitei people broke out in May 2023.

headline: Fraudsters use AI to create fake websites of 126 religious sites, dupe 21,985 people
full_text:
Fraudsters use AI to create fake websites of 126 religious sites, dupe 21,985 people
Police said an interstate gang created fake booking websites for religious destinations and cheated devotees through advance payments. Investigators say the probe has widened across states as they trace domains, funds and other possible links.
Fraudsters allegedly used Artificial Intelligence to create 126 fake websites of religious sites, hotels, dharamshalas and ashrams across 11 states, duping nearly 22,000 people across the country, the Gujarat Cyber Center of Excellence said. The interstate racket, which allegedly targeted devotees looking for online bookings, puja and VIP darshan services, has led to the arrest of two people.
The accused allegedly created 126 fake websites across 11 states, including around 40-41 portals targeting religious destinations in Gujarat alone. Police said the gang used these websites to offer online bookings for rooms, puja, VIP darshan and other services, collecting advance payments from unsuspecting devotees.
An investigation by the Gujarat Cyber Center of Excellence found that around 21,985 people across the country were allegedly cheated by the accused, with the fraud running into crores of rupees.
The arrested accused have been identified as Vicky Gupta, a B Tech engineer from Delhi who is alleged to be the mastermind, and Shailesh Saini, a resident of Bharatpur, Rajasthan. Police said Gupta operated the network from his home, while Saini allegedly assisted with financial transactions and other technical aspects of the operation.
AI USED TO MAKE FAKE WEBSITES LOOK GENUINE
According to investigators, the accused used their technical expertise and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated images to make the fake portals resemble genuine websites of hotels, dharamshalas and ashrams.
The websites appeared when devotees searched online for services such as room bookings, online puja, VIP darshan and accommodation near famous religious sites. Once a victim contacted the operators, they were asked to make advance payments. The fraud came to light when devotees reached the destination and found that their bookings did not exist.
Police said the gang had been operating the racket for around eight months and frequently changed the domain names of the websites to evade detection by cyber agencies.
GUJARAT RELIGIOUS SITES AMONG BIGGEST TARGETS
Investigators found that devotees visiting religious destinations in Gujarat were among the major targets. Around 40 fake portals were allegedly created in the name of prominent religious sites in the state.
The fake websites included multiple portals targeting Salangpur Kashtabhanjan Dev, along with websites created in the names of Somnath at Prabhas Patan, Dwarka Jagat Mandir, Palitana Jain shrine, Girnar/Ambaji in Junagadh and Akshardham in Gandhinagar.
The gang also allegedly created fake websites targeting devotees visiting major religious destinations such as Tirupati Devasthanam, Tirumala, Katra, Shirdi, Jagannath Puri, Vrindavan, Rishikesh and Haridwar.
OVER 70 CYBER FRAUD COMPLAINTS FILED
Police said around 70 cyber fraud complaints linked to the racket have been registered across the country so far. Dr Rajdeepsinh Jhala, Superintendent of Police, Cyber Center of Excellence, said the investigation has now expanded beyond Gujarat. Two special police teams have been deployed outside the state to trace the people who purchased the 126 domains and created the websites.
Investigators are also probing the source of funds used to operate the network and whether more people were involved in the interstate racket.
Police are now working to identify additional victims and determine the total amount siphoned off through the fake booking portals.

full_text:
HYDERABAD
Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) senior leader and former Minister S. Speaking to media persons at Jupadu Bunglow in Kurnool district, where he was stopped by the AP police from proceeding towards PRP-HR on Thursday, he said the Revanth Reddy government had failed to prevent AP from “siphoning off” Krishna water to the non-basin areas, when the areas within the basin in Telangana were facing water shortage due to poor inflows into the Krishna Basin projects.

On the Telangana side, only 0.2 tmc ft water was being drawn every day for Kalwakurthy Lift Irrigation Scheme even if all three pumps were run and drawing one-tmc ft water would take 5-6 days. Stating that the effect of El Nino would be the same both for Telangana and AP, he said Telangana was allowing AP to draw huge quantities of water.

headline: Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting
full_text:
Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting
NEW DELHI: With the National Cancer Registry Programme covering only a fraction of Indiaâs population and rural cancer surveillance remaining particularly limited, the Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting. The court on Tuesday asked the 19 States and Union Territories that have not yet notified cancer as a notifiable disease to consider doing so, a move that could make reporting of newly detected cases to public health authorities mandatory.Such notification could help plug gaps in cancer surveillance by giving health authorities a more complete picture of the countryâs cancer burden, including where cases are rising and which populations are most affected. The data could in turn help shape policies on prevention, early detection, treatment capacity and allocation of healthcare resources.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant passed the order on a plea filed by a retired AIIMS doctor after his lawyer Gaurav Bansal told the court that NCRP covers only 10% of population and rural coverage is less than 1%.The push assumes greater significance against the backdrop of the WHOâs latest Global Status Report on Cancer, which estimates that 92% of people globally will be affected by cancer either directly or through a close family member.
The report also projects annual cancer cases to rise to nearly 35 million by 2050.The Supreme Court was informed that 17 of Indiaâs 36 States and UTs have already notified cancer, following recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare. The remaining 19 have now been asked to consider similar action.
Dr Pragya Shukla, Head of Clinical Oncology at Delhi State Cancer Institute, said standardised, disease-specific and timely data was essential to track India's changing cancer burden, identify regional and demographic trends, and assess the impact of prevention and treatment programmes. Such a system, she said, would complement existing cancer registries, help identify high-burden areas, improve planning for treatment infrastructure and medicines, and strengthen evidence-based cancer control. Govil added that reliable data would be critical for planning prevention, early detection and resource allocation.The Indian Cancer Society welcomed the intervention, saying national notification could help build a comprehensive cancer surveillance system. âThe Supreme Courtâs intervention is a significant development, and we welcome its direction to the remaining States and Union Territories to move towards cancer notification,â said Jyotsna Govil, Chairperson, Indian Cancer Society, Delhi. However, she stressed that notification alone would not suffice and called for a uniform national framework with common definitions, reporting standards and data protocols to ensure comparable and interoperable data across states.

headline: Tamil Nadu passes resolution against delimitation
full_text:
Tamil Nadu passes resolution against delimitation
The Tamil Nadu assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution urging the Union government to freeze the number of Lok Sabha seats at 543 and ensure 33% women’s reservation in legislative bodies on the basis of this
The Tamil Nadu assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution urging the Union government to freeze the number of Lok Sabha seats at 543 and ensure 33% women’s reservation in legislative bodies on the basis of this. The move that comes amidst efforts by the government to mobilise the required numbers in Parliament to legislate the constitution amendment bill that seeks to fast track the reservation, already cleared by both Houses of Parliament, by delinking it from the ongoing national census and subsequent delimitation, and instead prescribe an alternative mechanism for delimitation.
The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government led by chief minister C Joseph Vijay was supported by the main opposition party in the state assembly, Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), and its own allies such as the Left parties and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK).
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK), Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK), the late actor-politician Vijaykanth founded Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK) opposed the resolution.
In April 2026, the Union government introduced The Constitutional (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in Parliament to remove the 50 year freeze on delimitation and take up delimitation exercise based on the 2011 census and increase the number of Lok Sabha members from 550 to 850 but failed to garner the numbers required to pasws this. The main reason for this was a lack of clarity about how the delimitation exercise would be carried out; while the government said that each state would see its Lok Sabha seats increase by 50%, the bill itself was silent on this.
To be sure, if the government were to change the bill to incorporate this, some of the opposition to delimitation could vanish.
Vijay said if the aforementioned constitutional amendment bill is brought again, the parliamentary representation of southern states including Tamil Nadu which have successfully controlled population growth would be permanently affected.
“We request all honourable members of this assembly, across all party lines, to pass this resolution unanimously,” he said.
Leader of Opposition and DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin said the firm stance of the DMK was that under no circumstances should Tamil Nadu be affected in the name of the delimitation.
Udhayanidhi said, “The critical issue here is this — the freeze on the delimitation exercise from 1971 to 2026 must be extended for another 25 years.”
Responding to the resolution, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami said, “There is nothing wrong with redrawing the boundaries of the Lok Sabha and legislative assembly constituencies for administrative convenience.”
“AIADMK rejects the resolution regarding delimitation brought forward by the TVK government for political reasons. We support only the resolution concerning the reservation for women,” he said.
BJP’s lone legislator Bhojarajan (Nilgiris) questioned the TVK government on why the resolution is being tabled in a “hurried manner”.
In his remarks, Bhojarajan said, “Honorable Speaker Sir, I do not understand why so much hurry in this (for passing a resolution)...It (delimitation bill) is still only in a preliminary draft stage and under consideration.”
“The BJP does not accept bringing such a resolution in immense haste. We oppose this resolution,” he said.

A police officer said the nurse was on duty on Wednesday night when she disappeared around 9:40pm. “While looking for her, the hospital staff found the door of a toilet locked for an unusually long time. They shouted her name, but there was no response. They broke the door and found her lying inside,” the officer said, requesting anonymity.

Anaesthetic vials, syringe found
He added that some empty vials of anaesthetic injection and a syringe were found inside the toilet. “Doctors declared the nurse dead upon examination. No suicide note was found anywhere. The nurse’s phone has been seized to check the call records. Her husband has been asked to come here,” the officer said.
Police said the nurse was found dead on the first floor of the maternity ward at the 150-year-old hospital and that the zone was cordoned off.

Nurse married in March
The hospital staff said that the nurse got married in March to a man whose family lives in Delhi. The nurse’s family lives in East Midnapore district. The hospital staff said the nurse lived with her husband in a rented flat near Kolkata.

headline: ₹10,000 penalty for delay in ambulances, NHAI tweaks norms
full_text:
₹10,000 penalty for delay in ambulances, NHAI tweaks norms
The authority has also set a one-hour limit for accident victims to reach the nearest hospital after an emergency ticket is accepted, with a ₹10,000 penalty for every delay.
The National Highway Authority of India has mandated that ambulances deployed on all of its projects must reach crash sites within 10 minutes when the incident is within 10 km of toll booths, failing which a ₹10,000 penalty will be imposed for each delay. The authority has also set a one-hour limit for accident victims to reach the nearest hospital after an emergency ticket is accepted, with a ₹10,000 penalty for every delay.
For incidents located farther away, the permissible time will increase proportionately based on distance. Compliance will be checked through GPS data and the NHAI Care dashboard, with a ₹10,000 penalty for each incident where the prescribed time is exceeded.
Under the new norms announced on Wednesday, ambulance movement after an emergency ticket is accepted must take less than two minutes, with the movement to be verified through GPS data and the IMS (Intelligent Medical Software) Care dashboard. An additional ₹5,000 penalty will apply for every extra minute or part thereof. The circular also notes that the delay in response to accidents has been flagged by the Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety and in a performance audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Similarly, contractors have to ensure AIS-140-compliant GPS devices must be available on on-road units with a ₹2,500-per day penalty for non-compliance. Ambulances must also remain visible on the IMS Care dashboard at all times, with the same ₹2,500 daily penalty for failure.
The rejection of any emergency ticket by an on-road unit will attract a ₹10,000 penalty per incident. NHAI has also prescribed a ₹10,000 penalty per inspection where equipment, medicines or staff are found unavailable or deficient against the requirement of the relevant contract.
Ambulances have also been asked to additionally conduct a daily dry run or mock drill and travel at least 5 km every 24 hours. The circular exempts a day from this requirement if the ambulance is attending an accident and its total movement that day exceeds 5 km.
Prof Venkatesh Balasubramanian, head of Centre of Excellence for Road Safety in IIT Madras, said the 10-minute response-time target was a “very welcome move” as it would introduce measurable service standards for ambulance operators and help improve survival after crashes. “Response time of 10 minutes is slightly high and should be actually lesser, but this is a good starting point,” he said.
Prof Balasubramanian said the next step should be to make ambulance deployment data-driven, including dynamically adjusting base locations according to accident patterns and time of day. This will help reduce the time taken to reach crash sites. He cited models tested in Madhya Pradesh for using MDT and TAEI in Tamil Nadu, where data and vehicle tracking have been used to optimise ambulance operations.
However, he said reaching the crash site quickly was only one part of emergency care. “It is okay that I reach the spot, from there where will I go?” he said, stressing the need to map trauma facilities and ensure hospitals are equipped to handle specific injuries.

headline: Heavy rain lashes Odisha, IMD issues 'red warning' for entire state

Heavy rain lashes Odisha, IMD issues 'red warning' for entire state
Bhubaneswar, Heavy rain lashed Odisha for the last 24 hours as the low-pressure area in the Bay of Bengal has become "well marked", the IMD said on Thursday.

A depression is a weather system stronger than a low-pressure area but less intense than a tropical cyclone.

headline: Supreme Court to test legality of Delhi Police's use of facial recognition of NEET protesters at Jantar Mantar
full_text:
Supreme Court to test legality of Delhi Police's use of facial recognition of NEET protesters at Jantar Mantar
The Supreme Court will examine the legality of Delhi Police’s alleged facial recognition and biometric surveillance of Jantar Mantar protesters.
The Supreme Court on Thursday agreed to examine whether the Delhi Police’s use of facial recognition technology and biometric surveillance to monitor protesters at Jantar Mantar has legal backing, and whether such mass surveillance violates fundamental rights to privacy, dignity, free speech and peaceful assembly.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Centre and the Delhi Police commissioner on a public interest litigation filed by CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP AA Rahim, challenging the alleged use of facial recognition technology, AI-powered surveillance systems and biometric identification tools against protesters.
Also read: 20 FIRs filed in Delhi over CJP protest violence
SC seeks Centre, Delhi Police response on surveillance
Senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy, appearing for Rahim, told the bench that the petition specifically challenged the use of facial recognition technology by the Delhi Police against protesters and alleged that the data collected was being held by private companies. “This is very specific prayer concerning facial recognition being used by the Delhi Police against protesters, and the data is held with private companies,” Guruswamy said.
Also Read: ‘Hands off our Jantar Mantar’: CJP reacts sharply to HC’s remarks on protest site
She said that the surveillance involved both a facial recognition vehicle and smart glasses, with data collected without the permission of those being monitored. “One maps your face and one is a vehicle. So spectacles are used and a vehicle is also used. And that data is all taken without permission. These private entities host the data. In violation, we will argue, of the DPDP Rules, CrPC and a variety of things,” she said.
The bench then directed that notice be issued and the plea be tagged with other pending petitions concerning the July 20 “Sansad Chalo” protest, which raise allegations of police excesses, including the use of pellet guns and violence against protesters and police personnel.
Also read: Biometric scanners in Delhi to be placed under CCTV watch
Plea alleges protesters subjected to biometric surveillance
The petition, filed through advocate Subhash Chandran KR, claims that since the commencement of the sit-in at Jantar Mantar on June 20, thousands of protesters, journalists and ordinary citizens have been subjected to “continuous and pervasive biometric surveillance”.
Rahim has sought a declaration that indiscriminate deployment of facial recognition and biometric surveillance against peaceful protesters is unconstitutional. He has also sought directions restraining the Delhi Police from deploying such technologies until Parliament enacts a law specifically authorising their use.
Also read: Police identify 2,873 protesters with ‘criminal backgrounds’
Petitioner seeks deletion of protesters’ biometric data
Among other reliefs, the petition seeks disclosure of the surveillance technologies, databases, standard operating procedures and vendor agreements used during the Jantar Mantar protest; deletion of protesters’ biometric data from NAFIS, CCTNS and allied databases; and a mechanism enabling individuals to ascertain whether their biometric information was collected and seek its deletion.
It has also sought directions to private vendors to permanently delete biometric information collected during the protest and certify such destruction, besides restraining them from using the data to train, develop or improve facial recognition or artificial intelligence systems.
According to the plea, the surveillance was carried out through CCTV cameras, drones, a Mobile Command and Control Vehicle and handheld devices, besides real-time facial recognition using the “Ikshana” surveillance vehicle and “AjnaLens” smart glasses. It also alleges collection of fingerprints through the NCRB’s “Abhigyan” application and their matching against the National Automated Fingerprint Identification System (NAFIS).
Plea questions legal basis for facial recognition at protests
The plea contends that there is no law authorising the biometric surveillance of people participating in a lawful protest. It argues that neither Delhi Police standing orders governing protests nor the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Act, 2022 permit such surveillance of peaceful demonstrators.
The petition relies on RTI responses obtained from the Delhi Police to claim that no privacy impact assessment was conducted before the surveillance was undertaken. It further alleges that an 80% similarity score is treated as a positive facial recognition match, despite the absence of any publicly available validation of the threshold.
It also claims that Delhi Police’s stated use of facial recognition technology is limited to tracing missing persons and identifying deceased persons, rather than policing peaceful assemblies.
Petition invokes privacy, free speech and assembly rights
The petitioner has invoked the Supreme Court’s 2017 privacy judgment in the KS Puttaswamy case, arguing that the alleged surveillance fails the constitutional requirements of legality, legitimate aim and proportionality. It contends that the indiscriminate deployment of facial recognition creates a chilling effect on the exercise of the rights to free speech and peaceful assembly under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b), apart from being arbitrary and disproportionate under Article 14.
The plea also raises concerns over the retention and possible integration of the biometric information with national criminal databases, alleging that the data could be retained indefinitely without adequate statutory safeguards, purpose limitation or a defined retention policy.
Also read: ‘Jantar Mantar Season 2 going to start very soon’: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke's big remark
Two private companies have also been made respondents to the PIL, Aditya Infotech Ltd, which allegedly supplied the “Ikshana” facial recognition vehicle, and Dimension NXG Pvt Ltd, which allegedly supplied the AjnaLens smart glasses. The plea alleges that the companies participated in the policing exercise and may continue to possess footage, facial templates and other biometric information of protesters. It also questions whether any data-processing or data-sharing agreements, or other contractual safeguards governing access to such sensitive information, were put in place.

headline: The Comptroller and Auditor General raised concerns about the inadequacies within the Green India Mission program, noting that the goal of increasing forest cover was far from realized over a decade. The audit pointed to significant issues in plannin...
full_text:
The Comptroller and Auditor General raised concerns about the inadequacies within the Green India Mission program, noting that the goal of increasing forest cover was far from realized over a decade. The audit pointed to significant issues in planning and financial oversight, which severely undermined the mission's objectives. Key vulnerable areas were neglected during afforestation, diminishing efforts to combat climate change.
NEW DELHI: Red-flagging lapses in the countryâs ongoing programme to increase and improve green cover, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) has pointed out non-achievement of forest cover targets, noting that the observed increase in forest cover fell short by nearly 98% during 10 years of implementation (2015-16 to 2024-25) of the Green India Mission (GIM).Releasing the performance audit report on the Mission, CAG highlighted the wrong choice of landscape for planting trees, absence of convergence of various schemes to increase green cover, financial mismanagement, improper planning, lack of coordination and deficient monitoring behind non-achievement of the GIMâs goals.The broad objectives under the Mission were to increase forest/tree cover, improve the quality of forest/non-forest lands, improve ecosystem services, including biodiversity, hydrological services and carbon sequestration because of forest land/non-forest land, and to increase forest-based livelihood income of households living in and around forests.Underlining its key audit findings, the CAG in its report tabled in Parliament on Wednesday said, âAs against the target of 1.4 million hectares (mha), improvement of forest cover quality was observed in only 0.11 mha (nearly 92% shortfall). Similarly, an increase in forest cover was observed in only 0.03 mha as against the target of 1.4 mha (nearly 98% shortfall).â
It also noted that despite vulnerability being a key criterion, landscapes with low to moderate priority were selected over those more vulnerable to climate change for afforestation under the Mission.
The performance audit examined the planning, implementation and monitoring of the GIM interventions in 16 states and UTs for which physical and financial targets were approved by the environment ministry during the period 2015-16 to 2024-25.Pointing out deficient monitoring, the CAG noted that 14 states even failed to provide required public web links for transparency. It flagged that audit evaluations revealed inflated data and overstated achievements, and GIS analysis showed that 70% of sampled sites had no noticeable changes attributable to GIM.

He has been covering Parliament since 2003 to see how politics shaped up domestic policy and Indiaâs position at global platform. headline: Hydraulic pressure, autopilot disconnect: Turbulence-hit Air India Phuket-Delhi flight logged 9 warnings in a minute
full_text:
Hydraulic pressure, autopilot disconnect: Turbulence-hit Air India Phuket-Delhi flight logged 9 warnings in a minute
Air India Phuket-Delhi flight: Warnings indicated low reservoir levels in the Yellow and Blue systems, autopilot disconnect and elevator flight-control fault.
A post-flight Centralised Fault Display System log from an Air India Phuket-Delhi flight that suddenly lost altitude and dropped 300 feet, leaving 24 people injured, revealed a series of warnings linked to the aircraft’s hydraulic systems, flight controls and autopilot.
The August 4 incident, which left 20 passengers and four crew members injured on flight AI2379, an Airbus A320 registered as VT-EXO, was classified as serious and led to an investigation by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB).
The pilot’s initial post-flight drug screening was recorded as “non-negative”, meaning the sample had been flagged for further testing. His confirmatory test later returned positive for cannabis.
Multiple warning signs during aircraft plunge
Deep Dive
The log, seen by HT, shows nine warning messages appearing within a minute at 9.32am IST, when the aircraft had crossed the Odisha coast after flying over the Bay of Bengal.
The warnings indicated low pressure in the Green, Blue, and Yellow hydraulic systems, in various combinations. They also showed low reservoir levels in the Yellow and Blue systems, an autopilot disconnect and an elevator flight-control fault.
Notably, the aircraft’s hydraulic systems rely on pressurised fluid to transmit power and operate heavy mechanical components.
Two emergency-exit door sensor warnings were then recorded at 9.33am and 9.35am. No additional warnings involving the hydraulic systems or elevator were recorded for the following 43 minutes.
An engine anti-ice fault appeared at 10.16am, followed by another autopilot disconnect at 10.52am. Unlike the first disconnect, the second was not recorded alongside any hydraulic warnings. The log does not provide a reason for the disconnect.
The pressure readings changed across different system combinations within the same minute, rather than showing a single system failing and remaining in that state. This could indicate a temporary event, such as a sharp vertical movement or sudden loss of altitude. Such an event can briefly move fluid inside the hydraulic reservoirs, based on a reading of the log by HT against standard A320 fault-code references.
A sustained mechanical fault would likely have generated additional warnings, including messages indicating that the issue had recurred.
Flightradar24 data places the altitude change within the same minute as the cluster of warnings. The aircraft was flying at 36,160 feet when an altitude anomaly was recorded at 9.33am IST. It then descended to around 35,800 feet, representing a loss of about 360 feet, according to Flightradar data.
Pilot slept 30-35 minutes during flight
The pilot told investigators that he slept for 30 to 35 minutes during the flight, went to the washroom and then returned to stand behind the first officer, according to two people familiar with his account to the AAIB.
They said he was talking about the air conditioning system when the altitude event occurred and that he was thrown to the cockpit floor. The first officer was operating the aircraft, while the commander was acting as the pilot monitoring, the two people said.
A cabin crew member seated in the observer seat, which a departing pilot is required to assign when leaving the cockpit, helped the commander back up, the people said. This was the first detailed account from the cockpit crew about what happened aboard flight AI2379.
The complete sequence of events inside the cockpit could not be independently confirmed by the pilots' accounts to investigators.

headline: Vijay Mallya seeks closure of pending matters, Bombay HC wants ED's reply first
full_text:
Vijay Mallya seeks closure of pending matters, Bombay HC wants ED's reply first
The court, however, declined to proceed without first hearing the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and directed that the matter be taken up on September 9.
Fugitive businessman Vijay Mallya on Wednesday sought closure of a long-pending matter before the Bombay High Court, claiming that his civil liabilities had effectively been settled after banks recovered around Rs 15,000 crore against an original claim of about Rs 6,203 crore, including interest.
The court, however, declined to proceed without first hearing the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and directed that the matter be taken up on September 9.
A bench of Justice Milind Jadhav said Mallya’s claim of settlement would have to be verified by the consortium of lenders, particularly the lead bank, State Bank of India (SBI), as well as the ED.
The court also sought details on the present status of the agency’s proceedings against Mallya before deciding the future course of his application.
Mallya had approached the Bombay High Court in January 2020, challenging a December 2019 order of a Mumbai Sessions Court that permitted the consortium of creditor banks to use confiscated assets for recovering their dues.
The petition remained pending for nearly six years and came up for consideration after the High Court recently began taking up old matters that had remained on the shelf.
Senior Advocate Amit Desai, appearing for Mallya, argued that the application had been filed in 2018 when discussions over a possible settlement were underway.
He said most of the assets identified and attached by the ED during the original proceedings had since been dealt with, making the dispute essentially a commercial matter that now required closure.
The bench, however, made clear that the ED’s position had to be established before any further steps could be taken.
The court said, "It is clarified that only after hearing ED, this Court will decide the further course of action in the present Application and consider issuing notices to the other Respondents, (other banks)".
MALLYA IN UK SINCE 2016
The development comes against the backdrop of Mallya’s wider legal battle over his status as a fugitive economic offender.
He left India in March 2016 after the collapse of Kingfisher Airlines, which had borrowed thousands of crores from a consortium of banks.
He was declared a fugitive economic offender in 2019, allowing authorities to confiscate his properties under the law, while India has continued efforts to secure his extradition from the UK.
The High Court’s latest order does not amount to acceptance of Mallya’s claim that his liabilities stand settled.
The court is expected to examine the banks’ recovery figures and the ED’s position at the next hearing before determining whether the long-pending application can proceed and whether other respondents, including the creditor banks, need to be formally heard.

headline: Telangana govt warns of fake SIR messages stealing voters' bank details
full_text:
Telangana govt warns of fake SIR messages stealing voters' bank details
The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau has warned voters about fraudsters posing as Election Commission officials through fake SIR messages. The advisory says the scam uses small payment requests and malicious links to steal banking details during the electoral roll revision.
The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TGCSB) has issued a public advisory warning citizens against a new cyber fraud in which scammers are impersonating Election Commission officials and targeting voters through fake Special Intensive Revision (SIR) messages to steal banking information.
According to the bureau, cybercriminals are circulating fraudulent messages through WhatsApp and other digital platforms, claiming that a person's voter details are incorrect or that their SIR application has been rejected.
The messages contain links that falsely promise to help voters update or correct their electoral information. Once contacted, the fraudsters, posing as Election Commission officials, ask victims to click on malicious links or join WhatsApp chats to complete the verification process.
IT STARTS WITH RS 5
The TGCSB said the scammers often demand a nominal payment, such as Rs 5, claiming it is required to verify or update voter details.
After gaining the victim's trust, they attempt to obtain sensitive financial information, including internet banking credentials, debit and credit card details, PINs, passwords and other confidential data.
The bureau clarified that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process is completely free of cost and that the Election Commission does not charge any fee for updating voter information or processing applications.
Citizens have been advised not to respond to unsolicited calls or messages seeking payment for SIR-related services.
AVOUD CLICKING ON SUSPICIOUS LINKS
The TGCSB also urged people to avoid clicking on suspicious links received through messaging platforms or social media and to verify any election-related communication only through official Election Commission channels.
The cyber security agency further cautioned the public never to share confidential banking information, including internet banking usernames and passwords, debit or credit card details, PINs or One-Time Passwords (OTPs), with anyone claiming to be an election official.
The advisory comes amid the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, with authorities warning that fraudsters may attempt to exploit the exercise to target unsuspecting voters. The TGCSB urged citizens to remain vigilant and immediately report any suspicious messages, phone calls or online links to the appropriate authorities or the cybercrime helpline.

headline: Remove pre-ride tipping prompts, government directs ride-hailing aggregators
full_text:
Remove pre-ride tipping prompts, government directs ride-hailing aggregators
The Union road transport and highways ministry said tipping shall be entirely voluntary and be offered only after completion of the journey
The Union road transport and highways ministry has directed ride-hailing aggregators to remove any tipping prompts or interface features shown before a ride is completed, saying such mechanisms could improperly influence passengers’ decisions and create an impression that paying extra could improve service.
“Tipping shall be entirely voluntary and shall be offered only after completion of the journey,” said the ministry. It cited Clause 14.15 of the Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025, and said a tipping option can be provided only after completion of the journey and cannot be available at booking, before commencement or during the ride.
Also read: No Marathi, no licence: New rule for auto, taxi, cab drivers in Maharashtra from August 18
The directive, issued on Tuesday, came after the ministry’s attention was drawn to prompts displayed by some aggregators, including “Advance Tip”, “Choose an Add-on” and messages suggesting that a tip could improve the chances of quicker ride confirmation or driver acceptance.
The ministry said no feature, prompt, message, add-on, payment option or other user-interface element should be displayed before completion of a ride if it directly or indirectly encourages passengers to pay an additional amount to influence ride confirmation, driver acceptance, allocation, waiting time or quality of service.
The directive specified that the entire tip amount must be credited to the driver without any deduction by the aggregator. It prohibited tipping mechanisms that are misleading, manipulative, or violate the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
The ministry advised all motor vehicle aggregators to immediately review their mobile applications and digital platforms and modify any interface or functionality inconsistent with the guidelines.

headline: India retail inflation holds steady at 4.45% in July despite stress over rise in food, fuel prices
full_text:
India retail inflation holds steady at 4.45% in July despite stress over rise in food, fuel prices
Retail inflation rose marginally to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June, with food and fuel prices driving the recent increase.
Retail inflation was flat in India between June and July, barely changing from 4.38% in June to 4.45% in July. This vindicates the position of RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), which ruled out any widespread inflation pressure in the economy in its meeting held last week. The latest inflation reading is also in line with analyst expectations. A Bloomberg poll of economists expected this number to be 4.5%.
The plateauing of retail inflation numbers, as measured by the annual change in Consumer Price Index (CPI), follows a continuous rise in monthly data in the new inflation series which has a base year of 2024. Data from the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE) shows that inflation fell to a near-zero level (0.04%) in October 2025 and has risen every month since to 4.45% in July.
Also read: The RBI is emerging as an Asian rate outlier. Five charts show why
Food, fuel drive recent rise in inflation
Most of the recent increase in inflation has been in food and fuel prices, as can be seen in the trends in core and non-core inflation.
Core inflation measures the non-food non-fuel part of the CPI basket and is immune to seasonal fluctuations. According to CMIE data, core inflation in July 2026 was 4%, the same as in June and not very high from the 3.3% in January, the earliest period for which data is available in the new series. Non-core inflation, on the other hand, increased from 1.9% in January to 5.1% in July. Food inflation increased from 2.1% to 5.2% between January and July. Food items have a 36% weight in the new CPI basket.
Also read: How US bill proposing 100% tariffs over Russian oil purchase could hurt India
Transport fuel inflation rises amid West Asia war
While fuel is not a consolidated category in CPI data, it have nevertheless seen an increase in inflation because of the war in West Asia. LPG and PNG inflation (with a combined weight of 1.98%) has increased from 1.7% in January to 5% in July.
Fuels and lubricants for personal transport equipment (this category includes petrol, diesel, and CNG with a combined weight of 4.85%) has seen inflation increase from 0.07% in January to 7.55% in July.
To be sure, June and July numbers for personal transport fuels are almost exactly the same and likely to continue at almost the same level unless prices are lowered. This is because petrol and diesel prices were flat in 2025 and saw hikes in instalments that started and ended in May 2026.
Also read: World youth unemployment rate rose last year: UN
RBI sees inflation averaging 5% in 2026-27
MPC’s latest forecast, which was released earlier this month, expects annual CPI inflation to be 5% in 2026-27 with quarterly values being 4.7%, 5.9% and 5.5% in the quarters ending September 2026, December 2026 and March 2027. Inflation for the June quarter came at 4.3%, which was 30 basis points (one basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point) lower than RBI estimate.
“As increases in inflation continues to be driven by food and administered price increases, we expect the MPC to look through these higher inflation outcomes and persist with a pause for the remainder of 2026,” Aastha Gudwani, Chief India Economist at Barclays said in a note.

Under his leadership HT’s data journalism work has established itself as a niche product in Indian journalism and pushed the boundaries of marrying academic rigour with news sense and speed. headline: From Dalit student denied drinking water to President: Kovind reflects on his journey in new memoir
full_text:
From Dalit student denied drinking water to President: Kovind reflects on his journey in new memoir
Ram Nath Kovind’s memoir traces his journey from a Dalit student to President, covering political experiences, One Nation, One Election and key leaders.
In the early years of Independence, Dalit students at a primary school in Paraunkh village of Uttar Pradesh were not free to drink water as they pleased. They had to inform their teacher, who would then ask another student to give them water. This protocol was not required for students from savarna families.
On July 25, 2017, one of those students, Ram Nath Kovind, took charge as India’s second Dalit president, tracing a stunning arc – “of a village lad from the rural hinterlands of Uttar Pradesh to the Central Hall of Parliament to be sworn in as the First Citizen of India”.
The former president details this broad journey in his memoir, Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles, released on Wednesday by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi.
Also Read | ‘My election as President shows greatness of our democracy’: Kovind writes in his autobiography
“I believed that my elevation to the highest post in the country symbolized the greatness of our democracy,” he writes in the 334-page book, published by Rupa Publications.
Kovind also leaves insights into his life after demitting office in July 2022 and offers personal accounts of his interactions with and experiences of Modi, Atal Bihari Vajpayee and LK Advani. It offers a glance into his interaction with Opposition leaders through his political career – as a BJP worker, as an MP, as governor, as President, as well as head of the high-level committee to take a call on simultaneous elections.
At the launch event, at Vigyan Bhagwan, Modi said Kovind’s life was a case study in how a person should treat society as “an equal partner in his success” rather than blame it for difficulties.
Modi recalled that Kovind lost his mother in a house fire when just four years old, saying the tragedy made him stronger. A neighbour helped raise him, while his father became his “hero”.
Also Read | Create good human beings, not just good engineers, says former President Ram Nath Kovind
Drawing a parallel, Modi said he was fortunate his mother Heeraben “lived beyond 100,” but he could still “feel her absence”. Heeraben died on December 30, 2022.
The 80-year-old throws his weight behind the “One Nation, One Election” plan, drawing on experiences through his career.
“ONOE…is aimed at enhancing the efficiency of our electoral system, reducing the cost of elections, and enabling the government to focus on development without the frequent interruptions of staggered elections,” writes Kovind.
“While it is a challenging endeavour, I believe it is essential for a more stable and cohesive democratic process,” he adds.
He says the panel held 65 meetings over 191 days, consulting political parties, constitutional experts, political leaders and the public.
Of 62 political parties approached, 47 responded: 32 supported ONOE while 15 opposed it. The BJP and a clutch of regional parties – including the BJD, Shiv Sena, JD(U), SAD and AIADMK – supported the proposal, while the Congress opposed it.
Kovind’s account of his entry into the BJP is closely linked to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.
He recalls attending a massive VHP rally at Delhi’s Boat Club on April 4, 1991, organised in support of the construction of the Ram temple in Ayodhya. Atal Bihari Vajpayee and VHP leader Ashok Singhal were present, as was Modi, then a volunteer in the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. Kovind says Modi was instrumental in a 1991 signature campaign for the temple.
Kovind describes Vajpayee’s speech on an inclusive society, tolerance and peaceful coexistence as a “powerful catalyst” in his decision to join the BJP. He eventually joined the party in April 1991.
Also Read | PM Modi remembers his mother at ex-president's autobiography launch: ‘Even today, I feel the void’
He also writes that the BJP’s support for the Ram Janmabhoomi movement represented “a burning issue of cultural nationalism” and a struggle between “pseudo-secularism and real equal respect to every religion”.
The former president also discusses BR Ambedkar’s influence on his life and work.
He recalls that former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, at the 2001 Dalit Sangam rally at the Red Fort, declared that his government would function on the basis of “Bhim Smriti” rather than “Manusmriti”.
Kovind’s Modi account stretches back to the latter’s days as BJP general secretary (organisation). He describes Modi as “meticulous and methodical”, recalling working with the Prime Minister on the 2001 rally.
Through his decades in the political space, Kovind recalls his interactions with the Opposition.
Also Read | Peace must become personal commitment, not govt duty alone: Ex-President Kovind
He speaks warmly of former prime minister Manmohan Singh.
“Dr Manmohan Singh was one of those rare politicians in our country whose humility, modesty and gentleness uniquely defined his persona... One had so much to learn from the erudite and soft-spoken Dr Manmohan Singh,” he writes.
At the same time, Kovind recalls his time canvassing support during his presidential campaign, when he met leaders across the political spectrum. He recalls support from several opposition or regional parties, while noting that former Uttar Pradesh chief ministers Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati ultimately did not vote for him, “perhaps guided more by political interests”.

headline: Mumbai: A relative of Maharashtra minister Girish Mahajan is among two persons arrested for allegedly cheating a person of Rs 2.17 crore by promising lucrative contracts linked to works for the upcoming Kumbh Mela in Nashik..BJP leader Mahajan has ac...
full_text: Mumbai: A relative of Maharashtra minister Girish Mahajan is among two persons arrested for allegedly cheating a person of Rs 2.17 crore by promising lucrative contracts linked to works for the upcoming Kumbh Mela in Nashik..BJP leader Mahajan has acknowledged that the accused is a distant relative, but a "gone case", and called for stringent action against those found guilty..The police made the arrests after unearthing an alleged scam of Rs 305 crore related to fake work orders for the Kumbh Mela..The arrested persons, identified as 32-year-old Tanay Mahajan (relative of the minister) and Narendra Totaram Mahajan (51), allegedly cheated a person of Rs 2.17 crore under the pretext of helping him secure a housekeeping order for Kumbh Mela work, police said on Wednesday..The accused duo and their accomplice allegedly won the complainant’s trust by showing him a fake work order with a “list of Kumbh Mela works” containing the Government of India emblem and the name of Nashik Trimbakeshwar Kumbh Mela Authority, they said..Girish Mahajan acknowledged Tanay was a distant relative and that criminal cases had been registered against him.."He is a gone case. Similar cases had previously been registered against Tanay... I spoke with Nashik Police Commissioner Sandeep Karnik, and three to four names had surfaced in the crime. I believe six to seven persons were involved and should face strict action," the minister said..Nashik Kumbh Mela to draw 8–10 times more devotees: Fadnavis.Nashik DCP Kirankumar Chauhan on Wednesday said Girish Mahajan had alerted Karnik about incidents of cheating by a gang under the pretext of Kumbh Mela work orders.."The investigation revealed that two accused had shown fake documents and allotted fake work orders for works worth Rs 591 crore to complainants who have come forward so far. In return, they took Rs 305 crore from them and cheated them. Accordingly, three cases were filed with Nashik Road Police on August 11, and two persons have been arrested so far," Chauhan said..Girish Mahajan had said the Kumbh Mela tender process is conducted online. "However, a racket is working to cheat people by saying that the process of some tenders is on in an offline manner also," he said..The minister clarified that work orders are not issued in the name of officials and do not bear authorised QR codes..He said that 12 such incidents of cheating have been reported, following which Nashik Police registered three cases.

headline: Lok Sabha passes bill restricting states’ power to tax minerals amid protests
full_text:
Lok Sabha passes bill restricting states’ power to tax minerals amid protests
The bill, which amends the Mines and Minerals (development and regulation) Act, 1957, was introduced on Monday by minister of coal and mines G Kishan Reddy.
The Lok Sabha on Wednesday passed the Mines and Minerals (development and regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which aims to restrict state governments from imposing taxes, cesses or levies on minerals rights and ‘mineral-bearing lands’, via voice vote sans debate amid opposition protests.
The bill, which amends the Mines and Minerals (development and regulation) Act, 1957, was introduced on Monday by minister of coal and mines G Kishan Reddy. It was passed in the second half of the Lok Sabha session on Wednesday, with Jagdambika Pal, who was in the chair, beginning proceedings by asking the Opposition to maintain decorum.
Also Read | Bill to bar state taxes on minerals tabled in Parliament, Oppn calls for committee review
The amendment bill introduces a new section that says that “no tax, cess or such other levy (by whatever name called) shall be imposed by the state Government on mineral rights; or mineral bearing lands, either based on mineral quantity or mineral value or royalty payable…except in accordance with such conditions or restrictions as may be prescribed by the Central Government..”
The bill also proposes to expand the central government’s powers to regulate mines to mineral bearing lands having ore content in accordance with the parameters prescribed under the MMDR Act.
The proposed amendments are the fallout of a July 2024 ruling by the Supreme Court that upheld the power of states to levy taxes on mineral rights and and mineral-bearing lands.
Also Read | 'Cowards': Congress on Amit Shah's 'no show' in Lok Sabha, Rijiju hits back
The bill clarifies any tax, cess or other levy which is not deposited with the state government or recovered by it before the commencement of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, will be deemed to be invalid at all material times. However, those already deposited, will not be liable to be refunded.
PMK chief Anbumani Ramadoss urged the Centre to immediately withdraw the proposed amendment bill, warning that it usurps the taxation rights of state governments.

headline: Govt says Track-2 dialogues with Pakistan outside its purview: ‘Individuals interacting in private capacity’
full_text:
Govt says Track-2 dialogues with Pakistan outside its purview: ‘Individuals interacting in private capacity’
On question asked by Kharge about Track-2 talks with Pakistan, MoS Kirti Vardhan Singh said participants act in private capacity.
The Indian government said on Thursday that engagements between Indian and Pakistani think tanks and academicians, including Track-2 dialogues, are outside its purview, with individuals participating in such interactions in their private capacity.
Responding to a question by Leader of Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge in the Rajya Sabha on the government’s assessment of, and any advisory issued regarding, the participation of retired Indian diplomats, military officers and civil society figures in Track-2 dialogues with Pakistani counterparts, Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said their views do not reflect those of the Government of India.
“Individuals participate in Track 2 dialogues in their private capacity, and their views do not reflect the views of the Government of India,” said Singh, via a statement.
Indian and Pakistani experts comprising retired military officials, diplomats and politicians participated in Track 2 discussions on the sidelines of a regional security conference in Colombo in June.
In a separate response, Singh said India and Pakistan currently maintain their respective diplomatic missions in each other’s capitals and continue to have functional engagements, including DGMO-level talks, exchange of pre-notification of flight testing of ballistic missiles, exchange of lists of nuclear installations and exchange of lists of prisoners in each other’s custody.
IWT still in abeyance?
Responding to a question on whether the abeyance of the Indus Waters Treaty, declared after the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year, continues and whether India has received any communication from Pakistan on the matter, Singh said India had taken several diplomatic measures following the April 22, 2025 attack, including holding the treaty in abeyance.
“The Treaty will continue to be held in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross-border terrorism,” Singh said.
India put the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance as part of a package of punitive diplomatic and economic measures soon after The Resistance Front (TRF), a proxy for Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), killed 26 civilians at Pahalgam in April 2025. India launched Operation Sindoor in May last year to target terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan in retaliation for the attack.

headline: A new notice has gone up in Panchakattu Dosa, a popular restaurant franchisee in Hyderabad, that listed how the prices of various items that affect food business have changed. Gas is up by 85%, urad dal by 17%, disposables by 10% and rice upto 10%.
full_text:
A new notice has gone up in Panchakattu Dosa, a popular restaurant franchisee in Hyderabad, that listed how the prices of various items that affect food business have changed. Gas is up by 85%, urad dal by 17%, disposables by 10% and rice upto 10%.
The notice left a message: “Due to increased costs of all the raw materials in the last six months, we have no choice but to increase our prices”.
In another part of the city, Kakatiya Deluxe Mess pegged its new ‘all-you-can-eat’ thali price at ₹250 from August 1. Just eight months earlier, on January 1, the same meal at the same restaurant cost ₹200. Between the jump from ₹200 to ₹250 or a 25% jump in prices, is the impact of food inflation in Hyderabad, or as Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman called it, the impact of ‘thalinomics’.
Smaller restaurants too, have increased the prices in Hyderabad by upto 20% over the last six months, since the outbreak of the war of Israel and US combine against Iran that has spilled over to much of the Middle East.
“How can I reduce the price? The government has executed only one price drop while it hiked multiple prices, like taking the price of a commercial cylinder above the ₹3,000 mark. It was less than half that before the war began,” says a food kiosk owner in Ameerpet, where a street is filled with food carts selling everything from bhajjis to biryani.
The rise in price is across the board from restaurants inside malls to standalone cafes and restaurants. At the newly-opened Lakeshore Mall, a vegetarian north-Indian thali’s price has gone up from ₹325 to ₹399 in a span of four months.
The price of a commercial 19 kg LPG cylinder in Hyderabad is currently ₹2,985 after a reduction of ₹209 at the beginning of August. The same gas cylinder was priced at ₹1,742 on January 1, showing a price jump of 71%. Added to this is the factor that a majority of small and medium food businesses rely on private parties to supply the LPG cylinders, who add their own share to the high price.
“The food prices are up everywhere, and it makes it really difficult for those with student-sized pocket money to not only go out, but even to eat at home, because even the prices of groceries have increased, so we are buying ready to eat meals like cup noodles or bread, which would use less gas, rather than proper meals with rice, dal, etc,” said a student preparing for the Telangana Group-1 exam at S.R. Nagar.
The anecdotal accounts are backed by statistics released by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. According to MOSPI’s the All India Consumer Price Index data, Telangana recorded the highest inflation in the country at 6.32%, while the national average is 4.45% year-on-year inflation rate based on All India Consumer Price Index (CPI) with base year 2024 for the month of July 2026 over July 2025.
Nationally, the year-on-year inflation rate based on the All India Consumer Food Price Index for the month of July this year, compared to July 2025 is 5.52%.

headline: A 21-year-old pickup van driver was found dead in his vehicle near Old Maggi Point on the Mussoorie-Dehradun highway in Uttarakhand early Thursday morning, police said.
full_text:
A 21-year-old pickup van driver was found dead in his vehicle near Old Maggi Point on the Mussoorie-Dehradun highway in Uttarakhand early Thursday morning, police said.
The deceased, a resident of the Kempty area of Tehri Garhwal district, was found by his elder brother, who was travelling along the same route and noticed his brother’s pickup van parked on the roadside in suspicious circumstances.
Police said they are investigating the circumstances surrounding the death from all possible angles.
Station House Officer (SHO) of Mussoorie police station Devendra Chauhan said the deceased’s 28-year-old brother informed the Kolukhet police outpost and approached the vehicle to check on his brother. “He found him hanging from a thin white rope tied to the left exterior cargo rail of the pickup,” Chauhan said.
A police team subsequently reached the spot and inspected the area. Police secured and sealed the site to preserve evidence and called a forensic field unit to collect scientific evidence, Chauhan said.
The police also conducted the legal inquest proceedings and sent the body for a postmortem.
Officers said they are investigating the circumstances surrounding the death from all possible angles. Police are also examining the call details and other information from the deceased’s mobile phone as part of the investigation.

headline: Teacher beats class 10 girls, leaving them unable to write exam in Tamil Nadu, booked
full_text:
Teacher beats class 10 girls, leaving them unable to write exam in Tamil Nadu, booked
The incident took place on July 20 at a Government Higher Secondary School in VK Pudur near Surandai in Tamil Nadu.
A school teacher in Tamil Nadu’s Tenkasi district has been booked for allegedly beating ten female students studying in Class 10 with a cane, leaving them with severe hand injuries, police said.
The incident took place on July 20 at a Government Higher Secondary School in VK Pudur near Surandai.
Enraged teacher beat students
According to a police statement cited by news agency PTI, the accused, identified as Thenmaria Suganthi, was conducting a Class 11 session when she became angry over noise coming from an adjacent Class 10 classroom.
She allegedly entered the Class 10 room and caned the students, leaving around 10 of them with severe injuries to their hands. The students were taken to VK Pudur Government Hospital and nearby private healthcare facilities for treatment.
One of the injured students was later shifted to Tenkasi Government Hospital, where she remained admitted for three days, officials said, according to a PTI report.
The students were unable to attend school or appear for their exams due to swelling in their hands. Following this, one of the parents approached the District Collector and filed a formal complaint.
Also Read | 'Tamil Nadu waiting to see CM Vijay pick Trisha as deputy CM': AIADMK leader
Based on the complaint, Veerakeralampudur police registered a case against the teacher under Section 115(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for voluntarily causing hurt, along with relevant provisions of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act. Further investigation into the matter is underway, said the report.
The incident reminded of a 2024 episode in Tamil Nadu in which a football coach was seen kicking and slapping players, triggering widespread outrage and calls for strict action against him.
In a video of the incident, members of the football team are seen sitting on the ground while the coach speaks to them. He then slapped a player sitting at the end of the line before turning to others and assaulting them. The coach was also seen kicking some players and pulling the hair of others, as the students attempted to shield themselves from the assault.

headline: Madhya Pradesh to deploy over 100 guards, check posts to combat illegal sand mining at Chambal sanctuary
full_text:
Madhya Pradesh to deploy over 100 guards, check posts to combat illegal sand mining at Chambal sanctuary
Surveillance measures include 35 CCTV cameras and AI systems, prompted by Supreme Court actions against the ongoing threat to wildlife and ecological integrity.
The Madhya Pradesh forest department will deploy more than 100 armed guards, permanent check posts and a surveillance system to protect the Chambal Wildlife Sanctuary from illegal sand mining, officials said on Wednesday.
“By September, we will set up 16 permanent check posts, install 35 CCTV cameras, and an Artificial Intelligence (AI) monitoring system at 44 sensitive ghats, where rampant illegal mining has been reported. The decision follows the Supreme Court’s suo motu action against sand mining in the sanctuary,” said Shyam Singh, superintendent of Chambal Wildlife Sanctuary.
Also Read | Supreme Court orders states to shield Chambal forest staff from prosecution
He added that the forest guards would get 12-bore pump-action guns after the state government granted immunity to the forest officials in firearm use cases. Training sessions under police supervision will be conducted for forest guards to use firearms in emergencies. According to officials, 145 forest guards and 45 foresters from Morena division will undergo training before deployment.
Principal chief conservator of forests Subhranjan Sen said, “We have already provided the required number of forest guards and foresters with firearms to check the illegal mining menace in Morena. Training will now be conducted with a standard operating procedure (SOP) to deal with those involved in illegal sand mining.”
The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of illegal sand mining in the Chambal Wildlife Sanctuary, which spans 732 sq km across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. This mining has adversely impacted the home of gharials, dolphins, and tortoises.
Also Read | Illegal mining at Aravalis: HC asks Haryana, Centre for satellite imagery of Charkhi Dadri area
In its observations, a Supreme Court bench of justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said, “The duties discharged by forest officers and forest guards within the National Chambal Gharial Sanctuary are not confined merely to protection of forests and wildlife. These personnel are entrusted with the highly dangerous task of safeguarding ecologically fragile and strategically significant wildlife habitats from organised illegal sand mining, poaching, and other unlawful activities.”
Also Read | Illegal mining crackdown: ₹46L recovered in penalties in a month
The Supreme Court directed Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh to provide legal protection and prosecution immunity to frontline forest guards.

headline: 6 farm labourers killed in lorry-auto collision in Telangana’s Sangareddy district
full_text:
6 farm labourers killed in lorry-auto collision in Telangana’s Sangareddy district
When the autorickshaw was taking a U-turn on the highway near Satwar, a heavy tanker travelling at high speed from Mumbai towards Hyderabad crashed into it
At least six people, including the driver of an autorickshaw, were killed while six others sustained serious injuries, when a speeding tanker rammed into their vehicle in Telangana’s Sangareddy district on Tuesday night, police said on Wednesday.
The incident happened near Satwar village in Zaheerabad mandal when the autorickshaw carrying 11 women agriculture labourers, was taking a U-turn on the Hyderabad-Mumbai national highway (NH-65) at around 8:30pm.
An official from Zaheerabad police station said the agricultural labourers from Rajagiri in Bidar district of Karnataka had come to the Budhera area of Munipally mandal in Sangareddy district to work in agricultural fields.
“After completing their work, they were returning in an autorickshaw. When the autorickshaw was taking a U-turn on the highway near Satwar, a heavy tanker travelling at high speed from Mumbai towards Hyderabad crashed into it,” the police official told local reporters.
The impact of the collision was so severe that the autorickshaw was badly mangled.
Also Read: Four youths killed, two injured in road accident on Pune-Satara highway
“Four persons died on the spot, while two others succumbed to their injuries while undergoing treatment,” the police said.
The deceased were identified as Rekhamma (36), Kavitha (40), Sridevi (45), Reshma (28), Nikhita (30) and autorickshaw driver Devadas (35).
Six other persons travelling in the autorickshaw suffered serious injuries and were shifted to the government hospital at Zaheerabad for treatment. The condition of two of them is said to be critical, police said.
“We have registered a case of accident and taken up an investigation into the accident,” the official said.
Similar accident on same highway
Two persons were killed when a car crashed into a divider near Venkatapur junction in Kohir mandal.
According to the police, the car was travelling from Zaheerabad towards Sadashivpet when it hit the road divider. Following the impact, the vehicle went out of control, crossed into the opposite lane and collided with vehicles coming from the other direction.
The two occupants of the car, Shankar (52) and Mallikarjun (50), both from Sadashivpet mandal, died on the spot.
“This case, registered for negligent driving, is also under investigation,” the police added.
Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy expressed his condolences over the death of agriculture labourers in the Zaheerabad road accident.
A statement from the CMO said the chief minister instructed the district authorities to extend all possible help to the families of the deceased and ensure that the injured get the best possible treatment.

headline: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government signed 97 memoranda of understanding, involving more than ₹67,542 crore in investment, at its first major investment conclave, ‘Vettri Tamil Nadu Investment Conclave 2026’, on Thursday. The MoUs were exch...
full_text:
The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government signed 97 memoranda of understanding, involving more than ₹67,542 crore in investment, at its first major investment conclave, ‘Vettri Tamil Nadu Investment Conclave 2026’, on Thursday. The MoUs were exchanged in the presence of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay.
“With today’s announcements, cumulative investment commitments in the first 100 days of our government will cross ₹1 lakh crore, capable of generating more than 1.2 lakh jobs. On an average, this is a ₹1,000-crore committed capital for every single day we have been in office,” Minister for Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce S. Keerthana said in her address, broadcast live through a YouTube feed from the venue.
“All these projects are expected to be grounded within six months to one year,” Industries Secretary S. Vijayakumar told The Hindu.
“Around 25 companies are coming to Tamil Nadu for the first time. This shows they continue to see the State as an attractive investment destination. At the same time, the expansion plans of the existing players demonstrate policy continuity and confidence in Tamil Nadu,” said Deepak Jacob, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Guidance Tamil Nadu, the nodal agency for investment promotion. “The conclave also marks a new chapter in Tamil Nadu-Russia economic cooperation through an MoU with Sberbank, focused on skilling and technology transfer,” he added.
One of the highlights of the conclave is that Ramanathapuram has secured its first major investment from the Phoenix Kothari Footwear Limited. This is a ₹1,000-crore project that could boost the economy of the district and the condition of women. “The Chief Minister wanted us to invest in some backward district, and that’s how we shortlisted this location. We will set up a footwear park where we will bring in allied component makers. Most components come from Vietnam. We want to make all of them in India. headline: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday called for value addition to the beach sand minerals available in abundance in the State, especially the rare earth minerals, in a manner that would contribute to the development of both...

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday called for value addition to the beach sand minerals available in abundance in the State, especially the rare earth minerals, in a manner that would contribute to the development of both the State and the country.
He stressed the need to manufacture value-added products within the State to reduce the country's dependence on other nations for rare earth minerals. He also called for adoption of advanced technologies required to achieve this goal.
A delegation led by Karan Adani, Managing Director of Adani Ports and SEZ Limited, met Mr. Naidu at the State Secretariat on Wednesday. The delegation briefed the Chief Minister on the titanium plant proposed by the Adani Group in Srikakulam district with an investment of ₹16,000 crore.
The representatives explained the proposed beach sand mining activities, the products that could be manufactured from the minerals, and their applications and market demand. They said the ilmenite mineral in beach sand could undergo value addition to produce titanium slag, titanium dioxide and titanium sponge.
The delegation also explained that titanium dioxide could be used in a range of sectors, including paints and coatings, cosmetics, plastics and polymers, and products providing protection against ultraviolet radiation.
Mr. Naidu said the State should focus on manufacturing value-added products rather than limiting beach sand mineral development to the extraction of raw minerals. The entire value chain should be developed in a manner that would maximise benefits to Andhra Pradesh and the country, he said.
Referring to rare earth minerals, the Chief Minister said India should move towards self-reliance and avoid dependence on other countries. Mining of rare earth minerals should contribute to nation-building while also strengthening the State’s economy, he said.
He directed the officials and the industry to focus on identifying the resources available in the State, the required technologies and suitable technology partners for the extraction, processing rare earth minerals and their value addition. The entire process should be designed to serve the interests of both the State and the nation, he said.
The Adani Group representatives briefed the Chief Minister on its proposed initiatives in Visakhapatnam, including skill development, an Adani University, an international school, a 1,000-bed hospital and a 150-seat medical college.
The delegation also presented details of the master plans for the proposed Adani data centre and IT park in Visakhapatnam.
Minister Kollu Ravindra and senior officials of the Mines Department attended the meeting.

headline: Former Punjab CM Beant Singh’s murder convict declines custody parole offer, seeks regular parole
full_text:
Former Punjab CM Beant Singh’s murder convict declines custody parole offer, seeks regular parole
Custody parole is a short-term, supervised release of a convicted prisoner from jail. An armed police escort stays with the inmate the entire time.
Former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh’s assassination convict Jagtar Singh Hawara on Wednesday declined the Delhi Prisons Department’s two-day custody parole offer to meet his ailing octogenarian mother, as he sought regular parole, said people familiar with the matter.
Custody parole is a short-term, supervised release of a convicted prisoner from jail. An armed police escort stays with the inmate the entire time as they attend urgent family events. Hawara is currently lodged in Central Jail, Mandoli.
Hawara seeks regular parole
The development comes hours after CM Bhagwant Mann met Punjab governor and UT administrator Gulab Chand Kataria to push for a 10-day parole to Hawara, saying his government was willing to take full responsibility for maintaining the law and order situation during the release period.
Deep Dive
“Based on the court’s directions and security review, top officials granted Hawara custody parole of two days. However, he denied it, saying he does not want police protection. He’s a high-risk prisoner and we have to deploy staff with him,” said a senior official posted at the Delhi Prisons Department headquarters in Tihar, on the condition of anonymity. “Top officials will take a final call whether he’ll be given custody parole or normal parole,” he added.
Parole conditions still being discussed
Till the filing of this report, meetings were on between Hawara and Mandoli jail officials to negotiate the parole conditions. Hawara’s counsel Maninder Singh, however, said they have not received any communication regarding parole from the authorities so far.
Earlier, after meeting Kataria, Mann said he was hopeful Hawara would be granted parole as the governor assured him that he would speak to the Union home secretary.

headline: The ‘untainted’ teachers who lost their jobs in the West Bengal school recruitment scam resumed their protest in Kolkata on Wednesday (August 12), after the counselling process for their reappointment was adjourned indefinitely following a fresh recr...
