The ‘untainted’ teachers who lost their jobs in the West Bengal school recruitment scam resumed their protest in Kolkata on Wednesday (August 12), after the counselling process for their reappointment was adjourned indefinitely following a fresh recruitment process ordered by the Supreme Court.
“Some of us here have proved our merit twice. We kept faith in the system even though it failed us the first time. We passed the exam again after nine years, yet the counselling process has stopped. We are headed towards death now,” a protesting teacher said.
The ‘untainted’ teachers had reappeared for the recruitment process after their appointments under the 2016 panel were scrapped by the Supreme Court over irregularities in the recruitment process.
Most of the 15,403 ‘untainted’ teachers had made it to the final merit list of the 2025 recruitment process after clearing the examination and were awaiting counselling to finalise their appointments. The latest development has left them in limbo.
In a notification issued on August 11, the West Bengal Central School Service Commission stated that the counselling process for candidates empanelled under the 2nd State Level Selection Test (Assistant Teachers), 2025, for Classes XI-XII, scheduled to begin on August 14, had been “adjourned until further notice”.
Some candidates who had made it to the merit list had already appeared for counselling, while others were awaiting their turn. The suspension of the process has triggered protests among the teachers.
Meanwhile, the reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBC) candidates has been reduced from 17% to 7% by the new government, even though the examination was held in September 2025, under the previous reservation rules.
“This has added an unnecessary level of complication to the recruitment process. What is the need for this new rule in the middle of the hiring process? When Suvendu Adhikari was not in power, they had promised that the ‘untainted’ teachers and staff members would get their jobs back. We want him to keep his promise,” Mehboob Mondal, a leader of the Joggya Sikkhak Sikkhika Adhikar Mancha (Deserving Teachers’ Rights Forum), said.
In 2025, the ‘untainted’ teachers had held months-long protests in Kolkata, demanding that their jobs be restored with dignity. Several protesters were also subjected to police action during the demonstrations.
The teachers had repeatedly appealed to the Calcutta High Court and the Supreme Court for restoration of their jobs, arguing that no investigation had found evidence of corruption against them. The courts, however, did not restore their appointments and directed the State to conduct a fresh recruitment process, requiring the ‘untainted’ candidates to appear for the examination again.

NEW DELHI: There is little chance of the Lok Sabha continuing with Justice Varmaâs removal motion despite the inquiry committee finding the charges relating to discovery of unaccounted currency notes in his official residential premises proved.As per Article 217(1) of the Constitution, a judge ceases to hold office if he/she resigns by sending a resignation letter written âunder his hand addressed to the Presidentâ. Justice Varma had on April 10 resigned as a judge of Allahabad High Court and had withdrawn from the inquiry proceedings, finding the writing on the wall.
How does a resignation of a constitutional court judge take effect? This question was answered by a five-judge bench of the SC in the Gopal Chandra Misra case on Feb 15, 1978. It was unanimous that once the judge sends his resignation to the President, he/she is deemed to have ceased to be a judge.In that case, the judge had set a prospective date for his resignation taking effect and before the arrival of the appointed date, he had withdrawn his resignation. SC had by four to one majority ruled that since the resignation was prospective, the judge had every right to withdraw it prior to the appointed date.

headline: Ram Mandir CEO race narrows to three after 5,585 applications, 16 finalists
full_text:
Ram Mandir CEO race narrows to three after 5,585 applications, 16 finalists
Final interviews for the Ram Mandir's first CEO have concluded in Ayodhya. The appointment will shape administration as the temple prepares for growing devotee numbers.
The race to become the first Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya has entered its final stage, with the selection committee set to recommend three names to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust.
The Trust said the final round of interviews was completed at the Ram Janmabhoomi complex in Ayodhya on August 11 and 12. The Trust will make the final appointment after considering the three names recommended by the selection committee.
FROM 5,585 APPLICATIONS TO 16 FINALISTS
The selection process began with 5,585 applications for the CEO post. Of these, 3,877 applicants submitted detailed CVs.
Candidates were assessed on several parameters, including management skills, experience in handling large events and crowds, individual capabilities, language skills, vision and strategic thinking.
Following the initial screening, 1,580 applications and submissions were evaluated in detail. Around 111 candidates were then shortlisted for online interactions. The online stage assessed communication skills, professional experience, personality, vision, leadership ability and technical understanding.
The field was subsequently reduced to 16 candidates for face-to-face interviews in Ayodhya.
ARMY VETERANS, FORMER IAS AND IPS OFFICERS IN RACE
The 16 finalists include experienced professionals from defence, bureaucracy, the corporate and industrial sectors, education and information technology.
According to the official press note, the shortlisted candidates are between 50 and 70 years old and have significant professional achievements and leadership experience. The pool includes retired military officers, former IAS and IPS officers, and senior professionals from government and the private sector.
The diversity of the shortlist reflects the responsibilities expected of the first CEO, who will be required to oversee a large and complex institution serving a huge number of devotees.
The role is expected to involve administration, pilgrim management, security coordination, staff management, technology, institutional operations and long-term planning.
THREE-MEMBER COMMITTEE CONDUCTED INTERVIEWS
The search committee comprises retired Justice Pramod Kohli, Lieutenant General (retired) VK Chaturvedi and nuclear scientist Dr Suresh Haware.
The committee brings experience from the judiciary, defence, science, administration and institutional leadership.
It will now undertake an overall assessment of the candidates before submitting a panel of three names to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. The Trust will then select the final candidate from the three-member panel.
The appointment is expected to play a key role in strengthening the administrative structure of the Ram Mandir as the institution expands its operations and prepares to manage growing numbers of devotees.
The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust said the selection process was being conducted on the principles of merit-based selection, institutional excellence and transparency.

full_text:
It also directed the state govt to pay Rs 25 lakh as interim compensation to the family of the deceased
NEW DELHI: Accusing top administrative and police officials of Chhattisgarh of trying to "cover up" a custodial death case, Supreme Court on Wednesday expressed lack of confidence in the state administration's catching the errant officials and handed over the case to CBI. It also directed the state govt to pay Rs 25 lakh as interim compensation to the family of the deceased.A bench said that the case warranted immediate registration of an FIR and a thorough investigation into the circumstances leading to the death of Shravan Suryavanshi, which the state authorities had "conveniently and deliberately tried to cover up".It said that state authorities were adopting a "dilatory approach" and could not be trusted to conduct an impartial probe. Shravan was arrested on Jan 18, 2024, after he was found in possession of raw Mahua liquor and lodged at Central Jail, Bilaspur, from where he was referred to hospital on Jan 21.He died a day later.Referring to the high court order, bench said the death of the deceased was on account of violence perpetrated on him in custody. In compliance with the court's directive, the DGP, director general (Prisons) and principal secretary (Home), virtually appeared before the court, which found their explanation "perfunctory and pedantic".
"In this backdrop, the stance of blissful ignorance taken by the senior officers of the State of Chhattisgarh, including the Principal Secretary (Home), the DGP and the DG (Prisons), is sacrilegious and reflects a disturbing disregard for the statutory procedure governing custodial deaths. The explanation offered that neither any police action nor any disciplinary action was taken against the persons responsible because the judicial inquiry report had not been served upon the police officials is a cover-up story and an attempt to pull the wool over the Court's eyes," bench said.
"We have seen the medical reports of the deceased Shravan and find that a clear attempt was made to mislead the inquiry because, in the medical report prepared at jail at the time of his death, the cause of death was recorded as cardiopulmonary arrest with aspiration pneumonitis, with the diagnosis being alcoholic withdrawal and delirium tremens," it said.The court thereafter asked CBI director to ensure immediate registration of a regular case over Shravan's custodial death, ordering that the investigation be entrusted to a senior officer and conducted expeditiously. The report of the investigating officer is to be placed before the court on the next date of hearing. It further said that the conduct of state officials concerned in failing to take appropriate steps pursuant to submission of the judicial inquiry report should also be examined and made a part of the investigation.

headline: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has opened the service lane of Chennai-Bengaluru National Highway (NH-48) near Christian Medical College (CMC) at Puttuthakku village for public use on Wednesday, after relaying the carriageway with cem...
full_text:
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has opened the service lane of Chennai-Bengaluru National Highway (NH-48) near Christian Medical College (CMC) at Puttuthakku village for public use on Wednesday, after relaying the carriageway with cement concrete to prevent inundation during rains.
NHAI officials said that the bitumen carriageway of the service lane, especially towards Bengaluru, was washed away after excess rainwater from abandoned quarries in Puttuthakku village flooded the stretch during monsoon in December 2025. “During last year’s monsoon, traffic on the stretch was stopped after the top bitumen layer got washed away. Huge potholes on the carriageway prevented motorists from using it since then,” said a NHAI official.
Subsequently, NHAI finished patchwork on the damaged service lane a few months ago to allow motorists to use the stretch. NHAI also decided to lay a concrete carriageway on the service lane to prevent similar incidents in the future. “The re-opening of the service lane with concrete carriageway is a welcome measure to ensure safety of motorists, especially during monsoon. Better street lights and reflectors should be installed on the service lane,” said R. Gowri Sankar, a motorist.
NHAI officials said that the service lane measures 300 metres long and 20 ft wide - enough for buses to use the stretch. Work to re-lay the stretch began after Assembly polls in April, and traffic on the route was diverted to the newly opened elevated corridor on the highway.
Divided into small portions, the service lane was milled before it was filled with bluemetal for a depth of two feet to ensure road level. Concrete mixture was laid on the carriageway to a depth of one foot. After more than one month of curing, the re-laid stretch was inspected for any cracks.
NHAI officials said the concrete carriageway will help excess rainwater from abandoned quarries to discharge to nearby canal and lakes before draining into Palar river without affecting traffic movement. Also, the carriageway will not get washed away due to a large volume of rainwater.
Motorists said that earlier, the pot-holed service lane along the national highway was used by vehicles including government town buses, autorickshaws, cars and two-wheelers. Farmers also use the stretch to transport farm produce in tractors to government paddy procurement centres in nearby towns like Arcot, Walajah and Vellore.
Ambulance drivers found it challenging to drive on the bumpy service lane with patients on board. On an average, 8-10 ambulances use the stretch every day to reach nearest government hospitals and CMC.

It is alleged that the BJP government was trying to bring in an officer from outside the bracket of three senior most IPS officers for the top post. Similarly, in what it seems as shadow fight to favour IPS officers of their choice for the top post, activists have jumped in to filing PIL and sending petitions to Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
Present Odisha DGP, Mr. Khurania, a 1990 batch IPS officer, was appointed as the Head of Police Force of Odisha, on August 16, 2024. After completion of two years, he would demit office on August 16, 2026.
The process of DGP appointment should have been started months before retirement of outgoing DGP. As per Supreme Court’s laid down procedure, the Mohan Majhi Government had sent names of three senior most officers including Sudhanshu Sarangi (1990 batch), Susanta Kumar Nath (1993) and R.P. Koche, (1993) for consideration UPSC.
Before the Commission could take a call on the three names, the State government expanded the list of officers for consideration of UPSC from three to 11 by including eight senior IPS officers from 1994 batch to 1996.
The State government on Monday (August 10, 2026) promoted two 1994-batch officers Sanjeeb Kumar Panda and Yeshwant Kumar Jethwa to the grade of DG of Police. If the list of original three names recommended to UPSC is altered, Mr. Panda and Mr. Jethwa would automatically come into contention.
Senior lawyer and former Home Minister P. Chidambaram has already appeared in PIL arguing that Odisha government violated the Prakash Singh judgment on appointment of DGP. headline: Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) announced that the government’s Marathi language requirement for commercial passenger vehicle drivers will be mandatory for app-based cab drivers also. The cab aggregators, ...
full_text:
Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) announced that the government’s Marathi language requirement for commercial passenger vehicle drivers will be mandatory for app-based cab drivers also. The cab aggregators, including Ola, Uber and Rapido, will have no exception from the State’s language rules.
“The cab drivers have to have practical working knowledge of Marathi and should communicate with passengers,” said Mr. Sarnaik.
The move comes as the deadline to complete the required Marathi-speaking training is nearing. After August 15, the transport department will conduct verification drives and take stricter action against those who fail to comply with the rule of mandatory Marathi.
Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, facilitate mandatory Marathi proficiency for taxi, autorickshaw and app-based cab drivers in the State, which was implemented this year under the Maharashtra Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Rules, 2026. The government announced that drivers have to demonstrate Marathi knowledge from May 1 onwards, but it received outrage from unions. Due to this, the three-month functional Marathi training programme was launched, with an extended deadline to August 15.
Rule 4(4), Rule 78, and Rule 85 of the Act made working knowledge of Marathi compulsory for permit renewals. The same will be applied to app-based motor cab drivers operating vehicles having electronic meters.
If any driver fails to comply with the rules, then under Provision 22(3A) they will face action for non-compliance, including suspension of licences for up to three months or cancellation.
Over 1.10 lakh non-Marathi passenger vehicle drivers completed the four-hour-long programme and will receive certificates from Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and DCM Eknath Shinde on August 17.

The directive came as the bench found that the prosecution was yet to start producing its witnesses despite having cited 700 of them. The accused, a functionary of the outlawed hardline Islamist group PFI, has been in jail for four years. The SC on Aug 5 asked the state govt to submit a prosecution plan specifying how many protected witnesses were to be examined and within what timeframe.Karnatakaâs counsel Rooh-e-Hina Dua said the state intended to examine three protected witnesses and 50 other witnesses against the petitioner Shahid Khan and said it could take a year for the prosecution to complete its evidence and examination of witnesses.The bench said, âIt shows the lackadaisical approach of the state.
The prosecution does not give a clear picture of the trial process when the accused is languishing in jail for nearly four years without a trial.âFor the petitioner, who was arrested on Sept 22, 2022, for allegedly radicalising youth and being involved in violent activities, senior advocate Aditya Sondhi said the HC rejected his bail plea without considering the right to liberty and right to expeditious trial.
The bench said the charges against the petitioner were serious and directed the prosecution to complete examination of the three protected witnesses in three months. It asked the prosecution, the petitioner and the co-accused, who are on bail, not to repeatedly file applications.The petitioner is accused of helping raise funds for PFI between 2011 and 2019 and helping teams of the banned outfit which had planned attacks in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala against CAA and NRC, and judgement relating to hijab and Babri demolition.

headline: Union MoS Jitendra Singh speaks in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament
full_text:

NEW DELHI: A key objective of the govt under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033, minister for department of atomic energy Jitendra Singh said in a written reply in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies, including the 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor (BSMR-200) and 55 MWe SMR-55 for power generation. BARC is also developing a high temperature gas cooled reactor (HTGCR) of up to 5 MW capacity, which can be coupled with a suitable thermochemical cycle for hydrogen production.Singh said India is steadily strengthening its indigenous nuclear energy ecosystem with a focus on advanced reactor technologies, SMRs, domestic manufacturing capabilities, private-sector participation and long-term utilisation of the countryâs abundant thorium resources. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition. This includes deployment of large indigenous reactors such as 700 MWe pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and advanced reactor designs at greenfield sites, alongside development and deployment of SMRs at brownfield locations, including retiring fossil-fuel-based power plants, captive plants for energy-intensive industries and off-grid applications in remote areas.
The minister also highlighted continuing work of the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) in advancing the second stage of Indiaâs nuclear power programme. IGCAR is pursuing multidisciplinary scientific research and advanced engineering development for sodium cooled fast breeder reactors and associated closed fuel-cycle facilities, technologies that remain a cornerstone of Indiaâs long-term nuclear strategy.
On thorium, Singh said India is pursuing its three-stage nuclear power programme, based on a closed fuel cycle, to optimise utilisation of its uranium resources and progressively harness its abundant thorium reserves. Thorium, being a fertile material, needs to be converted into fissile uranium-233 in a nuclear reactor before it can be used for energy generation.India has already undertaken sustained R&D towards thorium utilisation. Thorium Oxide (Thoria) pellets have been used in the initial cores of operating PHWRs, while Thoria-based fuels have also been irradiated in BARC research reactors. The irradiated Thoria pins have been reprocessed to obtain uranium-233, which has subsequently been fabricated as fuel for the KAMINI reactor at IGCAR, Kalpakkam. Singh said the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, 2025 has been enacted to enable wider participation of both public and private entities in the nuclear sector.

headline: These are not matters where the family or the widow should be expected to go to the court to obtain relief, Supreme Court said
full_text:
These are not matters where the family or the widow should be expected to go to the court to obtain relief, Supreme Court said
NEW DELHI: Official apathy sometimes doesnât spare even the families of those who lay down their lives for the country. A case in point is the decades-long struggle of the widow of âShaurya Chakraâ awardee Mohan Singh, who had to wait for 26 years to get her rightful Special Family Pension â that too only after the Supreme Courtâs intervention.Singh, an overseer with General Reserves Engineering Force, was in charge of construction of a key border road. On July 10, 2000, when a boulder from a hilltop rolled down with debris, he helped move workers from the site but could not get out of its way himself and was killed. The Centre posthumously conferred on him in 2001 the âShaurya Chakraâ â the third-highest peacetime gallantry award.However, his widow received relief under Workmenâs Compensation Act and not the Special Family Pension under the CCS (Extraordinary Pension) Rules, to which she was entitled. It was rejected on the ground that since payment under Workmenâs Compensation Act had been made, no liberalised pensionary award was due to the deceasedâs kin, as per CCS (Pension) rules.She moved Punjab and Haryana HC, which held she was entitled to extraordinary pension but restricted payment of arrears from date of the filing of petition, denying relief from the date of death of her husband. When the matter reached the SC, a bench of Justices K V Viswanathan and Arun Palli said the Centre had erred and should have categorised her case under the correct category âCâ of CCS Pension Rules and extended the benefit soon after Singhâs demise.
âThese are not matters where the family or the widow should be expected to go to the court to obtain relief,â SC said.AG R Venkataramani said Rs 14.28 lakh had been paid to the widow and pension will be processed as per HC order. Arrears, calculated at Rs 4.12 lakh, had also been released. SC said a consolidated amount of Rs 10 lakh be paid to her for the period between Singhâs death and HC order.

A 24-year-old tea stall owner has been arrested in Karnataka's Raichur after police found he was in contact with a foreign contact operating social media accounts under the name “Rana Bhai”, who encouraged him to create unrest in India and offered money and a pistol.

headline: Seven children have lost their lives and about 100 have fallen ill in some villages of the tribal community in Madhya Pradesh’s Balaghat district in about 45 days, due to an outbreak of monsoon related diseases while suffering skin infections, offici...
full_text:
Seven children have lost their lives and about 100 have fallen ill in some villages of the tribal community in Madhya Pradesh’s Balaghat district in about 45 days, due to an outbreak of monsoon related diseases while suffering skin infections, officials said, even as they flagged lack of accessibility in remote areas and the community’s reliance on ritualistic healing.
According to officials, about five villages of the Baiga tribe have reported 100 cases of malaria, typhoid, viral infections and skin infections among children aged between one and 13 years since June, showing symptoms like high fever, stomach infection, and rashes and spots on their bodies.
The villages are Bondari, Adori, Machhurda, Korka and Kundekasa in Baihar tehsil, about 85 kilometres from the district hospital.
Additional Collector, Balaghat, Abhishek Saraf told The Hindu that 24 children are currently under treatment at district and civil hospitals while 76 children have recovered so far.
Officials say that the administration came to know about the problem after three children had already died, which prompted authorities to launch measures in the remotely located villages. The first death occurred on June 26 in Bondari village.
The authorities have also collected blood samples from patients and sent them to ICMR-National Institute of Research in Bacterial Infections, Kolkata, and the ICMR-National Institute of Virology, Pune, to check for the exact cause of the outbreak. Whereas, a team from Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Medical College, Jabalpur, is also investigating the situation.
Mr. Saraf said that special health camps have been setup in the villages to provide early treatment to children and door-to-door screenings are being conducted to check for new cases by deploying ASHA and ANM workers, and special medical teams for diseases like malaria and typhoid.
“We have deployed a team led by a medical officer for each village who will assess the situation and decide if a patient needs to be admitted to the civil or district hospital,” he said.
Mr. Saraf also said that officials have also been deployed to survey houses to collect water samples and assess hygiene conditions.
“They have also been directed to clean water bodies and ensure clean water in the affected areas,” he said.
The official, however, highlighted the challenges in tracing the affected children and as well as in convincing their families to accept the treatment.
The Baiga community, a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG), is known for its ancient practices and rituals, with members of the group often opting for faith healing over modern medicine. Largely located in forest covered districts of eastern and southern Madhya Pradesh, lack of accessibility and awareness also keeps a large section of the community still cut off from the administration and modern infrastructure. The five villages have houses scattered on different hills in dense forest.
“While remote terrain was one problem in reaching the villages and tracing patients, convincing their families to admit their kids to hospitals was more difficult. Many families officials visited refused medicines too. But we have now connected with their spiritual leaders and are convincing the people with their help,” Mr. Saraf said, adding that the situation was now improving.
Balaghat Chief Medical and Health Officer (CMHO) Paresh Uplap said that various families have refused to go to hospital despite senior officials trying to convince them.
“There are about 15 houses atop a hill in Bondari village. The houses are cut off from the rest of the area and two children from a family died there about two weeks ago. The families did not inform anybody or seek help when they fell ill at night,” he said.
“We have deployed ambulances in some villages so that kids can be immediately shifted to the district hospital if needed. People from the community often reach out to faith healers when someone falls sick and think that they will go to hospital once the condition is a little better,” he said.
He said that multiple meetings have also been held with village heads and local people to convince them to take treatment.
Dr. Uplap also said that ANM and ASHA workers are also conducting surveys in all the hostels and schools in the area.
However, Amaar Singh Dhurve, a resident of Bondari who lost his two children, said that he had approached both doctors and faith healers in the nearby areas when his children fell ill.
“We don’t know any medication so I went everywhere but no vaidya or doctor ever comes here. We have gotten tired of calling. Even the villagers don’t come up here [on the hill]. At one point, all six members of my family were sick but there was nobody to take care of us. So, what could I do. I called faith healers and did jhhaad phoonk [ritualistic healing practice] myself too.
A government official also said that practices of animal sacrifice have also been reported from a village, conducted to get rid of the outbreak.

headline: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday said the changing nature of crime required the police to constantly evolve their methods, strengthen technology integration and focus on the “golden hour” immediately after a crime is committed.
full_text:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday said the changing nature of crime required the police to constantly evolve their methods, strengthen technology integration and focus on the “golden hour” immediately after a crime is committed.
Addressing a virtual meeting of the police officers, from the DGP to the Station House Officer, Mr. Naidu said protecting evidence at the crime scene and acting swiftly were crucial to successful investigations.
Around 1,650 officers from nearly 1,200 police stations, including law and order, traffic and GRP personnel, participated.
The State had integrated 14,770 government CCTV cameras with privately installed cameras, taking the network to about one lakh cameras, he said. Facial recognition and DNA-based detection were also being increasingly used in investigations.
“We are moving forward by correcting shortcomings in maintaining law and order. Peace and security are essential for people to live peacefully and for investments to come into the State,” the Chief Minister said.
Mr. Naidu called for zero tolerance towards crimes against women, and urged police to secure crime scenes and act swiftly.
Referring to the Y.S. Vivekananda Reddy murder case, he termed lapses in preserving evidence a “costly mistake” and cautioned against any leniency towards criminals.
The Chief Minister said that political parties had no licence to violate the law or cause inconvenience to the public in the name of rallies or condolence visits.
He said even a small lapse in maintaining law and order could leave a stain on the entire police system. Referring to recent incidents involving political rallies, he questioned the need for motorcycle stunts on public roads during a political party programme at Ibrahimpatnam.
He said there had also been situations in which police personnel were attacked while performing their duties.
“Whatever the political party, there can be no permission for stunts on public roads. It is the responsibility of all political parties to ensure that their activities do not inconvenience the public,” he said.
Mr. Naidu said political leaders could not expect to be let off merely because they belonged to a political party. He alleged that 94% of those currently creating disturbances on roads belonged to one particular party.
He clarified that visiting people to offer condolences was not wrong, but said large-scale road demonstrations during such visits caused serious inconvenience.
Mr. Naidu said the government would provide police personnel complete freedom to discharge their duties and take steps to enhance their dignity and respect. He said an “invisible police, visible policing” approach should be adopted to strengthen public confidence.
He also directed police to intensify action against ganja, drugs and social media-driven criminal activity, and called for wider promotion of the “Drugs Vaddhu Bro” campaign.
Mr. Naidu said Andhra Pradesh should emerge as the best State in law and order. Police should publicise successful investigations and improve conviction rates, while implementing friendly policing in full.
He directed the department to release a monthly police performance report, highlighting best practices and successful cases. Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha, DGP Harish Kumar Gupta and other senior officials attended the meeting.

headline: The Awami Ittehad Party (AIP), headed by Member of Parliament Engineer Rashid, on Wednesday said the high-level committee on demographic changes ignored the families displaced from their ancestral homes along the Line of Control (LoC) in Kashmir.
full_text:
The Awami Ittehad Party (AIP), headed by Member of Parliament Engineer Rashid, on Wednesday said the high-level committee on demographic changes ignored the families displaced from their ancestral homes along the Line of Control (LoC) in Kashmir.
“The committee cannot claim to undertake a comprehensive demographic assessment of Jammu and Kashmir while overlooking the families and entire pockets of population that were displaced from their ancestral homes along the LoC,” said its spokesperson Inam Un Nabi.
The AIP demanded that the committee’s focus must extend beyond alleged demographic inflows to the outflow of indigenous populations caused by violence, prolonged shelling and insecurity. “The committee must answer a simple question: what about the families who crossed the LoC because they were running for their lives? They did not cross to take up arms or join militancy. They crossed because they wanted to save their children, their elderly and their families from a conflict that had made their homes unsafe. What is the government doing today to bring such families back?” said Mr. Nabi.
Kashmir’s forward areas like Jumgund, Machil, Keran, Karnah, Gurez, Uri, Poonch and Mendhar have witnessed migrations since 1947.
“If demographic correction is the objective, then restoring the population driven out by conflict must be part of that agenda. You cannot discuss demographic change while ignoring the empty homes, abandoned land and families that were forced to establish their lives elsewhere,” Mr. Inam said.
Taking strong exception to the committee’s reported interaction with the Rohingya, he said its first responsibility should be to hear the people of Jammu & Kashmir who have borne the direct consequences of conflict.
‘Hear Pandits’
The AIP said it must also hear Kashmiri Pandits living in Kashmir and migrated Kashmiri Pandit families, whose migration remains an essential part of the region’s demographic history.
“Do not prepare a demographic report by ignoring this important part. Go to the people who have actually lost their homes, villages and livelihoods. Their story is the missing chapter in any honest assessment of demographic change in Jammu & Kashmir,” the AIP spokesperson said.
The high-level committee studying demographic changes, headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Prakash Prabhakar Naolekar, arrived in J&K on Monday.

headline: Rajni Rani, a national-level sportswoman with multiple medals, was denied a promotion in 2013 despite a directive by the Central Administrative Tribunal in Sept 2012 to consider her case.
full_text:
Rajni Rani, a national-level sportswoman with multiple medals, was denied a promotion in 2013 despite a directive by the Central Administrative Tribunal in Sept 2012 to consider her case.
NEW DELHI: A national-level sportswoman, employed as a safaiwala (group D employee) in railways since 2003, has been awaiting promotion to group C level for last two decades despite the railway ministryâs policy to grant out-of-turn first promotion to medal-winning employees, a criterion she had fulfilled by winning two medals in national events.A decade after winning medals but not getting promotion as per the policy, Rajni Rani moved Punjab and Haryana HC in 2016 with a writ petition, which got dismissed on technical grounds. Her appeal against the HC order has been pending in SC since Nov 2016.
It was last heard on Jan 9, 2017, when a bench of Justices J Chelameswar and A M Sapre admitted her petition and asked the Union govt to file a response in eight weeks. On May 15, 2018, registrar Kapil Mehta had recorded that statement of case had not been filed by any of the parties despite expiry of the time granted. He had asked for the case to be listed before the court as per rules. However, her petition continued to gather dust till her counsel Wednesday requested a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant for an early hearing. A visibly unhappy CJI directed the registry to list the petition for hearing on Aug 21.Rajni said she was due for promotion in 2005 after winning medals but was denied the benefit of first promotion on the ground that one of the four events she had participated in did not qualify as a national event. She said the rules prescribed participation in only two events. Rajni said she had won a bronze medal at 52nd Northern Railway Athletic Meet in Feb 2005, gold medal at 44th Senior National Inter-State competition in July 2004 and represented railways in open National in Mumbai in Sept 2004, securing fourth position.Rajni was denied a promotion in 2013 despite a directive by Central Administrative Tribunal to railways in Sept 2012 to consider her case. When she challenged the decision, both CAT and HC dismissed her petitions.

headline: Caught on CCTV: Couple goes to see house for rent, gets attacked by Pitbull
full_text:
Caught on CCTV: Couple goes to see house for rent, gets attacked by Pitbull
A pet pitbull attacked Shifali Sabharwal and injured Ankit Sabharwal when he tried to save her in Patiala's Ghuman Nagar. Police have verified the viral video and will act after medical reports and investigation findings.
A husband and wife were hospitalised after a pet pitbull attacked them in Patiala, leaving the woman with severe injuries that required plastic surgery and injuring her husband when he tried to rescue her.
The victims have been identified as Shifali Sabharwal, a professor at Chandigarh University, and her husband Ankit Sabharwal, a manager at a private bank.
According to the family, the couple had visited a house in Ghuman Nagar when the incident occurred. As soon as the gate was opened, a pet pitbull allegedly charged at Shifali and attacked her, causing serious injuries.
Seeing his wife being mauled, Ankit intervened to save her but was also attacked by the dog during the struggle. Both suffered injuries and were rushed to Amar Hospital for treatment.
Shifali's condition was reported to be serious enough to require plastic surgery, while both she and her husband remain under medical care.
The incident came to light after a video of the attack circulated on social media, prompting police to take cognisance of the matter.
DSP Jangjit Randhawa said police verified the viral video and contacted the affected family. He confirmed that the injured woman had undergone surgery and that further legal action would be taken after medical reports are received.
Police said an FIR could be registered under Section 291 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with negligent conduct involving animals that endangers human life or causes injury.
Randhawa added that authorities would also examine compliance with court directions and regulations concerning dangerous dog breeds. He indicated that a verification drive related to such breeds could be launched after August 15.
Police said further action will be based on medical reports and the findings of the investigation.

headline: A protest staged by Rajasthan Minister of State for Forest Sanjay Sharma in support of sanitation workers outside the Municipal Corporation in Alwar on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) created a political storm. The local Congress leaders also joined the ...
full_text:
A protest staged by Rajasthan Minister of State for Forest Sanjay Sharma in support of sanitation workers outside the Municipal Corporation in Alwar on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) created a political storm. The local Congress leaders also joined the protest and clashed with Mr. Sharma’s supporters.
The sanitation workers have been demanding the issuance of appointment letters to the candidates selected in a recruitment drive in 2012. Despite the Rajasthan High Court’s order to the Directorate of Local Bodies (DLB) in 2019 to form a committee and take a decision, the matter has been put on hold.
Mr. Sharma, who represents the Alwar Urban constituency in the State Assembly, extended support to the workers’ demand and joined their dharna at the Municipal Corporation. The municipal authorities had reportedly sought the DLB’s guidance and were about to issue appointment letters to 69 candidates after several months of communication.
Though the sanitation workers’ union had agreed to the appointment of 69 candidates, against the original figure of 329 selected in 2012, the municipal authorities allegedly backed away from the appointments.
The Minister blamed the Alwar Collector and the Municipal Commissioner for the delay and announced that he would not leave the protest site until the workers were issued appointment letters. “I spoke to the Collector, but she said she was not the competent authority to give appointments, as the Municipal Commissioner has been transferred,” Mr. Sharma told journalists.
Tension escalated at Municipal Corporation’s office when the Opposition Congress workers, led by District Congress Committee president Prakash Gangawat, arrived at the dharna site. The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Congress party workers, who raised slogans and clashed inside the Municipal Commissioner’s chamber, were pacified by the police personnel.
The protest was called off after about five hours when Additional District Magistrate Yogesh Dagur reached the site with five appointment letters. Mr. Sharma handed over the letters to a representative of sanitation workers and said the appointment letters for the remaining eligible candidates would be distributed during an official event on August 16.
The Congress leaders targeted the BJP government over the issue, saying the bureaucracy in the State had become so powerful that the Ministers were not being heard and MLAs were being ignored. The party leaders said it was the State government’s “biggest embarrassment” that its own Minister was forced to stage dharna against the administration.
Former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot said Mr. Sharma’s protest was an open admission of the administrative machinery being “thoroughly corrupt and out of control”. “The BJP government should be ashamed of itself… The Ministers have been reduced to mere rubber stamps. They have been rendered helpless before the system,” Mr. Gehlot said in a post on X.
Pradesh Congress Committee president Govind Singh Dotasra and Leader of Opposition Tika Ram Jully — representing Alwar Rural in the Assembly — said the Minister’s protest and allegations had raised serious questions over the functioning of the BJP government. “When even a Minister is fed up with the system, on what grounds should the public trust this government?” Mr. Jully asked.

headline: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann, Arvind Kejriwal flag off 15 pilgrim buses in Hoshiarpur

Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann, Arvind Kejriwal flag off 15 pilgrim buses in Hoshiarpur
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal flagged off 15 buses carrying pilgrims from Hoshiarpur to key religious destinations. The launch expands Punjab's Mukh Mantri Tirath Yatra Yojana, which offers free travel, stay and food.
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Wednesday flagged off 15 buses carrying pilgrims from Hoshiarpur for religious destinations including Haridwar-Rishikesh, Mathura-Vrindavan and Salasar-Shri Khatu Shyam.
The flagging-off ceremony marked the expansion of the Punjab government's Mukh Mantri Tirath Yatra Yojana, under which pilgrims aged 50 and above can undertake pilgrimages along with up to two eligible family members.
Under the scheme, the government covers the cost of AC sleeper bus travel, accommodation and food for the pilgrims.
Speaking at the event, Kejriwal said the scheme would allow people to undertake pilgrimages without having to bear the expenses themselves. He said comfortable AC buses and accommodation had been arranged for the devotees.
"Today, 15 buses are going to Haridwar-Rishikesh, Mathura ji-Vrindavan Dham and Salasar-Shri Khatu Shyam," Kejriwal said, adding that many of the pilgrims were visiting these destinations for the first time.
He said the government plans to take 1.5 lakh people from Punjab to different pilgrimage destinations in the coming months.
Mann said the buses were carrying devotees from Hoshiarpur, Jalandhar, Kapurthala, Pathankot and Gurdaspur.
"A total of 15 buses carrying devotees from five districts... have departed from Hoshiarpur for different religious destinations," he said, adding that the pilgrims were happy and singing bhajans as they began their journey.
Under Phase I of the Mukh Mantri Tirath Yatra Yojana, the government said four lakh pilgrims have so far visited Sri Amritsar Sahib and Sri Anandpur Sahib-Naina Devi.

headline: RS Chairman regrets disruptions during Monsoon Session; House productivity only 39 pc
full_text:
RS Chairman regrets disruptions during Monsoon Session; House productivity only 39 pc
New Delhi, Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan on Thursday expressed "deep concern" over disruptions that "derailed" the business of the House during the Monsoon Session.
As he adjourned the House sine die, he urged the members to uphold the dignity of the august House and discharge their parliamentary responsibilities in the highest traditions of Indian democracy.
During the Monsoon Session that started on July 20, Radhakrishnan highlighted that 12 Bills were either passed or returned even as the productivity was only 39 per cent because of disruptions.
"As the 271st Session of the Rajya Sabha draws to a close, I reflect on its proceedings with a deep concern. It is a matter of regret that the Session was marked by persistent disorder and frequent disruptions, which repeatedly derailed the business of the House," the Chairman said.
The loss of precious working hours also deprived the House of meaningful discussion and debate on matters of national importance, he added.
The Upper House saw several disruptions and adjournments as Opposition parties were protesting on several issues, including police action on students protesting against NEET paper leak and alleged theft of donations at Ram temple in Ayodhya.
Despite the disruptions, Radhakrishnan noted that the House managed to fulfil its core legislative duties by considering, passing or returning 12 Bills.
"Things would certainly have been different if we had collectively participated, contributed our valuable inputs and engaged in meaningful deliberations," he observed.
Elaborating on the performance, the Chairman said the House functioned for only 37 hours and 49 minutes, recording a productivity of 39.17 per cent.
As many as 285 Starred Questions were raised while there were 380 Zero Hour submissions and 380 Special Mentions. Only 16 Questions, 52 Zero Hour Submissions and 93 Special Mentions could be taken up.
Radhakrishnan rued that members did not make the fullest use of the opportunities to raise the voice of the people.
"As the House of Elders, this august Chamber has a unique responsibility to uphold reasoned debate, dignified dissent and thoughtful legislation. Repeated disruptions ultimately affect the trust and aspirations of the people. We must therefore strive to uphold the highest standards of parliamentary conduct and preserve the dignity and sanctity of this institution," he said.
The Chairman informed that an orientation programme was organised for the newly elected and nominated Members. The two-day programme provided valuable insights into parliamentary practice, procedure and the standards of conduct expected of Members.
As many as 35 Members attended the programme.
"I hope that when we meet again, we shall do so with a renewed resolve to uphold the dignity of this august House and discharge our parliamentary responsibilities in the highest traditions of our democracy, thereby strengthening our democratic institutions and our democracy at all times," Radhakrishnan said.

headline: Messi event row: Kerala CM flags GST fraud, lapses in picking private sponsor
full_text:
Messi event row: Kerala CM flags GST fraud, lapses in picking private sponsor
Kerala CM VD Satheesan stated that a preliminary inquiry report submitted by the sports department is being examined and warrants further investigations
Kerala chief minister VD Satheesan on Thursday flagged serious charges, including Goods and Services Tax (GST) fraud and lapses in the way the private sponsor was picked by the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government in connection with the cancelled visit of the Lionel Messi-led Argentina national team to play a friendly in the state.
The chief minister stated that a preliminary inquiry report submitted by the sports department is being examined and warrants further investigations.
“What was the procedure adopted in selecting a private firm to sponsor the event? Was there an Expression of Interest? A firm was picked, but parameters including its source of funding and financial capability were not considered. Did the previous government know about this? There are already a lot of contradictory statements coming out,” the CM said at a press briefing in Thiruvananthapuram.
He said that the finance department, which he oversees, will take action and make efforts to recover the state’s losses in GST collection.
“Prima facie, GST fraud has taken place. There are some serious allegations. It happened during the tenure of the previous government and even a notice was served (to the private sponsor). But it seems the inquiry was frozen,” he said.
On whether central agencies will be invited to probe aspects of possible money laundering, the CM said,
“Let the state government examine it first. If there is a need for central agency probes, we will refer it to them. Have the State’s interests been protected? Did the private firm take advantage of the situation? Everything will be examined.”
The CM also rejected allegations made by a top official of the private firm that the state government was targeting the firm.
“The inquiry report has just been submitted to me. I have not taken any action on it,” he said.
In 2023, then sports minister V Abdurahiman had announced that the state government was partnering with RBC to host the Messi-led Argentine side to play a friendly exhibition match at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Kochi at no cost to the public exchequer. The former minister even travelled to Spain on one occasion to reportedly hold talks with the Argentina Football Association (AFA) officials and had claimed at one point that AFA had agreed to send the delegation, including Messi, to Kerala. However, the event failed to materialise.
The inquiry report has pointed to several violations in the way the event was planned, including the absence of any formal agreement between AFA, the Kerala government and the private sponsor, all formal communications being restricted to the sports minister’s office, service tax fraud on foreign remittances and the lack of a transparent tender process before the sponsor was finalised.
Abdurahiman and the private firm have rejected the allegations made in the inquiry report.

headline: 'No backdoor entry': Supreme Court gets UPSC undertaking on Odisha DGP selection
full_text:
'No backdoor entry': Supreme Court gets UPSC undertaking on Odisha DGP selection
The UPSC told the Supreme Court it will not finalise recommendations for Odisha’s next DGP until the court hears a plea challenging the selection process.
The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) on Thursday assured the Supreme Court that it would not convene a meeting to finalise its recommendations for the appointment of Odisha’s next director general of police (DGP) until the court hears a challenge to the state government’s move to expand the pool of officers being considered for the post.
The undertaking came after a bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant indicated that it was inclined to restrain the UPSC from making any fresh selection until the matter is heard on August 18.
“Any backdoor entry is not acceptable…UPSC must not finalise till the next date of hearing,” the bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said.
The court’s intervention followed an application alleging that the Odisha government was attempting to circumvent the Supreme Court’s prescribed procedure for the appointment of DGPs by introducing officers who were not part of the original list of three senior-most eligible officers sent to the UPSC.
Senior advocate P Chidambaram appeared for the petitioner.
Also Read: Odisha DGP selection delayed amid procedural, integrity concerns
The controversy comes days before incumbent DGP YB Khurania, a 1990-batch IPS officer appointed as Odisha’s police chief on August 16, 2024, is due to demit office on August 16.
Under the procedure laid down by the Supreme Court in its 2006 judgment in the Prakash Singh case, states are required to send proposals of eligible officers to the UPSC, which prepares a panel of three officers from among those meeting the prescribed criteria. The state government is then required to appoint the DGP from that panel.
The plea alleges that the Odisha government initially forwarded the names of three senior officers -- Sudhanshu Sarangi, a 1990-batch IPS officer, and Susanta Kumar Nath and R P Koche, both from the 1993 batch, for consideration by the UPSC.
However, before the UPSC could take a call on the three names, the state is alleged to have expanded the list to 11 officers by adding eight IPS officers from the 1994 to 1996 batches.
The issue gained significance after the Odisha government on August 10 promoted two 1994-batch IPS officers, Sanjeeb Kumar Panda and Yeshwant Kumar Jethwa, to the rank of DGP. The petition alleges that their elevation could bring them into consideration if the original list of three officers is replaced or expanded.
The UPSC’s empanelment committee was expected to meet in New Delhi on Thursday to shortlist three officers for the post, a day after the PIL was mentioned before the Supreme Court.
On August 11, Chidambaram had told the CJI-led bench that the state was attempting to breach the procedure prescribed in Prakash Singh.
“The State of Odisha is breaching the Prakash Singh judgment. On August 7, the UPSC was scheduled to meet to select from among the three DGPs. Odisha withdrew the list. They are now making another list to send,” he had submitted.
The senior counsel had alleged that the state was attempting to promote an ADGP and include the officer in the fresh list of candidates for consideration.
The CJI had then pointed out that under an earlier Supreme Court order, the UPSC was duty-bound to approach the court in case of non-compliance with the prescribed directions.
The Supreme Court reiterated in February 2026 that states must adhere to the procedure laid down for the appointment of DGPs. Under the framework, the UPSC is required to prepare a panel of eligible officers, following which the state government must appoint the police chief from among those empanelled. The court has also made clear that prescribed eligibility criteria cannot be bypassed merely because the number of eligible officers is limited. The DGP post at Level 17 is to be filled through selection from among officers holding DGP-level posts at Level 16.
The Prakash Singh judgment, delivered in 2006, had laid down a series of measures aimed at insulating the police from political interference and improving professionalism and accountability in policing. The procedure for selection of state police chiefs was among the key safeguards prescribed by the court.

headline: Assam CM Himanta Sarma calls for peace as fresh clash erupts along border with Arunachal Pradesh
full_text:
Assam CM Himanta Sarma calls for peace as fresh clash erupts along border with Arunachal Pradesh
Fresh clashes erupted between protestors from Assam and Arunachal Pradesh in Dhemaji district amid the ongoing call for an economic blockade of Itanagar.
Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has called for peace after reports of clashes along the border with Arunachal Pradesh emerged on Thursday.
Fresh clashes erupted between protestors from Assam and Arunachal Pradesh in Dhemaji district, reported news agency PTI.
The escalation prompted Arunachal police to fire into the air to control the mob as the protest over an indefinite economic blockade against the Himalayan state entered its second day.
"When the blockade was going on, some people from Arunachal Pradesh indulged in stone pelting on protesters from Assam, and some persons sustained minor injuries. This led to a scuffle between the two sides," an official told news agency PTI.
Assam CM urges for ‘peace and harmony’
Addressing the clashes, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma urged for peace and calm.
"I appeal to the people of Assam and Arunachal to maintain peace and harmony. Boundaries may define our States, but they can never divide our hearts," he wrote on X.
Along with the chief minister, MPs from Assam and Arunachal Pradesh also called for peace and calm in the region.
“We must live together harmoniously as brothers and sisters and settle any land dispute through peaceful negotiation only,” said union parliamentary affairs Kiren Rijiju in a video message on X.
What led to the clash?
The Takam Mising Porin Kebang (TMPK), the apex student organisation of Assam's Mising community, launched an indefinite economic blockade against Arunachal on Wednesday against the alleged firing in which 12 indigenous people from Assam were injured over land-encroachment issues.
Along with TMPK, other local social groups like Mising Mimag Kebang (MMK) and Takam Mising Mahila Kebang (TMMK) have supported the blockade and stopped all vehicles, barring emergency and school transportation, from coming or going to Arunachal Pradesh at the entry points.
The organisations have called for an early resolution of the Assam-Arunachal Pradesh border dispute, action against the "miscreants" who had fired and an end to alleged encroachment on Assam land.
The conflict between Assam and Arunachal also dates back to 1987, when Arunachal attained full statehood.
After Arunachal Pradesh became a state, a tripartite committee was appointed, which recommended that certain territories be transferred from Assam to Arunachal Pradesh.
In 2022, chief ministers Himanta Biswa Sarma and Pema Khandu signed the Namsai Declaration to narrow down disputes from 123 villages to a manageable subset through regional committees.
Referring to this, Sarma wrote on X: "Only 52 villages remain, and both Governments will continue discussions in the same spirit to resolve the dispute completely."

headline: Din, disruptions and a dozen bills: Monsoon Session comes to a close
full_text:
Din, disruptions and a dozen bills: Monsoon Session comes to a close
The disruptions had two key flashpoints. One was the police crackdown on students at Jantar Mantar and the other was the alleged theft of Ram Temple donations.
Parliament's 25-day monsoon session ended in acrimony on Thursday, with both Houses adjourned sine die after a stretch that saw proceedings disrupted almost daily, with Lok Sabha going without a completed Question Hour on even a single sitting day.
The disruptions had two key flashpoints. One was the July 20 police crackdown on students protesting at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak — an episode that led to Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation as Union education minister, and that the opposition wanted Union home minister Amit Shah to explain in the House.
The other was a running opposition allegation of theft of donations collected at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.
The Lok Sabha played all six stanzas of the national song Vande Mataram soon after convening on Thursday, after which speaker Om Birla adjourned the House sine die. He skipped the traditional valedictory address, which typically highlights the session's performance and productivity. The Congress, the Samajwadi Party and the Trinamool Congress boycotted the customary meeting with Birla thereafter.
Also Read | Lok Sabha Om Birla urges Opposition to end Parliament logjam
The Rajya Sabha was also adjourned sine die, ending the session. Chairman CP Radhakrishnan expressed "deep concern" over disruptions that "derailed" the business of the House. Overall, the Lok Sabha functioned for 17.5 hours while the Rajya Sabha worked for 37.4 hours.
Jantar Mantar crackdown dominates session
The session was dominated by a showdown between the Opposition and the Centre over the former's demand for a debate and a statement by Shah on the police crackdown on protesting students at Delhi's Jantar Mantar last month, which led to the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.
On the penultimate day, the Centre's push for a debate failed as the Opposition rejected Shah's offer of a two-day discussion on the NEET paper leak and other issues, followed by a reply from him. "The Centre is ready for discussions. The House should be allowed to run, the Opposition should submit a letter to the speaker by 2pm today. We are ready to start discussion at 3pm today," Shah told reporters outside Parliament on Wednesday.
Also Read | Rijiju defends Shah amid Oppn persistent demand for HM’s statement
He also wrote to Birla conveying the government's readiness to participate in the discussion. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi called it a “last-minute attempt” and said the Opposition was not interested in listening to Shah’s lecture.
The bills Parliament dealt with
Despite repeated disruptions and protests inside and outside Parliament, both Houses tabled and in some cases, passed a series of bills.
Foreign contribution bill referred to JPC after Opposition, church pushback
A bill proposing contentious changes to India's foreign contribution law was referred to a 31-member joint parliamentary committee (JPC) amid a standoff between the government and the Opposition, and repeated disruptions in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.
Among the key concerns are a plan to empower a "designated authority" to take over, manage or sell assets built with foreign funds by non-governmental organisations whose licences are cancelled, suspended or not renewed.
The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill - it was introduced in the previous session but held back - drew objections from the Opposition, several church delegations and four chief ministers of Christian-majority states.
Minister of state for home affairs Nityanand Rai moved the resolution in the Lok Sabha to form the JPC, comprising 21 Lok Sabha members and 10 Rajya Sabha members. A BJP member is expected to head the panel. The Opposition, which had pushed the government to scrap the bill, said it would join the committee.
Centre, Opposition united over paper leak
The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 — brought against the backdrop of protests by students after the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak — was the only legislation passed in both Houses after a full debate this session. The bill overhauls the 2024 law by introducing stricter jail terms, enhancing penalties, and setting timelines for probe and trial in fast-track courts.
According to PRS Legislative Research, the Lok Sabha spent over 10 hours discussing the bill and the Rajya Sabha over six hours. Opposition parties led by the Congress staged a walkout before the bill was passed in the Rajya Sabha, with leader of the Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge saying it was incomplete in its current form. Leader of the House JP Nadda condemned the move.
"It is indeed an achievement to clear a number of bills with one week left in the session. But we should not be blamed for passing the bills amid din," a senior government functionary told HT on condition of anonymity.
New law brings banking records into the digital age
Both Houses passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, replacing a 135-year-old British-era statute with a framework that makes electronic, digital, virtual and cloud-stored bank records admissible and enforceable evidence in court.
The law it replaces, the Bankers' Books Evidence Act of 1891, was built for a world of physical ledgers, and was never designed for cloud-based, electronic, digital or other storage formats even after several amendments.
Delayed registration of births, deaths made more stringent
Parliament also passed the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, tightening one of India's oldest civil laws. The change is narrow on paper — a single sub-section of the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 — but it re-routes how births and deaths reported more than two years late are registered.
Beyond that threshold, cases now go to a judicial magistrate of the first class, a judicial officer under the high court, instead of an executive magistrate, a district-cadre administrator under the state government.
This is the second time in three years that Parliament has amended a statute most people encounter only once — to prove they were born.
"The government wants that every child born in the country should be registered and every death should also be registered... Anyone who has died, cannot continue to remain in the voter lists to benefit some parties," minister of state for home affairs Nityanand Rai said.
Several members of the National Democratic Alliance backed the bill as necessary, while the Opposition pressed for Shah's presence in the House. CPI(M)'s AA Rahim, among those raising the demand, cited the deaths of more than 20 students linked to the NEET paper leak.
'Vande Mataram' gets legal protection on a par with national anthem
Both Houses cleared a bill giving Vande Mataram the same legal status as the national anthem — the first bill passed amid din this session. President Droupadi Murmu gave her assent on Tuesday.
The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 went through on a voice vote after 14 minutes of debate, with only three MPs — DMK's K Kanimozhi and A Raja, and BJP's Sambit Patra — speaking.
It makes insulting or obstructing the national song a criminal offence, punishable by up to three years in jail and a fine, extending protections currently reserved for the national flag, anthem and Constitution.
Patra said the timing coincided with Vande Mataram's 150th anniversary. The Opposition said nationalism cannot be legislated. The move follows the Centre's earlier decision making all six stanzas mandatory, departing from the two-stanza version adopted as the national song in 1950.
Sitharaman assures no UPI tax, but bill gives Centre power to redefine what stays free
Parliament passed the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, with finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman ruling out any tax on UPI. Digital payments stay free for consumers, she said.
Cleared by the Lok Sabha last week, the bill was passed in the Rajya Sabha by a voice vote after a brief debate and Sitharaman's reply. It severs the link between the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and the Income Tax Act, and gives the government legal backing to alter the zero-MDR framework for UPI and RuPay.
Banks and payment providers cannot currently charge users on UPI or RuPay debit transactions, directly or indirectly. The bill lets the Centre decide, by notification, which payment modes stay free.
Supreme Court judges to increase
Parliament also passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, raising the top court's sanctioned strength from 34 to 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India.
The bill, which replaced a May ordinance, received the President's assent on Tuesday and comes amid a mounting case backlog. It cleared on a voice vote as Opposition members walked out, with Union minister Arjun Ram Meghwal saying the government was committed to judicial independence.
Kerala set for a new name: Keralam
Kerala will soon be known as Keralam. The Rajya Sabha passed the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, by voice vote on Wednesday, a day after the Lok Sabha cleared it.
"The bill provides that the State of Kerala will be known as the State of Keralam," Rai said. The Constitution's First Schedule will be amended under Article 3 to reflect the new name.
Parliament clips states' powers to tax minerals
Parliament also passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, curbing states' powers to tax mineral rights and "mineral-bearing lands". The bill went through on a voice vote, without debate, amid Opposition protests.
A new section bars states from imposing "any tax, cess or such other levy (by whatever name called)" on mineral rights or mineral-bearing lands — whether linked to mineral quantity, value or royalty — unless the central government prescribes otherwise. It will take effect once the President gives assent.
Parliament passes bill to fix delayed payments to MSMEs
Parliament passed the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, aimed at the long-standing problem of delayed payments to MSMEs. The bill seeks to improve the sector's administrative structure and streamline payment mechanisms.

headline: 2020 Delhi riots: Court says 'unsafe' to rely on tainted witness testimony
full_text:
2020 Delhi riots: Court says 'unsafe' to rely on tainted witness testimony
New Delhi, A court here has acquitted 13 accused in a 2020 northeast Delhi riots case, saying the testimony of the key prosecution witness was under a "shadow of doubt".
Additional Sessions Judge Parveen Singh said the CCTV footage relied upon for identification was too poor to establish the identity of the accused persons.
"Considering the fact that this witness had suddenly become an eyewitness and in view of the above discussion that the testimony of PW8 as an eyewitness is under a shadow of doubt, it will be unsafe to rely upon the testimony of PW8 ," the court said in its recent order.
The case pertained to an incident on February 25, 2020, in the New Usmanpur police station area, where Raman Chauhan was allegedly attacked during the communal violence. Chauhan told the court that he could not identify any of the rioters who had attacked him.
An FIR was registered at New Usmanpur police station against 13 accused identified as Mohammad Anas, Mobin, Mohd. Javed Khan alias Shanu, Faisal, Shahjad Khan alias Montu, Imran Khan, Badshah Khan, Irfan Khan, Siraj Khan, Arman alias Arbaz, Aman alias Suhail and Iqbal Khan alias Sonu.
The accused faced charges including rioting, rioting armed with deadly weapons, attempt to murder, criminal conspiracy and disobedience of an order promulgated by a public servant.
The court said the prosecution witness had initially stated during investigation that he had not witnessed the incident but subsequently appeared before the court as an eyewitness and identified two accused from CCTV footage.
The court held that such material improvements rendered his testimony unsafe to rely upon. It also noted that the CCTV footage was black-and-white, dark and grainy, while the FSL had been unable to give an opinion on facial identification because of poor pixel resolution.
The court also made a strong observation on the alleged criminal conspiracy, holding that the recovery of weapons by itself could not establish a conspiracy. It noted there was no evidence showing when, where or how the alleged conspiracy was entered into or who had joined it.
The court also found that the prosecution had failed to establish the mandatory procedure for proclamation proceedings against several accused charged under Section 174A of the IPC.
"In view of the above discussion, all the accused are accordingly acquitted of all the charges framed against them," the court said.

headline: Audit reveals BOAT Mumbai diverted ₹17.3 cr SC/ST grant to pay General quota stipend
full_text:
Audit reveals BOAT Mumbai diverted ₹17.3 cr SC/ST grant to pay General quota stipend
CAG found BOAT Mumbai used ₹17.34 crore meant for SC/ST apprentices to pay stipends to General-category candidates.
The Board of Apprenticeship Training (BOAT), Mumbai used ₹17.34 crore meant for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe (SC/ST) apprentices to pay stipends to General-category candidates, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) has found.
The findings are part of CAG’s report on central autonomous bodies, comprising a series of audit on institutions under the education ministry.
Also read: ₹843 cr of pollution cess unspent, 280 days’ data missing: CAG report in Delhi Assembly
According to the report, tabled in Parliament on Wednesday, BOAT Mumbai had received separate grants for SC, ST and General-category apprentices. During 2020-21 to 2022-23, it engaged 142,393 apprentices, including 10,736 SC and 3,607 ST candidates. The audit found a 25% shortfall in SC engagement and 72% shortfall in ST engagement against the required numbers.
Rather than retaining the unutilised funds for their sanctioned purpose or seeking the necessary approval, BOAT Mumbai used ₹17.34 crore of SC/ST grants to pay stipends to General-category apprentices, it said.
The report also flagged that the National Testing Agency (NTA) paid ₹54.24 lakh in avoidable penal interest for delaying the deposit of TDS over three financial years; accreditation and technology deficiencies at the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC); ₹23.57 crore of infructuous expenditure by IGNOU’s Gyan Vani network; procurement irregularities involving ₹8.16 crore at the Central University of Tamil Nadu.
The CAG also flagged a series of governance, financial, procurement and human resource lapses at the IIM Rohtak, including an overstatement of its corpus fund by ₹267.45 crore and payment of ₹88.64 lakh in salaries to 10 individuals without complete recruitment records.

headline: PM Modi enquires about Sukhbir Singh Badal's health after ‘kirpan attack’ in Nanded
full_text:
PM Modi enquires about Sukhbir Singh Badal's health after ‘kirpan attack’ in Nanded
Narendra Modi inquired about former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhbir Singh Badal’s health in a phone conversation with his wife.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday spoke to Shiromani Akali Dal MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal and inquired about the health of her husband and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, who was injured in an attack at a gurdwara in Nanded, Maharashtra, sources said.
Badal was accompanied by his wife, Harsimrat, at the time of the incident.
Badal was reportedly attacked by a man dressed in Nihang attire with a kirpan at Gurdwara Mata Sahib Kaur on Thursday. He sustained an injury to his hand and was subsequently taken to a nearby hospital for treatment.
The incident took place when Badal was reportedly heading towards the langar hall after paying obeisance at the gurdwara. The shrine is located around 15 km from Takht Sri Hazur Sahib, one of the five Takhts, or temporal seats, of Sikhism.
The attack comes days after Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on August 7, a meeting that had sparked speculation about a possible rapprochement between the SAD and BJP ahead of the Punjab Assembly elections, reported news agency PTI.
Fadnavis orders inquiry
Meanwhil, Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has ordered an inquiry into the reported attack, a PTI report said.
This was the second reported attack on Badal in less than two years. In December 2024, he survived an assassination bid outside the Golden Temple in Amritsar when former militant Narain Singh Chaura allegedly opened fire at him from close range. A security officer intervened, causing the bullet to miss Badal and hit a wall. Chaura was later overpowered and arrested.
Deep Dive
SAD calls it ‘close-range’ attack
Sharing update after the attack, the Shiromani Akali Dal said Badal was doing well and remained in “high spirits”. The SAD described the incident as a “close-range” attack.
SAD spokesperson Arshdeep Singh Kler said the attacker attempted to target Badal but was stopped by security personnel accompanying the party chief.
Kler said Badal suffered a minor injury to his arm and was undergoing treatment at a hospital. “Badal sustained a minor injury on his arm and is undergoing treatment at a hospital. He is completely fine and in 'Chardi Kala' (high spirits),” he said.
Alleging that “panthic leaders” were being targeted repeatedly, Kler said, “Some 'panth virodhi' (anti-panth) forces are hatching such conspiracies.”
Kler said the state Police would investigate the incident and determine whether there was any conspiracy behind the attack.
