headline: In a video made in Hindi and posted Thursday on X, Singh sought these details from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, stating that it could not have been done without the PM’s approval.
full_text:
In a video made in Hindi and posted Thursday on X, Singh sought these details from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, stating that it could not have been done without the PM’s approval.
He questioned whether Shera Point 5 is the only patrolling point which the Chinese have occupied, or “are there other patrolling points which were given up by this government.”
“Patrolling points which were being patrolled, where our patrols used to go before 2014?”
Shera Point 5 is a patrolling point for the Indian forces ahead of Taksing, which is the last village on the border with Tibet in Upper Subansiri district. ThePrint earlier this week reported details of the stand-off at Taksing.
The government, the former home secretary said, needs to answer these questions as it concerns the whole country.
“And this also gives a message about how pusillanimous, I will call it, this government is—that it can’t stand up for even its claims, even the claim of the country. Let the government come clean on this issue. And let the government come clean on how many patrolling points they have abandoned since 2014.”
Singh added that the entire nation is asking this question of the Modi government. “This is the question which the nation is asking. And the defence minister needs to answer, the prime minister needs to answer. Because giving up a claim on any point is not possible without the approval of the prime minister.”
The former minister, who resigned from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 2025, had been critical of the ruling party, especially the Bihar unit. Singh had been critical of the BJP as well as the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) leadership. The former MP from Arrah had levelled a series of charges against the Nitish Kumar-led government in Bihar. He was later suspended by the BJP for “anti-party activities”.
On Wednesday, All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) chief Asaduddin Owaisi also questioned the government over the situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh, alleging that the Chinese had entered Indian territory as well as blocked Indian patrols and pitched tents.
Singh, meanwhile, recalled his about eight-year stint in the Ministry of Defence and seven years in the Ministry of Home Affairs to assert that he knew about border management.
— R. K. Singh (@RajKSinghIndia) August 13, 2026
A former bureaucrat, Singh served as the home secretary during Manmohan Singh’s tenure. He had been the secretary in the Department of Defence Production between 2009 and 2011. He joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 2013 post retirement. Singh was elected MP from Bihar’s Arrah twice—in 2014 and 2019.
He served as the Minister of State (Independent charge) for Power and New and Renewable Energy (2017-2024). He then went on to become the Minister for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship from 2019 to 2024. Singh was elevated to the Cabinet rank in July 2024.
The former minister stated that he read it in a news report about the incident which worried him and “should worry all the citizens.”
“It appears that we have abandoned a patrolling point called Sera 5 in Taksing in Arunachal. And the Chinese have established a permanent presence there. I will tell you what this means. The Chinese and we have a dispute about the borders. And that dispute has been carrying on ever since the Chinese occupied Aksai Chin,” he said, referring to the 1962 India-China war.
“The Chinese do not accept the McMahon line as a border. They also are not willing together to demarcate the LAC. Because they have made huge claims into our territory, including the entire Arunachal Pradesh. Now, because of this totally differing perceptions about where the border is and where the LAC is, we carry out patrolling. Our patrols go up to points along our perceived Line of Actual Control,” he explained.
The Chinese, he said, come up to patrolling points along their perceived Line of Actual Control.
“This patrolling is a markup. It shows that this is where our claim line lies. So that when the negotiations do happen, our perceptions of the claim line is very clear. That’s why patrolling up to these points is essential. So that our claim line is specifically communicated to the other side. And that is why the Chinese also patrol up to points along their claim lines.“
“Now, when you abandon a patrolling point along your claim line and the Chinese occupy it, that means you have given up your claim. Now, one patrolling point where we have given up our claim has been reported in the newspapers. I want to know and the nation wants to know as to how many other patrolling points has the government given up since 2014?”
His post evoked immediate reactions from the opposition including the Congress.
“Listen to the former Home Secretary of the Government of India who was also the former Union Minister of the Modi government. He is revealing a very serious matter, saying that China has captured a significant portion of Arunachal,” Congress national spokesperson Akhilesh Singh said.
Rajya Sabha MPs Pawan Khera and Randeep Singh Surjewala took up the cue on X and questioned the Modi government.
“When will Narendra Modi himself object to the actual distortion of the Indian map being done by China in Arunachal Pradesh?” Khera asked.

— Pawan Khera 🇮🇳 ಪವನ್ ಖೇರಾ (@Pawankhera) August 10, 2026
“When Mr. R.K. Singh—who served as a Cabinet Minister in the Modi government for seven years and has worked in the Home and Defence Ministries for nearly 15 years—himself states that China is now encroaching upon Indian territory and occupying our land in Arunachal Pradesh (following Ladakh), why does the Modi government remain silent? The country has every right to know the truth,” Surjewala posted.
In the video post, Singh said while there was complete faith in the valour, capability, and resolve of the Indian Army, “our questions concern the policy, intent, and accountability of the Modi government, which has tied its hands.”
“On one hand, a red carpet is being rolled out for Chinese investment and the PLI scheme; on the other, is China’s growing hold over our territory and patrolling points being ignored? The nation wants to know: what is the Modi government’s actual policy regarding China?”
During his stint with the BJP, Singh had flagged alleged irregularities in the commissioning of a power plant in Bihar, which led to a political controversy days before the assembly polls there.
The 1975 batch IAS officer of the Bihar cadre had contested the 2024 Lok Sabha election from Arrah but lost to the Communist Party of India (Marxist–Leninist) Liberation candidate. Singh had alleged that his electoral loss was due to the ‘machinations’ of some senior BJP leaders in Bihar.

headline: How Tata Sons will pick N Chandrasekaran's successor and who will choose him
full_text:
How Tata Sons will pick N Chandrasekaran's successor and who will choose him
The Trusts specifically acknowledged Chandrasekaran's contribution during a period of "significant change, growth and transformation" across the Tata group.
The Tata Trusts on Thursday initiated the process of finding N Chandrasekaran's successor to lead Tata Sons, the holding company of the diversified Tata group, a day after Chandrasekaran announced that he would not seek reappointment for a third term as chairman.
The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT), which is among the charitable trusts that together hold nearly two-thirds of Tata Sons, said its trustees had decided to begin the process of setting up a selection committee to recommend the next chairman of the Tata Sons board, according to a PTI report.
The Trusts specifically acknowledged Chandrasekaran's contribution during a period of "significant change, growth and transformation" across the Tata group.
Deep Dive
Chandrasekaran, who has led Tata Sons since 2017, announced on Wednesday that he would not offer himself for reappointment as chairman for a third term.
The decision came amid a lack of unanimity within the Tata Sons board over his continuation, according to his statement, the report added.
Also Read | ‘Respect his decision’: Tata Trusts on Chandrasekaran’s call to step down
How will Chandrasekaran's successor be chosen?
The Tata Trusts are expected to play a central role in the appointment process because of their significant ownership of Tata Sons. The charitable trusts together own about 66% of the holding company.
Under Article 118 of the Articles of Association of Tata Sons, a selection committee has to be constituted for the appointment of the chairman, as long as the Tata charitable trusts continue to hold the required stake in Tata Sons.
The selection committee will be tasked with identifying and recommending a candidate for the position. The final appointment will then be made in accordance with the governance framework of Tata Sons.
The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust said its trustees have passed a resolution to initiate the setting up of the selection committee as soon as possible “in accordance with the Articles of Association of Tata Sons, for the purpose of recommending a person for appointment as the new Chairman of the Board of Directors.
Also Read | N Chandrasekaran's decision to step down creates immediate succession challenge for Tata Sons
What happened when Cyrus Mistry was removed?
The process of finding Chandrasekaran's successor has some similarities with the succession exercise that followed the removal of Cyrus Mistry in October 2016, although the circumstances are different.

headline: Maharashtra cab, auto drivers should learn Marathi; BJP demands 100-day extension

Maharashtra cab, auto drivers should learn Marathi; BJP demands 100-day extension
A demand has been made for 100 more days to help non-Marathi-speaking cab and auto drivers complete language training in Maharashtra. The request comes as ministers signal flexibility while stressing the push to implement the Marathi rule.
The Maharashtra government’s move to make Marathi knowledge mandatory for auto-rickshaw and taxi drivers has prompted the BJP to demand for an additional 100 days for non-Marathi-speaking drivers to complete their language training.
Haji Arfat Sheikh, president of the Maharashtra BJP Transport Cell, has submitted a request to Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik, seeking the extension.
The state government had given non-Marathi-speaking auto-rickshaw and taxi drivers time from May 1 to August 15, 2026, to learn Marathi. However, Sheikh said heavy rainfall during this period disrupted the training process, with halls, schools and classrooms unavailable at several locations.
He also claimed that trainers could not reach several locations on time in cities including Mumbai, Thane, Pune, Malegaon, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Akola, Parbhani and Nanded.
75% DRIVERS HAVE BASIC MARATHI KNOWLEDGE, SAYS SHEIKH
According to Haji Arfat Sheikh, around 75 per cent of auto-rickshaw and taxi drivers across Maharashtra have acquired basic knowledge of Marathi.
He said the remaining drivers should also be given an opportunity to complete their training and should not face immediate punitive action.
Sheikh has therefore sought an additional 100 days for the drivers to complete the required training. He said the BJP Transport Cell would extend full cooperation in ensuring that auto-rickshaw and taxi drivers receive the necessary training and that the government's objective is achieved.
YOGESH KADAM SAYS EXTENSION CAN BE CONSIDERED
Amid the demand for an extension, Minister of State for Home and FDA Yogesh Kadam said additional time could be considered for drivers who need it.
Kadam said Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik had initiated the move concerning the Marathi language, but pointed out that a law relating to Marathi already exists. He said the government was now working towards implementing the existing law.
"If auto-rickshaw and taxi drivers need additional time to learn Marathi, there is no objection to it," Kadam said. He added that drivers who require more time can approach the concerned minister with their request, following which an extension could be considered.
Kadam stressed that a positive approach was needed on the issue and that drivers should be willing to learn Marathi.
He said there should be no problem if a driver needed an additional 10 or 15 days to learn the language. The government's objective, he said, was not to impose Marathi forcibly or solely through punitive measures.

headline: Meghalaya HC panel seeks urgent action plan to curb illegal coal mining
full_text:
Meghalaya HC panel seeks urgent action plan to curb illegal coal mining
The Meghalaya HC-appointed Justice BP Katakey committee urged the state to notify an action plan against illegal coal mining and fence abandoned rat-hole pits.
The Meghalaya high court-appointed justice BP Katakey committee has urged the state government to urgently notify a comprehensive action plan to curb illegal coal mining and transportation and formulate a policy for the closure and fencing of thousands of abandoned rat-hole mine pits.
In its 39th Interim Report filed before the high court on Thursday, the one-man committee expressed concern that its earlier recommendation for a state action plan was yet to be implemented despite the continuing threat posed by illegal mining and unsecured abandoned mine openings.
The panel said immediate notification of the plan was essential to strengthen prevention, detection and enforcement against illegal mining.
The Mining and Geology Secretary, at a meeting on June 29, informed the committee that a draft State Action Plan had already been prepared and was awaiting final approval. “The comprehensive plan of action would be notified within 2 (two) weeks’ time,” the Secretary assured the committee.
The panel also raised serious concerns over the thousands of abandoned mine openings that remain unsecured, posing a continuing danger to people and livestock.
It noted that the Central Mine Planning and Design Institute Ltd (CMPDIL) had prepared restoration detailed project reports (DPRs) for two pilot sites — Sutnga in East Jaiñtia Hills, estimated at ₹92.78 lakh, and Arenggtim in South Garo Hills, at ₹63 lakh.
However, the committee pointed out that the proposals did not include interim safety arrangements pending implementation. “The aforesaid two project proposals… do not have any proposal for taking of adequate measures, including fencing of the mine openings, to prevent danger to human life and livestock till implementation,” the report said.
The two proposals are currently awaiting clearance from the Oversight Committee constituted by the National Green Tribunal (NGT).
Katakey said Meghalaya could not afford to wait for restoration projects to be implemented before securing dangerous mine openings. He called for an immediate state policy for closure and fencing of hazardous pits, with priority given to abandoned mines located close to villages and other habitations.
Katakey also sought fixed timelines for identifying and securing such sites, given their large numbers across the state.
Following earlier directions from the panel, deputy commissioners have begun consultations with traditional authorities. Officials in East Jaiñtia Hills and South Garo Hills have consulted headmen and nokmas on measures to protect and permanently close mine pits near settlements.
At the June 29 meeting, the deputy commissioners of South West Khasi Hills, West Khasi Hills, West Jaiñtia Hills and East Jaiñtia Hills committed to submit final proposals to the Mining Department within 10 days, while South Garo Hills sought 15 days.
Beyond enforcement and mine safety, the committee recommended setting up independent grievance redressal committees at both state and district levels to receive complaints of illegal mining.
It proposed a transparent, technology-driven mechanism with emergency powers, fixed disposal timelines and protection for whistleblowers.
The panel also recommended that the government frame an ex gratia policy under Article 162 for families of persons killed or injured in illegal mining accidents.
The policy, it said, should clearly prescribe eligibility, compensation amounts, verification procedures and payment timelines, while allowing the government to recover the compensation from mine owners, landowners and operators.
“A provision for appeal by the aggrieved person to the higher authority may also be made,” the report said.
The matter will now return before the Meghalaya High Court for further consideration.

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) suspended the licence of Sapphire Foods-operated Pizza Hut outlet at Karad in Satara district of the state over alleged violations of food safety and hygiene norms, officials said.
At the Pizza Hut outlet in Karad, the FDA found that separate ovens and pans were not being used to prepare vegetarian and non-vegetarian pizzas.
During another inspection at a Sapphire Foods outlet in Akola, the FDA seized 55 kg of frozen paneer, which it classified as misbranded and substandard.
Maharashtra FDA's inspection drive
The FDA's special drive covered 104 chain restaurant establishments across Maharashtra. Two establishments were ordered to stop operations, 95 were issued improvement notices, and the licences of five establishments were suspended, the FDA said.
The drive covered brands such as KFC, Pizza Hut, McDonald's, Subway, Burger King, Starbucks, and Monginis.
In Nashik district, the FDA suspended the licences of five food establishments - Hotel Sayali Restaurant and Bar in Satpur, Hotel Chhote Miyan on College Road, Mani Mark on Peth Road in Panchavati, Abhishek Bakery and Sweets in CIDCO and Mohanlal Namkeen in Dindori. The action followed inspections that found deficiencies in areas including cleanliness, food storage, water supply, equipment and pest control.
In Mumbai, the authority also suspended the licences of Mumbai Metro Dhaba in Mulund and Gulshan-Da-Punjabi Dhaba in Bhandup. Inspections found shortcomings in basic facilities, cleanliness, water supply, ventilation, pest control and food storage.
Blinkit Malad (West) outlet licence suspended
This comes a day after the Maharashtra food safety and drug administration suspended the licence of Blinkit’s Malad (West) facility over serious food safety and hygiene violations.
The facility was found to have a large-scale cockroach infestation, improperly stored food, and expired and tampered products, HT reported earlier.
Officials found food items kept on rusted racks. The cold storage areas also lacked adequate cleanliness, and expired or spoiled packaged food was found at the facility.
The establishment has been prohibited from selling or distributing food or carrying out any food business during the period of the licence suspension, according to a statement.

Rahim who had moved the Supreme Court on the deployment of facial recognition technology and allied mass-surveillance measures against students and persons who participated in the Cockroach Janta Party-linked protests over the NEET-UG exam paper leaks.
A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant addressed senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy and advocate Subhash Chandran that Mr. Rahim’s petition would be tagged with the main NEET-UG protest petitions, which have questioned the police crackdown on students and the use of pellet guns.
Ms. Guruswamy submitted that the surveillance was done by the police on the ground and the data was hosted with private agencies.
“One maps your face. Spectacles are used and a vehicle is also used. The data is taken without permission. Then private entities host the data in violation of DPDP Rules, CrPC and a variety of things,” Ms. Guruswamy submitted.
The MP said that the use of facial recognition technology and covert surveillance on peaceful protesters was unconstitutional.
“The gravamen of the challenge is the automated, algorithmic extraction and matching of the biometric identifiers of thousands of peaceful protesters, and the interlinking of such data with permanent national criminal databases. Since the commencement of the sit-in on July 20, the Delhi Police have subjected thousands of protesters, journalists and ordinary citizens to continuous and pervasive biometric surveillance,” the petition said.

The plea said the surveillance was done through the acquisition of videos and photographs through CCTV cameras, drones, a mobile command and control vehicle and hand-held devices.
“The real-time processing of such footage through automated facial recognition technology using the ‘Ikshana’ vehicle and ‘AjnaLens’ smart spectacles and the collection and matching of fingerprints through the National Crime Records Bureau’s ‘Abhigyan’ mobile application against the National Automated Fingerprint Identification System. This surveillance was carried out in a complete legal vacuum,” the petition said.

Delhi Police busted a major human trafficking network across three states, rescuing 10 minor girls and arresting six accused. The traffickers used social media to lure girls with promises of lucrative jobs before sending them to spas and hotels outside Delhi.
Delhi Police has busted a major human trafficking network and rescued 10 minor girls after conducting raids across three states. Police have arrested six accused and detained three minors in connection with the case.
The network allegedly operated through social media, where its members targeted minor girls with promises of a better life and high-paying jobs. They lured the girls with offers of employment at spa centres and hotels. Once a girl responded to their messages, the traffickers allegedly took her outside Delhi.
The case came to light on May 9, when police received a complaint about the disappearance of a 15-year-old girl. Police began investigating the case but initially found no useful clue from CCTV footage in the area.
The police then examined the girl's mobile phone and found clues on her social media account. An account had sent her several messages promising a better life and a good salary. The investigation subsequently revealed that the girl had been taken out of Delhi.
The police traced the girl's Instagram activity and found that she had been taken to Mundra in Gujarat. A Delhi Police team then travelled to Mundra and, with the help of local police, rescued the girl from a spa centre operating inside a hotel.
During the operation, police caught spa operators Damni, Sushil and Haresh Lakshya, along with two minors.
The investigation then led the Delhi Police team to Ballia in Uttar Pradesh. There, police rescued seven girls from Melody Spa Centre and arrested Monu, Sonu and Sanjeev Maurya.
Police subsequently reached Ganesh Nagar in East Delhi, where they rescued two more girls and arrested a woman named Khushi.

headline: UAE-based Pravasi Bandhu Welfare Trust has urged the Kerala government to tap the savings, skills, and business networks of Non-Resident Keralites (NRKs) to create jobs and support economic growth.
full_text:
UAE-based Pravasi Bandhu Welfare Trust has urged the Kerala government to tap the savings, skills, and business networks of Non-Resident Keralites (NRKs) to create jobs and support economic growth.
Trust chairman K.V. Shamsudheen made the suggestions in a memorandum submitted to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, proposing measures to channel NRI savings into infrastructure, industry, and other productive sectors.
The trust said more than ₹3 trillion was held in Non-Resident External (NRE) deposits in Kerala banks, earning less than 7% interest. It suggested mobilising part of these funds for investments that generate jobs and economic activity.
“Kerala receives an estimated ₹2.3-2.5 lakh crore in remittances from expatriates each year, accounting for nearly 20% of India’s inward remittances,” the memorandum said.
Mutual funds for NRKs
Mr. Shamsudheen suggested that the government-owned Cheraman Financial Services Ltd. (CFSL) launch professionally managed mutual fund schemes for NRKs. Expatriates could invest through systematic investment plans (SIPs) and receive regular income through systematic withdrawal plans (SWPs) after retirement.
The trust said this could help NRKs plan for retirement while directing part of their savings into Kerala’s economy.
Bonds for infrastructure
The trust suggested raising funds from NRKs for the proposed high-speed railway between Thiruvananthapuram and Kasaragod through a secured, redeemable and tax-free non-convertible bond.
Mr. Shamsudheen said the Konkan Railway’s use of tax-free bonds could serve as a model. He said he had promoted the bonds among NRIs in the UAE and witnessed strong investor participation when veteran technocrat E. Sreedharan led the project.
The trust also suggested a CIAL-style public limited company to raise equity from NRKs and residents.
Manufacturing and agro-processing
The memorandum called for incentives to FMCG companies such as Hindustan Unilever, Nestle, and Britannia to establish manufacturing units in Kerala. It also sought investment in processing and value addition of coconut, spices, rubber, mango, and jackfruit.
The trust said Kerala could develop coconut-based industries and tap Gulf demand for products such as jackfruit and tender coconut. It also called for expanding SME opportunities for Gulf returnees by using their skills, experience, and business networks.

headline: Drastic decline: Panel flags 73% dropout before higher secondary in govt schools
full_text:
Drastic decline: Panel flags 73% dropout before higher secondary in govt schools
A parliamentary panel has warned that nearly 73 per cent of students drop out before completing higher secondary. It has also flagged serious gaps in Divyang-friendly infrastructure and urged faster action on school upgrades and special educator recruitment.
A parliamentary panel has flagged a "drastic decline" in the number of schools and students as education levels rise, and said nearly 73 per cent of students drop out before finishing higher secondary.
The recommendation is part of the Tenth Report (Eighteenth Lok Sabha) of the Committee on Estimates (2026-27) on "Budget and Policy aspects for providing Affordable and Quality Education in the Country, including Review of Central Board of Secondary Education", which was presented in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.
The committee also pointed to a major shortfall in facilities for Divyang students, saying more than half of schools across the country do not have Children with Special Needs-friendly infrastructure. It called on the Ministry of Education to improve budget use, complete projects on time, and speed up the recruitment of special educators.
Citing UDISE 2024-25 data, the committee said that out of 10,92,671 government and government-aided schools, 9,11,032 are at the primary level, 4,12,805 at the upper primary level, 1,61,808 at the secondary level, and only 90,866 at the higher secondary level. On enrolment, it said there are 6,18,45,033 students in primary classes and 4,08,93,978 in upper primary classes from 6 to 8, but the number falls to 2,36,68,220 in secondary and then to 1,64,17,949 in higher secondary.
"The committee are concerned to note this drastic decline in number of schools and students as education levels rises," it said.
"From the above information, the Committee note that out of over 1 million government schools, the vast majority are only primary schools, and nearly 73% of students drop out before finishing higher secondary," it added.
The panel strongly urged the ministry to prioritise upgrading existing primary and secondary schools into full higher secondary schools so that a high school is physically accessible to students from different communities and to check the student drop-off rate.
"The Committee are of the view that there is an urgent need to increase the number of schools at secondary and higher secondary levels," it said. As education is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and most schools come under state governments and Union Territory administrations, the committee asked the ministry to impress upon states and UTs to set up more secondary and higher secondary schools to increase enrolment.
On inclusive education, the committee said the Ministry of Education provides financial support to states and UTs under the Samagra Shiksha scheme to strengthen infrastructure and human resources for Divyang students. The scheme provides for barrier-free and differently-abled-friendly infrastructure such as ramps, handrails and accessible toilets.
However, as per UDISE+ 2024-25, out of 14,71,437 schools across the country, only 5,23,143 have CwSN toilets and only 8,08,466 have ramps with handrails. During 2024-25, a budget of Rs 482 lakh was allocated for construction of 186 CwSN toilets, but only Rs 2.60 lakh was utilised and there was no progress on physical targets.
"The severe gap in the availability of CwSN friendly infrastructure shows that more than half of the schools across the country are devoid of CwSN friendly infrastructure," the committee said.
The panel also noted that only Rs 80.50 lakh was used under financial support for new special educators against a budgetary grant of Rs 962 lakh for the elementary section, and said only meagre progress had been made in recruiting and retaining special educators for CwSN students. It said the ministry's approach to promoting education for Divyang children is rights-based, inclusive and holistic.
It referred to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, which provides free education up to the age of 18 for children with benchmark disabilities, and to the NEP 2020, which lays down a Zero Rejection Policy to ensure no child is denied schooling because of disability and stresses teacher preparation for inclusive classrooms.
"In view of the above, the Committee strongly recommend the Ministry to adhere to yearly targets of budget utilisation and execution of CwSN related projects in a time bound manner," it said.
In its recommendations, the committee asked the ministry to expand access to secondary and higher secondary schools, provide safe and accessible infrastructure to Divyang students in a time-bound manner, and assess the requirement of special educators across the country so that recruitment can be completed at the earliest.

headline: Cybersecurity has become an economic imperative and governance priority as digital technologies become deeply embedded in everyday life, said N. Manjula, Secretary, Department of Electronics, IT and BT, Government of Karnataka, here on Wednesday.

Held under the theme “Stronger Together. Secure Tomorrow,” the dialogue was organised as part of Karnataka’s ongoing international technology partnerships under its Global Innovation Alliance (GIA), in collaboration with the Consulate General and Trade Mission of Israel in South India and the Centre for Cybersecurity Karnataka (CySecK).

A delegation of 10 Israeli cybersecurity companies participated in the programme, with the engagement extending beyond the roundtable to technology demonstrations and B2B meetings aimed at identifying opportunities for practical partnerships.
The discussions focused on four key areas: Innovation and Start-ups, Industry Partnership, Talent & Skills, and Policy & Trust, with an emphasis on translating knowledge exchange into practical collaboration and strengthening the resilience of critical digital infrastructure, businesses and public institutions.
Dr. Manjula highlighted Karnataka’s Global Innovation Alliance, through which the Government engages with countries on areas of shared interest and builds partnerships across technology and innovation sectors. She further said the Karnataka-Israel cybersecurity engagement represented an opportunity to build on these international partnerships and explore collaboration across cybersecurity innovation, start-up partnerships, talent development, research, technology validation and critical infrastructure protection.
Orli Weitzman, Consul General of Israel to South India, said the Karnataka-Israel engagement reflected the growing India-Israel partnership and the natural alignment between the two ecosystems.

headline: Rape survivors, with pregnancies up to 24 weeks, do not require the permission from a court to seek a legal termination of pregnancy, the Madhya Pradesh High Court has said.
full_text:
Rape survivors, with pregnancies up to 24 weeks, do not require the permission from a court to seek a legal termination of pregnancy, the Madhya Pradesh High Court has said.
A Single Bench of Justice Sandeep N. Bhatt in Indore on August 11 made the remarks hearing a petition filed by the father of a 16-year-old sexual assault survivor who sought the court’s approval for the girl’s 18-week pregnancy. The petition cited extreme mental trauma for the survivors to continue with the pregnancy.
Saying that the matter did not require court intervention, Justice Bhatt disposed off the plea while citing a February 20, 2025, verdict that the High Court’s Division Bench in Jabalpur had earlier clarified that under the provisions of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971, survivors of sexual assault, rape, or incest, with pregnancies up to 24 weeks, who want to undergo an abortion do not require judicial proceedings under Article 226 of the Constitution.
The court also issued directions to State’s Health Commissioner to communicate the Jabalpur Bench’s judgement to hospitals in the State for future reference.
“The Commissioner, Health Department, may also communicate the aforesaid order passed by the Division Bench to all the concerned hospitals more particularly the Government Hospitals, so that they can also take care of the situation in future,” the Indore Bench order read.
“With the above directions, since no intervention is required in the matter, present petition is dismissed,” it said.
In February, 2025, the Division Bench headed by the then Chief Justice Suresk Kumar Kait had laid out standard operating procedures (SOPs) to be followed by concerned officials and medical officers while dealing with pregnancies of rape or incest survivors for both cases where the pregnancy is of less than 24 weeks and beyond it.
It had asked the authorities to not demand any legal or magisterial requisition or other documentation as a pre-requisite in cases with pregnancies up to 24 weeks, while saying that court’s permission was only required if the pregnancy is of more than 24 weeks.

headline: Allahabad HC asks UP if 16-year-old contractual teachers will be regularised
full_text:
Allahabad HC asks UP if 16-year-old contractual teachers will be regularised
The Allahabad High Court asked the Uttar Pradesh government to clarify whether long-serving contractual teachers will be regularised. It said a teacher cannot be left without livelihood after 16 years of service.
The Allahabad High Court on Wednesday questioned the Uttar Pradesh government over the treatment of a teacher who has worked on a contractual basis for 16 years, saying a teacher seen as a "builder of the nation" cannot be "left to fend for herself" after such prolonged service.
The Lucknow bench said the case raised a larger issue involving contractual teachers who have served for more than 15 years. It directed the Uttar Pradesh government to file a personal affidavit from the additional chief secretary, basic education, stating whether any steps were being taken to regularise such teachers.
The court also ordered the authorities to allow the petitioner to continue on the post on a contractual basis till the next hearing. The matter came up on a petition filed by Archana Boodh, a teacher at a Kasturba Gandhi Residential Girls School in Amethi, whose contract was not renewed through an order dated June 16.
Boodh has been working since January 16, 2010, with her contract renewed from time to time. Her counsel told the court that after 16 years of service, instead of considering her regularisation, the authorities refused to renew her contract. The petitioner is now around 39 years old and, according to her counsel, would not be eligible to apply afresh for teaching posts in schools, affecting her livelihood.
The court noted from the instructions submitted by the authorities that three teachers had been transferred from different schools following disciplinary issues involving students. However, it recorded that there was no personal allegation against the petitioner.
Justice Pankaj Bhatia said the issue required consideration, particularly as the petitioner had been serving for 16 years and the decision to discontinue her contractual engagement could leave her without livelihood. The court directed the respondents to file their counter-affidavits and listed the matter on September 8 to consider the larger issue.
In sum, the high court has sought the state government's response on the regularisation of teachers working on contract for over 15 years, while allowing the petitioner to continue in service till the next hearing.

headline: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested one accused in connection with the attack involving an improvised explosive device (IED) at a residential house in Tronglaobi Awang Leikai, of Manipur’s Bishnupur district, stated an official state...
full_text:
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested one accused in connection with the attack involving an improvised explosive device (IED) at a residential house in Tronglaobi Awang Leikai, of Manipur’s Bishnupur district, stated an official statement issued on Wednesday.
The incident occurred on April 7, 2026 and resulted in the death of two minor children and injuries to another person.
The arrested individual has been identified as one S. Palal Thadou, stated the official statement.
The statement stated that the case was originally registered at Moirang Police Station, Bishnupur district following an attack where unknown militants launched an explosive device from a hillside towards Tronglaobi Awang Leikai of the same district. The explosion struck the residential wall of a house, causing serious injuries to three family members, including two minor children who later succumbed to their injuries. An unexploded improvised RPG was also recovered near the site.
The investigation was subsequently taken over by the NIA and re-registered on April 23, 2026 under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Explosive Substances Act, and Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. During the course of the investigation, the involvement of accused S. Palal Thadou has surfaced in the commission of the offence.
“Accused S. Palal Thadou was initially arrested by Churachandpur Police in connection with FIR No. 17(02)2026 and subsequently by Bishnupur Police in connection with FIR No 12(03)2026 of Phougakchao Ikhai police station (PGCI) Police Station. NIA has arrested him as part of its efforts to unravel the larger conspiracy behind the terror act, making him the first accused to be arrested in the case,” the statement stated.
The accused was produced before the Special NIA Court Imphal and has been remanded to ten days police custody.

headline: The report by the committee headed by Supreme Court judge Aravind Kumar was tabled in Lok Sabha Wednesday
full_text:
The report by the committee headed by Supreme Court judge Aravind Kumar was tabled in Lok Sabha Wednesday
NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha Speaker appointed inquiry committee in its report has recommended further action while indicting Justice Yashwant Varma for recovery of wads of 500-rupee notes at his official residence in Delhi in March last year, its unexplained disappearance and an evasive judge failing to explain "presence, source or ownership" of the huge money.The report by the committee headed by Supreme Court judge Aravind Kumar, which was tabled in LS Wednesday, recommended "such further action as may be considered in accordance with law" against Justice Varma, who withdrew from inquiry proceedings after failing to come up with convincing replies to questions put to him and, in what was seen as a move to pre-empt his removal by Parliament, resigned as Allahabad High Court judge.Also read: Can Parliament still remove judge from office?What shape the "action" recommended by the committee might take is not clear but sources did not rule out the possibility of Parliament initiating removal proceedings against Justice Varma despite his resignation. A CBI inquiry was also being discussed as a possible course of action.The committee said Justice Varma's explanation for the pile of cash "remained evasive and unsatisfactory when tested against evidence of independent official witnesses and corroborative material" and returned a finding that all three charges against the judge stood proved.
Judge's testimony evasive, misleading: Parl panel Justice Yashwant Varma's reply to Delhi HC Chief Justice on March 22, 2025 - a week after the fire incident that led to discovery of huge cash at his official residence - and his subsequent stand "did not exhibit the candour, transparency and institutional responsibility expected in the circumstances", the Lok Sabha Speaker appointed inquiry committee said in its 121-page, 299-paragraph report.On the judge's testimony, the committee said, "It was evasive because it did not engage with the central circumstance of substantial currency notes seen by independent officials inside the storeroom. It was incomplete because it did not disclose the factual steps allegedly taken by him, the details of inquiries made, the answers received from staff or household members, or any action taken to preserve the site... It was misleading in effect because the earliest broad denial gave way to successive alternative hypotheses, none of which was substantiated when opportunity to lead defence evidence was available." On Justice Varma's decision to withdraw from inquiry proceedings and resign from judgeship, the committee said the judge withdrew at a stage when he was required to substantiate with evidence his theories relating to foul play, planting of money and possible role of staff. "He did not lead evidence to substantiate them," it said. The committee recorded the shifting shape of the defence put forth by Justice Varma. "The defence moved from denial of presence to absence of seizure and verification, to possible fake currency notes, to possible removal by first responders, and to suspicions regarding staff. Each of these hypotheses required some factual foundation if it was to displace the evidence of independent official witnesses and the corroborative electronic material," it said.By alleging that the first responders had removed the burnt currency notes, the judge admitted these were at the storeroom inside his residential premises, the committee said, referring his writ petition in SC in which he had indirectly admitted to presence of cash at his residential premises.
"No satisfactory explanation has been furnished as to how currency notes seen by several official witnesses disappeared or became unavailable. These facts establish failure to preserve...material evidence," it said."What stands established is that substantial unexplained currency notes were found within the official premises occupied by the judge..."it said.The report may come up for discussion in Parliament's next session, and a further course of action against Varma will then be decided.

headline: The consortium named Allied Orbits Private Limited is led by Pixxel Space India and includes Dhruva Space, PierSight Space and Satsure Analytics India
full_text:
The consortium named Allied Orbits Private Limited is led by Pixxel Space India and includes Dhruva Space, PierSight Space and Satsure Analytics India
NEW DELHI: Space regulator IN-SPACe has approved and signed under the PPP model an agreement with a private consortium for the countryâs first indigenous, fully commercial earth observation constellation, with a view to enhancing the countryâs space-based observation capabilities and building a self-reliant earth observation (EO) ecosystem in the country, minister for department of space Jitendra Singh informed Lok Sabha on Wednesday in response to a Parliament question.The consortium named Allied Orbits Private Limited is led by Pixxel Space India and includes Dhruva Space, PierSight Space and Satsure Analytics India. It will invest more than Rs 1,200 crore for setting up the constellation, which is to be developed and operationalised by 2029.
The consortium will design, build, own and operate the 12-satellite constellation, which will have panchromatic, multispectral, hyperspectral and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) capabilities, supported by indigenous ground infrastructure. All satellites are to be manufactured domestically and launched on Indian launch vehicles, with mission control based in the country.The programme includes designing, fabrication, integration and the testing of EO satellites, including five ultra-high resolution optical satellites with 4 bands, 3 multispectral satellites with 8 bands, 2 hyperspectral optical satellites with 250 bands and 2 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites in X-band, by the Indian industry. The EO programme will use Indian launch vehicles (either private or Isro facilities) for placing the satellites into orbit. The programme also allows collaboration with academic and research institutions for capacity building and application development, the minister said.

headline: The Greater Chennai Corporation’s (GCC) property tax reassessment drive has drawn heavy backlash over sharp increases and a lack of prior consultation and transparency.
full_text:
The Greater Chennai Corporation’s (GCC) property tax reassessment drive has drawn heavy backlash over sharp increases and a lack of prior consultation and transparency.
A GCC official said the revised tax was based on self-declared property area. The first revision was carried out in 2018, followed by a major one in 2022, but the collection was subsequently paused. The revised rate should have been collected 2022 onwards, and is now being implemented, he said.
T.K. Shanmugam, chairman of the Federation of North Chennai Residents’ Welfare Associations (FNCRWA), said a resident, who had been paying a property tax of ₹295, was demanded ₹3,255 following the reassessment, without receiving any explanation. Mr. Shanmugam said the residents were not given details such as the rate per square foot or the basis for the revised assessment.
He further questioned whether the residents would be able to approach the Revenue Department officials to raise objections, given the large number of properties involved.
He said many houses in North Chennai had undergone additions over the years that may not have been reflected in earlier assessments. However, he criticised the manner in which such changes were being reassessed using only drone and GIS-based methods, without manual confirmation.
Many also took to social media, saying the sudden move and close deadline had put several residents between a rock and a hard place.
Sandhya Vedullapalli, secretary of the Federation of Anna Nagar Residents’ Associations, said that for her, the tax was revised from ₹895 to ₹1,835 — a 100% increase. She alleged that in an apartment complex, only one flat had received the reassessment notice, raising questions about uniformity in the exercise.
For Vijaykumar, who owns a space in Mogappair, the rate went up from ₹6,500 for six months to over ₹31,000, nearly a five-fold increase. “I am yet to raise an objection. Such sudden increases could affect businesses, especially small ones,” he said.
‘Received information’
Meanwhile, Tiruvottiyur CPI(M) councillor R. Jayaraman said several residents in his ward had received information regarding the revision.
He said the GCC had taken the decision without passing a resolution in the Council. “There was no prior information. When there is an online gateway to register complaints about all issues, there ought to be one for this too. We will put forth our objection in the next Council meeting,” Mr. Jayaraman said.
Pointing out that the earlier property tax increases had contributed to public dissatisfaction with the previous regime, CPI(M)’s G. Selva said the new government should reconsider the decision.
Some residents of Thoraipakkam and Neelankarai had received information about the revision, A. Francis of Thoraipakkam Residents’ Welfare Association said.
Buffer zone
Kumararaja of Velachery said some residents of Tansi Nagar, Annai Indira Nagar, Vijay Nagar, Mahatma Gandhi Street, and Nehru Street had received reassessment notices.
He said the properties in these localities had been classified as having “zero value”, as they fell within the buffer zone of the Pallikaranai marshland. Since further development was not possible in the area, he questioned the basis for revising the property tax, and said the decision should be reconsidered.
A resident of Nanganallur said: “The GCC has increased the tax for the apartment owned by my bedridden mother. From the earlier half-yearly rate of ₹900, the tax has now been revised to ₹3,300. The property is held exclusively by my mother aged 80. As she has been bedridden since last year, her family pension is not adequate to meet the mounting medical expenses. Either the basic street rate should be reduced or it should be reduced on a par with core areas of Chennai. Nanganallur has higher rates than some core areas,” he said.
Arun, a resident of Adambakkam, welcomed the move, saying it corrected under-assessed properties rather than imposing a uniform hike. Though he agreed that a reassessment of under-valued properties would increase revenue for the GCC, he said there should have been greater transparency and awareness among the public.
Chairman of the Standing Committee on Taxation and Finance Sarbajaya Das told The Hindu that the decision had been taken by the Commissioner and the Deputy Commissioner (Revenue and Finance).
She said the reassessment had initially been intended for commercial buildings, followed by around 6,000 residential properties. The committee had not been informed that residential properties would also be reassessed under the new government, she said.
Stating that the Council had not been informed that objections could be raised, Ms. Das said they would demand a portal to address the issue and greater transparency at the next meeting of the Standing Committee on August 23 or 24.
She added that the GCC was facing a severe fund crunch, with no maintenance or ward development funds released and a liability of ₹2,000 crore.
GCC’s response
The GCC has issued notices to three lakh assessees for under-assessment of property tax. It expects to generate an additional revenue of ₹83 crore per annum from the revision of property tax on under-assessed properties.
Corporation Commissioner G.S. Sameeran, in a statement, said: “The change is only for properties that were under-assessed and those that were converted to commercial. It is based on GIS, satellite imagery, other government databases, and the owner’s self-declaration of area. The assessee can request remeasurement and reconsideration to RDCs. The same will be disposed of within a month,” he said.

headline: HAL partners Adani Defence, BEML to ramp up Prachand helicopter production
full_text:
HAL partners Adani Defence, BEML to ramp up Prachand helicopter production
HAL has signed agreements with Adani Defence and BEML to make fuselage structures for the Prachand Light Combat Helicopter. The move brings private industry into helicopter fuselage production for the first time and is meant to raise output.
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) has partnered with Adani Defence Systems and Technologies Limited and Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML) to manufacture fuselage structures for the indigenous Prachand Light Combat Helicopter (LCH), marking the first time private industry has been integrated into helicopter fuselage production in India.
The agreements are aimed at expanding India's domestic helicopter manufacturing capacity and strengthening the indigenous aerospace ecosystem.
Under the partnership, BEML will manufacture 48 fuselage structures, while Adani Defence Systems and Technologies Limited (ADSTL) will produce 42 fuselage structures for the Prachand programme.
The agreements were signed by Tushar Ranjan Behera, General Manager of HAL's Helicopter Division, with Commodore (Retd.) RGK Rao, Executive Director (Aerospace & Maritime) at BEML, and Prasanna Karthik, Vice President of Adani Defence Systems and Technologies Limited.
Senior officials from HAL, BEML and ADSTL were present during the signing ceremony.
SIGNIFICANT MILESTONE FOR AEROSPACE; HAL CHAIRMAN
HAL Chairman and Managing Director Ravi K described the collaboration as a significant milestone for India's aerospace sector, saying it marks the first time the private sector has been integrated into the production of helicopter fuselage structures.
He said the partnership would help expand manufacturing capacity, strengthen the domestic supply chain and further boost indigenous aerospace manufacturing capabilities.
The development comes as HAL ramps up production of the 156 Prachand Light Combat Helicopters ordered by the Indian Armed Forces.
Manufacturing has already commenced at HAL's new helicopter production facility in Tumakuru, Karnataka, which has been established to support the large-scale production of the combat helicopter.
According to HAL, the addition of two more production lines through the partnerships with BEML and Adani Defence is expected to significantly enhance overall manufacturing capacity and help ensure the timely delivery of the helicopters to the Army and the Indian Air Force.
The expanded production ecosystem is also expected to benefit a wider network of Indian micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), component manufacturers and aerospace suppliers by creating new business opportunities across the supply chain.
HAL said the initiative would contribute to developing specialised manufacturing capabilities within the country while reducing dependence on external suppliers.
The Prachand Light Combat Helicopter is India's indigenously developed attack helicopter designed for operations in diverse terrain, including high-altitude regions, and forms a key part of the country's push towards self-reliance in defence manufacturing.

headline: No widespread injuries: Kiren Rijiju rejects claim of excess force at Gen Z protest
full_text:
No widespread injuries: Kiren Rijiju rejects claim of excess force at Gen Z protest
Kiren Rijiju spoke to India Today TV a day after Parliament was adjourned sine die after a largely disrupted Monsoon Session, during which the government and Opposition remained locked in confrontation over several issues, including the police crackdown on students during the July 20 NEET paper leak agitation and the Ram Temple donations theft.
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju has rejected allegations of excessive force during the Gen Z student protest over the NEET paper leak in Delhi, saying there were no widespread injuries among protesters.
Rijiju spoke to India Today TV a day after Parliament's Monsoon Session was adjourned sine die on August 13, following a largely disrupted session in which the government and Opposition remained locked in confrontation over several issues.
The Opposition alleged that excessive force, including the use of pellet guns, was used against protesters and had sought an explanation from the government in Parliament.
“There were no widespread injuries,” Rijiju said, rejecting the charge of excessive force.
However, India Today had earlier reported exclusively that a 25-year-old protester suffered around 20 pellet wounds during the July 20 Parliament march. Medical records accessed by India Today showed pellet injuries on his back and elbow. India Today had also reported that another protester suffered a serious eye injury during the protest.
The reports came after allegations that pellet guns had been used to disperse protesters, with Delhi Police denying the use of pellet guns.
But when asked about reports of pellet gun use, Rijiju questioned how many people would have been injured if such weapons had been used during a protest involving thousands of people.
“Pellet guns have multiple pellets; they are not a single bullet. If only one person has been hit, then we will also have to see how that happened. In such a large protest, where thousands of people were present, if pellet guns had been used, how many people would have been injured?” he said.
Rijiju was also asked about petitions pending in the Supreme Court over the alleged use of pellet guns. He said the court would first examine the matter and that nothing could be said at this stage.
“There are petitions in the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court will first investigate. We cannot say anything about this at the moment,” he said.
Rijiju also referred to the use of pellet guns in Kashmir during previous Congress governments. “Pellet guns were used in Kashmir during the Congress period. Pellet guns were used at several places during the Congress regime,” he said.
When asked about reports of pellet injuries among protesters, Rijiju again referred to the size of the gathering and questioned how many people would have been injured if pellet guns had been used.
“As I said, if 4,000-5,000 people are sitting somewhere and protesting, and pellet guns are fired, how many people would get injured? At least 300-400 people?” he said during the interview.
Rijiju also defended the police response to the Parliament March, pointing to the size of the gathering.
“Thirty to 40 thousand people came together during the Parliament March protest. The police managed the protest well. If 30,000-40,000 people are marching towards Parliament, isn't it the police's duty to stop them? Won't the police have to use force to do so?” he said.
The Opposition had repeatedly demanded an explanation from the government over the police action during the July 20 protest and sought Home Minister Amit Shah's statement in Parliament.
The government, meanwhile, maintained that it was ready to discuss the issue. Rijiju had said Shah was prepared to give a detailed reply on the student protests, provided the Opposition allowed Parliament to function.
The issue remained part of the wider confrontation that marked the Monsoon Session, which ended on August 13 after repeated disruptions.
Rijiju's comments came after the session had concluded, with the government continuing to defend the police response to the protest and the Opposition maintaining its allegations of excessive force.
The minister said the government was ready to discuss the concerns raised by the Opposition and respond to them in Parliament.

headline: 80 years free, India’s biggest independence challenge is its bureaucracy with colonial mindset
full_text:
80 years free, India’s biggest independence challenge is its bureaucracy with colonial mindset
PM Narendra Modi today took to X to remind the citizens that only cowards leave their future to fate.
On the 75th Independence Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi introduced 'Paanch Prans' (five pledges), which included the clarion call for the removal of the colonial mindset that plagues Indian society. Tomorrow, we celebrate the 80th Independence Day, with the nation defying the doomsday sayers and moving forward towards the 2047 goal of a developed nation.
Remembering the horrors of 1947 Partition, where no less than two million Indians were slaughtered, PM Modi today took to X to remind the citizens that only cowards leave their future to fate, while asking the countrymen to contribute to the nation's growth through courage, enterprise, persistence and hard work.
While the Centre and the BJP ruled state governments have made efforts to remove traces of colonial servitude since the five pledges, symbols of most ruthless conquerors of India’s dark past are still celebrated in the name of diversity and inclusivity. Some of them still occupy free rent space as the foundation of public policy even today, particularly in education and the social sector.
Deep Dive
One of the biggest symbols of the colonial past is the Indian bureaucracy, which has been the slowest to reform itself and continues to increase the cost of doing business in India through lethargy and, more often than not, corrupt practices. If India wants to achieve the 2047 dream of a developed country, a total overhaul of Indian bureaucracy is required, as the corrupt must be thrown out and merit must be rewarded. Only PM Modi has the will and determination to do so, as his political base still rocks.
While there has been an effort to view India’s past with pink glasses, the chaos and mayhem of the past three centuries have been glossed over, with marauders from Iran and Afghanistan putting India to the sword and looting it to the bare bones. Ahmed Shah Abdali, after the sack of Delhi and Mathura during the 1757 campaign, took loot back to Kandahar in 28000 camels with not one lifting his finger from Attock to Agra. The British occupation was even more horrible as the country was economically, politically and culturally raped for nearly 200 years.
Today, a rising China, which also suffered a lot in foreign invasions and occupation, makes it a point to remind its adversaries of the past century, like imperial Japan and Korea, to apologise for the excesses committed and remind them that the horrors of the colonial past have not been forgotten. Forget the reparation of nearly USD 43 trillion which the British looted from India, have we even made the English apologise for the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre, 1943 Bengal famine and the Partition of India based on the two-nation theory? Millions of innocent lives were snuffed out in these catastrophic events, but India and its rulers continued to suffer from humongous historical amnesia. China only suffered a century of humiliation, but India suffered a millennium of dishonour, degradation and subjugation.
The Indian colonial mindset has been strengthened by the political and bureaucratic leadership who have been sending their children to study and settle abroad since Independence for better economic prospects. China today has put a bar on the career growth of any official whose children have studied in the West.
With rising India facing challenges and hurdles from both the democratic US and Communist China, the country needs decisive reforms, not endless debates and never-ending protests, for a better future. Hard decisions are required to make India an industrial-military power, as its main adversary is its northern neighbour with an ever-festering boundary dispute, triggered by the Chinese occupation of Tibet in 1950. After making Pakistan into a supplicant state, China has made very serious inroads into Bangladesh, Nepal, Myanmar and Sri Lanka in order to throttle India and curtail its global ambitions. The West is no different, as the Anglo-Saxon policy of supporting Pakistan and generating discontent within India has not changed. India’s dark and horrid past alone should ensure that impotent politics and colonial mindset are thrown out into the Bay of Bengal.

headline: Usha Uthup: ‘Strongly attached to idea of India even though much has changed’
full_text:
Usha Uthup: ‘Strongly attached to idea of India even though much has changed’
While music entered her life without warning, Uthup was thrown out of her class choir “because the teacher could not find a proper place for my voice”.
When asked to reflect on Ramba Ho, the 1981 hit finding a fresh lease of life through Dhurandhar, Usha Uthup simply says, “A song is bigger than a singer. You have to give it time to become a classic – the kids have made it so. The Gen-Z today is going retro even at Trincas.”
Trincas is the iconic heritage restaurant and tea room, and a much-sought out venue for live music in Kolkata, where Uthup performed in her early years, and continues to do so occasionally.
Also Read | ‘Beginning of another’: How Hindustan Times reported freedom on August 15, 1947
There is no triumphalism in her voice about the song she first struck to life decades ago being reinvented; instead, a quiet acceptance that only someone who spent many years under the sun can understand.
Likewise, when the 79-year-old artiste-performer – born in the year India got her Independence from colonial rule – looks back, there is little rose-tinted nostalgia, but a measured remembrance of a country that shaped her.
“I am strongly attached to the idea of India even though much has changed over a period of time,” she says. “I am the fifth of six children from a middle-class family bearing orthodox and patriotic values – everything was black and white. It was a privilege to have been brought up at a time like that.”
Also Read | Independence Day 2026: Is it 79th or 80th Independence Day? Theme, significance and history explained
Brought up in the police quarters in Byculla (her father was deputy commissioner of police in the crime branch), Mumbai, she grew up in a world without barriers, she says. “The value of money and equality was instilled in us strongly and we were taught human values. I grew up with Muslims as neighbours and Christians in school; and as a Hindu I felt close to Christ when I rang the Anglican bell.”
The house in Byculla was a sprawling two-level British-era bungalow that was converted into apartments for separate families to reside in. While they lived on the ground floor, the upper floor was taken by a Muslim neighbour, the Pathans. The girls of that house – Shameem and Jameela – were to become Uthup’s friends for life. From their mother she learnt how to do the namaaz and stitch salwar kameezes. “I am still a great seamstress,” she says.
While Hindu pujas were celebrated at home, she learnt to keep roza with Jameela and Shameem. A special serving of khichda without mutton would be set aside for her every Eid. They also taught her how to drape a dupatta over her head, “which is aesthetic”.
“I want to belong to the place I am in.”
“We grew up watching Jawaharlal Nehru and Mahatma Gandhi – we heard stories about them every time Congress leaders came to Bombay and my father was on bandobast duty,” she says. “I urge those who express critical views about Gandhi today to look at what he had achieved and ask themselves if they have been able to achieve even a fraction of that.”
Also Read | Freedom the same night, but different dates: Why Pakistan marks its Independence Day on August 14
Independence and a free-thinking way of life at the time was completely instinctual. “I never thought about it, and only felt it during the Chinese aggression, when we packed shoes and blankets for the jawans,” she says. “We were Indians first; I don’t know how people argue that today.”
“I wish that feeling of secularism had survived – we have lost that amazing value to arguments, fights and endless debates,” she says, with a throwback to the time when she was introduced to Dilip Kumar and Meena Kumari’s films on a projector, seated along with Jameela and Shameem at their home.
“I still call Jameela, who runs a boutique with her daughter Simran, in Bengaluru, when I want to check on an Urdu word or the other,” she says. “While we don’t have the time to think about the old days, it is also up to us to bring it back. We are happy and in-love people. In love with love.”
The family’s three-storeyed ancestral home in erstwhile Madras perfectly captured the breezy spirit of that era.
A born performer, “known to stand up on the table and sing”, her earliest memories of music is that of an uncle listening to Beethoven or Mozart on one floor, another playing the Kingston Trio on another floor, and her aunts listening to Kishori Amonkar or MS Subbalakshmi. “That was our post-Partition eclectic way of life.”
While music entered her life without warning, Uthup was thrown out of her class choir “because the teacher could not find a proper place for my voice”. “But I wasn’t unhappy about that. I started playing the tambourine.”
An untutored singer, she started performing at 21, not confined into boxes, which led her to sing in varied Indian languages. After singing at Nine Gems, a nightclub in Madras, she moved to Talk of the Town in Bombay and Trincas in Calcutta. Persuaded by an aunt, she stepped into the clubs at a time when they were dominated by Anglo-Indian performers. She turned heads equally with her powerful textured voice that held a deep bass resonance and by turning up in decorous silk sarees paired with traditional jewellery, an arresting bindi and flowers in her hair. She commanded the stage as she moved with the music turning rhythm into absolute power. “I was a change at the clubs -- I wore sarees because I had no other garment of choice. And as I moved from club to club, I drew in families because women did not look at me as a threat. I was no sex symbol,” she says.
She sang Frank Sinatra, Barbra Streisand, Tom Jones, and continues to draw from those legends. She has borrowed from contemporary artistes – Adele’s Skyfall has been on every performance playlist since the Bond film released in 2012. Over time, Uthup tweaked her style quotient as well: she started pairing her Kanjeevaram sarees with what she calls Kanjeevaram sneakers – Reebok sneakers lined with the border of a Kanjeevaram saree.
“I sang in English, Bengali, Punjabi. I had no hard luck. I took everything in my stride. I did it my way. I wasn’t anxious about late shifts at work – I worked like nurses and air hostesses.”
If Uthup had to encapsulate the time between the 1950s and now in five snapshots, what would they be? Security and safety for all, cleanliness and hygiene, education, less poverty and more human connection with time for family.

headline: Lok Sabha Secretariat seeks Rahul Gandhi’s response to privilege notices over Amit Shah remarks by August 28
full_text:
Lok Sabha Secretariat seeks Rahul Gandhi’s response to privilege notices over Amit Shah remarks by August 28
The notice by BJP's Thakur alleged alleged that Rahul Gandhi levelled "grave allegations" against Amit Shah without giving advance notice under Rule 353.
The Lok Sabha Secretariat has sought a response from Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi over two notices alleging breach of privilege and contempt of the House. This follows notices filed by BJP MPs over the Congress leader's remarks against Union home minister Amit Shah during a debate on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.
Rahul has been asked to submit his response by August 28.
Also Read | Kangana Ranaut slams Rahul Gandhi over remarks on Amit Shah: ‘He makes mockery of the country’
BJP's Sanjay Jaiswal shared a copy of the Lok Sabha secretariat's communication to Gandhi in a post on X (formerly Twitter).
Sharing the letter, Jaiswal said in the post, "I had submitted a notice regarding a breach of privilege concerning the objectionable remarks made by Rahul Gandhi against the Hon'ble Home Minister, Shri Amit Shah, as these comments violated the dignity of the Member of Parliament (Shah) and decorum of Parliament."
"I am grateful to the Hon'ble Speaker of the Lok Sabha for taking cognisance of my notice and referring the matter to the Privileges Committee. The committee has granted Rahul Gandhi an opportunity to submit his explanation by August 28," he added.
"I am fully confident that the Committee will take appropriate action in this matter to ensure that no Member of Parliament attempts to undermine the dignity and decorum of the House in the future," Jaiswal emphasised in the post.
Also Read | Relief for Rahul Gandhi, SC quashes criminal defamation complaint in Savarkar remarks row
What the letter said
In a letter dated August 14, Joint Secretary H Ram Prakash noted that the notices were submitted by BJP MPs Anurag Singh Thakur and Sanjay Jaiswal.
The notice by Thakur, dated July 30, 2026, alleged that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi used "unparliamentary and derogatory language" and levelled "grave allegations" against the home minister without giving advance notice under Rule 353 during the debate.
Furthermore, in a letter by Jaiswal, dated July 29, 2026, the MP requested that cognisance should be taken of the "alleged use of unparliamentary expressions" by Rahul Gandhi against Amit Shah.
"I am directed to forward herewith a copy each of the notices, dated 29 July, 2026 and 30 July, 2026 of question of breach of privilege given by Dr Sanjay Jaiswal, MP and Anurag Singh Thakur, MP respectively against your goodself on the above subject," the letter by the joint secretary of the privileges committee of the Lok Sabha said.
"I am, therefore, to request you kindly to furnish your reply/comments in the matter by 28 August, 2026 for the kind consideration of the Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha," it added.

Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026
The Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, passed by both houses of Parliament after an elaborate debate, has now become a law.
This came after Delhi, for weeks, witnessed protests led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) over alleged examination irregularities, including the NEET paper leak. The protesters also demanded the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, who resigned from the post on July 25.

headline: Telecasting Gurbani for genuine religious purpose not copyright infringement: Delhi HC
full_text:
Telecasting Gurbani for genuine religious purpose not copyright infringement: Delhi HC
The court was dealing with copyright infringement suit filed by Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee to restrain channel GTC, from broadcasting/rebroadcasting Gurbani from Golden Temple
Live broadcasting of Gurbani from the Guru Granth Sahib Ji at the Golden Temple for a genuine religious purpose may not amount to copyright infringement when there is no commercial exploitation, the Delhi high court said on Friday as it refused to immediately restrain a private channel from live telecasting the Gurbani.
“It’s a literary cum musical work. You are reciting the Gurbani by way of musical performance. There is a literary work called Guru Granth Sahib which you sing by way of musical work. Therefore, you are a literary and a musical work which, if used for bona fide religious ceremony, is not an infringement,” a bench of justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani remarked.
“On prima facie appreciation of the matter, this court is not inclined to pass any ad interim order at this stage,” the court said in the order.
The court made this remark while dealing with a copyright infringement suit filed by Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee to restrain a private channel Galactic Television and Communications (GTC), from broadcasting/rebroadcasting Gurbani from the Golden Temple.
Also Read: Takht backs SGPC stand on ‘ unauthorised ‘ Gurbani broadcast
In the suit, senior advocate Chander M Lall, appearing for the SGPC, argued that the channel was infringing the SGPC’s broadcast reproduction rights under Section 37 of the Copyright Act by retransmitting Gurbani, which is exclusively broadcast on YouTube by it.
Section 37 specifically protects the special rights of broadcasting organisations. He further submitted that as of date, SGPC has not licensed the broadcasting rights to any party whether on charge or otherwise.
GTC represented by senior advocate PS Patwalia submitted that the channel was not charging any money from the public for viewing the telecast.
The court however, issued summons in the suit and fixed September 24 as the next date of hearing.

Class 8 girl killed as DTC bus runs over scooter in Delhi's New Ashok Nagar
The girl’s body was taken to Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital in Kalyanpuri for medico-legal proceedings.
A girl studying in class 8 died on Friday after being run over by a DTC bus in East Delhi's New Ashok Nagar area.
According to the police officials cited in a report by news agency PTI, the victim was riding a scooter with her uncle to her school when a bus hit them at around 8am on Friday morning.
The officials cited above informed that the girl’s body was taken to Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital in Kalyanpuri for medico-legal proceedings.

70-year-old woman killed as ‘drunk’ son of Haryana cop crashes Mercedes in Delhi
A 70-year-old woman was killed, and a family of three, including an eight-year-old girl, were injured when an allegedly drunk 27-year-old man, the son of a police officer, crashed a speeding Mercedes sedan into a hatchback near Narela in northwest Delhi last Saturday.
Officers at the scene confirmed that beer and empty liquor bottles were recovered from the Mercedes. Police said the driver was returning from a party. According to police, the silver Mercedes E-Class was travelling at such high speed that when it struck the grey Maruti WagonR, in which a couple in their 40s was travelling with their daughter, the hatchback was flung away, crushing a woman pedestrian against a parked three-wheeler.
Police identified the Mercedes driver as Shubham Sharma, a Narela resident and son of a Haryana Police sub-inspector. Sharma was arrested and booked for rash and negligent driving, causing death and injuries. An FIR was registered under Sections 281 and 106 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) at Narela police station.
The couple in the WagonR – Narender and Geeta, both in their 40s – and their eight-year-old daughter sustained minor injuries and were admitted to a hospital. Geeta and her daughter were discharged after preliminary medical attention, while Narender underwent a CT scan to check for internal injuries.
According to at least two police officers, Sharma had “recently purchased” the Mercedes from a friend but had not completed the ownership transfer paperwork. Police identified the woman killed in the crash as Urmila Devi. Her husband, who died in 2019, was an administrative official from the Delhi Transport Department. She is survived by two sons. Urmila’s family and passersby alleged that Sharma was “inebriated” and driving recklessly when the crash occurred around 8am.
