Husband called wife 'barren', she called him 'impotent': HC quashes cruelty case
The Allahabad High Court quashed proceedings against a husband accused of cruelty after he allegedly called his wife a barren woman during a marital dispute. The court said the exchange had to be read in the context of mutual verbal abuse and unsupported allegations.
Calling a wife a “barren woman” during a marital dispute does not automatically amount to cruelty under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), the Allahabad High Court has ruled, while quashing criminal proceedings against a husband.
According to a report by Bar & Bench, Justice Indrajeet Shukla was hearing a petition filed by the husband challenging a Lucknow court order that had summoned him in a complaint alleging cruelty, dowry demand and intentional insult.
The case arose from a troubled marriage in which the couple had been unable to have a child. During the dispute, the husband and his relatives allegedly called the woman a “barren woman”, while she, in turn, called her husband “impotent”.
COURT SAYS CONTEXT MATTERS
The High Court noted that the alleged remarks had to be viewed in the context of the matrimonial discord and the exchange of offensive language between both sides.
The court observed that the husband’s alleged reference to his wife as a “barren woman”, though “insensitive and reprehensible”, could not by itself constitute cruelty under Section 498-A IPC in the circumstances of the case.
“Mere taunts regarding childlessness, refusal to undergo medical examination, or verbal altercations arising from such domestic discord cumulatively without fulfilling essentials of cruelty envisaged under Section 498-A IPC, cannot by themselves constitute the offence of cruelty,” the court said.
The Bench also noted that there was no allegation suggesting that the remark was made with the intention of driving the woman to suicide or causing grave injury or endangering her life, limb or physical or mental health.
NO DOWRY DEMAND, MEDICAL EVIDENCE
The court also found that the complaint did not contain even a single specific allegation of a dowry demand. The allegations against the husband were described as general and omnibus in nature. The court further noted that the allegation of physical assault was not supported by medical evidence.
The Bench also considered whether the alleged use of the term “barren woman” amounted to intentional insult under Section 504 IPC. It held that, in the circumstances of the case, the allegation did not satisfy the legal requirements of the provision, which requires an intention or knowledge that the insult could provoke a breach of peace.
‘498-A NOT MEANT TO CRIMINALISE EVERY MARITAL DISAGREEMENT’
The High Court said the allegations essentially reflected an unhappy marriage and incompatibility between the couple.
It stressed that Section 498-A was not intended to criminalise every disagreement between spouses or every instance of unpleasantness in a marriage. “Criminal prosecution is not a panacea for all evils arising out of matrimonial discords,” the court underscored.
The Bench concluded that the issue of childlessness had become the source of frustration in the marriage, resulting in allegations, counter-allegations and verbal abuse from both sides.
It found the prosecution story, if read in its entirety and left uncontroverted, to be “highly improbable” and quashed the criminal proceedings against the husband.
The ruling, however, does not mean that using derogatory language against a spouse can never amount to cruelty. The court's finding was based on the specific facts and circumstances of this case, including the reciprocal nature of the verbal exchanges and the absence of material supporting the other allegations.

headline: These Americans take me for a fool: Inside Indira Gandhi's troubled ties with US
full_text:
These Americans take me for a fool: Inside Indira Gandhi's troubled ties with US
Rahul Gandhi shared an anecdote from Indira Gandhi's 1982 US visit while he attacked PM Modi's foreign policy. While it was intended to take a dig at PM Modi, the episode underlined the turbulent India-US tensions under Indira Gandhi.
Former US President Ronald Reagan, Nancy Reagan, with Indira Gandhi at the White House
While taking a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "hug diplomacy" with foreign leaders, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi shared an intriguing anecdote from Indira Gandhi's 1982 state visit to the US. The anecdote by Rahul was intended to give a glimpse into how Indira viewed diplomacy. However, his recollection seems to have inadvertently brought to the fore the turbulent India-US ties during Indira's era.
Rahul said he was about 12 then, and accompanied his grandmother to the US. During the visit, Rahul recounted an instance when a furious Indira returned from a state dinner that was hosted by then US President Ronald Reagan and his wife Nancy. "These Americans take me for a complete fool," Rahul recalled Indira telling his mother, Sonia Gandhi.
The reason? Indira believed that the US First Lady had deliberately worn a dress that was the same colour as her saree.
"You aren't just visiting a friend's house. In this role, the Prime Minister of India doesn't engage in mere friendship. They have no interest in friendship; their job is to protect the country," Rahul emphasised.
Now, whether Nancy's dress was the same colour as Indira's saree is a different story for another day.
THE TURBULENT INDIA-US TIES UNDER INDIRA GANDHI
While Rahul's anecdote was intended to take a dig at PM Modi, the episode underlined the India-US tensions under the Indira era. It would be, however, wrong to say that India-US ties were uniformly hostile. Stay with us till the end, and we will explain why.
When Indira first became the prime minister in 1966, India was grappling with a severe food crisis. The economy was under strain. Just two months after taking over, Indira made her first visit to the US as prime minister.
The then US President Lyndon B Johnson offered India wheat shipments under its PL-480 program. However, in exchange, Washington wanted Delhi to align more closely with US strategic priorities. The Cold War with the Soviet Union was at its peak. The demand by the US was a tough call for India, which has always adhered to a strict Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) policy.
For Indira, the whole experience was deeply humiliating. "I don't ever want us to have to beg for food again," Indira reportedly told her press adviser.
India's open criticism of the US during the Vietnam War further sowed the seeds of friction.
It was under Richard Nixon that the India-US relationship entered into a more turbulent phase. Nixon viewed Pakistan as strategically important, particularly due to its overt support for the US during the Cold War. Crucially, Pakistan also became a secret back channel for the Nixon administration to open relations with China.
INDIRA AND THE NIXON-KISSINGER ERA
At the centre of the Nixon administration's South Asia policy was Kissinger, who greatly influenced global affairs at that time.
Pakistan's role played a large part in the US standing by it even as Islamabad carried out a brutal crackdown in East Pakistan in 1971. It sent thousands of refugees streaming into India and eventually triggered the Bangladesh Liberation War.
Indira spent much time trying to persuade Nixon to act against Pakistan by pointing to what was unfolding on India's eastern border. When Kissinger met her in New Delhi on July 7, 1971, Indira reportedly told him that she wanted to give diplomacy a chance, and did not want to use force. However, the US turned a blind eye.
The Nixon administration suspected that India was preparing for military intervention. A leaked tape from a May 1971 conversation saw Nixon complaining that the "goddamn Indians" were promoting another conflict.
In between, India signed a treaty with the Soviet Union for strategic cooperation in August 1971. It angered the US further, even though India assured the US that it was not directed against Washington.
Indira travelled to Washington that year in November for a last-ditch effort. It turned out to be unproductive.
However, taped conversations between Nixon and Kissinger, after Indira left, reflected the deep hostility of the US towards India. The conversations were declassified by the US in 2005.
Nixon and Kissinger are heard engaged in a heated conversation about Indira. While Nixon refers to Indira as an "old witch", Kissinger is heard calling her a "b**ch". "The Indians are b***ards anyway. They are starting a war there," Kissinger further says.
In 2005, Kissinger expressed his regret over the foul language. Indira, however, died in October 1984 when she was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards.
The war eventually broke out in December. As Indian forces closed in on Dhaka, Nixon ordered the deployment of the USS Enterprise carrier group in the Bay of Bengal. While the US framed it as a move to evacuate American citizens, it was viewed as a show of force to unsettle India.
It failed to deter India. Pakistan's forces eventually surrendered on December 16, 1971. While India emerged victorious, it left a deep scar on Delhi-Washington ties. The relationship deteriorated further after India's first nuclear test in May 1974.
The bitterness of the Nixon-Kissinger years cast a long shadow on India-US ties. However, things started to improve gradually in the first half of the 1980s. The 1982 Reagan state dinner that featured in Rahul Gandhi's anecdote was itself billed as an attempt to repair India-US ties.
Indira herself told reporters upon her arrival in Washington that she had come precisely to better the ties. However, it would take until the late 1990s and the early 2000s - well after Indira's murder in 1984 - for India and the US to decisively move beyond the mistrust of the troubling Nixon-Kissinger era. It was China's rise that eventually shaped the strategic partnership that exists today.

headline: Lucknow: There was a time when former comrades and alumni of Delhi’s Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) ruled the roost in the Uttar Pradesh Congress. Many of them were associated with the All India Students Association (AISA), the students’ wing of t...
full_text:
Lucknow: There was a time when former comrades and alumni of Delhi’s Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) ruled the roost in the Uttar Pradesh Congress. Many of them were associated with the All India Students Association (AISA), the students’ wing of the CPI(M-L) Liberation, which traces its roots to the Naxalbari uprising.
They made the leap of faith and ideology to enter what the Left considered a party of the bourgeoisie: the Congress. They soon came to be seen as Rahul Gandhi’s team in the Congress before he attached them with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra to help her in her Mission UP ahead of the 2019 Lok Sabha election.
They have been left out in the cold now as Rahul Gandhi has revamped the Congress in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the assembly election early next year.
At a meeting of Uttar Pradesh Congress functionaries at the party headquarters in Delhi on Monday, AICC general secretary in charge of organisation K.C. Venugopal said the state Congress was divided by factionalism and needed to free itself from it now. Rahul and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge were on the stage.
What caught the attention of party leaders was the absence of Priyanka. She had always attended meetings related to the Uttar Pradesh Congress in the past seven years. None of her core team members were present either.
Several party leaders ThePrint spoke to saw this as a clear indication that the Congress is preparing to place the responsibility for its 2027 Uttar Pradesh campaign largely in the hands of Rahul Gandhi’s team, rather than in the hands of the team that had effectively run the state organisation under Priyanka since 2019.
The appointment of Rajendra Pal Gautam as the new UP in-charge has strengthened that perception. Gautam, who joined the Congress after leaving the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in 2024, is considered close to Rahul’s close aide Alankar Sawai.
The six new co-in-charges of different zones are also seen within the party as Venugopal’s choices: former Uttarakhand MLA Sanjeev Arya, former Madhya Pradesh MLA Kunal Choudhary, Delhi Congress leader Abdul Hannan, former NSUI national president Varun Choudhary, Rajasthan leader and former MLA Jagdish Chandra Jangid, and Delhi Congress leader Abhishek Dutt.
Seven years of Priyanka’s team
Priyanka’s sway over the Uttar Pradesh Congress organisation dates back to 2019, when she was appointed the party’s general secretary in charge of eastern UP.
Despite the Congress’s weak electoral performance, winning just one Lok Sabha seat in 2019 and two Assembly seats in the 2022 elections, Priyanka’s core team continued to exercise considerable influence over the party’s state organisation and political decision-making.
Sandeep Singh, Priyanka Gandhi’s personal secretary and a former JNU Students’ Union president, was regarded as a key link between her and the state organisation. His close associates Dheeraj Gurjar, Pradeep Narwal and Tauqeer Alam were appointed as AICC secretaries and became closely involved in UP affairs.
Rajesh Tiwari, a leader considered close to former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel, also served as an AICC secretary in the state.
Another member, former JNU Students’ Union president Mohit Pandey, was associated with Priyanka’s social media operations, while Anil Yadav was given a key role in state organisation.
Together, these leaders formed what party insiders described as Priyanka Gandhi’s core UP team.
Even when Avinash Pande replaced Priyanka as the state in-charge before the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, much of the organisational network remained intact. According to party insiders, the team continued to exercise considerable influence over appointments and electoral decisions.
The equation began changing after Sandeep Singh was sidelined last year. He was considered an important channel of communication between Priyanka and the state organisation.
However, even after his exit from the active organisational setup, several AICC secretaries and other members of the old core team influenced decisions related to Uttar Pradesh.
Party insiders say former state president Ajay Rai and former in-charge Avinash Pande also had limited freedom in making key organisational appointments. That arrangement now appears to have changed ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.
A senior UP Congress leader said Priyanka Gandhi’s team had effectively come to dominate the state unit. “The UP Congress had become synonymous with Team Priyanka,” the leader said, claiming that the group influenced appointments of district presidents and even several ticket decisions.
According to the leader, recommendations from this team played a significant role in ticket distribution during the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, the 2022 Uttar Pradesh polls and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.
The leader also claimed that the same group influenced several state-level appointments.
Some senior leaders, including Jitin Prasada, R.P.N. Singh and Lalitesh Pati Tripathi, had reportedly felt sidelined because of differences with Team Priyanka and eventually left the Congress.
“After seven years, the UP Congress has finally got freedom from this team,’” the leader said.
However, another senior leader has a different view. The leader acknowledged that the Priyanka Gandhi-led team failed to deliver the electoral revival the party had hoped for and that several leaders blamed the group for getting sidelined, but he argued it would be unfair to view its tenure only through the lens of failure.
“Several young leaders were given Congress tickets in the 2022 Assembly elections who otherwise may never have imagined contesting on a Congress ticket,” the leader said.
The team also helped the party build organisational structures across all 75 districts, something the Congress had struggled to achieve consistently over the previous two decades.
“Therefore, it is not correct to say that this team only harmed the Congress in Uttar Pradesh,” the leader said.
At the same time, the leader questioned whether the new leadership structure would be able to deliver similar organisational depth.
According to the leader, there does not yet appear to be strong coordination between the newly appointed in-charge and the state president. The new team would also need time to understand the political and caste equations across all 403 Assembly constituencies.
“Priyanka’s team was stronger when it came to research and ground-level information,” the leader said.
Where are core team members now?
The members who were identified with Priyanka Gandhi’s core UP team currently do not have clearly defined organisational assignments in the state.
AICC secretaries Dheeraj Gurjar, Pradeep Narwal and Tauqeer Alam have not been given a specific UP responsibility for now and are planning to increase activities in local politics in their respective home states.
Sandeep Singh continues to be an AICC member from Pratapgarh district of Uttar Pradesh, but does not currently hold a formal organisational assignment in the state. Mohit Pandey has also not been given a major organisational role and is no longer part of Priyanka Gandhi’s social media team.
Another key member Dinesh Singh, whom Sandeep Singh considers his mentor from his Allahabad University days, had been serving as the party’s in-charge of administration (Prashasan Prabhari) since 2020.
However, he was removed from the responsibility last year. Singh remains associated with the UP Congress but currently does not hold any organisational post.
Similarly, Shahnawaz Alam, another Allahabad University alumnus, is currently an AICC secretary in charge of Bihar but holds no organisational position in Uttar Pradesh. He was also considered a core member of Priyanka’s team during her tenure as Congress general secretary in charge of the state. He is now eyeing a seat to contest the polls in UP.
Anil Yadav, meanwhile, remains active in Uttar Pradesh and is preparing for the elections. He is also involved in research work for Priyanka and was recently given responsibility for Prayagraj during the party’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme, but it was given by the AICC.
(Edited by Sugita Katyal)

headline: Karnataka BJP MLA’s daughter booked for slapping woman police sub-inspector after spat over skipping temple queue
full_text:
Karnataka BJP MLA’s daughter booked for slapping woman police sub-inspector after spat over skipping temple queue
The FIR was registered at the Kyathanahalli police station on a complaint by PSI Savitha, who was deployed at the temple during the Bhima Amavasya rush.
A case was registered against Aishwarya, daughter of Tumakuru Rural MLA B Suresh Gowda, after she allegedly abused and slapped a woman police sub-inspector (PSI) during crowd control at the Arathi Ukkada temple in Srirangapatna taluk of Karnataka’s Mandya district on Wednesday, police said.
The FIR was registered at the Kyathanahalli police station on a complaint by PSI Savitha, who was deployed at the temple during the Bhima Amavasya rush.
Police booked Aishwarya under Sections 132, 115(2), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Srirangapatna circle inspector B G Kumar said. The provisions relate to deterring a public servant from discharging official duty, voluntarily causing hurt, intentional insult intended to provoke a breach of peace and criminal intimidation.
Also Read: FIR registered against BJP MP Anant Maharaj over alleged Netaji remarks: Police
What happened?
According to Savitha’s complaint, thousands of devotees were at the temple and Aishwarya sought to enter the sanctum sanctorum. The PSI asked her to wait because allowing her to move ahead of devotees in the queue could trigger protests.
Aishwarya reportedly questioned Savitha about why circle inspector Lakshmi, who was wearing civilian clothes, was permitted to go towards the sanctum. Savitha told her that Lakshmi was the circle inspector and was at the temple on duty, according to the complaint.
The exchange turned into an argument, with Aishwarya allegedly using offensive language against Savitha before slapping her in front of the crowd.
Also Read: Vigilance summons Dharamshala MLA in disproportionate assets case
Gowda's statement
Suresh Gowda later apologised publicly for his daughter’s conduct, adding that he did not have complete information about the incident.
“My daughter had gone to the temple with two small children. While she was standing in the VIP queue, the sub inspector on duty allegedly did not allow her to proceed but allowed others to enter. There will naturally be a reaction to an action. One thing led to another and the unfortunate incident occurred,” he said.
“If my daughter is at fault, I am ready to apologise publicly. She may have lost her temper at that moment, but those of us in public life should not behave in this manner. Therefore, I publicly apologise for my daughter’s conduct,” he added.

headline: Karnataka BJP MLA's daughter booked for 'assaulting' woman cop over temple entry queue
full_text:
Karnataka BJP MLA's daughter booked for 'assaulting' woman cop over temple entry queue
TOI News Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Aug 14, 2026, 18:02 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small

Police registered an FIR after a woman sub-inspector alleged that the BJP MLA's daughter tried to bypass the queue and assaulted her. (Photo: Instagram)
NEW DELHI: The daughter of Karnataka BJP MLA B Suresh Gowda was booked for allegedly abusing and assaulting a woman police sub-inspector following an argument at a temple in Mandya district in Karnataka, police said on Friday.The incident took place on August 12 at the Maramma Temple in Ukkada village during Bhima Amavasya celebrations, news agency PTI reported.According to the complaint filed by the woman police officer, she was deployed at the temple for security duty when Aishwarya, the MLA's daughter, allegedly sought permission to enter the sanctum without waiting in the queue.The police officer alleged that she asked Aishwarya to wait to avoid inconvenience to other devotees. According to the complaint, Aishwarya then identified herself as the daughter of an MLA and questioned why she was being stopped.The argument allegedly escalated, with Aishwarya abusing the officer and hitting her on the head. The complainant also alleged that she was threatened and prevented from performing her official duties.Based on the complaint, the Kyathanahalli police registered an FIR under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including charges related to assaulting a public servant, causing simple hurt, intentional insult and criminal intimidation, a senior police officer said.
However, the case has taken another turn, with Aishwarya filing a counter-complaint against the police officer.Police said an inquiry into her allegations has been initiated, but no FIR has been registered on the basis of her complaint so far. Further action will depend on the findings of the inquiry.Speaking to reporters, Tumakuru Rural MLA B Suresh Gowda apologised for his daughter's conduct and said that anyone found guilty should face legal consequences."If she has committed a mistake, it is wrong. Whoever has done the mistake should face the consequences under the law," he said.The BJP legislator said his daughter had visited the temple with her two young children and had requested permission to enter briefly because waiting in the queue could have caused inconvenience.
He also claimed that another person had been allowed to enter ahead of her, prompting his daughter to question the decision.While acknowledging that the argument had escalated, Gowda said his daughter should have shown greater restraint, particularly because she comes from a political family."I apologise on behalf of my daughter if she has made a mistake," he said.The MLA also called for a departmental inquiry into the incident and urged authorities to take action against anyone found responsible.

headline: Class 5 boy saves mid-day meal worker's finger in Dakshin Kannada school, CM Shivakumar lauds presence of mind
full_text:
Class 5 boy saves mid-day meal worker's finger in Dakshin Kannada school, CM Shivakumar lauds presence of mind
Class 5 student’s quick thinking averts major accident at Dakshina Kannada school
A Class 5 student's presence of mind averted a potentially serious accident at a Government Higher Primary School in Dakshina Kannada district after a mid-day meal worker's finger got caught in an electric grating machine, officials said on Thursday.
The incident occurred on Wednesday at Narikombu when the Akshara Dasoha (mid-day meal) worker was operating the machine, and her finger got caught in it, they said.
She cried out for help, prompting students and others nearby to rush to her aid, officials said.
ALSO READ: Karnataka seeks nationwide tattoo rules over concerns about ink chemicals and infections
According to education department officials, class 5 student Manvith, who was playing on the school premises, immediately responded to the cries for help.
Realising the danger, he rushed to the machine and switched off the power supply, preventing the worker from suffering further injury.
School Development and Monitoring Committee president Ravi Anchan and its members praised Manvith for his quick thinking.
Akshara Dasoha Assistant Director Nonayya Naik, and Cluster Resource Person Jyothi also visited the school and commended him.
ALSO READ: Karnataka bans sale of gutkha, pan masala containing tobacco or nicotine for 1 year
Taking to social media platform X, Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar commended the boy for his presence of mind and courage, describing his act as "truly heartwarming".
He congratulated Manvith for saving the kitchen staff member from danger, saying that when the Akshara Dasoha staff member cried out in pain, the boy immediately realised the seriousness of the situation and switched off the power supply, thereby averting a major accident.
"Manvith's alertness and right decision at a crucial moment saved the staff member's finger. His compassion, courage and presence of mind should serve as an example to everyone," he said.
Shivakumar wished the boy a bright future and hoped that he would grow up to be a responsible citizen who always responds to the needs of society and brings pride to the state.

headline: India secures return of fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya from UAE, Amit Shah hails ‘new milestone’
full_text:
India secures return of fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya from UAE, Amit Shah hails ‘new milestone’
Union home minister Amit Shah announced the return of the fugitive drug kingpin on Friday as he hailed the ‘milestone’ of ‘zero-tolerance against narcotics’.
The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has secured the return of fugitive drug kingpin Virender Singh Basoya from the United Arab Emirates, Union home minister Amit Shah announced on Friday as he hailed the ‘milestone’ of ‘zero-tolerance against narcotics’.
In a statement posted on X, Shah wrote, “Modi govt is relentlessly tracking down drug traffickers hiding abroad and destroying their entire ecosystem with a ruthless approach."
He called the development a "new milestone" in the government's “zero-tolerance policy towards narcotics”.
"By tracing the criminal through a top-to-bottom and bottom-to-top approach, our agencies have once again proven that no matter where drug traffickers hide, they cannot escape the long arm of Indian law," he said.
Basoya has been accused of masterminding an international drug syndicate.
Shah on 3-year plan to end drug trade
In June this year, Shah unveiled the government’s Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029) and the Narcotics Control Bureau Annual Report-2025. The documents were released alongside a three-year national plan aimed at dismantling drug trafficking networks.
He said the Centre would act against the entire narcotics ecosystem with such force that “it will not be able to recover for decades.”
More than 40 ministries and departments are part of the plan, which seeks to tackle the narcotics ecosystem through joint efforts in enforcement, intelligence, prevention and rehabilitation, HT reported earlier.
Shah also said the Centre was examining gaps in the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. It is also reviewing the classification of precursor chemicals and psychotropic substances that are used in drug production.
‘Operation Global-Hunt’
Earlier in April this year, the NCB secured the deportation of alleged global drug kingpin Mohammad Salim Dola, 59, from Turkey under 'Operation Global-Hunt'.
Dola, who had links with the Dawood Ibrahim syndicate, was detained by Turkish agencies in Beylikduzu and deported to India on April 28, 2026. The NCB took him into custody after he arrived at Delhi's IGI airport.

full_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam from August 14-17, while strong surface winds reaching 40 to 50 kmph are likely at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema through August 18.
The district-level warning shows thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and winds reaching 40 to 50 kmph in several districts of North Coastal Andhra Pradesh and South Coastal Andhra Pradesh during the first four days. In Rayalaseema, strong surface winds are forecast at isolated places, with speeds varying between 30 and 50 kmph depending on the district and day.
In North Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Vizianagaram, and Alluri Sitharamaraju districts are under the thunderstorm and lightning warning through August 17. Visakhapatnam has the same warning through August 16, followed by a 30-40 kmph wind warning on August 17. Anakapalli has a thunderstorm warning through August 16. Kakinada, East Godavari, Yanam and Dr B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema have 30-40 kmph wind warnings through the five-day period.
In South Coastal Andhra Pradesh, thunderstorms are forecast in NTR, Krishna and Palnadu districts through August 17. Bapatla and SPSR Nellore are also covered by thunderstorm warnings on some of the first few days, while other districts have varying wind warnings.
The seven-day forecast indicates isolated light to moderate rain or thundershowers in several districts, with light rain forecast in parts of the State on subsequent days. Visakhapatnam is likely to receive light to moderate rain or thundershowers through August 16, followed by light rain on August 17 and 18.
Day temperatures remained above normal on Friday. Visakhapatnam recorded 34.5°C, 3°C above normal, while Kalingapatnam recorded 36.1°C, 4.1°C above normal. Jangamaheswarapuram recorded the highest maximum among the stations monitored at 38.8°C.

headline: AVNG Developers LLP on Friday signed a Hotel Management Agreement with hospitality company Atmosphere Core to build and operate a five-star luxury eco-resort, Atmosphere Hillora Eco Resort Visakhapatnam, in the Eastern Ghats overlooking the city.
full_text:
AVNG Developers LLP on Friday signed a Hotel Management Agreement with hospitality company Atmosphere Core to build and operate a five-star luxury eco-resort, Atmosphere Hillora Eco Resort Visakhapatnam, in the Eastern Ghats overlooking the city.
Minister for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and NRI Empowerment, Kondapalli Srinivas, described the ₹180-crore investment by a home-grown developer as “definitely a proud moment for us”.
He said bringing a brand such as Atmosphere to Visakhapatnam was “not an easy thing” and credited the State’s tourism policy with attracting the investment. He added that the resort would become a venue for high-end weddings and corporate events.

headline: Even as a row broke out over the Chief Secretary’s directive to government departments to ensure the recital of Vande Mataram in its entirety during the Independence Day celebrations, a circular from Director of General Education (DGE) Snehil Kumar S...

Even as a row broke out over the Chief Secretary’s directive to government departments to ensure the recital of Vande Mataram in its entirety during the Independence Day celebrations, a circular from Director of General Education (DGE) Snehil Kumar Singh makes no mention of the rendition of the national song.
The circular dated August 11 to all school head teachers, besides General Education department officials such as deputy directors of education (DDEs) and district education officers (DEOs), directs all school head teachers to hoist the national flag and recite the national anthem as part of the 79th Independence Day celebrations.
It directs them to celebrate the occasion in an appropriate and dignified manner. Everyone should stand up as a mark of respect during the national anthem. They should ensure that the provisions of the Flag Code of India, 2002, are strictly followed during the flag hoisting. Rendition of patriotic songs and other programmes should be organised, according to the circular that was issued in the wake of another circular from the General Administration (Protocol) department on August 4. The GAD circular too does not make any mention of Vande Mataram recital as part of Independence Day celebrations.
The DGE’s circular underscores that the manufacture, distribution, sale, and use of national flags manufactured using plastics is banned, and that green protocol should be observed for all programmes.
The Chief Minister had a day ago said the Chief Secretary’s directions were related to the Union government’s Har Ghar Tiranga campaign.
The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, had become a law, but the Congress-led UDF government in the State had a clear stand on this, he said.
He had added that the State government’s stand would be clear to everyone on Independence Day.

headline: Kerala schools told to sing national anthem, not Vande Mataram on Independence Day
full_text:
Kerala schools told to sing national anthem, not Vande Mataram on Independence Day
Kerala's Education Department has told schools to hoist the flag and sing the national anthem on Independence Day. The omission of Vande Mataram has intensified a political row over the Centre's guidance.
Amid a controversy in Kerala over the singing of the full version of Vande Mataram, the state General Education Department has issued a directive for Independence Day celebrations asking schools to hoist the national flag and sing the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana. The directive does not ask schools to sing Vande Mataram, the national song.
The guidelines, issued by the Director of Public Education for schools and other educational institutions, say the head of the institution should hoist the national flag at 9 am or later and conduct the national anthem. The instructions were issued on the basis of a circular from the Protocol Officer.
The absence of any direction on Vande Mataram comes amid a row over an earlier communication from the Chief Secretary to the Local Self Government Department, forwarding the Centre's instructions on the national song. The opposition CPI(M) sharply criticised the Congress-led government over the issue and accused it of trying to implement the RSS agenda.
V D Satheesan said on Thursday that the Chief Secretary had not issued any circular and had only forwarded the instructions received from the Centre. "The letter does not contain the policy or stand of the state government," he said, adding that the state government would decide the Independence Day programmes in Kerala and had a clear policy on the matter. "There are just a few days for August 15. You will see then," he said, while noting that the Congress and the UDF had a clear policy on the singing of Vande Mataram.
Earlier on Friday, the BJP said the state government had a moral obligation to implement the law in the country concerning the rendition of Vande Mataram. The party also alleged that the Congress-led government was being controlled by the Indian Union Muslim League, a key UDF ally, and was therefore unable to take a firm stand on the issue.
In a July 9 communication, the Centre directed that the official version of the national song be played along with mass singing during the unfurling of the national flag and at cultural or ceremonial functions other than parades. It said singing the national song on such occasions, with or without instrumental accompaniment, along with mass singing, was desirable. The letter also said that in all schools, the day's work may begin with community singing of the national song and that school authorities should make adequate provisions in their programmes to popularise the singing of the national song and the national anthem, and promote respect for the national flag among students.
With Independence Day approaching, the state's school directive has limited the programme to flag hoisting and the national anthem, even as the political debate over Vande Mataram and the Centre's communication continues.

headline: Delhi govt mulls restructuring of DSEU
full_text:
Delhi govt mulls restructuring of DSEU
Delhi govt mulls restructuring of DSEU
New Delhi, The Delhi government is considering restructuring the Delhi Skill and Entrepreneurship University or demerging the government polytechnic institutes merged with it after an expert committee report found some problems with its functioning, officials said.
The government is evaluating an expert committee's report on the university's functioning.
"The committee report is under evaluation and a decision will be taken soon. The report has found for sure that there are some problems with the functioning of the university," an official told PTI.
The official said two options were under consideration: reworking the structure of DSEU or demerging the polytechnic institutes from the university to ensure technical education is taken forward effectively.
"The two ways forward are either to rework the structure of the university or at least demerge the polytechnic institutes if we want to take forward technical education properly. The committee report is being evaluated and experts are being contacted," he added.
Earlier this year, officials had said that the government has been considering a wider round of consultations with stakeholders and experts to review the overall functioning of DSEU, including the impact of the merger of government polytechnics and skill centres with the university.
Officials had said that a four-member committee constituted earlier to undertake a comprehensive review of the university, had met on January 30 and deliberated on issues concerning DSEU's governance, academic processes, recruitment of teaching and non-teaching staff, human resources, programme design, utilisation of assets and facilities at merged campuses and other administrative matters.
Senior officials and academicians from Delhi Technical University, the Directorate of Training and Technical Education and the University of Delhi had also attended the meeting. The DSEU vice-chancellor was also requested to depute the university registrar for the deliberations, according to the meeting notice.
The review assumes significance amid repeated complaints from students and employees over alleged mismanagement, infrastructure gaps, fee hikes, faculty-related issues and falling enrolment.
Student groups and employees have also raised concerns over academic standards and whether the university has been able to retain its original focus on providing skill and technical education to students from marginalised sections.
The proposed restructuring or demerger also comes weeks after the Gazetted Officers Forum for Technical Education, Delhi demanded a high-level inquiry into the merger of 10 government polytechnics with DSEU.
The association, representing gazetted officers, teachers and employees of Department of Training and Technical Education , had alleged that the merger was marked by legal, administrative and academic irregularities and sought demerger of the polytechnic institutes.
GOFTED had also alleged that students faced academic instability, changes in curriculum, deficiencies in admissions, faculty and laboratory facilities and higher fees following the merger. It had demanded that the government's committee report be made public.
DSEU was established under the Delhi Skill and Entrepreneurship University Act, 2019, with the university beginning operations in October 2020.
As part of the restructuring of technical and skill education, 23 World Class Skill Centres were merged with DSEU in January 2021, followed by 10 government institutes of technology, commonly known as polytechnics, in April that year. GB Pant Engineering College and two Delhi Institute of Tool and Engineering institutions were subsequently merged in May 2021.
According to the university, posts of the merged institutes were also transferred to DSEU, while teaching and technical staff were placed on deemed deputation.
The government-appointed committee's recommendations are expected to guide the next course of action on DSEU and the future of the merged institutions, officials said.

headline: Bodies of 2 missing friends found buried behind temple in UP's Baghpat
full_text:
Bodies of 2 missing friends found buried behind temple in UP's Baghpat
They allegedly confronted the temple's mahant about his relationship with Ankit's sister, leading to their murder. Investigations continue.
The bodies of two men, who had been missing for nearly three weeks, were found buried behind a temple in Lahchaura village in Uttar Pradesh’s Baghpat district on Thursday, police said.
“The bodies of Ankit, 25, and Israr, 32, were recovered after police excavated the premises of mahant Naresh Nath, who is now absconding. Two people have been detained for questioning in the matter,” said superintendent of police (SP) Suraj Kumar Rai.
“Based on evidence gathered during the probe and information obtained from the detained persons, police learnt that the bodies had allegedly been buried on the mahant’s premises. The bodies were subsequently recovered on Wednesday,” the SP added.
The two victims were friends
According to their families, said police, Ankit and Israr were close friends and lived opposite each other. Ankit was unemployed and the only brother among five sisters, while Israr worked as a labourer and supported his wife and three children, they said. Both the men left home on a motorcycle on July 25 and did not return. Their phones were switched off from the evening of July 27. “A missing persons case was registered at Chandinagar police station on July 29. Police examined call records, mobile locations and other evidence before tracing the men’s last known movements to the temple,” Rai said.
Police said Ankit and Israr had allegedly confronted Nath over his relationship with Ankit’s sister. Investigators suspect the confrontation escalated and the men were killed and buried behind the temple.
“The bodies were in an advanced state of decomposition and were identified through their clothes and belongings. They were sent for post-mortem examination after inquest proceedings. A forensic team also collected evidence from the site,” the SP said.
The exact sequence of events and the motive were being investigated, police said.

headline: Mothers Against Vaping backs Maliwal's Parliament intervention on vapes, e-cigarettes
full_text:
Mothers Against Vaping backs Maliwal's Parliament intervention on vapes, e-cigarettes
New Delhi, Mothers Against Vaping has welcomed Rajya Sabha MP Swati Maliwal's intervention in Parliament on the growing menace of vaping among children and adolescents and called for strict enforcement of India's ban on e-cigarettes and action against networks supplying them to minors.
Mothers Against Vaping is a collective of concerned mothers working to protect children and young people from new-age gateway nicotine products, including vapes, e-cigarettes, Heated Tobacco Products , heat-not-burn devices, nicotine pouches, and similar products.
Maliwal warned that vapes are increasingly being presented to school-going children as "safe", "cool" and harmless, while social media, influencers and illicit sellers are making these nicotine products increasingly accessible to young users.
"These days, young school-going children are harming their health by considering vapes and e-cigarettes 'safe'. This is a matter of serious concern. The government took a commendable step by imposing a ban on the sale of vapes, but even today, some suppliers are reaching children through social media, and certain shopkeepers are covertly distributing these products," Maliwal said in a post on X.
"This is not a cool, harmless trend. It is pushing children towards nicotine addiction and playing with their health, focus and future. All states should strictly enforce this ban. Schools, parents, police and local administration must work together to take immediate action against such networks. I raised this issue in Parliament because there can be no compromise with the health and future of children," she said.
In a statement, MAV expressed its appreciation to Maliwal for bringing the issue of new-age nicotine products to Parliament and drawing attention to their growing accessibility and normalisation among the youth.
"Such interventions are important in strengthening public awareness and ensures that the issue receives the attention it deserves at the national level," it said.
"MAV believes that more Members of Parliament should come forward and support stronger action to protect India's children and adolescents. MAV believes that protecting young people from new-age nicotine products is not a political issue and should not be viewed through partisan lines," the MVA said.
It said the issue was a matter of child safety, public health and the future of the country, requiring collective action from all groups of society.
India's existing prohibition must be comprehensively enforced across the expanding range of nicotine products and devices, including e-cigarettes, ENDS, vapes, HTPs, heat-not-burn and other novel formats, MAV said.
It also urged vigilance against foreign vested interests seeking to expand these products among young Indians, stressing that the country's large youth population must not become a target market for new-age nicotine products.
MAV urged the government to hold social media and e-commerce platforms accountable for the promotion, sale or distribution of prohibited new-age nicotine products.
"There should be stringent legal provisions and penal action against any platform or entity that facilitates or enables the promotion of banned products, particularly where such content or products adversely affect the health and safety of children and young people," it said.
Commenting on the issue, Dr Bhavna Barmi, clinical psychologist, founder of Happiness Studio, said, "India's biggest social and economic dividend is its young population. We therefore cannot lose our next generation to designs of international addiction industry, seeking new markets.
"All parliamentarians should come together to strictly enforce ban on vapes and heat-not-burn devices and introduce ban on all forms of novel and new-age products like nicotine pouches, patches and gums."
MAV said collective action from Parliament and governments to schools, parents, law enforcement, healthcare professionals and society at large is required to ensure that India's children do not become the next generation of nicotine users.

headline: Cockroach Janta Party calls for Manan Mishra's resignation as CJI slams move against NALSAR batch
full_text:
Cockroach Janta Party calls for Manan Mishra's resignation as CJI slams move against NALSAR batch
Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said the Council had “no business” getting involved in the students’ right to protest.
Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das on Friday demanded the resignation of Bar Council of India (BCI) chairman Manan Kumar Mishra after Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant slammed the BCI for intervening in the NALSAR University of Law enrolment row.
“Moral responsibility commands that Manan Kumar Mishra resigns. Cockroaches both inside and outside courts should ensure this happens,” Das wrote on X.
Deep Dive
CJI Kant slams BCI action
The chief justice said the Council had “no business” getting involved in the students’ right to protest. He also made it clear that the court would not permit students to be prevented from raising their concerns through lawful and peaceful protests.
He also barred the BCI and all state bar councils from taking any punitive or criminal action against students or faculty members of any national law university or university in connection with the dispute, HT reported earlier.
Meanwhile, the Supreme Court admitted a petition seeking directions to stop the BCI from issuing similar directives in the future and issued notice to the Council. A bench led by CJI Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, asked the BCI to submit its counter-affidavit within two weeks.
“The BCI is unnecessarily taking action in this matter. If students have a cause or a reason to protest, they have a right to protest. Nobody can stop them, and we will not allow this,” said the CJI after senior advocate K Parameshwar raised the issue before the bench.
Parameshwar said the BCI had “no business” dealing with matters inside a university and argued that its action infringed on the students’ fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression. He said the BCI’s decision to withdraw its first letter freezing enrolment did not remove the cause of action against the Council. “It spells a lot about the functioning of the BCI,” Parameshwar said.
The CJI responded: “We are with you. This is absolutely uncalled for. They had no business to interfere. The students have written a letter to me, and it is between me and the students. There is a dialogue between us.”
BCI halts enrolment, then withdraws order
In its first order, BCI Chairman Mishra directed all state bar councils not to enrol any 2026 law graduate from NALSAR University as an advocate until further orders.
The BCI issued the order after a section of NALSAR students objected to the proposed participation of CJI Kant as the chief guest at the university’s convocation.
The students raised objections over remarks made by CJI Kant in the Supreme Court while hearing a plea concerning alleged police excesses against protesters during the student demonstration at Jantar Mantar on July 20.
They referred to CJI Kant’s reported comments that the bench was not interested in watching videos when the lead counsel offered to show footage of the alleged police excesses during the July 20 protest.
The BCI’s first order also directed the university to submit an authenticated report identifying those who had started, organised, coordinated or mobilised the campaign opposing the CJI’s proposed participation in the convocation.
Hours after issuing the directive, the Bar Council of India withdrew the order following a backlash on social media, including from the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) president Vikas Singh, and a threat of protest by CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke.
The BCI initially said its factual inquiry into the controversy would continue, but later reversed this decision as well.

President Murmu on Indus Water Treaty suspension: ‘Decisive step in interest of nation, farmers'
We have succeeded in bringing more than 25 crore people out of poverty, President Murmu said in her address to the nation.
President Droupadi Murmu on Friday said Operation Sindoor sent a “clear and firm message” to terrorists and their supporters that they would face consequences for their actions, regardless of where they hid. She also said the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) with a country that “harbours terrorism” was a decisive step in India’s national interest, particularly for farmers.
Addressing the nation on the eve of Independence Day, Murmu spoke about the capabilities of the Indian armed forces and said Operation Sindoor, launched in response to the Pahalgam terror attack, showed their ability to act with precision.

Deep Dive
“On May 7, we commemorated the completion of one year since the launch of Operation Sindoor. We remembered the unmatched valour of our Armed Forces. That historic operation against terrorism demonstrated the capability of the Indian Armed Forces to act with precision. It sent a clear and firm message to terrorists and those who support them, that no matter where they hide, they will have to face the consequences of their actions,” the President said.
“Suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty with the country that harbours terrorism is a decisive step in the interest of our nation, especially the farmers,” she added.
IWT suspension
The President did not name Pakistan while referring to the suspension of the treaty, saying India had suspended the IWT with a country that “harbours terrorism”.
The Indus Waters Treaty was signed between India and Pakistan in 1960 and governs the sharing of the waters of the Indus river system.
India announced that the treaty would be held in abeyance with immediate effect until Pakistan “credibly and irrevocably abjures” its support for cross-border terrorism.
This came after the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 people were killed.
Operation Sindoor
Murmu recalled the armed forces’ role in Operation Sindoor, which India launched in response to the Pahalgam attack.
The operation targeted terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK), with India saying the strikes were aimed at terror camps and training facilities linked to the perpetrators and planners of the attack.
India and Pakistan later agreed to a ceasefire following an escalation that saw attacks on military targets.
The President also recalled Kargil Vijay Diwas, observed on July 26, and said India took pride in its tradition of overcoming forces hostile to humanity while upholding truth and justice.

- “We have set an example of digital revolution.”

The Sector 49 police station received information through Dial-112 that a boy had jumped in front of metro train at the Sector 52 station.
A 16-year-old boy allegedly killed his father at their rented accommodation in Noida and later died by suicide after jumping in front of a metro train at Sector 52 station, police said on Friday.
The incident took place on Wednesday and came to light in two separate stages. While the teenager's death at the metro station was reported shortly after it happened, his father's body was recovered from their rented room only late Thursday night, news agency PTI reported.
According to the preliminary investigation, the teenager had been staying with his father, who worked as a tutor, at a rented apartment in Garhi Chaukhandi village for around three months.

"Early Wednesday morning, while his father was asleep, he killed his father. Afterward, he went to the Sector-52 Metro station, where he attempted to take his own life by jumping in front of a train," police said.
After allegedly killing his father, the boy left the rented accommodation and travelled to Sector 52 Metro station.

headline: 'Who are you to question govt policy?': SC stays Madras HC order on jobs for relatives of Karur stampede victims
full_text:
'Who are you to question govt policy?': SC stays Madras HC order on jobs for relatives of Karur stampede victims
The Madras high court had held that public employment had to conform to Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
The Supreme Court on Friday stayed a Madras High Court decision striking down a Tamil Nadu government order of compassionate appointments to the families of 41 people who died in the Karur stampede last September, observing that a policy decision by the State to provide succour to victims of an unfortunate tragedy should not be interfered with lightly.
A bench of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran issued notice on the state government’s plea challenging the high court judgment and ordered that its decision “shall remain stayed”.
During the proceedings, the bench questioned the basis for challenging the State’s decision to provide employment to the bereaved families.
“Stampede took place. Unfortunate incident happened. The government has decided to compensate them. Should government not give employment?” asked the bench.
Senior Advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for the state government, submitted that the state had taken the decision as a policy measure under Article 162 of the Constitution. “If the state wants to give out (compassionate appointment) out of killings as a policy decision under Article 162, how can the high court interfere?” he asked, pointing out that the government circular itself had not been challenged.
Singhvi also questioned the maintainability of a PIL seeking to interfere with employment decisions.
The intervention by the Supreme Court comes against the backdrop of the high court’s finding that the state could not create a special category of beneficiaries for public employment outside the existing framework governing compassionate appointments.
The high court had held that public employment had to conform to Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution and warned that allowing the State to make such appointments on the basis of a particular tragedy could open the “floodgates” to similar claims arising from other unfortunate incidents.
On Friday, however, the bench questioned why the state could not provide employment as part of its policy to rehabilitate families that had lost their sole earning members.
“A stampede took place, something very unfortunate happened, some hundreds of people died. Now if the government decided that the family members should be provided with some succour, and suppose they would have decided to compensate them with money, would you have objected?” the bench asked the lawyer appearing for the PIL petitioner in the high court.
“Suppose if the sole earning member has died in the stampede and there is nobody else in the family who is earning, shouldn’t the government give some employment to son or daughter or wife as per their educational qualifications?” it added.
At one point, a lawyer representing a political party opposed the appointments, arguing that compassionate appointment could not be left to the discretion of the state and alleging a conflict of interest since the party allegedly responsible for the stampede was now in power in Tamil Nadu.
But the bench questioned the lawyer’s role in the matter, asking: “Who are you representing?” When told that he appeared for a political party, the judge asked, “What is the role of a political party here? Don’t bring politics here.”
The high court had, while quashing the government order, noted that several thousand persons eligible for compassionate appointments under the existing scheme were already awaiting employment. The State could not overlook their claims and create a separate class of beneficiaries through an executive order, it had held.
The high court had also said that public employment could not become a form of compensation outside the constitutional framework, while suggesting that the government could instead consider technical education, skill development and entrepreneurship programmes for members of the affected families.
The state, however, had defended the decision as an “exceptional measure” under Article 162, arguing that the victims constituted a distinct class requiring rehabilitation beyond monetary compensation. It had said the appointments were limited to entry-level posts intended to provide long-term financial security to the bereaved families.
The petitions before the high court had challenged the government’s decision to provide jobs to the kin of the 41 victims of the September 2025 stampede at a Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) rally in Karur. The tragedy is currently being investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).
The state decided to offer employment to the victims’ families after the TVK, led by chief minister C Joseph Vijay, came to power following the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections in April 2026.

headline: Jaipur Class 12 student dies after eating canteen patty, family alleges school negligence
full_text:
Jaipur Class 12 student dies after eating canteen patty, family alleges school negligence
The family alleged that the school administration did not take him to the hospital and instead kept him on the premises for around 45 minutes.
A 17-year-old Class 12 student died after he allegedly fell unconscious at his school in Jaipur's Jhotwara area, with his family claiming that he became ill after eating a patty from the school canteen, officials said on Thursday.
The deceased was a resident of Brijmandal Colony in Jhotwara, Assistant Sub-Inspector Narendra Kumar of Jhotwara police station said, according to a PTI report.
Also Read | DU student dies in canteen
Students family staged a protest
The student's family staged a protest at the school on Thursday, alleging that he fell ill after eating a patty at the school canteen and later collapsed unconscious in his classroom on Wednesday, the police said.
The family alleged that the school administration did not take him to the hospital and instead kept him on the premises for around 45 minutes before the family arrived and took him to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
Police said they reached the school and recorded statements from students and teachers regarding the incident.
Also Read | 19-year-old DU student jumps to death from Delhi mall
Patties at the school canteen
According to the family, he had not brought his lunchbox to school on Wednesday and went to the canteen with his friends, where they ate patties.
The family alleged that he vomited soon after eating the patty and that his condition subsequently deteriorated. He then returned to his classroom and informed a teacher that he was unwell before collapsing.
The teacher informed the school administrator, following which he was taken to another room, the family said.
Also Read | Family of 4 dies after chicken biryani, watermelon meal; cops suspect food poisoning
Parents demand action against school administration
A relative, Ravi Kumar, alleged that at around 11 am, the unconscious student was taken from the classroom to a room by a teacher, administrator and others. The family was subsequently called to the school.
The family alleged that the school administration continued asking them to bring a four-wheeler to the school until around 11.45 am, instead of taking the student to the hospital.
The family eventually reached the school and took him to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead, they said.
Following the incident, shopkeepers belonging to the Swarnkar community near Brijbal Chauraha shut their establishments, while hundreds of people gathered outside the school to protest.
The family also brought his body to the school and demanded action against the administration, alleging negligence.
Police said the exact cause of the student's death would be established only after the post-mortem report.

headline: The Madras High Court administration on Friday (August 14, 2026) issued a revised circular clarifying that the State song Tamil Thai Vazhthu, national song Vande Mataram, and the national anthem should be played/sung during the Independence Day celeb...
full_text:
The Madras High Court administration on Friday (August 14, 2026) issued a revised circular clarifying that the State song Tamil Thai Vazhthu, national song Vande Mataram, and the national anthem should be played/sung during the Independence Day celebrations at its principal seat in Chennai, the Madurai Bench, and all district judicial units, both in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry on Saturday (August 15, 2026).
The revision came after a section of the Bar members expressed concerns over a circular issued on Tuesday (August 11, 2026) not having made any mention about the playing of Tamil Thai Vazhthu and restricting itself to the playing of the national song and the national anthem alone in view of an advisory issued by the Centre under the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Campaign 2026’ to commemorate 150 years of Vande Mataram.
Listing the sequence in which the anthem and songs must be played, the previous circular had stated the national song must be played first, followed by the hoisting of the national flag, and then the playing/singing of the national anthem. However, the revised circular clarified that the Tamil Thai Vazhthu would be played first followed by the national song before the hoisting of the national flag. The absence of any mention about the playing/singing of the State song Tamil Thai Vazhthu in the August 11 circular had become a cause for concern among a section of the legal fraternity. The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court Bar Association (MMBA) had written to the Registrar General on Thursday (August 13, 2026), expressing its concerns.
“It is a long-standing convention that in all the programmes conducted by the honourable High Court, the function will start by playing/singing the Tamil Thai Vazhthu,” the association said. It highlighted a Government Order issued on August 12, 2026, making it mandatory to sing/play the State song during specific events.
‘Not merely a song’
“Tamil Thai Vazhthu is not merely a song but an enduring symbol of Tamil identity, language, culture and heritage of Tamil Nadu. The Madras High Court, being one of the foremost constitutional institutions of Tamil Nadu, has a special responsibility to uphold the dignity of the State, its Constitutional values and its rich linguistic and cultural heritage... Therefore, we request you to include the State song in the events of Independence Day celebrations,” the communication sent by MMBA general secretary P. Jessi Jeeva Priya read.

headline: Class 8 boy dragged 25 metres under car in Kanpur, driver flees after leaving him roadside
full_text:
Class 8 boy dragged 25 metres under car in Kanpur, driver flees after leaving him roadside
The incident took place around 6 pm on Wednesday near Awas Vikas-1, when the boy, was riding his bicycle close to his home.
A 14-year-old Class 8 student was trapped under a car and dragged for nearly 20-25 metres in Kanpur’s Kalyanpur area before the driver stopped, left him by the roadside and fled, police said. The alleged driver, Ashish Diwakar, was arrested on Thursday after public uproar.
The incident took place around 6 pm on Wednesday near Awas Vikas-1, when the boy, was riding his bicycle close to his home. CCTV footage shows a car approaching the boy and hitting him. The boy appears to get trapped beneath the vehicle as the car continues moving before stopping further ahead.

Drive fled on foot
According to police, the driver then got out, moved the injured boy to the side of the road and fled on foot. He was taken to hospital in serious condition.
The footage has since circulated widely on social media.
He is the son of Sandeep Tiwari, a resident of Awas Vikas-1. His father has alleged that the incident may have been deliberate and raised the possibility of a conspiracy. Police said they were investigating the allegation.

The car was seized on Wednesday. It is registered in the name of Saurabh, a resident of Gadruali in Fatehpur, and a police team was sent there as part of the investigation.
DCP West Qasim Abidi said Kalyanpur police had arrested Diwakar in connection with the case. A case has been registered under Sections 281 and 125(B) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, and further legal proceedings are underway.

headline: Reliance Industries, Rolls-Royce partner to make engine for India’s AMCA programme
full_text:
Reliance Industries, Rolls-Royce partner to make engine for India’s AMCA programme
Reliance, Rolls-Royce partner to make engines for India's Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft programme.
Reliance Industries and British aerospace major Rolls-Royce announced a partnership to develop and manufacture an engine for India’s Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme on Friday.
In a statement, the company announced plans to partner and offer capabilities for the design, development, delivering an indigenous combat engine for India’s Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme.
Also Read | Reliance Infra wins ₹157.64 cr award in Metro 1 dispute
“As part of the partnership, Reliance and Rolls-Royce will explore the formation of a dedicated Aerospace Gas Turbine Complex that will be a centre of excellence for power and propulsion technology in India,” the statement read.
The partnership will offer a proposition for joint development of the AMCA engine in India.
According to the statement, this aligns with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s "Atmanirbhar Bharat" vision for the nation's defence ecosystem to deliver an indigenous engine to power India’s fighter jet programme.
"This marks a step towards realising the vision set out by the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, for India’s defence ecosystem to deliver an indigenous engine to power the country’s fighter jet programme," it added.
Also Read | Anant Ambani, Radhika Merchant enjoy late-night drive on Mumbai's Sea Link in top-down Rolls-Royce. Watch
Statements from the leadership
Anant Ambani, Executive Director of Reliance Industries Limited, said, “India’s strategic autonomy requires sovereign capability in critical technologies. Our intent with Rolls-Royce is to combine their world-leading expertise in advanced propulsion with Reliance’s technology, manufacturing, scale and execution capabilities to build an indigenous aero-engine ecosystem in India.”
“Together, we aim to build an enduring national capability that can make India self-reliant and, over time, globally competitive in advanced propulsion technologies. This is our contribution to the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of an Atmanirbhar Viksit Bharat,” he added.
Furthermore, Tufan Erginbilgiç, CEO, Rolls-Royce plc, said, "I welcome the opportunity to join forces with Reliance Industries, bringing together our century-long heritage in advanced engineering and proven engine expertise with their homegrown leadership in Indian industry. Together, with our existing partnerships and capabilities in India, this marks a major milestone towards building a robust, self-reliant aerospace ecosystem in the country."
Also Read | Delhi man spots Rolls Royce patrol car of Dubai Police, internet stunned
Key highlights of the partnership
Joint development: Rolls-Royce will contribute its global engine leadership, while Reliance will provide its industrial strengths.
"By combining Rolls-Royce’s global leadership in engines with the established industrial strengths of Reliance, the Aero Gas Turbine Complex will build sovereign, end-to-end Indian capability across design, development, manufacturing, testing, production and through-life support. This will also unlock opportunities to explore wider collaborations across defence, civil aerospace, and new power and propulsion systems," the statement said.
‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ vision:
"The alliance will support India’s ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ vision for technology indigenisation and help position the country as a global leader in advanced propulsion capabilities," it noted.

headline: Rebel Trinamool Congress leader in Lok Sabha Sudip Bandyopadhyay
full_text:
Rebel Trinamool Congress leader in Lok Sabha Sudip Bandyopadhyay
NEW DELHI: Breakaway Trinamool Congress leader in Lok Sabha Sudip Bandyopadhyay has urged PM Narendra Modi to appoint a NDA convener, saying it will allow the governing alliance parties to convey their views to him and exchange ideas, more so when Parliament is not in session.He made the suggestion to Modi as he met him at the tea hosted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla for leaders of different parties on Thursday."I made the request as there is no connection and communication, especially when session is over," he said, adding that a convener will serve as a point of contact for other parties and keep the communication line open.With Birla also present, the sixth-term Lok Sabha MP urged him for an early decision on the merger of his faction 20 MPs with Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI).
While they are now part of NDA and its second biggest constituent after BJP, they are shown as AITC (All India Trinamool Congress) MPs by Sansad TV when they speak in Lok Sabha. "Our issue should be sorted out soon," he said, adding that it allows TMC, which is now left with only eight MPs in the House, to question their group's legitimacy.While BJP allies like George Fernandes and Sharad Yadav served as NDA convener in the past, especially during the Vajpayee govt, no one has held the position for several years.
TMC is, however, preparing to move the Supreme Court against the rebel Lok Sabha MPs to seek their disqualification.Party general secretary Abhishek Banerjee had met Birla on Jul 27, urging him to expedite his decision on its petition seeking disqualification of the 20 MPs.
Banerjee, a Lok Sabha MP, had also sought revocation of changes made to the seating arrangements of his partyâs MPs to allow the rebel members to sit separately. He had submitted separate letters to the speaker on each of his concerns.He had met the Speaker on Wednesday over the issue."If the Speaker does not decide on these petitions within the period required by law and applicable judicial directions, I will be compelled to approach the Supreme Court and seek its intervention,â Abhishek said.

headline: Pushpa Singh: 'Only a few of us champions are left, the rest are out'
full_text:
Pushpa Singh: 'Only a few of us champions are left, the rest are out'
Born in May 1947, Singh has been playing competitive games for most of her life.
At 79, Pushpa Singh is playing. One rainy evening, a table at her apartment complex in Ghaziabad is at the centre of a koat pees, or court piece, tournament. A newspaper is spread across it, partly covered by mobile phones, glasses, and keys. Around the table, players are sitting with their cards as others watch behind them.
Singh stands by the table for a quick photo, holding her cards in a fan. She is in the semi-final. She has already played three rounds this week, with her neighbour Priya Sachan as her partner. “Only a few of us koat pees dhurandhars (champions) are left, the rest are out,” she says.
If Singh and her partner win, the final will be played later that night. The winners will receive their prizes on August 15, when their gated apartment complex celebrates Independence Day, marking 79 years of India’s freedom.
Deep Dive
ALSO READ | Freedom the same night, but different dates: Why Pakistan marks its Independence Day on August 14
Born in May 1947, Singh has been playing competitive games for most of her life. She was a schoolgirl in Nagina, in Uttar Pradesh’s Bijnor district, when her father, a teacher, told her, “Jao, khelo [Go play].” Singh grew up in the early years of independent India, a time often thought of as more restrictive than now for girls. But her story underlines that in some families and small towns, girls could still achieve some freedom through sport. She frequently participated in district tournaments, spending days outside her home without her parents accompanying her.
By Class 8, at Nagina’s Dayanand Vaidik Kanya Inter College, Singh was already a javelin champion. She also regularly competed in shot put, high jump, long jump, hurdles, relay and rope climbing. She and fellow athletes in the college often travelled to multi-day tournaments at girls’ colleges in nearby towns such as Dhampur, Bijnor and Seohara, staying in hostels. They played in salwar suits, tying their white dupattas around their waists.
Independence Day: HT full coverage
By Class 10, Singh had collected three state-government trophies for relay, high jump and rope climbing. None of her three brothers played sports. Once, she missed a tournament. Her parents were away in their village and her elder sister refused to let her go. When her father returned, he asked her sister why she had stopped her.
After Class 12, at 20, Singh was married to a public works department engineer employed by the UP government. Her husband’s postings took the family to various towns, and her sporting life changed. In Nainital, where the family once lived, there was rowing. Singh, then a young mother in her early 30s, would take a wooden boat onto Naini Lake and row by herself. In a photograph from those days, she is in the boat in a sari, both hands on the oars.
In another town where her husband was posted, she once saw some men playing badminton. “Let us also play,” she told her women friends. They did, and routinely.
Singh would play in a sari. Not used to sports shoes, she played in slippers. Once, she and her playmate entered a badminton tournament at a club in Lucknow. Singh was in her 50s. The other three women were in their 30s. Before the final, Singh told her partner to guard the net while she covered the back court. Her partner lost a point at the net, and they lost the match by a point.
ALSO READ | ‘Beginning of another’: How Hindustan Times reported freedom on August 15, 1947
Gradually, the games became less about running and jumping. Bridge arrived in her life. Singh learnt the complex card game when her husband was posted in Pilibhit, a town in the Terai. Friends in the PWD Colony took turns hosting the game at their drawing rooms every evening after dinner. Singh’s reputation as a formidable bridge player quickly spread through Pilibhit’s high society. An elderly bridge enthusiast, the father-in-law of the district magistrate, the “DM Sahib,” often visited from Delhi. He would call Singh’s husband and ask him to come over for a game, along with “Mrs Singh,” the bridge champion.
At home, there was carrom with her children after school. Now that the children are busy with their own lives and have their own children, Singh spends every afternoon with her retired husband, playing Paplu, another card game.
Singh’s passion for sport has percolated to the next generation. Her eldest daughter Parul is a working professional in her 50s who lives in Mumbai and frequently treks in the Himalayas. Earlier this year, Parul with her daughter trekked to the Everest Base Camp. Singh’s younger daughter Payal also has a career and lives in Delhi-NCR. Payal practises yoga, while her daughter spends 1.5 hours every day at the neighbourhood gym, working out with battle ropes.
Some years ago, Singh’s knees began to trouble her. Eventually, she underwent knee replacement surgery. But the games stayed.
Singh and her koat pees partner, Priya Sachan, face Geeta Chaudhary and Rajiv Mohan. The girl who once travelled to tournaments in the early years of independent India is, decades later, sitting down for another game. India has changed dramatically since then. Singh has too, though something of that girl remains.
The cards are dealt. Singh looks at her hand and declares the trump: “Chidi.”
