headline: Minister of Handlooms, Textiles and Khadi M. Vijay Balaji inspected remote tribal hamlets atop Alleri hillock, which is part of Jawadhu Hills, in Vellore on Friday after residents demanded basic amenities.
full_text:
Minister of Handlooms, Textiles and Khadi M. Vijay Balaji inspected remote tribal hamlets atop Alleri hillock, which is part of Jawadhu Hills, in Vellore on Friday after residents demanded basic amenities.
Accompanied by Collector P.S. Leela Alex and M. Vijay Chandran, District Health Officer (DHO), Mr. Balaji interacted with tribals in the hamlets. They also inspected government facilities, including a school and a fair price shop, which were functioning in a rented building. “We have apprised about the need for basic facilities like road, health centre, borewells, and regular power supply in the hills,” said K. Veeran, a tribal.
At present, Alleri hillock has three big tribal villages namely Peenjamanthai, Jarthankollai, and Palampattu villages. Alleri tribal hamlet was part of Peenjamanthai village panchayat before the hamlet was bifurcated to become a seperate panchayat in 2025. The hamlet has around 300 families.
DRDA officials said that the proposed bitumen road will connect Varadalampattu with Nelli Marakollai village, a distance of 8 km, in the hills. Of the total eight km, five kilometres of the stretch will be laid in Alleri Reserve Forest (RF). The new stretch will help eight remote hamlets of Alleri village panchayat, which comprises 12 hamlets with a population of around 2,000 tribals.
The new road will be at least five-metre-wide. The new stretch will have at least 15 culverts to discharge excess rainwater and prevent damage to the carriageway during monsoon. The entire work, which will be completed in six months once started, will cost ₹17 crore.
Another long-standing demand of residents was a full-fledged government health centre. The Minister said that a special tribal health centre will be set up. The proposed centre will have two duty doctors and staff nurses. Separate wards for treatment, especially for snake bites will be set up. Laboratory facilities, fully furnished pharmacies with adequate stock will be available.
At present, Peechamandai and Aravatla along the Tamil Nadu-Andhra Pradesh border are the only two tribal hamlets that have government health centres in the district. Both hamlets are accessible by bitumen roads.

headline: After returning to India, he continued to write about the poor conditions of Indians legally settled in South Africa. In an Aug 29, 1919 letter, Gandhi blamed the âgreedy Europeans of Natalâ for importing Indian indentured labour
full_text:
After returning to India, he continued to write about the poor conditions of Indians legally settled in South Africa. In an Aug 29, 1919 letter, Gandhi blamed the âgreedy Europeans of Natalâ for importing Indian indentured labour
A fast unto death announced by Mahatma Gandhi in Puneâs Yerawada jail in 1932 was to change the course of Indiaâs political history. Imprisoned for the Civil Disobedience Movement, Gandhi announced the fast in a Sept 13 letter to British PM Ramsay MacDonald that was shared with the press. His aim was to oppose a separate electorate for Dalits, proposed under the Communal Award of August 1932.âI have to resist your decision with my life,â Gandhi wrote, saying his fast would begin on Sept 20. âAs a man of religion that I hold myself to be, I have no other course left open to me.âThe award classified Dalits as a minority whose representatives would be elected only by Dalit voters, just as Muslims, Christians and Sikhs would elect their own representatives. Gandhi believed this would divide Hindu society; BR Ambedkar supported it as a safeguard for Dalit political representationGandhi acknowledged that he might be wrong. If his judgement was âwarpedâ, he wrote, his death would be âa penance for my errorâ and would lift the burden from those who had âchild-like faithâ in his wisdom.His week-long fast led to the Poona Pact, negotiated by Madan Mohan Malaviya and Ambedkar and accepted by Gandhi. It abandoned a separate electorate but reserved seats for Dalits within the general electorate, becoming a milestone in Dalit representation and a precursor to reservations for SCs and STs in independent India.
Suspending Satyagraha
Gandhi also used a letter to the press to announce the suspension of Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act.
Writing on July 21, 1919, he asked satyagrahis to âswallow the bitter pillâ and halt their campaign after protests had turned violent.The act allowed the colonial government to detain political prisoners for two years without trial. Gandhiâs campaign against it, launched in March 1919, was his first nationwide political mobilisation after returning from South Africa. Despite his appeals for peaceful hartals, fasts and prayers, violence erupted in several places. Gandhi was prevented from entering Punjab and arrested; the Jallianwala Bagh massacre on April 13 made the situation explosive. Attacks on police stations and railway property, and deadly clashes between protesters and authorities, led him to pause civil disobedience.
For Gandhi, non-violence was not merely tactical. Amid divisions within Congress and Subhas Chandra Boseâs different course, he wrote from Sevagram on July 21, 1941
In the July letter, published under the headline âSATYAGRAHA. Civil Resistance Suspendedâ, Gandhi disclosed that the governor of Bombay had conveyed âa grave warningâ from the Government of India that renewed civil disobedience could threaten public security.Writing from Mani Bhavan in Bombay, Gandhi conceded that the suspension was painful. Yet he remained unyielding on the law: âSatyagrahi will pay for its removal with their lives if it cannot be removed by lesser means.â He also warned the Raj: âIf my occasional Civil Resistance be a lighted match, Rowlatt legislationâ¦is a thousand matches scattered throughout India.âFor Gandhi, non-violence was not merely tactical. Amid divisions within Congress and Subhas Chandra Boseâs different course, he wrote from Sevagram on July 21, 1941: âWith me, no doubt non-violence is an end in itself, though it is also a means for the attainment of the freedom of the country.â A year earlier, he had underlined its voluntary nature: âNon-violence cannot be imposed upon anyone. It has to come from within.â
The South Africa Years
Gandhiâs letters to the editor predated his emergence as a leader of Indiaâs freedom struggle. During his 21 years in South Africa, where he first used Satyagraha as a method of resistance, he repeatedly drew attention to discriminatory laws against IndiansIn a Dec 19, 1901 letter, he described the restrictions in the Transvaal, where Indians could not hold land, were required to live and trade only in designated areas, and were barred from footpaths. In the Orange River Colony, he wrote, an Indian could not even enter without special permission, except as a domestic servant or labourer.After returning to India, he continued to write about the poor conditions of Indians legally settled in South Africa. In an Aug 29, 1919 letter, he blamed the âgreedy Europeans of Natalâ for importing Indian indentured labour at miserably low wages while ignoring local Zulu workers, all in pursuit of âenormous profitsâ.
Cow Slaughter And Eid
Gandhiâs correspondence also addressed social fractures, particularly Hindu-Muslim relations. In a 1919 letter written around Bakrid, he recounted a conversation with Maulana Abdul Bari of Lucknowâs Firangi Mahal, a prominent supporter of the Khilafat Movement.
Gandhi quoted the Maulana as saying: âIslam will fall to pieces if it ever takes and never givesâ¦. If we take from you, we must give to you.â Abdul Bari had urged his followers to abstain from cow slaughter. On Bakrid, he sent Gandhi a telegram: âIn celebration of Hindu-Muslim unity, no cow sacrifices in Firangi-Mahal this Bakri-Id.âMore than a century later, these letters are more than historical records. They reveal Gandhi not only as a politician confronting colonial power but as a public figure wrestling with representation, violence, communal division and moral responsibility. Through TOIâs pages, his words travelled beyond the immediate battles of the freedom struggle, leaving an intimate record of how he tried to shape public opinion â and India itself.

headline: FIR registered against BJP MP Anant Maharaj over alleged Netaji remarks: Police
full_text:
FIR registered against BJP MP Anant Maharaj over alleged Netaji remarks: Police
Police said the FIR against Anant Maharaj was registered over his alleged ‘war criminal’ remark about Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose at a Siliguri event.
Police have registered a First Information Report (FIR) against Nagendra Ray, a BJP Rajya Sabha member popularly known as Anant Maharaj, for his alleged derogatory comments against Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
“He has done something which is unforgiveable. But he is a senior citizen. He has uploaded a video on social media on Thursday night. Looking at his age I think it should be taken with a positive note. Rest law will take its own course. I have nothing to say on that,” Suvendu Adhikari, chief minister, told the media in Kolkata.
Days after his alleged derogatory comments against Netaji, the Rajbanshi leader from north Bengal released a video statement saying that his comments were intentional.
“With respect to Netaji, I would like to state that if unintentional comments have hurt anyone emotionally, then I am sorry from the core of my heart,” Ray said in the video message.
Also Read:Bengal revokes BJP MP Anant Maharaj’s Banga Bibhushan after Netaji remarks
Ray had allegedly described Netaji as a “war criminal” at a public meeting in Siliguri on August 9. A video in which the Rajbanshi leader from north Bengal could purportedly be seen making the comments was widely circulated on social media.
In an earlier statement on July 19, the 64-year-old leader had questioned Netaji’s organising prowess and the role played by the Azad Hind Fauj in India’s freedom struggle. A complaint was lodged against Ray on August 7 for his comments at the Kotwali police station in Cooch Behar.
“His comments against Netaji were so derogatory that we were forced to lodge a complaint. He has insulted the National icon. He should be arrested and expelled from the Rajya Sabha,” Gopal Dey, a worker of the All India Forward Bloc who lodged the complaint against Ray, told the media on Friday.
On July 12, Adhikari directed the state police to initiate strict action against those making derogatory remarks against Netaji.
“We have already registered a FIR against Ray on the basis of a complaint we received on August 7. The FIR has registered under sections 196 (promoting enmity), 299 (malicious act to outrage religious feelings) and 353 (circulating false information),” said a senior officer of Cooch Behar.
Ray, in the face of criticism, had claimed that Netaji was described as a “war criminal” by former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. He also said that he had documents to support his claims.
Soon after the chief minister’s warning, at least six FIRs were lodged against various persons who uploaded derogatory comments against Netaji. Five persons were arrested to date. At least 282 social media accounts have been suspended by the state police.
“Ray is a BJP Rajya Sabha member and the BJP has to take his responsibility. This is a criminal offence. Already a few persons have been arrested. Why shouldn’t he be arrested?” Saugata Roy, TMC MP, told reporters.

headline: NEW DELHI: Television channels will no longer be restricted to 12 minutes of advertisements per hour, with the government deciding to scrap the two-decade-old cap in a move it says will put traditional broadcasters on a more level footing with digita...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Television channels will no longer be restricted to 12 minutes of advertisements per hour, with the government deciding to scrap the two-decade-old cap in a move it says will put traditional broadcasters on a more level footing with digital platforms.The restriction, introduced in 2006 under the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994, will cease to apply once the amended rules are notified in the Gazette, the information and broadcasting ministry said.The government has argued that the television landscape has changed substantially since the cap was imposed. India had only 62 TV channels in 2006, compared with more than 900 now. Cable television, then the dominant distribution platform, was largely analog and offered limited capacity and consumer choice.With digitisation, platforms including cable TV, direct-to-home, HITS and IPTV can now carry 300 to 500 channels or more, significantly expanding viewer choice and competition, the ministry said.The decision could give broadcasters greater flexibility to determine advertising inventory, an important consideration for an industry that remains heavily dependent on advertising revenue across both pay and free-to-air channels.
The ministry also cited the growing competition television faces from digital media, where there is no comparable statutory cap on advertising duration.It said the existing restriction had created a ânon-level playing fieldâ for conventional television broadcasters and that removing it would promote âfair competitionâ and ease of doing business.The change, however, will become operational only from the date the amendment to the Cable Television Networks Rules is formally notified.

headline: Kerala court sentences seven to life for 2016 murder of 19-year-old
full_text:
Kerala court sentences seven to life for 2016 murder of 19-year-old
A special court in Nedumangad sentenced seven men to life for Vishnu's 2016 murder at his Kannanmoola home. The verdict also brought acquittals, exposed investigative lapses and closed a case marked by gang rivalry.
A special court in Kerala's Nedumangad on Friday sentenced seven people to life imprisonment for the 2016 murder of a 19-year-old man, Vishnu, at Kannanmoola. The court also found an eighth accused guilty, but did not pronounce the sentence as he had died.
The court acquitted five others in the case. The accused were found guilty under various sections of the Indian Penal Code and the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
Nedumangad SC/ST Special Court Judge A Shajahan sentenced Arun alias Paratta Arun, Lallu, Rajesh alias Poocha Rajesh, Sanalkumar alias Sanju, Vijesh alias Vishnu, Manu alias Shetty Manu and Sreenath alias Bolji to life imprisonment. The court acquitted Dini Babu, Jayan, Ajees, Unnikrishnan Nair and Dileep. The eighth accused, Suresh alias Ashir, was also found guilty, but the sentence was not pronounced as he had died.
Vishnu was murdered on October 7, 2016, after the accused allegedly broke into his house following a fallout between two criminal gangs led by Puthenpalam Rajesh and Dini Babu. He was allegedly targeted because he was close to Puthenpalam Rajesh, who was involved in the murder of Dini Babu's brother, Suni Babu, in December 2015. Vishnu's parents, Anil Kumar and Bindu, and his aunt Laila sustained serious injuries in the attack.
The case was first investigated by Pettah police and was later handed over to the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Shangumugham. After lapses were found in the investigation, another Assistant Commissioner took over the probe and a revised chargesheet was filed. During the trial, the prosecution examined 48 witnesses and produced 144 material objects and six documents before the court.
Vishnu's cousin Adithyan, who was seven years old when he witnessed the murder, also testified before the court.
The case ended with life terms for seven accused, the conviction of an eighth who had died, and the acquittal of five others in the murder of Vishnu, who was attacked at his home in 2016.

headline: Man dances, bathes for hours before stealing KTM bike from Varanasi showroom; caught on camera
full_text:
Man dances, bathes for hours before stealing KTM bike from Varanasi showroom; caught on camera
The CCTV footage showed the suspect arriving outside the Varanasi dealership around 11:30 pm wearing a white shirt and jeans.
An unidentified man stole a motorcycle from a showroom in Varanasi’s Manduadih area on Monday night, but it was his unusual behaviour inside the dealership that has drawn attention.
CCTV footage from inside the shop showed the man dancing, drinking coffee, taking a bath and even changing clothes before riding away with a KTM Adventure 390 S bike, police said.
The incident came to light in the early hours of Tuesday after showroom manager Rohit Kumar Singh received a call from the security guard saying the dealership’s main door had been damaged. Upon rushing to the store, Singh found that a section of the gate had been cut from the bottom, while another part had been broken. Glass shards were scattered inside and outside the premises.
Also Read | Delhi airport, high court, other sensitive locations receive bomb threat ahead of Independence Day
Singh then checked the motorcycles kept inside and found that his bike, which he had parked at the showroom before leaving for home, was missing. A branded T-shirt and cap, along with a vehicle cover, were also found missing from the accessories stock. He subsequently informed the police.
Thief danced, made coffee before fleeing
The CCTV footage showed the suspect arriving outside the dealership around 11:30 pm wearing a white shirt and jeans and carrying a picture of a goddess, Singh said.
He added that the man first pushed against the door and looked inside before taking out a cutter and starting to cut through the glass.
When heavy rain began, the man moved to the rear of the showroom. He tore down a banner, wrapped it around himself for cover and sat there for some time before returning to the door and continuing to cut it.
The man finally entered the showroom around 12:06 am. Once inside, he switched on the computer at the reception and sat in the chair, spinning around for a while. He then walked around the showroom, examining several motorcycles.
The CCTV footage also showed him helping himself to water from a mini-fridge before making coffee using the coffee machine.
His behaviour became even more unusual as he spent time inside the showroom. He took a bath in the washroom, spread his clothes over a motorcycle and tore a bike cover to make a lungi-like garment. He then danced to music, jumping and moving vigorously around the showroom.
The man later took a showroom T-shirt and cap before making his final move. He selected the KTM Adventure 390 S and rode out of the dealership.
Police launch hunt
Manduadih station house officer (SHO) Ajay Verma said an FIR had been registered on the basis of the showroom manager’s complaint.
"Information was received about the theft of a bike. We inspected the scene, and the forensic team collected evidence. A team has been deployed to ensure arrest of the accused," Verma said.
Police said teams were working to identify and trace the suspect and that the accused would be arrested soon.

headline: Air India A320 briefly lost key flight controls during 300-foot drop, Airbus analysis shows
full_text:
Air India A320 briefly lost key flight controls during 300-foot drop, Airbus analysis shows
AIR INDIA-SAFETY/ (PIX):Air India A320 briefly lost key flight controls during 300-foot drop, Airbus analysis shows
By Abhijith Ganapavaram
NEW DELHI, - An Air India Airbus A320 that dropped about 300 feet this month, injuring 24 people on board, briefly lost key flight controls after registering losses in all three hydraulic systems, according to a preliminary Airbus analysis reviewed by Reuters.
The August 4 incident occurred on Air India flight AI2379 from Phuket to Delhi, which landed safely in Delhi despite the altitude loss. The aircraft's elevators and ailerons, which control its pitch and roll, were unavailable for about four seconds, during which the plane pitched upward, Airbus said in a communication responding to an Air India request for an assessment.
Deep Dive
During that period, the first officer applied a full nose-down input, but there was "no direct response" from the flight-control surfaces before the hydraulic systems recovered within seconds. In the analysis, Airbus asked Air India to conduct checks on the plane's systems and sensors and to provide more information about the incident. It did not establish the root cause.
Air India and Airbus did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Indian authorities have classified it as a serious incident, and the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau is investigating, with technical assistance from Airbus and France's BEA.
The flight's captain tested positive for marijuana in a confirmatory drug test, according to a source familiar with the matter. No link between the test result and the altitude loss has been established to date, but Air India on Thursday began mandatory substance testing for all pilots, according to an internal memo.

headline: Palaniswami slams TN CM Vijay over office shift, says farmers’ woes being ignored
full_text:
Palaniswami slams TN CM Vijay over office shift, says farmers’ woes being ignored
Chennai, AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami on Friday took a swipe at Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, saying he chose to shift his office to a modern room while farmers faced several problems.
As Palaniswami targeted the ruling TVK, AIADMK rebel MLAs S P Velumani and Natham R Viswanathan skipped the statewide protest, objecting to the party leadership's decision to ask them to lead the agitations outside their home districts.
Palaniswami had assigned Velumani to lead the protest in Theni and Viswanathan in Ramanathapuram.
The two senior leaders defied the party leadership and skipped the protests. In a joint statement earlier, they had said they would not travel outside their strongholds of Coimbatore and Dindigul to lead the agitation.
The two were among the 25 rebel MLAs who defied the party diktat and voted in support of the TVK government during the floor test on May 13.
Later, fearing disqualification, the rebel legislators led by Velumani reconciled with Palaniswami and agreed to function under his leadership. However, six of the 25 legislators later resigned and joined the TVK, accepting Vijay's leadership.
Palaniswami had called for Friday's protest to condemn the state government's alleged failure to secure Tamil Nadu's share of Cauvery water.
AIADMK workers led by Palaniswami staged protests across Tamil Nadu on Friday, demanding a complete waiver of crop loans taken by farmers. The party claimed the water shortage had contributed to drought and disrupted Kuruvai paddy cultivation in the Cauvery delta districts.
Addressing party workers at a protest near the Head Post Office in Thanjavur, Palaniswami criticised the CM for focusing on shifting to a modern office instead of using his official chamber at Fort St George, where former chief ministers C N Annadurai, M Karunanidhi, M G Ramachandran, J Jayalalithaa, he himself and M K Stalin had worked.
"The CM seems to be concerned about the aesthetics of his office while farmers in the state are struggling and working day and night in harsh weather conditions," Palaniswami said.
He urged the government to waive agricultural loans instead of ignoring the plight of farmers.

How August 15 is celebrated
India celebrates Independence Day every year on August 15 to mark the country’s freedom from British colonial rule. India became independent on August 15, 1947, after decades of political struggle and the sacrifices of countless freedom fighters.
Why August 15?
The British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act in 1947, which made way for the creation of two independent dominions - India and Pakistan. India formally became independent at midnight between August 14 and 15.
India’s first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, addressed the nation at the historic moment with his famous “Tryst with Destiny” speech. He spoke of India’s transition from colonial rule to freedom and the responsibilities that came with independence.

NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu on Friday addressed the nation and extended her greetings ahead of the 80th Independence day. On the eve of Independence Day, Murmu praised India's growth and said that "every citizen is contributing to nation building".
Here's are some of the key quotes from President Murmu's national address:
- Duty of every person associated with judicial system to ensure that no one is deprived of justice due to lack of resources.
- Citizens across all walks of life are making valuable contributions to nation-building, with the Armed Forces, CAPFs, police personnel, sanitation workers and the Indian diaspora playing a special role. India remains committed to building a Viksit Bharat by 2047 through inclusive development, while drawing inspiration from its rich heritage and the ideals of the freedom struggle.
- Operation Sindoor demonstrated Indian Armed Forces' capability for precision strikes against terror networks.
- People from different ideological streams shared one common goal, Indiaâs independence. During the Swadeshi Movement, Vande Mataram became the song of the masses. Under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi, countless Indians joined the freedom struggle, while Dr BR Ambedkar set high ideals of social reform and national commitment.
- Suspension of Indus Waters Treaty with country harbouring terrorism a decisive step in national interest, particularly for farmers.
- Terrorists and those supporting them will have to face consequences no matter where they hide.

When our country became independent, along with the serious consequences of Partition, integrating more than 550 princely states with the newly independent India was also an extraordinary challenge. Sardar Patel integrated the princely states into our independent republic.
- Over 25 cr people lifted out of poverty in past decade through inclusive development initiatives.
- Free ration programme ensuring food security for more than 80 cr beneficiaries.
- We are moving forward with a balance between heritage and development. The world's largest and most advanced digital infrastructure has been developed in our country. Digital payments are being made even at small shops in villages and on roadside stalls. More than half of the world's real-time digital transactions are taking place in India. Our citizens and the government, working together, have presented an example of a digital revolution to the global community.

headline: ‘India on our radar’: Trump aide Peter Navarro's big remark after White House's ‘shadow trans-shipment’ report
full_text:
‘India on our radar’: Trump aide Peter Navarro's big remark after White House's ‘shadow trans-shipment’ report
Peter Navarro's remarks come amid a White House report that accuses India and other nations of helping Chinese goods evade tariffs.
White House advisor Peter Navarro, who is infamous for his anti-India rhetoric in the past over trade issues, has made yet another remark, this time with reference to a US report naming India as part of a “shadow trans-shipment network” that helps Chinese goods evade tariffs.
The White House report is by Navarro, White House trade and manufacturing adviser. He claims that the US is losing some $19 billion to $26 billion in annual tariff revenue to goods, mostly from China, that are transshipped through third countries to escape US import duties.
During his remarks on the matter, Navarro said: “India is well on our radar screen”.
The White House adviser said that new trade frameworks pursued by the Trump administration are going to contain provisions that ensure trade partners that engage in the practice will be penalized, the Associated Press reported.
Navarro also alleged India and other countries could be using the trans-shipment shadow network to avoid new tariffs, referring to fresh tolls imposed by the US administration over Russian oil purchase. India, along with China, Slovakia, Hungary and Azerbaijan face 100% tariffs under Russia sanctions bill for continued significant purchases of Russian energy.
White House report on shadow-transshipment network
The report identifies about 40 countries, including India, that have an elevated risk of being sources of illegal transshipments of goods, many of which are linked to minimally processing, relabeling and repackaging of Chinese-origin components, Reuters reported.
In a report, 'The Great Transshipment Scam', Navarro said the transshipments became more prevalent after 2018, when the Trump administration imposed Section 301 tariffs on China to counter "unfair trade practices."
"For years, the great transshipment scam has let Communist China launder its exports through more than 40 countries," Navarro was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.
The countries that comprise China's Shadow Transshipment Network include many of America's largest trading partners, ranging from Mexico and Canada on US land borders to the European Union, India, Japan, and South Korea.
"China began using these third countries for minor processing, relabeling, repackaging, reinvoicing, or routing changes that created the appearance of a new national origin while leaving the underlying Chinese content largely intact," Navarro has alleged in the report.
Navarro's remarks against India
Navarro has repeatedly criticised India, even calling it the “Maharaja of tariffs,” while defending US retaliatory tariffs in response to India's purchase of Russian oil. He earlier claimed that India was not involved in the Russian oil trade before the Ukraine war began in 2022. He said India's involvement increased after the war started.
Early this week, he responded to criticism in India over his comments on New Delhi and its trade policies, telling his critics not to attack him as he said such an approach is not how problems are resolved in America.
“I actually got firebombed by the Indian continent on the internet with all sorts of nasty little attacks. And all I would say is, don't do that. That's not how we resolve problems here in America,” he told reporters at the White House.

headline: 'Rehabilitation centres for retired judges': CJI Surya Kant raps consumer forums over case pendency
full_text:
'Rehabilitation centres for retired judges': CJI Surya Kant raps consumer forums over case pendency
SC directed an audit of consumer commissions, questioning effectiveness of retired judges in these roles and need for better accountability and infrastructure.
The Supreme Court on Thursday ordered a performance audit of consumer commissions across the country, including an assessment of the work done by former judges and judicial officers appointed to these fora, as it questioned whether they had become "rehabilitation centres" for retired people without adequate accountability.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took strong exception to reports of prolonged pendency and poor disposal of consumer disputes, saying appointments to these bodies could not be treated merely as post-retirement rehabilitation.
Also Read | SC expresses concern over pendency of cases at NCDRC, bats for regional, circuit benches
"Have these places become a rehabilitation centre for retired people? That is what is bothering us. You appoint retired district and high court judges and then there is no accountability. We are not willing to accept this. There has to be some kind of a performance evaluation," said the bench.
SC seeks 3-year performance reports from consumer commissions
It directed the presidents of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) and state consumer commissions to conduct an evaluation of the performance of the commissions under their jurisdiction over the last three years and furnish reports to the court.
The court also sought a report from the president of the National Consumer Commission within two weeks detailing the total pendency, composition of the commission, average disposal by its different benches, the estimated time required to clear the backlog and whether its strength needed to be increased.
The bench’s intervention came after it took note of a newspaper report highlighting the “pitiful and poor performance” of consumer commissions.
The court also asked senior counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan, who is assisting the court as amicus curiae, to submit a separate report on the functioning and pendency of state consumer commissions, including the oldest pending cases.
During the proceedings, the bench identified two broad concerns -- inadequate infrastructure and deficiencies in appointments, even as it said that the issue of accountability of those manning the consumer fora could not be ignored.
“In district commissions, the problem is of quality. They do not usually bother about the nature of the dispute and how they are decided on merits,” the bench said. It further observed that while the state commissions may not necessarily have significant arrears, cases ultimately travel to the National Consumer Commission in appeal.
Also Read | SCDRC upholds ₹8.5 lakh insurance award against AIG in stolen vehicle case
SC says more benches alone won't solve consumer case backlog
When additional solicitor general (ASG) Aishwarya Bhati appeared for the government, the bench said that if arrears were piling up at the National Consumer Commission, its strength would have to be increased and more benches created.
The court, however, made clear that merely increasing infrastructure or providing additional facilities would not address the problem unless there was corresponding accountability.
The government told Parliament last month that 593,109 consumer cases were pending across the country, including 16,915 before the NCDRC, 1,27,507 before state commissions and 4,48,687 before district commissions.

headline: Police forced to retaliate: Bihar DGP defends response during encounters
full_text:
Police forced to retaliate: Bihar DGP defends response during encounters
Bihar's DGP said police retaliate only when fired upon during encounters. He said any excess is punished as the state cites falling crime and stricter oversight.
Bihar Director General of Police Vinay Kumar on Friday said security personnel are "sometimes forced to retaliate in self-defence" during face-offs with criminals, amid controversy over recent police encounters in the state. Addressing a press conference, he said police personnel follow standard procedure but are required to respond when suspects open fire in order to protect themselves and maintain law and order.
Without naming any specific incident, Kumar made the remarks when journalists asked about allegations over the role of police personnel in recent encounters. His statement comes amid a political row over the alleged encounter of Bharat Tiwari in Bilauti village of Bhojpur district two months ago.
Kumar said, "Wherever police excess is found, swift action is taken against officials concerned." On allegations that an AK-47 rifle was used by police during a students' protest in Siwan district on July 22, he said, "the police officer concerned was suspended immediately and investigation is underway in the case".
Home Department Secretary Pranav Kumar, who was also present at the press conference, said murder cases had fallen by 10.1 per cent, dacoity by 31.32 per cent and riot cases by 18.97 per cent since the beginning of the year. He said the number of Naxalism-affected districts in Bihar had come down from 22 in 2013 to zero at present. The DGP said the government's focus was not only on eradicating Naxalism but also on building infrastructure and public facilities in affected areas so that there was no room for any resurgence.
Pranav Kumar said, "The Economic Offences Unit (EOU) of Bihar Police has registered 13 cases of disproportionate assets against public servants since the beginning of this year. Similarly, regarding the NEET exam paper leak, 33 accused have been arrested in four cases." He added that 1.14 lakh online complaints had been registered against cybercrimes on the NCRP portal this year, Rs 104 crore had been frozen in suspicious accounts, Rs 9.99 crore had been refunded to victims, and action on the remaining amount was under way. A total of 522 cybercriminals have been arrested this year, while 2,942 cases have been reported at cyber police stations, he said. He also said the average response time of Dial 112 had dropped to 11 minutes.
On public safety measures, Pranav Kumar said, "'Abhaya Brigade' has been formed under the direction of the chief minister to ensure the safety of women and vulnerable groups. The state government is in the process of buying 1,500 scooters to provide greater mobility to the brigade. It will be completed soon." Overall, the press conference centred on the state's response to questions over encounters, action in cases of alleged excess, and the government's claims on crime control, cybercrime and public safety.

headline: Delhi Master Plan 2047 floats ‘congestion pricing’ for vehicles entering key city areas
full_text:
Delhi Master Plan 2047 floats ‘congestion pricing’ for vehicles entering key city areas
Delhi's Master Plan 2047 proposes congestion pricing to manage traffic, requiring further policy development by the government and collaboration among agencies.
Delhi’s Master Plan 2047 has proposed introducing congestion pricing in identified parts of the city, allowing authorities to levy charges on private vehicles entering areas with high traffic volumes and vehicular pressure. The proposal, which places road pricing alongside parking management as a tool to regulate private vehicle use, is part of the transport strategy outlined in the long-term planning document.
The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) approved MPD-2047 on August 12, paving the way for the plan to be sent to the Union housing and urban affairs ministry for final approval and notification. It is the first time a Delhi Master Plan has proposed congestion pricing; a review of MPD-2021 and MPD-2001 shows planners and officials had earlier avoided the measure, seeing it as restrictive and punitive.
Approval of the plan, however, does not by itself clear the way for a congestion charge to be levied. The Master Plan, notified under the Delhi Development Act, 1957, sets the policy direction on land use and development, but the authority to levy a road-use charge would require the Delhi government to formulate a policy around it, which would be implemented on ground by either Delhi Police, transport department and coordination between agencies, that do not share a common reporting line — road-owning bodies including PWD, MCD, NDMC and NHAI; the Delhi transport department under GNCTD; and the traffic police, which reports to the Union home ministry.
Under the congestion-pricing proposal, road-owning agencies and the transport department, in consultation with the traffic police, will identify areas that can be designated as congestion-pricing zones. The document specifically says these areas “may include areas around TOD nodes, Walled City Heritage Zone and the Metropolitan City Centre (MCC).”
TOD, or transit-oriented development, refers to high-density mixed-use zones built around Metro and other mass-transit stations; the MCC is the central business district designation used in the plan.
The plan also provides for technology-based implementation. “RFID tagging, etc., may be used for implementation of congestion pricing,” it says, indicating that vehicles could be identified electronically as they enter designated zones rather than relying on manual collection of charges. The document does not specify a rate structure, exemptions or the mode of revenue collection.
Also Read | MPD-2047: 9 heritage sites to be linked through ‘cultural precincts’
MPD-2047 links congestion pricing with a broader strategy of discouraging private vehicle use by managing the availability and cost of parking as well. It proposes restricting public parking at work centres, entertainment areas, cultural hubs and markets where such restrictions could deter private vehicle use.
“The public parking at work centres, entertainment or cultural hubs, markets, etc. shall be restricted which will be a deterrent to private vehicular trips,” the document says.
It further proposes restricting both on-street and off-street public parking in areas that have high accessibility to public transport. The strategy is to make parking demand management work alongside congestion pricing rather than treating the two measures separately, an official aware of the matter said.
Another provision calls for “dynamic parking pricing” based on location and time of day to be used as a tool to discourage the use of private vehicles. The approach would allow parking charges to vary according to where and when a vehicle is parked, with higher charges possible in locations and periods experiencing greater demand. The plan also calls for strict enforcement of parking regulations.
Urban planner and Raahgiri Foundation trustee Sarika Panda Bhatt said Connaught Place was an area where congestion pricing could be considered. “Connaught Place is one of the areas that is mature for congestion pricing. For this, enforcement should ideally be camera-based and this would also require adequate alternatives to private vehicles, needing augmentation of informal transport modes within the area,” Bhatt said.
The proposed framework comes after earlier attempts to introduce congestion pricing in Delhi. A 2016 central government committee on decongesting Delhi had recommended effective parking pricing and a congestion tax to discourage private vehicle use, but the recommendation which could have been mandated by the Delhi government by notification of a policy was never taken up.
Congestion pricing is already operational in several major cities. London has operated its central congestion charge for more than two decades, under which vehicles entering the central charging zone during specified hours pay a daily fee. Singapore uses electronic road pricing, with charges varying according to location and time, while Stockholm levies a congestion tax during specified hours and varies charges by time of day. New York became the first US city to introduce congestion pricing when its Manhattan central business district tolling programme began in January 2025.

headline: Pakistan envoy raises Kashmir issue at I-Day event in Delhi, cites UN resolutions
full_text:
Pakistan envoy raises Kashmir issue at I-Day event in Delhi, cites UN resolutions
Pakistan's envoy in India used an Independence Day event in New Delhi to raise Kashmir and highlight a new defence pact. The remarks underscored Islamabad's attempt to frame regional peace and security around long-standing disputes and alliances.
Pakistan's Charge d'Affaires in India, Saad Ahmad Warraich, on Friday raised the Kashmir issue at Pakistan's 80th Independence Day celebrations in New Delhi, saying the path to lasting and durable peace in South Asia lies in resolving the dispute in accordance with UN resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people. He also referred to a key joint defence agreement signed recently between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
In his address at the Pakistan High Commission, Warraich said Pakistan "firmly believes in the ideals of peaceful coexistence, dialogue and diplomacy". He also claimed that Pakistan's nuclear capability is a "stabilising factor in South Asia".
Warraich hoisted Pakistan's national flag at the ceremony held at the Chancery Lawns. Members of the High Commission and their families attended the event, and messages from Pakistan's president, prime minister and deputy prime minister were read out, according to a statement issued by the Pakistan High Commission.
In his speech, Warraich said the path to lasting and durable peace in South Asia lies in resolving the "Kashmir dispute in accordance with UN resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people". Referring to Pakistan's day of remembrance of the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, he said, "The Marka-e-Haq stands testimony to our unswerving resolve to protect and preserve the nation's sovereignty and the dignity of our people." He also said the creation of Pakistan under the leadership of Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was "not merely a triumph of the deep-seated and abiding conviction of the Muslims of the subcontinent to chart a future of their own, it was also a fulfilment of their ordained destiny to achieve a separate homeland".
On the 'Makkah Joint Defence Agreement', Warraich said, "The historic agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye represents another milestone in advancing the goal of regional stability and contributing to global peace." A joint statement issued earlier had said the agreement, signed on August 7, is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any action of aggression and stipulates that any armed attack against any of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all. Warraich also inaugurated a photo exhibition on the life, vision and historic struggle of Quaid-i-Azam, curated to mark the 150th birth anniversary of Pakistan's founder this year, the statement said.
The event in New Delhi saw Warraich combine Pakistan's Independence Day observance with remarks on Kashmir, regional security and the new defence arrangement with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, alongside references to Pakistan's founding and its 2025 conflict remembrance day.

headline: Karnataka to withdraw gutka ban after MLAs flag losses for arecanut growers
full_text:
Karnataka to withdraw gutka ban after MLAs flag losses for arecanut growers
Karnataka will withdraw its gutka and tobacco-containing pan masala ban after MLAs warned it could hurt arecanut growers and cause farmer losses.
The Karnataka government has decided to withdraw its yearlong ban on gutka and tobacco-containing pan masala, just two days after the order took effect, following protests from legislators across party lines who warned that it could hurt arecanut growers.
Chief minister D.K. Shivakumar directed officials to withdraw the order after a meeting with Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Congress legislators led by BJP MLA Araga Jnanendra and Congress MLA D.G. Shanthana Gowda, who raised concerns that the prohibition could hurt the market for arecanut and cause losses to growers.
“The issue also came up during Thursday’s Cabinet meeting. Shivakumar was reportedly displeased that the Food Safety Commissioner’s order was issued without his knowledge and questioned health department officials about why the matter had not been brought to him before the notification,” an official privy to the development said.
The prohibition, issued on Monday, covered the manufacture, storage, transportation, distribution and sale of gutka, pan masala and other products containing tobacco or nicotine. It applied to packaged and unpackaged products, including products sold separately in a way that allowed consumers to mix them.
Under Section 30(2)(a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the Food Safety Commissioner can prohibit the manufacture, storage, distribution or sale of food articles in the interest of public health. The August 10 order was issued under that provision and Regulation 2.3.4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011.
The reversal has been driven in large part by concerns over the agricultural economy in districts where arecanut cultivation is widespread.
Former chief minister and BJP MP Basavaraj Bommai said the government needed to protect public health without leaving growers exposed. “There are two matters. One is health, which must be ensured, but the interests of arecanut growers must also be protected,” Bommai said.
He said arecanut farming, once concentrated mainly in the Malnad region, had expanded into several districts, leaving large numbers of farmers dependent on the crop. “Farmers wait for five years for the arecanut crop. They invest throughout this period. Already, arecanut growers are facing problems. The government should provide compensation to farmers if such a decision is taken,” he said.
JD(S) MLA A. Manju also called for the ban to be withdrawn, warning that any measure affecting arecanut growers would meet resistance in the Malnad region. “The Chief Minister should know that there will be stiff resistance. In the Malnad region, a large number of people are dependent on arecanut farming. The government should reverse its decision to ban gutka. If the government wants to ban arecanut, it will get a bad name,” Manju said.
He said legislators would support farmers if they launched protests against the decision and urged the government to safeguard growers’ interests.
BJP MP B.Y. Raghavendra alleged that cigarette companies had lobbied for the prohibition and demanded its withdrawal within 24 hours. Speaking at a press conference in Shivamogga on Friday, he threatened that the BJP would take to the streets if the order remained in force. “The ban would impact arecanut growers. The price of areca had already come down in the market within a day of the order,” he said.
Raghavendra also questioned the government’s approach to other products, arguing that a public health policy should apply consistently. “If the government was concerned about the health of people, it should ban the sale of cigarettes and liquor. The Congress government has increased the number of liquor licences and the number of liquor shops have been increased at the hobli-level. Will they ban the sale of liquor?” he said.

headline: 'Between me and students': CJI Surya Kant slams Bar Council move against protesters
full_text:
'Between me and students': CJI Surya Kant slams Bar Council move against protesters
CJI Surya Kant expressed displeasure at the BCI's circular banning the enrolment of 2026-batch graduates of NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad, as advocates.
Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Friday came down heavily on the Bar Council of India (BCI) over its intervention in the NALSAR University of Law enrolment controversy, saying the Council had “no business” interfering with students’ right to protest and making it clear that the court would not allow students to be stopped from raising their voice through lawful and peaceful protests. He restrained the BCI and all state bar councils from pursuing any punitive or criminal action against students and faculty of any national law university or university in connection with the row.
The CJI’s observations came hours after BCI chairman Manan Kumar Mishra announced that the Council had decided to close its proceedings against the 2026 graduating batch of NALSAR, Hyderabad, after initially freezing their enrolment and then withdrawing the freeze while retaining an inquiry into those allegedly instrumental in the students’ campaign against CJI Kant being invited as chief guest at their convocation.
The Supreme Court, meanwhile, took on board a petition seeking directions to restrain the BCI from issuing such directives in future and issued notice to the Council. A bench headed by CJI Kant, along with justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, directed the BCI to file its counter-affidavit within two weeks.
“The BCI is unnecessarily taking action in this matter. If students have a cause or a reason to protest, they have a right to protest. Nobody can stop them, and we will not allow this,” said the CJI after senior advocate K Parameshwar mentioned the matter before the bench.
Parameshwar submitted that the BCI had “no business” dealing with what was happening inside a university and that its action violated the students’ fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression. He said the BCI’s withdrawal of the first letter freezing enrolment did not wipe out the cause of action against the Council. “It spells a lot about the functioning of the BCI,” Parameshwar said.
The CJI responded: “We are with you. This is absolutely uncalled for. They had no business to interfere. The students have written a letter to me, and it is between me and the students. There is a dialogue between us.”
The Chief Justice also drew upon his own experience as a student to underscore the importance of allowing dissent on university campuses. “In my younger days, I was also actively involved in student activities. They have a right to protest. Who can stop them? So long as they are lawfully and peacefully protesting, they have a right to raise their voice,” he said.
At another point, the CJI said: “We have to be large-hearted. They should be allowed to speak. Even if they are wrong, they have a right to speak.”
Justice Bagchi also sought to know whether the BCI Council had actually been convened to issue the resolution concerning the NALSAR students. “You will have to tell us about this in your reply,” the judge told advocate Radhika Gautam, who appeared for the BCI.
Parameshwar told the bench that he had been informed by a BCI member from Kerala that no meeting of the Council had taken place and questioned how such a decision could have been taken.
The court also asked BCI to ensure that the students’ enrolment was not held up, while sending a message to them through Parameshwar. “You tell all students they should enroll as soon as possible and take the SCBA membership,” the CJI told the senior counsel.
In its order, the bench said that, pending further proceedings, “no punitive or criminal action shall be taken against students or faculty of any national law universities or other universities.”
Deep Dive
The controversy
The controversy began after a section of NALSAR students objected to CJI Kant being invited as the chief guest for their convocation. The first representation was submitted on July 23 by 70 members of the outgoing LLB batch, with students from several other batches subsequently expressing solidarity.
The students had cited remarks made by CJI Kant during proceedings on a plea concerning alleged police excesses during student protests in Delhi. They argued that the choice of convocation chief guest should reflect NALSAR’s commitment to constitutional rights, access to justice and reasoned engagement with grievances.
The immediate judicial intervention on Friday came as the BCI itself made a third shift in its position on the controversy on Friday morning.
Mishra said in a post on X that the Council had decided to “close the proceedings altogether” against the NALSAR 2026 batch after considering representations and reactions from senior advocates, members of the Bar, law students and “public-spirited citizens”.
“After considering the representations and reactions of Senior Advocates, learned members of the Bar, law students and public-spirited citizens, and being satisfied that the 2026 batch of NALSAR, Hyderabad, had no role in any disturbance or movement, the Bar Council of India has decided to close the proceedings altogether. No further action is required from NALSAR,” Mishra said.
The announcement marked a further retreat from the BCI’s position just a day earlier.
On Thursday, Mishra had first directed all State Bar Councils not to enrol any student who had obtained a law degree from NALSAR in 2026 “till further orders”. The BCI had simultaneously sought an authenticated report from the university identifying those who had initiated, organised, coordinated or mobilised the campaign opposing CJI Kant’s participation in the convocation.
Hours later, the BCI issued a second communication modifying the enrolment freeze. It said the “vast majority” of the students were innocent and that “no student shall be made to suffer without any fault on his part”. However, it retained an inquiry into allegations that a handful of teachers and outsiders had instigated or misled students. The latest statement by Mishra now abandons even that inquiry.
The BCI chairman said the decision followed the representations received after the two communications issued on Thursday and the press release issued by NALSAR vice-chancellor Srikrishna Deva Rao. The vice-chancellor had said the university would first examine, under its governance regulations, whether an inquiry sought by the BCI was within its constitutional powers.
Mishra, while closing the proceedings, nevertheless advised the students to maintain institutional decorum. “A word of wisdom: we take immense pride in our legal institutions, and the day you enrol, you become vanguards. Voice your opinions freely, but with respect and institutional decorum. The highest judicial office is our collective pride. Dissent is welcome in a democracy; public ridicule of it is often counterproductive,” he said.

headline: Student’s murder over alleged campus drug whistleblowing sparks political row in TN
full_text:
Student’s murder over alleged campus drug whistleblowing sparks political row in TN
Coimbatore , The brutal murder of a 19-year-old mechatronics engineering student, whose family claimed he had exposed drug abuse on campus, has sparked a political controversy in Tamil Nadu, with the Opposition DMK raising the issue in the Legislative Assembly.
Amid protests by student organisations, both the college management and police have denied any drug-related motive for the killing, saying the attack stemmed from personal enmity and a retaliatory clash.
Police have arrested eight persons in connection with the murder and launched a hunt for 11 others who are absconding.
According to police, preliminary post-mortem findings at Singanallur ESI Hospital showed that the victim suffered severe blunt-force injuries from iron rods and wooden logs, resulting in fatal internal bleeding and acute respiratory failure.
The student's father, Kennedy, alleged that his son was targeted because he had exposed drug abuse and ganja trafficking on the college campus.
The family also alleged that the college management and local police had pressured him to identify students involved in drug abuse and later leaked his identity to the accused.
Police, however, said a preliminary inquiry indicated that the attack was linked to a retaliatory clash arising from a senior-junior dispute.
According to police, a group of students targeted the victim after suspecting him of involvement in a masked phone-snatching and extortion incident on the morning of August 10.
The victim, a third-year student at a private engineering college here, was intercepted near Malumichampatti and dragged to a nearby ground, where a group of youths allegedly assaulted him with iron rods and wooden logs.
He managed to return to his room but developed severe respiratory distress later that afternoon and was declared dead at a private hospital.
The murder has given rise to two sharply conflicting narratives over the motive behind the attack.
"My son was forced to provide names regarding drug abuse on campus. His identity was leaked to the perpetrators, leading to his brutal death," Kennedy alleged.
The college administration, meanwhile, said the victim and another student had been suspended on July 24 following an incident on July 21, in which they allegedly assaulted hostel cook Manoj after violating the campus curfew.
The management said it was unaware that the victim was staying in a rented room near Othakkalmandapam after being evicted from the hostel and claimed it learnt about the assault only on August 10, when he was taken to hospital.
The college has handed over details of 15 other students to police to help identify those involved in the clash.
The issue was raised in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, leading to heated exchanges between the government and the Opposition.
Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin raised the issue in the House and demanded accountability, citing the family's allegation that the student was targeted for acting as an informant against campus drug peddlers.
Minister for School Education, Tamil Development, Information and Publicity, A Rajmohan rejected the allegation, saying the investigation so far indicated a localised retaliatory clash between student groups.
Speaker J C D Prabhakar directed Rajmohan to submit a detailed report during an upcoming call-attention motion.
Opposition parties have demanded an independent, high-level inquiry into the incident.

headline: Indra Mohan Pandey: ‘Panditji just passed by us... I could see him clearly’
full_text:
Indra Mohan Pandey: ‘Panditji just passed by us... I could see him clearly’
India@79: Pandey has watched India move from radio and trunk calls to smartphones and from scarcity and protectionism to liberalisation and globalisation
Indra Mohan Pandey was 11 when he first saw Jawaharlal Nehru, the country’s first prime minister. The year was 1958, and children from across Delhi schools had been brought to the Red Fort to watch Independence Day celebrations. Pandey, an old Delhi boy, one of five siblings, was one of them.
“Panditji just passed by us and cheered us on… I was in the front row and I could see him clearly,” recalled Pandey, who was born 10 days after India gained independence. The stage was small, security was sparse and the distance between the leaders of the new republic and the children watching them was little.
Also Read | Pushpa Singh: Only a few of us champions are left, the rest are out
That child watching Nehru would go on to become a teacher, an economist and a management professor, spending more than five decades in classrooms across India and the US. He has watched India move from radio and trunk calls to smartphones, social media and artificial intelligence; from scarcity and protectionism to liberalisation and globalisation; from a country where higher education was largely a male preserve to one where women make up more than half the students in many institutions.
Born on August 25, 1947, in Pant Gaon, a picturesque village near Devprayag Sangam in present-day Uttarakhand, Pandey’s family was rooted in a tradition of Sanskrit scholarship and stayed in the village for about nine years. “My father, however, was determined that I should receive a modern education and have opportunities beyond the village. So, we moved to Delhi,” he said.
Also Read | ‘Beginning of another’: How Hindustan Times reported freedom on August 15, 1947
Home in Delhi was Bhagirath Palace near Chandni Chowk, a neighbourhood that today is known for wholesale electronics and medical markets. “Back then, Bhagirath Palace had many houses and even some offices of film distributors,” said Pandey.
There were few public schools at the time, and private education was beyond what the family could afford. While he was enrolled in Jain Sanskrit School in Dariba Kalan, it was Delhi that became his classroom.
“Politics and national security, especially during the 1962 Indo-China war, were discussed everywhere in this city. Even a bus ride was full of riveting discussions with agreements and disagreements,” recalled Pandey, who retired from IIM-Ahmedabad as professor in 2007.
Even though the India of his youth was poor and literacy low, Pandey remembers a country where political and intellectual life was alive. That came into sharper focus when he entered Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) in 1963. A B.Com (Honours) degree was considered prestigious, and Pandey, who had secured a first division, entered its top section. He joined the History and Political Science Society and the Literature Society, and student societies became his window into the wider world.
Also Read | Freedom the same night, but different dates: Why Pakistan marks its Independence Day on August 14
His time at SRCC also taught him that learning did not happen only inside classrooms. As a society office-bearer, he helped invite some of the country’s most prominent political figures. “Ram Manohar Lohia, V K Krishna Menon, and Balraj Madhok came to our college. During the Kamaraj Plan in 1963, when several senior Congress leaders resigned from ministerial positions, we took advantage of the unusual political churn to invite some of them, including Lal Bahadur Shastri,” he recalled.
Funding his own education required some financial jugglery. SRCC’s monthly fee was about ₹15, while his father’s salary was around ₹100, and so he secured a scholarship. “My father had other plans for me. He had started out as a teacher but then joined an Ayurvedic dawakhana. He didn’t want me to pursue teaching and insisted I become a chartered accountant. I resisted and for months, he didn’t speak to me… Having a fight with my father about becoming a teacher was worth it,” said Pandey, who lives in Delhi, with wife. His children, aged daughter Ruchika Pandey (50) and Abhishek Pandey (47), live in the US, and he also has two grandchildren.
He joined Delhi School of Economics (Department of Commerce) in 1966-1968 for a post graduate degree and completed his PhD from the same institute (1972-76) in finance. “We didn’t even have enough calculators. At the university’s computer division, near the vice-chancellor’s office, researchers punched cards and queued for access to an IBM machine. Shoes were not allowed inside. You submitted your calculations to a computer assistant, and were given a time slot in the evening and returned later to collect the output. Sometimes the result was simply a syntax error. A comma where a full stop was expected could mean starting over again,” he said.
In 1968, Pandey joined SRCC as a lecturer and spent nine years there; in 1981, he began his 27-year-old teaching stint at the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Ahmedabad, where he taught financial management, strategic management and other related subjects. In between, he also taught at Kansas State University as a visiting faculty member in 1985.
“New tools such as VisiCalc and Lotus 1-2-3 were beginning to transform computing. I had barely encountered them and I was desperate to learn. Lotus was later replaced by excel spreadsheets, and then came personal computers. Now it is an entirely different world altogether,” said Pandey.
He said that despite all the tech advancements and AI, human ability to ask questions will always remain essential. During the Emergency, his university colleagues gathered at a coffee house and decided to organise demonstrations and put up posters. The plan somehow reached the police. Policemen visited them and warned that they could be arrested. Some of his friends from left parties were arrested.
“Political discussions moved into drawing rooms after this but we found poetry to express ourselves. I wrote for Ganga, a Hindi magazine, about Patriotism and Struggles of middle-class,” he said.
The Mandal agitation triggered another churn. “Questions around reservation were some of the frequently asked ones in our interviews of candidates. We would like to know what their thinking was. We may like it, we may not. What was important was whether they were thinking or not,” he added.
When he was a young lecturer at SRCC, the college was, by default, an all-boys institution. He remembers having only one woman student. “Women studied at institutions such as Miranda House and Lady Shri Ram. Most of the remaining colleges were male bastions. Even when women obtained degrees, marriage and managing the household remained the expected trajectory for many,” he stated.
He remembers the excitement of buying his first car after returning from the US – a Maruti 800 with “original Japanese parts.” He has a Honda City, and rarely drives now. He uses social media apps and sees both the benefits and dangers of technology. The country has grown tremendously in front of his eyes, but progress has not been evenly distributed. “I see educated youngsters working for delivery apps. India’s next challenge is ensuring that the benefits of growth reach the lower sections of society too,” he said.
And then there is Gen Z. Pandey has watched young Indians take to the streets and use social media to organise, argue and express themselves in ways that would have been unimaginable in his student days. “Everyone is now making reels,” he said. The methods are different but the thread is familiar – young people are still asking questions.

headline: Who is Manan Kumar Mishra? Bar Council Chair at centre of CJP's 'isteefa do' post, NALSAR row
full_text:
Who is Manan Kumar Mishra? Bar Council Chair at centre of CJP's 'isteefa do' post, NALSAR row
The controversy began after reports of a campaign by some NALSAR students opposing CJI Surya Kant's participation in the university's convocation.
Bar Council of India (BCI) chairman Mannan Kumar Mishra has found focus amid the ongoing controversy linked to the NALSAR University convocation for which Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant was invited as chief guest.
Mishra recently became target of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) “isteefa do” post amid the row with the students of NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad.
The Bar Council had frozen the enrolment of the entire 2026 graduating batch, a move retracted hours later. The BCI decided to close all proceedings against the batch of NALSAR University after concluding that the students had no role in any disruption linked to CJI Surya Kant's proposed participation in the university's convocation.
Deep Dive
Mishra announced the decision through on X post on Thursday after the move sparked big backlash on social media, including from the CJP, with Abhijeet Dipke asking if it was time for “Mannan Mishra isteefa do”.
Who is Manan Kumar Mishra?
Manan Kumar Mishra is a senior advocate and a Rajya Sabha MP from Bihar, nominated by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He is also the Chairman of the Bar Council of India, the country's top legal regulatory body, a role central to the current controversy.
A native of Gopalganj district in Bihar, Mishra completed his BSc (Honours) from Rajendra College, Chapra, before earning his LLB degree from Patna Law College.
He began practising as a lawyer at the Gopalganj Civil Court before moving to the Patna high court in 1982. Later, he became a senior advocate in the Supreme Court.
Mishra has led the BCI since November 2014 and was re-elected as its chairman for a record seventh consecutive term in 2025. The chairman is elected for a term of two years.
Apart from his legal career, Mishra has also been active in politics. He contested the 2010 Bihar Assembly election on a Congress ticket before joining the BJP. In 2024, the BJP nominated him to the Rajya Sabha from Bihar, where he was elected unopposed.
The NALSAR controversy
The controversy began after reports of a campaign by some NALSAR students opposing CJI Surya Kant's participation in the university's convocation.
Reacting to the reports, the BCI had directed all State Bar Councils not to enrol any student from NALSAR's 2026 graduating batch until further orders. It also sought a detailed inquiry from the university to identify those who organised or participated in the campaign.
The Council argued that disrespect towards the country's highest judicial office was inconsistent with the values expected from future lawyers.
CJP enters the chat
Following the controversy, leaders of the CJP, including founder Abhijeet Dipke and Saurabh Das, criticised Mannan Mishra on social media.
Saurabh Das questioned why students were being threatened with punishment for expressing dissent and accused the BCI chief of calling them "anti-national forces." He also questioned Mishra's tenure as BCI chairman, alleging that the Council had spent nearly ₹14 crore on meetings and conferences in one year.
Abhijeet Dipke also posted on X, mulling if Mishra's resignation should be demanded, writing, “Time for Manan Mishra isteefa do?”
BCI changes stance
Soon after the criticism, the BCI reconsidered its decision. It withdrew the blanket enrolment ban, saying that most students were innocent and had no role in the reported campaign.
The Council, however, initially continued with its proposed inquiry into those allegedly involved.
Mannan Mishra later announced that even those proceedings had been closed after the BCI found that the graduating batch had no involvement in any disturbance.
He also advised students to express their views respectfully while maintaining the dignity of constitutional institutions.
CJP mocks U-turn
The CJP mocked BCI and its chairman over the U-turn, suggesting that it made the authorities pull an all-nighter. CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka reacted to Mishra's post, saying, “CJP ne night out padwa diya. Beijjati hui wo alag. [CJP made them pull an all-nighter, on top of it the humiliation]”.
Another CJP spokesperson, Saurav Das, argued that the BCI's earlier communication had not been fully withdrawn, citing the portion relating to an inquiry and the identification of students.
"Mr Mishra, the order has NOT been fully withdrawn. The part which seeks names of the students and orders for an 'inquiry' against them for their peaceful dissent still stands, as per your own new letter," Das said.
He demanded that the BCI withdraw the communication in full and guarantee that no action would be taken against NALSAR students for their dissent. "No student at NALSAR should face any inquiry or witch hunt for their democratic dissent against the Chief Justice of India," Das said.
Das also said the CJP's call for protests outside the BCI and Mishra's official residence would continue until the demand was met.
In a message to CJP's Dipke and Das on Friday, Manan Kumar Mishra told them that the BCI's interests are the same as theirs: "to protect the rights of the students."
"The Bar Council of India aims to protect the interests of the youth of India. I want to communicate to Abhijeet Dipke and Das (Sourav Das) that our interests are the same as theirs, to protect the rights of the students," Mishra said, speaking to ANI news agency.

The Kerala government has issued orders increasing the monthly assistance given to caregivers of chronically bedridden, disabled persons or persons with other terminal or chronic illnesses or the elderly, under Aswasakiranam Scheme, from ₹600 to ₹1,000 with immediate effect.

headline: 4 die after inhaling toxic gas inside well in Bihar's Gaya
full_text:
4 die after inhaling toxic gas inside well in Bihar's Gaya
The incident occurred at Garh Karmauni village in Dobhi police station area of the district.
Four people, including an 18-year-old boy, died of suffocation after inhaling toxic gas inside a well in Bihar’s Gaya district on Friday, police said.
The incident occurred in Garh Karmouni village under the Dobhi police station area when farmer Vijay Chaudhary, 45, went down the old well to repair or adjust a water pump motor and was overcome by toxic gases.
His 18-year-old son, Vikas Chaudhary, entered the well to rescue him, followed by two other villagers, Dilchand Manjhi, 28, and Chamari Manjhi, 65.

All four died of suffocation from toxic gases accumulated inside the old well, Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Sherghati-2 Rajan Kumar said.

Firefighter falls unconscious
A firefighter also fell unconscious after inhaling the toxic air during the rescue operation and was taken to a hospital, police officers said.
Local administration, police and fire brigade rescue teams were deployed at the site. During the rescue operation, firefighter Ajit Kumar also fell unconscious after inhaling the toxic air inside the well. He was rescued and taken to a hospital for treatment.

Bodies pulled out of the well
After considerable effort, all the bodies were pulled out of the well and sent for postmortem examination. Further legal action is underway, the SDPO said.

headline: 3 workers remain trapped as rescue ops continue at Uttarakhand tunnel
full_text:
3 workers remain trapped as rescue ops continue at Uttarakhand tunnel
Six rescue workers, who entered the tunnel to assist in the operation, have also been safely evacuated and are reported to be safe
The rescue operation at an under-construction tunnel at Mayapur in Uttarakhand’s Chamoli district continued through the night and into Friday morning, with three of the 22 workers still trapped. Nineteen workers have been rescued so far.
Seven deaths have been confirmed, and 12 injured workers are undergoing treatment. The seven have been identified as Pradeep Singh Pawar, 31, Mukesh (Uttarakhand), Durlabh Sharma (Bihar), Vijay, 28, Jitendra Kumar (Jharkhand), and Lokeshwar and Bhuneshwar.
Debris and water entered a stretch of approximately 1.5 km of the three-kilometre-long tunnel of the Vishnugad-Pipalkoti Hydroelectric Project after a landslide. Officials said top officials, including district magistrate Gaurav Kumar, were monitoring the rescue and relief operations at the site.
Deep Dive
Of the 22 people initially reported trapped, 19 were brought out during the overnight rescue operation. Seven were declared dead at a hospital. The search for the remaining three workers is continuing amid difficult conditions caused by the accumulation of debris and water inside the tunnel.
Six rescue workers, who entered the tunnel to assist in the operation, have also been safely evacuated and are reported to be safe.
Rescuers from the National Disaster Response Force, State Disaster Response Force, Indo-Tibetan Border Police, police, and other technical and specialist agencies have been deployed at the site.
Kumar directed officials to make effective use of all available resources and technical assistance to rescue the remaining workers. The administration is also ensuring medical treatment and other necessary facilities for the injured.
Chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami rushed to the site despite extremely bad weather to take stock of the rescue operation. His helicopter could not land due to adverse weather conditions. “The safe evacuation of every worker trapped inside the tunnel is the government’s top priority. All agencies involved in the operation have been directed to work on a war footing to rescue those still missing,” said Dhami.
