headline: Missing Rajasthan couple found dead, bodies stuffed inside trunk at Udaipur home
full_text:
Missing Rajasthan couple found dead, bodies stuffed inside trunk at Udaipur home
The bodies of 65-year-old Lahri Lal Paliwal and his wife Radha Devi, 62, were found in a trunk at their Rajasthan home after they went missing.
The bodies of a couple who went missing on Wednesday were found stuffed inside a trunk at their house in Poonawali village in Rajasthan’s Udaipur district on Friday morning, police said.
The couple had reportedly been missing since the morning of August 12.
Police identified the deceased as 65-year-old Lahri Lal Paliwal and 62-year-old Radha Devi. Paliwal used to sell milk for a living, and the couple lived alone at their house, officers said.
“The bodies of Lahri Lal Paliwal and his wife Radha Devi were found inside a trunk at their house. Prima facie, it appears that the couple may have been murdered late Tuesday night,” Station House Officer (SHO) of the Sayra police station Shaitan Singh Nathawat said.
Also Read: Rajasthan court acquits 40 in 2015 murder of 5 Dalits, cites probe lapses
“The bodies were allegedly packed in plastic bags and placed inside the trunk, which was then covered with bedding to conceal them. We are questioning suspects and neighbours and investigating all possible angles,” the SHO added.
Police said the couple’s neighbours became suspicious when Lahri Lal did not deliver milk. A neighbour who went to check found the door open and the house empty. The neighbours informed their son, Manohar, who works in Rajkot, Gujarat.
After failing to locate them, Manohar lodged a missing person report with the police. He told police that he had spoken to his mother over the phone on Tuesday night. The following morning, he was informed that both his parents were missing.
Also Read: Woman, 35, dies after husband allegedly sets her ablaze in Rajasthan: Police
On Thursday, villagers staged a protest and surrounded the Sayra police station, demanding that the elderly couple be traced at the earliest.
Police have begun questioning neighbours and other suspects. The exact motive behind the deaths and the circumstances in which the couple was killed are being investigated, officers said.

headline: ‘Some worked as gunners’: From carrying rifles to walking the ramp, surrendered Naxal women from Sukma tell their story
full_text:
‘Some worked as gunners’: From carrying rifles to walking the ramp, surrendered Naxal women from Sukma tell their story
Nine women from Sukma who recently surrendered participated in a fashion show held as part of a National Handloom Day event in Raipur.
Women Naxalites who once moved through the forests of Bastar with weapons such as INSAS rifles have now taken to the ramp, styled in heirloom sarees, and promoting Swadeshi products after surrendering.
Nine women from Sukma who recently surrendered participated in a fashion show held as part of a National Handloom Day event in Raipur. The programme was part of efforts to rehabilitate former Naxalites and provide them opportunities to engage in activities outside their previous lives.
The women wore heirloom sarees featuring traditional prints, paired with silver waist belts, jhumkas, and boots.
According to Sukma SP Mayank Gurjar, the women also helped spread awareness about Swadeshi products during the event.
Journey from Naxal ranks to ramp
One of the surrendered Naxalites, who said she had worked with the Pamed Area Committee, recalled her experience in Raipur, where the participants underwent six days of training.
"I used to work in the Pamed Area Committee. I surrendered in 2026. We went to Raipur recently. There, we were trained by people who had come from Bombay...prominent ministers also came. The training was of six days...it was the first time we did something like that...we enjoyed it," the former Naxalite said.
Another surrendered Naxalite, Poonam Devi, said she surrendered on July 12, 2025, after joining the Naxalite movement in November 2007.
"I surrendered on July 12, 2025. I liked the program...we were trained for it...I joined the Naxals in November 2007 and left in 2025," she said.
According to the SP, the nine women had held different roles within the Naxal organisation. Some had worked in the Pamed Area Committee, while others had served as gunners for major Naxalite commanders in Battalion Number 1.
"Among the nine surrendered women, some were working in the Pamed Area Committee. Some worked as gunners for major Naxalite commanders in Battalion Number 1. One of the surrendered women Naxalites was working as a teacher in a school," Gurjar said.
Rehabilitation efforts
SP Mayank Gurjar said the participation was part of the benefits being provided to surrendered Naxalites under the rehabilitation policies of the Government of India and the Chhattisgarh Government.
Gurjar said the women had previously carried weapons, with one of them having carried an INSAS rifle, and had surrendered about six months earlier.
He said their participation in the fashion show reflected a change in their outlook and growing trust in the government's rehabilitation policy.
"They are now actively promoting Swadeshi products and refining their artistic skills," he said.

headline: Jharkhand protest: 300 unnamed rioters booked for assault, vandalism in Ranchi
full_text:
Jharkhand protest: 300 unnamed rioters booked for assault, vandalism in Ranchi
According to the FIR, the protest march towards the Jharkhand assembly turned violent when miscreants clashed with security forces.
The Jharkhand police has registered a first information report (FIR) against unknown individuals at the Vidhan Sabha police station in connection with the August 10 march by job aspirants to the state assembly over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in the state, people aware of the development said on Thursday.
Talking to HT, a police officer familiar with the matter said the FIR was registered on Wednesday based on the statement of the magistrate on duty, Mohammed Nishat Ahmad. “The police have filed an FIR against unidentified rioters under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. Charges have been framed under Sections 109, 115(2), 117(2), 121, 132, 189(2)(3), 190, 191(2), 221, 223, 285 and 352 for obstructing government work, assaulting public servants and damaging public property. Sub-Inspector (SI) Anand Pandit has been assigned to investigate the case. The police are currently analysing video footage and photographs to identify the perpetrators,” the officer said.
ALSO READ: Protesting Jharkhand students face lathi charge, tear gas, water cannon during march to assembly
A copy of the FIR available with HT does not mention the number of alleged rioters. Ranchi superintendent of police (city) Paras Rana, however, told a news agency that the case had been filed against "300 unknown" people.
According to the FIR, the protest march towards the Jharkhand assembly turned violent when miscreants, allegedly operating under the guise of a student movement, clashed with security forces.
The mob damaged public property and attacked police personnel and magistrates on duty. Several police officers sustained serious injuries during the clash.
The FIR said a large crowd of students moving from the old assembly route towards the new Vidhan Sabha building forcibly broke through the initial defensive drop-gates and barricades erected by the administration, reaching near Niladri Bhavan by 12.15 pm.
ALSO READ: J'khand: Raghubar Das threatens hunger strike if CBI probe into exam irregularities not recommended
The on-duty magistrate, a revenue sub-inspector of Nagri Circle, used a public-address system to pacify the crowd, reminding them that section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was in force because the assembly session was underway. Ignoring the warnings, the miscreants in the crowd clashed with police and uprooted barricades near Yogoda Satsang. The situation quickly escalated, with the mob allegedly pelting magistrates and police personnel with slippers, shoes, water bottles and stones.
Several police officers were hurt in the stone-pelting with trainee constable Falguni Yadav sustaining head injuries and was rushed to hospital along with other injured personnel for immediate medical treatment. Students’ spokesperson Piyush Kumar Singh said the FIR should not be used to harass genuine students. “No genuine student should be harassed,” he said.

headline: Pune's iconic Camp Burger King sealed as Maharashtra FDA widens food safety drive
full_text:
Pune's iconic Camp Burger King sealed as Maharashtra FDA widens food safety drive
The FDA sealed Pune's long-running Camp Burger King and suspended its food licence after finding serious hygiene deficiencies. The move formed part of a wider Maharashtra crackdown that also flagged quick-commerce facilities and other food businesses.
Pune’s iconic Burger King outlet in the Camp area has been sealed after the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) found serious hygiene deficiencies and violations of food safety regulations during an inspection.
The outlet, located on East Street in Camp, was sealed by FDA officials and its food licence was suspended. The restaurant has been operating in the area since 1992 and is among Pune’s oldest Burger King outlets, making it a familiar food destination for generations of residents.
The action came as part of a wider food safety drive across Maharashtra under the ‘Safe Food, Safe Drug, Safe Maharashtra’ campaign launched on the directions of Food Safety Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe.
86 ESTABLISHMENTS INSPECTED IN STATEWIDE DRIVE
During the special inspection drive on August 13, FDA officials inspected 86 establishments across Maharashtra, including food businesses and online delivery platforms such as Zepto, Blinkit and Instamart.
The department said operations at one establishment were ordered to be halted immediately, while 60 improvement notices were issued. Fourteen food business licences were also suspended with immediate effect — five each for Blinkit and Zepto, two for Instamart, and one each for Bhagwati Store and Swinsta ENT Pvt Ltd.
At one of the raided stores, cockroaches were found nesting and moving on the racks used to store food packets.
ACTION AGAINST MILK PRODUCTS, BANNED FOOD ITEMS
The drive also targeted violations involving milk and milk products. The FDA seized 698 kg of milk products valued at Rs 34,302 during the inspections. Officials also seized another 1,270 kg of food items, including milk products, bakery products and edible oil, valued at approximately Rs 1.29 lakh.
In a separate crackdown on banned food products such as pan masala and gutkha, the FDA registered 10 FIRs related to their sale, distribution and transportation. Nine people were arrested and banned stock worth Rs 46.76 lakh was seized.
The total value of seized goods, including banned and other food items, was put at Rs 46,89,603.
109 HOTELS, RESTAURANTS AND DHABAS INSPECTED
The food safety department also inspected 109 hotels, restaurants and dhabas during the special drive. Of these, 49 establishments were served improvement notices, while the food licences of four establishments were suspended.
The Pune division separately carried out inspections between August 11 and August 14 at hotels, restaurants, e-commerce establishments and dairies. The FDA said licences or registrations of 16 establishments were immediately suspended after significant hygiene deficiencies and violations of food safety norms were detected.
Among the Pune establishments facing action were Fortune Enterprises (Hotel Sayaji) in Lonavala, Hotel Chul Mutton in Lohegaon, Simply South in Bhosari, Hotel Pawan in Kolhapur, Rajesh Chinese in Sangli, Domino’s Pizza and Pizza Hut in Karad, and the Camp Burger King.
JBM Hospitality, which operates a canteen at HDFC Bank in Wanwadi, Pune, was directed to stop operations for allegedly functioning without a licence.
ZEPTO, BLINKIT FACILITIES ALSO FLAGGED
Among the facilities found non-compliant were those operated by Blinkit Commerce Private Limited in Ghatkopar and Zepto in Lokhandwala. The Ghatkopar Blinkit facility scored 34 out of 74 marks (46 per cent) during inspection and was declared non-compliant.
At Zepto’s Lokhandwala facility, officials found inadequate temperature control for perishable food, no ante-room for frozen products, poor warehouse layout and improper segregation of food, non-food items and hazardous substances. The facility scored 65 out of 140 marks (47 per cent) and was also declared non-compliant.
The findings show that the FDA's scrutiny is extending beyond restaurants and traditional food outlets to quick-commerce warehouses and online food businesses involved in storing and handling food products.
FDA WARNS OF STRICT ACTION
The FDA said the special inspections are aimed at ensuring that food businesses comply with prescribed hygiene and food safety standards.
Officials have warned that establishments found violating the Food Safety and Standards Act and related regulations will face action, including improvement notices, suspension of licences and directions to stop operations.

headline: SAD leader Sukhbir Singh Badal's first reaction to attack in Maharashtra: 'Not afraid, never will be'
full_text:
SAD leader Sukhbir Singh Badal's first reaction to attack in Maharashtra: 'Not afraid, never will be'
SAD leader Sukhbir Singh Badal said, "Here in Nanded Sahib tenth Master Guru Gobind Singh ji have saved my life".
Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal, after being discharged from a hospital in Maharashtra, said he was not afraid and would continue to uphold his family's legacy of maintaining peace and communal harmony in Punjab.
Thanking the Almighty for saving his life during two attacks, Badal said, "Here in Nanded Sahib tenth Master Guru Gobind Singh ji have saved my life". He added that I am “not afraid and never will be.”
Badal said the SAD stood for peace and communal harmony in Punjab and across the country. Referring to his father and former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal, he said the two had worked to maintain peace in the state and that he would continue on the same path.
He also alleged that some forces were trying to disturb peace in Punjab and said he was prepared to make any sacrifice to protect it.
Badal was attacked at around 1.45 pm on Thursday inside a gurdwara near Maharashtra's Nanded district. He was rushed to a hospital, where he received two to three stitches on his right hand.
SAD says Badal is in ‘Chardi Kala’
Soon after the incident, the Shiromani Akali Dal said Badal was doing well and remained in “Chardi Kala”, or high spirits, after the attack in Nanded. SAD spokesperson Arshdeep Singh Kler said the attacker, who was dressed in Nihang attire, tried to target the SAD chief but was stopped by his security personnel.
Badal, who is a Z-category protectee, suffered a minor injury to his arm and was taken to a hospital for treatment. Kler said he was “completely fine” and in “Chardi Kala”. A local official in Nanded said Badal received two to three stitches on his hand.
Kler said Maharashtra Police would investigate the incident, as it occurred in the state, and determine whether there was any conspiracy behind the attack.
The SAD spokesperson also alleged that “panthic leaders” were being repeatedly targeted and said, “Some 'panth virodhi' (anti-panth) forces are hatching such conspiracies.”
Nanded attack
The man accused of attacking Badal has been identified as 63-year-old Jaspal Singh, who hails from Pune, police said. He had been serving as a sewadar at Gurdwara Mata Sahib Devan Ji Mugat for the past two years, according to a senior police official.
Nanded Superintendent of Police Neelabh Rohan said a case of attempt to murder had been registered against Singh under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
The attack took place while Badal was at the gurdwara, around 15 km from Nanded city. He was subsequently taken to hospital for treatment.
The incident marks the second attack on Badal in two years. In December 2024, he survived an assassination attempt outside the Golden Temple in Amritsar when a gunman opened fire at him from close range.

headline: Odisha appoints Vinaytosh Mishra as acting DGP amid police chief selection row
full_text:
Odisha appoints Vinaytosh Mishra as acting DGP amid police chief selection row
Vinaytosh Mishra will take charge as Odisha DGP on August 16 as the Supreme Court hears a plea challenging the state’s police chief selection process.
The Odisha government on Friday appointed senior IPS officer Vinaytosh Mishra as acting director general of police (DGP).
Mishra, currently director general of the Crime Branch and Criminal Investigation Department, will take additional charge as DGP after incumbent Y.B. Khurania retires on August 16, the state government said in a statement.
“After the retirement of incumbent DGP YB Khurania on August 16, Vinaytosh Mishra, DGP, CID, Crime Branch will remain in additional charge of DGP (Head of Police Force) until further orders,” the government said.
The appointment comes a day after the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) assured the Supreme Court that it would defer its selection process for the state’s next police chief until August 18. The court is hearing a public interest litigation challenging the state government’s selection process.
“Any backdoor entry is not acceptable…UPSC must not finalise till the next date of hearing,” a bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant had said.
The court’s intervention followed an application alleging that the Odisha government was attempting to circumvent the Supreme Court’s prescribed procedure for the appointment of DGPs by introducing officers who were not part of the original list of three senior-most eligible officers sent to the UPSC.
The dispute centres on the procedure laid down by the Supreme Court in the Prakash Singh case. In February 2026, the court reiterated that states must follow the prescribed process for appointing DGPs, under which the UPSC prepares a panel of eligible officers and the state government selects the police chief from that panel.
The court has also said eligibility criteria cannot be bypassed because the number of eligible officers is limited. Under the framework, the apex-level DGP post in Level 17 is to be filled from among officers holding DGP-level posts in Level 16.
Senior advocate P. Chidambaram, appearing for the petitioner in the PIL, told the SC that the state government had breached the Supreme Court’s directions by promoting an additional director general of police and seeking to include the officer among candidates for the DGP post.
“The State of Odisha is breaching the Prakash Singh judgment,” Chidambaram told the court, referring to the Supreme Court’s landmark 2006 ruling that laid down procedures for police reforms and appointments of state police chiefs.
Odisha’s Advocate General opposed the PIL, warning that Khurania’s impending retirement could leave Odisha with an acting DGP if the selection was not completed.
“The DGP is set to retire ... if no appointment happens, we will have an Acting DGP,” the Advocate General told the bench. Subsequently, the UPSC, which was to meet on Thursday for choosing the new DGP, deferred the meeting.
Chief Justice Kant said that if the court found that its directions had been violated, it could set aside the appointment. Justice Bagchi, who was also on the bench, said the court was not concerned with the credentials of the petitioner’s client while considering whether its earlier orders had been followed.

headline: 'Child surviving on streets can't…': Delhi HC upholds conviction of man who sodomised 11-yr-old
full_text:
'Child surviving on streets can't…': Delhi HC upholds conviction of man who sodomised 11-yr-old
The judge modified the trial court's 20-year jail term to 10 years on the grounds that at the time of the offence, the corresponding sentence was 10 years.
The Delhi High Court has refused to interfere with the conviction of a man accused of sodomising an 11-year-old homeless boy, asserting that a child surviving on the streets cannot be expected to share details of date, time or clothing with the same accuracy as a witness living in a settled environment.
In a judgment passed on the accused's appeal on August 10, Justice Chandrasekharan Sudha upheld the trial court's August 2025 decision to convict him under Section 377 (unnatural offences) IPC and Section 6 (Punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault) of the POCSO Act.
The judge, however, modified the trial court's 20-year jail term to ten years on the grounds that at the time of the offence, the corresponding sentence was a decade.
ALSO READ: Delhi airport, high court, other sensitive locations receive bomb threat ahead of Independence Day
Section 6 POCSO Act became punishable with a minimum term of 20 years with effect from August 16, 2019.
The minor alleged that in November 2016, the accused sexually assaulted him while he was sleeping under a railway bridge at Kashmere Gate.
The incident was reported on the police helpline by some social workers, who had organised a programme in the area for providing free medical aid to the homeless, after the minor informed them about it.
The accused's counsel claimed that he had been falsely implicated. He argued that the prosecution failed to prove the boy was under 12 years of age and that there were several inconsistencies in his testimony regarding the incident and the dress he was wearing.
Rejecting the defence, the court said the boy's inability to state his exact age or date of birth or other specific details would not benefit the accused.
It said although in his testimony, the survivor claimed that he was about 15 years of age, given his social background, it was "unrealistic" to expect him to know his exact age.
The school record showed his date of birth as October 12, 2005, making him 11 years old at the time of the incident, the court observed.
The court stated that the accused's identity, the place of incident, the nature of the sexual assault and the sequence of events immediately after the incident remained substantially unchanged throughout all versions testified by the minor boy.
The discrepancies with respect to the exact time, the description and colour of the clothes worn by the boy, the precise order in which the NGO workers and the police reached the spot, etc, do not "detract from the consistent allegation of forcible anal intercourse", it stated.
The court also held that the absence of any external injuries on the minor was not sufficient to discredit his otherwise "consistent and trustworthy testimony".
"The evidence on record reveals that PW1 was a homeless child living on the streets and earning his livelihood by rag-picking. In such circumstances, it would be unrealistic to expect him to possess exact knowledge of his date of birth or to narrate every detail of the incident with mathematical accuracy," observed the court.
"Minor discrepancies, omissions or improvements, which do not go to the root of the prosecution case, are natural consequences of normal errors of observation and memory, particularly when a child witness recounts a traumatic incident after a lapse of time. It must also be borne in mind that PW1 was a homeless child surviving on the streets and engaged in rag-picking and cannot be expected to give precise particulars regarding dates, time or clothing with the same degree of accuracy as a witness living in a settled environment," the court said.

headline: A group of concerned citizens, including writers, academics, filmmakers, activists and public figures, has written an open letter to the Chief Justice of India, urging him to intervene in the continued incarceration of activists Umar Khalid and Sharj...
full_text:
A group of concerned citizens, including writers, academics, filmmakers, activists and public figures, has written an open letter to the Chief Justice of India, urging him to intervene in the continued incarceration of activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam.
The two, accused in a larger conspiracy case related to the 2020 North-East Delhi riots, have been in custody for nearly six years.
“As Indian citizens, we have been deeply concerned about the life and liberty of those against whom special laws like the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act have been unjustly invoked, simply to keep them behind bars for inordinate lengths of time,” the letter, undersigned by more than 100 people, including Arundhati Roy, Amitav Ghosh, Prakash Raj, Ramachandra Guha, Yogendra Yadav, Rana Ayyub, Swara Bhasker and Jayati Ghosh, said.
The signatories, who wrote to CJI on the eve of India’s 80th Independence day, invoked the Supreme Court’s 2021 judgment in K.A. Najeeb, which held that prolonged incarceration can violate an accused person’s fundamental right to a speedy trial under Article 21 of the Constitution. The judgment emphasised that stringent bail provisions under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) cannot justify indefinite detention when there is no likelihood of the trial concluding within a reasonable period.
The signatories also pointed out to the CJI’s recent lecture in Sweden in which he himself referred to the K.A. Najeeb judgment and highlighted the Supreme Court’s power to grant bail where prolonged incarceration infringes the right to a speedy trial. They also noted that the CJI was also the part of the three-judge bench that delivered the landmark ruling.
Drawing comparison between Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam’s case case and K.A. Najeeb, the signatories said that the prosecution in the Delhi riots larger conspiracy case has arraigned approximately 900 witnesses, compared with 276 prosecution witnesses in K.A. Najeeb. They highlighted that the trial in the present case has not yet begun, despite the two continuing to remain incarcerated as undertrial prisoners.
“Their bail applications have been repeatedly rejected by different courts, including by a two-judge Supreme Court bench in January 2026,” the letter read.
The signatories also referred to the Supreme Court’s May 18, 2026 judgment in Syed Iftikhar Andrabi v. National Investigation Agency, which, according to the letter, criticised the January ruling in Gulfisha Fatima v. State for denying bail and also preventing another bail application for a year. The judgment emphasised that smaller Benches must follow the law laid down by larger Benches, including the three-judge ruling in K.A. Najeeb.
The letter said the matter has since been referred to a larger Bench to consider issues including liberty and national security, while Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam remain behind bars.
“We urge your intervention to reverse this travesty of justice unfolding before our eyes,” the letter said, warning against the use of UAPA to silence critics and dissidents. It urged the CJI to ensure that “bail is the rule, jail an exception” is followed consistently, arguing that after years of incarceration, even a subsequent acquittal cannot restore the lost years of liberty.

headline: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Friday (August 14, 2026) questioned the motives behind an aborted move by the Bar Council of India to stop the professional enrolment of the National Academy of Legal Studies and Research’s (NALSAR) batch of 2026,...
full_text:
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Friday (August 14, 2026) questioned the motives behind an aborted move by the Bar Council of India to stop the professional enrolment of the National Academy of Legal Studies and Research’s (NALSAR) batch of 2026, terming it an unwarranted interference in the ongoing “dialogue” between him and the students who do not want him as the chief guest for their convocation ceremony.
“Who is the Bar Council of India (BCI) to come between the students and me? The Bar Council of India has no business here… It is a dialogue between the students and me. Why is the BCI unnecessarily interfering?” asked Chief Justice Kant, heading a three-judge Bench, during a hearing against the BCI’s actions.
The court barred the BCI from taking any coercive actions against NALSAR students and staff and gave the Council two weeks to explain its directives.
‘Campaign against CJI’
The students had written to the law university’s administration, expressing their antipathy towards inviting the Chief Justice. Their objection had followed nationwide outrage over the CJI’s oral remarks referring to certain individuals as “parasites” and “cockroaches”. The students had also found offensive the top judge’s disinclination to view videos of police brutality against students protesting the NEET-UG paper leaks in Delhi on July 20.
On August 13, BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra, who is a BJP MP and a senior advocate, wrote to the NALSAR Vice-Chancellor seeking a report identifying the persons behind the “campaign” against the CJI. The same letter prohibited State Bar Councils from enrolling any “2026-passed-out student” from NALSAR.
The letter was quickly dropped in the face of intense public criticism. A second BCI communication, scripted within just two hours of the first one, declared the “vast majority” of NALSAR students “innocent”, but retained the direction to NALSAR to inquire and submit a report on the people behind the protest. NALSAR had released a statement that it would have to look into the constitutionality of such an inquiry. The BCI eventually withdrew its letters entirely on August 14.
‘Chilling effect’
However, the withdrawal of the letters did not stop the Supreme Court from condemning the BCI. Chief Justice Kant said the fundamental right to a profession cannot be threatened for expressing dissent.
“I was involved in student activities and campaigns too,” the Chief Justice said.
The court was hearing an oral mentioning by senior advocate K. Parameshwar, appearing for two former NALSAR students, seeking an urgent hearing and judicial action against the BCI.
“By launching into a fishing expedition and seeking to set up a case of wrongdoing from a genuine expression of grievance by students on a matter internal to the university, the BCI letters create a chilling effect on the freedom of speech, expression, and association among students. Legal education creates the space for questioning and courageous expression of one’s ideas,” Mr. Parameshwar submitted.
‘BCI has no jurisdiction’
The court barred the BCI from taking coercive actions against NALSAR students, faculty, and administrators on the basis of the incidents mentioned in the BCI letters issued on August 13. The court gave the BCI two weeks to file an affidavit explaining its actions.
The petition said neither the Advocates Act, 1961 nor the BCI’s Rules of Legal Education permit the BCI to regulate students’ conduct or direct universities to “inquire” against them. The BCI’s powers extended only to advocates and for prescribing standards of legal education, it said.
“The BCI has no jurisdiction over the admission of persons as advocates on the rolls of the State Bar Councils,” the petition said.
BCI overreach
Mr. Parameshwar submitted that the BCI letters virtually attempted to add ‘expression of dissent’ as a ground for disqualification for enrolment as an advocate. A person can be stopped from enrolment only in cases of conviction for offences involving moral turpitude or under the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, or in the case of dismissal from government service on a charge involving moral turpitude, he said.
The petition compared the current overreach of the BCI to an earlier episode when it had tried to bar anyone above 45 years of age from enrolling as an advocate. The Supreme Court had struck down that rule introduced by the BCI in a 1995 judgment in Indian Council of Legal Aid & Advice versus Bar Council of India.
Mr. Parameshwar said the BCI’s attempt to expose the identities of those who wrote to the university administration against inviting the CJI for the convocation was a violation of protected speech under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. He said even the modification and ultimate withdrawal of the letters would not suffice to undo the “chilling effect” caused by the actions of the BCI.
“Passing a blanket direction prohibiting all State Bar Councils from enrolling any 2026-passed-out student of NALSAR Law University without hearing a single student is inherently arbitrary and in stark violation of the principles of natural justice,” the senior counsel contended.

headline: Lt Gen Arvind Mahajan (Retd): ‘We were hailed as the generation of New India’
full_text:
Lt Gen Arvind Mahajan (Retd): ‘We were hailed as the generation of New India’
Serving during the Kargil War, he says, was among the most defining experiences of his military career.
Lieutenant General Arvind Mahajan (retired) takes pride in being part of a generation born into a free nation, one that held the promise of a newly independent India, witnessed its remarkable journey, and helped shape its transformation.
“While Gen Z may be the flavour of the times today, back then, it was we who were hailed as the generation of a New India. We were destined to witness and participate in the journey of a country determined to build its own future,” he says, sipping hot coffee in the basement of his Gurugram home on a rain-soaked afternoon.
Born on December 24, 1947, he retired in 2007 as director general of the Indian Army’s Corps of Electronics and Mechanical Engineers (EME), bringing down the curtain on a distinguished military career spanning almost four decades.
Also Read |‘Beginning of another’: How Hindustan Times reported freedom on August 15, 1947
A quiet corner in the basement serves as his study, where a fading photograph from his days as a cadet at the National Defence Academy sits alongside a portrait of him in the uniform of a three-star general; the commissioning parchment issued by the President in the late 1960s displayed beside a photograph of him receiving a military honour from the Supreme Commander decades later.
“It is not a study. I’d say it is a museum, a window into a life lived alongside a nation on the move,” says Mahajan, flipping through the pages of a book titled “Techno Warriors of the Indian Army: Corps of Electronics and Mechanical Engineers in Operations.” Published in 2007 during his tenure at the helm of the EME, the book chronicles the Corps’ role and contributions since Independence, from the 1947-48 Kashmir operations to the 1999 Kargil War.
The retired three-star general sports a black T-shirt commemorating the NDA’s 75th anniversary, a reminder of an institution founded in the early years of independent India and one that has since shaped generations of military leaders. For Mahajan, the milestone – marked in 2024 – also reflects the transformation India has undergone over the past eight decades.
Also Read | What's the quickest path to Inevitable India?: A Wknd Independence Day special
“The India I knew as a young officer was vastly different from the India of today. My service took me to forward areas including Ladakh, Joshimath and NEFA (North-East Frontier Agency)—now Arunachal Pradesh. In those days, border areas had few roads, poor communications and limited facilities. Reaching certain locations could take days. Today, highways, tunnels, bridges and modern communication networks have transformed these regions,” he says.
Mahajan points out that India has made remarkable progress in education, healthcare, technology and economic development, which has changed lives and expanded opportunities for its people. “The transformation of the energy sector has been equally striking. From limited electricity and fuel availability, we have moved to a vast network of power plants, refineries and pipelines. Windmills, solar parks and other sources of clean energy are increasingly contributing to India’s future.”
There are things he would rather forget, too—the setbacks, struggles and difficult chapters that tested the country.
“We witnessed the harsh realities of the Partition itself, including a period of shortages, especially of food and essential supplies, when rationing was the norm rather than the exception for many years. The nation, though being the land of the Buddha and Gandhi and of the peace they preached, was compelled to undergo the trauma of several wars that were thrust upon it. I must mention that the 1962 war with China really influenced my generation. It was the reason many of us chose to join the armed forces.” The greatest change today is in national confidence, he says.
Serving during the Kargil War, he says, was among the most defining experiences of his military career. “The conflict was fought in difficult terrain and harsh weather conditions. Overcoming that challenge required courage on the front lines, along with determined leadership, coordination, logistics and national resolve. Kargil demonstrated that when the country and its armed forces act with unity and determination, even the most difficult challenge can be overcome.”
“If I must draw a parallel between the nation’s growth and my own career, it would be in the field of technology. I was commissioned into the Corps of Electrical and Mechanical Engineers. It evolved into the Corps of Electronics and Mechanical Engineers. That change in name itself reflects a transition in technology.”
The EME is a technical Corps that provides maintenance and repair service to fighting formations for a range of equipment used in warfare. “At the time we were commissioned, understanding the functioning of a radio set was an early challenge. Today, our professionals handle complex computer systems with ease. And that is precisely how our nation too has evolved…from an importer of anything related to technology in its early days to a leading software developer. We now make complex missiles and gun systems and have demonstrated our capacity to reach the Moon and Mars. Each of these achievements gives immense joy to my generation.”
As someone born in 1947, does Independence Day hold a special meaning for him?
“Absolutely. My life has run parallel to the journey of independent India. Having served in the army for nearly four decades, Independence Day reminds me of the sacrifices that secured our freedom and of our continuing responsibility to protect it.”
He says the country’s defining military milestones include a firm and decisive response to terror, as demonstrated by Operation Sindoor and other strikes in Pakistan; improved border infrastructure; modernisation of the armed forces through advanced weapons, surveillance, communications and technology; a decisive push towards self-reliance in defence sector; and the growing role of women in the military.
“What is perhaps most important about our armed forces is, ironically, not a milestone at all. It is their steadfast commitment to remaining apolitical and professional, in letter and spirit—unlike the armed forces of several nations that gained independence alongside or around the same time as us.”

headline: Indian Army to get loitering munitions worth ₹1,577 crore
full_text:
Indian Army to get loitering munitions worth ₹1,577 crore
The defence ministry signed two contracts with Tata Advanced Systems and Nibe for loitering munitions and equipment to boost Army’s precision-strike.
The defence ministry on Friday signed two contracts worth ₹1,577 crore with Tata Advanced Systems Ltd and Nibe Pvt Ltd for loitering munitions (or kamikaze drones) and associated equipment to boost the Indian Army’s precision-strike capabilities.
“The loitering munition system is critical equipment that can enhance the capability of artillery regiments and boost the overall operational effectiveness of the Indian Army,” the ministry said.
Also Read | Military plans to add raft of weapons next year to bolster combat readiness
Why ₹1,577 crore contracts?
This comes as the army plans to induct tens of thousands of locally made unmanned aerial systems and loitering munitions over the next five years to boost its battlefield capabilities, given the growing impact of these systems on military operations and how they have reshaped modern warfare, as visible in ongoing global conflicts, including the US-Israel war with Iran.
“Procured from Indian vendors under the ‘Buy Indian’ scheme through a fast-track procedure, this initiative will further strengthen the vision of self-reliance in defence,” the ministry added while announcing the two deals.
The army’s requirement spans 80 different types of unmanned systems for specific roles, including intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, precision strikes, munition dropping, air defence, jamming, mine warfare, data relay and logistics, according to a Technology Roadmap for Unmanned Aerial Systems and Loitering Munitions unveiled in April. Defence minister Rajnath Singh earlier said India must take steps to position itself as a global hub for drone manufacturing by 2030.
Also Read | New weapons, specialist units to boost army’s capabilities
What do systems include?
The systems required by the army for surveillance include high-altitude long-endurance UAS (unmanned aerial systems), medium-altitude long-endurance UAS, high-altitude pseudo-satellites and unmanned air littoral systems (UALs) for long-, medium- and short-range surveillance, according to the roadmap.
The army is seeking loitering munitions to strike at long, medium and short ranges, drone swarms (for surveillance and strike), and FRV (first-person-view) drones with strike capability. It also wants to deploy unmanned systems in special roles, including hunter-killer-configured UALs and systems with guided/unguided bombs.
The roadmap aligns with India’s plans to raise a drone force under another roadmap, Defence Forces Vision 2047, which was released in March.

headline: Karnataka HC rejects actor Darshan's plea over Renukaswamy murder approver
full_text:
Karnataka HC rejects actor Darshan's plea over Renukaswamy murder approver
The Karnataka High Court dismissed actor Darshan's plea against a sessions court order in the Renukaswamy murder case. The ruling reinforces that co-accused cannot contest another accused's bid to become an approver.
The Karnataka High Court on Thursday dismissed a petition filed by actor Darshan, an accused in the Renukaswamy murder case, challenging a sessions court order that had refused to let him file objections to a co-accused's plea to turn approver.
Darshan, who is the second accused in the case, had sought to quash the August 10 order of the 58th Additional City Civil and Sessions Court in Bengaluru. The plea before the sessions court related to an application filed by co-accused Pradosh Rao, the 14th accused in the case, seeking pardon under Section 306 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, and permission to become an approver.
Justice M Nagaprasanna passed the order after hearing senior advocate Hasmath Pasha for Darshan and Special Public Prosecutor P Prasanna Kumar. The High Court made it clear that a co-accused has no right to make submissions when a court is considering an application by another accused seeking pardon and approval to become an approver under Section 306 of the CrPC.
The court also took note of the prosecution's submission that the High Court had earlier dealt with the rights of a co-accused under Section 306 of the CrPC. It further noted that the Supreme Court had already dismissed a petition challenging an order passed in connection with the Yogeshgouda murder case involving legislator Vinay Kulkarni.
Dismissing Darshan's petition, the High Court said the order passed in the Yogeshgouda murder case on granting approval to an approver, and the subsequent proceedings in that matter, would also apply to the present case. Darshan and his friend, actor Pavithra Gowda, are among the 17 accused in the Renukaswamy murder case, and he is currently in jail under judicial custody.

headline: The decision follows a campaign by the students againsts the participation of CJI Surya Kant in the convocation ceremony.
full_text:
The decision follows a campaign by the students againsts the participation of CJI Surya Kant in the convocation ceremony.
NEW DELHI: If the directive was unusual, the withdrawal was dramatic.Bar Council of India (BCI) on Thursday took back its communication â hours after issuing it â to Hyderabad-based Nalsar University of Law that said those who organised opposition to the invitation to CJI Surya Kant for the instituteâs convocation would not be enrolled as advocates.In a fresh communication late evening, BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra said the council had âthoroughly discussed and deliberatedâ on his earlier letter to Nalsarâs vice-chancellor and state bar council secretaries and modified its direction.BCI â the statutory regulating body for legal education and profession â is of the unanimous view that, according to the âlatest reportâ, vast majority of Nalsarâs 2026 graduating students were innocent and âwere not inclined to take part in the move of disrespectâ, he said. However, Mishra said, âIt has been further reported by some reliable sources that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in instigating innocent students.â BCI will wait for the âinquiry reportâ from Nalsar, he said in the fresh letter, which he posted on his X handle.SCBA president Vikas Singh reacted sharply to BCI chairpersonâs earlier letter to Nalsar by condemning its âarbitraryâ decision to stall enrolment of law graduates from the university.
Singh said the decision is illegal, disproportionate and fundamentally unsustainable. However, he said he did not support the section of students who opposed the invitation to the CJI.This story continues on page 10 in the newspaper. For your reading convenience we have added it below.Disrespectful law students are a liability, says BCI chiefIn his earlier letter to one of Indiaâs top law schools, Mishra had sought a âfactual reportâ about the persons instrumental in âintimidation of a constitutional functionaryâ by initiating, organising or mobilising the campaign against participation of CJI at the convocation ceremony.BCI chairperson had said, âTill further orders, no student of Nalsar University of Law, who has obtained law degree in the year 2026, shall be enrolled by any state bar council as an advocate.â He said a final decision on this issue would be taken on Aug 19 after receiving a report from VC.The council had requested Nalsar to differentiate between persons who have merely signed or supported the representations from those who organised or coordinated the campaign and those who proposed or mobilised an actual boycott, obstruction or disruption. âBCI does not, at this stage, record that any person stands disqualified from enrolment under Section 24A (of Advocates Act) merely on account of participation in the aforesaid representation or campaign,â Mishra had said in his first letter.TOI on Aug 10 had reported that a section of students at Nalsar had requested the university to reconsider inviting CJI Kant for its upcoming convocation taking exception to CJIâs remarks during the hearing on alleged police excesses against student protestersâ march to Parliament on July 20. The petitioner wanted the CJI-led bench to go through the video footage of police action. CJI turned down the plea saying he did not have time to watch videos.The university has not yet finalised the date of convocation, for which the CJI had been traditionally invited as the chief guest.In his first communication, the BCI chief had said, âA student of Law, having no regard or respect for the highest judicial office of the country, is not expected to be a responsible or sensible advocate, teacher or a judge. Such persons shall always be a liability on the profession. Such conduct reflects adversely upon the personâs suitability for entry into or association with the legal profession and is inconsistent with the dignity, discipline and ethical standards of the legal profession.
â He said, âAs per some reliable sources, there exists groupism and dirty politics among some of the academic staff and they have played a very active role in misleading, instigating and misguiding the students. This is a very serious matter. The teachers, instead of involving themselves in their teaching job, are doing nasty politics in the campus. BCI, being the regulator of Legal Education cannot be a mute spectator of such a serious situation.ââHowever, where material concerning the conduct of a particular applicant is under active statutory examination by the BCI and such examination may have a bearing upon regulatory considerations governing entry into the profession, completion of enrolment during pendency of such examination may create a fait accompli and render the statutory examination ineffective,â it had said asking the state bar councils to withhold registration of law graduates from Nalsar till further orders.

headline: Airbus has asked Air In- dia to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraftâs recent maintenance activi- ties as it continues its event assessment
full_text:
Airbus has asked Air In- dia to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraftâs recent maintenance activi- ties as it continues its event assessment
NEW DELHI: âThe elevators (control up and down movement of aircraft) and ailerons (controls left and right movement) surfaces were lost for around four seconds.â Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.âBased on analysis of the DFDR (digital flight data recorder),â Airbus found that within seven seconds between 9:32:44 am and 9:32:51 am, there was a loss of hydraulics systems â pressurised fluids which enable flight controls to move. At this point, the autopilot was disconnected and the aircraftâs nose went up (increase in pitch). All timings are in IST.The Airbus preliminary communication sent to AI on Aug 10 says âat (9:32:46 am) auto pilot 2 was disconnected, and full nose down (pitch down) input began being applied on first officer side with no direct response from the flight control surfacesâ due to the loss of hydraulics. Five seconds later, a single hydraulic system was recovered and a few seconds later the remaining two systems were back, leading to recovery of normal flight control.Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraftâs recent maintenance activities as it continues its event assessment. âSince load exceedances were detected during the sudden altitude change, (maintenance) inspections must be performed.
Please provide the inspection results once they are completed. Please provide more detailed pilot reports from the reported event clarifying what it is observed during the event,â the communication says.â...this event requires an analysis considering both aircraft systems and structural integrity, as airframe may have been affected by the movement,â it adds.While probe is on by Airbus and Franceâs accident investigator under the ambit of Indiaâs Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, several pilots are questioning why Air India decided to fly the aircraft all the way to Delhi after it had recovered from the technical events.

TNN / Aug 14, 2026, 03:17 IST

SC was hearing a plea filed by NGO '3S and Our Health Society'
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Thursday slammed the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) for not implementing its direction on 'front-of-pack warning labels' on processed food packages and said their top priority should be the health of citizens and not the interest of MNCs.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the court could not be taken for a ride. The bench said its Feb order was not merely a suggestion but a direction to FSSAI which had to be complied with. It said FSSAI was bowing down to the manufacturing industry and made it clear that if the food regulator didn't do it, the court would pass an order. It granted two weeks to FSSAI to reconsider its stance.In Feb, the court directed the Centre and the FSSAI to give top priority to the health concerns of citizens and not to the interests of multinational companies and asked it to implement a 'front-of-pack warning labels' system on processed food packages to ensure clear, front-facing symbols designed to instantly identify ingredients like sugar, salt and saturated fat, besides calories.It also rejected the Centre's contention that international standards could not be applied in India and asked whether India should remain underdeveloped.SC was hearing a plea filed by NGO '3S and Our Health Society'. The regulator informed SC consultations were held with all stakeholders in March, and a majority of industry organisations were opposed to the inclusion of 'warning labels' and favoured an approach intended to enable informed consumer decisions "without creating fear among consumers".
The court asked govt to respond within two weeks. "We have made ourselves abundantly clear that we are concerned with the health of citizens... We still impress upon the Union of India to seriously consider the suggestion and take appropriate action."

headline: Teaching job aspirants in Uttar Pradesh will run a social media campaign on August 16 to press the State government to initiate a recruitment drive for primary school teachers.
full_text:
Teaching job aspirants in Uttar Pradesh will run a social media campaign on August 16 to press the State government to initiate a recruitment drive for primary school teachers.
The aspirants alleged that the government had not conducted a major recruitment drive for primary-level teachers in more than five years, leaving lakhs of eligible candidates waiting for appointments.
“There hasn’t been a major teacher recruitment drive in Uttar Pradesh for over five years at the primary level. Millions of candidates are constantly waiting for teacher recruitment. It has been reported several times that the government will conduct recruitment, but the notification has not been issued,” said Vijay Pratap, an aspirant from Prayagraj.
The campaign, to be run across social media platforms, will seek the immediate issuance of a recruitment notification and a time-bound schedule for completing the appointment process. The organisers said they were targeting 10 million posts on X on August 16.
Several education-related social media platforms run by students and aspirants in the State have circulated the campaign announcement. “All friends should be ready and spread the information about this campaign to as many candidates as possible. Unity is our strength,” read a message that went viral on X.
The Prayagraj-based Sanyukt Pratiyogi Chhatra Hunkar Manch, an organisation of competitive examination aspirants, has also extended its support.
‘Prime years wasted’
Adarsh Tiwari, a D.El.Ed degree holder and another aspirant, said candidates had approached officials, including the Basic Education Minister and Deputy Chief Minister, but had received no assurance on recruitment.
“It has been over five years and no vacancy has come at the primary school level. People with D.El.Ed degrees are feeling helpless because of the neglect. Without appointments, what is the need for such degrees? Five years is a long time in one’s life and our prime young years are being wasted,” he said.
The Diploma in Elementary Education (D.El.Ed) is a two-year full-time teacher education programme for those seeking to teach Classes 1 to 8.
The Congress supported the proposed campaign and accused the BJP government of failing to provide employment opportunities to the State’s youth.
“The anxiety of aspirants is leading to such online campaigns. We fully stand with the youth of Uttar Pradesh,” said Abhishek Dutt, national secretary of the Congress and zonal in-charge of the Purvanchal zone.
Mr. Dutt said the party would support the aspirants in their efforts to press the government for recruitment.

Murugan, Forest Range Officer, Amirthi zoo, said.
Officials said that the zoo has been classified as a mini-zoo since its inception in 1967. Grading of zoos is done in terms of total area, total number of enclosures and annual revenue generation.
Currently, the zoo is spread across 25 hectares of land at the foothills of Jawadhu Hills and has 17 enclosures, mostly reptiles and peacocks. The zoo remains open between 8.30 a.m. and 5 p.m. on all days except on Tuesdays.
During the inspection, Collector Ms. Alex also advised zoo officials to make efforts to acquire additional forest land to increase the total zoo area, as it could enable the Central Zoo Authority (CZA) to give a nod to have more wild species, including carnivores for educational purposes.
At present, Amirthi Zoo includes Thellai and Puthur Reserve Forests in Jawadhu Hills. It also has waterfalls, birds, snakes, porcupines, crocodiles, white peacocks and star tortoises. Among them, spotted deer formed the majority of species in the zoo as their numbers grew to 150. A spacious lawn, children park and an interpretation centre are other attractions.
On an average, the zoo registers a footfall of 350-400 visitors every day. Three years ago, VOC Park Zoo in Coimbatore gave mugger crocodiles, star tortoises, and rat snakes to Amirthi Zoo after the Coimbatore Zoo was closed. Before it, the zoo got a Sambar Deer and a few pelicans from Vandalur Zoo in 2019.

headline: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) on Thursday assured the Supreme Court that it will not convene a meeting to finalise the selection of Director General of Police for the State of Odisha till the next apex court hearing on August 18.

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) on Thursday assured the Supreme Court that it will not convene a meeting to finalise the selection of Director General of Police for the State of Odisha till the next apex court hearing on August 18.
A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant intervened in a petition, represented by senior advocate P. Chidambaram, alleging that the Odisha DGP selection process was in violation of the apex court’s Prakash Singh judgment. It alleged that the Odisha government was trying to include a junior officer in the list of candidates.
A submission was made before the Bench that the UPSC meeting was scheduled to be held later in the day (August 13).
Mr. Chidambaram alleged that an officer was given promotion just a day back, preempting the Supreme Court hearing, so that he could be included in the list of candidates for the DGP post.
The Bench had also sought assistance from senior advocate Raju Ramachandran, the amicus curiae in the Prakash Singh matter.
The court, in a 2006 judgment in the Prakash Singh case, had made it clear that the office of DGP should be divorced from political or other external pressures.
It had invoked its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to direct that DGPs must be selected by State governments from among the three seniormost and meritorious officers empanelled by the UPSC. The court had thrown out the “concept” of acting DGPs. It had held that State police chiefs should have a minimum fixed tenure of two years.
Subsequent apex court orders in July 2018 and March 2019 detailed the appointments mechanism, which included the State concerned sending a proposal to the UPSC three months ahead of the retirement of the incumbent DGP. The UPSC would prepare a panel of suitable officers. The State would appoint one of the empanelled officers as DGP “immediately”.

headline: 32 million population, 4 million more homes: Inside Delhi's 2047 master plan
full_text:
32 million population, 4 million more homes: Inside Delhi's 2047 master plan
The population projection of 32 million for 2047 means that it will grow 10 million from what it is estimated to be right now.
The Capital’s population will likely touch 32 million by 2047 and require nearly four million additional houses, triple the current power generation capacity and double the current solid waste management capability, projections in the Master Plan for Delhi (MPD)-2047 say.
The plan — seen by HT, which sets out a long-term framework for the Capital’s housing, mobility, infrastructure, environment and economic development — was approved by the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) on Wednesday.
It will now be sent to the Union ministry of housing and urban affairs (MoHUA) for final approval and subsequent notification.
Also read: New master plan to allow commercial development in 70 peripheral villages
The plan outlined infrastructure interventions – including augmenting water supplies, expanding sewage treatment capacity, improving drainage, and implementing measures – to manage a substantial increase in municipal solid waste.
Migration likely to contribute 41% of population rise
The population projection of 32 million for 2047 means that it will grow 10 million from what it is estimated to be right now.
By 2041, the document stated that the Capital’s population will be 29.2 million.
The MPD-2047 added that “migration is estimated to contribute 41% of the population increase in Delhi during the plan period”, compared to 50% in the previous 2021 plan period.
The city was expected to see a rise in its working-age population, while the share of people aged 60 and above was also projected to increase, the plan added.
Delhi's housing requirements to rise
The increase in population will necessitate a proportional rise in housing requirements. The plan estimates the housing demand for the period 2011-47 at nearly four million dwelling units, based on an average household size of 4.5 persons. In 2011 – the last year when the census was conducted – Delhi had 3.11 million houses.
The demand calculation depended on the existing housing backlog, new demand arising from population growth, replacement of obsolete housing stock and vacant housing stock.
The MPD asked for new housing units in greenfield projects and regenerating or developing existing areas such as unauthorised colonies, including Sangam Vihar, or old areas.
Also read: DDA clears Delhi 2047 plan, opens door to development in 70 villages, parts of Yamuna floodplain
The increased population is set to place significant strains on the city infrastructure and require massive capacity augmentation.
Roadmap for meeting Delhi's water requirements
On drinking water, the MPD projected Delhi’s potable water requirement to reach around 1,600 million gallons per day (MGD) by 2047.
In 2021, the city’s water supply was 935 MGD against an estimated demand of 1,380 MGD. Now, the supply capacity is 1,000 MGD and the demand is at least 1,200 MGD.
The Delhi Jal Board has projected an additional water requirement of 401 MGD by 2047 in the master plan.
To bridge the gap, the plan proposes augmenting supply by 110 MGD through medium-term interventions over the next four to five years and another 291 MGD through medium - to long-term measures over the following 10-15 years.
These measures include replacing Yamuna water currently used for irrigation with treated wastewater, procuring additional raw water from Uttar Pradesh and developing upstream storage projects at Renukaji, Lakhwar and Kishau dams that are currently under construction.
“The plan also says achieving the augmentation targets will require coordinated efforts with neighbouring states, particularly Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh, along with facilitation by the Centre,” said an official aware of the matter.
On sewage treatment, the MPD said the infrastructure will need significant expansion.
The city currently has an installed sewage treatment capacity of 814 MGD and treats 744 MGD of wastewater.
By 2047, the plan proposes increasing the capacity to around 1,285 MGD, equivalent to 80% of the projected water supplied to the city.
The plan also identified gaps in sewer connectivity and untreated sewage entering drains as key infrastructure concerns.
Of the 22 major drains in Delhi, 11 have already been intercepted to prevent untreated effluent from reaching the Yamuna.
It proposed 28 decentralised treatment plants along all drains, along with decentralised wastewater treatment and interceptor sewer systems along smaller drains in areas where conventional sewer lines cannot be laid.
Waste generation to double in 20 years
Municipal solid waste generation is expected to almost double over the next two decades.
The master plan estimated that the national capital will generate around 13,500 tonnes per day (TPD) of municipal solid waste by the end of 2026, which will rise to 25,764 TPD by 2047.
“The existing landfill sites at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla have already exceeded their capacity. The plan notes that Delhi is flattening legacy landfills through biomining, with the process aimed at segregating, processing and clearing accumulated waste,” the official cited above added.
Higher electricity requirements
Electricity demand was projected to increase sharply alongside population and economic growth.
Delhi’s conventional power supply capacity was 7,161 megawatt in 2021, while renewable operational power purchase agreements accounted for another 923 MW.
The plan estimated that peak power demand could reach 25,500 MW by 2047, which is currently around 9,500 MW.
The plan called for the city to shift towards cleaner energy sources while expanding infrastructure to meet future demand.
The MPD asks for greater infrastructure requirements to address flooding and waterlogging.
It noted that the national capital’s drainage system was shaped by the Aravalli foothills, with stormwater generally moving from higher elevations in the west towards the Yamuna.
The proposed measures included rejuvenation of water bodies, using parks for rainwater harvesting, regulating solid-waste dumping in drains and preparing a Delhi Drainage Master Plan to meet requirements over the next 30 years.
What Delhi needs to meet housing requirements
Real estate experts said that meeting the housing requirement of 4 million homes by 2047 will require a substantial and skilled construction workforce.
This will create significant employment opportunities across construction, engineering, architecture and allied sectors. “Greater adoption of modern construction technologies can also improve productivity and reduce dependence on conventional labour-intensive methods. Delhi should focus on planned, high-density and efficient development, including group housing, TOD, redevelopment and affordable and mid-income housing. Greater use of modern and technology-driven construction methods will also help Delhi meet its housing requirements efficiently,” said Harsh Vardhan Bansal, President, NAREDCO Delhi.

headline: The State Health Department has ordered the rollout of ‘Samasta’, a digital platform for field-level data collection by ASHA workers and community health workers, with the aim of improving the accuracy and availability of health data.
full_text:
The State Health Department has ordered the rollout of ‘Samasta’, a digital platform for field-level data collection by ASHA workers and community health workers, with the aim of improving the accuracy and availability of health data.
The department has said that the volume of handwritten records has affected the accuracy, accessibility and analysis of the data.
Although data under various national health programmes is already collected through separate portals, the continued reliance on handwritten records at the field level has affected data quality. The new system seeks to digitise information at the point of collection itself.
485 data elements
Under Samasta, the 485 data elements currently recorded in the ASHA diary have been rationalised to 134 key data elements, with repetitive entries removed. This is expected to reduce the workload of field workers by about 75%, according to the department.
The platform can function in both online and offline modes, allowing data to be entered even in areas with limited connectivity.
Pilot in Udupi district
Samasta was initially piloted in Udupi district, where 95% of beneficiaries have been registered. The department said the pilot had shown significant improvement in data accuracy and operational efficiency.
Based on the experience of the pilot, the system will now be introduced across the State in a phased manner. The department has directed that all personnel be provided with the necessary training before implementation.
The order has also stressed the need to put in place appropriate measures to ensure data security and confidentiality while using the platform.
The department has instructed officials to train all personnel concerned and implement the Samasta digital system in phases across Karnataka.

headline: Lok Sabha productivity at 15% in Monsoon Session, among lowest in 2 decades: Data
full_text:
Lok Sabha productivity at 15% in Monsoon Session, among lowest in 2 decades: Data
The Monsoon Session ended with the Lok Sabha functioning for just 15 per cent of its scheduled time, according to PRS. The figures place it among the weakest Lok Sabha sessions since 2004 and underline persistent disruption in Parliament.
The Lok Sabha recorded one of its lowest productivity levels in more than two decades during the Monsoon session that ended on Thursday, according to data compiled by PRS Legislative Research. Among sessions since 2004, only two had lower functioning, the data showed.
PRS said the Lok Sabha functioned for 15 per cent of its scheduled time in the session, while the Rajya Sabha functioned for 33 per cent. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju, however, put the productivity figures at 19 per cent for the Lok Sabha and 39 per cent for the Rajya Sabha.
Data from the past 22 years shows sharp swings in parliamentary functioning, from sessions in which the Houses sat well beyond scheduled hours to sessions in which political confrontation took up much of the available time for business.
For the Lok Sabha, the session that has just ended ranks among the poorest in this period. At 15 per cent, it matches the Winter session of 2016 and is ahead only of Winter 2010 and Winter 2013, when the House functioned for five per cent and eight per cent of its scheduled time, respectively, according to data shared by PRS with PTI.
PRS, an independent, not-for-profit group that researches and tracks the functioning of Parliament and state legislatures, said it calculates House productivity by dividing the actual hours Parliament functioned in a session by the total planned sitting hours for that session. It said the figure can go beyond 100 per cent when a House sits past its scheduled hours. PRS said its historical comparisons use its own dataset to keep a common yardstick across sessions.
The worst washout since 2004 came in the Winter session of 2010, when the UPA-II government was in power. The Lok Sabha then functioned for just five per cent of its scheduled time, while the Rajya Sabha functioned for barely two per cent, as the session was stalled by the opposition's demand for a Joint Parliamentary Committee probe into alleged irregularities in the allocation of 2G spectrum.
The Winter Session of 2013 was another low point. The Lok Sabha functioned for only eight per cent of its scheduled time and the Rajya Sabha for 19 per cent amid repeated disruptions in the final months of the UPA government over the proposed bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh and the creation of Telangana, along with protests over coal block allocations.
The Budget session of 2014, the last before the general elections that brought the NDA to power, was also marked by low productivity. The Lok Sabha functioned for about 21 per cent of its scheduled time and the Rajya Sabha for 27 per cent amid turmoil over the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh.
The Congress-led United Progressive Alliance governed from May 2004 to May 2014, before the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance came to power on May 26, 2014.
The Winter session of 2016 brought Lok Sabha productivity down to the same level as the latest session, at 15 per cent, according to PRS. The Rajya Sabha then functioned for 18 per cent of its scheduled time as demonetisation became a major flashpoint between the government and the opposition.
At the other end of the scale, the Houses have on several occasions worked beyond their scheduled hours. During the UPA years, Lok Sabha productivity crossed 100 per cent in Winter 2004, Monsoon 2005 and Budget 2009. The Rajya Sabha also crossed 100 per cent in three sessions during that period.
Since 2014, Lok Sabha productivity peaked at 148 per cent in the February 2024 Budget session, followed by 145 per cent in Monsoon 2020 and 137 per cent in the 2023 Special session. The Rajya Sabha's highest level in the past 22 years was 137 per cent in the February 2024 Budget session.

headline: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Thursday virtually inaugurated infrastructure facilities for non-leather companies at a cost of ₹95.05 crore inside the SIPCOT complex at Panapakkam village in Ranipet.
full_text:
Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Thursday virtually inaugurated infrastructure facilities for non-leather companies at a cost of ₹95.05 crore inside the SIPCOT complex at Panapakkam village in Ranipet.
Officials of the Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO), which maintains the facility, said that key essential and infrastructure facilities were opened in the spacious complex. Collector Priya Ravichandran inspected the new facilities in the complex with TIDCO officials.
These new facilities will meet investors’ requirements to set up their units and the welfare of staff employed in these units. “The new SIPCOT in Panapakkam is meant only for companies related to manufacturing and non-leather sectors. The new facilities will attract more companies to set up their units in the complex,” P. Maheshwari, Project Officer (PO), SIPCOT (Ranipet), said.
Among the facilities that were inaugurated, two plug and play buildings, which were built at a cost of ₹51.80 crore, were opened for companies that function in the non-leather sector. Spread over two lakh sq.ft. of space, the new buildings have basic facilities like water and power supply, fire fighting equipment and an office.
TIDCO officials said that earlier, the government used to provide only land for companies to start their units. In contrast, the plug and play model provides customised infrastructure, including buildings, based on requirements of companies. Higher bidders will be allotted adequate space in these buildings in the coming weeks.
The Chief Minister also opened a three-storey administrative building in the complex. The new facility covers around one lakh sq.ft. and is built at a cost of ₹26 crore. A conference hall and a canteen also form a part of the facilities at the complex. For the welfare of employees, a medical centre for staff and a childcare centre were also opened.
Spread over 1,200 acres that covers Agavalam, Thuraiyur, Nedumpuli, and Peruvalayam villages, the Panapakkam SIPCOT complex got into the industrial map of the State after JLR and Tata Motors started a ₹9,000 crore car manufacturing plant in the complex. It will manufacture 2.5 lakh vehicles annually over the next 5–7 years for domestic and international markets. The 470 acre plant, which was inaugurated in February this year, is expected to provide jobs for around 5,000 persons, mostly locals, and would gradually increase to 25,000 persons in the next five years.
TIDCO officials said that remaining space in the complex has been allocated to set up a ₹400 crore footwear manufacturing park that would generate around 20,000 jobs, mostly for women. It will also enable leather manufacturers in the region to reduce the import of raw materials like soles, heels and synthetic materials from China and solve logistical issues. EOM

How to purchase tickets for Delhi parade?
Deep Dive
Tickets for the Independence Day Parade are usually available for booking online through the government's AAMANTRAN portal. Those wishing to attend the event need only follow the usual ticket booking process listed below.
STEP 1: Open the official Aamantran portal. It's advisable to avoid third-party apps or website links apart from the official governmental portal for user safety concerns.
STEP 2: Select the ‘Book your Tickets Here’ option and register your mobile number if not done already. If you are an active user of the portal, you need only log in.
STEP 3: Select ‘Independence Day 2026’ as the event from the drop-down menu option on the ‘Book Ticket’ tab.
STEP 4: Switch to the ‘Guest List’ tab. Input personal details and document verification credentials for each individual attendee. Add each one of them as a guest in the list. You may be required to add a picture of your government ID as well so make sure you have such documents on hand while booking. Make sure you are thorough and careful in this process for successful identity verification.

STEP 5: Switch back to the ‘Book Ticket’ tab and select the number of tickets you wish to book for the event. For each attendee, you must also select a ticket category and enclosure group.

• General-  ₹20
• Standard- ₹100

STEP 6: Proceed with completing your payment for the purchase via debit/credit cards or UPI.

Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren on Thursday strongly opposed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which seeks to restrict States’ powers to levy taxes on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands.
The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on Wednesday while the Rajya Sabha cleared it on Thursday, completing the parliamentary approval process. The Bill will become a law after receiving the President’s assent.
Calling the legislation a “black Bill” and an injustice to the people of Jharkhand, Mr. Soren warned of a massive agitation against the Centre’s move. “The entire nation will witness. In haste, the Central government passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 in both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, effectively tying Jharkhand’s hands and feet,” he wrote on X.
Jharkhand holds about 40% of the country’s total minerals.
“It is a severe blow to their development and future. Jharkhand will not tolerate this stepmotherly treatment. In Jharkhand, schemes providing social security to millions – such as the Maiya Samman Yojana, Abua Awas Yojana, pensions, education, health, and others – will be on the verge of closure. The Jharkhand Mukti Morcha strongly opposes this,” the Chief Minister said.
Mr. Soren added that there will be fierce opposition to the move in “every district, every block, every panchayat, every town”.
“If the Central government does not come to its senses and fails to restore to Jharkhand and its people their rights and entitlements, Jharkhand will not shy away from taking decisive and historic decisions either,” he said.

headline: Kanpur widow alleges SBI staff stole her Rs 50 lakh jewellery from locker
