Kanpur widow alleges SBI staff stole her Rs 50 lakh jewellery from locker
A Kanpur widow has accused SBI staff of emptying her bank locker of jewellery worth about Rs 50 lakh. The FIR has put bank locker security and record handling under police scrutiny.
A case of alleged theft of jewellery from a bank locker has surfaced in Kanpur, with a widow claiming that ornaments worth about Rs 50 lakh went missing from her locker at a State Bank of India branch. Police have registered an FIR against the branch manager and some unidentified staff members.
The complaint was filed by Rashmi Arora, who said she was allotted locker number 23 in 2003 when she opened a savings account at the then State Bank of Travancore branch. After her husband died, she moved to Lucknow and did not operate the locker for several years.
Arora said that when she visited the Swaroop Nagar branch around four months ago, she was told that the erstwhile State Bank of Travancore had merged with SBI. She alleged that even after the merger, locker charges continued to be deducted from her account, but she was initially not allowed to inspect the locker.
According to her complaint, bank officials confirmed her locker number on July 21 after she deposited the locker charges. She said she could not open the locker that day because she did not have the key with her. When she returned with the key on July 27, she allegedly found the locker completely empty.
In the FIR, Arora alleged that bank officials had first denied the existence of her locker and acknowledged it only after she produced account documents and records showing deduction of locker charges. She accused the branch manager and staff of conspiring to misappropriate the jewellery.
After the complaint reached Commissioner of Police Raghubir Lal, he ordered an investigation on August 6. Following this, Swaroop Nagar police registered an FIR on August 10 against the branch manager and unidentified employees.
Station House Officer Devendra Singh of Swaroop Nagar said police are examining the bank's records, locker-related documents and CCTV footage, and further action will be taken on the basis of the evidence. The case centres on Arora's allegation that jewellery worth around Rs 50 lakh disappeared from her SBI locker.

headline: ‘Every line of decency crossed’: Huge uproar over Rahul Gandhi's hug dig at govt's foreign policy
full_text:
‘Every line of decency crossed’: Huge uproar over Rahul Gandhi's hug dig at govt's foreign policy
Himanta Biswa Sarma said Rahul's remarks were not merely politically indecent but also an attempt to sabotage India's foreign relations.
Congress MP Rahul Gandhi's recent remarks against the government's foreign diplomacy has triggered huge uproar, with several senior BJP leaders condemning the “indecent” language.
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma accused Rahul Gandhi and the party of crossing “every line of decency” over remarks made during a Congress event involving Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.
Sarma said the remarks were not only politically indecent but also an attempt to damage India’s foreign relations. He made the comments in a post on X while reacting to Gandhi’s remarks at the Rachnatmak Congress National Convention.
Deep Dive
“Congress' dynastic leadership has once again crossed every line of decency - making objectionable remarks about a woman head of state who leads a friendly country, while women on the stage and in the audience laugh along,” Sarma said.
“This is not merely political indecency; it is also an attempt to sabotage India's foreign relations. When disrespect towards women becomes a source of amusement, it speaks volumes about the culture being encouraged,” he added.
Also Read: 'Foreign policy all about hugging?': Rahul Gandhi's jibe at Modi govt triggers row
What Rahul Gandhi said
Gandhi criticised the Narendra Modi government’s foreign policy, saying the Prime Minister’s job was to protect India’s interests rather than focus on “mere friendships” and public displays of warmth.
“You aren't just visiting a friend's house. In this role, the Prime Minister of India doesn't engage in mere friendship. They have no interest in friendship; their job is to protect the country,” Gandhi said.
“I don't know where it came from; this idea got into their heads. I don't know who put it there or where it came from, the idea that foreign policy means hugging politicians,” he added.
Gandhi then hugged Congress leader Sandeep Dikshit on stage to demonstrate his point about the Modi government’s diplomatic approach.
Dikshit subsequently asked Gandhi if he had hugged him “thinking he was Meloni (Italian PM Georgia Meloni)”, to which Gandhi replied, “I have not reached there yet.”
BJP hits back
BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan called Gandhi’s act a “shameful stunt” and accused him of making “vulgar insinuations” against Modi’s foreign policy.
“Rahul Gandhi's shameful stunt and the vulgar insinuations against PM Modi's foreign policy only reflect the third-rate, filthy politics of Rahul Gandhi. Rahul Gandhi's most uncivilised and crude antics exposed the debased, degenerated and twisted mentality of the entire Congress leadership,” Kesavan said.
He added that if Gandhi wanted to discuss foreign policy, he should first talk about Jawaharlal Nehru’s tenure as foreign minister, which he described as being “riddled” with fiascos and failures.
Also Read: Relief for Rahul Gandhi, SC quashes criminal defamation complaint in Savarkar remarks row
BJP MP and spokesperson Sambit Patra also hit out at Gandhi. “The level of Rahul Gandhi’s language and political conduct is deteriorating day by day. The kind of objectionable and indecent language used against constitutional and esteemed figures such as the country’s Prime Minister and Italy’s Head of State is shameful for any civilized democratic and political culture,”
RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha said Gandhi’s remarks should be viewed in the context of the political message he was trying to convey, but called Dikshit’s comment inappropriate.
“Look at its political message. Often, when a political message goes into the custody of language, the message veers off in another direction, but fundamentally, it was a political message, and it should be viewed in that context,” Jha said.
On Dikshit’s remark, he said, “This is entirely inappropriate, indecent. I'm not saying this just today. I've been consistently writing about this. Can't opposition be dignified, can't competition be decorous... Generally speaking, such remarks about women are not appropriate in our public life...”

headline: An apex body of an indigenous community has set the Meghalaya government a 10-day deadline to guarantee the protection of rights of landowners and farmers before paving the way for an integrated cement plant and limestone mining project in the Lum Sy...
full_text:
GUWAHATI
An apex body of an indigenous community has set the Meghalaya government a 10-day deadline to guarantee the protection of rights of landowners and farmers before paving the way for an integrated cement plant and limestone mining project in the Lum Syrman area of the State’s East Jaintia Hills district.
The ₹1,800-crore project has been controversial since May, when opposition from a section of local stakeholders forced the district authorities to call off public hearings.
On Thursday (August 13, 2026), a Jaiñtia National Council (JNC) team submitted a memorandum to Chief Minister Conrad K. Sangma, seeking immediate government intervention into the proposed 217.394-hectare limestone project of Shree Cement Limited in Lum Syrman. The organisation’s general secretary, Wanshwa Suting, led the team.
“The rights of the landowners and farmers of Sutnga and Nongkhlieh Elakas (traditional administrative units) must be protected and preserved before any further irreversible step is allowed in favour of the proposed mining project,” the JNC said.
It said the customary, possession, cultivation, and user rights of the landowners and farmers of the two Elakas were connected to the Lum Syrman area.
The JNC said the issue of land “cannot simply be treated as an environmental or industrial clearance matter” without addressing the concerns raised by the locals to be affected by the project. It demanded a time-bound, transparent verification of revenue, registration, customary, cultivation, and other official records first.
The organisation also said that the livelihood of farmers “cannot be brushed aside in the name of mineral development”, and a “fair and lawful compensation for the loss (resulting from the project)” must be ensured, subject to the determination of the respective legal and customary rights.
“It seems that the State government is favouring these cement companies, even to the extent of blocking residents from attending the public hearing held on July 31. If the government is confident that everything has been done fairly and transparently, why should ordinary residents and affected landholders face obstacles in exercising their right to participate?” Mr Suting said.
The JNC clarified that its fight was not against development, but for justice, transparency, and the rights of the local stakeholders.

headline: Hapur Police on Thursday (August 13, 2026) arrested two men in connection with the death of Mohd Azeem, who succumbed to injuries in a Delhi hospital on August 04, four days after he was allegedly assaulted by kanwariyas following a road accident nea...

Hapur Police on Thursday (August 13, 2026) arrested two men in connection with the death of Mohd Azeem, who succumbed to injuries in a Delhi hospital on August 04, four days after he was allegedly assaulted by kanwariyas following a road accident near Shiva Dhaba in Garhmukhteshwar.
According to a statement by Hapur police, Lokesh, son of Kanwarpal Singh, and Shivam, son of Naresh, both residents of Bheda Khurd village under Pilkhuwa police station were arrested following Azeem’s death. They were booked for murder and rioting.

The auto-rickshaw was being driven by 19-year-old Mohd Farman and was ferrying Kanwariyas.

The case, however, has competing accounts.

headline: After N Chandrasekaran's exit, Tata trust begins search for next Tata Sons chairperson
full_text:
After N Chandrasekaran's exit, Tata trust begins search for next Tata Sons chairperson
In a statement on Thursday, Sir Dorabji Tata Trust said its trustees have passed a resolution to initiate the setting up of a panel to appoint new chairman.
Less than twenty-four hours after Tata Sons chairman N. Chandrasekaran resigned and said he won’t continue beyond 20 February 2027, when his tenure ends, the largest shareholder of Tata Sons accepted his resignation and moved to begin the process of finding his replacement, even as procedural hurdles to the exercise remain.
In a statement on Thursday, Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) thanked Chandrasekaran for his contribution to the Tata Group, and said its trustees have passed a resolution to initiate the setting up of a selection committee as soon as possible to appoint the new chairman.
“We extend our full support to Tata Sons in ensuring a smooth, timely and orderly transition of leadership, consistent with the values and long-term interests of Tata Sons and the Tata group,” the statement said.
Deep Dive
Why bid to find Chandra's successor remains stalled
Despite the start of this formal process, the formation of a selection panel to find a successor to Chandrasekaran remains stalled because another important Trust, Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT), cannot conduct any business and did not meet on Thursday.
Also read: ‘Respect his decision’: Tata Trusts on Chandrasekaran’s call to step down
A Maharashtra charity commissioner order dated 15 May currently prevents SRTT from holding board meetings or making decisions, following allegations by two of its trustees and a third complainant of wrongdoing in the Trust’s composition.
Tata Sons is majority owned by SDTT and SRTT, which hold 27.98% and 23.56% stake, respectively.
The wider Tata Trusts, including SDTT and SRTT, own 65.9% of the Tata Group holding company.
Tata Trust meeting on Thursday
Thursday saw a series of separate meetings for the boards of SDTT and seven smaller trusts affiliated with it. The meetings started at 9:30am and the last meeting ended at 6pm, according to an executive familiar with the matter.
Also read: How Tata Sons will pick N Chandrasekaran's successor and who will choose him
SDTT has six trustees—Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata, his son Neville Noel Tata, former Titan Company chief executive officer (CEO) Bhaskar Bhat, TVS Motor Corp chairman emeritus Venu Srinivasan, former defence secretary Vijay Singh, and Mumbai-based lawyer Darius Khambata.
Srinivasan and Singh attended the meeting virtually, according to the executive. Srinivasan recused himself from the other Trust meetings after the SDTT meeting.
“Chandrasekaran’s announcement yesterday not to seek a renewal changed the nature of the meeting,” the executive said, requesting anonymity.
SRTT’s board members include Noel Tata, Venu Srinivasan, Ratan Tata’s younger brother Jimmy Tata; Khambata; and Pune-based businessman and philanthropist Jehangir H.C. Jehangir. Singh stepped down from its board earlier this week.
How will the next chairman be chosen
Under Tata Sons’ articles of association, the next chairman will be appointed by a five-member selection committee. Three members are jointly nominated by SDTT and SRTT. One is nominated by the Tata Sons board, and one independent member is selected by Tata Sons. The chairman of the selection committee is chosen by SDTT and SRTT from among their three nominees.
“One option available for the Tata Trusts to fast-track this entire process is to file a writ petition before the Bombay High Court asking to intervene and direct the charity commissioner to allow them to go ahead with the setting up of a selection committee,” said senior Supreme Court lawyer H.P. Ranina.
Another Tata Group executive acknowledged that the option of seeking a legal route has not been exercised yet, as it remains hopeful of getting a favourable verdict from the Maharashtra charity commissioner.
“We have addressed all the questions asked by the commissioner,” the executive said, also requesting anonymity. “We remain hopeful we will be allowed to conduct our business soon—sometime in the coming days if not weeks.”
However, the executive added that Tata Trusts does not expect to get a favourable verdict from the charity commissioner before 18 August, when Tata Sons’ annual general meeting (AGM) is scheduled. In such a situation, the AGM would have to be adjourned for lack of quorum.
“This will mean the resolution seeking shareholder approval for dividends payable to shareholders, including Tata Trusts and SP Group, will be on hold. So, this will then impact the philanthropic spending of Tata Trusts,” said the first executive.
Chandrasekaran wrote to the six-member board of Tata Sons on Wednesday morning, stating that he would not seek a third term, which would have started on 21 February next year. Chandrasekaran, who was first appointed in February 2017 and served a second term starting in 2022, said his reappointment resolution, brought before the board of Tata Sons on 24 February, did not receive the support of one board member.
“My current tenure as the Chairman of Tata Sons comes to an end on Feb 20, 2027. Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust had unanimously resolved and recommended the extension of my next term for a period of five years, which was recorded and recommended by the Tata Sons Nomination and Remuneration Committee and the Board,” Chandrasekaran wrote in his letter on Wednesday.
“Subsequently, the resolution was tabled in the Tata Sons Board on Feb 24, 2026. However, the proposal was not carried through because one of the Board Members did not support it, and in the absence of unanimous support, I chose to defer the decision."

headline: Complainant alleges bias, state says claim baseless
full_text:
Complainant alleges bias, state says claim baseless
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked Union Public Service Commission to defer the selection of a panel of three officers from which the Odisha govt was to choose the successor of present DGP Y B Khurania, who retires on Aug 16.Appearing for applicant Jayant Das, senior advocate P Chidambaram told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that a certain ADGP was hurriedly promoted to DGP rank and included in the panel of names sent by Odisha govt to UPSC, which was against the DGP selection procedure laid down by SC in the two decade-old Prakash Singh judgement.When amicus curiae and senior advocate Raju Ramachandran said the matter required consideration, Odisha advocate general Pitambara Acharya said the state had followed Prakash Singh guidelines scrupulously and sent names of 11 DGP-rank police officers to UPSC for preparation of a panel of three-most suitable officers.âThe complainant has seven criminal cases pending against him and is a habitual offender. He might have a certain axe to grind against some officers. There is no breach of any procedure. We will present a clear picture before court,â Acharya said.
CJI Kant pointed out that none of the aggrieved officers who might have been overlooked in the choice of 11 empaneled names have complained. UPSC, through senior advocate Hrishikesh Baruah, informed the court that the selection authority was meeting on Thursday itself.
But the bench said it should not finalise the panel.Baruah then said UPSC would postpone the meeting till next date of hearing. SC asked Odisha govt to file its response to the application and posted the matter for hearing on Aug 18. This means Odisha would have to either ask Khurania to continue as DGP till further orders or appoint an ad hoc DGP till the matter gets decided by SC.On Sept 22, 2006, SC laid down guidelines for selection of DGPs in states to insulate them from political influence and had given them a tenure of two years. For last two decades, it has been supervising the appointment process for DGPs and entertaining applications which point out irregularities or illegalities in that process.

headline: CM Vijay asks PM Modi to retain 543 Lok Sabha seats, ensure 33% women quota
full_text:
CM Vijay asks PM Modi to retain 543 Lok Sabha seats, ensure 33% women quota
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to amend the Constitution and keep the Lok Sabha at 543 seats. The move seeks to shield southern states from post-Census seat losses and secure 33 per cent reservation for women.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Thursday wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, asking him to bring in Constitutional amendments to make the strength of the Lok Sabha permanent at 543 members. In his letter, Vijay referred to a resolution passed by the Tamil Nadu Assembly on August 12, 2026 on the proposed delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly constituencies.
He also drew the Prime Minister’s attention to the Assembly’s demand that 33 per cent reservation for women be ensured in the upcoming Lok Sabha elections and the subsequent Assembly polls. Vijay said the resolution called for the present distribution of Lok Sabha seats among the states to remain unchanged.
Quoting the resolution, the Chief Minister said the “total number of members of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) should be made permanent at 543”. He added that the number of Lok Sabha seats allotted to the states should also be kept permanent at the current level.
In his letter to Modi, Vijay said, “I enclose a copy of the resolution passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly. I kindly request you to consider the resolution passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and bring in necessary Constitutional amendments in this regard.”
The Assembly had deliberated on August 12 that after the Census, the southern states could lose seats if Article 81(2)(a), which deals with the allotment of seats, was applied. It noted that this had happened in 1967, when Tamil Nadu’s number of Lok Sabha seats was reduced from 41 to 39.
The resolution said any delimitation based on post-1971 population figures that changes the existing strength would cause lasting injustice to the southern states, which it said had efficiently implemented population control programmes and achieved economic growth, healthcare progress and public welfare outcomes. It also urged the Union government to ensure one-third reservation for women in the next Lok Sabha elections and the Assembly elections that follow.
In summary, Vijay has asked the Prime Minister to amend the Constitution to keep the Lok Sabha strength at 543, retain the current state-wise seat allocation, and implement 33 per cent reservation for women in the coming Lok Sabha and Assembly elections.

headline: NEW DELHI: Over 5,000 pilots of Air India and Air India Express have started undergoing "mandatory substance screening" from Thursday. The airline took this move to "protect and sustain" passenger trust - which had taken a hit after last June's Ahmed...
full_text: NEW DELHI: Over 5,000 pilots of Air India and Air India Express have started undergoing "mandatory substance screening" from Thursday. The airline took this move to "protect and sustain" passenger trust - which had taken a hit after last June's Ahmedabad crash and was slowly being restored - but has been shaken yet again after the badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight's pilot-in-command failed his dope test. After this one-time mega exercise, AI will conduct dope tests according to regulatory requirement, which as of now mandate at least 10% crew members be tested annually. DGCA is reviewing its rules and may go in for stricter consequences for those testing positive due to addiction issues and adopt a different approach for those who do so after taking medicines for pain, allergy and other issues. Pointing out that AI has over the decades "earned trust of millions of passengers and the wider community," AI senior VP (flight ops) Captain Manish Uppal wrote to all pilots Thursday: "...This trust is our most important asset, and it is vital that we do all possible to protect & sustain it."

headline: The Kerala High Court has denied bail to Muhammed Najeeb Kallatra who was accused of engaging in organised organ trafficking under the guise of lawful organ donation through Kallatras Medical Tourism Private Ltd.
full_text:
The Kerala High Court has denied bail to Muhammed Najeeb Kallatra who was accused of engaging in organised organ trafficking under the guise of lawful organ donation through Kallatras Medical Tourism Private Ltd.
Justice Kauser Edappagath observed that there was a prima facie case of a premeditated criminal act by the accused. The court noted in the analysis of WhatsApp chats that Kallatra had transmitted documents to the other accused to prepare forged documents for the alleged illegal operations. The Google Pay account history also disclosed multiple monetary transactions, and a WhatsApp voice recording was recovered where Kallatra had instructed another accused person to prepare a forged laboratory report to facilitate illegal organ transplants.
A statement by one of the donors had revealed that he received ₹9 lakh in cash for donating his kidney, and all the necessary documents had been arranged by Kallatra for the purpose. The donor accused Kallatra of exploiting his financial distress for illegal organ trade.
Expressing concern over the gravity of the offence, the court said that organ trafficking exploited vulnerable populations, fuelled transnational crime networks, and undermined public trust in legitimate medical systems, and held that Kallatra could not be released on bail.

headline: Ambala Sikh protest turns violent; cops use tear gas, lathi charge to clear highway
full_text:
Ambala Sikh protest turns violent; cops use tear gas, lathi charge to clear highway
A Sikh community protest over the delayed FIR against GurSimran Singh Mand led to a highway blockade in Ambala and police action. The standoff continued even after the FIR was filed, as protesters sought the release of detained youths.
A protest by members of the Sikh community over the alleged delay in registering an FIR against GurSimran Singh Mand in the Panjokhra Sahib dispute turned tense in Ambala on Thursday, with police using tear gas and a lathi charge to clear a highway blockade.
A large number of Sikh protesters gathered on the highway demanding that a case be registered against Mand. The protesters had earlier held a meeting and announced that they would block the National Highway if their demand was not met.
As the protesters moved towards the highway from the gurdwara, police put up barricades and used tear gas to stop them. The protesters, however, broke through and blocked the highway, leading to a long traffic jam and the deployment of heavy police forces.
Amid mounting pressure, police later registered an FIR against Mand. However, the protest did not end. The protesters then demanded the immediate release of Sikh youths who had been detained by the police.
Several rounds of talks between police officials and Sikh representatives failed to break the deadlock. As darkness fell, police presence on the highway was further increased and protesters were asked to clear the road.
When they refused to move, police used tear gas and resorted to a lathi charge to disperse the protesters. The highway was subsequently cleared and traffic restored.
Several police personnel were injured during the operation. Haryana DGP Ajay Singhal visited the Military Hospital and Civil Hospital in Ambala to meet the injured personnel and enquire about their condition.
According to preliminary information released by the Haryana Police, six to seven personnel were injured. Those injured include DSP Virender Sharma, who suffered a serious thumb injury, along with Constables Rakshit and Naveen Kumar, Head Constable Sandeep Kumar, ASI Satish and ASI Pankaj, who sustained finger injuries.
Singhal said maintaining law and order was the police's foremost responsibility and appealed to people to raise grievances peacefully and avoid blocking public roads.
Inspector General of Police Pankaj Nain, Deputy Commissioner Sachin Gupta and SDM Kanika Goyal were also present.

headline: Centre delists 18 protected monuments since 2021, Parliament told
full_text:
Centre delists 18 protected monuments since 2021, Parliament told
The Centre told Parliament it has delisted 18 protected monuments since 2021 after finding they were no longer of national importance. The disclosure also highlighted ASI's vast conservation load, artefact recoveries abroad and a legal gap in records audits.
The Centre has delisted 18 monuments from the list of protected monuments since 2021 after finding that they had ceased to be of national importance under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. Among the sites named in data shared in Parliament on Thursday are Delhi's Bara Khamba Cemetery and a banyan grove of "great antiquity" containing traces of ancient buildings.
In written replies in the Rajya Sabha, Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat also said the Archaeological Survey of India has 3,688 centrally protected monuments and sites under its care, that 662 artefacts have been retrieved from four countries till June 2026, and that no audit has been conducted in the last 12 years on compliance with the Public Records Act, 1993, because the law does not provide for such an audit.
Shekhawat shared the figures in response to a question on the number of centrally protected monuments de-notified since 2021. "The central government has delisted 18 monuments from the list of protected monuments since 2021 as they were found to have ceased to be of national importance as per the provisions of Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958," he said.
Replying to another query, the minister said there are "3,688 centrally protected monuments/sites under the care and maintenance of Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). ASI undertakes the conservation, maintenance and development works on these monuments/sites as per the requirement and availability of resources and it is continuous process."
In response to another question, Shekhawat said the central government has retrieved 662 artefacts from the US (589), Australia (51), the UK (21), and the Netherlands (1), till June 2026.
In a separate reply, when asked whether the government had conducted any audit during the last 12 years to assess compliance by ministries, departments, PSUs, autonomous bodies and statutory institutions with the Public Records Act, 1993, the minister said, "No such audit has been conducted during the last twelve years, as the Public Records Act, 1993 does not provide for such audit."
The replies in the Rajya Sabha covered the delisting of 18 protected monuments since 2021, the ASI's oversight of 3,688 sites, the retrieval of 662 artefacts from abroad till June 2026, and the absence of an audit under the Public Records Act because the law does not provide for one.

This was a win for the students and youth of the country. What they did till July 20, we the MPs had to just carry that forward. Just from criticising the govt it went to ridiculing the govt,â he added citing examples of slogans coined by Gen Z to attack the govt during the protests. The TMC leader further said that a key takeaway from this session was that the opposition worked in a coordinated way.On Thursday all opposition parties had a casual meeting in the lobby of Rajya Sabha just to tell each other that all had worked as a team, an opposition MP said. He added that it was basically an assessment that the opposition really did well in the way it went about raising issues and there was a lot of unity.
Opposition members highlighted that not just the INDIA bloc members but the opposition also found the way to create room for AAP which is no longer part of the grouping to speak and also DMK to make their point amid the protests in the House. The DMK distanced itself from the wider opposition INDIA bloc following friction with Congress since the latter severed its longstanding alliance with it and decided to support the TVK govt in Tamil Nadu.
Going forward, the INDIA bloc parties have decided to keep up the momentum and build on the unity seen in the current session to counter the ruling dispensation till the winter session. There was also consensus that if the INDIA bloc is meeting anytime soon then the date should be announced in August itself. The bloc had held its last meeting on June 8 and had announced that they propose to meet next in Hyderabad in August. However, the date of the meeting is yet to be decided.

headline: The invitation for the event has been extended by Afghanistan charge d'affaires Mufti Noor Ahmad Noor
full_text:
The invitation for the event has been extended by Afghanistan charge d'affaires Mufti Noor Ahmad Noor
New Delhi: As India and Taliban-ruled Afghanistan further intensify their pragmatic engagement focused on trade, humanitarian aid and regional security, Taliban will celebrate the fifth anniversary of the Victory Day in the Afghanistan embassy in Delhi Monday. Victory Day is observed annually by Taliban on Aug 15 to commemorate the group's return to Kabul in 2021, following the withdrawal of US-led Nato forces.The invitation for the event has been extended by Afghanistan charge d'affaires Mufti Noor Ahmad Noor and carries the emblem of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan. Sources said the event is not just endorsed by the Indian side but will also see participation by senior Indian officials.India doesn't officially recognise the Islamic Emirate, maintaining that its position on the issue is in consonance with the international community, although it has allowed Taliban to take control of the Afghan embassy. However, its position is also marked by pragmatic engagement with Taliban, leveraging its historic goodwill and development presence to protect its regional interests.
The efforts have been further aided by the dramatic shift in Taliban's ties with Pakistan.
India and Afghanistan continue to back each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity, with India standing by Kabul in the latter's border conflict with Pakistan. Much to Pakistan's chagrin, Taliban also backed India's sovereignty over J&K in a joint statement with India last year by endorsing a mention of the UT as located in India, while condemning the Pahalgam attack. While restoring its own embassy in Kabul last year, India had agreed to the appointment of Taliban diplomats.The development followed a landmark visit by Afghanistan foreign minister Amir Khan Muttaqi to India that further cemented the relationship.

headline: Failed exam, bought fake certificates: 3 'doctors' arrested in Rajasthan
full_text:
Failed exam, bought fake certificates: 3 'doctors' arrested in Rajasthan
The three accused paid between Rs 25 lakh and Rs 29 lakh to obtain fake FMG screening certificates after repeatedly failing the examination conducted by the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS).
Three men have been arrested in Rajasthan for using forged Foreign Medical Graduate (FMG) screening certificates to obtain medical registration and practise as doctors despite failing the mandatory exam.
The three accused paid between Rs 25 lakh and Rs 29 lakh to obtain fake FMG screening certificates after repeatedly failing the examination conducted by the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS).
One of them went on to treat patients in an emergency ward without registration with the Rajasthan Medical Council (RMC).
The arrests are part of a wider investigation into a suspected racket involving foreign medical graduates, brokers and others who allegedly helped candidates obtain forged FMG certificates and use them to secure internships and medical registrations.
According to the police, more than 100 foreign medical graduates have so far come under the scanner, while 30 accused have been arrested in connection with the case.
The case, registered in Jaipur on February 4, 2026, involves allegations of cheating, forgery and criminal conspiracy.
FAILED FMG EXAM, BOUGHT CERTIFICATE FOR RS 25 LAKH
One of the arrested accused, Ashish Kumar, 30, allegedly obtained his MBBS degree from Pakistan in 2021. He appeared for the FMG screening examination three times but failed to clear it.
Police said Ashish subsequently obtained a forged FMG certificate through accused Shubham Gurjar, paying Rs 25 lakh for it. He then used the certificate to apply for registration with the RMC.
Gurjar has already been arrested and is in judicial custody, police said.
Ashish is currently preparing to appear for the FMG screening examination again.
FAILED 8 TIMES, PAID RS 29 LAKH
The second accused, Rajendra Kumar Yadav, 39, obtained his MBBS degree from China between 2006 and 2012. According to the police, he appeared for the FMG screening examination eight times in 2012 but failed to qualify.
He then procured a fake FMG certificate through a person identified as Sandeep, paying Rs 29 lakh. Using the certificate, he applied for registration with the RMC.
Police said Rajendra currently manages Narayan Hospital in Jaipur, which is run by his wife. The role of Sandeep in arranging the forged certificate is also being investigated.
WORKING IN EMERGENCY WARD WITHOUT REGISTRATION
The third accused, Naresh Rolania, 26, obtained his MBBS degree from Pakistan in 2021. He too failed the FMG screening examination three times.
The police said that Naresh's relative arranged a fake FMG certificate for him in exchange for Rs 26 lakh. Naresh then used the certificate to secure an internship, which he completed at Udaipur Medical College.
Investigators found that Naresh was subsequently working in the emergency ward of Pulse Hospital in Kotputli, where he was treating patients despite having neither cleared the mandatory FMG screening examination nor obtained registration with the RMC, police said.
OVER 100 FOREIGN MEDICAL GRADUATES UNDER SCANNER
Police said the probe has so far identified more than 100 foreign medical graduates involved in obtaining fake FMG certificates.
Of these, 30, including candidates who allegedly used the certificates to secure RMC registrations, have been arrested.
The investigation has also focused on the involvement of brokers and other persons who helped candidates procure the forged documents.
The police said around 25 foreign-graduate doctors, brokers and RMC employees have been arrested so far in connection with the wider racket.

headline: By 6 a.m. on August 9, Har Ki Pauri in Haridwar was already a wall of saffron. Steam rose off the Ganga in the early light as men and boys ranging from their teens to their late 60s – barefoot, dressed in T-shirts bearing images of Hindu gods, speake...
full_text:
By 6 a.m. on August 9, Har Ki Pauri in Haridwar was already a wall of saffron. Steam rose off the Ganga in the early light as men and boys ranging from their teens to their late 60s – barefoot, dressed in T-shirts bearing images of Hindu gods, speakers strapped to bamboo kanwars blaring remixed bhajans – waded into the river that Hindus believe is holy.
By the afternoon, these men had become a river of their own. They flowed down National Highway 58, headed back to their homes, mostly across Delhi, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh. Some were travelling as far as Jammu, Rajasthan, and Bihar, walking hundreds of kilometres with pots of Gangajal (water) balanced on rods across their shoulders: the kanwars.
Among the 50 million that the Uttarakhand government said came to Haridwar to gather water, was Rajat Singh, 21. A Rajput and a first-time kanwariya, or carrier of the kanwar, from Kathua in Jammu, Singh began his 600-km journey on July 17. He walked 25-30 km every day and slept in roadside camps for 26 days.
Singh dropped out of college two years ago and has not been able to find a job. He feels the weight of his responsibility to support his family. His father owns a marginal farm in the Bani hills, but is unable to support a family of five, including Singh’s mother and two younger siblings. Amid the uncertainty around his employment, Singh decided to start blogging. His Instagram profile, which has 41,000 followers, describes him as a ‘kattar Hindu’ (staunch Hindu). He has 99,000 followers on Facebook.
During his 26-day Kanwar Yatra, he blogged daily, documenting his journey on social media, mostly through reels set to remixes of devotional songs and timestamped with mile markers. He gained 10,000 followers during the journey.
“Initially, I used to blog about some scenic places near my village, but that hardly worked. I gained over 10,000 followers when I completed the Amarnath Yatra for the first time, three years ago. The second time, this number crossed 15,000 when I visited Himachal Pradesh’s Bharmour for the Manimahesh Kailash Yatra,” he said.
This time, he knew exactly what he had to do: document everything – picking up the Gangajal, carrying the water, walking barefoot, and making sure it didn’t touch the ground before he offered it at the temple.
He has sketchy details on the pilgrimage’s origins and traditions though. “Maybe I would know that from mythological books,” he says, adding, “I am not well-versed in Hindi and Sanskrit. We were taught Urdu rather than Hindi in school,” he explained. Singh is one of at least 50 people The Hindu spoke to at the Haridwar ghat, where between 2 and 4 million descended, to scoop up river water each day, from July 30 to August 11. Like him, most did not know the history of the yatra, nor had they paused to question its now Mardi Gras-like vibe. In some aspects the kanwariyas were like the youth from the protests at Jantar Mantar. Both worried about the future and jobs, and were adept at using social media. But the kanwariyas deferred to the state, and celebrated what they saw as the government taking care of them, not seeing themselves as a vote bank.
Half the highway had been cordoned off for them to walk and for oversized religious tableaux to move in procession with DJs belting out music, not always religious. There were roadside camps set up for their rest and refreshment. Rose petals were showered on them from a helicopter as they walked. All this, they felt, was due to them.
They didn’t think it was a contradiction that many had found fault with Muslims offering Namaz on the road. Nitin Chaudhary, 26, said the minority community enjoyed similar privileges when the socialist Samajwadi Party (SP) was in power in Uttar Pradesh from 2012-17.
Walk this way
Among those filling their kanwars at the Ganga ghat was 24-year-old Aniket, who uses only his first name and identifies himself as a Dalit. A linesman with the electricity department in Uttar Pradesh’s Muzaffarnagar, he had taken six days of unpaid leave to make the journey for the fifth year running.
He earns ₹9,500 a month and a little extra from a side hustle. This pilgrimage costs him a substantial part of his monthly income, even though he took the cheapest bus to reach Haridwar and a langar (community kitchen) will feed him on his walk back. He slept in a dormitory near the Ganga ghat, which cost him ₹1,000. He also spent ₹3,000 on repairing and decorating his kanwar.
“A few hundred rupees went on mobile recharge and some on souvenirs for friends and family,” he said. The expenditure did not seem to trouble him. Nor did the prospect of walking hundreds of kilometres carrying several litres of holy water. But when asked why a kanwariya carries Gangajal in the first place, he shrugged.
Aniket had never heard the stories commonly invoked in popular accounts of the Kanwar tradition, including mythological legends connecting Ravana and Parashuram with journeys involving Shiva and sacred water. He did not know how the pilgrimage had begun or why devotees, or for that matter he himself, carry the water to Shiva temples. He was not embarrassed by the gap. “Nahi pata iske baare mein (I don’t know about it),” he said, simply.
He had never questioned it. For him, religion was simply something people had practised this way for generations. He could not say what the water was meant to accomplish. He simply knew that it had to be carried.
Aniket stood drenched on the top step of the Ganga ghat, swamped by the excesses of humanity overcrowded in an area meant for not more than 10,000. Around him were sadhus on torn mats, people discarding old clothes on the steps after a dip in the river. There was the sight of leftover food and the stench of garbage.
Both sides now
After the nationwide protests that began in Delhi and spread across India, Gen Z’s liberal face showed itself clearly: Neha, from a fauji family that votes for BJP, who chose to align with the left; Mohammad Irfan, the vendor whose daily wisdom resonated with many; the swathes of people from across the gender spectrum who came because it felt like a safe space to be in.
About 270 km away at Haridwar, it was mostly men. Nishi Kumar, 26, from Meerut, was one of the few women kanwariyas. She said it was the same as at the sports goods manufacturing factory where she worked. She spoke little and kept her eyes on the road, watching her steps and the people around her to avoid brushing against the men in the crowd. “Women are competing and going ahead of men in almost everything. Then why not in the Kanwar Yatra?” she said.
Nishi wore full-length pants and a dupatta; her brothers wore shorts. She was also unsure of whether the camps would have separate toilets and sleeping arrangements for women. She had to convince her family to let her go for the yatra. They were reluctant for her to join a procession dominated by men.
Uttar Pradesh has recorded the highest absolute number of reported crimes against women in the country, according to the 2024 National Crime Records Bureau data.
Nishi wanted women to go to college and have a career, though she herself has not been able to go beyond school because of her family’s financial constraints. She also felt men must be more involved in household chores, but called live-in relationships ashleel (vulgar), and inter-religious marriages “totally unacceptable”.
Not everyone around Nishi agreed that women belonged in the Yatra. Tushar Kumar, 24, an electrician at a mobile repair firm in Delhi’s Shahdara, was uncomfortable with her presence. “Women should only go to places where their safety is ensured,” he said.
Tushar is a Thakur but uses Kumar instead of Chauhan as his surname. He said his parents believed it would improve his chances of getting a government job. He was more accepting of live-in relationships, but “they should remain limited to cities and not reach smaller towns”.
Politics at the yatra
Shivam Sharma, 22, from Katha village in Baghpat, U.P., who joined his father’s business of agriculture exports, arrived in Haridwar with a group of 29 people. The group was led by a 63-year-old, who was undertaking his 40th Kanwar Yatra. The group crossed caste lines. It included Vivek Yadav, 28, a teacher from an OBC community.
Vivek, who earns just enough to support himself from the private school he works at, objected to the language and tone of the Jantar Mantar protesters, but agreed with what they were demanding. He had himself appeared several times for police constable recruitment exams. On some occasions, he said, examination papers were leaked, on others, the results were withheld.
“They should have minded the language they used for [Prime Minister Narendra] Modi,” said Vivek, who accepted that he too abused, but only with friends or when he was angry, never with “elders or gods”.
All the men said the Uttar Pradesh government, led by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, had done wonderfully well with the arrangements for them. They weren’t as appreciative of the Uttarakhand government, which, they said, were making them walk extra with “unnecessary barricades”. There were also no arrangements for free food or camps to rest.
Shivam has another complaint: Uttarakhand didn’t bring in singers to perform the aarti at the Ganga. “They are still stuck running Anuradha Paudwal’s aarti on an old tape recorder. When the yatra is getting modern, the State is stuck in old ways,” he added.
He felt the music shouldn’t go the other extreme either, with Bollywood tunes and the frenzy of throbbing noise-polluting boom boxes. “There are anti-social elements everywhere, but that cannot be used to defame the entire yatra,” he said. “I don’t drink, I don’t smoke and we (his group) don’t carry any music,” he added.
A DJ mounted atop a vessel that flashed multi-coloured lights, blasted a song in praise of U.P.’s Chief Minister. “Bhole nachwa diye Yogi ne, rang jama diye Yogi ne. Akhilesh ne hukum sunaya tha, DJ par ban lagaya tha. (Yogi made Shiv dance, Yogi brought the celebration alive. Akhilesh had ordered a ban on DJs).” Then the punchline: “2017 ke election mein Bhole ne ise haraya tha (In the 2017 election, Bhole – a reference to Yogi Adityanath – defeated him).”
The burden of tradition and expectation
“The Gangajal is not the heaviest thing these young men carry,” said Sachin Gupta, 34, a journalist who has been covering the Kanwar Yatra since 2015 for two major Hindi publications. He has watched the yatra grow in scale and change in character since Adityanath came to power in U.P. in 2017. This year, he remained on NH-58 through the yatra, covering it as a freelancer.
Gupta said the yatra had become increasingly loud and rowdy over the years. When he began covering it, he said, the focus was more on the pilgrimage itself. Now, the spectacle around it has grown bigger.
“DJs, modified vehicles, slogans, and displays of strength often seem to compete with the religious purpose of the journey,” he said, adding that instances of kanwariyas thrashing people had also risen.
He sees the young kanwariya men carrying the expectations of their parents, of society: what it means to them to be a son, a man, a Hindu, and a member of the local community is reflected here. “Those expectations may not surface when they talk about the yatra, but become visible when the conversation moves to attitudes around women, relationships, religion, or politics,” Gupta said.

headline: Congress leaders failed to function: Revanth Reddy says 21% Telangana voters face deletion under SIR
full_text:
Congress leaders failed to function: Revanth Reddy says 21% Telangana voters face deletion under SIR
Revanth Reddy on Thursday blamed Congress leaders at various levels for failing to discharge their responsibilities fully.
Telangana could see more than 73 lakh voters drop off its electoral rolls, with Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy warning that nearly 21 per cent of votes face deletion during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
Reddy on Thursday reportedly blamed Congress leaders at various levels for failing to discharge their responsibilities fully.
During a video conference with ruling Congress leaders on the SIR process, Reddy directed in-charge ministers to hold reviews with those overseeing Parliamentary and Assembly constituencies in their respective districts and address the issues, news agency PTI reported, citing sources.
The ministers have been asked to conduct reviews across the districts over the next two days and prepare a report for every constituency, Congress sources said.
Also Read: 18 million voters in state could get deleted from rolls in SIR exercise
Reddy also instructed constituency in-charge leaders to remain in their respective constituencies for four days, identify issues related to the revision process and work to resolve them.
The chief minister warned that the party would not tolerate any failure to draw up and implement a proper action plan in line with the directions of the AICC.
He cautioned that a lack of vigilance among party leaders could cause significant political damage in the future.
Reddy further directed Congress leaders to expose what he alleged was a conspiracy by the BRS and BJP to delete votes, the sources said.
The concern comes as the number of electors in Telangana is expected to fall by more than 73 lakh following the SIR process, with enumeration forms for these voters classified as "uncollectable".
According to Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C Sudharshan Reddy's statement issued on August 11, the state had 3,38,26,448 voters in all. Of these, enumeration forms for 2,64,87,214 voters, or 78.30 per cent, had been digitised.
The remaining 73,39,234 forms, accounting for 21.70 per cent of the total, were classified as "uncollectable", he said.
House-to-house visits by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) as part of the SIR began in Telangana on June 25 and concluded on August 10. The draft electoral rolls are scheduled to be published on August 17.
SIR exercise updates
On the other hand, as many as 18.46% or 18 million of 97.8 million registered electors across Maharashtra are expected to be deleted from the electoral rolls in the ongoing SIR exercise.
These voters are either dead, duplicate, not traceable at the given address or shifted from there. Mumbai accounts for 29.6% of deletions, with Muslim-dominated areas such as Mankhurd, Colaba and Mumbadevi being even higher at almost 40%.
According to data released by the Election Commission (EC) on Wednesday, of the 9,78,54,049 registered voters, 7,60,98153 electors have been enumerated while the enumeration of 1,80,60,697 (18.46% of total electors) could not be completed. The deadline for completing the SIR exercise is August 17.

headline: Independence Day 2026: How to properly display, handle the Indian flag - Your six-point tricolour guide
full_text:
Independence Day 2026: How to properly display, handle the Indian flag - Your six-point tricolour guide
India's Flag Code covers several aspects of handling the tricolour, including how it should be displayed and stored. Knowing them can help avoid mistakes.
India will mark its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026 (Saturday), commemorating the country's freedom from British rule and remembering the sacrifices of the freedom fighters who fought for a free nation.
As Independence Day approaches, the Indian national flag will be seen fluttering high across the country. But once the celebrations end, questions often arise about how the flags should be kept.
The Flag Code of India sets out guidelines for displaying and handling the national flag.
How to keep the flag properly
Deep Dive
Citizens can keep the tricolour even after Independence Day. However, it must be kept and handled in accordance with the Flag Code of India so that the national flag is treated with due respect.
It should not be used like ordinary disposable decorations or kept in a condition that causes it to become torn or damaged.
The Flag Code covers several aspects of handling the tricolour, including how it should be displayed and stored. Knowing these rules can help avoid mistakes while preserving the flag.
How to handle the tricolour
When the national flag is displayed, it should be given a place of honour and shown prominently, and it must never be displayed if it is damaged or in a dishevelled condition.
There is also no provision prohibiting citizens from keeping the flag after August 15. Citizens can display the national flag on all days and occasions, provided its dignity is maintained as required under the Flag Code.
Following amendments to the code, the flag can be displayed during both day and night. When flown at night, however, it should be properly illuminated.
How to fold the flag
While the Flag Code provides instructions on the use and handling of the national flag, it does not provide a detailed method for folding it at home. It should nevertheless be handled with care and must not be crumpled or damaged.
The Union ministry of culture had shared the flag-folding method in a social media post last year. These are the steps to fold and preserve the tricolour respectfully:
- Place the flag horizontally.
- Fold the white band so that the Ashoka Chakra remains visible, along with parts of the saffron and green bands.
- Bring the saffron and green bands underneath the middle white band.
- Use your palms or arms to carry the folded flag before placing it in storage.
How and where to keep the national flag
The Flag Code states that the tricolour “shall not be used or stored in such a manner as may damage or soil it”.
It also states that the flag “shall not be allowed to touch the ground or the floor or trail in water”.
Keep it in a clean, dry location, away from moisture, dirt, and objects that could damage, tear, or stain the fabric.
What to do if the flag is soiled
The Flag Code states that “when the Flag is in a damaged or soiled condition, it shall not be cast aside or disrespectfully disposed of”.
It “shall be destroyed as a whole in private, preferably by burning or by any other method consistent with the dignity of the Flag,” as per the Flag Code.
What to do with the small paper flags
The Flag Code allows the public to wave paper flags during important national, cultural and sports events.
Paper flags should also not be placed on the ground, left on roads or thrown into drains.
“As far as possible, it should be disposed of in private consistent with the dignity of the Flag,” the Flag Code states.

headline: Woman damages airport property worth ₹49,000 after IndiGo flight cancellation in Bhubaneswar, FIR lodged
full_text:
Woman damages airport property worth ₹49,000 after IndiGo flight cancellation in Bhubaneswar, FIR lodged
The FIR was lodged against the passenger for alleged unruly behaviour, damage to airport property, and creating a ruckus in the airport's departure lounge
A woman passenger allegedly damaged property worth ₹49,000 at Bhubaneswar’s Biju Patnaik International Airport (BPIA) on Thursday, with authorities lodging a police complaint against her.
The FIR was lodged against the passenger, identified as Mamoni Kharat, for alleged unruly behaviour, damage to airport property, and creating a ruckus in the airport's departure lounge after an IndiGo flight to Kolkata was cancelled due to a technical snag.
According to the complaint filed with the Airfield police station, the passenger was scheduled to fly on IndiGo flight 6E 7352 to Kolkata.
The complaint stated that the passenger lost her cool in the presence of officials from the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), IndiGo, and the Airports Authority of India. The incident allegedly occurred around 6 pm on Thursday.
A video purportedly showing the passenger's unruly behaviour at the airport surfaced on social media and quickly went viral.
The footage shows a heated altercation and alleged damage to airport infrastructure following the flight cancellation.
"IndiGo flight 6E 7352, scheduled to operate from Bhubaneswar to Kolkata on August 13, 2026, was cancelled due to a technical snag identified during the mandatory pre-departure inspection of the aircraft. We regret the inconvenience caused to our customers and took all efforts to minimise the same, including offering them regular updates, refreshments, accommodation and alternate travel options or full refunds as applicable," IndiGo said in a statement.
AAI alleged that the passenger damaged a monitor, a keyboard, and a passport-swiping machine, resulting in an estimated loss of ₹49,000.
"During this, one of the customers who caused damage to the airport property was declared unruly and handed over to the relevant security agencies in line with standard operating procedures. We thank our customers for their patience and understanding. At IndiGo, the safety and comfort of our customers and crew remain our top priorities," the IndiGo spokesperson added.
BPIA authorities requested that the police take appropriate action and recover the cost of the damaged equipment from the passenger.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed âstrong disapprovalâ of the Bar Council of Indiaâs (BCI) now-revoked order barring the enrolment of 2026 graduates of Hyderabadâs NALSAR University of Law as advocates after a section of students objected to the university inviting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at its convocation ceremony.Also Read | 'What if all legal cockroaches come together?': CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke reacts to BCI action against NALSAR graduatesKant, heading a bench also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said students have a right to protest peacefully and described the episode as a âdialogueâ between him and the students.

headline: Minority kids can reassemble Rafale, but forget what they study: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy
full_text:
Minority kids can reassemble Rafale, but forget what they study: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy
Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy said minority students are skilled workers who can dismantle and reassemble a Rafale aircraft but "forget what they have study". His remarks on students at the Minorities Excellence Summit, along with those on electricity consumption in the Old City, have sparked a political row.
Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy referred to minority students as "skilled labourers" who have the technical acumen to dismantle and reassemble a Rafale fighter jet, but struggle to retain what they study from books. Reddy also highlighted his government's welfare schemes for minority communities. His remarks at a minorities summit in Hyderabad on Thursday drew a sharp response from the BJP, which accused the Congress government of "appeasement" and questioned its approach to electricity dues in the Old City of Hyderabad.
"Students from the minority communities can dismantle and reassemble Rafale [aircraft], but cannot remember lessons from a book," Reddy said while speaking at the Minorities Excellence Summit at Adivasi Bhavan in Banjara Hills on Thursday (August 13).
The Telangana CM said children from minority communities were "skilled labourers" who might forget what they read but could dismantle and reassemble a Rafale aircraft if given one.
Reddy also highlighted several welfare schemes of the Telangana government, including Shaadi Mubarak, Kalyana Lakshmi, Indiramma Indlu and the Gruha Jyothi scheme, under which households consuming up to 200 units of electricity a month receive free power.
Referring to criticism over electricity consumption in Hyderabad's Old City, Reddy said, "People, including MLAs in the Assembly, often complain that members of minority communities steal electricity in parts of the Old City [of Hyderabad] and do not pay their bills."
"Today I want say that with confidence 200 units of electricity that the Congress government in Telangana is giving for free is more useful for our brothers and sisters of minority communities," he added.
The Telangana chief minister also cited the government's other welfare programmes, including free bus travel for women under Maha Lakshmi, financial assistance to farmers through Rythu Bharosa and housing assistance under Indiramma Indlu.
HINDU AND MUSLIMS ARE MY TWO EYES: CM REDDY
CM Reddy said that the Congress government in Telangana was committed to ensuring that Muslims received the same welfare benefits as Hindus.
"For me, Hindus and Muslims are not different. They are like my two eyes. Our government is working to ensure that Muslims get the same benefits as Hindus," he said.
Recalling the Congress government's earlier initiatives for minorities, Reddy referred to former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister YS Rajasekhara Reddy, former minister Mohammed Ali Shabbir and Congress leader Azad.
He said the Congress had sought to make minority youth stakeholders in governance and described the party as committed to secularism. Reddy also highlighted the 4% reservation provided to minorities in the state under the earlier Congress government.
Without naming anyone, Reddy accused some people of creating an atmosphere where minorities are "branded as anti-India".
"Some people have created an atmosphere where if anyone speaks about minorities everyone feels like the community is anti-India," he said, adding that it was a strategy of division and provocation.
The Telangana chief minister added that minorities could contribute to the country as teachers and produce "heroes for the nation".
BJP ACCUSES REVANTH REDDY OF APPEASEMENT POLITICS
The BJP sharply criticised the remarks made by CM Reddy.
BJP Telangana secretary Tulla Veerender Goud, in a post on X on Friday, said the government should enforce the law instead of providing what he described as preferential treatment to a particular community.
"If you cannot enforce the law, step down. But do not surrender!" Goud said.
Reacting to Reddy's remarks about electricity bills in the Old City, Goud said that if consumers were not paying their dues, the government should take action under the rules.
"Giving free electricity in the name of schemes simply because bills are not being paid is unconstitutional," he said.
Goud further questioned whether a government unable to collect electricity dues could effectively ensure law and order and protect citizens.
"If Congress means Muslims and Muslims mean Congress, then are you Revanth Reddy or Revanth Uddin?" Goud said, accusing the Congress government of minority appeasement.
"As Chief Minister, govern without discrimination," he said. "Surrendering to one particular community is not governance," the Telangana BJP secretary added.

headline: 'Baseless': Chhattisgarh IPS officer on ₹1 cr bribery charge in cyber-fraud case
full_text:
'Baseless': Chhattisgarh IPS officer on ₹1 cr bribery charge in cyber-fraud case
Rahul Bansal said a complaint is currently under consideration by a court, and he has complete faith in the law
Rahul Bansal, a 2022 batch Indian Police Service officer posted in Chhattisgarh’s Surguja district, who allegedly received ₹1 crore to settle a cyber-fraud case along with two other police personnel, has refuted the allegation as baseless. “The complaint is currently under consideration by the court, and I have complete faith in the court and law,” said Bansal.
Bansal said that a case was registered in July 2025 with Surguja’s Cyber Police Station over an alleged fraud of around ₹21 lakh in share trading. “During the investigation, it came to light that an organised gang, which was initially operating from Dubai and later shifted to India, allegedly lured victims through social media advertisements to invest money on fake trading platforms,” said Bansal.
Bansal claimed that the probe into the flow of funds led investigators to a fintech company, which allegedly converted the fraud proceeds into cash and subsequently routed them through hawala channels. “Further investigation revealed transactions of around ₹1,880 crore in cryptocurrency wallets over approximately four months, which were allegedly linked to the gang’s operators.”
Bansal said 23 accused have been arrested from eight states, and five charge sheets running into thousands of pages, along with digital evidence, have been filed before the concerned court.
Bansal has been named in the case along with assistant sub-inspector Praveen Kumar Rathore and constable Anshul Sharma.
Also read: Chandigarh: Bapu Dham Chowki incharge, ASI caught taking bribe by CBI
A special court in Delhi has sought action taken reports from the Chhattisgarh Police chief and the Central Bureau of Investigation director. The complainant has submitted alleged WhatsApp chats and call recordings as supporting material.
According to the complaint, the alleged ₹1 crore payment was made through hawala channels in two instalments of ₹50 lakh each in May 2026. The allegations emerged from the investigation of a cyber-fraud case registered in Surguja.
Ravi Mohan Goswami, the complainant, alleged that he was cheated of ₹21.15 lakh through 84 online transactions. He was allegedly lured into investing in the stock market and forex trading through online platforms.
What began as a complaint involving ₹21.15 lakh expanded into an alleged multi-layered cyber-fraud network involving fake trading platforms, overseas call centres, mule bank accounts, fintech payment gateways, dummy firms, hawala channels and cryptocurrency transfers.
Chhattisgarh Police said the investigation against the alleged masterminds and other members of the network continues.
The charge sheets allege that the fraud was presented to victims as a legitimate investment business. Callers, including those based in Dubai, contacted potential investors and persuaded them to invest in platforms such as MoneyTrade365, SmartTrade365 and VTFX. The platforms were allegedly designed to look like genuine trading applications.
One of the charge sheets said a software allowed operators to control trading points, withdrawals and account access. When victims attempted to withdraw their money, their accounts could be put on hold, or they could be told that there was a software problem.
In some cases, small amounts were allegedly returned to investors to build confidence and persuade them to invest more. Tele-calling was allegedly a key part of the operation. Several accused are alleged to have worked from Dubai, contacting potential victims and persuading them to invest through the fake platforms.
One alleged caller worked under a handler and contacted victims through Money Trade 365, while another was allegedly recruited by the suspected masterminds and paid ₹35,000 to ₹40,000 a month.
Inspector general Deepak Jha said they have identified Anshul Ginotra and Garvit Jain among the alleged owners or masterminds of the syndicate. “They are among those being investigated and are absconding. The software infrastructure formed another crucial part of the alleged operation.”
Jha said police have identified Limbani Avnik Mansukhbhai, alias Chirag, as the alleged master software architect. He added investigators reportedly recovered source code for 38 trading websites from his devices. “These platforms allegedly catered to around 19,340 users.”
Also read: CBI nabs IRCTC official, hospitality firm director in ₹3.98L bribery case
MoneyTrade365 and SmartTrade365, the two platforms examined, were linked to 4,109 users. Jha said their cryptocurrency transaction trail exceeded ₹1,880 crore over about four months.
Investigators said that money was routed through multiple accounts and entities to distance the proceeds from the people controlling the operation.
Jha said some accused allegedly gave corporate current accounts opened in the names of dummy firms such as SS Enterprises and Guru Enterprises. One alleged account provider is accused of arranging over 15 corporate current accounts with IDBI Bank, Axis Bank, Bandhan Bank, State Bank of India and Bank of Maharashtra. ₹1.5 lakh was allegedly charged for each account.
Another alleged account provider, described as a relative of one of the suspected masterminds, allegedly floated Kalpana Enterprises and provided 11 current accounts. The probe has also pointed to the alleged misuse of Go-Payment’s payment infrastructure.
According to a charge sheet’s summary, some regional and state-level officials within the fintech operation allegedly helped bypass KYC requirements. An advocate and facilitator allegedly created 15 to 20 agent or distributor IDs using unverified SIM cards, incomplete KYC documents, and fake shop banners.
One virtual ID registered in the name of a mule allegedly processed ₹8.86 crore through 822 transactions on a single day on October 6, 2025.
Investigators said that after the money moved through the payment system, a portion was converted into physical cash and subsequently into cryptocurrencies. The digital assets were allegedly transferred internationally. Investigators suspect that some of the money was used to settle gaming or betting-related balances and server costs.
The accused allegedly used pseudonyms, virtual numbers and mobile connections registered in other people’s names. The use of dummy firms, mule accounts and payment gateways created multiple layers between victims and the alleged ultimate beneficiaries, making the money trail more difficult to trace.
Investigators say the cryptocurrency trail recovered from the phones of absconding accused Ginotra and Jain showed transactions of around ₹1,880 crore over roughly four months. The trail subsequently led investigators to other alleged beneficiaries and another arrest, pointing to a larger network through which fraud proceeds were allegedly moved outside India.
Digital evidence indicated that the network may have been operating since 2022, according to investigators.

headline: Public exams gateways to opportunities, govt taking steps to curb unfair means: Murmu on I-Day eve
full_text:
Public exams gateways to opportunities, govt taking steps to curb unfair means: Murmu on I-Day eve
President Murmu said the government is taking steps to curb exam cheating while highlighting youth opportunities, Operation Sindoor and the Indus Waters Treaty.
Public examinations are “gateways to the opportunities” available to students, and the government is undertaking “comprehensive steps” to curb unfair practices and make the system more transparent, secure and trustworthy, President Droupadi Murmu said on Friday, as she highlighted the opportunities opening up for India’s youth and outlined the country’s progress in her address to the nation on the eve of the 80th Independence Day.
Addressing the nation, Murmu said 65% of India’s population is below the age of 35, describing the country’s youth as its “most valuable asset” and highlighting their role in entrepreneurship, space research, innovation and job creation.
“Our students are the architects of India’s future. Just as the government and society must remain united to ensure national security, everyone must contribute through joint and concerted efforts to safeguard the present and future of our students,” she said. “Public examinations become gateways to the opportunities for our students. The Government is undertaking comprehensive steps to reform these examinations. The objectives of these reforms are to completely curb the use of unfair means in public examinations, make the examination system more transparent, more secure, and more trustworthy for the youth.”
Following student protests over the NEET-UG paper leak, the Centre amended the 2024 anti-cheating law, enacting the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026, which came into force on July 31. It provides tougher penalties, including up to 10 years’ imprisonment and ₹50 lakh fine for individual offenders, and up to ₹10 crore for organised syndicates. It also includes provisions for Special Fast Track Courts to ensure speedy, day-to-day trials of exam malpractice cases, with investigations mandated to be completed within two months. The government has also formed a high-powered exam-reforms task force chaired by Nandan Nilekani to formulate comprehensive, tech-driven, and leak-proof exam-reforms recommendations to restore systemic transparency and public trust.

headline: Odisha floods worsen as heavy rain inundates villages, roads in north
full_text:
Odisha floods worsen as heavy rain inundates villages, roads in north
Heavy rain has worsened flooding across northern Odisha, with rivers swelling, villages inundated and roads disrupted as the IMD warns of more rain.
Flooding in several northern Odisha districts threatened to worsen on Friday as heavy rain pushed up river levels, inundated villages and farmland, disrupted road links and forced residents to take shelter on rooftops and embankments.
The Central Water Commission (CWC) warned of a flash-flood risk in 11 districts, while the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast heavy rain in parts of northern Odisha through August 17 and in western districts until August 15. Balasore, Mayurbhanj, Keonjhar, Sundargarh and several other districts have been affected by the latest spell of rain.
In Mayurbhanj, flooding in the Budhabalanga river submerged several areas of Betanati block, affecting 16 gram panchayats and inundating farmland, roads and villages.
Near the Nakhara bridge, about three feet of floodwater was flowing over the old and vulnerable structure, bringing traffic on the busy Baishinga-Manatri-Udala road to a halt. Vehicles were stranded on both sides of the flooded stretch.
The situation was also critical in Jajpur district, where the fourth flood of the season in the Baitarani river has inundated villages in Dasarathpur block.
The flooding has compounded the woes of hundreds of families who have faced repeated inundation for nearly a month. The first flood occurred on July 6 after the Kani river breached at Kantapada. During the second flood on July 28, two breaches occurred at Dovabil Patana and another in the Baitarani ring embankment near Jayantara Mahapatra Sahi. A third flood on August 8 caused repaired breaches to give way again. Some families have still not returned home and are living on rooftops or under makeshift tarpaulin shelters near the river embankment.
In Keonjhar, heavy rainfall disrupted road communication in Telkoi block, with floodwater flowing over bridges and roads at several locations. The Telkoi-Jagamohanpur road was cut off after water from the Hanumantia canal rose to about three feet over the road near the Kenduleaf Office, disrupting connectivity between Telkoi and Jagamohanpur and access to National Highway 49.
The latest rainfall has also affected other parts of northern Odisha. Five blocks of Balasore district were affected by heavy rain, while parts of Baripada town in Mayurbhanj were flooded as the Budhabalanga rose, with water entering wards 7 and 8. Torrential rain also flooded roads in Shamakhunta block, prompting the district administration to begin evacuation operations.
Almost the entire Rourkela city experienced severe waterlogging, with Civil Township, Basanti Colony, Chhend Colony, Railway Colony and Power House among the worst affected. The city received 105.4 mm of rain between 8:30 a.m. and 5:30 p.m. on Thursday.
The IMD Bhubaneswar, meanwhile, warned of a flash-flood risk in Balasore, Bargarh, Bhadrak, Deogarh, Jharsuguda, Kendrapara, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, Sambalpur, Sonepur and Sundargarh as a well-marked low-pressure area over coastal West Bengal and adjoining Bangladesh and the northwest Bay of Bengal moved northwestwards and intensified into a depression.
“It is very likely to move northwestwards across Gangetic West Bengal and Jharkhand during next 24 hours. Under its influence, heavy rainfall will occur in part of North Odisha till August 17 and a few districts of Western Odisha till August 15,” said Manorama Mohanty, director of the Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre.
The IMD forecast heavy to very heavy rain in parts of Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Bargarh and Sambalpur on Friday, with heavy rain also expected in Balasore, Deogarh, Angul, Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, Sonepur, Boudh, Nuapada and Balangir. Further heavy rainfall was forecast in Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Bargarh, Nuapada and Balangir on Saturday.
