headline: 'To completely curb use of unfair means': President Murmu underlines push to protect exams
full_text:
'To completely curb use of unfair means': President Murmu underlines push to protect exams
Murmu described the country’s youth as its “most valuable asset” and highlighting their role in entrepreneurship, space research, innovation and job creation.
Public examinations are “gateways to the opportunities” available to students, and the government is undertaking “comprehensive steps” to curb unfair practices and make the system more transparent, secure and trustworthy, President Droupadi Murmu said on Friday, as she highlighted the opportunities opening up for India’s youth and outlined the country’s progress in her address to the nation on the eve of the 80th Independence Day.
Track live updates on Independence Day celebrations
Addressing the nation, Murmu said 65% of India’s population is below the age of 35, describing the country’s youth as its “most valuable asset” and highlighting their role in entrepreneurship, space research, innovation and job creation.
“Our students are the architects of India’s future. Just as the government and society must remain united to ensure national security, everyone must contribute through joint and concerted efforts to safeguard the present and future of our students,” she said. “Public examinations become gateways to the opportunities for our students. The Government is undertaking comprehensive steps to reform these examinations. The objectives of these reforms are to completely curb the use of unfair means in public examinations, make the examination system more transparent, more secure, and more trustworthy for the youth.”
Anti-paper leak bill after NEET row
Following student protests over the NEET-UG paper leak, the Centre amended the 2024 anti-cheating law, enacting the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026, which came into force on July 31.
Also read: President Murmu on Indus Water Treaty suspension: ‘Decisive step in interest of nation, farmers'
It provides tougher penalties, including up to 10 years’ imprisonment and ₹50 lakh fine for individual offenders, and up to ₹10 crore for organised syndicates. It also includes provisions for Special Fast Track Courts to ensure speedy, day-to-day trials of exam malpractice cases, with investigations mandated to be completed within two months. The government has also formed a high-powered exam-reforms task force chaired by Nandan Nilekani to formulate comprehensive, tech-driven, and leak-proof exam-reforms recommendations to restore systemic transparency and public trust.
Murmu also pointed to new avenues opening up for young people through government initiatives and emerging economic activities, including self-employment, entrepreneurship and the expanding start-up ecosystem, urging them to explore these paths to success.
She said India’s young population was talented, committed and skilled, and cited the example of a recent successful rocket launch by a young team whose average age was 28.
On July 18, the Hyderabad-based space startup Skyroot Aerospace—driven by a young team with an average age of just 28—successfully executed “Mission Aagaman,” launching India’s first privately developed orbital rocket ‘Vikram-1’ from Sriharikota and placing multiple payloads into a 450 km low Earth orbit.
Murmu said efforts to promote sports were also aimed at youth development and nation-building, with the government making “unprecedented investments” through initiatives such as Khelo India.
The President also highlighted the growing participation of women in education, entrepreneurship and leadership. More than 100 million women are members of self-help groups, she said, adding that the target of creating three crore “Lakhpati Didis” had been achieved and the country was now moving towards creating another 30 million. “In the recently concluded Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, women have won 8 out of India’s total tally of 13 gold medals. Our women are increasingly achieving economic self-reliance. More than 10 crore women are members of Self Help Groups,” she said.
The President also devoted a significant part of her address to national security, terrorism and internal security.
Recalling Operation Sindoor, launched in May last year in response to the Pahalgam terror attack, which killed 26 people, Murmu said the operation demonstrated the capability of the armed forces to act with precision and sent “a clear and firm message to terrorists and those who support them”.
Lauding India’s decision to suspend the Indus Waters Treaty on April 23, 2025, a day after Pahalgam terror, Murmu said, “Suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty with the country that harbours terrorism is a decisive step in the interest of our nation, especially the farmers.”
Murmu also stated that making India “Naxal free” was a major achievement, saying regions once affected by Naxalism were now witnessing enthusiasm and development. She cited the Bastar Olympics and Bastar Pandum as examples of growing participation in sports and cultural activities in the region.
On the broader development agenda, the President said India was moving towards the goal of a “Viksit Bharat” by 2047, with the government seeking to ensure that the benefits of development reach every citizen.
She highlighted the expansion of highways, waterways, railways and airways, saying modern infrastructure was creating opportunities for enterprises, generating employment and boosting investor confidence.
Murmu also underlined India’s digital transformation, saying more than half of the world’s real-time digital transactions now take place in India. She said the country’s economic progress, digital infrastructure and Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan had strengthened the foundations of economic progress and national security.
The President also paid tribute to freedom fighters and recalled Partition, saying the country must remember those who lost their lives or were displaced during the violence. She also invoked the legacy of social reformers Mahatma Jyotiba Phule and Savitribai Phule, highlighting their contributions to social justice, education, women’s empowerment and equality.
She concluded her address by calling for an “all-inclusive spirit of patriotism” and urged citizens to devote themselves to transforming independent India into a developed nation.
The address was preceded and followed by the National Song Vande Mataram and the National Anthem.

headline: Manipur health centre detects syphilis in pregnant woman, prevents mother-to-child risk
full_text:
Manipur health centre detects syphilis in pregnant woman, prevents mother-to-child risk
A routine antenatal check-up at a telehealth-supported primary health centre in Manipur detected syphilis in a pregnant woman and started treatment. The case underlines how digital primary care can curb congenital infection risks in remote areas.
Digital healthcare support helped detect and begin treatment for syphilis in a 25-year-old pregnant woman during a routine antenatal check-up at a primary health centre in a remote part of Manipur, a healthcare provider said.
The intervention reduced the risk of the infection being passed on to her unborn child.
The woman, from Miran village, visited an Apollo TeleHealth-supported primary health centre, where routine pregnancy screening found syphilis, a bacterial sexually transmitted infection that can pass from a mother to her baby if it is not treated.
Her laboratory report was then validated through Apollo TeleHealth's digital quality assurance system.
After the result was confirmed, she was counselled, referred for confirmatory testing and her treatment was started. She has received the first of the recommended weekly Benzathine Penicillin injections.
Her husband also tested positive and was given treatment to prevent reinfection.
Apollo TeleHealth said congenital syphilis can lead to miscarriage, stillbirth, premature birth, newborn death and lifelong physical and developmental disabilities.
An obstetric ultrasound has been advised for the woman as she could not recall her exact last menstrual period.
She will continue to be monitored at the e-PHC, with repeat serological testing planned after treatment to assess her response.
The initiative, run by Apollo TeleHealth in partnership with the Manipur government, has served more than 6,000 patients and facilitated over 10,000 teleconsultations, besides supporting more than 1,500 antenatal care visits.
Women account for 56 per cent of its beneficiaries and men 44 per cent.
The digitally enabled primary health centres operate in Borobekra, Henglep, Senvon and Thanlon, with doctors, nurses, pharmacists and laboratory technicians on site and specialist support provided through teleconsultations.
The case showed how digital healthcare support at primary health centres in Manipur helped identify syphilis in pregnancy, begin treatment quickly and continue follow-up care while also treating the woman's husband to reduce the risk of reinfection.

headline: UP man gets life imprisonment for rape, murder of 16-year-old student
full_text:
UP man gets life imprisonment for rape, murder of 16-year-old student
A special POCSO court in Mainpuri sentenced a 22-year-old man to life for abducting, raping and killing a Class 11 student. The court acquitted his father and a friend, underscoring how the verdict turned on the evidence presented.
A special POCSO court in Uttar Pradesh's Mainpuri has sentenced a 22-year-old man to rigorous imprisonment for life for the rape and murder of a 16-year-old Class 11 student in the Bewar area last year. The court also acquitted two other accused in the case, saying there was not enough evidence against them, according to the prosecution.
Special POCSO Court Judge Jehendra Pal Singh convicted Karan alias Alok after hearing the prosecution and defence, state prosecutor Sheilendri Rajput told PTI. The two others acquitted were the convict's father, Jetendra, and his friend.
According to the prosecution, the girl left her home for college on May 15, 2025. On the way, the accused and another man, both from the same village, allegedly intercepted and abducted her to a secluded place, where she was raped.
The prosecution said the girl resisted and raised an alarm, after which she was strangled to death. Rajput said that after the killing, the man allegedly called his father and the two took the body to Kansepur village, where they allegedly hanged it from a gular tree using her chunri to make the death appear to be suicide.
The following day, the man's father allegedly informed the girl's father that she had died by suicide. The girl's father then lodged an FIR at Bewar police station against the main accused, his friend and father, after which the police filed a chargesheet against all three following an investigation.
The prosecution examined witnesses and produced documentary evidence before the court. After considering the evidence and arguments, the court convicted Karan alias Alok and sentenced him to rigorous imprisonment for life, while acquitting his father and friend for want of sufficient evidence, Rajput said.
The case centred on the abduction, rape and killing of the teenager on her way to college, and ended with the court awarding life imprisonment to the main accused and acquitting the two co-accused due to insufficient evidence.

headline: Gurupadagouda Sanganagouda Patil, four-time Congress MLA from Ron in Gadag district, was unanimously elected Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly on Friday. He is the 18th Speaker of the Assembly since 1972.
full_text:
Gurupadagouda Sanganagouda Patil, four-time Congress MLA from Ron in Gadag district, was unanimously elected Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly on Friday. He is the 18th Speaker of the Assembly since 1972.
Popularly known as G.S. Patil, his name was proposed by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and seconded by Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara.
From a political family
The 78-year-old Mr. Patil comes from an agrarian political family. His elder brother, R.S. Patil, was a former MP who represented the Bagalkot constituency, while another brother, B.S. Patil, served as Chief Secretary of Karnataka during the S.M. Krishna government. He contested eight Assembly elections and won four. Mr. B.S. Patil was present at the officers’ gallery in the House today.
A sportsperson, the newly elected Speaker was a wicketkeeper-batsman and played for the Mysore State team. He married Annapoorna in 1974 and has two sons and a daughter. His elder son, Prashanth, is a doctor, while his other son, Mithun, is a civil engineer.
More than a dozen members spoke on Mr. Patil’s elevation as Speaker, describing him as a person who has donned many hats with equal ease. Besides being a politician, he is a farmer, educationist, sportsperson and cooperative leader.
‘Police Patil’
Mr. Patil, whose extended family is popularly known as the “Police Patil” or “Ron Gowdru” family, is the chairman of the Rajiv Gandhi Educational Institutions and is associated with various organisations in Gadag district. He has also held several positions in the cooperative sector.
Former Minister H.K. Patil, MLA from Gadag, noted that prominent personalities such as Bharat Ratna awardee and Hindustani vocalist Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, classical musician Pandit Puttaraj Gawai and his father, K.H. Patil, hailed from Gadag district. Former Indian cricketer Sunil Joshi is also from the district.
Pro-tem Speaker T.B. Jayachandra, who presided over the proceedings, declared Mr. Patil elected after a voice vote.
Amid thumping of desks by members, Mr. Shivakumar, Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok, Mr. Jayachandra and Dr. Parameshwara accompanied Mr. Patil to the Speaker’s chair.
BJP boycotts
The BJP boycotted the election, protesting against the Congress high command’s decision to communicate Mr. Patil’s name on AICC letterhead. Mr. Ashok said the Speaker was elected by the Assembly and not the AICC, and appealed to Mr. Patil to discharge his duties impartially.
The post had fallen vacant following the resignation of U.T. Khader ahead of his induction into the Shivakumar-led Council of Ministers on June 3.
Perhaps for the first time, presiding officers of both Houses hail from north Karnataka.

headline: Would the world look different if we had more women leading us? More parliamentarians, more scientists and more authors, whose voices were heard?
full_text:
Would the world look different if we had more women leading us? More parliamentarians, more scientists and more authors, whose voices were heard?
Yes, our world would look significantly different and better. The absence of patriarchal systems would reshape societal structures, relationships, and life itself.
But the truth is Patriarchy has deep roots in our minds and has been instrumental in creating gender imbalances in society for centuries.
#CancelPatriarchy is a new, thought-provoking initiative by The Times of India that questions the normalisation of this practice and encourages introspection. It makes us stop and think about how we as individuals can help cancel such behaviour.

The Aggarwal family, including three generations, perished in the blaze. Their abandoned Mercedes outside the gutted building stands as a silent testament to the unimaginable loss.
